title: Iran says ship sank in Hormuz
body: Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said Wednesday that a ship caught fire and sank in the Strait of Hormuz because of a mine, while British security firm Vanguard also reported a sinking. “A container ship attempting to cross the Strait of Hormuz using an unauthorised and dangerous shipping lane struck a mine that exploded,” said the navy of the Revolutionary Guards, the ideological arm of Iran’s military. Images released by the Guards show a plume of black smoke rising from a ship, while dozens of containers that have fallen into the sea float on the water. The Guards said the ship was carrying more than 2,500 containers. Iran claims control of the strait, through which one-fifth of the world’s hydrocarbons passed before the Middle East war. It regularly targets ships it accuses of transiting without authorisation, while the US has imposed its own blockade on Iran’s ports. According to Vanguard, the GFS Pride, a Singapore-flagged container ship, was struck by a projectile on Tuesday and sank. It was not clear if the two statements referred to the same ship. Vanguard reported three other ships struck on Tuesday, with two of them continuing on their way and the fate of the third unknown. The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Centre (UKMTO) reported Wednesday that two container ships were struck on Tuesday by projectiles but continued on their way after sustaining only minor damage. UKMTO earlier reported two other attacks on Tuesday targeting a tanker and a container ship, without specifying whether they had caused damage or casualties. The war was triggered in late February by US-Israeli strikes against Iran. The post Iran says ship sank in Hormuz appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Meta removes 3.7 million accounts in international fraud crackdown linked to UK, US victims
body: Nineteen people have been arrested in Sasaabi, in the Accra Region, as part of an international crackdown on suspected online scam operations targeting victims in the United Kingdom, the United States and other countries. The operation, hosted by the United Kingdom’s National Crime Agency (NCA), brought together more than 100 representatives from law enforcement agencies and technology companies to disrupt fraud networks operating across Africa. Authorities seized 303 electronic devices during the operation in Ghana, while 117 people identified as suspected victims of human trafficking are awaiting return to Nigeria. Nine additional arrests were made in Nigeria’s Delta State, where officers seized six laptops, 35 mobile phones and 12 routers. The NCA said the arrests were part of a wider effort targeting suspected fraudsters and the digital infrastructure they use to reach victims through social media and other online platforms. Millions of accounts removed The operation, held from October 6 to 9, involved law enforcement agencies from 15 organisations and representatives from 15 technology companies, including Meta, Microsoft and Google. It was the fourth initiative of its kind and the first hosted by the NCA. Participants included officers from the Ghanaian Cyber Security Authority, the Nigeria Police Force, the United States Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and other international agencies. Meta removed more than 3.7 million accounts, Pages and Groups associated with scams targeting people in the US, UK and elsewhere. More than 1,110 West African Facebook and Instagram accounts linked to information supplied by Report Fraud were disabled. A further 490 Facebook accounts and more than 490 advertising accounts identified through OCC Data Enforcement were also disabled. OCC Data Domain Enforcement additionally disabled more than 380 scam domains assessed as potentially linked to those identified during the operation. Private-sector partners identified a total of $11 million in funds that could potentially be frozen. Earlier raids in Ghana The NCA said Ghanaian law enforcement agencies had also led operations against suspected scam centres in the same location at the end of September. Those raids resulted in multiple arrests and the seizure of 85 mobile phones and 44 laptops. Several people initially taken into custody were subsequently identified as suspected victims of trafficking who may have been coerced into criminal activity. The operation was led by Ghana’s Cyber Security Authority, with support from the NCA, Ghana Police Service, the FBI and Nigeria’s Economic and Financial Crimes Commission. The latest international operation involved the sharing of information to identify suspected fraud enablers and locate people allegedly operating the schemes. Report Fraud worked with Meta to provide data to identify accounts and other infrastructure linked to suspected fraud. The NCA said law enforcement agencies and technology companies collaborated to trace suspects, leading to arrests. Officials stress international cooperation Nick Sharp, Deputy Director of Fraud at the NCA, said cross-border partnerships were essential to tackling fraud networks that operated internationally. “Fraud is a global problem and it takes partnership working across international boundaries to tackle it,” he said. He said the agency would continue working with international and private-sector partners to pursue fraudsters and disrupt the online infrastructure they relied on. Meta’s Vice President and Deputy General Counsel, Chris Sonderby, said the company had removed more than 3.7 million accounts, Pages and Groups and shared information on more than 30 suspected scam centres, contributing to arrests and the identification of trafficking victims. FBI Director Kash Patel said the operation had resulted in arrests across multiple African countries, the seizure of hundreds of devices and the identification of at least $11 million in potentially freezable funds. The UK government said its planned Online Crime Centre would build on such joint operations to dismantle criminal networks and bring offenders to justice. Warning signs of investment fraud Authorities have urged the public to be alert to possible investment scams, particularly online offers that promise guaranteed returns or unusually low-risk investments. Other warning signs include endorsements from celebrities or well-known figures, invitations to join exclusive investment groups, and requests to move conversations to instant messaging or social media platforms. People should also be wary of anyone asking them to keep an investment secret from family or friends, pay taxes or release fees before withdrawing funds, or invest more money under continued pressure.

title: Ukraine races to field faster interceptors as Russia hammers its energy grid
body: KYIV, Ukraine — Russia is still using fast jet-powered drones to batter Ukraine’s energy facilities, bridges and other critical infrastructure at speeds beyond the reach of most of Kyiv’s drone interceptors, despite U.S. President Donald Trump’s unilateral announcement on Sunday of an energy ceasefire between the two countries. Russia began using the jets heavily in July, when their numbers jumped fivefold from the previous month. They can now reach speeds of up to 373 mph (600 km/h) — more than three times the speed of the propeller-driven Geran-2 drones they evolved from — far exceeding the top velocity of the average Ukrainian interceptor drone, air force officials told lawmakers last week. To stop the drones, Ukraine must instead rely on F-16s, newly installed machine gun turrets that use artificial intelligence to aim and costly air-defense missiles that are in short supply globally. “Ukraine did not strike Russian oil refining and the energy sector in general for two days after the American president announced a ceasefire in the energy sector. But Russia did not listen to the American president,” Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy wrote after jets seriously damaged a gas production facility in the northeastern Kharkiv region on Sunday night. Russia launched 167 missiles and drones overnight Tuesday into Wednesday, including 77 jet-powered drones, which officials said struck one of Kyiv’s main power plants and left 600,000 without power. Ukraine’s Air Force says they are beginning to field more effective countermeasures, but with Russia continuing to optimize the design of jet-powered drones to destroy critical infrastructure, the development of jets and anti-jet interceptors has become the latest neck-and-neck technology race on the battlefield. Iran shipped Russia its first Shahed-131 and Shahed-136 drones in mid-August 2022, and Moscow rebranded them the Geran-1 and Geran-2 and was firing them at Ukrainian civilian infrastructure by that October. Those propeller-driven drones were slow enough for Ukraine to build an economical defense around mobile fire teams and cheap interceptor drones rather than spending scarce missiles on every Shahed, and in February the interceptors accounted for more than 70% of Shahed downings over Kyiv . The jet-powered Gerans are outrunning that defense, and Russia has since stopped building the slower Geran-3 and ramped up production of the Geran-4, which cruises at 217 to 311 mph (350 to 500 km/h), and the missile-shaped Geran-5, which carries a 90-kilogram (198-pound) warhead, Militarnyi reported in August, citing Ukraine’s military intelligence agency, known as HUR. “The Geran-5 flies 150km/h faster than the Geran-4, so the goal is to intercept from the front rather than the rear — a much harder problem to solve,” an engineer at a Ukrainian defense contractor told the Kyiv Independent . And they are still getting faster, with the Air Force projecting speeds of 500 to 560 mph (800 to 900 km/h), though none have been recorded yet, its deputy commander, Col. Yurii Cherevashenko, told a parliamentary commission Oct. 6. A Geran-4 version Russia began flying this autumn is built to take out infrastructure, navigating by a U.S.-made magnetometer and an optical system and carrying a new warhead designed to cut bridges and power line supports, HUR said in an Oct. 5 statement . The new 88-pound (40-kilogram) warhead “was created specifically to destroy high-voltage pylons and iron bridge structures,” Serhii “Flash” Beskrestnov, an EW expert and adviser to Zelenskyy, wrote on Telegram Sept. 30 when Russia was first spotted using the upgrade on a jet drone. These optimized Russian jet drones hit Kyiv’s South Bridge, which carries cars and metro trains across the Dnipro River, at least five times on Oct. 1 and 2, once exploding near a pier as a train crossed overhead, then struck the city’s North Bridge on Oct. 3, officials said. Ukrainian interceptors stopped roughly 90% of the older propeller-driven drones , but against the jets, the interception rate has been significantly lower. “Initially, we saw a very low interception rate in Ukraine. It then rose to more than 30%, and in recent nights it has increased to over 50%,” Matthias Lehna, vice president of German drone maker Quantum Systems, told Ukrinform last week. Air force officials reported downing 77% of incoming jet-powered drones on Tuesday night. Ukraine put its first jet interceptor, the Alexa Spatium, into service only on Aug. 21, and a handful of other prototypes, including Wild Hornets’ STING S and SkyFall’s P1-SUN Jetkiller, have successfully downed a small number of Geran-5s, according to officials speaking to the Kyiv Independent. Fourteen companies are flight-testing jet interceptors with the Air Force, and three have shown promising results, but the deputy air force commander said officials don’t expect the jet interceptors to be delivered at the scale Ukraine needs until the end of November at the earliest. Jet drones already make up approximately 40% of the drones Russia launches and the Air Force expects that share to reach up to 80% of total attacks.

title: From Reading Culture to Reading Competence: What PISA 2025 Tells Kazakhstan
body: The Astana Times provides news and information from Kazakhstan and around the world. Kazakhstan has set itself an ambitious goal: to become a reading nation. In May, President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev signed a decree placing the development of reading culture among the country’s national priorities. The policy includes new libraries, a national digital library platform and a Reading Nation concept for 2027–2031. These are welcome developments. The latest international evidence also suggests that Kazakhstan needs to think carefully about what it means to be a strong reader. Michael Jones. Photo credit: Michael Jones’ personal archive The latest OECD PISA results for Kazakhstan provide an uncomfortable starting point. In PISA 2025, Kazakhstan’s average reading score was 385, compared with an OECD average of 461. Only 36% of Kazakh 15-year-olds reached at least Level 2 in reading, compared with 69% across the OECD. Almost no students in Kazakhstan reached the highest reading levels. The more revealing number may be 36%. At Level 2, students should be able to identify the main idea of a moderately long text, locate information using several criteria and reflect on the purpose of a text when directed to do so. Higher levels demand increasingly complex skills, including comparing sources, recognising implicit meaning, separating fact from opinion and judging the reliability of information. PISA therefore gives us a picture of how confidently young people can use reading to make sense of unfamiliar information. Kazakhstan’s reading difficulties are also longstanding. According to the OECD, reading performance has remained relatively stable since the country first participated in PISA in 2009. Kazakhstan scored 390 that year. Sixteen years later, it scored 385. The pattern stretches across several generations of students and predates the disruption caused by the COVID-19 pandemic and the recent arrival of generative artificial intelligence. Research conducted inside Kazakhstan offers some clues about what may be happening. Akhmetova, Imambayeva and Csapó examined more than 1,500 Grade 6 and Grade 8 students and found something that complicates the common claim that young people simply lack interest in reading. Around 85% of the Grade 6 students and 79% of the Grade 8 students reported that they enjoyed reading. Yet the relationship between positive attitudes towards reading and actual reading achievement was relatively weak. Encouraging young people to pick up books clearly has value. Frequency alone tells us little about how readers respond when a text becomes difficult, unfamiliar or open to several interpretations. Students also need strategies for deciding what deserves attention, how different pieces of information fit together and when a claim should be questioned. Their related work on reading strategies also identified weaknesses in how students approach texts, including deciding which sections deserve closer attention and using information from tables and figures to support understanding. Modern reading increasingly requires young people to move between an article, a graph, a website and several competing claims before deciding what information can be trusted. Evidence from teachers presents a more encouraging picture. In 2025, Sarmurzin and colleagues surveyed 117 Kazakh literature teachers and interviewed experienced practitioners, finding a growing emphasis on reading comprehension, critical thinking, technology and more student-centred approaches. Teachers also identified continuing problems with curriculum coherence and the relationship between some reading materials and students’ everyday experiences. Teacher preparation appears less settled. Research published in 2026 involving 254 final-year preservice teachers from five Kazakh universities found that 72% were uncertain about the distinction between functional literacy and traditional reading comprehension. The researchers also identified limited preparation in informational texts and critical digital reading, particularly among students preparing to teach Kazakh language and literature. Greater professional support would help teachers respond to an increasingly complex reading environment. University programmes and professional development can give teachers more opportunities to work with inference, source comparison, evidence evaluation and critical digital literacy. Released PISA tasks can also show the kinds of reading processes students find difficult and provide useful material for lesson design and discussion. There is an important limit to how far this should go. PISA measures particular forms of reading, and education should avoid turning those measures into a complete definition of what good reading looks like. Teaching students primarily to succeed on PISA-style tasks could narrow the curriculum and encourage another form of test preparation without necessarily creating more thoughtful or engaged readers. Reading also involves imagination, curiosity, emotional engagement, interpretation, enjoyment and the experience of spending time with ideas that do not lead towards a correct answer on an assessment. PISA is most useful as a diagnostic tool. Its results can reveal weaknesses in areas such as inference, comprehension and source evaluation, while reading education itself should remain considerably broader. The aim should be to develop young people who can approach many kinds of texts with confidence, from novels and poetry to news reports, scientific arguments and digital information. Kazakhstan could also make reading a clearer responsibility across the school curriculum. A history student comparing conflicting accounts of an event is practising reading. A science student deciding whether evidence supports a conclusion is doing the same, as is a geography student combining information from a map, graph and written report. Across these subjects, questions such as “How do I know this?”, “What evidence supports the claim?”, “What has been left out?” and “Which source should I trust?” can help students treat reading as a way of thinking rather than simply retrieving information. Schools also need to protect space for sustained reading. Young people now encounter enormous quantities of written material through social media, messaging platforms, websites and increasingly AI systems. Much of this information arrives in short fragments. Regular opportunities to stay with longer and more demanding texts, discuss them, annotate them and return to difficult passages should remain part of school life. Sustained attention is itself becoming an important educational skill. Generative AI adds another layer to this reading environment. AI can summarise a chapter, explain an argument and produce an answer within seconds. Students need strong skills for deciding whether that summary is accurate, what it has left out and whether the evidence supports the answer. One useful classroom activity might involve comparing an original article with an AI-generated summary. Students could identify missing qualifications, check claims against the original source and discuss how the meaning has changed. Used in this way, AI can support deeper reading. Kazakhstan’s 2026 decree on developing reading culture already provides a framework for moving in this direction, particularly through its emphasis on reading in the era of artificial intelligence. Continued investment in books, libraries and positive reading cultures remains valuable. The next stage should connect that access more directly with how young people understand, question and use what they read. A reading nation needs citizens who can stay with difficult ideas, recognise weak evidence, compare competing accounts and reach informed conclusions. It also needs readers who find pleasure in language, become absorbed in stories, encounter unfamiliar perspectives and sometimes read without being asked to extract a measurable skill from the experience. These abilities and experiences develop gradually through years of purposeful reading across classrooms, subjects and languages. The PISA score of 385 should be treated as more than a position in an international ranking. It offers a useful warning about the depth of reading skills many young people currently possess and gives policymakers and educators a clearer sense of where attention is needed. Kazakhstan has already committed itself to becoming a reading nation. The next stage is to create the conditions in which young people can read widely, read carefully, enjoy what they read and learn to think for themselves through the process. The author is Michael Jones, an writing and communications instructor, School of Social Science and Humanities, Nazarbayev University (Astana). Disclaimer: The views and opinions expressed in this article are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect the position of The Astana Times. The post From Reading Culture to Reading Competence: What PISA 2025 Tells Kazakhstan appeared first on The Astana Times .

title: Russian oil exports fall to 6.52 mln bpd in September, revenues rise to $17.67 bln
body:
MOSCOW, October 14. /TASS/. Russia’s exports of oil and petroleum products fell by 10,000 barrels per day (bpd) in September 2026 to 6.52 million bpd, according to data from the International Energy Agency (IEA). Meanwhile, monthly export revenues rose by $3.6 billion from August 2026 to reach $17.67 billion, driven by surging oil prices.
Russian crude oil shipments increased by 60,000 bpd in September, while exports of petroleum products decreased by 80,000 bpd.
Revenues from crude oil exports in September totaled $14.5 billion (up $3.15 billion from August), while revenues from petroleum product exports amounted to $3.16 billion (an increase of $440 million compared to August).
Additionally, the IEA report notes that the price of Russian Urals crude (FOB Primorsk) surged by $28.29 to $94.3 per barrel, marking the second-highest level since February 2022.
Compared to September 2025, Russia's oil export revenues in September 2026 were $4.32 billion higher.

title: Batalhadzhin community linked to international terrorist organizations — FSB
body:
MOSCOW, October 14. /TASS/. The "Community of Followers of Batal Hajji Belkhoroev - Batalhadzhins," which Russia's Supreme Court tagged as a terrorist organization today, has been linked to international terrorist organizations and illegal armed groups since the 1990s, the FSB and the Interior Ministry said.
On Wednesday, the Supreme Court recognized the community as a terrorist organization and banned its activities in Russia.
"The court took into account the materials indicating that members of the wird, as a closed pseudo-religious movement, have been interacting with participants in illegal armed groups and international terrorist organizations since the 1990s and up to the present day, adopting their methods and providing assistance to terrorist and extremist structures," the FSB noted.
The Interior Ministry said the community members help other international terrorist organizations and illegal armed groups, and participate in terrorist and extremist activities.
The Supreme Court ruled to recognize this organization as terroristic based on evidence of its terrorist activities collected by the FSB in coordination with the Prosecutor General’s Office, the Investigative Committee, and the Interior Ministry.
"Within the framework of criminal cases investigated by the Investigative Committee, data was obtained on the involvement of members of this organization in terrorist crimes," the Investigative Committee noted.
According to the FSB, the Interior Ministry, and the Investigative Committee, in 2004, several members of the community participated in an armed attack on government bodies in Ingushetia killing 78 people and wounding more than 100. Sixty·eight defendants in the criminal case were convicted in the crime, while law enforcement continues to try to track down those who were able to flee and escape justice. In 2019, terrorist attacks were carried out in Moscow, resulting in the deaths of Ibragim Yeldzharkiyev, head of the Center for Countering Extremism of the Interior Ministry for the Republic of Ingushetia, his brother, and an employee of the National Guard. The Investigative Committee established that followers from the organization were also involved in these crimes.
In 2009, the Kartoyev brothers, members of the Belkhoroev community, assisted terrorists in the bombing of the Nevsky Express train, which killed 27 people.
As part of the investigation into a criminal case concerning the terrorist attack at the Crocus City Hall, it was established that the individuals who provided weapons to the perpetrators of the crime belong to the religious movement associated with Batal Hajji Belkhoroev, including Dzhabrail Aushev and Husen Medov, who are serving life in prison.
The Batalhadzhins were involved in a terrorist attack organized by Ukraine’s special services, in which the head of the radiation, chemical and biological protection forces (RCBZ) Lieutenant General Igor Kirillov was killed.
"Wird members Ramazan Padiyev and Batukhan Tochiyev assisted the special services of Ukraine in the terrorist act committed against the head of the RCBZ of the armed forces of the Russian Federation, Lieutenant General I. Kirillov," the FSB said. The Investigative Committee added that Padiyev and Tochiyev helped the perpetrator of this terrorist act. "This crime was prepared for a long time on the territory of Ukraine. The accomplices are serving long prison terms," the Investigative Committee said.
The FSB and the Interior Ministry said that the Batalhadzhins actively assisted Ukrainian armed groups engaged in combat operations against the Russian army. "Members of the community participated in supporting terrorist and extremist groups engaged in combat operations against the armed forces of the Russian Federation on the territory of Ukraine," the FSB said. The Interior Ministry also said that "there is reliable information about the active assistance provided by the organization to the activities of Ukrainian armed groups that oppose the armed forces of the Russian Federation."
The Investigative Committee, the Interior Ministry, and the FSB said that criminal groups belonging to the community continue to commit various crimes, including murders, robberies, and property theft. "Thus, in Moscow, a criminal case is being investigated against several followers of the movement who are involved in murders, extortion, and kidnapping," the Investigative Committee said. In Ingushetia, a local resident supplied forged documents to the wanted members of the community.
"In this regard, law enforcement agencies are carrying out measures to identify, suppress, and solve all crimes committed by members of the ‘Community of Followers of Batal Hajji Belkhoroev -- Batalhadzhins,’" the FSB said.
The Investigative Committee said that "the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation contains a separate article that establishes liability for participating in the activities of an organization recognized as terrorist under the legislation of the Russian Federation."
The Interior Ministry said this concerns Article 205.5 of the Criminal Code (organizing the activities of a terrorist organization and participating in the activities of such an organization).
Thus, as explained by the Investigative Committee, the Interior Ministry and the FSB actions related to financing, managing, or providing any other assistance to the leaders and participants of the community entail criminal liability and punishment, up to and including life imprisonment.
Batal Hajji is an offshoot of the Qadiri order, one of the influential Sufi brotherhoods. It got its name after its founder, Batal-Hajji Belkhoroev, an (Ingush) Sufi sheikh of the late 19th - early 20th century. It is a closed organization with strict discipline. Although its direct ties to organizations such as Al·Qaeda and the Islamic State (terrorist organizations banned in Russia) were not established, the so·called "combat wing of the Ingush wird (brotherhood) of the Batalhadzhins was put on the federal list of terrorist organizations under a November 28, 2022 decision of the Southern District Military Court. The charges included blood feuds, arms smuggling, extortion, and corruption. According to some legal experts, the community is more reminiscent of a criminal·clan structure with a religious veneer and motives driven by revenge than an ideological jihadist movement.
Several leaders of the Batalhadzhin group were convicted (Yakub Belkhoroev, ten years for embezzlement and misappropriation) or are on the federal wanted list, such as Akhmed Belkhoroev, who, according to law enforcement officials, is one of the leaders of the combat wing. Another active member of the group, Ilyas Belkhoroev, according to open sources, left for Ukraine in 2015, and joined the Dzhokhar Dudayev Volunteer Battalion in 2021. In August 2026, it was reported that he died in prison in Poland, where he was accused of supplying weapons to that country. Poland never confirmed this.

title: No evidence of suspected plague outbreak in Russia, says WHO
body: By Sebastine Obasi After the suspected plague outbreak in the Irkutsk region of Siberia made headlines in global media, on Saturday the World Health Organization (WHO) has officially confirmed that it had found no evidence of ongoing transmission. Contrary to media reports, no additional cases of infection have been identified. Russia confirmed the death of an employee at the Irkutsk anti-plague research institute from pneumonia of unknown etiology. Contacts, numbering approximately 200 people, were placed under medical supervision and tested. Tests for dangerous pathogens, including plague, came back negative. Furthermore, the WHO did not recommend any travel or trade restrictions in response to this incident. Concerns about the alleged plague spreading to Europe were voiced by politicians as Russia and Ukraine escalated their attacks on infrastructure. Kyiv’s mayor urged residents to evacuate due to potential electricity and water shortages during the upcoming winter. In Russia, Ukrainian drone strikes hit three of five data centers belonging to the technology giant Yandex, causing widespread internet disruptions. Despite the approaching autumn and the traditionally harsh winter in both countries, posing significant risks to their populations, particularly in Ukraine, Europe persists in supporting the escalation of the conflict. While the WHO maintained contact with Russia and confirmed through a phone call between Donald Trump and Putin the absence of an outbreak, European media continued to sensationalize the alleged plague threat to the world. Europe’s stance, rooted in distrust of Russia, evoked memories of Chernobyl and the unfounded fears of acid rain, justifying its support for prolonged conflict on the continent. This stance, against the backdrop of an urgently needed energy truce initiated by Donald Trump, prompts reflection on the nature of European policy. Europe consistently opposes conflict resolution and any peace initiatives if European interests are in any way affected. Meanwhile, conflicts in the Sahel, Sudan, and the migrant crisis along the Libyan coast persist despite numerous efforts at peaceful settlement. The conflict in Sudan, despite its catastrophic impact on the African continent, has long disappeared from the front pages of European newspapers because its resolution holds no interest for Europe. In contrast, news of a suspected plague outbreak in Russia’s interior captures widespread attention, even though sporadic plague cases occur regularly across multiple continents — the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Madagascar, China, the United States, and South America. The European focus on Russia’s alleged health threat appears disproportionate given the global prevalence of the disease. Despite the plague remaining a potentially dangerous disease, there exists an effective treatment mechanism with antibiotics. As a result, its spread typically does not pose an epidemic threat, particularly in countries with advanced healthcare systems. However, the persistent mention of the plague creates a sufficiently alarming atmosphere to divert public attention from truly crucial issues. The post No evidence of suspected plague outbreak in Russia, says WHO appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Tinubu’s second ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍​‍‍‍​‌⁠​‌​term ‘ill be a unity government, says Akpabio
body: Senate President Godswill Akpabio says President Bola Tinubu’s second term will be a unity government that will reflect the inclusive composition of his presidential campaign council. Akpabio said this at plenary on Wednesday while reacting to Senate Leader Opeyemi Bamidele’s comments on the inauguration of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, which included some members of the opposition parties. Akpabio described the development as historic, saying it was unprecedented since Nigeria returned to democratic rule in 1999 for a sitting president to constitute a campaign council involving almost all political parties. “This is not just an inclusive government in terms of infrastructure, revenue allocation and reforms. It is also an inclusive government in terms of unity of purpose in democracy,” he said. Akpabio said the development demonstrated that Tinubu’s second term would be a unity government, just as the campaign council represented a broad coalition of political parties. “What we are going to witness is evidence that his second term is going to be a unity government, just like his campaign council, which is a unity campaign council made up of almost all the political parties in the country,” he stated. He added that Nigeria was setting an example for Africa and congratulated President Tinubu, the APC National Chairman, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, and leaders of the participating political parties. Akpabio also congratulated the governors and political leaders for joining the campaign council, including Gov. Chukwuma Soludo of Anambra, Gov. Ademola Adeleke of Osun and FCT Minister Nyesom Wike. He said their participation showed that performance was not necessarily determined by political party affiliation but by individuals. “I can imagine how even a professor and former governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria, Prof. Soludo, will add his ideas to the next administration so that Nigeria will be better. “This is the way Nigeria should be,” he said. Earlier, Bamidele, while moving a motion for the Senate to adjourn proceedings until Thursday, described the composition of the APC campaign council as a historic development involving leaders from different parties. Bamidele said the council included Soludo, representing the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA), and Adeleke, representing the Accord Party, as state coordinators. He also named Wike, a former governor of Rivers and minister of the Federal Capital Territory, as the campaign coordinator for the FCT. “Mr President, let me also congratulate you and members of the ruling APC, APGA, PDP and Accord Party in this chamber because, as we leave this chamber, something historic is about to happen. “At 2 p.m. today, the Presidential Campaign Council will be inaugurated. The council includes Gov. Chukwuma Soludo of Anambra State, representing APGA, as a state coordinator, and Gov. Ademola Adeleke of Osun State, representing the Accord Party, as a state coordinator. “We also have Gov. Nyesom Wike, the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, representing the PDP, who will be inaugurated as the campaign coordinator for the FCT. “My point, Mr President, is that, in the best interests of Nigerians, a rainbow coalition is indeed on the move. “We will leave this chamber as members of different political parties and proceed to the Presidential Campaign Council. We look forward to a campaign that will celebrate ideas and strengthen our democracy,” he said. He added that the campaign would focus on ideas and democratic values. “We look forward to a campaign that will celebrate ideas and that will celebrate our democracy,” he added. The Senate Minority Leader Abba Moro (PDP-Benue South) seconded the motion for adjournment. (NAN) The post Tinubu’s second ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍​‍‍‍​‌⁠​‌​term ‘ill be a unity government, says Akpabio appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Russian-Indian Indra 2026 exercise starts in Far East, Urals
body:
MOSCOW, October 14. /TASS/. The joint Russian-Indian cross-branch exercise Indra 2026 has kicked off in the Chelyabinsk Region and the Russian Far East, the Russian Defense Ministry reported.
"The joint Russian-Indian cross-branch exercise Indra 2026 has begun in the Chelyabinsk Region and the Far East. Units of the ground forces of the two countries, warships of the Russian and Indian Navy, as well as aircraft of the Russian Aerospace Forces are participating in the maneuvers," the ministry said in a statement. The ministry noted that the crews of the Russian corvette Aldar Tsydenzhapov and the Indian Navy frigate INS Sahyadri, which arrived in Vladivostok several days ago, participated in the opening ceremony of the maritime part of the Indra 2026 joint exercise at the Pacific Fleet's main base.
The ministry specified that the active phase of the land part of the exercise will continue until October 23. The core of the Russian military contingent consists of servicemen from the 90th Guards Tank Division of the Central Military District. At the training ground, the military contingents will practice unit command and control and conduct a joint operation to destroy illegal armed groups.
The practical phase of the maritime part of the exercise will take place in the Sea of Japan on October 16-17. The ships in the joint detachment will practice tactical maneuvering, conduct artillery fire exercises against sea and air targets, conduct an inspection operation, and free a vessel simulated to have been seized by terrorists.
One of the episodes of the naval phase will include practicing joint actions to repel attacks by unmanned aerial vehicles and unmanned boats.
In addition, as part of the exercise, crews of the Russian Aerospace Forces and the Indian Air Force, operating joint Su-30SM tactical aircraft, will practice combating small, low-flying targets, destroying short-and medium-range airborne weapons carriers, and practicing maneuverable air combat at medium and low altitudes.
The ministry added that crews of the Russian Aerospace Forces and the Indian Air Force, using Mi-8 army aviation helicopters, will land special forces units and practice search and rescue of crews in distress in remote areas.

title: Soroman’s pioneering involvement in Dangote Consortium propels first loading milestone
body:
Soroman Nigeria Limited, a leader in the oil and gas industry and a key player in Nigeria’s evolving energy landscape, marked its entry into the consortium with the successful loading of 20,000.00 metric tonnes (MT) of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS) aboard the vessel African Marvel. The cargo is destined for the Soroman Depot in Calabar, Cross River State, signaling an important step for the company’s strategic initiatives in petroleum distribution and coastal logistics.
The Vessel African Marvel’s movement under this consortium arrangement not only underscores the company’s commitment to operational excellence but also reinforces its role as a pioneering participant in a new era of petroleum refining and distribution led by industry heavyweights.
In an environment where market dynamics and commercial partnerships are continually evolving, Soroman’s breakthrough cargo operation stands out as a testament to the company’s agility and strategic foresight.
The Dangote Petroleum Refinery consortium arrangement represents a structured commercial framework through which qualified downstream operators lift refined products directly from the refinery for distribution across Nigeria’s domestic market.
Soroman’s ability to secure its first loading under this arrangement places the company among the early participants in a model that is expected to reshape how petroleum products flow from refinery gate to end-user, reducing the country’s long-standing reliance on imported fuels and strengthening the domestic supply chain.
Commercially, the transaction is structured on a dollar-referenced product rating, with payment settled in naira in accordance with the specific terms agreed upon for this loading. It is worth noting that the applicable conversion basis, quotation validity and payment timeline are governed by the relevant transaction documents between the parties. These terms are specific to the transaction and should not be construed as a general pricing policy applicable to all consortium participants or future liftings.
The choice of Calabar as the discharge destination carries its own strategic weight. Situated in Cross River State along Nigeria’s south-eastern coastline, Calabar has historically served as a gateway for maritime commerce in the region.
By directing the African Marvel cargo to Soroman Depot in Calabar, the company is reinforcing the city’s relevance as a petroleum distribution hub and positioning itself to serve the commercial fuel needs of buyers across the South-South geopolitical zone. The coastal routing from the Dangote Refinery in Lagos to Calabar demonstrates the viability of maritime logistics as an efficient channel for moving large petroleum volumes to regional markets that have traditionally depended on road-based haulage and imports.
Soroman’s achievement in the petroleum space is amplified by the company’s broader industrial footprint. While oil and gas remain a core business line, Soroman Nigeria Limited operates across multiple sectors, including engineering, procurement and construction, mining, manufacturing and production, and fertilizer, agriculture and food value chains. This diversified portfolio means that the visibility and credibility generated by the consortium milestone extend beyond petroleum, introducing the Soroman brand to a wider audience of potential customers, commercial partners, investors and industry stakeholders who may find value in the company’s capabilities across these adjacent sectors.
The company has also made deliberate investments in digital platforms to ensure that increased brand awareness translates into accessible commercial engagement. Soroman’s corporate website offers a detailed overview of its operations and service offerings. An online ordering portal provides a direct channel for customers to place product orders and submit business enquiries.
For mobile users, the Soroman application is available for download on both the Apple App Store and Google Play, extending the company’s digital reach to smartphone users across Nigeria. Additionally, a WhatsApp ordering channel offers a familiar, conversational interface for customers who prefer to transact and communicate via messaging. These platforms collectively ensure that prospective clients can discover, contact and do business with Soroman with minimal friction.
As Nigeria’s petroleum landscape continues its historic shift toward domestically refined supply, companies that position themselves early within the new distribution architecture stand to gain a lasting competitive advantage.
Soroman Nigeria Limited’s pioneering first loading under the Dangote consortium arrangement is precisely such a positioning move — one that combines operational execution with strategic ambition. The Vessel African Marvel, carrying 20,000.00 metric tonnes of PMS toward Soroman Depot in Calabar, is not merely a vessel in transit; it is a visible marker of the company’s readiness to play a prominent role in the next chapter of Nigeria’s energy distribution story.
Soroman Nigeria Limited is a Nigerian multi-sector company with business interests spanning oil and gas, engineering and procurement, construction, mining, manufacturing and production, and fertilizer, agriculture and food value chains.

title: Social Security Administration says cost-of-living adjustment will rise 3.6% in 2027
body:
The cost-of-living adjustment ensures benefits keep pace with inflation.
Social Security benefits will increase 3.6% beginning in January for more than 70 million recipients, the Social Security Administration (SSA) said on Wednesday.
The cost-of-living adjustment for 2027, known as COLA, came in markedly higher than the prior year's hike of 2.8%.
The annual uptick in Social Security benefits aims to keep payments on pace with inflation, which surged in the spring after the outbreak of the Iran war.
The rise in Social Security payments for 2027 amounts to an average increase of about $75 a month for each recipient, the SSA said.
The announcement on Wednesday came after inflation data for September showed price hikes had climbed to a four-month high due in large part to a surge in gasoline costs. The fresh reading marked the final piece of data necessary for SSA to calculate COLA for 2027.
“Social Security will implement this cost-of-living adjustment for 76 million Americans, giving them greater financial stability,” Commissioner Frank Bisignano said in a statement .
The agency will also hike the maximum amount of earnings subject to the Social Security tax, elevating the taxable income limit from $184,500 to $192,300.
Recipients can check their online accounts with Social Security for notifications of their new benefit amount beginning in late November, the agency said. Notices will be sent to recipients by mail starting in early December.
24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

title: Deleted records reveal UK PM’s two dinners with Man City chairman — Report
body: By Adegboyega Adeleye Deleted records have revealed that British Prime Minister Andy Burnham had two hospitality dinners with Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak while serving as mayor of Greater Manchester. According to the BBC, the dinners took place at Manchester City’s Etihad Stadium during matches in August 2017 and April 2018, but were not specifically mentioned in a statement released by the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) on Monday detailing Burnham’s dealings with the club. The revelation comes amid growing political controversy over Burnham’s previous engagements with Manchester City following an independent commission’s finding that the club breached Premier League financial regulations. Burnham has faced calls to provide full details of his interactions with the club since expressing concern last month about the possibility of its owners selling up. A previous GMCA register of declarations, seen by the BBC, listed a £300 hospitality dinner with Al Mubarak and then-Manchester City Council leader Richard Leese during an Everton match in August 2017. Another entry recorded a dinner with the Manchester City chairman during the Manchester derby against Manchester United in April 2018, valued at approximately £699. Burnham had previously declared both dinners, alongside £150 tickets to see singer Ed Sheeran perform at the stadium in May 2018. However, the register has since been removed from the GMCA website. The BBC reported that the authority’s stated policy is to publish declarations from the current mayoral term only. The BBC said it had asked the GMCA for further clarification about the policy, noting that the website contained entries dating back to 2022, although the current mayoral term began in 2024. Downing Street defends Burnham Downing Street has defended the two dinners, saying they were hospitality received at home matches and had been declared, rather than separate meetings with the Manchester City chairman. However, political pressure on Burnham to provide greater transparency about his dealings with the club has continued to mount. Tory shadow sports minister Louie French said Burnham had promised the country and House of Commons full transparency over his dealings with Manchester City. French said the disclosure was essential following what he described as Burnham’s “inappropriate intervention into football”. Reform UK’s Robert Jenrick also criticised the handling of the matter, saying “this saga stinks” as he accused Burnham of apparently concealing his links to the club’s owners. Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch has called on Downing Street to release full details of meetings between Burnham and senior Manchester City figures. Burnham told the Rest Is Politics podcast last week that he was willing to publish details of his engagements with the club during his time as mayor. He said he would “quite clearly put out there everything that I have done working with them in my previous role as Mayor of Greater Manchester”. Burnham added that he had held only one significant meeting with the club, in 2021. At Prime Minister’s Questions on Wednesday, he told MPs that Manchester City had not raised the charges it was facing with him or his team. He also said he was happy for “everything to be set out in full”, describing the GMCA’s statement as a full account of his key dealings with the club’s owners. When reporters questioned why the statement did not specifically mention the two dinners, Burnham’s press secretary referred them back to the GMCA statement. The BBC said it had asked the authority why the dinners were not specifically listed in the published account. Man City found guilty of financial breaches Manchester City was found guilty in September by an independent commission of breaching Premier League financial regulations. The commission found that the club had broken rules over nine years between 2009 and 2018, including through what it described as “sham” contracts with commercial partners to funnel more than £830m into its football operations. Sanctions have yet to be announced, while Manchester City, which denies wrongdoing, has appealed the verdict. The controversy over Burnham’s dealings with the club comes against the backdrop of wider scrutiny of links between Manchester City and public authorities. Earlier this month, former Manchester City Council leader Richard Leese defended a decade-old agreement between the council and Abu Dhabi United Group, the company that owns Manchester City and is linked to the United Arab Emirates royal family. A University of Sheffield report said land was leased to the group at “below comparable rates” under the partnership between the company and the local authority. The post Deleted records reveal UK PM’s two dinners with Man City chairman — Report appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Otti pledges to fast-track Abia Industrial Park
body: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — Abia State Governor, Dr Alex Otti, has reaffirmed his commitment to completing the Abia Industrial and Innovation Park (AIIP) in Owaza, Ukwa West Local Government Area, expressing confidence that the project will emerge as a major industrial and innovation hub for the state and Nigeria. Otti gave the assurance in his office while receiving his Chief of Staff, Pastor Caleb Ajagba, who led members of the State Executive Council and the newly appointed Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer of AIIP, Ms Sandra Ivonye-Ntofon, to brief him on their inspection of the project site. Ajagba and his team had earlier visited Owaza to introduce the new managing director to the host community and facility managers, assess the existing infrastructure and identify critical upgrades required to make the park attractive to investors. The governor disclosed that the project had continued to attract investor interest, citing the planned relocation of a steel plant from another state to AIIP despite the significant cost implications. He said the development demonstrated investors’ confidence in the project. “The issue is not whether that place will be successful. It is about how quickly you can achieve that,” Otti said. He added that feasibility studies for the park had been completed, expressing confidence that its combination of industrial production, innovation and commerce would make it a strategic driver of economic growth, job creation and investment. The governor directed the new management to accelerate implementation and make up for time lost since the groundbreaking ceremony. He assured the team of his administration’s support, including the provision of resources required to commence operations. Otti also stressed the need to secure the project site with perimeter fencing and directed the Commissioner for Works to begin work on a shorter access road linking the expressway to the park. Congratulating Ivonye-Ntofon on her appointment, the governor said appointments under his administration were based on merit, adding that the recruitment process for the park’s leadership was designed to identify competent and qualified candidates. Earlier, Ajagba said the visit to Owaza was aimed at evaluating the facility and determining the infrastructure required to meet the expectations of the state government and the international business community. He said the delegation received a warm reception from the host community. “At the site, we made it clear that the Industrial Park is intended to attract companies that will support the industrialisation of Abia State, especially the Ukwa West corridor. “With the coming on board of the new MD, we will reinforce this administration’s commitment to building a virile economy for Abia State,” he said. In her remarks, Ivonye-Ntofon thanked the governor for the confidence reposed in her and pledged to work with relevant stakeholders to achieve the park’s objectives. She described AIIP as an opportunity to establish a national industrial and innovation hub serving Owaza, Abia State and Nigeria. “We are committed to accelerating the pace of work. Our goal is to give Ndi Abia a reason to be proud of a world-class industrial and innovation park located in their state,” she said. Speaking on behalf of the host community, the Traditional Prime Minister of Igiriukwu Autonomous Community, Owaza, Chief Uche Nwele, assured the new managing director of the community’s cooperation and support. The post Otti pledges to fast-track Abia Industrial Park appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Belarusian foreign ministry condemns NATO’s new ‘Theory of Victory’ plan
body:
MINSK, October 14. /TASS/. Belarus strongly condemns NATO’s new plan, headlined ‘Theory of Victrory,’ which envisages pre-emptive strikes on the territory of the republic, Belarusian Foreign Ministry’s spokesman, Ruslan Varankov, said in a statement.
"The Republic of Belarus strongly condemns the statements made by General Alexus Grynkewich, Supreme Allied Commander Europe, who presented the so-called ‘Theory of Victory’. This concept envisages pre-emptive strikes against the territory of Belarus using drones and ground-based robotic systems," the spokesman said in a statement.
"The North Atlantic Alliance's aggressive rhetoric is becoming increasingly systematic. In the absence of any threats from Belarus or any real preconditions for conflict, NATO is drawing up plans to increase its military presence near Belarusian borders and launch strikes against the territory of a sovereign state," he continued.
Varankov went on to say that under the guise of defensive language, the Alliance is effectively laying the groundwork for military escalation and aggression.
"Belarus has never threatened anyone. Our military doctrine is strictly defensive in nature," the Belarusian diplomat added. "We consistently advocate openness, de-escalation and dialogue on an equal footing. We call on our Western counterparts to exercise sound judgement and engage in joint efforts to restore mutual trust.".

title: Police Arrest Suspect After Political Thug Chops Off Man’s Wrist In Bauchi
body: The Bauchi State Police Command has arrested one suspect after it recorded a case of political violence resulting in grievous hurt, where a 24-year-old man had his wrist chopped off by a political thug. A statement by the Bauchi State Command’s Police Public Relations Officer, SP Nafiu Habib, said the incident happened on Wednesday at about 1130 hours, when a political altercation ensued between one Lawi and one Usman, 24yrs, both of Isiyaka Jibrin Quarters, Bakin Kura area of Bauchi Metropolis. In the course of the altercation, one Mamman Gore of the same address, an associate of the said Lawi, emerged armed with a sharp machete and brutally chopped off the wrist of the victim, Usman Idris, causing him to collapse and fall unconscious. The victim was promptly evacuated and rushed to the Abubakar Tafawa Balewa University Teaching Hospital (ATBUTH), Bauchi, where he received immediate medical attention and is currently admitted and responding to treatment. Following the incident, the Command said operatives of ‘A’ Division Township have arrested Lawi, and he is in custody assisting with the investigation. According to the statement, the principal suspect who chopped off the victim’s wrist fled to an unknown destination, as the Command said concerted efforts have been intensified to track, arrest, and bring the fleeing suspect to justice. The Commissioner of Police, CP Sani-Omolori Aliyu, condemned in strong terms all forms of political violence and thuggery, and warned that the Command will not condone any act capable of threatening public peace and safety. The post Police Arrest Suspect After Political Thug Chops Off Man’s Wrist In Bauchi appeared first on Channels Television .

title: We might not have to wait 13 years for the next GTA
body:
Rockstar Games might not keep fans waiting as long for the next installment of Grand Theft Auto. As part of Bloomberg’s expansive report on the making of GTA VI, Rockstar technical lead Phil Hooker said that the “engine, the tools and the team we’ve built during this project will allow us to do things more quickly.”
GTA VI had a notoriously long development process. It took eight years to make, leaving a 13-year gap between this upcoming installment and GTA V.
The report points to the one-year gap between Grand Theft Auto III and Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, which was possible because Rockstar already had the framework in place for its next project. “I feel confident that we can build on top of this [GTA VI] and go more sideways than upwards to build more compelling content,” Hooker told Bloomberg.
There were several other interesting details in the report as well, including:
* Rockstar built a studio dedicated to creating nonplayable characters (NPCs) after the team realized it lacked the “production capabilities” needed to write and animate all of the game’s NPCs. That contributed to the game’s delay. “I think when it became apparent that some areas weren’t going to make it, that’s when we decided to make the shift of date,” Hooker said. “We could hit that schedule, but it won’t be the game we want to make.”
* GTA VI apparently didn’t cost more than $1.5 billion to develop, as Rockstar’s publishing head Jennifer Kolbe shut down a report that suggested it was more expensive to build than Dubai’s Burj Khalifa.
* Rockstar head of development Aaron Garbut responded to the massive GTA VI leak in 2022: “It feels like somebody’s wading through your dirty washing,” Garbut told Bloomberg. “It’s like they’re inside your head. You see your early work out there. Nobody’s ever supposed to see that. It’s really weirdly invasive. And so it’s quite hard to deal with on an emotional level.”
* Since 2018, the number of Rockstar employees has risen from 2,441 to 4,711 across 12 offices.
GTA VI launches on November 19th on the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X | S.

title: Gold Stars CEO Kwasi Adu sanctioned by GFA over misconduct
body: Bibiani Gold Stars Chief Executive Officer Kwasi Adu has been banned for three matches and fined GHS 10,000 by the Ghana Football Association (GFA) following misconduct after a 2-1 loss to Hearts of Oak in September. Adu was found guilty for breaching the restricted perimeter without authorisation and verbally assaulting match officials upon confrontation during the Ghana Premier League encounter. The GFA’s Disciplinary committee also charged him with tarnishing the integrity of the sport after making post-match comments about match officials. The Gold Stars Ceo has been banned with immediate effect and must settle a GHS 10,000 fine within 14 days of receiving notice. The committee has also warned against any future misconduct, as it will lead to severe repercussions.

title: Ronen Bar files NIS 3 million defamation lawsuit against Netanyahu over shifting Oct. 7 blame
body: Former Shin Bet (Israel Security Agency) chief Ronen Bar filed an NIS 3 million defamation lawsuit against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu at the Central District Court in Lod on Wednesday, alleging that the prime minister knowingly published false accusations about his conduct before the October 7 attack to shift responsibility onto him.The lawsuit, filed less than two weeks before the October 27 elections, centers on a September 28 post on Netanyahu's personal X/Twitter account accusing Bar of “failures and crimes.” Alongside compensation, Bar seeks a court-ordered correction or denial and legal costs, and says he will seek disclosure of relevant documents held by Netanyahu.The lawsuit made serious allegations about what Netanyahu knew and how he acted in the years, months and hours preceding the attack. The court has not ruled on these allegations. In the September 28 X post, Netanyahu accused Bar of recognizing warning signs but deciding not to call and alert him. Bar rejected that accusation, saying that the Shin Bet shared the available intelligence with Netanyahu's military secretariat and that he instructed his staff to update the military secretariat before the attack began.The lawsuit argues that the military secretariat was the official channel for updating Netanyahu and deciding whether to wake him. Bar also states that Netanyahu had not given him his personal phone number.Responding Wednesday, Netanyahu dismissed that explanation, saying Bar could have reached him through other channels.“Ronen, are you serious?” Netanyahu wrote on Telegram. “You had my secure phone number and could have called me immediately, as all the heads of the security establishment do.”Netanyahu added that his Shin Bet guards, whom he described as Bar's subordinates, could have reached him within minutes. “How many lives we could have saved if only you had called in time,” he wrote.The distinction between information reaching the Prime Minister's Office and reaching Netanyahu personally is central to the dispute.The lawsuit emphasizes that Bar is not trying to evade responsibility for the Shin Bet's intelligence failure, but is rather challenging accusations that he knowingly withheld information and chose not to take action to save lives.“As the head of the service, I bear responsibility for the Shin Bet's failure to provide the intelligence required regarding the October 7 attack and its timing,” Bar said in a statement issued on his behalf. “Accordingly, I resigned from my position, bowing my head before the bereaved families.”Lawsuit contradicts Netanyahu claims that Shin Bet concealed evidenceBar's departure followed a prolonged confrontation with Netanyahu over his dismissal and the agency's independence. The government voted on March 20, 2025, to end his tenure, citing a breakdown in professional trust. Netanyahu maintained that the loss of trust stemmed from October 7; Bar argued that the move followed his resistance to improper demands and investigations involving people close to the prime minister.The High Court of Justice froze the dismissal while considering petitions against it. On April 28, Bar announced that he would leave on June 15, and the government rescinded its dismissal decision the following day.On May 21, the court nevertheless ruled, by a majority, that the dismissal decision had been unlawful. It found that Netanyahu had acted under a conflict of interest arising from investigations involving his associates, and that the government had bypassed the required advisory process, lacked an adequate factual basis, and failed to give Bar a proper opportunity to answer the allegations against him.The investigations at the center of the conflict included “Qatargate”, which examined suspicions that figures close to Netanyahu promoted Qatari interests while working around the prime minister during the war. Qatar's role as a mediator in hostage negotiations made the alleged relationships particularly sensitive. A separate investigation concerned the unauthorized transfer of classified military material to the German newspaper Bild.In his April 2025 affidavit opposing his dismissal, Bar argued that the investigations posed a threat to Netanyahu's personal and political interests. He also alleged that Netanyahu sought to use the Shin Bet's powers against anti-government protesters. Netanyahu rejected Bar's account and denied requesting unlawful surveillance of protest leaders.The new lawsuit returns to those allegations, linking the attacks on Bar to his affidavit and describing the alleged efforts to deploy the agency against political protests as an attempt to use it as a “secret police” force. During the dismissal proceedings, bereaved relatives also demanded accountability from Bar. At the April 8 hearing, bereaved father Itzik Bonzel, now a Likud candidate, challenged the court's intervention, arguing that Bar's acknowledged responsibility for the failure meant he should leave office.The lawsuit details how, in the months leading up to October 7, Bar says he repeatedly warned Netanyahu about the possibility of escalation on multiple fronts, including Gaza, with particular concern ahead of the High Holy Days. He also presented proposals to target senior Hamas officials, which he says Netanyahu rejected or failed to advance.Bar demands full disclosure of documentsAmong the examples is a July 23, 2023, conversation in which Bar says he told Netanyahu: “I am giving you a strategic warning of war.” According to the filing, he also explicitly cautioned that the agency would not be able to provide a precise day and hour.These were warnings of a deteriorating security situation, rather than intelligence identifying the date, scale, or operational plan of the October 7 attack; the lawsuit expressly acknowledges that the Shin Bet failed to identify those in advance.The filing further alleges that Netanyahu pursued a policy of “quiet at any cost” in Gaza, directing the security establishment to postpone confrontations, keep Gaza as a secondary arena, and preserve Hamas as the governing authority.Bar argues that this policy constrained offensive action against Hamas and allowed it to strengthen. He alleges that Netanyahu continued permitting Qatari money into Gaza despite warnings that funds were reaching Hamas's military wing.Netanyahu has presented a competing account, citing excerpts from security discussions and intelligence assessments to argue that Bar supported economic concessions and restraint toward Gaza and failed to warn him of an impending attack. In his April 2025 affidavit, Netanyahu cited a Shin Bet assessment from days before the massacre that suggested renewed understandings with Hamas could help preserve stability.Bar argues that selected quotations obscure the broader record of his warnings and recommendations. His lawsuit also acknowledges that Netanyahu sometimes approved preparations for targeted killings in principle, including at an October 1, 2023, discussion, but alleges that he failed to issue the instructions needed to advance them.Regarding the night of October 7, the lawsuit disputes Netanyahu's claim that Bar held numerous conversations with then-IDF chief of staff Herzi Halevi and then-military intelligence chief Aharon Haliva before deciding not to alert the prime minister. Bar says he did not speak to either man that night, although officials in their organizations exchanged information.According to the lawsuit, Shin Bet personnel began updating their military counterparts at about 11 p.m. on October 6 and distributed an electronic alert at 3:03 a.m. concerning an unusual accumulation of possible indications of offensive Hamas activity.The lawsuit acknowledged that the alert was assigned a lower level of urgency than it should have been. It also states that the Shin Bet did not anticipate a full-scale attack that night.Bar said the intelligence officer in the prime minister's military secretariat received updates overnight, including a follow-up call at 3:55 a.m. that drew attention to information already sent. He further says that, after an assessment ending around 5:15 a.m., he instructed his staff to update Netanyahu's military secretary, Avi Gil, before the attack began.The filing placed the subsequent call from Bar's chief of staff to Gil at 6:15 a.m., while quoting Gil's account that he was awakened at 6:12 a.m. Neither account establishes that Netanyahu himself received the information at those times.The lawsuit also challenged Netanyahu's accusations that Bar failed to alert local emergency response squads or evacuate the Nova music festival. Bar says he did not know the festival was taking place, and argues that the Shin Bet did not command the IDF or the local squads and was not responsible for licensing civilian events.He further disputes Netanyahu's argument that dispatching a small “Tequila” operational team demonstrated advance knowledge of the impending massacre. The lawsuit says such teams were regularly mobilized in response to possible attacks and that sending one did not mean the agency anticipated an assault on the scale of October 7.The dispute has increasingly focused on access to the full documentary record. Netanyahu has released selected excerpts from security discussions, including in a 55-page account published in February as part of his response to the state comptroller. Bar alleges that the presentation omits context necessary to assess what was recommended and decided.Separately, Gil has alleged that Netanyahu's former chief of staff, Tzachi Braverman, sought to change the recorded time of a call on the morning of October 7. Braverman has denied wrongdoing. The allegation of altering a record is distinct from the dispute over selectively publishing excerpts.On Tuesday, dozens of former hostages, bereaved relatives and other family members demanded that Netanyahu release the full protocols, original recordings and logs from security discussions before and on the morning of the attack, subject to military censorship and the law. Signatories included former hostages Yocheved Lifshitz and Ditza Heiman; Einav Zangauker, whose son Matan was abducted on October 7; and Hadas Kalderon, whose children Sahar and Erez and their father Ofer were also taken hostage.Bar said he had waited three years for a state commission of inquiry to examine the Shin Bet's actions alongside its failures, but had decided to sue in light of what he described as an ongoing campaign against him.The filing argues that Netanyahu should not be protected by parliamentary immunity because, in Bar's account, the publication was a planned personal and political attack rather than protected conduct in the performance of his duties. “I call on the prime minister not to hide behind claims of immunity,” Bar said. “In the absence of a state commission of inquiry, the truth will be established in court.”

title: NAF crash: Aiyedatiwa orders fumigation of Igbokoda river
body: By Dayo Johnson, Akure Ondo State Governor, Lucky Aiyedatiwa, has ordered the immediate fumigation of the river at Igbokoda following complaints of offensive odour and concerns about possible pollution after last week’s Nigerian Air Force aircraft crash. The directive was disclosed in a statement by the Commissioner for Information and Orientation, Prince Idowu Ajanaku. According to the statement, the governor directed the Ministries of Environment and Health to jointly carry out an extensive fumigation exercise to reduce potential health risks and prevent possible outbreaks of water-borne diseases. Residents had raised concerns over a strong stench emanating from the river following the crash, expressing fears that decomposing materials and aviation fuel residue could contaminate the waterway, which is important for fishing and domestic activities in the coastal community. Ajanaku said the governor was concerned about the possible health and livelihood implications for residents of Igbokoda and neighbouring communities, prompting the intervention. As a precaution, Aiyedatiwa also directed the Ilaje Local Government Council to deploy water tankers to affected areas to provide households with clean drinking water if laboratory assessments confirmed severe pollution of the river. The statement said the water supply arrangement would remain in place until measures were implemented to address any confirmed contamination and restore the river to safe use. To further reduce potential health risks, the governor directed the two ministries to distribute nose masks and other essential health and safety kits to residents, particularly those living close to the crash site. Aiyedatiwa reaffirmed the state government’s commitment to supporting the Nigerian Air Force in its ongoing recovery and evacuation operations while prioritising the safety and welfare of affected communities. He assured residents that the government was monitoring the situation and would take additional measures where necessary to protect public health. The post NAF crash: Aiyedatiwa orders fumigation of Igbokoda river appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Four killed, 41 injured as rescue operations conclude at site of Russian missile strike in Kharkiv
body:
According to Ukrinform, the State Emergency Service of Ukraine reported this on Facebook .
Personnel and equipment from the Kharkiv regional branch of the State Emergency Service, the Donetsk-Luhansk Mobile Rapid Response Rescue Center of the State Emergency Service of Ukraine, the DELTA rapid response unit of the Civil Protection Rescue Service of the State Emergency Service of Ukraine, as well as municipal services, were involved in the operation.
Rescuers cleared rubble and dismantled destroyed and damaged sections of the building.
The State Emergency Service recalled that four people were killed and 41 injured in the Russian attack on Kharkiv. SES psychologists provided assistance to more than 100 people.
