title: Tinubu Seeks Senate Approval to Establish National School of Government
body: * Proposed institution to replace ASCON, strengthen leadership development, policy delivery Sunday Aborisade in Abuja President Bola Tinubu has asked the Senate to approve a bill seeking to repeal the Administrative Staff College of Nigeria (ASCON) Act and establish the National School of Government, Nigeria, as a national institution for leadership development, policy delivery and executive capacity building. Senate President Godswill Akpabio read the president’s letter transmitting the National School of Government Bill 2026 to the upper chamber during plenary on Wednesday. In the letter, Tinubu urged the Senate to give the proposed legislation expeditious consideration, stressing the need to establish a dedicated institution to strengthen leadership development and improve the capacity of public officials to deliver government policies. The president invoked Section 58(2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, to formally transmit the bill to the Senate for legislative consideration. “Pursuant to Section 58 (2) of the 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, as amended, I forward herewith the National School of Government Bill 2026 for the kind consideration of the Senate,” Tinubu stated in the letter. He expressed the hope that the lawmakers would give the bill the necessary attention and facilitate its consideration. The proposed legislation seeks to repeal the Administrative Staff College of Nigeria Act, A-4, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria 2004, and replace the existing legal framework with one establishing the National School of Government, Nigeria. According to the president, the proposed institution would serve as a national centre for leadership development, policy delivery and executive capacity building. The initiative, as outlined in the presidential communication, would place the proposed school at the centre of efforts to develop leadership capacity and strengthen the ability of government officials to translate public policies into practical outcomes. The bill’s transmission marks the beginning of the legislative process required to determine its provisions, institutional framework and other matters necessary for the establishment of the proposed school. After reading the president’s letter, Akpabio informed senators that the clauses and provisions of the bill had been attached to the communication for their consideration. He subsequently referred the bill to the Senate Committee on Rules and Business for further legislative action. The committee is expected to take the next procedural steps towards the bill’s consideration in accordance with the Senate’s legislative processes. The proposed repeal of the ASCON Act would bring the existing statutory framework governing the institution under review as the Federal Government seeks legislative backing for the National School of Government. However, the presidential letter, as read on the floor of the Senate, did not provide further details on the proposed institution’s governance structure, funding arrangements, location or the specific relationship it would have with existing public service training institutions. These and other provisions will depend on the contents of the bill and the subsequent legislative process. The bill will now proceed through the Senate’s established procedures for further consideration.

title: Planned capacity of 12,000 interceptors a year, under 100 seconds to target: US firm pitches a low-cost drone killer
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); US defense-tech company CHAOS Industries introduced its Vespid interceptor family in Washington on 12 October, as the Association of the US Army (AUSA) annual meeting opened there, the company announced . CHAOS pitches the drones as low-cost defense against small and mid-size drones and one-way attack munitions. The company expects initial production capacity of 12,000 interceptors a year, expandable to 50,000 as demand grows. The pitch lands as Russia moves its strike drones to jet power. Russia has stopped building the Geran-3, an earlier jet model, and makes about 3,000 faster Geran-4s and Geran-5s a month, Ukraine’s military intelligence (HUR) told Militarnyi in August. In mid-September, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said two Ukrainian companies had passed combat tests with interceptors against such drones, while 67 were still working on them. Ukrainian defense outlet Defense Express measured the new US drones against exactly that threat. One to carry, one to launch in batches The Mk 1 made its first public appearance on 12 October aboard a Forterra MESA autonomous ground vehicle, Army Recognition reported . It fires from tubes on launchers such as the 10-round ISS Aerospace HAL10. It takes midcourse guidance from CHAOS radars or external command systems, then an AI-assisted infrared seeker handles the final approach, the company says . An electric ducted fan rather than a jet engine drives it, which CHAOS says cuts cost and logistics compared with turbojet interceptors. The smaller Mk 0 is man-portable and needs no operator input once fired, its product page says . Both are rated to reach a target in under 100 seconds, with a listed range of 10+ km. Defense Express called that range a serious weakness that more launchers around a city could offset. Explore further Most drone interceptors ram or explode. This Ukrainian one just throws a net—six shots to a module CHAOS lists cruise speeds of 100 m/s (360 km/h) for the Mk 0 and 150 m/s (540 km/h) for the Mk 1. Defense Express said those speeds may be enough to intercept the Geran-4 and Geran-5, which it puts at 340 km/h and 450–600 km/h. Ukrainian makers say their interceptors already down jet Gerans Wild Hornets’ Sting interceptors downed several of the slower jet-powered Geran-3s in November 2025. An unnamed Wild Hornets representative told NV, in an interview published on 22 September, that the company’s new interceptor had destroyed about ten Geran-4s and several Geran-5s in limited use. The company plans mass production within a month of finishing combat tests. On 12 October, former Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov said he and Pavlo Yelizarov, commander of Lasar’s Group, had created a new interceptor with troops and engineers. He said it downed two Geran-5s headed for Kyiv. Crews from Lasar’s Group, which Fedorov has called a National Guard special unit, flew those combat tests, he said. Separately, Fedorov reported in August that a Ukrainian jet interceptor with a top speed above 600 km/h had entered combat testing. title: Sports Fund Administrator urges boxing fraternity to pursue partnerships beyond government funding
body: The Administrator of the Ghana Sports Fund, Dr David Kofi Wuaku, has urged boxing stakeholders to pursue stronger partnerships with corporate organisations and other institutions to address funding challenges confronting the sport. Dr Wuaku said sustainable sports development would require practical collaboration between the Fund, sporting associations, athletes and potential sponsors, particularly as sporting disciplines compete for limited financial resources. He made the call during a meeting with boxing representatives, who outlined difficulties in financing training, equipment and participation in international competitions. The representatives said financial constraints had affected their ability to participate in important competitions and appealed for assistance to support athletes seeking international exposure. Dr Wuaku acknowledged the concerns and encouraged the team to submit detailed proposals identifying its immediate needs and the expected benefits of proposed interventions. He said the Fund would consider practical programmes based on their merits, feasibility and likely impact, while also exploring opportunities to attract partners who could contribute to competitions, training and athlete development. The Administrator emphasised that the Fund could not necessarily meet every need presented by sporting associations. He therefore encouraged stakeholders to identify additional sources of support rather than depend exclusively on government financing. For boxing, potential areas for structured partnerships could include equipment provision, athlete preparation, competition sponsorship, coaching development and support for international participation. Such arrangements would require sporting associations to present credible programmes, define the support needed and demonstrate how sponsorship would contribute to measurable outcomes. Dr Wuaku also stressed the importance of accountability, saying the Fund would expect resources directed towards sports development to produce tangible benefits. The approach places responsibility on sports administrators to strengthen programme planning and establish credible relationships with prospective partners. For businesses, clearly defined programmes and transparent reporting could help provide a basis for assessing the value and impact of sports sponsorship. The meeting did not establish any confirmed sponsorship agreement or financial commitment. Instead, it highlighted the need for structured proposals and further engagement to identify practical opportunities for collaboration. Dr Wuaku reaffirmed the Fund’s willingness to work with the boxing fraternity and encouraged the representatives to develop proposals that could attract support and advance the development of the sport.

title: Assessment of OPEC+ maximum production capacity to be ready by end of 2026 — Novak
body:
MOSCOW, October 14. /TASS/. The assessment of maximum production capacities of OPEC+ countries will be ready by the end of 2026, Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak told reporters on the sidelines of the Russian Energy Week forum.
"The end of 2026. At least such tasks were set there. The OPEC Secretariat is working in this area," Novak said.
Russia will restore and increase its production as possible, the deputy prime minister said. "Production will recover and grow in line with capabilities of our infrastructure and the refining segment," he noted.

title: NATO may eventually have to shoot down missiles over western Ukraine – former Polish security chief
body:
Former Head of Poland’s National Security Bureau Stanisław Koziej said this in an interview with Ukrinform , answering a question about whether NATO countries would eventually be able to agree on shooting down missiles over western Ukraine.
According to Koziej, he has been proposing for the past two or three years that NATO establish what is known as an advanced missile defense zone, which would provide for the interception of at least dual-purpose missiles, including those capable of carrying nuclear warheads.
Koziej acknowledged that reaching consensus within the Alliance on such an initiative would be difficult. At the same time, he believes that further escalation of Russian aggression and an increase in the number of aerial incidents could force NATO to take this step.
Koziej separately emphasized the need to deepen security cooperation between Poland and Ukraine.
“We need to be as close to each other as possible. We should put political and emotional disputes aside as soon as possible and move toward pragmatic cooperation in the security sphere, especially along the border,” he said.
According to the former head of Poland’s National Security Bureau, the two countries need to exchange information about drones and missiles in order to respond to threats in advance. He also stressed the importance of ensuring an uninterrupted supply of aid to Ukraine and urged that historical disputes not be allowed to obstruct efforts to address urgent security issues.
Koziej described Russian disinformation as one of the problems that Poland currently finds most difficult to counter. At the same time, he said Poland is beginning to pool efforts in this area, including by establishing a special center to counter disinformation.
He expressed hope that the center’s work would help develop a strategy to protect society from Russian manipulation aimed at exacerbating divisions between Poles and Ukrainians.
As Ukrinform reported, unidentified debris was found on a beach in Karwia, Pomeranian Voivodeship, Poland. Preliminary findings indicate that it may be drone debris, but the type of object has not yet been established.

title: Gold worth millions seized in three smuggling bids on UAE-Delhi routes
body: Three separate gold smuggling attempts from the UAE to India have been foiled in recent weeks by customs officials at Indira Gandhi International (IGI) Airport in New Delhi. Officials recovered gold concealed inside trolley bag linings, hidden in passengers' socks and disguised as silver chains. In the biggest case, officials seized 6.5kg of gold valued at around Dh3.8 million. The accused sprayed the gold chains with silver and black paint and hid them under seats on Emirates flight EK-514 from Dubai to Delhi. Airport police arrested eight passengers and remanded them to judicial custody. On October 10, customs officers intercepted a passenger arriving from Sharjah and recovered 241g of 99.31 per cent pure gold. The passenger moulded the gold and hid it as wire linings in the corners of two trolley bags. A video posted by Delhi Customs shows an official cutting through the seams of the passenger's red bags to extract the rod-like gold. Gold Smuggling Attempt Foiled at IGI Airport, Delhi! Delhi Customs officers intercepted a passenger arriving from Sharjah on 10.10.2026 and recovered 241 grams of gold (99.31% purity) ingeniously concealed as wire linings in the corners of two trolley bags. The recovered gold,… pic.twitter.com/6f7CCzleZz — Delhi Customs (Airport & General) (@AirportGenCus) October 12, 2026 The recovered gold was valued at approximately Dh149,000. Customs seized the gold, and further investigation is under way. On the same day, customs officers at Terminal 3 intercepted an Indian passenger arriving from Muscat on Oman Air flight WY-241. The passenger had travelled from Dubai to Muscat on connecting flight WY-612 on October 9. A personal search found two rectangular pouches containing gold paste concealed inside his socks. The pouches weighed 725g gross, including wrapping and concealment material. After finding gold in his socks, officials also recovered a 587g gold bar. A karatometer test confirmed 100 per cent purity. Customs assessed the gold’s tariff value at approximately Dh323,000 and its market value at approximately Dh364,000. The passenger told investigators the gold was brought from Dubai and concealed to avoid declaration and customs duty. Customs seized the gold under Section 110(1) of the Customs Act, 1962. Delhi Customs has reiterated its vigilance against smuggling and its commitment to strengthening enforcement at the country’s busiest international airport. According to a Reuters report in July, unofficial gold inflows in India have risen since the government raised import tariffs on the precious metal earlier this year. The World Gold Council said grey market inflows and the disruption they cause are hurting organised players. India, the world's biggest gold consumer after China, more than doubled import tariffs to 15 per cent on May 13 to curb demand, cut the trade deficit and ​ease pressure on the currency. India's net gold imports fell 23 per cent year-on-year to 98.1 tons in the June quarter, the lowest quarterly level since September ​2020, when Covid-19 pandemic lockdowns curbed demand, the WGC said in ​a report.

title: Finnish cities pushing for mandatory school attendance law
body:
A total of around 1,000 children in Finland are home-schooled, with many choosing the option for health or wellbeing reasons.
Helsinki and five other Finnish cities are calling for stricter laws on homeschooling.
According to Helsinki Mayor Daniel Sazonov (NCP), homeschooling should only be allowed in exceptional cases, for example for health reasons.
In practice, the cities are proposing that in-school attendance should be compulsory.
"Going to school is much more than just learning defined academic content, it is also a social process," Sazonov said.
Attending school is also a tool for integration, according to the mayor.
"In Helsinki, many pupils speak a language other than Finnish or Swedish as their mother tongue; it is also essential from an integration perspective that they are at school and part of the school community," he said.
Homeschooling is not a widespread phenomenon in the capital. Just over 200 children in Helsinki were being home-schooled this year, accounting for about 0.4 percent of all pupils. The number has increased in recent years, however.
A total of around 1,000 children in Finland are home-schooled, with many choosing the option for health or wellbeing reasons.
Last week, the Helsinki City Council decided to tighten supervision of homeschooled pupils.
But according to Sazonov, the jurisdiction of municipalities regarding homeschooling is limited.
Not all home-school instructors have accepted more active supervision, Sazonov said.
He noted that there have been no major problems with homeschooling in Helsinki. However, he did point to concerns raised by the Finnish Security and Intelligence Service (Supo) that homeschooling can carry the risk of promoting radicalisation.
Supo's national security review suggested that homeschooling could, over time, heighten security risks linked to social fragmentation. Its report warns that isolated educational settings may enable the spread of extremist ideologies, including radical Islamist or far-right teachings.
Helsinki University terrorism researcher Leena Malkki noted that Finland should not close its eyes to these concerns.
"Finland is a society built on trust. Supervision, and even support, is not always the strictest when it comes to home schooling," she said.
Tampere is among the cities calling for educational law change. But according to Tampere Deputy Mayor for cultural services, Anne-Mari Jussila , radicalisation risks are not the reason.
"I would prefer to see children among their peers at school, learning together with other children," she said.
Tampere currently has about 50 home-school pupils.
Jussila emphasised that radicalisation is not a problem in Tampere, even though it may be a problem elsewhere.
Newspaper Helsingin Sanomat on Tuesday queried parliamentary groups regarding homeschooling.
Left Alliance leader Minja Koskela told HS that Finland needs to introduce mandatory school attendance, arguing every child has the right to education.
Some Swedes have moved to the Åland Islands, attracted by the option of homeschooling .

title: Khaldoon Al Mubarak meets China's Wang Yi to strengthen bilateral ties
body: Khaldoon Al Mubarak, Presidential Special Envoy to China and Chairman of the Executive Affairs Authority, travelled to Beijing this week for high-level talks with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi. Mr Al Mubarak met Mr Wang in the Chinese capital on Tuesday, as part of a trip aimed at deepening the UAE-China Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. The two delegations reviewed bilateral relations under the framework of the partnership, which has served as the foundation for growing co-operation. Both parties exchanged views on issues of shared interest, with particular emphasis placed on the importance of sustained co-ordination and close consultation between Abu Dhabi and Beijing. The talks were attended by Hussain Al Hammadi, UAE ambassador to China, along with senior officials from both sides. China remains one of the UAE's most significant trading partners, and the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, established in 2018, has provided a structured platform for co-operation spanning trade, investment, technology and energy.

title: Dangote Group, Botswana Exchange Laud NGX Group for Driving Cross-Border Collaboration
body: Dangote Industries Limited and the Botswana Stock Exchange (BSE) have commended Nigerian Exchange Group (NGX Group) for bringing African exchanges together to expand cross-border investment opportunities through the ongoing roadshow for the Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals FZE offer. The commendation came on Wednesday at an investor engagement in Gaborone, following an earlier engagement in Nairobi, Kenya. The roadshow forms part of NGX Group’s wider initiative to deepen collaboration among African exchanges and widen access to investment opportunities across the continent. The Group Chief Financial Officer of Dangote Industries Limited, Murat Erden, praised NGX Group, under the leadership of Group Chairman, Alhaji Umaru Kwairanga, and Group Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer, Temi Popoola, for galvanising African exchanges around the initiative, which began with an engagement convened by NGX Group in Lagos in April 2026. He also highlighted the role of digital innovation in broadening access to the offer, citing the addition of WhatsApp to NGX Invest, and acknowledged the partnership between NGX Group and participating exchanges in reaching investors across their respective markets. The Chief Executive Officer of the BSE, Aobakwe Aupa Monyatsi, also welcomed the collaboration, highlighting the value of partnerships among African exchanges and the opportunity to widen participation by encouraging additional markets to join the initiative. At the earlier engagement in Nairobi, President and Chief Executive of Dangote Industries Limited, Aliko Dangote, lauded Kwairanga and Popoola for their role in advancing collaboration among African capital-market institutions. He highlighted how stronger ties between exchanges could enable companies to raise capital across multiple markets rather than being limited to their home markets. Citing the planned refinery in Mokowe-Lamu, Kenya, as an example, he pointed to the potential for businesses operating across Africa to list in more than one market. NGX Group Chairman, Kwairanga, said: “Our vision is to build stronger connections among African capital markets, making it easier for businesses to access capital and for investors to participate in opportunities across the continent. The collaboration around the Dangote Refinery offer demonstrates what African exchanges can achieve when we work together towards a shared objective.” Group Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer, Popoola, has similarly emphasised the importance of translating continental ambition into practical partnerships. He said: “When we began this engagement, our objective was continental: to bring African exchanges together and explore how we can create stronger connections between African capital markets.” NGX Invest, NGX Group’s electronic public-offering platform, supports subscriptions through more than 180 distribution channels, including stockbrokers, banks and fintech companies. The addition of WhatsApp as an access channel further expands the ways investors can access the offer. The roadshow continues with engagements at the Egyptian Exchange (EGX) and the Ethiopian Securities Exchange (ESX), extending the initiative’s reach and creating further opportunities for African exchanges to collaborate on cross-border investment.

title: Yemen fighting overwhelms hospitals, cuts aid to 800,000 people, relief agencies say
body: Hospitals across Yemen are struggling to cope with a sharp rise in war casualties, while intensified fighting along multiple front lines has cut off aid to around 800,000 people, humanitarian agencies said on Wednesday.Front-line hospitals in areas including Marib, Taiz and Yemen's Red Sea coast are seeing unprecedented numbers of weapon-wounded patients, with some facilities admitting more than 700 casualties in a single week, according to the Red Cross.'Trauma care staff are under enormous pressure'More ⁠than 200,000 people have ⁠been displaced from their homes since fighting ​in the country began in recent weeks, sparked by renewed ⁠fighting between ⁠the Iran-backed Houthi group and Saudi-backed government forces in Yemen, according to ‌the United Nations' International ‌Organization for Migration."Trauma care staff are under enormous pressure," ICRC health coordinator Feras Abusamra said in a statement. Only a small proportion of Yemen's functioning health facilities are capable of providing comprehensive trauma care, he said, while hospitals face large numbers of wounded people amid shortages of surgical supplies, anesthesia, oxygen and medicines.Yemen's health services, battered by more than a decade of conflict, economic crisis, displacement and disease outbreaks, may have limited capacity to absorb a new surge in mass casualties if fighting intensifies further, the ICRC warned.The fighting has also cut off life-saving humanitarian assistance for 800,000 people in Taiz - Yemen's third-largest city, which currently hosts the largest number of people fleeing the fighting - and other areas impacted by the conflict, the UN World Food Program said on Wednesday.Some districts are now inaccessible because of fighting and road closures, the WFP said, adding that wheat flour stocks are nearly exhausted and remaining food in local markets may last only a short time."This is the kind of situation that can rapidly spiral into a humanitarian catastrophe if assistance cannot move safely and reach those who need it most," said El-Khidir Daloum, WFP Representative and Country Director in Yemen, in a statement.

title: 2027: I’ve handed everything over to God, says INEC chairman
body: By Folarin Kehinde The chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Ojo Amupitan, has said he has handed everything over to God as he confronts the responsibility of conducting the 2027 general election. Amupitan, who spoke on Wednesday at the Artificial Intelligence and Democracy Forum 2026 in Abuja, said his faith in God remained his anchor amid the enormous demands of his office. He said, “I’m being reminded of the enormity of the task on me. I’m also encouraged by the word of God, which is, ‘Come unto me, all you that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.’ So that has been my anchor. “And sometimes people say, ‘You are not bothered.’ I said, I’ve handed over everything to God.” The INEC chairman spoke at the forum organised by Yiaga Africa, which had as its theme, “Safeguarding the 2027 General Election in the Age of Artificial Intelligence.” Addressing participants, Amupitan assured Nigerians that artificial intelligence would not determine the outcome of the 2027 general election, insisting that the power to choose the country’s leaders rested with the electorate. He said, “No, algorithms will not and must never decide the 2027 votes. Algorithms will not decide the vote because the choice of who leads Nigeria belongs exclusively to the Nigerian people.” According to him, while AI would influence the information voters receive, electoral logistics and political communication, the technology must remain a tool for strengthening democracy rather than undermining it. “Our task, therefore, at this forum and within the Commission is to ensure that AI remains a servant of democracy, not its master,” he said. Amupitan said the 2027 general election would involve more than 103 million registered voters across 176,846 polling units in the 36 states of the federation and the Federal Capital Territory. He noted that the scale of the exercise, coupled with difficult terrain, insecurity and poor network coverage in some communities, posed significant logistical challenges for the commission. The INEC chairman disclosed that the commission had completed 10 of the 14 major activities on its election timetable, despite the strict timelines prescribed by the Electoral Act 2026. He added that INEC had procured and begun receiving additional Bimodal Voter Accreditation System devices to strengthen its technological capacity ahead of the polls. Amupitan also said the commission had digitised its candidate nomination process through the INEC Candidate Nomination Portal, which had processed more than 15,000 nominations across 22 political parties. He further disclosed that INEC had introduced online voter registration and was implementing a decentralised, multi-phase Permanent Voter Card collection exercise nationwide. On the use of AI in election administration, the INEC chairman said the technology could improve the deployment of election materials and personnel through predictive modelling and geospatial analysis. According to him, AI-driven systems can analyse traffic patterns, weather forecasts, road conditions and security incidents to determine suitable routes for transporting electoral materials to polling units. He said such systems could also provide early warnings of weather-related disruptions and help the commission identify logistical challenges before election day. On electoral integrity, Amupitan said biometric voter accreditation and electronic transmission of polling-unit results had helped address vulnerabilities associated with manual accreditation and arbitrary manipulation of results. He added that AI could assist in auditing uploaded polling-unit result sheets by identifying mathematical inconsistencies, unusual entry patterns and discrepancies in image quality. However, he stressed that human collation remained the statutory standard for declaring election results, while AI could provide additional support in detecting anomalies. The INEC chairman said the commission would continue to work with civil society organisations, technology firms, regulatory bodies and security agencies to harness the benefits of AI while addressing potential threats to the electoral process. He maintained that the ultimate responsibility of electoral stakeholders was to ensure that technological advancements strengthened democratic institutions without compromising the right of Nigerians to freely choose their leaders. title: Women in Tech Uzbekistan Forum Highlights Growing Demand for AI Skills
body: Uzbekistan is attracting foreign technology companies, expanding IT education, and training young people to work with artificial intelligence. But employers’ needs are changing faster than educational programs can adapt. Just a few years ago, companies were looking for programmers, then cloud technology specialists. Now they need developers capable of building AI systems and autonomous digital agents. Against this backdrop, discussions in Tashkent are focusing on how to increase women’s participation in the technology industry and enable them not only to learn new tools but also to develop their own products. These issues took center stage at the Women in Tech Leadership Forum , held on October 13 at Uzbekistan’s Ministry of Digital Technologies. The event brought together approximately 300 representatives of government agencies, international organizations, technology companies, and the business community. It was organized by the ministry and Women in Tech Uzbekistan, the national chapter of an international organization working to expand women’s participation in technology. Kamola Sobirova, an adviser to Uzbekistan’s Minister of Digital Technologies /ТСА Employers Need More Than Programmers Kamola Sobirova, an adviser to Uzbekistan’s Minister of Digital Technologies, explained in an exclusive interview with The Times of Central Asia how international companies’ requirements for local specialists have changed. “A few years ago, there was high demand for programmers. A year or two later, companies started asking us for cloud technology specialists. Then artificial intelligence emerged, and companies needed AI architects and prompt engineers,” Sobirova said. According to Sobirova, employers are now looking for specialists who can develop AI agents – software systems capable of independently carrying out sequences of tasks using artificial intelligence. “We cannot afford to stand still because technology continues to evolve. We must train specialists with up-to-date skills and create the right conditions for them,” she said. Uzbekistan previously ran the One Million Uzbek Coders program and has since launched the Five Million AI Leaders initiative. These programs are designed to provide large-scale training in digital skills, including programming and working with artificial intelligence. AI and the future of women’s work The question of whether AI will eliminate jobs was also raised during the interview. Sobirova rejected the idea that the main effect of AI would simply be widespread job losses. “There is a trend that everyone thinks AI will take over many professions and replace them, or that artificial intelligence has arrived and we will lose our jobs, but it is not like that,” she said. “Artificial intelligence will take the jobs of people who do not have artificial intelligence skills.” She argued that AI should increasingly be viewed as a tool that allows people to work more efficiently rather than simply as a replacement for workers. “Life has become much faster, and in this process artificial intelligence can help us become full users of AI and optimize our work,” Sobirova said. She also said the same principle applies to journalism and other media-related work, where AI can be used to support different parts of the workflow. “Coursera [an online learning platform] recently identified Uzbekistan as a role model, because in terms of the number of users studying artificial intelligence, women in Uzbekistan have reached first place globally,” she said. “Among users taking generative AI courses, 58.9% are women.” The forum therefore placed particular attention on whether women can move beyond simply using new technologies and become people who develop and lead them. She said some international online courses can be expensive, but Uzbekistan has introduced mechanisms to reimburse certain educational expenses after participants complete approved courses and submit their certificates through the my.gov.uz system. “Recently, Google’s training in the field of artificial intelligence became free in the Uzbek language specifically for Uzbekistan,” Sobirova said. “A $60 training became free for Uzbek students and users in Uzbekistan. This is also a very big opportunity.” She said the government’s approach is intended not only to increase the number of people with technical skills but also to strengthen Uzbekistan’s position as a technology destination. Makhliyo Muksinova, Director of Strategic Development at IT Park Uzbekistan/ТСА A Young Population and a Growing IT Sector Makhliyo Muksinova, Director of Strategic Development at IT Park Uzbekistan, linked the industry’s growth to economic reforms and the arrival of international companies. According to figures she presented, Uzbekistan has a population of approximately 39 million, with around 65% under the age of 35. About 650,000 young people enter the labor market each year. For the IT sector, this represents both a potential source of employees and a need to create new jobs every year. Muksinova said Uzbekistan has more than 220 universities, with approximately 25,000 students graduating annually in IT-related fields. According to figures presented at the forum, the number of women enrolled in higher education increased almost fivefold between 2018 and 2025. Women now account for approximately half of all university students. The number of technology companies is also growing. According to Muksinova, IT Park Uzbekistan has more than 4,000 registered resident companies, including over 1,000 foreign companies and more than 1,000 export-oriented businesses. These companies employ more than 56,000 people, while their combined revenue reached $2.8 billion in 2025. Muksinova valued Uzbekistan’s startup ecosystem at $4.3 billion. She said more than 100 Uzbek startups had already opened offices abroad. From Education to Leadership in Technology Companies “Women in Tech has brought leaders from different parts of the world to the region to inspire the next generation,” Ayumi Moore Aoki, founder and president of Women in Tech Global, told TCA . The Uzbekistan chapter of Women in Tech was established in March 2024 in cooperation with the Ministry of Digital Technologies. Its activities include mentoring, supporting women entrepreneurs, and narrowing the gender gap in the digital sector. Aoki believes Uzbekistan’s young population gives the country an advantage in adopting new technologies. At the same time, she emphasized the importance of combining AI skills with human knowledge and experience. The international organization aims to reach five million women and girls by 2030. According to Aoki, expanding its programs will require women leaders capable of building their own teams and supporting other participants. The forum also hosted the Women in Tech CCA Awards, a regional awards program recognizing women working in technology across Central Asia and the Caucasus. The 2026 finalists included 46 women and projects, including 15 representatives from Uzbekistan. Award categories covered startups, technology diplomacy, Web3, and other fields. Emel Gümüş, founder and CEO of EGG Global Group, who has lived in Tashkent for four years, highlighted the opportunities for cooperation. “We have an opportunity to work together — women from Uzbekistan and other countries — and create something new,” she told TCA . Skilled Workers Matter More Than Presentations Uzbekistan aims to expand its exports of digital services and attract international companies. Achieving these goals requires specialists capable of working with technologies that were in limited demand just a few years ago. Sobirova described the challenge through her experience working with foreign investors: “No matter how much we praise ourselves and say, ‘Look, we have wonderful conditions, come here,’ when they arrive, the first thing they encounter is the specialist. If they struggle to find the specialists they need, they won’t believe our beautiful words. They will believe in our specialists.” Image: TCA

title: Call of the Wilde: Montreal Canadiens win their second straight in a shootout shading the Buffalo Sabres
body:
They were separated by only a goal last spring in Game Seven of their second-round playoff series. This season, though, many believe the Buffalo Sabres aren’t as strong without Alex Tuch and Bowen Byram. However, Buffalo has drafted impressive talent to fill the gaps, including Noah Ostlund and Konsta Helenius, both of whom could become stars.
In the immediate future, though, anxiety lingers in the Sabres organization after Rasmus Dahlin’s back injury, as he stayed in Buffalo for Tuesday night’s contest at the Bell Centre.
The Montreal Canadiens dominated the Sabres over 60 minutes, outshooting them 34-17, yet the game went to overtime and then a shootout, with the Canadiens winning 4-3. Justice got the last word.
The Canadiens had to switch defensive pairings after Mike Matheson went day-to-day. Thankfully, the club has seen Kaiden Guhle return, pairing with Alexandre Carrier. That left Lane Hutson to find Noah Dobson on his right. The final pairing had Adam Engstrom and Arber Xhekaj.
It may sound unusual, but as Guhle’s play improves, the pecking order could change as Matheson ages. Matheson is the senior citizen on a very young blue line.
Guhle has the most upside, but he’s been injured so often that he hasn’t had a chance to live up to his first-round draft-pick status or his MVP award in the Western Hockey League playoffs for the Edmonton Oil Kings.
At only 24, Guhle still has upside. In his first two games back from a core injury that required surgery, he looks poised. It’s hard to keep up at the start of a season, but Guhle has had no issue, especially on penalty kills, where he brings the right skill set.
After the overtime concluded, Guhle cross-checked every Sabres player he could find, then punched Ryan McLeod. He didn’t care. He was hungry to be involved. Alexandre Carrier made a decisive, courageous block, killing the final penalty with three seconds remaining.
Hutson leads the blue line as he continues his point-per-game pace, as he did last season. In the first, with a two-man advantage, the Canadiens had to seize the moment. Hutson did, firing a shot into the top corner from 30 feet. Guhle and Hutson were locked in for most of the night.
Late in the second frame, Hutson delivered a masterclass. He took a pass from Zachary Bolduc, then deked two, looked at the net as if only a shot was on his mind, moved within 15 feet, and fed a backhand pass onto the tape of Josh Anderson, who one-timed it home.
That put a bow on an outstanding first two periods as the Sabres mustered only nine shots on goal. That’s a far cry from what they were able to achieve offensively last playoffs when they broke down the Canadiens’ defence.
The other Canadiens goal in the first two periods was from Cole Caufield as he ripped a pass from Juraj Slafkovsky home for his third of the season. Nick Suzuki with the helper for his eighth point of the year in six games. A second point for both Caufield and Slafkovsky.
Another strong performance was turned in by Alex Newhook. He continues to look comfortable centring the line with Anderson and Chris Kreider. In the first period, Kreider and Anderson had a two-on-one that they handled beautifully with some give-and-go passes, but Anderson couldn’t convert.
Jake Evans hasn’t found the scoresheet yet, but he’s contributing. Evans work on the penalty kill was superb implicating all over the ice. He met attackers at the Buffalo blue nine stymying them, then he fought hard to clear pucks with good puck pressure. Evans stood out as intelligent all night.
This one went to an eventful shootout. The Canadiens scored on all three attempts. Caufield and Alexandre Texier ripped their shots, then Bolduc made a stunning move opening up the goalie’s legs then sliding it home mid-deke.
The Canadiens deserved to win. They dominated through out.
With the Matheson injury, it was a chance for Engstrom to prove the organization made a sound move allowing Jayden Struble to play more minutes in Nashville. However, it was a not-ready-for-prime-time moment for Engstrom on his first shift.
Engstrom had a chance to clear and gave the puck away with little pressure and a lot of time. That’s a combination that shows a defender is not ready. He couldn’t make a proper decision with all the factors in his favour.
To compound the anxiety, the point shot went off his leg when he wasn’t looking at the play and ricocheted in to the net. Jacob Fowler had absolutely no chance as the shot was heading wide by four feet.
In the third period, it happened again. Josh Norris fired a harmless looking shot from 50 feet. Engstrom tried to block it and it hit the inside of his leg for another perfect deflection leaving Fowler no chance.
The Sabres tying marker was also a weak point shot just thrown at the net, and for a third time, it was a Canadiens player who put it in as this one went off Hutson. Domination by the Canadiens, but the Sabres get three goals to tie it.
Hockey is a game of chaos. All three goals for Buffalo could have just as easily hit the Canadiens defender and defected into the corner.
It was more frustration for Kirby Dach. In the first period, Dach took a penalty on the back-check as he didn’t keep his feet moving, then had to hold an attacker who was getting away from him. Dach is struggling.
They’d dress someone else, if they thought someone else in the organization could do better, but they are a bit thin with injuries to Oliver Kapanen and Ivan Demidov.
The Canadiens are in desperate need of a second line centre. The management team may look for that hole to fill as soon as this trading deadline, but if they don’t find the right match, Michael Hage is showing he is ready for the assignment.
Hage is too good for college hockey in his third year. In his first four games of the season, Hage has 12 points. A point-per-game in college hockey is an excellent number. His average of three will go down, but it’s still an amazing start.
The competition has been easy so far allowing for the big totals. Bowling Green and Alaska are not dominant programs. This weekend, will be the real test to see if Hage can maintain these numbers. The Michigan Wolverines play the Denver Pioneers on the road on Thursday and Friday.
The other sparkling performance among the prospects so far this season for the Canadiens is a surprise. It’s Luke Middlestadt playing for the Laval Rocket. He has been an absolute star in the American Hockey League to start the season.
As a defender, Middlestadt has seven points in only four games. This, after a tremendous training camp in Montreal. Middlestadt had a strong four year career at the University of Minnesota. He may be a stunning steal in the seventh round 197th overall.
The fear is that he is too small at under six feet, but he didn’t have any issues in camp being pushed around, nor does he have any issues in Laval. Middlestadt is only one point off the league scoring lead. That lead is held by another Rocket player Laurent Dauphin.
Brian Wilde, a Montreal-based sportswriter, brings you Call of the Wilde on globalnews.ca after each Canadiens game.

title: Commandos build underground hospital near Glasgow
body: Commando engineers have dug and built an underground field hospital near Glasgow so that surgeons can resuscitate and operate on casualties below ground, in a trial drawing directly on how Ukrainian medics have been forced to work, according to the Royal Navy. Soldiers of 24 Commando Royal Engineers spent six days building the facility at Barnsford Bridge, excavating around 243 cubic metres of rock and soil to create a space twenty metres square, about the size of one and a half tennis courts. Medical specialists from the Special Operations Surgical Team and the Commando Forward Surgical Group then used it to resuscitate and operate on simulated casualties during Exercise Strike Warrior in south west Scotland. Chief Petty Officer Ellie Walls of the Commando Forward Surgical Group set out why the work is being done at all. “As an organisation we see the need to develop our ability to build, survive, work and live in these spaces as medics now are not always protected by the Red Cross and can be routinely targeted,” she said. “We can look at the lessons learnt from Ukraine and other medical uses of the subterranean space but we have to start experiencing the issues for ourselves to really understand and work through the problem. When looking at using the subterranean space, we have to evaluate if the risks from being below ground outweigh the risks from being above ground.” She added: “However, our demands can be quite specific, we have to take into account the needs of the casualty and ensuring the environment does not negatively impact their outcome.” Lieutenant Michael Mathers, Access Troop Commander of 54 Commando Squadron, whose troops were given the task, said: “By designing, constructing, and handing over this facility, our troops gained first-hand experience of the realities of modern peer-on-peer conflict, where survivability, protection, and concealment are critical to success. “Beyond delivering a unique capability, the project provided invaluable engineering training across multiple trades, challenging our soldiers to develop new skills and adapt established techniques to a novel environment. “Equally important, it highlighted where we must continue to innovate, ensuring lessons identified are refined, shared, and integrated in future designs and shared across UK Commando Force and the Corps of Royal Engineers.” Putting a clinical environment into what amounts to a hole in the ground threw up problems a tented field hospital never has to solve as soil contaminants, bacteria and pests all bear on whether a patient survives, and once it was handed over the medical teams worked out how to allocate power, how to move casualties through the compartments according to their injuries and how to move around at all. Surgical teams are used to light, air circulation, plumbing, electricity and the room to move and resupply, none of which a trench offers, and the effect of working without them on the clinicians themselves came under examination too. “Whilst it has given us some answers it has generated a lot of questions and thoughts,” CPO Walls said. “If we can prepare our equipment and people to work in such areas, we give our patients a better chance of survival.” The Navy described the facility as a prototype, part of an effort to develop, trial and standardise subterranean facilities for use across the UK Commando Force and the Corps of Royal Engineers, with the intention of taking the concept through to full operational capability. Small attack drones and loitering munitions have made the ground behind the front line as dangerous as the front itself, and both sides have pushed stabilisation points, casualty collection and surgery underground into cellars, dugouts and bunkers. The post Commandos build underground hospital near Glasgow first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: NHRC laments rising cases of rights violations, receives 338,810 petitions
body: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA — The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) on Wednesday expressed concern over the increasing cases of rights violations in the country, revealing that it received a total of 338,810 complaints in September alone. According to the Commission, the majority of petitions lodged before it were from the North-Central geopolitical zone, with most cases originating from Benue, Plateau and Niger states. The Executive Secretary of the NHRC, Dr. Tony Ojukwu, SAN, said the Commission’s human rights dashboard showed an increase of 40,867 complaints, approximately 14 per cent, compared with the 297,943 recorded in August. “This figure is significant and calls for sustained attention. While an increase in complaints may reflect greater public awareness of human rights and improved access to the Commission’s services, it equally underscores the enormous responsibility placed upon the Commission and other duty-bearers to respond effectively to allegations of violations. “Our concern must therefore extend beyond the number of complaints received to the quality of investigations conducted, the remedies secured for victims and the preventive measures put in place to address recurring violations. “The human rights landscape in Nigeria during September 2026 continued to present serious challenges, particularly in relation to the right to life, personal liberty, human dignity, security of persons and the protection of vulnerable populations. “Insecurity remained a major concern, with reports of killings, kidnappings and attacks on communities in different parts of the country. “Of particular concern were the continuing reports of mass abductions in Niger State, where families and communities expressed anguish over the prolonged captivity of their loved ones. The Commission reiterates that the protection of life and property is a fundamental obligation of the State. “We therefore call on relevant security agencies to intensify efforts towards securing affected communities, rescuing abducted persons and ensuring that perpetrators of these crimes are brought to justice,” Ojukwu, SAN, added. He said the Commission was also concerned about the persistent vulnerability of women and children to sexual and gender-based violence, exploitation, abuse and other forms of discrimination. “These violations demand stronger preventive mechanisms, survivor-centred responses, effective investigations and improved access to justice. “In this regard, we welcome the national stakeholders’ engagement held in September on the review of the Child Rights Act, 2003. “This presents an important opportunity to strengthen Nigeria’s child protection framework and address gaps in the prevention of violence, exploitation and abuse against children. “We urge relevant authorities to ensure that these reform efforts translate into stronger institutions, adequate resources and practical protection for children, particularly those in vulnerable and underserved communities. “The Commission remains committed to improving its monitoring and reporting mechanisms, strengthening investigations and complaints resolution, and ensuring that its findings inform policies and institutional reforms. “Our objective is not merely to document violations after they occur, but to contribute to a system where violations are prevented, victims obtain justice and public institutions are held accountable,” the NHRC boss added, even as he called for increased funding for the Commission. Meanwhile, a Special Human Rights Adviser to the Commission, Mr. Hillary Ogbonna, who gave a breakdown of some of the cases in the dashboard, said a total of 208 killings by non-state actors and 210 kidnappings were recorded in September. He said the Commission visited 113 detention centres across the federation and issued 56 summons to the police over cases of human rights abuses. The post NHRC laments rising cases of rights violations, receives 338,810 petitions appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Kremlin comments on Kiev fighting with Trump, strikes on data centers, protective measures
body:
MOSCOW, October 14. /TASS/. Russian authorities are in touch with the business on the topic of Kiev regime strikes against datacenters, Kremlin Spokesman Dmitry Peskov said.
He noted that Russian companies are taking measures to safeguard themselves against Kiev regime strikes.
Peskov also stressed that the Kiev regime’s harsh statements directed at US President Donald Trump will not help Vladimir Zelensky and will not contribute to accelerating a peaceful settlement.
TASS has compiled the Kremlin spokesman’s key statements.
Russian authorities are in touch with the business on the topic of Kiev regime strikes against data centers: "The leadership of the country is certainly thinking about these problems and the government is in the dialogue with the business."
Russian companies are taking measures to safeguard themselves against Kiev regime strikes: "All the companies are taking measures to ensure physical security, although these are clearly very complex and rather costly measures."
The Kiev regime’s harsh statements directed at US President Donald Trump will not help Vladimir Zelensky and will not contribute to accelerating a peaceful settlement: "The [negotiation] style of the Kiev regime’s representatives is well known to us and to the whole world. I don’t think spatting with the US president will help the Kiev regime in any way. At this point, it’s unlikely anything can help it. But the fact that this spatting does not contribute to accelerated progress toward a peaceful settlement is unequivocal."
A trilateral meeting in China between Russian President Vladimir Putin, US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping would be highly beneficial, but it remains unclear whether the leaders’ schedules will coincide: "There is a shared view that it would be good to hold such a meeting. But we do not yet know how well the leaders’ schedules align, and we do not yet know what the agenda for such a meeting might be. However, there is a shared understanding that it would be highly beneficial."
Nuclear arsenals are unlikely to feature on the agenda of such a meeting, should one take place: "Nuclear arsenals are not an appropriate topic to bring up."
Moscow respects Beijing’s position that China’s nuclear arsenal is currently incomparable to those of Moscow and Washington: "You know that our Chinese friends believe their nuclear potential is currently incomparable to the nuclear capabilities of Russia and the United States; they believe there is no subject for discussion. That is China’s position, and we respect it. Therefore, it is unlikely that this issue could be discussed in a trilateral format,"
A meeting between Russian President Vladimir Putin and his US counterpart Donald Trump has not yet been agreed upon, but if they happen to be at the same venue during the APEC summit in China: "No, not yet. But if they happen to be together in China, then, of course, one can assume that such a meeting will be discussed."
There has been no official statement from the US on the slowdown of the Starlink service for the Ukrainian armed forces, so it is too early to jump to conclusions: "How do we know this? This is just completely scattered information. ‘What if…’ Indeed, there is a lot of information suggesting that there are some restrictions on the provision of intelligence and early warning information about our missile launches. But, on the other hand, there have also been statements from Washington that the assistance is continuing."
"We need to wait for some more or less specific information here,"
"We don’t know what the US has done. How can we speculate about what it can or cannot do? We haven’t heard any official statements from representatives of [Elon] Musk’s company [which owns the service], nor have we heard any official statements from representatives of the Kiev regime on this matter."
"We’ve heard statements from [US President Donald] Trump that aid is continuing. Let’s analyze the information as it comes in and not rush to conclusions."
Asked if Moscow had taken part in the consultations, the Kremlin spokesman answered in the negative.
Russia did not participate in consultations on a package agreement on resolving the Ukraine conflict, allegedly prepared by Washington, and so far has no plans to take part in any trilateral talks on the issue: "We don’t expect them at the moment. You know that the president said: after Ukraine tried to disrupt our elections, we will think about when to resume trilateral talks."
Moscow will decide whether to resume trilateral consultations on the Ukrainian settlement with Kiev and Washington at a later date and strictly in accordance with Russia’s national interests: "We will do so strictly in accordance with our national interests.".

title: Saudi Crown Prince meets Iraq's Prime Minister in Riyadh
body: Saudi Crown Prince Mohamed bin Salman received Iraq's Prime Ali Al Zaidi in Riyadh on Wednesday, in the first visit by a foreign leader to the Saudi capital since a deadly Houthi attack on its airport . The Saudi Press Agency published footage and pictures of the meeting between the Crown Prince and Mr Al Zaidi. The Iraqi Prime Minister's office said they discussed “the latest regional developments and co-ordination of efforts in a way that enhances the security and stability of the region”. Saudi Arabia has faced widening Houthi strikes over the past week, including an attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Saturday that killed 13 people. The airport has come under attack four times, ​including Saturday's attack, which was the deadliest in Saudi Arabia in a decade. Authorities have closed the airport until October ​17, and airlines have cancelled ‌flights to Saudi Arabia. It is not known how Mr Al Zaidi travelled to the country. Saudi Arabia intervened in Yemen's civil war in ⁠support of the government in 2015, fearing the rise of Iranian influence and the prospect of chaos on its borders, after the Houthis seized the capital, Sanaa. The UN brokered a 2022 truce between the warring ⁠sides in Yemen that kept a fragile peace until this year. Saudi Arabia resumed its military campaign in Yemen in support of the internationally recognised government in a bid to reverse the Houthis' sudden gains last month, when they swept along the Red Sea coast to the critical Bab Al Mandeb strait. The Red Cross said on Wednesday that hospitals across Yemen are struggling to cope with a sharp rise in war ​casualties as fighting intensified along multiple front lines. The UN World Food Programme (WFP) warned that life-saving assistance had been cut off to the government-held city of Taiz, which was encircled by Houthi fighters earlier this month. “WFP and its partners cannot access more than 600,000 people in Taiz who depend on humanitarian assistance, including more than 200,000 women and children,” the WFP said in a statement.

title: Moscow Hails Trump Diesel Deal, Promises Direct Exports to U.S.
body:
The Kremlin said on Thursday that Russian diesel had begun to reach global markets following an agreement with U.S. President Donald Trump.
Trump said last week that Russia had agreed to supply diesel to global markets in an effort to lower fuel prices, while Moscow partially lifted its ban on diesel exports from Oct. 10 following the agreement.
"The diesel has started reaching global markets and is expected to have a positive effect on stabilising oil markets, although it will not be enough to fully stabilize them," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters on a daily conference call.
LSEG data showed on Wednesday that Russia had resumed diesel export loadings from the Baltic port of Primorsk.
According to the shipping data, a tanker carrying around 40,000 metric tons of ultra-low sulphur diesel was loaded on Tuesday and was heading towards Morocco.
Under the terms announced by Trump last Friday, Russia agreed to immediately release more than 300,000 metric tons of diesel onto global markets, followed by an additional 500,000 metric tons in November.
The initial 300,000 metric tons (2.25 million barrels) is less than a day's supply for the U.S. transportation sector alone, according to U.S. Energy Information Administration data, which shows daily use of around 2.94 million barrels.
The U.S. Treasury Department issued a license authorizing transactions involving Russian diesel through April 7, 2027.
The deal has sparked pushback from European and Ukrainian officials, who argued that unlocking Russian energy revenues directly fuels the Kremlin’s war effort.
Russia has rejected European criticism of the diesel deal as "cynical," given that Europe continues to buy some Russia n oil and liquefied natural gas.
Peskov's comments came a day after Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said the diesel supply deal with the U.S. would boost Russia’s economy and include direct exports to the U.S. market.
“Without a doubt, this is a positive signal for our economy,” Novak told reporters on the sidelines of the Russian Energy Week forum in Moscow, according to the state-run news agency TASS.
“In accordance with the agreements, supplies will go to world markets, as well as the U.S. directly,” he said .
He added that Russia aims to restore monthly diesel exports to 3.5 million metric tons by the end of 2026, bringing its share of the global market above 10%.
