title: Nigeria secures 172 votes for UN Human Rights Council seat
body: By Favour Ulebor Nigeria has been elected to the United Nations Human Rights Council for the 2027–2029 term after securing 172 votes in an election conducted by the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday, October 13, 2026. The Federal Government announced the election in a statement issued on Wednesday and signed by the Spokesperson of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Oluwafemi Adeniyi. According to the statement, Nigeria was elected alongside 14 other countries to serve a three-year term beginning January 1, 2027, and ending December 31, 2029. The 47-member council is responsible for promoting and protecting human rights globally and strengthening international cooperation on human rights issues. The Federal Government expressed appreciation to United Nations member states for supporting Nigeria’s candidature. It also reaffirmed the country’s commitment to dialogue, cooperation and mutual respect in advancing the council’s mandate. “The Federal Government of Nigeria wishes to announce Nigeria’s election to the United Nations (UN) Human Rights Council for the 2027–2029 term, having secured 172 of 181 votes during the Council’s election held on 13 October 2026 by the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA),” the statement said. “Nigeria was elected alongside fourteen other countries to serve a three-year term commencing on 01 January 2027 and ending on 31 December 2029.” The government said Nigeria looked forward to working closely with other council members to strengthen international efforts towards the promotion and protection of human rights. It added that the country remained committed to constructive multilateral engagement and initiatives that uphold human dignity, justice and fundamental freedoms. Nigeria is expected to begin its three-year membership in January 2027, joining other elected members in addressing human rights concerns and promoting international cooperation on the protection of fundamental rights. The post Nigeria secures 172 votes for UN Human Rights Council seat appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Russia, Egypt agree to expand direct air service opportunities
body:
MOSCOW, October 14. /TASS/. Russia and Egypt has signed a memorandum making it possible for nominated air carriers to increase the number of direct flights between the countries, the Russian Ministry of Transport said.
"Russia and Egypt expand opportunities for the direct air service. A memorandum of understanding was signed in conclusion of talks between air authorities of the two countries. The Russian delegation was headed by Deputy Transport Minister Vladimir Poteshkin, and the Egyptian one - by President of the Egyptian Civil Aviation Authority Sameh Fawzy. The document will enable nominated air carriers to make more direct flights," the ministry said.
This will make flights more affordable for nationals of both countries, the ministry noted. The parties also intend to continue forging cooperation in the civil aviation sphere.

title: Fire Spreads at Rostov Oil Terminal After Drone Attack
body:
Another storage tank exploded at an oil terminal in Russia’s southern city of Rostov-on-Don late Tuesday, as a fire sparked by a drone attack continued to burn for a fourth day, monitoring channels reported.
The blaze at the Novoshakhtinsk oil refinery’s terminal has spread to eight of its 12 storage tanks, the independent news outlet Astra reported . The Ukrainian monitoring channel Supernova+ said another tank exploded late Tuesday.
Footage from the site showed tanks engulfed in flames beneath columns of black smoke. The local Telegram channel Rostov Glavny reported a bright flash on the city’s left bank at 11:50 p.m. Tuesday.
Drones struck the terminal, formerly known as Yug Rusi, in Rostov’s Zheleznodorozhny district overnight on Oct. 10. NASA’s FIRMS satellite monitoring system detected a fire at the site.
Authorities had not announced that the blaze had been extinguished as of Wednesday morning.
The terminal’s storage tanks have a combined capacity of 60,000 cubic meters. The facility can handle 3.5 million metric tons of petroleum products a year, loading sea and river tankers for export. It has also been used to supply fuel to the Russian military.
Separately, Rostov region Governor Yury Slyusar said the region came under a large-scale drone attack overnight Wednesday. More than 160 drones were shot down over the city of Kamensk-Shakhtinsky and eight districts, he said, without providing information on casualties or damage on the ground.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he had ordered his military to halt strikes on Russian oil refineries from Oct. 11 at U.S. President Donald Trump’s request as part of an “energy ceasefire.”
Moscow has yet to confirm that it is observing the arrangement. The strike that sparked the terminal fire preceded the announced halt.

title: Total number of jobs advertised increased 32% year-on-year to 3,578 in 7 months of 2026
body: The number of jobs advertised in selected print and online media, which partially gauges labour demand in the economy, increased in July 2026 relative to what was observed in the corresponding period a year ago. In total, 3,578 job adverts were recorded in July 2026, the September 2026 Monetary Policy Report has stated. This is compared with 2,703 for the same period in 2025, indicating an increase of 32.4% year-on-year. Conversely, on a month-on-month basis, the number of job vacancies in July 2026 marginally declined by 1.4% from the 3,629 jobs advertised in June 2026. Cumulatively, for the first seven months of 2026, the total number of advertised jobs increased by 8.2% to 23,052 from the 21,307 recorded during the same period in 2025. Private Sector Pension Contributors Meanwhile, the total number of private-sector SSNIT contributors, which partially gauges employment conditions, improved by 6.1% to 1,178,451 in July 2026. This is compared with 1,110,976 for the same period in 2025. On a month-on-month basis, the total number of private-sector SSNIT contributors remained largely unchanged from the 1,176,723 individuals recorded in June 2026.

title: Nord Stream blasts should be classified as war crime, German prosecutor says
body:
HAMBURG, October 14. /TASS/. The Office of Germany’s Federal Prosecutor believes that the actions of Sergey Kuznetsov, a suspect in the Nord Stream blast case, should be considered a war crime.
The trial is underway at the Hamburg Higher Regional Court. The first hearing today lasted a little over two hours.
"Since he committed the acts while being a Ukrainian army officer and with the knowledge of Ukrainian government agencies, they should be regarded as a war crime," the prosecutor said. The Ukrainian is charged with carrying out the blasts, destroying structures and disrupting the operation of a public enterprise.
The German prosecution believes that Kuznetsov, who allegedly led a subversive group, and his accomplices devised a plan to blow up the gas pipelines on orders from Ukrainian state agencies. Another Ukrainian citizen was detained in Croatia recently. Investigators believe that the saboteurs used forged documents to rent a sailing yacht from a German company and transported explosives to the Nord Stream pipelines. Kuznetsov was detained in Italy in 2025 and transferred to Germany.
The court has scheduled 24 hearings through the end of the year. Further hearings are planned for February, but they have yet to be finalized. The next hearing is set for October 27.

title: FACE Consortium opens membership to NATO countries, Japan, South Korea
body:
SAN FRANCISCO, Calif. The Open Group Future Airborne Capability Environment, or FACE, Consortium announced that it will open membership to organizations from NATO member countries, Japan, and South Korea, a move that substantially expands the international community that can participate in the Consortium.
Through the expanded membership, eligible organizations will be able to participate in defining and evolving the FACE Technical Standards, gain early access to documents and tools, network with government and industry experts, and participate in select events with Consortium members.
According to the announcement, FACE Consortium membership will be open to any business or organization incorporated in or registered to do business in NATO countries, plus Australia, Japan, New Zealand, or South Korea. Organizations will be able to sign up for three different levels of membership -- Principal, Sponsor, or Associate -- each of which carry unique benefits. Once an organization becomes a member of the FACE Consortium, all its employees are eligible to participate, provided they are persons of one of the 26 countries and complete the appropriate paperwork to become onboarded .
Alicia Taylor, The Open Group FACE Consortium Director, said: “The eligibility expansion will help us build a broader international community in the Consortium. By bringing together a wider range of government and industry stakeholders, we can strengthen collaboration, share expertise, and continue to develop practical approaches that support the delivery and reuse of software across airborne platforms. We look forward to working with our new members and the valuable perspectives they will bring.”
The FACE Technical Standards go beyond military aviation into commercial avionics, shipboard systems, ground vehicles, uncrewed air/ground/maritime systems, and training and simulation systems. The expansion is also aimed at addressing common software development and integration challenges enabling better alignment of requirements and greater reuse across national boundaries.

title: Yemen's Houthis vow more attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities after Aramco HQ hit
body: Yemen's Houthis vowed on Wednesday to press on with attacks on airports and oil facilities in Saudi Arabia and said they struck the headquarters of oil giant Saudi Aramco, which was hit the day before.The Iran-aligned group said it had launched ballistic missiles, cruise missiles and drones at Saudi Aramco facilities in the eastern city of Dhahran, King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and an Aramco refinery in Riyadh, without saying when.Saudi Arabia has faced widening Houthi strikes over the past week, including an attack on Riyadh airport on Saturday that killed 13 people.The Houthis say they have been retaliating for the kingdom's backing of Yemeni government forces in the Yemen war that restarted last month, reignited by the US-Iran confrontation in the Gulf.In a broad threat, the Houthis urged "international shipping companies," civilians and workers to evacuate airports and oil facilities, which they declared legitimate military targets.Saudi-led forces say they intercept missileThe Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted a ballistic missile fired by the Houthis towards Riyadh on Wednesday, and several loud booms were heard in the Saudi capital.Saudi authorities earlier issued an alert for a possible aerial threat in Riyadh on Wednesday before the warning was lifted, a witness said. It wasn't immediately clear what caused the booms and there was no immediate comment from the authorities on their source.The escalating conflict has dealt a blow to Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's ambitious plans to transform and diversify the Saudi economy and reduce its reliance on oil.Saudi Aramco headquarters suffered extensive damage in Houthi attack, sources sayOil giant Saudi Aramco's headquarters in Dhahran suffered extensive damage in an attack on Tuesday, with a fire spreading across several floors, three people with direct knowledge of the matter told Reuters.Operations at the complex in eastern Saudi Arabia have continued normally but some employees have been asked to work from home, according to two of the people.A fourth person said some functions had been shifted to global offices, adding that the fire was still burning into the early hours of Wednesday.The facility hosts an operations center which helps the world's largest oil company oversee onshore and offshore oil rigs, refineries, export terminals and thousands of kilometers of pipeline.Saudi Arabia's energy ministry said in a statement that Tuesday night's attack, which came as fighting between Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis and the kingdom intensified, had caused a limited fire.Two of the sources said a fire started on the ninth floor of the south wing of the office block, and spread between the sixth and 10th floors.Another source added that the top three floors of building, where the office of Aramco CEO Amin Nasser is located, were severely damaged, with part of the ceiling caved in and windows and doors blown out.Aramco did not immediately reply to a Reuters request for comment. Saudi Arabia to let executives attend 'Davos in the Desert' remotely after attacksSaudi Arabia plans to make its flagship investment conference a hybrid event, giving executives the option to tune in remotely, after deadly weekend attacks on Riyadh airport prompted a rethink of travel to the kingdom, two people familiar with the matter said.Some participants were still expected to fly in and could land at airstrips outside Riyadh, or even in neighboring Gulf states, and then drive to the capital to attend the Future Investment Initiative scheduled for later this month, one of the people said.Earlier this month, organizers said the event would go ahead despite missile and drone attacks in the kingdom, which have struck key targets.Asked for comment, an FII media representative pointed Reuters to a joint statement from the CEO and the chairman of the FII Institute sent before Saturday's attacks."As we prepare to welcome thousands of delegates to Riyadh for the exceptional 10th edition of the Future Investment Initiative, their safety and well-being remain our highest priority," CEO Maha Al Saud and Richard Attias, chairman of the executive committee, said.On Monday, major oil bosses dropped out of an international conference in Riyadh which continued in person as planned at a convention center 10 km (6 miles) from Riyadh airport.The move to a hybrid model for FII shows how Saudi Arabia is trying to maintain its push to attract global investment despite an escalating war with the Houthis that has challenged its efforts to turn Riyadh into a hub for global events. The kingdom has used the FII to showcase its plans to diversify its economy from oil and attract foreign investments.The typical attendance of a large number of world leaders, corporate chieftains and financiers has led the event to be nicknamed "Davos in the desert," in a nod to the World Economic Forum's annual meeting in Switzerland.

title: Almaty Facade Renovations Leave Small Businesses in the Dust
body: When Gaukhar Osmonalieva rented a space in central Almaty for a pet grooming salon and coffee shop, renovations to the building’s facade were already underway. She was assured the work would be finished soon. Her business opened in August, but instead of a busy street and an outdoor terrace, she found herself surrounded by scaffolding, a torn-up sidewalk, and constant dust. By mid-October, construction was still underway, and the customers she had hoped to attract by choosing the location were coming less frequently. “At one point, the construction workers dug up the entire road, and foot traffic dropped noticeably. We chose this location because it was convenient and had heavy pedestrian traffic, but those are precisely the advantages we have now practically lost,” Osmonalieva told The Times of Central Asia . Almaty is Kazakhstan’s largest city and commercial hub. In 2026, the city launched a large-scale renovation of residential building facades, many dating back to the Soviet era. The original program covered 176 buildings in three central districts – Almaly, Bostandyk, and Medeu. More than 25.8 billion tenge (approximately $57 million) was allocated for the work. Many of the buildings house cafes, shops, and small businesses on their ground floors. Classes continue as normal at a language school on Abay Avenue as restoration goes on outside. City officials promised to update the facades while preserving the buildings’ architectural features. But questions about how the work was organized emerged as early as spring. Local news outlet Vlast found that construction had begun at some sites in March, before public tenders were announced and contracts signed. Under the tender terms, renovating a single building was supposed to take three to five months. By August, only nine of the 178 buildings listed in updated district administration figures had been fully renovated. Authorities in Bostandyk expected to complete most of the work by September, while those in Almaty targeted October. Osmonalieva was initially told the renovations would take three weeks, then that they would be completed by September. After complaining via e-Otinish, Kazakhstan’s government complaints platform, she was given a new deadline: October 15. “But today is already October 12, and judging by the condition of the facade, I wouldn’t say even half the work has been done,” she said. According to Osmonalieva, there are often only three or four construction workers on the building. Tools are left near the entrance, while workers cut cladding materials beside the salon, filling the area with dust. A coffee shop on Kunaev Street, with construction materials stacked outside. The coffee shop has suffered most. Osmonalieva had planned to open an outdoor terrace, a popular feature in Almaty, where warm weather lasts for several months. But scaffolding made it impossible to set up tables outside. “As a result, we missed the entire season. This had a significant impact on the coffee shop: demand was lower than expected, and we couldn’t reach our planned targets,” she said. The construction has created additional difficulties for the grooming salon, too. Some dogs become frightened by the noise and machinery before they even reach the entrance. Because of the dust, employees have to wash the entrance area more frequently, using more water. Sometimes construction workers ask permission to plug their tools into the salon’s electrical outlets. “And we agree, because we also want them to finish the work as quickly as possible,” Osmonalieva explained, adding that her utility bills rose in October. She has not been offered compensation or financial relief during the renovations. Nor has she asked her landlord to reduce the rent, believing he is not responsible for construction organized by the city. Osmonalieva’s experience echoes the findings of a study by Urban Forum Kazakhstan, a nonprofit focused on urban development. The study, titled “This Is for Your Future,” surveyed 340 people affected by street reconstruction in Almaty during the summer of 2026. It found that 90% of respondents learned about construction only after it had begun. The same proportion reported having no convenient, safe, clearly marked route around construction sites. Nearly 68% had been forced to walk in the roadway, while 51.5% had to pass directly through construction zones. Respondents also complained about dust, particularly when stone and paving tiles were being cut. Construction workers take a break outside an opticians on Abay Avenue. Urban Forum Kazakhstan concluded that requirements for pedestrian protection and construction dust control were not adequately incorporated into construction regulations and contractor agreements. The survey was conducted from July 13 to August 14 and covered street and public-space reconstruction. Its sample is not representative of all Almaty residents, but it illustrates the difficulties people encounter in areas affected by construction. Urban Forum Kazakhstan recommends requiring contractors to establish safe pedestrian routes in advance, install clear barriers and signs, and use dust suppression equipment. The organization wants these requirements written directly into municipal regulations and contracts. Residents have also complained about the results of the renovations. In October, residents of a building on Nazarbayev Avenue, one of Almaty’s main streets, complained about selective renovation : neighboring buildings had been refurbished, while theirs was left untouched despite previously appearing on renovation lists. At another building, workers painted only the end wall facing the avenue. The akimat, or local administration, said the contractor had done so on its own initiative and that the building was not part of the approved program. Osmonalieva does not oppose Almaty’s renovation program. She believes the work could make the city more attractive, particularly if the architectural features of older buildings are preserved. But she argues that business owners should receive advance notice of construction schedules and support during prolonged renovations. “It’s one thing when business owners know the exact schedule in advance and can prepare for temporary inconvenience. It’s quite another when you’re constantly promised that the renovations will be finished soon, but weeks and months go by and nothing fundamentally changes,” she said. Both her coffee shop and salon continue to serve customers amid scaffolding and dust, with the October 15 completion deadline just a day away. Judging by the condition of the facade, she doubts the workers will meet it.

title: Nigeria seeks more Hungary scholarship slots for students
body: … Ambassador Braimah asks Tempus Foundation to increase allocation By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Nigeria’s Ambassador to Hungary, Engr. Abass Braimah, has called for an increase in the number of scholarship slots allocated to Nigerian students under the Stipendium Hungaricum Scholarship Programme. Braimah made the appeal on Tuesday during a working visit to the headquarters of Tempus Public Foundation in Budapest, Hungary, describing the current allocation of 50 slots to Nigeria as inadequate for a country with a large population. The ambassador urged the foundation to increase the allocation to enable more qualified Nigerian students to benefit from the programme. He also encouraged eligible Nigerians to apply when the application window opens in November 2026. In a statement issued by his office on Wednesday, Braimah said the visit was part of the Nigerian Embassy’s efforts to strengthen bilateral relations between Nigeria and Hungary and support Nigerian students pursuing their studies in the European country. He was accompanied on the visit by the Deputy Head of Mission and Minister Plenipotentiary, Mrs Vivienne Ekwora Ogonyi. The delegation was received by the Director-General of Tempus Public Foundation, Mr Péter Tordai, and the Director of Study in Hungary, Ms Orsolya Jánosik. According to the statement, discussions focused on strengthening educational cooperation between both countries, particularly through the Stipendium Hungaricum Scholarship Programme, which provides opportunities for Nigerian students to study at Hungarian universities. The embassy said the engagement formed part of its broader efforts to deepen Nigeria-Hungary relations and promote educational opportunities for Nigerian students in Hungary. title: Russian Drone Strike Kills 6, Injures 13 in Lutsk as Zelensky Urges G7 to Force Moscow to Stop
body:
President Volodymyr Zelensky called on G7 leaders – including the US, which recently struck a dieseldeal with Russian President Vladimir Putin – to force Moscow to stop its war after a Russian Shahed strike killed six people and injured 13 in Lutsk on Wednesday, Oct. 14.
The strikes came while repair crews were still restoring Kyiv, Kyiv region and Kharkiv region after a massive overnight strike on the energy sector, as Russia launched a new wave of drones. A residential building and a store were damaged.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“This is exactly why Moscow must not be persuaded but forced to stop – through increased pressure, sanctions and assistance to Ukraine that makes it possible to protect people from such attacks,” Zelensky said in a statement on Telegram.
He described the attacks as deliberate pressure on civilians and said Russia was pressing on with the war “despite the calls of America and the American President.”
The death toll rose to six killed and 13 wounded according to the latest statement by Zelensky.
“There must be action,” the President said. “Because as long as Russia does not feel enough pressure, it continues to bring death.”
Ukraine’s State Emergency Service (SES) raised the death toll in Lutsk to six, with 12 people injured, including a child, in its previous update .
The Volyn Regional Military Administration had earlier reported damage to the Eurohurt food wholesaler and a nine-story residential building. Firefighters put out the blaze at the wholesaler, and emergency crews continued assisting people at the affected sites.
In Rivne, five people were wounded, including a child born in 2012, according to the SES ⁠.
Rescuers pulled a woman from beneath the rubble and handed her over to medical workers.
Four privately owned cars and the roof of a three-story residential building caught fire. Windows were blown out and a neighboring residential building was also damaged.
Firefighters extinguished the blaze. Emergency crews continued clearing rubble and dousing damaged structures.
Across the Rivne region, eight people were injured in the night and morning attacks: five at the residential site in Rivne and three at an agricultural enterprise. Two agricultural enterprises were hit, regional authorities said.
The latest attack on Rivne came one day after a Russian drone attack on the Rivne State University of Humanities wounded 30 people ⁠ and severely damaged premises used by its music department. The university moved students to remote learning.
Russia also launched 39 missiles and 128 drones across Ukraine overnight ⁠, according to the Ukrainian Air Force. Attacks were recorded at 22 locations, while debris from intercepted targets fell at eight others.

title: Russia, China can discuss Power of Siberia 2 gas pipeline at APEC summit — Novak
body:
MOSCOW, October 14. /TASS/. Russia and China can discuss the topic of Power of Siberia 2 gas pipeline construction at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak told reporters on the sidelines of the Russian Energy Week forum.

title: DRAKKAR and AtkinsRéalis Sign MoU for Made-in-Canada Defence
body: DRAKKAR, a Canadian leader in aerospace and industrial services programs and AtkinsRéalis , a world-class engineering services and nuclear company with offices around the world, have signed a non-binding Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to explore strategic collaboration in support of Canadian defence. DRAKKAR and AtkinsRéalis Sign MoU to Advance Made-in-Canada Defence Solutions Announced during DEFSEC Atlantic in Halifax, the MoU was signed at the Québec Pavilion in the presence of Investissement Québec and brings together two proudly Canadian, Montreal-headquartered companies with complementary capabilities. DRAKKAR and AtkinsRéalis are joining forces to explore made-in-Canada defence solutions. The collaboration will pursue opportunities across the air, land and maritime domains, including services such as acquisition, modernization, mobilization, in-service support, and the long-term sustainment of complex defence platforms, systems and infrastructure. This could create a Canadian lifecycle-delivery model that connects engineering and program integration with industrial execution, maintenance, logistics, manufacturing services and scalable operational capacity. The President and CEO of the DRAKKAR Group, Benoit Hudon, reiterated the importance of creating defence partnerships in the current context, which is particularly favourable to the development of the Canadian markets. “Building strong partnerships with established Canadian companies that already have the capabilities, infrastructure and workforce in place is essential to strengthening Canada’s defence industrial capacity. By combining complementary expertise such as AtkinsRéalis and DRAKKAR Group’s existing Canadian footprint, we can accelerate defence readiness, deliver greater value to government and contribute meaningfully to Canada’s sovereignty objectives,” said Mr. Hudon. “AtkinsRéalis and DRAKKAR bring together complementary Canadian capabilities to support defence programs from acquisition and modernization through long-term sustainment,” said Stéphanie Vaillancourt, President, Canada, AtkinsRéalis. “By combining our engineering, systems integration, program management, operations and maintenance, and asset management expertise with DRAKKAR’s capabilities in aerospace maintenance, logistics and manufacturing services, we can help strengthen Canada’s defence capacity, supply-chain resilience and long-term operational readiness.” DRAKKAR & AtkinsRéalis: a Uniquely Canadian Team AtkinsRéalis’ global Defence expertise includes supporting the Global Combat Air Programme (GCAP) in the UK, which Canada has announced its intention to join as an observer. The Company has been a top five supplier of Defence Construction Canada over the last five years, with an active presence on the majority of military bases in Canada. AtkinsRéalis previously provided operations and maintenance services for the Royal Canadian Navy’s minor warships and auxiliary vessels fleet. DRAKKAR complements these capabilities through an integrated Canadian industrial operation in the sectors of aerospace, defence and ground transportation. Through its three lines of service, DRAKKAR Group is ready to support defence programs. Its aircraft maintenance operations, strategically located in Mirabel, Quebec, include heavy maintenance, cabin integration, line maintenance, mobile repair services and ground handling. It also provides third-party logistics services, including warehousing, inventory management, kit preparation, freight, and transportation, with a footprint in North America. Finally, its integrated manufacturing services, delivered across borders, cover manufacturing engineering, production support, assembly, production, retrofit, field services and technical workforce across key sectors, providing valuable support to its customers. Potential areas of collaboration include fleet sustainment, defence aviation support, supply-chain solutions, platform modernization, Arctic mobility, program transition, localization, knowledge transfer and the development or expansion of Canadian in-service support capabilities. By bringing their services together, DRAKKAR and AtkinsRéalis aim to provide Canadian government customers, prime contractors, and original equipment manufacturers operating in Canada’s defence industry with access to a broader domestic delivery capability. The collaboration is intended to strengthen Canadian industrial participation, specialized skills and supply chains, while offering large foreign contractors a made-in-Canada option.
