title: Trump's Russian diesel deal offers little relief for Americans — and a political win for Moscow
body:
Russian President Vladimir Putin delivers a speech during the 23rd Annual Meeting of the Valdai Discussion Club in Moscow, Russia, on Oct. 1, 2026. (Sefa Karacan / Anadolu via Getty Images)
When U.S. President Donald Trump announced Oct. 9 that Washington had agreed to buy millions of tons of Russian fuel, he pledged that the deal would mean lower gas prices for ordinary Americans.
"Russia will immediately supply over 300,000 Tons of Diesel Fuel to the American and Global Marketplace, another 500,000 Tons during the month of November, and 1,000,000 Tons immediately thereafter," Trump wrote on Truth Social.
"Between our TOTAL CONTROL of the Strait of Hormuz, and this great announcement on Russian Energy, Diesel Prices for Americans and, indeed, the World, will be COMING DOWN, IN RECORD NUMBERS, AND FAST!" he said.
The statement is far from reality, experts warn. The initial shipments, as announced by Trump, are small and unlikely to significantly lower prices in the long term.
Although Trump is hoping for a midterm boost, the only winner is the Kremlin.
The deal is putting new strain on Kyiv-Washington relations, as Ukraine is forced to press pause on one of its most successful war tactics.
Meanwhile, Moscow is buoyed by the prospect of weakened sanctions, which could boost its economy, its war chest, and its global image.
Global diesel prices are soaring. In its most recent report on Oct. 5, the U.S. Energy Information Administration put the cost of U.S. diesel at $6.20 per gallon — a rise of $2.49 in just 12 months.
The main factor driving those soaring prices is the U.S.-Iran war. The conflict has not only disrupted the flow of oil tankers passing through the Strait of Hormuz but has also driven up security costs for those ships making the journey.
A study by Ukraine's KSE Institute, shared with the Financial Times, assessed that the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran had a far bigger impact on global diesel and gasoil supplies than Ukrainian drone strikes, estimating that exports from the Persian Gulf fell by 152 million barrels between March and August, compared with a 68 million-barrel drop in Russian exports over the same period.
But Ukrainian drone strikes against Russia’s oil refineries have also made their mark.
In a report published in September, the International Energy Agency said that the amount of crude oil moving through Russia’s refineries had fallen to a 20-year low, with diesel production down by nearly 30%.
Global energy markets operate on a razor-thin balance between supply and demand, meaning any drop in output will affect prices, says Jeff Krimmel, founder of consulting firm Krimmel Strategy.
He says that Trump's deal could trigger a small drop in diesel prices, but that those changes are unlikely to last.
While the numbers in Trump's announcement are impressive at first glance, they are a small drop in the global energy market.
In October 2026, the U.S. Energy Information Administration reported that the country was using 493,000 tons of distillate fuel oil — a category that includes diesel and certain heating oils — in a single day. If that rate continues, the total of Russia’s first two deliveries, or 800,000 tons, would supply U.S. needs for less than 48 hours alone.
Real change would need a much wider shift, says Krimmel.
"The U.S. administration wants some visible demonstration that they're responding to this diesel supply crunch and the price rise that comes with that crunch," he says.
"(But) there is no single deal that the U.S. president can make with any foreign leader to change the shape of diesel markets in the near term."
Meanwhile, the planned diesel shipments place increasing pressure on Ukraine.
Kyiv's long-distance drone strikes against Russia’s oil infrastructure have become one of Ukraine's most effective weapons, slowly eating away at the Russian economy. Russia was plagued by fuel shortages throughout the summer, with some regions suspending civilian sales. Notably for world leaders such as Trump, the shortages also led the Russian government to place a temporary ban on diesel exports in July.
A lack of available data from Russia means that it's difficult to know how quickly the country has been able to repair its drone-damaged refineries. But the fall in Russia’s refinery output has been great enough for experts to express doubt that Moscow would be willing or able to fulfill the export numbers outlined by the U.S. president.
However, with his eyes now focused on U.S. opinion polls rather than global affairs, Trump has started to intensify his criticism of Ukraine for carrying out such strikes.
"The relationship with the U.S. (and Ukraine) is right now probably as bad as it was on Feb. 28, 2025, when we had this massive bust-up between Trump and Zelensky in the Oval Office," says Stefan Wolff, professor of international security at the U.K.'s University of Birmingham.
Shortly after the diesel deal was announced, Kyiv halted strikes on Russian refineries, following the terms of a unilateral, U.S.-led "energy ceasefire." Moscow has continued its attacks.
Even so, Trump threatened Kyiv with the withholding of intelligence and other assistance in a bid to protect Russian oil refineries, Ukrainian officials told the Kyiv Independent.
President Volodymyr Zelensky later shared that several missile strikes on Ukraine took place with "no early warning from our partners" — a suggestion that the U.S.-Ukraine intelligence sharing had been, at least partly, disrupted.
Ukraine's Starlink access was also restricted without warning on Oct. 14, severely disrupting "several" military missions, presidential adviser Serhii "Flash" Beskrestnov said.
"Obviously, this action cannot be a coincidence and is associated with the current political situation," Beskrestnov said.
Ukraine could keep exerting pressure on Russia’s energy infrastructure without targeting refineries, says Wolff. In particular, oil tankers in Russia’s shadow fleet are among the potential targets.
But Kyiv will be pressured to keep Washington onside to keep receiving vital aid, such as air defenses, to protect civilians under Russian bombardment.
“Air defences are clearly depleted,” says Wolff. “There's not a lot that the Europeans can put in to backfill what the Ukrainians have used. So, I mean, in that sense, they still very much depend on the U.S., as do the Europeans.”
While Russia won't make large amounts of money from the small shipments outlined by Trump, the shift signals new possibilities for further sales down the line — greater revenues to fund Russia’s war machine.
But the real win for Russia is not only the breathing space to bring its refineries back online, but the outsized political statement that Trump's deal sends.
The U.S. Treasury is suspending sanctions on Russian diesel exports until April 7 to make Trump's deal happen. That decision from a powerful global player such as the United States — a country that has, until recently, publicly pledged to support Ukraine — may prompt other countries to rethink their own stance on sanctions.
It could also open the door for countries buying Russian oil products at lower prices to start paying more, says Daniel Spiro, a professor at Uppsala University specializing in resource and political economics.
"The fact that Trump is now saying it's okay to buy from Russia, that could mean that those buying that oil and diesel are going to think, now it's safe, so we can pay full price for it," he says.
While Russia won't make large amounts of money from the small shipments outlined by Trump, the shift signals new possibilities for further sales down the line — greater revenues to fund Russia’s war machine.
"From Russia's perspective, it's symbolic. It shows that Russia can negotiate with others. It gives a green light; it shows that the world is reliant on Russia," says Spiro. "I do think it's mainly symbolic. But, sometimes, symbolism matters."
Katie Marie Davies is a freelance journalist who has worked in Russia and the UK. She has previously worked as a news editor at The Moscow Times and features editor at The Calvert Journal.

title: KNUST to receive 2,000 additional laptops for One Million Coders Programme
body: The Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) is expected to receive an additional 2,000 laptops to expand access to digital skills training under the government’s One Million Coders Programme (OMCP). The Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Samuel Nartey George, announced the planned provision during a working visit to the university as part of his tour of the Ashanti Region to assess the implementation of the programme and identify expansion opportunities. The additional laptops will support the establishment of 40 new learning centres on the KNUST campus, increasing the number of centres from the existing 10 to 50. The university initially received 500 laptops to equip the first 10 centres under the initiative. During the visit, the Minister toured some of the learning centres and interacted with students to assess their experiences with the programme. He also encouraged greater participation as the government seeks to widen access to digital education and equip more young people with skills relevant to the changing employment landscape. The expansion is expected to make digital skills training more accessible to students and other prospective learners within the university community. It will also provide additional opportunities for beneficiaries to develop competencies that can support innovation, entrepreneurship and employment in Ghana’s growing digital economy. Mr George further disclosed that the Ministry was exploring opportunities to extend the programme to other tertiary institutions in the Ashanti Region, including Kumasi Technical University. Such partnerships could broaden the initiative’s reach beyond KNUST and enable more students to benefit from structured digital skills training. The working visit forms part of the Ministry’s efforts to monitor the implementation of the One Million Coders Programme, identify operational challenges and determine areas where additional resources and institutional partnerships could improve its reach. The programme is designed to equip Ghanaians with relevant digital skills to enhance their employability, support innovation and prepare them to participate more effectively in the digital economy. The planned provision of the additional laptops is expected to strengthen KNUST’s capacity to deliver the training, although the Ministry did not specify a delivery date for the new equipment in the announcement. One Million Coders Programme: Samuel Nartey George targets 50 learning centres at KNUST The Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Samuel Nartey George, has announced plans to increase the number of One Million Coders Programme (OMCP) learning centres at the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) from 10 to 50, in a major expansion of digital skills training at the university. The expansion will be supported by an additional 2,000 laptops to be provided to KNUST, building on the initial allocation of 500 laptops used to establish the first 10 learning centres. The move is expected to extend access to technology-enabled training and provide more learners with opportunities to acquire digital competencies. Mr George announced this during a working visit to KNUST as part of his tour of the Ashanti Region to assess progress under the government’s flagship digital skills initiative. The visit included tours of some learning centres and engagements with students to understand how the programme is operating on campus and identify opportunities to improve participation. The proposed expansion will add 40 learning centres to the existing facilities, potentially increasing the university’s capacity to accommodate more students and other prospective participants. The Minister also disclosed that the Ministry was exploring possible partnerships with other tertiary institutions in the region, including Kumasi Technical University, to extend the programme beyond KNUST. The move would create opportunities for more students to access digital skills training without relying solely on the facilities available at one institution. The One Million Coders Programme is intended to equip Ghanaians with practical digital skills that can improve employability, promote entrepreneurship and support the development of a workforce capable of responding to the demands of an increasingly technology-driven economy. The initiative also forms part of the government’s broader digital transformation agenda, which places emphasis on expanding access to technology, strengthening digital capacity and preparing young people for opportunities in the digital economy. The Ministry’s engagement with KNUST is expected to inform further decisions on the programme’s implementation and expansion in the Ashanti Region. However, the announcement did not indicate when the additional laptops would be delivered or when the 40 new learning centres would become operational.

title: Neurologist to continue testifying at inquest into Toronto woman’s fatal balcony fall
body:
A neurologist who examined Regis Korchinski-Paquet’s records after her death says it would be “nearly impossible” to determine that someone is acting aggressively due to delirium or psychosis after an epilepsy seizure without knowing their medical history.
Dr. Julien Hébert told a coroner’s inquest today that agitated or aggressive behaviour stemming from postictal delirium or psychosis is “indistinguishable” from the same behaviour from other causes, and it would be extremely difficult for a lay person to tell them apart.
Hébert was the first witness to be called at the inquest, which comes more than six years after Korchinski-Paquet fell to her death from a Toronto balcony while police were in her home.
He faced additional questions today from lawyers representing Korchinski-Paquet’s family, the Black Legal Action Centre, and others who have standing at the inquest.
Hébert said Tuesday that in the years preceding her death, Korchinski-Paquet on several occasions showed symptoms in keeping with postictal delirium or postictal psychosis, both mental states that can occur after seizures.
The inquest heard Korchinski-Paquet had a long history of seizures from epilepsy, often followed by confusion, aggressive behaviour and temporary amnesia.
She had two seizures the morning of the day she died.
The inquest was announced earlier this year and is slated to last 14 days.
Korchinski-Paquet’s mother, father and brother have been named as potential witnesses, as have five of the six police officers who attended the scene.

title: Nigeria woos foreign investors with 65 projects worth $78.5bn
body: *Energy, transport account for $61.4bn; 17 mega-projects require $72.3bn *Foreign investors to enjoy 100% foreign ownership, tax incentives *FG promises clearer business rules, new incentives to attract investment *Nigeria’s next reforms to focus on food, power, jobs, business efficiency — Oyedele *Naira stability, rising reserves strengthen economy against shocks — Cardoso *Dangote Group credits reforms for $17bn refinery investment By Babajide Komolafe, Economy Editor Bangkok, Thailand: The Federal Government has unveiled 65 investment projects requiring a total of $78.5 billion in capital, as it intensifies efforts to attract foreign investors into Nigeria’s energy, transport, agriculture, manufacturing and other critical sectors of the economy. The government, which presented the investment opportunities to foreign investors at an Investors Forum organised by the Nigerian delegation to the ongoing International Monetary Fund (IMF)/World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand, said it was developing an investment Deal Room to provide prospective investors with detailed information on projects seeking funding and facilitate investment decisions. Speaking on the initiative, Idris Bellow Osagie, Special Adviser on Economic Strategy to the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, is designed to bridge the information gap between project sponsors seeking capital and investors looking for viable opportunities in Nigeria. Osagie urged foreign investors to look beyond concerns about the Nigerian economy and take advantage of the investment opportunities being assembled by the government, insisting that the country was open for business. He explained that the government had consulted federal and state governments, government agencies and private-sector participants to identify transactions requiring financing and assemble the relevant information in a centralised investment platform. According to him, the Deal Room would provide prospective investors with information about projects, including their sponsors, capital requirements, minimum investment thresholds and other financial details needed to assess the opportunities. The objective, he said, was to make it easier for investors to identify projects that matched their investment capacity and interests, obtain further information and engage directly with the relevant project sponsors and government officials. Osagie acknowledged that investors might question some of the economic data and conditions in Nigeria. However, he urged them to assess the investment opportunities available alongside the challenges. He said the government was working to make information on the projects accessible and facilitate meetings between prospective investors and relevant officials. Describing the initiative as part of the government’s efforts to improve investment mobilisation, Osagie urged foreign investors to take a closer look at Nigeria. He said the information on the projects would be updated, while investors could arrange meetings with relevant officials to obtain additional details. The government, he added, was seeking to make it easier for investors to move from identifying opportunities to assessing specific transactions and engaging with project sponsors. Energy, transport dominate $78.5bn pipeline Details of the investment pipeline presented at the forum showed that oil, gas and power projects account for the largest share of the capital requirement, with 25 projects requiring $36.4 billion. Transport and maritime follow with eight projects requiring $25 billion, while agriculture and agro-processing account for six projects requiring $9.8 billion. Industry, manufacturing and mining have 17 projects requiring $6.6 billion, while technology, health and urban services account for nine projects with a combined capital requirement of $700 million. The figures indicate that energy and transport alone account for $61.4 billion, or about 78 per cent of the total investment requirement. The presentation also showed that the 65 projects offer opportunities across different investment sizes, ranging from $1 million to $15 billion. Of the total, 29 projects require less than $100 million each, while 18 require between $100 million and $499 million. One project requires between $500 million and $999 million, while 17 projects require at least $1 billion each. The 17 mega-projects account for $72.3 billion of the overall capital requirement, underscoring the concentration of financing needs among a relatively small number of large transactions. The median capital requirement per project is $153 million, while 48 of the 65 projects require less than $500 million each. The pipeline therefore offers opportunities for investors with different financing capacities, from those interested in relatively small transactions to institutional investors and strategic partners capable of participating in large-scale infrastructure and industrial projects. FG outlines next phase of reforms Meanwhile, the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, while speaking at the forum, outlined five priority areas for the next phase of economic reforms, identifying agriculture, power, inflation, regulatory efficiency and data transparency as critical to improving Nigeria’s investment environment. Responding to questions from investors at the forum, Oyedele said the government was developing targeted interventions to address structural problems affecting production, business operations and the cost of living. On agriculture and food inflation, he said the government was examining the underlying causes of rising food prices to ensure that interventions addressed the sources of inflationary pressure. “One of the drivers of inflation is food, so we are now trying to piece it together to find where these problems are coming from,” he said. Oyedele argued that the government needed to distinguish between the factors commonly blamed for inflation and the actual sources of price increases, stressing that policies must be based on evidence. He said the government’s objective was not merely to reduce inflation to single digits but to ensure that it remained at that level. “We know where the inflation and the pressure for it is coming from, and we’re going to tackle it there, not only just to bring it down to a single digit, but to keep it there,” he stated. On the power sector, Oyedele said Nigeria could not achieve its economic ambitions without addressing electricity supply and transmission challenges. “You cannot power a $1 trillion economy in darkness. It’s impossible,” he declared. He said the government was examining strategies to address electricity pricing and transmission constraints, while improving efficiency across the power sector. According to him, resolving the electricity challenge was critical to expanding production, lowering business costs and encouraging new investments. The minister also identified regulatory inefficiency as a major constraint on private-sector investment, arguing that excessive regulations, unclear rules, multiple fees and licensing requirements impose substantial costs on businesses. “We estimate that overregulation, regulatory burden, lack of clarity, and all of those excessive burdens that we put on businesses actually are costing us more than the combined revenue from corporate tax, personal income tax and VAT combined,” he said. Oyedele described regulatory reform as an opportunity to improve the business environment without imposing significant additional costs on the government. “If you ask me, what is the best example of a win-win outcome where the government wins, the private sector wins even more, and it costs the government nearly nothing? It’s solving the problem around regulatory efficiency,” he said. He disclosed that the government had started developing an economic policy framework intended to improve regulatory consistency and prevent the arbitrary introduction of new rules, fees and licences. “So you don’t just wake up one day and introduce a new rule or a new fee or new licenses. No, not anymore,” he stated. The minister also promised improvements in the availability and credibility of fiscal and economic data, saying the government was working to make information more accessible and ensure timely updates. He acknowledged that inconsistent data across government institutions had made it difficult for investors and analysts to assess Nigeria’s economic performance. The Ministry of Finance, he said, was finalising arrangements to publish fiscal data on its website, with commitments to ensure that the information was accessible, credible and regularly updated. FG targets decent jobs, offers new incentives On employment, Oyedele said the government’s priority was to create decent jobs capable of improving living standards rather than focusing solely on the official unemployment rate. “We are clear in our minds that we don’t just need to create jobs; we need to create decent jobs,” he said. He noted that although Nigeria’s official unemployment rate was around five per cent, the poverty rate remained above 50 per cent, indicating that many Nigerians who were working were still struggling financially. “Officially, our unemployment rate is around five per cent and poverty rate is higher than 50 per cent, so you have a lot of working poor,” he stated. The minister said the government was also seeking to make it easier for investors to establish factories and access incentives through the Investment Deal Room. On requests by investors for tax holidays, Oyedele said Nigeria’s reformed tax system had introduced an alternative incentive framework designed to reward qualifying investments. “We’ve transformed our tax system. We have something that is better than a tax holiday. It’s called the Economic Development Incentive, where you get a tax credit,” he said. He explained that the incentive was structured to minimise abuse because investors would have to meet the applicable requirements to qualify for the tax credit. “The good thing about it is it’s hard to abuse, so you have to earn it to get the credit,” he added. Oyedele said the Deal Room would also guide investors through the process of establishing factories and pursuing investment opportunities in the country. “They will show you, they will handhold you, and make it easy for you to do what you have to do,” he said. He further disclosed that the government was working with monetary authorities to improve liquidity and ensure investors could exit naira-denominated investments without additional risk. On taxation of government securities, he said the government was committed to providing clarity so investors could make decisions based on predictable rules. “I cannot guarantee you that there will be no tax, but I can guarantee you there will be clarity so you can price correctly,” he stated. The minister also said the government was engaging the National Bureau of Statistics to improve the timeliness and usefulness of economic data, including information on jobs and producer prices, to support more effective policy decisions. Cardoso links stability to reforms The Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), Olayemi Cardoso, said monetary reforms had helped strengthen Nigeria’s capacity to withstand external shocks, pointing to exchange-rate stability, naira appreciation and improved external reserves. In his remarks at the forum, Cardoso said Nigeria’s external reserves had reached their highest level in 18 years, providing a stronger buffer against global economic headwinds. He argued that the reforms implemented by the authorities had helped prepare the economy to withstand pressures arising from geopolitical tensions and international trade uncertainties. “What we’ve been able to accomplish in terms of having very robust external reserves, highest in 18 years, is also something that affects the ordinary person,” he said. He explained that without the stronger external buffers, Nigeria could have faced some of the pressures confronting other economies, potentially with more severe consequences. Cardoso also linked the relative stability and appreciation of the naira to the reforms, saying the exchange-rate performance had helped cushion the economy against external pressures. “The good thing was that the reforms and the policies were things that were thought through, and we started to implement early enough, such that when those headwinds started to come, not only from the war, but also from the discussions around putting on tariffs, our exchange rate has held stable. In fact, it appreciated,” he said. The CBN governor maintained that exchange-rate stability had broader implications for ordinary Nigerians, even when the benefits were not immediately apparent to households. “What does this mean for me? I’m not feeling it. You do, you definitely feel it. If it wasn’t there, then you would feel it in a very negative way,” he said. Cardoso identified inflation as one of the biggest threats to household welfare, describing it as a tax on the poor because it erodes purchasing power and makes basic goods and services less affordable. “The reason why we felt it was important to give ourselves this as a target is to recognise the fact that inflation is probably the biggest tax on the poor, and so it is critical that we bring it down to levels that are more manageable,” he said. He noted that Nigeria’s inflation rate had declined from about 34 to 35 per cent to around 15 per cent, describing the reduction as significant but insufficient. “I mean, in this instance, inflation has gone from about 34 per cent, 35 per cent to about 15 per cent, and yes, that’s a significant decrease, very significant. But what we are saying basically is that we are not going to rest,” he stated. Cardoso said the medium-term objective remained to bring inflation down to single digits, adding that the CBN’s transition towards inflation targeting would improve transparency and help the public understand the direction of monetary policy. He said the combination of lower inflation, exchange-rate stability and stronger external reserves would help establish a more stable foundation for investment and economic growth. Dangote Group endorses reforms Supporting the government’s investment drive, Hassan Mammud, Group Chief Economist, Dangote Group, said the consistency and credibility of Nigeria’s fiscal and monetary policies had helped restore investor confidence and improve the operating environment for businesses. Mammud, who represented the Dangote Group at the forum, said the reforms had helped the conglomerate overcome difficulties associated with the previous economic environment and improve its ability to plan and make investment decisions. He said the transparency and credibility of monetary policy had significantly improved the group’s capacity to make projections and stabilise its operations, particularly in relation to its investment of about $17 billion in the Dangote Refinery. “The transparency and the credibility we have seen in that has significantly enabled the Dangote Group to have good projections and was able to come out of the woods from his investment of about $17 billion dollars in the refinery,” he said. “That cannot happen in an economy where there are no consistencies, where there are no credibility of fiscal and monetary policy, and also the incentives that goes with operating in an export-free zone.” Mammud described the group’s experience as a confidence-builder for prospective investors considering Nigeria and other African countries, arguing that investment decisions depended not only on market opportunities but also on the credibility of government policies and the regulatory environment. He urged foreign investors to take advantage of the opportunities available in Nigeria. “Please come into Nigeria, bring your investment. Nigeria is actually a symbol to other African countries now,” he said. Mammud also cited the Dangote Group’s investment expansion into Kenya as an indication of the potential for Nigerian businesses to support industrial development across Africa. He stressed that investors needed to be bold, but added that such boldness depended on credible policies and regulatory reforms. Investor protections, incentives To strengthen the investment proposition, the presentation outlined several protections and incentives available to foreign investors. These include permission for 100 per cent foreign ownership in most sectors and full repatriation of capital and profits, subject to obtaining a Certificate of Capital Importation. The government also highlighted 17 double-taxation agreements and 13 bilateral investment treaties, alongside Nigeria’s membership of the International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes (ICSID). Under the incentives presented, qualifying capital expenditure may attract a tax credit of five per cent per annum for five years through the Economic Development Tax Incentive. The measures are intended to address investor concerns about ownership, returns, taxation and investment protection. Interested investors were encouraged to review the 65 project profiles available through the online investment directory and the Projects Nigeria Special Edition, which provide details of project sponsors, deal structures and scorecards. Osagie also encouraged investors to visit the Deal Room office, where Ministry of Finance officials and Nigerian business leaders could provide further information on individual projects. The post Nigeria woos foreign investors with 65 projects worth $78.5bn appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: President Mahama urges churches to provide safe spaces for children and vulnerable people
body: President John Dramani Mahama has urged religious bodies, particularly churches, to provide safe spaces for children and vulnerable people. Addressing the ongoing World Assemblies of God Congress 2026 in Accra, the President said churches must uphold the trust placed in them as places of safety. He called on religious institutions to ensure that people seeking refuge and support within their communities receive protection and care. “Let us all be mentors to our younger generation. Let us be mentors who listen, offer opportunities to serve and set an example of integrity that these young people can follow. The church should also be a safe place for children and vulnerable people,” he said. He added, “Spiritual authority entails a duty of care; we must safeguard that trust through responsible conduct, clear conduct and accountability.” The President’s appeal came at the opening of the three-day congress, which runs until 16 October under the theme, “Commissioned: One Mandate, Every Nation”. The programme includes plenary sessions, workshops and revival rallies, with the opening session held at the Grand Arena of the Accra International Conference Centre. The gathering is the 10th Triennial World Assemblies of God Fellowship Congress and marks the first time the event has been hosted in Africa. It brings together church leaders and ministers to discuss the Church’s mission and its role in communities worldwide. Ahead of the congress, the General Superintendent of Assemblies of God, Ghana, Rev. Stephen Yenusom Wengam, said organisers expected more than 10,000 participants from about 100 countries.

title: Senate Hails Cross-Party Alliance, Says Rainbow Coalition ‘On The Move’
body: The Senate leadership has congratulated the Minister of the FCT, Nyesom Wike, the governors of Osun and Anambra States, and other political leaders, stating that the emergence of the Wike-led Rainbow coalition is advancing unity. Speaking during plenary on Wednesday, the Senate leader, Sen. Opeyemi Bamidele, described the coalition as a move towards an inclusive political campaign ahead of the forthcoming presidential election. The Senate leader noted that as members proceed to the inauguration of the Presidential Campaign Council, there is optimism that the campaign would be driven by ideas and democratic principles. He also expressed satisfaction that former Gombe State Governor, Senator Ibrahim Dankwambo, would coordinate the Rainbow Coalition in Gombe State. However, the Senate minority leader, Sen.Abba Moro, declined to comment on the development and simply seconded the motion for adjournment. Reacting, the President of the Senate, Sen. Godswill Akpabio, said Sen. Moro’s action implied that he had adopted the speeches made before the motion. Sen. Akpabio described the inclusion of leaders from other political parties in President Tinubu’s Presidential campaign council as a historic development, unprecedented since 1999. ‘Let me note that this is historic since 1999, that a sitting president would constitute a presidential campaign council with other parties included. This shows an inclusive government in terms of unity of purpose. Nigeria is setting an example for Africa. I will not predict the outcome of the election, but Sen. Abdul Ningi knows who will win. He asserts that President Tinubu’s second term will be a unity government. The Senate President again commended leaders of other political parties for what he described as the bold decision to collaborate, expressing hope that the alliance would contribute to a better Nigeria. The post Senate Hails Cross-Party Alliance, Says Rainbow Coalition ‘On The Move’ appeared first on Channels Television .

title: EFCC Reopens Atiku Probe, Adopts Agbonayinma’s Petition
body: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has reopened an investigation into allegations involving former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar following a petition by a former member of the House of Representatives, Hon. Ehiozuwa Johnson Agbonayinma. The commission acknowledged receipt of the petition, dated August 27, 2026, and received on September 1, 2026, confirming that investigation has commenced. The former lawmaker through his lawyer, Chief Hannibal Uwaifo (SAN), is seeking a review of the allegations arising from an earlier investigation involving the former vice-president. As part of the process, the EFCC invited Agbonayinma to its headquarters in Jabi, Abuja, on October 12, where he adopted his petition and responded to questions from investigators. He arrived at about 9:58 a.m. and left at approximately 4:07 p.m. after the interview. The commission’s acknowledgement letter, referenced CR:3000/EFCC/HQ/SDC-2/VOL.3/398, forms part of the ongoing investigative process. He told newsmen that his petition sought to revisit an investigation conducted by the former EFCC chairman, Mallam Nuhu Ribadu, involving Atiku. He argued that the matter deserved renewed attention in the interest of accountability and the rule of law. “I want to thank Nigerians, the EFCC and those praying for me in this struggle. The laws are meant for both the rich and the poor. After the EFCC has done a fantastic job, it should not be kept under the table,” he said. Agbonayinma added that he considered reporting alleged wrongdoing a constitutional responsibility, insisting that nobody was above the law. He also disclosed that he had written a petition on the matter to United States President Donald Trump, calling for attention to the allegations.

title: Netherlands denies visas to 3 Russian athletes, barring them from world championships
body:
Dutch authorities refused to grant visas to three Russian gymnasts, preventing them from taking part in world gymnastics championships held in Rotterdam later this month, the Russian Gymnastics Federation said on Oct. 13.
Angelina Melnikova, Viktoria Listunova, and Anna Kalmykova were denied entry as "one or more Schengen area member states consider the athletes a threat to their international relations," the federation said on its Telegram channel.
Participation of Russian athletes in international competitions remains controversial and, in some sports, restricted due to Russia's ongoing full-scale invasion of Ukraine .
At the same time, Dutch authorities approved visas for five other gymnasts, the Russian Gymnastics Federation said later on Oct. 13, noting that 47 of the 61 members of the Russian delegation had been granted entry so far.
Listunova publicly expressed support for Russian aggression in Ukraine and was previously denied visas for a gymnastics competition in Croatia in August.
Melnikova has also voiced backing for Russian President Vladimir Putin and even ran as a candidate for the ruling United Russia party in local election primaries last year.
Both Melnikova and Listunova are Olympic gold medalists.
Kalmykova, in turn, holds a sports contract with the Russian National Guard, according to Kyiv .
The Russian Gymnastics Federation denounced the decision and said it would appeal to the International Olympic Committee and World Gymnastics.
Rotterdam will host the World Artistic Gymnastics Championships from Oct. 17 to 25, serving as the first stage of team qualification for the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles.
World Gymnastics imposed sanctions on Russian and Belarusian gymnasts at the outbreak of the full-scale war in 2022, but allowed them to compete as "neutral athletes" two years later.
The international association finally lifted its ban in May 2026, allowing Russian and Belarusian gymnasts to compete under their national flags, as part of a broader loosening of restrictions on Russian athletes.
Kyiv continues to urge global sports organizations to maintain sanctions against Russian and Belarusian athletes.
Russia's all-out war has taken a heavy toll on Ukraine, with hundreds of Ukrainian athletes and coaches killed and hundreds of sports facilities destroyed by Russian missile and drone attacks.

title: One killed, 19 injured in bus-truck collision on Route 91 in northern Israel
body: One person was killed, and 19 others were injured in a collision between a bus and a truck on Route 91 in northern Israel on Wednesday, Israel Fire and Rescue Services announced.The accident occurred between Machanayim and Mishmar Hayarden, where three firefighting and rescue teams from the Galil-Golan station were dispatched to the scene.Firefighters extricated a person who had been trapped inside the bus and was pronounced dead at the scene by Magen David Adom (MDA) personnel.Another person sustained serious injuries and was evacuated by helicopter, while 18 others with minor injuries received medical treatment at the scene.This is a developing story.

title: Regulator expects Man City appeal to be heard by January
body: The chair of English football’s Independent Regulator has said he expects Manchester City’s appeal after being found guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules to be heard by January. City, who have repeatedly maintained they are innocent of the charges, are currently top of the Premier League table with six wins out of six following their 3-0 defeat of Liverpool last weekend. No sanction has yet been announced, but City could face a heavy points deduction leading to relegation and there is even been speculation they could be stripped of the three Premier League titles they won between 2009 and 2018. “The Premier League have said that they want to get this resolved within season, and actually, of course, it’s not the Premier League, it’s an independent commission that’s actually going to hear this, made of three retired either judges or lawyers,” Independent Football Regulator (IFR) chair David Kogan told Times Radio on Wednesday. “My understanding is that there is a prescribed process, which is 12 weeks, and so people are assuming this will actually be heard by the middle or the end of January. “But as I say, it’s not our process, it’s that of the Premier League’s independent commission. What I don’t think we can do is take any judgment until we’re quite clear.” Kogan said Tuesday he would resign if there was political interference in any future IFR investigations of City. – Burnham ‘concern’ – British Prime Minister Andy Burnham was criticised for his comments saying he would be “really concerned” if City’s Abu Dhabi owners left the club following the verdict. Downing Street subsequently had to backtrack, insisting no one was “above the rules”. Burnham, who was mayor of Greater Manchester from 2017 to June 2026, has since published all of his dealings with the City hierarchy. On Monday, the Greater Manchester Combined Authority said Burnham had met Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak at an investment summit several years ago when he was mayor of the city. It was also revealed Burnham had spoken to him in the stands at former City captain Vincent Kompany’s testimonial and was accompanied by staff from the club on official overseas visits. Burnham was pressed on the issue during Prime Minister’s Questions in the House of Commons on Wednesday. Jerome Mayhew, an MP for the main opposition Conservative party, asked Burnham if anyone associated with the running of Manchester City had raised the issue of the charges either with him or any member of his team. Burnham replied: “They did not raise those issues with me.” Kogan said earlier Wednesday: “We’ve had absolutely no interference from anybody since we created the regulator a year ago. “We cannot, when regulating football, be subject to political interference on decisions we make about owners, directors or anything else.” He added: “And I won’t actually be prepared to run an organisation which is subject to that degree of interference.” Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca said last week he “completely trusts” the club and believes it will win its appeal. The post Regulator expects Man City appeal to be heard by January appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: PINL Deepens Community Ties as Stakeholders Renew Pledge To Protect Pipelines
body: *Stakeholders call for replacement of 60-year-old oil, gas pipelines The Pipeline Infrastructure Nigeria Limited (PINL), under the leadership of its Managing Director, Osahon Okunbo, has deepened its community relations drive across the Niger Delta, as stakeholders in Rivers and Bayelsa States renewed their commitment to peaceful relations and the protection of critical pipeline infrastructure at the company’s October 2026 Stakeholders’ Engagement Forum. The two-day forum, held on October 9 and 10, 2026, in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, and Yenagoa, Bayelsa State, brought together traditional rulers, youth leaders, environmental advocates, community representatives and other regional leaders. It is part of a sustained engagement programme driven by Okunbo, who has made direct, regular contact with host communities the foundation of PINL’s pipeline surveillance operations in the communities that host the pipelines the company safeguards”, a statement issued by the company said. While speaking at the event, the General Manager, Community and Stakeholders Relations (PINL), Dr. Akpos Mezeh said PINL had recorded two consecutive months without any pipeline vandalisation within its operational areas in the Niger Delta, which he attributed to good collaboration among stakeholders, which include host communities, security agencies, surveillance personnel, and industry operators. Mezeh, who also called for sustained cooperation among stakeholders to protect critical national infrastructure, maintain peace, and promote development in the Niger Delta, added that infrastructure could deliver value only when adequately protected. “Sustainable production and development depend on peaceful communities and trust among industry operators, government and host communities,” he said. He said host communities and stakeholders along the Trans Niger Pipeline (TNP) and the Eastern Gas Network (EGN) will play a pivotal role in ensuring that Nigeria meets its oil and gas production targets for 2027 and 2030. According to Mezeh, NNPCL Ltd’s recently released audited results for 2025, which reported a Profit after Tax of ₦7.2 trillion, up 33 percent from ₦5.4 trillion in 2024. “More importantly for our discussion today, crude oil and condensate production averaged 1.77 million barrels per day in 2025, the company’s highest production level in five years, and natural gas production averaged 7.2 billion standard cubic feet per day, the highest in three years,” he said. He further stated that PINL’s surveillance operations had provided employment for more than 35,000 youths, while its scholarship programme had awarded over ₦2 billion to more than 1,500 undergraduate and postgraduate students. The PINL official also urged stakeholders to disregard what the company described as a campaign of calumny against it by individuals whose motives were unclear. “Allegations should not be presented as established facts, particularly when they concern public expenditure, contractual arrangements or the reputation of individuals and institutions,” he said. Meanwhile, stakeholders at the meeting expressed satisfaction with PINL’s operations and urged the federal government to sustain and expand its contract. Engr. Omojevwhe Akponime, Head, Field Operations, Eastern Corridor, at the NNPC Project Monitoring Office, said NNPC’s daily reviews show the lines in PINL’s area of coverage running green, as he related to a recent NNPC management session. “There is no question for PINL. They said so because they are doing well. “He said. In his remarks, Eze Eberi-Ugo IX of Omuma Kingdom, Onyekachi Amaonwu, said national output targets are only achievable if there are grassroots cooperation across host communities. “For you to achieve these targets, there is no pipeline in Abuja; the pipelines are located right here in our communities,” Amaonwu said, as he urged other traditional rulers and community leaders to support PINL. Also speaking, the Eze Ekpeye-Logbo, Kelvin Anugwo, hinted that communities across Ekpeye land in Rivers State had returned to farming and fishing activities due to a decrease in crude oil theft along the corridor. “Before PINL came on board, we were unable to fish in our rivers because spilled crude oil had ruined the environment,” Anugwo stated. On his part, the spokesperson for the Niger Delta Ethnic Youth Leaders Forum, Legborsi Yamaabana, commended the federal government for renewing PINL’s contract. He said, “As Niger Delta people, we have adopted PINL as our own,” adding that dissenting voices would not alter the region’s endorsement of the company. Also, at the forum in Bayelsa, stakeholders called on oil companies and relevant authorities to address the environmental risks posed by ageing pipelines, abandoned wellheads and continued gas flaring, as they warned that these dangers could threaten livelihoods and damage the environment. King Bubaraye Dakolo Agada IV, King of Ekpetiama Kingdom who made the call said efforts to prevent pipeline vandalism must go hand in hand with measures to address risks associated with oil and gas infrastructure. The monarch noted that increased oil production could generate more revenue for Nigeria, but warned that oil spills could leave host communities struggling with environmental damage and loss of livelihoods for years. He urged residents to discourage pipeline vandalism and other activities that could cause spills in their creeks and communities and also stressed that oil companies and relevant authorities must also take responsibility for preventing spills linked to ageing infrastructure. According to him, PINL should draw the attention of relevant authorities and oil industry operators to the dangers posed by old pipelines, abandoned wellheads and gas flaring, urging them to take preventive action before incidents occur. He said pipeline protection should not be limited to stopping sabotage but should also cover infrastructure-related risks that could harm the environment and the people living in host communities. In his remarks, the President of the Ijaw Youth Council (IYC) Worldwide, Doubra Okotete, commended the leadership of pipeline surveillance contractors, saying there had been no reports of fatalities since the company took over the contract. He described the development as a departure from the past, when such operations were, in his words, “plagued by fatalism”. Okotete said the surveillance operations had helped secure oil and gas infrastructure while ensuring that host communities benefited from the resources flowing through the facilities they protected. “Our appeal today is for the Federal Government, the NNPCL and the President of our great country to ensure that oil and gas pipelines that have lasted for over 60 years are replaced,” he said.

title: Kremlin comments on restrictions on Ukraine’s access to Starlink, settlement process
body:
MOSCOW, October 14. /TASS/. Reports about restrictions on Ukraine’s access to Starlink, the settlement process and the potential weaponization of artificial intelligence were among the main topics of the October 14 briefing by Kremlin Spokesman Dmitry Peskov.
TASS has compiled the Kremlin spokesman’s key statements.
- Moscow has taken note of the risk that Europe could sabotage agreements on resolving the Ukraine conflict: "The risk of sabotage by European countries does exist."
- Unlike European countries, the US is working to steer the Ukrainian crisis toward a peaceful settlement: "The US, specifically its negotiators and President [Donald] Trump, is making efforts to help steer the settlement of the Ukrainian crisis toward peace."
- European countries, unlike the United States, which is seeking a peaceful solution, are doing everything they can to prolong the hostilities in Ukraine: "Europeans are taking a different approach: they are doing everything they can to ensure that this war continues."
- There is currently a lot of "media hype" around proposals for a settlement in Ukraine, and much of this hype does not correspond to reality: "There’s a lot of media hype around all of this right now, and much of it doesn’t correspond to reality; it’s pure fiction."
- Work on the possibility of an "energy ceasefire" is continuing.
- No international meetings on the Ukraine issue have been agreed upon at present: "There are no agreed-upon meetings on the agenda."
- Efforts to resolve the Ukraine conflict continue discreetly and will remain so: "This work is ongoing discreetly and it will continue discreetly."
- The Kremlin has seen media reports about restrictions on the Ukrainian army’s access to the Starlink satellite internet service but has no further information: "No, we know nothing beyond the media reports that we have read about it."
- Brilliant technologies such as Starlink would be better off not being used for military purposes at all: "In general, of course, it would be better if brilliant technologies such as Starlink were not used for military purposes at all."
- It is too early to conclude that Washington has changed its approach to military support for Kiev: "It is too early to draw any systemic conclusions. We proceed from the information available from the statements that are being made."
- "We have seen numerous media reports on the matter. On the one hand, there are statements that assistance continues to be provided, while on the other, there are reports of various technical restrictions and disruptions in information supplies to Ukraine. We have been carefully recording it all."
- Russia sees difficulties in recovering assets frozen by the European Union but will fight to get them back: "In any case, the Russian side will make every possible effort on all fronts, including legal work, court proceedings and litigation, to fight for the return of its stolen assets."
- The detention of a Japanese journalist on Sakhalin is evidence that Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB) is carrying out its duties to identify and detain spies: "The FSB has made relevant statements [on this matter]. The Federal Security Service is carrying out its duties: if there are spies, they are caught."
- Some countries are weaponizing artificial intelligence: "Attempts by a number of countries to turn these new technologies into weapons, the so-called weaponization of artificial intelligence, pose threats to entire sectors of any country’s economy, and, of course, we are no exception."
- The technology itself remains necessary, as it brings many benefits: "Artificial intelligence technologies bring many benefits, improve efficiency and do a lot of good."
- Russia must be prepared for its use as a weapon: "We must be prepared for these challenges."

title: Trial for man accused in Pearson gold heist set to hear more from key figure in case
body:
The man who received a prison sentence for his role in the Toronto Pearson airport gold heist is expected to continue his testimony Wednesday at the trial of another man accused in the case.
Arsalan Chaudhary was sentenced this spring to four years in prison after pleading guilty to theft over $5,000, and he was given 40 years to pay back $22 million in restitution.
He took the stand Tuesday in the Brampton, Ont., trial of Parmpal Sidhu, who has pleaded not guilty to charges of theft over $5,000 and conspiracy to commit an indictable offence in the 2023 heist.
Chaudhary said he planned the heist with another man who is still wanted by authorities, and he ended up taking 30 per cent of boxes full of one-ounce gold bars.
Prosecutors allege that Sidhu, an Air Canada employee at the time, provided a doctored waybill that allowed another man to pick up more than $22 million in gold and currency from a Pearson airport cargo bay.
Peel regional police have said 6,600 gold bars weighing more than 400 kilograms were stolen from the airport on April 17, 2023, after the shipment arrived from Switzerland.

title: George Dadzie Junior highly tipped in NDC regional secretary race due to grassroots experience
body: George Dadzie Junior, a former Western Regional Youth Organiser of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), is seeking to become the party’s next Western Regional Secretary, with supporters pointing to his experience in party organisation, grassroots mobilisation and member engagement as key strengths. As the party prepares for its regional elections next month, his backers believe his previous leadership role has given him an understanding of the NDC’s organisational structures and the challenges facing the party in the region. Yaw Asomaning, an NDC activist, said hard work was one of the qualities associated with Dadzie Junior’s political career. According to him, Dadzie Junior is regarded by many supporters as a committed party activist who understands the importance of grassroots mobilisation and sustained engagement with members. His supporters believe these qualities would be useful in the Regional Secretary role, which involves coordinating party activities and maintaining communication between regional leadership and the party’s structures. Experience in party organisation Dadzie Junior’s tenure as Western Regional Youth Organiser is another aspect of his candidature highlighted by supporters. They argue that the experience exposed him to grassroots organisation, mobilisation and the coordination required to sustain party activities. Ali Mahad, a long-standing party member, also pointed to his previous experience as relevant to his bid for the position. His backers further cite his interpersonal skills and ability to engage people from different backgrounds, arguing that these could help him work with regional executives, constituency officers and branch members. Samad Sulemana said the Regional Secretary’s role required administrative competence, coordination and the ability to work effectively with other party executives. Supporters believe Dadzie Junior’s relationship-building skills could help promote cooperation within the regional administration. Focus on unity and members’ welfare Party unity and the welfare of grassroots members also feature in the case being made for Dadzie Junior. His supporters say he recognises the need for party members to feel included in decision-making and for their concerns to be addressed beyond election periods. They also cite his willingness to support colleagues and his tolerance of differing views as qualities that could help manage disagreements within the party. In a contest involving aspirants with different support bases, they argue, the ability to listen to opposing views and encourage dialogue would be important in maintaining cohesion. His backers also point to his character and discipline, saying the Regional Secretary must be able to defend the party’s interests while respecting its constitution and established procedures. Delegates to decide The NDC’s Western Regional Secretary contest will test the appeal of the aspirants and their ability to convince delegates of their suitability for the position. For Dadzie Junior’s supporters, his previous leadership experience, knowledge of grassroots politics and emphasis on cooperation make him a credible contender. Ultimately, however, the outcome will depend on the choices of delegates as the party selects its next regional leadership.

title: 2027: Police’ll make Nigerians proud in elections – IGP assure
body: By Davies Iheamnachor PORT HARCOURT: The Inspector General of Police, Olatunji Rilwan Disu, has assured Nigerians that police would ensure professionalism during the forthcoming general election. Disu stated that the conduct of police personnel before, during and after the election would make Nigerians happy and proud of the force. Disu spoke in Port Harcourt on Tuesday while fielding questions from newsmen after the Launch of a book, “The Origin of Women in Nigeria Police Force”, written by 96-year-old Dame Stella Okuyiga, DCP (rtd), one of the 20 pioneer female Officers of NPF. Disu, who was responding to the questions on the police stance on the 2027 election, said the Force had, in preparation, organised a meeting with Commissioners of police across the country to ensure professionalism during the polls. He said: “I want to let you know that we just finished a conference of all commissioners of police and other senior officers. “We have had two or three elections recently, and you can see that the police came very well and we did so well. We now brought all these experiences together, where we did well and where we did not do well, so that we can perform better in this big election that everybody is looking up to. “I give you my word. Nigeria Police will do so well, and we will make Nigeria Police so proud, and we will make Nigerians proud. On Okuyiga’s book, Disu noted that the author was among the first set of women to join the Nigerian police in 1955, adding that the force is pleased with her recorded achievements. He said: “Mama is 96 years old and she has taken her time to put all her experience, institutional knowledge that she has down in the book for us to be able to study it for generation coming for women police in the next generation coming to have something to look up to. “We in the police, we are starting up the history of not leaving our own, not forgetting our own. “We are going to ensure that we get copies of this book for all police training institutions, for all police officers to go through to see what it was like to be police officers.” However, the author, Okuyiga, DCP (rtd), expressed happiness that the publication was not just a book, but a part of her that would live on. She said: “This book launch today is an important day in my life because the book itself is there. But I still live on my life. I still live on because this book will be in libraries all over the world and they’ll be reading it. “So I’m so happy that with all that is happening today, I will continue to live forever.” The post 2027: Police’ll make Nigerians proud in elections – IGP assure appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Ukraine’s MoD in contact with US, SpaceX, NATO partners over Starshield restrictions – source
body:
A source in the Defense Ministry told Ukrinform.
According to the source, overnight on October 14, SpaceX imposed a speed limit of 160 km/h on the terminals without warning the Defense Forces of Ukraine, causing the connection to be lost when that speed is exceeded. Depending on the equipment and unit, the connection is lost at different speeds, ranging from approximately 72 to 161 km/h.
This is complicating the operation of drone missions, including interceptor and mid-strike missions, and reducing capabilities for frontline logistics, reconnaissance and communications relay.
“As of now, the Defense Ministry is in contact with the United States, SpaceX and NATO partners, collecting data from all units, while backup communications channels are being reviewed and established,” the source said.
As Ukrinform reported, Serhii “Flash” Beskrestnov, a freelance adviser to the President on technology, said SpaceX had imposed speed restrictions on Starlink terminals while in motion overnight without warning Ukraine’s Defense Forces.
A Defense Ministry source also said the Starlink restrictions detected overnight had complicated the operation of Ukraine’s unmanned systems, logistics and mid-strike capabilities.

title: Are US, Israel racing to deploy space-based lasers or orbital weapons first? - analysis
body: In September, two consecutive top US military officials made public, for the first time, that America has offensive weapons already deployed in space.That the US, China, and Russia have anti-satellite weapons available is no secret and has been assumed in recent years, with China unofficially demonstrating old space weapons in 2007, and Russia and China both demonstrating newer weapons since 2021.But a public declaration by the US set off speculation about whether the deployed weapons are focused on the area of: either directed-energy weapons such as lasers; or kinetic anti-satellite weapons such as missiles; or platforms for disrupting or disabling satellites' activity without actually destroying them, which is also known as rendezvous and proximity operations (RPOs).A fourth method could be nuclear, but it is assumed that this was not the focus of the US announcement since the terrible consequences in space would impact the attacker as much as the defender.In April, Unit 9900 officer Lt. Col. “S” and space-war expert Tal Inbar discussed Israel's efforts to defend its space assets against adversaries.Also, on June 24, with the Post noting that Russia, China, and Iran have all worked on ways to attack, damage, jam, or drag satellites in space, IDF Brig. Gen. Yael Grossman responded, “There are threats from space. We work with the Defense Ministry with a lot of power; with the broader defense establishment, we can all bring forward achievements.”Developments in space vehiclesRegarding the US announcement, so far those space experts who are commenting are leaning toward category 3 of RPO.This is especially true for deploying RPOs, which can fight off other RPOs.The reason is that RPOs have existed in one form or another since the US used multiple space vehicles to repair one another in the 1960s. In that sense, the largest jump was developing the technology and tactics for sending one space vehicle or satellite to match the orbit of another.Once a country makes that major scientific jump, adding on a robot arm to attack or an additional system to jam is just a matter of time and energy.Another reason RPOs may be favored would be to avoid the debris problem caused by using kinetic anti-satellite weapons, such as missiles.The US has said it is hoping to make major advancements in stationing anti-missile physical interceptors in space that can protect satellites by 2028.Despite all this focus on RPOs for the US, China, and Russia, Israel has expressed keen interest regarding space weapons in relation to lasers.On June 29, Defense Minister Israel Katz told a briefing of military reporters that Israel is developing space lasers to carry out attacks above the Earth.This was an expansion and more specific version of a statement which Katz made earlier in June, when he committed Israel to becoming the leading player with space attack capabilities.“One of the central goals which the prime minister and I set is that we are recruiting the best minds,” since “as of today, no country has the ability to mount attacks in space. We must be the leading country in the world with this capability,” said Katz.The defense minister continued, “If we achieve this, it will ensure the advantage of deterrence, of the ability to attack, destroy, and all of the other matters, versus our enemies with large resources.”Lasers to be used to defend Israeli assetsBut Monday was the first time that Katz specifically mentioned space lasers.Israel is already a leading country in developing Iron Beam as a land-based space laser, and during a visit to Elbit earlier in the summer, The Jerusalem Post saw and heard about work on presumed future fighter-jet-based lasers.Overall, it seemed clear that Katz on June 29 was referring to Iran.This is especially true since during the 2026 war, Israel struck multiple Iranian space war-related facilities, including facilities working on developing capabilities to attack satellites in space.It was unclear if he indirectly also wanted to deter Russia and China from assisting Iran in this and other spheres.According to foreign reports, lasers might be able to destroy enemy satellites and also burn up any debris that an attack in space by other means might cause.Some have already speculated that Israel could destroy enemy space satellites using the Arrow 3 missile system, given that it already strikes ballistic missiles in space.Yet, due to the same issue that Russia and China already fell into regarding debris, many countries are working on other techniques, such as paralyzing, damaging, jamming, dragging, or using lasers against satellites in space.While some Israeli officials have hinted at such efforts, Katz's public statements on June 29 were the clearest one to date by a senior Israeli official.Why the US's first focus is on RPOsIn contrast, if Iran or other enemies advanced past Israel in space, they could attack Israeli satellites and reduce its surveillance capabilities.After all of this, why then do most experts believe that the US's first and current focus is on RPOs, and not lasers?It is not that the US and the other countries with space programs are not working on developing space lasers. They are.Also, Israel's success with developing the Iron Beam for actual deployments as a ground laser has spurred other countries forward in the more general laser defense area.But lasers in space or on aircraft are still a distant solution, as they involve a series of more complex physics and engineering problems, which invariably will take longer to solve than RPOs.RPOs are thereby an immediate answer to help deter enemies from attacking, since they can be used to attack enemy satellites, as well as providing defense against other countries' potential RPO attacks.If enemies have existing and immediate weapons to attack an object, such as a satellite, the US and other countries, potentially even including Israel, are likely to focus on immediate solutions, with the focus on space lasers being a longer-term goal.In that sense, the US statement in September was about immediately deterring China and Russia from attacking American satellites.In contrast, Katz's June statement was less about immediate attack, defense, or deterrence.Rather, it was more about either bragging to the Israeli public about a future distant achievement, or psychological warfare against Iran to the extent that the Islamic Republic might believe it can work with Moscow and Beijing to go after Israel's satellite advantage.

title: Fulham manager Arbeloa fined £25,000 after Man Utd outburst
body: Fulham manager Alvaro Arbeloa has been fined £25,000 ($33,000) by England’s governing Football Association after he claimed officials would “not let Manchester United lose”. Arbeloa made his remarks following Fulham’s 1-1 draw with United in the Premier League at Craven Cottage in September. Matheus Cunha equalised for visitors United in the 89th minute. Arbeloa, who admitted the charge, has also received a warning for his comments, with the FA saying the Spaniard “acted in an improper manner by making comments in a post-match interview that imply bias and/or question the integrity of a match official”. London club Fulham are currently bottom of the Premier League with just two points from their opening six games. title: Aklerh returns to reggae roots with new single ‘Wo Dor’
body: Dancehall Queen Aklerh is returning to her reggae roots with Wo Dor , a new lovers’ rock single scheduled for release on Monday, 19 October, under the Revolution Records label. After two Afrobeat hits that grew her audience and showed a playful new side, Aklerh is returning to the reggae dancehall and lovers’ rock sound that first shaped her voice. Wo Dor , which means ‘My Love’, is a lovers’ rock slow burn, featuring soft, melodic rhythms, mellow bass and harmonies that complement Aklerh’s honeyed vocals. It is the kind of song that feels like a late-night conversation with someone you care about: simple, honest and full of feeling. “After exploring afrobeat in my last two singles, Wo Dor is a return to what first inspired me,” Aklerh says. “It’s a demonstration of my versatility: my ability to swing between various genres and freely express my creativity.” “Tubhani Music did well with this song, which marks my return to reggae,” Aklerh adds. “‘Wo Dor’ captures the authenticity of lovers rock while highlighting my journey as an artist: it’s soulful, timeless, and sure to connect with listeners across generations.” Her previous Afrobeat singles, Amele and Good Vibes , showcased Aklerh’s ability to move crowds with contemporary rhythms and groovy hooks. With Wo Dor , she slows the tempo and embraces a timeless warmth, offering longtime fans and new listeners a tender, melodic counterpoint to her dancehall and Afrobeat work. Known for her electrifying performances, Dancehall Queen Aklerh continues to bridge modern sounds and musical tradition, making songs that move both feet and heart.

title: Russia's opponents trying to derail diesel deal with US — Dmitriev
body:
MOSCOW, October 14. /TASS/. Many of Russia's opponents are trying to derail the diesel deal with the US, yet it benefits all parties involved, Kirill Dmitriev, head of the Russian Direct Investment Fund and Special Presidential Envoy for Economic Cooperation with Foreign Countries, told reporters on the sidelines of Russian Energy Week (REW).
"Opponents of the diesel deal - including those from Europe - forget that Europe itself purchased $320 billion worth of Russian energy resources, as [Deputy Prime Minister] Alexander Novak noted. They try to dispute this figure, but I believe it is accurate. Therefore, many opponents are attempting to derail the deal with the US. At the same time, we see that this deal is beneficial for global markets, for Russia, and for the United States of America," he said.
The Russian Energy Week international forum is taking place in Moscow from October 14 to 16, supported by the Russian government, the Ministry of Energy, and the Moscow government. The forum is organized by the Roscongress Foundation. TASS is an information partner of the event.

title: Starlink restrictions complicate work of interceptors, Defense Ministry in contact with US, SpaceX, backup communication channels in use – sources
body:
The restriction on the operation of Starshield terminals (the "military package"), which SpaceX imposed unilaterally overnight into October 14 without warning the Defense Forces, complicates the work of UAV missions, including interceptors.

According to Interfax-Ukraine sources in Ukraine's Ministry of Defense, the ministry is now in contact with the United States, SpaceX and partners in NATO, and is collecting data from all units, while backup communication channels are being checked and used.

title: Pakistani PM meets SG of Mecca Agreement Nauman Mahmood
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 14 (MNA) – Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has received for a meeting Nauman Mahmood, the Secretary General of Mecaa Agreement.
Accoridng to a report by Pakistani premier's office, in the meeting, which was held in Islamabad, Sharif congratulated Nauman Mahmood on assuming the post of the first secretary general of the Mecca agreement coalition.
Sharif also said that the Mecca Agreement is "a historic turning point for peace, unity and stability in the region."
Following the signing of the Mecca Agreement, repeated meetings between officials from Pakistan, Türkiye, and Saudi Arabia in the capitals of the three countries led to the appointment of the Nauman Mahmood as the fist Secretary-General of the Mecca Coalition.
Sharif also said: “Pakistan stands by Saudi Arabia in the framework of the Mecca Defense Agreement to safeguard its sovereignty, defense and regional security.”
Without referring to Saudi Arabia’s aggression against Yemen and its blockade of the impverished country, the Pakistani prime minister said: “Pakistan fully supports Saudi Arabia’s legitimate right to defend itself. We reiterate Pakistan’s firm commitment to protecting the sovereignty, territorial integrity and security of Saudi Arabia.”
According to Sharif’s office, “the Secretary General of the Mecca Defense Coalition briefed the prime minister on the strategy to enhance defense and strategic cooperation within the framework of the Mecca Defense Pact.”

title: Emirates unveils Tokyo travel store, to increases flights to Japan
body: Emirates announced on October 14, 2026, that it has opened a new travel store in Tokyo’s Otemachi business district, expanding its retail presence in Japan as it prepares to add more flights to the country. The Tokyo store follows the opening of the Emirates Travel Store in Osaka in July 2025. A ribbon-cutting ceremony was attended by Shihab Ahmed Al Faheem, the UAE’s ambassador to Japan; Orhan Abbas, Emirates’ senior vice president of commercial operations for the Far East; Satish Sethi, the airline’s country manager for Japan; and Tetsuya Mori, director of the International Air Transport Division at the Japan Civil Aviation Bureau, as well as members of the local travel trade and media. Otemachi store offers bookings, travel planning and a Boeing 777 Business Class seat on display The store is staffed by multilingual travel consultants who serve both Japanese and international customers. They can assist with flight bookings, travel information and tailored itineraries. The space also includes a self-service kiosk, a queue management system and a selfie mirror with backdrops of destinations in Emirates’ network. A Business Class seat from the airline’s Boeing 777 is on display for customers to try. The store is located on the first floor of Otemachi One, 1-2-1 Otemachi, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo. It is open Monday to Friday from 11:00-19:00 local time and closed on weekends and public holidays. Additional Narita brings Emirates to 28 weekly services in Japan Emirates currently flies from Dubai International Airport (DXB) to three Japanese airports: Narita International Airport (NRT) and Tokyo International Airport (HND), also known as Haneda, in the Tokyo area, and Kansai International Airport (KIX) in Osaka. From October 26, 2026, the airline will add more flights to Narita, bringing its total passenger services to and from Japan to 28 per week. The additional flights will be operated by a Boeing 777-300ER, adding more than 300 seats in each direction and 20 metric tons of cargo capacity per day. Emirates said the expansion is intended to meet growing demand for travel to Japan while giving travelers departing from Japan more options.
