title: Starlink restrictions undermining Ukrainian army effectiveness — expert
body:
MOSCOW, October 14. /TASS/. The reduced scope of intelligence data received from the United States, as well as restrictions on Starlink operations, are undermining the Ukrainian armed forces’ capabilities, Dmitry Kuzyakin, an unmanned aviation expert and chief designer at the Center for Integrated Unmanned Solutions, told TASS.
"The United States is testing the Ukrainian regime’s strength and flexibility. They are twisting the Ukrainian armed forces’ arm by reducing the amount of intelligence data transmitted, cutting back on arms supplies, stopping direct payments ‘to keep them going,’ and artificially degrading Starlink satellite communications. The main reason for the current tightening of the screws on Ukraine is that the US State Department is beginning to lose control over the Ukrainian regime," he said. According to Kuzyakin, the Kiev regime's uncontrolled actions are irritating both US President Donald Trump personally and that part of the American establishment that has invested heavily in Ukraine.
On Wednesday morning, Sergey Beskrestnov, an adviser to Vladimir Zelensky on communications and unmanned systems, reported that SpaceX had limited the speed of Starlink satellite Internet terminals used by the Ukrainian army to 160 km/h overnight. According to him, this disrupted "a number of operations."

title: Stacy Mense’s ‘W’ahyira Me’ gains airplay on radio, digital platforms
body: Ghanaian contemporary gospel artiste Stacy Mense is gaining attention with her debut single, W’ahyira Me , which has received airplay and is performing well on digital platforms. The song speaks of God’s goodness and the blessings that come with trust in and obedience to His word. Stacy Mense, born Anastasia Hannah Amuzu, is a Ghanaian contemporary gospel artiste, singer, songwriter, worship leader and registered nurse whose life and artistry are deeply rooted in faith, worship, service and a desire to inspire others through music. Her musical journey began in childhood and has evolved through years of church worship, gospel ministry, songwriting, vocal performance and service. Today, Stacy brings together heartfelt worship, personal testimony and contemporary gospel expression to create music that glorifies God while encouraging listeners to remain anchored in faith, hope, gratitude and the promises of God. THE ARTIST For Stacy Mense, music is more than creative expression; it is an extension of her faith and a form of ministry. Her musical journey began at an early age, singing alto alongside her siblings as part of a family singing band within a well-established family fellowship. This early exposure to music nurtured her vocal ability and established a lasting passion for worship and gospel music. That foundation continued to develop through her involvement in church ministry. Stacy became an active member of The Church of Pentecost, Avenor Branch, where she served on the worship team and ministered during Sunday services. Through this experience, she began to understand worship not simply as music, but as an opportunity to serve God and His people. She later became a member of the gospel trio Victorious Sisters, founded by Christopher Baffour Awuah, the younger brother of Reverend Owusu Ansah. The group was managed by Reverend Gabriel Ansah and Mr Kankam and featured Stacy alongside Esther Saforo and the late Cynthia Tetteh. Stacy’s musical development continued through her involvement with gospel music groups, including One Family and Marko and the Urban Worshippers, where she contributed as both a singer and songwriter. She has written songs for these groups as well as for individual gospel artistes, including Nicole King. Her experience also extends to backing vocals and collaborative gospel ministry. She has ministered alongside Ghanaian gospel musicians, including the late Sampson Annor and Nana Yaw Asare. Her engagements included a performance of Nana Yaw Asare’s Odumankoma during the launch of the All-Gospel Stars song in Kumasi. These experiences have played an important role in shaping Stacy’s development as a vocalist, songwriter, worship minister and contemporary gospel artiste. A LIFE ROOTED IN WORSHIP Stacy’s ministry journey has continued across several Christian communities, each contributing to her spiritual growth and development as a worshipper and servant of God. She was a committed member of International Central Gospel Church (ICGC), Osu Branch, where she worshipped under the ministry of Rev. Kofi Okyere, now the resident pastor of ICGC Milton Keynes Branch. She later became a member of ICGC Tesano Branch, which was more convenient to her place of residence. There, she worshipped under the leadership of Rev. Gabriel Dela during a significant period of her life before marriage and her relocation abroad. Stacy currently worships with Lighthouse Chapel International (Mustard Seed Chapel International), Liverpool Branch, where she served as a praise and worship leader under the ministry of Rev. Kenneth Abubakr. Her commitment to ministry extends beyond music and worship. Through her involvement with the children’s ministry at Save Church within Mustard Seed Chapel International, Stacy has also developed a heart for nurturing, encouraging and positively influencing the next generation. Whenever she visits Ghana, she continues to worship with ICGC The New Wine Temple under the leadership of Rev. Albert Ocran, maintaining a meaningful connection with the Christian community and spiritual heritage that have contributed to her journey. For Stacy, worship extends far beyond the microphone. It is expressed through service, encouragement, mentorship, compassion and a willingness to make a positive difference in the lives of others. ‘W’AHYIRA ME’: THE DEBUT On 13 July 2026, Stacy Mense entered a defining new chapter in her musical journey with the release of her debut official single, W’ahyira Me . The song is a heartfelt declaration of God’s goodness, faithfulness and blessings through every season and circumstance of life. Drawing from her personal faith and testimony, Stacy uses the song to acknowledge God’s hand throughout her journey while reminding listeners of His unwavering presence, love and faithfulness. More than simply a debut release, W’ahyira Me represents a statement of faith and the beginning of Stacy’s public recorded music ministry. Through the song, she encourages listeners to recognise God’s goodness even in challenging seasons, remain hopeful through adversity and celebrate His blessings with gratitude. The release represents not only a new musical beginning, but also the culmination of years of worship, preparation, personal growth, ministry and faith. MUSIC WITH PURPOSE Stacy’s musical identity is centred on authenticity, faith and purpose. Her artistry explores themes of God’s faithfulness, gratitude, hope, perseverance, testimony, worship and divine goodness. Through her distinctive voice and heartfelt delivery, she seeks to communicate messages that are both deeply personal and spiritually uplifting. Rather than viewing music solely as entertainment, Stacy sees gospel music as an opportunity to create moments of reflection, worship, encouragement, healing and connection with God. Her aspiration is to create music that speaks to people wherever they may be in their journey, whether they are celebrating a breakthrough, navigating a difficult season, searching for encouragement or simply longing to draw closer to God. At the heart of her artistry is a simple conviction: music can become a vessel through which faith is strengthened, hope is restored and lives are encouraged. THE HEART BEHIND THE MUSIC Alongside her musical ministry, Stacy is a registered nurse, a profession that reflects another important dimension of her commitment to serving others. Her nursing career has strengthened qualities such as compassion, empathy, patience, attentiveness, responsibility and genuine care for people. These qualities naturally influence the way she approaches music and ministry. For Stacy, caring for people through nursing and encouraging people through music are complementary expressions of service. Both allow her to connect with others, offer support, provide encouragement and contribute positively to their lives. This intersection of healthcare, faith, ministry, worship and music gives Stacy a distinctive perspective as an emerging contemporary gospel artiste. Her experiences have taught her that people need more than words: they need hope, compassion, reassurance and reminders that they are not alone. These values continue to influence the message she carries through her music. THE JOURNEY AHEAD Stacy Mense stands at the beginning of a new chapter in her musical career. From singing alto alongside her siblings as a young girl to serving in church worship teams, participating in gospel music groups, writing songs, leading praise and worship, serving children and ultimately releasing her first official single, her journey has been shaped by one consistent thread: faith expressed through service and music. Her debut single, W’ahyira Me , marks the beginning of her recorded music journey while representing the culmination of years of worship, ministry, personal development and preparation. As she continues to develop her artistry, Stacy remains committed to creating music that is authentic, uplifting, inspirational, worshipful and centred on God. Her vision is to reach wider audiences, share her testimony through music, encourage people through every season of life and use her God-given gifts to make a meaningful spiritual impact. With a heart for worship, a passion for people and a growing musical voice, Stacy Mense is stepping into this new chapter with faith, purpose, humility and gratitude, trusting God to guide every step of the journey.

title: South Korea, US, Japan seek nuclear alliance against regional countries — Russia’s MFA
body:
MOSCOW, October 14. /TASS/. South Korea, the United States and Japan are essentially working to create a nuclear alliance directed against other countries in the region, Konstantin Vorontsov, deputy head of the Russian Foreign Ministry’s Department for Nonproliferation and Arms Control, said.
"South Korea has decided to bring ‘peace and stability’ to the Korean Peninsula by brandishing the US nuclear bludgeon at North Korea," he pointed out at a meeting of the First Committee of the United Nations General Assembly.
"First, it deployed nuclear weapons to its territory in 1958-1991. In 1976, it started to engage in joint drills with the US that practice nuclear strikes and carpet bombings of North Korea, an activity that continues to this day. Now, building on this years-long aggressive policy, Seoul has teamed up with Washington and Tokyo, effectively seeking to form a nuclear alliance directed against the countries of the region," Vorontsov added.
The Russian diplomat highlighted "Seoul’s regular attempts to blame Russia for its own years-long deliberate escalatory moves, which are the root cause of the current crisis facing the Korean Peninsula."
"In Resolution 3390B, adopted at the 30th session of the UN General Assembly, the First Committee already outlined specific steps required to provide strong guarantees of peace on the Korean Peninsula, which include withdrawing all foreign troops stationed in South Korea and replacing the Armistice Agreement with a peace treaty," Vorontsov emphasized. "Since none of the above features in the long-term plans of Washington and Seoul, no comprehensive solution to the nuclear issue on the Korean Peninsula should be expected in the near future," he concluded.

title: Delivering the integrated force at DSEI UK in London
body: DSEI UK will run under the theme of delivering the integrated force in 2027, with four sub-themes covering innovation, industrial capacity, international collaboration and digital technology, the show’s senior defence adviser has told the UK Defence Journal. Organisers are forecasting around 2,000 exhibitors and up to 60,000 visitors at ExCeL in September next year. Air Vice-Marshal (Retired) Gary Waterfall CBE is senior defence adviser to Clarion Defence and Security, the company that runs the show. He left the Royal Air Force at the end of 2019, retiring from the Permanent Joint Headquarters as a two-star, and joined Clarion the following year. His job, he said, is to stand with his back to Clarion and look at the Ministry of Defence. Themes have to be set at least a year ahead of the doors opening, “If you can tell me what’s going to happen in September 27, right here, right now, on the world stage, then please fire away,” he said. The 2025 theme had to survive a defence review landing part-way through the cycle, and Waterfall said it did. Sub-themes are built from research among the people who come to the show, Clarion’s own view of the market and talks with the department. “We don’t set the theme in isolation,” he said. “We confer with the Ministry of Defence.” Defence and security exports used to sit in the Department for Business and Trade, and have now moved into the Ministry of Defence under the National Armaments Director. Waterfall said that gives the show one door to knock on in Whitehall, and he expects it to change what the department puts on its stand. “When it’s the MOD capability showcase, that’s going to be a much broader aspect,” he said. Waterfall said the theme follows from the same reform drive, and that it is broad enough to mean something to everyone on the floor. “Everyone talks about integration and being that integrated force,” he said. “Therefore the theme for next year is delivering the integrated force. There’s a lot in those four words, but you can hang your hat on that.” He said it applies to an SME with reservists on the books as much as to a prime, to CSOC or to a frontline command, and that it does not stop at the UK border. The four sub-themes are innovation and emerging technologies, supply chain and industrial capacity, deepening global defence collaboration and partnerships, and digital transformation, AI and cyber. Waterfall said the digital strand runs through all of them. Choosing the wording for the collaboration sub-theme took some arguing inside the company. “We agonised, would you believe, over the global defence collaboration. Is that NATO?” he said. “It’s not just NATO.” He cited Royal Navy, Royal Air Force and British Army units working with regional partners around Iran, and British activity in the High North through the Joint Expeditionary Force, both outside the alliance. Waterfall also made a case for the show itself as a form of deterrence. “Those that would wish harm to us will be sat there watching the power of DSEI, seeing it as that convening authority across the global allied defence sector,” he said. Asked what rising British and European budgets will mean for the conversations on the floor, he spoke about procurement speed. Three years of war in Ukraine have made a 10, 15 or 20 year acquisition cycle impossible to defend, he said, and smaller firms have gained most from that. “The winners are the small and medium enterprises that can work at a pace that outstrips the routine of a big prime,” he said. The primes have noticed, he added, and are buying into them while trying to leave them alone to work. Waterfall said buyers now arrive wanting the part of a system that lets it keep changing. “I want it yesterday, please.” James Samuel took over this year as managing director for live events at Clarion Defence and Security. The job covers DSEI UK, the company’s Japanese business and a conference portfolio that includes UDT in Europe and a UDT Australia launching in December. He has been at Clarion for seven years and has worked in exhibitions for 26. Around 1,750 companies exhibited at the 2025 show, and Samuel is forecasting 2,000 to 2,100 next year, with the floor growing in square metres as well. The last edition drew 45,000 attendees and he expects 55,000 to 60,000 next time, “if there’s no tube strikes or DLR strikes during our week”. Samuel said he judges the show on connections made instead off floor space sold. “We can’t just rely on the industry to meet itself,” he said. Registration answers and what visitors then do on the show platform are used to push suggested sessions, events and contacts at them before they arrive. Samuel said the size of the venue makes that necessary. “It’s a kilometre from one end to the other. You could walk there three or four times and you’ve done that before you’ve even met anyone.” The 2025 show hosted 114 official delegations from 66 nations, and Samuel said the list is drawn up with government. “This isn’t just us picking out who would like to come to the show,” he said, describing a test of whether there is real business for a delegation to do with British government and British industry. Clarion is launching DSEI Germany in Hannover in March 2027, six months before London, and DSEI Japan follows in April. Samuel said its offices in Berlin and Tokyo let exhibitors and national pavilions carry one pitch across all three. “Their narrative continues, whether it be from Germany to London to Tokyo,” he said. Between shows the company runs smaller events of 150 to 200 people under the name DSEI Gateway, on the basis that four days every two years leaves a long gap. Asked what he looks forward to most, Waterfall picked the first morning, telling me that he envisions, “There’s a Nigerian delegation talking to a Polish delegation. The interaction is just unbelievable,” he said. “We are facilitating this show for His Majesty’s government to stand on a stage and project soft power around the world, and that’s a real humbling factor.” DSEI UK 2027 runs from 7 to 10 September at ExCeL London. The post Delivering the integrated force at DSEI UK in London first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Ukraine caught off guard by Starlink restrictions — newspaper
body:
LONDON, October 14. /TASS/. A slowdown in the operation of Starlink satellite Internet terminals has taken the Ukrainian military by surprise, with the change introduced without warning, The Financial Times reported, citing sources.
"Frontline logistics and the ability to carry out medium-range strikes are severely limited," an unnamed Ukrainian official told the newspaper. He noted that the restrictions were imposed "without warning, in the middle of the night."
According to the newspaper, Ukrainian military drones that rely on Starlink terminals are experiencing signal disruptions at speeds above 160 km/h.
Earlier, Sergey Beskrestnov, an adviser to Vladimir Zelensky on communications and unmanned systems, reported that SpaceX had restricted the speed of Starlink satellite Internet terminals used by the Ukrainian army to 160 km/h overnight. According to him, this disrupted "a number of operations."
A slowdown in Starlink service is rendering the launch of medium-range drones virtually impossible, and some missions involving them have already been scrapped since the start of the day, the 7th Corps of the Ukrainian airborne assault troops reported on Telegram.

title: ‘Black Rus’ Sabotage Group Likely Responsible for Latvian Incursion
body:
In a video statement released on Telegram on Wednesday, Oct. 7, a little-known group calling itself Chernye Rusy (Black Rus) claimed responsibility for the incursions of the Latvia-Belarus border on the night of Oct. 5-6.
As previously reported , armed and masked men attempted to smuggle around 20 illegal migrants into the country and, in a later separate raid, damaged and vandalized an electrical distribution cabinet and removed border surveillance cameras before retreating back into Belarus .
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
According to the “Black Rus” masked spokesman calling himself “Neman,” three members of the group “assume responsibility for the incident on the Latvian-Belarusian border in Kaplava parish, Krāslava region,” who then “re-entered Latvian territory near the village of Matuliški, stole video surveillance cameras, damaged the equipment, and remained unnoticed.”
The statement then went on to say that this was just the start of a sabotage campaign aimed at the European Union and NATO, which it called “a colossus on feet of clay that will collapse after our first strike.”
According to Latvia’s LSM state media outlet, citing Jānis Sārts, director of the NATO Strategic Communications Centre of Excellence in Riga, “Black Rus” is a front for Russian or Belarusian intelligence services established to carry out sabotage or other hybrid operations.
Exiled Belarusian military journalist Dmitry Khalko agreed, saying that “Black Rus” is a “proxy” just like Russia’s “little green men” who seized Ukraine’s Crimea in 2014, saying that they are a “fig leaf” intended to cover up special services involvement, allowing them to say, “it’s not us, we don’t know anything.”
At a “readiness review” meeting of the Belarusian interior ministry’s 7th Separate Special Police Brigade on Tuesday, Oct. 13, Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko claimed the cross-border incident was a “false flag” operation “orchestrated by Latvians themselves as a publicity stunt to secure funds from the European Union.”
The BelTA state news agency, reporting on the event , cited Lukashenko as saying, “We had absolutely nothing to do with this, with the claim that we – allegedly – crossed into their territory, with masked men or military personnel seizing someone or pushing a group of migrants across. You couldn’t dream up a more ridiculous story.”
Lukashenko went on to dismiss reports in the Western media of a military threat from Russia and Belarus, describing it as utter nonsense before claiming the Baltics possess military ambitions against Minsk.
“They need money. Neither the three Baltic states nor Poland possess the power to satisfy their [military] ambitions,” Lukashenko said.
“Take Poland, for instance: It is purchasing tanks and other weaponry, which are not cheap these days. There is no firewood for the population, yet they feel compelled to buy tanks and other military hardware.”
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Economic activities mixed in 7 months of 2026; Cement sales decline by 10%
body: Consumer spending, proxied by domestic VAT collections and retail sales, posted a mixed performance in July 2026, compared with the corresponding period in 2025, the September 2026 Monetary Policy Report. Domestic VAT collections increased by 11.5% on a year-on year basis to GH¢2.142 billion, from GH¢1.922 billion. Cumulatively, total domestic VAT for the first seven months of 2026 went up by 13.8% to GH¢13.617 billion compared with GH¢11.965 billion for the corresponding period of last year. Retail sales, however, declined by 1.5% (year-on-year) to GH¢236.41 million in July 2026, down from the GH¢239.89 million recorded in the same period in 2025. On a month-on-month basis, retail sales moderated by 0.8% in July 2026 from GH¢238.25 million in the preceding month. In cumulative terms, retail sales for the first seven months of 2026 went up by 2.2 percent compared to the same period of last year. Manufacturing Activities Also, activities in the manufacturing sub-sector, gauged by trends in the collection of direct taxes and private sector workers’ contributions to the Social Security and National Insurance Trust (SSNIT) Pension Scheme (Tier-1), improved in July 2026. The total direct taxes collected increased by 53.5% (year-on-year) to GH¢8.085 billion in July 2026, relative to GH¢5.265 billion recorded in the corresponding period in 2025. Cumulatively, total direct taxes collected for the first seven months of 2026 went up by 27.7% to GH¢60.771 billion, from GH¢47.592 billion for the same period in 2025. Als, the total private sector workers’ contribution to the SSNIT Pension Scheme (Tier-1) increased by 11.2% in year-on year terms to GH¢570.59 million in July 2026, from GH¢513.34 million collected during the corresponding period in 2025. Cumulatively, for the first seven months of 2026, the contribution grew by 10.7 percent to GH¢3.856 billion, relative to GH¢3.482 billion recorded in the same period in 2025. Construction Sector Activities Furthermore, activity in the construction sub-sector, proxied by the volume of cement sales, declined by 4.9% (year-on-year) in July 2026 to 202,218.17 tonnes, from 212,735.33 tonnes recorded a year ago. Similarly, on a month-on-month basis, total cement sales moderated by 0.6 percent in July 2026 compared with the 203,435.35 tonnes recorded in June 2026. Cumulatively, cement sales for the first seven months of 2026 declined by 10.3 percent to 1,475,115.01 tonnes, from 1,644,413.19 tonnes for the same period of 2025. According to the report, the relative decline in total cement sales, year-on-year, was due to a moderation in construction activities during the review period. Vehicle Registration For vehicle registration, transport sector activities, gauged by new vehicle registrations by the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Authority (DVLA), improved by 51.7% to 31,909 in July 2026, from 21,038 vehicles registered during the corresponding period of 2025. Cumulatively, the number of vehicles registered by the DVLA within the first seven months of 2026 increased by 52.7% to 228,261 from 149,440 recorded a year ago.

title: Iran not shy away from dealing with violating vessels
body:

If the Americans want to see whether the Strait of Hormuz is open or closed, let them enter the violated route in the strait, IRGC Navy Chief General Ali Ozmaei underlined.

“We will deal with violating vessels in the Strait of Hormuz,” he reiterated.

title: US Navy completes first F-35C landing on Ford-class aircraft carrier
body:
A US Navy F-35C Lightning II fighter aircraft has made the first arrested landing aboard the future USS John F. Kennedy (CVN 79), marking a milestone in aircraft compatibility testing for the navy’s Ford-class aircraft carrier.
The aircraft, assigned to Air Test and Evaluation Squadron 23 (VX-23), known as the “Salty Dogs,” landed on the carrier’s flight deck on October 13, 2026, while the ship was underway in the Western Atlantic.
The testing assesses the operational capabilities of John F. Kennedy’s aircraft launch and recovery equipment with U.S. Navy aircraft. It is part of the work required to evaluate the carrier’s ability to support naval aviation operations.
The F-35C is the carrier variant of the Lightning II stealth fighter, designed for catapult-assisted takeoff and arrested recovery aboard aircraft carriers. Its first landing aboard John F. Kennedy represents a step in evaluating the compatibility of the fifth-generation fighter with the Ford-class carrier’s flight deck and aviation systems.
John F. Kennedy is the second ship in the Ford class, following the lead ship, USS Gerald R. Ford (CVN 78). The class incorporates new aircraft launch and recovery technologies intended to support carrier air operations.
The ship recently achieved preliminary acceptance of the aircraft carrier. Preliminary acceptance is the final step before formal delivery to the navy. It allows the navy to begin testing and evaluation of the carrier’s systems underway while its crew continues to build operational proficiency.
Following preliminary acceptance, the carrier departed HII’s Newport News Shipbuilding facility in Virginia and is scheduled to transition to Naval Station Norfolk.

title: FG Trains 100 On Anti-Money Laundering, Counter-Financing Terrorism
body: Nigeria has commenced a five-day capacity-building programme for 100 members of its Mutual Evaluation Working Groups (MEWG), geared towards strengthening preparations for the country’s forthcoming third-round Mutual Evaluation on anti-money laundering, counter-financing of terrorism and counter-proliferation financing (AML/CFT/CPF). A statement by the NFIU Chief Executive Officer, signed by the Chief Executive Officer, Hafsat Abubakar Bakari, noted that the training is being facilitated by the Inter-Governmental Action Group against Money Laundering in West Africa (GIABA), with support from SecFIN Africa at Nigeria’s request. The training runs from October 12 to 16, 2026, in Abuja. It aims to establish a common understanding of the assessment methodology and prepare participants for the national Mock Mutual Evaluation Exercise scheduled for November 2026. Speaking at the opening, Bakari said Nigeria must demonstrate the strength of its laws and institutional frameworks and their effectiveness in practice. “Nigeria must be ready to not only explain its laws, policies and institutional arrangements, but also to demonstrate the results they deliver. This workshop builds on our successful exit from the FATF Grey List in October 2025 and reflects our continued commitment to strengthening the integrity of our financial system,” she said. Participants at the NFIU training Representing the Director General of GIABA, Giwa Siman Sechap, Director, Evaluations and Compliance at the GIABA Secretariat, emphasised the importance of a shared understanding of the mutual evaluation methodology and credible evidence of implementation. “Mutual evaluation is a collective national responsibility. Beyond technical compliance, countries must demonstrate that their systems are delivering results. This training provides an opportunity to strengthen the knowledge, coordination and practical readiness required to present a clear and evidence-based account of Nigeria’s efforts,” he informed. Professor Shehu Abdullahi, SecFIN Africa’s Country Representative, underscored the importance of sustained capacity development and collaboration among institutions. “Effective preparation requires more than individual expertise; it depends on institutions working together, sharing reliable information and taking collective ownership of national priorities. Building this capacity now will help Nigeria identify gaps, consolidate progress and demonstrate the effectiveness of its financial integrity framework,” he said. The programme brings together representatives of key institutions whose collective responsibilities underpin Nigeria’s financial integrity framework. Participating agencies include the Bureau of Public Procurement (BPP), Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), Code of Conduct Bureau (CCB), Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC), Defence Intelligence Agency (DIA), Department of State Services (DSS), Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), Federal Ministry of Justice, Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC), Mining Cadastral Office (MCO), National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP), National Counter Terrorism Centre (NCTC), and the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA). Others include the National Insurance Commission (NAICOM), Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit (NFIU), Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), Nigeria Export Processing Zones Authority (NEPZA), Nigeria Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (NEITI), Nigeria Police Force (NPF), Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS), Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Oil and Gas Free Zones Authority (OGFZA), Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), Special Control Unit Against Money Laundering (SCUML), among other relevant institutions. Their contributions and knowledge shared span financial intelligence, regulation and supervision, suspicious transaction reporting, investigations and prosecutions, asset recovery, border control, beneficial ownership transparency, revenue enforcement and national security. The Unit noted that their collaboration is essential to demonstrating that Nigeria’s AML/CFT/CPF framework delivers measurable results. Over the past two years, Nigeria has expanded its pool of accredited global experts in the FATF Standards from fewer than 10 to 25. The current training forms part of a wider capacity-building plan, with further cohorts of 100 to 150 participants envisaged quarterly and possible future extension to the private sector. Sessions will cover financial intelligence, regulatory supervision, virtual assets, beneficial ownership, investigations and prosecutions, asset confiscation, international cooperation, targeted financial sanctions and proliferation financing risks. Practical exercises and simulated assessment interviews will prepare participants to respond to assessors with accurate information and verifiable evidence. The training also builds on the national stocktake and gap analysis coordinated by the NFIU, with support from the EFCC, DSS, ICPC, CBN, NAICOM, and SEC, through the Inter-Ministerial Committee (IMC). Drawing on contributions from participating institutions, the exercise assesses implementation, identifies strengths and outstanding gaps, and establishes priorities for corrective action. The NFIU boss noted that the collaborative process provides a shared basis for strengthening the overall AML/CFT/CPF regime of the country and ensuring that national preparations reflect the work and responsibilities of the institutions involved. He noted that the objective was to translate collective effort into measurable improvements. “The real value of this exercise lies in the improvements it helps us deliver. By bringing our institutions together around evidence, shared responsibilities and measurable results, we can build a stronger and more effective system for detecting and disrupting financial crime,” she added. The initiative reinforces Nigeria’s commitment to sustained inter-agency collaboration, stronger institutional capacity and demonstrable progress ahead of its next Mutual Evaluation. The post FG Trains 100 On Anti-Money Laundering, Counter-Financing Terrorism appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Under siege: Taiz isolated and afraid as Houthis and Yemeni forces fight over city
body: Medical warehouses are unsafe and inaccessible, fuel is not arriving, fleeing is not an option, and food is simply running out. The 800,000 people in the city of Taiz in south-western Yemen are largely isolated, with all roads leading in and out blocked for the past three days. Taiz was already struggling for food before full-scale war returned to Yemen, and the UN has warned that wheat and flour could now run out in less than three weeks. Speaking to The National , an aid worker in the suburbs who tracks violations by the Houthi rebels and Yemeni government forces said people were unable to flee. “People cannot leave. They are afraid, even of speaking,” he said. “Whatever little does manage to enter is being taken over by bandits.” As supplies dwindle, prices have skyrocketed. Saeed Saif, a co-ordinator for Taiz and Yemen's west coast with the UN Population Fund, said traders had “hiked up prices” during the crisis. “Food prices have gone up by more than 50 per cent since the escalation,” he told The National from Aden. The UN and other international organisations have pulled staff out of the province due to security risks. Mr Saif was in Taiz until September 18. People have been asking family and friends outside the city for help. But some of these requests cannot be met, and the situation is only becoming more desperate. “We had sent some fuel to people who needed it two weeks ago. It still hasn't arrived because of the siege,” one source said. Taiz is the third-most populous city in Yemen. It has remained largely under government control until the Houthis began waging battles in recent weeks, aiming to capture the city and the wider province. Victory would pave the way for the rebels to seize areas further south, towards the government's interim capital in Aden, and expand their already substantial territory. Taiz province is also home to the Kahboub Mountains , over which the two sides have been fighting. The mountain range overlooks roads leading to the Bab Al Mandeb strait, where Houthi threats could disrupt up to 15 per cent of global shipping. The World Food Programme warned that the situation could quickly turn into a “humanitarian catastrophe” if aid continues to be blocked. In the suburbs where the Houthis are in control, there is slightly more access to supplies, but witnesses say the situation is complicated in different ways. “As a woman, it's not safe. I can't even go to the souq without facing issues,” another aid worker told The National . “Someone told me that she was harassed with her daughters by the militias. This is becoming increasingly problematic.” The National could not independently confirm the source's claims. Overall, the sentiment seems to be one of desperation, fear and isolation. Mr Saif said that many Yemenis feel “let down” by aid organisations that were supposed to, but are unable to, help them. “People lost trust. They make us feel like we disappointed them. I felt guilty (leaving).” Others have simply given up. They feel that being displaced several times as front lines change is no longer viable, sometimes because they can't afford the move. Most people are terrified, Mr Saif said. “They need immediate psychological support.” One of the many fears is that the fighting will be protracted, as the battle for control continues.

title: GFA and Sports Ministry must not rush Black Stars head coach appointment – Nana Fitz
body: Veteran football administrator Fitzgerald Barkers Woode has cautioned the Ghana Football Association (GFA) against rushing the appointment of a new head coach for the Black Stars. His advice comes following Carlos Queiroz’s mutual exit after Ghana’s humiliating start to the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifiers. The Black Stars suffered a 2–0 defeat to Côte d’Ivoire in Bouaké, followed by a disappointing 4–2 loss to The Gambia on home soil. Following Queiroz’s departure, the GFA and the Ministry of Youth and Sports established a five-member search committee to evaluate, interview, and shortlist potential candidates for the vacant post. The GFA set October 15 as the deadline for applications. Ghana is scheduled to face Somalia in a back-to-back qualifier this November at the Accra Sports Stadium. An interim technical crew is expected to manage the team through those fixtures before a substantive manager is formally appointed. Speaking to Graphic Sports, Barkers Woode popularly known as Nana Fitz urged the football authorities to remain patient during the hiring process despite the mounting pressure to turn the team’s form around. Nana Fitz stressed that the next head coach must possess a deep understanding of Ghanaian football, its unique challenges, and the cultural context surrounding the national team. According to him, the GFA needs to appoint someone who truly recognizes our local football environment, the country’s footballing philosophy, and the realities of the resources available. Nana Fitz noted that such insight would help the new coach adapt swiftly and deliver the expected results. The Black Stars currently sit at the bottom of Group C without a point.

title: Bishkek Metro Plans Resurface Despite High Costs and Low Demand
body: Bishkek is once again talking about building a metro, despite an assessment by the Kyrgyz capital’s own planners that it would attract too few passengers and cost roughly ten times as much as a tram network. Officials have now raised it with French and European development partners. Plans for the new transport systems were discussed on October 9 by Bishkek First Deputy Mayor Kubanychbek Imanaliev, French Ambassador Nicolas Faye, and representatives of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development. The French side expressed its willingness to help finance a feasibility study. Alexander Baranov, one of the developers of the city’s master plan through 2050, said in December 2025 that a tram network would be much quicker to build and better suited to the city’s passenger volumes . Mayor Aibek Dzhunushaliev said on October 2 that the city would consider building a metro if a viable project and investors emerged. Meanwhile, Bishkek is still struggling to provide enough buses. The mayor said on October 12 that the 1,600 buses purchased earlier were insufficient and that the fleet needs to expand to approximately 2,500. Bishkek’s master plan through 2050, approved earlier this year, includes tram lines and a bus rapid transit (BRT) system, using dedicated bus lanes and specially equipped stops. This approach can carry more passengers and reduce travel times without requiring underground tunnels. The proposed tram network would connect several districts of the capital. A BRT line could link parts of the city with Manas International Airport. No construction timetable has been established. According to official estimates, the city’s road network was originally designed for approximately 50,000 vehicles. Today, around 468,000 vehicles are registered in the capital, while as many as 700,000 use its streets daily when traffic from the suburbs and neighboring regions is included. Nearly 80% of Bishkek’s registered cars were more than 15 years old, according to figures published by Kyrgyzstan’s Ministry of Natural Resources, Ecology, and Technical Supervision in 2025. A World Bank study identified transport as one of the city’s main pollution sources, accounting for approximately 27% of annual fine particulate matter (PM2.5) concentrations. Bishkek regularly experiences severe smog, particularly in winter, when vehicle emissions are compounded by pollution from residential heating and other sources. Authorities previously proposed prioritizing public transportation and gradually reducing the use of private cars.

title: Ankara Kids Fashion Show: How ShakaraSquare Celebrated African Prints and Young Talent in Lagos
body: Lagos came alive with a burst of colour, and runway swagger on Saturday, October 10, as ShakaraSquare hosted the much-anticipated Ankara Kids Fashion Show. Convened by Ijeoma Ude, founder of ShakaraSquare.ng, the event transformed the runway into a joyful celebration of African heritage, where young runway stars, leading fashion houses, and proud parents gathered for an unforgettable afternoon of style and culture. From the moment the show kicked off, the energy in the room was electric. High-energy dance routines by talented kids’ dance troupes and soulful song performances set the stage, paving the way for the main highlight: the young trendsetters themselves. Aged between five and twelve, the mini models owned the catwalk with the poise and confidence of seasoned professionals. Walking majestically in custom-cut African print ensembles, the kids captivated the audience as they showcased a wide array of contemporary Ankara designs, ranging from structured regal attire to playful, modern street style. Speaking on the inspiration behind the showcase, convener Ijeoma Ude emphasized that the initiative goes far deeper than simply wearing pretty clothes. “The Ankara Kids Fashion Show is about giving the next generation a platform to build unshakeable self-confidence, express their creativity, and wear their cultural identity with pride,” Ude shared. Expressing deep gratitude during her official address, Ude extended warm thanks to the corporate sponsors and creative minds whose support brought the vision to life. “An ambitious event of this scale is only possible when you have partners who truly believe in nurturing young talent and preserving our culture,” Ude noted. “I am profoundly grateful to our corporate sponsors, government bodies, and brand partners for believing in this vision and investing in our children’s future. “To our brilliant designers, thank you for your craftsmanship, patience, and tireless dedication. You didn’t just stitch clothes; you created masterpieces that made these children feel like royalty on that stage.” Ude also praised the hands-on dedication of participating mothers and guardians, whose active support during auditions and fitting sessions proved instrumental to the show’s success. The runway featured vibrant collections from seven standout fashion houses, including U-JAY Fashion, Prime Start Apparel Concept, Rose & Michell, RA-Jaz Clothiers, DE LOOK, BY CANDY Luxury Costumes, and Kingstrybe. Complete with tailored styling, bespoke accessories, and professional makeup, each brand delivered a polished presentation that proved high fashion isn’t just for adults. The cultural extravaganza drew major backing from corporate giants and government institutions alike, with support from Kellogg’s, Zenith Bank Plc, Mikano International Limited, Amuwo Odofin Local Government, Lagos State Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture, Wendy’s Cold, Paddysco Sports Limited, and Stylenest Hair & Beauty. More than just a fashion presentation, the ShakaraSquare Ankara Kids Fashion Show delivered an uplifting, wholesome cultural experience—leaving parents, fashion lovers, and supporters inspired by the incredible potential of Nigeria’s youngest creatives.

title: Houthis Claim Attack On Saudi Oil Giant Aramco, Threaten To Carry Out More Attacks
body: Yemen’s Houthis on Wednesday said they had targeted facilities belonging to Saudi Aramco, after Saudi officials reported a strike on a building in an area housing the energy giant’s operations centre. Meanwhile, powerful explosions rattled the Saudi capital, as the coalition fighting the Houthis said it had intercepted a missile fired by the Iran-backed group towards Riyadh. Saudi Arabia, the world’s top crude oil exporter, has in recent days come under sustained attack in a dramatic escalation in the war with the Houthis. It has hit back with strikes against the group’s stronghold in the Yemeni capital Sanaa, which for years has been under their grip. An air traffic control tower is seen at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on September 19, 2026. Photo by – / AFP Yahya Saree, Houthi military spokesman, said their forces had conducted “a high-quality military operation targeting Aramco in Dhahran” as well as strikes targeting Riyadh airport and a refinery in the capital. “This was carried out using a large number of ballistic missiles, cruise missiles and drones,” he said, adding that “operations toward Saudi depths will continue in the coming days, targeting Saudi enemy airports and oil facilities”. Earlier, a Saudi energy ministry official said a building belonging to Aramco in Dhahran was struck, resulting in a “limited fire” but “no casualties or fatalities”. Dhahran is home to Aramco’s headquarters, a vast complex comprising numerous buildings and residential compounds. According to two company employees who spoke to AFP on condition of anonymity, a tower in the headquarters was hit overnight. “Top three floors have gone,” said one of the employees. A second source briefed on the matter confirmed the strike and that the building was hit. AFP has not been granted access to the site and was not able to independently verify the degree of damage. ‘We Heard An Explosion’ Most strikes on Saudi Arabia have targeted infrastructure on the outskirts of the capital, but the barrages appear to be getting closer to the city centre. In the city’s downtown, residents have been seen parking their cars to stop and look up at the sky, an AFP journalist said. On Tuesday night, the white plumes of air defence missiles could be seen streaking across the sky followed by explosions. Passengers walk across the Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka on October 12, 2026, as Saudi Arabia-bound flights remain cancelled a day after a Houthi strike at Riyadh’s international airport. Photo by PIYAS BISWAS / AFP While walking down a major avenue, a witness told AFP he “saw a projectile cutting across the sky” above a mall, saying it left “a yellowish trail of light followed by a trail of smoke. Then, we heard an explosion”. “People were calm; no one was speaking. We were scared and all looking up at the sky,” he added, requesting anonymity. More blasts were heard on Wednesday, AFP journalists in Riyadh reported, as messages were received on phones warning of an “aerial threat” and urging people to take shelter. The alert was lifted a few minutes later. Strikes On Yemen The Saudi-led coalition meanwhile struck oil sites across western Yemen, with spokesman Turki Al-Malki saying the attacks targeted facilities used to supply the Houthis’ effort to “threaten the kingdom, Yemen, the southern Red Sea and waterways”. An AFP correspondent in Sanaa reported an explosion, while a breaking news alert on the Houthi-affiliated Al-Masirah TV channel said “Saudi aggression” targeted an oil firm. The coalition has supported Yemen’s government militarily against the Houthis since 2015 in a long-running civil war that has created a humanitarian crisis. Many civilians in the Houthi-controlled Yemeni capital, fearing shortages, have rushed to queue in front of fuel stations, an AFP journalist said. Renewed Threats The latest escalation follows a strike on Riyadh’s international airport on Saturday that left 13 people dead in the worst attack on the kingdom since 2015. Saudi Arabia-bound passengers remain stranded at the Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka on October 12, 2026, after their flights were cancelled a day after a Houthi strike at Riyadh’s international airport. Photo by PIYAS BISWAS / AFP The Saudi cabinet vowed in a meeting led by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman that it “will not allow its security or freedom of navigation in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandeb Strait to be threatened”. Many countries have issued travel warnings to their citizens in Saudi Arabia, with France telling its nationals on Tuesday to avoid Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam airports. Traffic in perennially gridlocked Riyadh was noticeably lighter this week as remote learning for all schools and work-from-home orders for some companies took effect, according to AFP journalists. Saudi Arabia faces a major economic contraction this year, with GDP expected to shrink 3.3 percent, the International Monetary Fund said on Tuesday, predicting a regional drop over Iran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. The kingdom was already facing headwinds from Iran’s chokehold on Hormuz since the start of the Middle East war in February, when the United States and Israel attacked Iran. But the restart in July of Yemen’s frozen war has further roiled the kingdom and brought the fight to its own soil. Houthi attacks have also targeted oil tankers in the Red Sea — Saudi Arabia’s alternative export route. title: Russia received no requests to mediate conflict in southern Arabian Peninsula — MFA
body:
MOSCOW, October 14. /TASS/. Russia has not yet received any appeals to mediate a settlement of the conflict in the southern Arabian Peninsula, Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Georgy Borisenko told reporters.
"We have not received any specific requests for mediation so far. However, we remain in contact with our Saudi friends and, as I have already said, have also conveyed to representatives of the Ansar Allah movement the message that strikes against civilian infrastructure are unacceptable," Borisenko said.

title: President Zelensky arrives in the UK
body:
The head of state announced this on Facebook , according to Ukrinform.
“Already in the UK together with my team. Today, I will have an audience with His Majesty King Charles III. There will also be an important meeting with Prime Minister Andy Burnham. We will discuss a wide range of security issues. We are preparing decisions that will strengthen us. I thank the King, the Prime Minister, and all of Britain for their support!” Zelensky said.
Earlier, President’s Spokesperson Serhii Nykyforov confirmed that the President flew to the UK from the Polish city of Rzeszów. This was the first such departure since June, when Polish President Karol Nawrocki stripped Zelensky of the Order of the White Eagle over the naming of a military unit after UPA heroes.
Zelensky’s previous visit to the UK took place on July 27.
On October 14, the British government announced that it would accelerate deliveries to Ukraine of British-made Lightweight Multirole Missiles (LMM), which have proven highly effective against jet-powered drones.
