title: Father set to be sentenced in New York for the murder of 9-year-old Montreal girl
body:
A Montreal man has been sentenced to life in prison for killing his nine-year-old daughter and leaving her in a marsh in rural New York.
The sentence comes two months after a jury in Essex County Court convicted Luciano Frattolin of second degree murder and concealment of a human corpse in the death of Melina Frattolin.
Judge Tatiana Coffinger delivered the sentence after rejecting a defence motion to set aside the guilty verdict.
“I hope, at some point in your life, you realize what you have done,” Coffinger said in court.
Frattolin would not be eligible for parole before 25 years and is expected to serve his sentence in New York.
The defence issued a notice of appeal following the sentence.
The girl had been living in Montreal with her mother and had gone on a road trip to the U.S. with her father in July 2025. On the night they were scheduled to return home, Luciano Frattolin called 911, reporting she had been kidnapped after he had stopped the car he was driving on the side of the road.
“Mr. Frattolin, you live in a world of self-made delusion of wealth and image,” Coffinger said. “When the greatest accomplishment of your life would have been to be a great father, that is not what you are going to be remembered for.”
The girl’s family and other loved ones watched the sentencing from the back of the courtroom and some wiped their eyes after hearing the judge’s ruling.
“We continue to suffer deeply since the day Melina was brutally murdered,” the family said in a statement read outside the courthouse by District Attorney Michael Langey. “Nothing can bring Melina back, but we are relieved that this chapter is over. We are sincerely grateful to everyone who worked on the case. Your dedication and persistence, your efforts helped bring a measure of justice for our family.”
During the three-week-long trial, the defence tried to argue that local police had not adequately investigated Frattolin’s claims that his daughter was kidnapped.
The prosecution called several police officers and experts over the trial who used car location data, cellphone data and surveillance camera footage to recreate Frattolin’s movements on the day his daughter died and prove his story was false.
“The community of Montreal, the school (and) teachers all felt a great loss from the defendant’s selfish actions,” Langey told the court before Coffinger delivered her sentence.
The jury spent an hour deliberating on Aug. 10 at the end of the trial, before concluding that Frattolin was guilty.

title: Canada-Based Doctor Equip, Renovates Health Centre in Anambra
body: A Canada-based medical doctor, Dr Charles Kene Ojukwu, has donated medical equipment to the Primary Health Centre at Christ the King Parish, Abatete, Anambra State, to support maternal and newborn healthcare. The equipment was blessed by the Archbishop of Onitsha and Metropolitan of the Onitsha Ecclesiastical Province, Most Rev. Valerian Maduka Okeke, on October 11. The donation was made through the Charles Kene Ojukwu Initiative Foundation. The items include an autoclave machine, suction machine, cardiac monitor, oxygen cylinder with trolley, delivery bed, digital fetal Doppler, nebuliser machine, diagnostic ultrasound machine and phototherapy machine. Other items include labour and minor surgical equipment. The health centre was also repainted as part of the intervention. The donation is intended to improve access to essential maternal and newborn healthcare services at the facility. According to the donor, the equipment will enable pregnant women to access ultrasound scans at the centre and help healthcare workers provide phototherapy for newborns with jaundice. The nebuliser and suction machines are expected to support emergency interventions, while the autoclave will facilitate the sterilisation of medical instruments. The delivery and minor surgical equipment will also assist midwives in carrying out procedures, including suturing lacerations and episiotomies. The initiative is aimed at strengthening healthcare delivery and contributing to efforts to reduce maternal and child mortality in Abatete and neighbouring communities.

title: Iran executes monarchist accused of supporting Israel, Reza Pahlavi
body: Iran executed mountaineer and musician Ali Sina Mostafavi, 38, on Wednesday, according to state sources, continuing the Islamic Republic's use of executions as punishment against protesters. The judiciary said he carried out armed attacks during the six-week war with Israel and the United States earlier this year, supported exiled Crown Prince Reza Pahlavi, and maintained links with Israel.Mostafavi, from Bam in Kerman province, was executed after the Supreme Court upheld a death sentence handed down by a Revolutionary Court in Kerman, the judiciary-affiliated Mizan news agency reported.Human rights groups had warned less than 24 hours earlier that he had been moved to solitary confinement and his family summoned for a final visit. Pahlavi's communications team then issued an urgent appeal, saying he had been tortured into confessing and convicted in a sham trial.Mizan said Mostafavi carried out a series of shootings in Kerman during the war, which Iranian authorities call the Ramadan War. It said he opened fire in Azadi Square on March 24, wounding a civilian and a young girl. On April 21, it said, he fired at conscript soldiers and passing vehicles, injuring several people. It also accused him of two failed shooting attempts targeting police on the Kerman-Mahan road.Authorities said a search of his hideout turned up a scoped Brno rifle, two shotguns, 246 rounds of ammunition and 30 Molotov cocktails.The judiciary also said Mostafavi sent photographs and videos of sites struck during the war to Persian-language opposition media abroad. It said he expressed willingness to carry out an operation at Kerman airport. According to the authorities, messages on his phone included exchanges with Persian-language broadcasters and messages to Israel's official Persian-language account.Mizan said he took part in the nationwide protests that began in December 2025 and continued into January, and sent footage of the unrest to media outside Iran.The judiciary said the case was heard with a defense lawyer present. It said the conviction rested on investigative findings, security reports, and Mostafavi's confessions. The public account did not include the defense's arguments or independently verifiable evidence. Iranian authorities have not released evidence that he acted under the direction of Pahlavi or Israeli officials, while human rights groups have raised concerns about his treatment in detention and the circumstances of his conviction.'A political prisoner and young athlete'Pahlavi's team described him as “a political prisoner and young athlete” in “immediate danger of execution.” The account said in Persian that he was a patriotic mountaineer and alleged his conviction followed “forced confessions under torture” and a “show trial.” The League for the Defense of Human Rights in Iran said armed security officers arrested Mostafavi at his home in the early hours of April 25. The group alleged he was beaten during the arrest.Branch 1 of the Kerman Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Hadi Aghaei, sentenced him to death on charges including moharebeh, or waging war against God, acting against national security, and gathering and colluding. Branch 41 of the Supreme Court upheld the sentence on September 28, according to human rights reports.On Tuesday, rights groups reported his transfer to solitary confinement at Kerman prison.Iran sees sharp rise in the use of the death penaltyBefore his arrest, Mostafavi was an experienced mountaineer. IranWire and Human Rights for Sports said he climbed Island Peak in Nepal and attempted Ama Dablam, reaching about 6,600 meters. Records in Kerman mountaineering club archives show he joined a 2016 expedition to Alam-Kuh, one of Iran's highest mountains. Human rights reports also describe him as a musician.The execution follows a sharp rise in the use of the death penalty against people accused of involvement in the January protests, opposition activity and war-related security offenses.On Tuesday, Amnesty International condemned the executions of five men between September 30 and October 5 who had been convicted in connection with the January uprising. “The arbitrary executions of these five young men serves as another chilling reminder of how the Iranian authorities weaponize the death penalty to render the cost of dissent so high that it terrorizes the population into silence,” said Diana Eltahawy, the group's deputy regional director for the Middle East and North Africa.

title: Show HN: Busymail – an IMAP email client with an MCP server for AI agents
body:
Busymail connects to your Gmail, Yahoo, or any IMAP server Busymail can reach, and surfaces the few things that need you - the reply, the bill, the flight . Give an AI client a token and it can work the same mailbox: read it, tidy it, draft mail. Nothing it writes sends until you approve it.
Works with Gmail, Yahoo, Fastmail, or any public IMAP server on port 993 with an app password. Microsoft 365 and Outlook cannot connect yet.
Grouped by what it is, with the dates, amounts and actions pulled out of the mail.
It drafts the message; the send waits here until you approve it, with every recipient and attachment spelled out .
Free for 14 days, no card. Then $15 a month plus VAT or sales tax where it applies. The trial covers one mailbox; the plan covers every mailbox you connect.
Busymail sorts every message into groups - finance, travel, code, security, personal and the rest - and pulls the dates, amounts and actions out of the mail, so you can see what a thread wants without opening it. Nothing is deleted and nothing is hidden. When something changes, it comes back up.
Search, pins, an archive that really archives, and apps for macOS, Windows, Linux and Android.
Once you have an account, you create a token in Settings and point an AI client at your mailbox. You choose what it may do , and you can revoke it in one click. It is not a mailbox you move to - you keep your accounts where they are.
Your feed, any conversation in full, your sent mail, what is inside a file attached to it, and search across all of it.
Archive, unarchive, pin and unpin. Archiving really moves the mail out of your inbox on your mail server, so it changes what you see in every other mail app too.
A reply, or a new message to anyone. It writes, and the message waits for you. It can attach files too.
No token can change your settings, your password or your two-factor, add or remove an email account, or create and revoke tokens. Those stay with you. How to connect a client →
A token can never send mail. When an assistant writes a message, it waits under Approvals until you approve or reject it - the recipients, the subject, the body, and every attachment named and sized. Approving happens while you are signed in, so the token that wrote a message cannot approve it.
It gets flagged, Approve stops being the filled button, and Reject takes the warning outline. The domain of every recipient is spelled out, because that is the part the eye skips.
The queue updates itself without a refresh, and the notifications that tell you about new mail tell you an approval is waiting too.
A message nobody decides on is discarded after a week, and nothing reaches the recipients in the meantime.
Add your email with an app password. Gmail and Yahoo have step-by-step instructions, and any other provider works when its mail server is on the public internet, reachable over TLS on port 993, and still issues app passwords. A server on port 143, one only reachable on your own network, or a provider that has closed the password path cannot be added. Google only creates an app password once 2-Step Verification is on, and the form walks you through turning it on first. Microsoft 365 and Outlook accounts cannot be connected: they need an OAuth sign-in Busymail does not have.
An AI pulls out the dates, amounts, and actions hiding in your mail. Reading changes nothing - your mail stays exactly where it is.
Grouped, ranked, and quietly resurfaced when things change. Nothing is deleted, nothing hidden.
Your credentials are encrypted , and your data is stored in the EU (Amsterdam).
Busymail never sells your data , and never uses it to train AI.
To find signals, your email is processed by a third-party AI under zero data retention - never stored there, never used to train models. Read the details .
Give an AI client a token and it can read your mail - your feed, conversations and searches. Only if you choose to, and only until you revoke it.
You can let it tidy up too, and archiving really moves the mail - out of your inbox into your archive folder on your own mail server, so it changes what you see in Apple Mail as well.
You can let it draft mail too, and it still cannot send - anything it writes waits for you to approve or reject it here first.
Revoke access whenever you like , in one click.
Free for 14 days, no card. Then $15 a month plus VAT or sales tax where it applies. If it turns out not to be for you, ask within 14 days of your first payment and you get it back, no questions asked.

title: Kyiv Mayor Faces Questioning as Russian Attack Triggers Fresh Water Cuts
body:
Kyiv is experiencing water supply issues once more on Wednesday after another Russian attack on Ukraine’s energy grid.
The attack, comprising ballistic missiles, hit Kyiv’s CHP-4 power plant and a nine-story residential building, killing at least three and injuring 26.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
The Kyiv City State Administration reported reduced water pressure in multiple districts as a result of the attack, with reduced voltage preventing the pumps from operating normally.
“Due to the power outage of some water supply facilities in the capital, the pumping equipment was stopped in an emergency,” it wrote in a statement , adding that restoration work is ongoing.
According to the agency, the upper half of the Pecherskyi district has no water, while the lower part has reduced pressure. The Solomyansky and Shevchenkivskyi districts also suffer from reduced pressure.
State media Ukrinform noted that Kyivvodfond, a municipal water-management firm, has developed an online map of available manual water pumps around Kyiv.
In October, the capital reported multiple water outages caused by Russian attacks, two months ahead of the cold spell. Most Ukrainians interviewed by Kyiv Post on Tuesday named water disruptions as their top concern for the upcoming winter, as signs of an energy truce touted by Washington remain elusive, with Ukraine’s energy grid not included.
Kyiv also said it was not warned by its allies for the first wave of ballistic missile strikes amid rumors of a US intelligence cutoff .
Kyiv authorities urged locals to stock up on food and water on Sunday, Oct. 11, after a Russian attack left over half of Kyiv’s households without running water.
On Wednesday, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko was summoned to the Verkhovna Rada to answer questions about the city’s readiness for Russian attacks on power facilities.
The session is ongoing at the time of publication, and it was preceded by President Volodymyr Zelensky’s criticism of Kyiv’s response to the impending energy crisis, arguing that the capital trails behind other regions in preparedness.
However, Klitschko has defended the city’s preparedness , noting that progress is being made through backup systems despite limited funding, as facilities can’t be fully shielded without adequate air defense.
The standoff is also part of a longstanding animosity between the two that predates Russia’s full-scale invasion.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Sikorsky Aiming For Black Hawk ‘Nose Jobs’ To Be Available Within The Next Year
body: Sikorsky is aiming to start offering a new modular and readily swappable nose for the venerable H-60 family of helicopters within the next year or so. The noses will be made available on new-production H-60s, as well as be retrofittable to helicopters in service now. The ‘nose jobs’ will help operators relatively quickly reconfigure their H-60s for very different missions, from cargo-carrying to serving as gunships , as required. It also opens new avenues to integrating autonomous capabilities and other advanced functionality. Our Howard Altman had a chance to speak with representatives from Sikorsky, now a subsidiary of Lockheed Martin, about the plans for the new nose for the H-60-series at the Association of the U.S. Army’s (AUSA) main annual convention today. This is part of a larger vision for keeping the design operationally relevant into the 2070s, which also includes uprated engines and increased total payload capacity. You can read more about the overall Black Hawk 2070 strategy here . Of the different elements of Black Hawk 2070, “the nose is a good one, and it’s one that’s on a pretty accelerated timeline. Within the next, I would say, year or so, the nose will be available to be retrofitted or to be coming off the line,” Jason Wrigley, Sikorsky’s director of business development for Black Hawk, said. “We’ve gone through a design cycle with it.” As it stands now, the new nose structure will offer roughly double the physical space of the standard nose on current-generation H-60s today. “We’ve done the design. We then 3D-printed the noses, and we did that so that we can physically interact with it, because the whole point of this is for maintainability and access to be able to integrate these different sensors and comms gear,” he continued. “We’ve gotten some feedback from the engineers, from operators, from maintainers, and that goes back into the next cycle of the design.” Exploring ways to optimize accessibility to areas of the new nose was a major focus of this ‘test print,’ according to Wrigley. Sikorsky has a scale model on the show floor at AUSA this week that highlights how the current design opens from the top, as seen below. Ensuring that it will be possible to keep any systems inside sufficiently cooled has also been an important design consideration already. Jamie Hunter Overall, “we just are kind of confirming, can we reach everywhere we need to? What are the different configurations?” he added. There’s been “a lot of work with the [U.S.] Army around what do you envision potentially could go in here?” “This is one of those cases also where our whole engineering team gets more comfortable. It’s not something where the Army came to us and said, ‘this is exactly what I want. Here’s my spec,'” he also noted. “It was more, ‘here’s what I want to achieve. Here’s what I want to be able to do.’ And so we went off and designed that.” Another look at the long-nosed Black Hawk model on display at AUSA. Jamie Hunter “I like to highlight this, because it’s part of the way we’re also changing the way we design and deliver the Blackhawk,” Wrigley added as an aside. “So we’re very much in a model-based environment.” While Wrigley mentioned sensors and communications equipment as possible payloads to fit into that extra space initially when talking with us today, he made clear later on that these are just some of the potential options. “It’s using the old term, but it’s open architecture, and so the whole point is whatever the mission requires” can go into these new extended noses, he explained. “There’s always a demand for real estate up front.” It’s very true that more specialized variants of the H-60, such as the MH-60s operated by the U.S. Army’s elite 160th Special Operations Aviation Regiment , often have modified noses loaded with radars, other sensors , and additional systems. The new HH-60W Jolly Green II rescue helicopters for the U.S. Air Force are another prime example of this, and there are many more . A head-on look at one of the 160th Special Operations Aviation Regiment’s MH-60s, with a nose absolutely crammed with sensors and other systems. USN A look at the distinctive nose on the HH-60W Jolly Green II packed with sensors and other gear. USAF “There’s a big focus on open architecture and that ability to quickly plug-and-play,” Wrigley also told TWZ earlier this month in the context of the larger Black Hawk 2070 plan. “The new modular nose will change the look of the Black Hawk up front to provide even more space for equipment that will work directly with the new digital architecture.” In terms of swapping out modular noses on individual helicopters, Wrigley said that it is still too early in the design process to know exactly how that would be done and how long it might take to do so in practice. “Part of the design process is to also write up the documentation for the retrofit, but we don’t see this one as very invasive,” he explained. It is not hard to imagine use cases for long-nosed H-60s, especially ones that can then be reconfigured between missions, and not just for the U.S. Army. As Wrigley already underscored, there is long-standing demand for H-60s with longer and larger noses to accommodate additional mission systems. Modular noses, in general, have been becoming more and more common in aviation design for some time now. The ability to readily swap modular noses could also allow operators of even relatively small H-60 fleets to gain a valuable new degree of multi-mission capability. As one example, cargo-carrying helicopters could be converted into gunships, and back again, as required, using a small common pool of noses with the requisite sensors, laser designators, and other equipment. All of this could offer cost benefits when it comes to sustainment and logistics, as well as added operational flexibility. The long-nosed Black Hawk model on display at AUSA is notably configured as a gunship. Sikorsky has also talked previously about leveraging the new nose to reconfigure H-60s for search and rescue, airborne drone control, and other missions. A full view of the model of the gunship-configured H-60 with the new modular nose on display at AUSA. Jamie Hunter Just being able to install a radar for one series of missions, and then quickly switch over to an electro-optical wide-area surveillance system or another kind of sensor for the next run of sorties, would bring new adaptability to the already very flexible Black Hawk. Defensive systems could also be readily swapped from aircraft to aircraft, as well as more quickly upgraded, as needed. The modular nose also opens the door to a new way to integrate advanced capabilities, including autonomy packages, which Wrigley said is also driving demand for more space at the front end of the helicopter. Sikorsky has been developing various tiers of autonomous capabilities for the H-60 family for years now, including artificial intelligence-driven ‘copilots’ designed just to help reduce the workload of human crew members and increase safety margins. Autonomous flight capabilities require additional sensors, such as LIDAR and cameras, to help with navigation and to provide additional situational awareness. At least some of those components could be hosted within new modular noses. At the same time, integrating higher degrees of autonomy could require more substantial modification. Sikorsky is now developing a fully uncrewed version of the H-60, and has been doing so with an eye toward converting older Black Hawks to this configuration as they are retired from service, as you can read more about here . In line with the Black Hawk 2070 vision, the modular noses could be part of a broader equation for modernizing existing H-60 fleets, as well. “In our conversations with the Army, I think they’ve been using a phrase that they call targeted modernization,” Wrigley told us, speaking more generally. “There’s a daunting task that says there’s 1,000-1,500 Black Hawks in inventory. If you literally tried to upgrade every one of them, it’s a very expensive proposition, and it probably takes a long time.” “I don’t think that’s the way they’re thinking about it. I think they’re thinking about it more on a battalion basis or a unit basis,” he continued. “Like, what’s the mission, and maybe certain Black Hawks get upgraded with autonomy, and other Black Hawks get upgraded with sort of the expanded launched effects capability, the engine, the structural upgrades, the [stub] wings, stuff like that.” “Maybe some of them become ‘Superhawks’ or whatever, [and] get the whole package,” he added. There is certainly still work to be done on the development of the new modular nose and then actually integrating it onto the H-60 platform. At the same time, Sikorsky clearly already sees demand for this new feature, which could lead to a breadth of new opportunities for new and old helicopters in the H-60 line. Contact the author: joe@twz.com The post Sikorsky Aiming For Black Hawk ‘Nose Jobs’ To Be Available Within The Next Year appeared first on TWZ .

title: Russian drone attack on western Ukraine kills 6, injures 20 in Lutsk, Rivne
body:
Russian drone attacks on cities in Ukraine's western Volyn and Rivne oblasts killed three people and injured 20 others on the morning of Oct. 14, regional authorities said.
Wreckage of a Russian drone fell on the western city of Lutsk in Volyn Oblast, killing six people and injuring 10 others, regional governor Roman Romaniuk said .
As a result of the wreckage falling, a large-scale fire broke out in the 'Eurogroup' warehouse, killing five people at the scene, and injuring a sixth person so heavily they succumbed in hospital, Romaniuk said. Ten more people were injured in the incident, he added.
Elsewhere in the city, wreckage damaged a nine-story residential building, injuring two people including a child.
In Rivne, a Russian drone crashed into the city, injuring 8 people, including a child born in 2012, according to the regional military administration . The attack also damaged the roofs of two residential buildings, several windows, and four cars, the administration added.
Since midnight, air raid alerts had been issued six times in Volyn Oblast, as Russia hammered Ukraine with ballistic missiles and drones.
In total, Zelensky said Russia struck Ukraine with 39 missiles including Iskander-M, KN-23, S-400, Zircon, and Onyx missiles from Kursk, Bryansk, Voronezh, and Rostov regions in Russia, as well as with 128 Shahed-type UAVs, including 77 jet-powered ones.
Ukraine's Air Force said it neutralized four ballistic missiles and 115 Russian drones overnight.
Russian attacks have struck several locations in western Ukraine, distant from the front line, over the past day.
On Oct. 13, a Russian drone struck a university building in the northwestern city of Rivne, in neighboring Rivne Oblast, injuring 25 people, Rivne's National Police branch said on Oct. 13.
In Lviv Oblast, Russian drone attacks injured three people over the past day, said regional governor Maksym Kozytskyi.

title: Lebanon's power failure: Diesel generators, $300-a-month bills - and a corrupt system milking the profits
body: Lebanon now relies on diesel-powered generators for about half of its electricity supply, further exposing the crisis-hit country to financial, environmental and operational risks, according to data for an upcoming report. Behind that alarming figure lies a deep-rooted crisis decades in the making. Interviews with officials, as well as government statistics, studies and testimonies gathered by The National reveal how a largely unregulated industry has been lining the pockets of high-ranking officials and neighbourhood generator owners alike. The electricity sector has been regarded as one of the most corrupt parts of Lebanon’s sectarian system of government since the end of the civil war in 1990. Those who benefit from the dysfunction have allegedly resisted efforts to repair the sector, preserving a system that lets them continue profiting from its failures. Figures being compiled by the Lebanese Centre for Energy Conservation for their upcoming report show that private generators accounted for 50 per cent of Lebanon’s electricity supply at the beginning of 2026, while Electricite du Liban, the state utility, provided only 31 per cent. EDL's share is likely to have shrunk even further over the summer, according to the LCEC, a national agency affiliated with the Energy Ministry. Meanwhile, the Lebanese people are left to foot the bill. The country's dependence on expensive diesel imports to run generators has sent energy bills rocketing in recent months amid rising global oil prices due to the Iran war, further straining households and businesses already struggling after years of economic crisis. Among a dozen people interviewed by The National , the median generator bill was $310 in August. Dependence on generators increased dramatically after a severe economic crisis began in 2019, driving the final nail in the coffin of the dilapidated electricity sector . As the bankrupt state struggled to secure fuel for its power plants, EDL production fell by nearly 80 per cent between 2018 and 2023, from 15.4TWh to 3.37TWh, according to a 2025 report by the LCEC. Over the same period, diesel-powered generators' share of Lebanon's electricity supply more than doubled, from 23.1 per cent to 51.5 per cent. Beirut’s roughly 9,300 generators have barely stopped their relentless humming since then, spewing polluting exhaust into the air and wrapping the capital in a yellowish smog, as they supply electricity to those who can afford it. “We can’t go on like this,” said Ayman, manager of a shawarma restaurant in Beirut’s vibrant Hamra neighbourhood, who gave only his first name. With state electricity available for only a few hours a day, and at unpredictable times, the restaurant is almost entirely reliant on a private generator, he said. The small restaurant’s electricity bill for August alone came to almost $20,000. “We’re losing money,” Ayman sighed. The usually bustling summer season, which he had been banking on to shore up the restaurant’s finances, proved disappointing. With the war between Hezbollah and Israel resuming in March, tourists and even Lebanese expatriates largely stayed away. “If nothing is done, we will have to close. And not just us, everyone else too,” said Ayman. While generator bills vary considerably from one area to another because of limited state oversight, data from New Energy Consult and The National 's interviews with residents show that monthly bills often exceed $300 – roughly equivalent to the entire monthly minimum wage of 28 million Lebanese pounds. By comparison, the average household electricity bill in the UK is about $95 a month for a medium-sized household of two to three people. In one neighbourhood of the capital, a 25-amp generator subscription cost as much as $750 in August, according to New Energy Consult, a consultancy founded by Lebanese energy expert Jessica Obeid. Ms Obeid said some generator operators had taken advantage of the global surge in oil prices to increase their profit margins. “The problem is that nobody has provided state electricity over the past three decades, and nobody has implemented any serious reforms,” she explained. “Generators eventually just reflect the failure of the state, the failure of policies and the failure of institutions. So it’s time for state institutions to stand up and do what they’re supposed to be doing: provide electricity.” 'Mass bribe system' People strolling along Hamra’s main street express their exasperation over soaring energy costs. “It’s insane,” said Karim Agha, 33, who recently returned from Dubai. He said his parents’ electricity bill reached $600 in August, three times what he used to pay in the Emirates. “I’m scared to look at the bill,” said Talal Fayed, a 67-year-old driver who paid a $300 generator bill in August. Asked what he expected from the Lebanese state, he sighed and replied with a faint smile: “What state?” Such vast sums flowing each month from consumers’ pockets into the private generator industry raise the question: why have the Lebanese authorities failed to implement energy reforms that would redirect that money to the state? Energy experts say vested interests and a lack of political will have prevented a transition towards cheaper, cleaner energy and locked the country into a dangerous dependence on generators. The diesel generator industry is lucrative: Ali Ahmad, a World Bank expert, estimated its value at around $3 billion in 2020, with roughly $1 billion going to the generator market and $2 billion to diesel importers. Opposition MP Paula Yacoubian said the generator “cartel” benefitted politically connected individuals and companies that had little incentive to give up their bread and butter. Generator owners are part of Lebanon’s clientelism networks, she argued, able to offer benefits such as forgiving unpaid bills in exchange for political support. “It's a mass bribe system,” she told The National. A systemic lack of investment and squandering of public funds have left Lebanon’s energy sector in shambles. About 40 per cent of electricity entering EDL's network is lost between technical distribution and commercial losses such as theft and illegal connections, according to a 2024 EDL report. With its battered financial sector and unstable security situation, Lebanon has struggled to attract foreign capital since 2019. But lack of investment in the energy sector is not new. The state has not built a major power plant in decades. Its newest large plants, Deir Ammar and Zahrani, date back to the late 1990s. “With $1 billion, you can build a 1,000MW power plant. It's nothing. People are already paying for it with their generator bills,” Ms Yacoubian said. EDL has about 3,000MW of nominal installed capacity, but in 2023 it supplied electricity equivalent to just 13 per cent of its theoretical maximum output. The country needs about 3,000MW of electricity to meet daily demand. Only two of Lebanon’s seven thermal power plants are operational, because the cash-strapped state cannot buy enough fuel and badly maintained infrastructure limits production. A 1,000MW plant operating at an 80 per cent capacity could produce about 7TWh annually, more than twice EDL’s total electricity supply in 2023, which stood at roughly 3.4TWh, according to LCEC. “This is not a technical problem,” Ms Yacoubian said. For over two decades, political bickering has stopped all major investment projects in Lebanon. “Power plants are routinely built everywhere else in the world. Anyone, my aunt Salma included, could bring electricity,” she said. “But there are no politically affiliated politicians who were able to do it in Lebanon.” Powerful oligopoly Energy Minister Joseph Saddi said he was well aware that the remedy to the country’s dependence on generators was in investment in electricity generation. “We are now engaging with the private sector,” he told The National . The Energy Ministry has given the International Finance Corporation, the private-sector arm of the World Bank, a mandate to secure the necessary private-sector investment. “There are investors who are interested, but they require a certain number of financial guarantees. So what we are focusing on now is how we can provide those guarantees,” Mr Saddi said. The IFC’s role is notably to act as the lead transaction adviser on a public-private partnership for a new 825MW combined-cycle gas turbine plant, a project that has been in the pipeline for years. Meanwhile, the World Bank has approved a $250 million loan to EDL to upgrade its infrastructure. Experts say that, even more than generator owners, diesel importers wield significant influence over policy decisions, thanks to their close connections with politicians. A 2022 investigation by Beirut-based research centre Triangle revealed direct links between several of Lebanon’s 13 licensed fuel-importing companies and current or former politicians. For energy expert Marc Ayoub, who has investigated the sector for years, Lebanon’s diesel importers form an oligopoly with far-reaching political connections. Rather than competing with one another, he said, they collaborate to maximise their margins, sharing the cost of vessels and associated shipping fees before dividing the imported quantities among themselves. They then sell the diesel, locally known as mazout, according to the price set by the Ministry of Energy, currently about $30 for 20 litres, which Mr Ayoub said allowed them to make comfortable margins. The tariff “contains a lot of hidden profits for importers, in addition to margins for distributors, lorry owners, petrol stations and everyone else involved”, he said. The Energy Ministry could reduce additional premiums it pays to importers, which he said could lower diesel tariffs by at least 15 per cent. But instead, he said, the state kept “protecting the interests of these private players”. There is also an issue on the generator side. While the Energy Ministry sets generator tariffs – which have risen by almost 60 per cent in six months – many operators do not comply with them, or even bother to install mandatory electricity meters. Instead, they charge residents a fixed monthly rate based on the amperage of their subscription, which determines how many appliances consumers can run at the same time. Despite occasional government crackdowns for overcharging customers and failing to install electricity meters, generator operators have largely been able to set prices at their discretion. One silver lining of the near-collapse of state electricity supply is that solar panels have soared in popularity, accounting for 19 per cent of electricity production in 2026, up from just 0.4 per cent in 2018, according to LCEC. None of the people interviewed by The National said they had installed solar panels. Mr Fayed, the taxi driver, said this would be the only way to move beyond dependency on generator owners and the state, neither of which he trusts. But, like many Lebanese living from pay cheque to pay cheque, he does not have the upfront capital to install solar panels. “Too expensive,” he sighed. With Lebanon experiencing one of the fastest-growing cancer rates in the world, experts have urged the country to move to cleaner sources of energy. According to a 2024 study led by scientists from the American University of Beirut, the level of carcinogenic pollutants from diesel generators in the capital's air has doubled since 2017, increasing the risk of developing cancer by 50 per cent. “It’s suffocating, it’s killing us, it’s loud, it’s expensive … And we know that it is all due to corruption,” Ms Yacoubian said. “I'm telling the Lebanese people to wake up – wake up, and smell the mazout.”

title: Nkrumah Showboy: Chief Moomen’s play to explore Ghana’s first President’s early years
body: Bambu Heritage Productions will preview Nkrumah Showboy: Part One: The Boy from Nkroful , a new theatre production exploring the early life of Ghana’s first President, Osagyefo Dr Kwame Nkrumah, in Accra on Friday, 16 October 2026. The production, written by celebrated Ghanaian poet and playwright Chief Moomen, will be staged at the National Theatre at 7.30 pm. It takes audiences beyond Nkrumah’s political leadership to explore the formative years, experiences and influences that helped shape the man who would lead Ghana to independence. Part One follows Nkrumah’s journey from his childhood in Nkroful through his education at Achimota and his subsequent experiences at Lincoln University and the University of Pennsylvania in the United States. Through music, drama and dance, the production offers audiences a closer look at a relatively less explored chapter in the life of one of Africa’s most consequential leaders. For Chief Moomen, the production represents a major creative undertaking and forms part of a broader effort to bring Ghana’s history to life through compelling cultural experiences. Nkrumah Showboy is also part of Bambu Heritage Productions’ wider historical storytelling initiative being developed ahead of Ghana’s 70th anniversary of independence in 2027. The initiative seeks to explore the country’s history, from ancient to modern times, through theatrical productions, publications and curated exhibitions. The production is expected to contribute to renewed public engagement with Ghana’s history, particularly among younger generations, by presenting the lives and experiences of historical figures through live performance. The first part of Nkrumah Showboy focuses on the early years of Nkrumah’s life, with a second instalment planned to explore his journey through the independence struggle, presidency, overthrow and exile. Bambu Heritage Productions has built a reputation for bringing African heritage stories to the stage, most notably through Mansa Musa and the Trail of Lost Gold , which has reached audiences in Ghana and internationally. The upcoming preview offers audiences an opportunity to experience the new production as Ghana prepares for the milestone anniversary in 2027. Event details Production: Nkrumah Showboy: Part One: The Boy from Nkroful Date: Friday, 16 October 2026 Time: 7.30 pm Venue: National Theatre, Accra Website: www.nkrumahshowboy.com

title: NASU: Nigerian Workers Deserve Living Wage, Not Minimum Wage
body: Onyebuchi Ezigbo in Abuja The Non-Academic Staff Union of Educational and Associated Institutions (NASU) has said Nigerian workers are seeking for wage increase that are in line with current economic reality. NASU President, Comrade Makolo Hassan, who spoke at the National Executive Council (NEC) meeting of NASU on Tuesday, said that the N70,000 national minimum wage has become a “slave wage”, insisting Nigerian workers deserve a living wage that guarantees dignity and survival. He said that apart from a living wage, the. university workers are demanding affordable electricity with universal metering, end to estimated billing, and fair tariff system, as well as decisive intervention in housing crisis through workers’ housing schemes and protection against unreasonable rent increases. Hassan said while the N70,000 minimum wage was a hard-won victory, prevailing economic realities have rendered it grossly inadequate. “With the increase in pump prices, astronomical rise in cost of food, transportation, housing, electricity, healthcare and other essential commodities, the current minimum wage has effectively become a slave wage that can no longer sustain Nigerian workers and their families,” he said. He therefore called on the Federal Government to immediately set in motion machinery for urgent review of the wage in line with cost of living, and institutionalise periodic wage reviews and cost-of-living adjustments. “Nigerian workers deserve not merely a minimum wage, but a living wage that guarantees decent living conditions and preserves purchasing power,” he said. The NASU president described as landmark achievement, the successful conclusion and signing of the Year 2026 FGN/NASU Agreements after negotiations that started since 2017. He said agreement for universities and inter-university centres was signed on June 29, 2026, while those for polytechnics and colleges of education were signed on September 3, 2026, commending the negotiating team for resilience. On cost of living crisis, Hassan said that government’s statistics on inflation improvements do not reflect reality in homes and markets. He noted that with food inflation at 20.31 per cent in July 2026, the Federal Government needs to provide urgent support for farmers, security for farming communities, storage and transport infrastructure and investment in domestic food production, He warned that nearly 35 million Nigerians could face acute food insecurity in 2026 lean season. On fuel subsidy removal, he said every increase in fuel cost quickly impacts on fares and food prices. Domestic refining, he said, must translate to measurable relief, not higher margins for operators, while government must expand affordable mass transportation and assess CNG interventions. He also demanded affordable electricity with universal metering, end to estimated billing, and fair tariff system, as well as decisive intervention in housing crisis through workers’ housing schemes and protection against unreasonable rent increases. Hassan rejected increasing casualisation of labour and exploitation of contract employment to deny workers job security and benefits, demanding equal pay for equal value and regularisation of casual workers. He reaffirmed collective bargaining and freedom of association as fundamental rights. On the economy, he said youth unemployment remains critical, with millions entering labour market yearly to meet casualisation. NASU demands national employment strategy anchored on apprenticeship and vocational education, and organising of informal sector workers. He decried de-industrialisation, noting that Monetary Policy Rate at 26.5 per cent creates high-cost credit hostile to manufacturing, demanding affordable developmental finance. He said GDP growth of 3.89 per cent in Q1 2026 means little if wages cannot feed families, insisting progress must be measured by decent jobs and living wages. Hassan lamented mass poverty, citing World Bank estimate that 63 per cent of Nigerians lived below poverty line in 2025, calling for progressive tax system where wealth is taxed, scrutiny of borrowing and debt servicing, and accountability for increased revenues to states. He also raised healthcare and education crisis, brain drain of doctors, nurses, academics and technicians due to poor conditions, demanding prompt payment of pensions and gratuities. On insecurity, he said banditry and kidnapping threaten decent work, insisting protection of farmers and rural workers must be national labour priority. He urged labour to set agenda for 2027 elections around jobs, living wages, public services and security, saying workers must assess every candidate on those standards. Earlier while declaring the event open, the Minister of Labour and Employment, Dr. Muhammad Dingyadi, said that the Federal Government is aware of challenges economic reforms pose for workers and is committed to cushioning their effects. He said that was why the administration implemented N70,000 minimum wage with unprecedented speed and continues engagement with labour to enhance purchasing power. “I assure you Ministry of Labour remains your partner. My doors are always open,” Dingyadi said, pledging to address legitimate demands through social dialogue and collective bargaining. He urged members to promote efficiency, accountability and high work ethics, commending NASU President, Dr. Makolo Hassan, and General Secretary, Prince Peters Adeyemi, for maintaining industrial peace. He commended NASU for maintaining industrial harmony and being antagonistic, noting that the union is expected to advance workers’ welfare through constructive engagement while safeguarding educational system stability.

title: The Download: faking blood and the future of batteries
body: This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. The US military’s race to make fake blood In February 2007, a US military helicopter carrying blood to a field hospital was shot down in Iraq, killing all seven crew members. The mission was a reminder of the risks of transporting blood, which has a limited shelf life and is often in short supply. Now, a $73 million DARPA effort aims to create shelf-stable versions of plasma, platelets, and red blood cells. The idea is to develop dried blood products that can be stored for long periods and deployed quickly on the battlefield. The project aims to have bags of dried blood products deployed in the field by 2029. But getting it all done will be tough, and researchers still have major questions about the safety and effectiveness of synthetic alternatives. Discover how the military hopes to make blood last longer . —Andrew Rosenblum This story is from the next issue of our print magazine. Subscribe now to get your hands on a copy as soon as it lands on Wednesday, October 21! 10 Climate Tech Companies to Watch: WeLion New Energy and its semi-solid-state batteries WeLion New Energy is one of MIT Technology Review’s 10 Climate Tech Companies to Watch 2026 , available exclusively to subscribers . WeLion New Energy is on a quest to make safer, better batteries. The Chinese company’s liquid-solid hybrid cells aim to pack more power into electric cars, boats and drones, potentially improving safety and offering greater energy density than lithium-ion batteries. In 2023, WeLion released a battery pack with EV-maker Nio that offered a range of over 1,000 kilometers. Now, the company is developing batteries with even higher energy density. But scaling up production and competing on cost remain major challenges. Explore WeLion’s push to make safer, higher-capacity batteries . —You Xiaoying Subscribers can now access the full 10 Climate Tech Companies to Watch , spanning everything from geothermal power plants to carbon dioxide batteries . MIT Technology Review Narrated: Weight-loss drugs show signs of slowing biological aging, say drugmakers Popular weight-loss drugs may do more than help people shed pounds. They might also slow the aging process. Drugmakers Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk say patients taking their GLP-1 drugs age less quickly, according to molecular “aging clocks” that track changes in DNA or levels of key proteins. The findings add to speculation that GLP-1 drugs could be acting on basic causes of aging and might be true longevity treatments. But how much can we read into these results? This is our latest story to become an MIT Technology Review Narrated podcast, which we publish each week on Spotify and Apple Podcasts . Just navigate to MIT Technology Review Narrated on either platform, and follow us to get all our new content as it’s released. The must-reads I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology. 1 The FBI has arrested an OpenAI engineer accused of snooping A Saudi national is accused of planting a covert recording device. ( Guardian ) + The camera-and-microphone tool sells online for $13.99. ( Gizmodo ) + It was allegedly discovered plugged into a TV’s USB port. ( Verge ) + He reportedly used chatbots to plan the covert recording. ( Wired $) + OpenAI says its AI models helped identify the employee. ( Reuters $) 2 Ukrainian drones have hit Russia’s largest data centre But Sberbank claims its systems and services were not disrupted. ( Reuters $) + Ukraine’s data center strikes have thrown Russia into turmoil. ( FT $) + But they haven’t stopped Russian bot farms from trolling. ( Verge ) + Europe has a drone-filled vision for future wars. ( MIT Technology Review ) 3 Weight-loss drugs are being tweaked to treat brain disorders New GLP-1 trials are targeting addiction and depression. ( Nature ) + But we’re still figuring out their side effects. ( MIT Technology Review ) 4 Tesla robotaxis have been accused of speeding in school zones US regulators are reviewing the claims. ( Verge ) + Tesla’s security features thwarted a federal tracking attempt. ( 404 Media ) 5 US defense startups are turning to Taiwan to build China-free drones At least 13 joint agreements have been signed since 2025. ( WSJ $) + Taiwan’s “silicon shield” could be weakening. ( MIT Technology Review ) 6 A war game exposed the risks of a solar geoengineering arms race Participants feuded over rules for dimming the sun. ( Wired $) + Geoengineering also faces practical challenges. ( MIT Technology Review ) 7 AI company Character.ai has filed for bankruptcy It’s been accused of stealing content and harming kids. ( CNBC ) + Disney has offered $20 million for its chatbot tech. ( Ars Technica ) + Its filings expose common issues with AI business models. ( 404 Media ) 8 Apple has a new smart-home lineup built around a revamped Siri HomeView pairs a 7-inch screen with face recognition. ( Guardian + While the Home Collection adds cameras, locks, and thermostats. ( Wired $) + Siri AI powers the experience, but still needs to prove its smarts. ( WSJ $) 9 Scientists have identified a new dinosaur in a century-old fossil Invictibellatrix amberina may be Europe’s first megaraptoran. ( New Scientist $) 10 SpaceX’s latest launch lit up the skies with a “space jellyfish” Rocket exhaust expanded into tentacles high in the atmosphere. ( WP $) Quote of the day “It is like a thumb on the scale that we haven’t really ever seen.” —Danielle Citron, a University of Virginia law professor, tells The Washington Post that Elon Musk’s ability to amplify conspiracy theories on X could give misinformation an unprecedented influence in the midterms. One more thing Is the Pentagon allowed to surveil Americans with AI? The ongoing public feud between the Department of Defense and the AI company Anthropic has raised a deep and still unanswered question: Does the law actually allow the US government to conduct mass surveillance on Americans? Surprisingly, the answer is not straightforward. More than a decade after Edward Snowden exposed the NSA’s collection of bulk metadata from the phones of Americans, the US is still navigating a gap between what ordinary people think and what the law allows. Today, the legal complexity has a new edge: AI is supercharging surveillance—and our laws haven’t caught up. Here’s how the Pentagon’s use of AI has exposed legal gray areas . —Michelle Kim We can still have nice things A place for comfort, fun, and distraction to brighten up your day. (Got any ideas? Drop me a line .) + Pygmy raccoons have taught each other to make toys out of paper and sand. + See how chocolate goes from a strange-looking cacao pod to Hershey’s Kisses . + Stowaway invites you to take the window seat on any plane flying over you right now. + A new photography project depicts an attractive architectural response to rising sea levels: designer floating homes .

title: Ukraine’s Lyman/Vivaldi Offensive Concludes With Solid Terrain Gains, Russian Losses
body:
A senior Ukrainian field commander on Wednesday announced his troops had ended a months-long offensive that had inflicted 1,000s of casualties on Russian forces and pushed them back dozens of kilometers, both of which claims were confirmed by internal unit information feeds and independent observers.
Brig. Gen. Andriy Biletsky, commander of the Armed Forces of Ukraine’s (AFU) 3rd Corps, in a statement released to news agencies and social media said that his troops had successfully wrapped up the fourth and final phase of Operation Vivaldi, in the process liberating 101 km² (40 square miles) and hitting Russian troops in the north-eastern Lyman sector with 3,000+ new casualties.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Independent analysts have widely confirmed the Vivaldi Operation launched in July has gained substantial ground and seriously damaged Russian units, with the US-based Institute for the Study of War (ISW) in an Oct. 1 campaign review crediting Biletsky’s troops for re-capturing close to 300 square km (120 square miles) of Kremlin-controlled territory in operations east of Lyman.
Biletsky, in a Sept. 28 briefing about the third phase of the Vivaldi Operation, said his troops to that date had liberated 176 square kilometers, re-captured five villages and inflicted about 2,000 Russian casualties, among them 250+ prisoners of war. During the fourth phase, Biletsky said on Wednesday, three more villages – Zelena Dolyna, Lypove, and Kolodiazi – had been liberated by Ukrainian troops. He did not mention his forces having taken Russian prisoners.
Third Corps forces carried out the attacks using combined arms tactics with dismounted and mounted infantry working in tandem with drone swarms, first to infiltrate to Russian positions and then to cut them off from supply and isolate them, before systematically mopping them up, Biletsky said.
“[T]he key to the operation was speed. We did not give the enemy time to replace his losses or to construct a viable defense. The disoriented commanders of the enemy made mistake after mistake,” Biletsky stated.
Overall, throughout Vivaldi operation, 3rd Corps forces returned Ukrainian control to “more than” 16 towns and villages and 277 km² (120 square miles) of Ukrainian territory, and inflicted total enemy losses of at least 8,000 troops, Biletsky said. Kyiv Post review of battle reports and OSINT trackers found battle lines in the Lyman sector generally consistent with Biletsky’s statements.
Accounts in 3rd Corps internal unit feeds reviewed by Kyiv Post found multiple reports of accumulating Russian casualties mostly to drone strike. Neither Russia nor Ukraine publish their own actual casualty counts.
“Vivaldi has demonstrated that an offensive is possible with outnumbered forces using asymmetric tactics. It is possible to, simultaneously, maintain an effective defense in other sectors,” Biletsky said.
In an evaluation generally shared by Ukrainian military analysts, Biletsky said that his 3rd Corps troops, by gaining ground and defeating defending Russian troops in positions east of Lyman, had scored an operational success by pushing Kremlin forces away from the logistically critical Slovyansk-Kramatorsk highway, thereby ensuring defenses in both those cities – named by Kremlin leader Vladimir Putin as top objectives for Russian conquest – would stay well-supplied.
A parallel offensive led primarily by Ukrainian air assault infantry and paratrooper units has since mid-summer used similar drone + infiltrating-infantry tactics to turn back Russian assaults further south in the Donetsk region, to the east of the cities of Slovyansk and Kramatorsk.
Together those successes made Ukrainian aggregate terrain gains in September 2026 slightly greater than Russia’s for the first time since June 2025.
Biletsky, in closing comments , suggested a possible follow-up to the Vivaldi Operation was being planned, saying, “At the very least there is still Wagner and Bach.”
Russia’s Defense Ministry during the Lyman/Vivaldi operation has steadfastly insisted Kremlin forces are holding their ground, and, in some places, advancing.
Russian milbloggers – even vehemently pro-Moscow content-creators, in contrast – have warned for weeks of a worsening situation and Russian forces under heavy pressure from Ukrainian drone swarms and infantry assaults.
Popular milblogger Mikhail Zvinchuk (450,000+ followers), in an Oct. 6 post on the Lyman battles, said Russian defenses were unable to stop infiltrating iUkrainian infantry, and that Ukrainian drone strikes were preventing Russian troops from digging in.
“The enemy has numerical superiority and a significant advantage in drones,” Zvinchuk wrote.
In the Wednesday announcement, 3rd Corps named combat units participating in the Vivlaldi operation, many of which were among the most combat-experienced in the entire AFU.
Among 3rd Corps units involved in the offensive, Biletsky said, were the 3rd Assault Brigade, the 60th Separate Mechanized Brigade, the 125th Separate Territorial Defense Brigade, the 3rd Separate Reconnaissance Battalion, the 25th Separate Anti-Tank Battalion, and the 21st Separate Special Operations Battalion “Kraken,” a unit raised in Kharkiv at the start of Russia’s second invasion of Ukraine, in February 2022, from retired commando civilians at the time, who volunteered to return to service to fight Russia.
The 3rd Assault Brigade, a regular army unit raised in Kyiv originally as untrained militia on the first day of Russia’s second invasion, is widely considered one of the AFU’s most effective fighting outfits and an early proponent of closely coordinated infantry-drone tactics.
Reinforcements attached to the 3rd Corps included the 66th Separate Mechanized Brigade, the 3rd Border Detachment, the 10th “Dozor” Mobile Border Detachment, and commando groups from the 8th Special Operations Forces Regiment, Biletsky said.
Along with Kyiv’s 3rd Assault, four units participating in the Vivaldi offensive – the 3rd Reconnaissance, the 21st Kraken, the 10th Dozor, and the 8th Special Operations – are long-established, veteran infantry outfits with excellent fighting records, specializing in infiltration, raiding, and behind-the-lines operations supported by drones, Kyiv Post research found.
Biletsky named the National Guard’s “Lasar’s Group,” the special operations battalion from the regular army’s K-2 Regiment, and unmanned air vehicle (UAV) units from the Special Operations Center A as the drone units giving the Vivaldi operation air support. All three are long-established, crack flying outfits with average pilots having flown hundreds of combat sorties and experienced operators thousands.
The K-2 Regiment, formally known in the AFU as the 20th Separate Brigade Unmanned Systems K-2 (Ukrainian: 20-та окрема бригада безпілотних систем «К-2») was raised in 2017 as a squad of drone enthusiasts. According to AFU lore, it probably was one of the first military units in history to employ civilian MAVIC drones in a war and then modify them for combat purposes.
K-2 was, reportedly, the first AFU unit to convert a commercial drone into a bomber jury-rigged to drop grenades, and to employ 24/7 small drone presence with a “cab rank” of strike drones ready to attack over a battlefield target. In 2025, according to a unit statement, K-2 became the world’s first military unit to field a dedicated Unmanned Ground Vehicle (UGV) sub-unit.
Stefan Korshak is the Kyiv Post Senior Defense Correspondent. He is from Houston Texas, is a Yalie and since the mid-1990s has worked as correspondent/photographer for newswire, newspapers, television and radio. He has reported from five wars but most enjoys doing articles on wildlife and nature. You can read his weekly blog on the Russo-Ukraine War on Facebook, Substack and Medium. His new book on the 2022 Siege of Mariupol is available on Amazon UK and Amazon US .

title: Russia Announces Visas for Citizens of Montenegro in Reciprocal Move
body:
Russia will introduce visa requirements for citizens of Montenegro in retaliation to Podgorica’s decision to end its bilateral visa-free travel agreement with Moscow as it seeks to join the EU in 2028.
Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova confirmed that Montenegro’s foreign ministry notified Moscow of its intent to cancel the 2008 mutual travel agreement on Sept. 28.
“In practice, this means that starting Nov. 1, our citizens will only be able to enter and remain in Montenegro with visas. Accordingly, citizens of Montenegro will also have to obtain visas for trips to Russia,” Zakharova said.
Montenegro announced in July that it would end visa-free access for citizens of Russia, Belarus, China, Saudi Arabia and Turkey to align with EU standards.
Zakharova argued the decision would curb Russian tourism, harm local businesses and degrade Montenegro’s investment climate.
Montenegro has for years remained one of the few European countries to offer visa-free entry to Russians for up to 30 days and absorbed a large wave of anti-war Russian emigres after the invasion of Ukraine.
Local media reported earlier this year that two-thirds of registered Russian residents had left Montenegro in anticipation of the new visa rules.
“It’s pointless for Montenegro to expect Brussels to compensate them for their inevitable losses,” Zakharova said.
She warned that EU accession would require prospective members among the Balkan nations to adopt a “confrontational anti-Russian course” that would go against their national interests.
The subject of tightening border controls recently drew the attention of the founder of the popular pro-war Telegram channel Rybar, who was detained and deported from Montenegro on claims that he was seeking to film a documentary portraying EU integration as an externally imposed process.
Russian-Montenegrin relations have been strained since 2016, when Podgorica accused Russia of plotting a failed coup with Serbian ultranationalists. The Kremlin denied that claim.
Ties worsened further after Montenegro joined NATO in 2017 and aligned with EU sanctions over Russia’s 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
Montenegro has also banned Russian state media and expelled Russian diplomats for espionage, prompting Moscow to add the country to its list of “unfriendly” states.

title: Sharjah turns to AI to identify foreign investment opportunities in seconds
body: Sharjah is using artificial intelligence to help foreign investors identify investment opportunities within seconds, as the emirate seeks to attract more foreign direct investment despite mounting geopolitical uncertainty . A new AI-powered platform, called Najm, will initially help investors find sites for factories and warehouses across the emirate. It was launched by the emirate's investment promotion agency, the Sharjah FDI Office, also known as Invest in Sharjah. The AI agent is designed to help investors make “informed investment decisions”, Mohamed Al Mushrrakh, chief executive of Invest in Sharjah, said at the Sharjah Investment Forum on Wednesday. For the introductory phase, Invest in Sharjah has teamed up with property portals Bayut and Property Finder, as well as e-commerce platform Dubizzle . Najm will use commercial and industrial real estate data from the online portals and will provide instantaneous information to investors. “Investors could struggle to find information they need to make an investment decision, so we asked ourselves a simple question: how can we deliver the right information at the right moment, when they need it,” Mr Al Mushrrakh told delegates at the Sharjah Investment Forum. “Najm is the answer to that question. It is Invest in Sharjah's new tool for global investors.” The launch of the AI agent is driven by the need to cut the noise around the investment ecosystem in Sharjah and find new ways to bring foreign direct investment to the emirate. Sharjah, the third largest emirate in the UAE after Abu Dhabi and Dubai, is home to 33 industrial zones. Sharjah’s real estate sector recorded more than 16,000 transactions during the first half of this year, with the emirate’s Muwaileh commercial area accounting for the highest value and volume of deals in the first six months, according to Invest in Sharjah data. Sharjah received Dh7.74 billion in FDI last year, an 8.8 per cent increase on an annual basis. The count of projects in the emirate that received FDI also soared by 45 per cent year-on-year, to reach 142 developments, data showed. In the second phase, the Najm platform will expand its sector horizon to cover a broader range of assets and investment opportunities in the healthcare and education sectors, Mr Al Mushrrakh said. “What you have seen today is just the beginning ... Najm stands to cover investment opportunities across multiple sectors from industry to education and technology and beyond,” he said. “We will continue to invest in human capital, technology, infrastructure and partnerships between the public and private sectors. "Through these efforts, we can build a resilient economy, attract new investments into opportunities that we will build together."

title: Ukraine-NATO AI built to forecast Russia’s front-line drone attacks from past data and weather is ready to plug into the army
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Ukraine and NATO have unveiled two artificial intelligence (AI) tools in Vilnius, Lithuania, Ukraine’s Defense Ministry reported on 13 October. One forecasts Russian drone attacks near the front and is ready to join the Armed Forces’ situational awareness systems. The other helps plan artillery fire and is still in testing. A forecast of where, when, and which drones will fly targets the main source of losses near the front. In March, Ukraine’s military put the share of front-line casualties caused by FPV drones at up to 80%. In May, Ukraine’s drone forces commander Robert Brovdi said Russia was copying Ukraine’s model to grow its drone forces. A month earlier, Presidential Office head Kyrylo Budanov wrote that adding more drones no longer fundamentally changes the battlefield. The next stage, he said, is full integration of AI. Forecasting Russian drone attacks The NATO-Ukraine Joint Analysis, Training and Education Center (JATEC) presented both at a three-day seminar in the Lithuanian capital. NATO’s Allied Command Transformation and Ukraine’s Armed Forces built the tools with JATEC’s support. “The solution has already been validated using real-world datasets. It has been refined and is ready for integration into the Armed Forces of Ukraine's situational awareness systems,” the ministry said. Model No. 13 works from past data, weather, and the current battlefield situation. The ministry said it can identify the intensity of attacks, the areas, the time windows, and the types of drones with a high probability. Ranking artillery options Model No. 32 is a decision-support module. It tests whether artillery plans can be generated automatically. It weighs the mission’s requirements and current operational data, including available weapons, ammunition, firing positions, and constraints. Explore further Ukraine’s new military AI does more than watch the battlefield—it helps commanders plan what comes next First, it applies logistics, ballistics, and impact-zone parameters to throw out unworkable options. Then it scores and ranks the rest. That means less hand-based comparison, faster decisions, and a more efficient fire loop, the ministry said. The prototype is now with the Ukrainian military for trials. If the trials succeed and it is validated, it could be expanded to other units that strike Russian forces. title: Indian Navy concludes maiden command of CMF maritime training task force
body:
New Delhi, Oct 14. The Indian Navy will hand over command of Combined Task Force 154 (CTF 154) at a ceremony in Manama, Bahrain, on October 14, completing its first-ever tenure as commander of a task force under the Combined Maritime Forces (CMF), a multinational maritime security partnership.

During its tenure, which began on February 11, 2026, the Indian Navy conducted an extensive programme of multinational training and capacity-building activities, generating more than 7,800 training hours and involving personnel from 39 countries.
CTF 154 is the CMF’s dedicated maritime training task force, mandated to strengthen professional capabilities, interoperability and operational preparedness among the 47 nations participating in the partnership.
India joined the CMF as an associate partner in 2022 before becoming a full member in 2023. Its assumption of command of CTF 154 earlier this year marked a significant step in the Indian Navy’s engagement with the multinational coalition.

Under Indian leadership, the task force conducted a sustained series of training activities under the CMF’s Maritime Domain Enhancement Training framework. These included 20 Staff Enhancement Training engagements, Operation Compass Rose 26-1, Operation Southern Readiness 26-2 and the first Subject Matter Expert Exchange on Piracy and Armed Robbery, designated SPAR 2026.
The training programme covered a broad spectrum of maritime security issues through virtual, hybrid and in-person engagements. It drew on expertise from the Indian Navy, CMF task forces, partner nations, regional maritime agencies and specialised international organisations.
The Indian Navy-led tenure also expanded professional exchanges with operational task forces, regional partners and specialist institutions, strengthening cooperation in multinational training and laying the groundwork for future capacity-building initiatives.

The handover in Bahrain marks another milestone in India’s growing participation in the CMF and underscores its contribution to cooperative maritime security efforts in the Indian Ocean Region and beyond.
The tenure has further strengthened the Indian Navy’s standing as a preferred security and training partner in the region, reflecting India's commitment to enhancing collective maritime capabilities through international cooperation.

title: Lufthansa beats Air France-KLM to acquire minority stake in TAP Air Portugal
body: Lufthansa Group has beaten rival bidder Air France-KLM to acquire a minority stake in TAP Air Portugal, concluding a process that began over a year ago. On October 14, 2026, the Portuguese government and Prime Minister Luís Montenegro, announced that Lufthansa Group had successfully secured minority control of TAP Air Portugal . Lufthansa Group will hold a 44.9% stake in TAP Air Portugal, plus up to 5% if employees do not exercise their right to purchase. The Portuguese government will remain the majority shareholder. “The total value of the operation, including the 5% reserved for employees, amounts to €1.201 billion,” the government said. Ian Dewar Photography / Shutterstock.com “The final decision, between Air France/KLM and Lufthansa, fell on the financially stronger proposal presented by Lufthansa, which also presented an ambitious growth plan for TAP and the possibility of new investments in Portugal,” the government added. “The government considers that this operation safeguards national strategic interests, being convinced that Lufthansa has the scale, resources and ambition necessary for the sustainable growth of TAP.” Both Lufthansa Group and Air France KLM submitted proposals for the acquisition of a majority stake, to be implemented in a possible second phase. “In terms of finance, Lufthansa’s proposal to acquire up to 49.9% of TAP’s share capital is up to 16% higher than that presented by Air France/KLM,” the Portuguese government explained. The Government said it believes the integration into Lufthansa will allow TAP to grow globally, strengthen its presence in Latin America, reinforce its presence at Porto airport (OPO), and increase the TAP fleet (up to 130 aircraft), in addition to safeguarding national strategic interests such as connections to the islands, maintaining the TAP brand and headquarters, and strengthening the hub in Lisbon. Preparation of the process for the sale of the majority of the capital (2nd phase) will be launched shortly with the closing of the operation expected by the beginning of 2028. Air France-KLM Group “This is a strategic decision, which, as was our wish, was not confined to price. We are in a position to guarantee that we have safeguarded the interests of TAP and the Portuguese people,” the Minister of Infrastructure and Housing, Miguel Pinto Luz, said. He added that the decision approved today “allows us to launch a new phase in the history of the airline, with greater capacity and competitiveness, enabling the State and Portuguese taxpayers to recover a much higher amount than initially expected”. British Airways owner also considered bid Lufthansa and Air France-KLM submitted their final bids to Parpública , the government entity running the airline’s re-privatization process, on September 30, 2026. The two airline groups first entered the race to acquire a minority stake in TAP Air Portugal at the end of 2025. At one stage British Airways owner International Airlines Group (IAG) was also considering a bid. According to Reuters , the Lufthansa Group bid was favored as the company was offering an all-cash deal, while Air France-KLM’s offer included a combination of cash and shares. In July 2026, Air France-KLM said if its bid was successful, it would “position Lisbon as its unique Southern European hub”. Air France-KLM also emphasized plans to develop new Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul (MRO) activities in Portugal, generate highly skilled jobs and increase Portuguese connectivity. Lufthansa Group said in July 2026, that its offer “goes beyond a financial investment” with the carrier having “been active in Portugal for more than 70 years”. The German firm stated that it was “presenting an offer that combines strategic, industrial, social, and financial aspects”. Lufthansa Group already includes Lufthansa, SWISS, Austrian Airlines, Brussels Airlines, and most recently ITA Airways. Air France-KLM includes Air France and KLM Royal Dutch Airlines plus Transavia. The Portuguese government’s decision to sell a minority share in TAP Air Portugal was first annnounced in July 2025.
