title: Hunger changed my mind — Timini Egbuson on embracing YouTube movies
body: By Enitan Abdultawab Nollywood actor Timini Egbuson has reflected on his changing perception of YouTube movies, joking that he might have struggled financially had he continued to look down on productions made for the video-sharing platform. Egbuson shared the thought in a post on X Tuesday night, writing, “Can’t believe I was looking down on YouTube movies at some point. Hunger go don kpai me by now.” His remark highlights the growing commercial appeal of YouTube movies in Nigeria’s entertainment industry, where actors and filmmakers are increasingly using the platform to reach audiences and generate revenue from their productions. Egbuson, who has now featured in YouTube movie productions, has embraced the growing market, adding to his work across Nollywood’s film and streaming landscape. Many Nollywood actors have long prioritised cinema movies, often seeing them as more prestigious and commercially rewarding than YouTube productions. As a result, some overlook online films, despite their growing audiences and earning potential. However, the success of YouTube movies is gradually changing perceptions within the industry. Reports show that Nigerian filmmakers were increasingly turning to YouTube amid the pullback by global streaming companies, with the platform offering easier access to audiences and fewer barriers to distribution. The post Hunger changed my mind — Timini Egbuson on embracing YouTube movies appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: FAST FACTS: What changed in final version of the under-18 social media ban bill?
body: MANILA, Philippines – The Senate has approved a bill seeking to ban children below 18 from accessing social media and other digital services considered high-risk, introducing stricter age verification requirements and new obligations for technology companies, with a copy of the bill made available online this week. Senate Bill No. 2424, or the proposed Safe Media Access and Responsible Technology for Kids in Digital Spaces (SMART KIDS) Act, takes a stricter approach than the House of Representatives’ version, which proposes restrictions for children aged 13 and below and tiered access for older minors. A comparison of the original proposal and the Senate-approved bill reveals six major changes. An outright ban for children below 18 The original proposal sought to prohibit children below 16 from accessing age-restricted social media platforms. The approved version raises the age threshold to 18. The new version also explicitly states that the prohibition cannot be overridden by parental consent, authorization, or supervision. So this means even 16- and 17-year-olds would be barred from covered platforms, with no provision for graduated access for older teenagers. Expanded coverage to ‘high-risk digital services’ The approved bill introduces the term “high-risk digital services,” covering social media platforms and online gaming services with social networking functions. These include features allowing users to communicate, maintain social connections, join online communities, or share user-generated content, including livestreams. Roblox and Gorebox are explicitly cited as examples. These two games were tagged as potential avenues for youth radicalization and violent behavior; Roblox for its communication functions, and Gorebox for its supposed violent content. However, the bill exempts email, certain private messaging services, educational platforms, digital news services, and professional collaboration tools. There is also no minimum audience size or revenue threshold for coverage. Smaller livestreaming platforms and online communities could therefore be subject to the same requirements as major technology companies. Government IDs required for age verification Unlike the original proposal, which allowed various age-assurance methods, the approved bill requires primary authentication through PhilSys or another government-issued ID. Age estimation and other verification technologies may supplement, but cannot replace, government ID authentication. Simply entering a birthday would no longer suffice. As a measure of data minimization, platforms are prohibited from retaining copies of government IDs and should receive only information that users meet the age requirement. Nevertheless, this requirement raises questions about online anonymity, surveillance risks, and access for adults without acceptable identification documents. Restrictions on addictive social media features The new version introduces requirements for platforms to mitigate potentially addictive design features, specifically mentioning autoplay, infinite scrolling, push notifications, engagement metrics, and algorithmic amplification, also requiring “safety-by-design” and “privacy-by-default” protections. However, it does not specify how exactly such mitigation can be enforced nor does it delve into technical benchmarks for determining whether these features have been sufficiently mitigated. The Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) will be tasked with monitoring for compliance. Violating platforms face fines ranging from P5 million to P20 million per violation, with additional daily penalties of up to P100,000 for continuing violations. Emergency response to harmful content The approved bill requires platforms to take immediate, proportionate action against harmful content following detection or credible reports. Measures may include suspending livestreams, removing content, restricting its distribution, or stopping algorithmic amplification. Foreign platforms must maintain an emergency escalation channel and designate a legal representative or authorized contact in the Philippines. Notably, the approved version drops the original proposal’s explicit requirement for foreign platforms to establish a physical local office. The Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) must petition a Regional Trial Court, through the Office of the Solicitor General, to restrict an entire platform — a change from the unilateral banning actions that the DICT has performed, highlighted by the controversial Discord ban. However, the DICT may still issue account-specific disabling orders if continuing harm can be proven. – Rappler.com Must Read Social media bans are no cure-all, but governments may still find them necessary

title: Kyiv prepared almost 700 generators for heat and water supply facilities and 70 mobile boiler houses – Klitschko
body:
The capital has completed its initial general plan for organizing energy resilience and significantly increased backup power sources during the full-scale war, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said in a speech in the Verkhovna Rada on Wednesday, an Interfax-Ukraine correspondent reported.
"What has been done in the city of Kyiv during the full-scale war? The capital has been building up backup sources. Kyiv has prepared almost 700 generators of various capacities for heat and water supply facilities, 70 mobile boiler houses, three diesel power plants have already been built, and a backup water intake," he said.
According to the mayor, Kyivvodokanal currently has 103 generators and is awaiting additional large foreign-made generator systems. In addition, under the city's energy resilience target programs for the housing stock, more than 6,000 units of equipment have been purchased, including generators, inverters and batteries.
The mayor noted that all of the capital's educational institutions are provided with generators of various capacities, including 285 high-capacity units. Healthcare facilities have 480 generators, and 11 hospitals are already equipped with autonomous heat supply from their own boiler houses. By the end of the year, 21 medical institutions will have autonomous heating systems.
Klitschko added that Kyiv continues to prepare for the heating season and to ensure the functioning of municipal services.
"Kyiv is working, repairing, ensuring the functioning of the city in conditions of a shortage of workers at utility companies, halted payments, and conditions in which the enemy is wrecking our city every day and every night," Klitschko stressed.
After the Kyiv mayor's speech, MPs tried several times to summon him to the Rada again, but none of the proposals gathered the required votes.

title: Ukraine’s Business Leaders to Tackle War Risks and Economic Resilience at 12th Kyiv International Economic Forum on Oct. 26
body:
Kyiv will host the 12th Kyiv International Economic Forum (KIEF) on October 26, bringing together more than 500 participants, including owners and executives of Ukrainian and international companies, government officials, investors, diplomats, and experts. This year’s theme, “People. Business. Economy. What’s Next?”, will guide discussions on how businesses and Ukraine’s economy can withstand mounting challenges, adapt to changing conditions, and return to growth.
Now in the fifth year of Russia’s full-scale invasion, Ukraine’s economy faces growing pressure. Russian attacks continue to target industrial facilities, energy infrastructure, ports, railways, logistics hubs, and other assets critical to business operations. According to Ukraine’s Ministry of Economy, direct damage from destruction could reach approximately $10 billion annually. Combined with the blockade of seaports, these losses have already cost Ukraine an estimated 1.5 percentage points of GDP in 2026.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
In its October forecast, the World Bank projects that Ukraine’s economic growth will slow to 1.2% in 2026 and reach just 1.5% in 2027 if active hostilities continue. The Bank previously projected 4% growth in 2027, assuming hostilities would end by late 2026.
“While discussions previously focused on Ukraine’s reconstruction, the priority today is how to strengthen economic resilience here and now. Businesses need solutions that will help them protect their assets, maintain production, and continue investing even during wartime”, says Vasyl Khmelnytskyi, KIEF initiator, founder of UFuture holding.
KIEF 2026 will feature 14 panel discussions addressing the most pressing challenges facing Ukraine’s economy. Key topics will include protecting business facilities, maintaining operations during air raid alerts, decentralizing logistics and energy supply, ensuring reliable communications, insuring against war-related risks, securing compensation for lost assets, accessing finance, and maintaining macroeconomic stability.
Discussions will also explore how Ukraine can adapt its industrial development strategy and energy policy to new realities, redefine national economic priorities, strengthen international cooperation, and advance European integration amid emerging challenges. Special attention will go to frontline cities and the practical solutions they have already implemented to keep their economies functioning.
Ukraine’s economy has already demonstrated its ability to adapt rapidly to major disruptions. In 2022, following the destruction of the Kremenchuk oil refinery and the resulting fuel shortages, the country rebuilt its fuel supply chains, while thousands of businesses relocated from frontline regions to safer areas further inland.
In 2023, Ukraine launched its own maritime corridor after traditional shipping routes were blocked. Following large-scale attacks on the power grid last year, businesses and the government also accelerated the development of distributed power generation.
“Today, any discussion about the future must start with practical decisions that businesses, the government, and international partners can make right now to sustain economic resilience and restore growth. This is precisely what KIEF 2026 is about”, says Yuriy Pyvovarov, CEO of KIEF.

Forum Partners: Sense Bank, NEQSOL Holding, FUIB, DTEK, Ajax Systems, Uklon, TERWIN, Eclectic Talents Group, BALEX, CEO Club Ukraine

title: World Cup Visa Scandal: There is no ‘justification’ to dismiss me – Kofi Adams
body: Minister for Sports and Recreation Kofi Adams has rejected calls by the Minority in Parliament for his dismissal over an alleged visa scandal linked to the FIFA World Cup. About 90 people reportedly paid between $10,000 and $15,000 each, but only five of them obtained visas for the global showpiece, which was staged in the USA, Canada and Mexico. Yaw Ampofo Ankrah has already been suspended as National Sports Authority (NSA) boss, and further heads are expected to roll at the Sports Ministry as the Presidency is set to launch a probe into the matter, JoySports can confirm. When asked about calls for his removal, Adams said: “Government money has not been lost,” he told Citi News. “Well, I don’t see the justification. Both the American Embassy and TRIBE Culture Fest, the NSA and the GTA were doing their thing behind the Ministry. The Ministry didn’t know. “The first time I ever sat and had a conversation in relation to that matter was when the May 19 letter requested the forwarding of event coordinators and volunteers to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Embassy. That’s when I got to know the details of what was happening.”

title: Alleged Financial Misconduct : El-Rufai’s Trial Continues Today At Federal High Court
body: The alleged corruption trial of former Governor of Kaduna State, Nasir El-Rufai, continues on Wednesday at the Federal High Court sitting in the state capital, barely a day after an eight-hour session at the Kaduna State High Court. The former governor was arraigned on Tuesday before Justice Darius Khobo of the Kaduna State High Court by the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission over alleged financial misconduct and abuse of office during his tenure as governor of Kaduna State. He is facing similar charges at the Federal High Court, despite being granted bail some months ago. During yesterday’s sitting, a forensic investigator with the State Security Service, Segun Kayode, alleged that the defendant and some of his associates earmarked $600,000 to settle officials of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission and intermediaries. Kayode, the first prosecution witness in the ongoing trial, said $500,000 and $100,000 were allegedly set aside for the payments, adding that forensic audio recordings captured conversations involving El-Rufai and some of his suspected associates. According to him, the recorded conversations centred on alleged efforts to frustrate an EFCC investigation into a company identified as Singularity. Kayode named a Senior Advocate of Nigeria and Bashir El-Rufai among those allegedly mentioned in the conversations. He told the court that they were allegedly directed to meet one Ahmadu Sule to obtain a template previously used to liquidate another company, with the intention of applying a similar process to Singularity. The investigator further alleged that the discussions included plans to liquidate the company in Nigeria and Mauritius, where it was reportedly under investigation by the Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit. Kayode also alleged that the recordings contained discussions about preventing the EFCC from investigating IHS, which he said was listed on the New York Stock Exchange. The allegations were presented as part of the prosecution’s evidence against the former governor. They remain allegations and have not been established by the court. The proceedings lasted nearly eight hours, from 12:26 pm to 8:18 pm, with about two hours devoted to playing the recorded conversations. Earlier, El-Rufai’s lead counsel, Paul Erokoro (SAN), objected to Kayode’s testimony, arguing that the witness’s name and summary of evidence were not included in the prosecution’s proof of evidence. Erokoro argued that the omission undermined his client’s right to a fair hearing, insisting that the defence was entitled to know the evidence it was expected to answer. However, counsel for the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission, Ayodeji Adedipe (SAN), told the court that Kayode was a subpoenaed witness and that the omission did not automatically render his testimony inadmissible. The resumed hearing came days after the Court of Appeal in Kaduna dismissed El-Rufai’s appeal challenging the refusal of bail by the state high court. In its judgment delivered on October 9, the appellate court upheld the lower court’s decision, ruling that the former governor had failed to establish sufficient grounds to warrant interference with the refusal of bail. El-Rufai has been in ICPC custody since February 18, 2026, over allegations of financial misconduct linked to his administration of Kaduna State between 2015 and 2023. The post Alleged Financial Misconduct : El-Rufai’s Trial Continues Today At Federal High Court appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Five Things To Know Today
body: 1. INEC gives parties October 24 deadline to challenge omitted candidates This photo shows the INEC Chairman Joash Amupitan at the Citizens’ Townhall over the 2026 Electoral Act held in Abuja on Sunday, March 1, 2026. Photo: Taiwo Adesina/Channels TV The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has explained its decision to exclude several governorship candidates from its final list for the 2027 elections. In a statement issued on Tuesday, INEC said it acted in compliance with the Supreme Court’s September 24 judgment upholding provisions of the Electoral Act requiring political parties to submit membership registers before conducting primaries. The affected candidates include Isa Pantami in Gombe, Ladi Adebutu in Ogun and Aminu Gwarzo in Kano. INEC says parties that believe their candidates were wrongly excluded have until October 24 to formally challenge the omissions under Section 32(2) of the Electoral Act. Meanwhile, the APC is scheduled to inaugurate President Bola Tinubu’s presidential campaign council in Abuja today. Why it matters: The commission’s explanation establishes the legal basis for the exclusions but leaves individual disputes unresolved. The outcome could affect governorship contests in several states. Watch: Formal objections from affected parties, INEC’s responses and possible court proceedings. 2. US places Nigeria on child-soldiers list, threatening military assistance US President Donald Trump speaks to the press in the Oval Office of the White House in Washington, DC, on June 3, 2026. (Photo by Mandel NGAN / AFP) | Mandel NGAN / AFP The United States has included Nigeria among 14 countries identified under its Child Soldiers Prevention Act, raising the possibility of restrictions on military assistance and defence cooperation. The designation appears in the US State Department’s 2026 Trafficking in Persons Report, released on October 11. The report identifies Boko Haram and the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) as armed groups continuing to recruit and use children, including some as young as 12. Under US law, the designation can restrict military training, foreign military financing, equipment transfers and certain arms-sales licences, subject to presidential waivers and other exemptions. The listing does not, by itself, establish that Nigerian government forces currently recruit child soldiers. Why it matters: Nigeria relies on international cooperation, including with the United States, in counterterrorism operations. Restrictions could complicate aspects of that cooperation. Watch: The Nigerian government’s formal response, whether Washington grants a waiver, and any changes to existing defence arrangements. 3. UN report says 113 million Nigerians face multidimensional poverty The United Nations headquarters building is pictured in New York on July 13, 2023. (Photo by Daniel SLIM / AFP) | Daniel SLIM / AFP A new United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) report estimates that approximately 113 million Nigerians, representing 48.7 per cent of the population, experience multidimensional poverty. The 2026 Global Multidimensional Poverty Index, released on October 12, measures overlapping deprivation in health, education and living standards rather than income alone. The report highlights substantial differences between rural and urban communities, with poverty particularly widespread in the North-West and North-East. Lack of clean cooking fuel and electricity are among the major contributors. The report also indicates that earlier improvements in poverty reduction have been reversed. Its historical comparisons use survey data from earlier years and should not be confused with a direct measurement of conditions in October 2026. Why it matters: The findings highlight the scale of deprivation despite recent improvements in Nigeria’s economic-growth outlook. Watch : Federal and state responses, spending on basic services, and whether economic reforms produce measurable improvements in household welfare. 4. Ondo air crash: National Assembly orders military aircraft audit as Air Force establishes investigation board This file photo shows the red chamber of the Nigerian Senate. The Senate and House of Representatives have called for a comprehensive audit of Nigerian Air Force aircraft following the fatal October 5 crash near Igbokoda, Ondo State. The Senate has directed its Air Force and Aviation committees to examine aircraft serviceability, airworthiness and maintenance funding. Lawmakers also want the Air Force’s maintenance budget scrutinised, and the investigation findings made public. Separately, the Nigerian Air Force announced on Tuesday that it had established a 12-member Aircraft Accident Investigation Board, headed by Air Vice Marshal F.O. Ankeli. The board includes representatives of civilian aviation authorities and will examine technical, operational, environmental and human factors. The cause of the crash has not been established. Why it matters: The investigation now extends beyond identifying the immediate cause to examining aircraft maintenance, fleet safety and the use of public funds. Watch : The legislative audit, recovery of remaining evidence, preliminary investigation findings and publication of safety recommendations. 5. Shell agrees to sell Nigerian gas distribution business to local energy company This photo shows a gas pipeline. Shell has announced an agreement to sell its entire interest in the Shell Nigeria Gas Group to Vaaris Energy, a privately owned Nigerian company. The transaction, announced on Tuesday, covers Shell’s domestic gas distribution operations. The financial terms were not disclosed. Shell says the sale forms part of its strategy to concentrate on deepwater oil production and integrated gas projects in Nigeria. The company maintains that Nigeria remains an important part of its global operations. Why it matters : The transaction represents another transfer of energy assets to Nigerian ownership and could influence future investment in domestic gas distribution. Reliable gas supply remains important for manufacturers, industrial users and Nigeria’s energy-transition plans. Watch : Regulatory approvals, completion of the transaction, Vaaris Energy’s investment plans and the implications for existing industrial customers. The post Five Things To Know Today appeared first on Channels Television .

title: RENK and KNDS extend contract for Leopard 2 transmissions, with deliveries from 2029
body: RENK will supply HSWL 354 transmissions, TCS-354A control units and G4MA11 gear selectors. KNDS said the extension supports its production ramp-up and the expansion of Leopard 2 fleets in Germany and other NATO countries. “The LEOPARD 2 is the backbone of Western armed forces,” said Dr. Alexander Sagel, chief executive of RENK Group. “For decades, our HSWL 354 has ensured that troops can rely on the mobility of their vehicle under all conditions.” “The extension of the order reflects the trust that KNDS has in our technology and ability to deliver,” Sagel said. “Together, we are making our contribution to help the Bundeswehr and NATO forces acquire the capabilities they need to defend Europe.” “The expansion of this contract is an important milestone for the growth of the LEOPARD 2 fleet, which clearly strengthens the defense capabilities of Germany and other NATO countries,” said Dr. Axel Scheibel, chief technology officer of KNDS Deutschland. “The RENK Group is a strategic partner of KNDS, supporting us—not least as part of our production ramp-up—to provide customers with the best possible equipment in a timely manner.” RENK began production of its 4,000th HSWL 354 transmission in June 2026. Its hydromechanical transmission, reversing and steering systems have supported Leopard 2 mobility for more than four decades. Around 3,300 Leopard 2 tanks and related vehicles are operated by armed forces in 23 countries, according to KNDS. RENK’s systems are in service with NATO members and partner countries. The companies announced the contract extension on October 14 during AUSA 2026 in Washington, D.C. Both are displaying their product portfolios at the exhibition.

Scarborough soldier, Lance Corporal (LCpl) Claude Stanley Dell, has been laid to rest more than a century after his death in World War 1.
Lance Corporal April Farthing stands ready to sound Last Post as the coffin of LCpl Dell is born to the graveside (Crown Copyright)
A young Scarborough soldier of World War 1, killed just a week after his arrival in France, has finally been laid to rest with full military honours. LCpl Claude Stanley Dell of the 5th Battalion Yorkshire Regiment was laid to rest today (13 October 2026) at Commonwealth War Graves Commission’s ( CWGC ) Poelcapelle British Cemetery in Belgium.
In 2021, workmen digging a rainwater cistern in Hazeweidestraat, St Juliaan, Belgium spotted human remains in their trench. A few days later an archaeological excavation was undertaken by the Flanders Heritage Agency. Artefacts recovered alongside the remains showed them to be those of a soldier who had served in the 5th Battalion Yorkshire Regiment.
The Ministry of Defence’s Joint Casualty and Compassionate Centre ( JCCC ), known as the ‘ MOD War Detectives’, launched an investigation to name him. Research identified twenty men from the regiment missing in the area, all of whom died in the Spring of 1915. Following genealogical investigation, living descendants of the missing men were traced one by one until eventually DNA testing proved that the remains were those of LCpl Claude Stanley Dell.
LCpl Dell joined up alongside his brothers Charles and Guy at the outbreak of war. All three joined the 5th Battalion Yorkshire Regiment, whilst their older brother Leighton was in the Royal Field Artillery, and another brother - Frederick - served with the Yorkshire Hussars.
5th Battalion left the UK on 17 April 1915 and arrived in Boulogne the following day. On 23 April they arrived on the Ypres Salient, and just two days later on 25 April 1915 LCpl Dell was killed in action. Claude’s brothers wrote home to tell their parents, ‘poor Claude met his end…whilst doing his duty’.
Today, LCpl Dell was buried with full military honours in the presence of both his military family, and his great-niece Judith.
The burial service was led by Padre David Jeal CF (Crown Copyright)
The service, organised by JCCC , was supported by serving soldiers of the Royal Yorkshire Regiment, as well as staff from the CWGC .
It has been a privilege to research this case, to have been able to identify LCpl Dell, and to have been able to lay him to rest today. I am extremely grateful to 2nd Battalion the Royal Yorkshire Regiment who have provided the bearer party for the funeral, and to the members of Claude’s family who have been involved in his commemoration.
The military party and Claude's family stand at his graveside (Crown Copyright)
Claude’s grave will now be cared for in perpetuity by the Commonwealth War Graves Commission, ensuring his sacrifice is never forgotten. Dr Daniel Seaton, Commemorations Case Officer at CWGC , said:
Lance Corporal Dell lay in an unmarked grave on the former battlefields for well over 100 years. It is a great privilege to have worked alongside the JCCC and our Belgian partners in the effort to restore his identity. He is now laid to rest in a Commission cemetery not far from where he fell, ensuring that his grave can be visited in perpetuity and his sacrifice remembered.
