title: Ukraine National Bank eases lending rules for defense and energy sectors
body:
The National Bank of Ukraine (NBU) has adopted a third package of regulatory measures to support lending to the economy, focusing on the defense-industrial complex (DIC), the energy sector and businesses affected by the war, the regulator said.
In particular, the collateral liquidity coefficient for property rights to revenue under contracts with entities in the security and defense sector, guaranteed by the electricity buyer and the transmission system operator, has been raised from 0.3 to 0.75.
The National Bank expects this measure to increase financing for defense-industrial and energy companies that hold state contracts but have limited ability to provide banks with traditional collateral.
Banks have also been authorized to take into account the value of goods held in inventory or undergoing processing and pledged as collateral for loans with terms of up to 18 months, based on their actual balance on the valuation date. This relaxation will remain in effect until September 1, 2027.
In addition, the central bank has expanded the ability to assess whether legal entities generate sufficient operating financial results to service their debt using projected figures if their property has been significantly damaged, destroyed or mined. Previously, this option was available to businesses operating in territories adjacent to the front line.
For loans under the 5-7-9% program, banks will be allowed to continue applying collective credit risk assessments or a simplified approach and will not be required to initiate nonperforming asset management procedures if the overdue payments arose solely because of delays in partial compensation for interest rates by the National Development Institution.
The amendments were approved by NBU Board Resolution No. 118 dated October 11, which entered into force on October 14.
As reported, in August and September, the NBU adopted the first two packages of regulatory measures to support lending amid intensified Russian shelling. They concerned, in particular, lending to the agricultural sector, manufacturers and companies implementing projects to restore critical infrastructure.

title: Sybiha after overnight Russian attack on Ukraine: Putin openly defies US
body:
Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha made the statement on X, according to Ukrinform.
"Putin has delivered yet another negative 'response' to the proposal of an energy ceasefire announced by President Trump and supported by President Zelensky. Instead of one 'yes' to peace efforts — 39 missiles and more than 120 drones. Cynically, the main targets of this strike were Ukraine's energy objects," the foreign minister said.
Sybiha emphasized that Putin was not merely attacking Ukraine but was openly challenging the United States and showing contempt for any attempts to end the war.
Aggression must not be rewarded economically, the minister warned. He called for no easing of sanctions and no concessions that would allow Russia to finance another wave of terror.
"Every dollar that reaches Moscow's war budget is another resource for attacks on Ukrainian civilians and threats to transatlantic security. We urge our partners to respond with stronger sanctions, tougher enforcement, and immediate additional air defence support for Ukraine," Sybiha stressed.
He expressed his conviction that Putin must be held accountable for rejecting peace rather than receiving incentives to prolong the war.
As Ukrinform previously reported, President Volodymyr Zelensky said that during the night of October 14, Russia had launched 39 ballistic missiles and more than 120 attack drones and loitering munitions against energy and critical infrastructure in Kyiv, the surrounding region, and Kharkiv. Approximately 600,000 people remain without electricity.
According to Zelensky, the Donald Trump administration had also warned that it could suspend intelligence sharing with Ukraine if Kyiv did not stop striking Russian oil refineries.

title: 40 Lagos Public School Pupils Advance in Sweetthinkers Competition
body: Iyke Bede Forty public primary school pupils have emerged from the second-stage screening of the Sweetthinkers Academic Competition for Lagos State public schools. They were selected from close to 200 participating schools across 20 Local Government Education Authorities (LGEAs). Hosted by the Sweetthinkers Academic Awards Initiative (SAAI), a non-profit organisation driven by a passion for celebrating academic performance in underserved communities, the competition seeks to shine a light on the public school system by recognising high-performing pupils and encouraging others to strive for academic excellence. The tests were held at three centres: Maryland, Lagos Island and Oshodi. The Oshodi centre accommodated the most participating schools, representing 10 LGEAs, with 20 pupils qualifying for the next stage. The Lagos Island centre hosted schools from six LGEAs, with 12 pupils qualifying, while four LGEAs participated at the Maryland centre, producing eight successful candidates. The screening test comprised Mathematics, English, General Studies, Science, Verbal Reasoning and Quantitative Analysis. It lasted 30 minutes, assessing both the pupils’ subject knowledge and speed of thought. The tests were processed and graded in real time. The 40 successful pupils will proceed to the third stage of the competition, ahead of the final stage. A teacher at Bishop Crowther Memorial Primary School, one of the qualifying schools, said competitions of this nature could motivate pupils to improve their academic performance and recognise their abilities. “Programmes like these should be encouraged so that children in school can see that their mates are doing well, educationally. It encourages the students to put in their best, knowing fully well that at the end of the day, they will be rewarded.” During the screening exercise, UAC Foods, BOLAD Catering Services and Hothobs provided refreshments for the participating pupils.

title: IDEAS Project Will Creat 80,000 Young Entrepreneurs
body: Oghenevwede Ohwovoriole in Abuja The National Coordinator of IDEAS Project, Mrs. Blessing Ogwu, has disclosed that the federal government is training and equipping 80,000 young Nigerians with technical skills to make them job creators and not job seekers She made the disclosure at the official flag off of the Federal Ministry of Education (FME), IDEAS-TVET Cohort 03 sponsored by the federal government and financed by the world bank on Friday in Abuja. With over 200 beneficiaries in attendance. Mrs. Ogwu who was represented by the Chief Manager of TVET, Prof. Ndem Ayara stated that government is training 80,000 Nigerian youth who will be paid N30,00 monthly stipends as long as they meet the 65% attendance requirement. “Through Ideas Projects, the federal government of Nigeria is training over 80,000 young people in various skills as enumerated during my presentation. And the trainees are done in cohorts. We’ve already done cohort one across the country, cohort two, this is cohort three. ” It’s done in all the states of the federation through the use of Training Service Providers (TSPs). TSPs , provides workshops, the equipment, and instructors to train these young people.” Speaking on the qualifications to be a beneficiary he said, “the qualification is for you to be a Nigerian, provide your NIN, provide your BVN, so that, your bank account is known, and a stipend of 30,000 Naira per month is sent straight through remitter to your account after the confirmation that you’ve attended 65% of the training time or days.” According to him, “the trainees will be supported with training kits. With tools that are relevant to the skill that they are learning, so that they can use those skills and tools to practice the skill that they are training. When asked why the government decided to equip the youth with skills, he said it was to bridge the skill gap, curb unemployment and create jobs. “We’ve identified lack of skill as a major factor to unemployment. Once people have skill, they can either be employed by others or they can become self-employed by putting their skill into practice and can even employ other people to work with them.” In his speech the MD/CEO of New Horizons, Tim Akano said “the training is collaboration between the federal government through the World Bank through the federal ministry of education while New Horizons is Training Service Provider. “We are providing the space, equipments, instructors, training modules and certifications in ten different skills in hardware maintainance.” The Special Guest of honour, the CEO/Registrar African Institute of Public Health, Dr. Bankole Ayodele applauded the government for initiating the programme and advised for the nation’s education to be more practical than theoretical. “This is an innovation that should be encouraged in Nigeria because most of the things you learn in the University are not useful to you. But what you have learnt here you can effectively do hardware maintainance. “Unfortunately Nigeria is a country of certificates but the organisation through the world Bank is equipping you with skills that you can become an employer of labour and reduce the social vices in the society. The Chinese are better because of this kind of programmes and that is why they are giants today.” “My appeal to the federal Ministry of education is that our education should be more practical than theoretical. One of the female beneficiaries, Destiny Sunday, said, “I have learnt how to repair phones and am now learning how to repair computers. I thanks the federal government and the World Bank for this opportunity. And with the N30,000 monthly stipends I can pay my transport to this training. As a teacher I’ll teach others the skills that I have learnt here so that they to can be productive and teach others too.”

title: Russians won't enter the European Union? Visas suspension proposal
body:
Estonia will support the Finnish proposal to suspend tourist visas for Russian citizens in the European Union, the Estonian Minister of Foreign Affairs, Margus Tsahkna, has confirmed.
“Visa policy must reflect the gravity of Russia’s ongoing aggression. The EU should continue strengthening pressure on the Kremlin by all available means. We also call on the EU to swiftly adopt the necessary implementing acts to establish a comprehensive entry ban for Russian combatants,” Margus Tsahkna wrote on the X platform.
Estonia joins Finland’s call to suspend tourist visas for Russian citizens across the European Union. As Russia continues its relentless assault on Ukraine, bombing cities, destroying civilian infrastructure, and killing innocent people, it is unacceptable that Russian citizens can still enjoy unrestricted leisure travel within the Schengen area. Visa policy must reflect the gravity of Russia’s ongoing aggression. The EU should continue to strengthen pressure on the Kremlin through all available means. We also urge the EU to swiftly adopt the necessary implementing acts to establish a comprehensive entry ban on Russian combatants.
The Estonian minister’s post refers to an appeal published several hours earlier by the Finnish Minister for Foreign Affairs, Elina Valtonen. Finland’s top diplomat announced that member states had been invited to join a letter addressed to the European Commission. “Issuing visas to Russians for non-essential travel was already banned in Finland in 2022. The same must finally happen at the EU level,” she wrote, adding that it is also necessary to introduce an entry ban to the Schengen Area for individuals directly linked to Vladimir Putin’s regime.
The appeal by the Foreign Ministers of Finland and Estonia aligns with an idea put forward in early September by the Polish Minister of Foreign Affairs, Radosław Sikorski. During a meeting of the Foreign Ministers of the Weimar Triangle countries, the head of Polish diplomacy stated that a significant reduction in the number of Russian diplomats in Europe is necessary. “Russia has far too many diplomats in the European Union. We estimate there are over 2,000 of them, and we calculate that at least 40 per cent are performing tasks inconsistent with their diplomatic status,” Sikorski said. These are not the only initiatives to emerge recently. Previously, the head of Polish diplomacy had proposed, among other things, the introduction of biometric passports for Russian diplomats and a ban on them leaving their country of accreditation.
According to European Commission data obtained by PAP (Polish Press Agency), the number of visas issued to Russian citizens by Schengen Area member states is increasing. In 2025, they issued approximately 623,000 such visas, up 10 per cent from the previous year. The majority — 478,000 — were tourist visas. France, Italy, and Spain issued the highest number of visas to Russian citizens.

title: Zenith Bank deepens commitment to girl-child development, empowers 300 school girls
body:
Zenith Bank Plc has launched the maiden edition of its Girl-Child Empowerment Programme, themed “Banking on Her Tomorrow,” bringing together 300 schoolgirls aged 13 to 17 from selected schools across Lagos for a day of learning, mentorship and personal development.
Held on Monday, 12 October 2026, at the Civic Centre, Victoria Island, Lagos, the programme featured sessions on finance and investment, etiquette and personal development, social media ethics, and social relationships and interactions, equipping participants with practical knowledge and skills for their personal, educational and future career journeys.
The initiative, a brainchild of the Bank’s Group Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer, Dr Adaora Umeoji, reflects Zenith Bank’s commitment to nurturing the potential of young girls and helping them make informed choices about their futures.
In her welcome address, Dr Umeoji urged the participants to believe in their abilities, pursue their ambitions and remain focused and disciplined. Drawing on examples of young girls who have achieved remarkable feats, she challenged them to look beyond their present circumstances and envision the women they aspire to become.
“To all my amazing young ladies here today, each of you possesses gifts, talents, and ideas that are capable of revolutionising the world. You can revolutionise the world with your ideas,” she said.
The GMD/CEO further encouraged the girls to explore their interests and resist societal limitations, stressing the importance of taking ownership of their futures.
“Never allow gender or age to limit your goals. Whatever interests you today, explore it. Whatever you choose to pursue in life, give it your best shot,” she said.
Delivering the keynote address, Her Majesty, Olori Atuwatse III, Queen Consort of the Warri Kingdom, encouraged the girls to embrace their identities, develop resilience and use their abilities to make a positive difference in the lives of others.
Using the mangrove tree as a metaphor for resilience, she reminded the participants that challenges need not define their futures and that their worth extends beyond academic results and external expectations.
“Every time you affirm the truth about who you are, you are building confidence. Every time the tide of life goes out and you are still standing, you are building resilience. And every time you use your gifts for another person, you are discovering your purpose,” Olori Atuwatse III said.
The programme featured interactive sessions led by accomplished professionals and personalities:
Ayanime Edem, founder of The Elite Finishing School and modern etiquette educator, discussed confidence, communication, self-presentation and etiquette.
Nigerian actress and content creator Bukunmi Adeaga Ilori, popularly known as Kie Kie, addressed responsible social media use, authenticity and digital boundaries.
Representing Zenith Bank, Thelma Okonye and Adesola Adeyemo introduced the girls to saving, responsible money management and investment, highlighting the importance of developing sound financial habits early.
While Nigerian filmmaker, creative executive and educator, Praise Onyeagwalam, Director Pink, led a session on healthy relationships, self-awareness and effective communication.
The sessions encouraged active participation, giving the girls opportunities to ask questions and engage with the speakers on issues relevant to their experiences and aspirations.
The programme also featured competitions, with cash prizes totalling over ₦1 million awarded to winners. The participants received books to encourage reading and personal growth, while musical performances by Nigerian singers Qing Madi and No. 11 added to the lively atmosphere. The event was hosted by Temi Badru, public speaker, communications coach and lawyer, with Darasimi Destiny Nadi serving as mini host.
Delivering the closing remarks, Executive Director, Zenith Bank Plc, Dr Adobi Nwapa, highlighted the GMD/CEO’s vision for the initiative and the Bank’s commitment to sustaining its impact.
“The programme is the vision of our GMD/CEO, who conceived and championed it, demonstrating her unwavering commitment to the empowerment of the girl child. Through her leadership, she has shown the girls what is possible when a woman dares to lead. At Zenith Bank, our commitment to the girl child extends beyond today, and we will continue to nurture their aspirations through this annual initiative,” she said.
Dr Nwapa thanked the speakers and participants for contributing to the programme’s success and encouraged the girls to apply the lessons learnt, remain confident and pursue their aspirations with determination.
The initiative builds on Zenith Bank’s longstanding commitment to advancing opportunities for women and girls through programmes including its annual International Women’s Day Seminar, the Zenith Women’s Basketball League, the Women of Honour Awards in partnership with the Ford Foundation, the Pad-a-Queen Initiative and Z-Woman, which supports women-owned businesses through business support and access to credit at discounted rates.
Through “Banking on Her Tomorrow,” Zenith Bank is extending this commitment to a younger generation, equipping girls with the knowledge, skills and confidence to pursue their ambitions and contribute meaningfully to their communities and society.

title: Starlink restrictions may strip Ukraine of one of few effective defenses against jet-powered Shaheds – presidential adviser
body:
Restrictions on Starlink satellite communications affect not only long-range missions and frontline logistics, but also the deployment of interceptor drones used to protect Ukrainian airspace from jet-powered Shahed drones, Presidential Advisor Serhiy Flash Beskrestnov has noted.
"Starlink is used in what is currently the most effective solution [interceptors] for defending our skies against jet-powered Shaheds," he wrote in a Facebook post on Wednesday.
According to Beskrestnov, the Starlink restrictions could deprive Ukraine of one of its few remaining defensive tools against jet-powered Shaheds.
"In fact, through their actions, partners are stripping us of one of our few chances to defend the country against jet-powered Shaheds," Beskrestnov wrote.
As reported earlier, Beskrestnov stated that SpaceX had restricted the operational speed of its Starlink terminals in motion, leading to the disruption of several missions. "Currently, the restriction applies to the 'military package' of StarShield services and is set at a speed of 100 miles per hour [160 kilometres per hour]. Our defense forces received no prior warning of such a restriction, and this led to the disruption of a number of missions," he wrote on Telegram, calling the move clearly linked to the current political situation.
Former advisor to the Minister of Defense and volunteer Serhiy Sternenko confirmed the information citing military personnel, who reported that connection begins to drop at speeds of 60–70 km/h.

title: Korniyenko announces Honcharenko’s expulsion from European Solidarity faction
body:
First Deputy Chairman of the Verkhovna Rada Oleksandr Korniyenko announced the expulsion of MP Oleksiy Honcharenko from the European Solidarity parliamentary faction during a plenary meeting on Wednesday.

An Interfax-Ukraine correspondent reported that, under the Verkhovna Rada’s rules of procedure, an MP is considered expelled from a faction after the decision is officially announced at a plenary meeting of parliament.

As reported, the European Solidarity faction said on Oct 6 that it had expelled unaffiliated MP Honcharenko from its ranks following his statements.

On Oct 2, Honcharenko published a series of posts on Telegram calling for negotiations with Russia to begin with agreements to halt strikes on ports, businesses, schools, hospitals, residential buildings and bridges. He said more difficult issues, including Donbas and Ukraine’s neutral status, could then be discussed.

title: Kadyrov says Houthis should have targeted US bases instead of Riyadh airport
body: Chechen Head Ramzan Kadyrov has said that Yemen’s Houthis should have targeted US military bases in the Middle East rather than civilian facilities in Saudi Arabia. He made the statement on his Telegram channel on Tuesday, commenting on attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. Fourteen civilians were killed and more than 300 people were injured in Houthi attacks on the airport on Tuesday and Sunday. Among the casualties were pilgrims travelling to Mecca. ‘Deliberate missile strikes on civilian facilities cannot be justified by any arguments. They make no sense, either politically or religiously’, Kadyrov wrote . He suggested that the attacks might have been a response to the military operation by the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen. In that case, the Chechen leader said, the Houthis should have chosen different targets. ‘It would have been more logical to direct their strikes at the relevant facilities. Take, for example, the American bases located throughout the region’, Kadyrov said . He added that attacks on civilians demonstrated neither courage nor strength. Russia’s Foreign Ministry also condemned the missile attack on Riyadh International Airport. On Monday, the ministry issued a statement calling on the parties to the conflict on the Arabian Peninsula to refrain from strikes on civilian infrastructure. It also expressed condolences to the families of those killed and wished the injured a speedy recovery. According to preliminary information from the Russian Embassy in Saudi Arabia, no Russian nationals were among the casualties. In March 2026, following the start of the US and Israeli military operation against Iran, Kadyrov had already expressed support for strikes on US military facilities in the Middle East. He described Iran’s retaliatory attacks on American bases as an ‘expected response to the enemy’, while also condemning strikes on civilian infrastructure in Arab countries of the Persian Gulf. According to Kadyrov, the US and Israel had deliberately provoked Iran into retaliatory action that drew other countries in the region into the conflict. On 8 April, Kadyrov commented on reports that Chechen units were prepared to deploy to Iran in the event of a possible US ground offensive. He said such a deployment could take place if Iran were fighting only the US and Israel. However, Tehran had also been striking Arab states, whose leaders Kadyrov described as his ‘brothers’. ‘Without a doubt, I support Iran’s side, with one “but”: I do not support Iranian strikes on civilian facilities and civilian infrastructure in the Arab countries of the Persian Gulf’, Kadyrov wrote. He stressed that he maintained relations with the leaders of the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, and Saudi Arabia. Russian officials have also condemned US and Israeli strikes on Iran while opposing attacks on Arab states. In early March, President Vladimir Putin offered to use Moscow’s relations with Tehran to help de-escalate the conflict during telephone conversations with leaders of Persian Gulf countries. Following a conversation with UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the Kremlin said Putin was prepared to convey the Emirates’ concerns over strikes on its territory to the Iranian leadership. The Russian president also called for a ceasefire and a return to diplomatic negotiations. On 11 March, Russia’s Permanent Representative to the UN, Vasily Nebenzya, said Moscow considered strikes on the territory of Arab countries in the Persian Gulf, particularly attacks on civilian infrastructure, unacceptable. However, he stressed that the situation could not be considered as a separate issue to what he described as ‘aggression’ by the US and Israel against Iran. Russia abstained from voting on a Bahraini draft resolution condemning Iranian strikes on countries in the region.

title: Eastern Equatoria deploys 1,722 vaccinators for polio campaign
body: Health authorities in Eastern Equatoria state have launched a four-day polio vaccination campaign, deploying 1,722 vaccinators to reach children across communities and prevent the disease, which can cause permanent paralysis. Vaccination teams are expected to visit households, schools, markets, churches and other public gathering places to ensure eligible children receive the vaccines. Speaking at the launch at Torit Freedom Square on Tuesday, Dr. Amin Gordiano, director general at the state Ministry of Health, said the campaign would deploy 1,722 vaccinators and 159 supervisors to improve immunization coverage. “No community is to be missed, and no child should be left behind,” Gordiano said, urging parents and communities to welcome vaccination teams into their homes. The campaign will use two oral vaccines: the novel oral polio vaccine type 2 (nOPV2), which targets poliovirus type 2, and the bivalent oral polio vaccine (bOPV), which protects against types 1 and 3. John Sokwarto, an Expanded Programme on Immunization representative in Eastern Equatoria, said teams would use a house-to-house approach, alongside temporary vaccination posts at markets and other public gathering places. Dr. Emmanuel Timothy, representing the World Health Organization (WHO), said reaching every eligible child would require joint efforts by health authorities, partners, parents and community leaders. He warned that children missed during vaccination campaigns could remain vulnerable to poliovirus infection and its potentially life-altering consequences. Opado Godfrey, a representative of Health Link South Sudan, said the government and communities are leading the campaign, with implementing partners supporting delivery at the grassroots level. Godfrey urged chiefs, religious leaders and other community representatives to help vaccination teams reach families, particularly in hard-to-reach areas. He also stressed the importance of accountability in vaccine distribution and administration, saying every dose given should be properly recorded. Osuru Peter, representing the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF), urged parents to ensure children aged zero to 59 months received the vaccine. He said polio had no cure but could be prevented through vaccination. Peter also called on community leaders to counter misinformation about immunization and encourage families to cooperate with health workers. Polio is a highly infectious disease that primarily affects children under five and can cause permanent paralysis. The post Eastern Equatoria deploys 1,722 vaccinators for polio campaign appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: IRGC has achieved more advanced weapons after 40-day war
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 14 (MNA) – A spokesperson for the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) on Wednesday said, “We have achieved more advanced weapons following the 40-day war of aggression imposed by the US against Iran.”
Speaking in an exclusive interview with an English language paper based in Tehran on Wednesday, Brigadier General Hossein Mohebbi has emphasized that the powerful Armed Forces of the country are fully prepared to respond to any potential aggression since the country has been equipped with more advanced weapons.
General Mohebbi did not rule out the possibility of a new war against Iran, stating, “Although initiating such a conflict would be irrational for the United States, the possibility remains as the Trump administration, according to his view, needs an achievement to show before the midterm elections.
Iran is prepared to respond to any renewed aggression with greater force than before, and the consequences of such an action for the United States would be "more painful.", he underlined.
The IRGC spokesman also lashed out at the media coverage of US foreign wars, stating, “His belief that the US’s public is not informed of the reality of these conflicts and that mainstream media conceal the truth about what it is termed "ruthless acts of aggression."
General Mohebbi dismissed statements raised by US officials regarding existence of gaps and a lack of cooperation among Iranian officials as "completely false," stating that these claims are made to justify Washington's failures in the war waged against Iran.
He also lashed out at the way the US public is informed about foreign wars, saying Americans are being kept from understanding the realities of their country’s military campaigns because mainstream media actively conceal the truth about such brutal acts of aggression.

title: Human trafficking: NAPTIP, ICMPD, ECOWAS move to tighten airport surveillance
body: By Matthew Johnson The National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP), the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) and the International Centre for Migration Policy Development (ICMPD) have called for stronger collaboration among aviation stakeholders to prevent human trafficking through Nigerian airports. The call was made on Tuesday, October 13, 2026, at a three-day awareness and sensitisation workshop for aviation stakeholders in Lagos. The workshop aimed to strengthen the implementation of the Trafficking in Persons (Control of Activities of Organisations and Centres) Regulations, 2019, and improve inter-agency cooperation in the fight against human trafficking. Speaking at the workshop, NAPTIP’s Director of Intelligence in charge of Research and Programme Development, Mr Josiah Emerole, who represented the agency’s Director-General, Binta Bello, said many stakeholders operating at airports did not fully understand their responsibilities under existing anti-trafficking laws. Emerole said the workshop was organised to equip airport personnel, labour recruiters, civil society organisations and other migration-sector actors with the knowledge needed to identify suspected trafficking victims and report suspicious activities. He explained that traffickers often presented their victims as ordinary passengers with apparently valid travel documents, making it necessary for frontline personnel to look beyond documentation and examine the circumstances surrounding their journeys. According to him, officers should be alert to inconsistencies in passengers’ travel plans, financial circumstances, destinations and explanations for travelling, as these could indicate possible exploitation. He said, “It is not just about looking at the person’s documents. It is a question of talking to the person, using some psychological and emotional strategies for the person to tell the truth.” Emerole noted that some victims were unaware of the exploitation awaiting them at their destinations, adding that timely intervention by airport personnel could prevent them from falling into the hands of traffickers. He said that although traffickers continued to exploit international airports, increased surveillance and awareness had contributed to a reduction in the use of Nigerian airports by some criminal networks, forcing them to explore alternative routes through other countries. He, however, stressed the need for sustained training and stronger cooperation among agencies to close existing gaps. Emerole disclosed that NAPTIP would establish a working group involving relevant stakeholders to coordinate activities and monitor progress through reports from agencies operating at different airports and other relevant data. He said, “I will say immigration officers, aviation personnel, labour recruiters and other stakeholders should understand their responsibilities under the Trafficking in Persons (Prohibition), Enforcement and Administration Act, 2015, and the 2019 regulations.” Also speaking, the Project Manager at ICMPD, Mr Matthias Esene, said the organisation was supporting Nigeria and other West African countries in strengthening migration management and preventing trafficking while protecting the right to freedom of movement. Esene, who represented the head of the organisation’s Nigeria office, said the workshop was supported through regional migration initiatives, including the Free Movement of Persons and Migration project, organised by ICMPD in collaboration with NAPTIP and funded by the European Union and the Kingdom of Denmark. He explained that ICMPD worked with government institutions and civil society organisations to improve their capacity to respond to migration-related challenges and strengthen cooperation among agencies responsible for protecting migrants. According to him, the 2019 regulations provide a framework for identifying trafficking-related indicators, referring suspected victims to appropriate services and providing psychosocial support. He said the challenge was to ensure that stakeholders understood and implemented the provisions effectively, particularly those relating to their individual responsibilities and cooperation with other agencies. He added that frontline officials were responsible for identifying vulnerable persons and suspected trafficking victims without unnecessarily restricting the movement of legitimate travellers. “Freedom of movement remains a right under the ECOWAS Protocol. Efforts to prevent trafficking should not undermine legitimate migration. “Freedom of movement is a right. Human trafficking is not something we appreciate,” Esene said. In his remarks, the ECOWAS Commission’s expert on anti-trafficking in persons and migration, Mr Osandu Ekeh, said trafficking remained a significant challenge in Nigeria and across West Africa, with criminal networks increasingly exploiting legitimate transport systems and travel services. Ekeh, who delivered remarks on behalf of the Acting Director of Humanitarian and Social Affairs at the ECOWAS Commission, Dr Mohamed Ibrahim, said the aviation sector was strategically positioned to help prevent, detect and report trafficking-related activities. He said the commission had been coordinating regional anti-trafficking interventions through its regional action plan covering 2018 to 2027. Ekeh explained that ECOWAS, its member states and ICMPD had also worked on initiatives to strengthen prevention, particularly in protecting women, children and other vulnerable groups from trafficking and related crimes. He said the commission had supported assistance programmes for trafficking victims, including medical care, psychological support, reintegration and vocational training. Ekeh emphasised that effective implementation of the 2019 regulations required greater awareness and cooperation among immigration officers, aviation personnel, travel agencies, labour recruiters, maritime regulators and other frontline actors. He urged participants to move beyond awareness creation and develop practical mechanisms for sharing information, identifying suspected cases and supporting victims. Similarly, Bamidele Jomole called for strict enforcement of the regulations and closer cooperation among aviation authorities, immigration, customs, labour and justice officials, as well as civil society organisations. Jomole said the participation of controllers from the country’s three international airports was a significant development in efforts to strengthen the fight against trafficking. He urged relevant authorities to verify that licensed labour recruitment agencies had the appropriate NAPTIP clearances and ensure that recruitment and travel arrangements complied with existing regulations. “The workshop should produce concrete commitments and a communiqué that would guide participating institutions in identifying loopholes exploited by traffickers and coordinating measures to close them,” Jomole said. Earlier, an ICMPD representative, Ifeoluwa Sinkaiye, said the workshop was designed to strengthen stakeholders’ understanding of trafficking trends, risk indicators and their respective obligations under existing laws. Sinkaiye said participants would examine relevant legal frameworks, discuss emerging trafficking methods and undertake practical exercises to improve coordination in responding to suspected cases. She explained that the programme would also produce recommendations and a communiqué to guide future interventions, while an evaluation would assess participants’ knowledge and readiness to apply what they had learnt. Sinkaiye urged stakeholders to translate the knowledge gained into practical action in their daily duties, noting that effective collaboration among agencies was essential to preventing trafficking and protecting vulnerable persons. The workshop brought together representatives of relevant government agencies, airport operators, labour recruitment organisations and other stakeholders from Lagos, Abuja, Kano, Ghana and other locations. The post Human trafficking: NAPTIP, ICMPD, ECOWAS move to tighten airport surveillance appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Iran tensions, Syria talks put Iraqi Kurdistan at the center of Middle Eastern diplomacy - analysis
body: The Kurdistan Region of northern Iraq has been playing an increasingly important role in reducing tensions in the region, often behind the scenes. At a 2026 MERI Forum conference in Erbil, several Kurdish leaders described recent initiatives that the region has undertaken.According to their remarks, the Kurdish leadership sought to navigate the recent conflict between the United States/Israel and Iran. Although the Kurdistan Region came under attack by over 1,000 Iranian missiles and drones, the Kurdish leaders sought to reach out to Iran and the US. They also worked to broker talks between Damascus and Kurds in eastern Syria.Who were the key leaders involved? Kurdistan Region President Nechirvan Barzani and Prime Minister Masrour Barzani have played a major role. Both men, related to each other, are leaders of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP). Additionally instrumental were members of the Talabani family, primarily Bafel and Qubad Talibani, from the rival Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) party.'We are part of the solution'“We are very pleased today to see that Kurds are part of the solution – whether in Syria, as marked by the presence of Comrade Mazloum [Abdi] here; or in Iraq, where we are part of the solution,” Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) Deputy Prime Minister Qubad Talabani said at the MERI Forum, according to Rudaw. Talabani explained that “Erbil expressed readiness to facilitate discussions between Kurds and the countries where they live in the Middle East, including in Iran.”He said, “We are very pleased today to see that Kurds are part of the solution, whether in Syria, as marked by the presence of Comrade Mazloum [Abdi] here, or in Iraq, where we are part of the solution.”Rudaw reported that Nechirvan Barzani had played a key role in talks in Syria and Turkey. He is a unique figure in Kurdish politics today because of his long experience and his ability to navigate the complex politics in Iran, Turkey, Syria, and Iraq.The Kurdistan Region is involved in a variety of talks, partly due to its geographic position. Northern Iraq borders Iran, Turkey, and Syria. It is a crossroads for various major regional policies.US forces were concentrated in the KRG before they left on September 30. Iran, as noted, has attacked the region 1,000 times, mainly targeting Kurdish Iranian opposition groups based in northern Iraq.Turkey is dealing with peace talks with the PKK, which also has forces in the KRG.With the US leaving Syria in 2025 and the US-backed Kurdish-led SDF expected to integrate with the new government in Damascus, the KRG sought to make sure Kurds would not be harmed in Syria.“As the political forces in the Kurdistan Region, we stand ready for any coordination and role assigned to us. Furthermore, the Kurdistan Region has significantly contributed to the advancement of the integration process of the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF), now absorbed into the Syrian state system,” Talabani said, according to Rudaw.SDF commander Mazloum Abdi praised the Kurdistan Region for its support. There are still many tensions in Syria, and the role of the KRG is likely not over.The Syrian Kurdish political authorities, the AANES, never built a prosperous region like the KRG. They were also linked to the YPG and the PKK, and therefore generally rivals of the KDP.When the chips were down, the Kurdish leadership in Erbil went to help Kurds in Syria, despite the politicians' past disagreements.Not everything has been smooth sailing.Barzani was critical of the Kurdish Iranian opposition groups, which have bases and camps in the KRG. Some of the Kurdish Iranian groups are closer to the KDP, aka PUK.However, Iran has made clear that it will continue its attacks until the KRG can assure Tehran that these groups are not a threat.In March, media reports suggested the US was willing to arm the Kurdish Iranian groups. The idea of American weapons moving through northern Iraq to Iran was certainly seen as a threat by Iran.“Rojhelat's [western Iran's Kurdish region] opposition forces, unfortunately, behaved very irresponsibly,” Barzani said at MERI. This was tough criticism for these groups.Barzani's comments shed light on the issues facing the Kurdish Iranian groupsThe Amargi, a local grassroots media network, noted that Barzani's comments shed light on the complexities the Kurdish Iranian groups have faced. There are at least six of these groups. The centrist KDPI and PAK, as well as the more left-leaning Komala and PJAK groups, with PJAK often seen as closely linked to the PKK. Another group, Khabat, is part of the Kurdish Iranian opposition alliance.The groups formed an alliance in January and February, shortly before the US and Israeli strikes began. Iran may have seen this development as alarming.Meanwhile, the parties had begun preparing. According to accounts circulating within their ranks, former Peshmerga fighters returned from abroad, while light weapons and vehicles were acquired.These preparations do not substantiate Trump's allegations that Kurds diverted or kept weapons intended for Iranian protesters. The parties concerned rejected those accusations, which have not been publicly substantiated,” The Amargi noted.“For some Iranian Kurds, including activists, party supporters, and observers, the 39-day war appeared to offer a long-awaited opportunity after what they considered a missed chance during the Jin, Jiyan, Azadi (“Women, Life, Freedom”) protests.“They hoped that a weakened regime would pave the way for a ground operation, but events did not unfold as they had expected,” it said.The Amargi added that “Iranian Kurdish parties explained their decision not to intervene by pointing to the absence of international guarantees and protection. Without air cover, external coordination, and a broader uprising in Iran, they feared that an operation would fail, leaving civilians exposed to retaliation.”Barzani's critique of the groups was not everything it appeared to be on the surface. His comments were aimed at reducing tensions with Tehran.As long as Iran believes that the KRG will rein in these groups, or at least prod them not to send forces over the border, the Islamic regime may reduce its attacks.A recent statement from KDPI, one of the Kurdish Iranian groups, also indicated that it would not send its forces over the border. It tends to be politically close to the KDP, and will not want to cause the KRG any trouble.KDPI members have resided in the Kurdistan Region for decades, and their facilities near Koya have been frequently targeted by Iran.The Iranian regime knows it can't eliminate the entire Kurdish opposition: It likely prefers the groups weakened and abroad to fighting in Iran. It is willing to wait and see whether the KRG can make sure the groups' activity is curtailed.Barzani's comments were aimed at reducing tensions with Tehran.

title: Latvia Formally Blacklists Russian Journalist Leonid Ragozin
body:
Latvian authorities have formally declared Riga-based Russian journalist Leonid Ragozin persona non grata, local media reported, and Ragozin himself confirmed on Wednesday.
Latvian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Līga Jermacāne told the outlet Delfi that an unidentified Russian national was added to the persona non grata list last Wednesday. Foreign Ministry adviser Toms Sadovskis said the basis for the decision will be withheld for “national security” reasons.
On Wednesday, Ragozin confirmed that he was notified of his expulsion the day before.
Ragozin claimed he was blacklisted in retaliation for his critical reporting and commentary on Western policy and far-right political networks.
He argued that Latvia intentionally declared him persona non grata to prevent him from appealing his expulsion in Latvian courts.
“For me it is a huge personal tragedy. I am being evicted from my only beloved home, deprived of my circle of friendship and support,” Ragozin posted on X.
In a Meduza interview published Tuesday, Ragozin said he was outside Latvia and expressed concerns that returning to Russia could put him at risk of imprisonment.
Ragozin is a former producer for the BBC Russian Service and editor at Russian Newsweek. His freelance commentary has appeared in recent editions of Al Jazeera, Jacobin and The American Conservative.
Ragozin drew public ire for comments he made on a far-left podcast where he argued that the Kremlin felt compelled to use “brute force” in response to Western encroachment on its sphere of influence.
In Wednesday’s X post, Ragozin said, “I condemn the Russian aggression and support Ukraine’s sovereignty.”
“But I’ll continue to criticize Western countries for mishandling this conflict,” he wrote.
In an August column for The American Conservative, Ragozin argued that ordinary Russians perceive greater threats from Western nations than from their own government.
Latvia has declared more than 150 Russian cultural figures, state journalists and commentators personae non grata since the start of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

title: F-35C Lands for the First Time on a Ford-Class Aircraft Carrier
body: An F-35C Lightning II made an arrested landing on the PCU John F. Kennedy (CVN 79), marking the first time an F-35C lands on a Ford-class aircraft carrier. The U.S. Navy has released photos of the first arrested landing of an F-35C Lightning II on the PCU (Pre-Commissioning Unit) John F. Kennedy (CVN 79). The operation, conducted on Oct. 13, 2026, marks the first time an F-35C lands on a Ford-class aircraft carrier, shortly after the Kennedy achieved preliminary acceptance by the service. The aircraft carrier is currently underway conducting Aircraft Compatibility Testing, which assesses the operational capabilities of the ship’s aircraft launch and recovery equipment with U.S. Navy aircraft. The Kennedy employs the Electromagnetic Aircraft Launch System (EMALS) catapults and the Advanced Arresting Gear (AAG) for launch and recovery, respectively. The F-35s employed in the test, part of the Patuxent River F-35 Integrated Test Force (ITF), are attached to the “Salty Dogs” of Air Test and Evaluation Squadron (VX) 23 . Two F-35s are visible in the images, with the second aircraft also carrying inert GBU-38 JDAM bombs as external stores. The Navy has not yet released details about the ACT campaign for the second Ford-class vessel. The USS Gerald R. Ford (CVN 78), the lead ship of the Ford class, completed ACT in January 2020 after 16 days at sea and the launch and recovery of 211 aircraft. A U.S. Navy F-35C Lightning II, attached to the “Salty Dogs” of Air Test and Evaluation Squadron (VX) 23, makes an arrested landing on the flight deck aboard PCU John F. Kennedy (CVN 79), marking the first time an F-35C lands on a Ford-class aircraft carrier. | Source: U.S. Navy photo by Mass Communication Specialist Seaman Kaitlyn Bailey It is unclear if the Kennedy’s ACT will be shorter, however it is likely to similarly conduct testing with all the aircraft types currently in service with the Navy. Notably, the F-35C was the only aircraft type that was not included in the ACT of the USS Ford, while the C-2 Greyhound will be the only aircraft tested on the USS Ford which will not be tested on the Kennedy as it was recently retired . PCU John F. Kennedy (CVN 79) The PCU (Pre-Commissioning Unit) John F. Kennedy (CVN 79) is currently completing the required testing ahead of the commissioning into the U.S. Navy, after which it will assume the designation USS (United States Ship), replacing the PCU designation. The aircraft carrier is scheduled for delivery to the Navy in March 2027. The ship set sail for the first time under its own power from the HII facility in Newport News, birthplace of all U.S. Navy nuclear aircraft carriers, on Jan. 28, 2026, after being laid down in 2015. The Kennedy took longer than Ford to be completed because of various delays which shifted the timelines, as well as a Congressional mandate to deliver the new ship with the modifications required to operate F-35C Lightning II fighters , which are missing on the Ford. The Kennedy incorporates some major design changes compared to the Ford, including the AN/SPY-6(V)3 radar, whose variants are being retrofitted on Flight III Arleigh Burke class guided missile destroyers and developed to equip the Navy’s newest frigates, aircraft carriers and amphibious warships. This replaces the AN/SPY-3 Multi-Function Radar (MFR) and AN/SPY-4 Volume Search Radar (VSR) combo carried by the Ford. Two F-35 test pilots from Air Test and Evaluation Squadron Two Three (VX-23), Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWCAD), fly F-35C Lightning II fighter aircraft to the PCU John F. Kennedy (CVN 79) in the Western Atlantic Oct. 13, 2026. | Source: F-35 Lightning II Pax River ITF/Dane Wiedmann Similarly to the Ford, the Kennedy will retain the Electromagnetic Aircraft Launch System (EMALS) catapults, Advanced Arresting Gear (AAG), and Advanced Weapons Elevator (AWE) weapons handling systems. While these systems have faced well-documented reliability and maintenance challenges , the Navy is working to fix the issues and improve the performance. “At 1,092 feet in length and 100,000 tons, CVN 79 incorporates more than 23 new technologies, comprising dramatic advances in propulsion, power generation, ordnance handling, and aircraft launch systems,” says the Navy on the Kennedy’s official page . “These innovations will support a 33% higher sortie generation rate at significant cost savings when compared to Nimitz-class carriers.” The service also explained the Gerald R. Ford class offers a reduction of approximately $4 billion per ship ( a second page mentions over $5 billion) in life cycle operations and support costs during its 50-year service life, compared to the earlier Nimitz class. For comparison, the Navy said the total ownership cost for a Nimitz-class ship is $32.1 billion in FY 04 constant year dollars, and the total ownership cost for a Ford-class carrier is expected to be $26.8 billion, half of which is allocated to the direct and indirect costs of manpower for operations and maintenance of the ship. After entering service, the Kennedy is due to be homeported at Naval Base Kitsap-Bremerton in the state of Washington. This will make it the first Ford-class aircraft carrier based on the U.S. West Coast. An F-35 test pilot from Air Test and Evaluation Squadron Two Three (VX-23), Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWCAD), flies an F-35C Lightning II fighter aircraft to the PCU John F. Kennedy (CVN 79) in the Western Atlantic Oct. 13, 2026. | Source: F-35 Lightning II Pax River ITF/Dane Wiedmann

title: Canada’s Dominion Dynamics, Ukraine’s TENCORE Sign Deal to Build TerMIT Ground Vehicles in Canada
body:
Canadian defense technology company Dominion Dynamics and Ukraine’s TENCORE signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) to manufacture TerMIT unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs) in Canada, with initial production targeted for 2027, according to the press release.
TENCORE is a leading Ukrainian developer and serial manufacturer of UGVs for military and dual-use applications. Since the start of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine, the company has delivered over 4,000 robotic platforms to Ukraine’s Armed Forces (AFU), actively deployed across more than 50 combat brigades.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“The biggest lesson from Ukraine is speed. Battlefield requirements change in weeks, so production, operational feedback, and engineering have to run as a loop: build, deploy, learn, change, scale. Canada gives us the manufacturing base, suppliers, and reliable power to run that loop alongside allies who need these vehicles,” the press release quoted TENCORE co-founder Roman Tkachenko.
The MOU, signed at the Canadian Pavilion during the AUSA 2026 defense conference in Washington, also provides for integrating AuraNet, Dominion’s autonomy stack for pan-domain command and control, as the onboard intelligence layer for TerMIT. Nadia Theodore, Canada’s deputy ambassador to the US, attended the signing ceremony.
“Canada has the workforce and the suppliers to build at scale. This agreement is how two companies start turning that commitment into vehicles, and we intend to move fast,” the press release quoted Eliot Pence, founder and CEO of Dominion Dynamics.
The deal follows a joint declaration on defense cooperation that Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and President Volodymyr Zelensky signed in September. Both countries committed to manufacturing thousands of battle-tested drones and unmanned systems in the next two years, with one-third earmarked for Ukraine’s defense, the companies wrote.
The partnership will support the deployment and continued development of AuraNet for Ukraine’s front lines, according to the press release. It will also create high-skilled jobs in Canada and strengthen the country’s sovereign defense technology base.
Dominion plans to manufacture TerMIT in Canadian facilities. A TENCORE team will lead the initial technology transfer and train technicians in Canada to build the UGV, the companies wrote. Since 2024, TENCORE has delivered more than 5,000 UGVs to Ukrainian military units, the press release says.
Dominion also aims to develop an Arctic-hardened TerMIT for Canadian operations and for export to NATO allies. The companies will continue to work toward definitive agreements.
Dominion Dynamics was founded in 2025 and builds autonomy, sensing, and command-and-control systems. According to them, it has deployed its technology with the Canadian Armed Forces across the High North.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Unlike US, EU doing everything to prolong war in Ukraine — Kremlin spokesman
body:
MOSCOW, October 14. /TASS/. European countries, unlike the United States, which is seeking a peaceful solution, are doing everything they can to prolong the hostilities in Ukraine, Kremlin Spokesman Dmitry Peskov said at a briefing ahead of a cybersecurity meeting with the Russian president.
"Europeans are taking a different approach: they are doing everything they can to ensure that this war continues," he said.
"Sabotage [of a settlement in Ukraine] by the Europeans is possible," he added.

title: Russian forces destroy railway infrastructure facility in Vinnytsia region
body:
A railway infrastructure facility sustained significant damage in a Russian strike overnight into Wednesday in the Zhmerynka district of Vinnytsia region, Vinnytsia Regional Military Administration head Natalia Zabolotna said.

"A large-scale fire broke out. Work at the site was complicated by repeated threats of UAV and ballistic missile strikes. Because of the danger, rescuers had to suspend efforts to deal with the aftermath and resume work after the all-clear. All fires have now been extinguished. There were no fatalities or injuries, " Zabolotna said on Telegram.

She did not specify which facility was hit or in which settlement of the district it was located.

Ukrainian Prime Minister Serhiy Koretsky earlier said Russian forces had struck railway facilities in five regions of Ukraine overnight into Wednesday, but “thanks to advance evacuation, no one was injured.”

title: 2028 Olympic Games qualification ‘really tough’ – Black Queens coach Björkegren
body: Black Queens head coach Lars Kim Björkegren has described the path to qualifying for the 2028 Olympic Games as “really tough” but says he “believe[s] in the girls” to get the job done. Having received a bye in the first preliminary round of the qualifiers, the Queens dispatched Mauritius 10-0 to progress to the next phase. The senior women’s national team will face Zambia in the third round, scheduled for 23 February to 6 March 2027. A total of 16 nations will compete in the third round of the African qualifiers, with the continent having just two slots at the global showpiece. “We have the potential to go all the way,” Björkegren said. “In football, there is no easy game, especially when it comes to qualifying for the Olympics, as only two countries from Africa will go to Los Angeles. “It is really tough and to get there, we need to win. I believe in the girls and I think we [will] be there.” The Black Queens have never qualified for the Olympic Games in the country’s history.

title: Top court brands 'Community of Batal Hajji Belkhoroev’s followers' as terrorist group
body:
MOSCOW, October 14. /TASS/. Russia’s Supreme Court has recognized the international organization "Community of Followers of Batal Hajji Belkhoroev - Batalhadzhins" as a terrorist organization, banning its activities on Russia’s territory.
The court granted the application of the Prosecutor General’s Office, a TASS correspondent reported from the courtroom.
"The Supreme Court of Russia has decided to grant the application, to recognize the organization "Community of Followers of Batal Hajji Belkhoroev - Batalhadzhins" as a terrorist organization and to ban its activities on Russian territory," the judge announced.
The court’s decision enters into force immediately.

title: You can’t add senior discount on top of other deals – SC
body: MANILA, Philippines – The Supreme Court ruled on Wednesday, October 14, that a senior citizen’s discount cannot be availed of by consumers simultaneously with other discounts. “The SC explained that senior citizen discounts cannot be combined with other discounts. When goods or services are offered at promotional prices, senior citizens may choose either the promotional discount or the 20% senior citizen discount, whichever gives them greater savings,” the High Court said in its decision . “Granting an additional discount beyond what the law allows would unfairly benefit the customer at the business’s expense,” it added. In its decision, the High Court said that while Republic Act No. 7432 or the Senior Citizens Act protects and supports senior citizens, the law’s implementation must be fair and reasonable to businesses. Under the law, Filipinos aged 60 and above are entitled to benefits and privileges, including 20% discount on services like hotel, restaurants, and recreation centers. “[The] State’s pursuit of public welfare cannot be allowed to impose undue or confiscatory burdens on private establishments, whose continued viability is essential to the long-term effectiveness of the law,” the SC said. The case stemmed from a case filed against a certain Orville Ong, general manager of a hotel in Bacolod City, for alleged violation of the Senior Citizens Act, as amended. The High Court acquitted Ong in the said case after he was charged for refusing to grant a senior discount to hotel guests Paul Alcazaren and Eric Gadiana. In his case, Ong argued that the hotel already applied a 20% discount on the room rate for the Cebu Bikers Club. Alcazaren and Gadiana are members of this group. Ong was later found guilty by the Municipal Trial Court in Cities, Regional Trial Court, and the Court of Appeals. But the High Court reversed the rulings, explaining that the guests already received a 20% discount through the club’s negotiated rater. Therefore, the hotel was not obliged to give an additional 20% discount. – Rappler.com

title: GRFU, GOC Women’s Commission hold breast cancer awareness, expresses gratitude to Sunda International Ghana
body: The Ghana Rugby Football Union (GRFU), in collaboration with the Women’s Commission of the Ghana Olympic Committee (GOC), has held a breast cancer awareness education programme for female athletes, coaches, officials and community members. The initiative focused on the importance of early detection, regular self-examination and screening in the prevention and management of breast cancer. The organisers said the programme was aimed at improving awareness among women involved in sports and encouraging them to take early action when they notice potential symptoms. President of the Ghana Rugby Football Union expressed appreciation to Sunda International Ghana Ltd, makers of Softcare, for supporting the initiative. “Breast cancer affects all women, including our athletes,” the President said. The President said the partnership had helped educate and encourage participants to pay greater attention to their health. The GRFU and the GOC Women’s Commission said they remained committed to promoting women’s health, safety and well-being through sports. They also thanked Sunda International Ghana for its support towards the breast cancer awareness activities. Credit: Ghana Rugby Football Union

title: Polish FM responds to Musk over Starlink slowdown in Ukraine: European customers watching you
body:
Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski said he was watching the actions of SpaceX owner Elon Musk following reports that the speed of Starlink satellite communications terminals in Ukraine had been restricted overnight into Wednesday.
"Hey, Elon Musk, big man, are you playing politics with your products again? As your European customers, we are watching you, " Sikorski said on X on Wednesday.
Poland continues to finance the operation of more than 29,000 Starlink satellite communications terminals in Ukraine.
Ukrainian presidential adviser Serhiy Flash Beskrestnov earlier said SpaceX had restricted the speed of Starlink terminals while in motion, disrupting a number of missions.
"At present, the restriction applies to the StarShield ‘military package’ of services and is set at 100 miles per hour. Our defense forces were not warned about this restriction, and this disrupted a number of missions, " Beskrestnov said on Telegram.
Beskrestnov said it was obvious that the restriction could not be a coincidence and was linked "to the current political situation. "
Former Ukrainian Defense Ministry adviser and volunteer Serhiy Sternenko also confirmed the information, citing military personnel.
"Reports are coming in from the military that restrictions on the use of Starlink satellite communications terminals by our operators have just been tightened. The speed at which communications begin to disappear is 60-70 km/h, " Sternenko said.
Musk earlier denied Ukraine the possibility of using Starlink satellite Internet for strikes on Russian territory, saying it was time for Ukraine to reach a peace agreement with Russia. At the same time, a bipartisan U.S. congressional delegation that visited Kyiv in October called for expanding Ukraine’s access to Starlink to help counter Russian aggression.
Earlier, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said work was underway on a satellite system similar to Starlink.
In August, Sikorski threatened to review Poland’s spending on Starlink satellite communications, namely the nearly $50 million a year the country spends on Starlink terminals for Ukraine. He made the statement in response to Starlink’s decision to exclude Poland from the common European roaming zone covering more than 30 countries, including Germany, the Czech Republic, Slovakia and Lithuania, where users can move terminals between countries without additional restrictions on international use.
This is not the first dispute between Sikorski and Musk over Starlink. Last year, Musk told the Polish minister to “be quiet, small man” after Sikorski warned that Warsaw might seek alternative providers for the satellite service it finances for Ukraine.

title: SpaceX limits Starlink operations in Ukraine, disrupting military ops., missile defense capability
body: SpaceX has placed a limit on some Starlink services in Ukraine, stopping the operation of its military-grade version for vehicles moving above 100 miles per hour (160 km/h), disrupting combat missions, Presidential Adviser Serhiy Beskrestnov said on Wednesday.“Our defense forces did not receive a warning about this limitation, and this led to the disruption of several missions,” he wrote on Telegram, adding: “It is clear that this action is not coincidental and is related to the current political situation.”A Ukrainian official told The Jerusalem Post that Starlink internet speeds in Ukraine dropped further on Wednesday evening, to 60–80 km/h.Ukrainian officials fear the move was made at Trump's requestUkraine's security services detected disruptions to Starlink terminals across the country overnight on Tuesday night, a source familiar with the matter confirmed to the Post. Ukrainian officials fear the move by the company, owned by Elon Musk, may have been made at the request of US President Donald Trump.Starlink terminals are one of the key tools enabling Ukrainians to maintain internet access amid Russia's invasion. The disruptions reportedly interfered with several critical operations.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said in a social media post that Ukraine had not received an alert about incoming Russian strikes. “This is already the second time this has happened,” Zelensky wrote.“During the first wave of drone and missile strikes, no warning was received, but an alert was issued during the second wave,” a source familiar with the matter added in a statement to the Post.Trump himself claimed on Tuesday that the United States had not halted intelligence-sharing cooperation with Ukraine. “We are helping them, and we are sharing intel,” Trump told reporters. “We want the war to end, so we're working with them and Russia on getting the war to end.”Zelensky said Russia launched 39 ballistic missiles and more than 120 drones overnight on Tuesday night, targeting energy facilities and critical infrastructure across Ukraine. According to the Ukrainian president, approximately 500,000 people were left without electricity following the attack.Ukrainian negotiators traveled to the US on Friday and Saturday to urge US President Donald Trump to increase sanctions pressure on Russia.Zelensky accuses US of inaction as Russian strikes kill over 70 in two daysUkrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky accused the US of being unwilling to help Ukraine after a Russian bomb attack on Thursday killed at least 35 people in the east, sending the two-day death toll from Russian strikes to over 70.Hours after the strike on the embattled city of Kramatorsk tore through two buses, Zelensky criticized Washington's effort to pursue economic ties with Russia while also seeking to mediate the more than four-year war.Speaking to reporters in Pryluky, the Ukrainian leader urged the US to accede to his requests to expand Ukraine's access to the Starlink satellite service to help it target Russian ballistic-missile launchers.“Open Starlink for Ukraine. You did open it when you were responding to Iran ... I've said quite openly — give it to us, help us defend our skies and dominate there. And then Putin will sit down at the negotiating table,” he said in an emotional statement.Ukraine has in recent months aimed to wrest the battlefield initiative from Russia, whose gains have slowed this year, but is still suffering from Moscow's increasingly brutal air war.“So where's the truth here, where's the honesty? Where's the stalemate? ... That's called unwillingness,” he said, referring to US Secretary of State Marco Rubio's assertion earlier on Thursday that the war is at a stalemate and that the United States would keep working toward a settlement.“One cannot, on the one hand, negotiate with the Russians about future economic projects, whilst on the other hand say that we find ourselves in some sort of ... diplomatic stalemate,” Zelensky added.

title: Opinion | SPLM’s election preparations: Political drama or a genuine democratic exercise? (Part 2 of 2)
body: Confidence in Victory: Performance or Institutional Influence? The SPLM appears confident that it will win the elections. However, its critics argue that this confidence rests less on its achievements since it began governing Southern Sudan in 2005 than on its influence over institutions that are supposed to serve the public impartially and independently. The concern is that the Political Parties Council, the National Elections Commission, and the security sector may be used to preserve the SPLM’s hold on power rather than guarantee fair political competition. These allegations strike at the heart of public confidence in the electoral process. Institutions entrusted with regulating political parties, administering elections, and protecting citizens must serve the country rather than the political interests of those in power. Their legitimacy depends on their ability to demonstrate independence through their decisions and conduct. The ruling party should seek a renewed mandate by presenting its achievements, acknowledging its failures, and explaining how it intends to address them. Confidence in victory should come from public trust, not from the belief that competitors cannot challenge the ruling party effectively. The Danger of Recycling Political Elites Recycling political elites within the SPLM through elections that lack genuine competition will not resolve South Sudan’s underlying governance problems. Instead, it will allow the same leadership to remain in power without adequately accounting for its record. The danger extends beyond party politics. Preserving political power while leaving governance failures unaddressed threatens the national interest, weakens public confidence, and raises concerns about national security and South Sudan’s future as a nation. Elections should provide an opportunity to assess leadership and demand accountability. They should not become political theatre through which existing elites renew their positions while citizens continue to face insecurity, unpaid salaries, displacement, inadequate services, and unfulfilled development promises. The fundamental test is whether the electoral process gives citizens a meaningful opportunity to reward good performance, reject failure, and choose a political alternative. The issue is not the existence of the SPLM as a political organisation, but whether its leadership has implemented its stated objectives and translated them into tangible improvements in people’s lives. Similarly, the central concern is not simply that one political party dominates the government. It is why its leaders have failed to implement national strategic plans and why questions continue to arise about their respect for national and state constitutions and laws. The debate must therefore move beyond the question of who occupies public office to examine how public authority is exercised. Do leaders honour their commitments? Do they implement development plans? Do they respect legal obligations and manage public resources in the national interest? At the heart of these questions lies accountability. Neither a political party’s historical role nor its continued dominance can substitute for responsible governance and measurable results. The SPLM’s stated objectives should serve as a standard against which its leadership is assessed, rather than merely as political language used to justify its continued rule. Lessons from China and the Gulf Monarchies Comparisons with China and the Arab Gulf countries illustrate the argument that political continuity, in itself, is not necessarily the central problem. China’s one-party system and the ruling-family systems of Gulf monarchies are often cited as examples of development under concentrated political authority. Why, then, does the SPLM not seek to learn from the development experience of the Communist Party of China? If one political family aspires to dominate South Sudan’s political future, why not study the governing and development experience of Saudi Arabia’s royal family? The purpose of these comparisons is not to argue that South Sudan should adopt either system. Rather, it is to question why those seeking continued political control do not demonstrate a corresponding commitment to effective governance, service delivery, and the achievement of national development objectives. Citizens judge leadership by what it delivers, not merely by the identity of those in power. The argument is that functioning public services and tangible development may matter more to citizens than the political labels under which they are governed. However, political continuity cannot, by itself, justify poor performance. Those seeking to remain in power must accept the obligations that accompany authority: respect for the law, responsible management of public resources, and sustained efforts to improve people’s lives. Elections Must Serve the National Interest The SPLM’s election preparations should be judged by more than the collection of nomination fees or the selection of party candidates. The real test is whether the process enables peaceful competition, meaningful political participation, and a credible expression of the people’s will. The memory of the 2010 elections makes institutional impartiality particularly important. Unresolved questions concerning salaries, insecurity, public revenues, infrastructure, displacement, national unity, and implementation of the peace agreement make scrutiny of the government’s record equally necessary. An election campaign should not merely provide an opportunity to renew promises or exchange political slogans. It should offer a platform for reviewing leadership performance, holding officials accountable, discussing national priorities, and presenting practical programmes that respond to citizens’ needs. Accordingly, the SPLM and its candidates must provide clear answers about past failures and identify measurable commitments for the future. Electoral and security institutions also have a responsibility to guarantee a level playing field, protect political rights, and respect the will of the electorate. The question is: Will the coming elections provide a genuine opportunity for democratic change and national accountability, or will they become a political drama designed to reproduce the existing ruling elites? The answer will not be determined by the number of nomination forms sold or the number of candidates competing for the SPLM’s internal nominations. It will depend on the integrity of the electoral process, the freedom of citizens to participate, the ability of voters to choose their leaders without fear or coercion, and the willingness of those in power to provide an honest account of their performance. South Sudan’s future should not be reduced to a struggle among political elites for public office. It must be linked to building a state that respects the law, protects its citizens, manages its resources responsibly, delivers peace and development, and ensures that public authority is a means of serving the people rather than an end in itself. Genuine democratic elections are not measured merely by whether they take place. They are measured by their ability to empower citizens to make free choices, hold leaders accountable, and bring about peaceful political change when those in office fail to fulfil their obligations. South Sudan’s national interest demands that elections become a means of renewing political legitimacy through performance and accountability, rather than an instrument for reproducing existing power structures without meaningful change. The writer, William Sunday D. Tor , is a political and social researcher and currently a Lecturer of Security Studies, International Development, and Regional Planning at Starford International University, Juba. (Part 2 of 2) appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Russian jet-powered Shahed drone strikes civilian infrastructure in Lutsk, injuring six
body:
