title: US decries 'embarrassing' case against Lebanese envoy over contact with Israel
body: The US government has criticised Lebanon's handling of a complaint filed against the Lebanese ambassador to Washington, Nada Moawad. The case stems from contact the envoy made with Israel's ambassador to Washington, Yechiel Leiter, to inquire about his son, who was critically injured in a car-ramming attack at a checkpoint in the occupied West Bank. A representative said the US State Department was aware of the complaint lodged by Hassan Adel Bazzi, whom Washington described as a “pro-Hezbollah lawyer”. The State Department said it was “embarrassing” that Lebanon's military court was handling the case. The US government, along with Israel, has exerted intense pressure on Lebanon to disarm Hezbollah, the influential Iran-backed Lebanese political party and armed group. Lebanon’s public prosecutor referred the complaint to the government commissioner to the military court, a procedural step that does not itself constitute a prosecution or referral for investigation, according to Lebanese media. The two ambassadors have been at the forefront of direct negotiations between Israel and Lebanon, which have technically been in a state of war since 1948. The talks were supposed to pave the way for Israel's withdrawal from south Lebanon and the disarmament of Hezbollah , two goals that have been almost entirely unsuccessful. Some in Lebanon, including Hezbollah and its supporters, have been deeply critical of the government for engaging in negotiations with Israel and the agreements reached as a result of those talks. “The Lebanese military judiciary should use its limited resources to prosecute Hezbollah operatives plotting against the Lebanese government and people instead of those working on their behalf,” the State Department said. “Laws and practices that enable this kind of politicised targeting of civilians and diplomats, while systematically shielding Hezbollah operatives, must be repealed. We have no patience for obstruction.” While Ms Moawad and the Lebanese government have not officially commented on the complaint, she has received backing from her supporters and Hezbollah critics. Michel Moawad, a member of parliament who is unrelated to the ambassador, described it as an “empty complaint” of a kind “that was routinely referred to the military court”. He called for an end to “using the judiciary as a tool for domination, intimidation, and settling political scores”. Lebanon's military court has in the past been accused of being influenced by Hezbollah. The court is investigating two men whose vehicle was stopped last week with half a tonne of explosives bound for Beirut's southern suburbs, where Hezbollah holds sway.

title: Ecology trail to Olor Waterfall opened near Putorana Plateau in Krasnoyarsk Region
body:
KRASNOYARSK, October 14. /TASS/. An ecology trail leading to the Olor Waterfall in the Putorana Plateau foothills opened in Taymyr. While walking along the trail, visitors will be able to see various representatives of the northern flora and fauna, press service of the Expert Center at the Arctic Development Project Office (PORA) told TASS.
"The Five Ethnic Groups of Taymyr ecological trail has been opened," the press service said. "It leads to the Olor Waterfall on the Kharayelakh Range slopes, in the foothills of the Putorana Plateau."
"The name - Five Ethnic Groups of Taymyr - refers to the peninsula's five indigenous peoples - the Dolgans, Nganasans, Ents, Nenets, and Evenks," the press service continued. "Wooden sculptures about four meters high, created with traditional ornaments and symbols, are dedicated to their cultural heritage."
As the number of tourists has been growing over recent years, on the peninsula appeared natural trails, bonfires, debris and damage to vegetation - right in the direction to the Olor waterfall, the Expert Center said. The new ecology trail with an entrance group, navigation poles, information stands and themed art objects will guide visitors along an organized route.
According to the organizers, while walking along the new trail, visitors will be able to see rare representatives of the northern fauna, for example, gyrfalcon, peregrine falcon, white-billed loon and tundra swan. Special attention is paid to mosses, lichens and other plants that are sensitive to trampling.
"The development of tourism in the Arctic should not conflict with objectives to preserve its unique nature. Right on the contrary, a properly-organized tourist flow can reduce the burden on the fragile northern ecosystems, and at the same time it can make natural attractions more accessible. The ecology trail to the Olor Waterfall is a good example of this approach," Maxim Dankin, Director General of the PORA Expert Center and a member of the Russian Federation's Civic Chamber, said commenting on the event.
At the ceremonial opening of the trail, representatives of Taymyr's low-numbered indigenous peoples conducted the sacred Dolgan ceremony, dubbed "Alastyr", which included the symbolic purification of the sculptures with the smoke of rosemary and juniper - for good luck, they said.

title: A UAF turned RCE
body:
In the curl 8.23.0 release we shipped a fix for one of the worst vulnerabilities in curl in a long time. We grade it severity HIGH. It is known as CVE-2026-92392 with the title HTTP/2 upload Use-After-Free .
This post explains the bug, what the problem can lead to, and something about why it happened and what we have done to make it harder to introduce a problem like this in curl again in the future.
This is a much simplified explanation. Please refer to the original report for all the details and the full reproducible Docker image for all the low-level fun and education you could possibly want. I highly recommend doing that; the report and the reproducible are awesome.
It is a use-after-free , which is a classic problem in memory-unsafe programming languages, like C, where we erroneously have a lingering pointer left, pointing to memory that is already freed, and yet we use that pointer and the memory it points to.
This family of errors is especially bad when a malicious actor can affect the content that gets stored into that memory area that is still used even though it was freed. Tricking the program to do something unintended.
This problem involves HTTP/2. HTTP/2 is a multiplexed protocol, meaning that it handles multiple logical transfers over the same physical connection. curl needs to keep track of a number of transfers at the same time, and when data arrives or is to be sent off, it needs to keep things apart appropriately.
For every transfer done using libcurl, the application creates and sets up a dedicated handle . We call it an easy handle . This handle is kept around for as long as the transfer is in progress, and the application can close and free it once the operation is completed. When doing multiple transfers, multiple handles are used.
libcurl also has multi handles , which is a super handle type that holds any amount of easy handles . This handle, and the corresponding multi interface, makes it possible to drive any amount of concurrent transfers. A transfer done with libcurl always has at least one multi handle and one easy handle. (Sometimes the multi handle is hiddenly used under the hood.)
In order to trigger this problem, we need an application (such as the curl command line tool) to do an upload over HTTP/2 to a server. By default, libcurl negotiates HTTP/2 when a HTTPS:// URLs is used and the server agrees.
When the upload has started, the server pauses the send by zeroing the HTTP/2 window size, returns a piece of the response and then it resets the stream, which shuts down the transfer – but not the connection. curl then correctly pulls down the entire transfer, but it accidentally leaves a lingering pointer to the involved easy handle .
When the application finds out that the transfer completed (with an error), it subsequently frees the easy handle and then, and here comes the problematic part: cleans up the multi handle.
At this point, the easy handle was just freed but there is still a reference to that handle. When libcurl shuts down the multi handle, it misunderstands the situation, allocates memory to download data into, finds the still dangling pointer and manages to download data from the server that ends up in the very same memory previously used for the easy handle.
In this process, it sends off a request that leaks internal client details, which includes information about local addresses, which is crucial. Modern operating systems use Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR), so a server needs this clue in order to generate a good attack payload.
Subsequently, when libcurl deals with this received data (using the handle the dangling pointer points to) in the download buffer, it uses a function pointer that now has been modified by data just downloaded from the server, and then it runs remote code .
Here’s a simplified 6-step illustration.
In order to actually successfully execute remote code, lots of several specific conditions need to be met and we deem it extremely difficult to meet these requirements in the wild, which is why we decided this is “only” severity HIGH and not CRITICAL.
The most likely outcome of an attempted attack is rather just a crash. We estimate that the chance for a successful attack is slim.
This problem was found and reported by Luna Tong at Anthropic using their new OSS Scanner. Presumably this involves their AI models.
In general we have over the last few years been working on reducing the amount of internal pointers to handles that needs to be correct, and instead we store transfer identifiers that we look-up on demand. While this is a tiny bit slower, it is more foolproof when there are logical mistakes like the one mentioned here.
We also of course continue to add more tests and we verify the code with more tools and analyzers in order to find additional similar mistakes.
Multiplexed protocols like HTTP/2 have this challenge that there are many concurrent transfers going and they all have different life-times and with memory-unsafe languages, dangling pointer mistakes can indeed be fatal.
This is of course no guarantee that we do not have or will not introduce another use-after-free in the code now or later.
libcurl is written in C – a memory unsafe language. With a memory-safe language, this mistake could probably have been avoided.
We have worked on curl for almost thirty years, and have over this time manage to make a rather polished transfer engine. For the longest time there really was no memory-safe alternative that also allowed libcurl to be a low-level library available on hundreds of operating systems and several dozen CPU architectures. It even barely exist alternatives now.
We do not rewrite curl. Not into another language but also not in C. We are set to iterate, polish, improve, refactor over and over until the end of time.
Porting curl to another language (like rust) would be a monstrous undertaking that would be slow and introduce lots of new short to medium term problems. Not to mention that the existing curl team is not rust experts and that libcurl is currently portable to many more platforms and environments than rust itself is.
When this vulnerability was confirmed by the curl security team just hours after it was submitted to us on September 15. We immediately realized the significance and decided to rush the pending next release. However, we still wanted to be careful, follow the procedures and not create any further problems or mistakes by stressing it too much. That’s how we ended up just shortening the release cycle with two weeks. Down from eight to six weeks from the previous release. This allowed us to also merge and fix many more vulnerabilities and general bugs in the same release.
We never provide CVSS for our published vulnerabilities as we don’t think we can do a job there. Others will provide them even for our flaws.

title: Yakutia's experts to study how regulated reindeer grazing affects permafrost preservation
body:
YAKUTSK, October 14. /TASS/. Experts will study the role of reindeer grazing in permafrost preservation and in prevention of carbon dioxide and methane emissions in the Arctic. The study will be conducted under an agreement signed in Yakutsk at the Northern Sustainable Development Forum, Maxim Dankin, Director General of the Expert Center - Project Office for the Development of the Arctic (PORA), posted on Telegram.
"We are beginning our second voluntary climate project, for which we have chosen the Primorskiy reindeer breeding farm in the Bulunsky District," he wrote. "In August, together with the region's Arctic Research Center, we conducted an expedition and began preparations. The project is based on the idea of preserving permafrost through regulated reindeer grazing."
The project's goal, he continued, is to prevent carbon dioxide and methane emissions, additional carbon uptake by vegetation, and the task is to create a working model in Yakutia that could be replicated in other Arctic regions.
Animals affect the moss cover, contributing to the grassy vegetation development, and in winter they compact the snow, he said. This, in turn, allows the cold to penetrate deeper into the soil, slowing down the permafrost thawing and the stored carbon release. "The Arctic has been warming up 3-4 times faster than the rest of the planet. The permafrost degradation threatens infrastructures, leads to additional greenhouse gas emissions, and endangers the traditional way of life of the North's indigenous peoples," he explained. "Most revenues from the possible sale of carbon units will remain in the farm, to be directed to its development and to support for the indigenous people's traditional way of life."
The PORA Expert Center already has experience in implementing the first forest climate project in the Arctic, on the Yamal Peninsula. The project has been validated and right now it is at the stage of carbon units' registration.
According to Mikhail Zheleznyak, director of the Melnikov Permafrost Institute (the Russian Academy of Sciences' Siberian Branch), in Central Yakutia, the temperature varies depending on landscape conditions, and the soil temperature at a depth of 3-3.5 m varies towards warming at the depth of the seasonal thawing layer. In some woodlands, this difference over 50 years has reached 0.3 degrees, and there are areas where this temperature has changed by 2 degrees. "There are territories where the surface has thawed or sunk to almost three meters over 50 years," he told participants in a round table discussion - "From Yakutsk to Antalya: Forming a unified Arctic voice for COP31." "We are talking about a very complex system. Can it be predicted? Of course it can. What is missing? We need to know the trend."
The permafrost degradation process has points of no return, and permafrost has never been stable or permanent, the scientist said. "If we are talking about engineering structures for thousands of years to come, this is one aspect, but if we are speaking about a hundred years, then we can manage it. We must learn to manage it and to be building facilities properly. The problem is only with us. We need good design solutions and we need to know how the changes are developing. That is, we are missing an observation network."
The 7th Northern Sustainable Development Forum took place in Yakutsk on October 7-10. Human capital development in the artificial intelligence era was the event's key topic. The forum featured participants from Russia's 20 regions and from twelve countries.

title: Operation Vivaldi: Ukrainian Defence Forces liberate three more settlements in Donetsk region
body:
Ukrinform reports this, citing a Facebook post by the Third Army Corps.
According to Brigadier General Andrii Biletskyi, the Third Army Corps and attached units liberated three more settlements: Zelena Dolyna, Lypove, and Kolodiazi. During the fourth phase of Operation Vivaldi, Russian forces lost approximately 3,000 soldiers, while Ukraine regained control of 101 square kilometres of territory.
The operation, which began with the elimination of Russian infiltration, developed into a rapid, large-scale offensive. Disoriented Russian forces began losing control of their units, triggering widespread chaos.
"We prevented the enemy from outflanking the Sloviansk–Kramatorsk agglomeration and encircling it, and we also secured the Kharkiv–Sloviansk highway. The enemy failed to cut off a key logistical artery serving our forces in the Donbas. We disrupted the offensive by the Zapad (West) grouping and forced it to redeploy some units of the 1st Tank Army, which eased the pressure on Kupiansk-Vuzlovyi," Biletskyi said.
According to him, "over the entire course of the operation, we have brought 16 settlements fully back under Ukrainian control and liberated 277 square kilometres. Enemy losses amount to 8,000 soldiers."
As Ukrinform previously reported, the third phase of Operation Vivaldi concluded in late September with the liberation of Nove, Ridkodub, and Katerynivka, and the restoration of Ukrainian control over Karpivka and Novomykhailivka.

title: GoldBod targets 150 hectares of forest reclamation in 2027
body: The Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) is targeting the reclamation of an additional 150 hectares of degraded forest land in 2027 as part of efforts to restore areas damaged by illegal mining, popularly known as galamsey. The initiative, being undertaken in partnership with the Ghana Armed Forces and the Forestry Commission, has already seen reclamation works covering 80 hectares begin this year. GoldBod said the programme would be expanded next year to cover 150 hectares across 30 forest reserves as part of efforts to restore degraded landscapes. In a Facebook post on Wednesday, October 14, the Board emphasised the need to balance Ghana’s gold production ambitions with environmental protection, insisting that the economic benefits of gold must not come at the expense of the country’s forests. “No amount of foreign exchange is worth a lost forest,” GoldBod stated, reaffirming its commitment to responsible and sustainable gold production. The Board said the reclamation programme formed part of its broader effort to ensure that Ghana’s gold economy benefits communities without undermining the natural resources on which they depend. The collaboration with the Armed Forces and the Forestry Commission is expected to support the restoration of damaged forest reserves and strengthen efforts to protect the country’s environmental heritage.

title: El-Rufai planned to stifle EFCC investigation with $600,000 bribe, witness tells court
body:
A forensic investigator with the State Security Service (SSS) has alleged that former Kaduna State Governor Nasir El-Rufai planned to bribe Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) officials and intermediaries with $600,000 to stifle an investigation.
Testifying on Tuesday as the first prosecution witness in the former governor’s trial before Justice Darius Khobo of the Kaduna State High Court in Kawo, Segun Kayode narrated how $500,000 and $100,000 were allegedly set aside for the illicit payments.
According to Channels Television, the witness informed the court that forensic audio recordings captured conversations between Mr El-Rufai and several suspected associates.
The alleged discussions focused on strategies to frustrate an EFCC investigation into a firm named Singularity.
Mr Kayode testified that those mentioned in the recordings included a senior advocate of Nigeria (SAN), another unnamed individual, and a son of the former governor, Bashir El-Rufai.
He alleged that the SAN and the associate were directed to obtain a template from one Ahmadu Sule—previously used to liquidate another firm—to apply to Singularity.
The witness further alleged that the discussions detailed plans to liquidate Singularity in both Nigeria and Mauritius, where the firm was reportedly under investigation by the Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit (NFIU).
Additionally, the audio recordings contained plans to prevent the EFCC from investigating an undisclosed company listed on the New York Stock Exchange.
The allegations form part of the prosecution’s evidence against the former governor and have yet to be established by the court.
Tuesday’s trial proceedings spanned nearly eight hours, with roughly two hours dedicated to playing the recorded audio evidence.
Earlier in the session, lead defence counsel Paul Erokoro (SAN) objected to Mr Kayode’s testimony, arguing that the witness’s name and a summary of his evidence were omitted from the prosecution’s proof of evidence.
Mr Erokoro contended that this omission violated his client’s right to a fair hearing, emphasising that the defence was entitled to prior notice of the evidence it had to meet.
Countering the objection, lead counsel for the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC), Ayodeji Adedipe (SAN), explained that Mr Kayode was a subpoenaed witness, meaning the omission did not render his testimony inadmissible.
Citing judicial precedents, Mr Adedipe noted that the subpoena had been issued and signed by the court on 30 June, 2026, and that the defence would have full opportunity to cross-examine the witness.
In response, Mr Erokoro clarified that his objection centred on whether the defence had been given adequate notice to prepare, relying on Section 210 of the Administration of Criminal Justice Law, 2017, to argue that the prosecution was required to serve the subpoena on the defence.
In the ruling, Justice Khobo acknowledged the absence of the witness’s name and evidence summary in the proof of evidence but noted that court records confirmed he was subpoenaed.
The judge ruled that the omission did not automatically invalidate the testimony, provided the defence was granted the opportunity to cross-examine the witness.
Following the admission of Mr Kayode’s hard-copy findings into evidence as Exhibit 1, the defence raised further concerns regarding late service.
Justice Khobo ruled that the defence could obtain a Certified True Copy (CTC) of the document for detailed examination.
By consensus of both prosecution and defence teams, the court adjourned the case to 30 November and 1 December 2026, for the continuation of cross-examination.
Mr. El-Rufai arrived at the court under heavy security around 11:50 a.m., ahead of the scheduled noon hearing, accompanied by Isah Ashiru, the governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Kaduna State.
His appearance followed an explicit order by Justice Khobo directing the ICPC to produce him in court.
The hearing took place days after the Court of Appeal in Kaduna dismissed Mr El-Rufai’s appeal challenging the High Court’s refusal to grant him bail.
In its 9 October judgement, the appellate court affirmed the lower court’s decision, ruling that the former governor failed to establish sufficient grounds for intervention.
Mr El-Rufai’s ongoing prosecution by the ICPC stems primarily from recommendations in a 2024 Kaduna State House of Assembly probe report that accused his 2015–2023 administration of mismanaging public funds.
The ICPC filed multiple charges against the former governor in federal and state courts, including one alleging that he tapped the phone of the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu.
Mr El-Rufai has pleaded not guilty to all charges, maintaining that his prosecution is politically motivated.
He remains in ICPC custody under court-authorised remand orders while his legal team challenges his continued detention.
Mr El-Rufai has been in ICPC detention since 18 February.

title: Don’t restore fuel subsidy, IMF tells FG
body: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has advised the Federal Government not to restore broad petrol subsidy, but deploy targeted support for vulnerable households to cushion the impact of rising energy costs. IMF argued that blanket petrol subsidies were expensive, often benefited higher-income consumers disproportionately and could worsen fiscal pressures amid rising borrowing costs. Rodrigo Valdés, director of the IMF’s fiscal affairs department, made the disclosure during a press briefing on the fund’s fiscal monitor at the 2026 annual meetings of the IMF and World Bank in Bangkok, Thailand, on Wednesday. His comments followed a question on how the fund could recommend allowing energy prices to reflect scarcity when higher fuel prices in Nigeria could raise transport costs, worsen inflation and deepen poverty, particularly when the government was facing calls to restore petrol subsidy ahead of an election year. Catholic diocese shuts Benue institutions after attacks Nigeria’s next economic test is turning stability into better living standards “Protecting people is not the same as protecting the price of fuels,” Valdés said. He said fuel subsidies or measures preventing prices from adjusting fully to an energy shock had cost countries between 1 percent and 1.5 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 2026. “It’s first fiscally very costly, and second, if you look at the pattern of consumption, it’s easy to see that that subsidy is readily regressive in many places,” he said. Valdés said governments should instead use social safety nets and household data to identify people who need assistance. “There are better tools to deal with this,” he said. The federal government recently announced a 30-day petrol discount at Nigerian National Petroleum Company (NNPC) Limited retail stations, with priority for public transport operators, to cushion the impact of rising fuel prices.

title: Comedian Russell Brand was a sexual predator, UK prosecutors say
body: LONDON, United Kingdom – British actor and comedian Russell Brand was a ruthless sexual predator who sexually abused six women despite their protestations, prosecutors said on Wednesday, October 14. Brand, 51, once one of Britain’s most high-profile broadcasters and former husband of US singer Katy Perry, faces three counts of rape , three counts of sexual assault, and one count of indecent assault relating to six women from 1999 to 2009. He denies all the accusations. “Today I feel blessed,” he said as he arrived at London’s Southwark Crown Court. “I feel of course concerned but hopeful that this process will lead to good outcomes for everybody involved.” Opening the case against him, prosecutor Riel Karmy-Jones said that regardless of who the women were or what they said or did, he was not deterred in targeting them. “Some of the women involved protested and said no, others had no opportunity to react to his advances but it mattered not to the defendant,” she said. “His desire, his strong desire, for some form of sexual contact was indiscriminate and voracious,” she said. “He could be nice when he wanted to be, funny — undoubtedly — charming, likable even – when he wanted something in return. “But then demanding, entitled, a flirt with a huge sexual appetite, child-like in his expectation that his every desire should be met. “He was ruthless, he was calculating, he was manipulative and, the prosecution say, he was a sexual predator.” His trial is expected to last about six weeks. The comedian, known for his flamboyant style and appearance, was a regular on British television screens in the 2000s and also worked as a radio presenter for the BBC. He went on to star in a number of films including Get Him to the Greek in 2010, the same year he married Perry. They divorced in 2012 after 14 months of marriage. More recently Brand has mainly appeared in online broadcasts, with content often focused on US politics, religion and free speech. – Rappler.com

title: Who Is Planting Backdoors in Ledger Crypto Wallets?
body:
The theft last week of an estimated $100 million in crypto using a hardware backdoor planted in Ledger wallets points to a sophisticated and systematic attack aimed at subverting crypto wallets sold by legitimate resellers in Asia and Europe
After crypto wallet maker Ledger announced Friday that a backdoor embedded in a handful of Ledger wallets sold in SouthEast Asia allowed thieves to hijack around $102 million in crypto from their owners, news has emerged of other Ledger wallets sold in Germany also having implants.
The hardware implants were originally found on an unknown number of Ledger Nano X wallets sold by an authorized Ledger reseller called CryptoBilis based in Malaysia. Ledger said the implants were found on a limited number of devices , all sold by the same seller. But a Ledger device owner in Europe has since said that he found an implant on a Nano X that he purchased at a large European electronics chain store in August and a second one he purchased this weekend at another store in the same chain. He believes these indicate that Ledger’s supply-chain has been compromised.
Since then, users and researchers have also reported finding implants in Ledger Flex and Ledger Stax devices – two of Ledger's more recent line of devices used for securely storing keys used to access a device owner's crypto accounts.
The implants are not the first to be found on Ledger wallets. Famed hardware hacker Joe Grand found implants on several Nano X wallets earlier this year and notified Ledger about them in March, raising questions about Ledger's urgency in addressing the issue. Many of the implants discovered more recently appear to be more sophisticated iterations of the ones that Grand found.
The implants Grand discovered were also all in wallets sold by unauthorized online sellers who seemingly ran fly-by-night operations that weren’t in business for long. But the implants found in wallets sold by CryptoBilis and the European electronics chain indicate the attackers have switched tactics and may be deliberately compromising wallets sold by authorized resellers now. Ledger and its competitor Trezor have cautioned users for years to buy wallets only from their web sites or from authorized resellers. But the recent compromises indicate that attackers are deliberately targeting authorized sellers to exploit customer trust in them and to get wider distribution for implanted devices. What’s more, the attackers have become more skilled and systematic in their method for compromising the wallets, making it more difficult to detect the implants, Grand and other researchers say.
It's not clear how long the implants have been sitting in the sold devices, but last week a coordinated heist resulted in millions of dollars in crypto being stolen from the device and accountholders. According to blockchain research company Bitquery, crypto was stolen from about 315 accounts connected to compromised CryptoBilis Ledger devices alone, and is currently valued at around $102 million . The stolen funds include Bitcoin, Ethereum and Tron and other cryptocurrencies. Some of the funds have reportedly been frozen in the accounts to which the thieves transferred it, and other funds appear to be in accounts that have been flagged for fraud. And it's not clear if funds were also stolen from Ledger owners who purchased their devices from other sellers.
Ledger, based in France, wrote in statement posted to X that it had asked CryptoBilis to halt all sales and shipments of Ledger devices until it could conduct an investigation. CryptoBilis — which is authorized to sell Ledger wallets in Malaysia, Indonesia and the Philippines — wrote on its web site that it is cooperating with Ledger’s investigation.
But a user going by the name Johannes wrote on X over the weekend that he had purchased a Ledger Nano X wallet in person from a MediaMarkt store that had an implant. MediaMarkt is Germany’s equivalent to BestBuy and has 1,000 stores in ten European countries. It’s listed as an authorized reseller of Ledger wallets in Austria, Germany, Spain and Turkey.
Johannes told Zero Day he purchased the wallet in August in a MediaMarkt store in Germany but only took the device apart this weekend following reports that implants had been found. He posted photos of an antenna and implant in his device. Johannes said that he has had no crypto stolen.
In an update to X this weekend, Ledger suggested the implant problem may stem from authorized resellers obtaining Ledger wallets from illegitimate sources or reselling wallets that were bought and returned to them — after being compromised.
“We are reminding our authorized resellers and distributors to source products only through authorized channels and never to restock returned products,” Ledger wrote . “This is an ongoing threat that doesn’t just impact Ledger, but the whole ecosystem, and we are calling others in the space to work with us on making improvements for users…. Raising the bar on physical supply-chain integrity benefits the entire ecosystem.”
But Johannes, who purchased a second Ledger wallet from another MediaMarkt store on Monday and found an implant in it as well thinks this suggests that Ledger’s supply chain has been compromised.
“This indicates a widespread issue rather than an isolated incident, potentially affecting Ledger inventory across MediaMarkt and Saturn stores throughout Europe,” he wrote on X. He says he initially thought his two compromised devices might have been return items that the store then resold as new, but a MediaMarkt employee told him they were new devices and that returns are sent back to Ledger, not re-sold.
Ledger did not respond to an inquiry from Zero Day, but the company wrote on X that there is currently "no indication that Ledger's security infrastructure, systems or services have been compromised.
The issue raises questions about Ledger’s response to the implants and its transparency to customers. After Grand notified the company last March about implants he found in Ledger wallets, the company told him it would investigate to determine who was behind the implants. But Grand says he never received any followup until months later when he asked about it, and someone at Ledger told him they had found no evidence that someone had used the implants to steal crypto from device owners.
But the situation began to change after this.
If you find this article valuable, you can leave a one-time tip to express appreciation to the author.
In April and May, Grand published his implant findings online and gave two presentations about them at conferences in April and May. Mark Karpelès, a French businessman and former CEO of the infamous bitcoin exchange Mt. Gox who was charged with fraud following the collapse of his business, saw Grand's research online and decided to purchase Ledger wallets to see if he could find implants in them as well. He obtained two wallets and found more advanced iterations of the implant Grand discovered and published his findings online last month.
Karpelès's notoriety in the crypto world caused information about the implants to spread widely in the crypto community, which may be why the heists occurred last week. The attackers may have been waiting until they had amassed many wallets with large balances associated with them before pulling off a widespread heist of funds. But once news about the implants began to spread, this may have spurred the thieves to quickly grab as much crypto as they could from wallets already compromised, before wallet owners could move to protect those funds. Some people online have been praising Karpelès for exposing the implants and an operation that might have gone unnoticed for years until he wrote about it.
Grand began looking at Ledger wallets in August 2025 after someone published a Reddit post indicating he had found something in his Ledger Nano X wallet. The owner, who purchased the wallet from an online marketplace in Thailand, cracked opened the wallet’s casing and found extra circuitry that should not have been there. He sent the wallet to Grand to see if he could confirm it was a backdoor and determine what it was designed to do.
Inside the device, Grand found an extra board as well as an antenna, LTE module and eSIM. He determined that the implant was stealing the recovery seeds of infected wallets and transmitting them to the attackers. The implant would sit silently on the device until the owner initialized it and caused it to generate a random seed phrase – essentially a password stored on the Ledger device to allow the device holder to access their crypto account. As the device sent each character of the seed phrase to the device's small screen to display to the owner, the implant copied them and stored the data before subsequently using the LTE module, antenna and eSIM to connect to a nearby cell tower and transmit the seed to the hackers.
Grand, who runs Grand Idea Studio, was thrilled with the finding because although there have long been rumors and theoretical claims about hardware implants on wallets he had never seen one in the wild. He purchased eight more Ledger wallets from several online sellers in Thailand and found that four of them were compromised with similar implants. All of the ones Grand purchased came from "sketchy" sellers on Lazada, an e-commerce platform in SouthEast Asia that is a subsidiary of the Chinese company Alibaba Group. The devices were shipped from Thailand.
On March 4, Grand reported his findings to Ledger and had a Zoom call with a team there, and subsequently gave two talks about the backdoors at the Tropicon conference in April and at the Hardwear.IO conference in May and posted his slides online . He also continued to have some e-mail conversations with Ledger before moving to a Signal group chat with some technical staff there as well as with a researcher based in Japan who had purchased some wallets through online sellers there in March and found implants in them.
Video of Joe Grand's presentation about the Ledger implants given earlier this year at Tropicon.
In September, Karpelès saw Grand’s research and obtained two Ledger wallets, including one purchased at half price from a Chinese seller on Amazon that arrived in a “flawless” shrink-wrapped box from Malaysia. He found implants inside both wallets and published his findings last month on the web site for Tibane Labs, which Karpelès owns and uses to conduct blockchain research and produce open-source tools. The implants operated similar to the ones Grand had found, but they were much more sophisticated in their design and more cleverly hidden to make them harder to spot inside a device.
Karpelès said the version Grand found appeared to be a prototype that had evolved over time. That first-generation involved a bundle of hand-soldered wires that stood out to anyone who opened the devices. The wires connected the implant to the Nano’s screen to grab each character of the randomly-generated seed as they were displayed on the screen.
The more advanced implant used an orange-colored, transparent, custom-built flexible circuit laid over the wallet’s original board and laminated flat onto it and soldered in select places, eliminating the need to solder wires that could be easily seen. To make room for the additional circuit, the hackers had replaced the original battery with a smaller one. Based on some markings, the implant appeared to have been assembled in December 2025 or later.
The second implant, which he found in the device shipped from Malaysia, was the most advanced. Inside the wallet, there appeared to be nothing to distinguish it from an unmodified Nano X device. But a thin black antenna running along the top edge of the board was a giveaway. But every other giveaway from the previous design had been eliminated. The orange flex circuit had been coated with the same black color as the legitimate Ledger board, allowing it to blend in with that component. Part numbers were scraped off, and the original battery was still there. The attackers had simply removed some padding that normally sat behind the screen to make room for the implant. Notably, the attackers had silk-screened a parts number — AC-A2016-NANO-V1.1 — onto the antenna, suggesting it was a custom-built component that had been manufactured to hijack Nano wallets at scale.
“‘NANO' names the target,” Karpelès wrote, “and ‘V1.1’ says it has already been through at least one revision. Someone designed and ordered RF parts for this one device. That is a production run, not a one-off.”
This third-generation version of the implant was “not a hobbyist’s build,” he wrote. “A flex PCB keyed to the Ledger’s own parts, a custom antenna already at its second revision, colour-matched coating and scraped markings all point to planning, a real budget, and a goal of mass production.”
On October 8, the day before the crypto heists went public, Karpelès began posting a series of messages on X about his findings and responding to questions about the implants he found. This is when news of the implants began to spread. The next day, news of the crypto heists emerged, raising questions about whether the attention Karpelès brought to the implants caused the attackers to launch their crypto heister sooner than they had originally planned.
Need free data? Buy a cheap ledger off a dodgy seller, pull the sim out of the spy implant and enjoy while you can (law enforcement may visit you thinking you are the one making these). https://t.co/ycMuv98UHh pic.twitter.com/4tVCkrqlF0
Over the weekend, questions have arisen online about the founders of CryptoBilis and the fact that the company quietly switched owners in March — an acquisition that was not publicly disclosed until this weekend when users on X began pointing fingers at the founders and suggesting they might be behind the compromised devices or at least cooperating with the crypto thieves who stole money from the owners of compromised Ledger devices.
CryptoBilis co-founder Arravind Prabu rejected the accusations and revealed that his company had been acquired by someone else earlier this year and that he and his cofounder had “fully stepped down from all operations, system access, and management” in March. When asked why the acquisition was never made public, Prabu claimed in a lengthy statement that the deal was under an NDA until mid-October, which only enhanced suspicions.
“Since the completion of the handover, we have held zero access, credentials, visibility, or administrative control over CryptoBilis backend systems, customer databases, order histories, or corporate communication channels,” Prabu and his cofounder wrote in their statement. “Under the formal acquisition agreements, all parties were contractually bound to hold off on issuing a joint public announcement until mid-October 2026.”
He says that all suppliers — presumably Ledger among them — were “previously notified of the corporate acquisition and new management structure.”
Several people Zero Day spoke with say the months-long silence around the acquisition is "very shady" and question whether this was intended to keep Ledger customers in the dark while the implants spread through online sales. But Prabu says the suspicion, at least against them, is misplaced.
Oddly, Prabu did not identify who acquired CryptoBilis. He wrote that anyone who has questions about Ledger devices sold by CryptoBilis should contact Nicholas Chang. Chang, however, is identified in old postings to Facebook and X as a director of marketing for CryptoBilis, not the owner. Chang did not respond to an inquiry from Zero Day.
There is currently no evidence that anyone associated with CryptoBilis is behind the implants or the heist of cryptocurrency last week.
But the security researcher in Japan who has participated in conversations about the implants with Grand and Ledger since the spring, told Zero Day that he uncovered some intriguing findings from data he extracted from Ledger implants he purchased.
The researcher, who doesn't want to be publicly identified, purchased several Nano X wallets last March for his own use and put them in a drawer, intending to analyze them at some point when he had free time. After seeing Grand post his Tropicon slides online last spring, he took apart his own Ledger devices and found implants in them. He ended up purchasing ten Nano X devices from unauthorized Ledger sellers, most of them through the Amazon marketplace in Japan. One of the devices shipped from Malaysia, several came from Thailand, and two of them were shipped to him from an address in Osaka – essentially a shipping hub. All of them had implants. He found five different versions of implants among them, including the sophisticated implants Karpelès had found, as well as two additional designs.
"Some were very advanced and some were very basic," he says. "When I say versions [I mean] some of the layouts or components are different."
All of the implants operate in similar ways to record the randomly generated seed phrase as it's sent to the compromised device's screen and transmit the data to the attackers. He says he can't tell if the same group is behind all of the designs or if different actors took inspiration from an original design created by one person and advanced it.
In the case of the devices he received from Osaka, the seller's address was listed as a house in another city in Japan. That house, the researcher says, is used as an address for numerous companies engaged in various businesses, including criminal enterprises.
More interesting, he says, is that he was able to trace the transmission of the stolen seed data to servers in Hong Kong. The eSIM the attackers planted in Ledger devices is designed to work in any country, and the researcher says that if a device owner doesn't initialize their new wallet, the eSIM still retains the location of the last cell tower it connected to, which he was able to extract from the eSIMs in his wallets.
"This allowed me to find [what I think are] some manufacturing hubs for the implant," he says.
He says additional data contained in the compromised device's microcontroller firmware can be used to trace the location of the command and control servers used to receive the stolen seed phrase. He says he was able to trace the transmissions to servers hosted at a data center in Hong Kong that is managed by Alibaba and determined that in June at least 90 implants on infected Ledger devices were sending seed phrases to those servers, though he thinks the true number of devices communicating with the servers is likely much higher than this.
Although most of the compromised Ledger devices so far have been Nano X devices, there is evidence that the attackers have begun to pivot to Ledger Flex and Stax devices. Over the weekend someone posted images of their Stax device on X, which also appears to be compromised. It's not clear if this has been independently confirmed by Ledger or researchers. Separate to this, the researcher in Japan says he purchased two Ledger Flex devices and found implants in them as well.
He says that sometime in July or August he was monitoring a number of online sites that were selling Nano X devices when several of them stopped selling Nano X devices and switched to selling Ledger Flex devices.
"My sense is that they simply developed a new implant that is only for Flex," he says.
He says he has spoken with Japanese law enforcement about his findings as well as with technical contacts at Ledger, but the latter has not shared any information with him about its own investigation.
In the meantime, the list of compromised devices is growing. Over the weekend, Karpelès has been posting information from other Ledger device owners who have since found implants in their devices.
Ledger Flex sold at Singapore Airport confirmed to contain a spy implant! @BenYorke found suspicious marks on his @Ledger and sent it to me rather than using it, that was probably the best decision here. https://t.co/aP7gDEbvtq https://t.co/3VumJyBFD2 https://t.co/PfPyzYA2RW pic.twitter.com/2NtXWIbJYs
Update 12:30pm EST: SatoshiLabs, the Czech company that makes the Trezor wallets that compete with Ledger products, just announced that in light of implants found in Ledger devices sold by authorized sellers, SatoshiLabs is dramatically reducing its own list of approved sellers. Danny Sanders chief commercial officer for Trezor, wrote on X that the move is a "preventive step" and "there is not a single piece of evidence that Trezor devices have been compromised." In a letter Trezor sent to sellers who will be losing their authorization, Trezor wrote that they continue to sell devices they already have in stock but they will receive no new inventory, and as of January 1, 2027 Trezor will remove them from its list of authorized sellers.
To the resellers who helped build Trezor: thank you, and I’m sorry 💔 pic.twitter.com/RK7KBJOshp

title: 2027: Atiku urges Nigerians to collect PVCs, promises economic relief
body: By Ayobami Okerinde The presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has pledged to make life more affordable and improve security across Nigeria, blaming President Bola Tinubu’s administration for the rising cost of living. Atiku made the promise in a post on his official X account on Wednesday, while urging registered voters to collect their Permanent Voter Cards ahead of the 2027 elections. The former vice-president said Nigerians of different ages and economic backgrounds were grappling with financial hardship and insecurity. “Parents go to bed worried about what they will feed their children tomorrow. Pensioners must choose between buying medicine and buying food. Young people work hard, yet transport, rent and basic needs consume what they earn,” Atiku said “And across the country, families live with the fear of kidnapping, attacks and whether their loved ones will return home safely,” he added. Atiku warned that Nigerians should not have to contend with hunger and insecurity at the same time, urging the country to prevent the current challenges from becoming the inheritance of future generations. He called on eligible voters to collect and keep their PVCs, describing the cards as a means of exercising their democratic rights and seeking change through the ballot. “If you are a registered voter, please go and collect your PVC. Hold on to it. It is your voice, your choice and your peaceful power to demand change,” he said. Atiku also accused Tinubu’s administration of making life more expensive and pledged to reverse the trend if given the opportunity to govern. “Bola made life expensive. I will work to make life affordable again and restore the security every Nigerian deserves,” he said. “Let us stand together, across generations, and vote for a Nigeria where every family can live with dignity, safety and hope,” he added. The post 2027: Atiku urges Nigerians to collect PVCs, promises economic relief appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Houthis claim strikes on Saudi Aramco facilities, Riyadh airport
body:
DOHA, October 14. /TASS/. Yemen’s Ansar Allah rebel movement, the Houthis, has struck facilities belonging to Saudi state-owned oil company Saudi Aramco and King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, the insurgent-controlled SABA news agency reported, citing a statement made by the rebels.
"The Yemeni armed forces [as the Houthis refer to themselves - TASS] conducted a military operation during which they struck Saudi Aramco facilities in Dhahran and the Eastern Province, King Khalid International Airport and a Saudi Aramco oil refinery in Riyadh," the statement said. The rebels asserted that the attack involved "a large number of ballistic and cruise missiles, as well as drones."
The Houthis threatened to continue attacking airports and oil facilities in Saudi Arabia. They called on international transport companies, as well as civilians and personnel, to leave these facilities immediately, describing them as "legitimate targets." The rebels said their actions were in response to airstrikes by the Arab coalition on Sanaa and other Yemeni provinces.

title: Moscow reports overnight attack involving nearly 500 drones, four airports suspended operations, media report
body:
Ukrinform reports this, citing the ASTRA Telegram channel.
According to Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin, approximately 493 drones had been heading toward the Russian capital since the evening of October 13.
He claimed that 180 drones had been destroyed as they approached Moscow.
Moscow's Sheremetyevo, Domodedovo, Vnukovo, and Zhukovsky airports suspended operations because of the drone threat.
Vnukovo Airport was closed for more than eight hours, and passengers were removed from all flights.
As Ukrinform previously reported, drones attacked the Shatura State District Power Plant in Russia's Moscow region.

title: Trump’s Phantom Ceasefires Are a National Security Problem
body:
On Sunday, Oct. 11, at 10:16 a.m., President Donald Trump announced on social media an immediate ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine covering attacks on energy infrastructure. He asserted that both parties had agreed. In the same post he issued an unmistakable warning: “Do not break it!”
Within half an hour of Trump’s announcement, a senior Ukrainian official told the press that Kyiv had no information about the purported agreement. Within the same hour, Zelensky’s own response was public: the announcement “was news for me.” He added that Ukraine would agree to a ceasefire if Russia did the same.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Exactly 59 minutes after Trump announced the purported ceasefire, Russia attacked Kharkiv’s CHP-5 power plant.
This was the second time in one month that the president issued a false claim about a negotiated ceasefire.
On Sept. 14, Trump declared: “Ukraine has agreed not to hit Russian Energy Targets. Russia has agreed to do likewise!”
Yet a senior Ukrainian official made it clear that they had not heard of such a ceasefire. Zelensky expressed willingness to reciprocate if Russia halted its attacks, while saying Kyiv awaited details. Meanwhile, Russia continued to target Ukraine’s energy infrastructure.
There are several possible explanations for President Trump’s repeated misrepresentations about ceasefires to the world:
Yes, and it is a matter of national security.
Repeatedly announcing ceasefires that have not been established is a grave failure of presidential responsibility. Such statements can shape military calculations, diplomatic decisions, financial markets, and the expectations of civilians whose lives depend on whether the bombing will actually stop.
When a president declares that both parties have agreed, he places American credibility behind that assertion. If the agreement does not exist, he undermines trust in future American commitments, creates confusion about who has promised what, and risks allowing continued aggression to disappear beneath a headline proclaiming peace.
Congressional leaders have a duty to call immediate hearings, establish what the president knew, identify who supplied his information, and determine what corrective action is required. Whether the explanation is deliberate deception, gross negligence, confusion, or something else, announcing an international agreement without establishing the consent of its participants raises serious questions about the president’s competence to oversee American foreign policy.
Congress must treat this as a matter of national security and demand an explanation. A president’s words about war and peace carry the authority of the United States; they cannot be excused as a salesman’s harmless exaggeration.
In the meantime, the world must respond advisedly to such claims by President Trump. “Fool me once, shame on you. Fool me twice, shame on me.”
The views expressed in this opinion article are the author’s and not necessarily those of Kyiv Post.
DW Phillips is a filmmaker, attorney and journalist who is director for Ukraine Story, a foundation for documentary reporting. He covered the story of Ukrainian athletes from the Paris 2024 Olympics, and is presently working an episodic series for streaming, Ukraine Story Anthology, which presents the humanity and hope of the people of Ukraine in wartime, including the stories of war orphans, soldiers, religious leaders and everyday Ukrainians. DW has served as a presidential appointee, and specialized in constitutional and civil rights issues as an attorney. He lives in Texas, USA.

title: Despite substantial accommodation capacity, room demand still weakens – GSS report
body: The Accommodation Occupancy Report from March to June 2025 released by the Ghana Statistical Service (GSS) has revealed that even though the country had substantial accommodation capacity, but room demand still weakened. The report pointed out that, though around 5 million room-nights were available each month, monthly occupied room-nights fell from 2.14 million in March to 1.99 million in June, about 7 percent in monthly totals and about 4 percent on an average daily basis. According to the GSS, the issue was therefore not simply capacity, but how effectively existing capacity was being used. The report said national room occupancy remained around 40 percent. This was 41.7 percent in March, 41.9 percent in April, 39.7 percent in May and 40.0 percent in June. Put simply, only four in every ten available rooms were occupied. It added that bed occupancy was higher, ranging from 46.2 percent to 49.2 percent. “National averages masked wide differences across the industry. Hotels provided about seven in every ten available rooms, but their room occupancy remained around one-third. In contrast, hostels recorded 92.9 to 96.1 percent room occupancy, while establishments with 100 or more rooms consistently exceeded 83 percent”, the report said. The Central and Western regions recorded some of the highest room occupancy rates, with Central Region reaching 56.8 percent in June and Western Region remaining above 50 percent throughout the period. Eastern, Bono East and North East regions remained below 25 percent. Ghana’s accommodation market therefore differs substantially across regions. Domestic guests were the backbone of demand. About 1.78 million to 1.86 million domestic guests were recorded monthly, compared with only 23,000 to 30,000 foreign guests. The Central Region recorded the most domestic guests, while Greater Accra Region attracted the most foreign guests. Foreign guests were fewer but generally stayed longer, averaging three to nine nights, compared with about one to two nights for domestic guests. The report emphasized that “overall, the evidence points to substantial capacity, relatively stable national occupancy, weakening room demand and large differences across regions and accommodation segments. These differences matter for where Ghana promotes tourism, expands capacity and directs business and investment decisions”. Implications The report explained that Ghana has substantial accommodation capacity, but how well it is used varies sharply by location, establishment type and market segment. The priority is therefore not only to expand capacity, but also to make better use of what already exists. Government’s approach For government and tourism institutions, planning should focus on where demand is strong, where capacity is underused and why. Regional differences mean that one national approach will not fit every part of Ghana. For accommodation businesses, occupancy alone is not enough. Occupancy, ADR and RevPAR should be used together to guide pricing, marketing, operations and investment. Persistently low occupancy should be understood before additional capacity is created. Investors approach For investors and financial institutions, national averages can hide opportunities and risks. Investment decisions should consider location, establishment type and size, occupancy, revenue performance and guest profile. For the tourism industry, domestic travellers should remain central because they account for the overwhelming majority of guests. At the same time, the generally longer stays of foreign guests highlight the value of attracting international visitors and encouraging longer stays. “For GSS, GTA and accommodation establishments, sustained production of timely, high-quality accommodation statistics is essential. A longer time series will strengthen understanding of seasonality, demand, pricing and emerging investment opportunities”, the report advised. title: Europe risks exclusion from Ukraine settlement without dialogue with Russia — politician
body:
PARIS, October 14. /TASS/. Europe needs to establish dialogue with Russia to avoid being left out of the Ukraine settlement process, Marion Marechal, leader of France’s right-wing Identity and Freedoms Party and niece of National Rally parliamentary faction leader Marine Le Pen, said.
"How can the conflict be resolved? How can the war be ended without engaging in diplomatic dialogue with the direct participants at some point? I think that sooner or later, such a move will become inevitable. If Europeans don’t take the step, the Americans, Middle Eastern countries or Turkey will. However, in that case, we will be completely left out of the negotiation process," she told the French broadcaster LCI.
Marechal believes that France cannot benefit from cutting ties with Russia. "There are diplomatic challenges that will have to be addressed at some point," she noted.

title: Yemen's Houthis use Chinese parts to build Iranian ballistic missile, boost attack range - report
body: Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis are developing their own version of Iran's Kheibar Shekan precision-guided missile using parts imported from Chinese companies, according to a Tuesday Wall Street Journal report citing new data from UK-based independent monitor Conflict Armament Research. The missile would have a maximum range of approximately 1,200 miles, according to the WSJ. This would put all of Saudi Arabia and Israel in range. The Houthis, a US-designated terrorist organization under a United Nations arms embargo that controls large parts of Yemen, have been fighting the Saudi-backed Yemeni government in a civil war since 2014. The Yemen conflict has resumed as a spillover from the wider US-Iran war that began with the US-Israeli attack on the Islamic Republic on February 28. Iran, Saudi Arabia's longtime regional rival, has offered to mediate between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis, its foreign minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday in statements reiterated by the ministry on Monday.The Conflict Armament Research report was based on information from Yemeni authorities in July after officials interdicted two shipments in 2025, which included the missile equipment hidden among a range of other goods, according to the WSJ.“When you have imports like that, there is a possibility that they are already manufacturing or that they are trying and it doesn't really work out,” Fabian Hinz, a senior analyst at Conflict Armament, told the Wall Street Journal, adding that because the Houthis weapons facilities are well camouflaged, it is unclear how far along missile production has proceeded.China says it is respecting arms sales banChina claims to be adhering to the UN arms embargo on the Houthis, per the WSJ. However, the report noted that while some of the Houthi-imported materials could have civilian uses, some were parts specifically designed for missile production.The imported parts include custom-made metal missile components, including parts of the motor and of the airframe, the missile's basic structure, the Wall Street Journal noted, adding that Yemeni authorities also found fins which stabilize the missile in flight and parts of a solid-propellant rocket motor of a Kheibar Shekan-series missile.Yemeni authorities also seized tools, testing equipment, and raw materials, including the ablative material which protects sections of the missile from the intense heat produced by a ballistic missile, the WSJ added.Why are Iranian Kheibar Shekan missiles particularly advantageous?Iran has been using Kheibar Shekan missiles, cheap, mobile, and accurate missiles, which have a range of at least 1,400 kilometers in their strikes against US assets across the Middle East, the Wall Street Journal cited US officials as saying in July. The solid-fuel, medium-range Kheibar Shekan missiles differ from older Iranian missiles that require prelaunch fueling, a lengthy process which the Kheibar Shekan can bypass by being kept fueled and are capable of being loaded quickly into trucks or other vehicles for launching, making it easier to evade US and Israeli warplanes seeking to knock out Iranian missile launch sites, military experts told WSJ at the time.Danya Saperstein and Reuters contributed to this report.

title: No amount of foreign exchange is worth a lost forest – GoldBod
body: The Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) has stressed that Ghana’s efforts to earn foreign exchange from gold exports must not come at the expense of the country’s forests, as it intensifies efforts to restore lands degraded by illegal mining. In a Facebook post on Wednesday, October 14, the Board said sustainable gold production must generate economic benefits without destroying the natural resources on which communities depend. It maintained that the country’s gold economy must balance revenue generation with environmental protection and responsible resource management. “No amount of foreign exchange is worth a lost forest,” GoldBod stated, emphasising the need to ensure that gold contributes to national development without causing lasting damage to the environment. The Board said its commitment was to build a gold economy that is responsible, sustainable and beneficial to all Ghanaians. As part of that commitment, GoldBod is collaborating with the Ghana Armed Forces and the Forestry Commission to reclaim degraded forest reserves. Reclamation works covering 80 hectares are underway this year, with plans to extend the programme to an additional 150 hectares across 30 forest reserves in 2027.

title: Men Can’t Stop Faking How Much They Know About AI
body:
In a new survey of more than 5,400 Americans, 73 percent of male respondents told Harvard researchers they knew who Altman was. A little over half—53 percent—said they knew of Murati, Milner, and Dalton.
There’s one problem. Murati is a real person: she’s the former CTO of OpenAI and the current CEO of Thinking Machine Labs. Milner and Dalton, on the other hand, do not exist.
Compared to women, “we're seeing that men are more optimistic and more confident” across the board when it comes to AI, Harvard Kennedy School’s Shorenstein Center executive director Laura Manley tells WIRED. Sometimes, that veers into overconfidence—like claiming to recognize fictional AI executives. (For context, 40 percent of women claimed to know who Milner and Dalton were; 38 percent said they recognized Murati.)
While Manley notes that men are more overconfident in general when surveyed, the report, published on Wednesday, digs into what the confidence gap on AI looks like, as well as the repercussions of gendered divides.
Researchers found that men use AI more frequently and are, on average, better able to correctly answer factual questions about AI. But men and women answer questions incorrectly at around the same rate. The discrepancy is based on how often women said they weren’t sure of an answer—an average of 3.3 questions out of 12 compared to 2.3 questions for men.
Researchers wondered if this predilection toward certainty colors coverage of AI. Across a year of media coverage, men were named in headlines about AI more than 14 times as often as women. Because top AI executives skew heavily male, researchers decided to reexamine coverage, looking solely at people who were quoted as subject experts. Three-quarters of these experts were men—a higher proportion than the actual AI talent pool, which is roughly 29 percent women.
“Maybe there should be more women prominently featured as experts or given the platform to express: not sure,” Manley says.
Besides intellectual bluster, Americans were generally in agreement that AI was freaking them out—men and women both rated “concern” as their top emotional response. However, female respondents were more concerned, fearful, and worried than their male counterparts. Men, meanwhile, rated every positive feeling—including curiosity, enthusiasm, and excitement—higher than women did.
In the current discourse, “there's so much confidence in either doom or abundance,” Manley says. “It just drowns out all of the voices that should be saying ‘not sure.’” There are many unanswered questions on proper uses for and the future of AI. One gender is simply less likely to acknowledge such uncertainty.
“We have to be able to be able to say ‘not sure’ more often,” Manley says.

title: US Army transfers 600 enlisted soldiers to Space Operations Branch
body: The U.S. Army bolstered its Space Operations Branch by 600 soldiers, the service recently announced , officially creating the branch’s first permanent enlisted cadre. The soldiers, drawn from across the force, voluntarily applied and were selected to reclassify as MOS 40D Tactical Space Operations Specialists, the Army said. “We had nearly 3,000 soldiers apply, and selected over 600 of the most capable, professional soldiers in the Army,” Command Sgt. Maj. Rickey Jackson, command sergeant major of the U.S. Army Space and Missile Defense Command, said in the release. “We drew talent from Military Intelligence, Air Defense Artillery and the Signal Corps, but the 40D MOS is open for anyone to apply. “Ultimately, we are looking for soldiers who master their current jobs and consistently stand apart from their peers.” The Army announced in January that it was opening applications for the specialty to soldiers in grades E-4 through E-9 across the active-duty Army, National Guard and Army Reserve. Previously, the service temporarily pulled soldiers from other specialties to help with space operations. However, the soldiers’ experience was often lost when they returned to their original branches. “For too long, enlisted soldiers with specialized space training and experience rotated through critical space assignments, eventually returning to their basic branches,” Lt. Gen. John L. Rafferty, commanding general of U.S. Army Space and Missile Defense Command, said in a separate release. “The rotational system served the U.S. Army well in the past but will not meet the demands of the future, which requires a professional and sustainable approach to training, career progression and leader development for Army Space soldiers. The Army’s Space Operations Branch was officially established in June, bringing together the newly-created enlisted occupational specialty and functional area 40As, the Army’s Space Operations Officers. Though 40As have been part of the force since 1999, they have not had enlisted peers until now. The newly minted Tactical Space Operations Specialists will receive training at the Space and Missile Defense Center of Excellence in Colorado Springs, Colorado. “Our space operations soldiers bring unmatched value to the Army and joint force because of the education and training they receive to execute space integration and interdiction missions — specifically counter-SATCOM, stratospheric warfare, navigation warfare and counter-sensing,” Col. Felix Torres, commandant of the Space and Missile Defense Center of Excellence, said in the release. Space systems, the Army said, help soldiers with navigation, weather, communication and early warnings. Soldiers in the 1st Space Brigade, the Army’s only singularly-focused space unit, have theater missile warning capabilities and long-distance satellite communications, for example.
