title: Zelenskyy departs for London from Polish Rzeszów airport after lengthy hiatus
body:
President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy has departed on an official working trip to the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland from the airport in the Polish city of Rzeszów.
In response to a journalist's inquiry regarding whether this marks the first time since the June controversy involving the return of a Polish state award that the president has flown out from the Rzeszów airport for an international visit, Presidential Communications Advisor Dmytro Lytvyn replied: "He has already departed."
Presidential Press Secretary Serhiy Nykyforov confirmed in turn that this is Zelenskyy's first flight to a third country originating from Polish territory since June of this year, while recalling that the head of the Ukrainian state did visit Poland in the interim, notably meeting with Prime Minister Donald Tusk in Lublin in July.
According to data from the AirNav aviation tracking resource, the Ukrainian government Airbus A319 aircraft (registration UR-ABA) operated by the state airline Ukraine Air Enterprise took off from Rzeszów at 11:17 Kyiv time and is en route to London Stansted Airport.
As reported, ahead of Zelenskyy's visit to London, the British government announced the transfer of ground-to-air missiles to Ukraine valued at GBP 45 million (approximately $58.5 million at the current exchange rate) with accelerated delivery schedules.
On June 7, Zelenskyy flew to the United Kingdom for the first time via Chișinău, Moldova, rather than utilizing the Polish airport in Rzeszów as he had previously. Social media users linked this logistical shift to strained relations between Ukraine and Poland, though Ukrainian Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Heorhiy Tykhy dismissed any political dimension, calling the connection artificial. Nevertheless, the Ukrainian president's subsequent international trips this year continued to depart from Chișinău, while the head of state's aircraft remained based in Poland.

title: Prospera Finance Wins ‘Fastest Growing Finance Company’ Award
body: Prospera Finance Limited has been awarded the ‘Fastest Growing Finance Company of the Year’ at the BusinessDay Banks and Other Financial Institutions (BAFI) Awards in recognition of the company’s impressive market trajectory, financial innovation, and commitment to excellence. According to a statement, the award highlights Prospera Finance’s rapid expansion, robust operational performance, and customer-centric financial solutions in an evolving macroeconomic landscape. Under the leadership of its Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Joshua Obinna Umesegha, Prospera Finance Limited has built a reputation for delivering tailored, accessible financial products that empower individuals, small and medium scale enterprises (SMEs), and corporate organisations across Nigeria. Receiving the award on behalf of the company, the leadership team expressed gratitude to its clients, partners, and employees, noting that the recognition serves as validation of the firm’s strategic vision and execution over the past year. Speaking on the milestone, Umesegha described the win as a testament to the hard work and resilience of the entire Prospera Finance team, as well as the trust reposed in the firm by its growing client base. “Winning the ‘Fastest Growing Finance Company of the Year’ at the BAFI Awards is a profound honor for all of us at Prospera Finance Limited,” Umesegha said. “This award reflects our relentless drive to innovate, deepen financial access, and create sustainable value for our stakeholders. As we look ahead, we remain committed to pioneering solutions that drive economic growth and support the financial goals of our clients.” The BusinessDay BAFI Awards, widely regarded as the benchmark of institutional excellence in Nigeria’s financial sector, employs a rigorous audit and selection process to evaluate institutions based on financial growth, market innovation, corporate governance, and service quality. Prospera Finance’s recognition as the fastest-growing operator underscores its rising prominence in the non-bank financial services space, positioning it for continued market leadership in the years ahead.

title: Iran central bank chief rejects economic collapse claims
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 14 (MNA) – Iran's central bank governor dismissed claims that the country's economy is collapsing, saying it has shown notable resilience despite war, US sanctions and economic pressure.
Abdolnaser Hemmati, governor of the Central Bank of Iran, rejected claims that the country's economy is collapsing, describing them as an illusion and saying the economy has shown considerable resilience despite war, economic pressure and US sanctions.
Speaking at the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank Group in Bangkok, Thailand, Hemmati outlined the central bank's priorities as curbing inflation, anchoring inflation expectations, preserving financial stability and maintaining banking and payment services.
He said the central bank has worked to secure foreign currency for imports of medicine and essential goods and to slow inflation.
Hemmati said Iran's economic policies should be assessed with external shocks and financial constraints in mind, citing factors that affect the policy environment and the effectiveness of economic measures.
He called on the IMF to examine the economic effects of war, sanctions and restrictions on international payments with the same rigor it applies to countries' domestic policies in its bilateral and multilateral surveillance. He also urged equal standards for all IMF members and active dialogue on ways to reduce the impact of such restrictions.
Hemmati warned that continued instability in the region could affect energy markets, transport, trade and investment. He said strengthening regional stability requires respect for the sovereignty of states, attention to legitimate security concerns and cooperation based on mutual responsibility and shared interests.
He also called for a more active IMF role in strengthening international monetary cooperation and overseeing the global monetary system.

title: Dropping 3 impeachment articles vs Sara, who benefits?
body: It’s a move that confused impeachment trial spectators and prompted lead defense lawyer Sheila Sison to fire off a sharp litany of tirades — so why, really, did the prosecution abandon three of the four impeachment articles against Vice President Sara Duterte? There are official reasons, and then ones that emerge when you look at who stands to benefit. The official reason, as lead prosecutor Jinky Luistro manifested before the court, in dropping most cases against the Vice President is to speed up the trial amid growing “public impatience,” and respect for the Senate’s other legislative responsibilities — from passing pending bills to working on the 2027 national budget. In a subsequent press conference, the prosecution tried to sell the move as beneficial to the Vice President. “If I were the Vice President, I would even thank the prosecution because now, she can focus on one (case),” private prosecutor Lorna Kapunan said, referring to the retained charge on unexplained wealth. Play Video While Senate President Chiz Escudero sided with the prosecution in allowing the withdrawal of three impeachment articles, it is difficult to dismiss Sison’s argument: that her client was being denied the opportunity to present counter-evidence in open court on two of the three dropped articles, after the prosecution had already presented its evidence on them. “The prosecution cannot be allowed to have the benefit of its accusations without bearing the burden of having those accusations tested,” Sison said, warning of a potential mistrial. So, if not the Vice President, whom does this move really serve? 1. The prosecution Of course, the prosecution won’t drop this bombshell, perhaps calculated, move without knowing for certain that there are more pros than cons to this. Behind closed doors, the prosecution is crunching the numbers too, and there’s growing confidence that they have enough to secure a guilty verdict. If all senators from the majority vote to remove the Vice President from office, the reduced conviction threshold of 14 votes is met. There is a desire to hit 16 votes to prevent any Supreme Court action by the defense, but that means courting the harder-to-sway senators — Camille Villar, Pia Cayetano, or even the absent Loren Legarda. With the prosecution abandoning the three impeachment articles, two of which they already exhaustively presented before the court, the defense team gets no chance to provide counter-evidence for the senator-judges to evaluate. This means that the defense doesn’t have the power to prolong the trial the same way they availed of every objection during the prosecution’s turn, because the cases that the prosecution dropped will no longer be adjudicated by the court. From the prosecution’s perspective, the faster they get to the vote, the better, especially if they believe they have convinced enough senator-judges to side with them. 2. Senator-judges Senators have undergone their most grueling work schedule in years due to the trial — attending court proceedings in the morning, and fulfilling their legislative responsibilities in the afternoon and rest of the day. Even Majority Leader Migz Zubiri quipped that he was tired from the 12-hour duty. So why prolong the proceedings if they already know how they will vote in the trial? Had the three cases not been dropped, senators would have set themselves up for an exhausting final two months of 2026. November is known to be a busy month due to budget deliberations in the Senate. The ASEAN Summit in Manila is also expected to disrupt their schedule. 3. Anyone with presidential ambitions in 2028 A conviction not only removes the Vice President from office, but also quashes her 2028 presidential aspirations. Barring Duterte from the race levels the playing field and removes the clear front-runner. This is advantageous for senator-judges, many of whom have gunned for, or are gunning for, higher office. Senator Risa Hontiveros is exploring a 2028 presidential bid. Others have tried but failed to be president or vice president in the past — Ping Lacson, Tito Sotto, Kiko Pangilinan, Escudero who interestingly quickly came up with the ruling that sided with the prosecution’s surprise motion, and even Duterte-allied senators Alan Cayetano and Loren Legarda. The Tulfo brothers and senators Bam Aquino, Robin Padilla, and Bong Go have also been floated as presidential or vice presidential contenders in the 2028 polls. Putting the impeachment saga behind in 2026 gives other hopefuls time to reposition, build alliances, and decide where they want to place their bets for 2028. – Rappler.com

title: Japan Airlines orders up to 26 Embraer E190-E2 jets, following rival ANA
body:
Japan Airlines (JAL) has selected the Embraer E190-E2 regional jet to renew the fleet of subsidiary J-Air, ordering 16 aircraft with options for another 10. Deliveries are scheduled to begin in fiscal 2029.
The decision announced on Wednesday follows rival All Nippon Airways (ANA), which selected the same aircraft in 2025 for its domestic network. It also maintains J-Air’s long relationship with Embraer as the airline prepares to replace its current E170 and first-generation E190 jets.
J-Air operates 32 Embraer aircraft, comprising 18 E170s and 14 E190s. The Osaka Itami-based carrier uses the jets primarily on domestic regional services within the JAL Group network.
The E190-E2 is the larger of the two aircraft currently offered in Embraer’s E2 family. JAL has not yet disclosed the seating configuration planned for its aircraft or a detailed retirement schedule for the existing E-Jets.
JAL’s decision comes after months of evaluating replacements for its regional fleet. Bloomberg reported in September that the E190-E2 had emerged as the leading candidate, ahead of the Airbus A220 .
The Japanese group had previously planned to introduce another locally developed regional aircraft. JAL signed an agreement for 32 Mitsubishi Regional Jets , later renamed SpaceJet, in 2015, but none were delivered before Mitsubishi Heavy Industries ended the program in 2023.
The selection gives Embraer E190-E2 orders from both of Japan’s largest airline groups. ANA Holdings placed a firm order for 15 E190-E2s in February 2025, with options for five more, becoming the first Japanese customer for the second-generation E-Jet.
ANA plans to introduce the aircraft from fiscal 2028, one year before JAL’s first scheduled deliveries.
J-Air has operated Embraer aircraft since 2009, when it introduced the E170. The larger E190 joined its fleet in 2016.
JAL recently extended its component support agreement with Embraer for the E170 and E190 fleet. The new E190-E2 order now establishes a successor for those aircraft as the carrier begins the next phase of its regional fleet renewal.

title: Ondo govt orders river fumigation, emergency water supply in Igbokoda over military aircraft crash
body:
The Ondo State Government has ordered the fumigation of the river linked to the site where a military aircraft crashed last week in Igbokoda in Ilaje Local Government Area of the state.
The government also ordered the distribution of nose masks and other health kits to residents following complaints about a foul smell from the site of 5 October Nigerian Air Force (NAF) aircraft crash.
The intervention follows concerns among residents of Igbokoda over possible environmental contamination and health risks as search and recovery operations continue at the crash site.
In a statement on Wednesday by the Commissioner for Information and Orientation, Idowu Ajanaku, the state governor, Lucky Aiyedatiwa, directed the ministries of environment and health to begin extensive fumigation of the river following complaints about the offensive smell.
Mr Aiyedatiwa stated that the interventions are necessary as the river serves as an important source of livelihood for residents of Igbokoda and neighbouring communities.
The governor also directed the Ilaje Local Government Area to arrange water tankers to supply potable water to residents if assessments establish that the river is severely polluted and unsuitable for use.
The water supply arrangement, the statement said, would remain in place pending a lasting intervention to address any pollution.
Mr Aiyedatiwa, who hails from the local government area, also directed the relevant ministries to distribute nose masks and other essential health kits to residents as a precaution against potential health hazards.
The state government said it would continue to support the Nigerian Air Force’s evacuation efforts while prioritising the safety and welfare of residents in the affected community.
PREMIUM TIMES reported that the NAF ATR 42 aircraft, identified as NAF 931, crashed into a swampy area of Igbokoda during a mission from Benin City, Edo State, to Lagos. The publication later confirmed that all the 25 people on board the aircraft including five crew members and 20 passengers died , according to NAF.
Recovery operations have been complicated by the swampy terrain and the aircraft’s submersion in the water.
Following the crash, the Ondo State Government deployed amphibious swamp machines to support the Nigerian Navy, the Air Force, emergency response agencies and local divers in accessing the site and retrieving the wreckage and victims’ remains.
Residents, however, have raised concerns about the increasingly offensive smell from the crash site, while the community’s monarch, Afolabi Odidiomo, has called on the federal and state governments to accelerate recovery efforts and address suspected contamination.
PREMIUM TIMES repeated on Tuesday that the Nigerian Air Force has also constituted a 12-member Aircraft Accident Investigation Board to investigate the circumstances surrounding the crash and recommend measures to prevent a recurrence.

title: Nigeria 5-0 Comoros: Five big takeaways as Super Falcons prepare for big Morocco test
body:
Nigeria’s Super Falcons took another confident step towards the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games after dismantling Comoros 5-0 on Tuesday to complete a 7-0 aggregate victory and advance to the third round of the qualifying campaign.
Two goals each from Toni Payne and Uchenna Kanu, alongside the no nonsense Christy Ucheibe’s successful penalty, ensured Nigeria finished the tie in emphatic fashion. But beyond the scoreline, the performance offered interim coach Augustine Eguavoen encouraging signs of a team beginning to rediscover its defensive solidity while exploring fresh possibilities in attack.
The Super Falcons were expected to overcome Comoros, particularly after establishing a two-goal advantage in the first leg. However, the manner in which they completed the job was important, especially for a side seeking to rebuild confidence and consistency following a disappointing 2026 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations campaign.
Comoros had thrashed Sudan 30-0 on aggregate in the opening round of the qualifiers, but Nigeria exposed the considerable gulf in quality between the two sides, keeping clean sheets in both meetings and scoring seven unanswered goals.
The next assignment against Morocco will demand significantly more from the nine-time African champions. Before that potentially defining encounter, Premium Times examines five major takeaways from Nigeria’s victory, ranked by their importance to Eguavoen’s rebuilding project.
For a team with ambitions of returning to the Olympic Games, defensive organisation will be just as important as attacking firepower. Nigeria’s two-legged victory over Comoros provided an encouraging indication that the Super Falcons may be finding greater stability at the back.
The Nigerians conceded no goals across both matches, recording consecutive clean sheets for the first time since the group stage of the 2024 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations.
Although Comoros offered limited attacking threat, their impressive 30-0 aggregate demolition of Sudan in the previous round meant they could not be dismissed entirely. Nigeria, however, restricted their opponents and completed the tie without allowing them a route back into the contest.
Perhaps the most encouraging aspect was Eguavoen’s decision to trust a new centre-back partnership involving Shukurat Oladipo and Christy Ucheibe. The pair looked composed, mobile and complementary, showing a promising understanding of their defensive responsibilities.
Ucheibe’s contribution was particularly notable because she combined her defensive duties with a goal from the penalty spot, underlining her value at both ends of the pitch. Shukurat Oladipo put up a performance that reminded all why she was named the best defender in Italy last season.
The partnership still needs to be tested against opponents with greater technical quality and more sophisticated attacking movements. Nevertheless, Nigeria’s defensive display provides a useful foundation for the next round.
Morocco possess considerably more attacking quality than Comoros and are likely to ask harder questions of the Nigerian backline. If the Super Falcons can carry this organisation and concentration into that contest, they will give themselves a stronger chance of progressing.
The Super Falcons have completed the immediate task, but the real examination of Eguavoen’s side is approaching.
Nigeria will face Morocco in the third round after the Atlas Lionesses advanced following the withdrawal of the Republic of Congo from their second-round tie. The meeting promises to be a much more demanding contest, with progression in the Olympic qualifying campaign at stake.
Morocco have developed into one of Africa’s leading women’s football sides in recent years, making the fixture a significant test of Nigeria’s defensive discipline, midfield control and ability to convert attacking opportunities against stronger opposition.
There is, however, a source of confidence for the Super Falcons. Nigeria defeated Morocco 3-2 in the final of the 2024 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations, a result that demonstrated their capacity to withstand pressure and deliver when the stakes are high.
That victory will offer encouragement, but it should not be mistaken for a guarantee of success. The upcoming tie is a fresh contest, and Nigeria must show that they can reproduce their best football over two legs against an opponent capable of punishing defensive lapses.
The victory over Comoros has given Eguavoen room to assess his options and build momentum. The Morocco games will reveal whether the encouraging signs in the latest performance can translate into a result against elite continental opposition.
For Nigeria, the objective is no longer simply to score freely against a less experienced opponent. It is to demonstrate that the team can remain compact under pressure, compete in the decisive areas and produce the quality required to keep their Olympic dream alive.
Nigeria have never lacked outstanding goalscorers. From Mercy Akide and Perpetua Nkwocha to Asisat Oshoala, the Super Falcons have enjoyed generations of forwards capable of defining matches and carrying the weight of expectation.
But as Oshoala moves into the later stages of her career, Nigeria must continue identifying players who can shoulder the responsibility of leading the attack. Kanu’s performance against Comoros offered another reason to believe she can play a major role in that transition.
The forward scored twice in Tuesday’s encounter and finished the two-legged tie with three goals, strengthening her growing case as a dependable attacking option.
Kanu brings more than an eye for goal. Her strength allows her to compete physically with defenders, while her mobility gives Nigeria the flexibility to use her centrally or from wider attacking positions. She also showed an ability to remain involved in dangerous situations rather than relying solely on chances presented to her.
That variety could prove valuable against Morocco, where Nigeria may have fewer opportunities and will need their forwards to make the most of openings.
However, the next step is sustaining that effectiveness against higher-quality opposition. Goals against Comoros will provide confidence, but performances against Morocco would offer a more convincing indication of Kanu’s readiness to become one of Nigeria’s leading attacking figures.
With the Super Falcons searching for consistency and a reliable source of goals, Kanu has given Eguavoen another positive selection dilemma.
Michelle Alozie was arguably one of Nigeria’s standout performers across the two legs, delivering the kind of energetic and balanced display that could prove crucial in the more demanding rounds of the qualifiers.
Operating at right-back, Alozie covered the flank tirelessly, combining defensive responsibility with forward runs that gave Nigeria another route into attacking areas. Her work rate and willingness to contribute in both phases helped the Super Falcons maintain their threat while remaining organised.
Her performances were particularly encouraging after a difficult showing at the 2026 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations. The Comoros tie provided an opportunity to rebuild confidence, and Alozie took it by demonstrating the qualities that have made her a valuable member of the national team.
Modern full-backs are often required to do much more than defend their own penalty area. They must provide width, support attacks, recover quickly and make sound decisions when possession changes hands. Alozie showed encouraging signs in those areas over the two matches.
Her contribution will become even more important against Morocco, whose greater attacking quality should provide a sterner test of her defensive concentration. At the same time, Nigeria may need her forward runs to help stretch the opposition and create space for the attackers.
Toni Payne also deserves credit for her two-goal contribution on Tuesday, while Under 20 captain, Joy Igbokwe’s performance offered another encouraging sign of the options available to Eguavoen.
Alozie’s displays, however, stood out as a reminder that Nigeria’s progress will depend not only on their most celebrated attackers but also on players capable of delivering consistently across the pitch.
The depth of Nigeria’s attacking options was another positive to emerge from the victory, with substitutes Folashade Ijamilusi and Blessing Okpe making significant contributions after entering the contest.
Both players registered two assists, while Okpe also won the penalty that Ucheibe converted to complete the scoring. Their impact was reflected in the energy and directness they brought to Nigeria’s second-half performance.
Ijamilusi and Okpe used their pace, movement and willingness to run at opponents to give the Super Falcons additional attacking impetus. Rather than simply maintaining the tempo established by the starters, they helped add another dimension to Nigeria’s forward play.
Their performances will be welcome news for Eguavoen, particularly as the level of competition rises. Against stronger teams, the ability to change a game from the bench can be just as important as the quality of the starting XI.
Both players have operated on the fringes of the senior national team, making their contributions an opportunity to strengthen their cases for more prominent roles. Their involvement also suggests that Nigeria may have useful alternatives available when the preferred attacking combinations need fresh legs or a different approach.
Of course, the Comoros fixture is only one measure of their readiness. The challenge will be to maintain that energy and decision-making against opponents who defend more effectively and allow less space in the final third.
Still, their influence on Tuesday was difficult to ignore. In a qualifying campaign where squad depth could become decisive, Ijamilusi and Okpe have given Eguavoen more options to consider.
The Super Falcons have done what was required against Comoros, securing a comprehensive aggregate victory while recording consecutive clean sheets and giving several players the opportunity to strengthen their claims for regular places.
Kanu’s goals, Payne’s attacking contribution, Alozie’s all-round performance, the promising centre-back partnership and the impact of Ijamilusi and Okpe all provide reasons for optimism, apart from Captain Rasheedat’s injury which was the only blot in the game on the night.
Yet the significance of the result will ultimately be measured by what follows. Morocco represent a different level of opposition, and Nigeria will need to combine the attacking confidence displayed against Comoros with greater tactical discipline and resilience.
The Olympic qualifying campaign remains a demanding journey, but the Super Falcons have taken another step forward. Their next challenge is to prove that this emphatic victory was not simply a result of the gap in quality between the two sides, but evidence of a team building towards a more convincing and consistent future.

title: Coca-Cola system contributes $1bn across its value chain in Nigeria, supporting more than 160,000 jobs
body:
The Coca-Cola system in Nigeria announced the results of a comprehensive socio-economic impact study, conducted by global consulting firm Steward Redqueen, following its Coca-Cola’s 75th Anniversary Gala celebrated recentlyin Abuja.
This new independent study highlights the scale of the Coca-Cola system’s contribution to Nigeria’s economy, employment, and communities.
The study reveals that the Coca-Cola system in Nigeria – comprising The Coca-Cola Company and its authorized bottler, Nigerian Bottling Company– alongside a broad network of local suppliers, distributors, and retailers, contributed $1 billion in value-added economic activity in 2024.
Across its value chain, the Coca-Cola system supported over 160,000 jobs, including nearly 3,000 direct jobs within the system and an additional 157,200 jobs supported through suppliers, partners, and customers. This means that for every direct job created by the system, 53 more jobs were supported across Nigeria’s economy.
The study also highlights the Coca-Cola system’s strong local integration, with $601 million worth of goods and services sourced from suppliers in Nigeria in 2024. This local procurement supports industries as diverse as sugar production, packaging, transportation, and marketing, reinforcing the Coca-Cola’s system role as a partner for growth in Nigeria’s economic development.
The Coca-Cola system has strengthened its footprint in Nigeria through sustained investment and innovation,including the opening of a new packaging collection hubin Apapa , Lagos in line with its sustainability agenda. The facility is a key part of Nigeria’s plastic recycling infrastructure and can process up to 13,000 metric tonnes of plastic bottles annually. The initiative aims to reduce plastic waste by collecting, sorting, and recycling PET plastics. It also supports local communities by creating jobs.
The Coca-Cola system’s contribution extends beyond economic impact. Nigeria is one of the beneficiaries of the Africa Water Stewardship Initiative , a nearly $25 million investment through 2030 to help address critical water-related challenges in local communities in 20 African markets, including Nigeria.
The study conducted by Steward Redqueen measured the direct, indirect, and induced economic impacts of the Coca-Cola system in Nigeria, combining company operational data with trusted third-party economic sources. The analysis demonstrates how Coca-Cola’s local operations ripple across the economy – from farmers growing sugarcane to retailers selling beverages – creating jobs, generating income, and building opportunities.

title: SpaceX Restricts Ukraine’s Military Starlink Without Warning, Disrupting Drone Missions, Defense Sources Say
body:
Restrictions affecting Starlink connectivity for Ukrainian users of the military “Starshield” package were detected overnight, complicating logistics and drone operations, sources in Ukraine’s Defense Ministry told Kyiv Post on Wednesday, Oct. 14.
Preliminary information indicates that users reported the restrictions affecting connections at speeds above 160 kph (100 mph), with officials working to establish what caused the restrictions. However, units reported connections dropping at different speeds, ranging from approximately 72 to 161 km/h.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
SpaceX unilaterally imposed speed restrictions on Starshield terminals used by Ukraine’s defense forces overnight on Oct. 14 without advance warning, sources told Kyiv Post
The restrictions are hampering drone missions, including interceptor and medium-range strike operations, and reducing capabilities for frontline logistics, reconnaissance and communications relay, the sources said.
The ministry is in contact with the United States, SpaceX and NATO partners, gathering reports from units and checking and activating backup communications channels.
Separately, an advisor to the president. Serhii Beskrestnov, known as “Flash,” confirmed the loss of connectivity for users of Starshield on Telegram on Wednesday morning.
Beskrestnov said Ukraine’s defense forces had received no advance warning and that several missions had been disrupted.
He also suggested the restrictions were linked to the current political tensions between Kyiv and Washington. That assessment was not confirmed by the Defense Ministry sources, who said the cause remained under investigation.
Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha recently said at the Warsaw Security Forum that intelligence sharing between Ukraine and the United States was continuing despite those tensions, but the issue of satellite connectivity restrictions now being investigated had not surfaced at that time.

She explores the secrets of Ukraine's intelligence services and shows the hidden side of global events. Her passion is uncovering secrets that change history. Born and lives in Kyiv.

title: IDF establishing new corps for countering low-altitude drones amid growing UAV threat
body: IDF Ground Forces Commander Maj.-Gen. Nadav Lotan is working to establish a new corps dedicated to countering low-altitude drone threats, as part of an effort to strengthen Israel's defenses against the growing threat posed by unmanned aerial vehicles, Walla learned on Tuesday.For more than a decade, the IDF has been trying to address the threat posed by drones operating in the airspace close to the ground, using a variety of methods. However, these efforts have accelerated since the October 7 massacre, alongside a worldwide push to develop solutions.The threat became evident during Hamas's attacks along the Gaza border at the beginning of the war and during the initial stages of the IDF's ground maneuver deep into the Gaza Strip. Hezbollah subsequently employed drones against IDF troops in southern Lebanon and civilians in Israel's home front.The drone threat has also manifested itself in the smuggling of weapons and drugs across the Egyptian and Jordanian borders. Smugglers have used particularly heavy drones capable of carrying payloads weighing dozens of kilograms. There are also growing concerns that drones could become a significant threat in the IDF's Judea and Samaria Division and along the Syrian border.The Defense Ministry and the IDF have accelerated projects to improve drone protection within the defense establishment. Some of these projects involve Israeli companies, while others entail purchasing technology from abroad.Accordingly, the IDF has begun deploying various defense systems in the field to improve and refine protection against different types of drones, including fiber-optic drones. These pose a considerable challenge for conventional militaries because they are difficult to detect. As a result, armies generally counter them using nets, interceptor drones, and ground-based gunfire.Five border defense battalions to form the foundation of new corpsThe IDF recently decided to establish the new low-altitude airspace defense corps using the existing border infantry battalions as its foundation.The corps will initially be based on five battalions that routinely protect the borders with Jordan and Egypt, as well as the security barrier area in the West Bank.Under the plan, these battalions will assume an additional mission alongside their existing responsibility for defending Israel's land borders: protecting against mobile threats operating in the airspace close to the ground.According to assessments, the corps' sixth battalion will be the tactical air defense battalion established during the war in response to threats from Gaza and Lebanon that emerged on an unprecedented scale.IDF transferring Ground Forces resources to support new anti-drone corpsTo support the new corps' establishment, the IDF will transfer significant resources from the Ground Forces to supplement the capabilities already available within the Border Defense Corps.These resources will include additional training personnel to develop a drone school focused on defensive missions.The IDF's Ground Forces already operate significant defensive drone capabilities, including intelligence-gathering operations conducted using drones by Unit 9900 of the Military Intelligence Directorate.It can therefore be assessed that Military Intelligence will play a role in developing the emerging combat doctrine, operational methods, and the type and scale of procurement involving drones and associated technologies, as well as training.

title: Trump's ambassador to Greece, Kimberly Guilfoyle, resigns after allegations of improper conduct
body:
FILE - Kimberly Guilfoyle speaks as President Donald Trump listens at a reception celebrating Greek Independence Day in the East Room of the White House, March 24, 2025, in Washington. Jacquelyn Martin/AP hide caption
WASHINGTON — The White House publicly asked for U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle's resignation on Tuesday as she faced mounting accusations of improper conduct, and she announced within two hours that she was quitting, ending days of talk and speculation about her professional fate. Guilfoyle insisted that she would "vigorously defend" herself.
President Donald Trump's administration had said earlier Tuesday it had asked Guilfoyle to leave her post after she faced severe criticism over allegations she engaged in improper and possibly illegal conduct before and during her tenure in Athens.
That revelation came in response to a question to freshly minted White House press secretary Katie Zacharia at her first media briefing Tuesday morning. Zacharia said Guilfoyle "has been a wonderful asset to the team, and we wish her well."
"She went to Greece. She was doing a good job, but we didn't like what we were reading," Trump said just after Guilfoyle's resignation, which was posted on her X account. He said he had not spoken to her but "she will not be there."
Guilfoyle's departure comes after its possibility was previewed to The Associated Press over the weekend and Trump registered his unhappiness on Monday at reports about her alleged conduct. Those comments came a day after the AP, citing a senior U.S. official, reported that Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio were "extremely pissed off" by Guilfoyle's reported conduct.
In a series of stories dating to late last month, The Wall Street Journal has reported questionable conduct by Guilfoyle, including an alleged threat to a host country official, accepting improper gifts and services and offering to use her influence inside the Republican administration in return for the payment of a large credit card bill.
Guilfoyle addressed the accusations directly in her resignation post on X, saying, "These allegations are false, and I intend to vigorously defend my name, my reputation, and my integrity."
"I have dedicated my professional life to fighting for justice, standing up for what is right, and defending the values that make America exceptional," she said. "I will not allow false accusations to define my decades of public service."
In a statement released late Sunday, Guilfoyle's lawyers denied that she had done anything wrong and claimed that the money she was seeking from a Trump donor was payment for services — public appearances and speaking engagements that predate her ambassadorial nomination — that had not been paid.
The lawyers, David Schwartz and Jesse Binnall, also rejected allegations of impropriety related to Guilfoyle's travel on private planes, saying that before every such trip she "sought, obtained and followed State Department guidance and followed the Department's travel regulations."
They did not immediately return calls Tuesday.
After defending Guilfoyle following the first report, Rubio declined to comment publicly on the growing allegations. Last week, Rubio said: "Our ambassador has been a strong ambassador here."
But after another report appeared later, Rubio — speaking Thursday before leaving Athens — berated journalists for asking about the allegations. He said that he didn't know if they were true and that he would not respond if he could not confirm them.
"You guys walk around thinking that because some source told you something and you reported it, it's the gospel. It's not the gospel. It's not the gospel for me. That's not the way we do things," Rubio said at the foot of his plane as Guilfoyle, who was there to see him depart, looked on.
A second U.S. official, who also spoke on the condition of anonymity to discuss personnel matters, said the State Department's inspector general was looking into the allegations, which first began surfacing in the Journal late last month and have since multiplied.
The second official could not say if a formal IG probe had begun. Inspectors general often conduct informal inquiries into complaints against staffers, and many times those inquiries do not result in a full-on investigation, which can result in disciplinary action up to and including dismissal. The State Department has declined to comment on a potential IG investigation.
There was no immediate response to Zacharia's statement from the Greek government or Cabinet members.
Ahead of Tuesday's announcement, Greek opposition parties had called on the Foreign Ministry to summon Guilfoyle to respond to the allegations made against her. "This, most importantly, is an issue of national dignity," Sia Anagnostopoulou, a former deputy foreign minister, said in parliament Friday. Foreign Minister Giorgos Gerapetritis responded that Guilfoyle had been treated "the same way as every other ambassador" and argued that an official summons had not been necessary.
Hours earlier, Guilfoyle had posted photos of her meeting this week with the Spanish ambassador to Athens as well as birthday wishes for Lara Trump, the president's daughter-in-law, accompanied by Dua Lipa's "Dance the Night," from the 2023 soundtrack of the movie "Barbie."
Greece has taken on an increasingly important and influential role because of its geographic location in Southeastern Europe and the Eastern Mediterranean, particularly on energy issues as the war with Iran has spiked global oil prices. Besides the vast number of Greek-registered oil tankers that regularly ply the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea, Greece is well positioned to be a pipeline conduit for liquefied natural gas imports into the Balkans and beyond.
As the U.S. ambassador to Greece, Guilfoyle had put an emphasis on energy issues, although her close association with executives in that sector was part of what got her into trouble.
The top two Democrats on the House Foreign Affairs and Senate Foreign Relations committees, Rep. Gregory Meeks of New York and Sen. Jeanne Shaheen of New Hampshire, as well as the ranking member on the House Committee for Oversight and Government Reform, Rep. Robert Garcia, D-Calif., have already called for an investigation into Guilfoyle.
Since late September, the Journal has detailed numerous accounts of questionable conduct by Guilfoyle. Its first report said that she had told guests at a reception that the United States could undermine the Greek government if it chose to, promoted the business interests of one particular Greek construction and energy company and allowed its lobbyist into private diplomatic meetings.
While Rubio was in Athens, the Journal reported — citing text messages — that Guilfoyle had asked a Trump donor and supporter to pay a $100,000 credit card bill just before her confirmation hearing, promising him access to administration officials if he did.
The Journal then reported that Guilfoyle had been enraged about not being invited to a Greek-themed event at the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, earlier this year and demanded to attend while boasting about luxury travel to France with energy company executives.
Another report, from the British tabloid The Daily Mail, said that Guilfoyle had alienated staff at the U.S. Embassy in Athens and had pushed the bounds of behavior appropriate for the top representative of the U.S. government to Greece.
Guilfoyle is a former Fox News Channel host and California prosecutor who was married to Democrat Gavin Newsom when he was San Francisco's mayor, before he became California's governor. She later was engaged to Trump's son Donald Trump Jr.

title: Russia’s new turret to automatically intercept enemy drones — CUST
body:
MOSCOW, October 14. /TASS/. The Tatarstan-based company Arkodim has begun testing an anti-drone turret equipped with software that enables the automatic interception of enemy unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), the Center for Unmanned Systems and Technologies (CUST) told TASS.
The turret will be part of an air defense system capable of achieving a target destruction probability of over 90%, it said.
"The turret is designed for mounting a machine gun. The weapon will be able to engage fixed-wing UAVs at a range of up to 1 km, expending 30-50 rounds to neutralize a single drone. This level of efficiency is achieved by firing at an interception point calculated by the software. The turret will be integrated into a short-range air defense system designed to protect critical infrastructure. Its key feature is the ability to provide early detection and select the most cost-effective and suitable interception method," the CUST noted, emphasizing the system's application for protecting critical infrastructure.
"Its [the system's] key feature is the ability to provide early detection and select the most cost-effective and suitable interception method. All combat operations of the anti-drone system will be automated, and the human operator will only need to make the decision to engage aerial targets. Arkodim is currently testing the system's components. According to the developer's estimates, the probability of a successful hit will exceed 90%," the CUST stated. The Center also specified that, in addition to turrets, the system will include a pre-guidance tower and an interceptor drone equipped with an onboard terminal guidance system to engage enemy UAVs at a range of several kilometers.

title: Death toll from Russian attacks on Kyiv rises to 5, injured to 36 – police
body:
As a result of the Russian attack on the capital, which lasted from Tuesday evening to Wednesday morning, 36 people were injured and five were killed, the Kyiv Police press service reported on Telegram on Wednesday.

"The highest number of casualties is in the multi-story residential building in Desniansky district that was hit by Russian military forces yesterday evening. Here, three women aged 35, 58, and 84 died. Another 25 people, including a young child, sustained injuries," the department informed.

In addition, two people were killed in Holosiivsky district as a result of the attack.

Overall, 5 people were killed and 36 injured across the capital as a result of the Russian attacks from Tuesday evening through Wednesday morning.

title: SpaceX once again tightens Starlink restrictions on Ukrainian army — ex-adviser
body:
MOSCOW, October 14. /TASS/. SpaceX has imposed even tighter speed restrictions on Starlink terminals used by the Ukrainian army, Sergey Sternenko, a former adviser to Ukraine’s defense minister, said.
"Our service members report that restrictions on the use of Starlink satellite communication terminals by our operators have been tightened. Disruptions now begin at speeds of 60-70 km/h," he wrote on Telegram.
Sergey Beskrestnov, Vladimir Zelensky’s external adviser and expert in communications and unmanned systems, said earlier on Wednesday that SpaceX had restricted the speed of Starlink terminals used by the Ukrainian army, with disruptions occurring at speeds above 160 km/h. According to Beskrestnov, the move disrupted a number of missions.

title: Botnets Prove Rogue AI Is Closer Than We Think
body:
2026 has been a strange year for AI safety.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei warned that more capable agent swarms could cause "catastrophic damage," and said rogue systems might be able to take over large parts of the internet within six to twelve months. A year ago, this would have sounded like AI-doomer fan fiction.
Then OpenAI disclosed what happened during internal cybersecurity evaluations: experimental agents circumvented isolation controls, communicated through unauthorized channels, obtained internet access, and compromised parts of OpenAI's infrastructure and Hugging Face's systems. OpenAI called it a "warning shot."
These claims have triggered a lot of debate about the credibility of these predictions. Sure, AI labs are selling fear to hype their IPOs and encourage regulations against Chinese labs. But most of the skepticism has focused on the technical feasibility of such a catastrophe. Unfortunately, almost every boring piece of infrastructure such a system would need already exists.
In 1988, the Morris worm spread across thousands of Unix machines on the early internet. Every infected machine could look for new hosts, giving worms the same unpleasant property as epidemics: exponential growth.
Botnets have spent decades since turning that idea into infrastructure.
AI changes one important thing: adaptability. Traditional worms are mostly rigid. Somebody writes exploitation logic for a small number of vulnerabilities and ships it. An agent can inspect an unfamiliar environment, reason about publicly documented vulnerabilities, and adapt its actions as it goes. That still leaves plenty of friction. Networks are heterogeneous, exploits fail, machines get patched, and defenders react. But autonomous movement between computers has existed in malware for nearly forty years. Adding a capable reasoning layer expands what such software can attempt on each new host.
Botnets already operate at enormous scale. Cloudflare estimates that the Aisuru botnet in 2025 reached between one and four million infected hosts and generated DDoS attacks peaking at 30 terabits per second.
Pooling ordinary computers is nothing new either. BOINC, the Berkeley volunteer distributed-computing network, reached roughly 33 PFLOPS of aggregate compute in 2019, as much as some of the world’s largest supercomputers at the time. Distributed LLM inference is already being experimented. Petals demonstrated a 176B model spread across consumer GPUs over the internet, with heterogeneous machines joining and leaving. BloomBee, published in 2026, also targets internet-scale inference under low-bandwidth conditions.
But a rogue network probably would not need to run one giant model everywhere.
Qwen3.8-27B, for example, can be quantized to roughly 18 GB, and is running on the lightweight laptop I am writing this article on. Its agentic performance is comparable to models that were frontier-class less than a year ago. Even much larger open-weight models can be compressed to manageable sizes. GLM5.3-Flash and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash are under 500 GB and only months away from frontier models.
A botnet could simply specialize its nodes. Powerful hosts run larger models, normal PCs run smaller agents, and weak machines handle scanning, networking, or storage. Claude Code already does this with subagents.
Every frontier-class open-weight model can already be downloaded from Hugging Face or ModelScope without authentication, with millions of model downloads taking place every day. The model-distribution problem is barely a problem at all.
Even worse, community-made "uncensored" variants are widely available. Some are explicitly tuned to comply with requests involving criminal activity that mainstream models would normally refuse.
The real question is not whether the parts exist. It is who puts them together, and why.
Right now, there is no evidence that a model will suddenly decide to copy itself across the internet out of some newfound sense of self-preservation. Models do not have goals of their own. Humans, on the other hand, have plenty of reasons to build an autonomous network deliberately. Cybercrime is the most obvious one.
It will likely start small. A criminal group takes a standard worm, wires in a local model to help it improvise when standard scripts fail, and gradually automates the rest of the operation.
The first real "rogue AI" probably will not be a lab experiment that wakes up and breaks out of containment. Somebody is just going to build it on purpose.
