title: Wednesday, 14 October 2026
body: Regional Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan explained that his vision of the peace deal with Azerbaijan includes an Armenian border of 29,743 square metres, the exchange of enclaves and exclaves, and open transit links. Armenia’s Foreign Minister Ararat Mirzoyan suggested during the Warsaw Security Forum that the Eastern Partnership should evolve from a common framework into a flexible platform that lets each partner find its own way to Europe. Armenia Labour Minister Arsen Torosyan said that state programmes for Nagorno-Karabakh refugees aim to help them settle and integrate into Armenian society. However, he added that this policy should not prevent displaced people from pursuing their rights through international conventions. The Yerevan City Council has granted the Hrazdan Gorge the status of a specially protected natural area of local significance. The Yerevan municipality is demolishing what it describes as illegal buildings located on the pavements in the Ajapnyak district. Azerbaijan Sheikh-ul-Islam Allahshukur Pashazadeh, head of the Caucasus Muslims Board, has said that Azerbaijan has not banned the hijab in schools. ‘Azerbaijan separates religion from the state, and schools from religion,’ Pashazadeh said. He added that certain forces, both inside and outside the country, were trying to spread claims that Muslims were being mistreated in Azerbaijan. A protest was held yesterday outside the Azerbaijani Embassy in Ankara by members of the Köklü Değişim movement. Köklü Değişim is a media and publishing platform closely associated with Hizb ut-Tahrir’s activities in Turkey. Hizb ut-Tahrir is an organisation founded in Palestine that advocates for the establishment of a state governed by Islamic law. Georgia Constitutional Court Judge Manana Kobakhidze has resigned from her post after asking to not be involved in the government’s plan to ban the opposition. The other judges rejected her request. She was one of the founders of Georgian Dream, served as the party’s chair, and was a member of parliament. Georgia’s Constitutional Court has accepted Georgian Dream’s lawsuit seeking to ban opposition parties for substantive review. According to a court notice published yesterday, the case will be heard by the court’s Plenum, consisting of seven judges. The Georgian Orthodox Church has denied accreditation to opposition-leaning TV channels TV Pirveli and Formula for the Mtskhetoba (Svetitskhovloba) celebration. Church spokesperson Andria Jaghmaidze has accused both channels of repeatedly violating internal rules despite several warnings. He said their reporters had left the areas designated for the media without permission, disrupting religious services. An activist who accused court bailiffs of violence is now facing a complaint from the same officers over alleged insults. Ruska Mchedlidze says the Interior Ministry has launched administrative proceedings against her. She is accused of insulting court bailiffs on 29 July. Abkhazia Alik Agrba, former CEO of SP Put-A (‘SP Path-A’), has been found guilty of abuse of authority that caused damage to the Abkhazian Railway state unitary enterprise. According to the case materials, the former director of Abkhazian Railway signed a contract with Agrba for the supply of two used electric trains worth ₽18 million ($220,000) each, despite Agrba was knowing that they could only be used for scrap metal. South Ossetia President Marat Kambolov has nominated former judge Soslan Margiev for the post of head of government of the republic. According to unconfirmed reports, former Deputy Interior Minister Atsamaz Sagkaev distributed 400 firearms to his subordinates as awards, including weapons intended exclusively for special forces units. He allegedly did so in preparation for retaining power by force. A criminal case has been opened against him on suspicion of abuse of official powers. The North Caucasus Since the beginning of 2026, 260 people have been detained in the North Caucasus on suspicion of preparing terrorist attacks, financing terrorist activities, and promoting or justifying terrorism. Most of them were under the age of 20, and some were minors, Federal Security Service (FSB) Director Aleksandr Bortnikov said at a meeting of the National Anti-Terrorism Committee. Last year, 280 people were detained over the course of the entire year. Following the Yemeni Houthis’ attack on Saudi Arabia’s Riyadh airport, Chechen Head Ramzan Kadyrov has said that US bases in the Middle East should be targeted, but that civilian facilities ‘cannot be justified’. Human rights defenders helped a gay man who fled Chechnya obtain protection in Europe. According to NC SOS Crisis Group, he had previously been detained in Chechnya during a set-up meeting organised by security force officers. Ramina Gandaloeva, a resident of Ingushetia, appealed to Kadyrov to intervene in a family dispute over a child. According to Gandaloeva, her former husband, Mikail Gandaloev, took their six-month-old child and subsequently stabbed one of her brothers during a confrontation. After the parties reconciled and a court ruled that the child should be returned to the mother, he pressed charges against her brothers. A court has rejected a lawsuit by former senator from Karachay–Cherkessia Rauf Arashukov, who is serving a life sentence at the Black Dolphin penal colony, seeking to have his status as a prisoner considered prone to attacking prison staff and law enforcement officers revoked. Since 2022, the authorities in Adygea have allocated almost ₽7.7 billion ($90 million) to support soldiers fighting in Ukraine and their families, Head Murat Kumpilov said during a meeting with Sergei Usmanov, executive director of the Defenders of the Fatherland state foundation. Adygea’s annual budget revenue amounts to around ₽40–50 billion ($470–$600 million). In Ingushetia, a resident of the village of Ekazhevo was detained for forcibly holding his wife in their home and firing a shotgun towards a police officer who had arrived to help her. For ease of reading, we choose not to use qualifiers such as ‘de facto’, ‘unrecognised’, or ‘partially recognised’ when discussing institutions or political positions within Abkhazia, Nagorno-Karabakh, and South Ossetia. This does not imply a position on their status.

title: Israel returns 22 artifacts to Greece in first antiquities repatriation between Jerusalem, Athens
body: Israel on Tuesday returned a collection of 22 artifacts illegally removed from Greece, in the first repatriation of its kind between the two countries, as Athens renews its push to recover illegally taken and stolen antiquities from around the world.Among the artifacts returned are fifteen ancient Attic vessels, six vases from Corinthian workshops, and one bronze statue of a female figure, all dating to between the 8th and 4th centuries BCE.Of the Attic vessels, 11 are black-and-white, three are red-and-white, and one is ambergris, dating to the ancient and classical periods. The six Corinthian vases date to the ancient period, while the authenticity of the bronze female statuette requires further investigation.The antiquities were seized in 2020 during a joint investigation into illegal antiquities trafficking conducted by the IAA's Theft Prevention Unit, Israel Police, and the Israel Tax Authority. As part of the operation, the forces raided a gallery, warehouses, and apartments in the Gush Dan area, where thousands of illegally acquired archaeological items from Israel and around the world were found.They were officially returned in a Tuesday handover ceremony at the National Archaeological Museum in Athens, attended by Greek Culture Minister Lina Mendoni, Israeli Ambassador to Greece Pninat Yanay, and Israel Antiquities Authority's (IAA) Theft Prevention Unit Director Amir Ganor.“This celebration is not only about returning antiquities to their rightful home. It is also a celebration of something much greater and deeper: the special, strong, and profound friendship between the State of Israel and Greece,” she wrote.Combating illegal antiquities trade“Two modern states, two ancient nations, and two great civilizations that deeply understand the meaning of history, the importance of heritage, and the responsibility to preserve it for future generations. These antiquities belong to Greece's past. Today, through their return, they also become part of the shared future of Israel and Greece.”“Let us try to imagine a child looking at one of these ancient vessels today and feeling a spark of wonder,” Yanay added. “They see what another child might have seen and felt 2,000 years ago, and thus become another link in the chain of generations that had been broken.”“For me, there is also something deeply moving in the thought that I have the privilege, as Ambassador of Israel, of placing this ancient object into your capable hands, and that my country had the honor of contributing to this significant moment and mission.”“The illegal trade in antiquities knows no borders, neither the boundaries of the law nor the borders between countries,” Ganor said. “Antiquities that are looted in one country find their way to another, causing irreversible damage to the cultural heritage of the country of origin.”“The illegal trade in antiquities serves as a cover for the financing of terrorism and organized crime, and it serves as a means of money laundering. Cutting off smuggling chains and preventing continued illegal profiting on the back of antiquities helps to thwart and prevent various types of criminal activity, and certainly helps to protect cultural heritage assets.”Today, I had the great honor of taking part in a particularly moving and meaningful ceremony at the National Archaeological Museum in Athens, in the presence of Greece's @cultureGR , Dr. Lina Mendoni, and other distinguished officials, during which the State of @Israel returned to Greece ancient artifacts dating back more than 2,000 years. Behind this moving moment stands the determined and thorough work of the Israeli authorities, who carried out complex investigations, never gave up, and left no evidence unchecked. Once it was established that the antiquities had reached Israel through illegal channels and that they rightfully belonged to Greece, the way was opened for their return home. Antiquities are much more than historical objects. They are moments from the past, frozen in time through art. They tell us who the people who created them were, what they believed in, how they lived, and remind us how deeply the past remains part of who we are today. For more than 2,000 years, these ancient objects have witnessed the rise and fall of empires, wars, revolutions, and enormous changes in our world. And through it all, they have survived. What I find truly remarkable is that although they are silent, they continue to speak. They are alive. They tell a story. During my speech, I invited the audience to imagine a Greek child standing today in front of one of these ancient objects, looking at it with eyes full of wonder and excitement. It is very possible that 2,000 years ago, another child stood before that very same object and felt exactly the same excitement. This is the power of history. This is the unbreakable chain connecting generations, linking the past to the present, and connecting who we once were to who we are today. I also said that it is a great privilege for me, as Israel's Ambassador to Greece, to take part in this moment, when we return these precious antiquities to the faithful hands of Greece and its people, to whom they rightfully belong. I would also like to express my heartfelt thanks to Greece's Minister of Culture, Dr. Lina Mendoni, for her warm welcome and the genuine emotion she showed throughout the ceremony. Her excitement touched everyone in the room and reminded us all just how important and meaningful this moment is for Greece, its rich history, its proud heritage, and its future. And today is certainly a day worth celebrating. But this celebration is not only about returning antiquities to their rightful home. It is also a celebration of something much greater and deeper: the special, strong, and profound friendship between the State of Israel and Greece. Two modern states, two ancient nations, and two great civilizations that deeply understand the meaning of history, the importance of heritage, and the responsibility to preserve it for future generations. These antiquities belong to Greece's past. Today, through their return, they also become part of the shared future of Israel and Greece.— Ambassador Pninat Yanay (@Amb_PninatYanay) October 13, 2026Becoming links in the chains between generationsHeritage Minister Amichai Eliyahu added that “The State of Israel is well aware of the deep connection between a people and its heritage, and the importance of preserving the historical evidence that tells its story.”“The return of these antiquities to Greece expresses our commitment to protect cultural heritage assets, and to act resolutely against the illegal trade in antiquities, wherever it takes place.”He continued, congratulating the IAA and both Greek and Israeli law enforcement agencies for their actions that led to the return of the artifacts.“The strengthening cooperation between the countries expresses a shared responsibility to preserve the treasures of the past, for the sake of future generations,” he said.Israel, Greece expected to sign a heritage MoUAs a result of cooperation between the IAA's Theft Prevention Unit and the Greek Antiquities Police in this case, a joint international enforcement workshop was held for representatives of the two units last month.During the workshop, the two units discussed the possibility of expanding information sharing, identifying items suspected of being looted, and tracing antiquities trade routes.In her remarks at the handover ceremony, Mendoni noted that during her visit to Jerusalem in March 2025, she discussed the expansion of cultural cooperation between Israel and Greece with Culture and Sports Minister Miki Zohar.According to Mendoni, the return of these antiquities is a practical expression of the commitment that the two ministers discussed at their meeting. A memorandum of understanding is expected to be signed between the countries, which will anchor their cooperation in the field of protecting cultural heritage assets.

title: IMF Warns Nigeria Against Restoring Petrol Subsidy
body: Peter Uzoho The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has advised Nigeria against restoring broad petrol subsidy, recommending targeted support for vulnerable households to cushion the impact of rising energy costs. IMF said blanket petrol subsidies were expensive, often benefited higher-income consumers disproportionately and could worsen fiscal pressures amid rising borrowing costs. Director of the IMF’s Fiscal Affairs Department, Rodrigo Valdés, gave the warning Wednesday during a press briefing on the fund’s fiscal monitor at the 2026 annual meetings of the IMF and World Bank in Bangkok, Thailand. His comments followed a question on how the fund could recommend allowing energy prices to reflect scarcity when higher fuel prices in Nigeria could raise transport costs, worsen inflation and deepen poverty, particularly when the government was facing calls to restore petrol subsidy ahead of an election year. “Protecting people is not the same as protecting the price of fuels,” Valdés said. He said fuel subsidies or measures preventing prices from adjusting fully to an energy shock had cost countries between 1 percent and 1.5 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 2026. “It’s first fiscally very costly, and second, if you look at the pattern of consumption, it’s easy to see that that subsidy is readily regressive in many places,” he said. Valdés said governments should instead use social safety nets and household data to identify people who need assistance. “There are better tools to deal with this,” he said. The federal government recently announced a 30-day petrol discount at Nigerian National Petroleum Company (NNPC) Limited retail stations, with priority for public transport operators, to cushion the impact of rising fuel prices. Minister of Finance, Taiwo Oyedele, said NNPC retail would sell petrol at cost by foregoing its retail profit margin, describing the measure as temporary relief rather than a return to petrol subsidy. The government also proposed negotiating a ceiling of N1,350 per litre on petrol’s ex-gantry or landing cost, subject to monthly reviews The IMF also recommended targeted interventions to cushion the effect of higher fuel prices on transportation costs. A division chief in the fund’s fiscal affairs department, Davide Furceri, said governments could redirect some of the resources spent on blanket subsidies towards vulnerable consumers. “For example, you mentioned transportation costs. Yeah, gasoline could go up, and perhaps bus fees may be subsidised in a way that is a much better policy at the end of the day than just a blanket subsidy for everybody,” Furceri said. He also suggested alternatives such as school feeding programmes, geographical targeting and assistance for vulnerable farmers. Furceri acknowledged that some countries lacked household registries and digital payment systems needed to deliver targeted support effectively. However, he said governments could adopt alternative approaches in the short term while developing stronger systems. He recommended that assistance should be limited, targeted and temporary. Valdés explained that fuel subsidies could worsen global energy pressures by preventing demand from adjusting when supplies were constrained. “When you subsidise, you don’t allow, at the end of the day, demand to adjust,” he said. “And reality is that we have less fuels in the world economy. That means that someone else has to adjust more, and the market produces a higher price for that.” The IMF official said subsidies were not only costly and regressive but could also have spillover effects on the global economy.

title: AG Mortgage Bank Appoints Chieduzie Ogbuehi as Company Secretary
body: AG Mortgage Bank Plc has announced the appointment of Chieduzie Ogbuehi, as its substantive Company Secretary, effective from September 24, 2026. Chieduzie is a corporate services executive and legal professional with over 15 years of experience advising Boards and executive management on personnel management, legal, regulatory and dispute resolution matters. According to a statement, his appointment further strengthens AG Mortgage Bank Plc’s commitment to sound corporate governance, regulatory compliance and effective institutional management as the Bank continues to advance its position in Nigeria’s mortgage and housing finance sector. Prior to joining AG Mortgage Bank Plc, Chieduzie held leadership roles including Head of Corporate Services at James Cubitt, where he headed the Human Resources, Legal and Company Secretariat functions. Before then, he served as the Head of Corporate and Commercial Transactions at Canaan Partners. He began his mortgage Banking journey as a Legal Officer at Haggai Mortgage Bank Limited. Chieduzie is a member of the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA), Associate of the Chartered Institute of Secretaries and Administrators, Nigeria (ACIS), Associate of the Chartered Institute of Taxation of Nigeria (ACTI), Fellow of the Institute of Credit Administration (FICA), Member of the Nigerian Institute of Chartered Arbitrators (MCArb), and is registered with the Financial Reporting Council of Nigeria (FRCN). As substantive Company Secretary, Chieduzie will continue to support AG Mortgage Bank Plc’s commitment to strong corporate governance, regulatory compliance and effective Board and management processes, while contributing to the Bank’s continued growth and institutional development.

title: Save the Children country director freed after detention in Juba
body: Save the Children’s country director in South Sudan, Chris Nyamandi, was released from government custody without charge on Tuesday, the charity said. Nyamandi, a Zimbabwean national, was detained in the capital, Juba, on Oct. 8. The reasons for his detention remain unclear, the organisation said. “We are relieved that our Country Director in South Sudan, who was detained in Juba on 8 October and held in government custody, was released yesterday, Tuesday, with no charges laid,” Save the Children told Radio Tamazuj on Wednesday. “It remains unclear why he was detained,” it added. Nyamandi was reportedly detained alongside a colleague from the organisation’s business development department while the two were at a hotel in Juba. The colleague told ZimLive that authorities alleged the pair had been discussing politics. Radio Tamazuj could not independently verify the allegation. Nyamandi’s detention came amid travel restrictions in Juba and political uncertainty in South Sudan, where preparations for long-delayed general elections have been complicated by disputes over the country’s political transition. South Sudan gained independence from Sudan in 2011 and has struggled to implement a 2018 peace agreement that ended five years of civil war. The post Save the Children country director freed after detention in Juba appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: US-Russia Diesel Deal: What’s The Big Idea?
body:
US President Donald Trump announced on Friday that he had reached a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin on diesel shipments and a temporary easing of US sanctions against Russia. The deal, which is aimed at bringing down domestic fuel prices, foresees an initial shipment of 300,000 tonnes of Russian diesel in October, with further deliveries to follow. Europe’s media discuss wider implications and the impact on the US’s credibility as an ally.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Dagens Nyheter (Sweden) is appalled by the US President’s antics:
“What we are witnessing is a complete moral collapse – and a collapse of logical thinking. ... Donald Trump’s poll ratings continue to plummet. The mid-term elections are just a month away. He may soon find himself facing a Congress intent on investigating the rampant corruption in the White House. He is terrified that he and his family will be held to account. ... And when he hits rock bottom, his first instinct is to turn to Putin – and stab Ukraine in the back yet again. It is almost impossible to put into words how despicable this is.”
Europe’s criticism lacks credibility, Iltalehti (Finland) stresses:
“Time and again, people in Europe express horror at the idea that the United States is abandoning Ukraine and leaving Europe at the mercy of Russia – but that has not happened. Although it is true that Europe has had to take on much greater responsibility for European defence, this is not just Trump’s idea but the result of a long-term trend in US security policy. In their moral zeal, Europeans should bear in mind that the deal announced by Trump is, after all, far smaller than the volume of Russian gas and oil that Europe continues to purchase every year. Europe’s calls for sanctions would be more credible if it cleaned up its own act first.”
US companies need Ukraine as testing ground
Will Trump lead the US into the Russian camp by switching sides entirely? wonders Neatkarīgā (Latvia) :
“Ukraine and the EU have already prepared for a complete US withdrawal from Ukraine. However, this is unlikely to happen, because Ukraine is currently the main testing ground for state-of-the-art military technologies. In other words: if you are not present in the Ukrainian war zone, you are not part of the defence industry or the arms trade. Whatever one may think of Trump, it would be difficult for him to become Putin’s direct ally on the battlefield, even if he genuinely wanted to. The US public simply wouldn’t understand.”
Trump’s diesel deal will do more harm than good, says The Independent (United Kingdom):
“His deal to buy diesel from Vladimir Putin’s gangster regime is as shocking in its cynicism as it is counterproductive. Mr Trump and the average US floating voter may not care that they are pumping money into the Russian war machine, prolonging the war and killing Ukrainians. But they ought to care that the deal will not bring down the price of diesel – and that it makes Mr Trump look weak. ... There is, in truth, little that the British government, or the governments of our allies in Europe and around the world, can do about Mr Trump’s misjudgment of Mr Putin – except to remain steadfast in our support for the Ukrainian people.”
Trump has destroyed his credibility for a few drops of diesel, notes Jutarnji (Croatia) list:
“By opening the doors to Russian diesel, Washington is de facto breaching its own sanctions and filling the Kremlin’s coffers with foreign currency that will fund the continuation of its aggression against Ukraine. This has left the White House under fire from its allies. While Washington is peddling a fairy tale about economic salvation, in practice Trump has given the Kremlin a diplomatic gift and money in exchange for fuel enough for half a working day, the BBC has calculated. Moscow wants to send 300,000 tonnes of diesel to make life easier for US motorists and farmers. But the US consumes around 3.6 million barrels of diesel [around 500,000 tonnes] every day.”
On news website Adevărul, former journalist and military attaché Laurențiu Sfinteș wonders why the US president wants to strike this deal in the first place (Romania) :
“At the end of the day, every politician in the world is accountable only to their own electorate. ... However, if they only have to stand for election once every four, five or even seven years, things are straightforward. If they have to face major elections every two years, things becomes extremely complicated. ... Then all that matters is the ever-changing nature of the factors that influence the voter’s mobility and sentiment. And US voters are well-educated citizens who spend half their life in powerful cars – usually running on diesel – and who quickly lose their tempers when they see the prices at the filling stations.”
Delfi columnist Rimvydas Valatka (Lithuania) is outraged:
“The US doesn’t need Russian diesel. It has more than enough of its own. Last year, it exported 62 million tonnes – almost twice as much as Russia, which is now suffering from a diesel shortage itself. ... It has gone from being an exporter to an importer. Trump needed a pretext to lift the sanctions against Russia. This is yet another of his lies. A smokescreen for the Maga idiots. ... The diesel from Russia is just a drop in Putin and Trump’s blood-soaked ocean. The US President is extending a helping hand to Russia, the aggressor at a time when Russia is no longer even hiding the fact that it is deliberately targeting Ukrainian civilians. ... America has openly sided with the Russian terrorists.”
In a Telegram post republished by Echo, journalist Dmitry Kolezev (Russia) does not see the deal as a disaster for Kyiv:
“For obvious reasons, the EU does not welcome Trump’s renewed outpouring of affection for Putin. But even if all this poses a major problem for Zelensky and Ukraine, it’s unlikely that these developments spell disaster or the end of US support. With less than a month to go before the US mid-term elections tensions are running high, and in all likelihood we will simply have to weather this storm. It is possible that against the backdrop of this pressure, Kyiv will scale back its attacks on Russian oil refineries. However, it is by no means certain that this will make things any easier for Russia.”
Novinky.cz is unequivocal in its stance (Czech Republic) :
“One thing is clear after the US’s latest move: transatlantic ties are a thing of the past. Trump doesn’t honour commitments and is prepared to step on anyone’s toes or stab them in the back. To feel reassured by Trump’s repeated promises that the US would honour its NATO commitments and come to the aid of a country under attack would be self-deception. If it suits him, he’ll come. But then again, perhaps he won’t. Trump’s America is not a reliable partner but a frenemy – something between a friend and an enemy – and one must behave accordingly.”

title: India's Bank of Baroda to 'defend interests' after BR Shetty's $15bn lawsuit
body: India's Bank of Baroda on Wednesday ​said ​it would protect ​its interests, a day after UAE-based ⁠businessman and founder of NMC Health BR Shetty filed ⁠a $15 billion case against the lender and ​25 other defendants at Bombay High Court. Mr Shetty alleged ⁠the Bank of Baroda and several current and former employees helped facilitate a fraud that contributed to the collapse of the Middle East healthcare group, according to a ⁠court filing reviewed by Reuters. The firm, then the Gulf's largest private healthcare provider, ​was ⁠placed under administration in 2020 ‌after months of financial mismanagement and disclosed debts of $6.6 billion, way above previous estimates ​of $2.1 billion. Representatives for Mr Shetty did not immediately respond to requests for comment. In a stock exchange notification on Wednesday, the country's second-largest state lender said: “The bank has not been served with such a suit and cannot comment on the contents of pleadings, which are untested in court. If and when the bank is served, the bank will defend the suit firmly and take all steps necessary to protect its interests.” The Bank of Baroda added that it was pursuing recovery and enforcement proceedings in India and the UAE against Mr Shetty for outstanding dues of 28 billion rupees ($294.5 million) and had obtained several decrees against him. The lender will ​not bear any immediate liability until any order is ‌passed or until it ⁠is required to make a provision on ​account of potential damages, the lender said. Bank of Baroda ​shares dropped ‌2.6 per cent on Tuesday after the legal action was reported. The lawsuit, which centres on the bank's lending to ⁠NMC Health and affiliated entities in the UAE, comes three months after the lender agreed to pay $600 million to settle claims brought by administrators of NMC. Mr Shetty alleged that bank officials enabled round-tripping transactions, ignored repeated anti-money laundering warnings and ​accepted documents bearing forged signatures. He is seeking $5 billion in direct damages, $5 billion in consequential damages and an additional $5 billion for reputational harm, the filing showed.

title: Sber services operating normally after drone attack on data center in Balakovo
body:
MOSCOW, October 14. /TASS/. Sber confirms that a drone attack targeted a data center in Balakovo, Saratov Region, but all the company’s systems and services are operating normally, Alexander Vedyakhin, First Deputy Chairman of Sberbank’s Executive Board, told reporters.
"We confirm that an attack on the data center took place. However, all Sberbank systems and services are operating normally," he said.
A drone attack was reported in Balakovo, Saratov Region by Governor Roman Busargin on the morning of October 14. According to him, a woman was killed, several residential buildings were damaged, but all infrastructure facilities in Balakovo are operating normally. Schools in Balakovo have canceled classes, and kindergartens will remain closed, Balakovo Municipal District Head Sergey Barulin said on Max.

title: Drone hit a boat off southern Iran port of Sirik, 3 injured
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 14 (MNA) – Three fishermen have been injured after a fishing boat was struck in an incident involving an unidentified drone near Sirik port in southern Iran’s Hormozgan province, the provincial governor general’s office announced.
Deputy Governor General of Hormozgan province for the Political and Social Affairs Ahmad Nafisi stated that the fishing boat was struck in what it is described as an attack by a US drone.
According to initial reports, no fatalities have so far been reported.
Following this incident, and in coordination with relevant authorities, the Sirik County hospital has been placed on standby position to admit and treat the injured, and an ambulance has been dispatched to the pier.
The incident is being investigated and followed up by the responsible authorities, and further information will be announced subsequently.

title: Ukrainian Drones Hit Sberbank Data Center After Yandex Attacks
body:
Ukrainian drones targeted a major data center under construction for Russian state lender Sberbank in the Saratov region overnight, First Deputy CEO Alexander Vedyakhin said Wednesday, as attacks on Moscow disrupted more than 500 flights.
Vedyakhin said all banking systems and online services continued to operate normally and no employees were injured in the attack in the Volga River city of Balakovo, according to the state-run news agency TASS.
Users across Russia nevertheless reported disruptions to Sberbank and its GigaChat artificial intelligence service, as well as several other major online platforms, according to outage tracker Detector404. The reports did not establish a link between the disruptions and the drone attacks.
NASA’s satellite fire-monitoring system showed multiple fires in Balakovo.
Saratov region Governor Roman Busargin said “all infrastructure facilities” were operating normally, without identifying Sberbank’s data center as a target. He said one woman was killed and several homes were damaged in the drone strikes.
The attack on Sberbank follows three consecutive Ukrainian drone strikes that disabled half of tech giant Yandex’s data centers. Ukraine says it is responding to Russian attacks on its own data sites.
“You didn’t think it would stop with just Yandex, did you?” Ukraine’s Fire Point arms company said in a social media post Wednesday morning.
Sberbank began construction of the 55,000-square-meter (592,000-square-foot) facility in 2021, promoting the 122.2 billion ruble ($1.4 billion) project as one of Europe’s largest data centers, with completion expected in 2030.
Sberbank and its main domestic rival, Yandex, are leading Russian developers of artificial intelligence, with their respective GigaChat and YandexGPT models. State media reported in 2024 that Sberbank’s Balakovo center would host Russia’s biggest supercomputer, which was scheduled to go into operation in 2027.
Russia’s Defense Ministry said its air defense systems destroyed 902 Ukrainian drones over 19 Russian regions and annexed Crimea between Tuesday evening and Wednesday morning.
Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said “most” of the 493 Ukrainian drones flying toward the region were neutralized, 180 of them on direct approach to the capital.
The attacks on Moscow prompted civil aviation authority Rosaviatsia to restrict arrivals and departures at all four Moscow airports after 10 p.m. Tuesday, in the second prolonged shutdown of Moscow’s airports in less than a week.
Russia’s Defense Ministry said its forces struck seven Ukrainian energy infrastructure facilities and a data center with ground-launched missiles and long-range strike drones overnight.
Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak later accused Ukraine of attacking two oil refineries in the Saratov and Ryazan regions Wednesday, saying Kyiv was showing no signs of moving toward an energy ceasefire announced by U.S. President Donald Trump.
Ukrainian presidential adviser Dmytro Lytvyn denied those statements, telling reporters that Ukraine struck a data center and another unnamed target but not refineries.
