title: Board of Peace preparing for Gaza field survey to find locations for Hamas weapons handover
body: US officials and representatives of the Board of Peace are preparing to conduct a field survey and mapping operation in the Gaza Strip to identify geographically suitable locations where Hamas members would surrender their weapons under US President Donald Trump's 20-point plan, Walla learned on Tuesday.Israeli defense officials have expressed their confusion at the American approach to the reconstruction of the Gaza Strip after the war, particularly Washington's desire to accelerate processes that appear to run counter to developments on the ground.Security officials familiar with the details of the regional process said there was an enormous gap between Hamas's conduct and US aspirations to advance reconstruction in exchange for the surrender of weapons.Under Hamas's original demands, the terrorist organization would be willing to hand over its weapons to a third party that would safeguard them inside the Gaza Strip, subject to commitments regarding reconstruction and an Israeli withdrawal."If two months ago Hamas was still trying to create a false impression that it was willing to disarm, now it is not even doing that, and it is investing its efforts in preparing for a return to fighting,” one security official stressed.Military officials told Walla that the Gaza Strip is currently closer to escalation than to reconstruction and a negotiated arrangement.They pointed to attempts by Hamas's military wing to rebuild its capabilities and strengthen its forces, ongoing training exercises, attempts to provoke confrontations with IDF troops along the Yellow Line, and intelligence warnings of planned terrorist attacks.These include concerns about attempts to carry out attacks in the period leading up to Israel's elections, with the aim of influencing the results.Israel striking Hamas 2-3 times daily in GazaMeanwhile, the IDF and Shin Bet (Israel Security Agency) are carrying out an average of two to three targeted operations daily against Hamas operatives and commanders in the Gaza Strip.Some of those targeted were involved in the October 7 attacks, while others are currently organizing terrorist attacks or attempting to cross the Yellow Line.Security officials maintain that, according to assessments in Jerusalem, Israel will oppose any reconstruction measures unless Hamas is disarmed in practice and the Gaza Strip is demilitarized, including the removal of terrorist infrastructure, weapons, and terrorists.

title: Moscow, Washington vs. Kyiv: Can Trump Force Ukraine to Capitulate?
body:
US President Donald Trump’s recent statements have by now fully aligned with those coming from the Kremlin.
Meanwhile, on the front line, the Russian army has had no advantage for almost a year. Indeed, the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) is counterattacking and liberating settlements in the Donbas itself – the region Putin has identified as a key objective for the Russian military.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Against this backdrop, Trump has partially lifted energy sanctions on Russia and announced an agreement to import several hundred thousand tons of diesel fuel from Russia to the US.
Then, under the guise of a peace plan, Trump began issuing ultimatums to Ukraine, demanding that it stop striking Russian oil refineries, and calling for “no strikes on oil refining facilities.” The plan is supposedly bilateral but is, in practice, one-sided in Ukraine’s case, since Ukraine has only one oil refinery, which Russia has already destroyed.
After the ultimatum, Trump went further, declaring that Ukraine “should get” a new president because he was dissatisfied with Zelensky’s refusal to sign a “peace agreement.”
Predictably, this was followed by threats to stop supplying Ukraine with intelligence about Russian ballistic missile strikes against Ukrainian civilian targets.
By Oct. 13, after the initial emotions and passions had subsided, new US proposals for a peace agreement were revealed by Washington Post columnist David Ignatius. There has been some progress: the Russian demands for territorial concessions are no longer repeated.
The reaction of most Ukrainians to the latest developments is extremely sharp.
“Trump’s energy truce means that Ukraine does not strike Russian oil refineries that are operating, while Russia does not strike the Ukrainian refinery that is not operating. The next step in Trump’s incredible plan will be to announce a ceasefire. Ukraine will have to promise not to strike the Russian army, and Russia will give its word not to strike the Russian army. And peace will immediately follow,” investment banker Serhiy Fursa wrote.
“The overall strategy has long been clear: blame Ukraine for your own miscalculations and use Russian oil refineries as an example, while shielding a target that is genuinely painful for the Russians. The figures for Russian diesel supplies to the US are not what matters here. What matters is the violation of laws passed by Congress, as well as the creation of new precedents for cooperation and business with the Russian war machine,” said Olha Aivazovska, head of the OPORA civil society analytical group.
“By refusing to provide us with intelligence on the trajectories of missile attacks against Ukraine, America is, in effect, becoming complicit in Russia’s murder of Ukrainian civilians,” said Oleksandr Shvets, editor-in-chief of the Fakty newspaper.
A member of the Cabinet of Ministers told Kyiv Post that Trump’s move had come as a complete surprise to Ukrainians.
“This is simply unthinkable. It is a betrayal of every allied position. It is worse than the Russians,” he said.
The US president’s motives are clearly an attempt to forestall an Election Day disaster for Republicans on Nov. 3. He hopes, at the very least, to convince Americans that he is doing something about sky-high fuel prices.
Putin’s motives, however, are more perhaps more complex. Despite the negligible export volumes, Russian experts believe he can present the deal to a war-weary Russian population as a victory –signaling renewed warming of relations and rapprochement with the US.
“What does Putin need this for? To damage Trump’s relations with Zelensky and Europe, which, like Zelensky, has condemned the deal. And to try to use it as leverage, so that Trump pressures Zelensky to restrict Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries,” wrote Russian economist Kirill Rogov.
Among other things, Trump said that Ukraine should “have a new president” because, supposedly, Zelensky did not want to sign a peace agreement – a capitulation in a war that Ukraine is not losing.
Numerous analyses have been published in Ukraine and elsewhere showing that the various peace-plan proposals put forward by Russia through US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner were effectively one-sided. They took into account only the aggressor’s demands, in a form that was absolutely unacceptable to Ukraine. In particular, Russia wanted to obtain, without a fight, territories where its army had made no progress over the preceding four years despite suffering heavy losses.
Trump’s statements about the need to replace Ukraine’s president are fundamentally at odds with the principles of a democratic country – the kind of country Trump represents.
First, elections cannot be held in Ukraine during wartime because most people living near the front line, in occupied territories, or as refugees, as well as those currently fighting on the front line, would be unable to vote.
Second, holding elections during the war without the participation of Zelensky’s main competitors – who are senior officers or generals and therefore cannot leave their posts while martial law remains in force – could produce a result Trump would not expect: Zelensky would have a strong chance of winning.
Third, the issue goes far beyond the president. According to opinion polls, the overwhelming majority of Ukrainians do not want to make concessions to Moscow . Nor is there any evidence of declining morale in the army or of soldiers wanting to hand over anything to Russia.
The main reason is that everyone understands that as soon as Putin gets one territory, he will use it as a base to attack others and demand those as well – endlessly.
“The issue is not Zelensky. It is the Ukrainian army and Ukrainian civil society that do not want to capitulate to Moscow. To think that changing the president will change Ukrainians’ approach to the war is nonsense. But Donald Trump has demonstrated a complete lack of understanding of the nature of Russian aggression against Ukraine since the very beginning of his presidency. He likewise fails to understand the essence of Ukrainian resistance,” said writer and journalist Radomyr Mokryk.
Ukraine’s political discourse includes not only the determination to continue resisting Russia but also a willingness to hold peace talks with Russia and make some concessions to the aggressor as a compromise for peace.
This tendency is represented by various politicians. Some are trying to establish themselves among the military “heavyweights,” while others are seeking to appeal to Trump. Still others are simply trying to capitalize on the war fatigue felt by part of society, along with constant power outages and the fear of being killed by shelling far from the front line.
These politicans from different parties are not taking part in one initiative, but informally known among journalists as the “peace party” (with ironic sense of this term).
Among them - many politicians associated with this tendency are figures of varying stature.
They include popular lawmakers Oleksiy Honcharenko and Danylo Hetmantsev, Kharkiv Mayor Ihor Terekhov, etc.
It is important to note, however, that none of them supports capitulation exclusively on Russia’s terms, let alone handing over territories that the Ukrainian army firmly controls.
For example, Honcharenko, who has faced a wave of public condemnation and accusations of “capitulationism” (in commentsaries on his pages in social media), explained his position as follows:
“Peace cannot be achieved with a single decision. Yes, we will have to discuss compromises, but compromise is not capitulation. It means finding terms under which Ukraine can end the war, obtain real security guarantees, and preserve its national interests. We must not give Russia anything. Every agreement must take Ukrainian interests into account,” Honcharenko said.
Even with such wording, however, he faced criticism on social media.
The issues of existential survival and capitulation lie largely outside the political sphere and do not depend on the identity of the president or members of parliament.
Attempts to change or dismiss this reality are naturally perceived as a form of coercion into capitulation, and anyone engaged in such efforts is seen as Putin’s accomplice and complicit in Russian aggression.
This is the dividing line between “peace” and “capitulation.”

title: Plateau attacks: Three killed, two injured, 114 cattle rustled
body: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Three persons have been killed, two others injured and 114 cattle rustled in separate incidents reported in Riyom, Barkin Ladi and Mangu Local Government Areas of Plateau State in the past few days. The incidents also involved the killing of two cattle and the destruction of crops and farmlands, according to separate statements issued by the Berom Youth Moulders-Association, BYM, and the Mwaghavul Youth Movement, MYM, and made available to newsmen in Jos on Wednesday. The BYM, in a statement signed by its National Publicity Secretary, Rwang Tengwong, said 114 cattle were rustled in Wereng, Riyom LGA, between October 6 and 12, 2026, while a 42-year-old man, David Danjuma, was killed. The association said the cattle were rustled by gunmen suspected to be terrorists, adding that the incident resulted in Danjuma’s death. It also reported the killing of James Joro Dung, 48, at Tafan, Barkin Ladi LGA, on October 13, adding that two of his cattle were killed during the incident. The association expressed condolences to the families of the deceased and called for investigations into the killings and the recovery of the rustled cattle. It also called for improved security in vulnerable communities, including increased surveillance along routes where attacks had been reported and adequate protection for farmers ahead of the harvest season. The BYM further commended the establishment of Department of State Services (DSS) camps in vulnerable communities, urging the authorities to provide adequate funding and equipment and expand their operations where necessary. Meanwhile, the Mwaghavul Youth Movement reported the killing of Dauda Shamaki, 65, during an attack on Nchiya community in Mangu LGA on Monday night. In a statement signed by its Director of Public Affairs, Tubwot Joël Sunday, on behalf of its President, Comr. Jonathan Kyesmang Yusuf, the group said, a security operative, was shot and injured around Aloghom community earlier that day. According to the statement, the incident occurred after cattle allegedly entered farmlands and destroyed crops belonging to local farmers. The group said gunmen later invaded Nchiya community, where two men keeping watch at a local vigilance point were attacked with firearms and machetes. The statement said, “Tragically, the attack led to the untimely death of Mr. Dauda Shamaki, aged 65, one of the two men keeping vigil. The second vigilant narrowly escaped.” The Movement also alleged that two of the attackers wore uniforms belonging to security operatives and called for an investigation to establish their identities and determine the circumstances surrounding the attack. It said, “While there is no concrete evidence yet that security operatives provided cover for the attackers, the presence of individuals in uniform among the attackers is highly suspicious and must be thoroughly investigated.” The group urged the Plateau State Government and other security agencies to investigate the incident and ensure that anyone found responsible was brought to justice. Both organisations urged residents to remain vigilant, report suspicious activities and avoid reprisals or the circulation of unverified information. The post Plateau attacks: Three killed, two injured, 114 cattle rustled appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: FAA awards Heart Aerospace US$2.9 million to develop ES-36 hybrid-electric propulsion system
body:
Heart Aerospace has received a US$2.9 million award from the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to develop and test the hybrid-electric propulsion system of its ES-36, a 36-seat regional airliner. The manufacturer will contribute an equal amount, bringing the total investment to US$5.8 million over two years.
Announced on October 12, the funding comes under Phase IV of the FAA's Continuous Lower Energy, Emissions, and Noise (CLEEN) program, a public-private initiative supporting aircraft technologies designed to reduce fuel consumption, emissions and noise.
Follow Air Data News: WhatsApp | Instagram | LinkedIn | Twitter | Facebook
The investment will support Project HYPER (Hybrid Propulsion Environmental Readiness), which focuses on developing a megawatt-class turbogenerator for the ES-36's propulsion system.
The aircraft will use two electrically driven propellers, each powered by a 1.65-megawatt motor. A turbogenerator installed in each nacelle will produce electricity during flight, allowing the aircraft to operate beyond the range provided by its batteries alone.
Unlike conventional turboprops, the ES-36 will have no mechanical connection between its gas turbines and propellers. Instead, the turbines will generate electricity to supplement battery power during longer flights.
Under the FAA-funded program, Heart will initially conduct ground tests to evaluate how the turbogenerators, batteries and electric motors operate together under different conditions.
The company then plans to demonstrate the system aboard a preproduction ES-36, which is scheduled to make its first flight in 2028.
The tests will collect information on energy consumption, fuel burn, emissions and noise. Heart expects the results to support certification of the ES-36 and help the FAA establish procedures for evaluating hybrid-electric aircraft.
The latest award follows previous FAA support through the Fueling Aviation's Sustainable Transition (FAST) program. In August 2024, Heart received US$4.1 million to develop its Total Hybrid Electric Management and Integration System (THEMIS), which coordinates the aircraft's motors, batteries and turbogenerators.
Heart introduced the ES-36 in September as the successor to its earlier ES-30 project, increasing passenger capacity from 30 to 36 seats.
The redesign also replaced the previous four-propeller configuration with two propulsion nacelles, each housing an electric motor and a turbogenerator.
Heart is targeting an all-electric range of 125 miles (200 km) and a hybrid-electric range of up to 745 miles (1,200 km), both with additional reserves. The turbogenerators will operate on conventional Jet A fuel or sustainable aviation fuel (SAF).
The manufacturer plans to certify the ES-36 under FAA Part 25 regulations and introduce it into commercial service in 2031.
The company completed the first flight of its X1 battery-electric demonstrator in August 2026. The experimental aircraft was developed to validate technologies for Heart's regional aviation program.
In September, US charter operator JSX signed a deposit-backed purchase agreement for 50 ES-36 aircraft, with purchase rights for another 50.
Heart, originally founded in Sweden and now based in the Los Angeles area, reports more than US$9 billion in customer commitments, including agreements involving United Airlines, Air Canada and JSX.

title: French politician warns Ukraine’s EU accession to amount to EU’s 'hara-kiri' — newspaper
body:
LONDON, October 14. /TASS/. Ukraine’s membership of the European Union would mount to the EU "committing hara-kiri," resulting in a loss of sovereignty and "absolutely huge economic losses" for France, Marine Le Pen, National Rally candidate in the 2027 French presidential election, said.
In an interview with the Financial Times , she expressed doubt that Paris would continue to support EU funding for Ukraine if she won the election. "We’ve already done 90 billion euros of loans, that’s 18 billion euros for France; 18 billion euros is really a lot," Le Pen said.
She added that if elected president, she would try to prevent the adoption of the EU’s new seven-year budget, which contains a Ukraine funding instrument worth up to 100 billion euros, by withholding half of France’s contribution.
France is due to hold the first round of its presidential election on April 18, 2027. If no candidate secures more than 50% of the vote, the two candidates who receive the most votes will face off in the second round on May 2. Under the French Constitution, incumbent President Emmanuel Macron cannot run in the 2027 election after completing his second term in office.

title: Iosevka is an open-source, sans-serif and slab-serif, monospace font
body:
The Iosevka’s monospace family is provided in a slender outfit by default: glyphs are exactly 1/2em wide . Compared to the competitors, you could fit more columns within the same screen width.
Iosevka provides two widths, Normal and Extended . If you prefer more breeze between the character, choose Extended and enjoy.
Terminal emulators have a stricter compatibility requirements for fonts. Therefore, Iosevka and Iosevka Slab all contain two specialized families, Term and Fixed , targeting terminal users.
In these families, the symbols will be narrower to follow terminals’ ideology of column count. In the Fixed families, the ligation will be disabled to ensure better compatibility in certain environments.
Iosevka provides 146 configurable characters with 19 stylistic sets, which gives you incredible ability to customize one variant that fills exactly what you need. You can either select one pre-defined stylistic set, or cherry-pick your flavor.
Iosevka’s monospace families supports not only one ligation set , but also language-specific ligations . Enable the corresponded OpenType feature in your editor, and the correct ligation will appear.
Leveraging advanced OpenType techniques, Iosevka also supports long ligatures like long arrows or horizontal bars built up with equal signs.
The quasi-proportional families: Iosevka Aile , and Iosevka Etoile , are made for documents and writing . They provide more variety on character widths, including a slightly wider letter w and m , and narrower i and l .

title: FBI arrests Saudi OpenAI engineer over covert recording device, DOJ says
body: US federal agents arrested a Saudi national who was an OpenAI engineer and charged him with installing a hidden audio recording device in an executive conference room at the AI company, the Justice Department said on Tuesday, October 13. The case highlights growing security concerns around sensitive AI research as companies and governments compete fiercely for the talent and technology that could confer economic and strategic advantages. Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, had worked as an engineer at OpenAI since July 2025, the Justice Department said in a statement. An email sent to an address associated with that name did not elicit a response, and it was not immediately clear who his lawyer was. OpenAI discovered the recording device plugged into a USB port on the back of a television in an executive conference room at one of its San Francisco buildings on September 30, according to the department. The thumb-sized device, which had a microphone and could connect to a camera, was concealed in toilet paper, according to an FBI complaint. It was installed on or about September 28, while its stored data was encrypted and inaccessible. Investigators later found a similar customized device in Alfozan’s personal bag. OpenAI said in a post on X that it used its internal AI models to identify the person responsible for planting the device and trace its origins. The company said it had evidence that the employee intended to place additional recording devices in sensitive areas of its offices to secretly record meetings. “At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data. The employee was terminated,” the company said. OpenAI referred the matter to the FBI, which is continuing to investigate. The Saudi embassy in the United States did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. “Abdulrahman Alfozan allegedly concealed a covert recording device inside his employer’s executive conference room to secretly capture sensitive communications about the company’s super intelligence technology,” FBI Director Kash Patel said in a statement. Alfozan also used an AI productivity agent to seek information about meeting-room calendars and capabilities for about a month through September 16, according to the FBI complaint. He has been a legal permanent resident of the US since September 2020. If convicted, Alfozan faces up to five years in prison, a $250,000 fine and three years of supervised release. A LinkedIn profile showed that Alfozan studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and the University of California, Berkeley. He previously worked at Meta and Microsoft, it said. Reuters could not independently verify the details mentioned in his LinkedIn profile. Separately, the Information reported that OpenAI was in early talks to acquire Trail of Bits, a startup that identifies and fixes vulnerabilities in open-source software. The talks were ongoing and could fall apart, the report said, citing people familiar with the matter. OpenAI and Trail of Bits did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment. OpenAI said on Friday it fired three researchers after an investigation found they had violated company policies on handling sensitive information. The researchers, Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak and Mikita Balesni, had published a letter detailing the circumstances of their dismissal and arguing that the abrupt firings could create uncertainty among employees and undermine a culture in which researchers could raise safety concerns. – Rappler.com

title: Umahi seeks four more years for Tinubu to complete road projects
body: By Clare Nnabuike, Minna The Minister of Works, David Umahi, has appealed to Nigerians to give President Bola Tinubu another four years to complete the road construction projects initiated by his administration. Umahi made the appeal on Tuesday in Bida Local Government Area of Niger State during the groundbreaking ceremony for the reconstruction and dualisation of the 401-kilometre Lambata–Kontagora Highway, valued at ₦1.5 trillion. He described the project as part of Tinubu’s infrastructure development programme, saying the President needed another four years to complete the numerous road projects initiated across the country. Umahi said the Niger highway project was the fifth legacy road project of the Tinubu administration, citing its scale, the use of reinforced concrete pavement and the involvement of the Dangote Group under the Federal Government’s infrastructure tax-credit scheme. He said, “President Bola Tinubu needs another four years to complete the numerous road construction projects which he started in this tenure across the country. The administration is committed to improving road infrastructure in all geopolitical zones. “President Bola Tinubu’s ongoing infrastructure programme covers several states, with Niger benefiting from a substantial share of the road construction projects. “One hundred and sixty-two kilometres of roads and 115 metres of bridges have been completed in the North-Central region.” The minister also commended Niger State Governor Mohammed Umaru Bago for his investments in infrastructure, saying the governor had constructed more than 300 kilometres of roads, over five flyovers and an underpass. The Special Adviser to the President of the Dangote Group, Mansir Ahmed, said the company was pleased to participate in the project through the infrastructure tax-credit scheme, describing the highway as a strategic corridor for Nigeria’s economy. Ahmed said the road would be constructed with concrete pavement rather than conventional asphalt, adding that work would commence from four locations to accelerate delivery. He said the completed highway would facilitate the movement of agricultural produce, commercial goods and industrial materials, while creating opportunities for businesses and young people. “The road project is expected to improve transportation, reduce travel delays and strengthen access to markets for farming communities along the corridor,” he said. Bago, who represented the President at the ceremony, described the highway project as a major intervention in a strategic transportation corridor linking communities and facilitating the movement of people and goods across different parts of the country. The governor pledged to deliver the highest number of votes nationwide for Tinubu in the next election, citing the Federal Government’s infrastructure investments in Niger State. Bago thanked the President for approving major road projects expected to improve transportation and economic activities across the state. The post Umahi seeks four more years for Tinubu to complete road projects appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: What is known about one of largest attacks on Moscow Region, Sber data center
body:
MOSCOW, October 14. /TASS/. Air defenses shot down 902 Ukrainian drones over Russian regions overnight, the Defense Ministry said in a statement.
The attempted Ukrainian drone attack on the Moscow Region was one of the largest in two years, according to TASS calculations based on data published by Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin.
The drone attack paralyzed operations at Moscow’s four airports: Vnukovo, Domodedovo, Zhukovsky and Sheremetyevo suspended arrivals and departures for varying periods. All four airports resumed operations at 6:44 a.m. Moscow time [3:44 a.m. GMT].
One person was killed in the drone attack in Balakovo, Saratov Region. Several residential buildings were also damaged.
Later, Sber confirmed that a drone attack targeted a data center in Balakovo, Saratov Region, noting that all the company’s systems and services are operating normally.
TASS has compiled the key details of the aftermath.
- Air defenses on duty destroyed 902 Ukrainian unmanned aerial vehicles over the Belgorod, Bryansk, Volgograd, Voronezh, Vladimir, Kaluga, Kursk, Lipetsk, Novgorod, Oryol, Rostov, Ryazan, Saratov, Smolensk, Tver, Tula, Moscow, Krasnodar and Stavropol regions, as well as Crimea and the Sea of Azov, last night, between 8:00 p.m. Moscow time on October 13 and 8:00 a.m. Moscow time [5:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. GMT - TASS].
- The attempted Ukrainian drone attack on the Moscow Region was one of the largest in two years, according to TASS calculations based on data published by Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin.
- He said that 493 drones were heading toward the Moscow Region between 8:30 p.m. Moscow time on October 13 and 7:00 a.m. Moscow time on October 14 [5:30 p.m. to 4:00 a.m. GMT - TASS].
- Most were intercepted by air defenses before they approached Moscow, with 180 destroyed as they were closing in on the capital.
- More than 160 drones were destroyed overnight in Kamensk-Shakhtinsky and the Kamensky, Kasharsky, Millerovsky, Morozovsky, Tarasovsky, Tatsinsky, Chertkovsky and Sholokhovsky districts of the Rostov Region, Governor Yury Slyusar said on Max.
- Air defenses destroyed 20 Ukrainian drones over the Kaluga Region overnight, Governor Vladislav Shapsha wrote on Max.
- Air defenses destroyed 11 Ukrainian drones over the Tula Region, Governor Dmitry Milyaev said on Max.
- A drone attack was repelled in the Stavropol Region, Governor Vladimir Vladimirov wrote on Max.
- On the evening of October 13, three Moscow airports, Vnukovo, Domodedovo and Zhukovsky, introduced temporary restrictions on arrivals and departures, the Federal Air Transport Agency reported.
- Sheremetevo later also suspended flight operations.
- All four airports resumed operations at 6:44 a.m. Moscow time [3:44 a.m. GMT] on October 14.
- Vnukovo did not handle flights for more than eight hours. During the restrictions, all passengers were returned from aircraft to the terminals.
- Sheremetyevo said that flight schedules could change and that departures would take place as aircraft became ready.
- Domodedovo also warned of possible schedule changes. Airport services are operating in an enhanced mode to dispatch delayed flights and receive arriving aircraft as quickly as possible.
- Aeroflot continues to adjust its flight schedule for October 14 to stabilize operations as quickly as possible following temporary restrictions at Sheremetyevo, the airline said in a statement on Max.
- The airline is also continuing to notify passengers of schedule changes using the contact details provided at the time of booking.
- Passengers waiting to have their tickets reissued at Sheremetyevo are being offered bottled water.
- Depending on the length of the wait, some are also being provided with drinks, meals and hotel accommodation.
- Aeroflot representatives continue to assist passengers at alternate airports.
- Flights to Moscow are being organized in accordance with crew working-hour regulations.
- Rossiya Airlines said on Max that it was adjusting the schedules of some flights, including those operated under its shuttle service between Moscow and St. Petersburg, due to the earlier restrictions on departures and arrivals at Sheremetyevo and Vnukovo.
- A woman was reportedly killed in a drone attack in Balakovo, Saratov Region, Governor Roman Busargin said on Max, citing preliminary information.
- Several residential buildings were also damaged.
- Emergency response services are working at the scene.
- Schools in Balakovo have canceled classes, and kindergartens will remain closed, Balakovo Municipal District Head Sergey Barulin said on Max.
- All infrastructure facilities in Balakovo are operating normally, Busargin said later.
- The district head has been instructed to organize an on-site task force and maintain regular communication with residents of the damaged buildings.
- The local administration has opened a hotline.
- Temporary accommodation will be arranged if necessary.
- The family of the woman who died will receive all necessary assistance.
- Sber confirms that a drone attack targeted a data center in Balakovo, Saratov Region, but all the company’s systems and services are operating normally, Alexander Vedyakhin, First Deputy Chairman of Sberbank’s Executive Board, told reporters.

title: US senators urge Trump to drop Russian diesel deal, use Graham's sanctions law
body:
A bipartisan group of U.S. senators on Oct. 13 called on U.S. President Donald Trump to rescind his deal to buy Russian diesel, joining other colleagues in Congress who lambasted the controversial agreement.
"This deal is a gift to our adversary and a betrayal of our Allies; it should be rescinded," says the letter signed by six Democratic and six Republican senators, including Democrat Richard Blumenthal and Republican Mitch McConnell, and shared with the Kyiv Independent.
The lawmakers instead urged Trump to deploy sanctions under the late Republican Senator Lindsey Graham 's law , which was passed in September and authorizes the president to impose up to a 100% tariff on the top five countries buying Russian gas and oil, among other measures.
"These authorities require you to apply economic pressure on Russia and the chief enablers of its war, in particular China," the senators wrote.
The news follows a deal announced Oct. 9 between Russian President Vladimir Putin and Trump, allowing Moscow to export diesel fuel to the U.S. and other markets despite sanctions imposed due to the full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
The U.S. Treasury Department said that, following Trump's direction, "the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) is immediately issuing a temporary general license to allow the supply of Russian diesel to the global market."
In response to the deal, the Russian government partially lifted the diesel export ban, permitting the sale of 500,000 metric tons of diesel to foreign markets, effective Oct. 10.
"Granting Moscow the ability to sell Russian diesel freely in global markets damages American security interests and is a betrayal of the people of Ukraine, who continue to defend themselves from Putin's murderous, illegal war," the letter read.
The agreement was announced as Trump ramps up pressure on Kyiv to halt attacks against Russian refineries as part of his unilaterally announced energy truce, with his administration threatening to cut off intelligence and arms shipments to Ukraine.
Ukraine has said it had paused attacks against Russian refineries, despite Russia continuing to strike the Ukrainian power grid, most recently overnight on Oct. 14.
In the letter, the senators said they recognize the need to lower energy costs for U.S. families, but warned that the Russian diesel deal will have a "negligible impact on fuel prices" while filling the Kremlin's war chest.
Earlier, on Oct. 11, seven bipartisan members of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee released a statement condemning the decision, urging the White House to "immediately reverse course."

title: GRA identifies about 100 additional foreign digital service providers for VAT collection
body: The Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA) has identified about 100 additional foreign digital service providers that are not charging Value Added Tax (VAT) and plans to bring them into its tax collection system. The Commissioner-General of the GRA, Anthony Kwasi Sarpong, disclosed this on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show on Wednesday, 14 October, during a discussion on the 20% tax applicable to Netflix, Spotify and other cross-border digital services. He said the providers would be brought into the system gradually as the Authority expands compliance. “We have identified about a hundred new emerging ones who today are not charging the VAT,” he said. Mr Sarpong explained that about 92 foreign companies currently remit VAT to the GRA. He said the new collection mechanism would not add another 20% to charges from providers whose prices already include the tax. “Nothing will change in terms of pricing from 92 merchants or entities,” he stated. However, bringing providers that are not currently charging VAT into the system would extend collection to their qualifying services. According to Mr Sarpong, the obligation for foreign companies supplying services to consumers in Ghana to charge VAT has existed since 2013. He said the latest intervention seeks to improve collection and give the Authority a complete view of transactions involving those companies. Under the existing arrangement, service providers collect payments, report their transactions and subsequently remit the tax component to the GRA. Mr Sarpong said this leaves the Authority dependent on the companies’ declarations, with limited means of independently verifying the number and value of transactions. The new system would separate the tax component at the point of payment, transfer it to the government and remit the remainder to the service provider. “We are using technology to smartly account for and collect the component that belongs to the government of Ghana,” he said. The intervention forms part of the GRA’s Real-Time VAT framework for qualifying cross-border digital services. In an earlier report, Elsie Appau-Klu, Technical Advisor to the Commissioner-General, said the framework collects existing VAT at the point of payment through participating financial institutions. The combined 20% charge comprises 15% VAT, a 2.5% National Health Insurance Levy and a 2.5% GETFund Levy. Mr Sarpong clarified that the collection system would cover qualifying payments made through mobile and other digital payment platforms, as well as bank cards. “So it’s not only for a card,” he said. He also stressed that the initial rollout applies to services, rather than physical goods bought from foreign online platforms. He explained that imported goods are already assessed for applicable duties and VAT when they enter Ghana through its borders. “So it is not going to affect goods or products, tangible products at the moment,” he stated.

title: Demonstrating Deterministic Trust and Formal Proof for AI-Generated Code
body:
High-integrity software runs the world quietly; traffic lights, point-of-sale terminals, industrial manufacturing, medical devices, cars, trains, airplanes. We rarely notice it until it fails. And when it fails, the consequences are real: breaches of privacy, financial loss, injury, and even loss of life.
That's why people refer to software for these systems as high-integrity software , and high-integrity software is built differently. It is rigorously reviewed and thoroughly tested before deployment. Building high-integrity software takes more focus, more time, more people, and hence costs more. Building to a standard of high integrity keeps us safer, but the increased cost creates tension: we want more high-integrity, safe, and secure software, yet too often the economics don't allow it to be built or bought. The result is a world less safe and secure than it could be. AdaCore believes that AI has the potential to reverse these economics. Using AI, we should be able to deliver safer, more secure software faster and at lower cost.
The key barrier to realizing this potential is trust. How can we trust that the output of AI is correct and complete, especially given the importance of both in high-integrity systems? The answer to date has been âhuman review of all AI outputsâ. But this is slow and doesnât scale. We propose a different answer: our tools, driven by an AI with a well-defined workflow, can help furnish the required trust, dramatically lowering the barrier to using AI.
We built a demonstration project of how we think this can work and published it as GNAT Foundry: Intersection on GitHub. It showcases how our tools bring deterministic trust to AI-powered workflows. If you want to dive right in, clone the demo repository here and follow the instructions in the README. To understand better why we think our approach is unique, credible, and will change high-integrity software development, read on.
AI brings two key challenges to high-integrity software development:
In high-integrity software development, humans must remain accountable for the artifacts that are produced, whether AI- or human-authored. To date, the typical answer to the question âhow do we ensure trust in this AI-authored codeâ has been âhuman reviewâ. But that approach doesnât scale and doesnât play to human strengths.
GNAT Foundry demonstrates a stronger alternative: leverage deterministic trust furnished by non-AI tools everywhere possible, so that humans can focus their attention where it is required.
Since its inception, AdaCore has promoted languages (like Ada and SPARK 1 ) and built tools (like GNATprove, GNAT DAS, CodeSonar, and others) that enhance the safety and security of high-integrity software through deterministic trust. Now, weâre showcasing how our tools can be applied to AI-powered high-integrity software development at speed.
We took a familiar, easy-to-understand system and made it the foundation of our first GNAT Foundry demo: a four-way intersection with protected left turns and pedestrian crosswalks. We call this demo GNAT Foundry: Intersection.
To get started, we built a set of comprehensive systems- and software-engineering artifacts:
The CONOPS is derived from and traces to the US Department of Transportation Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices .
For demonstration purposes, we added a simulation harness that stands in for the physical hardware with which the software would interact. The simulation harness runs on Linux, but the Ada code can just as well be run on a microcontroller with an RTOS or bare-board without an RTOS.
We then developed comprehensive artifacts that verify the LLRs:
Finally, we developed a comprehensive traceability matrix that is presented through an interactive HTML report.
The report clearly identifies where human review is essential:
Aside from this trust core, the report relies entirely on evidence produced deterministically by AdaCoreâs tools to establish trust in the software.
The GNAT Foundry: Intersection demo is hosted on GitHub here . The demo:
Clone the demo, then runÂ make setup-community to use the GNAT FSF tools orÂ make setup-pro if you have the complete set of GNAT Pro tools.
Run the baseline withÂ make run-native . Youâll see a graphical representation of the intersection, the traffic lights, and the crosswalks. Play around with the simulation for a bit to get a feel for how things work.
Then, runÂ make report . The baseline report shows all green: the human-reviewed elements are signed off; the deterministic trust is intact: all of the traceability, requirements verification, proof, and structural coverage evidence is present and correct. Play around with the report: follow the traceability links, read some of the documents, compare what you see to the simulation. You should come away from your review of the report confident that the baseline system is correctly and completely implemented, based on the verification evidence presented.
Finally, the meat of the demo: the change request, which adds countdown timers to the pedestrian control heads. Fire up your AI agent and instruct it to read and follow the prompt contained inÂ demo/demo-prompt.md . The agent will apply a patch to the CONOPS that represents the initiation of a formal change-request process. This patch is preapproved, so no new/additional human review is needed. From there, the agent follows a rigorous workflow to:
The result will be a report thatâs at leastÂ mostly green: all of the elements of deterministic trust will be green; the agent may introduce one or more additional items for human review.
This step illustrates how detailed workflows can be applied to guide the AI agents in going from CONOPS, via HLR, LLR, to code and tests, and how they can measure correctness and completeness. GNAT Foundry includes definitions for subagents that are invoked to drive the change-request process from start to finish.
The central message of GNAT Foundry is that you should trust the deterministic evidence furnished by our tools. You donât have to review all of the code to know that it does all and only what you intend; the evidence furnishes this trust and focuses your review on the key artifacts in which the trust is rooted. Hereâs how that trust is built.
While GNAT Foundry: Intersection is not demonstrating any particular certification process, all of the tools listed above have been qualified against various standards across many different target environments.
The report that GNAT Foundry produces offers a quick entry into the artifacts and supports drilling down to the lowest level of detail, exposing all of the requirements, code, tests, outputs from the verification tools, and, critically, traceability between all of these artifacts. Our claim is that by verifying that the report is green after the agent has finished its work, you have the evidence you need to conclude that the work is correct and complete. Of course, in a certified software project, you would need to review the edits to the HLRs, LLRs, and confirm that the test cases are correct and complete for their requirements. But the key elements of trust are automatically and deterministically put in place by the workflow the agent follows and the tools it uses.
GNAT Foundry: Intersection is unique. Nowhere else will you find an agent driving a complete chain of deterministic trust from a single vendor that includes formal proof, MC/DC coverage, qualifiable tools, certifiable runtimes, and support for embedded targets. Brownfield v Greenfield
GNAT Foundry: Intersection demonstrates brownfield AI-powered development. Because we start from a complete baseline with an existing, complete chain of deterministic trust, the AI agent both benefits from whatâs already there (via in-place learning) but also has to fit into whatâs already there (constraining the choices it may make). Many high-integrity systems fit this pattern: an established, existing system with established, existing evidence into which teams are struggling to figure out how to use AI in a trustworthy manner. If youâre such a team, we built GNAT Foundry: Intersection for you.
But GNAT Foundry also works in a greenfield context. The workflow that the AI agent follows enables trustworthy use of AI for brand new systems as well, instructing the agent how to write and verify all of the artifacts demonstrated, from the CONOPS to the tests. Weâll have a follow-up demonstration soon that illustrates using GNAT Foundry in a greenfield context; in the meantime, you can try it yourself using the resources provided in the GNAT Foundry: Intersection demo.
GNAT Foundry: Intersection demonstrates deterministic trust in AI-produced outputs in the context of a high-integrity system. If you canât run the demo yourself, reach out to us and we'd be happy to show it to you.
If you want to learn more about AdaCoreâs tools and how the deterministic trust they provide can help your team develop high-integrity software, with or without AI involvement, reach out to us here .
And stay tuned for more. This is just the beginning.
1 For people who are not familiar with Ada and SPARK: Ada is a modern programming language that has been used in the delivery of high-integrity systems for decades. Ada has object orientation, built-in concurrency, generics and is inherently type-safe and memory safe. SPARK is the formal subset of Ada that enables the use of formal methods to prove the absence of runtime errors (absence of undefined behavior) and can prove functional correctness of an implementation against a specification.
No, it is not an actual implementation of a traffic light control system. We used the traffic light example as it is something that is easy to understand, still sufficiently complex and safety related. This project demonstrates how a software development team can use artificial intelligence to develop high integrity software. The project uses Ada SPARK and formal methods to deliver deterministic trust in the artifacts generated by AI.

title: Marwa Canvasses Prioritisation of Mental Health By FG
body: *Says NDLEA rehabilitated 53,800 In 5 Years Onyebuchi Ezigbo in Abuja Chairman of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA), Brig. Gen. Mohammed Buba Marwa (rtd), has urged the Federal Government to prioritise mental health funding, personnel and community-led interventions. Against the background growing concerns about drug abuse and mental health cases, Marwa said that over 53,800 persons have been rehabilitated through the agency’s facilities in the last five years. Marwa spoke in Abuja on Monday while chairing The Conversation Conference (TCC) 5.0 organised by Intersect Consortium to mark World Mental Health Month. He said he chaired the first edition in 2022 and has watched it grow into one of Nigeria’s largest gatherings on mental health, commending the consortium led by Dr. Vincent Udenze and its Chairperson, Hajiya Ammuna Lawan Ali. “For too long, we treated mental health as a private burden, hiding behind shame and silence. In my work at NDLEA, I see the cost of that silence daily,” Marwa said. He said behind many drug abuse cases is untreated pain, depression and trauma. “A young person who found substance before finding help. Drug use and mental illness feed each other. If we only arrest symptoms, we will keep missing the cause,” he warned. Marwa said the conference theme – strategic investments, partnerships and community-led action – reflects NDLEA’s approach. He said mental well-being cannot thrive where hopelessness and poverty drive people into harm. In three pilot communities, NDLEA worked with residents to build legitimate livelihoods for families who once depended on illicit drug cultivation, with plans to scale to other geopolitical zones. “When people have hope, income and a stake in their future, stress eases, families stabilise and communities grow resilient. These were solutions designed for communities, not imposed on them,” he said. On prevention, Marwa cited the War Against Drug Abuse (WADA) campaign reaching young people in schools and campuses early and without judgment, and the agency’s 24/7 toll-free helpline where a frightened teenager or worried mother can be heard at no cost. “Over 53,800 persons have passed through our rehabilitation facilities across Nigeria in the last five years. Behind that number are parents and kids who return to families and people who return to school and work,” he said. He lamented that media focuses on arrests, seizures and forfeited assets, not on counselling and rehabilitation. Marwa said mental health financing must be at the centre of national planning. “Mental health cannot remain the poorest relation in our health budget. Every naira spent on prevention, trained personnel and accessible treatment returns to us in productivity, safer communities and stronger families,” he said. He called for more psychiatrists, psychologists, counsellors, community health workers and integration of mental health into primary healthcare so that no one travels hundreds of kilometres to get help. “Financing must also be equitable. Care that only the well-off can afford is not a system, but a privilege,” he added. He said focus on women and children was right. Women carry unseen load of families, often suffering in silence and surviving violence, including displaced mothers and girls with no one to turn to. Children absorb stress of homes long before they can name it. “The same is true of persons living with disabilities and families displaced by conflict. A system that does not treat them is not yet inclusive,” he said, noting that when mother, child and household are supported together, recovery lasts longer. Marwa said no single ministry can handle it alone, urging synergy among health, education, security, justice and social welfare ministries. Earlier, Hajiya Ammuna Lawan Ali said TCC grew from a single-day gathering into a movement, now in its fifth edition. She said this year’s edition asks what conversations must lead to. “Mental health does not begin in a hospital. It begins in the home, the school, the workplace and community. That is where people experience stress, loneliness, trauma and exclusion. It is also where support and early intervention can begin,” she said. She urged strengthening of trusted first contacts – family members, teachers, religious leaders, community leaders, primary health workers – and connecting them to professional services. Managing Director of Intersect Consortium, Dr. Vincent Udenze, shared story of Elizabeth, a mother from Kwara State who produced a first-class graduate but was found stark naked on the street, her luggage stolen, people throwing things at her. He said he gave her food and took her to his facility where she was treated and regained her health. Marwa urged participants to commit to financing what works, scaling proven community models, putting women, children and vulnerable first and making help-seeking an act of courage. “Let TCC 5.0 mark renewed commitment so that mental health becomes integral part of national development agenda and access to quality care is reality for all, not privilege for few,” he said.

title: 2027: CSOs, Nigerians Told To Hold Politicians Accountable
body: Nigeria Forward, a socio-political group, has urged civil society organisations and Nigerians to hold politicians accountable for their statements and actions ahead of the 2027 general elections. The group warned against hate speech, personality attacks and fake news, saying such practices could deepen divisions in the country. Its Co-Convener, Comrade Ibrahim Abdullahi Waiya, PhD, made the call in a statement issued on Tuesday. The statement followed the commencement of public political campaigns by candidates and political parties. Nigeria Forward expressed concern over what it described as the growing use of character assassination and campaign of calumny by political actors. It urged candidates to focus on policies, manifestoes and programmes that would help voters make informed decisions. The group also condemned the alleged misuse of digital platforms to spread misinformation and hate speech for political advantage. It said political ambition should be pursued with decency, mutual respect and patriotism. “Our politicians must take a cue from their contemporaries in the advanced and developed democracies, where electioneering campaigns are based on issues, manifestoes, policies and programmes that are intended to be implemented for the benefit of the electorates,” the statement read. The group urged politicians to avoid inflammatory statements capable of threatening national unity and peaceful coexistence. It also called on civil society organisations, corporate bodies and well-meaning Nigerians to scrutinise politicians’ conduct and hold them responsible for divisive remarks. Nigeria Forward said the 2027 campaigns should promote issue-based debates rather than personal attacks. It added that responsible political engagement was necessary to sustain peace, unity and development in the country.

title: Trump threatens renewed military action against Iran
body: US President Donald Trump has warned of further action against Iran, saying Washington will decide its next move “very soon” as Tehran steps up attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Mr Trump, speaking outside the White House late on Tuesday, described Iran as a “failed country” and said its economy was collapsing under severe inflation and financial pressure. “They have no economy … they have no money,” Mr Trump said. “We’ll make a decision on Iran very soon.” The US President later struck a more threatening tone at a campaign event in Alaska, warning of further action against Tehran. “Wait till you see what we do to Iran. We’re going to do a number … wait till you see what we do to Iran, because we’ve sort of had it,” he said. “The big thing is, they’re not going to have a nuclear weapon. That’s buried under thousands of tonnes of rock.” The remarks came after Reuters reported two Iranian officials said Tehran was using new ⁠tactics to target ships sailing through the Strait of Hormuz. The officials declined to ​provide ⁠details but one ‌said Iran had started using different offensive tactics about ​10 days ago, leading to an increase in attacks on such ships. At least 12 vessels have been attacked in and around the Strait of Hormuz in the past week, the UK Maritime Trade Operations agency has said. Six were struck on Sunday alone – five tankers and a container ship. Five incidents occurred in the strait and one near Oman’s Sohar anchorage. “The aim is to frustrate efforts by the United States and its allies to bring down global oil prices,” one was quoted as saying. A second official said Tehran would prevent Washington from lowering oil prices ahead of the US midterm elections on November 3. Back-channel diplomacy The US military rejected a claim by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps that it is in control of the Strait of Hormuz, saying it does not possess an actual naval force. “US forces and their regional partners clearly control the Strait of Hormuz . Just yesterday, US forces assisted their Gulf partners in shipping more than 19 million barrels of crude oil through the strait,” said Central Command, which oversees US military operations across the Middle East. Officials in Tehran have rejected Washington’s latest response to its proposal to end the conflict , which began with US and Israeli strikes across Iran on February 28. Mohsen Rezaei, head of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, described the US response as “insufficient” and warned of possible attacks on regional digital infrastructure if hostilities resumed. 🚫 CLAIM: The navy commander for Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed today that the Strait of Hormuz is under IRGC control and any approaching U.S. Navy warships would be "sunk." ✅ FACT: IRGC's navy commander has no navy. American forces and regional partners… pic.twitter.com/n9dhNsyI8O — U.S. Central Command (@CENTCOM) October 13, 2026 Washington has maintained a naval blockade of Iranian ports and expanded sanctions, while seeking an agreement. The Pentagon has also directed US Central Command to complete preparations for possible major combat operations, Axios reported, citing sources familiar with the matter. Mr Trump said last week the US would not attack Iran before the midterm elections, citing progress in negotiations. Israel is also considering its options. Mr Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu have discussed the possibility of renewed military operations against Iran, Axios reported, as the Israeli leader prepared for a general election on October 27. Qatari mediators are awaiting Tehran’s response to a US counterproposal.

title: Ukraine 200% dependent on Starlink, needs to negotiate with US on restrictions — lawmaker
body:
MOSCOW, October 14. /TASS/. The Ukrainian armed forces depend entirely on Starlink satellite internet, so the Kiev authorities must travel to the US to negotiate lifting the restrictions on access to it, Verkhovna Rada lawmaker Alexey Goncharenko (listed in Russia as a terrorist and extremist) said.
"We are 200% dependent on Starlink, absolutely. <…> What needs to be done urgently? Make every phone call to the US. Call, talk, negotiate, find common ground. A Ukrainian delegation should be on its way to the US right now," he wrote in a post on his Telegram channel.
That morning, Sergey Beskrestnov, an advisor to Vladimir Zelensky and an expert in communications and unmanned systems, reported that SpaceX had limited the operating speed of Starlink terminals for the Ukrainian military to 160 kilometers per hour overnight. According to him, this "disrupted a number of operations." Later, Sergey Sternenko, a former adviser to the country’s defense minister, said that SpaceX had further restricted the terminals’ operating speed to 60-70 kilometers per hour that morning.

title: In the AI era, coding means thinking like a systems architect
body:
Jacques Cornwell is a PhD student in pathology at the University of Cambridge, UK.
Until just a few years ago, my journey in learning to code as a wet-lab clinician-scientist was marked by frustration. I regularly found myself staring at a flashing cursor, scouring jargon-filled forums for clues to why my script had crashed and spending hours hunting down a single missing comma or mismatched bracket. For scientists whose work bridges the gap between experimental observation and computational analysis, the barrier to entry was steep.
The release of advanced large language models (LLMs) and autonomous artificial-intelligence agents has since completely changed the situation. Now, anyone can prompt an AI model to construct complex computational pipelines that would otherwise require days or weeks of troubleshooting, and more patience than any researcher could reasonably be expected to have. This begs the question: if AI can generate these complex statistical analyses and bespoke data visualizations in seconds, do you still need to learn to code?
The answer, to my mind, is an emphatic ‘yes’. But the way we learn must change. The bottleneck is no longer mastering coding grammar and syntax; it is learning how best to prompt and guide AI tools to answer our scientific questions. In many ways, early-career scientists are now stepping straight into roles historically reserved for senior software engineers: supervising, critiquing and refining output generated by others, or, in this case, an automated assistant.
Here are six tips to help get the most out of the process.
When I started using AI to help me code, I worried that I would quickly lose the skills I had developed. I had spent years learning how different functions could be used to merge data sets, generate figures and run statistical analyses. Using AI felt like cheating, even if the answers to my problems were already available online and LLMs were simply quicker at finding them.
Eventually, I realized I didn’t need to remember the exact syntax required to run a hierarchical clustering algorithm or pivot a table using Python’s pandas library (a collection of data-analysis tools in the Python coding language). I simply needed to know that these methods existed, roughly how they worked and when best to use them. By reading the function documentation, I learnt what different functions could do, but using AI meant I didn’t have to worry about exactly how to make them do it.
By thinking like a systems architect, I could direct the AI system towards robust, reproducible solutions without getting bogged down in syntactic minutiae.
When you have an AI model capable of writing hundreds of lines of code instantly, the temptation is to ask for a miracle: a single monolithic script that ingests your raw data, cleans them, runs the statistics and outputs a formatted figure for publication.
I quickly found that this was a fragile and fundamentally flawed approach. Monolithic scripts are a nightmare to troubleshoot. If a single variable changes, or if the AI system hallucinates a step midway through the analysis, the entire architecture collapses, leaving you to sift through a wall of code in search of the error.
Instead, I embraced modular programming. I prompted my LLMs to write small, discrete, single-purpose functions — for instance, one to ingest and format raw data, another to normalize their values and a third to generate a visual representation of the data.
Pipelines built from such self-contained blocks of code are easier to debug than are their monolithic counterparts. If a specific transformation fails or an error occurs, I can isolate, interrogate and fix the faulty function without jeopardizing the rest of the pipeline. And because the code blocks are modular, I can reuse them across projects. In this way, I have seeded a personal library of trusted, AI-generated tools.
Because AI reduced the friction of writing code, I found myself generating scripts, code iterations and data outputs faster than ever before. Inevitably, my project directories quickly devolved into an unnavigable mess of files with names such as analysis_final_v3_really_final.py.
Worse, I realized that, during one project, I had accidentally overwritten my raw data files (luckily, I had a backup). Through this, I learnt the importance of good data-project organization — a practice that is embedded in resources such as the Cookiecutter Data Science framework .
Adoption of a specific framework to compartmentalize projects is no longer just best practice for coding, but a necessity in the AI era. It mandates a rigid separation between input files and analytical scripts. For example, a standard Cookiecutter structure dictates that all raw, primary data (such as sequencing files or clinical spreadsheets) are kept in one folder that is strictly read-only. Active analysis scripts are kept in another, and all outputs are funnelled into a third folder. By enforcing this structure, I no longer worry that an AI-generated script will accidentally overwrite or corrupt my primary data sets.
The integration of AI into scientific workflows introduces significant ethical and regulatory vulnerabilities. Public models are often trained on user inputs, meaning that if one user feeds sensitive patient data into a public, cloud-based LLM, those data could theoretically be regurgitated to another user somewhere else.
To mitigate that risk, I learnt to generate ‘dummy data’. Before asking an AI system to write an analysis script, I provide it with the column headers, expected data types (for example, integers, strings or floating-point numbers) and the dimensions of my data table, while explicitly ensuring that no real values are shared (see ‘Example AI prompts’).
I then ask the model to write, test and debug analytical code using this fictional data set, which is structurally identical to the real one. Once the code is working, I can copy it into my secure, local environment and use it with my real, protected data. The LLM never sees the sensitive information, and data protection remains intact.

title: Digital VAT collection system will not add another 20% to existing charges – GRA clarifies
body: The Commissioner-General of the Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA), Anthony Kwasi Sarpong, says the new digital Value Added Tax (VAT) collection system will not impose an additional 20% charge on subscriptions to platforms already collecting the tax. Speaking on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show on Wednesday, 14th October 2026, during a discussion on VAT on Netflix, Spotify and other digital services, he explained that the system changes how existing taxes are collected. “So this system is not adding another 20 per cent to what you already pay. It is already embedded, and consumers are paying,” he said. Mr Sarpong said the GRA currently receives VAT remittances from about 92 foreign service providers, whose customers should not experience price increases arising from the change in collection. “Nothing will change in terms of pricing from 92 merchants or entities,” he stated. However, he disclosed that the Authority had identified about 100 additional providers that were not charging VAT and would gradually bring them into the collection system. His assurance on unchanged charges therefore applies to services whose prices already include the applicable tax. Explaining the reform, Mr Sarpong said the GRA currently relies on foreign providers to report their transactions and remit the tax collected from consumers in Ghana. This arrangement, he said, limits the Authority’s ability to independently verify the number and value of transactions. Using Netflix as an example, he explained that the new system would separate the tax component at the point of payment, transfer it to the government and send the remaining amount to the provider. “We are using technology to smartly account for and collect the component that belongs to the government of Ghana,” he said. The system would also allow the Authority to establish how many transactions had taken place, their value and the corresponding tax due, rather than relying solely on information supplied by the companies. The clarification follows the introduction of the GRA’s Real-Time VAT framework for qualifying cross-border digital services. In an earlier report, Elsie Appau-Klu, Technical Advisor to the Commissioner-General, said the framework collects existing VAT at the point of payment through participating financial institutions. The combined 20% charge comprises 15% VAT, a 2.5% National Health Insurance Levy and a 2.5% GETFund Levy. The framework covers electronically supplied services from non-resident providers paid for using Ghana-issued payment instruments, including cards, mobile money accounts and digital wallets. Streaming subscriptions, cloud computing, online gaming and digital advertising are among the services covered. READ ALSO : Banks to charge 20% VAT on payments for Netflix, Zoom, TikTok and others Mr Sarpong confirmed that collection would extend beyond bank card payments. “So it’s not only for a card,” he said, explaining that mobile payments and other digital payment platforms would also be captured when qualifying transactions pass through the payment system. He further clarified that the initial rollout covers services rather than physical goods purchased from platforms such as Amazon and Alibaba. According to him, imported goods already undergo tax assessment at Ghana’s borders, where the applicable duties and VAT are calculated. “So it is not going to affect goods or products, tangible products at the moment,” he said. Although physical goods could be considered in future, Mr Sarpong stressed that they were outside the initial rollout.

title: Jimoh Ibrahim-led UN Committee Considers $3.3bn Budget As Nigeria Wins Human Rights Council Seat
body: By Funke Babs-Kufeji Nigeria has secured a three-year seat on the United Nations Human Rights Council, while Dr Jimoh Ibrahim chaired the General Assembly’s Fifth Committee during the presentation of Secretary-General António Guterres’ proposed $3.3 billion budget for 2027. Nigeria was one of 15 countries elected to the 47-member council by secret ballot. Its term begins on January 1, 2027. The country received 172 votes, behind Zambia with 177 and Ghana with 173. Burundi won the fourth African seat with 160 votes. For Nigeria, the election comes alongside Ibrahim’s work as chair of the Fifth Committee on Administrative and Budgetary Matters, where discussions are underway on how the UN will fund its programmes and manage its operations. Guterres has proposed a core budget of $3.302 billion for 2027, covering 11,150 posts. When major construction projects in Nairobi and the Strategic Heritage Plan in Geneva are included, the total rises to $3.408 billion. The core budget is $40.8 million, or about 1.2 per cent, below the approved 2026 figure. The proposal also includes $423 million for special political missions next year. Guterres congratulated Ibrahim on his election as committee chair and thanked him for his support. He said the committee’s work with the Secretariat had helped move reforms forward and address difficult administrative and budgetary issues. Much of the proposed budget is tied to the UN80 Initiative, which aims to reduce duplication, improve services and lower operating costs. Some changes are already in place. Payroll operations have been consolidated, shared administrative platforms launched in New York and Bangkok, and some functions moved to cheaper locations. The UN plans to extend the shared platforms to Geneva, Nairobi, Vienna and Addis Ababa. These changes have come with job cuts. Guterres said 3,116 regular budget posts had been removed. The Secretariat also introduced a voluntary early separation programme and reassigned staff to vacant positions in an effort to reduce the impact on employees. The next phase includes 44 additional relocations across 12 UN entities, with Nairobi receiving the largest share. The budget also proposes abolishing or downgrading 14 senior-level posts to reduce management costs. Guterres said the savings would be redirected to programme activities, rather than simply removed from the budget. The proposal still provides funding for development programmes, disability inclusion, investigations relating to Afghanistan and upgrades to the UN’s internal systems. It also includes an additional $22 million for after-service health insurance, as healthcare costs rise and more retirees receive coverage. Despite the cuts, Guterres said the organisation would continue working on peace and security, sustainable development and human rights. He also called for stronger accountability, with clearer links between spending and results. The bigger concern, however, is whether the UN will receive the money it needs to do its work. Guterres warned that cutting costs would not solve the organisation’s financial problems if member states failed to pay their contributions on time. “Efficiency alone cannot compensate for an unstable financial foundation,” he said, urging countries to meet their financial obligations in full and on time, as required by the UN Charter. The Fifth Committee will examine the proposed budget before it proceeds to the General Assembly for approval.

title: Three days after Washington announced an energy ceasefire, Russia fires 39 ballistic missiles at Ukraine’s grid
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Russia fired 39 ballistic missiles and more than 120 drones at Ukraine’s energy system overnight into 14 October, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said . The barrage came three days after US President Donald Trump announced an energy ceasefire, which the Kremlin never confirmed, saying on 12 October only that contacts were continuing . Ukraine held off strikes on Russian energy for two days after the announcement, Zelenskyy wrote on 13 October. Russia’s barrage opened that evening with a ballistic strike on Kyiv. For the second time in two days, it came without a launch warning from partners. How the night unfolded The Air Force described one massive combined strike that began at 18:00 on 13 October. By 09:00 the next day, it had counted 39 missiles on ballistic trajectories and 128 drones, aimed mainly at Kyiv, Kyiv Oblast, and Kharkiv Oblast. Air defenses downed or suppressed four missiles and 115 drones, but missiles and drones hit 22 locations, the Air Force said. Explore further Russian ballistic missiles hit Kyiv before sirens, gap that lands hard amid fears that Washington could cut data that warns of launches The first wave hit Kyiv late on 13 October. Its primary target was CHP-4, a key power plant in the city, and there were hits, Zelenskyy said . Ukrainian systems spotted the missiles only on approach, with no warning from partners. title: IEA cuts global oil demand forecast, expects 2.6 mln bpd drop in 2026
body:
MOSCOW, October 14. /TASS/. The International Energy Agency (IEA) forecasts a 2.6 million barrels per day (bpd) decline in global oil demand in 2026 as the fallout from the Middle East conflict continues to weigh on global markets, according to the agency's latest report.
This represents a 100,000 bpd downward revision from September, when the IEA projected a 2.5 million bpd drop. The agency notes that global oil demand will fall by 2.5 million bpd in the fourth quarter.
According to the agency, in the third quarter of 2026, supply volumes contracted by 3.7 million bpd year-on-year, indicating a slight improvement compared to the 5 million bpd slump seen in the second quarter. For most of the first six months of the conflict [in the Middle East], global demand remained close to 2019 levels. However, it is now expected to grow, driven by a gradual rise in supplies from Persian Gulf nations, the IEA stated.
The agency estimates that oil consumption growth will not return to positive territory until March 2027 at the earliest, which will drive a 2 million bpd demand increase for the full year 2027. According to the IEA, global oil demand in 2026 will average 102.377 million bpd, down from 104.994 million bpd in 2025. For 2027, the agency projects demand at 104.377 million bpd.

title: URCS responds to overnight Russian missile attack sites in Kyiv
body:
The Rapid Response Team of the Ukrainian Red Cross Society (URCS) worked at the sites of the aftermath of the overnight Russian missile attack in Kyiv.

"In Desniansky district, volunteers, alongside other emergency services, worked at the site of a strike on a multi-story residential building," the URCS reported on Facebook on Wednesday.

Volunteers conducted door-to-door checks to identify those affected and helped rescuers evacuate five people. They also provided pre-medical aid to the injured and psychological support to individuals experiencing acute stress reactions.

According to the latest data from the State Emergency Service of Ukraine, three people were killed as a result of the Russian attack on Kyiv. In Desniansky district, 21 people were injured, including one child, and 16 residents of the damaged apartment building were rescued. In Holosiivsky district, one person was killed and another injured following a strike on a non-residential building.
