title: Asaba Massacre: Only Apology from a Sitting President Can Assuage Our Pain, Says Asagba Azinge
body: Omon-Julius Onabu in Asaba The Asagba of Asaba, HRM Obi Prof. Epiphany Azinge (SAN), has reiterated that no force under the sun would sweep away the mindless and baseless massacre of hundreds of innocent Asaba people by the federal troops in early October 1967 during the Nigerian Civil War. Asagba Azinge underscored the point that only a formal apology from a sitting Nigerian president could assuage the deep pain and sense of monumental injustice against the people and kingdom of Asaba, saying that it was a matter of regret that his people have received nothing but a deafening silence from successive governments in Nigeria several decades after the bloodletting in Asaba. The monarch was speaking in Asaba, Delta State, at the 59th anniversary of the tragic incident, when the Convener of the Asaba Massacre Memorial, Chief Chuck Nduka-Eze, unfolded to stakeholders the preparations for the 60th anniversary of the massacre and plans towards the actualisation of the proposed Asaba Massacre Memorial Centre or complex. The occasion also featured the presentation of a special audio-visual message from Nigeria’s former President, Chief Olusegun Obasanjo, who appealed for forgiveness and reconciliation while regretting the unfortunate massacre of Asaba indigenes, who were mainly men, in 1967. Obasanjo, who was scheduled to chair the 59th anniversary of the memorial programme, described the massacre as “one of the most painful, one of the most terrible aspects” of the Nigerian Civil War. Obasanjo said: “This marks the remembrance of one very sad aspect of the Nigerian Civil War. Of course, the war in its entirety was an unfortunate event which should never happen. “However, the Asaba Massacre -as it is called – was one of the most painful, one of the most terrible aspects of that war.” He admitted that he wept after receiving documents on the massacre from Chief Chuk Nduka-Eze, as the full import of the incident dawned on him. A visibly shaken Obasanjo said: “To all of you assembled, let us keep one thing in mind: forgiveness, forgiveness, and forgiveness again.” On his part, the Asaba royal father emphasised that the curtains could not be drawn on the unprovoked 1967 mass killings in Asaba unconditionally, and without any expression of remorse by the country’s authorities. Asagba Azinge said: “We may not forget, but certainly we have to forgive. Indeed, we have shown resilience and unwavering commitment to peace as a people, without any sense of animosity towards anybody. “However, there will be no closure or healing until a sitting president-not an ex-president-publicly apologises to us.” He acknowledged the fact that a former military Head of State, General Yakubu Gowon, had apologised while out of office, just as former President Olusegun Obasanjo had done at the 59th anniversary celebration. “We need a sitting president to apologise to the Asaba people, and only that will bring closure,” the Asagba maintained. He also picked holes in Obasanjo’s “never again” chorus, recalling that the outrageous Odi killings occurred during his reign as Nigerian president. Obi Azinge observed that: “Coming from him, I was a bit taken aback. How long do we say ‘never again’? But it happened at Odi. Odi came years after Asaba, and he was the president when that happened.” While acknowledging the deep sense of responsibility and uncommon courage exhibited by Major-General Ahmed Ibrahim Taiwo (retired), the son of the late Colonel Ibrahim Taiwo, a top military officer allegedly involved in the military operation that culminated in the Asaba massacre, the monarch stressed the need to forgive and forge ahead as a people. He said: “On behalf of the Asaba community, and as the prescribed authority, the Asagba of Asaba, I hereby publicly proclaim that we have forgiven the Taiwo family. “Yes, there is every need for us to forgive them. We may not forget, but certainly, we have to forgive.” The monarch stated that Asaba as a people “have moved on” despite the deep scarring of their hearts by the incident. Earlier, the youthful retired army general said that he was in Asaba “to render our deepest regrets and apologise on behalf of our father and family for any act of omission or commission on his part that led to this heinous massacre. “I know it will not right the wrong, but I believe and pray it is a start towards reconciliation.” The Asagba responded by stressing that forgiveness was part of the community’s character, saying Asaba people had the strength “to accept that apology.” In a solidarity message, the Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, represented by the Secretary to the State Government (SSG), Dr Kingsley Eze Emu, said that researchers and community historians had estimated that more than 1,000 people lost their lives in the Asaba Massacre. “Let us speak clearly: the killing of unarmed civilians can never be justified,” the governor noted. However, he pledged continued support for the overall development of Asaba and obtaining national recognition for the massacre as well as the establishment of a fitting national memorial in Asaba. Nduka-Eze said the 60th anniversary would be used to further tell the story to Nigerians and the world, stressing that “Nigerians live matter.” Nduka-Eze disclosed that preparations were already underway for next year’s 60th memorial, including efforts to actualise the Memorial Centre as a permanent place for remembrance, documentation, and education. The event also featured remarks by Mr. Enotie Ogbebor, son of the late Col. Paul Ogbebor, who is credited with intervening to save lives during the tragedy, and Chief Chike Ogieh, whose father fled with his whole family from Benin City to eastern Nigeria to escape the Asaba massacre. “The Asaba massacre should be remembered all over the world, not just in Nigeria,” Ogbebor said, adding that the memorial would be “a reminder for humanity that no innocent lives should be lost unfairly for any reason.” Also, the Obi of Onitsha, His Majesty, Igwe Nnaemeka Alfred Ugochukwu Achebe (Agbogidi), who was among the notable personages at the event, harped on the need for restitution, reconciliation, and forgiveness.

title: Greek Athletes Shine at European Sailing Championship in Turkey
body: Greek sailor Marios Stathas leads the overall standings in the men’s ILCA 7 class at the Open European U21 Championship in Bodrum, Turkey, after four races in a competition featuring 183 boats from 42 countries. Stathas tops the standings among 118 boats with 11 penalty points. He finished fourth, 30th, fourth and third in the four races, discarding his 30th-place result as his worst score. Five Greek sailors sit among the top 33 competitors, with the team still having room to improve their positions. Nikolaos Komianos ranks 17th overall with 28 points and fourth in the U19 category. His results were 16th, 17th, second and 10th, with the 17th-place finish discarded. Adamantios Petrianos stands 26th with 40 points, after finishing 26th, 20th, 18th and second. He discarded his 26th-place result. Konstantinos Portosalte ranks 31st with 43 points, having recorded first, 13th, 29th and 39th places. He discarded the 39th-place finish. Alexandros Kyfidis sits 33rd with 44 points, after finishing 13th, 17th, 14th and 22nd. He discarded his 22nd-place result. The remaining Greek competitors in the men’s ILCA 7 fleet are Georgios Kypraios in 57th place with 70 points, Georgios Bougiouris in 67th with 82, and Emmanouil Anastasios Vomvylas in 88th with 111. In the women’s ILCA 6 class, which features 65 boats, Ermoni Gkika ranks 19th with 52 points, while Miranda Papadaki sits 46th with 103 points. Gkika’s results were 33rd, ninth, 20th and 23rd, with her 33rd-place finish discarded. Papadaki recorded ninth, 42nd, 52nd and 56th places, discarding her 56th-place result. title: Niger Gets 1,055KM Of Federal Roads As Bago Flags Off Lambata-Bida-Mokwa Highway
body: Niger State accounts for 1,055 kilometres of the 5,500 kilometres of new and ongoing federal road projects being executed nationwide under President Bola Tinubu’s administration. Governor Umaru Bago, who represented President Tinubu at the ceremony, performed the flag-off of the project, which is expected to improve road connectivity, facilitate trade and boost economic activities across the country. Representing the President, Governor Bago thanked the Federal Government for approving major road projects in Niger State, describing the highway as a strategic intervention that would connect communities and ease the movement of people and goods. He expressed confidence that the project would improve transportation, enhance access to markets and stimulate economic activities across the state and beyond. Bago also pledged to mobilise the highest number of votes nationwide for President Tinubu in the next election, citing the Federal Government’s infrastructure investments in Niger State. Speaking earlier, the Minister of Works, David Umahi, disclosed that Niger State accounts for 1,055 kilometres of the 5,500 kilometres of new and ongoing federal road projects being executed nationwide. Umahi made this known during the flag-off of the reconstruction and dualisation of the Lambata-Bida-Mokwa-Makera-Kontagora Federal Highway in Bida, Niger State. He described the highway as a major component of the Tinubu administration’s infrastructure development programme, noting that its scale, reinforced concrete pavement technology and the involvement of the Dangote Group through the Federal Government’s infrastructure tax-credit scheme could make it the administration’s fifth legacy road project. The minister disclosed that 162 kilometres of roads and 115 metres of bridges had been completed in the North-Central region. He commended Governor Bago for his commitment to infrastructure development, stating that the governor had constructed more than 300 kilometres of roads, over five flyovers and an underpass in Niger State. Umahi said the governor’s approach to road construction demonstrated a commitment to development, regardless of whether a road fell under federal or state government responsibility. Also speaking, the Minister of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris, who spoke on behalf of his colleagues in the Federal Executive Council, said he was delighted to witness the impact of President Tinubu’s reforms on infrastructure development in Niger State. Idris disclosed that the Federal Government was investing a total of 1.8 trillion naira in the road project, describing the intervention as a major step towards stimulating economic activities across the state. He said the project would extend from Mokwa through Lambata and beyond Kontagora towards Tegina, opening up communities and strengthening economic connections across the state. The minister noted that Niger State had never witnessed such a massive infrastructure development initiative, attributing the projects to policy decisions taken by President Tinubu. Idris thanked the President on behalf of the people of Niger State for approving the projects, expressing confidence that the investments would attract significant electoral support for the President in the next election. He maintained that the scale of the infrastructure projects demonstrated the Federal Government’s commitment to development, particularly in Niger State. In his remarks, the Special Adviser to the President of the Dangote Group, Mansir Ahmed, said the company was pleased to participate in the project through the infrastructure tax-credit scheme. Ahmed explained that the highway would be constructed using concrete pavement rather than conventional asphalt, adding that work would commence from four different locations to accelerate construction and ensure timely delivery. He said the completed highway would facilitate the transportation of agricultural produce, commercial goods and industrial materials while creating economic opportunities for businesses and young people. The project is expected to reduce travel delays, improve road safety and enhance access to markets for farming communities and businesses along the corridor. title: HD HHI Launches Third 2,400-Ton OPV ‘BRP Rajah Humabon’ for Philippine Navy
body: HD Hyundai Heavy Industries has launched BRP Rajah Humabon , the third of six 2,400-ton Offshore Patrol Vessels (OPVs) built for the Philippine Navy. HD Hyundai Heavy Industries press release Marking another milestone in a decade-long defense partnership, HD Hyundai Heavy Industries (HD HHI) launched the BRP Rajah Humabon , the third of six 2,400-ton Offshore Patrol Vessels (OPVs) built for the Philippine Navy, at its primary shipyard in Ulsan on Monday. The ceremonial launching—HD HHI’s first export naval vessel launch of the year—was attended by prominent diplomatic and military leaders from both nations, including Vice Admiral Jose Ma. Ambrosio Ezpeleta, Flag Officer in Command of the Philippine Navy; Bernadette Therese Fernandez, Philippine Ambassador to South Korea; Lieutenant General Rommel P. Roldan, Vice Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces of the Philippines; and Won-ho Joo, President & Head of Naval & Medium Size Ships Business Unit at HD HHI. Named after the 16th-century ruler of Cebu who played a pivotal role in early Philippine history, the Rajah Humabon is scheduled for official delivery in February 2027. BRP Rajah Humabon launching ceremony. HD HHI picture. Advanced Maritime Capabilities Designed to enhance maritime domain awareness and coastal defense capabilities across the Philippine archipelago, the state-of-the-art 2,400-ton vessel measures 94 meters in length and 14 meters in width. Capable of maintaining a cruising speed of 15 knots (approximately 28 km/h) with an impressive operational range of 5,500 nautical miles (10,186 km), the patrol ship is built for extended endurance at sea. The vessel is equipped with advanced defense systems, including a 76mm main naval gun, a 30mm secondary gun, decoy launching systems, surveillance radar, and electro-optical tracking equipment. A Decade of Naval Partnership The launch of the Rajah Humabon marks a decade of continuous naval cooperation between HD HHI and the Philippine Armed Forces. The relationship began in 2016 with a milestone contract for the Philippine Navy’s first modern frigates. Since then, HD HHI has secured orders for 12 naval vessels from the Philippines—comprising four frigates, two corvettes, and six OPVs—six of which have already been delivered. The first vessel in this OPV class, the Rajah Sulayma n , was delivered in February ahead of its scheduled deadline, while the second, the Rajah Lakandula , was commissioned into active service in June . The remaining three vessels (numbers 4 through 6) are scheduled for sequential delivery through 2028. “With the trust placed in us by the Philippines, we have established ourselves as a steadfast partner in the modernization of the Philippine Navy by delivering six vessels on time or ahead of schedule,” said Won-ho Joo, President & Head of Naval & Medium Size Ships Business Unit at HD HHI. “We will continue to fulfill our role as a strategic partner, ensuring stable operational support through maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) services.” Beyond Ship Construction: MRO and Global Expansion The collaboration between South Korea and the Philippines has evolved beyond shipbuilding into long-term sustainment. In November 2022, HD HHI established a dedicated Logistics Support Center at the Subic Naval Base in the Philippines, providing spare parts storage and technical training facilities to support the operational readiness of previously delivered frigates. HD HHI is leveraging its successful track record in the Philippines to expand its global naval enterprise, pursuing a strategy termed the “Pan-Pacific Belt.” This initiative focuses on establishing localized construction frameworks, standardized technology transfer packages, and strategic regional partnerships in key defense markets, including Peru, Saudi Arabia, and the United States. Demonstrating this global momentum, HD HHI recently launched the Chimbote, the Peruvian Navy’s new landing support ship, at the SIMA Shipyard in Peru. title: UAE orders recall of face mask batch over possible contamination
body: The UAE has ordered a recall of a batch of face masks because of concerns about possible contamination of the material used in its manufacture. The Emirates Drug Establishment issued the recall for Nin 160 FMB-NML Facemask C G blue, batch number 20251015. It is described as blue in colour and three-ply in structure. The Dubai Health Authority also issued a circular on Monday instructing healthcare centres to comply with the recall. Officials said Ningbo ETDZ Holdings Ltd in China manufactured the masks, and Globemed Care LLC distributed them in the UAE. The drug regulator said the recall was ordered after a quality complaint. Inspections identified foreign material or contamination in units from the affected batch. Healthcare professionals, hospitals and clinics and pharmacies must immediately stop selling, supplying, distributing or using the affected batch. They must identify and quarantine all available stock, then arrange for its return to the local supplier or distributor, Globemed Care LLC. They must also maintain records of quantities identified, quarantined, and returned. Residents who purchased the affected product should stop using any packs with batch number 20251015 and return them to the point of purchase or supplier. Healthcare providers must report any product quality complaints or adverse incidents related to the masks through EDE-approved reporting channels. Globemed Care LLC has also been ordered to retrieve all distributed quantities from the UAE market. It must also provide the regulator with details of quantities imported, distributed, returned, and remaining in stock, as well as a complete UAE distribution list. The regulator also urged people to report any quality concerns or adverse incidents involving the product directly to the authority.

title: Forces complete 4th stage of Vivaldi operation in northern Donetsk region, liberating over 88 sq km – Biletsky
body:
The 3rd Army Corps has announced the completion of the fourth stage of the Vivaldi offensive operation, during which corps units liberated an additional 101 sq km of Ukrainian territory and restored control over the villages of Zelena Dolyna, Lypove, and Kolodiazi in the Lyman community of Kramatorsk district, Donetsk region, reported the 3rd Army Corps Commander Brigadier General Andriy Biletsky.
According to a press release from the corps, Russian occupation forces lost over 3,000 personnel in this sector. Across all four stages of the operation, the 3rd Army Corps and attached forces have liberated 277 square kilometer of Ukrainian land and restored control over 16 settlements (nine de-occupied, seven cleared of infiltrated enemy forces). Total Russian personnel losses across the four stages exceed 8,000, with more than 250 Russian soldiers captured.
"Vivaldi proves that an offensive is possible even with smaller forces thanks to asymmetric actions. At the same time, it is possible to maintain a robust defense in other sectors," Biletsky emphasized.
In turn, the DeepState OSINT project reported on Wednesday morning that Ukrainian defense forces not only liberated Kolodiazi, Lypove, and Zelena Dolyna over the past day, but also restored control near the neighboring villages of Stavky and Shandryholove. According to project maps, 88.17 square kilometer of Ukrainian territory was de-occupied over the day, the area of Russian occupation decreased by 78.95 square kilometer, and the gray zone significantly contracted.
Biletsky cited the primary strategic achievement of the four stages of Operation Vivaldi as disrupting the enemy's plans to capture the Sloviansk-Kramatorsk agglomeration in northern Donetsk region from the flanks and encircle it. Ukrainian forces also secured the Kharkiv-Sloviansk highway, preventing the enemy from severing the key logistical artery for the Donbas grouping. Furthermore, the corps' offensive forced the Russian military command to withdraw units of the 1st Tank Army from the Kupiansk direction in Kharkiv region and redeploy them to the Lyman direction, easing Russian pressure on Kupiansk-Vuzlovy.

title: Starlink limit hits Ukraine’s drones. The battlefield depends on SpaceX
body:
SpaceX has introduced a speed restriction affecting StarShield terminals used by Ukraine. According to Ukrainian sources, connectivity began to fail when platforms exceeded around 160 km/h, disrupting part of Ukraine’s combat missions. Later reports claimed that the restriction may have been tightened further, with some operators losing communication already at 60–70 km/h. If confirmed, that would no longer affect only fast strike drones, but also a much wider group of reconnaissance and tactical UAVs.
The first point is technical, but crucial. This is not a general shutdown of Starlink for the Ukrainian military. The issue concerns terminals used in motion, especially under the StarShield military package. The initial figure of around 160 km/h is important because it affects faster unmanned platforms, including strike systems and drones operating beyond classic radio-control range. A lower threshold of 60–70 km/h would be far more serious, because many ordinary tactical UAVs operate in that speed bracket.
It is also wrong to describe Starlink mainly as a navigation system for drones. Its real role is communication: command link, video transmission, mission updates and contact between operator and platform beyond direct line of sight. A drone may still know where it is going through GNSS, inertial systems or autonomous navigation, but without a reliable data link, it loses flexibility, live control and battlefield value. In drone warfare, the link is often as important as the airframe.
Serhii Sternenko suggested that SpaceX’s decision could be connected to pressure from the Trump administration on Kyiv. Similar interpretations appeared in Ukrainian discussions, especially because the restriction comes amid tensions over Ukrainian strikes against targets in Russia. But this should not be presented as an established fact. SpaceX has not publicly confirmed such a motive. The White House has not confirmed that it ordered the change. Reuters has not established that the restriction came from the US administration.
The political context is obvious, but attribution is not the same as suspicion. What is already clear is that SpaceX can remotely change the operational parameters of terminals used on the battlefield. Even a narrow technical change, such as a speed limit, can immediately affect strike missions, reconnaissance and command links. For Ukraine, this is not only a question of one service update. It is a question of dependence.
Earlier this year, mechanisms for verifying and limiting Starlink terminals helped Ukraine counter Russian use of the system on drones. The same kind of technical control now appears to have affected Ukrainian military users. This shows both the strength and the weakness of the system. Starlink and StarShield give Ukraine resilient communications that are difficult to replace. At the same time, Ukraine does not fully control the conditions under which that communications architecture operates.
That is the real military issue. The war in Ukraine has shown that private satellite networks can become part of the battlefield. But private infrastructure also means private control, contractual limits, geofencing, service parameters and political exposure. A state can build drones, train operators and plan missions, but if the data link depends on one external provider, the whole system remains vulnerable to decisions made outside the chain of command.
If the 60–70 km/h reports were confirmed, the consequences would go beyond fast strike drones. They would affect a larger part of Ukraine’s unmanned architecture and force operators to adapt missions, platforms and communications methods. The problem is therefore not simply that Starlink has imposed a speed limit. The problem is that one technical decision by SpaceX can change the tempo of Ukrainian drone operations almost immediately.

title: Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis may conduct land or sea attack against Israel, defense officials warn
body: The threat posed by the Houthis in Yemen has intensified amid fighting with Saudi Arabia, Israeli defense officials assess, prompting heightened preparations for a possible surprise attack against Israel by land or sea.Israel is on heightened alert over the possibility of such an attack, given the Houthis' efforts to improve their ability to carry out attacks from both directions.As part of these preparations, the IDF is expected to establish a fire coordination center within the Edom Division.Over the past two years, the Houthis have released numerous videos documenting training exercises simulating ground raids against Israel, including scenarios involving mock military outposts and fortified guard towers.According to defense officials, the Houthis have increasingly warned in recent weeks and months that they could carry out ground attacks, including against Israel.Defense officials say the Houthis are unpredictable and have posed significant challenges to Saudi Arabia through their methods of warfare, as well as their extremist and uncompromising culture and ideology.As a result, Israel is taking no chances and is preparing for unexpected developments through several parallel measures.These include maintaining reserve and rapid-response troops in the Eilat area, conducting training exercises, deploying weapons systems, and improving coordination and connectivity among ground, naval, and air units.The preparations also involve shortening response times and conducting joint exercises with the Israel Police and Border Police operating in the area.In addition, Israeli defense officials are not ruling out the possibility of a chain reaction in which the Houthis significantly increase their attacks on the Saudi home front, causing additional casualties and substantial damage.Such a development could force Saudi Arabia to intensify its military response, potentially drawing the US military into a more forceful confrontation.Houthis could target US interests in IsraelUnder such circumstances, the Houthis could target American interests on Israeli territory, potentially requiring the IDF to respond."The Houthis have long since ceased to be regarded as proxies of the Iranians, and they are demonstrating operational independence with an inexplicable determination against the Saudis," one defense official said.The threat from Yemen features prominently in Israeli security assessments, alongside extensive intelligence-gathering efforts aimed at monitoring Houthi intentions and capabilities.At the same time, operational and intelligence coordination between the IDF and the US military's Central Command (CENTCOM) is aimed at refining early-warning mechanisms against attempts to catch Israel by surprise and reducing the likelihood of unexpected attacks as much as possible.

title: Irving Shipbuilding marks milestone in Canadian Navy's frigate refit
body:
HMCS Halifax has been floated up and undocked at Halifax Shipyard in Nova Scotia, with Irving Shipbuilding continuing refit work on the Royal Canadian Navy frigate ahead of its planned handover in 2027.
Irving Shipbuilding confirmed the milestone in an October 14 social media post, stating that the ship had been moved from the graving dock to a pier-side berth at the shipyard, where work will continue before the vessel is returned to the navy.
Commissioned on June 29, 1992, in her namesake city, HMCS Halifax was the first Halifax-class frigate to enter service with the Canadian Navy. The class comprises 12 Canadian-built, multi-role frigates designed initially for anti-submarine and anti-surface warfare. The ships also conduct operations against air threats and support domestic and international missions.
According to the Royal Canadian Navy, Halifax-class frigates have a maximum displacement of 4,770 tonnes, a length of 134.1 meters and a beam of 16.4 meters. They can reach a top speed of 30 knots, have a range of 9,500 nautical miles and accommodate a maximum crew of 225.
The refit is part of Canada's long-term maintenance program for its 12 Halifax-class frigates. In August 2019, the Government of Canada announced an investment of C$7.5 billion to maintain the fleet until the ships are retired in the early 2040s, ensuring they remain operational until the Canadian Surface Combatants enter service.
As part of the program, maintenance contracts initially totaling C$1.5 billion were awarded to three shipyards: Irving Shipbuilding in Nova Scotia, Seaspan Victoria Shipyards in British Columbia, and Chantier Davie in Quebec. The initial contracts covered a minimum of three frigates per shipyard, with their value expected to increase as additional work packages were added.
The maintenance program has already reached several milestones. Chantier Davie completed work on HMCS St John's in 2022, while Seaspan Victoria Shipyards delivered HMCS Calgary in 2025.

title: Trump Announces Major Oil and Gas Exploration in Greenland
body: US President Donald Trump says Greenland will play an “unparalleled” role in European and American security, while announcing plans for a major exploration drive targeting the island’s oil, natural gas and mineral resources. In a post on his Truth Social platform, Trump said US military personnel stationed permanently in Greenland would help defend against future attacks on the United States. “Any future attack on the United States would have to pass through Greenland, where our Defence would systematically shoot down drones, missiles or any other form of weapon that has not even been invented yet,” Trump wrote. The US president also announced that a “massive exploration” programme for oil, natural gas and minerals was about to begin in what he called “our new and wonderful Greenland”. Trump did not provide details of the proposed exploration plans. However, he claimed that experts believed Greenland held more easily accessible oil than almost any other territory in the world. The announcement comes less than a month after the United States, Denmark and Greenland signed an agreement aimed at easing tensions following Trump’s repeated threats to bring the strategically located, mineral-rich island under US control. The agreement expands the US military role in Greenland, paving the way for two new military bases and the deployment of the US Golden Dome missile defence system. It also reaffirms Danish sovereignty and Greenlanders’ right to self-determination. The post Trump Announces Major Oil and Gas Exploration in Greenland appeared first on Greek City Times .

title: The Iran war has driven Trump crazy
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 14 (MNA) – The Iran war has now become a factor in eroding the US president's political credibility and restricting his room for maneuver.
More than seven months ago, Donald Trump started a war against Iran that was supposed to showcase America's military power and force Tehran to accept Washington's demands, but now this war has become a factor in eroding the American president's political credibility and restricting his room for maneuver. The Atlantic magazine's report on Trump's anger and confusion in the face of his inability to end the war against Iran presents a picture of the White House's deadlock and the consequences of Washington's miscalculations.
The Atlantic magazine, citing sources close to Donald Trump, the American president, has reported that his inability to end the war with Iran has made him extremely angry and at the same time has unusually restricted his decision-making and maneuvering power. According to this report, Trump, who is accustomed to attracting the attention of world leaders and the media, now faces a situation in which neither his threats have been able to force Iran to retreat nor have political and economic pressures produced the result Washington wanted. In describing Trump's psychological and political condition, The Atlantic writes that he is losing control because Iran is not yielding to his demands. This report also refers to the resumption of tanker threats in the Strait of Hormuz and the rise in diesel prices in America; factors that have increased the economic costs of the crisis for American citizens and intensified Republicans' concern about its electoral consequences. The Gap Between Washington's Objectives and the Realities on the Ground The main problem for Trump is not only the prolongation of the conflict with Iran, but the gap that has formed between America's declared objectives and the results of this confrontation. The American government entered the war with the assumption that the weapons superiority and operational capability of American forces could change Tehran's calculations in a short period and provide the ground for imposing Washington's demands. However, military superiority alone does not guarantee the achievement of political objectives, and developments in this crisis have shown that converting military power into a strategic result depends on a set of factors beyond weapons capability. Under such circumstances, the greater the gap between the initial objectives and the final result, the more the political costs of the decision to continue the conflict also increase. The American president must, on the one hand, be accountable for the expectations he created by promising a display of power and achieving a quick result, and on the other hand, face the economic and political consequences of the crisis's continuation. This situation can restrict the White House's decision-making power; because retreating without achieving the declared objectives carries the risk of weakening political credibility, and continuing the conflict also brings increasing costs. The Strait of Hormuz and the Expansion of the Crisis's Costs One of the most important dimensions of this crisis is the linking of the region's security developments with the global economy and the daily lives of American citizens. The Strait of Hormuz, due to its role in the transfer of oil and energy products, has a strategic position in global markets, and any disruption in maritime transit through this route can change market expectations and lead to an increase in transportation and energy costs. The Atlantic report, referring to the average price of diesel in America exceeding six dollars per gallon, emphasizes one of the most important domestic consequences of this crisis. The rise in fuel prices is not limited to the direct costs of households; a large part of consumer goods in America are transported by truck, and the rise in fuel costs can increase transportation costs and ultimately the final price of goods. In this way, the consequences of a foreign crisis gradually become a tangible issue in the economic life of citizens. For the Trump administration, this issue is important because public opinion usually links economic costs with the performance of the incumbent government. Promises related to reducing living costs, controlling inflation, and strengthening the economy face doubt when fuel prices rise and more pressure is placed on households and businesses. In such an atmosphere, claimed military achievements also cannot necessarily compensate for the dissatisfaction caused by the rise in living costs.
Republicans' Concern About Electoral Consequences
According to The Atlantic's report, Republicans are worried that the rise in energy prices will strengthen the Democrats' position in the midterm elections and lead to the loss of control of the House of Representatives and the Senate. This concern shows that the consequences of the war for the White House are not limited to the realm of foreign policy or military relations and can also affect the balance of power inside America.
The midterm elections are of particular importance for the American president; because a change in the composition of Congress can make advancing the government's programs more difficult and provide the ground for increased political and oversight pressures on the White House. From this perspective, the rise in fuel prices and concern about the economic situation is, for Republicans, not merely a livelihood issue, but a factor influencing the evaluation of the government's performance and determining the fate of electoral competitions.
Under such circumstances, Trump faces a serious contradiction. To maintain the image of a powerful president, he seeks to show success and the imposition of America's will; but the continuation of a crisis whose economic costs are transferred to American citizens can weaken this very image. The longer the crisis lasts, the more difficult it will be for the government to explain the reasons for its continuation and prove the necessity of bearing its costs.
Ukraine; An Attempt to Escape Responsibility?
In another part of its report, The Atlantic writes that Trump has been searching for someone to blame for the current situation and appears to consider Ukraine responsible for part of the problems. This is while attributing the rise in global oil prices to a country that is struggling to confront its own existential threats faces serious difficulties. From this perspective, blaming Ukraine can be seen as an attempt to divert public attention from the American government's decision to start the war against Iran.
Of course, determining the factors affecting global oil prices requires examining a set of variables including supply, demand, market expectations, and geopolitical developments, and all fluctuations in the energy market cannot be attributed to a single factor. However, what is important in The Atlantic's report is the way Trump confronts the consequences of his own decision and his attempt to transfer responsibility to others.
Overall, The Atlantic's report shows that the war against Iran has become a difficult test for Trump; a test in which America's military power alone has not been able to provide an easy way out of the crisis. The narrowing of political options, the increase in economic costs, and concern about electoral consequences can all reduce the American president's room for maneuver. For Washington, the issue now is not only how to continue the confrontation, but finding a way to end it without accepting heavy political and strategic costs; a dilemma that, the longer it continues, the more the contradiction between Trump's initial promises and the realities facing him will become apparent.

title: Venice Commission Criticises Georgia’s 2025 Amendments Extending Party Ban to Individuals
body: The Venice Commission, the Council of Europe’s advisory body, has warned that Georgia’s October 2025 legislative amendments that allow for extending the party ban to individual members are contrary to international standards of pluralism and democracy, and “risk undermining” the country’s constitutional order “profoundly,” rather than protecting it. In a 22-page opinion published on October 13 at the request of the president of the Monitoring Committee of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe (PACE), the commission assessed a legislative package adopted by the Georgian Dream-led disputed Parliament on October 16, 2025, that extends restrictions beyond parties declared unconstitutional to individuals deemed “associated” with them. The amendments to several laws bar such individuals from establishing or joining political parties, running in elections, holding political office, and exercising other political rights, while also allowing for the termination of electoral mandates and the disqualification of party lists. According to the opinion, the amendments “further develop interconnected legal framework governing the prohibition of political parties and the consequences flowing therefrom for both political parties and individuals ‘associated’ with such parties.” “They introduce far-reaching and severe restrictions on such individuals in terms of their ability to participate in political life, including by establishing, joining or leading political parties, standing for election, retaining electoral mandates, holding public or political office, and engaging in electoral processes,” the Commission said. Citing international standards governing the prohibition of political parties and related sanctions, the Venice Commission stressed that such measures can be justified only under “very limited circumstances,” including “the necessity for a democracy to defend itself” and are “subject to strict legitimate aims and proportionality requirements.” However, “there is no evidence that the October 2025 package would have responded to such a necessity,” the Commission noted. “The restrictions imposed on individuals ‘associated’ to dissolved political parties raise serious concerns under international human rights standards,” the opinion reads. Moreover, the commission argues that “regulatory framework lacks legal certainty and foreseeability, as key triggering concepts, such as the notion of individuals ‘associated’ with a prohibited political party, are formulated in overly broad and imprecise terms, conferring excessive discretion on the authorities.” “It imposes severe consequences on the freedom of association and electoral rights of individuals which are triggered by the prohibition of a political party without ensuring a genuine, individualised assessment of personal conduct, responsibility, or intent, thereby raising concerns of guilt by association,” the commission said. It added that “the severity and disproportionality of the cumulative restrictions constitute an additional shortcoming, since the combined exclusions from political parties, electoral participation, public office, and representative mandates affect the core of political rights without clear temporal limits or effective review mechanisms.” The commission also warned that the measures “risk undermining electoral processes and political pluralism, as the removal of candidates or termination of mandates – particularly when applied through expedited procedures during electoral periods – may distort electoral competition and voters’ freedom of choice.” In its concluding assessment, the Venice Commission rejected the stated justification for the legislation, arguing that the measures do not serve their declared purpose of protecting Georgia’s constitutional order. “In light of these conclusions, the Venice Commission considers that the legislation under examination does not pursue the stated aim of protecting the constitutional order from violent constitutional change, threats to independence, territorial integrity, war propaganda, violence, incitement to national, regional, religious or social hatred,” the opinion reads. “It rather imposes disproportionate and unnecessary restrictions on the political freedom of the Georgian citizens, in particular preventing the formation and survival of a political opposition – especially when considering the cumulative and systemic impact of the legislative framework as a whole, including the recent amendments that expanded the grounds for banning political parties and which barred any individual working for a ‘foreign agent’ from joining a political party or an ‘organisation with declared party-political objectives’ for eight years,” the opinion says. “Rather than protecting the constitutional order, this legislation therefore risks undermining it profoundly. It is contrary to international standards on pluralism and democracy,” the commission concluded. The Amendments The legislative package, adopted by the Georgian Dream-led Parliament on October 16, 2025, amended four laws to extend restrictions applying to parties declared unconstitutional to individuals associated with such parties. The amendments were introduced amid GD’s push to seek the banning of key opposition parties through an appeal to the Constitutional Court. While the ruling party has resubmitted its constitutional claim several times, seeking to outlaw five parties, it has so far refrained from invoking the amendments that allow it to impose restrictions on individual members and figures. The Court announced on October 13 that it started considering the appeal on its merits, and scheduled first hearings on October 21-22-23. 13/10/2026 – Denied Recusal, Judge Manana Kobakhidze Quits Constitutional Court Under the amendments to the Organic Law on the Constitutional Court, such individuals are barred from founding, joining or leading political parties, holding political office or serving in party leadership bodies. The changes also allow for the termination of their electoral mandates and removal from party lists. Amendments to the Criminal Code introduce fines for political parties that fail to comply with or obstruct the enforcement of Constitutional Court decisions imposing these restrictions. Changes to the Law on Political Associations of Citizens and the Election Code allow authorities to deny registration to parties involving such individuals, bar them from running in elections and disqualify party lists containing them. The amendments also prohibit these individuals from donating to political parties. title: BBNaija wears a Nigerian crown, not an African one
body: Big Brother Africa (BBA), which debuted in 2003, was more than just a reality TV show; it was a significant representation of the entire continent. The program featured participants from Ghana, Nigeria, Kenya, and Zambia engaging in discussions over milk under one roof, symbolising Africa itself. Its mission revolved around promoting unity, culture, entrepreneurship, and beauty, embodying the principles of Pan-Africanism in practice. The diary sessions became a platform for cultural diplomacy, where contestants shared food, textiles, languages, and narratives from their respective countries. The event was sponsored by Pan-African brands like MTN and Coca-Cola Africa, and winners like Zambia’s Cherise Makubale and Namibia’s Dillish Mathews became celebrated figures across the continent. Although its pace was sometimes slow and uneventful, the authenticity of BBA was undeniable. In contrast, The Apprentice Africa (2008) represented a business-oriented experiment. Hosted by advertising mogul Biodun Shobanjo, it brought together 18 young professionals from six African countries- Nigeria, Ghana, Uganda, Kenya, Cameroon, and Guinea—who competed in Lagos for a $200,000 annual position. Ghana’s Isaac Dankyi-Koranteng triumphed, defeating Nigerian-American Eunice Omole in the final round, embodying the very essence of BBA’s mission: fostering African business collaboration across borders. It raised critical questions that remain unresolved: Can a Nigerian effectively manage a Ugandan? Can a Ghanaian successfully market to Kenyans? It was essentially BBA reimagined in a corporate setting. However, the show only lasted one season due to three main reasons, which also explain the decline of BBA: Lack of Pan-African Employment: No company operates across the entire continent. For instance, MTN Nigeria seeks a representative from Nigeria, while MTN Ghana prefers a Ghanaian. Who would hire a Pan-African winner? Cost vs. Commerce: The expenses incurred by flying 18 contestants from various countries and accommodating them in Lagos were prohibitively high. BBNaija circumvented this issue by focusing on a single country with one major telecom partner. Absence of a Supportive Ecosystem: In the US, winners often secure jobs with large corporations like Trump’s. In Africa, no continental enterprise was substantial enough to employ the winner, resulting in cash prizes rather than career opportunities. BBNaija, which launched in 2006, has outlasted its continental predecessor. While BBA concluded its ninth and final season in 2014, BBNaija evolved into a lucrative phenomenon: loud, dramatic, and rife with memes. A housemate in 2025 can earn more in three months than a BBA winner made in three years. The show effectively promotes Nigerian businesses, from Innoson to Flutterwave. However, it has also limited the broader vision, predominantly reflecting the cultures of Lagos and Port Harcourt, adhering to a singular beauty standard and accent. While this is advantageous for Nigeria, it raises questions about its impact on the entire continent. BBA did not cease to exist; rather, it was overshadowed. We traded the experience of unity for mere entertainment. What is needed now is a revival of BBA, one that combines the high production quality of BBNaija with the original spirit of BBA. Until such a revival occurs, BBNaija retains the crown, albeit a Nigerian one rather than a truly African one. The Big Question arises: “What next?” – By Alfred Mensah-Onumah | Executive Director, Ignite Incept Africa LBG

title: 2026 Ballon d’Or: Final power rankings revealed ahead of ceremony
body: Barcelona forward Lamine Yamal has emerged as the leading contender for the 2026 Ballon d’Or, moving ahead of Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane in the latest power rankings. Yamal’s impressive performances for Barcelona and Spain have strengthened his chances of claiming the prestigious individual award, with the ceremony scheduled to take place in London on October 25, according to the report. Kane, who enjoyed a prolific 2025/26 campaign with Bayern Munich, remains a strong contender. However, Yamal’s contributions to Spain’s World Cup triumph and his excellent start to the new season have improved his position in the race. Paris Saint-Germain forward Ousmane Dembele, who won the previous edition of the award, is sixth in the rankings, while Manchester City striker Erling Haaland occupies eighth place. Below are the top five players in The Independent’s 2026 Ballon d’Or power rankings. 1. Lamine Yamal — Barcelona and Spain Yamal tops the rankings after another outstanding season with Barcelona and a successful World Cup campaign with Spain. The 19-year-old reportedly scored 24 goals and provided 18 assists across competitions during Barcelona’s previous campaign, helping the club secure the LaLiga title. He has also made an impressive start to the new season, scoring eight goals in his first eight appearances. His performances for Spain further strengthened his case, particularly during the Nations League encounter against England at Wembley, where he scored in a 3-2 victory. With his club form and international achievements working in his favour, Yamal is considered the leading candidate to win his first Ballon d’Or after finishing as runner-up in 2025. 2. Harry Kane — Bayern Munich and England Kane occupies second place despite his remarkable scoring record for Bayern Munich during the 2025/26 season. The England captain reportedly scored 61 goals in 51 appearances across all competitions, helping Bayern win the league and cup double. He also contributed six goals to England’s World Cup campaign as the team secured its best finish at the tournament since winning it in 1966. Although Kane remains a major contender, Yamal’s recent performances for Spain have shifted the balance in the Barcelona forward’s favour. Kane acknowledged that the outcome was beyond his control, saying: “Of course, now it is out of my hands, it is down to the voters and the people who decide it,” he said. “The season I had was my best season by far and we’ll have to wait and see.” 3. Kylian Mbappe — Real Madrid and France Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe ranks third as he continues his pursuit of a first Ballon d’Or title. The Frenchman finished the World Cup as the tournament’s top scorer with 10 goals, surpassing previous scoring records associated with Miroslav Klose and Lionel Messi. His club performances also strengthened his credentials, with the report crediting him with 42 goals in 44 appearances during the previous season. Mbappe has continued his scoring form under Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho, registering eight goals in his first eight appearances of the new campaign. Despite Real Madrid’s trophyless season, his individual numbers keep him among the leading candidates for the award. 4. Rodri — Barcelona and Spain Rodri sits fourth after playing a significant role in Spain’s World Cup success. The midfielder was named the tournament’s best player after controlling the midfield and helping Spain maintain a strong defensive record throughout the competition. However, his chances of winning a second Ballon d’Or have been affected by his relatively limited involvement in Barcelona’s early-season matches following his return from injury. The report notes that Rodri had completed only two full 90-minute appearances in seven matches at the time of publication. His World Cup performance remains a major advantage, but his club form may prove decisive in determining whether he can overtake the players above him. 5. Lionel Messi — Inter Miami and Argentina Eight-time Ballon d’Or winner Lionel Messi completes the top five after an impressive World Cup campaign with Argentina. At 39, Messi scored eight goals to help Argentina reach the final, where they lost to Spain. Although Argentina fell short of retaining the title, Messi’s individual performances kept him in contention for another Ballon d’Or. His chances are also supported by his historical success in the award, having won it eight times, including in 2023 after Argentina’s previous World Cup triumph. Former England captain David Beckham has also backed Messi to win the award following his contribution to Inter Miami’s Campeones Cup success. However, his position in the rankings reflects the challenge of securing the prize without another World Cup title.
