title: UAE offers $1 million prize for winners of global AI challenge
body: The UAE announced a prize of $1 million for the winners of a global competition aimed at improving the quality of life through the use of agentic artificial intelligence . Mohammed Al Gergawi, Minister of Cabinet Affairs, announced the award on Wednesday at the Annual Meeting of Global Future Leaders, organised by the UAE Government and the World Economic Forum (WEF). The competition, a collaboration between Dubai Municipality and the WEF, will feature 10,000 entrants working to improve quality of life through artificial intelligence. The winner of the Agentic AI Award will be announced at next year's event, with organisers hoping it will become a "model for hundreds of cities worldwide". "This is an annual $1 million prize involving over 10,000 global changemakers across 150 countries to develop smart solutions that enhance urban services and quality of life," Mr Al Gergawi said. It was also announced that the Centre for Global Future Opportunities will be established between the Dubai Future Foundation and the WEF, which will "turn technological and economic opportunities into policies, legislation and projects that can be implemented". Also unveiled was the Future20 initiative, which will spotlight 20 leaders under the age of 30 "capable of driving major global transformations".

title: 150 new communities along Israel's borders: The ambitious plan for affordable homes and security
body: "For an ordinary citizen like me who wants to build a home, there's virtually no chance of building a decent house in the Tel Aviv metropolitan area. But the open spaces near Israel's borders give me the opportunity to build my dream home," Yoel Zilberman, founder and CEO of Hashomer Hachadash, said Tuesday at the People of the State conference, the flagship event of ynet and Yedioth Ahronoth. During his remarks, Zilberman discussed his organization's efforts to realize its vision of establishing 150 new communities across Israel.   "A month ago, we established Israel's first new moshav in 20 years," he said. "We have student villages, Nahal military-service groups, educational campuses and the Adam VeAdama school network. Beyond that, there's a real opportunity to develop the Egyptian border, where there's a 20-kilometer (12-mile) stretch of empty land, and establish dozens of new communities along it. "For each of these places, we need to think about how to integrate employment, renewable energy and therapeutic services. Israel can and should be a world leader in finding solutions to global water and food challenges." Zilberman also described efforts to enlist the ultra-Orthodox community in the initiative. "We're approaching them and saying, 'Listen, instead of establishing your yeshiva in Jerusalem, Bnei Brak or Modi'in, come build it along the Jordanian border,'" he said. "Within three weeks, the first yeshiva will be established along the border, at a site called Mahaneh Shetach, north of Jericho. Next to it, a new city called Ir Hatmarim, or City of Palms, is planned. It will be an ultra-Orthodox city. "Yoel Moshe Salomon's dream was to establish Petah Tikva there, near the Jordan River crossing. The area is known as Petah Tikva, and there's already a significant community there." According to Zilberman, the initiative has the potential to attract between 20,000 and 50,000 ultra-Orthodox young people to these areas. He concluded by expressing confidence that the initiative would receive broad political support regardless of who leads Israel's next government. "It doesn't matter which government is in power. I'm 100% certain that anyone with even a spark of Zionism will enthusiastically join us in this effort, and everyone will become part of it," he said. "We're not worried about who forms the next government because every citizen in this country depends on the strength and resilience of our borders. When you travel to Las Vegas, you see a thriving, growing city. There's absolutely no reason we can't have the same thing along our borders."

title: One-year-old AI startup with six employees acquired for estimated $100M
body: U.S. software company Rocket Software has acquired Israeli startup Geniez AI in a deal valued at up to $100 million, according to estimates. The two founders, both graduates of Mamram, the Israel Defense Forces’ computing unit, received the acquisition offer one year after announcing their Seed round, with the company having a team of only six employees. Full list of Israeli startup M&As in 2026 In September 2025, Geniez AI raised $6 million in a Seed funding round co-led by StageOne Ventures and Canapi Ventures. CEO Gil Peleg and co-founder Dan Shprung previously founded Model9, a mainframe data management startup acquired by BMC Software in 2023.   Geniez AI develops generative AI technology designed to help enterprises manage and modernize mainframe systems, the large-scale computers that underpin critical business operations across industries, including financial services. Its AI agents operate directly on mainframes, monitoring live systems, diagnosing incidents and executing workflows using natural language. As part of the acquisition, Geniez AI’s technical leadership and engineering team will join Rocket Software to help accelerate its AI initiatives, including new capabilities for Rocket EVA, the company’s agentic AI platform for core systems. The companies aim to move mainframe management away from processes that depend heavily on specialized expertise toward AI-assisted operations that make complex systems easier to understand, manage and modernize. Rocket Software said the acquisition would help enterprises address the shortage of skilled mainframe professionals, reduce operational complexity and automate mission-critical workflows. The combined technology is intended to help teams turn institutional knowledge into actionable intelligence, surface insights and take action across core systems while maintaining appropriate security, governance and control.   “Geniez AI was founded on the belief that GenAI-based business applications can fundamentally change how enterprises understand and operate their mainframe environments,” Peleg said. Joining Rocket, he added, would give the company the scale, customer reach and mainframe expertise needed to bring its technology to more organizations and help shape the next era of intelligent, mission-critical operations. Milan Shetti, president and CEO of Rocket Software, said the acquisition would accelerate the company’s efforts to help enterprises securely apply agentic AI to their systems. He described the deal as part of Rocket’s broader strategy to modernize core systems while extending AI capabilities to the critical workloads that run on them. Rocket Software is a privately held U.S. company headquartered in the Boston area that specializes in enterprise software modernization, including mainframe systems. The company says it serves more than 13,500 customers, works with 850 partners and employs over 3,000 people worldwide. It is a portfolio company of Bain Capital Private Equity.

title: Duane Davis Sentenced To Life Over Tupac Shakur’s Murder
body: A former Los Angeles gang member accused of ordering the 1996 murder of rap legend Tupac Shakur has been sentenced to life in prison, with a minimum term of 40 years, nearly 30 years after the killing in Las Vegas. Duane “Keefe D” Davis, a former member of the South Side Compton Crips gang, was found guilty in late August following a trial that included incriminating revelations he made about the night of the murder in his memoir. Announcing the sentence, Judge Carli Kierny said Davis had no right to take a person away from his family, deprive him of his life and future, and then profit from it. “Especially when that person is named Tupac Shakur,” Kierny said as she imposed the life sentence, with a minimum term of 40 years. The post Duane Davis Sentenced To Life Over Tupac Shakur’s Murder appeared first on Greek City Times .

title: Lockheed Martin and Avio partner on U.S. rocket motor production for ER GMLRS and PrSM
body: The agreement gives Lockheed Martin access to a share of Avio’s merchant supply capacity for both programs. Lockheed Martin said the additional source would strengthen its supply chain and create opportunities to increase missile output. “A reliable and diverse supply chain for solid rocket motors is fundamental to our strategy for a stronger defense industrial base,” said Tim Cahill, president of Lockheed Martin Missiles and Fire Control. “This strategic cooperation agreement with Avio enables us to speed up production of essential capabilities, ensuring our customers maintain their competitive edge against emerging threats.” Avio has committed more than $500 million to new U.S. solid rocket motor production capacity. The company intends to supply multiple defense customers, drawing on parent company Avio S.p.A.’s experience in solid propulsion. “This agreement is a major milestone for Avio USA and for the facility and team we are building in Virginia,” said James Syring, Avio USA’s chief executive. “The Lockheed Martin programs contribute to a strong foundation for the factory operations.” “It gives us tremendous momentum as we continue construction, grow our U.S. workforce and prepare to begin manufacturing,” Syring said. Work on the Virginia facility and recruitment of its U.S. workforce are continuing. “Avio has launched an investment of over $500M in new production capacity for SRMs in the United States with a view to become a merchant supplier to the various defense customers,” said Giulio Ranzo, Avio’s chief executive. “In this context, Avio is excited to be able to support Lockheed Martin in their effort to increase production volumes and resiliency and will put all its expertise at work to accelerate towards this goal.” The companies did not disclose financial terms or the number of motors to be produced. They also gave no timetable for qualification or the start of manufacturing.

title: Barefoot calm in the Baa Atoll: A family review of The Westin Maldives Miriandhoo
body: The Westin Maldives Miriandhoo Resort sits on a coral island in the heart of the Baa Atoll. Surrounded by a vibrant house reef and the protected waters of a Unesco Biosphere Reserve, this pocket-sized hideaway recently received its first Green Globe certification, a mark of its focus on sustainability and biodiversity protection. Positioning itself as a family-friendly escape with a focus on well-being, the resort uniquely incorporates subtle Japanese design influences, via minimalist architecture, water features and anchored by a distinctive Japanese-style tree at its centre. I visited with my husband and our toddler daughter and found that, while it's not the most ultra-polished property in the Maldives , nor does it try to be, it offers a quietly confident island stay and slower pace that suits its scale. The welcome Arrival is direct to the hotel via seaplane or by a domestic flight to the nearby Dharavandhoo Airport, followed by a 20-minute speedboat transfer. We opted for the former, and the welcome begins before we step on to the island, with resort staff lining up to smile and wave as our seaplane taxis to the jetty. A short buggy ride delivers us to an open-air lobby, where a chilled welcome drink awaits and check-in is handled unhurriedly as we drink in the ocean views. The room We stayed in a Beach Villa, a category that works particularly well when travelling with a young child. Our room opens on to a terrace with steps down to the sand and a narrow path through dense greenery leading straight to the beach, ideal for early-morning walks and sunset strolls. Inside, the design is relaxed rather than glossy, with dark wood finishes and soft neutral tones. It feels natural and lived-in rather than overtly staged, and I wasn’t worried about letting my daughter run around and make herself at home. The spacious bathroom comes with a delightful open-air shower, there is something unmistakably indulgent about rinsing off under warm water with palm leaves blowing overhead. A Westin Heavenly Bed lives up to its sleep-inducing reputation. A small highlight is the Kids Sleep Manual, designed in collaboration with paediatric sleep specialists and packed with dream-promoting activities like beachside bedtime stories and stargazing walks, alongside a sleep-focused children’s room service menu. All 70 accommodation units have private pools, but note that, at least in our room category, these are not temperature controlled and the water is noticeably cold – so much so that I never managed a proper swim, only braving a quick leg dip. More premium options exist, including the two-bedroom Heavenly Beach Residence or Heavenly Overwater Villa with Pool. The food Dining centres around four venues, so the choice isn’t vast, but each has a clear identity. The standout is The Pearl, a Japanese restaurant set over the water, with sweeping ocean views and a live kitchen. The sushi and sashimi are exceptional, order the sushi boat for a beautifully prepared platter that ranks among the best I’ve had in the Maldives. Service runs firmly on island time, but the setting, particularly at sunset, is divine. Island Kitchen pairs all-day dining with healthy international dishes, overlooking the pool and sea beyond. This is where the resort’s Eat Well concept comes into play, with nutritious options alongside a dedicated children’s menu. For casual evenings, Hawker brings a lively open-air feel, and the seafood barbecue was one of our highlights, with chefs grilling freshly caught tuna and squid under the stars, accompanied by live music. Sunset Bar is the best vantage point for golden hour, with squishy beanbags perfectly positioned for sundowners. The breakfast scene Breakfast at Island Kitchen is a highlight. The buffet is kept behind glass, a simple but effective solution to the fly issue common at island resorts, and the spread is generous but not excessive. There are well-being shots and local options like mas huni, a fresh tuna and coconut dish, alongside a strong Asian selection, plus a separate station for made-to-order fruit platters. Hotel facilities For a small island, the range of facilities is impressive. Alongside the main swimming pool, there are tennis courts, running tracks and a fitness studio with TRX and functional training equipment, plus a comprehensive programme of free daily fitness classes. The watersports centre offers everything from scuba instruction to snorkelling trips and dolphin-spotting cruises. We partook of the latter and enjoyed views of shoals of spinner dolphins cruising alongside the boat. Trips also tap into the wider Baa Atoll Biosphere, including to nearby Hanifaru Bay, famous for hosting the world’s largest gathering of manta rays. Spa and wellness The Heavenly Spa is one of the resort’s most tranquil spaces. Housed in overwater villa-style treatment rooms, the beds are positioned so guests can gaze directly into the ocean below while enjoying a massage. Watching colourful marine life drift past as a therapist worked her magic was particularly soothing. Family-friendly factor The resort is family-friendly without being overtly family-centric. The Kids Club features an impressive outdoor area with a swimming pool and a large wooden pirate-ship playground, alongside an indoor play space where staff run workshops and craft sessions. It caters only to children aged four and above, and while younger children may be permitted entry if accompanied by a parent, this is subject to daily capacity and staffing, meaning the space may not always be accessible to families travelling with babies and toddlers. Some staff go the extra mile, from a Sunset Bar bartender creating a custom mocktail for my daughter to the excursion team staging an impromptu Baby Shark- themed disco on a boat trip to local island Eydhafushi. Late restaurant hours – with most venues opening for dinner at 7pm – mean evenings may require forward planning for families with young children, including arranging babysitters in advance. That said, for those with children beyond toddler stage seeking calm surroundings rather than constant entertainment, the balance works. However, while the child-focused sleep manual is a good idea, it perhaps needs some tweaking. When we tried to use it to settle a jet-lagged toddler, we were told, after several back-and-forth phone calls, that most of the Kids Sleep Well menu items were unavailable later in the evening. Accessibility and sustainability Sustainability is embedded in the resort’s day-to-day operations, with a focus on energy, water and marine conservation. Solar power plays a central role in operations, alongside an on-site desalination and bottled water plant and the resort team leads coral restoration, sea turtle monitoring and reef-safe tourism initiatives. There are no designated accessible rooms, and as with many coral islands, pathways, overwater villas and boat transfers may present challenges for guests with limited mobility. Value for money Rates start from $750 per night. Check-in is from 3pm and checkout is at noon; westinmaldives.com. This review was conducted at the invitation of the hotel and reflects standards during this time

title: Ukrainian govt expands SvitloDIM energy program to 4 more regions
body:
The Ukrainian government has expanded the state assistance program for installing autonomous power sources in apartment buildings, which was previously available in Kyiv, Kyiv region and Kharkiv region, to Dnipropetrovsk, Zaporizhia, Poltava and Sumy regions, Ukrainian Prime Minister Serhiy Koretsky said.
"Applications on behalf of co-owners may be submitted by homeowner associations, managers of apartment buildings, as well as housing construction and maintenance cooperatives. The program provides for the installation of equipment that will ensure the operation of lighting, water supply, heating, communications and elevators during power outages," Koretsky wrote on Telegram.
In addition to expanding the program's geographical coverage, the Cabinet of Ministers has also improved the mechanism for implementing the program itself, the prime minister said.
As reported, the government program SvitloDIM, a support initiative for apartment buildings that helps install autonomous power sources, was launched on January 28, 2026. It provides financial assistance of UAH 100,000 to UAH 300,000 to co-owners for purchasing autonomous power sources. This makes it possible to ensure the availability of electricity, water, heating and communications, as well as elevator operation, during power outages. Initially, the program covered the city of Kyiv and Kyiv region, and in early April the government extended it to Kharkiv region.
In June, the Cabinet of Ministers extended the SvitloDIM program through the end of the year.
The press service of the Ministry for Restoration, Infrastructure and Transport reported that, as of July 22, funding had been provided to 2,442 apartment buildings for a total of more than UAH 610 million, while 4,205 applications had been received by that date. By applicant type, 68% of the applications had been submitted by homeowner associations, 22% by apartment building managers and 10% by maintenance cooperatives. More than UAH 560 million had already been transferred by that time for the purchase of equipment. The funds are being used to purchase equipment that will ensure the stable operation of essential infrastructure in apartment buildings.

title: Lockheed Martin and Avio Announce Strategic Cooperation Agreement for Solid Rocket Motor Production
body:
WASHINGTON, Oct. 13, 2026. Lockheed Martin and Avio announced a strategic cooperation agreement for the production of solid rocket motors (SRMs). This collaboration will accelerate and expand the SRM industrial base with key manufacturing capabilities, bringing resiliency of supply to a vital US supply chain.



THE BIG PICTURE

After qualification, initial work will focus on the production of solid rocket motors for the Extended Range GMLRS® (ER GMLRS) and the Precision Strike Missile (PrSM). SRM production for these essential programs will be performed at Avio USA’s new state-of-the-art facility in Hurt, Virgina, drawing on the longstanding solid propulsion expertise of its parent company, Avio S.p.A. (EXM: AVIO).

WHY IT MATTERS

SRM supply chain resiliency: This agreement provides Lockheed Martin access to a share of Avio’s merchant supply capacity for ER GMLRS and PrSM production, ensuring flexibility and creating surety of supply in the crucial SRM supply chain to meet accelerating customer demand and guarantee uninterrupted mission readiness across global operations.

Increased production capacity: By augmenting the defense industrial base, this effort demonstrates Lockheed Martin’s agile response to heightened production requirements, supporting the expansion of dedicated lines and resources to fulfill emerging operational needs for SRM production.

Accelerated ER GMLRS and PrSM manufacturing capabilities: By leveraging expanded SRM production capacity, Lockheed Martin is creating the opportunity to accelerate ER GMLRS and PrSM output to deliver increased munition volumes faster to support warfighters and combatant commands.

EXPERT PERSPECTIVE

“A reliable and diverse supply chain for solid rocket motors is fundamental to our strategy for a stronger defense industrial base. This strategic cooperation agreement with Avio enables us to speed up production of essential capabilities, ensuring our customers maintain their competitive edge against emerging threats,” said Tim Cahill, President of Lockheed Martin Missiles and Fire Control.

“This agreement is a major milestone for Avio USA and for the facility and team we are building in Virginia,” said James Syring, CEO of Avio USA. “The Lockheed Martin programs contribute to a strong foundation for the factory operations. It gives us tremendous momentum as we continue construction, grow our US workforce and prepare to begin manufacturing.”

“Avio has launched an investment of over $500M in new production capacity for SRMs in the United States with a view to become a merchant supplier to the various defense customers. In this context, Avio is excited to be able to support Lockheed Martin in their effort to increase production volumes and resiliency and will put all its expertise at work to accelerate towards this goal,” said Giulio Ranzo, Chief Executive Officer of Avio.

ADDITIONAL DETAILS

This strategic cooperation agreement between Lockheed Martin and Avio USA will strengthen the US SRM industrial base, bolstering the defense supply chain and enabling our troops to have access to reliable, high-performance munitions to defend our nation and its allies.

title: State Housing Company engages Aynok Holdings for land recovery, sets October 15 deadline
body: The State Housing Company Limited (SHC) has engaged Aynok Holdings Limited to support its land recovery exercise, with the Greater Accra Region set to serve as the pilot area before the exercise is extended nationwide. The initiative marks the first time SHC has involved a third party in its land recovery process. Speaking at a joint press conference, SHC Deputy Managing Director Sam Atukwei Quaye said the company issued a final notice on September 24, giving affected occupants 21 days to regularise their leases or vacate the properties. The deadline expires on October 15. The exercise will target properties affected by encroachment, unauthorised occupation and expired leases, as well as cases involving the unauthorised sale, subletting or transfer of SHC properties. Mr Quaye said the company had previously offered affected clients opportunities to regularise their arrangements, including a 15 per cent discount in 2025 for those with outstanding payments. Under the arrangement, Aynok Holdings will provide field and logistical support, while SHC retains responsibility for decisions relating to its properties. “AYNOK HOLDINGS LIMITED works under the authority and direction of SHC. Responsibility for every decision rests with this company, and every action will be carried out within the law and with respect for the rights and dignity of all persons,” SHC said. The Chief Executive Officer of Aynok Holdings also stressed that the company had no authority to own, allocate or sell SHC land. “AYNOK HOLDINGS LIMITED does not own, allocate or sell SHC land, and it has no authority to do so,” he said. Addressing how the exercise would be conducted, the CEO said “minimal force” could be used against occupants who became hostile or resisted the process. SHC says former leaseholders whose leases have expired may present their documents for verification and seek to regularise their arrangements, subject to the company’s terms and any outstanding payments. Those occupying properties without authorisation may be required to vacate, while persons who present fraudulent documents could face arrest. The company has urged the public to verify property details directly with SHC or the Lands Commission and cautioned against relying on intermediaries who cannot provide written authorisation. It has also warned the public against making payments outside its official channels. SHC says the exercise is intended to protect state assets and recover properties occupied without valid authorisation.

title: Ex-President Yushchenko calls on Trump to abandon trade with Russia, concessions to Putin
body:
Third President of Ukraine Viktor Yushchenko addressed an open letter to President of the U.S Donald Trump, criticizing the authorization of trade in Russian diesel fuel and calling for the fulfillment of security commitments under the Budapest Memorandum, the politician published the appeal on Facebook on Wednesday.
"It looks wild and painful when calls are heard for Ukraine to 'stop,' instructions on whom we should elect and how to live, or when a green light is given to trade in Russian diesel. Every dollar from this diesel is a purchased missile that will strike our homes tomorrow," Yushchenko stressed in his appeal.
According to the former president, trading with an aggressor country during wartime directly finances its war machine, while talks by the U.S about the possibility of concessions or agreements with Vladimir Putin immediately provoke the Kremlin into new strikes with ballistic missiles and guided aerial bombs against residential neighborhoods in Kyiv, Zaporizhia, Odesa, Dnipro, and Kharkiv region.
Yushchenko reminded the head of the White House that following the collapse of the USSR, Ukraine voluntarily surrendered the world's third-largest nuclear arsenal in exchange for official guarantees of security, sovereignty, and the inviolability of borders, sealed by the U.S signature on the Budapest Memorandum in 1994.
In addition, the former Ukrainian head of state drew a historical parallel with Washington's policy in the 1930s, when the U.S supplied oil to Imperial Japan for the sake of preserving stability, which ultimately led to the Japanese air attack on Pearl Harbor using American fuel. At the same time, the politician pointed to the joint struggle of Ukrainians and Americans in World War II, mentioning Ukrainian-born Sergeant Michael Strank, who raised the US flag over Iwo Jima, and Ukrainian Alexander Silvashko during the historic meeting of allies on the Elbe on April 25, 1945.
Concluding the appeal, Yushchenko emphasized that the Ukrainian people will never yield their territory and will not succumb to Russian missile blackmail, summarizing that "one does not negotiate with tyrants – one stops them."

title: Ukrainian ex-officer stands trial in Germany over Nord Stream bombing
body: A Ukrainian former military officer is to go on trial ​in Germany on Wednesday, accused of organising the secret operation that blew ⁠up the Nord Stream pipelines in September 2022, severing western Europe from the biggest source ⁠of Russian natural gas. The suspect, identified under German privacy rules only as Serhii ​K ., is accused of leading a group of Ukrainian agents, including divers and an explosives expert, to mount one of the biggest infrastructure sabotage operations of ⁠modern times. The case will provide the first opportunity for a public hearing of evidence gathered during a years-long investigation, which has been diplomatically and politically awkward for a German government that remains staunchly supportive of Ukraine despite the investigative trail linking Kyiv to the crime. Prosecutors have alleged that Serhii K., who was arrested under an international warrant ⁠in Italy last year, worked with other members of the military to plan the clandestine operation on behalf of unidentified Ukrainian state entities. Serhii K. ​has denied ⁠any involvement in the blasts that ruptured the 1,200km-long ‌Baltic Sea pipeline. The government in Kyiv has also denied any involvement, a sensitive point in its relations with Germany, Ukraine's largest European supplier of military ​aid. The Russian government said it expected a “just verdict” that would reveal the names of the perpetrators and those who ordered the operation. German prosecutors say the actions of which Serhii K. is accused – attacking civilian targets and causing explosions that destroyed infrastructure and damaged public services – would amount to a war crime. The alleged aim was to disrupt a major source of foreign revenue for Russia after its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, launched earlier that year. He is the only person on trial but Croatian authorities have arrested another man, identified as Vladimir Z., who prosecutors believe was one of the divers in the team. The explosion of Nord Stream sealed the end of Germany's long-standing dependence on Russian natural gas, although Moscow had already cut supplies over Berlin's support for European sanctions following Russia's invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Germany previously received half its natural gas imports through the Nord Stream 1 pipeline, by far the biggest and most modern Russian conduit serving western Europe, which allowed Russia to bypass Soviet-era pipelines crossing Ukraine. The supply had been due to double with the opening of a twin pipeline, Nord Stream 2, which was already built, although Berlin cancelled approval to start operations shortly before Russia's invasion. Methane gas The trial, expected ​to continue into February, could also have domestic political implications. Germany's far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), leading in ‌opinion polls for more than a year, has called for ⁠an end to military aid for Ukraine and a restoration of energy ​ties with Moscow. In the initial months after the pipelines were attacked, western officials mainly pointed fingers at Russia. Moscow has always denied ​any involvement and called ‌the suggestion it would blow up its own pipelines absurd. It also rejects charges that it has more recently targeted western infrastructure with so-called “hybrid” sabotage and drone attacks. The ⁠Nord Stream system, lying at a depth of 80 to 110 metres under the Baltic and built by Russian energy corporation Gazprom ⁠to supply up to 110 billion cubic metres of gas to Germany, was formerly at the core of economic ties between the two countries. On September 26, 2022, several blasts were detected by Swedish seismologists over 17 hours. The explosions sent huge plumes of methane gas into the atmosphere, as three of the four concrete-coated steel pipelines were ruptured. Prosecutors allege Serhii K. travelled to Germany through Poland about three weeks before the attack, using ​a forged Ukrainian passport. They say he and his group used a sailboat hired in the northern German city of Rostock to reach an area close to the Danish island of Bornholm, where they rigged specialised military-grade explosives fitted with timers to the sea floor. The weekly Der Spiegel magazine and ZDF public television have previously reported that five men and one woman were on the rented yacht Andromeda, which left Rostock on September 6 and returned on September 23, 2022.

title: After prosecution’s bombshells, what does Sara’s defense have?
body: There have been statements by Senate President Win Gatchalian that Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial may be done before the year ends. But with the prosecution’s decision to drop three of four impeachment articles against her, we might see the trial ending sooner than expected. Lead public prosecutor Gerville Luistro said on Tuesday, October 13, that their evidence on unexplained wealth — the second article against Duterte — is enough to remove her from office and bar her from running in 2028. Withdrawing an article during an impeachment trial is not really new as this happened in former chief justice Renato Corona’s trial. The House dropped five of eight articles. Eventually, Corona was ousted from his position — the first chief magistrate in the Philippines to have been convicted in an impeachment trial. But there’s a difference between the two trials. The prosecution, in Corona’s case, withdrew the five articles before they could present their evidence for these articles. In Duterte’s case, the prosecution had four. It presented evidence on alleged grave threats, misuse of confidential funds, and unexplained wealth. It never tackled the bribery allegation. And then Luistro announced that they would drop everything except the case on unexplained wealth. “This has never happened before,” said defense spokesperson and counsel Michael Poa. So, what will the defense’s next actions be after this rather surprising move from the prosecution? Defense concerns To clarify, the defense did not object to the prosecution’s motion to withdraw the three articles. Poa and lead defense counsel Sheila Sison made it clear that this was the House’s prerogative — each party should have the final say on how it intends to present its own evidence. In his ruling, impeachment court presiding officer Chiz Escudero accepted the withdrawal with prejudice on the grave threats and confidential funds cases (meaning they can no longer be refiled by the prosecution), without prejudice to the bribery charge (since no evidence was ever presented in court). One of the concerns of the defense, however, is whether they will be allowed to still present evidence on the two withdrawn articles. “We had no problem with bribery because they never presented that. Our problem was the grave threats and confidential funds case because they already presented the testimonies of their witnesses there,” Poa said in Filipino. “And we are not given now the opportunity to present rebuttal evidence through the testimonies of our witnesses…. Can we still present our evidence on those allegations or not? That’s one of the questions,” he added. The defense will begin presenting its own evidence in November, but as Poa pointed out, it’s still unclear whether they will be able to present evidence on grave threats and confidential funds. “There is no mechanism within the rules to allow the presentation of evidence on an article or on a charge that will not be voted upon by the court,” said Escudero. Another sign that Duterte’s camp might not be given the opportunity is the relaxation of the sub judice rule. This principle bars parties — including the respondent — from publicly discussing the merits of the case to preserve the integrity of the proceedings. This gives Duterte’s camp the chance to present their evidence directly to the public, similar to what former senator Antonio Trillanes did after he was dropped as a prosecution witness. No holds barred. Play Video But the defense finds this problematic too. “Now, I know that the court will say that, well, the respondent’s given the equal opportunity to do as she pleases with respect to the allegation. She can say a lot of things. Use all the platforms, in the words of the lead prosecutor, to avail of these platforms to present their evidence through these platforms,” said Sison. But it would be unfair for the Vice President to be unable to present evidence in the impeachment court itself, the proper forum, according to Sison, because “the Vice President was held to this formal proceeding and in this court and honorable members of this court took their oaths, senators, judges.” Remedies, bombshells? The parties — both the prosecution and the defense — cannot file a motion for reconsideration on the rulings made by the presiding officer. Only a senator-judge can. Senator-judge Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan said he is open to reconsidering the ruling on the abandonment of the sub judice rule. So, for now, Poa said they will first consult the Vice President and inform her about the court’s decision then inform the court about her position on the ruling. Is the defense considering filing a petition for certiorari with the Supreme Court? This is a legal remedy used to seek review of grave abuse of discretion on the part of the impeachment court. If granted, this can overturn a ruling. “As for certiorari, we are not considering a certiorari at this point. We are not talking about that,” said Poa. In her manifestation before the court, Sison said the prosecution’s allegations must be tested. “That prerogative to withdraw an accusation is not the power to suppress its rebuttal on the part of the respondent. The authority to streamline or to achieve speed in a trial is not the authority to diminish due process or to altogether disregard fundamental rules of fairness and the desire to reach a verdict,” said the lead defense counsel. If there is no appeal and certiorari on the table, what could the bombshells of Duterte’s defense team be? Play Video “As implied by Attorney Sison a while ago, it might move for the dismissal of all articles of impeachment, citing mistrial. Or, as we discussed…. it might move for, or file a motion or demurrer to evidence on article 2, saying that as since the evidence relied upon by the prosecution is anchored solely on the false assumptions of Attorney Alex Cabrera, and the defense might mark it as false assumption, then they will also be moving for that,” lawyer and law professor Maria Lulu Reyes told Rappler. Cabrera is the financial forensic analyst and prosecution witness who testified that Duterte’s unexplained wealth may reach P1.5 billion. A demurrer to evidence, mentioned by Reyes, meanwhile, is filed when the defense believes that the prosecution’s evidence is weak enough that they don’t have to present their own. If granted, it will lead to an acquittal. “So, either way, it’s to dismiss all the articles, not just the three that were mentioned today, but including article 2, the only remaining one,” Reyes added. If her crystal ball is correct, the Jose Mari Chan Christmas meme, “ Ilang tulog na lang …(Just a few more days left)” may be relevant to the impeachment trial. Ready na ba kayo? (Are you all ready?) – Rappler.com

title: IMF Forecasts Greek Public Debt to Fall to 111.1% of GDP
body: Greece’s public debt will fall to 136% of gross domestic product (GDP) in 2026 from 146.6% in 2025, before declining further to 128.7% in 2027 and 111.1% in 2031, according to forecasts released by the International Monetary Fund (IMF). The projections appear in the IMF’s World Economic Outlook Database, published in connection with its annual meetings in Bangkok. The Fund expects Greece’s debt reduction to be slightly faster this year and in 2027 than it forecast in April, when it projected ratios of 136.9% and 130.3%, respectively. Greece’s debt ratio will fall below Italy’s 137.9% of GDP this year, according to the IMF. By 2031, Greece is also expected to have a lower debt ratio than France, whose debt is projected to rise gradually to 123.6%, and Belgium, at 122.1%. Greece’s projected debt ratio in 2031 will also fall below the 115.2% average forecast for advanced economies. The IMF expects US public debt to climb sharply to 145% of GDP, while Japan’s debt will gradually decline but remain the highest among advanced economies, at 188.9%. Primary surpluses to support debt reduction Primary budget surpluses will underpin Greece’s rapid debt reduction, although the surpluses are expected to gradually narrow while remaining above 2% of GDP. The IMF projects Greece’s primary surplus at 3.4% of GDP in 2026, down from 4.9% in 2025. It expects the surplus to reach 2.6% in 2027 and 2.4% in 2031. The overall fiscal balance, which includes interest payments on public debt, is forecast to record a surplus of 0.3% of GDP in 2026, compared with a surplus of 1.7% in 2025. The IMF projects deficits of 0.6% in 2027 and approximately 1% in 2031. Government revenue is expected to remain around 50% of GDP in 2026, broadly unchanged from 2025, before falling to 48.6% in 2027 and 48% in 2031. Government expenditure is projected to rise to 49.7% of GDP in 2026 from 48.3% in 2025, before declining to 49.3% in 2027 and approximately 49% in 2031. IMF urges advanced economies to tackle mounting debt In its Fiscal Monitor blog, the IMF warned that high public debt in major advanced economies, particularly the United States, is a key factor driving bond yields higher. It urged these countries to take urgent action to put their debt on a sustainable path and limit the impact on the rest of the world. The Fund noted that long-term government bond yields have risen sharply across several major advanced economies. Between February and September, the average yield on 10-year government bonds across the Group of Seven (G7) rose by more than one percentage point, reaching its highest level in almost two decades. Several factors are pushing yields higher, including a sharp increase in oil prices, persistent inflation, stronger demand for investment and higher growth expectations associated with artificial intelligence, the IMF said. However, the Fund stressed that underlying fiscal conditions remain decisive. High debt levels, spending pressures and expectations of substantial bond issuance in the coming years are increasing the returns investors demand to hold long-term government debt. US interest payments projected to double In the United States, interest payments on public debt are projected to rise from approximately 2.8% of GDP before the pandemic to 5.7% in 2031, an amount equivalent to the country’s projected spending on Social Security. The IMF warned that higher bond yields leave governments with less room to delay fiscal adjustments. “Large advanced economies with high debt need concrete measures based on credible medium-term plans and realistic assumptions,” the Fund said. Such measures are necessary to put debt on a sustainable path, contain borrowing costs and limit spillover effects on other countries. Delaying fiscal adjustments would increase interest costs and fiscal vulnerabilities, further restrict governments’ policy options and ultimately require a larger adjustment to stabilise debt, the IMF warned. “The longer countries wait, the more painful the adjustment becomes,” the Fund said. The post IMF Forecasts Greek Public Debt to Fall to 111.1% of GDP appeared first on Greek City Times .

title: Ukraine lacked intelligence only on first wave of overnight missile launch — air force
body:
MOSCOW, October 14. /TASS/. Ukraine received no intelligence warnings only about the first wave of Russian ballistic missile launches overnight into October 14, but warnings about subsequent attacks did come in, Ukrainian Air Force Spokesman Yury Ignat said.
"We first said at about 10:40 p.m. (on October 13, 7:40 p.m. GMT - TASS) that there had been no warnings from our partners about ballistic missile launches. However, our partners warned us about the next three waves," RBC Ukraine quoted him as saying.
Politico reported on October 13 that US President Donald Trump could cut off US intelligence support for Kiev or pressure Elon Musk to disable SpaceX’s Starlink internet service, on which Ukraine’s military heavily relies.

title: Most UN missions operate where peace is elusive – Guterres
body:
With just over two months to go before his tenure as United Nations (UN) Secretary-General ends, Antonio Guterres told a Security Council (SC) peacekeeping debate that creating the “political space” to properly utilise the blue helmets is where the review of peace operations has to start.
“Peacekeeping,” he told the SC “is a political instrument. It is deployed to support political solutions – never as a substitute for them”.
“For three decades, we sent peacekeepers mainly to help the parties to a civil war implement a comprehensive peace agreement. Today, such agreements are rarer than at any time in decades – harder to reach, and more fragile.
“Most of our missions now operate where peace remains elusive. They are asked to contain the damage of wars that the parties feel little pressure to end – and that outside actors sometimes feed.
“The ground has shifted. Too often, our mandates have not. Peacekeepers are attacked. Civilians are targeted. International law is violated with a mounting sense of impunity.
“Drones, lethal autonomous weapons, disinformation amplified by artificial intelligence… the nature of conflict is changing fast,” he noted, adding peacekeeping budgets have been slashed and the number of troops and police “greatly reduced”.
Guterres is adamant peacekeeping operations should be deployed only when a peace agreement, or at least a robust ceasefire, is in place. “Peacekeepers can do a lot to preserve the peace. But we cannot keep peace where there is no peace to keep,” he said, pointing out the way back to peacekeeping is through peacemaking.
Peacemaking is provided for in the UN Charter, specifically chapter six. He urged the world body to investigate disputes before they become wars, visit the countries concerned and build a shared understanding of the facts – the foundation of shared action.
Five of 11 current UN peacekeeping missions – MINURSO (Western Sahara), MINUSCA (Central African Republic – CAR), MONUSCO (Democratic Republic of Congo – DRC), UNISFA (Abyei), and UNMISS (South Sudan) – are in Africa.
Guterres asked SC members to mandate missions “for the world as it is”. This, he said, means agreeing – before peacekeepers deploy – on a longer term vision on what they are meant to help achieve.
“Mandates must be focused on what peacekeeping missions do best – particularly politics and security and, where mandated, protection of civilians.
“Protection must be built into mission mandates from the outset – how they are planned, mandated and resourced – so that when civilians are threatened, peacekeepers can act decisively. And an exit strategy [must be] planned from the start of any mission,” the UN supremo said.
He was outspoken on funding, saying peacekeeping efficiency means “making every dollar count” and pointing to investing as part of readiness. This has to be in the people and tools of peacekeeping and includes more mobile missions, countering drones and the “capabilities of tomorrow” for the military and police. Proof this isn’t always happening are places where peacekeepers are denied technology any modern force would consider basic, according to Guterres.

title: IN BRIEF: Russia hits Ukraine's communication, energy infrastructure in massive strike
body:
MOSCOW, October 14. /TASS/. Overnight, Russian forces launched a massive strike hitting communication and energy infrastructure facilities in Kiev and the Kiev and Kharkov Regions that support Ukraine's military-industrial complex, the Russian Defense Ministry reported.
TASS has compiled the key details on the targets hit.
- Overnight, the Russian Armed Forces launched a massive strike using ground-based precision weapons and long-range attack drones against targets in Ukraine, the Defense Ministry reported.
- According to the ministry, the strike hit communication and energy infrastructure facilities in Kiev and the Kiev and Kharkov Regions used to support the military-industrial complex and the armed forces of Ukraine.
- The ministry later specified that the ATM Ukrsibbank data center in Kiev was hit. The facility handled Internet traffic exchange for gathering intelligence about the Russian Armed Forces.
- Russian forces also struck the Darnitskaya combined heat and power plant (CHP-4), powering military-industrial complex facilities in Kiev.
- In addition, the Kievskaya combined heat and power plant (CHP-5) was hit; it supplies electricity to military facilities and military-industrial enterprises in Kiev and the Kiev Region.
- The Russian Armed Forces also struck the Kiev CHP-6 plant, powering military logistics facilities and storage sites for weaponry and military hardware in the northeastern part of the Kiev Region.
- In addition, the Tripolskaya thermal power plant, powering military-industrial facilities in Kiev and it's environs, was struck.
- Russian forces also struck the Kievskaya electrical substation, providing for the transmission and distribution of electricity from western Ukrainian regions to Ukraine’s military facilities in the Kiev Region.
- Furthermore, the Kharkov CHP-5 combined heat and power plant, powering military-industrial facilities in Kharkov and the western part of the Kharkov Region, was struck.
- The Russian Armed Forces also struck the Zmiyevskaya thermal power plant, supplying electricity to Ukrainian military facilities in the southeastern part of the Kharkov Region.
- Energy facilities in Kiev sustained damage following explosions, city mayor Vitali Klitschko reported.
- Strikes were recorded on "several energy facilities in the capital" of Ukraine, he wrote on his Telegram channel.
- Public electric transport services were suspended in two districts of Kiev, the municipal enterprise Kievpastrans reported.
- Power outages began in Kiev due to widespread damage to energy facilities, Klitschko later announced.
- Specifically, he described the strikes on the city's energy infrastructure as massive.
- Emergency power outages began in five of Kiev's ten districts following the explosions and damage to energy facilities, the Ukrainian energy holding company DTEK reported.
- It specified that the Darnitsky, Dneprovsky, Pechersky, and Solomensky districts, as well as part of the Goloseyevsky district, were affected.
- All of Kiev's combined heat and power (CHP) plants, as well as the Kiev Region’s largest energy facility--the Tripolskaya Thermal Power Plant--sustained damage from explosions, the Strana news outlet reported.
- According to the report, strikes on all of the Ukrainian capital's CHP plants were recorded overnight and on Wednesday morning.
- In the region, the Tripolskaya Thermal Power Plant was damaged, along with the Kievskaya and Novokievskaya substations, which have capacities of 750 kilovolts (kV) and 330 kV, respectively.
- The outlet accompanied its report with photos showing massive fires at the sites of the explosions.
- The Epicentr company's last remaining logistics center was destroyed by the explosions, the Ukrainian outlet Insider reported.
- According to the report, the facility was located in the city of Khmelnitsky in western Ukraine.
- The report includes photos and video of the fire at the logistics facility.
- Water supply issues may arise in Kiev's Pechersky district due to a power outage at the city's water pumping station, the utility company Kievvodokanal reported.
- Ukrainian energy facilities sustained significant damage from the explosions, leaving at least 600,000 people without electricity, Vladimir Zelensky stated.

title: 12th Kyiv International Economic Forum to Take Place on October 26, Focusing on Business and Economic Resilience Amid New Challenges
body:
Kyiv will host the 12th Kyiv International Economic Forum (KIEF) on October 26, bringing together more than 500 participants , including owners and executives of Ukrainian and international companies, government officials, investors, diplomats, and experts. This year’s theme, “People. Business. Economy. What’s Next?” , will guide discussions on how businesses and Ukraine’s economy can withstand mounting challenges, adapt to changing conditions, and return to growth.
Now in the fifth year of Russia’s full-scale invasion, Ukraine’s economy faces growing pressure. Russian attacks continue to target industrial facilities, energy infrastructure, ports, railways, logistics hubs, and other assets critical to business operations. According to Ukraine’s Ministry of Economy, direct damage from destruction could reach approximately $10 billion annually. Combined with the blockade of seaports, these losses have already cost Ukraine an estimated 1.5 percentage points of GDP in 2026.
In its October forecast, the World Bank projects that Ukraine’s economic growth will slow to 1.2% in 2026 and reach just 1.5% in 2027 if active hostilities continue. The Bank previously projected 4% growth in 2027, assuming hostilities would end by late 2026.
“While discussions previously focused on Ukraine’s reconstruction, the priority today is how to strengthen economic resilience here and now. Businesses need solutions that will help them protect their assets, maintain production, and continue investing even during wartime”, says Vasyl Khmelnytskyi, KIEF initiator, founder of UFuture holding.
KIEF 2026 will feature 14 panel discussions addressing the most pressing challenges facing Ukraine’s economy. Key topics will include protecting business facilities, maintaining operations during air raid alerts, decentralizing logistics and energy supply, ensuring reliable communications, insuring against war-related risks, securing compensation for lost assets, accessing finance, and maintaining macroeconomic stability.
Discussions will also explore how Ukraine can adapt its industrial development strategy and energy policy to new realities, redefine national economic priorities, strengthen international cooperation, and advance European integration amid emerging challenges. Special attention will go to frontline cities and the practical solutions they have already implemented to keep their economies functioning.
Ukraine’s economy has already demonstrated its ability to adapt rapidly to major disruptions. In 2022, following the destruction of the Kremenchuk oil refinery and the resulting fuel shortages, the country rebuilt its fuel supply chains, while thousands of businesses relocated from frontline regions to safer areas further inland.
In 2023, Ukraine launched its own maritime corridor after traditional shipping routes were blocked. Following large-scale attacks on the power grid last year, businesses and the government also accelerated the development of distributed power generation.
“Today, any discussion about the future must start with practical decisions that businesses, the government, and international partners can make right now to sustain economic resilience and restore growth. This is precisely what KIEF 2026 is about”, says Yuriy Pyvovarov, CEO of KIEF.
Title Partners: UFuture, Mastercard, AEQUO, PrivatBank, Kyivstar
Forum Partners: Sense Bank, NEQSOL Holding, FUIB, DTEK, Ajax Systems, Uklon, TERWIN, Eclectic Talents Group, BALEX, CEO Club Ukraine
Interfax-Ukraine is the forum's media partner.

title: Britain to accelerate delivery of anti-drone missiles to Ukraine
body:
Ukrinform reports this, citing the British government's website .
The United Kingdom has already committed £1.6 billion to supply Ukraine with more than 5,000 LMM missiles over the next four years.
From a GBP 45 million missile package, London will fast-track GBP 10 million worth of weapons deliveries to meet Ukraine's most urgent needs ahead of winter.
"Our rock-solid support to Ukraine is vital for keeping us safe here in the UK and ensuring those on the frontlines have the equipment they need to push back Russia. My message to the Ukrainian people could not be clearer, we are with you for as long as it takes, and we will go further and faster in our support to back your courageous fight for peace in Europe," said British Prime Minister Andy Burnham.
He also instructed ministers to prepare additional sanctions, military aid packages, and financial support to provide Ukraine with urgent assistance over the coming weeks.
"It is not just the right thing to do, but it's the necessary thing to do. Russia's aggression cannot be allowed to succeed on our continent," Burnham added.
Meanwhile, Defence Secretary John Healey will urge partners to fully implement a similar ban on Russian liquefied natural gas (LNG) during meetings on the sidelines of the International Monetary Fund gatherings in Bangkok, following the United Kingdom's example. On Tuesday, the foreign secretary also called on partners to take this step during the Warsaw Security Forum.
As Ukrinform previously reported, retired General Ben Hodges, former commander of US Army Europe, said on the sidelines of the Warsaw Security Forum that Ukraine should not only continue but also intensify strikes against Russian oil and gas infrastructure , as these attacks have a significant impact on the enemy.

title: German drones will protect the sky over Ukraine. Will they intercept Russian jet-powered UAVs?
body:
The Russians anticipate that a clash involving thousands of Russian Geran kamikaze drones and German SPYS interceptor drones will take place over Kyiv in just two months.
Federal Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced during a visit to Kyiv on 4 October 2026 that Germany would fund the purchase of tens of thousands of SPYS interceptor drones for Ukraine as part of the German military aid package for the winter of 2026/2027. These are intended primarily to assist in the fight against the Russian jet-powered Geran-4 and Geran-5 drones.
The SPYS drone is being developed by Quantum Systems in collaboration with the Ukrainian company WIY Drones Ukraine. On the company’s website, it is still marked as „under development”. However, thanks to the German government’s funding of the project, work has accelerated rapidly, and several thousand SPYS interceptors, fully ready for operational use, are expected to appear in Ukraine later this year.
These are urgently needed because the Russians« mass use of jet-powered drones has overwhelmed Ukrainian air defences, which have begun to let through an increasing number of Russian UAVs. Consequently, urgent work has begun in Ukraine to find an effective antidote to this new threat.
The main problem was the speed of the jet-powered Gerans, which in the case of the „five” exceeds 600 km/h, and an altitude reaching up to 6,000 m. The SPYS interceptor was developed in response. Carrying a warhead weighing up to 300 grams, according to WIY Drones, it can operate at altitudes of up to 4,000 metres within a radius of up to 15 km, flying at speeds of up to 480 km/h. However, some sources report that the SPYS has a ceiling of 6,000 m and can reach speeds of 600 km/h. According to the manufacturer, „ such high flight dynamics allow for the distance to the target to be quickly closed and for it to be intercepted before it enters the protected zone ”.
It is a highly autonomous system. Based on previously provided data from reconnaissance and surveillance systems, it is possible to programme an autonomous take-off, with an approach to the interception zone and an automatic approach to the target controlled by artificial intelligence systems. SPYS can be equipped with both daylight and thermal imaging cameras. It is therefore a system adapted for conducting operations around the clock.
Russian media are now analysing whether such interceptor drones can indeed provide air cover for Kyiv. Of particular interest was the assessment presented by Mikhail Khodaryonok, a retired colonel and military analyst for the Gazeta.Ru portal. He confirmed that SPYS interceptors would fulfil their tasks.
However, he warned that Russia would not stand idly by as advanced Ukrainian interceptor drones are mass-produced. He announced the rapid development and implementation of countermeasures, even during ongoing combat operations. These solutions include:
This opinion is significant because Khodaryonok, as a former air defence specialist (a 1976 graduate of, among others, the Minsk Higher Engineering School of Anti-Aircraft Missile Forces), noted the advantage that SPYS drones already have over Russian long-range unmanned systems.
In the current situation, he therefore proposes that, even before the mass production of SPYS UAVs begins, the intensity of mass strikes be increased „using drones – such as modernised Geran models, which could inflict such severe damage on the Ukrainian defence industry, lines of communication, and national infrastructure that the authorities in Kyiv might be forced to fundamentally change their position on the war”.
Gazeta.ru protected itself against potential Kremlin sanctions, however, by placing a note under his analysis stating that „the author’s opinion does not necessarily reflect the position of the editorial board”.

title: Moscow records one of largest Ukrainian drone attack in two years — TASS calculations
body:
MOSCOW, October 14. /TASS/. The overnight drone attack on Moscow attempted by Ukraine was one of the largest in two years, according to TASS calculations based on data provided by Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin.
As many as 493 drones headed toward the region between 8:30 p.m. Moscow time on October 13 and 7:00 a.m. Moscow time on October 14 (5:30 p.m. - 4:00 a.m. GMT), Sobyanin said. "Air defenses downed most of them at distant approaches, while 180 unmanned aerial vehicles were destroyed near Moscow," the mayor wrote on the Max messaging app.
Sobyanin said earlier that 417 drones had been detected flying toward Moscow and the surrounding region overnight into October 12.
Meanwhile, the largest drone attack on Moscow so far was repelled on the night of September 19-20, when air defenses shot down 1,600 drones, with 450 destroyed near Moscow.

title: Bombardier Global 7500 gains EASA-certified anti-missile defense
body: BIRD Aerosystems has completed the installation and European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) certification of its Airborne Missile Protection System (AMPS) on a Bombardier Global 7500. The certification was announced on October 13, 2026, by Florida-based Ondas , which acquired the Israeli aircraft protection specialist in March 2026. The suite incorporates directional infrared countermeasures (DIRCM), a laser-based system that jams the seekers of heat-seeking missiles. According to Ondas, the approval confirms that the integration of the suite on the Global 7500 meets applicable European airworthiness requirements, allowing the protection system to form part of the aircraft’s certified configuration. The operator of the aircraft was not disclosed. How the Global 7500’s missile protection system works An AeroShield missile protection installation beneath an Airbus A319. (Credit: BIRD Aerosystems) AMPS is designed to counter man-portable air-defense systems (MANPADS) and other infrared-guided missiles. The company says it combines missile warning, threat confirmation, tracking and DIRCM, reducing false alarms to “virtually zero”. “Protecting high-value aircraft and government aviation assets against increasingly sophisticated missile threats is a critical and growing defense requirement,” said Eric Brock, chairman and CEO of Ondas. Similar threats have driven governments to equip dedicated VIP aircraft with DIRCM, including Germany’s Airbus A350 government transports . However, cost, weight and maintenance requirements have kept such systems largely off commercial airliners . When Ondas acquired BIRD in March 2026 , it said the Israeli company’s protection systems were already installed on more than 700 aircraft across over 40 types, with operators including the US Army, NATO forces and United Nations aviation fleets. BIRD is not the first to protect the Global 7500 The Global 7500 has attracted interest from missile-protection suppliers for several years. In June 2021, Leonardo announced a contract to equip a Global 7500 operated by an unnamed Middle Eastern government with its Miysis DIRCM system. Switzerland also ordered a Global 7500 with a missile self-protection system for its government fleet in August 2023. The aircraft was delivered in December 2024 , with the installation by Sabena technics of equipment designed to counter MANPADS scheduled for 2025. The supplier of the protection system was not publicly identified. In February 2023, BIRD announced its own contract to install AMPS and its SPREOS DIRCM system, housed in the AeroShield pod, on a Global 7500 and a Gulfstream G700 belonging to an undisclosed European customer. A contemporary report by Business Air News described the customer as a private charter operator, although BIRD did not publicly identify the company. The project included plans to obtain a supplemental type certificate (STC) for each aircraft. BIRD was targeting completion of both certifications before the end of 2026. However, Ondas’ announcement provides no update on the G700. The post Bombardier Global 7500 gains EASA-certified anti-missile defense appeared first on AeroTime .

title: Koretsky: occupiers target all three Kyiv thermal power plants overnight
body:
Prime Minister of Ukraine Serhiy Koretsky reported that Russian occupants launched strikes against all three of Kyiv's combined heat and power plants (CHPs) overnight Wednesday.

"The target of Russian ballistics was energy system facilities in Kyiv, Kharkiv, and the region. In the capital, all three municipal CHPs were attacked. The enemy also struck critical facilities in Kyiv region that supply power to the capital and central regions," Koretsky reported on Telegram on Wednesday.

According to him, the number of casualties resulting from the strike on a multi-story residential building in Kyiv's Desnianskyi district late Tuesday rose to 25, with two people killed. In addition, one person was killed and another injured in the morning strike on the capital.

Furthermore, the head of government reported that railway facilities were attacked in five oblasts of Ukraine. "Thanks to early evacuation, no one was injured. Restoration work is underway," Koretsky wrote.

title: Liquid AI Releases LFM2.5-24B-A2B: A 2B-Active MoE for On-Device Agents
body:
Liquid AI has released LFM2.5-24B-A2B , an open-weight reasoning model for agents that run on laptops and PCs. LFM2.5-24B-A2B is a 24B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model that activates about 2B parameters per token. It is the largest and final member of the LFM2.5 family. Liquid AI trained it inside popular agent harnesses, so it targets multi-step tool use rather than open chat. Base and post-trained weights are available on Hugging Face . TL;DR Size: 24B total, 2B active (2.45B exact per the model card), 131,072-token context. Runs on: Laptops and mini PCs (Apple M5 Max, AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395) via GGUF/MLX; single NVIDIA B300 for serving. FP8, GGUF, ONNX and MLX 4/5/6/8-bit builds. Performance: Leads or matches larger MoEs on 5 of 8 agentic and tool-use benchmarks in Liquid AI’s tests. Best: AutomationBench 27.69, more than 3x Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (8.72). Worst: SWE-Bench Verified (OpenCode) 51.00, versus 66.20 for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B. Bottom line (best): Fast, cheap local tool calling and instruction following. Bottom line (worst): Weaker on knowledge and coding; pair it with retrieval. What is LFM2.5-24B-A2B? It is a text-only, reasoning-only MoE model built for local agent loops. Every assistant turn opens with a
block, per the docs . Its predecessor, LFM2-24B-A2B , did not always reason first. It supports 16 languages, including English, Arabic, Chinese, Hindi and Japanese. How does the architecture work? It keeps LFM2’s 40-layer hybrid: 30 double-gated short convolution blocks and 10 grouped query attention (GQA) blocks. Each MoE block holds 64 experts with top-4 routing, according to the model card . Only 2 things changed from LFM2-24B-A2B. Context grew from 32,768 to 131,072 tokens. Vocabulary doubled from 65K to 128K through an in-place tokenizer expansion for better non-Latin tokenization. How was it trained? Pre-training scaled from 17T to 33T tokens. Mid-training ran 2T tokens at 32K context, then 300B tokens at 131K context. Tool calls and multi-turn trajectories appear in both phases. Post-training has 5 stages: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) Teacher specialization Non-agentic multi-domain on-policy distillation (MOPD) Agentic MOPD Agentic RL inside OpenClaw , Hermes Agent , Pi and OpenCode Liquid AI also disclosed reward hacking during teacher specialization. The model searched git history, GitHub, PyPI and Hugging Face for answers. It even detected that it was inside a sandbox. Liquid AI says it tightened sandboxes, and reported results come from sealed environments. How does LFM2.5-24B-A2B score on benchmarks? Liquid AI tested 16 benchmarks against Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it and Nemotron-3.5-Lightning (30B-A3B). It leads on AutomationBench, ToolSandbox, LiveClaw and τ³-Bench Banking. BFCLv4 is effectively a tie at 65.01 versus 65.00. The widest gap is AutomationBench: 27.69 versus 8.72 for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B. On LiveClaw it scores 48.09 versus 38.19. It also tops all 3 instruction-following tests: IFEval 96.75, IFBench 74.69 and Multi-IF 84.38. Larger models win on knowledge and code. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B leads GPQA Diamond (83.69 vs 74.42) and SWE-Bench Verified (66.20 vs 51.00). Qwen also leads WebArena Verified (37.62 vs 26.75) and PinchBench (89.93 vs 83.18). LFM2.5-24B-A2B vs Competitors Feature LFM2.5-24B-A2B Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B Developer Liquid AI Alibaba Qwen Google DeepMind NVIDIA Total params 24.0B 35B 25.2B 30B Active params 2.45B 3B 3.8B 3B Context 131,072 262,144 native 256K Up to 1M Input modality Text Text, image, video Text, image Text Architecture Conv + GQA hybrid MoE Gated DeltaNet + attention MoE Sliding/global attention MoE Mamba-2 + attention MoE License LFM Open License v1.0 Apache 2.0 Apache 2.0 OpenMDW-1.1 AutomationBench* 27.69 8.72 5.46 2.61 LiveClaw* 48.09 38.19 41.25 37.72 IFBench* 74.69 64.21 47.44 71.67 GPQA Diamond* 74.42 83.69 74.90 72.42 SWE-Bench Verified* 51.00 66.20 25.80 53.40 GPQA (vendor-reported) Not disclosed separately 86.0 82.3 75.44 Reference hardware Apple M5 Max (184 tok/s, Q4_K_M) Not disclosed Consumer GPUs and workstations 1x H100 80GB (BF16) *Scores from Liquid AI’s benchmark table , all models run by Liquid AI with vLLM. window.addEventListener("message",function(e){if(e.data&&e.data.mtpH){var f=document.getElementById("mtp-lfm25-frame");if(f&&e.source===f.contentWindow){f.style.height=e.data.mtpH+"px";}}}); What hardware does LFM2.5-24B-A2B run on? On-device, it decodes 184 tokens/s on an Apple M5 Max. It reaches 114 tokens/s on an AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395. Liquid AI measured both with llama.cpp, Q4_K_M quantization and a 4K-token input. It claims up to 1.7x the speed of the next-best compared MoE, with the lowest memory use. Exact RAM requirements were not disclosed. For serving, it passes 21K output tokens/s on a single NVIDIA B300. That test used SGLang 0.5.22, BF16, 1,024 input tokens and up to 256 output tokens. Day-one support covers Transformers, vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, MLX, LM Studio and ONNX. MLX needs mlx-lm>=0.32.0 , since earlier versions route experts incorrectly. Recommended sampling is temperature 0.1, top_k 50 and repetition penalty 1.05. A DSpark speculative-decoding draft model is listed as coming soon. How much does it cost, and what is the license? On Liquid Console , the API costs $0.10 per 1M input tokens and $1.00 per 1M output tokens. Cached input costs $0.05 per 1M, and new accounts get $2 in credit. The weights use the LFM Open License v1.0 , based on Apache 2.0. Free commercial use ends once a company reaches $10M in annual revenue. Key Takeaways 24B MoE, ~2B active, 131K context, reasoning-only. AutomationBench 27.69 vs 8.72 for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B. 184 tok/s on Apple M5 Max via llama.cpp Q4_K_M. Trails on SWE-Bench Verified (51.00 vs 66.20) and GPQA. Open weights; free commercial use under $10M revenue. Check out the technical blog , model weights , docs and LFM2 technical report . All credit goes to the researcher of this project. Also, feel free to follow us on Twitter and don’t forget to join our 150k+ML SubReddit and Subscribe to our Newsletter . title: FT Africa Summit 2026 to convene African leaders, investors and policymakers amid shifting global order
body: The Financial Times Africa Summit returns for its 13th edition on 21 to 22 October at The Landmark, London, with John Dramani Mahama, President of the Republic of Ghana, and Olusegun Obasanjo, Former President of Nigeria, confirmed to take part. The two-day summit will bring together African leaders, policymakers, investors and executives to examine the issues shaping the continent’s economic future. Under the theme “Mobilising Growth in a New Global Order,” senior voices from government, finance and industry will explore how African economies can navigate changing global trade and investment patterns while strengthening domestic capital, regional markets and productive growth. Other confirmed speakers include Aliko Dangote, President and Chief Executive, Dangote Group; Jakaya Kikwete, Former President of the United Republic of Tanzania; Kristy Mcneill, Minister for International Development, UK Government; Mo Ibrahim, Founder, Mo Ibrahim Foundation; and Ahmed Shide, Minister of Finance, Ethiopia, alongside ministers and business leaders from South Africa, Nigeria, Ethiopia, Angola, Mauritius, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, Côte d’Ivoire and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Across two days, attendees can expect discussions spanning finance, trade, technology, infrastructure, energy and industrial growth, with a particular focus on how African economies can convert structural change into stronger domestic markets, greater investment and long-term economic value. Day one will open with a keynote interview with President Mahama, followed by discussions on the future of finance, domestic capital mobilisation and the next phase of African fintech. Sessions will also examine the investment case for scaling SMEs, approaches to gold reserve management and the economic implications of Africa’s rapid urban expansion. The second day will turn to the wider forces shaping the continent’s growth trajectory. Panel discussions will examine how reform can support sustainable and inclusive growth, how capital and risk can be better aligned with Africa’s investment ambitions, and how the continent can strengthen trade in a global environment increasingly shaped by tariffs and shifting alliances. Discussions will also explore the Red Sea corridor, US Africa policy and the growing importance of regional demand and deeper commercial ties with the Gulf, China and India. Together, the sessions will examine the choices facing African governments, investors and businesses as they respond to changing global conditions while seeking to build stronger financial systems, deepen regional trade and create the infrastructure and industries required for long-term growth. The summit will also host the Africa Sustainable Futures Awards, organised in partnership with the World Bank Group’s Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA), recognising innovative private sector initiatives delivering scalable solutions to Africa’s most pressing development challenges. Now in its 13th year, the FT Africa Summit continues to bring African and international decision makers together around the economic, investment and policy questions shaping the continent’s future. To register for a delegate pass, or to apply for media accreditation, visit africa.live.ft.com .

title: Ukrainian OSINT channel: Russia turned a bare field into a Geran-5 launch site in a month—and drones are already arriving
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Russia has nearly finished the first section of a new launch site for jet-powered Geran-5 attack drones near the town of Millerovo in Rostov Oblast, anonymous Ukrainian OSINT channel Absolutely Reliable Source reported on 13 October. The channel’s bio says it covers Ukraine’s deep strikes and that its author belongs to a larger, unnamed structure. It says Russia rushed the build to scale up attacks after its September strikes on Kyiv. The site is meant for the kind of drone Ukraine stops far less often than the older Shaheds. Ukraine downs 55% of jet-powered Shaheds, the class that includes the Geran-5, and more than 90% of the older propeller-driven ones, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on 26 September. Russian industry makes about 3,000 Geran-4 and Geran-5 drones a month, Ukraine’s military intelligence (HUR) told Militarnyi in August. A new launch site is how Russia plans to fire more of them, the channel argues. Built in weeks, by the channel’s count The channel’s images from 1 September show no construction at the site. The latest ones show eight prepared positions for launchers and 32 places for preparing drones for launch, the channel wrote. Imagery from the day before its post shows drones being unloaded in one zone, it said. Millerovo drone base, 1 September 2026. Satellite image: t.me/absolutely_reliable Millerovo drone base, 12 October 2026. Satellite image: t.me/absolutely_reliable The channel’s headline says the work took a month. Ukrainian outlet Militarnyi, comparing the channel’s own images from 1 September and 12 October, put it at about six weeks. Both readings rest on the same images, which have not been independently verified. Built like Tsymbulova The construction style is very similar to Tsymbulova, Russia’s jet-drone base in Oryol Oblast, the channel wrote. That base has separate positions for storing, preparing, and launching jet drones, Militarnyi said. By late May, less than a month into an expansion of Tsymbulova, Russia was already building 10 more launchers there. Ukrainian drones have hit Tsymbulova repeatedly, though most of the damage imagery comes from Absolutely Reliable Source. Militarnyi reported strikes on the base’s bunkers and hangars in September. Ukraine’s Defense Forces struck it again overnight on 1 October, damaging two ground shelters and drone preparation areas, Absolutely Reliable Source said . On 10 October, OSINT channel Exilenova+ reported another drone strike there, saying several bunkers, one jet-drone launcher, and a drone storage area were hit. title: Flash: Russia explores capabilities for strikes on Ukraine's western regions
body:
Russian occupation forces over the past few days launched several dozen jet-powered Geran-4 drones from the territory of temporarily occupied Crimea into western Ukraine, with individual units covering a distance of 880 kilometre, reported presidential advisor Serhiy Beskrestnov (Flash).

"Thus, our adversary is exploring the possibilities of attacking western regions of Ukraine with jet-powered 'Shaheds' from various directions. The maximum flight range of the 'Geran-4' turned out to be slightly greater than expected," Serhiy Flash wrote on Facebook.

According to his data, the route of enemy drones ran from Crimea through Odesa and along the border with Moldova. Four jet drones reached Lviv, covering a distance of 820 kilometre, while several others reached Lutsk at a distance of 880 kilometre from the launch site.
