title: Nigeria-led ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍​‍‍​‌⁠​​‌​G-24 demands IMF reforms, debt relief, $300bn annual climate funding
body: Developing countries have demanded sweeping reforms of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), improved debt relief mechanisms and increased climate financing under Nigeria’s leadership of the Group of Twenty-Four (G-24). The demands were contained in the communiqué issued by the group’s 116th ministerial meeting in Bangkok, Thailand and obtained by the News Agency of Nigeria. Nigeria’s Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, chaired the meeting held during the IMF–World Bank Annual Meetings. The group called for reforms that would strengthen developing countries’ representation in global financial institutions and improve their access to affordable development financing. It warned that geopolitical tensions, rising commodity prices, trade restrictions and increasingly frequent extreme weather events were threatening economic stability. According to the communiqué, these developments were raising borrowing costs, weakening currencies and increasing debt distress in emerging markets and developing economies. The ministers expressed particular concern about highly indebted countries struggling with limited fiscal resources, external financing pressures and declining development assistance. They consequently urged the IMF to accelerate reforms of its quota system to reflect changing economic realities and strengthen developing countries’ voting power. It insisted that the reforms must protect the representation of emerging economies and the world’s poorest countries. The ministers also urged the IMF to adopt greater flexibility in designing financial assistance programmes for countries facing economic difficulties. They maintained that IMF-supported programmes should safeguard social spending, encourage investment and avoid excessive adjustments capable of undermining economic recovery. On sovereign debt, the group warned that mounting repayment obligations were restricting developing countries’ capacity to finance infrastructure, healthcare, education and economic transformation. “Debt vulnerability is a major barrier to inclusive growth in many developing economies,” the communiqué stated. The ministers consequently advocated more predictable debt restructuring, greater transparency, improved credit-rating assessments and stronger coordination among creditors. They welcomed initiatives aimed at strengthening sovereign debt management, including a new borrowers’ platform supported by the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development. The group also urged the World Bank to expand affordable financing through innovative instruments, including guarantees, risk-sharing arrangements and mechanisms for mobilising private investment. It emphasised the importance of strengthening domestic capital markets and expanding lending in local currencies to reduce foreign-exchange risks. On climate change, the ministers demanded full implementation of the international commitment to mobilise at least 300 billion dollars annually in climate finance by 2035. They stressed that developed countries should lead efforts to deliver the financing while substantially increasing resources for climate adaptation. The group further called for stronger international cooperation against tax avoidance, profit shifting and illicit financial flows that undermine developing countries’ revenues. Nigeria’s Permanent Secretary in the Federal Ministry of Finance, Raymond Omachi, chaired the G-24 deputies’ meeting earlier, while Central Bank Governor Olayemi Cardoso participated in the ministerial discussions. (NAN) The post Nigeria-led ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍​‍‍​‌⁠​​‌​G-24 demands IMF reforms, debt relief, $300bn annual climate funding appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Defence Minister addresses 1st ASEAN-India Defence Think Tank Forum at MP-IDSA
body:
India seeks an Indo-Pacific where all countries make their own choices, protect their interests & pursue development in peace: Defence Minister at 1st ASEAN-India Defence Think Tank Forum

 	
“Need to build trust, respect each other’s sovereignty, follow international law & keep channels of dialogue open to tackle borderless challenges”

 	
Strengthening maritime domain awareness, interoperability & underwater cooperation is key to a stable, rule-based maritime order, says Defence Minister Rajnath Singh

 	
“Self-reliance does not mean working in isolation; it can create opportunities for trusted partners to design, build, maintain & improve equipment together”

 	
“Co-development, co-production, MRO, training and long-term technical support can build local skills, support industry & make supply chains more reliable”


New Delhi, Oct 14. “India seeks an Indo-Pacific where all countries - large and small - make their own choices, protect their interests and pursue development in peace,” said Defence Minister Rajnath Singh as he called for building trust, respecting each other’s sovereignty, following international law and keeping channels of dialogue open to tackle both emerging and conventional “borderless challenges”. He was addressing the maiden Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) - India Defence Think Tank Forum at Manohar Parrikar Institute for Defence Studies and Analyses (MP-IDSA) in New Delhi on October 14, 2026.



Defence Minister asserted that India and ASEAN share a clear interest in peace, stability, prosperity and an open & inclusive Indo-Pacific. He emphasised that India’s Act East policy and the vision of SAGAR (Security and Growth for All in the Region) and MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions) advocate for an open and multipolar cooperation, and the nation aligns them through ASEAN-led mechanisms that are central to its Indo-Pacific vision. He noted that the region is witnessing rapid changes in the face of growing strategic competition and pressure & uncertainty created at times through actions at sea, in addition to threats such as terrorism, cybercrime, piracy, trafficking, illegal fishing, climate-related disasters and risks to vital supply chains. No country alone can address these challenges, he said.

Rajnath Singh underlined the need to discuss differences early and peacefully, before they become disputes, and pitched for a regional order where countries work together without being forced to choose sides. “India believes that security is strengthened when countries build capacity together, respect international law and maintain trust through dialogue,” he said.

Defence Minister highlighted the centuries-old close ties between India and Southeast Asia rooted in shared history, culture, trade & ideas, reiterating that the Act East Policy is a long-term commitment to working with the region as an equal partner. “India’s approach and ASEAN’s outlook on the Indo-Pacific can complement each other. We should strengthen cooperation, not create competition between regional forums,” he said.

Rajnath Singh stated that keeping the Indian Ocean and the waters of Southeast Asia safe is a shared responsibility as they are part of one connected maritime space, crucial for trade, energy, people and essential goods. Strengthening maritime domain awareness, interoperability, and collaboration in underwater awareness will be key to ensuring a stable, rule-based maritime order, he said.



Defence Minister stressed that as 2026 has been designated as ASEAN-India Year of Maritime Cooperation, it is an opportunity to turn shared interest into practical action. “We should improve the sharing of maritime information, strengthen cooperation among our navies and coast guards, and build the ability to respond together to emergencies. We should also work against piracy, trafficking, illegal fishing and other threats, in accordance with international law,” he said.

Terming defence technology as another crucial area, Rajnath Singh pointed out that Artificial Intelligence, drones, cyber capabilities and space-based systems are becoming increasingly important, with recent conflicts demonstrating that relatively low-cost drones can challenge expensive defence systems. He underscored the need to respond with practical, affordable and adaptable solutions.

“India believes that innovation should not remain limited to a few large organisations. Start-ups, universities, research institutions and smaller companies can all contribute. India’s initiatives like Innovations for Defence Excellence (iDEX) and Technology Development Fund (TDF) have created a way to collaborate with innovators for our defence needs,” stated Defence Minister as he called for exploring ways for innovators to work together on clearly defined problems, such as counter-drone systems, cyber defence, maritime surveillance and disaster response.

Rajnath Singh called for joint research projects, shared testing opportunities, exchanges among young researchers and carefully designed innovation challenges, emphasising that such cooperation must also protect sensitive information, respect intellectual property and ensure that technology is shared responsibly. “The aim should be to develop useful capabilities while strengthening trust between our countries,” he said.

On defence industrial cooperation, Defence Minister asserted that India is ready to explore cooperation with ASEAN partners in areas such as patrol vessels, radars, air-defence systems, helicopters, drones and other technologies, according to each country’s needs and priorities. He said the ‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’ initiative focuses on building stronger domestic capabilities, but self-reliance does not mean working in isolation. It can create opportunities for trusted partners to design, build, maintain and improve equipment together, he said.

Underlining the importance of co-development, co-production, maintenance, repair and overhaul, training and long-term technical support, Rajnath Singh said these arrangements can build local skills, support industry and make supply chains more reliable.  “Our researchers need to look closely at what makes such partnerships work: clear requirements, reliable after-sales support, appropriate technology safeguards, fair sharing of responsibilities and benefits, and opportunities for local companies and skilled workers. Our goal should be lasting partnerships, not one-time transactions,” he said.

Calling for enhanced cooperation to deal with natural disasters, Defence Minister stated that Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) should be a regular part of defence dialogue as cyclones, floods, rising sea levels and extreme weather can damage ports, disrupt trade and threaten lives and livelihoods. “We can learn from one another, share best practices and improve coordination before a crisis occurs,” he said.



On the crucial role of Think Tanks, Rajnath Singh said Governments need good analysis, but they also need ideas that can be put into practice. He suggested some practical outcomes from the forum, including development of a joint India-ASEAN research agenda on maritime security, cyber threats, emerging technologies, disaster response and defence-industry cooperation; regular exchanges among researchers, including young scholars, through fellowships, visiting programmes and joint publications; Identification of a small number of pilot projects such as a tabletop exercise on maritime disaster response, a joint study on counter-drone solutions, or a research project on secure maritime information sharing; Promotion of Track 1.5 and Track 2 dialogues for researchers, practitioners and policymakers to continue their discussions between formal meetings; and preparing a concise set of recommendations, identifying institutions that could take them forward, and reviewing progress at a future meeting.

In his welcome address, Director General, MP-IDSA Amb Sujan R Chinoy expressed gratitude to Defence Minister for his vision and support in strengthening India’s defence and security partnerships with ASEAN. Welcoming participants from all eleven ASEAN member states and India, he described the forum as an important institutional milestone in the evolution of ASEAN-India defence engagement. He expressed confidence that the forum would institutionalise enduring dialogue between India and ASEAN’s strategic communities and help identify practical areas for deeper defence and security cooperation.

About ASEAN - India Defence Think Tank Forum

Being held on October 14 & 15, 2026, the forum aims to strengthen strategic dialogue, promote joint analysis and identify practical avenues for enhanced defence and security cooperation between India and ASEAN. The initiative follows the announcement made by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh during the second ASEAN-India Defence Ministers’ Informal Meeting in Kuala Lumpur on October 31, 2025, on the sidelines of the 12th ADMM-Plus.

Across a two-day programme, the forum will deliberate on strategic stability, regional geopolitics, maritime security, grey-zone challenges, HADR, maritime domain awareness, defence technology, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, space, unmanned systems, defence industry collaboration and resilient supply chains. The discussions are expected to contribute to a stronger and more forward-looking ASEAN-India defence partnership.

title: Ebonyi govt denies converting airport to worship centre
body:
The Ebonyi State Government has acknowledged that staff at the Chuba Okadigbo International Airport hold prayers before work but denied that the facility has been converted into a worship centre.
The state Commissioner for Information and State Orientation, Ikeuwa Omebeh, initially dismissed a viral video showing a church service at the airport as AI-generated. He later acknowledged that staff had prayed there, insisting that a prayer service was different from a church service.
“It is not true, in all ramifications,” Mr Omebeh said.
“It has never been a worship centre, and we don’t intend to use it as a worship centre.”
He spoke in an interview on Arise Television on Tuesday, responding to criticism of Governor Francis Nwifuru’s administration and making a case for the governor’s re-election.
Mr Omebeh initially insisted that the viral video was AI-generated. He cited former President Goodluck Jonathan’s use of the airport about three weeks earlier while travelling to a burial in Cross River State as evidence that the facility was operational.
“I am sure that it is AI-generated; this is the same airport former President Goodluck Jonathan used about three weeks ago to a local government in Calabar,” he said.
When pressed to identify the AI tool used to verify the video, Mr Omebeh did not name one.
“I am coming from Abakaliki, and I’m on ground to tell you that those things are not correct,” he said.
During the interview, the presenter drew attention to an earlier statement by the state Commissioner for Special Duties, Valentine Okike-Uzo. Mr Okike-Uzo had also dismissed the video but said airport staff routinely hold communal prayers on Thursdays before work.
Mr Omebeh subsequently acknowledged that staff had prayed at the airport. He maintained that the gathering was a prayer session, not a church service organised by an external church.
“We welcome prayer, but not church service,” he said.
Mr Omebeh alleged that some protests and opposition to the state government were sponsored but did not identify those responsible despite repeated questions.
“We do not have any opposition,” he said, before listing what he described as the governor’s achievements.
Asked whether a governor could unilaterally remove elected local government chairmen who failed to deliver votes for the All Progressives Congress (APC), Mr Omebeh did not directly address the question.
Instead, he said Mr Nwifuru did not interfere with local government funds and was urging council chairmen to ensure their constituents benefited from democracy and earned their trust through performance.
“Every leader is rated by his performance,” he said. “Make sure that you perform.”
Charles Otu, spokesperson for the Ebonyi Civil Society Coalition Group, had alleged on Arise TV’s Morning Show on Thursday, 3 September, that a church had taken over the airport for midweek and Sunday services.
He also claimed that the only flights landing at the airport were private charters carrying the governor and his wife at public expense.
The airport, located in Onueke, Ezza South Local Government Area, has been controversial for years. Former Governor David Umahi said in April 2023 that the state spent N36 billion building the facility, although an unofficial figure put the cost above N42 billion.
The Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority had certified the airport for chartered flights and private jets only. A video showing church services in its departure lounge subsequently went viral.
The controversy over local government chairmen followed Mr Nwifuru’s remarks on 1 September. At the inauguration of new council chairmen in Abakaliki, the governor said, “we will remove any chairman who fails to win his local government.”
Governorship elections in most states, including Ebonyi, are scheduled for 6 February 2027, under the revised timetable of the Independent National Electoral Commission.

title: Today’s Ukrainian drone attack on Russia becomes one of most massive of 2026 thus far
body:
MOSCOW, October 14. /TASS/. The Ukrainian drone attack on Russia in the early morning hours of October 14, during which air defenses downed 902 drones, was one of the most massive of the year, according to TASS calculations based on the Russian Defense Ministry’s reports.
According to the military, 902 Ukrainian drones were shot down over Russia and the waters of the Sea of Azov in the early morning hours of October 14. The previous large-scale attack was repelled in the early morning hours of October 6, when 868 Ukrainian drones were downed over Russian regions.
The largest attack of the year and one of the largest since the beginning of the special military operation took place on September 20, the last day of the 9th State Duma elections. On that day, air defenses intercepted and destroyed 1,951 drones and eight missiles.

title: Novatek gas production up by 3.4% year-on-year to 64.8 bcm in January-September
body:
MOSCOW, October 14. /TASS/. Russian gas producer Novatek increased its natural gas output by 3.4% year-on-year to 64.8 billion cubic meters (bcm) in January-September. Production rose by 4.9% in the third quarter, reaching 21.12 bcm, the company reported.
Total hydrocarbon production grew by 3.3% to 514.4 million barrels of oil equivalent (boe), including 10.71 million tonnes of liquid hydrocarbons (up 2.6%). In the third quarter, hydrocarbon production totaled 168.2 million boe--an increase of 4.2% compared to the previous year.
"In the third quarter, hydrocarbon production amounted to 168.2 million barrels of oil equivalent, comprising 21.12 bcm of natural gas and 3.56 million tonnes of liquid hydrocarbons (gas condensate and oil). Compared to the third quarter of 2025, hydrocarbon production increased by 6.8 million boe, or 4.2%," the statement says.
Total natural gas sales volume, including LNG, amounted to 55.2 bcm over the nine-month period, down 1.1% from the previous year's figure. At the same time, sales in the third quarter fell by 3.1% to 15.8 billion cubic meters.
As of September 30, 2026, the company held 1.5 billion cubic meters of gas (including LNG) and 0.9 million tonnes of stable gas condensate and its derivatives in its inventory.

title: FBI arrests Saudi OpenAI engineer over covert recording device, DOJ says
body: US federal agents arrested a Saudi national who was an OpenAI engineer and charged him with installing a hidden audio recording device in an executive conference room at the AI company, the Justice Department said on Tuesday.The case highlights growing security concerns around sensitive AI research as companies and governments compete fiercely for the talent and technology that could confer economic and strategic advantages.Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, had worked as an engineer at OpenAI since July 2025, the Justice Department said in a statement. An email sent to an address associated with that name got no response, and it was not immediately clear who his lawyer was.OpenAI discovered the recording device plugged into a USB port on the back of a television in an executive conference room at one of its San Francisco buildings on September 30, according to the department.The thumb-sized device, which had a microphone and could connect to a camera, was concealed in toilet paper, according to an FBI complaint. It was installed on or about September 28, while its stored data was encrypted and inaccessible. Investigators later found a similar customized device in Alfozan's personal bag.OpenAI said in a post on X that it used its internal AI models to identify the person responsible for planting the device and trace its origins.OpenAI says employee intended to place additional recording devices in sensitive areas of its officesThe company said it had evidence that the employee intended to place additional recording devices in sensitive areas of its offices to secretly record meetings."At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data. The employee was terminated," the company said.OpenAI referred the matter to the FBI, which is continuing to investigate. The Saudi embassy in the United States did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment."Abdulrahman Alfozan allegedly concealed a covert recording device inside his employer's executive conference room to secretly capture sensitive communications about the company's super intelligence technology," FBI Director Kash Patel said in a statement.Alfozan also used an AI productivity agent to seek information about meeting-room calendars and capabilities for about a month through September 16, according to the FBI complaint. He has been a legal permanent resident of the US since September 2020.Alfozan may face up to five years in prisonIf convicted, Alfozan faces up to five years in prison, a $250,000 fine and three years of supervised release.A LinkedIn profile showed that Alfozan studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and the University of California, Berkeley. It said he previously worked at Meta and Microsoft.Reuters could not independently verify the details mentioned in his LinkedIn profile.Separately, the Information reported that OpenAI was in early talks to acquire Trail of Bits, a startup that identifies and fixes vulnerabilities in open-source software. The talks were ongoing and could fall apart, the report said, citing people familiar with the matter.OpenAI and Trail of Bits did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.OpenAI said on Friday it fired three researchers after an investigation found they had violated company policies on handling sensitive information.The researchers, Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak and Mikita Balesni, had published a letter detailing the circumstances of their dismissal and arguing that the abrupt firings could create uncertainty among employees and undermine a culture in which researchers could raise safety concerns.

title: Americans say Trump misusing presidency for personal wealth
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 14 (MNA) – A new poll has found that most Americans believe US President Donald Trump is misusing presidency for increasing his personal wealth.
More than half of Americans believe US President Donald Trump is placing his personal wealth ahead of the country’s interests, while roughly six in 10 think he is profiting from the presidency in ways they consider illegal or unethical.
According to a new survey by The Associated Press-NORC Center for Public Affairs Research, 56% of US adults believe Trump has placed “a lot” of emphasis on his personal business interests since returning to the White House.
By comparison, only about one-quarter said he had given the same level of attention to the interests of the country as a whole, while roughly one in 10 said he had focused heavily on people like them.
The survey also found that around 60% of Americans believe Trump is either illegally profiting from his presidency or engaging in unethical behavior that does not necessarily break the law.
About 40% said they believe he is doing something illegal, while approximately 20% considered his conduct unethical but not illegal. Only about one-fifth said he was doing nothing wrong.
“His wealth increases,” said Barbara Thaxton, an 87-year-old independent voter from Florida. “But the people in the country are just barely getting by.”
The findings come as Trump’s family business expands into new ventures, including cryptocurrency and overseas real estate deals, raising renewed questions about potential conflicts of interest between his private financial activities and his public responsibilities.
Trump has relaxed restrictions on his family’s overseas business activities that were in place during his first term and launched several cryptocurrency ventures since returning to office.
In a financial disclosure filed in June, the president reported receiving more than $1 billion from new cryptocurrency businesses, according to the report, according to Press TV.
One major venture received a $500 million investment from a United Arab Emirates business linked to the country’s royal family after Trump’s election victory.
The Trump Organization has also pursued eight foreign real estate deals during the first year of his presidency, including projects in countries where governments exert considerable influence over private business.

title: Netanyahu denies ever having met Egypt's foreign intelligence chief despite contradictory records
body: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu claimed in an interview with Channel 14's The Patriots on Tuesday that he had never met with a foreign intelligence chief in his capacity as prime minister, despite official records showing that he hosted Egyptian intelligence chief Abbas Kamel at his Jerusalem residence in May 2021 and discussed security and diplomatic matters with him."When does an intelligence chief come and speak to a head of state? It hasn't happened to me once, OK? There's no such thing," Netanyahu said during the interview.The remarks came after the prime minister confirmed that an Egyptian aircraft had landed in Israel in September 2023, just days before the October 7 Hamas attack.Netanyahu denied meeting with the Egyptian intelligence chief on that occasion, saying he had been attending a memorial ceremony for fallen IDF soldiers at the time.He also demanded to know whom the senior Egyptian official had met during his visit to Israel."I want to know who he met. I don't know," Netanyahu said, claiming that whoever had met the official was trying to "pin it on me."However, in attempting to explain why it would be unlikely for an intelligence chief to meet with a prime minister, Netanyahu made a sweeping assertion that contradicts the documented history of his own meetings.The official statement and photograph from May 2021On May 30, 2021, the Prime Minister's Office published a statement titled "Prime Minister Netanyahu meets with Egyptian General Intelligence Chief Abbas Kamel and a delegation of senior officials headed by him."The statement explicitly said: "Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu met today with Egyptian General Intelligence Chief Abbas Kamel and a delegation of senior officials headed by him at the Prime Minister's Residence in Jerusalem."According to the statement, the two discussed strengthening cooperation between Israel and Egypt and regional issues, and welcomed the ties between the countries and their joint efforts on security and diplomatic matters.The statement also said Netanyahu raised Israel's demand for the return of the soldiers and civilians who were being held in the Gaza Strip at the time.The meeting also addressed mechanisms to prevent Hamas from building up its capabilities and from using resources intended for the civilian population.The meeting was also attended by then-intelligence minister Eli Cohen and then-national security adviser Meir Ben-Shabbat, who had previously held an extended meeting with Kamel.The statement was accompanied by an official photograph of Netanyahu and Kamel shaking hands, taken by Government Press Office photographer Amos Ben-Gershom.A video of the meeting was also published on the prime minister's official YouTube channel.In other words, this was not a meeting revealed retrospectively through anonymous sources, but a diplomatic event that Netanyahu himself chose to make public through his office.Netanyahu also met with the CIA directorThe meeting with the Egyptian intelligence chief is not the only instance that calls into question Netanyahu's sweeping claim.In February 2024, Walla reported that then-CIA director William Burns had arrived in Israel and met with Netanyahu and former Mossad chief David Barnea as part of efforts to advance a deal to release the hostages being held in Gaza.Netanyahu and Burns met again in Jerusalem in May of that year, against the backdrop of negotiations over a ceasefire and hostage deal.Such meetings are a routine part of diplomatic and security relations between national leaders and the heads of foreign intelligence agencies, particularly when those officials are involved in sensitive negotiations or serve as envoys for their governments.

title: Progress or disaster? Armenia begins operations at Amulsar mine
body: Operations begin at Amulsar mine The Amulsar gold mine has begun operations in Armenia . Guests attending the official opening ceremony were shown the mining process and the production of the first gold bar. Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan also attended the ceremony. The Armenian government expects the project to generate $130m annually in tax revenue and other income for the state budget. Environmental campaigners, who have warned about the risks associated with the project for years, condemned the government’s decision. More than 60 organisations issued a statement warning that mining at Amulsar would lead to an “irreversible environmental catastrophe”. However, Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan maintains that concerns about environmental risks have been comprehensively addressed. He insists that all questions raised by environmentalists have received thorough and conclusive answers, dispelling their fears. “There were alarming statements and concerns, including about the possible poisoning of Lake Sevan and so on. And we are here today because we are convinced that none of these risks actually exist,” Pashinyan said. Economist Suren Parsyan expects the development of the Amulsar deposit to bring significant economic and social benefits. He also believes that the launch of the mine will demonstrate to investors that Armenia continues to operate in accordance with international standards and is ready to implement new projects. How Armenia is reacting to export restrictions on Russia: farmers’ views and official statistics Experts warn of pesticides in Armenian food, inspectors see no issues Preferential regime for Armenian exports to EU in response to Russian restrictions $750m already invested in the project The Amulsar mining project is being implemented as part of a strategic partnership between Lydian Armenia and the Armenian government. According to the government, Lydian Armenia has: introduced international best practices and standards at Amulsar; adopted the principles of modern, responsible mining; promoted a new culture of occupational safety, environmental management, social responsibility and the use of modern technologies. The company has already invested around $750m in the project. The Amulsar mine is expected to produce approximately 210,000 ounces (around 6.5 tonnes) of gold annually. “ According to expert estimates, the annual taxes and other contributions paid by Lydian Armenia to the state budget as a result of the mine’s operation will amount to approximately $130m, contributing an estimated 1.5–2% to Armenia’s GDP ,” the government said in a statement. The project is also expected to create more than 4,000 direct and indirect jobs. Under an agreement between the government and Lydian Armenia, the company will allocate 7m–9m annually to socio-economic development programmes in nearby communities throughout the mine’s operational lifespan. 'Copper is to us what oil is to other countries’ – expert on Armenia’s mineral wealth Geologist Arshavir Hovhannisyan says Armenia has large reserves of copper, whose global market price is “rising exponentially”, as well as molybdenum and gold. Pashinyan: ‘Country is entering a new stage of development’ Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan described the launch of operations at the Amulsar mine not only as a successful investment project but also as a new stage in the country’s development and an important milestone in the history of Armenia’s mining industry and economic development. “ In the context of Armenia’s history, this is a major step forward. But I hope and firmly believe that in the near future, such steps will become routine and part of our everyday practice. And what we consider a major step in the future will involve projects on an even larger scale .” According to Pashinyan, the project will provide Armenia with greater opportunities to invest in the security and well-being of its citizens. He stressed that the country’s mineral resources belong to the Armenian people and that the government’s key responsibility is to ensure that this wealth “serves the development and prosperity” of every citizen. Nikol Pashinyan inspected the facilities and infrastructure developed for the operation of the mine. The prime minister said that Lydian Armenia had imported modern equipment to develop the deposit. In his view, Armenia can now boast a high-quality mining industry: “ For any developed country, mining of this calibre, carried out in compliance with environmental and social standards, is a key driver of national development. “ Opinion: What’s behind Armenia’s economic growth figures? Economy Minister Gevorg Papoyan posted figures on Facebook that appear to signal an economic triumph. Economist Suren Parsyan explains what is driving these results. ‘ Ignoring the risks is unacceptable’: Environmental NGOs’ statement According to civil society representatives , they have still not received information about realistic and well-founded measures to address the environmental and socio-economic risks associated with the project. They described the ceremonial opening of the mine just days before the 17th Conference of the Parties to the UN Convention on Biological Diversity (COP17), due to take place in Yerevan, as “a very bold and irresponsible step”. “ By hosting COP17, Armenia is seeking to demonstrate its commitment to the green agenda to the international community, while an environmental catastrophe is unfolding within the country . Armenia’s natural environment, water resources and the future of local communities cannot be put at risk without proper public accountability and evidence that the project is safe. We consider it unacceptable to ignore these risk s,” the statement said. 'Chasing cheap profits' – how mining industry dominates Armenia In the small Armenian village of Karaberd, geological surveys for a new gold deposit are set to begin, even though a mine is already operating there. Expert commentary According to economist Suren Parsyan, Amulsar is the largest investment project in Armenia’s modern history. In an interview with Armenpress, he said the Amulsar deposit had sufficient reserves to sustain mining operations for at least 20–25 years. He therefore believes that the mine will have a significant economic impact not only on nearby communities but also on the country as a whole. Parsyan said the company’s turnover or exports would amount to around $930m, meaning that Armenia would gain a new “industrial giant” comparable to the Zangezur Copper and Molybdenum Combine. “ We now have the second-largest mining company, which will have a direct impact of around 2% on the economy. Its indirect impact could amount to another 1.5–2% .” He stressed that the company would become a customer for more than 200 small and medium-sized enterprises, serving as a “driving force for regional businesses”. The economist also believes that the mine’s operation will bring significant social benefits. Around 1,000 direct jobs are expected to be created, alongside 4,000–6,000 indirect jobs. “ Salaries here are quite high, averaging 900,000 drams ($2,356) or more. This is a fairly high figure, even exceeding the average salary at other mining companies in Armenia ,” he explained. Suren Parsyan pointed out that Vayots Dzor is one of Armenia’s poorest regions, with a poverty rate of around 25%, above the national average. He also noted that, in addition to creating jobs, the project includes a social component aimed at supporting nearby communities. “ The poverty rate could fall significantly, by around two to three times. In Vayots Dzor, where the population is small and employment opportunities are limited, this could provide a long-term solution to the problem ,” he concluded. title: Ga Mantse to co-host 5th edition of ‘A Night with the Diplomats’
body: The Ga Mantse, King Tackie Teiko Tsuru II, will co-host the fifth edition of A Night with the Diplomats at the Ga Mantse Royal Palace in Accra on December 3. The event, organised by Diplomatic Affairs Media and Communications (DAMC) Ltd, will be held under the theme, “Leveraging Royal Diplomacy for Africa’s Development Agenda.” The fifth edition was announced at a Diplomatic Affairs Media Soiree in Accra, where discussions centred on the role of the private sector in advancing economic diplomacy. The launch, held under the theme, “Economic Diplomacy: The Role of the Private Sector,” provided a platform for participants to explore how businesses can help strengthen Ghana’s international partnerships, promote its interests and contribute to national development. Chief Executive Officer of DAMC, Harriet Nartey, said the event represents a sustained effort to build bridges between diplomacy, government, business, traditional leadership, development partners and the media. She explained that the December event would bring together members of the diplomatic community, business leaders, government representatives, traditional authorities, and representatives of royal and monarchical institutions from other parts of the world. Ms Nartey said traditional institutions have historically played significant roles in preserving culture, promoting community development and strengthening relationships among people. “In an era where Africa is seeking stronger economic integration, greater investment and sustainable development, we believe there is value in exploring how royal diplomacy can complement conventional diplomacy and contribute to Africa’s developmental agenda. The Palace will therefore become more than a venue. It will become a meeting point for ideas, relationships, culture, enterprise and diplomacy,” she said. The Chief of Protocol and Communications to the Ga Mantse, Ambassador Parker Allotey, who spoke on behalf of the traditional ruler, said hosting the event at the palace would allow diplomats, representatives of international organisations and members of diplomatic missions to interact with the Ga Mantse and experience the culture of the palace. The Presiding Bishop of Beracha Ministerial Fellowship, Bishop Fred Korankye-Mensah, speaking on behalf of DAMC’s Board Chairman, said that economic diplomacy requires active participation from the private sector and cannot be driven by government action alone. He noted that although investors considered government pronouncements, their decisions ultimately depended on what businesses could deliver. “Diplomacy once seemed to belong mainly to governments, ambassadors and closed meeting rooms, but today some of our most influential ambassadors are business people. They carry products, investment plans, new ideas and jobs across borders. It is worth noting that Accra, being the home of the African Continental Trade Area Secretariat, is the best place to discuss this all-important topic, economic diplomacy, the role of the private sector,” he said. A Night with the Diplomats is an annual networking and engagement initiative organised by Diplomatic Affairs Media and Communications (DAMC) Ltd to bring together members of the diplomatic corps, government officials, business leaders and other influential personalities to exchange ideas and strengthen international relationships. Launched in 2021 by DAMC Chief Executive Officer Harriet Nartey, the initiative seeks to promote public understanding of diplomacy and foster collaboration between Ghana’s diplomatic community, corporate institutions, politicians and academia. Previous editions have attracted prominent personalities and members of the diplomatic corps.

title: Houthi attack hits Aramco's historic nerve centre in Saudi Arabia
body: A missile attack on an administrative building of Saudi Arabia's state energy company Aramco hit the historic centre of the kingdom's oil industry , sparking a fire that authorities said caused no casualties. The strike by the Yemeni Houthi rebels hit a complex that serves as the nerve centre of the world's largest oil exporter, housing key research and development site, energy operations and thousands of employees and their families. People living near the building described moments of terror as a powerful explosion shook the area. "This was the loudest explosion I have ever heard in my life," one woman told The National . Another resident said relatives living closer to the site had reported seeing smoke and flames rising from the area following the attack. While no further details have been released about the incident, the site is a key one for Aramco, serving as its central hub for oil, gas, and energy operations. More than an HQ Aramco, at the time known as the Arabian American Oil Company, moved its headquarters from New York City to Dhahran in 1952. Dhahran was where the kingdom’s first commercial oil was found in 1938, at Dammam No 7, the “Prosperity Well". The Saudi government gradually acquired the company, completing a full buyout in 1980, before it was renamed the Saudi Arabian Oil Company (Aramco) in 1988. Aramco’s headquarters is situated within a vast complex spread across 58 square kilometres, with a large residential area housing a reported 11,000 people, including employees and their families. The Dhahran district also has a research and development centre and the Expec Advanced Research Centre, which was inaugurated in 2008. Expec has been upgraded with a building to focus on upstream research and development. The Dhahran complex also houses a large-scale cooling plant, operated by Saudi Tabreed, with a 32,000 refrigeration-tonne capacity that includes thermal storage tanks for energy saving. The chilled water piping network stretches 16 kilometres to reach sites, meeting Saudi Aramco's requirements for cooling. The area also includes Ithra, the King Abdulaziz Centre for World Culture, which was built by Aramco as a cultural and creative destination for the public. The centre has attracted more than four million since its opening in 2018. Previous attacks The Dhahran area was attacked on February 25, 1991, during the Gulf War, when an Iraqi Scud missile struck a US Army barracks, killing 28 American soldiers and wounding 110. Aramco’s other sites in the Eastern province have also faced attacks in the past. Several drones and missiles hit Saudi Aramco’s Abqaiq and Khurais oil processing centres on September 14, 2019, knocking out about 50 per cent of the country’s crude oil production. The 17-minute strike by 18 drones and three low-flying missiles, claimed by the Houthis, caused a surge in oil prices and shut down more than 5 per cent of global oil supply. Saudi Arabia said about two weeks later that it had fully restored oil output. In March 2022, an Aramco plant in Jizan was also attacked by the Houthis with a drone laden with explosives, with a gas station in Khamis Mushait and a power station in Dhahran also hit. In early March this year, after the start of the Iran war, a fire broke out at Aramco’s Ras Tanura refinery , the kingdom’s largest, with 550,000 barrels per day of capacity, due to drone attacks. Operations were halted for 16 days. Ras Tanura, on Saudi Arabia's Gulf coast, hosts one of the world’s largest oil export terminals and a major refining facility. The port handles a significant share of Saudi crude exports. Other sites hit this year include Satorp in Jubail, a joint venture between Saudi Aramco and TotalEnergies processing 465,000 bpd and one of the world's largest export refining platforms, as well as Samref in Yanbu, a 400,000 bpd Aramco-ExxonMobil joint venture. Earlier this month, Aramco’s chief executive Amin Nasser said ​the company had ‌the ⁠strategic ​reserves and ​flexibility ‌to ⁠isolate or shift output ⁠as required. Aramco can ⁠make its maximum ⁠sustainable production ​capacity of ⁠12 million bpd available ⁠within days, ​he ​told the Energy Intelligence Forum in London. “Our system is intact,” he added. Aramco, which is listed on the Tadawul exchange, is majority owned by the Saudi government. It is due to release its third quarter financial results on November 3.

title: SpaceX restricts Ukrainian army’s Starlink access, Zelensky’s adviser confirms
body:
MOSCOW, October 14. /TASS/. SpaceX restricted the speed of Starlink satellite internet terminals used by the Ukrainian army overnight, Sergey Beskrestnov, Vladimir Zelensky’s external adviser and expert in communications and unmanned systems, said.
"I confirm that SpaceX introduced speed restrictions for Starlink terminals in motion last night. The restrictions currently apply to the 'military package' of Starshield services, with the speed limit set at 100 miles per hour (about 160 kilometers per hour - TASS). Our defense forces received no warning about the restrictions, which disrupted a number of missions," he wrote on Telegram.
According to Beskrestnov, "this action cannot be a coincidence and has to do with the current political situation."
Sergey Sternenko, a former adviser to Ukraine’s defense minister, said earlier that the Ukrainian army’s access to Starlink had been restricted. He suggested that SpaceX had acted at the request of the US administration.
Politico Europe reported earlier that US President Donald Trump could cut off US intelligence support for Kiev or pressure Elon Musk to disable SpaceX’s Starlink internet service, on which Ukraine’s military heavily relies.

title: Stirling Centre launches 4th cohort of its flagship COLP qualification, welcomes learning leaders from Ghana, other countries
body: The Stirling Centre for Strategic Learning and Innovation today launched the fourth cohort of its Certified Organisational Learning Professional (COLP) programme. The new cohort brings together professionals from Egypt, Germany, Ghana, Lebanon, Pakistan, Portugal, Scotland, the United Arab Emirates, Vietnam and Kosovo. COLP is the Stirling Centre’s flagship qualification. It equips managers, HR and learning professionals, quality leaders and public servants to turn everyday experience into lasting organisational capability. The programme draws on the Learning-Driven Organisation (LDO) Model, co-developed by Prof. Alaa Garad and Prof. Jeff Gold and published by Bloomsbury in 2021. The cohort runs for eight weeks through a hybrid approach of online and on-site sessions, held twice a week for two hours each. Participants work through practical tools that close real performance gaps, including benchmarking, feedback and listening systems, staff suggestion schemes and action learning sets. Each participant applies what they learn to a live challenge in their own organisation. This year, the Stirling Centre is applying the international mix as a deliberate platform for participants to test ideas against the experiences of colleagues, where deep learning situations are engineered. Prof. Alaa Garad, President and Founder of the Stirling Centre, said: “Every cohort teaches us something new, and this one will be no exception. When people from ten countries sit around the same table, they stop assuming their way is the only way. “That moment of curiosity is where organisational learning begins. Our aim is simple: graduates who return to their organisations are able to help them learn faster than the world around them changes.” Dr Donald Cog Senanu Agumenu, the African Director of the Stirling Centre for Strategic Learning & Innovation, observes that the fourth cohort is timely and strategic for business leaders and institutions in this current wave of artificial intelligence, where continuous learning is imperative. “This cohort certification has an embedded artificial intelligence framework that definitely answers how companies and institutions can continue to be very competitive in this digital revolution age. “I, therefore, call on all business captains, government agencies, as well as non-governmental organisations to register and be a part of this innovative programme.” The fourth cohort follows growing demand for the COLP suite, which now includes sector variants for educators (CLDE) and a dedicated government programme, COLP-GOV, currently being piloted with the Egyptian Government.

title: Lisandro Martinez attacks Man United hierarchy over failure to strengthen squad
body: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez has criticised the club’s hierarchy for failing to strengthen the squad adequately despite the team’s return to the UEFA Champions League, saying more investment was needed to compete at the highest level. Martinez made the remarks after United suffered a 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid on Tuesday, extending their winless run to five matches across all competitions. The Argentine defender said the club’s management should take responsibility for the team’s struggles rather than allowing the blame to fall solely on head coach Michael Carrick and the players. “We did a fantastic season last season and now we expect more from the top, more players to compete because many teams bring many players as well,” Martinez told Amazon Prime. “I expect more. 100 per cent. I expect more from our technical director, Jason Wilcox. “I have to be honest, as players we have to do more but it is also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night. “Tonight it is easy to blame the coach, easy to blame the players but also we have to see other areas.” United finished third in the Premier League last season to secure Champions League qualification for the first time in three years. The club spent about £155m on three midfielders but did not significantly reinforce other areas of the squad. Martinez also questioned the club’s tendency to change managers, arguing that other departments should be held accountable for the team’s shortcomings. “You can’t keep changing, changing, changing the manager. What about other areas? I can’t say more,” he said. “Last season we did everything, we created the base to create an amazing team.” The defender’s comments have drawn mixed reactions from former United players, with Wayne Rooney warning that the public criticism could damage the team’s unity. “Something like that will rip that dressing room apart,” Rooney said while analysing the interview on Amazon Prime. The former United captain said Martinez’s remarks were disrespectful to his teammates and could create further divisions within the squad. “It is disrespectful to his teammates. He is saying his teammates aren’t good enough,” Rooney said. Carrick, meanwhile, said he had not watched the full interview when asked about Martinez’s comments after the defeat. The United manager declined to make a detailed assessment, saying his immediate priority was to move the team forward. The defeat to Atletico has increased scrutiny of United’s recruitment strategy and the leadership of technical director Jason Wilcox, chief executive Omar Berrada and minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe. United have now gone five matches without a victory, with their last win coming against Azerbaijani side Sabah FK on September 10. Martinez, who joined United from Ajax in 2022, has one year remaining on his contract and has yet to agree an extension. title: New White House Press Secretary Under Fire After Brief Debut
body: New White House press secretary Katie Zachariah faced criticism after delivering a 14-minute briefing on her first day in the role, answering questions from just three journalists in an appearance that critics said failed to meet expectations. The former Newsmax commentator frequently read from her notes, paused during her presentation and stumbled over parts of her delivery. When she mentioned the “Department of War”, she smiled and briefly stopped. In response to a question about her personal background, she also confused the words “wife” and “president”. The questions came from journalists representing outlets that have generally taken favourable positions towards US President Donald Trump, prompting criticism that the briefing offered little meaningful scrutiny. A challenging role under Trump Zachariah faces a difficult task as Trump often acts as his own chief spokesperson, intervening frequently in public debate and setting the news agenda with statements, sometimes late at night. His confrontational relationship with the media also creates a demanding environment for anyone responsible for communicating his administration’s positions. Zachariah has said her goal is to promote and advance the president’s agenda. However, she did not mention the responsibility to provide the public with accurate information, an omission highlighted by critics of her first appearance. A long history of White House press secretaries The role has changed considerably since journalist George E. Akerson became the first White House press secretary under President Herbert Hoover in 1929. Over the decades, press secretaries have served as official sources of information, defenders of government policy and interlocutors — or adversaries — of journalists. During Trump’s second presidency, the position has taken on an increasingly confrontational character as the president frequently attacks media outlets over their coverage of his activities. Zachariah’s predecessor, Karoline Leavitt, left the position in August after adopting a consistently combative approach towards journalists. She regularly denounced what she considered biased reporting and once called a journalist’s question “stupid”. Trump, however, expressed satisfaction with Zachariah’s debut, calling her “excellent” shortly after the briefing as she stood behind him. Other reactions were less favourable. MS NOW cited an unnamed White House official who said Zachariah needed to improve quickly or risk breaking the record for the shortest tenure by Anthony Scaramucci, who served as White House communications director for just 11 days in 2017. Scaramucci commented on her first appearance on social media on Tuesday, writing: “I hope she does well.” Jen Psaki, a Greek-American who served as press secretary under former President Joe Biden and now presents programmes on MS NOW, offered a more pointed assessment on X. “This briefing was more like a Saturday Night Live skit… except it wasn’t,” she wrote. Praise for Trump and few questions Beyond the criticism of her delivery, Zachariah’s first briefing provided little new information. One of the most significant announcements concerned Kimberly Guilfoyle’s resignation as US ambassador to Greece following a request from the White House, according to the new press secretary. Most of the presentation focused on promoting the achievements and priorities of Trump’s second presidency. Zachariah described a “booming economy”, highlighted increased energy production and praised relations with Venezuela. She also used language underscoring the administration’s ambitions, saying Trump was working to secure the United States’ position in the Western Hemisphere “for centuries to come”. The question-and-answer session ended quickly. Zachariah called on journalists from Breitbart, Fox News and the Daily Mail, before answering one additional question as she prepared to leave. She also pledged to continue Leavitt’s policy of including so-called “new media” outlets in White House briefings. The category includes organisations that often take a favourable approach towards Trump. “We love new media and want to embrace them,” she said. Meanwhile, major news organisations, including CNN, MS NOW and Politico, are seeking to regain access to the White House after the administration excluded them the previous month. The government cited dissatisfaction with their coverage and accused them of spreading “fake news”. Whether Zachariah can meet the demands of the position will become clearer in the coming weeks. Her success will depend heavily on her relationship with Trump, who remains the dominant figure in his administration’s public communications. A longstanding tactic in political communication involves answering a different question when a journalist raises a difficult issue. In her first briefing, Zachariah adopted another approach: she took a small number of relatively unchallenging questions and brought the session to a swift close. The post New White House Press Secretary Under Fire After Brief Debut appeared first on Greek City Times .

title: Clergy Warns against New Age Excesses
body: Becky Uba Umenyili Nigerians have been advised to uphold the dignity of work and good labour against the fast-growing get-rich-quick syndrome acts like kidnapping, human trafficking, ritual practices and other illegal acts against human rights and societal development. In his message for the 2026 Catechetical Week programme held nationwide, the Chairman of the National Association Directors of Religious Education (NADRE), of the Catholic Church, Rev. Fr. Albert Ebosele, observed that most Nigerians, especially Christians, have engaged in excessive pursuit of power and wealth, occultism and syncretism (mixing Christianity with occultism), unhealthy attachments to irrelevant cultural practices for the purposes of sustenance, security and success. He noted that these immoral practices constitute auxiliary gods against the Biblical injunctions to have no other god except God Almighty and trust in Divine Providence and ethical business conduct, through observance of established norms and work ethics. The programme further enjoined all Christians and especially Catholics faithful to be agents of change against prosperity obsession and new-age idolatry, irresponsible use of social media, noting that without proper teaching, innocent people tend to believe that “every loud. voice has authority, every claimed miracle appears authentic and every trending spiritual practices seem harmless”, until proved otherwise. The programme therefore, called for perseverance in all good works and transparency in business deals for proper accountability in nation-building.

title: Partners warn Ukraine of ballistic missile threat during three waves of Russian attacks – military spox
body:
According to Ukrinform, Ukrainian Air Force Spokesperson Yuriy Ignat said this in a televised interview.
“A brief clarification on whether warnings were issued, as many people are asking whether our partners notified us. At around 22:40, we reported that no warnings about ballistic missiles had been received from our partners. However, during the next three waves of attacks, warnings from our partners about the use of ballistic missiles were issued,” he said.
As Ukrinform reported, President Volodymyr Zelensky had previously said that Ukraine received no warning from its partners about the ballistic missile strike on Kyiv involving five missiles in the evening of October 12.
The following day, Zelensky also said that Russian forces had attacked Kyiv with ballistic missiles the previous evening and that, once again, partners had provided no information about the missile launches.

title: [In This Economy] Will Sara Duterte be good for business and the economy?
body: Juicy revelations recently surfaced in the Senate impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, including alleged undeclared wealth that could reach P1.5 billion , continuing business interests (banned by the Constitution), and even supposed remittances from China and Hong Kong to a company linked to Duterte’s husband. The evidence is so overwhelming that the chances of a conviction seem to have spiked, at least from where I sit. In fact, as of Tuesday, October 13, the prosecution dropped 3 of 4 impeachment charges , seemingly confident that the remaining one on unexplained wealth can stand on its own. Until there is conviction, though, Sara Duterte continues to be a contender in the 2028 elections. In fact, based on the latest polling data , she’s a frontrunner. The problem that bugs me is that until now, Sara Duterte has said little about her specific plans or vision for the country, as well as economic reforms and policies she might put in place in case she wins. On October 13, she had an opportunity to lay out those plans at the Philippine Chamber of Commerce and Industry’s 52nd Philippine Business Conference and Expo ( watch video below ), held at the Manila Hotel. There, she called for respect for human rights, accountable government, and businesses free from political harassment. She also demanded integrity and competence from public officials. Play Video But are these exhortations credible? How did the Dutertes (Rodrigo and Sara) measure up to these standards when they had the power to put them into practice? Human rights Let’s start with a pretty bold statement: VP Sara said, “Imagine a Philippines where human rights are upheld, justice is fair, laws are applied and respected.” This one is jarring to hear because of everything that happened in her father’s drug war (2016–2022). Thousands were killed, possibly more than 30,000, and various human rights organizations documented widespread killings, arbitrary detention, and persistent impunity. All this culminated in the historic arrest in March 2025 of Rodrigo Duterte, who now awaits trial at The Hague. Will Sara do a repeat of the drug war? Will Sara assure the victims of the drug war that there will be no repeat, and that those who perpetrated abuses during her father’s regime will be held to account? Her speech offered no assurance that those abuses would never happen again. A few days ago, Thai authorities intercepted a drug shipment that’s supposed to be headed to the Philippines. VP Sara said in response: “We recognize the concerns surrounding the Philippines’ role in regional drug trafficking and express my deep regret that our country has become associated with this problem.” But during the impeachment trial, a bank witness testified that funds from Sara and Rodrigo Duterte’s joint account were used to purchase a manager’s check payable to Samuel “Sammy” Uy , whom former senator Antonio Trillanes IV has accused of involvement in the drug trade. Free speech, doing business In the PCCI speech, Sara also spoke of the need for people to freely express their opinions. Yet her father repeatedly threatened ABS-CBN over its franchise. In 2020, the broadcaster was ordered off the air after its franchise expired, and a House committee rejected its renewal . The Palace claimed neutrality despite Duterte’s very public hostility. Apart from this, Duterte also attacked Rappler and filed trumped-up charges left and right. Sara also asked her audience to imagine businesses that need not give to politicians just to be safe from harassment. She added: “Policies should be predictable. Businesses and individuals can plan for the future without fearing arbitrary government decisions.” But exactly the opposite happened during her father’s time. Policies were weaponized against Duterte’s perceived enemies, and Duterte infamously cursed and railed against prominent businesspeople . Who would forget Duterte’s capricious and abrupt closure of Boracay Island to tourists in 2018? Then in December 2019, Rodrigo Duterte threatened to jail the people behind Manila Water and Maynilad over their concession agreements . He also floated a military takeover of their operations. Sure, water contracts deserve scrutiny, but the government could’ve reviewed them through lawful processes without threatening businesspeople with imprisonment. This is what one might call “economic lawlessness,” and it’s a major turnoff for potential investors. Think about it: why commit money to a project that takes years to pay off if the president can threaten your company and upend its dealings with government? Such uncertainty makes investments riskier and political connections more valuable. Does Sara now think her father’s threats were wrong? Would she keep personal grudges out of regulatory decisions? These are basic questions for someone promising a predictable business environment. Competence and integrity Sara also declared that leaders should be open to investigation and held responsible for misconduct. Corruption, she said, drains resources from essential services. But this is precisely the reason why she’s been impeached not once but twice. Her father’s track record in this regard is also questionable. Recall the Senate investigation into pandemic procurement involving Pharmally . In October 2021, Rodrigo Duterte directed executive officials and employees to stop attending the Senate blue ribbon committee’s hearings on the 2020 Commission on Audit report. His government denied corruption allegations while obstructing the basic scrutiny that should have tested them. Meanwhile, Sara also has her own spending to explain, and this brings us to the current impeachment trial at the Senate. Her office spent P125 million in confidential funds in 11 days in 2022. State auditors disallowed roughly P73 million for violating confidential-fund rules, findings her camp contests. Sure, spending quickly alone proves no wrongdoing, and an audit disallowance is no criminal conviction. But how does she reconcile these findings with her talk of integrity? On education, Sara called for capable teachers and quality learning. As education secretary from 2022 to 2024, however, she defended a P150-million confidential-fund request for 2024 on national-security grounds, before eventually dropping it. Why prioritize secret spending in an agency struggling to provide the basics of education? Her father’s education record was disastrous as well. By August 2021, UNICEF reported that the Philippines was among only five countries that had not started in-person classes since the pandemic began. More than 27 million students were affected by the prolonged school closures, which meant lost learning and poorer prospects for future earnings and our economy’s productivity. Third plague? Sara’s concerns about the cost of living, jobs, and public services also invite a closer look at the previous Duterte administration. In my new book, Twin Plagues: How Duterte and Covid-19 Wrecked the Philippine Economy , I examine how her father’s governance compounded the pandemic’s damage. COVID-19 hit countries around the world. How to protect livelihoods and keep essential services working depended on government decisions, and to this day Duterte hasn’t answered for this. Even before COVID-19, Filipino households suffered under Rodrigo Duterte through the 2018 inflation surge. Higher world oil prices and food-supply problems contributed, while the administration’s excise-tax increases added to prices. Sure, the current Marcos administration deserves criticism for its failures. But is VP Sara well placed to do this? What exactly in her track record suggests that she can do a much better job, if at all? She needs to explain her own decisions and tell us which of her father’s policies she would continue or abandon. All in all, VP Sara’s speech on October 13 amounts to breathtaking hypocrisy. At the same time she turns on the current Marcos administration, she turns a blind eye to the disastrous presidency of her own father—and also the many red flags in her own track record. This country already paid dearly for twin plagues from 2016 to 2022, namely Duterte and COVID-19. We can’t afford a third plague come 2028 in the form of yet another Duterte. – Rappler.com Jan Carlo “JC” Punongbayan, PhD, is an associate professor at the University of the Philippines School of Economics. His professional experience includes the Securities and Exchange Commission, the World Bank Office in Manila, the Far Eastern University Public Policy Center, and the National Economic and Development Authority. JC writes a weekly economics column for Rappler. He is also co-founder of UsapangEcon.com and co-host of Usapang Econ Podcast. His first book, False Nostalgia: The Marcos “Golden Age” Myths and How to Debunk Them, was published by Ateneo de Manila University Press in February 2023. His second book, Twin Plagues: How Duterte and COVID-19 Wrecked the Philippine Economy, was published by Penguin Random House SEA in June 2026. Follow him on Instagram ( @jcpunongbayan ). title: Starlink restrictions disrupt Ukrainian army operations, ex-adviser says
body:
MOSCOW, October 14. /TASS/. SpaceX introduced restrictions on the operation of Starlink terminals for the Ukrainian army overnight, disrupting its operations, Sergey Sternenko, a former adviser to Ukraine’s defense minister, said.
"Retrictions on the operation of Starlink terminals were introduced last night. Internet access disruptions were recorded when moving at speeds of over 160 km/h. As a result, a number of important missions were disrupted," he wrote on Telegram.
Sternenko suggested that SpaceX had acted at the request of the US administration.
Politico Europe reported earlier that US President Donald Trump could cut off US intelligence support for Kiev or pressure Elon Musk to disable SpaceX’s Starlink internet service, on which Ukraine’s military heavily relies. Zelensky said the same day that the US had not warned Ukraine about Russian missile launches the previous night.

title: Odisha Governor Inaugurates Boeing Sukanya Program STEM Lab and Aeromodeling Training Center in Bargarh
body:
BARGARH. The Hon’ble Governor of Odisha, Dr. Hari Babu Kambhampati, on Oct 11, 2026 inaugurated a Boeing Sukanya Program STEM lab and Aeromodeling Training Center at The Kosala School in Bargarh district, Odisha. The facility will benefit more than 2,000 students annually.



The Hon’ble Governor was joined byMr. Nihar Ranjan Mahanand, Hon’ble MLA, Attabira; Mr.. Irasis Acharya, Hon’ble MLA, Bhatli; Mr. Aswini Sarangi, Hon’ble, MLA, Bargarh; Sri Aditya Goyal, IAS, Collector and District Magistrate, Bargarh; Mr. Murali Krishna Gannamani, Chairman, The Kosala School; the school principal; teachers; students; and leaders from Boeing and the Learning Links Foundation at the inauguration ceremony. The Governor toured the facility and interacted with students at a student innovation showcase, where students demonstrated projects, prototypes, and aeromodeling flight activities.

"Our vision is to continue to expand access to quality STEM education where it has not reached before," said Dr. Hari Babu Kambhampati, Hon’ble Governor of Odisha. "The Boeing Sukanya Program STEM lab and Aeromodeling Training Center at The Kosala School will help nurture a scientific temper that will inspire students to be part of India’s burgeoning technology industry.” 

Mr. Salil Gupte, President, Boeing India & South Asia, said, "We are honored that the Governor personally dedicated the STEM lab and the aeromodeling facility to the children of Bargarh. Both initiatives will provide an opportunity for Bargarh children to dream big and aspire to careers in Indian aviation and STEM.”

Mr. Murali Krishna Gannamani, CEO & MD, Fluentgrid Ltd. and Chairman of The Kosala School, said, “We are incredibly proud to host this facility at The Kosala School. Established in 1979, The Kosala School is a not-for-profit institution, affiliated to CBSE and one of the first Residential Schools in Western Odisha. Partnering with Boeing and Learning Links Foundation allows us to provide our students with exceptional learning opportunities and practical exposure beyond traditional textbooks. The Hon’ble Governor’s presence is doubly inspiring, and we sincerely thank him for making this launch a truly special occasion for all of us.”

Ananda Cityzen, the CSR wing of Fluentgrid Ltd., is pleased to partner with the Boeing Sukanya Program to set up this STEM lab and Aeromodeling Center. Ananda Cityzen has also added an AI lab to the facility. Together, these facilities will offer students of The Kosala School and surrounding schools the opportunity to learn, experience and experiment with STEM, aerospace, and AI concepts.



The newly inaugurated learning spaces feature:

 	The Boeing Sukanya Program STEM lab: A space enabling students to explore robotics, physical computing, electronics, artificial intelligence, rapid prototyping, and aerospace concepts.
 	The Aeromodeling Training Center: A center focused on teaching the practical mechanics of aviation, aerodynamics, aircraft design, flight, and model aircraft construction.

The Boeing Sukanya Program is implemented in partnership with Learning Links Foundation (LLF), a Boeing Global Engagement nonprofit partner for education and skilling initiatives in India. Earlier in January this year, the Boeing Sukanya Program STEM labs were inaugurated in the Sambalpur, Rairakhol, and Kuchinda districts of Odisha.



Dr. Anjlee Prakash, Chairperson, Learning Links Foundation, said, “We are proud to collaborate with Boeing to bring immersive, hands-on STEM learning to students in Odisha. By creating spaces where young people can explore, question, and experiment, these labs are nurturing curiosity and confidence while strengthening teachers and the broader school ecosystem. Our shared ambition is to inspire more students, especially girls, to see themselves as innovators and pursue pathways to STEM careers.” 

Launched in 2024 by the Prime Minister of India, Mr. Narendra Modi, the Boeing Sukanya Program aligns with India’s vision to increase women’s participation in aviation. As part of the program, Boeing and LLF continue to establish STEM labs in government schools across India. The program also offers scholarships to girls to pursue their dream of becoming pilots, helping build a strong talent pipeline to increase women’s participation in India’s aviation growth.

title: Ukrainian military says SpaceX restricted Starlink terminals without warning
body: SpaceX has restricted the Starlink satellite communication terminals used by Ukrainian troops at the front, slowing the drones that rely on them, according to Serhii Beskrestnov , an adviser to the Ukrainian president, and Serhii Sternenko , a former adviser to the Ukrainian defense minister and a volunteer. The news outlet Ukrainska Pravda, citing the military , reported that the restrictions targeted Starshield, the faster military version of Starlink used by drone operators. One commander sent the outlet a video showing two Ukrainian drones climbing into the sky with their connection “dropping out,” leaving them unable to continue their mission. A source in the Ukrainian Armed Forces told Ukrainska Pravda that standard Starlink terminals installed on drones work at speeds of up to 160 kilometers per hour (99 mph), but that speed is not enough for some missions, which is why drone operators use Starshield, the military version of Starlink. “Our defense forces did not receive any warning about these restrictions, and it led to the failure of a number of missions. It’s obvious that this action can’t be a coincidence and is connected to the current political situation,” Beskrestnov wrote. Volodymyr Zelensky said over the past two days that Western partners did not warn Ukraine about missile strikes on Kyiv. The United States told Ukraine it had not shared intelligence because of poor weather conditions, according to Politico. The United States threatened last week to halt intelligence sharing with Ukraine and block arms deliveries unless Kyiv agreed to halt strikes on Russian oil refineries, according to reporting from the Financial Times. title: IMF Warns Nigeria Against Restoring Petrol Subsidy
body: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has advised the federal government against restoring a broad petrol subsidy, recommending targeted support for vulnerable households to cushion the impact of rising energy costs. The Fund said blanket petrol subsidies are expensive, often benefit higher-income consumers disproportionately, and worsen fiscal pressures amid rising borrowing costs. The Director of the IMF’s Fiscal Affairs Department, Rodrigo Valdes, stated this during a press briefing on the Fiscal Monitor at the 2026 Annual Meetings of the IMF and World Bank in Bangkok. His comments followed a question about how the Fund could recommend allowing energy prices to reflect scarcity when higher fuel prices in Nigeria could raise transport costs, worsen inflation, and deepen poverty, particularly as the government faces calls to restore the petrol subsidy ahead of an election year. “Protecting people is not the same as protecting the price of fuels,” Valdés said. He said fuel subsidies or measures that prevented prices from fully adjusting to an energy shock had cost countries between 1 per cent and 1.5 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 2026. He said the government should instead use social safety nets and household data to identify people who need assistance. The Federal Government recently announced a 30-day petrol discount at Nigerian National Petroleum Company (NNPC) Limited retail stations, with priority for public transport operators, to cushion the impact of rising fuel prices.
