title: Education Minister appeals to GAUA to call off strike, resume work on October 19
body: Haruna Iddrisu, the Minister of Education, has appealed to the leadership of the Ghana Association of University Administrators (GAUA) to call off their strike and allow academic activities to resume at public universities by October 19, 2026. The Minister urged their leadership to return to the negotiation table with the Fair Wages and Salaries Commission (FWSC) to resolve the outstanding issues. “I will issue a directive to the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission by close of the week to request public universities to reopen by October 19, 2026,” the Minister announced at a meeting with the leadership of GAUA on Monday. He expressed the expectation that the striking workers – GAUA – would return to work by that date, subject to continued engagement on their outstanding concerns. The Minister said the strike had already affected the reopening schedules of the University of Ghana and the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, which had announced postponements of their reopening dates. He expressed the hope that the universities would reopen on October 19 to enable academic work to resume and prevent further disruption to the academic calendar. “I want to request GAUA to consider calling off the strike action for normal academic work to proceed and continue throughout all our university campuses across Ghana,” he said. The Minister clarified that his role in the discussions was to facilitate negotiations on behalf of the Government, explaining that salary negotiations fell outside the direct mandate of the Ministry of Education. He, however, acknowledged that the Government remained the employer of the affected workers and assured the unions that their legitimate concerns would receive priority attention. On issues that could be addressed immediately, the Minister said the Ministry would expedite action through the GTEC to request public universities extend the retirement rollover arrangement to all senior members, in line with previous practice. He disclosed that the Minister of Finance had issued a warrant for the payment of the one-off research allowance, adding that the relevant institutions were expected to complete the necessary administrative and payroll processes to facilitate payment. On the issue of market premium, the Minister said the matter, including the restoration of parity, had been referred to the FWSC for further engagement with the unions. He expressed optimism that the Commission would take the necessary action within its mandate and communicate the consequential steps required from the Ministry of Finance to address the unions’ concerns. The Minister recalled that the Minister of Finance had committed to a negotiated 40 per cent adjustment to the market premium and non-basic allowance, saying the Government considered that matter to have made progress towards resolution. He urged the union leaders to consult their members and reconsider the strike in the interest of students and the preservation of the academic calendar. The Minister said the Government’s efforts to align the reopening of schools at all levels in September were intended to improve the coordination of the country’s academic calendar, stressing that further disruptions could undermine that objective.

title: MI5 Chief calls Russia UK’s No. 1 aggressor
body:
This is stated in the annual threat assessment delivered by MI5 Director General Ken McCallum, Ukrinform reports.
“Russia remains aggressor number one, as Putin’s Kremlin continues to lash out at the UK and its allies,” McCallum said.
According to the agency, Moscow has no intention of starting a war with Western countries at present, but has launched a large-scale hybrid influence campaign across Europe.
“The Russian military and intelligence services are once again escalating their attempts at hybrid warfare – being careful to stay below the NATO Article V threshold it’d be foolish for them to cross. This means Russia is using tactics that stop short – though sometimes not much short – of conventional conflict,” the intelligence chief said.
According to him, hybrid attacks are often carried out through proxies, and Russia consistently denies any involvement. However, British security services are accumulating an ever-growing body of evidence to the contrary.
“With its traditional covert footprint eviscerated by almost 1000 expulsions since the invasion, the Kremlin’s global toolkit is weak. So we see them scrambling to pay criminals to do their bidding. Or exploiting naïve volunteers, as in the now-designated GRU Volunteer Corps,” the MI5 chief said.
“These are not the actions of a great power with the strategic upper hand,” he added.
As Ukrinform reported, Britain’s domestic intelligence agency MI5 issued a public warning that Chinese intelligence is using a front company to pay British researchers for access to research and steal secrets from high-tech projects. Beijing denies the allegations.

title: Aegean Airlines CEO Dimitris Gerogiannis Steps Down; Michalis Kouveliotis Takes Over
body: Aegean Airlines’ long-serving CEO and co-founder Dimitris Gerogiannis is stepping down after 20 years in the role. Deputy CEO and CFO Michalis Kouveliotis takes over immediately. Michalis Kouveliotis Takes Over Gerogiannis will remain as an advisor with oversight of the Technical Base and Training Center during the transition. Kouveliotis has been CFO since before Aegean’s listing and has served as deputy CEO since early 2025, coordinating the company’s business divisions. Chairman Eftichios Vassilakis said Kouveliotis had already demonstrated his ability to support the airline through growth and crisis and had led the transition process. He emphasised the need to empower the second generation of executives while preserving Aegean’s values of service quality and agility. Aegean plans to add long-haul destinations as Airbus A321LRs join the fleet. The airline has recently limited capacity growth into 2027 amid higher fuel costs and regional pressures. The post Aegean Airlines CEO Dimitris Gerogiannis Steps Down; Michalis Kouveliotis Takes Over appeared first on Greek City Times .

title: Mahama assures Assemblies of God of support for World Congress
body: President John Dramani Mahama has assured the World Assemblies of God Fellowship of the Government’s continued support for the successful hosting of its World Congress in Accra. He gave the assurance when the Executive Committee of the Fellowship, led by Reverend Dominic Yeo, Global Chairman, and Reverend Stephen Wengam, General Superintendent of the Assemblies of God, Ghana, paid a courtesy call on him. The Congress, being held on African soil for the first time in the 115-year history of the Assemblies of God worldwide, is expected to bring together church leaders and members from across the globe. President Mahama welcomed the delegation to Ghana and pledged the Government’s commitment to ensuring that the event was peaceful, successful and impactful. Reflecting on his personal association with the Assemblies of God Church, the President said: “I have no regrets.” He commended the current leadership of the Church for its growth and transformation over the years. Rev Wengam said preparations for the Congress had been completed and expressed appreciation to President Mahama and the Government for their support in organising the event. He explained that the morning session of the Congress, originally scheduled to take place at the Independence Square, had been relocated to the Grand Arena of the Accra International Conference Centre due to technical challenges. According to him, the new venue offers a more conducive environment for the programme. Rev Yeo congratulated Ghana on becoming the first African country to host the World Congress, drawing a parallel with the nation’s historic status as the first country in sub-Saharan Africa to attain political independence. He expressed the Executive Committee’s gratitude to President Mahama and the Government for the support provided towards the successful organisation of the Congress. The Global Chairman also commended the President’s leadership, describing it as visionary and transformational, and cited economic stability and road infrastructure development as evidence of that leadership. He encouraged President Mahama to continue to represent Christ well in politics and remain steadfast in his faith. As part of the visit, Rev Yeo presented Congress souvenirs to the President and led the delegation in prayers for him and the prosperity of Ghana.

title: El-Rufai’s case on alleged funds misappropriation adjourned to Nov 30
body: The Kaduna State High Court on Tuesday adjourned the alleged fund misappropriation case against former Governor Nasir El-Rufai until November 30 and December 1 for the continuation of the cross-examination of a Department of State Services (DSS) digital forensic expert. The adjournment came after the court overruled an objection by El-Rufai’s defence team to the testimony of the forensic expert, Shegun Kayode, who was subpoenaed to testify in the case. Presiding judge, Justice Darius Khobo, ruled that the prosecution could call the witness despite the fact that his name and summary of evidence were not included in the prosecution’s witness list. The judge held that the defence’s right to a fair hearing could be protected by allowing it to cross-examine the witness. 2027: Why APC opted for ‘Rainbow campaign council’ Strike: FCT council chairman begs teachers to resume work The ruling followed an objection by El-Rufai’s senior counsel, Paul Erokoro, SAN, who argued that the defence had not received the witness’s evidence summary or the subpoena. Erokoro said the omission denied the defence adequate notice to prepare for the cross-examination and understand the case it was required to answer. However, counsel to the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC), Ayodele Adedipe, argued that failure to include a subpoenaed witness in the proof of evidence did not automatically make the testimony inadmissible. In his ruling, Justice Khobo confirmed that the witness had been subpoenaed through an order signed by the court on June 30, 2026. The judge said the defence could address its concerns about fair hearing through cross-examination. Earlier, Kayode told the court that the DSS conducted a forensic examination of communication records and audio recordings allegedly linked to El-Rufai and some associates at the request of the ICPC. He said the exercise followed a formal request from the commission and approval by the director-general of the DSS. According to the witness, specialised software revealed two-way communications involving El-Rufai, his brother and another person between October 25 and 28, 2025. He said the findings prompted further analysis of audio recordings obtained from a communication intelligence server. Kayode said the DSS telecommunications intelligence unit provided the call data records through a secure server in line with the service’s procedures for preserving electronic evidence. He told the court that his team made four duplicate copies of the original audio recording while preserving the original to protect the integrity of the evidence. The witness said the examination involved analysing vocal characteristics, background noise and electromagnetic interference. He said the results indicated that the audio originated from a human voice in a natural environment rather than being artificially generated. Kayode added that he conducted biometric voice analysis using another forensic tool to examine the speaker’s voice. According to him, the recording allegedly contained a conversation between El-Rufai and his elder brother about plans to liquidate a company, Singularity, halt an ongoing Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) case involving the company and prevent an investigation into another company, IHS. He further alleged that the conversation referred to $500,000 and $100,000 purportedly set aside to settle EFCC officials and an intermediary. The allegations formed part of the witness’s account of the forensic findings and have yet to be established by the court. Kayode said he prepared a detailed forensic investigative report and submitted it to the court as evidence. However, Erokoro objected to the tendering of the document, arguing that the prosecution could not introduce additional evidence through a subpoenaed witness without following the appropriate legal procedure. In response, Adedipe described the objection as unfounded, arguing that the court had earlier ruled that evidence from a subpoenaed witness did not necessarily have to be included in the proof of evidence. After hearing arguments from both parties, Justice Khobo overruled the objection and allowed Kayode to continue his testimony. The judge also said the defence could obtain a certified true copy of the evidence through the court’s registry. The ICPC is prosecuting El-Rufai on nine counts bordering on alleged corruption and abuse of office during his tenure as governor of Kaduna State. The commission alleged that he induced the state government to release about N11 billion to an unregistered entity for a light rail project that was never executed. It also accused him of approving and receiving about N289.8 million as severance allowance, far above the approximately N20 million he was legally entitled to, thereby conferring a corrupt advantage on himself. In another count, the commission accused him of mismanaging more than $1.08 million from a World Bank loan to the state in violation of the loan agreement. The ICPC further alleged that he conspired with an associate, said to be at large, to offer monetary inducements to federal investigators to compromise an ongoing investigation involving a private firm. Other charges include the alleged unlawful award of a N4.6 billion CCTV contract in Kaduna metropolis in violation of procurement laws, as well as conferring undue advantage on an associate through the contract. El-Rufai had earlier denied all the allegations against him.

title: Google Finland head apologises for forest clearances at data centre sites
body:
Google's Finland chief says the company believed its forest clearances complied with the law, and that authorities knew of its plans.
Google’s Finland country manager Antti Järvinen has apologised for extensive forest clearances at the company’s data centre sites in Muhos and Kajaani.
330 hectares of forest have been cleared in Muhos and just under 200 hectares in Kajaani.
Järvinen spoke to the media on Tuesday after the company had previously commented on the controversy through written statements.
"The reason I am only speaking to the media now is that there has been a lot to investigate. I understand that people have been looking for me, too," Järvinen said.
Google has faced criticism since the Finnish Association for Nature Conservation accused the company of illegally clearing forests in Muhos and Kajaani without the required environmental impact assessments.
Last week, the Finnish Supervisory Agency (LVV) ordered Google to suspend the work .
Järvinen said Google and its subsidiary had acted to the best of their understanding of the law at the time. He said the projects had been advanced in cooperation with authorities and experts.
Google has repeatedly maintained that authorities were aware of its plans for the forest clearances.
However, when asked which authorities it believed had been informed and how that understanding had arisen, Järvinen declined to name them.
"We don't think it would be useful to start debating this publicly. This is our project, and we take full responsibility for what has happened," he said.
Järvinen said he would leave it to the authorities to comment on their own involvement.
Muhos municipality's building inspector told newspaper Helsingin Sanomat that Google's lawyers had pressured him into granting permission for preparatory work. Asked whether Google had pressured municipalities, Järvinen denied this.
"I don't recognise this kind of behaviour. I've seen the memo from that meeting, after which the permit was granted. There were no lawyers from our side present at that meeting. Our representatives and our construction consultant's representatives were there, after which the permit was granted," Järvinen said.
He also denied that Google had rushed the clearances to get ahead of environmental assessments, saying the project had been "advanced quite swiftly" but "very openly, in good cooperation with all the different partners and local authorities."
He also denied receiving pressure to speed things up from outside Finland.
Questions have been raised about how Google could have proceeded without understanding the requirements of Finland's environmental impact assessment legislation.
Järvinen said the environmental assessment process had been part of the project's development throughout.
"All decisions were made based on the best understanding we had of the legislation at the time," he said.
He denied that the company’s actions were due to a lack of expertise, inexperience or negligence.
"I am extremely sorry that we are in this situation. I want to apologise for that," Järvinen said.
In addition to Muhos and Kajaani, Google is building data centres in Hamina and Vaala.
Last month it was announced that the tech giant was investing 13 billion euro s in Finland.

title: Akpabio insists on jail term as Senate considers suicide bill
body: A bill seeking to decriminalise attempted suicide in Nigeria has passed second reading in the Senate, despite Senate President Godswill Akpabio insisting that survivors should remain liable to imprisonment. Akpabio argued that removing the penalties could encourage attempted suicide. “If you attempt suicide, make sure you die. Anyone who attempts and fails will go to jail,” he said during Tuesday’s plenary. Despite his position, the bill secured the support of a majority of senators through a voice vote. It was subsequently referred to the Senate Committees on Health (Secondary and Tertiary) and Judiciary, Human Rights and Legal Matters for further legislative action. Sponsored by Senator Asuquo Ekpenyong, representing Cross River South, the bill seeks to establish a legal framework for suicide prevention, treatment and support for survivors. Leading the debate, Ekpenyong said the National Mental Health Act recognises attempted suicide as a mental health emergency requiring medical intervention, while Section 327 of the Criminal Code and Section 231 of the Penal Code criminalise the act. He said the conflicting provisions required legislative intervention. The senator argued that criminalising attempted suicide could discourage survivors from seeking help, encourage families to conceal such incidents and prevent health workers from promptly reporting cases. He said the proposed legislation would replace punitive measures with medical assessment, treatment and continued support for survivors. Lawmakers supporting the bill said people experiencing severe emotional distress needed professional healthcare and empathy rather than detention. Under existing criminal laws, attempted suicide remains punishable by imprisonment, although the applicable provisions and penalties vary across jurisdictions. Section 327 of the Criminal Code provides for up to one year’s imprisonment, while Section 231 of the Penal Code prescribes up to one year’s imprisonment, a fine or both.

title: Greek Shipowners Order 12 Tankers from China’s Hengli Shipyard
body: Greek shipowners have placed new orders for 12 tankers at China’s Hengli Heavy Industries, including six VLCCs, two Suezmaxes and four LR2s. George Prokopiou’s Dynacom Tankers Management is among the buyers. Dynacom’s cooperation with Hengli already exceeds 50 vessels. The six VLCCs alone are valued at approximately $840 million, or about $140 million each. The total cost of the order is higher, as prices for the other six ships have not been disclosed. Over the past three years, Hengli has secured orders for 177 ships from Greek interests worth around $10.2 billion. Clients include Dynacom, Capital, Evalend, Thenamaris and Eurobulk. The yard currently holds a backlog of 69 VLCCs, ranking it first globally in that category. The orders come amid high tanker freight rates. Greek owners are seeking modern tonnage while managing the risk of future overcapacity. Source: Shanghai Securities News, Xinde Maritime News The post Greek Shipowners Order 12 Tankers from China’s Hengli Shipyard appeared first on Greek City Times .

title: Ghana must prioritise home-grown AI solutions to meet national needs – UNDP
body: Ms Shaima Hussein, Deputy Resident Representative of the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), has urged Ghana to prioritise locally developed artificial intelligence (AI) solutions that address national needs, strengthen public institutions and safeguard the country’s digital sovereignty. She said digital transformation efforts must focus on solutions that responded to Ghana’s development priorities rather than relying solely on technologies developed elsewhere. “What we need to support here is a local solution. And that’s actually the ultimate goal of our digital portfolio,” she said. Ms Hussein made the call at the opening of a three-day Digital and AI Champions Training for government officers selected from Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs), Monday in Accra. The training, organised by the Ministry of Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations in partnership with UNDP, with funding from the Government of Japan, is under the Accelerating Public Sector Digital Transformation through Capacity Building programme. The programme sought to equip public officials with the knowledge and skills to identify institutional challenges, adopt appropriate digital solutions and improve government efficiency. Ms Hussein said Ghana had established a strong foundation for digital transformation through initiatives such as the Ghana Card, interoperable payment systems and Ghana.gov, but needed to strengthen public institutions’ ability to use digital infrastructure, data and AI to improve service delivery. “We need to support local solutions, local systems, and systems that speak to the needs of the country and respect its sovereignty,” she said. She said responsible AI adoption required institutional capacity, effective data governance and ethical safeguards, adding that public officials must be equipped to assess AI solutions, protect public data and retain responsibility for decisions made using such technologies. The Digital and AI Champions Training, Ms Hussein would therefore help participants identify data gaps and institutional barriers within their respective ministries and determine where coordinated interventions could deliver the greatest impact. She said an AI accelerator component would provide a practical pathway for developing use cases by clarifying problems, assessing institutional readiness and risks, and designing responsible experiments. At the end of the training, Ms Hussein said the UNDP and the Ministry would convene a strategic dialogue to examine digital governance priorities and agree on next steps towards developing an integrated digital and AI portfolio across government. The initiative, she said, aimed to equip 50 government officers as certified Digital and AI Champions, while strengthening the capacity of 40 chief directors and 120 directors to commission, procure, govern and lead digital initiatives. Mr Emmanuel Ofori, Director of Innovations at the Ministry of Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, urged public sector institutions to treat AI adoption as a strategic management and decision-making priority rather than the sole responsibility of information technology professionals. “AI is for decision making. It’s a decision making or decision support technology. It is not IT,” he said. Mr Ofori noted that Ghana had made significant progress in digital transformation through initiatives such as digital government services, national digital identification and interconnected mobile money services, which had helped improve access, efficiency and interactions between citizens and public institutions. However, he stressed that the next phase of the country’s digital transformation must move beyond individual technologies and isolated projects towards a more coordinated, problem-driven approach. He described the Digital Champions initiative as an important step towards building the capacity needed to accelerate public sector innovation. He, therefore, urged participants to identify operational bottlenecks, improve the use of data and explore how digital technologies could address challenges within their institutions. “The success of this programme will be measured by what changes because you were here. When you return to your respective institutions, I hope you will carry with you new perspectives, practical ideas and confidence to question processes that can be improved,” he added. Madam Izumi Kume, Coordinator for Economic Cooperation at the Embassy of Japan, said the training reflected Japan’s commitment to supporting Ghana’s digital transformation through capacity building and local ownership. She encouraged participants to apply the knowledge acquired to improve public administration and deliver better services to citizens.

title: Sokoto Govt, WAEC review 2026 examinations
body: The Sokoto State Government and the West African Examinations Council (WAEC) have reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening the education sector as stakeholders met to review the conduct of the 2026 examinations, assess challenges, and discuss the way forward. The Permanent Secretary, Sokoto State Ministry of Basic and Secondary Education, Dr. Sanusi Aliyu Binji, stated this while chairing the meeting of the WAEC State Committee in Sokoto State. Dr. Binji said the state government valued its partnership with WAEC, noting that the council plays a vital role in the education sector, particularly in maintaining examination standards and promoting academic excellence. He stated that the administration of Governor Ahmad Aliyu Sokoto, FCNA, had paid examination fees for students, including WAEC fees, for the 2026 examination year. The Permanent Secretary also expressed the state government’s satisfaction with WAEC’s conduct of examinations in Sokoto State, reaffirming the government’s commitment to supporting initiatives that promote quality education. Speaking on behalf of the WAEC Zonal Coordinator in Sokoto, the Deputy Director, Engr. I. O. Omogbai, commended the Ministry of Basic and Secondary Education and the state government for their commitment to educational development. Engr. Omogbai explained that the annual State Council meeting provides an important platform for stakeholders to review examination activities, assess successes, identify challenges, and develop strategies for improvement. He noted that several issues relating to the conduct of the 2026 examinations were discussed, with participants sharing observations and recommendations aimed at improving future examinations. In his remarks, the Director of Examination Matters, Abubakar Abdullahi, welcomed members and highlighted the importance of the meeting in reviewing examination activities, addressing concerns, and strengthening collaboration among stakeholders. He observed that Sokoto State had not experienced any significant challenges in the conduct of the 2026 examinations so far. The Director of Senior Secondary Schools, Muhammad Rabiu, also contributed to the discussions, alongside other stakeholders in the education sector. Among the stakeholders who attended the meeting were the President of the All Nigeria Confederation of Principals of Secondary Schools (ANCOPSS), Sokoto State, Bello Abubakar; the Sokoto State Chairman of the Nigeria Union of Teachers (NUT), Comrade Murtala Muhammad; and the State Chairman of the Association of Private School Proprietors, Ahmed S/Fada, (Katukan Dange) Other relevant stakeholders in the education sector were also in attendance. The meeting reaffirmed the importance of sustained collaboration among the Sokoto State Government, WAEC, school administrators, teachers’ unions, private school proprietors, and other education stakeholders in ensuring credible examinations and improving educational standards across the state.

title: Mahama truly cares – Obuobia Darko-Opoku
body: Adjoa Obuobia Darko-Opoku, the Administrator, Ghana Medical Trust Fund (GMTF), has urged Ghanaians to always remember that President John Mahama feels their burden as his own and moves to act, not just sympathise. During the fourth stop of the Fund’s nationwide regional stakeholder engagement at Ho, she said the Fund was created to end the painful cycle where a single diagnosis like cancer, kidney disease, a cardiovascular condition, stroke or complications of diabetes threw an entire Ghanaian family into financial hardship. The GMTF, a national statutory fund established to mobilise sustainable financing for specialised medical care for people living with chronic Non-Communicable Diseases (NCDs), is an initiative of President Mahama to provide financial support and specialised care for Ghanaians suffering from chronic NCDs not fully covered by the National Health Insurance Scheme. Positioned at the apex of Ghana’s three-tier health financing system, the GMTF, popularly known as “Mahama Cares” complements Free Primary Health Care (FPHC) and the NHIS by closing the critical financing gap for high-cost, specialised treatment that often falls beyond the routine NHIS coverage. Madam Darko-Opoku noted that the burden went beyond the patient, as relatives were forced to abandon work to provide care, children’s education disrupted, savings depleted and family assets sold to keep treatment going. “These are the circumstances that led the government to establish the Trust Fund,” she said. “In line with President Mahama’s vision, we have been entrusted with building an institution that supports eligible Ghanaians who require high-cost treatment for chronic non-communicable diseases and strengthens the healthcare system.” Madam Darko-Opoku explained that the Fund embarked on a nationwide assessment of teaching hospitals and major referral facilities to understand the real challenges in specialised care. The exercise showed that financial support alone would not be enough if diagnostic services remained weak, equipment inadequate and specialist numbers were limited. She said that engagement informed the Fund’s current operational four interconnected pillars – financial support for eligible patients, provision of medical equipment and infrastructure, specialist training and capacity development, and research and innovation. Touching on progress so far, the Administrator revealed that the Fund had piloted its systems with 50 patients nationwide, developed a medicines list and tariffs in collaboration with specialists, and operationalised the GMTF Care platform. She added that infrastructure interventions had begun, including the restoration of the cardiac catheterisation laboratory at Korle Bu Teaching Hospital and ongoing cardiology centre projects at Komfo Anokye and Tamale Teaching Hospitals to expand access to dialysis and other critical services. Madam Darko-Opoku commended Ho Teaching Hospital and the University of Health and Allied Sciences (UHAS) for their role in clinical care, training and research, describing them as essential partners. She appealed to traditional leaders, Members of Parliament, religious leaders, health professionals and the media to help carry accurate information about the Fund’s mandate, eligibility criteria and access processes to communities across the region. “Always remember and never forget that truly, Mahama Cares,” she emphasised. Prof Lydia Aziato, UHAS Vice-Chancellor who is an oncology nurse and passionate about breast cancer described the GMTF as an answered prayer, recalling a quote from a breast cancer patient, in those days when there was no one to talk to patients. Patients were just left alone with the diagnosis, and many resorted to faith and by the time they realised it was not a spiritual problem, the disease had advanced, creating huge burden in terms of cost of care, Prof Aziato added. She commended government for the three-tier health financing system, saying the FPHC would help detect these cases early and by the time they got to the hospitals the disease could be treated successfully and, in most cases, cured so the women could live their full years on earth. Prof. Aziato urged women to detect early, treat early because someone cared, and encouraged all who had the disease not to hide, but be bold and take advantage of the opportunity to seek medical care at the hospital.

title: Google Releases Gemini 4 Argon API With 1M Token Output Limit
body:
Google DeepMind has made Gemini 4 Argon generally available to developers, enterprises and paid Gemini subscribers. Gemini 4 Argon is a sparse mixture-of-experts frontier model from Google built for long, multi-step work. Its target domains are coding, finance, legal, science and cybersecurity. Google first announced Argon on September 30 for a small group of cyber defenders. It now reaches the paid Gemini API at $2 input and $10 output per million tokens. The key change for developers is output length: Argon can write up to 1M tokens in one response. TL;DR Size: Parameter count not disclosed (sparse MoE). 1M token window shared by input and output. Runs on: Google’s cloud only, via Gemini API, AI Studio and Gemini platform. Trained on TPUs. No open weights. Performance: Leads Google’s table on knowledge work, long context and video. Mixed on agentic coding. Best: 91.7% on LVBench (long video understanding). Worst: 55.0% on FrontierSWE v2, last of 4 models in Google’s table. What is Gemini 4 Argon? According to the model card , Argon is a new model, not a fine-tune of an earlier Gemini. It is a large-scale sparse MoE transformer with native multimodal support. It accepts text, images, audio and video, and it outputs text. Google trained it on TPUs using JAX and ML Pathways. The knowledge cutoff is March 2026. Google has not disclosed total or active parameter counts. How does the 1M token output limit work? Google raised the output limit to 1M tokens, up from 64K on earlier Gemini models. The model card describes a combined input plus output window of up to 1M tokens. So a long prompt reduces the room left for output. Google documents a new continuation protocol for long decodes in its developer docs and enterprise docs . At introductory pricing, a full 1M token response costs $10 in output tokens. How does Gemini 4 Argon perform on benchmarks? Google compares Argon with GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Opus 5.5. Argon posts the top score on most rows. DeepSWE v1.1: 77.9%, ahead of Opus 5.5 (74.2%) and GPT-6 Astra (74.1%). Vals Index: 68.90%, ranked #1 by Vals AI ahead of Claude Sonnet 5.5 (67.04%). AutomationBench: 51.3%, versus 42.5% for Opus 5.5. Harvey’s Legal Agent Benchmark: 19.6%, nearly 3x the next model, but still a low absolute score. GraphWalks, 256K to 1M tokens: 84.2%, versus 71.8% for GPT-6 Astra. CWE-bench v1: 68.0%, tied with GPT-6 Astra. Google also reports 87% on the ERQA embodied reasoning benchmark . Read the evaluation methodology before drawing conclusions. Most rival scores are self-reported or pulled from public leaderboards. Argon’s DeepSWE score is self-computed with a mini-swe-agent harness. The rival DeepSWE numbers come from system cards and a leaderboard. Where does Gemini 4 Argon fall short? Argon trails on 5 rows of Google’s own table: FrontierSWE v2: 55.0%, versus 65.5% for GPT-6 Astra. Terminal-Bench 4.0: 57.4%, versus 66.4% for Opus 5.5. Terminal-Bench Science 0.1: 57.6%, versus 68.1% for GPT-6 Astra. PostTrainBench: 45.3%, versus 49.3% for Opus 5.5. OSWorld-2.0 (offline subset): 69.2%, versus 72.6% for GPT-6 Astra. The model card also lists hallucinations and occasional slowness or timeouts. Under Google’s Frontier Safety Framework, Google says it cannot rule out the biological and cybersecurity critical capability levels. It reports deploying safeguards it assesses as lowering that risk. Step through

title: 2027: Pantami, Gwarzo, Adebutu, others remain excluded – INEC
body: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has taken a final position on the fate of candidates intending to contest the governorship elections in their respective states affirming that those excluded from the list the commission released on Saturday remain excluded. Daily Trust reports that in the list released by INEC on October 10, frontline contenders like Isa Ali Pantami who was cleared by the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Gombe State and Ladi Adebutu of the PDP in Ogun State were excluded. Others not captured in the list include Comrade Aminu Abdussalam Gwarzo, of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Kano, and his counterpart in Kaduna State Danjuma Laah. Our correspondents report that INEC also excluded governorship candidates of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP), Action Alliance (AA) and Accord Party (AP) in Bauchi State. Abdullahi Yakubu; Musa Zubairu; Ahmed Shuaibu and Mohammed Aminu. Retirees now receive benefit within 48hrs – PenCom 9 die, 2 injured in Abuja-Lokoja road crash INEC explained after a meeting of its top officials in Abuja which lasted several hours that the candidates were excluded because their political parties failed to submit membership registers as required by law. The commission said the exclusion followed a September 24, 2026, Supreme Court judgement affirming the constitutionality of Section 77(5)-(7) of the Electoral Act, 2026, which makes the submission of membership registers mandatory for political parties. In a press statement issued on Tuesday, signed by Mohammed Kudu Haruna, National Commissioner and Chairman of INEC’s Information and Voter Education Committee, said the Supreme Court, in INEC v. Zenith Labour Party, Appeal No. SC/CV/495/2026, upheld the provisions requiring parties to submit their membership registers before conducting valid primaries. The judgement overturned an earlier Court of Appeal decision that had nullified the provisions. INEC stated that the apex court also upheld Item 2 of its timetable for the 2027 elections, which required political parties to submit their membership registers between April 21 and May 10, 2026, stressing that the Supreme Court further ruled that parties that failed to comply with the requirement would be ineligible to sponsor candidates in the elections. The commission explained that it applied the judgement while finalising the governorship candidates’ list in compliance with Section 287(1) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, which requires authorities to give effect to decisions of superior courts. It added that the final lists of presidential and National Assembly candidates had already been published on September 12, 2026, 13 days before the Supreme Court delivered its judgement. INEC said political parties that believed their candidates had been wrongly omitted could notify the commission in accordance with Section 32(2) of the Electoral Act, 2026. It said the deadline for such notifications was October 24, 2026. The commission reaffirmed its commitment to transparency, the rule of law and the credibility of the electoral process. Reactions after the list was released Former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy, Prof. Isa Ali Ibrahim Pantami, had on Monday, issued a three days ultimatum to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), over what he described as unlawful omission of his name from the final list of candidates for the 2027 governorship election in Gombe State. In a letter dated October 12, 2026, and addressed to the INEC Chairman, Pantami’s lawyers, Ahmed Raji & Co., demanded that the commission publishes his name as the candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) within three days. The Kwankwasiyya Movement also urged its members and supporters to remain calm saying the matter could be resolved through available administrative and legal channels, urging the NDC to act swiftly to protect the candidates’ interests. In a statement issued on Sunday, the movement’s spokesperson, Dr Habibu Sale Mohammed, said the development had generated concern among supporters but cautioned against speculation and the circulation of unverified information. Adebutu on his part explained that the circumstances surrounding his exclusion from the final list of governorship candidates released by INEC raised “serious questions” as all the other party’s candidates across the House of Assembly, House of Representatives and senatorial positions had appeared on the published lists, except him and his running mate, Yemi Sowunmi-Kolapo. “We will pursue this matter through the appropriate channels and insist that due process is respected,” Adebutu declared in a statement he posted on X and Facebook on Sunday morning. INEC Chairman, Prof Joash Amupitan had last week Tuesday confirmed that the commission had received the certified true copy of the Supreme Court judgement and that it is being reviewed. Yesterday’s meeting with top officials of the commission to our correspondents learnt represents thew final decision of the commission as regards the cleared candidates for the 2027 elections. There have been debates as to whether INEC has the power to disqualify candidates on its own based on the Supreme court judgement. Background to the crisis Daily Trust reports that the whole matter started when Zenith Labour Party (ZLP) had approached a Federal High Court sitting in Abuja, challenging provisions of the Electoral Act which it contended were inconsistent with the 1999 Constitution. At the trial court, the ZLP argued that the provisions conflicted with the 1999 Constitution and amounted to unconstitutional interference in the internal affairs of political parties. The party’s case was anchored, among others, on Sections 221 and 222 of the Constitution, which provide for the constitutional framework governing political parties. he Federal High Court, presided over by Justice Mohammed Umar, in a judgment delivered on May 5, 2026 dismissed the party’s action. Dissatisfied with the judgement, the ZLP approached the Court of Appeal, Abuja Division in appeal marked: CA/ABJ/CV/750/2026. The Court of Appeal, in its judgment delivered on July 16, 2026, allowed the appeal in part and voided provisions of the Electoral Act relating to party primaries and membership registers. The appellate court’s decision prompted INEC to approach the Supreme Court, according to the commission’s brief of argument filed in the appeal filed at the Supreme Court. After the hearing of the appeal and arguments from both parties last week, a seven-man panel of the apex court, presided over by Justice Adamu Jauro, reserved its judgement.

title: To the Ramparts: New missile shield 'protects warships from drone swarms'
body: A cost-effective missile system to defend civilian and military sites from drone swarms has been unveiled in France . Rampart, developed by Naval Group , can create a defensive shield around warships using large numbers of low-cost laser-guided rockets rather than expensive interceptors such as Patriot, that were expended at high rates in the Iran war. It has completed successful sea trials in the Mediterranean, including a French Navy counter-drone exercise off Toulon. “It is designed to build a defensive shield around a warship in drone warfare,” said Stephan Meunier, a former French navy commander involved with the programme. How it works Naval Group expects to produce up to 10,000 Rampart systems by 2028. In tests, the system struck an aerial drone as well as unguided rockets trained on surface targets. The system fires laser-guided 68mm rockets fitted with proximity fuses and has a range of up to 6km. The launcher consists of four modules, each carrying 20 projectiles, giving a maximum load of 80 rockets. It can be loaded with a combination of weapons, including surface-to-air and surface-to-surface missiles, decoys or precision missiles. An experienced crew can reload a single 20-round module in about 10 minutes. The system weighs about four tonnes, allowing it to be fitted to relatively small warships including corvettes. 'Cost-to-kill' During the recent Iran war, western forces used large numbers of expensive interceptors against relatively cheap drones. Patriot missiles costing more than $4 million each were used to take out Shahed-136 drones costing just $35,000, roughly the same price as a guided 68mm rocket. “The cost-to-kill ratio is very effective and it can tackle a drone swarm attack,” Mr Meunier said. “Rockets are cheaper and more efficient.” Airport attacks There is growing evidence that shipping in the Arabian Gulf and Red Sea could face “saturation attacks” by drones fired from Iran or the rebel Houthis. Naval ships equipped with Rampart would be able to provide significant close-in protection, Mr Meunier said. Rampart can also be deployed as a ground-based system to protect airports, military bases and civilian areas. “This system would provide good defences for fixed installations such as airports and to protect urban centres or military camps in the Gulf as well as on board warships,” Mr Meunier said. Over the weekend, Saudi Arabia’s main airport came under attack from Houthi rebels, with 13 people killed in two incidents. Missiles were also intercepted in Riyadh and Dammam. Aerial threats Naval Group has also developed a single Rampart module for its Sirenha unmanned surface vessel, allowing an autonomous drone boat to provide an additional defensive layer. The French company is also working with Emirates' defence group Edge to conduct trials of the UAE-developed SkyKnight air-defence missile, beginning with land trials before maritime testing next year. SkyKnight can engage aerial threats at ranges of up to 10km, potentially giving Rampart a more capable missile option alongside its 68mm rockets. There is also a possibility that Rampart could be battle-tested in Ukraine where Kyiv is getting desperately short of air defences against daily Russian drone and missile attacks. If successful, then it could well provide a major step in defending key military and civilians sites from the threat of drone saturation attack at low cost.

title: Geeing up for 6G: What the next mobile standard promises and challenges it faces
body: Over the past weeks, UAE telecom operators etisalat and du have announced further progress in their march towards 6G, the next generation of wireless communication. The industry is accelerating its preparations for the technology that being presented as vital to the world becoming more connected, underpinned by increasingly intelligent devices and services . Du said on Tuesday it has delivered commercial U6GHz connectivity on its 5G+ network, which will serve as a foundation for high-capacity services across homes, businesses and industries . Meanwhile, Abu Dhabi's etisalat – which recently rebranded back from e& – said it has commercially launched a service that increase upload speeds to smartphones threefold. What is 6G and when would it be available? 6G promises faster speeds and efficiency than the current 5G mobile phone technology, which also has more advanced forms under names such as 5G+, 5G Advanced and 5.5G. Historically, new generations of wireless technology have emerged with every new decade, suggesting 6G could become available in the early 2030s. This is a widely shared industry expectation. The US introduced the third generation in 2002, the fourth in 2010 and 5G in 2018. The second and first generations were in the 1980s and early 1990s, respectively, with the “zero G” before that. While a 6G rollout is predicted in the early 2030s, not all of its features are expected to be available at launch, as the industry would continue testing its deployment. How fast is 6G? 5G's maximum transmission speed is 20 gigabits per second, which is already 20 times faster that 4G's 1Gbps rate under ideal circumstances. However, 6G's theoretical maximum compared to 5G, has varied from anywhere between 50 times faster, or 1 terabit per second, to 1,000 times, or 2.5 terabytes per second. One can only imagine how much that will increase transmission speeds. A multi-gigabyte file that used to take seconds or a few minutes to download could be done in a snap. Where is 6G use ideal? The consumer proposition of 6G will always be front and centre, especially as digital consumption and reliance on connected devices will only become more widespread. But on an industrial scale, 6G is expected to power advanced iterations of immersive and mass communication, ubiquitous connectivity, integrated sensing and communication, low-latency and hyper-reliable communication and artificial intelligence communication, according to the International Telecommunication Union, which leads the framework and standards-setting of wireless communications. Communications, business and economic gains aside, the power of 6G will also play a critical role in society by enabling affordable, resilient and energy‑efficient networks for health, education, agriculture and disaster response, the Geneva-based UN agency said. “Advanced networks also present a way to close the persistent digital divide that today leaves many people in low-income countries behind,” it added. Transport, home appliances and security, payment networks, financial transactions and a host of other products and services expected to be highly connected in the future will also rely on the speed 6G would offer. The challenges There are a number of issues that need to be addressed to ensure the reliability of 6G networks. Arguably the biggest challenge is to build 6G networks resilient to any AI-induced compromises. Networks of the future should be able to detect threats and adaptive enough to respond to them, according to the EC-Council University in New Mexico. Encryption, especially that which can protect against quantum threats, and integration to blockchain would also be important to avoid unauthorised data access and manipulation, the university added.

title: CFTZ, Customs Command seeks stronger ties with security agencies
body: By Godwin Oritse The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), Cross River/Calabar Free Trade Zone/Akwa Ibom Area Command, is strengthening inter-agency collaboration and intelligence-sharing to tackle security threats, facilitate legitimate trade and improve operational efficiency. The initiative followed familiarisation visits by the Acting Area Controller of the Command, Deputy Comptroller Dr Nkiru Nwala, to the leadership of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), the Nigerian Correctional Service and the Department of State Services (DSS) on Tuesday, October 13, 2026. During the visits, Nwala held separate meetings with the NSCDC Commandant, Chima Okarazu; the Controller of Corrections, Nigerian Correctional Service, Aniekan Archibong Nya; and the State Director of the DSS, Dr Faluyi Oluwole. The engagements focused on strengthening existing inter-agency relationships, establishing direct communication channels and identifying areas for enhanced cooperation following Nwala’s assumption of duty. The collaboration is expected to promote intelligence exchange, improve coordinated responses to security challenges and reinforce institutional support for lawful trade and effective border and trade operations across the Command’s area of responsibility. The visits were aimed at strengthening existing relationships, deepening institutional cooperation and establishing direct communication channels with the leadership of the agencies following her assumption of duty. The engagements also focused on fostering a common front in addressing security challenges, promoting lawful trade and supporting national development through coordinated action among security and law enforcement institutions. The Command said the visits underscored the Nigeria Customs Service’s commitment to effective inter-agency cooperation, intelligence sharing and coordinated operations in the discharge of its statutory responsibilities. It added that the initiative aligned with the Comptroller-General of Customs’ strategic mantra of Consolidation, Innovation and Collaboration, which emphasises strengthening existing partnerships, adopting progressive approaches to operational challenges and sustaining unity among security agencies. The collaboration is expected to enhance communication and coordination among the agencies, particularly in tackling shared security concerns and supporting the effective enforcement of relevant laws.
