title: Germany joins Ukraine Transport Support Fund with EUR 1M contribution
body:
As reported by Ukrinform, Minister for Recovery, Infrastructure and Transport Mykola Kalashnyk announced this on Telegram .
Together with contributions pledged by Sweden, Norway, Lithuania and Estonia, the total announced funding amounts to €4.1 million, he said.
The initial contributions will allow the fund’s operating mechanism to be tested in practice, from Ukraine identifying urgent needs to the procurement and delivery of equipment.
At this stage, it is important to refine the procedures and assess how quickly partner assistance can reach transport companies, Kalashnyk explained.
“Among the most urgent needs are locomotives, specialized equipment to restore damaged transport infrastructure, and electronic queue management systems for 11 road border crossing points with EU countries,” the minister said.
He stressed that Ukraine sets the priorities, assistance is provided in the form of grants, and procurement is handled by Lithuania’s Central Project Management Agency, which contracts suppliers directly and makes payments to them.
“Russian attacks create new needs every day. Our task is therefore to establish a mechanism that will help us promptly provide the transport sector with the machinery and equipment it needs. The first projects will lay the groundwork for expanding the fund and attracting new partners,” Kalashnyk said, thanking Germany and all the countries that had supported the launch of the initiative.
As Ukrinform reported, in June, during the Ukraine Recovery Conference 2026, the Ukrainian delegation reached agreements on establishing the Transport Support Fund.

title: How did Escudero rule so fast on prosecution’s surprise move?
body: There were two surprises during Vice President Sara Duterte ‘s impeachment trial on Tuesday, October 13: the bombshell motion of the prosecution to drop three of the four articles of impeachment, and the extensive ruling of presiding officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero delivered less than an hour after the House prosecutors’ request. So how did Escudero manage to make the ruling in such a short period of time? Senate impeachment court spokesperson Reginald Tongol said that Escudero, with his staff as well as Senate Clerk of Court Renato Bantug Jr., anticipated different scenarios and prepared rulings based on all legal possibilities. “The presiding officer has prepared rulings for different scenarios but they were in skeletal in form. It still has to be drafted and finalized upon his delivery and formal manifestation in the court,” Tongol in a mix of English and Filipino during a press briefing after the trial on Tuesday, October 13. Tongol cited the prosecution’s October 6 manifestation signaling its intent to withdraw Article III, which covers bribery, as an example of how Escudero anticipated possible developments. “For example, the prosecution filed a manifestation to drop Article III on October 6, so with due diligence, the presiding officer prepared and anticipated whatever that is going to be thrown at him at the trial,” he said. The prosecution ultimately went further, seeking to withdraw Article I, which covers the alleged misuse of confidential funds, and Article IV, which covers grave threats. The court granted the request, leaving only Article II, which concerns Duterte’s alleged unexplained wealth. Tongol said Escudero continued working on his ruling until shortly before delivering it, incorporating inputs from his fellow senator-judges. “The presiding officer’s rulings considered the inputs of his fellow senator judges. That’s why up to the last minute, he was actually writing and editing his speech,” said Tongol. This also explained why Escudero was cautious when Duterte’s defense counsel requested a copy of the ruling. Tongol said the presiding officer wanted the written version checked against the ruling delivered in court and reflected in the journal. “That’s also the reason when the respondent’s counsel was asking for a copy of the ruling, he said he wanted to be careful and that his written speech should be compared to the delivered speech in the journal. The official ruling was the one delivered during the trial,” he added. Escudero himself explained during the proceedings that the court had prepared for various possible scenarios to ensure it could address issues raised by either party. The court sought to know “the same, if not more, than each party or both parties combined,” Escudero said, explaining that the preparation was intended to help the court address potential issues and consider different outcomes. – Rappler.com

title: Fire at GRIDCo Mallam substation disrupts power in parts of Accra
body: A fire outbreak at a substation operated by the Ghana Grid Company Limited (GRIDCo) at Mallam has disrupted electricity supply to parts of Accra, including Lapaz, Mallam and Awoshie. The blaze reportedly destroyed control boards and transformers at the facility, raising concerns about the impact on power transmission and electricity supply to affected communities. The extent of the damage and the time required to restore normal operations have not yet been confirmed. Firefighters from the Adjen Kotoku and Amasaman fire stations responded to the incident and worked to contain the blaze. Their intervention helped prevent the fire from spreading to other critical installations within the substation, limiting the potential damage to additional equipment. The cause of the outbreak remains unknown, with further investigations expected to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident. Technical assessments will also be needed to determine the full extent of the damage and the work required to restore affected installations. GRIDCo operates Ghana’s national electricity transmission network, transporting power from generation facilities to distribution companies for onward supply to consumers. Substations play a critical role in the system by housing transformers, control boards and other equipment used to regulate and manage electricity flows. Damage to these installations can complicate operations and delay the restoration of normal supply to affected areas.

title: Investigators hunt French supermarket fridge hackers, no claim of responsibility
body: PARIS, France – French investigators on Tuesday, October 13, were hunting the hackers who seized control of cooling units at hundreds of supermarkets in a cyberattack that underlined the vulnerabilities of connected systems, with no group publicly claiming responsibility. The investigation comes as Dutch supermarket company Ahold Delhaize grapples with a separate cybersecurity incident that disrupted online services, although Dutch authorities said they saw no connection between the two events. The absence of a claim of responsibility by hacktivists or a ransom demand by cybercriminals has puzzled French investigators, according to a source with knowledge of the probe. Typically, such groups tend to quickly seek to monetize their hacks or claim credit for them for political ends. The cyberattack, which manually overrode the temperatures at fridges in supermarket groups including Carrefour, Monoprix, Intermarche, and Cooperative U, appears to have been easy to pull off, three cyber experts told Reuters. Staff at some Paris supermarkets threw boxes full of perished meat and frozen goods into giant trash containers on Tuesday. At least 350 supermarkets — a small fraction of the total number in France — were caught up in the strike. Firm blames outdated software France’s cybersecurity agency has said the breach affected fridges that relied on software by Danish firm Danfoss, as well as Copeland and Dixell software. Danfoss said on Monday that many of the affected units had “reached end of life and no longer receive software or security updates” or were “running outdated firmware.” It said it had “advised customers to keep supported systems updated with the latest firmware and to migrate legacy systems to current-generation solutions”. The company declined further comment on Tuesday. Copeland, which owns Dixell, acknowledged the “vulnerability.” “We are currently working with impacted customers to mitigate the risk,” the company said, adding that it would strengthen cybersecurity. In Danfoss’ case, the serious vulnerabilities present in older versions of its firmware have been known for months. On August 9, cybersecurity firm Claroty detailed weaknesses — since patched — in the Danfoss AK-SM 800A controller that could have allowed intruders to bypass authentication and run code on compromised devices. ‘Basic cyber hygiene’ Although the precise mechanism by which attackers compromised the refrigerators has not been publicly disclosed, cybersecurity experts said all signs pointed to a basic stunt enabled both by the failure to adopt Danfoss’ updates and by exposing device interfaces to the internet. “This is about basic cyber hygiene,” said Ken Munro, a partner at the British cybersecurity firm Pen Test Partners. “Get it wrong and you get a smelly mess of defrosted food.” He said the well-known vulnerabilities meant the attackers were essentially pushing at an open door, something that meant the hack could easily be “kids messing around”. “If this was a nation state, why affect only a subset of French fridges? There are plenty of other nations with fridges on the internet,” he said. “No ransom or demand suggests a lack of appreciation of the potential commercial losses that the fridge owners may experience.” Problem still exists Plenty of fridges remain reachable via the internet. Using the internet scanning service Shodan, Reuters found at least 4,500 Danfoss interfaces still viewable on Tuesday. Reuters could not independently establish how many of them were running vulnerable software, but French internet scanning company Onyphe said only a small minority of the devices appeared to be running the latest version of the software. Outdated and vulnerable versions were “still widely represented among publicly accessible interfaces”, Onyphe said. Dutch disruption Separately, Dutch retailer Ahold Delhaize said on Tuesday it had begun “starting a controlled re-launch of certain systems” following a cybersecurity issue that began on Sunday evening. The Dutch cybersecurity watchdog NCSC said it did not believe the incident was linked to the French supermarket hack. Ahold operates the Albert Heijn chain in the Netherlands and several major US chains including Stop & Shop and Giant Food. Websites for stores in both countries remained offline late Tuesday afternoon, with online ordering and delivery services unavailable. – Rappler.com

title: Jewish American history museum moves closer to joining Smithsonian amid political tensions
body: Philadelphia's Weitzman National Museum of American Jewish History is moving closer to joining the Smithsonian Institution at a time of significant upheaval for the storied museum network.A new congressional commission will study whether to make the museum part of the Smithsonian. Its members were sworn in Tuesday, when they also held their first meeting.In an exclusive interview with the Jewish Telegraphic Agency, the commission's new chair Philip Darivoff, a former longtime chair of the Weitzman, and vice chair Dara Horn, a New York Times bestselling author, said that the Weitzman joining the Smithsonian would send a powerful message that Jews are a crucial component of the history of the country.“It's a different statement that our country makes when it says that the study of Jewish American history and culture is important to this nation,” Darivoff said. Both he and Horn also hope that a boost in the Weitzman's profile could combat what they called an “epidemic of ignorance” among Americans when it comes to knowledge of Jewish history and culture.“This really would be an elevation of the Jewish community,” Horn, author of People Love Dead Jews and The Final Solution to the Jewish Question, told JTA. “The place that Jews show up in a school curriculum is typically more about the Holocaust” - an area that the author has written critically about in the past as too limiting a view of Jewish life.Jewish contributions to American history and founding idealsHorn believes in the Weitzman project, she said, because she hopes to emphasize the ways that Jews have contributed to American founding ideals such as religious pluralism. “I'm really interested in the connections between the Jewish story and a lot of our foundational ideas in this country,” she said. Jewish ideas such as the Exodus from Egypt in the Passover story “were inspiring to Americans,” she added.The wheels for the Weitzman joining the Smithsonian began turning in 2024, when Congress passed legislation in 2024, then signed by President Biden, to establish the commission. The group spent the next two years putting the commission together, and has two years from its first meeting to research and publish a report on the feasibility of such a move — though Darivoff said he hopes to finish the work well before the deadline.Adding a new member to the Smithsonian has taken years, if not decades. The two most recent additions, the National Museum of the American Latino and the American Women's History Museum, were both long in the works. Founded in 1976, the Weitzman is already an existing, fully functioning institution — and also already a Smithsonian affiliate, meaning it can share resources with other museums in the system. Unlike a museum being built from scratch, the Weitzman already has a building and collection, which proponents hope could speed the process.Dan Tadmor, the Weitzman's CEO, told JTA that joining the Smithsonian would improve their educational mission.“We have a national footprint for our educational programming, but of course we'd like to widen it,” he said. “Who would say no to a curriculum that's been developed by a Smithsonian museum?”Smithsonian bid advances amid Trump administration scrutinyThe Weitzman bid for greater prominence within the Smithsonian comes as the Trump administration has sought to exert greater control over the latter- home to storied institutions such as the National Museum of American History, the National Portrait Gallery, and the National Zoo. This summer the White House issued a report alleging “radical ideology” in the museums' content, and Interior Secretary Doug Burgum recently announced plans for signs accusing Smithsonian leaders of ideological bias. Observers say such signs are indicative of larger administration priorities opposing the teaching of historical subjects such as slavery. Smithsonian Secretary Lonnie Bunch III is stepping down at the end of the year. A representative from the Smithsonian declined to comment to JTA on the Weitzman's bid, or on its current political conditions. The commission's chair and vice chair of the new Weitzman said that the current political upheaval shouldn't affect their work. The Smithsonian, Horn said, “has lasted through many political winds.” “I think we see this as a long-term project that's about the place of Jewish Americans in this country's history,” Darivoff said. “The Smithsonian is a really important institution for this country, and it is the great museum complex of our nation. God willing, it will be flourishing for centuries to come. It'd be an honor to be included in the Smithsonian.”

title: Israel could leave Syria but needs buffer zones in Gaza and Lebanon, ex-national security chief says
body: Retired Maj. Gen. Giora Eiland, former head of Israel's National Security Council, spoke Tuesday at the People of the State conference, the flagship event hosted by ynet and Yedioth Ahronoth. Eiland discussed what he described as Israel's fundamental mistake in 2007 that ultimately led to the October 7 massacre, as well as the differences between Israel's buffer zones in Gaza and Lebanon and the territory it holds in Syria. "The great mistake always begins with an incorrect description of reality," Eiland said, referring to the Gaza Strip. "From 2007, through October 7 and to this day, the State of Israel has continued to make the mistake of mischaracterizing the reality in Gaza. The description is that there are two million unfortunate people there, and one day a terrible terrorist organization called Hamas came along, forcibly took over the Strip, and therefore it is right for us to fight Hamas, but we have nothing against the two million unfortunate people who found themselves in this situation."   "This naive description has nothing to do with reality," he continued. "In 2007, Gaza became a state in every sense, with clearly defined borders, an effective central government capable of collecting taxes, managing all the health care, education and sanitation systems, and so on. It has a completely independent foreign policy and its own army. The correct way to define what happened on October 7 is that the State of Gaza launched a war against the State of Israel." Eiland argued that this flawed understanding of reality also shaped the IDF's assessment of Hamas. "For years, it was known that on the other side of the border there was a Nukhba force of at least 3,000 men, well-equipped and well-trained, with extremely high religious motivation, and just 10 minutes away from reaching any Israeli community or IDF base. Their clear and defined mission was to raid the State of Israel."   "In all IDF situation assessments over the years, from the division and command levels to the General Staff, when they discussed what might happen, they defined the worst-case scenario as a simultaneous attack by 60 terrorists. Wait a minute, you know they have 3,000, and you're saying the worst case is 60? How did such a huge gap emerge?" "The answer is very simple. It is entirely philosophical," Eiland explained, arguing that the military's assessment was shaped by its definition of Hamas as a terrorist organization conducting guerrilla warfare through individual terrorists. The sin of belief According to Eiland, the same mistake was evident along Israel's northern border on October 7. "In 2014, Hezbollah established the Radwan Force, numbering 6,000 terrorists. Gradually, they moved closer to the border, building bunkers and infrastructure. The formal mission of the 91st Division is to defend the Galilee, but it did not prepare for defense." "To do that, you need to implement the principles of defense: depth and reserves. What did the Galilee Division actually have at 6:30 a.m. on October 7? A thin line of outposts, no depth, no second line, no reserves and, most importantly, no available firepower capable of effectively delivering a large volume of fire against points of infiltration."   Eiland argued that the series of failures was not the result of a mistaken strategic conception, but something more fundamental. "You first adopt a belief about what will happen and what will not happen, and from that moment you arrange the facts to fit that belief," he said. "Your brain is flexible enough to adapt reality to the belief instead of the other way around." "That is worse than a mistaken conception, because a conception at least supposedly reflects a flawed thought process, but still a thought process. I'm talking about belief. Belief that has no rational basis, whose entire foundation is emotional and is built on many false assumptions that I developed over the years and never even examine." Despite his criticism, Eiland identified two areas in which he believes the IDF has improved over the past three years. The first is basic military discipline, which he described as "appalling on October 7." "The army has learned, and I think the improvement is real," he said. The second improvement, he argued, is the recognition that Israel needs buffer zones along its borders. "In both Lebanon and Gaza, Israel cannot defend itself when there are communities along the border and, on the other side, an enemy 200 meters away with offensive intentions," he said. However, Eiland argued that the situation along the Syrian border is significantly different. "There are many operational and tactical differences, and the need to hold territory in Syria is lower than in Lebanon," he explained. He stressed that he was not proposing a unilateral Israeli withdrawal from the territory. "Israel can return to the border line provided there is an American plan guaranteeing that advanced weapons manufactured in Turkey or Russia will not enter Syria," he said. "We can give up that particular enclave inside Syria. It is a risk worth taking, provided the strategic benefit we receive in return is far more important."

title: Your client is Parliament, not a party; remain honest even when unwelcome – Speaker
body: Alban Sumana Kingsford Bagbin, the Speaker of Parliament, has declared that the independence of parliamentary legal advice is not a technical detail but a democratic imperative. As a result, he has charged Legal Counsel to Parliaments across Africa that their ultimate loyalty was to Parliament as a constitutional institution and not to any political party or individual. Opening the 8th Africa Colloquium of Legal Counsel to Parliaments in Accra on Tuesday, he described legislative counsel and drafters as the quiet and indispensable architects of constitutional democracy. The Speaker made the remarks in a speech read his behalf by Reverend Ebenezer Ahumah Djietror, the Clerk to Parliament. He said politics was both a privilege and a profound institutional responsibility, and that they met not as isolated delegations, but as custodians of a shared constitutional aspiration and as joint architects of Africa’s democratic future. The Colloquium, hosted by the Parliament of Ghana from Monday, October 12 to Friday, October 16, 2026, on the theme: “Ethics, Integrity and Legal Accountability,” had brought together legal counsels from across the continent, to review 15 years of the Nairobi Principles. Speaking on impartiality, the Speaker said whether Parliament served the public or the powerful hinges on the independence of its legal advice: “Political eloquence alone has never built a durable nation, ordered national affairs or protected citizens from state overreach. That is where your work begins.” He stated that although parliamentary legal practice began with impartiality, it did not mean indifference. “It does not require counsel to feign neutrality or to pretend that all legal arguments are equally valid. It requires professional judgement without affection, ill-will, or partisan instruction,” he stated. Quoting the judicial oath to do right to all manner of people without fear or favour, affection or ill-will, he said that is the standard for parliamentary legal services. “Your advice must remain honest, even when it is unwelcome. A legal opinion that is welcomed by the majority may be correct. A legal opinion that frustrates the majority may also be correct. The test is not whether an advice pleases the institution at a particular moment, but it is whether it is legally written, professionally defensible, constitutionally sound and institutionally responsible,” he said. He was emphatic on where loyalty must lie, saying “Your professional loyalty must not be reduced to the interest of the majority party or the minority part, nor should it be understood as personal loyalty to an individual presiding officer. Your ultimate responsibility is to the institution of Parliament, the Constitution, and the public interest that Parliament exists to serve. In practical terms, your client is not a party nor a person. Your client is a constitutional institution,” he stressed. He said such responsibility required moral courage to tell leadership that a policy objective may be commendable, but the law had not been properly crafted. “Such advice is not disloyalty. It is the essence of constitutional responsibility,” he added. On Integrity, the Speaker said it was more than the absence of impropriety; it was fidelity to truth, law, duty and institutional purpose. He warned that Parliamentary counsel must resist the temptation to use legal reasoning to disguise political convenience, saying advice must not be shaped merely to produce the preferred answer. The Speaker further cautioned members against selectively commissioning legal opinions until a favourable conclusion was obtained, noting that where one opinion flagged serious risks on a fast-tracked Bill affecting fundamental rights and another indicated that the risk was manageable, presenting only the second opinion to leadership does not serve the law, but amounted to short-circuiting it. Touching on accountability and Artificial Intelligence (AI), the Speaker charged counsel to subject every Bill, amendment, application for constitutional validation, Private Member’s bill and subsidiary legislation to objective and analytically consistent scrutiny, regardless of political interest. “Every Bill drafted, every amendment written and every item of subsidiary legislation reviewed will have an encounter in the real world. In drafting, lack of precision creates ambiguity. In subsidiary legislation, absence of quality control means executive agencies may exercise powers Parliament never intended to confer,” he said. He explained that accountability meant being prepared to say in writing when a law was likely to be challenged, when delegation was too broad, or when procedure may not survive judicial review, and that parliamentary legal services themselves must be subject to codes of conduct, integrity training, annual reports, and transparent quality assurance. “We cannot demand accountability from the executive while insulating parliamentary legal services from legitimate institutional scrutiny,” he said. He warned that AI may assist in research and drafting but introduced risks of confidentiality breach, fabricated authorities, hidden biases, and weak audit trails. “Technology may accelerate the preparation of legislation, but it cannot determine whether the process is just, whether discretion is excessive or whether the legal framework will protect the vulnerable or empower the predator. That responsibility remains human,” he said. He therefore charged the Colloquium to adopt principles ensuring that no authority is drafted by AI that no human has reviewed; no draft is uploaded to insecure systems, and every use of AI can be audited. Proposing a forward agenda, the Speaker, urged delegates to strengthen respect for each country’s constitutional position, establish minimum standards on conflict of interest and confidentiality, institutionalise quality assurance through plain language drafting and post-legislative review, adopt a protocol for responsible AI use, and invest in continuous professional development. “You are guardians of constitutional boundaries, protectors of public resources and custodians of the legal processes through which citizenship can be lived with dignity and confidence,” he charged. “When you leave this court, let your measure not be how much was passed but how clearly it was written, how fairly it was processed and how justly it will operate,” he added. Dr Dominic Akuritinga Ayine, the Attorney-General and Minister for Justice, urged Legal Counsel to Parliaments across Africa to use the ongoing 8th Africa Colloquium to develop practical protocols on the use of AI and the handling of improper instructions. “I urge you to take advantage of these days to share how our respective offices handle improper instructions, work towards a practical protocol for the use of AI in legislative work, give the principles a measurable self-assessment and strengthen training and mentorship for the next generation of legislative counsel,” he said. He charged delegates to take the answers home to their respective Parliaments to make them responsive to the needs of citizens across the continent. He thanked counsel for their service to various Parliaments, including the support being provided to the Parliament of the Republic of Ghana. Mr Alexander Kwamena Afenyo-Markin, the Minority leader, said professional integrity demands that parliamentary lawyers refuse to draft legislation inconsistent with constitutional requirements. He said it also requires advising the Speaker and Committee Chairs with candour and intellectual honesty, even when that advice goes against the ambitions of influential political actors. “Professional integrity requires resistance to attempts to manipulate parliamentary procedures to marginalise minority voices, restrict legitimate scrutiny or suppress dissent,” he said. Mr Afenyo-Markin cited Principle Eight of the Nairobi Principles, which requires parliamentary legal offices to remain impartial and non-partisan. He stressed that non-partisanship must not be confused with neutrality, explaining that it entails a principled commitment to procedural justice. “The Constitution and the Standing Orders guarantee minority rights to ask questions, participate in debate, examine evidence and propose amendments. Parliamentary counsel has a responsibility to ensure that parliamentary majorities do not extinguish democratic fairness,” he stated. He said the 15-year review of the Nairobi Principles should not be an exercise in institutional self-congratulation but a rigorous, honest and fearless self-assessment. “We must ask ourselves deeper questions: In how many of our parliaments are legal counsel genuinely autonomous? Where has executive influence gradually reasserted itself to weaken parliamentary legal offices? Where are counsel being marginalised, under-resourced or denied the institutional authority necessary to fulfil their mandate?” he queried. He told delegates that as they return to their respective capitals, they carry the expectations of millions of African citizens who regard Parliament as the final institutional bulwark against authoritarianism, corruption, arbitrariness and abuse of power. “Be independent, be ethical, be courageous. Our parliaments will endure only on the foundations of integrity, constitutionality and accountability,” he said. Mr James Agalga, the Majority Leader, said good governance rests on certainty, institutional stability and fidelity to law. “Government programmes can endure only when their legislation is grounded in constitutional principle and sound legal principle. Legislation arising from complex reforms, fiscal policy or bilateral investment agreements must not receive uncritical approval or superficial scrutiny,” he said. He said what the majority requires and what the national interest demands is a parliamentary counsel capable of subjecting legislation to rigorous technical scrutiny, identifying constitutional vulnerabilities candidly, and improving legislative language to withstand judicial scrutiny. “Your foremost obligation is to the law, the Constitution and the integrity of the legislature,” he charged counsel. He said rigorous legal analysis during committee considerations does not obstruct government policy but rather strengthens it by identifying legal and constitutional risks, thereby preventing procedural invalidation, unnecessary litigation and constitutional uncertainty. Reflecting on the Nairobi Principles established 15 years ago in 2011, when parliaments assembled in Nairobi articulated a far-sighted vision for Africa’s parliaments to develop autonomous, professional and ethical in-house legal expertise, he commended the progress made across the continent. “From regional assemblies to national parliaments and county legislatures, the office of parliamentary legal counsel has evolved from an experimental administrative reform into an indispensable institution for legislative governance,” he said. On the theme of the Colloquium, “Ethics, Integrity and Legal Accountability”, he said it touches the very foundations of responsible statecraft at a time of rapid socio-economic transformation, heightened public expectations and complex international realities. “Ethical integrity cannot be treated as an abstract idea. It anchors public confidence and democratic legitimacy,” he added.

title: Why Did Kadyrov Visit Azerbaijan? Analysts Point to Putin’s Interests and a Possible Escape Plan
body:
Chechen leader Ramzan Kadyrov received an unusually lavish welcome from Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev during a visit to Baku on Saturday, Oct. 10, raising questions about whether the trip was intended to repair relations with Moscow or secure the future of Kadyrov’s family and business empire.
The visit, which was not publicly announced in advance, came nearly two years after Russian air defenses struck an Azerbaijan Airlines passenger plane near Grozny, killing 38 people and triggering one of the most serious diplomatic disputes between Azerbaijan and Russia in recent years.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
During his meeting with Aliyev , Kadyrov expressed condolences over the December 2024 AZAL plane tragedy, calling it a shared sorrow.
Two Azerbaijani political analysts, Arif Yunus and Tofik Aliyev (no relation to President Ilham Aliyev), speaking separately on the Osmanqizi Alternativa podcast , suggested that the visit had deeper political and economic motivations.
Yunus described the trip as a demonstration of the enduring relationship between Aliyev and Russian President Vladimir Putin, while Aliyev suggested that Kadyrov was exploring Azerbaijan as a potential refuge for his family, wealth and loyal security personnel if political power changes hands in Russia.
Political analyst Arif Yunus questioned why Kadyrov, who governs a Russian federal republic rather than an independent country, received treatment normally associated with visiting heads of state.
“The reception was not simply lavish or ceremonial – it was pompous,” Yunus told the podcast.
“This is how presidents of major countries, such as Trump or Putin, are usually received. But here they were welcoming someone who is not the president of an independent country. He is merely the governor of one of Russia’s many regions.”
Yunus said the welcome was particularly striking because Kadyrov’s name had repeatedly surfaced in public debate over the December 2024 plane tragedy.
The aircraft was struck by Russian air defenses while approaching Grozny and subsequently crashed near Aktau, Kazakhstan, killing 38 of the 67 people on board.
Yunus recalled that Kadyrov’s attempt to contact Aliyev after the crash reportedly angered the Azerbaijani leadership, which had expected a direct response from Putin.
According to Yunus, Putin’s initial handling of the disaster reflected his broader attitude toward former Soviet republics and their leaders.
“For Putin, there is no difference whether it is Ukraine, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan or Kazakhstan. They are all governors, just with different titles,” Yunus said.
In his interpretation, Kadyrov’s reception signaled that the Kremlin’s relationship with Baku had survived the diplomatic crisis.
“It was Putin sending his governor to meet another governor,” Yunus concluded.
Yunus dismissed suggestions that the aircraft disaster had fundamentally altered Azerbaijan’s political relationship with Russia.
He compared the two presidents to a married couple whose occasional disputes do not threaten their underlying partnership.
“They may quarrel, stop talking and sulk. But they will not divorce because they have too much in common,” he said.
According to Yunus, Aliyev and Putin remain connected through extensive business interests, energy cooperation and political calculations.
He recalled that shortly before the aircraft tragedy, Aliyev had described his relationship with Putin as so close that they were effectively “in the same boat.”
“They really are in the same boat,” Yunus said.
Tofik Aliyev, a US-based political analyst and former Azerbaijani KGB officer, suggested that Kadyrov’s visit may have been driven by a personal concern – the survival of his family and political clan after Putin.
Kadyrov, 50, has been the subject of persistent reports about serious health problems, raising questions about his future leadership of Chechnya.
A July 2026 analysis by the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI) , a London-based defense and security think tank, described Kadyrov as being in poor health, citing reports of potentially serious medical conditions.
Just a week before his visit to Azerbaijan, on Oct. 3, Putin promoted Kadyrov to the rank of army general – Russia’s highest active military rank. The insignia was presented in Grozny by Viktor Zolotov, head of the Russian National Guard.
Aliyev questioned the promotion, pointing to Kadyrov’s lack of formal military education and experience commanding a regular army.
“Imagine the chief of the Russian General Staff is an army general – and Ramzan Kadyrov is also an army general,” he said.
According to Aliyev, the promotion illustrated the extraordinary privileges Kadyrov enjoys under Putin’s protection, despite deep resentment toward him within Russia’s military and intelligence services.
He warned that even a future leadership emerging from Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB) could move against Kadyrov and his family.
“If the government in Russia changes and new forces come to power that have no obligations to Ramzan Kadyrov, as Putin does, an entirely different group could take control in Chechnya,” Aliyev said.
“Nobody can guarantee that repression against the Kadyrov clan and his numerous family members will not begin,” he added.
Aliyev believes Kadyrov is already preparing for that possibility.
“One of the most important questions Kadyrov may have been trying to resolve in Baku was where his family could go if such changes occurred in Russia and Chechnya,” he said.
There is no independent confirmation that Kadyrov discussed these issues during the visit.
Aliyev portrayed Kadyrov as the head of a powerful security and business empire extending far beyond Chechnya.
According to the analyst, approximately 30,000 Chechen personnel serve in Russia’s National Guard, or Rosgvardia, many outside Chechnya. Rather than fighting on Ukraine’s front lines, he said, they secure strategic locations and protect business interests.
Aliyev described the network as a mafia-style operation involved in protecting businesses and controlling lucrative commercial activities.
He called Kadyrov a billionaire whose wealth had grown through massive Russian federal subsidies and opaque business dealings.
“Nobody can calculate his fortune,” Aliyev said.
Investigations by the Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project (OCCRP) have exposed extensive wealth linked to Kadyrov’s family and associates.
Kadyrov’s decision to bring his adult sons to Azerbaijan and include them in official meetings and public appearances drew particular attention.
The delegation included Akhmat Kadyrov, Chechnya’s deputy prime minister, and Adam Kadyrov, secretary of its Security Council, alongside Russian State Duma deputy Adam Delimkhanov, Putin’s aide Ruslan Edelgeriyev and Chechen Deputy Prime Minister Anvar Usmanov, according to BBC News Azerbaijani.
President Ilham Aliyev personally accompanied Kadyrov and his sons on a tour of Baku White City, a major redevelopment project offering residential, commercial and hotel investment opportunities. Project director Ruslan Sadikhov briefed Kadyrov on the development and its facilities.
Political analyst Tofik Aliyev considers that the children’s public appearance alongside Azerbaijan’s president was more than a family gesture.
“This is called authorization,” he said, arguing that the images signaled Kadyrov’s sons’ access to Azerbaijan’s leadership, potentially helping them establish businesses, acquire property or relocate to the country.
The visit, Aliyev suggested, may reveal a deeper fear within Putin’s inner circle – that even the Kremlin’s most loyal allies are beginning to prepare for a future in which the system protecting their power and fortunes may collapse.
Sevinj Osmanqizi is an experienced journalist who writes extensively for Kyiv Post on foreign policy, international security and geopolitics. Based in Washington, D.C., her work focuses on Ukraine, Russia’s war and the broader post-Soviet space.

title: 'We expect more from the top': Lisandro Martinez takes aim at Manchester United hierarchy
body: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez did not hold back as he criticised the club's hierarchy ​after ​their ​Champions League defeat to ⁠Atletico Madrid on Tuesday. United slipped to a 2-0 defeat, which means Michael Carrick 's team have now gone winless for five consecutive games across competitions. Martinez, however, attempted to highlight issues outside the pitch, stating that he ⁠expected greater investment to help ​the team compete at the highest level. The Argentina international singled ⁠out director of football Jason Wilcox, saying United needed more signings to compete with their rivals. “I expect more from ​our ⁠technical director. I have ‌to be honest. And also, as players, we ​have to do more,” Martinez told Amazon Prime. “Tonight it is easy to [blame] the coach, easy to say the players but also we have to see other areas.” Atletico took the lead through Pablo Barrios inside the opening minute at the Metropolitano, before Ademola Lookman secured victory in the 79th minute, shortly after United defender Leny Yoro was sent off. United are on three points in the Champions League league phase, having opened their campaign with a 4-0 win over ​Sabah FK . United are returning to the ‌Champions League after a ⁠two-season absence, having finished ​bottom of their group in their previous appearance ​in ‌the competition in 2023/24. Lisandro Martínez did NOT hold back after United's loss to Atletico 😬👀 pic.twitter.com/OGo25Pzd30 — Prime Video Sport UK (@primevideosport) October 13, 2026 “We had a fantastic season last season ⁠and now we expect more from the top, from ⁠upstairs, to bring in more players to compete, because many teams have brought in many players as well,” Martinez added. “Atletico have an amazing team and they deserved to win today. “I have to be honest, as players we have to do more but it is also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night.” United, who are 13th in the Premier League , ​visit Leeds United on Sunday before travelling to Como for their next Champions League fixture on October 21. Former Manchester United star Wayne Rooney said Martinez's comments were unwarranted and could throw the dressing room into chaos. “It is disrespectful to his teammates,” Rooney was quoted as saying by the BCC. “He is saying his teammates aren't good enough. “Bruno [Fernandes] is the only one with any right to say that. Behind closed doors, it happens – but that interview isn't going to help. “[Martinez] has tried to speak on behalf of the players but done it the wrong way.” Barcelona rally Barcelona recovered well to defeat Galatasaray 4-1. Barca overturned a first-half deficit with Lamine Yamal supplying two assists. Galatasaray went ahead as Alexey Batrakov scored in the 28th minute. The hosts thought they had doubled their lead through a Baris Yilmaz header, only for VAR to identify an offside ​in the build-up. Joao Cancelo equalised just before half-time and Yamal then set up Fermin Lopez and Anthony ‌Gordon to score in the 50th and 53rd minutes. ⁠Karim Adeyemi completed the victory. Also, Arsenal scored three times in seven minutes to defeat Lille 3-0. Arsenal had to wait until the 64th minute for Jurrien Timber to break Lille's resistance from Noni Madueke's pass. Substitute Bukayo Saka then set up Eberechi Eze's goal before Kai Havertz supplied Saka for the ​third in the 71st minute.

title: First trial on Nord Stream explosions begins in Germany
body:
HAMBURG, October 14. /TASS/. The first trial on the Nord Stream and Nord Stream 2 pipelines’ explosions is beginning in Germany four years after the terrorist attack. Ukrainian national Sergey K. will appear before the Hanseatic Higher Regional Court of Hamburg.
The court has scheduled 24 hearings, continuing through late January. Additional hearings are scheduled for February, but the dates have yet to be finalized.
The German Federal Prosecutor General’s Office believes that Sergey K., whom German media have identified as the head of the sabotage group, and his accomplices planned the pipeline blasts on orders from Ukrainian government agencies. Another Ukrainian national was recently detained in Croatia and is expected to be extradited to Germany. Investigators believe the saboteurs used forged documents to rent a sailing yacht from a German company and transported explosives to the Nord Stream pipelines aboard the vessel.
On September 26, 2022, unprecedented damage was recorded on three strings of the Nord Stream pipelines and the never-commissioned Nord Stream 2 pipeline. The Russian Prosecutor General’s Office opened a criminal case over an act of international terrorism.

title: Mahama urges chiefs to help tackle galamsey, protect water bodies
body: President John Dramani Mahama has appealed to traditional authorities to intensify their support for the government’s fight against illegal mining, warning that community resistance and the lack of alternative livelihoods continue to undermine efforts to curb the menace. He made the appeal when he received a delegation from the Western North Regional House of Chiefs at the Presidency in Accra. The delegation, led by Ogyeahoho Yaw Gyebi II, was at the Presidency to congratulate the President on his victory in the 2024 elections, acknowledge development projects in the region and present concerns requiring government attention. Mr Mahama said enforcement operations had uncovered senior high school students working at illegal mining sites because their families could not afford to support their education. He disclosed that several young people had been arrested, with hundreds awaiting trial, but argued that law enforcement must be accompanied by economic opportunities. “Alongside enforcing the law against illegal mining, we must provide alternative livelihoods. That is why we are implementing the New Economy Policy,” he said, adding that investment in job-creating sectors, including tourism, could help steer young people away from galamsey. The President also called for stronger community cooperation with the National Inter-Ministerial Coordinating Committee on Illegal Mining (NAIMOS), particularly in forest reserves and around water bodies. He said resistance from some community members and traditional authorities had resulted in dangerous confrontations with security personnel, including incidents involving gunfire and fatalities. The President further announced that the government had allocated an additional GH¢400 million in the next Budget to recruit more Blue Water Guards to patrol water bodies and destroy changfang machines encountered during operations. Mr Mahama said the government had cleared all nine forest reserves previously classified as red zones because of extensive destruction and the presence of heavily armed illegal miners. He added that soldiers had been stationed in the areas to prevent miners from returning after earlier operations were followed by renewed incursions. The government, he said, was also working with the military and Forestry Commission through GoldBod-supported efforts to reclaim degraded land, level damaged sites and replant economic trees. Ogyeahoho Gyebi commended the President for development projects in the region and reaffirmed the chiefs’ commitment to supporting efforts to promote peace and national development. Mr Mahama reiterated that traditional authorities were essential partners in the fight against illegal mining because of their close ties to local communities and their ability to help build support for enforcement and alternative livelihood programmes.

title: Ollie Watkins on target for Al Hilal while Sardar Azmoun bags double as Shabab Al Ahli win in Jeddah
body: Sardar Azmoun struck both goals as Shabab Al Ahli picked up a superb away win at Al Ittihad in the AFC Champions League on Tuesday night. The victory took the UAE club to a perfect six points from six, while Saudi Pro League Al Ittihad have just a single point after opening their campaign with a draw against Al Shamal SC of Qatar last month. Backed by a full house in Jeddah, the home side started positively with Ahmed Al Julaydan forcing Matheus Donelli into a save from a tight angle in the sixth minute. Shabab Al Ahli , however, struck in the next phase of play when Guilherme Bala powered down the left before teeing up the unmarked Azmoun to slot home. Al Ittihad looked for an immediate response, with Steven Bergwijn testing Donelli from distance in the 13th minute, but the visitors doubled their advantage three minutes later. Reza Ghandipour, who had only just replaced the injured Bala, released Azmoun with a through ball and the forward outpaced his markers before converting from a tight angle. “We conceded two goals because of easy mistakes, which made the task difficult afterwards,” said Al Ittihad coach Jens Wissing. “My job as a coach is to work with the players. We were better in the second half and we reached the opponent's goal, but we were not successful.” He added: “We played with three forwards because we had more crosses, and it was possible to make use of one of the crosses. We did not play the game well. We had many chances and we could have been better.” Timing, composure, finish. 🎯 Sardar Azmoun did it all to cap a superb 🇦🇪 Shabab Al Ahli move for his second of the night. #ACLElite | #ITTvSAH pic.twitter.com/ITta4kYAkK — #ACLElite | #ACLTwo (@TheAFCCL) October 13, 2026 Watkins on target for Al Hilal Elsewhere, Al Hilal recorded their second successive victory after defeating Al Sadd 2-0. Ollie Watkins put Saudi Pro League leaders Hilal ahead in the first half before a Ruben Neves spot-kick confirmed the points as Qatar’s Al Sadd suffered a second consecutive defeat. “I am happy with the players' performance,” said Hilal boss Simone Inzaghi. “We produced a big performance and controlled most of the game, and I saw a wonderful display from the team.” The Italian also praised Gabriel Martinelli after the former Arsenal man gave the Al Sadd defence a difficult evening. “He is a big player and we are lucky to have him with us,” added Inzaghi. “He always proves his high quality and his ability to serve the team and benefit it in more than one different position.”

title: Female IDF officer denied entry to Haredi military base because of gender, IDF says
body: Haredi (ultra-Orthodox) soldiers serving in the Hasmonean Brigade refused to allow a female IDF officer to enter a military outpost on Mount Hermon because of her gender, KAN News reported Tuesday evening.The logistics officer arrived to help prepare for winter, including refurbishing fuel storage tanks that provide electricity and hot water to hundreds of soldiers.She arrived alongside civilian contractors working for the Defense Ministry. While the contractors were granted entry, the officer was turned away, even from the area outside the outpost where the fuel tanks are located.לוחמים חרדים מנעו מקצינה להיכנס למוצב החרמון, בניגוד להנחיות. קבלנים שהגיעו איתה נכנסו מיד, אבל לקצינה נאמר שלא תוכל לגשת אפילו לאזור שמסביב. צה"ל: "מדובר בתקלה, הכניסה הייתה צריכה להתאפשר" | פרסום של @ItayBlumental #מהדורתכאןחדשות עם @talberman https://t.co/iuDS11QvC0— כאן חדשות (@kann_news) October 13, 2026IDF General Staff regulations allow male and female personnel from other units to enter bases housing haredi troops to perform professional duties.The IDF clarified that although the Hasmonean Brigade operates under the "David" track, requiring all personnel serving in the unit to be observant Jews, the restriction does not apply to outside personnel."This was a mistake. The officer should have been allowed to enter the outpost, while creating the necessary conditions for her to perform her duties in accordance with the provisions of the order," the military said.Democrats candidate warns of growing exclusion of womenDemocrats Party candidate Moran Zer Katzenstein condemned the incident, warning of growing extremism and the exclusion of women."This is not Jewish law; this is extremism and a threat to security," she said."The moment soldiers dare to close a gate in the face of a female IDF officer and expel her from a military outpost is a glaring warning sign for all of us," she said.She added that "A female officer carrying out her duties is not a hazard that needs to be hidden from sight."Zer Katzenstein warned that such incidents could threaten women's military service, claiming that "Within four years, women will no longer serve in the military."Incident comes amid debate over haredi military enlistmentThe incident comes less than two weeks before Israel's October 27 elections, with haredi military enlistment remaining a contentious issue.Israeli authorities have arrested some haredi draft evaders, while the outgoing government has sought legislation limiting penalties for those refusing to enlist.The issue has fueled months of haredi protests, with demonstrators chanting "We would rather go to jail than the army" and "We will die and not enlist."The Hasmonean Brigade was established in June 2025, following IDF preparations to accommodate the haredi way of life.Givati soldiers jailed after refusing to serve alongside female paramedicA similar incident occurred in August, when 17 Givati Brigade soldiers refused to board a Namer armored personnel carrier alongside a female paramedic during a Gaza operation.According to the IDF, five soldiers received 10-day detention sentences, and 11 others received five-day sentences. The operation was canceled after they refused.

title: New 8 km dual carriageway to link Al Mabela with Muscat Expressway
body:
Muscat: Muscat Municipality has begun construction of a road project to link al Nuzha Street in al Maabilah with the Muscat Expressway, as part of efforts to improve the road network in Muscat Governorate and ease traffic flow amid rapid urban expansion. The project involves the construction of an 8.08-km dual carriageway, with additional lanes at intersections to increase the road’s capacity. It also includes 3.75 km of single-carriageway service roads to improve connectivity between Al Nuzha Street and the Muscat Expressway and facilitate access to nearby facilities, residential areas and planned developments. Eng. Sami bin Salim al Rahbi, the project manager, told Oman News Agency (ONA) that the project also includes four major intersections equipped with smart traffic signal systems. These are expected to improve traffic management, reduce congestion and enhance road safety for motorists. The project forms part of the municipality’s efforts to upgrade road infrastructure in the governorate and accommodate the growing demand on its transport network.

title: Bank of Ghana pilots digital cross-border payments with Rwanda, Nigeria
body: The Bank of Ghana is testing cross-border interoperability using central bank digital currencies, stablecoins, bank accounts and mobile wallets. This is being implemented in the corridors between Rwanda and Nigeria. The pilots in the two corridors have been designed to test whether different forms of money can move seamlessly across borders without passing through correspondent banks outside the continent. The central bank has also extended the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System, (PAPSS) to mobile wallets in the Ghana–Nigeria corridor, marking a shift from bank-only settlement to inclusion of mobile money. Dr Johnson Pandit Asiama, the Governor, Bank of Ghana, made the disclosure at a high-level event on the margins of the 2026 International Monetary Fund (IMF)/World Bank Group (WBG) annual meetings in Bangkok on Tuesday. The event was on the theme: “Digital innovations in payments; SSA future Agenda,” on the back of the continent moving beyond adoption to scaling digital payments that delivered efficiency, inclusion and stability across the region. “The Bank is testing cross-border interoperability using CBDCs, stablecoins, bank accounts and mobile wallets in the Ghana–Rwanda and Ghana–Nigeria corridors and has extended PAPSS to mobile wallets in the Ghana–Nigeria corridor,” Dr Asiama said. He explained that the objective was to move the pilots to live services, building on existing infrastructure such as PAPSS rather than creating new systems, with the interoperability testing to meet users where they already transacted. He said bringing mobile wallets onto PAPSS could allow a trader in Accra to pay a supplier in Lagos instantly in local currency, without needing a dollar intermediary or a foreign correspondent bank. The Central Bank Governor said with mobile wallets were dominant in both Ghana and Nigeria, and Rwanda becoming a key partner for regulatory innovation, the partnership between Ghana, Rwanda and Nigeria was strategically important. He stated that until now, PAPSS largely operated a bank-to-bank system, limiting its reach to customers who are already banked, while most cross-border trade was driven by mobile money users. The new approach, he said, reflected a growing consensus among African central banks that interoperability, not new infrastructure, was the key to reducing costs and improving speed and transparency. “The future of African payments will not be defined by a single technology, and central banks should not determine which technology succeeds. Our role is to ensure that emerging systems are safe, efficient, resilient and inclusive,” Dr Asiama said. He called for enhanced regional collaboration to build a safe, efficient, and inclusive payment ecosystem that supports Africa’s trade, investment, and long-term development ambitions. On regulation, the Central Bank Governor raised concerns over African fintechs facing costly and duplicative licensing in each market they entered, even where the activities and risks were similar. “Our Licence Passporting Framework with the National Bank of Rwanda offers a practical model, and we are engaging more than 10 countries to join. We would welcome its adoption as a regional approach, alongside common standards for payment messaging, payee verification, and fraud data sharing,” he said.

title: Retirees now receive benefit within 48hrs – PenCom
body: The Director General of the National Pension Commission, Omolola Oloworaran has stated that the ongoing pension reforms have improved the welfare of retirees and led to pension asset boost which now stands at N31.4 trillion. Speaking on Tuesday at the 2026 PenCom Conference for journalists in Abuja, Oloworaran said the theme of conference “Reform to Reality” is reflecting on retirees. The DG said for the first time under the Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS) retirees received across board increases through Pension Boost 1.0 which raised monthly pensions for more than 241,000 retirees from N12.15 billion to N14.83 billion, with some low level retirees seeing up to 100 percent increase. “The Federal Government has cleared pension liabilities inherited since 2007 after President Tinubu approved N758 billion intervention, with payments reaching 957,000 beneficiaries. “Other milestones listed include zero waiting time policy where federal retirees now receive pensions immediately after retirement and accrued rights credited up to December 2029 through verification exercise, approval of retirement benefits now in 48 hours against former 21 months and introduction of exit benefits scheme since January 1, 2026 where eligible Treasury funded MDAs’ employees with at least 10-year service receive 100 per cent of total annual emolument on top of normal pension,” she said. Oloworaran disclosed that the first set of 175 retirees received about N1.1 billion in August under the exit scheme. She said PenCom has also built a national distribution framework for the informal sector through accredited pension agents and announced that two more historic programmes will be launched during National Pension Week from October 26 to 30, 2026. The programmes are PenCare, retiree health programme to give 30,000 low income retirees free health care at start and minimum pension guarantee to set floor below which no eligible CPS retiree will fall. She also said pension assets rose from N20.7 trillion in July 2024 to N31.48 trillion in June 2026 representing over N10.7 trillion new retirement wealth while 938,229 Nigerians joined the scheme within the period. She warned employers that deduction of pension without remittance is a breach of law, noting that cumulative recoveries from defaulting employers now stand at N36.6 billion as of July 2026. She also said the Pension Industry Leadership Council approved an independent assessment of industry maturity and endorsed the first $250 million pension industry infrastructure fund with $200 million from operators and $15 million from government finance institutions.

title: Strikes on Russian data centers could be as disruptive as attacks on oil refineries, expert says
body:
Cybersecurity expert Kostiantyn Korsun said this in an interview with Ukrainian Radio , as reported by Ukrinform.
According to Korsun, Ukrainian data centers are essentially no different from those in Russia, the Netherlands, Germany, the United States or elsewhere.
“But the consequences of strikes are different. The point is that access to the internet and data centers in Russia – which are used not only for internet access, but also for data storage and hosting – is highly centralized. The data centers operated by Yandex are giants. They offer dozens and hundreds of different services and have virtually monopolized this market in Russia,” the expert said.
In Ukraine, he said, the system is decentralized and distributed, whereas in Russia it is highly centralized.
“That is why the consequences are so different. When we were hit, most users barely noticed anything; only some resource owners who had failed to make backups were affected. In Russia, meanwhile, there is an uproar: people are complaining that this or that does not work – taxis, smart homes, hubs, even payments at cafes,” Korsun said.
Internet access in Russia is also tightly controlled by the government and security services, which have installed so-called “black boxes” at providers to monitor traffic.
The expert believes that if Ukrainian strikes continue at the current pace, scale and effectiveness, Russian businesses could begin to collapse.
“They are now trying to save the most widely used services by moving them to other data-center facilities. This cannot be done quickly. They are looking for any available servers, and there is a global shortage of them,” he said.
Korsun noted that disruptions to services such as taxis could have broader economic consequences, as fewer people would be able to get to work, drivers would lose income, and economic activity and tax revenues would decline.
He also pointed to Yandex’s role as a major provider for the corporate sector, including banks.
“Banks need somewhere to run their processing systems. No infrastructure, no processing – the bank cannot operate, and card payments stop. These are already shock-level developments,” Korsun said.
He suggested that a major disruption to internet infrastructure could trigger a banking panic, with people rushing to withdraw their deposits and convert their money into cash.
According to the expert, this could lead to the collapse of Russia’s banking system.
Korsun also said that data centers could become an alternative target if an “energy truce” limits strikes on oil refineries and energy infrastructure.
“There are many data centers in Russia – roughly four to five times more than in Ukraine. If we have 50–60, they have around 230–240. But this is a promising area. If oil refineries and energy infrastructure cannot be targeted, there are warehouse complexes or IT infrastructure,” he said.
He added that Russia’s last major data center is located in Mytishchi, north of Moscow, and said that a successful strike could cause major disruptions for months.
As Ukrinform reported, President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukrainian strikes on Yandex data centers, carried out in response to Russian attacks on data centers in Ukraine, had reduced the presence of malicious bots on social media.

title: Cedi edges higher as GoldBod boosts dollar supply to banks
body: The Ghana cedi has recorded marginal gains against the US dollar on the interbank market for the second consecutive week, supported by improved foreign exchange liquidity. Market watchers estimate the appreciation at just under 1%, offering some relief after sustained pressure on the local currency since the third quarter. The pressure has been linked to increased demand for dollars by businesses financing imports ahead of December, as well as energy-related payments by the Bank of Ghana for crude oil and finished petroleum products. The recent gains follow near-weekly depreciation since last month. What is driving the recovery? Market players have attributed the recovery to increased foreign exchange support, particularly dollar sales by the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod). On Tuesday, GoldBod sold US$197 million to commercial banks at a rate of GH¢11.70 to the dollar. Joy Business understands that every participating bank received the full amount it requested, easing demand pressures and raising expectations of further gains for the cedi. The sales, conducted through GoldBod’s GoFX platform, complement other measures by the Bank of Ghana to support liquidity in the foreign exchange market. The intervention is in line with GoldBod’s plan to supply US$1 billion to commercial banks under its revised arrangements for foreign exchange receipts from gold exports in the artisanal and small-scale mining sector. Some commercial banks have told Joy Business that they expect the cedi to remain fairly stable if the improved liquidity support is sustained.

title: NAFDAC bursts Trade Fair Complex den of fake energy drinks, wine, whisky ‘manufacture’
body: By Chioma Obinna The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control, NAFDAC, has uncovered a suspected counterfeit drinks production facility at Zamfara Plaza, BBA Trade Fair Complex, along the Badagry Expressway, Ojo, Lagos State. Read Also: Toxic pesticides in food: NAFDAC warns of health risks, seizes ₦800m banned chemicals The Agency arrested two suspects allegedly involved in the illegal operation. The suspects, identified as Okafor and John, were arrested during an enforcement operation in a two-storey building where equipment and materials allegedly used to repackage and produce counterfeit alcoholic and energy drinks where discovered. The raid, according to NAFDAC, followed credible intelligence and surveillance on suspected counterfeiters operating within the Trade Fair International Market. Speaking during the operation, the Assistant Director of the Investigation and Enforcement Directorate of NAFDAC, Mr Kunle Ojo, said the agency caught some of the suspects in the act and recovered drums, filters, packaging materials, a heating device and other equipment allegedly used in the illicit production process. “Gentlemen of the press, as you can see today, when we came, we caught some red-handed producing all kinds of alcoholic drinks,” Ojo said. “What we have discovered today is a lot, and it’s mind-boggling. We are here to protect the lives of many Nigerians.” Ojo said the agency intensified its enforcement activities ahead of the festive season, when demand for alcoholic and other beverages typically rises. He warned that the circulation of counterfeit drinks posed a serious public health concern, urging suspected manufacturers to abandon the illegal trade. “You are killing Nigerians in order to make money, which is not good,” he said, appealing to those involved to stop the activities. The NAFDAC official disclosed that the agency would investigate the source of the products, the raw materials used and the individuals allegedly financing or directing the operation. “Where are they getting the products from? Where are they getting their raw materials? Who is employing them to do this kind of dangerous activity?” He added that the agency would evacuate the recovered materials and products to its warehouse for further action, including destruction in accordance with applicable procedures. “Those people that we have arrested today will be dealt with administratively and definitely will face the law,” Ojo said. Ojo also appealed to Nigerians to support the agency by providing credible information about suspected counterfeit production facilities. “If you see something, say something,” he said, assuring informants that their identities would be protected. Confession One of the arrested suspects, Okafor, who identified himself as a drinks dealer in the market, in an interview with Vanguard at the scene said: “I deal on drinks. I change the bottle of the drink. It’s not that the bottle is not good. It’s the drink in there, because the other one is already damaged. So that’s why we are putting it to the next bottle,” he said. Also speaking during the operation, Mrs. Christiana Obiazikwor, Deputy Director, NAFDAC Public Relations, said the agency routinely carried out surveillance, seizures, arrests and destruction of unregistered and counterfeit products, despite public criticism that it was not doing enough to tackle the menace. “NAFDAC is still at work. We are on the streets. We are in the markets. We are everywhere,” she said. Obiazikwor explained that enforcement teams often conducted operations without publicity to avoid alerting suspected offenders or triggering confrontations. She said the agency decided to take journalists along on the latest operation to demonstrate its activities and reassure Nigerians that it remained committed to protecting public health. “Most of the things they do, we don’t publicise them so that we don’t raise alarm,” she said, adding that enforcement officers continued to visit suspected production and distribution points. She urged members of the public to report suspected counterfeit production and distribution directly to NAFDAC rather than merely posting allegations on social media. “There’s no point going to social media to create fear. Report to NAFDAC and we’ll do the needful.” Obiazikwor assured informants that the agency would protect their identities, urging Nigerians to provide credible information that could assist investigations. Speaking, the Assistant Director, Head Public Relation, Investigation & Enforcement, Mrs. Victoria Jennifer Akudu, explained that the raid was part of the agency’s routine efforts to uncover illegal manufacturing activities and protect consumers. “Every day, our people are in the field. Our enforcement department, they are on the field trying to uncover this. And they do a lot,” Akudu said. She explained that the agency routinely confiscated products, carried out seizures and destroyed offending goods, adding that the latest operation was intended to demonstrate the work being done by enforcement officers. “This is just a routine activity of our enforcement directorate,” she said. Akudu further disclosed that the suspected operators had allegedly moved from an earlier location after enforcement action, prompting officials to continue tracking their activities. “We have confiscated and sealed off the place. They moved to another place. This time around, we passed through the back door. And that is how we are able to get them,” she said. She urged Nigerians to report suspected counterfeit products directly to NAFDAC rather than allow rumours and unverified claims to create unnecessary public fear. Akudu assured the public that the agency remained committed to its responsibilities, stressing that its enforcement teams were continuing operations against suspected manufacturers and distributors of illegal products. “I will ask Nigerians not to fear. We are alert and we are alive. We are doing our statutory function the way it should be,” she said. NAFDAC officials said the operation formed part of continuing efforts to remove counterfeit, adulterated and unregistered products from the Nigerian market. The agency reiterated that consumers could be exposed to serious health risks when drinks were repackaged under the labels of established brands without proper quality controls or verification of their contents.
