Those whose loyalties are less apparent can attract greater acceptance. “It appears that we have a certain level of discomfort in knowing that somebody is openly partisan and being sent to an independent constitutional body.” His comments come after President John Mahama swore in Dr Joseph Kwaku Asamoah and Emelia Afi Agbenyo as EC deputy chairpersons on Monday, October 12. They fill vacancies following Dr Bossman Eric Asare’s resignation and Samuel Tettey’s retirement. At the ceremony, the President charged the appointees with upholding electoral integrity, ensuring fairness, and strengthening public confidence. Dr Osae-Kwapong proposed assessing appointees against standards he described as the “Akufo-Addo test”. He drew those standards from remarks he said former President Nana Akufo-Addo made when swearing in EC appointees in 2023. “And he talked about things like, if the person can serve with integrity, the person can serve with fairness, if the person can be professional, and if the person can show independence of mind and judgment.” For him, the assessment should also examine the Commission’s internal safeguards. He questioned how much influence one openly partisan member could exercise among fellow commissioners. “Are there internal safeguards? Are we so worried that we are thinking one person who is publicly partisan can actually do the bidding of a political party in the midst of six other peers?” He said his concern would be reduced if the other commissioners could restrain a member seeking to advance partisan interests. His argument focuses on both the individual’s conduct and the institution’s capacity to check bias. An appointee’s public political image, he suggested, does not settle either question.

title: 2027: Tompolo Mobilises Lagos for Tinubu, Pleads Against Repeat of 2023 Election Outcome
body: Sunday Ehigiator Leader of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, Government Ekpemupolo, has urged the people of Lagos State to ensure that the outcome of the 2023 presidential election in the state was not repeated in 2027. He called on residents to take advantage of the ongoing Continuous Voter Registration exercise by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and obtain their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) to enable them to vote massively for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, whom he described as one of their own. Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, who was represented by Kestin Pondi, made the call in Lagos yesterday, during a campaign rally for Tinubu’s re-election. At the event, he also presented 57 campaign vehicles to the movement’s state coordinators. “What happened in 2023 must not be repeated. He must win convincingly in 2027,” he said. He described Tinubu as a selfless and courageous leader who was committed to implementing bold reforms, regardless of their implications for his re-election. He added that the reforms were already yielding results and benefiting many Nigerians. Ekpemupolo noted that Lagos had become a city for Nigerians from across the country because of the foundation laid by Tinubu, which successive governors had built upon. He said that, given Tinubu’s current national responsibilities, the people of Lagos needed to stand firmly behind him. “Lagos is the city for all Nigerians because someone stood firm to restructure and reform it. From the time he came into office in 1999 until he left in 2007, Lagos was the envy of other states. “Today, he has a higher responsibility and an opportunity to replicate the Lagos success story across Nigeria through reforms. There is massive development across the states today because reforms are working,” he said. Ekpemupolo urged the people of Lagos and Nigerians at large to take the campaign message to every community and household, insisting that Tinubu was the right candidate for the country. Also speaking, Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, said Nigeria was moving towards economic stability under the Tinubu-led administration. He urged residents to disregard opposition politicians whom he accused of lacking clear plans for the country and being more interested in winning elections. He also criticised politicians who had moved from one political party to another, describing such inconsistency as an undesirable quality in a leader. Sanwo-Olu said Tinubu had constructed more roads than previous administrations within three years, provided support for students, increased the minimum wage and made funds available for the payment of pensions. “Why won’t we vote for him? The entire Lagos is for Tinubu. All our votes are for Tinubu. You’ve done it before; you’ll do it again. We will touch every corner of Lagos with our message to re-elect Tinubu. Go out and convince everyone that Tinubu is the candidate to vote for,” the governor said. Earlier, the National Coordinator of the movement, Sunday Asuku, urged Lagos residents to obtain their PVCs and use them to vote massively for Tinubu. “We must stand our ground and deliver Tinubu with PVCs, not with guns or intimidation. Lagos must not put their son, Tinubu, to shame,” he said. Asuku added that Nigerians must make a bold statement in the 2027 presidential election by retiring what he called “serial contesters,” whom he described as “enemies of Nigeria.”

title: Senate Moves to Decriminalise Attempted Suicide, Provide Treatment for Survivors
body: • Seeks urgent ecological funds as erosion, landslides ravage Cross River communities • Declares Kebbi insecurity, mass displacement national emergency •Passes bill to establish legal framework for Yusuf Maitama Sule University of Education Sunday Aborisade in Abuja The Senate on Tuesday advanced a bill seeking to decriminalise attempted suicide in Nigeria and provide medical treatment and continuing support for survivors, while calling for urgent federal intervention over deadly erosion and landslides in Cross River State and declaring worsening insecurity and mass displacement in Kebbi State a national emergency. The upper chamber also passed a bill sponsored by the Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Jibrin Barau, to provide a statutory framework for the Yusuf Maitama Sule Federal University of Education, Kano. The four developments highlighted the Senate’s legislative and oversight interventions on public health, environmental disasters, national security, humanitarian relief and education. Leading debate on the bill to decriminalise attempted suicide, its sponsor, Senator Asuquo Ekpenyong, said the proposed legislation sought to resolve the contradiction between existing criminal laws and the National Mental Health Act, which recognises the need for medical intervention during mental health emergencies. He said the bill would replace punitive responses to suicide attempts with appropriate medical assessment, treatment and continuing support for survivors. “At the heart of this bill is a simple question. When a Nigerian survives a suicide attempt, should the first response of the state be persecution or protection?” Ekpenyong asked. The senator noted that while the National Mental Health Act recognised attempted suicide as a psychiatric emergency requiring immediate intervention, Section 327 of the Criminal Code and Section 231 of the Penal Code continued to expose survivors to criminal punishment. “Our law presently speaks with two voices,” he said, insisting that the contradiction needed to be resolved to ensure that people experiencing mental health crises received appropriate care rather than prosecution. Ekpenyong warned that criminalising attempted suicide could discourage people from seeking help, encourage families to conceal incidents and prevent health workers from reporting cases promptly. He also argued that treating suicide attempts as criminal offences could deepen the stigma surrounding mental health conditions and undermine efforts to obtain reliable data for national suicide prevention programmes. “The police station or correctional facility should not be the default destination for a person who requires urgent clinical care,” he said. The proposed legislation would establish a coordinated framework for suicide prevention, crisis response, referrals and continuing support for survivors. It would also promote public education and training for health workers, teachers, law enforcement personnel and emergency responders to help them identify warning signs and connect vulnerable people with appropriate services. Supporting the bill, Senator Adedayo Faduyile, representing Ondo South, drew on his medical experience to argue that attempted suicide should be treated as a medical emergency rather than a criminal offence. He said depression and other mental health conditions could impair a person’s judgment, making treatment and recovery more appropriate responses than punishment. “The best way to treat anybody who did not succumb to a suicide attempt is actually not to criminalise it. They need help,” Faduyile declared. He argued that placing survivors in police stations or correctional facilities would not address the underlying medical conditions responsible for their distress, stressing the need for professional care. Senator Abdul Ningi, representing Bauchi Central, commended Ekpenyong for bringing the issue before the Senate, describing it as an important legal and public health debate that deserved broader professional and public consultation. He said the bill should proceed to further scrutiny to enable psychologists, medical practitioners and other stakeholders to contribute to a more effective national response. However, the debate raised questions about the proposed amendment’s application across states operating under different criminal justice frameworks. Senate Leader Opeyemi Bamidele cautioned that provisions of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act were not automatically applicable in every state, depending on the legal framework adopted by the respective Houses of Assembly. He said the Senate needed to clarify the extent to which the proposed amendment would apply nationally before proceeding further. The bill advanced through second reading for further legislative scrutiny. In a separate intervention, the Senate urged the Federal Government to approve and urgently release adequate resources from the Ecological Fund to tackle gully erosion and landslides threatening communities in Cross River South Senatorial District. The resolution followed a motion of urgent national importance moved by Ekpenyong, who identified Atakpa, Edim Otop, Ikot Effangha Mkpa, Nyaghasang, Ikot Anwatim, Nasarawa/Bacoco, Akai Effa, Bayside and Summit Hills as among the affected communities. He also warned that landslides threatened Anansa. The senator recalled that a landslide at Ikot Anwatim in July 2026 killed five people, including four siblings from the same family, destroyed two houses and injured two residents. Another landslide at Edim Otop claimed the life of an eight-year-old girl. Ekpenyong said the disasters had caused deaths, destroyed property and displaced residents, leaving affected families traumatised and struggling to rebuild their lives. He attributed the recurring incidents to poorly designed drainage systems, rapid urbanisation, blocked drains, indiscriminate waste disposal, unregulated sand mining, vegetation removal and poor land-use practices. Warning that isolated remedial projects could transfer erosion risks to neighbouring communities, he called for coordinated watershed planning and comprehensive environmental interventions. “Further delay risks additional deaths, deeper displacement and greater destruction. This emergency demands immediate mobilisation of federal resources, including the Ecological Fund,” he said. The Senate urged the Federal Ministry of Environment to work with the Cross River State Government and relevant agencies to assess dangerous locations and commence emergency protective works. It also directed the National Emergency Management Agency, the state emergency management agency and local councils to provide immediate assistance to bereaved and displaced families, including temporary shelter, food, medical care and psychosocial support. The chamber called for early-warning systems and continuous monitoring of unstable locations, while urging the Ministries of Environment and Works to prioritise erosion-control projects based on appropriate geotechnical and hydrological assessments. Senate President Godswill Akpabio mandated the Senate Committee on Environment to inspect affected locations, assess existing interventions, engage relevant agencies on funding and implementation, and report back for further legislative action. The Senate also raised the alarm over worsening insecurity and mass displacement in Kebbi State, urging the Federal Government to treat the situation as a national security and humanitarian emergency. The resolutions followed a motion moved by Senator Adamu Aliero and seconded by Senator Francis Fadahunsi, representing Ondo South, over deadly attacks by bandits reportedly moving into Kebbi from neighbouring states following intensified military operations. The lawmakers called on the Chief of Army Staff, the Chief of Air Staff and the Inspector-General of Police, working with other security and intelligence agencies, to intensify coordinated operations, improve surveillance and intelligence gathering, and deploy adequate personnel and equipment to protect vulnerable communities. They also urged the Federal Government to provide the manpower, operational logistics and financial resources needed to prevent further attacks and stop residents from being driven out of their ancestral homes. On the humanitarian situation, the Senate called on NEMA to assess the needs of displaced persons and provide food, potable water, temporary shelter, clothing, bedding, medical supplies and sanitation facilities. It further urged the Federal and Kebbi State Governments to establish a joint security and humanitarian response mechanism to coordinate emergency interventions, ensure the effective distribution of relief materials and facilitate the safe, voluntary and dignified return of displaced residents when security conditions permit. The chamber also called for thorough investigations into the killings, including the reported murder of three employees of Hitech, and urged security agencies to identify and prosecute those responsible. Lawmakers observed a minute’s silence in honour of those killed and extended their condolences to bereaved families and affected communities. Meanwhile, the Senate passed a bill sponsored by Barau to provide a statutory foundation for the Yusuf Maitama Sule Federal University of Education, Kano, following the institution’s conversion from a federal college of education into a university. President Bola Tinubu approved the conversion of the Federal Colleges of Education in Kano and Zaria into federal universities of education in September 2024. He subsequently approved the renaming of the Kano institution after the late statesman Yusuf Maitama Sule on May 10, 2025, following a request by Barau on behalf of his constituents. Leading the debate on the bill, Barau said the legislation was necessary to provide the institution with the legal backing required for effective administration, management and the promotion of teacher education. “Mr Senate President, this institution has already been established by the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria,” he said. Barau recalled his previous efforts in the National Assembly to upgrade federal colleges of education into full-fledged universities, noting that earlier bills passed by the Senate had not received presidential assent. He said President Tinubu subsequently approved the conversion of the Kano institution after he conveyed the aspirations of his constituents, adding that the President also granted the request to name the university after the late Maitama Sule. “We cannot thank Mr President enough. He loves Kano and has consistently acceded to our requests,” Barau said, citing other federal education projects approved for Kano State. Akpabio commended Barau for sponsoring the legislation and thanked senators for supporting its passage, expressing optimism that Tinubu would assent to the bill when transmitted to him. The proposed law is expected to provide the university with the statutory and regulatory framework needed to discharge its mandate and contribute to national development.

title: Nigeria Records 1134 Confirmed Cases of Lassa Fever, 267 Deaths
body: Onyebuchi Ezigbo in Abuja The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) said Nigeria has recorded a total: of 1,134 confirmed cases of Lassa Fever with 267 deaths since January this year. In its latest update on Lassa Fever epidemic published last night NCDC said Situation Report for Week 39 (21st – 27th September 2026) and week 40 (28th September – 4th October 2026) showed a total: 1134 confirmed cases, 267 deaths have been recorded. It said the report also showed a case fatality rate CFR 23.6 percent (higher than 18.5 percent same period in 2025). According to NCDC, 24 states recorded at least one confirmed case across 119 Local Government Areas. The report said that 88 percent of confirmed cases were from Bauchi, Ondo, Taraba, Benue and Edo State. It said the predominant age group affected is 21- 30 years with no new healthcare worker affected in the reporting Week 39.

title: Vatican: Pope Leo Diagnosed with Lung Cancer, Undergoes Surgery
body: •Doctors remove lower lobe of his right lung •Vatican cancels pontiff’s engagements Emmanuel Addeh in Abuja Pope Leo XIV has been diagnosed with lung cancer and has undergone surgery to remove the lower lobe of his right lung, the Vatican confirmed yesterday, raising fresh questions about the health of the 71-year-old pontiff. The Vatican disclosed that tests conducted during the operation confirmed a diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma, a common form of lung cancer. The diagnosis had been suspected before the surgery, according to a medical bulletin issued after the procedure. The surgery, performed at Rome’s Gemelli Hospital, lasted approximately 90 minutes, while the pontiff spent about three hours in the operating room. The Vatican said the operation was successful and there were no complications. “To ensure a radical resection, the lower lobe of the right lung was removed using a video-assisted technique,” the Vatican said in a statement. “Intraoperative histological examination confirmed the diagnosis of pulmonary adenocarcinoma, as suspected from pre-operative tests,” it added. According to the Vatican, Leo regained consciousness normally after the procedure and was returned to his room on the hospital’s 10th floor. However, the Vatican did not disclose the stage of the cancer, whether it had spread beyond the affected portion of the lung or whether the pope would require additional treatment. The development comes after the Vatican announced on Sunday that Leo would undergo surgery following the discovery of a nodular lesion in his lung. Speaking during his Sunday noon blessing, the pontiff said he had accepted his doctors’ recommendation to remove the abnormal growth. “The doctors believe it’s best to take action, so, following their advice, I’ve decided to have surgery to remove it,” Leo said. “Thank you for your spiritual support, and I entrust myself to your prayers,” he stressed. The Vatican subsequently cancelled all the pope’s scheduled audiences through October 20, although it has yet to announce whether the disruption will affect his planned South American trip, scheduled to begin on November 6. Medical recommendations following procedures of this kind typically include avoiding air travel for approximately three weeks, potentially leaving the pontiff with little time to recover before the planned journey. CBS News, which reported the development, quoted Candida Moss, the Edward Cadbury professor of theology at the University of Birmingham in England, as saying the Vatican’s limited disclosures could make it difficult to determine the full extent of the pope’s condition. “The Vatican tends to keep these things under wraps, so there’ll be a lot of reading between the lines to try and detect what is the state of the pope’s health,” Moss told CBS News. Moss added that Vatican protocol provides for cardinals and aides to assume many of the pontiff’s responsibilities when necessary. “We should also expect that, in as much as is possible, Pope Leo is going to continue to work,” Moss said. “We have a long tradition of popes — not just Pope Francis, but also Pope John Paul II, who had Parkinson’s for 10 years — who continued to remain as active as they could, and as active in Catholic liturgies as they could, right up until the end of their tenures,” Miss explained. Leo is known for maintaining an active lifestyle, including swimming and playing tennis, factors that may have helped him prepare for the operation. Earlier on Tuesday, the pope walked through the main entrance of Gemelli Hospital and waved to dozens of well-wishers gathered to greet him before the procedure. The Vatican said the operation was conducted by a medical team led by the hospital’s chief thoracic surgeon, Dr Stefano Margaritora. Although Gemelli Hospital has a dedicated papal apartment used by previous pontiffs, complete with a private chapel on the 10th floor, Leo is staying in a nearby hospital room because the apartment is undergoing renovations, the Vatican press office said. Lung adenocarcinoma is the most common type of lung cancer in the United States, accounting for approximately 40 per cent of diagnosed cases, according to the Lung Cancer Foundation of America. The disease develops in glandular cells, often in the outer regions of the lungs. It can be detected at an earlier stage than some other forms of lung cancer because it may progress more slowly, although its behaviour varies from patient to patient. Possible symptoms include fatigue, shortness of breath, and pain in the chest or upper back. Treatment options depend on the stage and extent of the disease and may include surgery, chemotherapy, immunotherapy and radiation. The Vatican has not disclosed whether Leo will require any of these additional treatments following the removal of the affected lung lobe, the CBS report said.

title: NDLEA at UNGA: Nigeria Demands Global War on Drug Cartels, Illicit Finance
body: • Agency reports 38,242 arrests, 5.8mkg drug seizures, 6,232 convictions in 21 months Michael Olugbode in Abuja Nigeria has called for stronger international intelligence-sharing, intensified action against illicit financial networks and increased investment in drug-control institutions in developing countries, warning that criminal organisations are exploiting gaps between jurisdictions to expand the global drug trade. The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) made the call at the ongoing 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York, where it presented Nigeria’s evolving drug-control system as an example of how institutions can adapt to increasingly sophisticated criminal threats. The agency’s position formed part of Nigeria’s statement under the theme, “Restoring Trust, Managing Transformation: A United Nations that Delivers for All.” The statement was delivered on Monday by the NDLEA Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Brig. Gen. Buba Marwa (rtd.), who was represented by the agency’s Secretary, Shadrach Haruna. Marwa told the Assembly that the NDLEA had moved beyond a predominantly enforcement-driven model to become an integrated, intelligence-led and people-centred institution combining law enforcement, public health, technology, financial investigation, alternative livelihoods and international cooperation. He said the transformation was necessary because the nature of the drug threat had changed dramatically. “Trafficking networks have become more sophisticated, technology has opened new channels for illicit activity, criminal proceeds move rapidly across borders, and drug dependence continues to affect individuals, families and communities,” he said. “Nigeria therefore broadened its focus from drugs and offenders alone to the criminal networks, illicit profits and vulnerabilities that sustain the drug economy.” The agency said the new approach had produced significant results in both drug supply reduction and demand reduction. Between January 2025 and September 2026, the NDLEA recorded 38,242 arrests, seized more than 5.8 million kilogrammes of illicit drugs valued at over N2.5 trillion and secured 6,232 convictions. During the same period, more than 16,303 people received counselling, treatment or rehabilitation, while prevention and sensitisation campaigns reached millions of Nigerians. Marwa, however, stressed that the agency’s performance could no longer be measured solely by the number of arrests made or drug consignments seized. He said the NDLEA was increasingly focused on dismantling major trafficking organisations, disrupting organised criminal structures and tracing the financial networks that sustain the illicit drug economy. “The real measure of success is not only the volume of drugs seized or the number of arrests made, but the extent to which we dismantle the structures, profits and vulnerabilities that sustain the trade,” he said. The NDLEA chairman also highlighted Nigeria’s Alternative Development initiative, which is being piloted in three communities in Ondo State. The programme is designed to help residents move away from illicit cannabis cultivation and adopt legitimate agricultural production. Marwa said the initiative reflected the agency’s recognition that drug control could not succeed through enforcement alone. “Sustainable drug control requires more than removing an illicit crop. It requires credible economic alternatives that strengthen food security, community resilience and national security,” he said. He also cited the NDLEA’s Drug Integrity Test and Visa E-Administration System as examples of how digital technology could improve accessibility, efficiency, transparency and integrity in public administration. According to him, the reforms are being consolidated under the National Drug Control Master Plan 2026–2030. The plan is built around six pillars: drug supply reduction; drug demand reduction; access to controlled medicines; governance and coordination; alternative development; and disruption of the illicit drug economy. Nigeria urged member states to strengthen timely and reliable international intelligence-sharing, warning that delays and information gaps were enabling trafficking networks to move drugs, money and personnel across borders with increasing ease. It also called for intensified action against the illicit financial economy through financial investigation, asset tracing and asset recovery. The country further urged governments and international partners to expand prevention, treatment, rehabilitation and reintegration programmes alongside enforcement measures. It called for greater support for Alternative Development initiatives to ensure that communities abandoning illicit cultivation had sustainable and legitimate sources of income. Nigeria also appealed for increased investment in the capacity of law enforcement agencies, noting that drug cartels were deploying increasingly sophisticated technology, logistics and financial systems. The country urged the international community to invest in institutions responsible for drug control, particularly in developing countries, through technology, specialised training, forensic capabilities, treatment infrastructure and sustained technical assistance. Marwa described Nigeria’s experience as an ongoing process rather than a finished model, saying the country remained willing to share its lessons, learn from other nations and deepen cooperation with member states, the United Nations and international partners. He said the ultimate objective was to translate international commitments into practical results. “Our objective is to move from commitment to implementation, from cooperation to collective action and from transformation to measurable delivery,” he said. The NDLEA said Nigeria’s experience demonstrated that effective drug control required a coordinated response that combined enforcement with public health, economic empowerment, technology, financial intelligence and international cooperation. It warned that without such a comprehensive approach, criminal networks would continue to exploit vulnerable communities, weak institutions and jurisdictional gaps to expand the illicit drug economy.

title: Oborevwori Tasks African Youths on Leadership, Innovation
body: • As SILB Africa 2026 Bootcamp opens in Asaba Sylvester Idowu in Warri Governor Sheriff Oborevwori of Delta State has urged African youths to take active interest in leadership and politics, saying their participation is critical to shaping the continent’s future. He urged young people to move beyond complaints about governance and become actively involved in the political process to drive meaningful change in their communities and countries. Oborevwori spoke yesterday while declaring open the fifth edition of the Social Innovation and Leadership Bootcamp (SILB) Africa 2026, with the theme, “Architects of Change,” at Unity Hall, Government House, Asaba. Represented by the Commissioner for Transport, Onoriode Agofure, the governor said leadership demanded courage, service, commitment and the ability to translate ideas into practical solutions to societal challenges. He noted that Africa needed young people capable of innovating, creating opportunities, building sustainable enterprises and contributing to community development. The governor said the initiative aligned with his administration’s MORE Agenda, particularly its commitment to youth empowerment through skills acquisition, entrepreneurship and technological innovation. He cited the contributions of the Delta State Job and Wealth Creation Bureau, skills acquisition and entrepreneurship programmes, and the Delta State Innovation Hub in equipping young people with practical skills and opportunities for economic independence. Oborevwori also referenced targeted training programmes, including a recent workshop on electric vehicles for young Deltans, as part of efforts to prepare them for emerging industries. He commended the Senior Special Assistant to the Governor on Youth Mentoring and Development, Elvis Akpobi, alongside the organisers, mentors, facilitators and partners, for investing in the development of emerging African leaders. Earlier, Akpobi said the bootcamp was designed to equip young people with the leadership skills, knowledge and exposure needed to contribute meaningfully to Nigeria’s development and that of the African continent. He disclosed that about 50 international delegates were participating in the fifth edition of the programme in Asaba, stressing the need to create more opportunities for young people to participate actively in governance and policymaking. Akpobi commended Oborevwori for supporting youth-focused initiatives under the MORE Agenda, noting that the governor’s commitment to youth development went beyond rhetoric. Speaking with journalists, Barr. Eugene Uzum said sustainable good governance depended largely on the ability of leaders and other critical stakeholders to recognise the role of young people in nation-building. He described the bootcamp as an initiative aimed at nurturing a patriotic generation of young Africans capable of taking responsibility for the continent’s future. Also speaking, the founder of Connected Development, Hamzat Lawal, stressed the need to sustain youth participation in politics and governance, describing leadership training as essential to preparing young Africans for leadership responsibilities.

title: Sanwo-Olu Urges Lagosians to Stay Vigilant Against Cybercrime
body: • Calls for stronger digital safety practices as Lagos joins global Cybersecurity Awareness Month Sunday Ehigiator Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu of Lagos State has urged residents to remain vigilant against cybercrime and adopt basic digital safety practices as the state joins the global community to mark the 2026 Cybersecurity Awareness Month. Sanwo-Olu, in a statement yesterday, signed by the state Commissioner for Information and Strategy, Gbenga Omotoso, described cybersecurity as a shared responsibility, urging citizens to take proactive measures to protect themselves from cybercriminals. “Cybersecurity is a shared responsibility. Citizens must remain vigilant, understand common cyber risks, and take proactive steps to protect themselves from cybercriminals,” the governor said. He added that many cybercrime victims were vulnerable because they lacked knowledge of basic digital safety practices, stressing the importance of public education in preventing online fraud and other cyber threats. “Most victims of cybercrime are those who are unaware of basic digital safety practices, making public education essential.” The state’s participation in the annual campaign aligns with the global initiative led by the United States Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, which promotes safer digital practices, improved cyber hygiene and stronger protection of digital systems. According to the statement, the Sanwo-Olu administration has, over the past three years, pursued cybersecurity initiatives aimed at strengthening digital trust and improving the security of businesses, government institutions and residents. Through the state’s Cybersecurity Advisory Board and the Ministry of Innovation, Science and Technology, the government has implemented programmes designed to improve cybersecurity awareness and strengthen the state’s digital security infrastructure. The statement noted that Lagos earlier this year launched the Lagos State Cybersecurity Guidelines, a framework outlining security best practices for small, medium and large businesses. It said the guidelines provide practical and scalable security measures tailored to different categories of businesses, offering organisations clear guidance on protecting their digital assets. The state has also expanded cybersecurity training, awareness and professional development programmes across public institutions as part of efforts to build local capacity and strengthen digital resilience. In addition, Lagos is working towards achieving ISO 27001 certification and developing other advanced capabilities to enhance digital trust and safeguard critical digital infrastructure. As part of activities for the awareness month, the Ministry of Innovation, Science and Technology, in collaboration with the Cybersecurity Advisory Board led by Prof. Fene Osakwe, will conduct multilingual awareness campaigns across social and traditional media throughout October. The campaigns will be delivered in English, Yoruba and Pidgin English to ensure wider reach and accessibility across communities in the state. Residents will receive practical guidance on identifying and avoiding phishing scams, creating strong passwords, enabling multifactor authentication and regularly updating their digital devices. The government said the initiatives were consistent with global best practices and reflected its commitment to building a digitally secure, innovative and resilient economy. It urged Lagosians to remain informed, alert and security-conscious while using digital platforms and services.

title: INEC: Political Parties Have 14 Days to Notify Us Over Omission of Candidates From Final List of Governorship Election
body: Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has said that under Section 32(2) of the Electoral Act, 2026, political parties that believe their candidates were wrongly left off the list have 14 days from the date of publication to notify the Commission. INEC National Commissioner and Chairman, Information and Voter Education Committee, Mohammed Haruna in a statement issued Tuesday said said affected political parties have until 24th October, 2026 to make their complaints known. Recall that following the publication of the finalist list of Governorship candidates for the 2027 general election, opposition parties have accused the commission of bias. In Ogun State, Ladi Adebutu, the governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) was left out of the final list, ditto to the former Minister of Communication and Digital Economy and governorship candidate of PDP in Gombe state, Isa Pantami. Haruna noted: “The general public is aware of the recent decision of the Supreme Court in INEC v. Zenith Labour Party, Appeal No. SC/CV/495/2026 delivered on 24th September, 2026. “The decision arose from INEC’s appeal against the judgement of the Court of Appeal, which nullified the provisions of Section 77(5)-(7) of the Electoral Act, 2026 requiring the submission of membership registers as a prerequisite for the conduct of valid party primaries.” The National Commissioner recalled that the Supreme Court, in the aforementioned judgement, held that the provisions of Section 77(5)-(7) of the Electoral Act, 2026 are constitutional and mandatory for all political parties. He said in particular, the Court upheld the constitutionality of Item No. 2 of INEC’s Timetable and Schedule of Activities, which mandated political parties to submit their membership registers between 21st April and 10th May, 2026. Haruna further recalled that the Court held that failure to comply with the provisions of Section 77 (5)-(7), renders the defaulting political parties ineligible to sponsor any candidate for the election. He added: “In accordance with Section 287(1) of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (as amended), the Commission, while finalising the list of candidates for the Governorship election applied the above decision of the Supreme Court and excluded political parties that failed to comply with Section 77(5)-(7) of the Electoral Act, 2026, in relation to fielding of candidates. “Meanwhile, the final list of Presidential and National Assembly candidates had already been published on 12th September, 2026, thirteen days before the Supreme Court delivered its judgement. “Under Section 32(2) of the Electoral Act, 2026, political parties that believe their candidates were wrongly left off the list have 14 days from the date of publication to notify the Commission. The deadline is 24th October, 2026.” The Commission assured the public of its commitment to transparency, the rule of law and the credibility of the electoral process.

title: Catholic Church Challenges Lagos Govt Over Island Property
body: Wale Igbintade The Catholic Archdiocese of Lagos has approached the Court of Appeal, Lagos Division, seeking to overturn a judgment of the Lagos State High Court declaring the state government the owner of a disputed property at No. 17/19 Okoya Street, Idumagbo, Lagos Island. The archdiocese, through the Sole Trustee of the Catholic Archdiocese of Lagos, is challenging the judgment delivered by Justice I. O. Kasali on January 10, 2018, arguing that the government’s takeover of St. Patrick’s Catholic Primary School did not automatically confer ownership of the entire property on the state. In its proposed amended notice of appeal, filed in Appeal No. CA/L/W/644/2019, arising from Suit No. LD/120/2000, the church maintained that it acquired the property from the Lagos Executive Development Board through a conveyance dated September 15, 1938. The conveyance, according to the archdiocese, was registered as No. 27 at page 27 in Volume 483 at the Lands Registry, Alausa, and constitutes documentary evidence of its title to the land. The appellant argued that there was no evidence that its proprietary interest in the property had been lawfully acquired or revoked by the Lagos State Government. It described the disputed property as a large expanse of land comprising Block 1, Plots 1, 2, 3, 16, 17 and 18, on which St. Patrick’s Catholic Church and the primary school are situated. The church contended that the government’s claim related to the school and did not extend to the church premises or the entire property. It faulted the trial court for failing to distinguish between the school premises and other facilities on the land, including a dilapidated building that previously served as a school building and church hall before the construction of a new school. According to the Archdiocese, the old structure continued to serve as a church hall for Sunday services and other religious activities, adding that the government had never used the building after assuming control of the school. The appellant argued that the trial court erred in declaring the entire property government-owned and granting possession to the state without sufficient evidence establishing the precise boundaries and extent of the land allegedly acquired. It maintained that the government failed to produce the relevant acquisition instrument or establish the specific portion of the property covered by the purported acquisition. The church also challenged the trial court’s reliance on the parties’ alleged admission that the government assumed control and management of schools in 1979, during the administration of former Governor Lateef Jakande. It argued that an admission that the government took over the management of a school could not, in itself, establish ownership of the land on which the school stood. The archdiocese further contended that the government failed to demonstrate that the takeover of St. Patrick’s Catholic Primary School extended to the abandoned building and other portions of the property claimed by the church. It also faulted the trial judge for allegedly failing to properly evaluate evidence elicited from government witnesses under cross-examination, which the appellant said supported its position that the government took over the school rather than the entire property. The church equally challenged the dismissal of its counterclaim, insisting that its documentary evidence of title and longstanding exercise of ownership rights over the property entitled it to the reliefs sought. In support of its appeal, the archdiocese cited judicial authorities on proof of title to land, the requirements for granting declaratory reliefs and the obligation of parties in land disputes to establish the precise identity and extent of the property in contention. It also questioned the legal basis for the alleged acquisition, arguing that the government failed to establish compliance with applicable laws governing the acquisition of private property, including the Land Use Act and Section 44 of the 1999 Constitution. The appellant further faulted the trial court for allegedly failing to consider the decision in Archbishop Okogie v. Attorney-General of Lagos State (1981) 2 NCLR 337, which it cited in support of its arguments concerning the legal framework governing the acquisition of private primary schools in Lagos State. The archdiocese is asking the Court of Appeal to allow its appeal and set aside the judgment declaring the Lagos State Government the owner of the disputed property. It is also seeking an order dismissing the government’s counterclaim, setting aside the purported acquisition of the premises of St. Patrick’s Catholic Primary School at No. 17/19 Okoya Street, Idumagbo, and granting its own counterclaim in its entirety. The proposed amended notice of appeal contains 10 grounds challenging the trial court’s findings on ownership, the alleged acquisition, the evaluation of evidence and the dismissal of the church’s counterclaim.

title: Senate, House Begin Consideration of Tinubu’s N100.5bn Yobe Airport Reimbursement Request
body: • Akpabio gives upper chamber’s committee one month to report Sunday Aborisade and Juliet Akoje in Abuja President Bola Tinubu yesterday sought the approval of the Senate and the House of Representatives for a N100.5 billion promissory note programme to compensate the Yobe State Government for transferring ownership of the Muhammadu Buhari International Airport, Damaturu, to the federal government In the Senate, the request, which forms part of the federal government’s 70th Promissory Notes Programme, was referred to the Senate Committee on Local and Foreign Debts for scrutiny, with Senate President Godswill Akpabio directing the committee to submit its report within one month. In a letter read by Akpabio, the proposed reimbursement followed the Federal Executive Council’s approval of the takeover of the airport and repayment of the project cost incurred by the Yobe State Government. According to the President, the council approved the arrangement at its second extraordinary meeting held on May 23, 2023, under which the Federal Government would reimburse the state through the promissory notes programme. Tinubu told the Senate that the Bureau of Public Procurement (BPP) had completed its review of the project and recommended N100,509,017,234.55 as the amount payable to the state. “In the light of the foregoing, I urge the Senate to consider and approve the establishment and issuance by the Debt Management Office of a promissory note programme in the sum of N100,509,017,234.55,” the President stated in the letter. He also urged the lawmakers to expedite consideration of the request, expressing confidence that the Senate would act promptly on the proposal. “While looking forward to the expeditious action on this submission, please accept, Distinguished Senate President, the assurances of my highest esteem,” Tinubu added. The referral to the Committee on Local and Foreign Debts marks the next stage of legislative consideration before the Senate determines whether to approve the proposed programme. If approved, the arrangement would provide the mechanism for the Federal Government to settle its financial obligation to Yobe State for the construction of the airport, following the FEC-approved takeover. The committee is expected to examine the request and report its findings to the Senate within the one-month period stipulated by Akpabio. The proposed N100.5 billion reimbursement underscores the financial implications of the Federal Government’s decision to take over infrastructure projects initially financed by state governments, with the promissory notes programme serving as the proposed repayment mechanism in this case. In the House of Representatives, the request was conveyed in a letter read by the Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, when lawmakers resumed plenary after their annual recess yesterday. In the letter, the President requested the lawmakers’ authorisation for the establishment of the programme to facilitate the payment to the state government following the airport’s takeover. The President also appealed to the lawmakers to expedite consideration of the request. In a separate legislative communication, Tinubu forwarded the National Research Development Fund Bill to the House for consideration, alongside two proposed laws aimed at incorporating international humanitarian and criminal justice instruments into Nigeria’s domestic legal system. The two other proposals were the Geneva Conventions and Additional Protocols Bill, 2026, and the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court Enforcement Bill, 2026. Transmitting the bills, the President invoked Section 50A of Section 2 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, and requested the House’s consideration of the proposed legislation on the Geneva Conventions and the enforcement of the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court. The Geneva Conventions and Additional Protocols Bill, 2026, seeks to repeal the existing Geneva Convention Act and incorporate into Nigerian law the Geneva Conventions adopted on August 12, 1949, as well as the two Additional Protocols adopted on June 8, 1977. The proposed legislation is designed to modernise Nigeria’s legal framework for meeting its obligations under international humanitarian law, particularly in protecting individuals affected by armed conflicts. Similarly, the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court Enforcement Bill, 2026, seeks to give legal effect to the Rome Statute in Nigeria and establish provisions for the prosecution and punishment of genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes and other related offences. The bill also provides for a framework to facilitate Nigeria’s cooperation with the International Criminal Court in the discharge of its mandate. Responding to the President’s legislative proposals, Abbas assured that the House would give prompt and thorough consideration to the bills and other requests submitted by the executive. He reiterated the commitment of the 10th National Assembly to prioritising significant legislative proposals, specifically highlighting the National Research Development Fund Bill and the proposed laws seeking to domesticate the Geneva Conventions and their Additional Protocols. The Speaker stressed that the bills relating to the Geneva Conventions and the Rome Statute carried important national and diplomatic implications. He noted that their passage would strengthen legal safeguards for civilians, wounded persons and prisoners caught up in armed conflicts. Abbas however, commended Tinubu for forwarding the proposals to the legislature and expressed confidence that the House would discharge its constitutional responsibilities in examining and acting on the bills.

title: French Star Fanny Ardant Honours Messolonghi Exodus Anniversary
body: French actress Fanny Ardant recited poetry by Greek national poet Dionysios Solomos, French writer Victor Hugo and British poet Lord Byron at the Garden of Heroes in Messolonghi on Saturday, October 10, in an event marking 200 years since the Exodus of Messolonghi and commemorating the struggle for freedom. The Athens Epidaurus Festival organised the event in collaboration with the Municipality of the Sacred City of Messolonghi and the French Institute of Greece, under the auspices of the French Embassy in Greece. The audience gave Ardant an emotional round of applause as she recited excerpts in French from Solomos’ The Free Besieged , Hugo’s poem Les Têtes du sérail and Byron’s words before his death: “I gave Greece My time, My health, My fortune, And now I give her My life.” The event’s dramatic journey connected the statue of Solomos with the Tomb of the Unknown Fallen, the Lord Byron monument and the grave of Markos Botsaris. It also included a stop at the monument commemorating the French fighters who died in Messolonghi. Writer and cultural producer Giorgos Archimandritis curated the content, while Michail Marmarinos oversaw the artistic direction. Greece and France commemorate shared history Speakers highlighted the historic ties between Greece and France and the anniversary’s contemporary significance. Messolonghi Deputy Mayor Nikolaos Papanikolaou welcomed the guests and emphasised the international significance of the city’s sacrifice, declaring: “Here, the history of the city meets the history of Europe.” Before the event began, French Ambassador to Greece Nicolas Kassianides laid a wreath at the monument to the French fighters. In his address, Kassianides highlighted the European impact of Messolonghi’s sacrifice and its relevance today. He stressed that “freedom and democratic values are never definitively secured” and emphasised culture’s essential role in passing these values on to future generations. “Freedom can become a common cause,” he said. Marmarinos, director and artistic director of the Athens Epidaurus Festival, underscored the power of art with a brief introduction: “This is what art does. It brings people together from everywhere. For good.” He also spoke about his personal connection to Messolonghi and the continuing presence of Philhellenism in the city. Conductor and artistic director of the Messolonghi Municipal Conservatory Spyros Cholevas coordinated the event. Cultural initiative extends the festival beyond its traditional venues The event drew inspiration from the cultural programme Greece and France in the 19th Century , which the Hellenic Foundation for Culture organised in Paris in collaboration with the Sorbonne University’s Department of Greek Studies and the Delphys cultural association. The programme marked the 200th anniversary of the Greek Revolution and originated as an initiative by Archimandritis, a writer, creator of arts and culture radio documentaries, and doctor of comparative literature at the Sorbonne who previously served as the Hellenic Foundation for Culture’s cultural ambassador in Paris. Ardant’s appearance in Messolonghi forms part of the Athens Epidaurus Festival’s new initiative, EXODUS (Beyond the Walls), which expands the festival’s activities beyond its established venues. Through this initiative, the festival takes its programme directly to audiences, activates different locations throughout the city and creates new opportunities for artistic encounters. The post French Star Fanny Ardant Honours Messolonghi Exodus Anniversary appeared first on Greek City Times .

title: Chinese companies seek Gulf partnerships as physical AI takes shape
body: Chinese robotics companies are looking to the Gulf as a possible manufacturing centre for the next generation of AI-powered machines, as the region's capital, energy resources and industrial ambitions create opportunities for partnerships. Beijing-based robotics company LinkerBot is among those exploring opportunities in the UAE, where it is in talks with major institutions on potential partnerships, Weber Su, the company's vice president and head of global markets, said during the AIM Summit in Dubai on Tuesday. One model being considered would involve Chinese companies supplying advanced robotics parts, while the UAE provides capital-intensive assembly and automated production. Such an arrangement could allow Gulf countries to take part directly in making advanced robots, rather than mainly buying the technology. “That could be the business model that we are exploring with Middle Eastern countries, particularly in UAE,” Mr Su said. LinkerBot specialises in dexterous robotic hands, enabling machines to grasp and manipulate objects. It has expanded into components including reducers and micromotors that control robotic movement. The potential collaboration reflects a broader trend in which Asian companies seek international manufacturing partners, while Gulf economies use their capital, energy and infrastructure to build higher-value industries. In September, Chinese electric and extended-range vehicle maker ROX Motor began producing vehicles in Abu Dhabi . The UAE, meanwhile, is also boosting manufacturing and under its Operation 300bn strategy aims to increase the industrial sector's contribution to gross domestic product to Dh300 billion by 2031. The country's industrial exports rose 25 per cent last year to a record Dh262 billion, with medium and high-technology exports increasing 42 per cent to Dh92 billion, according to the Ministry of Industry and Advanced Technology. The UAE is also investing in automation to improve manufacturing competitiveness. Mr Su said Chinese companies could increasingly focus on specialised robotics parts, while Gulf partners develop the capital-intensive assembly operations needed to bring those technologies to market. Turning that potential into commercially successful partnerships will require investment agreements, viable production models and sustained demand for AI-powered machines. The next wave of AI? The potential partnerships come as the technology industry moves towards what investors and developers describe as the next stage of artificial intelligence: physical AI. Chinese AI developers including DeepSeek , Zhipu AI and Moonshot AI are becoming increasingly competitive with their US rivals, offering advanced models at lower costs, according to Joseph Zeng, founder and chief investment officer of Hong Kong-based Arcadia Fund Management Group. While generative AI has focused on chatbots, content creation and software applications, the next phase is expected to bring intelligent systems into the physical world. Physical AI combines advanced AI models with robotics, allowing machines to interpret their surroundings, make decisions and perform tasks traditionally requiring human intervention. Introducing vision-based tactile sensing on the LinkerHand. 320 × 240 per fingertip. 0.05 mm spatial resolution. 0.1 N force sensitivity. More than 380,000 sensing points across the hand. Touch, made visible. #LinkerHand #LinkerBot https://t.co/0u9e0MMyd0 — Linkerbot (@LinkerbotHQ) September 27, 2026 Unlike conventional industrial robots, which are generally programmed for repetitive movements, the ambition is to develop machines capable of adapting to different situations. Applications could include robotic hands manipulating unfamiliar objects, autonomous machines working across production lines and robots assisting hospital patients. Mr Su said advances in computing power and AI models were making these capabilities increasingly possible. LinkerBot is developing robotic hands with built-in movement ability that could eventually be combined with sophisticated AI systems to perform a wider range of tasks. “We're going to have skill stores similar to the app stores,” Mr Su said. China's manufacturing scale could give its companies an advantage as the technology shifts towards commercial production. The country installed about 295,000 industrial robots in 2024, accounting for 54 per cent of global installations, according to the International Federation of Robotics . The figures refer to factory robots rather than humanoids, but demonstrate the scale of China's industrial automation industry and supporting supply chains. SK hynix held 50 per cent of the global high-bandwidth memory market by revenue in the second quarter of 2026, while Samsung accounted for 33 per cent, according to Counterpoint Research data reported by the Yonhap news agency. Opportunities beyond robotics "Physical AI provides a lot of opportunities for investors,” said Mr Zeng, whose investments include ByteDance and Zhipu AI in China, as well as South Korea's SK hynix and Samsung. The next stage of AI would require advances in computing hardware and infrastructure, he added. He identified high-bandwidth memory, optical transceivers and robotics components among the technologies benefitting from rising investment. Health care could also become an important market. During a recent visit to Suzhou, near Shanghai, Mr Zeng said he encountered a company developing a voice-controlled robot designed to assist bedridden patients with repositioning and personal care. Mr Su said humanoid robots could eventually help to care for elderly people and children in smaller communities, where shrinking populations make it difficult to attract doctors and maintain healthcare services. While fully autonomous, general-purpose robots are still being developed, their potential to ease labour shortages, reduce care costs and extend essential services to underserved communities illustrates the social and economic impact physical AI could have beyond factories. For the Gulf, opportunities could include using autonomous systems in established industries. Mr Zeng highlighted electric and autonomous heavy-duty trucks for mining and industrial operations, alongside energy storage and cleaner power technologies. Energy is also becoming increasingly important to AI investment. Global data-centre electricity use is expected to more than double to about 945 terawatt-hours by 2030, according to the International Energy Agency . The forecast highlights the importance of electricity generation, storage and cooling infrastructure as AI adoption accelerates. For Gulf countries with substantial energy resources and growing renewable power capacity, this creates another potential area of collaboration with Asian technology developers.

title: Tinubu: Corruption Can’t Be Uprooted in Nigeria Without Independent, Reform-minded Bench
body: • Tasks judiciary to probe prosecution strategies, seal procedural gaps exploited by criminals Deji Elumoye in Abuja President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has declared that corruption in Nigeria cannot be eradicated without an independent and reform-minded bench. Speaking on Tuesday in Abuja during the annual EFCC/NJI Capacity Building Workshop for Judges and Justices, Tinubu maintained that there would be no meaningful progress in efforts to tackle graft “without an independent, progressive, and reform-minded Bench”. While commending the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) for convening the 8th edition of the Judges and Justices Workshop, the president, who was represented by Vice President Kashim Shettima, said the workshop was timely and necessary in “fostering the institutional cohesion required to confront corruption’s ever-changing architecture in Nigeria”. At the workshop, themed, “Investigation and Prosecution of Economic and Financial Crimes in a Digital Age,” Tinubu stated, “My Lords, we confront a rapidly shifting criminal landscape. Technology has amplified the audacity and reach of illicit actors, ushering in sophisticated crimes driven by destructive ingenuity. “The rise of blockchain technology and artificial intelligence has introduced unprecedented layers of complexity to traditional illicit activities. “Because these modern crimes constantly mutate, law enforcement and judicial authorities must continuously build capacity to adapt and respond effectively.” Tinubu also tasked the judiciary to dismantle the procedural loopholes and flawed prosecution tactics that allowed criminals to escape justice. He demanded an aggressive overhaul of the justice system to ensure that no well-connected individual could manipulate technicalities to evade the full, crushing weight of the law. The president urged the judiciary to interrogate existing statutory frameworks against the backdrop of emerging financial crimes. “Probe prosecution strategies, dismantle outdated precedents, and seal procedural gaps that politically exposed persons and organised crime actors exploit to delay or frustrate trial,” he stated. Tinubu warned that while financial and economic crimes posed an existential threat to Nigeria, corruption had no respect for status and spared no arm of government. According to him, framing the anti-corruption campaign as purely an executive agenda is a fundamental error because compromised public services equally affect the executive, legislature, judiciary, and ordinary citizens. Stating that corruption was a battle against the nation’s collective survival, the president said, “We must no longer permit legal pyrotechnics and procedural pedantry to shelter criminality. The Bench is not merely a mechanical arbiter of rules, but an active guardian of moral order and social equity. “Law is, by design, an instrument of social engineering; it must invariably prioritise the public good over narrow, selfish interests shielded by technical manoeuvres. Our courts must embody the spirit, and not just the arid letter, of the law.” Tinubu urged the judiciary to adapt to the shifting dynamics of financial crime, stressing that realigning the country’s investigative and prosecutorial strategies is critical to preventing institutional obsolescence. He explained, “We are already on the right trajectory. The EFCC’s recent momentum in tackling cryptocurrency fraud and its commendable strides in recovering virtual assets are highly reassuring. The agency has recovered billions of naira in cryptocurrency investment-related fraud cases. “In 2025, the agency secured the forfeiture of $22,417.91 (Twenty-Two Thousand, Four Hundred and Seventeen Dollars, Ninety-One Cents) worth of Bitcoin; 1,001,301.87 USDT (One Million, One Thousand, Three Hundred and One USDT and Eighty-Seven Cents) in digital assets; and US$5.6 million linked to the CBEX scheme, while 192 foreigners arrested for cyber-terrorism and cryptocurrency fraud were successfully prosecuted and deported afterwards.” Tinubu said while EFCC’s actions showed an agency that was proactive, forward-looking and resolved not to be outpaced by technological innovation, the judiciary “must complement law enforcement by rapidly upscaling its capacity.” He acknowledged efforts by Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN) to reform the judiciary. The president pledged the full support of the executive arm of government to ensure that the Nigerian judiciary was adequately equipped to meet the demands of justice delivery in the digital age. Earlier, Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN), Hon. Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, said the 8th edition of the event reflected the commitment of NJI and EFCC to sustain efforts to address challenges confronting stakeholders in Nigeria’s justice system. Kekere-Ekun said the trend in technology had impacted how digital evidence was obtained and recorded. She stated that the effective administration of criminal justice in the digital era required firm and disciplined case management, which capacity building programmes, such as the EFCC and NJI collaboration, aimed to strengthen. The CJN stated that sustained judicial education and capacity development in the justice sector was yielding positive results with the improved conduct of judicial officers especially judges in case management and the dispensation of justice in recent years. Chairman of Senate Committee on Anti-corruption and Financial Crimes, Senator Emmanuel Udende, said the timing of the workshop was apt given the increasing sophistication of financial crimes and corruption, particularly, cases involving politically exposed persons. Udende said such cases directly impacted timely case management and the dispensation of justice. He assured the stakeholders that the National Assembly remained committed to supporting the enhancement of the war against corruption and financial crimes in Nigeria through proactive legislation. Attorney-General of the Federation (AGF) and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, who was represented by Director of Public Prosecution, Mr Rotimi Oyedepo, urged synergy among stakeholders in addressing emerging challenges in Nigeria’s fight against corruption. Fagbemi stated that one arm of government alone could not effectively address the problem. He urged judicial officers, especially judges and lawyers, to leverage opportunities provided during the workshop to enhance their capacities to make investigation more thorough and prosecution more diligent. In his welcome address, Administrator of the National Judicial Institute, Justice Babatunde Adejumo, said the collaboration between EFCC and NJI in enhancing the capacity of judicial officers had become an integral part of government’s efforts to frontally tackle the dynamics and scale of financial crimes in the digital age. He said the presence of the vice president at the event was a practical demonstration of the commitment of the Tinubu administration to boost Nigeria’s war against corruption. Executive Chairman of EFCC, Mr. Ola Olukoyede, said the event was a national imperative that had become an important component of the annual programme of both EFCC and NJI. Olukoyede said the commission under his leadership was reform-minded and had recorded unprecedented convictions as well as financial recoveries over the past three years. He assured that transparent and judicious handling of recovered money and property. The EFCC chairman also regretted the effect of advanced technology on financial crimes as well as other forms of corruption, stating that digital innovation is fast outpacing legal instruments and provisions for prosecution.

title: Unaudited Results: Dangote Refinery Posts $22.5bn Revenue, $4.7bn Profit in 9 Months
body: • Revenue surges 144%, EBITDA jumps to $5.5bn as refining margins rise • Cash reserves hit $6.7bn, facility moves from $1.7bn net debt to $651m net cash Emmanuel Addeh in Abuja and Peter Uzoho in Lagos Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals has posted a net profit of $4.73 billion on revenue of $22.48 billion in the nine months ended September 30, 2026, marking a dramatic turnaround from a $117.2 million loss recorded in the corresponding period of 2025. The unaudited results, released yesterday, showed that revenue surged 144 per cent from $9.2 billion in the first nine months of last year, while earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) climbed nearly ninefold to $5.52 billion from $627.6 million. The performance, according to the company, reflected higher refining throughput, improved operational reliability and stronger refining margins, as the 700,000 barrels per day facility transitions from commissioning and production ramp-up to sustained commercial operations. Beyond the sharp increase in earnings, the refinery strengthened its financial position, with cash balances rising to $6.69 billion from $809.5 million a year earlier. Its balance sheet also swung from a net debt position of $1.73 billion in September 2025 to net cash of $650.8 million by September 2026. The figures represent a significant shift for the multibillion-dollar industrial complex as it pursues a landmark Initial Public Offering (IPO) intended to broaden African participation in its ownership and advance its expansion plans. Besides, the refinery’s EBITDA margin expanded to 24.56 per cent from 6.83 per cent in the corresponding period of 2025, indicating a substantial improvement in operating profitability. Operating cash flow also increased more than tenfold to $3.68 billion from $364.7 million, underscoring its growing capacity to generate cash from its core operations. The movement into a net cash position means the company’s cash holdings exceeded its reported debt obligations on a net basis, providing greater financial flexibility as it implements its expansion programme. The results also showed that the refinery’s financial performance accelerated in the third quarter, with substantial increases in revenue, operating earnings and net profit between June and September. According to the unaudited results, eevenue rose from $13.91 billion at the end of June to $22.48 billion by September, implying third-quarter revenue of approximately $8.57 billion. Similarly, EBITDA increased from $2.60 billion at the half-year mark to $5.52 billion at the end of September, suggesting that the refinery generated approximately $2.92 billion during the third quarter alone. In the same vein, net profit climbed from $1.82 billion in the first half of the year to $4.73 billion by September, representing an additional $2.90 billion in earnings in the three months to September. The figures highlighted the pace of the facility’s commercial expansion following its commissioning and initial production ramp-up. Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals, David Bird, attributed the strong results to increased throughput, greater operational stability and improved refining margins. Our third-quarter performance demonstrates the successful transition from commissioning and ramp-up activities to sustainable commercial operations. “Revenue increased to $22.5 billion from $9.2 billion in the corresponding period of 2025, while EBITDA rose to $5.5 billion from US$627.6 million, reflecting higher throughput, improved operational reliability and stronger gross refining margins,” Bird pointed out. Bird said the performance demonstrated the strength of the refinery’s integrated business model and provided a solid foundation for its next phase of growth. “These results reflect the strength of our integrated business model and provide a solid foundation as we progress through our IPO and execute our Vision 2030 growth strategy,” he stated. “With our expansion programme already underway, we remain focused on increasing refining capacity and broadening our product portfolio. We will continue to strengthen our distribution network across Africa and support energy security across the continent, while creating long-term value for stakeholders,” he added. The financial results come as the refinery advances its IPO, which is designed to give a broader cross-section of African investors an opportunity to own shares in one of the continent’s largest industrial investments. The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) recently approved an extension of the offer’s closing date from October 13 to October 27, 2026, to accommodate growing investor interest across Africa and facilitate wider cross-border participation. The offer has now been extended till October 27. The offer comprises 4.1 billion ordinary shares at N525 per share, translating to a total offering value of approximately N2.15 trillion. President and Chief Executive of Dangote Industries Limited, Aliko Dangote, had disclosed that subscriptions had already exceeded the company’s original fundraising target. He said the overriding objective was to broaden African ownership of the refinery rather than simply raise additional capital. The latest financial results provide investors with an indication of the refinery’s earnings capacity, cash generation and financial position as it seeks to attract a wider shareholder base. The IPO also coincides with the implementation of the group’s Vision 2030 growth strategy, which includes plans to increase refining capacity, expand petrochemical production and strengthen distribution networks across African markets. The expansion programme is expected to build on the refinery’s existing capacity and broaden its product portfolio, while reinforcing its role in meeting the continent’s energy needs. Located in the Lekki Free Zone in Lagos, Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals operates an integrated refining and petrochemical complex with a crude distillation capacity of 700,000 barrels per day. Built to international environmental, safety and product-quality standards, the facility is among the world’s modern large-scale refining complexes and represents a major investment in Africa’s energy and industrial infrastructure.

title: Tinubu Seeks Sweeping Reforms of Drug Enforcement, Safety Investigation Laws
body: • President transmits NDLEA, NSIB amendment bills to Senate, seeks expeditious passage Sunday Aborisade in Abuja President Bola Tinubu has asked Senate to consider two bills seeking to overhaul Nigeria’s legal frameworks for combating illicit drugs and investigating transportation accidents, including proposals to strengthen the powers of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) and expand the mandate of the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB) beyond aviation. Tinubu transmitted NDLEA Bill 2026 and NSIB Amendment Bill 2026 to Senate in separate letters addressed to Senate President Godswill Akpabio, pursuant to Section 58(2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended. While the proposed NDLEA legislation seeks to repeal the existing National Drug Law Enforcement Agency Act and the Indian Hemp Act and replace them with a consolidated legal framework for tackling drug-related offences, the NSIB amendment seeks to reposition the bureau as an independent, multimodal safety investigation authority. In his letter transmitting the NDLEA Bill, Tinubu said the proposed legislation would establish a consolidated framework to strengthen enforcement against the cultivation, processing, sale, trafficking and use of illicit drugs. The president explained that the bill sought to repeal the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency Act, Cap. N30, and the Indian Hemp Act, Cap. I16, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria 2004, in favour of a unified legislative framework. He stated, “The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency Bill 2026 seeks to repeal the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency Act, Cap. N30, and the Indian Hemp Act, Cap. I16, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria 2004, and to enact a consolidated framework to enforce the law against the cultivation, processing, sale, trafficking and use of hard drugs.” The proposed legislation also seeks to empower the agency to investigate persons suspected of involvement in drug-related activities, strengthening its capacity to tackle offences associated with illicit substances. Urging the senate to give the bill prompt consideration, Tinubu said, “While looking forward to the usual expeditious consideration of this submission, please accept, Distinguished Senate President and Distinguished Senators, the assurances of my highest consideration.” Following its presentation, Senate referred the NDLEA Bill to its Committee on Rules and Business for further legislative action. In a separate communication, the president transmitted the NSIB Amendment Bill 2026, seeking amendments to the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (Establishment) Act No. 35 of 2022. The proposed amendment seeks to transform the bureau from an institution primarily associated with aviation accident investigations into a multimodal safety investigation authority with responsibility for investigating occurrences across different transportation sectors. Under the proposed framework, NSIB’s mandate would extend beyond aviation accidents and incidents to cover occurrences involving rail, maritime, and other modes of transportation. The bill also seeks to transfer supervisory oversight of the bureau to the presidency while strengthening its institutional, operational and administrative powers. The proposed changes are intended to establish a broader legal and institutional framework for transportation safety investigations, covering multiple modes of transport under the bureau’s expanded mandate. In his letter to Senate, Tinubu said he was forwarding the proposed amendment for consideration in accordance with Section 58(2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended. He urged Senate to expedite consideration of the legislation. The NSIB Amendment Bill was subsequently referred to Senate Committee on Rules and Business for further legislative action.

title: Oba Ewuare II Pledges to Uphold Legacies of Oba Erediauwa at Memorial Lecture
body: Felix Omoh-Asun in Benin City The Benin monarch, His Royal Majesty Oba Ewuare II, has pledged to walk in the footsteps of his father, Oba Erediauwa, who was widely acclaimed as a philosopher king whose legacies remain indelible, and his wisdom and role in the cultural re-awakening of the Benin people are etched in their memory. Oba Ewuare gave the assurance at the first pre-inaugural lecture of the Oba Erediauwa Memorial Lecture Series, held at the University of Benin Auditorium in Benin City as part of activities marking his 10th coronation anniversary. The monarch was represented at the event by a delegation of palace chiefs led by Chief Enorense Ozigbo-Esere, the Eghaevbonore of Benin. His address was delivered by Professor (Chief) Victor Igbineweka, Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Academic) of the University of Benin. Oba Ewuare stated that Oba Erediauwa ranked among the first generation of African monarchs whose voices resonated beyond nation’s boundaries.
