title: European Clients for U.S. Armaments Face Years of Further Delays Due to Severe Shortages
body: European NATO members could face years-long delays in obtaining American weapons as the United States prioritises replenishing its own military stockpiles following its war against Iran, according to Washington’s ambassador to NATO, Matthew Whitaker. Speaking at the Warsaw Security Forum on October 12, Whitaker warned that American defence manufacturers would be largely occupied with meeting domestic requirements, leaving limited production capacity available for foreign customers. He urged European governments to expand their own defence industries to meet growing military requirements, stating: “The U.S. needs friends with manufacturing capacity.” The pressure on American weapons supplies is already affecting European procurement plans. Bloomberg reported in September that NATO members were facing delivery delays of up to several years as Washington prioritised rebuilding its own stockpiles. German requests for accelerated deliveries of Tomahawk cruise missiles were reportedly unlikely to be fulfilled within five years, illustrating the difficulties European governments may encounter when attempting to acquire advanced American weapons on an accelerated schedule. Such delays could complicate efforts to strengthen long-range strike capabilities at a time when European governments are seeking to reduce perceived vulnerabilities in their conventional forces. The effects of delayed deliveries to European states compound the effects of severe shortages resulting from the transfer of substantial quantities of military equipment to Ukraine. A European Defence Agency assessment presented in September identified significant gaps in air and missile defence, ammunition and other essential military capabilities. Efforts to establish domestic production of Patriot interceptors in Germany have yet to deliver the anticipated results, leaving European armed forces dependent on a limited international supply of critical weapons. Expanding domestic manufacturing could reduce this dependence, although developing production lines for sophisticated missiles and interceptors requires investment, specialised industrial capacity and time. The United States Armed Forces are facing a mounting crisis over the sustainability of its precision-guided munitions inventories, following multiple phases of high intensity combat operations against Iran that began in late February. According to retired Marine Corps Colonel and Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) analyst Mark Cancian, the United States may have by July already expended between one-third and one-half of its inventories of several critical precision-guided weapons during the conflict. Although exact figures remain classified, the assessment has added to growing concerns within Congress and the Pentagon regarding the ability of the American defence industry to replenish advanced munitions quickly enough to meet wartime requirements. A CSIS assessment in late May highlighted that this depletion had seriously weakened the U.S. force posture across much of the world.

title: Villarreal fight back to beat Napoli and end losing run
body: Villarreal secured their first Champions League win in eight matches after coming from behind to beat Napoli at the Estadio de la Ceramica. The La Liga side had suffered seven consecutive defeats in the competition since drawing 2-2 with Juventus in October 2025. After a narrow 3-2 defeat by Borussia Dortmund on the opening matchday, Villarreal looked set to become the first Spanish side to lose eight consecutive European matches when defender Amir Rrahmani found space at the back post to put Napoli ahead in the eighth minute. The visitors almost doubled their lead in the 22nd minute, but Rasmus Hojlund’s header struck the crossbar. Less than 60 seconds later, Villarreal drew level through Georges Mikautadze, who scored his first Champions League goal of the season after pouncing on an underhit backpass from Matteo Politano. Villarreal took the lead in the 25th minute when Uruguay midfielder Santiago Mourino arrowed a strike from distance past Vanja Milinkovic-Savic. Substitute Tani Oluwaseyi then ensured Villarreal ended their run of seven consecutive defeats with a composed finish from inside the area four minutes from time. Villarreal travel to Liverpool on 20 October (20:00 BST), while Napoli host Bodo/Glimt at the same time.

title: Ukrainian army attacks DPR settlements eight times in 24 hours, wounding two people
body:
DONETSK, October 14. /TASS/. The Ukrainian army attacked settlements in the Donetsk People’s Republic (DPR) eight times over the past 24 hours, leaving two people wounded, the DPR department for documenting Ukraine’s war crimes reported.
"Eight attacks by Ukrainian armed formations were recorded, including five [attacks] in the Gorlovka and one [attack] each in the Volodarsky, Telmanovo, and Yasinovataya directions. Reports indicate that two civilians were wounded. Ten rounds of various types of ammunition were fired," the report said.
Strikes damaged a truck and one civil infrastructure facility, according to the department.

title: Saudi Aramco facility catches fire amid Houthi attacks, Saudi airstrikes on Sanaa
body: A limited fire broke out Tuesday in an administrative building at Aramco, one of the world’s largest oil facilities, that was targeted in an attack in the country’s Eastern Province, Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Energy said. The ministry said no injuries were reported. The attack came as the Iranian-backed Houthis and the Saudi coalition fighting them exchanged attacks Tuesday night. The fighting marked a fresh escalation in the widening Middle East crisis and came shortly after the Saudi coalition reported a series of alerts for incoming missiles heading for the Eastern Province, a major oil-producing region, and the capital Riyadh.   Saudi Arabia’s Civil Defense said debris from two intercepted Houthi missiles fell on residential areas in Riyadh, injuring four people and damaging 15 homes. The coalition of forces in Yemen led by Saudi Arabia carried out new airstrikes Tuesday on the Houthi rebel-held Yemeni capital, the Houthi-run broadcaster Al Masirah and residents said. The strikes marked a fresh escalation in the Middle East crisis and came shortly after a coalition spokesman urged residents to evacuate the area for their safety. Witnesses reported hearing strong explosions in Sanaa hours after the coalition struck the Subaha fuel facility west of the city. In a rare statement earlier, the coalition had urged civilians in the Houthi-controlled capital to leave the Yemeni Oil Company site, on a hill overlooking the capital, and nearby storage areas ahead of a possible strike. Coalition spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki al-Maliki accused the Houthis of using the facility and its underground fuel depots for their arsenal of missiles and drones. Houthi officials appeared to have anticipated the attack. The oil company said its storage facilities were empty and that a Saudi strike would not affect oil reserves or supplies for residents. Still, witnesses in the city said lines of cars formed at some gas stations amid fears of a shortage. Shortly after the warning, Houthi military spokesman Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree said on Telegram that any Saudi attack on Sanaa would be met with a “firm and painful” response in the Saudi capital, Riyadh. Hours later, Saudi Arabia issued alerts for incoming missiles heading for Riyadh and the country’s Eastern Province, a major oil-producing region, but quickly said the danger had passed. The coalition said it had intercepted a series of Houthi-launched ballistic missiles, drones and cruise missiles in multiple areas in the country, including Riyadh and the southern province of Wadi al-Dawasir. Riyadh residents reported hearing loud explosions. Airlines moved a number of their planes out of Riyadh on Tuesday on the advice of insurers and government officials because of the threat of additional attacks. They needed to transfer the planes to other airports in the country so they can keep flying passengers to their destinations, said Osprey Flight Solutions Chief Intelligence Officer Matthew Borie, whose company advises airlines, insurers and countries on flight threats. This kind of move is common when conflict erupts.   “It’s not abnormal for this to occur especially in this day and age with the types of conflict zone situations that have occurred in the region,” Borie said. It was unclear whether the Tuesday strike in Yemen was a signal of military escalation or a carefully measured response to recent deadly attacks on the Riyadh airport. The warning and the attack show “the Saudis’ aims of upping the ante and striking deep in the heart of Houthi-controlled territory while attempting to control the narrative by presenting themselves as more careful and humanitarian actors than the Houthis,” said Adam Baron, a fellow at the Washington-based New America institute. “It may be a warning — or it may be a sign of things to come," he said. Fighting surged over control of key waterway Saudi Arabia is still scrambling to determine how its air defenses failed to intercept a barrage of missiles and drones fired by the Houthis, including an attack on Riyadh's international airport on Saturday that killed at least 13 people and wounded over 300. The latest conflict between the Saudis and the Houthis began last month after the rebels seized key areas along the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a critical waterway for the transport of Gulf oil and other goods at the southern end of the Red Sea off Yemen. The Saudi-led coalition, backing forces aligned with Yemen’s internationally recognized government, has been trying to retake them.   Saudi Arabia’s Cabinet on Tuesday warned the Houthis they would “face consequences” for their repeated attacks on the kingdom. “The Kingdom will not allow any threat to its security or to freedom of maritime navigation in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab Strait,” the Cabinet said in a statement carried by Saudi state-owned Al-Ekhbariya television. The Bab el-Mandeb is another area key to the flow of oil out of the Persian Gulf. The fight for a major Yemeni city On Tuesday, Yemen’s interior ministry said in a statement on X that Houthi strikes over the past day on Taiz, a major city in the country's southwest, had killed six people and injured 18 amid ongoing battles in the region. A commander with the Saudi-backed forces said rebels had fought through fierce resistance to reach the edges of Taiz, and some had entered the city. The fight was now critical for Taiz, which has long been a sought-after prize, he said. The commander, speaking on condition of anonymity to describe battlefield details, said rebel forces were surprisingly large, and bolstered by medium and short-range ballistic missiles. That fighting is leading to the large-scale displacement of people and growing shortages of food and other supplies, U.N. spokesman Stephane Dujarric said Tuesday, with cooking gas largely unavailable and food prices that have reportedly risen about 50%. The coalition commander said the fighting was fiercest over control of the Kahboub mountains, which overlook Bab al-Mandab and Aden, seat of the internationally backed government. The commander said his forces have called for reinforcements. Earlier Tuesday, the Houthis renewed their warning against using Saudi airspace, Houthi-controlled media reported. Several airlines have suspended service to the kingdom because of the Houthi attacks on airports. In a statement published by the Houthi-controlled SABA news agency, the Houthi-run foreign ministry referred to Saudi Arabia as the “Kingdom of the Horn of Satan” and said the kingdom “must realize that security, stability, and sovereignty must belong to everyone otherwise, no one will enjoy them.” Meanwhile, Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty called for the Houthis to immediately halt attacks on Saudi Arabia. “There is no justification for these attacks, and they cannot be accepted,” Abdelatty told Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi in a phone call Tuesday. Abdelatty also called for prioritizing diplomacy and a political solution to the conflict between Iran and the United States to avert “further escalation and instability” in the region, according to the Egyptian readout of the call. The Saudi-led coalition said earlier Tuesday that three drones had been intercepted north of Riyadh. The Associated Press couldn’t independently verify that claim. Saudi Arabia has been pushing for the U.S. military to provide more direct support in the fight against the Houthis. The U.S. has provided intelligence sharing, target identification and planning for a Saudi-led offensive, but has held off on carrying out strikes against the Houthis. A U.S. intervention could prompt the Houthis to try to halt shipping through the Bab el-Mandeb.

title: An OpenAI Employee Allegedly Used a Chatbot to Help Plant a Recording Device at the Office
body:
Abdulrahman Alfozan, whom federal prosecutors describe as a 35-year-old Saudi Arabian national and US permanent resident, allegedly spent several weeks querying an unspecified “productivity agent” and an “AI chatbot” to plan his alleged surveillance operation. He used an internal OpenAI tool to ask about meetings scheduled in the targeted conference room.
He also appears to have used a chatbot account associated with his spouse to ask various technical questions about setting up a covert audio recording device, according to prosecutors and the court filing.
OpenAI’s security team also allegedly found an additional recording device in Alfozan’s bag at the office.
Alfozan couldn’t be immediately reached for comment. He made an initial appearance in US District Court in San Francisco on Tuesday on one charge of “use of an electronic, mechanical, or other device to intercept oral communications.” If convicted, Alfozan faces up to five years in prison. He joined OpenAI in July 2025 and was fired last Friday to coincide with his arrest.
FBI director Kash Patel said in a statement that Alfozan aimed “to secretly capture sensitive communications about the company’s super intelligence technology,” but neither prosecutors nor OpenAI have offered any information so far about a potential motive.
“At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data,” OpenAI said in a statement on X. “We take protecting our technology, data, and people seriously, and as a matter of national importance.”
OpenAI discovered the bug—which was allegedly “concealed in toilet paper” and “inserted into a USB port on the back of a television” in the conference room—on September 30 during a countersurveillance sweep.
Alfozan previously worked at a cargo logistics startup and at Meta, according to a purported LinkedIn profile for him. In a recent podcast interview, Alfozan said he was also part of a group of Saudi engineers in Silicon Valley who offered consulting services to Saudi organizations.
The LinkedIn profile lists Alfozan as a part-time “venture partner” at RAED Ventures, a venture capital firm based in Saudi Arabia. Neither RAED Ventures nor Meta immediately responded to WIRED’s request for comment.
Last year, the Trump administration signed a pact with Saudi Arabia granting the kingdom access to advanced chips and AI technologies that might otherwise be restricted over national security concerns. Saudi investment firms remain a major source of capital for US tech companies.
Executives Only
According to the complaint, Alfozan allegedly planted the listening device “no later than on or about September 28, 2026.”
The conference room Alfozan targeted “can be reserved only by executives and executive assistants,” and is typically used “for internal leadership meetings,” “technical and product sessions,” and “external briefings” with business partners and government officials, according to the complaint. It is frequently used for discussions involving “highly confidential” information, including about research, products, business strategy, and government relationships, the complaint stated.
OpenAI’s statement called the recording device “sophisticated.” Authorities allege that the device Alfozan planted was called Seeed XIAO ESP32-S3 Sense, “a thumb-sized development board with a detachable camera sensor, digital microphone, and microSD storage.” It currently retails on Seeed’s website for $13.99. OpenAI’s security team tried to export the data stored on the microSD card, but were unable to review it because it was encrypted.
After discovering the device, OpenAI says it notified the FBI and was able to connect it to Alfozan after reviewing chat logs and surveillance footage, and searching a bag he left unattended at the office. The company then gradually disabled his access to company systems as the investigation was ongoing.
According to the complaint, OpenAI security personnel discovered the bag that Alfozan left unattended in a printer room on October 5. The security team went through the bag, which contained a second encrypted Seeed listening device and other personal items connected to Alfozan, including his wallet. Prosecutors say Alfozan later reported the bag as missing to OpenAI and subsequently recovered it from the company’s lost and found.
He followed up with unnamed personnel at OpenAI to say that some of the items that were supposed to be in the bag were still missing—including a credit card, about $500 in cash, and two AirPods—but neglected to mention the second listening device, which had been removed from the bag by OpenAI security.

title: Grevena Liberated by the Greek Army on 14 October 1912
body: During the First Balkan War, the Greek Army liberated Grevena in Western Macedonia on 14 October 1912, ending nearly five centuries of Ottoman rule. The Balkan League—Greece, Serbia, Bulgaria and Montenegro—declared war on the Ottoman Empire on 8 October 1912 and successfully drove Ottoman forces from most of Europe. For Greece, the war marked a major triumph, securing the liberation of Macedonia (including Grevena), Epirus and several Aegean islands—achieved 80 years after the Kingdom of Greece was established without many of its historic lands and people. READ MORE: October 8, 1912: Greece and allies launch First Balkan War against the Ottoman Empire. The post Grevena Liberated by the Greek Army on 14 October 1912 appeared first on Greek City Times .

title: Science Corporation implants its vision-restoring chip in its first Stargardt disease patient
body:
Science Corporation CEO Max Hodak announced that the company has implanted its vision-restoring chip , PRIMA, into its first patient with Stargardt disease, an inherited eye disease that gradually destroys central vision. Hodak, the former president and co-founder of Neuralink, the brain implant company, explained onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt how the company’s work with PRIMA fits into its broader pursuit of a novel brain-computer interface (BCI).
“The retina is part of the central nervous system,” Hodak said. “We consider cochlear implants, retinal prostheses, motor prostheses, these are all different types of BCIs.”
Hodak outlined a vision in which BCIs expand into a wide range of medical technology applications, rather than simply being a way to control computers.
While PRIMA is commercially available in Europe for patients who’ve lost their sight to geographic atrophy, an advanced form of age-related macular degeneration, the company believes its approach can be applied to multiple diseases, including Stargardt disease, which is currently considered incurable.
Stargardt disease affects the outer retina, causing the gradual death of the eye’s light-sensing cells while potentially sparing the inner retina, the part that passes visual signals onto the brain. It causes a central blind spot that gradually enlarges over time. Approximately 150,000 people worldwide have lost vision due to the disease.
“One of the nice things about this device approach, when I was saying the brain’s a computer, vision is electrical potential, like electrical activity down the optic nerve,” Hodak said. “That’s all vision is to the brain, and so if you can get the optic nerve to signal the rest of the brain correctly, then you can provide vision to it.”
The company says its first patient with Stargardt disease received the PRIMA implant in May as part of its ongoing trial at the Sydney Eye Hospital in Australia. During the patient’s first rehabilitation session, he saw a letter, and during the second, he was able to read a word.
To use the device, patients undergo an hourlong procedure that plants a small chip in the back of their eye, where the photoreceptors have degenerated. Then they wear camera-equipped glasses that transmit a view of the world to the chip. The implant essentially works like artificial photoreceptors.
“The device that this patient has is a two millimeter by two millimeter implant placed in the back of the eye, and so it’s like looking through a straw,” Hodak said. “It is not a big field of view color vision. It’s a patch in their central vision where … it’s black and white, but it is sharp. It’s high-contrast sharp, and so they can see a couple letters at a time. The next step is to make the field of view bigger. So to make a bigger implant, you have to deal with the curvature of the eye, and we need to make the electrodes smaller so that we get closer to native levels of detail.”
He continued, “I think we have a clear path. There’s a ‘next generation’ that’s being worked on that’ll be in humans in the next year, and over the next five years, I think we’ll be able to get pretty close to native acuity.”
When Hodak founded Science Corporation in 2021 after leaving Neuralink, the company outlined plans to develop advanced neural engineering and brain-computer interface technology. But first, the company wants to prove its methods work and develop a sustainable business, which is why it’s working to restore vision with the visually impaired.
As for Science Corporation’s brain-computer interface technology, it has previously said that its sensor will be implanted inside the skull and rest on top of the brain, unlike a Neuralink device, which is inserted directly into brain tissue.
The company has said it believes the device could help address neurological conditions, such as possibly monitoring neurological activity in patients with brain tumors.
“In the near term, we’re going to be applying our first clinical indication, which hasn’t been announced publicly, is a neurodegenerative disease that everybody’s heard of,” Hodak said. “We’re also looking at stroke. For example, if you’ve lost part of your brain because it’s been dead due to stroke, if you can get connections into the deep brain in two different areas, you can imagine adding new cortical areas, just like adding new brain areas entirely — something simply not possible with conventional electrodes. But, I’d say longer term, the long-term mission of the company is to understand how the brain creates the mind and to learn to build engineered brains.”
Hodak went on to note that Science Corporation’s belief is that many people will eventually use some kind of BCI. While the company isn’t designing for “healthy 40-year-olds,” he said, it believes people will eventually need some kind of BCI by the age of 60 or 70.
“We want to figure out how do we extend not just lifespan but health span,” Hodak said.

title: Tresoldi nets hat-trick as Club Brugge win Inter thriller
body: Nicolo Tresoldi scored a stunning hat-trick as Club Brugge handed Inter Milan their fourth consecutive Champions League defeat, the first of its kind in their history, in a seven-goal thriller. It took until the half-hour mark for the first of the seven strikes, when referee Rohit Saggi awarded a penalty for Club Brugge – which Tresoldi hammered into the top right corner for his first of the evening. On the brink of half-time, captain Lautaro Martinez made it 1-1 with his first Champions League goal since November 2025. But a costly mistake by Inter goalkeeper Josep Martinez, who rushed out of his goal and missed the ball, allowed Tresoldi to slot it into an open goal for his second of the night. Eleven minutes later came the hat-trick goal for Tresoldi, who latched on to Martinez’s save before powering into the bottom corner for 3-1. With less than 10 minutes to play, Martinez gave Inter hope of snatching a point with his second of the evening after pouncing on a loose ball in the box. That hope seemed to be snatched away when Romeo Vermant reinstated the Belgian’s two-goal lead three minutes from time. But even in the 93rd minute, the goals were still flowing as substitute Ange-Yoan Bonny cut in from the left before whipping a great finish into the far corner to make it 4-3.

title: UK to Fast-Track Air Defense Missiles for Ukraine as Burnham Hosts Zelensky in London
body:
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham will host President Volodymyr Zelensky at Downing Street on Wednesday, Oct. 14, with London announcing accelerated air defense missile deliveries and plans for further sanctions against Russia.
The visit comes as Moscow intensifies attacks on Ukrainian cities and energy infrastructure, prompting Britain to reaffirm its “rock-solid support” for Kyiv.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
According to a British government statement published Tuesday , Burnham has instructed ministers to prepare additional sanctions, military assistance and financial support packages for Ukraine in the coming weeks.
“Our rock-solid support to Ukraine is vital for keeping us safe here in the UK and ensuring those on the frontlines have the equipment they need to push back Russia,” Burnham said.
The British government said it would accelerate deliveries of Lightweight Multirole Missiles (LMMs), which have proved effective against jet-powered Russian drones capable of flying faster and higher than conventional Shahed-type drones.
Britain announced £45 million (approximately $60 million) in surface-to-air missile deliveries, including £10 million (approximately $13 million) to be accelerated to address Ukraine’s urgent winter defense requirements.
The deliveries form part of an existing £1.6 billion (approximately $2.1 billion) commitment to supply more than 5,000 LMMs over four years.
London is also pressing international partners to increase economic pressure on Moscow and support a ban on maritime services used to export Russian liquefied natural gas (LNG).
Chancellor John Healey is expected to raise the issue during International Monetary Fund meetings in Bangkok, urging other countries to adopt restrictions similar to those planned by Britain.
The proposed measures would limit Russia’s access to British shipping and insurance services, restricting a source of revenue supporting Moscow’s war effort.
Healey called for international backing to reduce the financial resources available to the Kremlin.
“I urge partners to back the ban on Russian LNG, like we have done in the UK, to curtail the war chest funding Putin so desperately wants,” he said.
The announcement follows fresh Russian ballistic missile strikes on Kyiv, including an attack on the CHP-4 power plant, as Ukraine faces continued threats to its energy system ahead of winter.
Britain is calling on Moscow to respect US President Donald Trump’s proposal for an energy ceasefire, which Kyiv has said it supports.
Burnham previously discussed the proposal with Zelensky during an Oct. 10 telephone call, when both leaders called for an immediate halt to Russian strikes on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure and attacks on shipping in the Black Sea.
The two leaders also met during the UN General Assembly in September, where they discussed sanctions, Ukraine’s winter energy needs and efforts to bring Russia to meaningful peace negotiations.
Ahead of his meeting with Zelensky, Burnham reaffirmed Britain’s commitment to Ukraine.
“My message to the Ukrainian people could not be clearer, we are with you for as long as it takes, and we will go further and faster in our support to back your courageous fight for peace in Europe.”
“It is not just the right thing to do, but it’s the necessary thing to do. Russia’s aggression cannot be allowed to succeed on our continent.”
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: BIC Recognised for Decade-long Brand Legacy
body: BIC Nigeria has received two major honors at the 2026 Edge Awards, winning the Edge Outstanding Legacy Brand Award of the Decade (Corporate) and the Edge Outstanding Legacy Brand Award (Shaving Razor). The awards, presented at Marketing Edge’s Edge Awards Night on Friday, September 25, in Lagos, recognize the brand’s sustained equity and performance in Nigeria’s fast-moving consumer goods sector over the past decade, alongside the continued relevance of its shaving razor brand to Nigerian consumers. The double recognition reflects the longevity of BIC in Nigeria and the trust its brands have earned across generations of consumers. It also highlights the company’s focus on delivering products that meet everyday needs while evolving with changing consumer expectations. “We are proud of these awards and thankful to Marketing Edge,” said Anthony Amahwe, General Manager, BIC Nigeria . “For us, a legacy is built through the trust people place in our products, day after day. These awards are a reflection of the work of our teams and partners, as well as the loyalty of consumers who have made BIC part of their everyday lives. They encourage us to keep building brands that remain relevant to consumers and the changing needs of the market.”

title: Cerebras CEO says we’re nearing a future where everyone has a personal AI assistant at home
body:
Cerebras Systems CEO and co-founder Andrew Feldman believes we’re nearing a future where everyone will have an AI appliance in their own home.
Speaking onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 on Tuesday, the chipmaker executive answered a question about what would need to happen for AI to become a home appliance, saying, “Actually, I don’t think that’s very far away.”
He pointed to the advances in consumer AI agents, like Meta’s Muse and Instinct, the startup now valued at $10 billion, as examples of how AI is finding its footing with everyday users.
As for home AI? He predicts that we’ll have personal AI assistants that run locally.
“Just like your cell phone, they’ll do some work on device and some work going back to the cloud,” Feldman explained. “But I think they will get to know you very well, and you will have a security perimeter around them. And they will certainly have access to credit cards and be able to buy things for you,” he continued. “I think they will make a meaningful impact in making our lives better.”
Of course, for an AI chipmaker, the vision of a home AI appliance, or at least widespread consumer adoption of agentic technology, is certainly appealing.
But Feldman isn’t just working on the hardware infrastructure; he’s a personal AI user himself, saying that he now uses “a collection of agents” to sweep his calendar, pull up information about the people he’s going to have a call with, and more. While AI is already doing many of the things we used to do manually, Feldman is most excited about the new possibilities — things that weren’t possible before.
He’s leaving it up to other founders to figure out what those might be, though.
“One of the reasons I love being in infrastructure is because I don’t need the consumer-facing idea … I like building the platforms that other people’s ideas take flight on,” he said.

title: Financial Trust Accuses NDIC of Withholding Liquidation Surpluses for 30 Years
body: .Demands release of audited accounts .Says funds owed to estate of late founder Sunday Ehigiator Financial Trust Group has accused the Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation (NDIC) of withholding liquidation surpluses and dividends due to the estate of its late founder, William Olufemi Olateju Ajayi, for more than 30 years following the liquidation of Financial Merchant Bank Limited and Republic Bank Limited in 1994 and 1995, respectively. The group, in a statement yesterday, condemned what it described as the NDIC’s “prolonged and unwarranted refusal” to account for and release the funds, demanding an immediate settlement of all outstanding entitlements due to the late founder’s estate. It said the corporation had continued to withhold the funds despite statutory provisions requiring the distribution of residual assets to shareholders and contributories after depositors and creditors had been fully paid. “For over three decades, the NDIC has withheld funds rightfully belonging to the Ajayi family and associated legacy entities, despite statutory mandates requiring the distribution of residual assets to shareholders and contributories once depositors and creditors have been fully settled,” the statement said. Financial Trust Group further alleged that the corporation had failed to provide a transparent, audited account of the assets realised from the liquidation of the two banks, despite reports indicating that depositors and creditors had long been settled. “Despite NDIC annual reports confirming that depositors and creditors of the defunct banks have long been fully satisfied, the NDIC has maintained a posture of opacity, refusing to provide a transparent, audited accounting of the asset realizations or to distribute the resulting liquidation surpluses,” it said. The group traced the dispute to the military era, alleging that the business interests of its late founder were severely affected under the administrations of Generals Ibrahim Babangida and Sani Abacha. It described Ajayi as a prominent pro-democracy advocate and publisher of The Republic, a newspaper that supported the presidential ambition of the late Chief Moshood Abiola under the Hope ’93 mandate. According to the group, the military regimes repeatedly proscribed Ajayi’s publications, targeted his businesses and eventually revoked the operating licences of the two banks. “The Babangida and Abacha regimes repeatedly proscribed his publications, hunted his enterprises, and ultimately engineered the revocation of the banks’ operating licences in January 1994 and June 1995, even as orderly rescue and acquisition offers were underway,” the statement added. Financial Trust Group said the prolonged dispute had continued to impose a burden on the family and the institutional legacy of its late founder, despite the contributions of the company to Nigeria’s financial markets. The group’s parent company, Financial Trust Company Nigeria Limited, marked its 50th anniversary in May 2026. Founded in 1976, the company said it holds the distinction of being the first indigenous stockbroking firm admitted as a dealing member of the Lagos Stock Exchange. While acknowledging recent developments in Nigeria’s capital market and the Federal Government’s ambition to build a $1 trillion economy, the group said the unresolved dispute remained a concern for accountability in the country’s financial system. It called on the NDIC management to act in line with the Federal Government’s Renewed Hope agenda by providing a full account of the liquidation proceeds and releasing the outstanding funds. It added, “Financial Trust Group calls upon the management of the NDIC, under the Renewed Hope agenda of the Federal Government, to immediately uphold transparency, adhere to statutory obligations, and disburse all accumulated liquidation surpluses and dividends owed to the Estate of Late Otunba W.O.O. Ajayi without further delay. Justice deferred for 30 years is accountability denied. The financial regulatory framework must honor the integrity of indigenous pioneers who built Nigeria’s financial architecture.” The NDIC could not be reached for comments as at the time of filing this report.

title: Expert Warns Pension Fund Managers of Post Recapitalisation Pitfalls
body: Ebere Nwoji As pension sector operators continue to race towards meeting the regulator’s recapitalisation requirements with June 30th, 2027 as deadline, their attention has been drawn to issues that lie ahead after recapitalisation. These issues have been summarised in an acronym titled SCOPE, which the expert described as scale, compliance and regulatory awareness; organisational adoption of technology, people strategy and culture, external engagement and differentiation. Former Chief Executive officer of Pension Operators Association of Nigeria (PenOp), Mr Oguche Aguda, stated this while delivering a paper titled, “Post Recapitalisation and Market Dynamics in Nigerian Pension Industry,” at the 11th Annual National conference of Nigerian Association of Insurance and Pension Editors( NAIPE). He said the need for scale manifested in business combination witnessed in pension sector some of which are the combination between Trust- fund Pensions and Premium Pension and the combination between Leadway and Pal pension. He highlighted the advantages of these as gaining economics of scale by the various firms involved, increasing complexity of operations , streamlining costs and competing effectively in the market place. On compliance and regulatory awareness, Aguda noted that pension was the most rejected sector and this has made the regulator to be at the centre of the industry ensuring that operators have sound compliance and culture. On adoption of technology, he said operators must ask themselves the question on how to leverage technology to make their operations quicker, simble and help them to scale. According to him, they should also meditate on how to use Artificial Intelligence to compete as well as how to manage cyber security threat. Aguda who featured as keynote speaker on pension matters at the conference highlighted fact about the on going recapitalisation exercise in pension sector as pension sector regulator PenCom having mandated all licensed pension fund administrators to raise their minimum capital from N5 billion to N20 billion, and one percent more if their Asset Under Management is above N500 billion by June 2027. Aguda said second fact about recapitalisation in the pension sector is PenCom mandating all licensed pension fund custodians ( PFCs) to raise their minimum capital to N25 billion by June 2027.

title: ICSAN: Sound Corporate Governance Strengthens Investor Confidence
body: Kayode Tokede The Institute of Chartered Secretaries and Administrators of Nigeria (ICSAN) has stressed the critical role of sound corporate governance in strengthening investor confidence, attracting investment and supporting Nigeria’s economic development. The Institute said this at the Closing Gong Ceremony of an event to mark its 60th anniversary. Speaking at the event,President and Chairman of the Governing Council of ICSAN, Mrs. Uto Ukpanah traced the Institute’s origins to the public sector. She noted that its founding principles of integrity, transparency and professionalism. She described the milestone as an opportunity to celebrate the Institute’s legacy while preparing the next generation of governance professionals for emerging challenges. “60 years is not just a milestone to celebrate; it is a call to prepare for the future. We must continue to strengthen a community of governance professionals who can promote accountability, reinforce investor confidence and support Nigeria’s development,” Ukpanah said. In his welcome remarks,Chief Executive Officer of NGX, Jude Chiemeka underscored the link between sound corporate governance and investor confidence, noting that effective governance is fundamental to the credibility and integrity of market institutions. “Corporate governance is fundamental to building and sustaining investor confidence. For the capital market to fulfil its role in mobilising long-term capital and supporting economic growth, investors must have confidence in the institutions and businesses in which they invest. This makes the work of governance professionals increasingly important,” Chiemeka said.

title: Lasaco Assurance Secures Approval to Underwrite Agric Insurance Business
body: Ebere Nwoji Lasaco Assurance Plc, has secured approval of the National Insurance Commission (NAICOM) to underwrite agricultural insurance for farmers, marking a pivotal advancement in the company’s strategic expansion and its commitment to Nigeria’s agricultural sector. Speaking on the development, Lasaco Assurance Managing Director, Mr Ademoye Shobo, said as part of its agricultural insurance offerings, Lasaco Assurance would provide a comprehensive range of products designed to support farmers and stakeholders across the sector. According to him, agriculture continues to be a vital driver of Nigeria’s economic development, sustaining livelihoods, contributing significantly to food production, and creating business opportunities nationwide. He said the availability of tailored agricultural insurance products through reputable financial institutions plays a crucial role in meeting the risk management needs of farmers, agribusinesses, and other sector participants. She expressed confidence that this approval would substantially boost the company’s revenue going forward. She emphasised that it presented a valuable opportunity for Lasaco Assurance to contribute meaningfully to the protection and growth of this niche market. Also speaking, Head of Strategy at Lasaco Assurance, Mr. Adedayo Adetokun, noted that the development aligned perfectly with Lasaco Assurance’s long-term vision to deepen sectoral diversification and strengthen its competitive positioning. He noted that leveraging strategic partnerships and innovative approaches would be key to maximising the potential of the agricultural insurance portfolio. “This milestone signals a new phase in Lasaco Assurance Plc’s business trajectory, enhancing its engagement within Nigeria’s agricultural market and setting the stage for continued expansion and value creation”, he said.

title: Stakeholders Urge Insurance, Pension Operators to Prioritise Customer Value
body: Ebere Nwoji Stakeholders in the insurance and pension sectors have urged operators of the two sectors to deploy funds raised through recapitalisation to improve services, develop innovative products and strengthen customer confidence. Speaking on the insurance sector, Managing Director, SanlamAllianz General Insurance, Mrs Jacqueline Agweh, said the post-recapitalisation era had given insurers an opportunity to develop products that would address customers’ specific needs. She said that insurers must work closely with customers to understand those needs and provide tailor-made products and services. Also speaking, Executive Director, NLPC Pensions, Mr Babalola Rufus urged operators to ensure that policyholders and Retirement Savings Account (RSA) holders had their funds secured, properly invested and paid when due. Rufus noted that shareholders and contributors had committed funds to the insurance and pension sectors expecting value from their investments and contributions. He said the success of recapitalisation in both sectors should ultimately be judged by the benefits delivered to customers. On his part, Managing Director, Zenith Pensions Custodian Ltd., Mr Peters Elendu, advised pension operators to invest in technology, artificial intelligence, data analytics and innovation to make pension services easier and more accessible. Earlier, Mrs Ebere Nwoji, Chairman of NAIPE said the conference was organised to bring together regulators, industry operators and investment experts to examine how the capital raised by insurance and pension institutions could be deployed prudently. Nwoji said this was because effective investment of the funds would help generate sustainable returns for investors, strengthen the economy and improve the long-term financial security of Nigerians.

title: Hezbollah assassination plot? Explosives seized on truck bound for Beirut
body: Lebanon's ongoing struggle to prevent weapons smuggling from Syria has taken a new turn after security forces intercepted a truck carrying hundreds of kilograms of explosives toward Beirut, fueling speculation about a possible political assassination plot involving Hezbollah. The seizure in the Dahr al-Baydar area of eastern Lebanon has become one of the country's most widely discussed security incidents, prompting a response from Prime Minister Nawaf Salam and reigniting debate over political assassinations, Hezbollah's weapons and growing internal tensions.   Saudi-owned Al-Hadath television reported Friday, citing a Lebanese security source, that 500 kilograms of explosives had been discovered in a vehicle at a security checkpoint in the Dahr al-Baydar area of Lebanon's Bekaa Valley. According to the report, the explosives were found in the possession of two Hezbollah members, who were transferred to the military police. The source suggested that the quantity of explosives indicated a possible plot to assassinate a senior figure. Lebanese broadcaster MTV also reported Friday that internal security forces had arrested two Hezbollah members in a vehicle containing hundreds of kilograms of the powerful explosive C-4. "The military police are questioning the Hezbollah members to determine whether others were involved," the broadcaster reported. Lebanese channel Al-Jadeed offered a somewhat different account, reporting Friday that the two men had actually been arrested the previous Monday. According to its report, authorities seized more than 250 kilograms of TNT, along with additional materials used to manufacture explosive devices. Al-Jadeed said the suspects were believed to have links to Hezbollah and that the vehicle had been heading toward the Beirut area. Lebanese media reports have provided conflicting figures concerning the exact quantity and type of explosives seized. ‘Just the tip of the iceberg’ On Saturday, Lebanese newspaper An-Nahar published an article under the headline: "More than half a ton of explosives and two arrests: Was Hezbollah planning an assassination?" The article noted that some media outlets had raised the possibility that the incident was connected to preparations for an assassination. Lebanese Justice Minister Adel Nassar addressed the seizure Saturday in a post on X. "The confiscation of illegal weapons, the fight against terrorism and the pursuit of all lawbreakers are an irreversible course that will gain momentum," he wrote. "The investigation into the seized explosives and all related matters will be pursued to the fullest."   MTV, which is known for its opposition to Hezbollah, reported Saturday that the two detainees belonged to the Amhaz and al-Kurdi families and were both affiliated with the terrorist organization. According to the broadcaster, the suspects admitted that a Honda vehicle had transported the explosives to the Baalbek area. They reportedly said they had received instructions from a man named Sajed to deliver the shipment to Beirut's Dahieh district, where it was to be handed over to a man named Dhu al-Faqar. The incident has dominated Lebanese media coverage since the weekend, against the backdrop of the government's attempts to bring all weapons under state control, including those held by Hezbollah. Hezbollah has refused to disarm, while continuing fighting in southern Lebanon and other challenges facing the country have intensified internal tensions. Lebanese lawmaker Najat Saliba also weighed in on the controversy. "The explosives seized in Dahr al-Baydar are the same materials that were used to assassinate Lebanese figures," she said. On Monday, MTV published an opinion piece calling for the immediate arrest of Hezbollah Secretary-General Naim Qassem. "Naim Qassem must be arrested immediately," the article declared. "It appears that what Hezbollah is planning inside Lebanon, at the push of an Iranian button, is something very big, and the Dahr al-Baydar explosives were only the tip of the iceberg. What remains hidden appears far greater." ‘No one should attempt to issue threats’ Prime Minister Nawaf Salam responded to the incident Monday in a statement posted on X, promising a thorough investigation and action against anyone found responsible. "No leniency and no turning a blind eye, only truth and accountability," Salam wrote. "It has become known that several days ago, a truck was stopped in the Dahr al-Baydar area while traveling from the Bekaa region toward Beirut, carrying hundreds of kilograms of explosives. First, I would like to commend the security forces who stopped the suspicious truck, seized the explosives it was carrying and handed the drivers over to the competent authorities for questioning." Salam acknowledged the concern generated by the discovery, particularly given Lebanon's history of political violence. "I understand the fears among the Lebanese public following the news of the truck and its cargo being seized, especially given that C-4 explosives have been used in political assassinations in Lebanon's modern history," he wrote. "However, in my capacity as prime minister, I wish to reassure all Lebanese citizens that we will not relent in our efforts to advance and expand the investigation." Salam said the government was committed to identifying everyone involved in the shipment, as well as those responsible for organizing it, uncovering their plans and objectives, and bringing them to justice. "Rest assured that our government will show no leniency toward anyone who dares to harm state security, public safety or stability," he said. "We will not hesitate to act decisively against any weapon held, transported or used outside the legitimate framework." The controversy has also prompted a response from Al-Akhbar, a Lebanese newspaper affiliated with Hezbollah, which accused political and media figures of exploiting the incident before investigators had established all the facts. "The interception of the truck in Dahr al-Baydar, loaded with hundreds of kilograms of explosives, is no longer merely a security issue," the newspaper wrote Tuesday. According to Al-Akhbar, the incident had been exploited politically and in the media "even before the shipment's destination and the party behind it were revealed."   The newspaper argued that instead of limiting discussion to the investigation and available evidence, official and media commentary had turned toward Lebanon's history of political assassinations. It said this had placed the incident at the center of the country's internal confrontation over Hezbollah's weapons and linked it to speculation about possible attacks inside Lebanon. Al-Akhbar criticized Lebanese authorities for insisting that the state alone should possess weapons despite what it described as continued Israeli occupation and attacks, and the government's inability to secure reciprocal commitments from Israel. "The truck incident has moved beyond its security dimensions and become part of a broader political struggle," the newspaper argued. It accused Lebanese authorities of attempting to centralize weapons under state control and reinforce their commitment to the American approach, while also working to undermine Hezbollah's image and domestic standing. Hezbollah lawmaker Ibrahim Mousawi also addressed the allegations Monday, rejecting suggestions that the organization could be involved in political assassinations. "If it is true that the vehicle belongs to the resistance, everyone should know that the resistance has nothing to be ashamed of," Mousawi said. "No one should attempt to issue threats, make unacceptable statements, level accusations or insinuate involvement in assassinations or similar acts. The history of the resistance is clear, clean and honorable. It has never been involved in a civil war and has never used its power in internal conflicts or disputes," he added. Mousawi asserted that Lebanon's strength depended on its resilience, internal unity and the prevention of any descent into civil confrontation. "The resistance recognizes that Lebanon's strength lies in its resilience, its internal unity and preventing a slide into civil conflict," he said. He also criticized agreements signed by the Lebanese state, arguing that they had failed to prevent attacks. "In fact, the destruction escalated significantly following the framework agreement," he said. Meanwhile, the Lebanese army reported Monday that it had intercepted a separate shipment of explosives in the al-Qasr-Hermel area near the Syrian border. According to the military, troops seized approximately 200 kilograms of explosives packed in sacks and prepared for smuggling from Syria into Lebanon. "The smugglers fled back into Syrian territory, the seized materials were transferred to the competent authorities, and efforts to locate those involved are continuing," the army said.

title: Nigerian AI Scientist to Roll Out Software That Cuts MRI Time By 90%
body: Peter Uzoho A United Kingdom-based Nigerian artificial intelligence (AI) research scientist and Founder of GenScan AI, Mary-Brenda Akoda, has disclosed plans to roll out her AI medical imaging solution in Nigeria and the UK by the second half of 2027 to help fast-track scan results and reduce patient backlogs globally. Akoda, a Google DeepMind Scholar, ex-Microsoft engineer and Imperial College London-trained researcher, said her flagship innovation, GenMRI, is a first-of-its-kind AI imaging software that makes MRI scans up to 90 per cent faster on existing scanners without hospitals spending millions on new machines. Speaking during an interactive session between 2026 NLNG Nigeria Prize Winners and journalists in Lagos, she explained that the software can reduce a 20-minute scan to as little as two minutes and an hour-long scan to six minutes, allowing hospitals and imaging centres to scan substantially more patients per day, cut waiting lists, reduce repeat scans and sedation costs, particularly for elderly patients, children and infants. According to her, the technology was built and validated on over 8,800 Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) images and later subjected to an early blinded assessment with a consultant radiologist at Buckinghamshire Healthcare NHS Trust in the UK. She said the radiologist was not told which images were conventional and which were GenMRI-enhanced. “The results came back scoring the GenMRI images as diagnostically equivalent to the conventional MRI images in all the cases assessed,” she said. She noted that technical evaluation before the blinded assessment had shown up to 99.7 per cent similarity to conventional MRI images, with speed-ups ranging from four times to ten times. Akoda said the system was developed on over 15,000 cardiac MRI images and validated on a separate set of over 7,700 images, with an additional out-of-distribution test on 1,125 knee MRI images it had never seen before, where it achieved up to 75 per cent shorter scans and outperformed state-of-the-art models in speed and image quality. She said the inspiration for the innovation came from personal loss and lived experience of an overburdened health system, noting that delays in diagnosis can be fatal in time-critical conditions such as stroke and cancer. She recounted how about three years ago, an elderly loved one suffered a stroke and could not get timely imaging due to long queues, leading to deterioration and death, an experience compounded by her own encounter with slow hospital processes. “Every second counts and the difference between life and death can be how quickly a patient gets diagnosed,” she said. She said stroke kills over 6.5 million people yearly worldwide and cancer over 10 million, with medical imaging often the first step to diagnosis, yet MRI scans take 15 minutes to over an hour, require patients to lie still in noisy enclosed spaces, and any movement leads to blurry images, repeat scans and sedation risks.

title: STL Trustees Emerges With Two Wins at BAFI Awards

title: Nine Banks Report N2.99tn Operating Expenses on Inflation, Regulatory Charges
body: Kayode Tokede On the bank of sustained inflation, Ecobank Transnational Incorporated (ETI), Zenith Bank Plc and seven other financial institutions operating in Nigeria and other Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) countries declared N2.99 trillion operating expenses (OPEX) in the half year ended June 30, 2026. Analysis of the banks audited/unaudited H1 2026 result and accounts showed that the N2.99 trillion OPEX is about 7.8 per cent increase over N2.78 trillion reported in H1 2025. Despite the increase in OPEX, the banks posted N3.2 trillion profit before tax in H1 2026, about 19.2 per cent increase over N2.69 trillion reported in H 2025. Inflation across SSA remained relatively contained during H1 2026 despite renewed global price pressures, supported by prudent monetary policy, easing food prices, and improving exchange rate stability in several economies. While inflation accelerated in Ghana to 5.2 per cent and edged higher in Nigeria to 15.91per cent, reflecting lingering domestic cost pressures, Côte d’Ivoire maintained low inflation at 1.8 per cent, while Kenya (4.5 per cent) and Tanzania (4.0 per cent) continued to record moderate price growth. Nigeria’s inflation remained on a broad disinflation path during H1 2026 despite a temporary uptick driven by higher global energy prices following geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. Headline inflation eased early in the year before rising to 15.93per cent in May and moderating slightly to 15.91per cent in June 2026. In response, the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), adopted a cautious monetary policy stance, reducing the MPR from 26.50 per cent in February to 23 per cent at the last Monetary Policy Committee meeting (MPC) to contain inflationary pressures, preserve exchange rate stability, and anchor inflation expectations. Further analysis of the banks’ results and accounts, showed that ETI, Zenith Bank and First HoldCo Plc declared the highest OPEX by value, while Jaiz Bank posted the highest by percentage difference. As of H1 2026, ETI reported N856.5 billion OPEX, a 0.34 per cent increase from N853.65 billion reported in H1 2025. Zenith Bank declared N633.76 billion OPEX, up by 9 per cent from N581.43 billion in H1 2025. On its part, First Holdco posted N608.09 billion OPEX, representing an increase of nearly 10 per cent from N552.83billion in H1 2025. This was closely followed by GTCO that announced N277.39 billion OPEX in H1 2026, a growth of 7.3 per cent from N258.5billion in H1 2025. GTCO in a presentation stated that its OPEX’s 7.3 per cent increase is with non-controllable costs accounting for 26.6% of total OPEX. “The increase was driven largely by higher regulatory charges, depreciation and infrastructure-related costs, as well as continued investment in people and customer service. These pressures were partly mitigated by reductions across technology, marketing and other discretionary expense lines, reflecting continued focus on cost efficiency,” GTCO said in a presentation to analysts and investors According to the lender, the key OPEX growth drivers was regulatory and statutory charges remained a significant component of the cost base, with AMCON expenses increasing 9.9% to N55.9billion and Deposit Insurance Premium rising 15per cent to N18.0billion. “The increase reflects the scale of the group’s balance sheet and deposit franchise, with these costs largely determined by regulatory and statutory requirements. The group continued to absorb higher infrastructure-related costs, with Depreciation and Amortisation increasing 41.8per cent to N54.3billion, while Occupancy Costs and Repairs & Maintenance rose 10.2 per cent to N19.8billion. The movements reflect the continued build-out and maintenance of the Group’s physical and operating infrastructure. “Investment in human capital and service delivery remained a priority, with Personnel Expenses rising 4.7per cent to N57.0billion and Customer Service Related Expenses increasing 98.3 per cent to N2.4billion. The increase in customer service costs reflects continued efforts to strengthen service capacity and customer experience. “4.7per cent growth in Personnel expenses (N57.0 billion vs N54.4billion) resulted from the full weight impact of staff promotion and increases in salaries of Core and non-Core employees done to cushion the impact of rising cost of living for employees across the Group’s Banking and non-Banking entities,” GTCO added. However, Jaiz Bank’s OPEX grew by 44.5 per cent to N26.6 billion in H1 2026 from N18.44 billion in H11 2025 to record the highest growth by proportion. Analysts believe the hike in inflation rate, among others, contributed to the companies’ cost of sales and OPEX, stressing that its impact affected not only their robust profit generation, but dividend payout at the end of the year. They predicted further hike in OPEX in 2026, stressing that its impact may cut down on earnings and dividend payout to shareholders. Speaking, Vice President, Highcap Securities Limited, Mr. David Adnori said the hike in cost of sales and operating expenses is a reflection of global economic unrest, stressing that financial institutions operating in Nigeria and in Africa do not operate in isolation. He expressed that the growth in cost of sales and operating expenses reported by listed companies would definitely have an impact on profit and dividend payout to shareholders. He said, “The world is currently facing a high inflation rate and Nigeria, Africa at large are not exempted from this experience, with countries on the continent witnessing record high inflation rate. The surge in inflation rate is following the rally in crude oil prices, amidst the face-off between Russia-IUkraine and USA-Israel/ Iran, among other nations.” “Reacting to the surging inflation rate, regulators of several countries where Nigerian companies operate have also raised their interest rates to curb the rising cost of goods and services. However, this is yet to yield any significant positive as the inflation rate above 30 per cent. With cost impacted, Nigerian companies may suffer slow profitability this year and it might impact on dividend payout,” he added.

title: PSG’s Luis Enrique hopes Man City avoid sanctions
body: Paris St-Germain boss Luis Enrique says he was surprised to learn Manchester City had been found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules and hopes the club can avoid sanctions. City host European champions PSG in the Champions League on Wednesday (20:00 BST) – their first home match since being found guilty of the majority of 115 charges . “There is a lot of noise around Manchester City and there is often noise around big clubs,” said Enrique when asked about City’s guilty verdict at a news conference at Etihad Stadium on Tuesday. “We just have to wait and see what the final decision will be. I hope everything works out well for Manchester City because I think what they have done on the pitch over the last few years has been incredible, and they certainly deserved to win all the trophies they have won. “Now we have to wait to see what the authorities decide or the judge is going to say.” An independent commission found City had broken rules over a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018 by creating “sham” contracts with commercial partners to secretly funnel more than £830m into their football operations. City insist they are innocent and have appealed. Luis Enrique added: “The first thing that you hear, it is a surprise, but we need to respect the process and wait for the final decision. “The authorities are responsible for making these decisions. But speaking only about football, they deserved those trophies. I love their football. Beyond that, we have to wait for the decision. “The trophies you win on the pitch remain on the pitch. They deserved to win that and I hope they can avoid the sanction. But we have to wait.” Enrique is friends with former City boss Pep Guardiola, who is expected to make his first return to Etihad Stadium on Wednesday since leaving at the end of last season after winning 20 trophies in 10 years. City were bought for £200m in 2008 by Abu Dhabi United Group, owned by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan – a senior member of the Abu Dhabi ruling family, who is a current vice president and deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates. PSG, who have won back-to-back Champions Leagues, are owned by Qatar Sports Investment. Both City and PSG were fined in 2014 by Uefa for breaching financial rules. PSG insisted at the time they had always operated within the regulations. Meanwhile, France forward Ousmane Dembele was asked if now was a good time to play City with everything the club is facing off the pitch. “It is always difficult regardless of it being a good moment or a bad moment,” said the PSG attacker. “They have a high quality team, world-class players and a top coach as well. It doesn’t really matter. It’s always tough playing Manchester City.”

title: England Crush Greece 5-0 to Advance in World Cup Play-Offs
body: England swept past Greece with a 5-0 victory at Leicester’s King Power Stadium, completing an 8-1 aggregate win in their Women’s World Cup qualifying play-off and setting up a two-legged second-round tie against Ukraine. Alessia Russo and Lauren James scored twice each, while Georgia Stanway added another goal as the Lionesses produced a dominant performance to progress. Chelsea forward James set up Arsenal striker Russo for the opening goal in the third minute, driving through midfield before releasing her teammate to beat the goalkeeper one-on-one. James doubled England’s lead in the 16th minute with a powerful strike into the top corner. Stanway then headed home Lauren Hemp’s cross in the 30th minute before James volleyed in her second goal four minutes later. England went into half-time with a commanding 4-0 lead and continued to create chances after the break. Stanway appeared to score her second goal in the 50th minute after controlling the ball and volleying home, but the video assistant referee (VAR) ruled it out for offside. Russo completed the scoring in the 75th minute, turning away from her defender before finishing from a tight angle. Wiegman Praises England’s Response England head coach Sarina Wiegman said her players had improved on their performance in the first leg, which England won 3-1 in Crete. “I saw a lot of good things. We wanted to do the things that we’re trying to do better than Friday and we’ve shown a lot better,” Wiegman told ITV Sport. “There’s always improvements but we scored some great goals.” She said Greece’s high pressing made the opening stages challenging, but England’s early goal helped the team settle into the match. Wiegman also explained that England were working to evolve their playing style and adapt their system to keep pace with developments in the women’s game. The coach said England would study Ukraine’s strengths and weaknesses before their next tie, while continuing to improve their own approach. Russo Highlights England’s Ruthless Start Russo said England had identified areas to improve after the first leg and delivered a more decisive performance in Leicester. “We were happy with the first game with getting the win but there were some things we wanted to work on which we saw tonight. We were ruthless early on,” she said. She also praised James, describing her as a technically gifted player who can operate anywhere in the attacking third. England will now face Ukraine over two legs in November and December, with the Lionesses aiming to move another step closer to World Cup qualification. The post England Crush Greece 5-0 to Advance in World Cup Play-Offs appeared first on Greek City Times .

title: Redesigning source control at Anthropic
body:
Redesigning source control at Anthropic ( via ) Interesting piece from Anthropic describing why and how they built their own custom alternative to Git, based on the dramatic increase in rate of changes to their code after the past six months.
In May 2026, Anthropic averaged around 2,500 code changes merged per day; as of September, we merged over 30,000 per day.
They included a chart showing those changes. I had Claude modify their chart ( code here ) to add markers for the public releases of each of their models in 2026:
This shows public release dates, not the date when models became available for Anthropic's internal use. My guess is that the introduction of Fable/Mythos class models is a key factor in the increased coding velocity.
"Antique" is their new code review system. The source control system is called Scion, and sounds to me like a reinvention of centralized source control along the lines of Subversion.
( Update : Anthropic credit Google's Piper and Meta's Sapling as "prior art" - it looks like the core concept of "derived data" was heavily inspired by Mononoke , the server component of Sapling.)
They had some pretty extreme requirements:
The history of our main branch alone is almost 100 GB, and a compressed working copy is over 25 GB. We perform on the order of 25 million code checkouts per day for CI, before counting developer environments, agent sandboxes, and research jobs. Fetched naively, that would be over 600 PB of git traffic per day.
The new system was built by a team of seven people, and the migration from Git was completed in five months.
When asked on Hacker News about the lack of offline support, Scion engineer Nick G replied :
Since Claude is by far the heaviest user of Scion and is necessarily online, this just wasn't important to do.
As an aside, I've been trying adversarial review in my own projects recently, where you have a model try and find flaws (I often play Claude and GPT off against each other). This note from the article reflected my own experience with that:
Anthropic also makes extensive use of adversarial review, and, while this is incredibly effective in many ways, it can also be myopic, so skilled engineers needed to steer Claude away from over-engineering parts of the system in response to hypothetical concerns.

title: What Do Brazil’s Elections Mean for its Foreign Policy?
body:
Running for the Presidency: Flavio Bolsonaro votes at the BarÃ£o Homem de Mello school in Vila Isabel, a neighbourhood in the Rio de Janeiro's North Zone. Image: PHOTO COM TATO SERVIÃOS FOTOGRÃFICOS LTDA / Alamy Stock
Whether Lula or FlÃ¡vio Bolsonaro wins Brazilâs presidential run-off, a right-leaning Congress and pressure from China, the US and Europe will constrain its foreign policy.
â Brazil is not for beginners â. The mantra coined by Brazilian songwriter Tom Jobim in the 1960s is more valid than ever. As we approach the second round of the 2026 presidential election, everyone â from financial analysts in Faria Lima (the financial heart of Brazil) to the residents of the small town of UbaÃ­ra ( home to large rare-earth deposits ) â is waiting for Brazilâs electoral results. Whatever the outcome of the ballot, it promises deep changes to their lives.
At the centre, there are two political, economic, institutional and social projects starkly different at first glance. On one side, there is President Luiz InÃ¡cio Lula da Silva, turning 81 years old and running for his fourth term. Lula is an experienced and skilful politician, having co-founded the Workersâ Party (PT) in 1980 . Before being elected president in 2002, Lula was defeated in the 1989, 1994 and 1998 elections. Lulaâs reputation is based on his capacity to build pragmatic alliances and reinvent himself while being able to communicate with the wide spectrum of Brazilian society. His administrations have been embraced by progressive sectors who advocated for economic development together with inequality reduction and advocacy for minority rights. Lulaâs foreign policy sought to diversify partnerships and strengthen regional ties through regional organisations, such as the establishment of UNASUR (Union of South American Nations), working together with Hugo ChÃ¡vez and funding infrastructure projects in Venezuela and Cuba through the Brazilian Development Bank ( BNDES ).
On the other side, there is FlÃ¡vio Bolsonaro, 45 years old. He was four times elected a legislative representative in Rio de Janeiro and was elected a senator in 2018, being the fourth most voted in the country . Similarly to his father, former president Jair Bolsonaro, FlÃ¡vio had numerous partisan affiliations . He was affiliated to the Partido Progressista (PP) for most of his legislative years. PP is a traditional and centre-right party that was in coalition with PT from 2003 to 2016, being directly involved with corruption scandals . FlÃ¡vio left PP in 2016 for the Partido Social CristÃ£o, when he ran for Mayor of Rio de Janeiro. In 2018, he affiliated to the Partido Social Liberal for his election to the Senate. After failing to establish their own party, FlÃ¡vio and Jair Bolsonaro had short periods in Republicanos (2020-21), and Patriota (2021), until they joined the Partido Liberal (PL) in 2021. In similar terms to PP, PL used to be a centre-right party from the centrÃ£o (âbig centreâ) and joined PTâs administrationsâ supporting base. Brazil has been known for its â coalition presidentialism â, where incumbents need to have legislative support to be able to govern. This supporting base represents a group of âphysiologicâ parties, as they exchange their support to incumbents for larger budget allocations and strategic positions in ministries.
Therefore, there is an interesting common element between Lula and FlÃ¡vio: their political pragmatism. Lulaâs administration made coalitions with the big centre whereas FlÃ¡vio and his father have been part of the big centre for many years of their political careers. Nevertheless, their differences seem to count much more to the markets and other foreign leaders, such as the US president, Donald Trump. FlÃ¡vioâs leading results in the first round of the 2026 elections was celebrated by Trump, describing results as âa very, very big victory. Amazing, actuallyâ. In US case, a potential victory for Flavio would confirm a Brazilian closer alignment to the US foreign policy and a progress of the â Donroe Doctrineâ in Latin America . For markets, there was also a striking optimism : Ibovespa, Brazilâs benchmark stock index, had an increase of 7.7% on the following day and broke a historical record, surpassing 200,000 points. Governability can explain this market enthusiasm, which stem from what FlÃ¡vio Bolsonaroâs potential victory means for Brazil, the region and the world.
PL (FlÃ¡vioâs party) transformed itself in 2021 when it welcomed the Bolsonaro family to its ranks. From the centre, PL became the institutional representation of Bolsonarismo , turning to a far more conservative political agenda. The party had an impressive performance in the 2022 election, moving from 33 to 99 representatives in the Chamber of Deputies . In 2026, PL moved to 121 of 513 seats. In the Senate, they secured 28 of 81 seats, meaning the party alone now has almost a quarter of the Chamber of Deputies and a third of the Senate. As other right and centre-right parties declared support for FlÃ¡vio Bolsonaro in this upcoming second round, his potential administration could benefit from majorities, allowing far more governability than Lula, with the latter risking facing a complete deadlock in his administration.
Supporting governability, there is favourable popular mood. As Lula seeks a fourth term, fatigue with PTâs political project progressively grows â a sentiment that traces its origin back to the 2013 protests against the cost of living . Lulaâs administrations from 2003 to 2010 inherited economic stability after years of hyperinflation and internal and external debt. A strong economic performance produced by favourable commodity prices together with a thriving Chinese economy to consume them elevated Brazilâs status as an âemerging economyâ. A new middle class was eager to occupy spaces and consume products that were once out of reach. This alignment of the stars gave Lula the political capital to elect his successor, Dilma Rousseff (2011â14).
Help your search results show more from RUSI. Adding RUSI as a preferred source on Google means our analysis appears more prominently.
However, Dilma Rousseffâs administration suffered from the worsening of Brazilâs economic performance. Poor economic results compounded by corruption scandals led to a disassociation between the countryâs aspirations and its real performance, not only by society but also in international forums. Popular discontent was quickly channelled by emerging civil society organisations, such as Movimento Brasil Livre and Vem Pra Rua , which not only forged an anti-corruption movement, but also provided new political figures to the Brazilian right-wing landscape based on a direct antagonism to PT and Rousseffâs administration. She won the second round by a slim margin, securing a fragile second mandate that immediately suffered from the lack of legislative support. Rousseff did not complete her mandate, being impeached in 2016 .
The ideological fracture deepened throughout the years. Lula was barred from running in 2018 following convictions that were later annulled . His political capital could not secure PTâs victory through Fernando Haddad either and Jair Bolsonaro won as an anti-system candidate. Once in power, he quickly built his legislative support and elevated the judiciary as his new nemesis. His mandate (2019â22) was marked by political clashes with the Supreme Federal Court and challenges to the electoral system. Internationally, Lula and Dilma sought to increase Brazilâs influence in the main international forums as the Global Southâs leading voice by participating in UN peace operations ( MINUSTAH in Haiti and UNIFIL in Lebanon ), and engaging with the BRICS since 2006 to counterbalance Western institutions. By contrast, Bolsonaroâs government was marked by a retreat of Brazilâs participation in international organisations, direct alignment with the US (during Trumpâs administration) and strong support for Israel . Therefore, the partisan configuration in 2027 reveals a divided country that has, since 2018, progressively leaned toward a right-wing conservative agenda â or, at the very least, distanced itself from the left progressive.
