title: Bail denied to U.S. suspect charged in connection with Tumbler Ridge school shooting
body:
The U.S. suspect charged in connection with the deadly shooting in Tumbler Ridge earlier this year will remain behind bars.
James Cody Bryant appeared in a Seattle courtroom wearing an olive green button-up shirt, black-rimmed glasses and long waist-length hair parted to the side.
Bryant appeared to be sniffling and crying at the beginning of the hearing.
Approximately eight people sat on the defendant’s side of the courtroom, while about a dozen sat on the opposing side.
Bryant had begun transitioning to a female before the shootings, according to authorities.
Bryant is accused of helping the shooter in Tumbler Ridge, 18-year-old Jesse Van Rootselaar, start their car after they had already killed their mother and step-brother, so that Van Rootselaar could drive to Tumbler Ridge School and carry out the mass shooting.
Bryant is charged with conspiracy to murder people in a foreign country .
In court filings, it states that Bryant gave Van Rootselaar “tactical advice” on how to carry out the shooting, offering suggestions for target locations and what type of guns Van Rootselaar should use.
On Feb. 10, Van Rootselaar opened fire at Tumbler Ridge Secondary School, killing five students and an educational assistant before taking their own life. At a nearby residence, Van Rootselaar’s mother and half-brother were found dead.
On Tuesday, the prosecution argued that Bryant should remain in custody because of the seriousness of the offence, the strength of the evidence and the potential danger to the community.
“It really doesn’t get much more serious, or much more dangerous for the community,” Assistant United States attorney Todd Greenberg said.
He emphasized that Bryant had been in daily communication for months with someone planning a mass murder in British Columbia and understood the potential scale of the killings.
“The defendant was for months in daily communication with someone who was planning a mass murder event in British Columbia,” Greenberg said.
Bryant had a “full understanding of how high the death toll could get.”
The prosecution then outlined several actions it said demonstrated Bryant’s involvement in the planning and preparation of the killings:
Greenberg also referenced Discord conversations, arguing that there was little factual dispute about what had occurred.
He argued that Bryant’s conduct over several months demonstrated a willingness to assist in planning a mass killing and an opportunity to intervene before it happened. “But most importantly… is Bryant’s own character,” Greenberg said.
“This is someone who helped plan a mass murder over the course of months… and most importantly, somebody who could’ve put a stop to all of this before it happened.”
Bryant kept their eyes fixed downward as the prosecutor read messages concerning not informing on Van Rootselaar.
According to Bryant’s roommates, there were at least five computers in their apartment and upwards of 10 additional internet-connected devices, including laptops and desktop computers.
The prosecution also raised concerns about Bryant’s mental health. Although Bryant denied suicidal ideation during a pretrial interview, they had previously told Van Rootselaar that they were suicidal, with one such statement reportedly dating to Jan. 12.
However, Greenberg did note that Bryant has no criminal history, has ties to western Washington and was employed, although it was unclear whether the job remained available.
Bryant’s defence counsel, assistant federal public defenders Gregory Murphy and Dennis Carroll, acknowledged the horror of the killings while arguing that the court must apply the usual legal standard for bail rather than be swayed by the emotional weight of the case.
The defence also questioned the government’s handling of the investigation and the timing of Bryant’s arrest, saying it is telling that the government made no effort to arrest her for a full seven months after her interview with the FBI in March.
Counsel noted that Bryant had sobbed during the FBI interview following the killings and during a subsequent interview in March. Although a warrant was obtained on Oct. 2, Bryant was not arrested until four days later, after a press conference had been organized and held. Counsel described the arrest as having been arranged by appointment.
The defence said Bryant and Van Rootselaar had become friends approximately three years earlier and that Van Rootselaar had experienced serious mental health issues, including repeated hospitalizations.
They said there was no evidence that Bryant knew the specifics of Van Rootselar’s plan that day.
Defence counsel emphasized that Bryant had community support, with people attending the hearing on their behalf.
The defence maintained that Bryant’s lack of a criminal record, community ties, cooperation with investigators and potential release conditions supported release pending further proceedings.
When considering the case, the judge framed the central issue as whether Bryant could be released under conditions that would adequately address the risks of failing to appear in court and posing a danger to the community.
The judge emphasized that the decision was not simply about which side had presented the stronger argument. The court had to determine whether reasonable and enforceable conditions could sufficiently mitigate the identified risks.
The judge also stressed the importance of considering the facts and circumstances of the alleged offence. Written statements submitted both for and against Bryant’s release were filed and read by the judge.
The judge noted that pretrial services had identified serious, deeply rooted mental health concerns involving Bryant, including substance abuse.
The judge also emphasized that the case involved internet communications, making any release conditions particularly difficult to design and enforce. Internet monitoring would be extremely important if Bryant were released, but the judge expressed concern about the ability to keep pace with technological developments.
The court would have needed to consider whether conditions involving mental health treatment, monitoring and ongoing evaluation could realistically succeed in mitigating the risks.
Ultimately, the judge concluded that the risks could not reasonably be addressed through release conditions.
Bryant was denied bail and ordered detained until further court order.

title: UCL Roundup: Lookman scores as Atletico beat Man United, Osimhen falls to Barca
body:
Ademola Lookman scored nine minutes after coming off the bench as Atlético Madrid defeated Manchester United 2-0, while Victor Osimhen played the full 90 minutes in Galatasaray’s 4-1 home defeat to Barcelona in Tuesday’s UEFA Champions League action.
Atlético took the lead after just 53 seconds when Pablo Barrios converted Alex Baena’s cutback.
Manchester United threatened through Bryan Mbeumo, but goalkeeper Jan Oblak made key saves to keep the visitors out. Alejandro Grimaldo also came close for Atlético, striking the angle of the post and crossbar with a free-kick.
Johnny Cardoso thought he had doubled Atlético’s lead, but his goal was ruled out after a VAR review found a handball by Marcos Llorente in the build-up.
Introduced in the 70th minute, Lookman struck in the 79th to seal the victory for Atlético, who claimed their first points of the league phase and extended their unbeaten run against United to five matches.
At Rams Park, Galatasaray took a surprise lead in the 28th minute when Aleksey Batrakov’s shot deflected off João Cancelo and into the net.
Cancelo made amends by curling in Barcelona’s equaliser shortly before half-time. The visitors then took control, with Lamine Yamal providing two assists in four minutes as Barcelona completed a 4-1 comeback victory.
Osimhen played the full match but couldn’t prevent Galatasaray from suffering a heavy home defeat. The result extended Barcelona’s winning run across all competitions to 10 matches.
Arsenal beat Lille 3-0 with Bukayo Saka and Eberechi Eze on target for the Gunners. Sporting CP also defeated Lens 2-0 while Villarreal overcame Napoli 3-1.
In a mouthwatering seven-goal thriller, Club Brugge edged Inter 4-3, RB Leipzig beat PSV 1-0, and Sabah Baku defeated Slavia Prague 2-0.
There was plenty of drama and goals in Norway, where Bayern Munich were held to a 3-3 draw by Viking.
Tunde Eludini is a graduate of the Obafemi Awolowo University Ile-Ife, Nigeria where he studied International Relations. He is a Senior Correspondent coordinating the sports section for PREMIUM TIMES. Twitter : @tundeyeludini

title: Greece Extends Free Obesity Medication to 43,500 Beneficiaries
body: Greece will provide up to eight doses of obesity medication to the 43,500 people already enrolled in its free treatment programme, Deputy Health Minister Irini Agapidaki announced, while confirming the return of free breast cancer screening for 2.4 million women and new cardiovascular checks from November. Speaking to Skai radio, Agapidaki said doctors would determine individually how many doses each beneficiary needs, ranging from one to eight. The programme paused in June, but the Public Health Experts Committee submitted its recommendation late last week, allowing the treatment scheme to resume. Agapidaki said bureaucratic procedures to transfer funding from European to national resources had caused the delay. “The programme continues normally and is completely free,” she said. The ministry will announce plans to admit new beneficiaries in due course, Agapidaki added, in coordination with Health Minister Adonis Georgiadis. Free Breast Cancer Screening Returns for 2.4 Million Women Greece is gradually sending electronic referrals to 2.4 million women aged 45 to 74 for free digital mammograms and breast ultrasounds as part of Breast Cancer Prevention Month. Agapidaki said screening through the national Prolambano prevention programme had helped at least 6,000 women receive diagnoses at an early stage, substantially improving their chances of full recovery. She stressed the importance of detecting abnormalities in healthy people before symptoms appear or they can feel a lump. “No woman should ignore the message,” she said, warning that Greece has a high mortality rate among women aged 55 to 69. Cardiovascular Screening to Expand in November Greece expects to begin sending text-message notifications for a new round of cardiovascular screening in early November. The programme will provide a free lipoprotein(a), or Lp(a), blood test to identify inherited cardiovascular risk associated with elevated levels of this type of cholesterol. Agapidaki said Greece would be the only European Union country to offer the test free of charge. Children may also undergo screening when results indicate high levels, while people with concerning findings may qualify for additional free examinations, including myocardial perfusion scans and stress echocardiograms. Agapidaki said the previous screening round identified more than 1,000 people with serious coronary artery disease. Cervical and Colorectal Cancer Screening Continues The Prolambano programme will continue offering free cervical cancer screening through HPV DNA tests, Pap smears, colposcopy and biopsies. The colorectal cancer screening programme also remains in place, using home self-tests followed, where necessary, by colonoscopies, biopsies and polyp removal. Agapidaki said the first round identified 2,600 people who had gastrointestinal cancer without knowing it, allowing them to receive an earlier diagnosis. The government’s wider prevention initiative aims to identify serious illnesses before symptoms develop and improve access to timely treatment through free screening services. title: Kimberly Guilfoyle Thanks Greek People for Their Hospitality
body: US Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle has described her diplomatic tenure as the greatest honour of her life, highlighted achievements in energy, defence and trade, and vowed to defend her name and reputation against what she called false allegations. In a statement posted on her personal X account following her resignation announcement, Guilfoyle thanked US President Donald Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio for entrusting her with the role. She also expressed gratitude to the Greek people for their hospitality, cooperation and warm welcome. Guilfoyle said she had worked from the beginning of her tenure to advance Trump’s “America First” agenda, strengthen the strategic alliance between Greece and the United States, and deliver results for the American people. Energy and Defence Cooperation Among Key Achievements Guilfoyle pointed to agreements aimed at increasing US liquefied natural gas exports to Europe, efforts to advance the Vertical Gas Corridor and reduce Europe’s dependence on Russian energy, and closer defence and security cooperation with Greece, a key NATO ally. She also highlighted efforts to expand opportunities for American businesses and investment across the region. “I am particularly proud of the role our Embassy played in strengthening American energy dominance, advancing economic cooperation and ensuring that the United States remains an indispensable leader in Southeast Europe,” Guilfoyle said. She credited Trump’s leadership, Rubio’s commitment to American diplomacy and the work of US diplomatic personnel for the achievements she outlined. Guilfoyle Vows to Defend Her Name Against Allegations Addressing recent allegations against her, Guilfoyle rejected them as false and vowed to defend her reputation and integrity. “These allegations are false, and I intend to vigorously defend my name, my reputation and my integrity,” she said. Guilfoyle added that she had devoted her professional life to pursuing justice, standing up for what was right and defending the values she believes distinguish the United States. She said she would not allow what she described as false accusations to define her years of public service. Guilfoyle also reaffirmed her loyalty to Trump and Rubio, saying her support for the president and his mission to “Make America Great Again” remained unchanged. “Although my time as ambassador may be coming to an end, my commitment to President Trump, the America First movement and the country I love will never end,” she said. Thanks Greek People for Their Hospitality Guilfoyle closed her statement by describing service to the United States as the greatest honour of her life and thanking Greeks for the way they had welcomed her. “I extend my deepest and most sincere thanks to the Greek people for their hospitality, cooperation and the warm welcome with which they embraced me,” she said. She concluded by invoking God’s blessing on Trump, US diplomats, members of the American armed forces and the United States. Her statement presented her tenure as one focused on strengthening Greek-American ties, advancing US energy interests in Europe and expanding regional economic and security cooperation, while firmly rejecting the allegations against her. The post Kimberly Guilfoyle Thanks Greek People for Their Hospitality appeared first on Greek City Times .

title: Ukraine sent a spiked tank and a Bradley into Russian drone fire. The spikes held, and Ukraine’s own drones got them home
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); A Ukrainian assault regiment continues to deploy mixed formations of drones and up-armored vehicles The vehicles do the shooting; the drones fly close top cover These mixed formations could rescue old-fashioned armored vehicles from obsolescence by helping protect the vehicles from drone attack For the second time in two weeks, Ukraine's 475th Assault Regiment has demonstrated how armored vehicles can fight and survive on a battlefield buzzing with enemy drones. The regiment encased a tank and an American-made M-2 Bradley infantry fighting vehicle in metal frames and welded hundreds of metal spines onto those frames, transforming them into "hedgehog" vehicles. The cage makes the tank impossible to identify from the footage, and the regiment hasn't said what model it is. The frames support the spines, which trigger incoming drones' warheads a safe distance from the vehicles' hulls. But that's not all. To shepherd the two-vehicle formation across the disputed gray zone for a close engagement with a Russian position, presumably somewhere in northeastern Ukraine's Kharkiv Oblast, the 475th Assault Regiment deployed drones: both single-use first-person-view models and grenade-dropping, reusable Vampire models. The Code 9.2 Regiment once again used the element of surprise, bringing a tank and a Bradley onto the battlefield—transformed into steel hedgehogs and covered by drones from the air. With a combined strike, the assault troops drove the enemy from several positions in… pic.twitter.com/Uq3mlWTsJq — MilitaryNewsUA (@front_ukrainian) October 11, 2026 The vehicles and their crews didn't fight alone. They fought in mixed ground-air "combined arms" formations. The tank and fighting vehicle provided the firepower. The escorting drones provided the aerial protection. Vampire drones drop grenades to suppress Russian positions and clear mines and loitering Russian drones. FPV drones dive down to intercept the Russians' own FPV drones as they zoom in to strike the vehicles. The 475th Assault Regiment cut together a video montage of the most recent assault. The video depicts the tank and the Bradley rolling along a well-traveled route as at least one friendly FPV and at least one friendly Vampire drone flew overhead and an additional drone watched from a short distance away. The vehicles repeatedly came under attack from Russian FPVs and heavier loitering munitions. An escorting Ukrainian FPV moved to intercept, with unclear results. A couple of Russian drones managed to score hits on the vehicles, but their hedgehog armor held—and both vehicles appear to have survived the there-and-back daytime trip into battle. Explore further Ukraine is now sending its tanks into battle with drone escorts: they can drive into a Russian kill zone and come back alive A way forward for vehicles It's at least the second time the 475th Assault Regiment has deployed vehicle-drone teams. The Ukrainian 3rd Army Corps used a related approach in its months-long counteroffensive in northern Donetsk Oblast, which began this spring: it sent in ground robots first, suppressing Russian strongpoints, fraying Russian supply lines, and clearing routes for manned vehicles to follow. The unmanned aerial escorts lend the 475th Assault Regiment's hedgehog vehicles situational awareness they might not have on their own. It's well known that hedgehog armor can obscure a vehicle crew's view of the surrounding terrain. But friendly drones flying directly overhead can act as eyes in the sky for the crews on the ground. The drones also help the vehicle crews compensate for a lack of mobility. The metal cages that support the metal spines that make up hedgehog armor tend to prevent a vehicle's turret from fully rotating. In order to aim its gun, a hedgehog vehicle has to meticulously point its whole self—turret and hull—at the enemy. Explore further Ukraine’s newest Abrams brigade just built the “dumbest” tank cage of the war. In 2026, that barely matters. That takes trial and error, and time. The longer it takes, the more vulnerable a vehicle is to enemy drones. Friendly drones, running interference for the vehicles, can reduce that exposure long enough for the vehicle to fire a few shots. The 475th Assault Regiment and 3rd Army Corps, among other units in Russia's wider war on Ukraine, are pointing the way forward for traditional armored vehicles in this new drone age. Yes, vehicles are more vulnerable to aerial attack than they were just a few years ago. But no, armored vehicles aren't obsolete or useless. They just need a little help—or a lot of it—from the same kinds of drones that also make their existence so perilous.

title: Saka responds to Arteta’s challenge with ‘huge impact’
body: Bukayo Saka responded to the challenge set by Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta, proving a game-changer in the 3-0 Champions League win over Lille. The England forward has been told he should aim to score “two or three” goals per game, such was his quality and his boss’s expectations. Saka did not achieve that tally against the French visitors, but shook off illness to come off the bench and assist Eberechi Eze’s strike that made it 2-0, before rolling in his side’s third goal. The 25-year-old has now scored four goals in nine games this season and looks to be taking the next step in his evolution as Arsenal ‘s key man. With the majority of his side’s attacking play involving him, he has always been an influential figure. But with opposition defenders doubling up on him and injury issues over the last two seasons, there were doubts over whether Saka could still do what was asked of him in attack or if he had lost a yard of pace. Arteta has tweaked Saka’s positioning this season and, prior to Lille’s visit, said it has been done deliberately to get him closer to the goal. ‘He delivered with real quality’ “That is where we need to get him,” said the Gunners boss before the game. “And if he misses the chance, so be it. At the end, the more volume we generate, the bigger the probability of him scoring more goals.” Saka’s strike against Lille was a confident one-touch finish and came after he missed a late one-on-one opportunity in Saturday’s Premier League victory over Leeds . “He has been getting in great positions, getting shots, getting one-touch finishes and tap-ins,” added Arteta. “That is the kind of unpredictability we have with that player, otherwise we know how the opponent is going to defend him. He is doing well, he could have had another four or five goals by now, easily. But if he continues like that, we know. “When he talks about scoring a certain amount of goals, he needs to be thinking about scoring a certain amount of goals per game. If that shifts, that mentality, he will get into those positions and score more goals.” Saka has scored 20 goals in a season just once in his career, which came in the 2023-24 campaign and 16 in the Premier League. But the winger has also been in good goalscoring form for England with five in his last four matches and scored a double in the 7-0 Nations League demolition of Croatia in the recent international break. Saka is now on 19 goals in major European competitions for Arsenal , only behind Thierry Henry (42), while he has nine assists in the Champions League which puts him behind Henry (16) and Cesc Fabregas (14). He has refused to disclose the targets he has set himself, but Arteta welcomed Saka’s response following his message to do more in front of goal. The Spaniard said: “I don’t know if that’s the case, but I am very happy. “He wasn’t feeling that good yesterday and today, as he had some sort of illness. He wasn’t ready to start but he was really wanting to contribute to the team if it was needed and he came on and made a huge impact and delivered with real quality.” Arteta revealed he also spoke to Saka after telling the media about his desire for the player to have a greater impact. “After the press conference… I said ‘Bukayo, I just killed you in the press conference, good luck tomorrow’. “He was laughing. He knows that we have discussed these kind of things and he takes it because he wants to be the best version of himself. “In order to do that, you have to put big objectives and challenges and try to reason by working and being consistent – and when it doesn’t work, keep going because he has the ability to do it.” Gyokeres struggles on mixed night for fringe players Arteta made five changes to the team that started the win over Leeds as the Gunners looked to navigate six matches in all competitions during this month. Noni Madueke moved to the right wing after putting in a good performance on the left at the weekend, with Mikel Merino, Eze and Viktor Gyokeres all coming into the starting XI. Eze had started just two games in all competitions before the match with Lille and Arteta had said his attitude had been “phenomenal” despite a lack of game time. The 28-year-old showed flashes of his undoubted quality and his finish for Arsenal ‘s second goal – and his first of the season – will give him confidence going forward. Madueke had a mixed night as he showed his ability to beat a defender, but questions remain over his end product – even if he provided the assist for Jurrien Timber’s classy opening goal. However, it was not a good night for Gyokeres. The Sweden striker scored 21 goals in all competitions last season as Arsenal won the title for the first time in 22 years and displayed his willingness to run and work hard. But Gyokeres had just 12 touches before being replaced and Kai Havertz, as he so often does, looked a much better and more natural fit for the Arsenal frontline, teeing up Saka’s goal too. Arteta brought on Saka, Havertz and Martin Odegaard after going 1-0 up and all three contributed to show why they are still the first names on the teamsheet and why the Arsenal boss will be so reliant on them if they are to achieve more honours.

title: Cerebras CEO pushes back on AI doomsday warnings
body:
Cerebras Systems CEO and co-founder Andrew Feldman thinks the AI doomer narrative isn’t doing the industry any favors. At TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 , the AI chipmaker exec quipped that “some of the leaders in the AI world maybe shouldn’t be allowed to talk in public.”
He’s referencing the negativity now spreading around the dangers of AI, from models breaking containment to AI insiders debating the percentage chance that AI may kill all of humanity by the end of the decade. The argument has become so mainstream that Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei was recently parodied in a skit on “Saturday Night Live,” where the fictional character summed up the discourse, saying, “We do not condone what we are doing.”
Feldman, however, thinks the promise and potential that go hand in hand with AI developments are getting overlooked. He thinks AI leaders should spend more time telling people that AI could lead to a world where your grandkids will “never meet anybody who dies of cancer,” for instance, even if they have concerns about AI risks.
Clearly, Feldman has a vested interest in AI being successful, as the company’s customers include big names working with the technology, like OpenAI, Block, Figma, pharmaceutical giant GSK, and Lovable.
However, he’s pragmatic about weighing the trade-offs between risk and reward.
“I don’t think there are powerful technologies that don’t come with the challenge of ‘what happens when powerful technologies are in the hands of bad people?’ I think you can’t make one and not have the other,” Feldman said during his interview at Disrupt.
“I think what we have to say is that this technology is powerful,” he added. “We have to be thoughtful about it. We have to regulate it reasonably,” he added.
The chipmaker CEO also suggested that some of the negativity around AI has to do with how the data center industry has approached the new buildouts created by AI demand.
“As an industry, we weren’t super good for the past few years at working with local communities, particularly in the U.S. We — the industry — didn’t do what others have done in the power industry in oil and gas. They didn’t work with the community. They didn’t engage the community as they should have, and that was a problem,” Feldman said.
He compared the NIMBY-ism — “not in my backyard!” — of what’s going on in the U.S. with other countries, naming Brazil, Canada, Finland, Iceland, Norway, Mexico, and Sweden as markets where they’re encouraging companies to build data centers.
Feldman also wasn’t concerned that efficiency improvements would create less demand for his chips, or those from other companies competing with Nvidia, as Cerebras is.
“We can do our job as hardware vendors to make our compute more efficient, and then the model makers can do improved work in making their models more efficient to achieve the same goals. All of this has to come together to make meaningful strides forward,” he noted.

title: Greece Plans Mass Production of Unmanned Naval Vessels
body: Greece aims to make its Navy Europe’s leading force in developing autonomous maritime platforms by 2030, Defence Minister Nikos Dendias said on Tuesday, 13 October 2026, as he inaugurated a new joint training school for unmanned and autonomous maritime systems at the Kanellopoulos Naval Base in Skaramangas. Dendias identified the accelerated development and operational deployment of autonomous and unmanned systems as a priority under Greece’s Agenda 2030 defence reform programme. He said the next step would involve producing large numbers of the Greek-designed Pyrpolitis unmanned surface vessel to strengthen the Hellenic Navy, alongside developing larger autonomous and unmanned vessels. “The next step includes producing the Greek-designed unmanned vessel Pyrpolitis in large numbers to reinforce the Navy, as well as developing larger autonomous and unmanned vessels,” Dendias said. The minister said Greece must develop its own defence technologies rather than rely solely on equipment acquired from abroad, even when foreign purchases include technology transfers and domestic production. “We must develop the ability to design systems ourselves and produce systems ourselves,” he said. Greece Develops Its Own Unmanned Naval Technology Dendias presented the Pyrpolitis as an example of Greece’s growing domestic defence capabilities. The Hellenic Navy designed, developed and built the unmanned surface vessel in Greece, incorporating autonomous operating capabilities that have reached the final stage of testing, according to the minister. The vessel can collect information, conduct surveillance and identify targets. It can also attack targets on the water. The Navy has also recently evaluated an autonomous surface vessel capable of surveillance, reconnaissance and coordinated autonomous operations known as “swarming”, Dendias said. He stressed that autonomous systems represent a further step beyond remotely operated or unmanned platforms. These systems use artificial intelligence while retaining human oversight, potentially expanding the Navy’s operational capabilities in the Aegean Sea. Under Agenda 2030, Greece is establishing the infrastructure needed to modernise the armed forces through changes to organisation, training and joint operations, alongside the adoption of new technologies. Dendias cited the establishment of the 309th Unmanned Systems Manufacturing Factory in June and the opening of a joint training centre for unmanned aerial vehicles in Tripoli in July. The new maritime school extends this programme to naval operations. Autonomous Systems to Support Surveillance and Maritime Security Dendias said unmanned and autonomous vehicles could undertake surveillance, reconnaissance, port protection, mine warfare and the protection of critical infrastructure. By assigning some surveillance and patrol duties to these systems, the Navy could reduce the time personnel must spend at sea and ease operational demands on fleet crews. He also emphasised the need to protect infrastructure beneath the sea, including energy and communications networks, alongside Greece’s national sovereignty and sovereign rights. “The new Navy must be able to protect not only national sovereignty and sovereign rights, but also critical infrastructure, such as energy and communications networks on the seabed,” he said. Greece is also seeking to strengthen its conventional naval capabilities. Dendias referred to the forthcoming raising of the Greek flag on the frigate Nearchos in France. He also reported an initial understanding reached during recent talks in Venice with Italy’s defence minister and the Italian Navy chief concerning the transfer of a number of mine-countermeasure vehicles to Greece to address operational needs. Greece Seeks European Leadership by 2030 Dendias said Greece aims to become the European Union’s strongest force in the operational use of autonomous vehicles by 2030, with the Navy leading Europe in autonomous platform development. The programme extends beyond maritime operations to land, sea and air systems, with the common objective of improving operational effectiveness and deterrence. The minister said Greece did not threaten any country but sought to defend its constitutional and legal rights. He added that achieving the government’s objectives would depend on personnel with the necessary knowledge, skills, determination and capabilities. The new school will help provide the training required to operate and maintain unmanned and autonomous systems, including basic repair work. New School Demonstrates Maritime Systems Following the inauguration, Dendias attended a static display of unmanned and autonomous maritime equipment. Demonstrations included the Pyrpolitis and Corsair surface systems, as well as the Pluto Plus and Plutino underwater systems. He toured the school’s facilities and received briefings from Rear Admiral Stefanos Sarris, commander of the Naval Training Command, and Captain Eleftherios Zervas, commander of the Palaskas Training Centre. Officers also explained maintenance procedures, basic repairs and practical training methods. The minister then watched demonstrations of the school’s main simulators and an operational scenario involving unmanned vessels and underwater systems at the Naval Training Command’s maritime testing area. Senior military leaders, parliamentarians, local government representatives and former defence officials attended the ceremony, including Chief of the Hellenic National Defence General Staff General Dimitrios Choupis and Chief of the Hellenic Navy Vice Admiral Dimitrios-Eleftherios Kataras. The post Greece Plans Mass Production of Unmanned Naval Vessels appeared first on Greek City Times .

title: Ex-Gang Leader Duane Davis Sentenced To Minimum Of 40 Years For Tupac Murder
body: Duane “Keffe D” Davis, the former Los Angeles gang leader who boasted for years about his involvement in the killing of rapper Tupac Shakur, only to deny it when he came to trial, has been sentenced to a minimum of 40 years in prison. The sentence, which will likely see him die in custody, comes three decades after the gunning down of one of the most influential hip hop artists of the late 20th century, and after years of criticism over investigations that went nowhere. Davis, 63, formerly ran a branch of the feared Crips, one of a patchwork of rival gangs that controlled parts of Los Angeles in the 1990s. He spent years evading justice and seemingly believed he was beyond the reach of the law when he wrote in his memoir that he had ordered the killing of Shakur. “For three years, I’ve heard you say some variation of the same thing to law enforcement… in your book, and it’s something like, ‘Yeah, I was involved in this, but I’m different. I’ve moved on. I got out of Compton. I’m a grandfather now,'” Judge Carli Kierny told Davis as she handed down the sentence in a Las Vegas courtroom on Tuesday. “I’m here to tell you that’s not how this works.” “You don’t get to take a man from his family. You don’t get to take his very life, his whole future from him, and just walk away from it. Especially when that man is Tupac Shakur,” the judge said. Shakur was a key figure in a hip-hop rivalry pitting the US East Coast against the West Coast. He was just 25 when he was gunned down in Las Vegas. A trial heard how Davis ordered the September 7, 1996 killing of the hip-hop artist after his own nephew had been beaten by members of Shakur’s entourage at a Las Vegas casino. The “California Love” artist was shot about two hours after the casino confrontation by a gunman in a white Cadillac that pulled up at a red light alongside the BMW in which the rapper was riding. Davis handed the gun to someone sitting in the back seat of the Cadillac and ordered that person to shoot Shakur, who died six days later. The name of that person has not been definitively revealed, and Davis is the only person who was in the Cadillac that evening who is still alive. The driver of the BMW, Death Row Records co-founder Marion “Suge” Knight, was wounded. The post Ex-Gang Leader Duane Davis Sentenced To Minimum Of 40 Years For Tupac Murder appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Spox Trehubov: Russian forces may seek to expand control zone along Kharkiv region border
body:
This was reported by Viktor Trehubov, a spokesperson for the Joint Forces Operation, during a television appearance, according to Ukrinform.
“We do not expect a rapid escalation, but while there has been a relatively stable lull in the Velykyi Burluk sector for some time—compared to our other sectors—there will now be an escalation there; they will now be pushing primarily toward the village of Anyshchyne and beyond,” he said.
According to the spokesperson, the Russians in this sector will attempt to penetrate Ukrainian positions and establish a zone of control directly along the border , as their control in the Velykyi Burluk sector is currently sporadic.
“They will most likely try to stretch it further and further; they will try to extend it along the entire border, not just in certain sections where they managed to gain a foothold earlier,” Trehubov added.
He assured that the Defense Forces are aware of the enemy’s plans and will not allow them to be carried out.
As reported by Ukrinform, a spokesperson for the Joint Forces Operation stated that in the Vovchansk direction, the tactical initiative generally lies with Ukraine.

title: Parrot Strengthens Its Position in U.S. Army Drone Procurement Programs
body:
Parrot, a European leader in professional micro-UAV systems, today announces significant progress in its engagement with the U.S. Army, combining initial commercial success through the newly launched UAS Marketplace with a further competitive selection milestone in the Army’s Short Range Reconnaissance (SRR) program. While strengthening its position within U.S. defense procurement channels, Parrot has already generated nearly $2 million in orders on the UAS Marketplace since going live in Q3 2026 and is actively supporting the broader deployment of its next-generation ANAFI UKR tactical reconnaissance systems.
U.S. Army UAS Marketplace: direct access to operational procurement
Launched in March 2026, the U.S. Army’s UAS Marketplace introduces a new approach to drone procurement, enabling military units, government agencies and allied partners to compare and purchase vetted systems based on their specific operational requirements.
Admission to the platform is subject to U.S. Army qualification and compliance procedures, including technical and cybersecurity assessments. Unlike traditional centralized procurement programs, the Marketplace gives operational units greater flexibility to select systems directly, creating a competitive purchasing channel driven by mission requirements and end-user feedback. Parrot went live on the platform in Q3 2026 and has already recorded approximately $2 million in orders for ANAFI UKR systems through the Marketplace, marking the first commercial results of this new sales initiative.
To support rapid deployment, Parrot is establishing the operational capacity to target delivery lead times of approximately two weeks, positioning the Group to respond efficiently to demand from U.S. military units and other eligible customers.
Short Range Reconnaissance: advancing through a competitive U.S. Army selection process
Parrot has also successfully completed the flight demonstration phase of the U.S. Army’s next-generation platoon-level Short Range Reconnaissance (SRR) evaluation process.
Following competitive flight trials conducted in June 2026, Parrot was selected as one of five manufacturers to advance to the manufacturing readiness assessment phase, alongside four U.S. companies.
The SRR initiative aims to equip frontline military units with advanced small unmanned aircraft systems capable of providing real-time intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance in demanding operational environments.
This latest milestone confirms Parrot’s ability to compete in rigorous U.S. military evaluations and brings the Group one step further in a procurement process that assesses both operational performance and the ability to support deployment at scale.
Supporting the next generation of tactical reconnaissance
These developments build on Parrot’s longstanding engagement with U.S. defense and government customers, including its participation in the U.S. Army’s Short Range Reconnaissance program since 2019 and the adoption of ANAFI USA by multiple U.S. Federal Agencies and State Public Safety & Law Enforcement.
With ANAFI UKR, Parrot brings a new generation of tactical reconnaissance capabilities to this established relationship, combining class-leading flight time, advanced autonomous flight, secure communications and the ability to operate in GNSS-denied and contested environments. Parrot remains committed to meeting the U.S. military’s exacting standards for performance, security and reliability, while supporting the evolving operational needs of U.S. forces.
Together, the UAS Marketplace and SRR program provide complementary opportunities to deepen Parrot’s engagement with U.S. defense customers, combining immediate access to operational procurement with continued participation in competitive programs for future deployments.
Chris Roberts, Parrot’s Senior Vice President & Chief Revenue Officer, commented: “The combination of immediate procurement opportunities through the UAS Marketplace and continued progress within the SRR program represents a significant step forward for Parrot in the U.S. defense market. These achievements reflect both the operational performance of ANAFI UKR and the dedication of our teams to delivering trusted capabilities at scale. We are encouraged by the strong initial demand and look forward to further strengthening our partnerships with U.S. defense and government customers.”

title: The Washington Post: U.S. and Europe are developing a new plan to end the Russia–Ukraine war, offering incentives and security arrangements in exchange for a ceasefire along the current front line
body: The U.S. and Europe are gradually working toward a joint proposal for a broad peace deal between Russia and Ukraine, built around financial benefits and security guarantees for both Kyiv and Moscow, according to Washington Post columnist David Ignatius. The proposal is intended as a starting point for a final agreement on territory that neither side will find fully acceptable. “We need to make the problem and the solution bigger to help both sides see what the postwar situation would be — and then make concessions,” an anonymous U.S. official familiar with the negotiations told The Washington Post. The official said the plan has four main components: Rebuilding Ukraine : The plan calls for establishing a funding mechanism involving the World Bank and the U.S. investment firm BlackRock. Negotiators have already asked Kyiv for detailed cost estimates and assurances that the money will not be stolen. Ukraine is expected to provide specific figures in the coming days. Security guarantees : Ukraine would receive security guarantees of some kind from the U.S. and European countries in the event of another Russian attack, modeled on Article 5 of the NATO treaty. Moscow is also expected to receive guarantees: Russia would be able to enter into agreements with Europe “that address its security concerns,” though their specific terms remain unclear. Economic integration of Russia, Ukraine, and Europe : The plan calls for a major energy deal under which cheap Russian oil and gas would resume flowing to Europe, with profits from transit and sales shared between Kyiv and Moscow. This part of the plan would also set out the process and timetable for lifting sanctions. Territory : The proposal would freeze positions along the current line of contact. This is the most difficult issue, and such a compromise would probably satisfy neither side. The other components were included in the plan as “bonuses” specifically to persuade Moscow and Kyiv to accept it. Although European leaders publicly expressed outrage at Donald Trump’s deal with Vladimir Putin on Russian diesel supplies, they remain determined to continue the diplomatic process led by U.S. presidential envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, The Washington Post reported. “It’s a moment to take heat out of the situation and get back to work,” an unnamed European diplomat told the newspaper. Reuters also reported today that Witkoff and Kushner met with Ukrainian representatives in Miami last Friday and sought to convince them that Trump’s diesel deal with Russia would help bring the Kremlin back to the negotiating table. “The idea was that the U.S. could go back to Russia and say ‘See, the Ukrainians stopped striking, and we gave you ​this deal. Now it’s your turn to do something,’” one source said. At the same meeting, however, Witkoff and Kushner said Putin was not ready to negotiate an end to the war. According to a Reuters source close to the Kremlin, the Russian president plans to return to negotiations only after capturing the rest of the Donbas. The war in photographs: Kharkiv On the evening of October 12, Russian forces struck Kharkiv, killing three people and injuring 15, according to Ukraine’s State Emergency Service. title: Viking hold Bayern in thriller as Kane breaks Messi record
body: Norwegian champions Viking produced one of the biggest results in their history, holding six-time European champions Bayern Munich to a thrilling draw in the Champions League. Viking, who were in Norway’s second tier as recently as 2018, scored two first-half goals to take control before England captain Harry Kane equalised with a penalty and a back-post header. Luis Diaz gave Bayern the lead with a tap-in, but Michael Olise was sent off shortly after for two yellow cards in the same phase of play, including throwing the ball in a Viking player’s face. That gave Viking, who are playing in Europe’s top competition for the first time since 1992-93, renewed energy. They were the better team after the red card and got a deserved equaliser when substitute Herman Haugen headed home at the back post. Viking captain Zlatko Tripic told Norwegian channel Tv2: “I could have played another 90 minutes. I’m so incredibly proud. I’ve waited 34 years for this. “We’re playing against some of the best players in the world, yet we still managed to take a 2-0 lead. I think we played an incredibly solid match. We used everything we had. We’ve gained a bit of European experience. I’m just so unbelievably happy.” Viking, who have two head coaches, Morten Jensen and Bjarte Lunde Aarsheim, are joint top of the Norwegian top flight with Bodø/Glimt, with eight games remaining. They took the lead after 71 seconds when Gianni Stensness rose highest to head home a corner, before Peter Christiansen superbly slotted past Jonas Urbig on the break in the 38th minute. Kane’s brace, which pulled Bayern level, means he has 36 goals in 40 Champions League games since turning 30, taking him one clear of Lionel Messi’s record of 35 strikes in his thirties. The 33-year-old has scored in nine successive Champions League games – a feat only achieved by Ruud van Nistelrooy, Robert Lewandowski and Cristiano Ronaldo, who holds the record with 11 games. Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany said: “We were dominant, but at the moment it feels like every chance for the opposition leads to a goal. “It was our own fault. This red card was super dumb… you can see in (Michael’s) eyes that he’s sorry about it and that he regrets letting the team down.” Bayern host Arsenal on 21 October and will be without Olise after his sending-off, while Viking visit Aston Villa on the same night. Who are Viking? Viking’s players lined up and linked arms to celebrate with their fans at full-time This continues Viking’s impressive rise. Last season’s top-flight Norwegian title was their ninth, but their first in 34 years. They responded to a shock relegation in 2017, under English manager Ian Burchnall and with several British players in the team, by winning the second-tier title at the first time in 34 years under the stewardship of club legend Bjarne Berntsen. That was achieved by Viking, who play on an artificial pitch in Stavanger, realising they needed to “go back to their roots”, podcaster Lars Risan told BBC Radio 5 Live last year. Bernsten followed that up with a domestic cup victory in 2019, but was surprisingly sacked after finishing sixth in the Covid-interrupted 2020 season. They turned to his assistants Aarsheim and Jensen, and they finished third in 2021 and 2024 before last season’s title success. Viking were knocked out of the UEFA Conference League in the third qualifying round by Turkish side İstanbul Basaksehir last season and had to overcome Croatian champions Dinamo Zagreb to qualify for the league phase of the Champions League. Their last involvement in the competition saw them defeated 1-0 on aggregate by Barcelona in the two-legged first round in 1992-93, while their only top-flight European Cup victory came against Czech Republic side Banik Ostrava in 1976-77. Perhaps their most famous European night was a 4-2 victory that helped them secure a 5-4 aggregate win over Chelsea in the UEFA Cup first round in 2002. Risan said “people were sceptical” when Aarsheim and Jensen were appointed, but added: “It seems like it just works for them even though people were laughing or asking questions. They figured out how they wanted to do it and stuck to it. They’re both from Stavanger and love the club.” After the trip to Villa, Viking have a home game against competition debutants Sabah before matches against Atletico Madrid, Feyenoord, PSV and Napoli.

title: Israel Returns 22 Ancient Artefacts to Greece in Historic First
body: Greece has received 22 antiquities that Israel recovered after their illegal removal from the country, marking the first time Israel has returned ancient artefacts to Greece and opening the way for closer cooperation against antiquities trafficking. Culture Minister Lina Mendoni received the objects from Israeli Ambassador Pninat Yanay during a handover ceremony in the Altar Hall of the National Archaeological Museum, attended by Amir Ganor, head of the Israel Antiquities Authority’s Unit for the Prevention of Antiquities Robbery. Israeli authorities located and seized the antiquities through the unit, which works to combat the illegal trade in cultural heritage. The collection comprises 15 Attic vases, six vessels from Corinthian workshops and a bronze statuette depicting a female figure. Of the Attic vases, 11 feature black-figure decoration, three feature red-figure decoration and one has a black-glazed finish. Experts date them to the Archaic and Classical periods. The six Corinthian vessels date to the Archaic period. Authorities say the bronze female statuette requires further investigation to establish its authenticity. Greece and Israel Strengthen Cooperation Against Antiquities Trafficking Mendoni described the return as a landmark in relations between the two countries and a starting point for closer cooperation to protect cultural heritage. “This is the first time Israel has returned antiquities to Greece, and it marks the beginning of closer cooperation between our two countries in protecting cultural heritage,” Mendoni said. She added that officials from both countries had already begun exchanging experience and good practices to prevent and combat the illegal trafficking of cultural objects. Mendoni said the return demonstrated how international cooperation could deliver tangible results in the fight against antiquities smuggling, which she described as a major crime. Yanay also highlighted the cultural significance of returning the artefacts, reflecting on how ancient objects can connect people across generations. She invited the audience to imagine a child looking at one of the vases today and experiencing a spark of wonder, much like a child might have felt 2,000 years ago. That connection, she suggested, restores a link in a chain of generations that had been broken. The ambassador said she felt deeply moved by the privilege of returning an ancient object to Greece and that Israel was honoured to contribute to the important mission of protecting cultural heritage. The post Israel Returns 22 Ancient Artefacts to Greece in Historic First appeared first on Greek City Times .

title: Anduril’s Palmer Luckey envisions missiles made in car factories, underground battles
body: During his “State of the Force” speech last week, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced Project Meridian , a 120-day effort to study and identify the weapons and battlefields of the future. Hegseth said the project was “not about developing new strategies or new policies,” but rather, “to creatively look to the future and identify the domains that we must conquer, and capabilities we must master.” Palmer Luckey , who is co-leading the workgroup alongside Elon Musk and Newt Gingrich, talked about his vision for the future of defense in an interview with the American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics days ahead of the speech. Luckey co-founded the defense technology company Anduril, which makes autonomous platforms like drones and submersibles. Before that, he founded virtual headset maker Oculus VR, which was acquired by Facebook in 2014. His two ideas would seemingly merge in the Army’s Integrated Visual Augmentation System , or IVAS. Sci-fi inspired tech Luckey explained that much of what he does in the defense space was inspired by science fiction movies like Stealth , which is about an autonomous fighter jet that goes rogue after becoming sentient, and classic science fiction novels that theorized how technology would evolve. “Turns out, everything we’re doing was predicted by guys who were really sharp [and] really knew what they were doing,” he said, referencing author Robert Heinlein as an example when he wrote about voice activation. “I love building the things that were invented by people who didn’t have to worry about how it was going to become real. They just knew it would be the right thing,” Luckey added. He went on to discuss a range of topics for keeping the U.S. wartime-ready, including developing trust in autonomous systems, open source versus patents for weapon designs, and balancing intuitive design with user skill, but he started with his thoughts on industrial manufacturing. Scaling the industrial base In response to the question of how the U.S. can regain battlefield dominance, Luckey talked about unified design and information sharing. “We need to have unified command and control. We need to have unified information sharing. You need to have every sensor be a sensor for every effector and vice versa. You can’t have these stove pipes across systems, across services, and especially across our ally and partner forces. We want everyone to be able to share everything,” he said. He added that he thinks everyone agrees with that notion, but he differs on how industry should be designed. “We need to design missiles that can be made in car factories. We need to design aircraft that can be made in tractor factories,” he said. “And we’ve done this before.” He argued that in World War II, military equipment was designed to be manufactured with commercial equipment and techniques. “We made weapons to be made by car and tractor and sewing machine factories, etcetera, and I think we need to start doing that again,” he said. He added that it would serve the practical purpose of meeting wartime demand while also sending a message to adversaries like China that U.S. factories could quickly switch gears and crank out weaponry. Subterranean fighting While it might seem obvious that future battlefields might be in space, Luckey listed “the subterranean domain” as a realistic option and “inevitable.” While the interpretation of “subterranean” is to mean fighting in tunnels or trenches, he said he’s literally talking about “the real deal no shit sub-T fight, where you are using the crust of the earth as a three-dimensional maneuver and battle space.” “Everyone says that I’m nuts for this and I’m going to keep saying it because it is true,” he said. “The U.S. used to believe this. The Soviets used to believe this. Both countries were working on subterrains, so vehicles that could move through the crust of the earth.” Why he thinks this is realistic, he argued, is that autonomous systems will make it easier to bore through subterranean environments, and the primary cost is moving forward. “Everything you drag through it afterwards is free,” he said. He added that the space could be used for battle or to launch attacks against enemies on the ground. According to Hegseth’s Project Meridian memo , the working group is expected to submit its findings and recommendations by Jan. 28, 2027.

title: Over 30 planes bound for Moscow diverted to other cities
body:
MOSCOW, October 14. /TASS/. More than 30 planes bound for Moscow have been diverted to other cities due to security restrictions at the capital’s airports, representatives of Moscow airports told TASS.
In particular, 19 aircraft have been unable to land at Vnukovo. Those include flights from Sharm El-Sheikh, Hurghada, Dubai, St. Petersburg, Astana, Baku, Pskov, Antalya, Istanbul, Dalaman, and Syktyvkar. According to the airport’s information service, they landed in Nizhny Novgorod, St. Petersburg, Minsk, Pskov, and Istanbul. Four flights bound for Domodedovo were diverted to Nizhny Novgorod and St. Petersburg. "Those are flights from Kaliningrad, Dushanbe, Baku, and Hurghada," the airport’s representatives explained. Twelve flights have so far been unable to arrive at Sheremetyevo, including those from Chelyabinsk, Saratov, Perm, Kazan, Mineralnye Vody, and Nizhnekamsk, according to the information desk and online flight boards.
Russia’s Federal Air Transport Agency (Rosaviatsiya) said earlier that temporary restrictions on the arrival and departure of aircraft required to ensure safety of flights had been imposed at all Moscow airports.

title: Pope Leo has lung cancer, the Vatican announces after surgery
body:
Pope Leo XIV arrives at the Agostino Gemelli Polyclinic in Rome, Tuesday, Oct. 13, 2026, where doctors operated to remove part of his lung. Alessandra Tarantino/AP hide caption
Pope Leo XIV had surgery on Tuesday to remove a cancerous growth in his lung, the Vatican announced.
The surgery, performed at Gemelli Hospital in Rome, involved removing the lower lobe of the Pope's right lung, according to a statement by Leo's doctors released by the church. Lung tissue examined after the surgery confirmed a previous test that revealed a diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma, the Vatican said.
Adenocarcinoma of the lung is the most common form of lung cancer in the United States, representing about 40% of all lung cancers, according to the Lung Cancer Foundation of America.
The Pope's surgery, which the doctors said was successful, lasted about 90 minutes, after which Leo awoke normally and, following a brief period of observation, returned to his room on the hospital's 10th floor.
At 71 years old, Leo is relatively young for a pope – and remains physically active. He works out weekly, including regular tennis matches with his personal secretary and enjoys riding horses at Castel Gandolfo, the papal retreat.
Leo has not been known to smoke, but there is a history of cancer in the pope's family. On Tuesday, the Vatican announced that Leo's older brother Louis, who lives in Florida, is currently hospitalized with a form of cancer. And Leo's mother, Mildred, died of cancer in 1990 at age 77. Back in 1984, while living in Rome, the future pope wrote to several friends saying, "my mother continues to undergo chemotherapy treatments. … She's a tough lady and handles it all well, which makes it a little easier for me being so far from Chicago."
The Vatican says the Pope has essentially cleared his public schedule for the next several days, until at least October 20. The Vatican has yet to announce any further treatments.

title: llm-gemini 0.35
body:
I added support to llm-gemini for the new Gemini 4 Argon model, made available today via the Gemini API and for customers of their $100/month subscription plan.
Here are the low, medium and high pelicans . As expected, they are all excellent: Gemini has a track record of producing great SVGs, and are the only lab where I know their staff have invested in SVG specifically (and who have boasted about their pelicans before.)
Here's the "high" illustration, which cost me 17.166 cents:
The pricing is interesting. At launch, Argon is $2/million input and $10/million output - the same price as GPT-6 Sol, half the price of Claude Opus 5.5 and 1/5th the price of Claude Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra.
But on December 1st Argon is set to double in price - so it will be the same price as Opus 5.5.
Prices like this aren't really comparable these days since what really matters is how many tokens a model takes to achieve a goal within an agentic harness.
One useful clue for that comes from Artificial Analysis, who publish the total cost to run their benchmark using each model. Argon is looking very good there - costing $2,407 to run the benchmark, putting it close to GLM-5.3 and significantly cheaper than OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta's latest models.
When the price doubles it will still be a little cheaper than GPT-6 Astra.
(I used ChatGPT to edit that chart ! The data is all correct, I checked - I needed to get that Gemini 4 Argon info box to display without overlapping the other numbers.)
Some bonus examples using Gemini 4 Argon: here's Generate an SVG of an armadillo in fishnet tights jaywalking on Mars , here's a Fabergé egg it created for me using Blender, and DeepMind staffer @fofrAI shared a video of a pelican riding a bike, using fourier epicycles . That's a fun new twist!
This is a beat by Simon Willison, posted on 13th October 2026 .
