title: Lozano: Army Giving Industry Another Shot To Offer IFPC Inc. 2 Second Interceptor, NGSRI Solutions
body:
A lead official confirmed Tuesday the Army plans to give industry another shot at proposing solutions for its effort to find a second interceptor for the Indirect Fire Protection Capability (IFPC) Increment 2 defeat system and its Stinger missile replacement program, both of which are currently in active competition.
Lt. Gen. Frank Lozano, program acquisition executive for fires, said the Army plans to conduct shoot-offs in late fiscal year 2027 for both initiatives, as it seeks additional solutions that could help get after fielding more rapidly.
On the IFPC Inc. 2 Second Interceptor competition, which just moved into the capability demonstration phase with Lockheed Martin [LMT] and a team of Boeing [BA] and Anduril , Lozano said the Army wanted to “turn up the heat on that program.”
“I constantly get frustrated when a funding profile emerges over the [five-year budget projection plan], and then magically we lay in a five-year program. I’m like, ‘No, I actually need that capability now,’ right? So, have we thought [about] maybe what if we ran a 24-month program or a 36-month program, right? And so, in that vein, what we have decided to do is, while those two companies continue to compete, we’re going to create a shoot-off opportunity in fourth quarter ‘ 27, and I want to run an in-parallel, what I call an in-strike, competition,” Lozano said during a discussion at the Association of the U.S. Army’s annual conference in Washington, D.C.
The current interceptor for IFPC Inc. 2, which uses Dynetics ’ [LDOS] Enduring Shield launcher platform, is RTX ’s [RTX] AIM-9X Sidewinder missile, but the Army has previously expressed interest in pursuing a second interceptor option to defeat supersonic cruise missiles and larger caliber rockets.
Lozano has said previously that for a second interceptor “what [he’s] been communicating is an AIM 120D-like capability in an AIM-9X package, because the key is magazine depth” ( Defense Daily , July 31, 2024).
The AIM-120D, better known as AMRAAM for Advanced Medium Range Air-to-Air Missile, has a longer range than the AIM-9X. AMRAAM is also built by RTX.
The Army held an industry day and has solicited information on potential additional second interceptor offerings, Lozano noted.
“We basically just said, ‘Hey, if there’s any other company who didn’t make the first cut in the phase one but, oh by the way, you continue to invest in an IFPC [Inc. 2] Second Interceptor capability, we’d love for you to come out to the range. We’ll give you range time. We’ll present targets. And we’ll allow you to recompete with an opportunity to get back into the program fold,” Lozano said. “That’s how focused and determined and hungrier we are to get that capability into the field.”
For the Army’s Stinger missile replacement program, dubbed Next Generation Short Range Interceptor (NGSRI), Lockheed Martin is currently competing against RTX, with both companies having conducted successful demonstrations of their offerings ( Defense Daily , July 15).
“We ran the same bread and butter play [with an] industry day, RFI. We’re going to do a fourth quarter ‘27 shoot off for any other industry vendors that want to get into the NGSRI program,” Lozano said.
A separate RFI from over the summer detailed the Army’s aim to build 11,000 NGSRI missiles over a ten-year period beginning in FY ‘28 ( Defense Daily , July 16).

title: Russian Missiles Hit Kyiv Power Plant, Killing 3, Injuring 26 – Zelensky Raises Alarm Over Missing Allied Warnings
body:
Russian ballistic missiles struck Kyiv’s CHP-4 power plant and a nine-story residential building late Tuesday, Oct. 13, killing at least three people and injuring 26, including an eight-year-old child, Ukrainian officials reported.
The missiles hit the capital at approximately 10:40 p.m., targeting one of Kyiv’s main energy facilities, according to President Volodymyr Zelensky.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Ukraine received no advance warning from its Western partners, he said, marking the second consecutive night that Russian ballistic missiles reached the capital without allied notification.
A Kyiv Post journalist recounted how a friend walking her dog on Kyiv’s left bank was caught off guard by the ballistic missile attack, with no advance warning.“The explosions were so loud that she [the dog] was terrified,” the journalist said.
In the Desnianskyi district, a missile struck a nine-story apartment building, igniting a fire that spread through apartments from the first to the eighth floors.
By 1:30 a.m. Wednesday, Oct. 14, rescue crews had recovered a second body from the damaged nine-story apartment building in Kyiv’s Desnianskyi district, Mayor Vitali Klitschko reported.
In a 7 a.m. update, the State Emergency Service (DSNS) confirmed that three people had been killed in Russian attacks on the capital. Emergency response operations were underway in several districts.
“At the site of the enemy strike on a high-rise building in the Desnianskyi district, firefighters extinguished a fire covering an area of 400 square meters (4,306 square feet). The number of casualties is rising as people continue to seek assistance. The bodies of two deceased individuals have been recovered,” the report said.
Prime Minister Serhiy Koretskyi reported on Telegram that the number of people injured in the evening strike on a high-rise building in Kyiv has risen to 25.
In the Holosiivskyi district, one person was killed and another injured after a non-residential building was struck.
In the Dniprovskyi district, a fire broke out in a disused building following a repeat attack. Meanwhile, firefighters extinguished a grass fire at a stadium in the Darnytskyi district.
In the Shevchenkivskyi district, a strike on a single-story disused building sparked a small fire, which was quickly extinguished.
Zelensky said the main target was CHP-4, one of the capital’s most important energy facilities, and confirmed that Russian missiles had hit the site.
“These missiles were detected by our system practically as they were approaching Kyiv,” he said.
The Ukrainian Air Force confirmed that no advance warning had been received through the usual channels from international partners.
Presidential adviser Dmytro Lytvyn said the lack of notifications had occurred on two consecutive nights, adding that military and intelligence services were investigating the reasons.
The previous evening, Oct. 12, Russia launched five ballistic missiles that struck civilian infrastructure in Kyiv, according to Zelensky. Explosions were heard before the air raid alert was issued.
The absence of warnings has raised renewed questions about the intelligence-sharing arrangements Ukraine relies on to detect incoming Russian ballistic missiles. Ukrainian officials have not established why the notifications were missing.
Zelensky said Ukrainian intelligence had obtained information indicating that Russian forces were preparing additional ballistic missile attacks.
He urged residents to remain vigilant overnight and throughout Wednesday, warning that the danger had not passed.
The president also criticized Moscow for continuing to strike Ukrainian energy infrastructure despite US President Donald Trump’s call for an energy ceasefire.
“Ukraine supported the energy ceasefire. Russia is targeting yet another power plant and the lives of our people,” Zelensky said.
He argued that Russia’s actions showed Moscow did not consider itself bound by Trump’s statements.
“It is important that the world does not remain silent about this,” he said, calling on Washington to recognize who was responsible for the war’s continuation.
Zelensky said Ukraine was working to replenish its air defense systems with interceptor missiles as Russia continued targeting critical infrastructure.
The latest assault came amid repeated Russian strikes on Ukrainian cities and energy facilities, increasing pressure on the country’s power infrastructure ahead of winter.
Deliberately targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure constitutes a war crime under international humanitarian law.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: The Ballot, The Breadline And The Battle For 2027
body: As Nigeria moves closer to the 2027 elections, three contests are unfolding simultaneously: a legal battle over who gets on the ballot, an economic argument over whether reforms are delivering relief, and a growing test of public confidence in the institutions that will oversee the vote. There is a curious contradiction at the heart of Nigerian politics today. The country is preparing for an election in which the candidates are increasingly visible, but the rules governing their participation are still being contested. The economy is showing signs of improvement, yet millions of households continue to struggle with the cost of everyday living. And while politicians are busy calculating their electoral fortunes, Nigerians are asking a rather more immediate question: when will things get better? These are not separate stories. They are becoming the defining issues of the 2027 election. And this Tuesday, the signals are getting clearer. The Ballot Before The Battle An election is supposed to offer voters a choice. But what happens when the argument over who qualifies to contest threatens to overshadow the contest itself? Today, the Federal High Court in Abuja fixed November 20 to rule on an application by Atiku Abubakar and the African Democratic Congress to amend their suit challenging President Bola Tinubu’s eligibility to participate in the 2027 presidential election. The case centres on allegations concerning the authenticity of the President’s National Youth Service Corps discharge certificate submitted in support of his nomination. Tinubu and the APC oppose the proposed amendment. The allegations remain contested, and the court has made no determination on their merits. The political significance extends beyond the courtroom. At a time when Nigerians should be comparing candidates’ programmes for the economy, security and national development, considerable attention is being directed towards legal eligibility. There is nothing inherently improper about challenging a nomination in court. Indeed, judicial scrutiny is an important safeguard in a constitutional democracy. But the increasing prominence of pre-election litigation raises a broader question: will the 2027 election be defined primarily by the choices voters make, or by the decisions courts must first resolve? That question becomes even more pressing when we turn to the Independent National Electoral Commission. INEC And The Credibility question The controversy surrounding INEC’s candidate lists is no longer confined to one state. In Gombe, former Communications Minister Isa Pantami and the PDP have given the commission until Wednesday, October 14, to include his name on the governorship candidates’ list, following a disputed nomination process and a court-ordered rerun. Pantami’s lawyers maintain that INEC has no authority to exclude him after the rerun. The commission has yet to publicly resolve the dispute. Meanwhile, in Edo State, two candidates have reportedly appeared on the final House of Assembly list under both the PDP and the Allied Peoples Movement. INEC’s state office has acknowledged the duplication and referred the matter to its headquarters. These are distinct disputes, with different legal and administrative circumstances. They should not be treated as evidence of a single coordinated problem. Nevertheless, together they underline the importance of accurate nomination records, timely corrections and transparent explanations. For INEC, credibility is not something that can be established only on election day. It begins with the register of voters, the nomination process, the publication of candidates’ names and the consistent application of electoral rules. Every unresolved dispute consumes time, invites litigation and potentially weakens public confidence. The commission must demonstrate not merely that it can conduct an election, but that it can administer the processes leading to it with transparency and consistency. The signal here is straightforward: confidence in the ballot begins long before the first vote is cast. The Economy: Good Numbers, Difficult Realities If the courtroom is shaping the legal contest, the economy is shaping the political conversation. The World Bank’s latest Nigeria Development Update offers the Tinubu administration grounds for optimism. According to the report, Nigeria’s economy grew by 4.2 per cent in the first half of 2026, compared with 3.9 per cent in the corresponding period last year. The Bank projects average annual growth of 4.4 per cent between 2026 and 2028, provided reforms continue and public service delivery improves. The Presidency has welcomed these findings as evidence that its economic reforms are producing results. But there is another side to the story. The Central Bank’s September survey showed business activity expanding for the fourth consecutive month, even as households expressed growing pessimism about their finances and economic conditions. There, in a single contrast, lies one of the central political questions of 2027. Can an economy be improving while the people living in it feel worse off? Of course it can. Economic recovery does not automatically translate into immediate improvements in purchasing power. And macroeconomic stability, however necessary, does not put food on the table unless its benefits reach households. The government can legitimately point to growth, improved fiscal conditions and the prospect of lower inflation. But voters will also be looking at food prices, transport fares, wages and the cost of running small businesses. The political debate, therefore, is moving beyond whether reforms are necessary to whether their benefits are sufficiently visible. Petrol, Wages And The Politics Of Relief The Federal Government’s temporary petrol discount has added another dimension to that debate. Under the arrangement announced last week, NNPC Retail is foregoing its profit margin for a limited period, with the government insisting that the intervention does not amount to restoring the petrol subsidy removed in 2023. The measure is intended to provide some relief from the sharp increase in international energy prices. Yet it has also raised difficult questions. If the intervention is temporary, what happens when it ends? Will lower pump prices translate into lower transport fares? And can relief at selected retail outlets meaningfully change the cost-of-living pressures facing households nationwide? These questions are especially relevant following the Nigeria Labour Congress’s two-week ultimatum, effective October 9, demanding lower petrol prices and negotiations over a new national minimum wage. Labour argues that the purchasing power of the current ₦70,000 minimum wage has been severely eroded. The government faces competing pressures: preserving fiscal discipline, maintaining market confidence and responding to immediate hardship. The opposition, meanwhile, has an opportunity to scrutinise the intervention’s effectiveness. But criticism alone is not an economic programme. Alternative proposals must also explain how relief would be financed and sustained. The deeper signal is that the economic argument is becoming less about the direction of reform and more about the distribution of its benefits. That distinction could become increasingly important as the campaign develops. Nigeria 2027 Election Watch: A crowded field, unresolved questions The publication of INEC’s final list of presidential candidates has brought greater clarity to the electoral field. Eighteen presidential candidates are listed, including President Tinubu of the APC, Atiku Abubakar of the ADC, Peter Obi of the Nigeria Democratic Congress and Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde of the Allied Peoples Movement. The emergence of these candidacies changes the focus of political analysis. It is no longer sufficient to speak generally about opposition unity or fragmentation. The relevant questions now concern actual candidates, party organisations, campaign programmes and the coalitions they are attempting to build. For the APC, the central task is to explain the administration’s record and the benefits it expects Nigerians to derive from its policies. For opposition parties, the challenge is to articulate credible alternatives on the economy, insecurity and governance while building effective electoral structures across the states And for voters, the task is to distinguish between campaign promises and proposals that can realistically be implemented. One constituency deserves particular attention: younger Nigerians. Youth participation cannot simply be measured by social media enthusiasm, large rallies or online criticism. The meaningful indicators will be voter registration, collection of permanent voter cards, turnout and the capacity of parties to engage young people beyond campaign events. The same applies to state-level contests. Governorship races, local party structures and the mobilisation of communities may reveal political dynamics that national campaign rhetoric cannot capture. As January approaches, the contest deserves to be examined not only through the personalities seeking office, but also through the policies, institutions and voters that will shape the outcome. Three developments deserve close attention over the coming days: Wednesday, October 14: INEC’s response to the Pantami ultimatum and whether the dispute moves further into litigation. October 23: The expiry of Labour’s two-week ultimatum and whether negotiations produce an agreement or lead to industrial action. November 20: The Federal High Court’s ruling on Atiku and the ADC’s application to amend their eligibility suit against Tinubu and the APC. Beyond these dates, the most important economic indicator may not be another growth projection, but evidence that inflation is easing in ways households can actually feel. There is an old temptation in politics to mistake activity for progress. A crowded courtroom is not necessarily evidence of a stronger democracy. A growing economy does not automatically mean rising living standards. And a crowded ballot paper does not, by itself, guarantee a meaningful electoral choice. Nigeria’s political institutions are approaching another important test. The courts must adjudicate disputes according to law. INEC must administer the electoral process transparently. Political parties must present credible alternatives. And those in government must demonstrate how economic progress can translate into tangible improvements in everyday life. For Nigerians, the questions are becoming increasingly practical. Will the electoral process be fair? Will the economy provide greater opportunity? Will communities become safer? And will the next government, whoever leads it, be accountable for the promises made during the campaign? These are the questions that deserve to dominate the road to 2027. Because elections are not simply contests between politicians. They are opportunities for citizens to determine the direction of their country. And perhaps that is today’s most important signal: Nigeria’s political future will be shaped not only by who appears on the ballot, but by the credibility of the process and the choices offered to the people. That’s The Signal for Tuesday, October 13, 2026. The post The Ballot, The Breadline And The Battle For 2027 appeared first on Channels Television .

title: US Ambassador Kimberly Guilfoyle Resigns Amid Allegations She Denies
body: US Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle resigns amid mounting allegations over her personal finances, leadership at the US Embassy in Athens and relationships with influential business figures, with fresh reporting raising questions about the circumstances surrounding her departure. The Daily Mail reports that Guilfoyle, 57, was asked to resign after US President Donald Trump expressed dissatisfaction with negative coverage of her lifestyle and conduct. The ambassador announced her departure while insisting the allegations against her were false. The latest report alleges that Guilfoyle approached several wealthy Greek businessmen in mid 2025 seeking a $250,000 loan to help pay for a luxury Mercedes G Wagon. Four sources described by the Daily Mail as Greek and US State Department insiders with direct knowledge of the matter claim the approaches took place as Guilfoyle was preparing to assume her diplomatic post. According to the newspaper, she did not receive the money she sought. The allegations add to scrutiny already surrounding the outgoing ambassador following a Wall Street Journal report about messages allegedly showing her seeking help from Republican donor Eric Deters to cover a $100,000 American Express bill. Guilfoyle’s lawyer has disputed the authenticity of the messages and denied wrongdoing. New Allegations Over Luxury Car Loan The Daily Mail reports that Guilfoyle approached wealthy Greek businessmen about financing the Mercedes G Wagon, with the alleged requests raising questions about her financial affairs before she took up the ambassadorship. The newspaper notes that the vehicle was not listed in her mandatory federal financial disclosure forms. However, the report identifies a separate declared liability for a boat advance valued between $100,000 and $250,000, with Azure Funding listed as the creditor. The distinction is important. The reported G Wagon loan requests have not been established as a formal debt, and the available material does not establish that Guilfoyle received the money. The allegations have emerged alongside questions about the financial disclosures and vetting of ambassadorial nominees. The earlier Wall Street Journal investigation examined messages allegedly showing Guilfoyle asking Deters to settle an American Express bill before her Senate confirmation hearing. The newspaper reported that the messages suggested she linked financial assistance with access to senior administration figures. Guilfoyle’s legal representative, Jesse Binnall, has challenged the authenticity of the messages. The dispute also involves claims about payments for public appearances, which Deters denies owing. Neither set of allegations should be treated as a finding of misconduct. State Department Investigation Under Scrutiny The new reporting follows earlier Daily Mail claims that the US State Department’s Office of Inspector General opened an investigation after complaints about Guilfoyle’s leadership and the alleged use of embassy resources and corporate hospitality. The newspaper says the investigation could attract renewed attention following her departure, as individuals with information may become more willing to come forward. The allegations reportedly include complaints about staff management, requests for complimentary hospitality and the handling of relationships with business figures. The Daily Mail also reports that Guilfoyle dismissed a veteran Greek economic adviser who had served several US ambassadors, leaving other embassy staff concerned about the loss of institutional experience. These claims have not been independently established in the material provided for this report. Guilfoyle has rejected the allegations in broad terms, declaring that she intends to defend her reputation. Reports of Diplomatic Isolation in Athens The controversy has also raised questions about Guilfoyle’s relationships with Greek officials and senior figures in Washington. According to the Daily Mail , Greek government officials were reluctant to meet Guilfoyle in the period before her departure. The newspaper further reports that she was excluded from a key one on one meeting between US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis during Rubio’s visit to Athens the previous week. The report also alleges that Alexandros Exarchou, chairman and group chief executive of AKTOR Group, was not permitted to attend an official state dinner associated with Rubio’s visit. The newspaper describes Exarchou as a key local ally of Guilfoyle and reports previous allegations that she promoted business interests connected to his construction and energy group. Those claims raise questions about the boundaries between diplomatic engagement and commercial interests. However, the available reporting does not establish that Guilfoyle improperly intervened on behalf of the company. The Daily Mail also describes a tense relationship between Guilfoyle and Rubio during the visit, despite the pair being photographed greeting each other warmly on the tarmac. These accounts are attributed to unnamed sources and have not been independently verified. Questions Over a Possible JD Vance Visit The report also says Guilfoyle had been telling contacts in Athens that US Vice President JD Vance would make an official state visit to Greece in February 2027. However, Vance’s team told the Daily Mail that it had no travel plans for 2027 to announce at that time. The newspaper reports that Vance had previously described questions about the allegations against Guilfoyle as hypothetical, while expressing dissatisfaction with the surrounding controversy. The reported disagreement over a possible visit adds another dimension to questions about the ambassador’s standing in Washington as her tenure came to an end. Guilfoyle Vows to Fight Allegations In her resignation statement on X, Guilfoyle presented her tenure as a success for the Trump administration’s energy, defence and economic agenda. She highlighted efforts to expand US liquefied natural gas exports to Europe, advance the Vertical Corridor energy route, strengthen defence cooperation with Greece and promote American investment in Southeast Europe. She also thanked Trump and Rubio for the opportunity to serve, praised the Greek people for their hospitality and reaffirmed her support for the administration’s America First agenda. Addressing the allegations, Guilfoyle wrote: “These allegations are false, and I intend to vigorously defend my name, my reputation, and my integrity.” She added that she would not allow the accusations to define her decades of public service. White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia confirmed that Guilfoyle had been asked to resign, according to the Daily Mail , while publicly describing her as a valuable member of the team and wishing her well. The resignation marks a significant turn for a diplomat whose appointment attracted attention because of her relationship with Donald Trump Jr., the president’s eldest son. The couple were previously engaged before he began a relationship with Bettina Anderson, whom he later married. Guilfoyle’s departure leaves questions about the status of the reported inspector general investigation, the outcome of the disputed financial allegations and the future of US diplomatic representation in Athens. For now, the claims against the former ambassador remain contested. Guilfoyle denies wrongdoing and says she intends to defend her name, while the reports about her finances, management and diplomatic relationships continue to draw scrutiny. The post US Ambassador Kimberly Guilfoyle Resigns Amid Allegations She Denies appeared first on Greek City Times .

title: Afrilition: Mental models, By Adéwálé Àjàdí
body:
Our world is a platform for our differences so we can disagree effectively and grow from it. Afrilition is the holding space for our differences to be the fertiliser for creating a sophisticated mental model for African civilisation, which is predicated on abundance, not scarcity.
The foundation of all systems is the mental model, and the work ahead of Africa that Afrilition raises will transform our future. Unfortunately, we in the African world function within the present global system in reaction to it and with wider acceptance of its current mental model. Based on history and cemented into our formal socialisation that we call education, we are indoctrinated into different forms of inferiority.
We accept a lot without critical review, but it is not just us; the wider world mostly also accepts that Westernisation is the surest and only route to modernisation. The depth of this mental model hides the Janus face of the system, which is White supremacist and based on the pseudoscience of race. It does not stand up to basic scrutiny by its own logical or empirical standards.
I have not practised law for a while, but yesterday I had reason to go to the Supreme Court of Nigeria to honour a friend and son who was being elevated to a senior role. I sat in the Foyer for hours, enduring the ceremony and the pomposity of performance. Intelligent people prancing as caricatures in European wigs and dressed for pageantry in 19th-century faux fashion. There were horsehair wigs – with the only missing thing being powdered faces. It exemplified the levels our elites have been reduced to.
On the other side, as speeches droned on for hours in their monotone, I fell asleep many times, hoping that I did not snore. My eyes fixed on the Statue of Lady Justice on the wall. She brought a smile to my face, telling me that hope is not lost. She stood black and dignified, resting on the wall, with what are Northern Nigerian features. She had her head wrap solid, holding the sword and scale with an elegant buba that just barely touched the scale.
Afrilition is a pathway to the place of confidence in our creativity, and to get here we must be honest enough to confront ourselves on the depth of our indoctrination into the current system, so that we can engage across the African world honestly and share understanding. Africa and its Diasporas are the most diverse breadth of humanity in the world.
The sword on the other side expressed the glamour of the abundance of her outfit. She seemed aware of the work that needed to be done to move even herself from an Africanised European symbol, as she stood on the Latin words beneath her feet with disdain. At least Lady Justice no longer borrows her robe. There was the crowd of well-wishers, many in the unique cultural refinements of their various people. A wonderful sight: the variety and diversity of ethnic excellence expressed in headgears and outfits from across the variety of people who are Nigerians. If there is a country in which people carry culture with dignity, it is in Nigeria, along with the contradictions of colonial mentality.
Afrilition is a pathway to the place of confidence in our creativity, and to get here we must be honest enough to confront ourselves on the depth of our indoctrination into the current system, so that we can engage across the African world honestly and share understanding. Africa and its Diasporas are the most diverse breadth of humanity in the world. The persistent calls for unity betray a lack of acceptance of our complexity and expose our failings. We need a maturing to understand that our disagreements are the engine of our growth. In our many perspectives, it is critical to recognise the diverse pathologies we must address. From colonial mentality, white supremacy, colourism, to exploitative capitalism, which are all diseases that are inevitable as a result of the systems we are all socialised into.
Afrilition is about how we can admit these challenges with vulnerability and honesty. For us to move beyond indictment and judgement towards a holding space for many perspectives. Understanding that building a Black identity and imbuing it with power is survival in the US, but it is not exactly the same in Ghana or Kenya.
They are not the problems of or for the ignorant, malevolent, or poorly educated people but the sea of mental architecture in which we were raised and continue to live. Despite resistance and reactions, especially when we are woke, the system remains pernicious and prevalent; it is not overcome by our individual victories but it adapts in ways to suck us back into other forms of reaction. Individually, we get sucked in, especially because we are embedded in the system that has become our lifeblood. From our schooling, where the languages are those of the colonisers and meanings are reduced to the dominant perspective.
Our success is defined by material acquisition, using the borrowed language of class and its performance as hierarchy for marriage, residence, or even basic social interactions. We champion being black as a global identity, ignoring that it is a faux pigmentation that reduces from the beautiful and complex humanity that we are. We are dragged into false Diaspora wars in which ethnicity and nationality are conflated for clicks, and identity is hastily constructed, rather than differences being engaged with curiosity.
Afrilition is about how we can admit these challenges with vulnerability and honesty. For us to move beyond indictment and judgement towards a holding space for many perspectives. Understanding that building a Black identity and imbuing it with power is survival in the US, but it is not exactly the same in Ghana or Kenya. Accepting that Xhosa, Zulu, Kikuyu, Hausa, Igbo, and Ndebele are not tribes but ethnic nationalities with systems based on mental models that still enforce withdrawals from emotional bank balances. Our world is a platform for our differences so we can disagree effectively and grow from it. Afrilition is the holding space for our differences to be the fertiliser for creating a sophisticated mental model for African civilisation, which is predicated on abundance, not scarcity.
Adéwálé Àjàdí , a lawyer, creative consultant and leadership expert, is author of the newly released Afrilition: 21st Century African Manifesto , and Omoluwabi 2.0: A Code of Transformation in 21st Century Nigeria .

title: Mining Week: Investors demand clear rules, stronger security
body: By Gabriel Ewepu ABUJA – Investors and key players in Nigeria’s mining sector have called for clearer regulations, improved security and stronger collaboration among government agencies to attract investment and unlock the country’s vast solid mineral resources. They made the call at the opening of the 11th Nigeria Mining Week in Abuja, identifying insecurity, regulatory conflicts, poor inter-agency coordination and inadequate infrastructure as major barriers to the growth of the sector. President of the Miners Association of Nigeria, Oba Ayandele Ayanleke, said insecurity along mining corridors and jurisdictional disputes between federal and subnational authorities were undermining operations and eroding investors’ confidence. Ayanleke urged the government to establish a clearer and more predictable regulatory framework, stressing that stronger partnerships between local and international stakeholders were critical to attracting capital, facilitating technology transfer, creating jobs and generating wealth. On a recent mining incident, he disclosed that the government had constituted an investigative panel, urging stakeholders to await the outcome of its findings. Meanwhile, the Country Manager, Segilola Resources Operating Limited, Austin Menegbo, said Nigeria must build on the achievements of its first large-scale commercial gold mine to establish a competitive and sustainable mining industry. Menegbo disclosed that Segilola produced 91,910 ounces of gold in 2025, with Nigerians accounting for 99 per cent of its workforce. According to him, the mine has demonstrated that responsible investment, technical expertise, effective regulation and sustained engagement with host communities can support globally competitive mining operations. He, however, identified regulatory uncertainty, illegal mining, insecurity, poor infrastructure and limited access to finance as challenges requiring urgent government intervention. He called for streamlined government approvals, predictable regulatory timelines and sustained engagement among operators, investors, host communities and other stakeholders to improve the sector’s investment climate. He also advocated the formalisation of artisanal and small-scale mining through safety training, improved access to finance, technical support and cooperative structures. He stressed that efforts to attract investment must go hand in hand with environmental protection, workers’ safety and responsible engagement with host communities. Similarly, Head of Mission of the Swedish Embassy in Nigeria, Ambassador Anna Westerholm, called for partnerships that prioritise local value addition, workplace safety, community welfare and transparency. Westerholm said Nigeria could leverage Sweden’s expertise in mining technology, automation, skills development and responsible mineral production to strengthen its mining industry. She noted that the long-term success of mining projects depended largely on their impact on host communities and the environment, adding that companies must earn public trust to operate sustainably. The Swedish envoy also underscored the importance of mineral traceability, saying the ability to verify the origin of minerals and the conditions under which they were produced would boost Nigeria’s competitiveness in international markets. She expressed Sweden’s readiness to deepen cooperation with Nigeria through technical assistance, trade and investment partnerships. Earlier, Partner and Mining Industry Leader at PwC Nigeria, Cyril Azobu, said the country must translate its abundant mineral resources and growing international interest into bankable projects and sustainable economic growth. He said achieving this would require a predictable investment environment, credible projects and partnerships capable of connecting local opportunities with international capital, technology and expertise. Azobu also called for a shift from exporting raw minerals to domestic processing and value addition, saying the move would enable Nigeria to retain more economic benefits from its mineral resources. He reaffirmed PwC Nigeria’s commitment to supporting the sector through technical expertise, regulatory guidance and engagement with industry stakeholders. The 11th Nigeria Mining Week is being held under the theme, ‘Unlocking Investment and Growth through Partnerships’. The post Mining Week: Investors demand clear rules, stronger security appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Participants in Bari discuss Ukrainian community safety and new cultural initiatives
body:
This was reported on the website of the Consulate General of Ukraine in Naples, according to Ukrinform.
The Consul General met with Bari Prefect Rossana Riflesso and briefed her on Russian attacks on Ukraine, which are resulting in the deaths of civilians and the destruction of hospitals, schools, and critical infrastructure. The parties also discussed cultural initiatives and opportunities for further cooperation.
In addition, Larysa Polishchuk held a meeting with Bari’s City Council President Annino Gargano. During the conversation, the parties raised the issue of the needs of the Ukrainian community, particularly its safety.
The Consul General also met with Bari Mayor Vito Leccese and thanked him for his support of Ukrainians and for the opportunity to provide on-site consular services at City Hall for Ukrainian citizens residing in the Puglia region.
Larysa Polishchuk spoke with representatives of the Ukrainian community and the association “Uniti per l’Ucraina.” They discussed ideas for joint cultural events for Ukrainians in Bari and prospects for further cooperation.
As reported by Ukrinform, a grand opening ceremony was held in Cluj-Napoca (Romania) for the Honorary Consulate of Ukraine, headed by Vasyl Ruskovan, a Romanian citizen of Ukrainian descent.
Photo: Consulate General of Ukraine in Naples

title: J7 global task force convenes in London to discuss combating global antisemitism
body: Leaders of the J7 Large Communities' Task Force Against Antisemitism gathered in London on Monday for a multi-day summit of international consultations focused on countering rising global antisemitism, before extending their mission to Ireland on Tuesday.The J7 coalition comprises major Jewish community organizations from the United States, the United Kingdom, Canada, France, Germany, Australia, and Argentina. Formed in response to soaring rates of antisemitic incidents worldwide, the task force unites these Diaspora organizations to coordinate policy strategies, tech policy, security initiatives, and educational approaches against Jew hatred.The multi-day summit comes as the J7's latest annual report found that 2025 was the deadliest year for Jews living outside Israel since 1994, with the UK among the countries that recorded an increase in antisemitic incidents.Statement following meeting between the J7 Task Force Against Antisemitism and the UK Foreign Secretary. https://t.co/zE0jdXuJvr— Board of Deputies of British Jews (@BoardofDeputies) October 12, 2026As part of the summit, delegates met with British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband in London on Monday to press UK officials regarding government stances under new leader Andy Burnham.The group expressed serious concern about recent UK Government measures and rhetoric targeting Israel and the detrimental impact this decision had on their own countries and communities.Sharp rise in global antisemitism, Iranian regime threat, proliferation of hateRepresentatives discussed the sharp rise in global antisemitism, the threat posed by the Iranian regime and its proxies, the growing proliferation of online hate, and the continued demonization of Israel, including in rhetoric, from many of those in elected office and public life, which all too often serves as a vehicle for antisemitic rhetoric, incitement, and behavior.The J7 welcomed Miliband's expression of the “abhorrence” of the motion against Zionism at the recent Green Party conference and his affirmation of the importance of the IHRA definition of antisemitism.During the meeting, J7 leaders also proposed a new international ministerial task force on antisemitism and welcomed Miliband's agreement to host an inaugural meeting.Antisemitism has no place in our society. This morning, I hosted a crucial discussion with the J7 Global Task Force to discuss how we can work together across countries to stamp out the scourge of antisemitism. https://t.co/67XbJJl01C— Ed Miliband (@Ed_Miliband) October 12, 2026ADL CEO and National Director Jonathan Greenblatt said, “We had a direct and productive conversation with Foreign Secretary Miliband. While there are areas of strong disagreement, we identified some common concerns, including our shared view on the bigoted anti-Zionism of the Green Party; the need to curb the wave of vicious harassment and hostile rhetoric directed at the British Jewish community; and the necessity of mitigating the expanding threat of online antisemitism enabled by AI and social media. But this was just the first conversation. We intend to keep pushing for action and demanding accountability.”Following the meeting, Miliband said in a statement, “Antisemitism has no place in our society. Jewish communities must be able to live freely and safely, without fear of discrimination, abuse, or violence. The rise in antisemitic incidents across a number of countries demands a coordinated international response. Today's discussion helped identify practical ways that governments, communities and international partners can work together to tackle antisemitism and share what works.”As the summit began on Monday, UK Interior Minister Shabana Mahmood announced in Parliament a public inquiry into the murders of two men, Adrian Daulby and Melvin Cravitz, killed in a terror attack carried out by Jihad Al-Shamie at the Heaton Park Synagogue in Manchester on Yom Kippur in October 2025.Continuing their mission on Tuesday, the task force traveled to Ireland and gathered in Dublin's Herzog Park to stand in solidarity with the local Jewish community and raise concerns over rising antisemitic rhetoric and actions in the country.Named in 1995 in honor of Israel's sixth president Chaim Herzog, the son of Rabbi Yitzhak HaLevi Herzog, a former chief rabbi of Ireland (1921-1936), the park was the center of a heated national controversy in late November and December 2025, when a city council push to strip away Herzog's name sparked opposition before being suspended and shelved.'No Jew... should ever feel they must choose between being proudly Irish and proudly Jewish'Addressing the gathering, Maurice Cohen, chairman of the Jewish Representative Council of Ireland, spoke about the historic vulnerability and resilience of the local community, telling the delegates, “We are a small community of just 2,200 people, but our roots in Ireland stretch back centuries. I can think of no more fitting place to welcome you than Herzog Park... The attempt to remove his name was deeply hurtful to our community and is typical of the ubiquitous, ambient antisemitism that reflects a growing hostility that Irish Jews increasingly encounter. No Jew in Ireland should ever feel they must choose between being proudly Irish and proudly Jewish.”Cohen noted that between “July 2025 and January 2026, we recorded 143 antisemitic incidents, a deeply troubling number for a community of our size. We are grateful for the increased attention of An Garda Síochána, but we need more than expressions of concern. We need practical security measures, political leadership, and a clear recognition that antisemitism, whatever language it is dressed in, has no place in Irish society. We are not asking for special treatment.”Delivering a statement on behalf of the J7, Jonathan Greenblatt told the delegates, “Today, we stand in solidarity with Ireland's Jewish community and sound the alarm about antisemitic rhetoric and actions here in Ireland, before they escalate further.Antisemitism has no place in our society. This morning, I hosted a crucial discussion with the J7 Global Task Force to discuss how we can work together across countries to stamp out the scourge of antisemitism. https://t.co/67XbJJl01C— Ed Miliband (@Ed_Miliband) October 12, 2026As Maurice mentioned, of all the places we visited today, we chose to gather here in Herzog Park... Last year, a campaign to strip his name from this park was rightly condemned by Irish government leaders as an act that transcends political debate and instead targets Jewish memory itself.”Greenblatt noted that although Ireland is not a J7 member country, the task force included a special chapter on Ireland in its latest annual report using data from the Jewish Representative Council of Ireland.“Anti-Israel rhetoric in Ireland is creating an increasingly hostile environment for Ireland's Jews, directly affecting the safety and daily lives of this small, historic Jewish community,” Greenblatt said.“While Ireland's national police have certainly increased their surveillance and security presence, there remains an urgent need for dedicated security funding for the Jewish community. Ireland cannot afford to wait for a tragedy before taking action. We are calling on the Irish Government to introduce concrete, preventative measures now. That means dedicated security funding for Jewish communal and educational institutions, consistent enforcement of hate crime legislation, and clear political accountability when rhetoric demonizes Jews or crosses the line into antisemitism,” Greenblatt said.The J7 met with Irish Taoiseach, Micheal Martin, and Secretary General of the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade, Joe Hackett.The J7 said in a statement, “We've seen in our own countries how an increasingly hostile environment for Jews can lead to deadly violence, as we witnessed in Bondi, Manchester, Boulder and Washington D.C. The demonization of Israel generates and fuels the surge in antisemitism in Ireland and beyond.”“We warned the Taoiseach and the Secretary General that the conditions for an antisemitic terrorist attack are sadly all too evident in Ireland, and Ireland cannot afford to wait for a tragedy before acting,” the J7 said.The task force also met on Monday with the Union of Jewish Students in London as well as the Community Security Trust – which provides advice, training, representation, security services, and research to the UK's Jewish Community – and will be meeting with government and Jewish leaders in the coming days.

title: York Space Systems to Support Space Force’s SDN
body:
York Space Systems [YSS] has received two task orders to support the U.S. Space Force's Space Data Network (SDN), a future network of low Earth orbit military communications satellites, the company said on Tuesday. The task orders "support development and demonstration activities intended to advance multi-vendor interoperability and Space Exchange Point (SEP) integration planning," according to York. title: OpenAI employee accused of planting recording device in office
body: An OpenAI employee suspected of secretly planting a recording device in one of the company's conference rooms has been arrested on criminal charges, the Justice Department said Tuesday.Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, a Saudi national, was arrested Friday and made his initial appearance in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California on Tuesday. Alfozan was charged with trying to use an electronic, mechanical, or other device to intercept oral communications.Prosecutors said that Alfozan had worked at OpenAI as an engineer since July 2025. On Sept. 30, the company's employees discovered the audio recording device inserted into a USB port on the back of a television inside an executive conference room. The company later determined that the recording device had been concealed in toilet paper and installed about two days before it was discovered. The meeting room where it was hidden was often used by OpenAI's employees to discuss highly confidential and proprietary matters, including research, product plans and business development, the Justice Department said.In a statement, OpenAI said that after discovering the device, it contacted the FBI and has terminated the employee accused of planting it."The FBI's investigation is ongoing and we will continue to support their work. At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data," the company said. "We take protecting our technology, data, and people seriously, and as a matter of national importance. Our security program is designed to protect against a wide range of threat actors, from insider risks to cybercriminals to nation states, and this case is an example of how AI can help address these sophisticated security threats."FBI Director Kash Patel said in a post on X that the FBI and its partners had carried out the arrest and that the investigation is ongoing.Alfozan's attorney, William Pernik, noted to CBS News that his client is presumed innocent, and cautioned against "jumping to conclusions at this very early stage of the case when very little information is known," or seeking to "politicize" a prosecution based on factors like nationality.The criminal complaint, made public on Tuesday, alleged that Alfozan used a productivity tool to make inquiries about OpenAI's building addresses, meeting rooms, meeting-room capacities and calendars, and locations of "leadership and exec" and external partner meetings. Other evidence gathered in the investigation, meanwhile, showed that a chatbot account associated with Alfozan's spouse had also submitted prompts between Sept. 24 and Sept. 30, related to building, customizing, installing, audio recording, testing, obfuscating and remote accessing a continuous audio recording device.A photograph included in the complaint also shows that Alfozan entered the conference room where the device was hidden on Oct. 5 and looked behind the television.That same day, the complaint says Alfozan left his bag unattended in another room, and the company's security personnel opened it and found his ID, wallet and another recording device similar to the one planted in the conference room.Alfozan is due to appear in federal court again on Oct. 19 for a detention hearing.

title: Lockheed Official Says New PAC-3 ACE ‘Could Be’ Solution For Army’s Low-Cost Interceptor
body:
Lockheed Martin ’s [LMT] newly-announced PAC-3 Adapted Capability Effector (PAC-3 ACE) “could be a solution” for the Army’s Low-Cost Interceptor (LCI) effort, a company official said Tuesday.
While Lockheed Martin is not currently part of the initial LCI competition, Paula Hartley, vice president of strategy and business development for missiles and fire control, noted the company would look at getting involved in Army’s plan to run another iteration next year.
“We’ve been in conversation with the U.S. government on our offering,” Hartley said during a briefing at the Association of the U.S. Army’s annual conference in Washington, D.C.
Lockheed Martin announced its new PAC-3 ACE in July, which it said is “less than half the cost” of the current PAC-3 MSE interceptor per unit and is designed to defeat “airbreathing threats, cruise missiles, close-range and short-range ballistic missiles” ( Defense Daily , July 20).
Hartley reiterated that Lockheed Martin plans to begin flight testing PAC-3 ACE in 2027 and that it could be ready for operational use “about 30 months from now.”
“It’s still very capable against a wide variety of threat sets. And it’s still interchangeable, from a launch perspective, with [PAC-3] MSE,” Hartley said.
The Army began accepting industry’s proposals for its LCI competition in July, seeking pitches for cheap rounds along with individual components, such as rocket motors, seekers and fire control and flight guidance capabilities ( Defense Daily , July 9).
A Request for Information notice published in May detailed the Army’s interest in all-up rounds that can integrate with the M903 launch station and the Northrop Grumman [NOC]-built Integrated Battle Command System (IBCS), with an aim for a total cost of less than $1 million per round.
A PAC-3 MSE interceptor is currently estimated to cost between $4 million-$5 million per unit.
The Army recently announced the initial 30 finalists for its LCI competition and selected the following companies to demonstrate their all-up round offerings in October and November to inform awards in December: Aerovironment [AVAV], Anduril and RTX [RTX] along with Aeon Industries , AirX Robotics , Furientis , Greenjets , QinetiQ , UDD Tech Corporation and Wardstone ( Defense Daily , Oct. 1).
Lt. Gen. Frank Lozano, program acquisition executive for fires, told reporters in September that the service will give industry “multiple bites at the apple” to compete for LCI beyond the upcoming initial demonstration and award effort, with additional shoot-off opportunities planned for late fiscal year ‘27 and FY ‘28 for those who may need time to continue developing their solutions ( Defense Daily , Sept. 10).

title: Panathinaikos Crushes Partizan 72-55 to Make It Five Straight
body: Panathinaikos extends its perfect EuroLeague start to five wins after dismantling Partizan 72-55 in Belgrade, delivering a defensive masterclass despite missing key guards Kendrick Nunn and Kostas Sloukas. The Greens produced their most convincing defensive performance of the season so far on Tuesday, October 13, restricting Partizan to just 55 points and taking control with a dominant third quarter. The victory gives Panathinaikos a 5-0 record after four earlier wins built on high scoring. This time, however, Ergin Ataman’s team showed it could prevail without relying on its usual offensive firepower. EuroLeague result: Partizan 55-72 Panathinaikos Quarter scores: 16-16, 12-19, 8-20, 19-17 Panathinaikos Breaks Partizan After Half Time The contest began evenly, with both sides scoring 16 points in the opening quarter as Partizan looked to use its home advantage. Panathinaikos gradually found its rhythm in the second period. Nigel Hayes-Davis delivered crucial offensive contributions, including two consecutive three pointers late in the half, helping the visitors establish a 35-28 lead. The decisive blow came after the break. Panathinaikos held Partizan to just eight points in the third quarter while scoring 20 of its own. The defensive pressure disrupted the Serbian side’s offence and pushed the Greek champions into a commanding 55-36 lead heading into the final period. Partizan outscored Panathinaikos 19-17 in the fourth, but the damage had already been done. Defence Delivers the Victory Partizan struggled badly from beyond the arc, converting just four of 24 three point attempts, a shooting percentage of 16.7 per cent. Karlik Jones managed only eight points on two of 11 shooting as Panathinaikos repeatedly disrupted the hosts’ offensive rhythm. The Greens also won the rebounding battle 38-35, demonstrating their ability to compete physically on a difficult away court. Mathias Lessort made an impact beyond scoring, collecting nine rebounds, four assists and three steals despite finishing with only four points. His performance highlighted the collective effort behind the victory. Panathinaikos did not need one player to dominate offensively because contributions across the roster helped control the game. Hayes-Davis Leads a Balanced Attack Hayes-Davis led Panathinaikos with 14 points, while Juancho Hernangomez added 10. Brancou Badio contributed nine points, Sylvain Francisco finished with eight points and five assists, and Guerschon Yabusele recorded seven points, five rebounds and three assists. The spread of contributions proved particularly valuable with Nunn and Sloukas unavailable. Partizan also missed Isaac Bonga, who was sidelined with a wrist injury. Panathinaikos demonstrated that its depth can help it navigate difficult fixtures even when key players are absent. The longer term challenge will be integrating everyone into a consistent rotation once the squad is fully available. Five Wins, Different Ways to Dominate Panathinaikos entered the Belgrade contest after victories over Paris Basketball, ASVEL, Maccabi Tel Aviv and Fenerbahce. Those four wins produced at least 90 points each. Against Partizan, the Greens scored only 72, but their defensive performance proved decisive. Across their opening five games, Panathinaikos has scored 447 points and conceded 347, averaging 89.4 points scored and 69.4 conceded per game. The numbers underline the strength of the start, although five games are not enough to establish how the team will perform across the full EuroLeague season. The important development is the ability to adapt. When the offence flows, Panathinaikos can overwhelm opponents with scoring. When shots are harder to find, the team has now shown it can lean on defence, rebounding and collective discipline. Obradovic Returns to Belgrade for a Statement Win The game also carried significance for head coach Zeljko Obradovic, who returned to Belgrade to face a Partizan club with which he has deep ties. The result was particularly notable given Panathinaikos’ previous struggles in Belgrade. title: Topgolf saved over $11.3 million after leaving VMware
body: Topgolf’s VMware costs were going to increase by 400 percent under Broadcom. To avoid that cost, the sports entertainment company moved 12,000 virtual machines (VMs) to VergeIO’s VergeOS and has saved over $11 million so far. Before migrating, Topgolf’s VMware connection “ran very deep,” Scott Forehand, Topgolf’s global infrastructure manager, told Ars Technica. Topgolf has over 100 locations worldwide featuring interactive golf games with real-time shot tracking and digital analytics. The company used vSphere and ESXi for decades and started using VxRail, the hyperconverged infrastructure (HCI) platform that VMware co-engineered with Dell, in 2017. Topgolf employees previously participated in numerous VMware customer councils and have been interviewed for books on how Topgolf used vSphere and Horizon (now Omnissa Horizon), per Forehand, who is a leader of the Dallas/Ft. Worth VMware User Group . Read full article Comments

title: Tinubu can’t handle insecurity: Why does he want another term?, By Ugoji Egbujo
body:
A nation that conscripts its graduates cannot lose them on a federal highway, allow exchange of ransom, and call the aftermath a rescue.
A few days ago, thirty prospective corps members left Oyo for the East. Twenty were taken near Owerri, on the Owerri–Onitsha road at Umunoha. Ten escaped. The local people who witnessed the abduction could not stand the apathy of the security agencies, so they blocked the road to force a chase. The situation borders on hopeless.
When the police woke from their slumber, they announced that their drones had located the hostages and their abductors. The impression sold to the public was that they had them surrounded. Perhaps the corps members would be luckier than the Chibok girls, who were taken away without the government knowing which way the terrorists went with them. The Owerri police said they could not immediately exrract the hostages because the area was mined. The story did not instill any hope. The nation listened with resignation.
Youth corps members are supposed to be the babies of the federal government. The government cannot conscript youths into a compulsory national service in far-flung places and fail to protecr them. The mass abduction of citizens, let alone corps members, should provoke any responsible government. But perhaps not a government that cares more about optics than substance, about politics and retaining power than purposeful leadership. The real tragedy is that the government has lost sense of shame .
A few days after the kidnap, the government announced triumphantly that it had rescued the corps members, crediting the rescue to the joint security team and emphasising that no ransom was paid. While the government was basking in glory, pictures emerged of the abducted, frazzled corps members moving furtively on a village street, all alone. Could they have been rescued and allowed to walk bush paths?
The parents then went on television. They had scraped, borrowed, and paid. The demand opened at ₦50 million a head and was bargained down to about ₦5 million or ₦6 million, some of it in dollars. The government that said it was watching captives and captors by drone had not noticed the families negotiating, gathering the money, and flying to Owerri to deliver it. It had not seen the captives leave. The Imo commissioner of police says he is not aware of any ransom. Claiming a rescue while the people who paid are on television is worse than silence. It is complicity.
Orire followed the same script. Only with a worse ending. Forty-four pupils and teachers were taken from Oriire in Oyo on 15 May and held for fifty-six days. The presidency said security forces rescued them, arrested eight, killed some, and paid no ransom. A surviving teacher, Zaccheaus Olatunde, told a different story. Two teachers were killed . Sone negotiatipn happened. No fighting took place. The survivors were shown the way home. No public accounting has yet matched the official version to a captured camp. Yet another ‘miraculous’ release passed off as military rescue .
The terrorists who carried out the Oriire abduction are not ghosts. The Oyo government insinuated as much. In the case of Owerri, two species of bandits operate in the neighbourhood where the kidnapping happened. Unknown gunmen have a camp and control the left side heading into Owerri, while rogue Fulani herdsmen operate in the forest on the right side. The security agencies are aware of the presence and identity of these groups. The Governor of Zamafara said the same thing. That was why the local people at Uumnoha went irate when the corps members were abducted and the agencies hesitated to give an immediate chase. What exactly is Tinubu’s strategy against the rampaging insecurity?
What, then, is the strategy? Mass kidnapping is now followed by a release, and the release is claimed as a rescue. The exchanges are mediated by ransoms. Kidnappers keep the money and the camp. Security agencies have not learned hostage work, and the public is asked to applaud a story the payers have already contradicted. A trade conducted on those terms can only fatten the crime. Ransom is not rescue. The scourge is festering.
Recently it was reported that NNPC booked ₦11.2 trillion as receivables from the federation for advances and the cost of protecting oil and gas assets. We pay local mercenaries and shadowy folks ungodly sums to do the basic work of the police and the military, which are massively underequipped and miserably understaffed. Why have we made being an outlaw so rewarding? Why is the nation-state so weak? We cant live by random ransoms.
Tinubu’s first tenure has been marred by insecurity. But Tinubu wants a second term even though he has no clue how to tackle it. Nothing in the first term shows a strategy. Mass abduction, a week of tales, a release, a denial of ransom, no convictions: that is the operating model.
Tinubu met this model. He has not broken it. The South-East unknown gunmen and north-west bands are known to local security agencies. But they are not cleared. The police are too thin for the territory. The army is spread across internal duties it was not built for. The pipelines are hired out to mercanaries who are paid hundreds of billions and who it appears are helping the reelection effort. What new idea has Tinubu got?
Tinubu wants a second term anyway. Nothing in the first has shown a plan that would make the second different. Kidnappers cannot keep walking away with the ransoms while the government blows its trumpets. What, exactly, would he come back to do?

title: Royal Mail losing 400 postal workers a week, says union
body: About 400 postmen and women are leaving Royal Mail each week, according to the Communication Workers Union (CWU), which claims the number has risen since the company introduced a new delivery system earlier this year. The CWU says the firm had been losing about 330 postal staff a week from a workforce of 83,000 before it rolled out DM26, which reorganised routes to improve delivery performance. The union claims the new system is not working in hundreds of offices, and BBC Your Voice has heard from staff warning of a “nightmare” Christmas ahead as the number of parcels increases. Royal Mail says the reforms are part of its plan to deliver a more “efficient and financially sustainable” service. Over the last year, we’ve been in touch with more than 30 postal staff across all four nations of the UK as they have switched to DM26. It allows second-class post to be delivered only every other weekday and is supposed to guarantee that first-class mail and parcels are delivered every day by grouping workers into teams of three and changing the walking patterns of their rounds. But posties speaking to us anonymously say that parcels are still being prioritised, letters are being left behind, and time is being wasted sorting and dividing mail into first and second class. “I didn’t take any first class mail out on my last shift because I was on a road that’s been behind for weeks,” a worker in the West Midlands told me. “But I’m sure a manager would have ticked a box to say all first class mail went out.” A Royal Mail spokesperson said the company always worked to ensure all mail, both letters and parcels, was delivered on time. Some postal workers we’ve spoken to say the new model is also increasing their workload. We asked eight workers in different areas to track their average step counts. Since the switchover all their steps increased by a quarter or even a third, often up to around 25,000 steps a day. Several fear this Christmas will be a “nightmare”. “We all think this Christmas will be the worst ever, for us and our customers,” said one postman in the East Midlands. Bryn Dymott says he is speaking out now because he wants people to know what’s really happening Bryn Dymott delivered post in the village of Wootton in Bedfordshire for nine years. For the most part he loved the job. But he left the company in July saying he couldn’t face another “shambolic” Christmas. “People put things in the post for them to be delivered, not for them to be delayed because Royal Mail hasn’t got the systems in place and enough people to get them delivered.” Bryn says he wanted to speak out after leaving the company because he was sick of the fact that posties aren’t able to say what’s really happening. He says the company is “proving it’s impossible to have four people’s work done by three people. It shouldn’t really come as a surprise.” ‘A boat taking on water’ So far DM26 has been introduced in about 1,000 of Royal Mail’s 1,200 delivery offices. Now the CWU has told its members to pause further roll-out of the new system until a plan can be agreed with Royal Mail to address problems. The union says that while it is operating successfully in around 500 offices, it has run into significant problems in hundreds of others. “Put simply, if a boat is already taking on water, adding more passengers is unlikely to solve the problem,” says Martin Walsh of the CWU. The union said most Royal Mail workers leaving the company were believed to be new starters on part-time contracts, but also said there had been an increase in staff on legacy contracts departing. Royal Mail, on the other hand, says the new system is on track to be up and running in all offices by Christmas. It says the roll-out is 90% complete and that it is now delivering to “95% of addresses every day across the UK, up from 88% before the roll-out. The roll-out continues across our network, and we expect quality of service to improve as deployment progresses.” The company says it is hiring, as usual, an additional 22,000 temporary workers over the Christmas period. The BBC saw returned post that couldn’t be delivered so ended up back on the frames in a Royal Mail office Royal Mail has battled with increased competition and falling demand for letter deliveries in recent years, and last week announced plans to cut 2,500 head office and other supporting roles by the end of 2027. The company has also faced years of criticism from politicians and the public over slow letter deliveries – something which has continued since the new system has been rolled out. The regulator Ofcom has fined Royal Mail more than £37m in the last three years for missing delivery targets. But some MPs think it is time for a new approach, and a group of them will meet the regulator later on Wednesday. “We need to think outside the box,” Dave Robertson, Labour MP for Lichfield, Burntwood and the Villages in Staffordshire. “We need to bring as many people to the table on this to make sure we come up with a long-term solution because what’s been tried up to now clearly isn’t working.” An Ofcom spokesperson said not only has it issued fines to Royal Mail in recent years but it has also demanded an improvement plan and reformed the obligations imposed on the company, adding: “We will continue to hold it to account using the full extent of the powers available to us.” Postal Services Minister Kate Dearden said Royal Mail’s improvement plan was “a step in the right direction, but it must deliver tangible improvements for customers. We will continue to hold them to account on their performance.”

title: Changes to prescribing safer supply drugs approved by Ontario medical regulator
body:
Ontario’s medical regulator approved significant changes Tuesday to the way doctors prescribe safer supply drugs, in an effort to reduce the amount of opioids making their way to the streets.
The College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario’s board of directors will soon implement several changes to the practice of prescribing safer supply, which are medications given to people at high risk of overdose as an alternative to illicit opioids.
The board met Tuesday and passed a motion to enact the changes following a discussion on the proposals.
The college will make it mandatory for physicians to prescribe safer supply medications only in conjunction with opioid agonist therapy. The therapy uses medications such as Suboxone and methadone to treat opioid addiction.
“We are just here to protect the public and we’re here to ensure that the public is safe,” said Dr. Patrick Safieh, the board’s chair, near the end of the meeting.
“So we’re trying to prevent diversion as much as possible and at the same time, ensuring that those that do require safer supply are taking (opioid agonist therapy) so that eventually no one is on this and needs this, that’s the purpose.”
The most common form of safer supply is hydromorphone, a powerful opioid often prescribed for pain but significantly less potent than fentanyl and its derivatives that dominate the illicit drug supply chain.
Patients will now have to take the safer supply medications in front of health-care professionals, rather than take the pills home.
The college will not go ahead with an eight-week time limit for physicians to prescribe safer supply to patients it had previously considered.
Police forces in Ontario have said that diversion of patients’ prescription hydromorphone to the black market is occurring, Safieh said.
The board heard from Dr. Anil Chopra, the college’s associate registrar, who said they have also received information from governments, Addiction Medicine Canada, the addictions section of the Ontario Medical Association and from public health officers that diversion of hydromorphone to the streets is occurring.
Chopra, Safieh and others agreed there is no data available to properly quantify where the hydromorphone on the street is coming from, but said at least part of it is from safer supply prescriptions.
Board member Peter Wiesner said he was concerned that the policy will not work for everyone, citing information sent in by the Ontario Drug Policy Research Network that shows more than 87 per cent of patients on safer supply are also on opioid agonist therapy.
“But what about the 12 per cent that it doesn’t work for?” he asked.
“We need to find, I think, some exemptions for the 12 per cent.”
He said the new policy will have an outsized effect on those living in rural Ontario who are not close to a pharmacy. Another concern he raised are for those people who are employed who are using safer supply drugs. Those people may have difficulties getting to a pharmacy every day to take their medicine if they are not allowed to take some home with them.
Safieh said the college will monitor the changes and make adjustments down the road if necessary.
The office of Health Minister Sylvia Jones has previously said she supports the changes.

title: Pope Leo has cancerous growth removed in lung operation
body: Pope Leo XIV had a cancerous growth removed from his right lung in a 90-minute operation on Tuesday and “woke up normally” after the procedure, the Vatican said. A Vatican source said further tests were being carried out to determine if the cancer had spread. “To ensure the procedure was radical, the lower lobe of the right lung was removed,” the Vatican said in a statement. The operation “confirmed the diagnosis of a pulmonary adenocarcinoma, as suspected from the pre-operative tests”, it said. The pope was in the operating room for a total of three hours and the operation lasted half that time. “The surgery was successful and there were no complications,” the Vatican said. A Vatican source said he requested dinner after the procedure. Leo had entered the hospital smiling and waving earlier on Tuesday hours before the surgery. The Vatican has said it expects the pope to stay in his room on the 10th floor of Rome’s Gemelli hospital to recover for several days. His audiences have been cancelled until October 20 and the operation raises questions about whether the pope will go on a lengthy visit to Latin America next month. – ‘I will pray a lot’ – The surgery marks the 71-year-old Leo’s first hospitalisation since he became head of the Catholic Church on May 8, 2025. In a surprise announcement following Angelus prayers on Sunday, Leo told crowds in St Peter’s Square that doctors had discovered a nodule “at a very early stage” during medical checks. “The doctors believe it would be right to intervene,” he said. The Vatican has historically been very secretive about the health of popes, but began to be more transparent during the illness of Leo’s predecessor Francis, an Argentine who freely discussed his ailments. Ahead of the operation, people outside the hospital expressed concern over the pope’s condition. Giorgia Fei, a 57-year-old Italian, said she had been worried. “However, the Holy Father is in very good hands here at the hospital because we have some outstanding doctors,” she said. “I will pray a lot for him.” Giuseppe Purpura, 72, said he too was concerned. “He’s still quite young and I really wasn’t expecting this. I thought he was in better health,” he said, noting that “thankfully it was caught in time.” The Vicar General for the Diocese of Rome, Cardinal Baldassare Reina, led a rosary prayer for the pope inside the hospital chapel which was broadcast by the Vatican. Dozens of people attended and Reina asked all the city’s parishes to join in. The Vatican secretary of state, Cardinal Pietro Parolin, told ANSA news agency that Leo had been “very calm” about his condition when they met on Monday. The Vatican told AFP the nodule was found during routine health checks, and there were no symptoms that led to checking the pope’s lungs. Chicago-born Leo, the first US pope, is sporty and believed to generally be in good health. He is scheduled to travel to South America from November 6-17 to visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru. It was not immediately clear what would happen if the pope was forced into a longer recovery. Under Church law, a figure known as the Cardinal Camerlengo — or chamberlain — takes over administrative duties if the pope dies, but pontiffs do not have a deputy to replace them if they become incapacitated. ide-dt/ach The post Pope Leo has cancerous growth removed in lung operation appeared first on Vanguard News .
