title: Olympiacos Warns Fans to Leave Marseille Before Match
body: Olympiacos FC urges its supporters to leave Marseille and tells others not to travel for its match against Olympique de Marseille after French authorities reverse a ban on visiting fans just two days before the fixture. In a strongly worded statement issued on October 13, the Greek club condemned what it described as the “unprecedented, unacceptable and dangerous” handling of the situation by French authorities. Olympiacos says authorities initially decided to prohibit its supporters from entering Marseille, not merely attending the match. According to the club, the decision was made early Tuesday morning before being reversed approximately 10 hours later. The sudden change has left thousands of supporters facing cancelled flights, hotel bookings and other travel arrangements, with the club reporting significant financial losses. Olympiacos says hundreds of fans who had already travelled to Marseille returned to Greece, while others abandoned their plans after the original prohibition was announced. The club argues that reversing the ban at such short notice creates further uncertainty and raises serious questions about supporter safety. Olympiacos Questions Supporter Safety Olympiacos says the original restrictions were justified by French authorities on public order and security grounds. It now questions how those same authorities can provide sufficient guarantees for supporters following the reversal. The club says it no longer has confidence in the authorities’ ability to manage the situation consistently and safely. “OLYMPIACOS FC will under no circumstances expose its fans to danger,” the statement said. The club has consequently called on supporters already in Marseille to leave safely and urged those who have not travelled to remain at home. It also confirmed that it would not accept tickets for the fixture, placing supporter safety ahead of participation in the match. Club Seeks Compensation and UEFA Intervention Olympiacos has pledged to support collective legal action by its supporters against the French authorities and any other parties deemed responsible. The club says it intends to pursue compensation for the financial losses supporters incurred because of the successive decisions. It will also formally ask UEFA to ensure that the section originally allocated to Olympiacos fans remains empty throughout the match rather than being reassigned to Marseille supporters. The Greek club argues that the handling of the situation risks undermining the credibility and reputation of European football competitions. Olympiacos says it will use all available institutional and legal channels to defend its supporters’ rights and interests. The dispute leaves the build up to the European fixture overshadowed by uncertainty over security arrangements, ticketing and the treatment of travelling supporters. Olympiacos has made clear that it will not accept responsibility for exposing its fans to risks arising from what it describes as contradictory decisions by the French authorities. / Olympiacos Fans Banned from Marseille Europa League Clash in Late French Security Order The post Olympiacos Warns Fans to Leave Marseille Before Match appeared first on Greek City Times .

title: Leonard gets warm welcome in Raptors’ re-debut
body:
TORONTO – As far as Kawhi Leonard was concerned, his first game with his new Toronto Raptors teammates felt like a seamless fit.
Leonard drew the loudest cheers of the night — especially when he scored each of his game-high 21 points — in his re-debut for the Raptors as Toronto rolled past the New York Knicks 148-98 on Tuesday. It was the two-time NBA Finals MVP’s first game for the Raptors since he was traded back to Toronto by the Los Angeles Clippers this past summer.
“We came in to look focused on defence, and that was my intentions,” said Leonard, who also had five rebounds in 17 minutes of play. “I wanted to just get out, get after it, and get tired. I still want to get in better shape. It was fun to play.
“The guys have been great (…) everybody else has just been helping me out and just trying to make the transition so easy.”
Leonard had previously played for the Raptors in the 2018-19 season, leading them to their only NBA championship. He then signed a lucrative free-agent deal to join his hometown Clippers the following off-season.
L.A. traded him back to Toronto this past summer in a deal delayed by an NBA investigation into Leonard and the Clippers for salary cap circumvention. Although the team, its owner Steve Ballmer and several executives were severely punished by the league, Leonard only received a relatively small fine.
Once the punishments were doled out, the trade was allowed to go through, sending Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, two unprotected first-round picks, a 2027 pick swap and two second-round selections to Los Angeles.
Because Leonard sat out Toronto’s first two exhibition games, Tuesday was the first time the Raptors fielded all of their starters this pre-season.
Scottie Barnes added 19 points, six rebounds and four assists for Toronto (2-1). RJ Barrett of Mississauga, Ont., had 17 points, four boards, and three assists. Leonard did not play in the second half and Raptors head coach Darko Rajakovic benched the rest of his starters with over three minutes left to play in the third quarter.
“I’m just here to fit in,” said Leonard. “But fit out a little bit just by trying to, you know, play great basketball and just being aggressive.
“I just want to help others and then help my team and hopefully play a good game.”
James Wiseman had 18 points for the Knicks (0-4), who didn’t use any of their top players in the exhibition.
Rajakovic said beforehand that his hope was for Leonard to click with his new teammates.
“I tried to get those guys as much as possible on the court together, so that they could figure out the chemistry and spacing and that kind of stuff,” said Rajakovic post-game. “Obviously, just his first game.
“He was very excited coming into this game, and I thought he did great.”
Rajakovic also said pre-game that he wanted Leonard to “just have fun” in his first game back in Toronto.
Leonard, who described himself as a “fun guy” when he first met with Toronto media back in 2018, clearly enjoyed himself against the Knicks’ depth players.
He was 6 for 12 on field-goal attempts, including 4 for 8 from three-point range. He had a plus-28 defensive rating in the game. Frequently injured over his career, Leonard only played in the first half as the Raptors easily built an 86-47 lead by intermission.
“(Rajakovic) always tells me just go play basketball,” said Leonard. “But I’m still learning play calls, schemes, and still trying to get in shape.
“I’ve got to just keep pushing through fatigue and just keep getting better.”
Toronto will visit New York on Thursday and then finish its exhibition schedule on Friday in Detroit against the Pistons. The Raptors’ home opener is on Oct. 21 when they face the Chicago Bulls.
This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 13, 2026.

title: Netherlands 'leading hotbed of antisemitism': Israel condemns Hapoel Be'er Sheva ban
body: Israel has condemned the Netherlands for the decision to ban Israeli football fans from attending a Europa League match just two years after the Maccabi Tel Aviv fans were attacked in Amsterdam while attending an Ajax match.Dutch news site Nieuwsuur was the first to report that Hapoel Be'er Sheva fans have been banned from attending a match against AZ Alkmaar in Alkmaar on Thursday over security concerns.Israeli Ambassador Zvi Aviner Vapni is understood to have held a telephone conversation with Alkmaar Mayor Anja Schouten, telling her that everything must be done to allow Israeli supporters to attend the match in a safe way, “if necessary, in limited numbers.”The mayor's spokesperson told Nieuwsuur that the decision to ban away fans is fixed and that football will be played in Alkmaar on Thursday without an away crowd.Israel's Foreign Ministry posted a statement on X/Twitter: “Two years after Israelis were hunted through the streets of Amsterdam, the Dutch answer is to ban the victims, not the attackers.”Reward to those who incite violence, counter the spirit of sportThe ministry said Alkmaar's exclusion of Hapoel Be'er Sheva fans “rewards those who threaten and incite violence and runs counter to the very spirit of sport.”It also noted that the exclusion of Israelis comes amid a wave of antisemitic attacks in the Netherlands.The ministry said that banning Israeli fans from attending the match, like boycotting Eurovision, is “yet another stain on the Netherlands,” adding that it is increasingly becoming “one of the world's leading hotspots for antisemitism.”Though the Israeli fans will not be attending, safety is still a concern as two anti-Israel demonstrations are planned before the match.'Insufficient space' to prevent disorderSchouten has moved the two registered protests to Rhijnvis Feithlaan, opposite the AZ stadium at hotel Alkmaar, but local police said there is insufficient space on the stadium site to separate protesters and football supporters and to prevent disorder.Avi Nir-Feldklein, Israel's ambassador to the European Union, said he had planned to drive to Alkmaar to support Hapoel Be'er Sheva before finding out all Israeli supporters were banned by the municipality due to “very high risk.”“When Hezbollah and Hamas cheerleaders are allowed to march and celebrate the October 7 massacre, no wonder it's “high risk,” he said. “Instead of stopping the extremists, they banned the fans. Stand against hate, not against football fans.”This is the second ban on Hapoel Be'er Sheva in less than a month.In September, the mayor of the Belgian city of Leuven, Mohamed Ridouani, blocked the city from hosting the 2026-27 UEFA Europa League match between Belgian club Union Saint-Gilloise and Israeli club Hapoel Be'er Sheva, which was scheduled for October 22, 2026.The team includes three Arab Israeli players: Muhammad Abu Rumi, Mohammed Kna'an, and Zahi Ahmed.

title: Trump’s diesel deal with Putin, a rebuke from Brussels, and a squabble over Europe’s enormous Russian energy bill
body: EU leaders are unhappy with Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin’s deal to supply Russian diesel fuel to the U.S. They believe it undermines sanctions and allows the Kremlin to continue its war against Ukraine. In response, Trump says Europeans themselves have paid Moscow $250 billion for energy since the war began. Russia says that figure is too low; the EU says it is too high. By any estimate, however, the Kremlin continues to receive very large sums from the EU — despite repeated statements from Brussels about ending imports of Russian fuel. Here’s the short version. Russia’s account ( as presented by Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak): Russia received even more from the EU than Trump said. Since 2022, the EU has paid $320.7 billion for energy. In the first nine months of 2026 alone, Russia supplied Europe with $21.3 billion worth of energy. The EU’s account ( as presented by an unnamed European Commission representative): From March 2022 to July 2026, Russia supplied the EU with 197 billion euros ($209 billion) worth of energy. The plan to phase out Russian energy is working: Without it, the EU would have spent 475 billion euros on Russian oil and gas, more than twice as much. What about before the war? In 2021, the EU paid Russia 99 billion euros for energy, according to official Eurostat data. For comparison, Russia’s sovereign assets frozen in European depositories are estimated at 210 billion euros. EU officials periodically discuss seizing those assets to fund Ukraine’s reconstruction. title: Champions League: Lookman scores as Atletico down Carrick’s struggling Man United
body: Atletico Madrid eased to a 2-0 win over Manchester United in the Champions League on Tuesday to pile pressure on Red Devils coach Michael Carrick. Pablo Barrios pounced inside the first minute for Diego Simeone’s side and after Leny Yoro’s 74th minute red card set United back further, Ademola Lookman added another for the hosts in Madrid. Man United have made their worst domestic start in 40 years and this league phase defeat in the Spanish capital was another blow, with the team now winless in five games across all competitions. Carrick handed Carlos Baleba his first start for the club since arriving from Brighton this summer, as well as pushing captain Bruno Fernandes out to the right side. Atletico were without their skipper Koke, after the death of his mother, while coach Simeone selected Julian Alvarez from the off for the first time this season at the Metropolitano stadium, after he tried to force a departure this summer. “Defend what we love,” Atletico fans ordered their supporters with a banner display before kick-off and the Rojiblancos were ahead after just 50 seconds. Manchester United’s English head coach Michael Carrick applauds at the end of the UEFA Champions League, league phase, matchday 2, football match between Club Atletico de Madrid and Manchester United at the Metropolitano stadium in Madrid on October 13, 2026. Atletico Madrid won 2-0. (Photo by Oscar DEL POZO / AFP) Alex Baena found a way in behind United’s defence and cut the ball across for Barrios, with Ayden Heaven unable to keep the midfielder’s shot from crossing the line. Bryan Mbuemo might have equalised for the visitors, nudging the ball through Cristian Romero’s legs but firing just wide. Alejandro Grimaldo came inches away from extending Atletico’s lead with a free-kick which hit the angle between post and crossbar. The hosts thought they had a second when Johnny Cardoso finished neatly from the edge of the box before half-time but the goal was disallowed after a VAR review showed the ball had struck Marcos Llorente’s hand during the build-up. Alvarez, yet to score this season for Atletico, hit the post early in the second half. United rallied and Fernandes’s lob drifted narrowly wide before the Portuguese playmaker hit the crossbar from the left of the box after a corner routine. However the three-time European champions suffered a setback when defender Yoro was harshly dismissed after a VAR review for bringing down Canada striker Jonathan David as the last man. It opened the door for Atletico to grab their second, with David foiled by goalkeeper Senne Lammens but London-born Nigeria international Lookman on hand to tuck home the rebound after 79 minutes. Carrick withdrew playmaker Fernandes, looking ahead to the weekend visit to face rivals Leeds in the English top flight, where improvement is badly needed. Atletico goalkeeper Jan Oblak saved from United substitute Matheus Cunha in the final stages but there was no way back for United. Simeone’s side were able to claim their first points after an opening defeat at Liverpool. title: Techiman South MP ends decades of water struggle in Asutia
body: For generations, the people of Asutia, a farming community in the Techiman South Constituency of the Bono East Region, have known only one reality—the daily struggle for water. A reality where children wake at dawn to trek long distances in search of a source that is neither clean nor reliable. A reality where the dry season doesn’t just mean harsh weather, but the disappearance of the very water they depend on. A reality where sickness lurks in every sip. But today, that reality has changed. For years, Asutia has been without a portable source of drinking water. Residents relied on an unclean water source that often ran dry during the dry seasons, forcing them to dig for water that was barely fit for consumption. The consequences were devastating. Waterborne diseases became a constant companion, affecting children and adults alike. Prince Richard Donkor, the Odikro of Asutia and former Assembly Member of the Asubrofo Electoral Area, has witnessed the suffering firsthand. “We have suffered. Our people have been drinking unwholesome water. We battle waterborne diseases constantly because we have no choice,” he recounted. “Sometimes, the stream dries up, and we have to dig for water that isn’t even fit for animals. It has been a painful existence.” The community’s prayers seemed to go unanswered year after year. That is, until now. After a long wait, hope arrived in the form of the Member of Parliament for Techiman South, Martin Adjei Mensah Korsah. Determined to end the community’s water crisis, the MP initiated the drilling of a mechanized borehole—a project that would require persistence and faith. It wasn’t easy. The first attempts yielded nothing. But the MP refused to give up. “I am incredibly happy today. This was not an easy task,” Hon. Adjei Mensah Korsah said during the handover ceremony. “We made three or four attempts trying to find water in this area. But I was determined that the people of Asutia must have clean water. Today, that determination has paid off. We have finally struck water, and the relief is immense.” The day of the handover was nothing short of a celebration. Women danced, children cheered, and elders smiled as clean, clear water gushed from the new borehole for the first time. For many, it was a moment they had waited for their entire lives. “We are so thankful to the MP. For years, we prayed for this day. Now, our children will drink clean water. We can bathe and cook without fear. God bless the MP for remembering us,” said an elated resident. The mechanized borehole is expected to serve the entire community, providing a sustainable and safe source of drinking water that will last for years to come. This project represents more than just access to clean water—it represents dignity, health, and hope. No longer will the people of Asutia suffer from preventable waterborne diseases. No longer will women and children walk miles in search of water. No longer will the dry season bring fear and uncertainty. For the MP, this is a promise kept. For the people, it is a new beginning. “The sound of this borehole is a song of freedom for us,” said one elderly woman, tears of joy streaming down her face. While celebrating this victory, community leaders are hopeful that more development projects will follow. They expressed gratitude to the MP for his intervention and urged him to continue championing the needs of rural communities like Asutia. For now, however, the focus is on the simple pleasure that many take for granted—the ability to turn on a tap and have clean water flow. For Asutia, that simple pleasure is nothing short of a miracle.

title: Air Force Tests New Sentinel Reentry Vehicle
body: The Air Force Nuclear Weapons Center tested its new intercontinental ballistic missile reentry vehicle Oct. 9, launching the developmental vehicle atop a Minotaur I rocket from Vandenberg Space Force Base, Calif. The Mk21A reentry vehicle, mated to the Sentinel ICBM, will eventually replace the Minuteman III as the land-based leg of the nation’s nuclear triad. Carrying the new W87-1 nuclear warhead, it will launch atop the Sentinel’s three rocket stages, blasting into space before reentering the atmosphere to strike its target. The Oct. 9 test launch carried no warhead and was the first announced test of the new vehicle since June 2024 . “The Mk21A is crucial to modernizing our ICBMs in response to the rapidly changing global threat picture posed by our adversaries,” said Maj. Gen. William Rogers, the Air Force’s portfolio acquisition executive for ICBMs, in a statement. “The reentry vehicle’s development will ensure a safe, secure and effective deterrent for generations to come.” The Mk21A is based on the Mk21 reentry vehicle used on the Minuteman III, and is being developed by Lockheed Martin. The Minotaur I launch vehicle, provided by Northrop Grumman, is based on the Peacekeeper and Minuteman rocket motors. The Space Force helped oversee the test through its Rocket Systems Launch Program, which provides commercial launch systems and excess ballistic missile assets for government payloads. The Air Force Nuclear Weapons Center awarded Lockheed a $996 million contract for the Mk21A in October 2023 and followed with an additional $453 million contract modification in November 2025 . According to an April acquisition report released by the Pentagon in September , the latest contract modification was part of a new baseline for the program intended to “decouple its schedule from external programs and continue development with an updated, more resilient plan.” The LGM-35 Sentinel program office is still working to overcome the cost and schedule problems that triggered a mandatory Pentagon review, and while officials claim progress, the program is undergoing a restructuring before it can meet Milestone B, which would authorize it to move into engineering and manufacturing development. The acquisition report offers scant details on the Mk21A rebaseline effort, beyond noting that it includes a new “alternate flight test strategy” and additional test assets. It does note, however, that the June 2024 test successfully flight-tested the vehicle’s heatshield, and that Lockheed was working on integrating the arming and fuzing subsystem in February 2026. Air Force budget documents released in April projected “flight test of heatshield test vehicle and W87-1 environmental flight test unit” in fiscal 2026 and 2027. A critical design review for the entire Sentinel system is planned by March 2027. The Air Force asked for almost $540 million to fund Mk21A reentry vehicle development in the fiscal 2027 budget request, up $184 million from 2026 as Sentinel ramps up integration and test activities. The post Air Force Tests New Sentinel Reentry Vehicle appeared first on Air & Space Forces Magazine .

title: Bank of America fined $1.2bn over claimed sanctions breaches
body: Bank of America was ordered to pay more than $1.2 billion in fines after the US Treasury Department said the company breached anti-money laundering and sanctions laws, the agency said on Tuesday. The authority said the fine is the third-largest in its history. Bank of America was also ordered to pay $750 million to the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, the largest ever issued by the OCC. The department's Office of Foreign Assets Control also announced an $11.6 million settlement with Bank of America over 475 “apparent violations” of sanctions against “ Russia , Belarus, Iran , Burma, Somalia, narcotics and global terrorism”. Bank of America is the second-largest bank in the US, with more than 70 million clients, and processes about $4.5 trillion in payments for customers every year. It enables more than $450 trillion of payments in employee payrolls, supplier payments and corporate credit cards. It also processes an average of $1.9 trillion in wire transfers a day globally for clients. “When a bank of this size fails to meet its anti-money-laundering and sanctions obligations, the consequences extend far beyond its own walls, exposing the entire us financial system to significant illicit finance risks,” Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a statement. “Today’s actions send a clear message that even the biggest financial institutions are not above the law." The Treasury Department said Bank of America admitted it willfully breached the Bank Secrecy Act, which requires banks to assist the Treasury in detecting and preventing money laundering. Bank of America said it has "invested billions of dollars" to tackle financial crime, and that it is "far along" in its remediation efforts with US regulators. "Financial crime compliance is serious, and we are responsible for getting it right", a Bank of America representative said. The department said the US bank failed to report to the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network more than $5 billion in suspicious transactions, with more than $1 billion implicating national security and other risks "indicative of Chinese Money Laundering Networks, fraud, and potential trade-based money laundering with a substantial nexus to the southwest border." The OCC issued a cease-and-desist order against the bank in 2024 over deficiencies related to its Bank Secrecy Act and compliance programmes. “The bank’s poor response to its BSA deficiencies is unacceptable,” said Jonathan Gould, Comptroller of the Currency. Tuesday's fine followed an action from the OCC last week, in which American Express was fined $350 million after its compliance programme allowed about $13 billion in suspected money laundering activity to go undetected for more than a decade. Bank of America is due to report its third-quarter earnings on Wednesday. The bank said its third-quarter results will include a $1.2 billion non-tax deductible charge, reducing income by roughly 17 cents per share. "We have already dedicated substantial personnel and resources to our ongoing remediation efforts, and those costs are in the current expense base," a bank representative said.

title: Ocius Technology opens NZ maintenance facility
body: Ocius Technology has opened its first overseas advanced maritime maintenance facility in Auckland through its wholly owned subsidiary, Ocius New Zealand (Ocius NZ). The Ocius NZ facility will provide onshore maintenance and technical support for the Royal New Zealand Navy’s Bluebottle Uncrewed Surface Vessel (USV) fleet, helping to maximise their availability for persistent surveillance across New Zealand’s vast maritime domain. The facility also gives Ocius a strategically located base in the Pacific as demand for autonomous maritime surveillance continues to grow across the region. The Auckland facility draws on New Zealand’s strong maritime and advanced manufacturing expertise and is creating highly skilled local roles in maritime autonomy and engineering. Ocius plans to expand the facility as demand for autonomous maritime surveillance increases. Its establishment comes as Australia, New Zealand and other Pacific nations increase their focus on maintaining persistent maritime surveillance across vast areas of ocean for defence, border security and the disruption of transnational organised crime. In March 2026, the Australian Government announced a $176 million investment to deliver a further 40 Australian-designed and built Bluebottles, in addition to the 15 Bluebottles operated by Australia’s maritime Border Command. Globally, uncrewed maritime systems are also demonstrating the asymmetric advantages of persistent, low-cost autonomous capability in increasingly contested environments. Powered by solar, wind and wave energy, Bluebottle USVs can remain at sea for extended periods, providing persistent intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance without the need for continuous crewed operations. Bluebottles support defence, customs and other agencies by providing real-time surface and sub-surface maritime awareness, operating alongside crewed and uncrewed platforms as part of a broader surveillance network. This capability is increasingly important as transnational organised crime groups exploit Pacific maritime routes to move illicit drugs towards New Zealand and Australia. Ocius NZ is currently expanding its Auckland-based team and recruiting people with relevant technical and engineering skills, including candidates with current New Zealand security clearances. Robert Dane, Chief Executive Officer, Ocius Technology, said, “We are excited to be expanding Ocius’ on-the-ground presence in New Zealand as we continue to grow our operations across the Pacific. Ocius has been working with the Royal New Zealand Navy and New Zealand Customs Service for 2 years, supporting efforts to strengthen maritime awareness and help combat transnational organised crime. The establishment of Ocius NZ means Bluebottles can be maintained locally and returned to the water as quickly as possible, helping maximise their availability and persistent presence at sea. It also gives Ocius an additional operational base in the Pacific as our fleet continues to grow across the region. We look forward to continuing to support New Zealand’s maritime security and its wider role in maintaining security across the Pacific.” Chief of Navy, Royal New Zealand Navy, Rear Admiral Garin Golding, said, “New Zealand is a maritime nation. Its prosperity, security and its role in the Pacific depends on knowing what is happening across a vast area of ocean. USVs are an important part of the Defence Force’s move towards smarter, more sustainable maritime surveillance. Our Bluebottles, Tahi and Rua, are enabling us to maintain a persistent watch over New Zealand’s maritime environment. The establishment of Ocius NZ’s facility means our Bluebottles can be maintained locally, maximising their time at sea and strengthening New Zealand’s national security.” For Editorial Inquiries Contact: Editor Kym Bergmann at kym.bergmann@venturamedia.net For Advertising Inquiries Contact: Group Sales Director Simon Hadfield at simon.hadfield@venturamedia.net

title: Three things we’ve learnt about the UK economy from the IMF
body: Countries around the world have had their future economic prospects assessed by an influential body, the International Monetary Fund (IMF). What the IMF says matters – it aims to keep the global economy stable, and its twice-yearly forecasts are among the most authoritative assessments of what is really going on around the world. Yet, like all forecasts, they can be incorrect, so they shouldn’t be treated as gospel. Here are three things we’ve learnt about the UK from the IMF’s latest report. 1. The UK is weathering the Iran war better than expected The global economy has been rocked by the US-Israel war with Iran. The transportation and production of energy in the Middle East have been severely disrupted, causing oil prices to jump and inflation to rise. To calm the rate of price rises, central banks, including the Bank of England, are expected to hike interest rates in the coming months. Despite all this, the IMF said the global economy is doing much better than expected, partly due to the surge in investment in artificial intelligence (AI). And this is good news for the UK. The IMF said its economy would expand by 1.3% in 2026, up from the 1% it predicted in July, before slowing in 2027. A growing economy means companies are investing more and hiring more people while shoppers have more money to spend. A shrinking economy means the reverse is true. 2. The UK is doing better than other major economies There is increased concern about how much money countries are borrowing, but the IMF said the UK is doing better than all other major economies at this. The IMF said the UK “basically stands out, along with India”, when it comes to addressing the problem, and that by 2031 it is projected to have the lowest annual borrowing among the G7, which includes Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, and the US. Sir Howard Davies, former deputy governor of the Bank of England, said this was largely because the UK has a government with a majority which has committed to tackling the situation, which it is expected to achieve either through tax rises, cuts to public services, or a mix of both. By contrast, he says the US has said little about reducing its deficit, while France and Germany don’t have majority governments. “So, we [the UK] are not great students, but we look somewhat better than some of the others we are sharing the class with,” he said. Meanwhile, the IMF’s growth forecasts for the UK mean it is expected to have the second-fastest-growing economy in the G7 this year, along with Germany. Sir Howard believes this should also be seen in context. “We’re still growing slowly. It’s almost like saying we’re winning a slow bicycle race here because other people are going backwards a bit more rapidly than we are.” 3. But things could get worse While the IMF boosted its projection for the UK’s growth in 2026, it slightly downgraded its forecasts for next year. While the UK has handled the economic fallout from the Iran war better than expected so far, it says this will change next year as high energy prices and elevated interest rates affect how much people spend in shops and how much companies are willing to invest. In addition, the IMF has said households are likely to continue feeling the pinch of rising prices. It forecasts inflation in the UK will average 3.3% this year, and it has raised its estimate for next year to 2.8% from its previous prediction of 2.4%. “There will be increasing inflationary pressure put on the UK and the Bank of England will have to consider further rate rises,” says Tim Armitage, investment strategist at Quilter Cheviot. He added that at least one rate hike is expected this year, with more expected next year.

title: Libya Warns Greece Over Crete Energy Work
body: Libya’s planned Crete surveys south of the island have prompted a Tripoli note verbale warning Athens that continuing the work may pause maritime border talks. The note, dated August, protests hydrocarbon exploration in seas not yet delimited between the two countries, Proto Thema reported on Tuesday. US firm Chevron is preparing to start work in blocks south of Crete. That timing makes Libya’s surveys a significant factor for toece’s energy plans. Tripoli also objects to a Greek invitation for tenders published in the Official Journal of the European Union on 17 August. The notice confirmed a 30 June Gazette entry. Under it, HEREMA would grant a licence for seismic work south of Crete, the Peloponnese and the Ionian Sea. “Such actions may negatively affect the course of bilateral negotiations,” the Libyan note said, according to the paper. It also raised the risk of a pause in the talks. Libya Crete surveys and MoU Libya argues the moves violate its continental shelf as declared to the United Nations on 27 May 2025. The Turkish-Libyan memorandum still shapes Tripoli’s map. Some Greek blocks overlap areas that the memorandum assigns to Libya, the report said. Tripoli also presses claims built on closing the Gulf of Sidra and denying full effect to islands such as Gavdos. Energy stakes at sea Libya urges Greece to avoid provocative acts. At the same time it seeks to lock the Turkish-Libyan memorandum into the talks, Proto Thema said. Greek City Times earlier reported that Cyprus gas is set for first export to Europe via Egypt and Greece , another Eastern Mediterranean energy strand. Primary law texts are available in the Official Journal of the European Union . The UN lists continental-shelf filings on the UN Division for Ocean Affairs . Delimitation talks between Athens and Tripoli continue. Still, Libya-Crete surveys remain contested after the August note. Source: Proto Thema The post Libya Warns Greece Over Crete Energy Work appeared first on Greek City Times .

title: Announcing Lix 2.96 “Bingsu”
body:
We at the Lix team are proud to announce our seventh major release, version 2.96 “Bingsu”.
This release focuses on security, debugger support, quality-of-life improvements, and continues the work towards both the new Cap’n’Proto RPC protocol and Rust support.
Bingsu is a milk-based Korean shaved ice dessert with sweet toppings that may include chopped fruit, condensed milk, fruit syrup, tteok, and red beans.
Lix is a Nix implementation focused on reliability, predictability, friendliness, developed by a community of people from around the world. We have long term plans to incrementally evolve Nix to work in more places, to make it more reliable and secure, and to update the language and semantics to correct past mistakes and reduce errors, all the while providing an amazing tooling experience.
WARNING : We do not recommend to use nix upgrade-nix , please follow the instructions in https://lix.systems/install/ with the Lix’s upgrade shell script.
The upgrade procedure depends on how you installed Lix or CppNix, and is fully described in the Lix installation guide .
If you are using Lix from nixpkgs on NixOS, you just need to upgrade your nixpkgs once the upgrade pull request has passed through the build farm into your channel; no other action is required.
If you want to help us test the next version of Lix, consider running main by following the beta guide .
Lix 2.96 builds on the work of previous releases to improve the daemon, the protocols spoken with the daemon (both on a single machine and the ones used for remote builds), and brings many much-needed improvements to the debugger infrastructure.
Here’s a short list of the most exciting changes in Lix 2.96. This list is not as exhaustive as the full release notes .
Thanks to the tireless work of blokyk the REPL and debugger are much improved in Lix 2.96. The debugger is now more stable, navigating within the debugger is much easier, and the information printed by the debugger is more readable.
eldritch horrors have also switched the REPL backend from editline to rustyline , finally bringing proper UTF-8 support to the REPL.
The experimental RPC protocol is now shipping under the rpc-sockets experimental feature. As one may guess this is still highly experimental and must be enabled not only with the experimental feature flag in your Lix config, but also requires system setup that is not yet done by the NixOS module. You can find an example configuration in the NixOS module in the Lix repo .
In future releases we plan to stabilize the RPC protocol and remove support for the legacy protocols we’ve been using to date to allow further evolution of Lix.
To enable further RPC work and resolve some long-standing security inconsistencies we must remove ssh:// store URIs. Lix 2.96 deprecates ssh:// store URIs , but retains support for them without deprecation warnings. ssh:// store URI support will be removed in Lix 2.97, ssh-ng:// URIs will remain supported.
If you are using ssh:// store URIs because ssh-ng:// is missing features you need please get in touch so we can figure something out together. Note that ssh-ng has stricter security checks than ssh and no longer allows untrusted users to copy unsigned outputs to remote stores, this is intentional .
Once again Lix must break sharp corners to make improvements possible and excise surprising behavior in user code.
flake.nix validation no longer relies on poorly documented triviality checks. Instead Lix now has only one rule for flake.nix : no function calls are allowed outside of outputs . This means that Lix now accepts let blocks and string interpolation in flake inputs , among other things. We consider this a breaking change because other Nix implementations may no longer be able to evaluate Flakes that were written using Lix.
Many thanks to piegames , Qyriad and eldritch horrors .
The floor and ceil builtins now throw errors if their operation would have resulted in precision loss during the conversion from floating point to integers. Precision loss does not sound dramatic, but with numbers of sufficient magnitude this could result in positive floats being converted to negative integers.
Many thanks to jade , NaN-git and rootile .
Many nix3 CLI commands no longer build their arguments. This surprising behavior was commonly seen when nix store delete was called with a path that was not present in the store, causing the path to be downloaded just so that it could be deleted.
Shadowing internal files via Nix search paths is now considered an error. Lix 2.95 already deprecated overriding the nix search path entry due to surprising effects that could have, Lix 2.96 now considers this an error if not explicitly configured otherwise.
Many thanks to thubrecht , jade and eldritch horrors .
Nested arguments can be set with --arg and --argstr .
Previously Lix would turn --arg foo.bar.baz 1 into the set { "foo.bar.baz" = 1; } , now it turns it into { foo.bar.baz = 1; } . Attribute set merging rules are applied to these sets, making it much easier to use function that expect sets as arguments (such as nixpkgs, which expects a config set). The old behavior can be recovered by quoting the name, e.g. --arg '"foo.bar.baz" 1' .
Inputs are now only fetched by one process at a time. This can be significant in CI situations where many processes may attempt to download the same input set concurrently. Previously all of them would download the set, now only one of them does and signals the others to wait for it to finish.
Use mimalloc for faster evaluation. We’ve seen 5-12% eval time improvements due to this
Many thanks to getchoo and lovesegfault .
nix doctor has been extended greatly, including general system information and remote builder configuration in its report. It can now also automatically connect to configured remote builders and check their state as well.
ssh-ng store URIs are now considered stable. The long-awaited feature parity between ssh and ssh-ng URIs has arrived, although only Lix 2.96 and newer will be able to take full advantage of this. Connecting to or from older Lixes or other Nix implementations will not see feature parity and silently fall back to the previous behavior.
Channel references now support zst -compressed tarballs. This can greatly improve unpacking speed when using channels.
Many thanks to raito and eldritch horrors .
The ssl-cert-file and netrc-file settings now report errors when set to files that don’t exist instead of being silently ignored.
Moving between stack frames in the debugger is now easier using offset instead of absolute numbers. While moving up or down some number of frames previously required remembering the frame number you were on you can now directly supply offsets, using :st +l to go from frame n to n+k and :st -k to go from n to n-k .
addErrorContext frames are always printed in backtraces now, even without --show-trace . This makes explicit report locations, for example in the NixOS module system, much more useful.
nix-copy-closure --include-outputs now actually works.
Hash mismatch diagnostics now work with structuredAttrs . This fixes hash mismatch diagnostics with fetchers from modern nixpkgs.
Subdaemons receive overridden settings from their parent daemon rather than using the system-wide configuration. This was broken by the switch to explicitly launched subdaemons in 2.95, making it impossible to configure subdaemons by providing command line arguments to the main daemon.
ssh and ssh-ng store URIs no longer honor the max-connections parameter. This parameter complicated the code immensely for no benefit to the average user and had many sharp corners when set explicitly.
The daemon-trust-override experimental feature has been removed. It can still be emulated by e.g. setting the NIX_CONFIG environment variable appropriately.
Many more changes have gone into Lix 2.96, most of them internal. We hope to ship a stable RPC-based daemon in one of the upcoming releases, including remote build support using this new protocol.
We are releasing 2.96 together with security releases on stable branches. A few things we wanted to finish for 2.96 have been delayed somewhat, and we expect to release 2.96.1 with a few more improvements soon:
Rust integration has moved along apace, and it is now possible to write significant portions of new features without touching too much C++ code. We’ve decided to use zngur for interop due to its great flexibility and active maintenance, and we’ve already ported a number of features to Rust like this. The REPL is now backed by Rust, as is remote builder configuration and much of the hash conversion code.
Following Lix integration in AFNix, Lix now has an Open Collective and can receive donations.
We run infrastructure across x86_64-linux, aarch64-linux, and aarch64-darwin. Some of it is in-kind and sponsored. Current costs are around 100€/month.
If you value self-hosting and benefit from Lix, please consider donating. Every contribution helps sustain the project.
Thanks, as always, to the following groups:
The large community who beta tested the upcoming release by running main in production since the 2.95 branch-off. We really appreciate having immediate feedback on our work and the trust of running main alongside us means a lot to us. We know we tested the patience of some of you, we thank you for that.
If you want to run Lix main yourself, see the beta guide for details.
Everyone who contributed by filing bugs and giving us feedback on Matrix.
All the first time contributors who made their first contributions to a Nix implementation in Lix. We are eternally grateful to everyone who helped us out on the numerous important but tedious issues.
All the contributors who have helped us with the backlog of bugs.
The CppNix contributors and CppNix team, without whom we would not have this software, and who wrote some of the improvements ported into this release.
Onwards and upwards for the next release. We look forward to continuing to work together with everyone to build a better foundation for the evolution of Nix.
Lix is an independent variant of the Nix package manager, developed by a team of open-source volunteers, and maintained by and for a passionate community of users.

title: Lockheed Martin debuts PAC-3 Edge for US Army’s future interceptor program
body: Lockheed Martin has debuted its new interceptor that will add a defensive capability against hypersonic and advanced missile threats. The new interceptor, called PAC-3 Edge, leverages combat-proven PAC-3 MSE technology and the latest, industry-leading capability to deliver decisive performance against the Army’s most critical threats. Lockheed Martin’s new interceptor is part of the U.S. Army’s Future Interceptor program currently in competition. The Army’s decision to progress Lockheed Martin into the next stage of development affirms its confidence in Lockheed Martin’s proven Integrated Air and Missile Defense (IAMD) experience and the company’s ability to deliver an advanced, layered defence against what’s next. Lockheed Martin will advance development and begin testing PAC-3 Edge in 2027 to prepare for rapid deployment by 2031. PAC-3 Edge delivers the highest level of performance through a transformative Lockheed Martin-built seeker designed by Lockheed Martin’s Strigo Product Center. This seeker will feature the most advanced defence technology available, enabling improved performance to counter the most advanced threats. PAC-3 Edge also features a multi-pulse solid rocket motor designed by Northrop Grumman, implementing advanced enhancements to deliver precision thrust throughout the interceptor’s flight. Lockheed Martin also implemented control system upgrades to deliver increased PAC-3 EDGE performance at range and altitude. “Lockheed Martin’s PAC-3 Edge interceptor leverages the combat-proven PAC-3 MSE, delivering even greater maneuverability, power and velocity to ensure the Army’s layered defensive architecture remains the most advanced in the world,” said Tim Cahill, Lockheed Martin, Missiles and Fire Control president. The new interceptor is designed to counter a wide range of air, missile and hypersonic threats at higher altitudes and longer ranges, expanding the Army’s IAMD coverage. PAC-3 Edge builds on the heritage of the PAC-3 family of missiles, which includes the lower cost PAC-3 ACE, legacy PAC-3 CRI and prestigious PAC-3 MSE, offering the most advanced interceptor capabilities to date. Lockheed Martin invested $250 million into the Strigo Product Center to fuel new, industry-leading seeker technology that enables increased precision and maneuverability against evolving threats. The new interceptor complements the Army’s existing IAMD capabilities, strengthening a multitiered shield that protects critical assets in the homeland and abroad. Integration through Innovation – PAC-3 Edge is designed to be integrated with existing and future IAMD capabilities including the Integrated Battle Command System (IBCS), the M903 launcher, containerized launchers and HIMARS Flex. title: Anduril awarded contract to expand US Army’s next-gen battlefield command system
body: The Army awarded Anduril Industries a contract on Sept. 30 worth up to $1.8 billion over five years to help the service transition its new battlefield software from the experimentation phase to the fielding phase. Anduril previously helped develop the prototype for the service’s Next Generation Command and Control, or NGC2, for the 4th Infantry Division, using its proprietary AI-powered operating system Lattice. “A common data layer allows the Army to integrate new systems without rebuilding the underlying architecture for every sensor, application, or weapon, so new capabilities can be fielded on the same foundation as those already in use,” Anduril said. The Army awarded $162.8 million to Anduril to continue working on NGC2’s common data baseline, or software foundation, as it begins to implement it across the service’s I Corps, which commands service members across the Indo-Pacific. The contract contains options that can grow its value up to $1.8 billion. Anduril, along with Palantir, Raft and Striveworks, have helped build out the baseline. The NGC2 system will allow technologies, weapons, sensors, devices and applications from across the force to operate on the same network and increase decision-making speed on the battlefield. By expanding the NGC2 system to the I Corps, technologies will have to figure out ways to connect to the same network despite being separated by thousands of miles and experiencing interrupted or degraded connectivity. This will provide the Army and Anduril an opportunity to test how well information flows between the systems as they access the NGC2 framework in a myriad of environments. During a July 2026 ten-day event at Fort Irwin, California, entitled Project Convergence-Capstone 6 , the Army asked 10,000 participants from U.S. and allied forces, as well as industry partners using 90 technologies to test software for the NGC2. Afterward, the Army awarded a contract to Anduril to develop the software prototype for NGC2 for the 4th Infantry Division. Over the past year, Anduril has conducted several operational exercises in collaboration with the Army to test the NGC2’s common data layer baseline. In May, Anduril deployed its NGC2 system at Fort Carson and Pinon Canyon, using over 160 tactical edge computers, over 2,500 devices and 40 applications while navigating simulated cyber and electromagnetic attacks. Two months later, after a joint force exercise at Fort Irwin, the service said the battlefield command system was ready to be scaled. The NGC2 is set to replace the Army’s first-gen command-and-control system, which helps control fire, logistics and airspace on the battlefield. The Army has made it clear that it wants to implement the NGC2 as soon as possible. “We know the biggest risk to our national security and our national defense is not moving too fast. It’s not moving fast enough,” said former Army Secretary Dan Driscoll. “The side that can sense a target, process the data, and deliver a kinetic effect the fastest, wins. That is the decisive advantage this capability provides.”

title: ASC and HIFraser extend Collins Class partnership to 40 years
body: ASC and HIFraser will extend their long-standing partnership supporting the Collins Class submarine program beyond 40 years under a new six-year contract. Valued at nearly $40 million, the agreement between Australia’s submarine company and the engineering and manufacturing specialists reinforces a long-standing commitment to Australia’s sovereign submarine capability. HIFraser, which has offices in Western Australia and NSW, has supported ASC and the Royal Australian Navy’s Collins Class submarines since 1992. As a long-standing Australian industry partner, HIFraser will continue delivering high-and low-pressure valves and on-board maintenance services that are critical to helping sustain the operational readiness of the fleet. Sustainment is the work that keeps submarines operating throughout service, and includes maintenance, repairs, upgrades and the specialist support needed to keep vessels safe, capable and ready for deployment. ASC Chief Operating Officer – Multi-Class Sustainment, Rebecca Brickhill, said the agreement recognised the important role trusted Australian suppliers play in sustaining one of the nation’s most important Defence capabilities. “ASC’s ability to deliver safe, reliable and effective sustainment outcomes for the Collins Class submarine fleet relies on strong partnerships with highly capable Australian suppliers such as HIFraser,” Brickhill said. “This new agreement builds on a proven relationship spanning decades and provides the certainty needed to continue investing in the people, skills and industrial capability required to support the Royal Australian Navy’s requirements.” HIFraser is an Australian component manufacturer and an approved subcontractor to Australia’s Collins Class fleet through-life sustainment activities. It is also one of a number of Australian businesses that has successfully qualified through a rigorous national qualification program to support the construction of US Virginia Class submarines. Established by the Australian Submarine Agency (ASA) in partnership with the US Government, the Defence Industry Vendor Qualification (DIVQ) Program, delivered by ASC, helps Australian industry lift its systems, processes and technical capability to meet US submarine requirements. HIFraser has been qualified to manufacture and supply specialised valves, fittings and other components for the Virginia Class submarines. HIFraser Group Chief Operating Officer, Peter Andrews, said the new agreement marked another significant milestone in the company’s long-standing relationship with ASC. “HIFraser is proud to have supported ASC and the Collins Class submarine fleet since 1992,” Andrews said. “Operating for more than 40 years, HIFraser has developed a reputation for highly specialised capabilities in advanced manufacturing, engineering and on-going sustainment services. These skills are critical to supporting Australia’s submarine fleet and position us strongly to meet future defence industry requirements. This achievement is evidence of how enduring partnerships with organisations like ASC can create pathways to future opportunities under AUKUS, while supporting highly skilled Australian jobs and sovereign industrial capability.” ASC is Australia’s Sovereign Submarine Sustainment Partner and is responsible for ensuring the ongoing availability of the Collins Class submarine fleet through sustainment and Life-of-Type Extension activities. ASC works closely with Australian industry partners to deliver sovereign capability while supporting skilled jobs and advanced manufacturing across the country.
