title: How Browser-Based IRC Chat Works Without Java
body: Browser-based chat has changed dramatically over the years. Not long ago, joining an online chat room often meant installing a desktop IRC client or enabling a Java applet in your browser. Today, users can join real-time conversations directly from Chrome, Firefox, Safari, or Edge without installing Java. But how does browser-based IRC chat actually work? What replaced Java applets, and how can modern web applications communicate with traditional IRC servers? Let's explore the technologies behind modern web chat. 1. A Brief History of Java-Based Chat During the early days of online chat, Java applets offered a convenient way to run interactive applications inside web browsers. Many IRC websites used these applets to connect visitors to chat servers. Users could select a nickname, enter a channel, and exchange messages without installing a separate desktop IRC client. However, Java applets eventually became impractical because of several problems: Frequent security concerns and browser restrictions Compatibility issues across operating systems Additional installation and update requirements Increasingly limited browser support Poor usability on smartphones and tablets Modern browsers no longer support the old Java browser plugin architecture. Fortunately, the web has evolved enough to deliver real-time messaging without it. 2. Java and JavaScript Are Not the Same One of the most common misconceptions about Java-free chat is that it also means JavaScript-free chat. These are entirely different technologies. Java is a general-purpose programming language historically used in browser applets, desktop applications, and server-side systems. JavaScript is a programming language widely used to build interactive web applications, including modern browser-based messaging interfaces. A chat website can work without Java while still relying on JavaScript for its interface and real-time communication. This distinction is particularly important when discussing modern IRC web clients. 3. How Browser-Based IRC Chat Works Traditional IRC clients communicate with IRC servers using the Internet Relay Chat protocol. A desktop application such as mIRC can establish a TCP connection to an IRC server and exchange protocol messages. Web browsers, however, cannot normally open arbitrary TCP socket connections using standard client-side JavaScript. This creates an interesting challenge. How can a browser communicate with an IRC server? One common solution is to introduce a WebSocket-to-IRC gateway. The architecture looks like this: [Web Browser] | | HTTPS / WebSocket | [WebSocket Gateway] | | TCP / TLS | [IRC Server] | | [IRC Channels and Users] The browser exchanges messages with the gateway through a WebSocket connection. The gateway communicates with the IRC server using the appropriate IRC protocol messages. This allows users to access traditional IRC networks through a modern web interface. Some platforms use a different architecture, such as server-managed IRC connections and application-specific messaging APIs. 4. Why WebSockets Matter WebSocket is a web communication protocol designed to provide persistent, bidirectional communication between a client and a server. Unlike traditional request-response patterns, WebSocket allows messages to move in both directions without establishing a new HTTP request for every chat message. This makes it especially useful for: Real-time chat applications Collaborative editing tools Multiplayer applications Live notifications Interactive dashboards For example, a browser application can establish a WebSocket connection using JavaScript: const socket = new WebSocket ( " wss://chat.example.com/ws " ); socket . addEventListener ( " open " , () => { console . log ( " Connected " ); }); socket . addEventListener ( " message " , ( event ) => { console . log ( " Message: " , event . data ); }); socket . addEventListener ( " close " , () => { console . log ( " Disconnected " ); }); This example demonstrates browser-to-gateway communication, not a direct connection to a traditional IRC TCP port. The gateway must still handle authentication, message validation, protocol conversion, and error recovery. 5. What Happens When Someone Joins an IRC Channel? Imagine someone opening a browser-based chat page and selecting the nickname WebVisitor . A typical connection process might involve the following steps: The visitor opens the chat page. The browser establishes a secure connection to the web gateway. The gateway creates or associates an IRC session. The IRC server processes nickname and user registration. The session joins a channel, such as #chat . Incoming channel messages are delivered to the browser. Messages written in the browser are forwarded to the IRC server. In an IRC implementation, the gateway may exchange commands such as: NICK WebVisitor USER webvisitor 0 * :Web Chat User JOIN #chat PRIVMSG #chat :Hello everyone! These commands are simplified examples. A production implementation must handle IRC registration responses, server-specific requirements, message framing, and other protocol details. 6. Why Mobile Compatibility Is Important Older IRC clients were designed primarily for desktop computers. Modern users expect chat applications to work comfortably on smartphones and tablets. A mobile-friendly web chat application should consider: Responsive layouts for different screen sizes Readable messages and accessible input controls Efficient bandwidth usage Connection recovery after network interruptions Clear notifications about disconnected sessions Touch-friendly navigation Mobile connectivity introduces additional challenges. When a user switches from Wi-Fi to mobile data or moves an application into the background, the browser connection may be interrupted. Developers should therefore implement reliable reconnect logic and clear session-state handling. However, browsers impose background execution restrictions. A web application cannot guarantee a permanently active connection when the device or operating system suspends it. 7. Security Considerations for Web-Based IRC Clients Removing Java applets does not automatically make a chat application secure. Modern chat platforms still need carefully designed security controls. Encrypted transport: Use HTTPS and secure WebSockets ( wss:// ). When connecting from a gateway to an IRC server, use TLS where supported. Input handling: Treat all user-submitted messages as untrusted. Display chat content safely to prevent cross-site scripting. Authentication: Protect passwords and session credentials. Do not expose IRC authentication secrets in publicly accessible client code. Abuse prevention: Introduce appropriate rate limits, connection limits, and moderation mechanisms. Session management: Handle reconnects, nickname collisions, unexpected disconnections, and expired sessions correctly. Security should be designed into the application rather than added after deployment. 8. Java-Free Chat in Practice For users, the main advantage of modern browser chat is simplicity. They can open a website, enter a nickname, and begin participating in a conversation without installing an old Java plugin. For developers, however, delivering that simple experience involves networking, protocol handling, interface design, and connection management. For a user-oriented explanation of Java-free chat, the Turkish-language javasız sohbet guide provides additional background about accessing chat rooms through a browser. Understanding both the user experience and the technical architecture helps developers build more accessible real-time communication systems. 9. Is Traditional IRC Still Relevant? IRC remains an interesting technology because of its relatively simple protocol and established channel-based communication model. Although modern messaging platforms offer additional capabilities, IRC continues to provide useful lessons about: Client-server architecture Message routing Network protocols Channel management Nickname registration Real-time communication Combining IRC with a modern web interface can make an established communication protocol accessible to users who have never installed a traditional IRC client. The important part is choosing an architecture appropriate for the application's requirements. Final Thoughts The transition from Java applets to modern browser technologies represents a significant improvement in web-based communication. WebSockets, JavaScript, secure gateways, and responsive user interfaces allow developers to create real-time chat experiences without requiring visitors to install Java. For developers interested in networking and web applications, building a basic browser-based IRC client can also be a valuable learning project. What would you choose for a new real-time chat application: an IRC gateway, WebSockets with a custom backend, or another messaging architecture? Share your thoughts in the comments.

title: I built a tutor that circles your math mistake in red pen
body: This is a submission for the MLH x DEV Writing Challenge What I Built Somo (Swahili for "lesson") is a math tutor you use by taking a photo. You snap a problem along with your handwritten working. Somo finds the exact line where the working goes wrong, circles it in red pen the way a teacher would, and then teaches the idea in English, Swahili or Spanish. What inspired it I grew up in Tanzania. Primary school is taught in Swahili. Secondary school switches every subject to English, and you sit the NECTA national exams in a language you're still learning. Plenty of students understand the math and get stuck on the words. I see the same thing with English learners in New York. Most AI tools will solve the problem for you. I wanted to explore something different: could an AI tell a student why they went wrong, in the language they think in? I built Somo in one day to find out. How it works Snap. Photograph the problem and your working. Diagnose. Gemini reads the handwriting and returns structured JSON with the transcription, the concept, the first wrong line, and why it's wrong. The UI circles that line in red. Confirm. Somo shows "Here's what I read," and you confirm it or correct it before any teaching happens. Teach. A short lesson streams in. It covers the idea, where it went wrong, an everyday analogy (a market scale, a subway fare), a worked example with different numbers so the answer isn't given away, and the English exam terms you'll need. Check. You answer one question. Get it wrong and you get a simpler re-explanation with a new analogy. Get it right and you can practice on a real past exam question found live on the web. What I learned Reliability is most of AI engineering. The prompts were the easy part. The work went into everything around them: Self-verification. A second, independent model call solves the problem without seeing the diagnosis . If the two answers disagree, the student sees "I'm not fully sure I read this right." Verification can't catch reading mistakes. One of my test photos was a printed question that had lost its formatting. Both model calls read it the same wrong way, and they agreed with each other. That's why the human-in-the-loop confirm step exists: the student can see the paper, and the model can't always. Failover is a feature. Gemini's free quota ran out mid-build. I routed every call through one function: try Gemini, retry once on a 503/429, then fall back to Claude, with a circuit breaker that skips Gemini for 60 seconds after a quota error. Diagnosis went from ~116 seconds (waiting on an overloaded model) to ~10 seconds . Honest labels. My pipeline once showed a UK worksheet as a "real past exam" question. Now every question is labeled past exam paper , practice question from the web , or written by Somo , and off-topic questions are rejected. In testing, Somo found the exact wrong line on all three of my handwritten test problems: a halving error (2B = 8 → B = 3), a dropped minus sign when rearranging, and multiplying the two sides of an equation by different numbers. No students have used it; every test problem was written by me. Demo The stack is a FastAPI backend with Server-Sent Events for streaming, plus a single-file mobile interface styled like a school exercise book: grid paper, a red margin line, and a handwriting font for the teacher's notes. Partner Technologies Google Gemini (and Gemma 4) Gemini ( gemini-flash-latest through the google-genai SDK) does the hard multimodal work. The key was structured output . Instead of parsing free text, the diagnosis is validated against a Pydantic schema: response = client . models . generate_content ( model = " gemini-flash-latest " , contents = [ photo , DIAGNOSE_PROMPT ], config = types . GenerateContentConfig ( response_mime_type = " application/json " , response_schema = Diagnosis , # transcription, concept, error_step, final_answer... ), ) diagnosis = response . parsed Because error_step is a real field, the UI knows exactly which line to circle. Gemini also streams the lessons and writes the check questions. Gemma 4 ( gemma-4-26b-a4b-it , served through the same Gemini API) handles the frequent, low-stakes work: grading answers and deciding whether two answers are equivalent ("x = 4" vs "4"). It's fast and cheap, so it's a good fit for checks that run on every answer. Nimble Nimble turned "practice more" into "practice the real exam." When a lesson starts, a background job asks Nimble to search the live web for past papers on the student's concept, starting with official sites: response = nimble . search ( query = f " NECTA CSEE Basic Mathematics past paper { concept } " , max_results = 5 , search_depth = " standard " , full_content = True , include_domains = [ " necta.go.tz " , " maktaba.tetea.org " ], ) US students get NY Regents question banks ( jmap.org , nysedregents.org ) instead, and if the official sites return nothing, Somo searches the open web. Nimble found the right documents: official NECTA (Tanzania's National Examinations Board) Basic Mathematics papers and examiner reports from 2017 to 2023. But for PDFs, search results came back as ~300–700 character summaries, with no questions in them. The fix was to treat Nimble as the finder : when a result is a short PDF, Somo downloads it, extracts up to 20,000 characters with pypdf (five papers in parallel), and Gemini picks one question that appears word for word and tests the same concept. NECTA's Candidates' Item Response Analysis reports turned out to be gold, because they quote every exam question verbatim. The first real result was a matrix word problem from the NECTA CSEE 2023 Basic Mathematics paper, which gets shown with an exam stamp and a link to the source. Results are cached to disk with fuzzy topic matching, so each topic is searched only once. Sentry Somo makes a lot of calls to several providers, so I wanted to see what it was actually doing. Every Gemini, Gemma, Claude and Nimble call is a Sentry span, and background jobs (verification, question prep, past-paper search) are their own transactions: with sentry_sdk . start_span ( op = " gen_ai.chat " , name = f " gemini { label } " ) as span : span . set_data ( " model " , model ) result = gemini_call () Every Gemini → Claude failover also raises a warning issue, so the issues list became a timeline of when and why the app switched providers. Then Sentry found a real bug. The trace waterfall for one past-paper search showed a single NECTA server taking 3.6 minutes to send one PDF. I had a 12-second timeout, but httpx applies it per chunk , so a server trickling data never trips it. The fix was a hard deadline on the whole download: deadline = time . time () + 12 with httpx . stream ( " GET " , url , timeout = 12 ) as r : for chunk in r . iter_bytes (): data . extend ( chunk ) if time . time () > deadline : raise TimeoutError ( " download took over 12s " ) The worst case dropped from about 4 minutes to about 30 seconds. I wouldn't have found that one from logs. No student photos or prompt text are sent to Sentry ( send_default_pii=False ). Hackathon Experience I attended the AI Engineer NYC Hackathon , a one-day MLH event on October 11, 2026. I came in without a team and without an idea, so the morning was brainstorming. I narrowed it down to education because of my own background, then spent most of the day building. What I'll remember most: Building alongside coding agents. I started with Gemini CLI, which hit its usage limit partway through, so I switched to working with Claude. It changed how I worked: I spent my time on design decisions and testing with real handwritten problems, and less on typing boilerplate. The sponsor talks paid off. I hadn't planned to use Nimble until the sponsor presentation. It ended up being the feature I'm proudest of. Real-world friction. The venue wifi wouldn't let my phone reach my laptop, my Gemini quota ran out, and a government server was very slow. Each one forced a better design. The 5 PM deadline was tight. I froze features at 3:45, then wrote the README, recorded a demo, and submitted with minutes to spare. Thanks to MLH and the sponsors for a great day of building.

title: Moving Daily Jobs from GitHub Actions to cron‑job.org for a Render‑Free API
body: Moving Daily Jobs from GitHub Actions to cron‑job.org for a Render‑Free API TL;DR: I replaced the internal setTimeout‑based schedulers and GitHub Actions cron with an external cron‑job.org trigger plus a lightweight “wake” endpoint. This prevents the Render free instance from sleeping and guarantees daily email, report, and cleanup jobs run on schedule. The Problem Our API ( playamxcrm-api ) runs on Render’s free tier. Render idles the container after ~15 minutes of inactivity, which means any setTimeout / setInterval ‑based internal schedulers never fire. The symptom was obvious in the logs: [cron] Scheduler started… [error] TimeoutError: Request failed with status code 503 (Service Unavailable) The daily jobs (email digests, monthly reports, tour cleanup) were supposed to be kicked off by a GitHub Actions workflow ( cron-diario.yml ). However, the workflow hit the same sleeping API, causing 30‑second request cut‑offs enforced by cron‑job.org and occasional 503 responses from Render. What I Tried First Rely on internal timers – startEmailCron() , startReportCron() , etc., were started on server boot. GitHub Actions cron – A workflow ran curl -X POST https://playamxcrm-api.onrender.com/internal/cron/daily at 07:00 UTC. Both approaches failed: The internal timers never resumed after the container slept. The GitHub Actions job sometimes executed before the container woke, hitting Render’s 30 s request timeout and returning 503 Service Unavailable . I attempted to add a “keep‑alive” ping from the workflow before the real job, but the 30 s limit on cron‑job.org made it unreliable. The Implementation 1. External Cron Service (cron‑job.org) I switched to a dedicated external cron that calls a lightweight endpoint every minute to keep the API alive, and a separate endpoint for the actual daily job at 07:00 UTC. .github/workflows/cron-diario.yml (trimmed diff) - name: ⏰ Cron diario — API PlayaMXCRM + name: ⏰ Cron diario — API PlayaMXCRM (respaldo manual) # The API runs on Render free plan, which sleeps after ~15 min without traffic. # We now rely on an external cron service (cron-job.org) to trigger the job. The workflow now only serves as a manual fallback; the real schedule lives in cron‑job.org. 2. New Environment Variable Added CRON_SECRET to differentiate external calls from internal ones. .env.example (diff) - # ── Cron externo ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── - # Si se define, los jobs diarios (correos, reporte mensual, resumen sema + # ── Cron externo ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── + # Si se define, los jobs diarios (correos, reporte mensual, resumen semanal) + # se ejecutan sin depender de los timers internos. + CRON_SECRET=super‑secret‑string The secret is read in the controller to bypass the internal “sleep guard”. 3. Cron Trigger Controller Refactored apps/api/src/cron/cron-trigger.controller.ts to: Detect external triggers via CRON_SECRET . Return early for keep‑alive pings (HTTP GET) and only run the heavy job on a POST with a valid secret. @@ - * Por qué existe: la API corre en el plan free de Render, que la duerme tras ~15 min sin - * tráfico. Los setTimeout/setInterval de startEmailCron() & cía. nunca lleg + * Por qué existe: la API corre en el plan free de Render, que la duerme tras ~15 min sin + * tráfico. title: Akpabio insists on jail term for attempted suicide as Senate passes decriminalisation bill for second reading
body:
A bill seeking to decriminalise attempted suicide in Nigeria has passed second reading in the Senate, despite Senate President Godswill Akpabio insisting that people who survive suicide attempts should remain liable to imprisonment.
during Tuesday’s plenary after a majority of senators supported it through a voice vote.
The bill was subsequently referred to the Senate Committees on Health (Secondary and Tertiary) and Judiciary, Human Rights and Legal Matters for further legislative action.
The bill, sponsored the senator representing Cross River South Senatorial District, Asuquo Ekpenyong, seeks to decriminalise attempted suicide and establish a legal framework for suicide prevention, treatment and support for survivors of suicide attempts.
It also seeks to address the conflict between existing criminal laws that punish attempted suicide and the National Mental Health Act, which recognises the need for medical intervention in mental health emergencies.
Leading the debate on the bill, Mr Ekpenyong argued that while the National Mental Health Act recognises attempted suicide as a psychiatric emergency requiring treatment, Section 327 of the Criminal Code and Section 231 of the Penal Code criminalise the act.
He said the provisions were contradictory and required legislative intervention.
The senator manitained that the bill seeks to replace punitive measures with appropriate medical assessment, treatment and continuing support for survivors of suicide attempts.
He warned that criminalising attempted suicide could discourage people from seeking help, encourage families to conceal such incidents and prevent health workers from reporting cases promptly.
He added that treating suicide attempts as criminal offences could deepen the stigma surrounding mental health conditions and undermine efforts to obtain reliable data for national suicide prevention programmes.
Most senators who participated in the debate supported the bill.
Dayo Faduyile, the senator for Ondo South and a medical doctor, said attempted suicide should be treated as a medical emergency rather than a criminal offence.
He argued that depression and other mental health conditions could impair a person’s judgement, making treatment and recovery more appropriate responses than punishment.
Mr Faduyile also noted that some people who survived suicide attempts had subsequently died by suicide while in detention.
He warned that imprisonment or police custody could not adequately address the underlying medical conditions that might lead to suicide attempts.
“The best way to treat anybody who did not succumb to a suicide attempt is actually not to criminalise it. They need help,” he said.
Bauchi Central Senator, Abdul Ningi, also argued that the circumstances surrounding suicide attempts were often linked to mental health challenges and should be addressed through medical intervention rather than punitive measures.
However, Senate Leader Opeyemi Bamidele cautioned that some provisions of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act did not automatically apply across all states, depending on the legal frameworks adopted by their respective Houses of Assembly.
Mr Bamidele said the Senate needed to establish the extent to which the proposed amendment would apply nationally before proceeding with the legislation.
Responding to the debate, Mr Akpabio argued that attempted suicide should remain punishable by imprisonment, warning that removing the penalties could encourage the act.
“If you attempt suicide, make sure you die. Anyone who attempts and fails will go to jail,” he said.
The senate president also called for adequate input from state Houses of Assembly, urging state lawmakers to express their views on the bill during the public hearing to avoid potential legal conflicts.
Under Nigeria’s existing criminal laws, attempted suicide remains a punishable offence, although the 1999 Constitution does not expressly criminalise the act.
Section 327 of the Criminal Code Act provides for up to one year’s imprisonment for anyone who attempts to take their own life, while Section 231 of the Penal Code prescribes up to one year’s imprisonment, a fine or both. The applicable provisions and penalties may vary across jurisdictions.
The existing legal framework has, however, raised concerns about its compatibility with the National Mental Health Act, 2021, which recognises attempted suicide as a psychiatric emergency requiring immediate intervention. The law defines psychiatric emergencies to include attempted suicide and provides a framework for mental healthcare and support.

title: Naftali Bennett unveils B’Yachad party plan to cut bureaucracy, boost support for olim
body: The next government will cut bureaucracy, address the challenges facing olim (new immigrants), and help them build successful lives in Israel, former prime minister Naftali Bennett, who leads the B'Yachad party, told The Jerusalem Post on Tuesday.B'Yachad is one of the leading parties in the opposition bloc seeking to replace Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in the October 27 election. On Tuesday, the party released the details of its plan for helping olim.“From my own family's experience, I know the challenges that face olim. Professionally, personally, and beyond. In many ways, aliyah, its growth, and the success of olim here is a canary in the coal mine for Israeli society as a whole,” Bennett said.“Is our government building an Israel where Jews believe they and their families can be safe, earn a living, and build their futures? Is our government making life easier here – or harder?” he asked.“By tackling the specific challenges facing olim head-on and fixing all that's broken in Israel, we will once again make the answers to those questions: 'Yes.'”Support for olim, cutting bureaucracy, assistance with homes and jobs“With that, we will bring even more olim who will continue to be a vital part of what makes Israel the amazing country it is. Together, we'll make it happen,” Bennett told the Post.The aliyah plan focuses on support for olim by calling to cut bureaucracy and help them find homes and jobs, while it calls to ensure they find their place as “integral members of Israeli society.”Some aspects of the plan include reducing bureaucracy by creating a single office for every new immigrant to attend to receive benefits and services, rather than needing to deal with many different agencies.The plan also demands streamlining the recognition of foreign higher education accreditation to make it easier for olim to work within their professions.Bennett added that another aim of the B'Yachad plan is to expand support for young olim by easing their transition into education, the workforce, and Israeli society as a whole, thus reducing the rate of departures.B'Yachad said it would work to “bring home the over 250,000 Israelis who have left the country in recent years.”The party said additionally that it would work to strengthen support for lone soldiers, giving them increased benefits and advance living stipends for discharged lone soldiers who require them.B'Yachad also called to work toward helping older citizens by advancing expanded employment, volunteering, and recreational opportunities to help combat loneliness among the senior population.Bennett's party called for Israel to be a “Jewish, democratic, liberal, and prosperous country that offers a promising future for both their careers and families.”

title: Adeleke Isn’t Our Party Leader, Can’t Compel Osun People To Vote Tinubu – Olawepo-Hashim
body: The Accord Party’s presidential candidate for the 2027 election, Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim, has dismissed suggestions that Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke’s endorsement of President Bola Tinubu would influence the state’s voters in the presidential election. Olawepo-Hashim spoke on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Tuesday, following the announcement of Adeleke, the Accord Party’s only elected governor, as a member of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council. He rejected the suggestion that Adeleke’s position as the party’s only elected governor made him its national leader. “He (Adeleke) can’t be the leader, he is a governor that was a beneficiary of office. When you have a party, you have the executive, the executive leaders of the party are the leaders of the party,” Olawepo-Hashim said. ﻿ Adeleke won re-election for a second term as Osun State governor in August and has reiterated his support for Tinubu’s re-election. However, Olawepo-Hashim argued that the governor could not dictate how the people of the state would vote in the presidential election. “The fact that he won his election as governor, Governor Adeleke cannot compel the people of Osun State to vote for Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu. Osun people let me repeat are incredibly honourable people, what we call Omoluabi in Yoruba parlance, they are ideological, they have great history, they are not conquered people, they do what they believe. “So, I still believe that regardless of what Governor Adeleke is doing, Osun people are still going to vote for Accord Party at the presidential election. I can bet on that by the grace of God.” The Accord Party candidate described the 2027 election as unusual, claiming that many Nigerians had already decided against voting for the APC and Tinubu. He accused the Tinubu-led government of mismanaging the economy, undermining national unity and worsening insecurity. He also accused the administration of showing little compassion for ordinary Nigerians, whom he said were living in abject poverty. Olawepo-Hashim maintained that the election would be determined by the performance of the Tinubu administration rather than the individual candidates. He also expressed confidence in his chances, claiming that Tinubu would not secure 20 per cent of the votes if the election were held today. title: Three-star will head Army’s new autonomy command, which will initially focus on corps-level systems
body: The Army’s new autonomy command will be led by a three-star general and start building autonomous systems at the corps-level as one of its first tasks, service officials said Tuesday. Acting Secretary of the Army Adam Telle established Futures and Autonomous Systems Command (FASCOM) on Oct. 1, a new unit the service wants to build out in the wake of the Pentagon’s autonomy focused combatant command announcement late last month. Now the Army is attempting to grow teeth for its new autonomy effort, also by designating Fort Rucker, Alabama as its “UAS Autonomy Center of Excellence,” highlighting several domains it intends to test autonomous technology, and redesignating a separate unit as FASCOM. “This goes beyond drones,” said Acting Army Chief of Staff Gen. Christopher LaNeve. “FASCOM will pioneer operational concepts that harness autonomous capabilities across all warfighting functions.” Some of the Army’s new Robotics Technician Integrators, the first batch of which graduated earlier this month, will get sent to FASCOM-supported experimental units as a way to help proliferate autonomous systems across the force, service officials said. While the announcement delivered during the annual AUSA conference in Washington, D.C. said a three-star will head FASCOM, the service did not disclose who that leader will be. A service press release said that LaNeve tasked FASCOM with developing corps-level autonomous capabilities, specifically mentioning autonomous fires and watercraft units, as well as armored reconnaissance, breaching, manned-unmanned rotary aircraft and aerial surveillance formations. The pairing of manned and unmanned rotary aircraft, which began at Rucker, according to the Army, is intended to give aviators access to UAS sensors for “over-the-horizon” targeting. Officials said that FASCOM will create “capability-based formations” focused on long-range fires, protection, tanks, logistics and obstacle breaching. LaNeve redesignated Futures and Concepts Command (FCC) as FASCOM, which will “integrate and ultimately accelerate” the work of FCC’s subordinate commands, according to the service, including Combat Capabilities Development Command, Medical Research and Development Command and the Joint Modernization Command. Lt. Gen. Michael McCurry is the current commander of FCC. title: Officials say N.S. had ‘most successful’ year for doctor recruitment, but gaps in care remain
body:
Officials in Nova Scotia say efforts to bring doctors to the province have been working, citing last year as a record year for recruitment.
Leaders in physician recruitment told a legislative committee Tuesday that the province has welcomed more than 1,000 doctors to the province since 2020.
“Last year was our most successful recruitment year,” said Katrina Philopoulos, Nova Scotia Health’s physician recruitment director.
“We welcomed 278 physicians to the province, including 111 family medicine physicians — a 25 per cent increase from the year before — and 167 specialists, resulting in a net gain of 199 doctors.”
She noted that the province is on track for another strong year in recruitment, with 126 physicians recruited and practising so far.
Internationally-trained physicians account for 40 per cent of all physician recruitment.
“These results are not by accident. They are the outcome of a deliberate strategy, a sustained investment, and strong partnership across the health-care system,” she said, adding there’s still more work to do.
Opposition critics point out the shortfalls in the health-care system, especially in women’s health.
“There are emails in my inboxes, folks who are determined that they’re never going to be able to have a child in Nova Scotia because their wait for gynecological care is so long,” said NDP MLA Lisa Lachance.
“I just want to say that there’s lots of places where we still have gaps.”
The province currently has two vacancies for OB/GYNs, or obstetrician-gynecologists.
Kathleen DeCoste, senior executive director with the province’s Office of Healthcare Professionals Recruitment, told the committee the government is working on improvements.
“What I can say is we’re looking at those numbers. We’re looking at those wait times. We’re looking at what Nova Scotians need,” she said.
“And we’re trying our best to plan for what the system needs to look like to meet those needs.”
Meanwhile, the latest doctor waitlist update shows that as of Sept. 1, there are 52,771 names registered. That’s a decline of just over 1,800 people from the previous month.

title: Russia, North Korea struggling together amid tectonic geopolitical shifts — diplomat
body:
MOSCOW, October 13. /TASS/. Moscow and Pyongyang are consolidating their efforts to establish a fair world order amid tectonic geopolitical shifts, Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Andrey Rudenko said at a gala reception on the 78th anniversary of diplomatic relations between Russia and North Korea.
"Today, amid challenging tectonic geopolitical shifts, Russia and North Korea are taking a consolidated stance on key issues on the regional and international agenda. They are struggling shoulder to shoulder to establish a truly just multipolar world order. We stand ready to continue doing everything in our power to achieve the goals set by the leaders of our countries, both within the framework of the strategic dialogue between the foreign ministers and through contacts at other levels," he said.
Russia, in his words, is satisfied to see the high dynamics of the development of bilateral cooperation in various spheres, including in practical fields.
The reception at the North Korean embassy was attended by Ambassador Sin Hong Chol, as well as high-ranking officials, diplomats, and experts from the two countries.

title: Senate asks FG to release ecological funds to tackle erosion, landslides in Cross River
body:
The Senate has asked the federal government to release funds from the Ecological Fund to Cross River State to address erosion and landslides that have claimed several lives and displaced residents.
The upper chamber made the call on Tuesday after adopting a motion sponsored by the senator representing Cross River South Senatorial District, Asuquo Ekpenyong, on the need to address the state’s worsening ecological crisis.
Moving the motion, Mr Ekpenyong said erosion and landslides threaten lives and property in several communities, particularly in Calabar metropolis, including Atakpa, Edim Otop, Ikot Effangha Mkpa, Nyaghasang, Ikot Anwatim, Nasarawa/Bacoco, Akai Effa, Bayside, Summit Hills and Anansa.
The senator referenced an incident in July in which a landslide at Ikot Anwatim killed five people, including four siblings from the same family. The incident also destroyed two houses and left two other residents injured.
He also reported another landslide in Edim Otop that killed an eight-year-old girl, warning that more lives could be lost if the underlying causes were not urgently addressed.
Mr Ekpenyong identified poorly designed drainage systems, indiscriminate waste disposal, unregulated sand mining, vegetation removal and vandalism of drainage infrastructure as factors worsening erosion in the state.
He urged the Senate to prevail on the federal government to approve, allocate and release adequate funding from the Ecological Fund for emergency stabilisation and comprehensive erosion-control measures, prioritising communities where lives have been lost and residents remain at immediate risk.
The senator also called on the Federal Ministry of Environment, in collaboration with the Cross River State Government and relevant agencies, to immediately assess high-risk locations and commence appropriate emergency protection works.
He further urged the Federal Ministries of Environment and Works to prioritise funding for erosion-control projects in the state and ensure that major interventions are supported by proper geotechnical and hydrological assessments, sound engineering designs, effective supervision and environmental safeguards.
The motion and its prayers received the support of the majority of senators during a voice vote.
Following its adoption, Senate President Godswill Akpabio directed the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) to work with the Cross River State Emergency Management Agency and affected local government councils to provide temporary shelter, food, medical care and psychosocial support to bereaved and displaced families.
Mr Akpabio also directed NEMA to facilitate the safe evacuation and temporary relocation of residents facing imminent danger, while establishing effective early-warning systems and monitoring unstable locations.
He further mandated the Senate Committee on Environment to inspect affected communities, assess existing interventions and engage relevant agencies on funding and implementation.
The committee is expected to report back to the Senate with recommendations for further legislative action.
The Ecological Fund was established in 1981 to enable the government to address serious environmental problems across the country, including erosion, flooding, desertification and other ecological emergencies. It is administered through a funding arrangement that provides shares for the federal, state and local governments to address ecological challenges within their respective jurisdictions.
Under the existing sharing formula, 1 per cent of the fund goes to the federal government, while states receive 0.72 per cent and local governments 0.60 per cent. The federal government’s share is further distributed among the Ecological Project Office and other designated agencies, including the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA).
The Ecological Project Office, domiciled in the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, coordinates ecological intervention projects across the country.
However, the fund faces competing demands from communities affected by environmental degradation. In May 2024, the Ecological Project Office called for increased funding, saying available resources were insufficient to meet the growing requests for intervention projects across the country.
Nigeria continues to face significant ecological challenges, including gully erosion, flooding, landslides and desertification. The World Bank has identified poor land and water management, inadequate planning, environmental degradation and climate variability as factors contributing to these problems. Such hazards threaten lives and livelihoods, destroy homes and infrastructure, and place additional pressure on public resources.

title: Port of Los Angeles Sets All-Time Cargo Record as Imports Surge
body:
Essential news coupled with the finest maritime content sourced from across the globe.
The Pier 300 channel at the Port of Los Angeles. Photo courtesy Port of Los Angeles
The Port of Los Angeles handled a record 1,042,652 twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs) in September, marking the busiest month in its 118-year history as strong consumer demand and shifting global trade routes continued to drive cargo volumes through the nation’s busiest container port.
September’s total surpassed the previous monthly record, set in July 2025, by more than 20,000 TEUs. It also capped the port’s busiest quarter on record, with nearly 3 million TEUs handled between July and September.
The port moved nearly 4 million TEUs over the four months beginning in June, another all-time high.
“September was a month for the record books, and it was part of an extraordinary run for the Port of Los Angeles,” said Executive Director Gene Seroka. “Consumer demand remains resilient, importers are replenishing inventories and more cargo is being allocated to Los Angeles as shippers navigate continued challenges along other global trade routes.”
Loaded imports reached 545,696 TEUs in September, up 19% from a year earlier, while loaded exports climbed 10% to 125,751 TEUs. Empty container movements totaled approximately 371,206 TEUs, also a monthly record.
Seroka attributed the strong performance in part to greater certainty around tariffs, which have fallen from levels seen earlier this year, allowing importers to replenish inventories. Continued consumer spending and disruptions affecting the Suez and Panama Canal routes have also contributed to the surge.
The results extend an unusually strong shipping season that has repeatedly defied expectations. In September, the National Retail Federation revised its import forecast upward , predicting September would become the busiest month of the year for container imports at major U.S. ports.
Earlier in the year, retailers accelerated shipments to get ahead of tariff changes and supply chain uncertainty, raising expectations that the traditional late-summer peak would arrive early. Instead, cargo volumes have remained elevated.
Los Angeles has been among the biggest beneficiaries. The port surpassed 1 million TEUs in June before recording another strong month in July and continuing its momentum through August and September.
Speaking during the port’s monthly media briefing, Harvard Business School professor Willy Shih said ongoing trade uncertainty is changing how companies manage their supply chains.
“Companies are moving from purely optimizing for cost to optimizing for options,” Shih said. “With so much uncertainty in global trade, businesses are looking for greater flexibility in where they source, manufacture and move their goods.”
For the first nine months of 2026, the Port of Los Angeles handled nearly 8.1 million TEUs, more than 3% ahead of the same period last year.
The record comes despite continued pressure on global shipping from tariffs, high fuel costs and geopolitical disruptions. Those challenges have complicated cargo forecasting and encouraged shippers to adjust traditional routing and inventory strategies.
Whether the momentum continues through the remainder of the year remains uncertain. The National Retail Federation’s September forecast called for U.S. import volumes to ease in October and November following the late-season surge.
For now, Los Angeles continues to handle cargo at a historic pace.
“Our waterfront workforce and supply chain partners have done a tremendous job handling these record volumes while keeping cargo moving,” Seroka said. “After the best month, quarter and four-month stretch in Port history, our focus is simple: finish the year strong and keep delivering for our customers.”

title: US, Israel prepare to resume hostilities against Iran before polls in both states — Axios
body:
WASHINGTON, October 13. /TASS/. The US and Israel are readying to resume a large-scale military operation against Iran before the parliamentary elections in Israel on October 27 and the midterm elections to the US Congress on November 3, Axios quoted US administration sources as saying.
According to it, US President Donald Trump and Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu last week discussed "the possibility of launching a major new operation against Iran before the Israeli and US elections." The portal said the discussion took place before Trump said on October 8 that the US would not strike Iran before the Congressional elections. "But the Israeli and US militaries are still on alert and concluding preparations to be ready in case he changes his mind," Axios said.
According to the portal’s sources, "Netanyahu and Trump spoke about a potential joint US-Israeli operation that would hit military and nuclear targets" of the Islamic Republic. According to Axios, the main proponents of resuming a large-scale military operation against Iran within the US administration are Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth and the US Central Command (CENTCOM). At the same time, most of Trump’s advisers advocate maintaining economic and other forms of pressure on Tehran. On October 13, Trump said the US would soon decide on further actions against Iran.
The US and Israel launched a war against Iran on February 28. In June, Washington and Tehran signed a memorandum of understanding providing for an immediate cessation of hostilities on all fronts, including in Lebanon. However, on the night of July 8, the United States resumed large-scale strikes against Iran, accusing it of violating the agreements on the Strait of Hormuz. About 25% of the world’s oil and about 20% of liquefied natural gas are transported through it. Later the American administration effectively signaled its intention to cease the use of large-scale military force against Iran and to shift to an attempt to choke it through sanctions.

title: Ukrainian scouts used a captured Russian soldier’s radio to gather intelligence for four days
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Ukrainian reconnaissance troops used a captured Russian soldier’s radio for four days to listen to Russian military communications and relay important intelligence to their command, according to a report by ArmyInform, which covered the episode. The soldiers serve in the 23rd Separate Reconnaissance Battalion, which operates in the Oleksandrivka sector, the report noted. Russia uses infiltration tactics involving small groups to slip through Ukrainian positions undetected, establish themselves into the rear of Ukrainian positionse, and create conditions for the further advance of its main forces. They are countered not only by reconnaissance drones but also by specialized reconnaissance teams, which sometimes cover several dozen kilometers on foot to reach their designated targets. Ukrainian scouts capture Russian soldier in the grey zone Ukrainian reconnaissance troops captured a Russian soldier in the grey zone as he was trying to enter a neighboring house, the report said. “He took off his body armour and set his rifle aside. He felt right at home. Our commander went over and offered him a chance to surrender, and he agreed. He then stayed with us for four days. He told us everything he knew,” a soldier with the call sign Kubik said in the report. The soldiers’ hideout was later discovered. Fleeing a Ukrainian drone, a Russian infantryman ran into the building where the reconnaissance troops were staying. The position was subsequently attacked by FPV drones, followed by an artillery barrage. Reconnaissance soldier with the call sign “Kubik” of the 23rd Separate Reconnaissance Battalion, 2026. Photo: ArmyInform One Ukrainian soldier sustained a minor injury, but the group managed to withdraw without suffering serious losses. Reconnaissance soldier Kubik spent 23 days on a combat mission For reconnaissance troops, the journey to their positions and the return trip remain perhaps the most dangerous parts of a mission. During his year of service, Kubik has completed five combat missions, one of which lasted 23 days, according to the report. During their most recent mission, the soldiers covered 20 kilometers on foot in one direction, moving mostly through tree lines, Kubik said. He added that they had to run across open areas and destroy enemy drones lying in wait before quickly retreating to cover. Because of the constant threat from the air, the length of time reconnaissance troops can remain at their positions depends on the weather and the situation, the report noted. Sometimes, staying in place longer is safer than risking exposure while a team is being replaced. Dzhus’s first mission: 20-year-old reconnaissance soldier chooses infantry Twenty-year-old Mykyta, whose call sign is Dzhus, is preparing for his first combat mission as part of the 23rd Separate Reconnaissance Battalion, the report said. He joined the military under the “18–24 Contract” program after leaving the police force. “Many people who join under the ‘18–24’ contract go into UAV operations, but I’m more interested in infantry work. We have many experienced reconnaissance soldiers, and the guys are constantly giving advice and sharing their experience,” Dzhus said. Reconnaissance soldier with the call sign “Dzhus” of the 23rd Separate Reconnaissance Battalion, 2026. Photo: ArmyInform He is heading out on the mission under the guidance of an experienced commander, he said. The soldiers prepare thoroughly for every mission, practicing at the training ground and rehearsing procedures tailored to the specific task, the media outlet noted. Russian troops seek new hiding places for infiltration along the front Russian forces continue to use small-group infiltration tactics. For example, the Russian army is likely increasing its infiltration efforts in Kharkiv Oblast, taking advantage of the remaining summer foliage for concealment, the Institute for the Study of War reported on 9 October. In particular, Russian forces are seeking to infiltrate the city of Kupiansk in small groups, according to an RBC-Ukraine report published on 7 October. Similar incidents have also been reported in Donetsk Oblast. Russian troops are attempting to infiltrate the gaps between Ukrainian observation posts in small groups and establish positions there, Artem Prybilnov, spokesperson for the 155th Separate Mechanized Brigade, said during a broadcast on Suspilne.Studio on 7 October, NV reported . Their aim is to build up forces for a further advance toward Dobropillia. Ukrainian infantry, working alongside drone operators, is repelling the ongoing Russian attacks and preventing them from achieving this goal, Prybilnov added. As autumn sets in and vegetation becomes thinner, Russian troops find it increasingly difficult to conceal themselves in tree lines, Prybilnov noted. During the summer, they used these areas for cover and to accumulate personnel, ammunition, and equipment, the spokesperson said. Russian forces are now attempting to infiltrate villages, where they can hide in buildings and basements and establish positions, he added. title: Nigeria condemns death of citizen in South African police custody
body:
The Nigerian Consulate General in Johannesburg has called for a thorough investigation into the death of a Nigerian, Chimezie Odueze, allegedly tortured by officers of the South African Police Service (SAPS) in Cape Town.
In a statement issued on Tuesday, the Consul General, Ninikanwa Okey-Uche, said Mr Odueze died on 9 October in the Parklands area of Cape Town.
The consulate said reports that Mr Odueze was tortured by police officers before his death had caused shock and pain to his family, the Nigerian community and Nigeria’s two diplomatic missions in South Africa.
According to the statement, Mr Odueze was arrested at a shopping centre on suspicion of drug possession and taken to his home for a search. The consulate said no drugs were found at the residence, but the Nigerian national was allegedly tortured to death.
The consulate described the incident as one too many, saying the recurring reports of extrajudicial killings of Nigerians in South Africa raised serious concerns about the safety of Nigerians and other foreign nationals in the country.
It also warned against the stereotyping of Nigerians, saying some elements were disregarding South African legal processes and wrongfully generalising Nigerians in the country.
The consulate called on South African authorities to conduct a thorough investigation and ensure that those responsible were brought to justice.
“No matter what the allegations may be, there are processes and steps to justice,” Ms Okey-Uche said in the statement, insisting that suspects must be given a fair hearing in court and that no one should take the law into their own hands.
The consulate also urged Nigerians in South Africa to remain calm, law-abiding and security-conscious amid ongoing xenophobic and Afrophobic attacks and threats against foreigners.
It extended its condolences to Mr Odueze’s family and assured Nigerians that it would continue to press for their welfare and fair treatment in South Africa.
PREMIUM TIMES reports that about 1,640 Nigerians have been evacuated from South Africa since the recent wave of xenophobia began in April. A batch of 33 Nigerians was repatriated in August and another 105 in September.
At least five Nigerians have been killed since the latest round of violence began.
PREMIUM TIMES reported the most recent incident in July. The victim, Chika Simon, died during an encounter with the South African Police Service (SAPS)
The Nigerian consulate said he died under questionable circumstances.
This paper also reported previous deaths. These are: Amaramiro Emmanuel, Ekpenyong Andrew, Emeka Iroegbu and Musa Joe.
The Nigerian government has demanded a thorough investigation into the death of Nigerians killed in South Africa. The investigations into these cases are still pending, and no arrests have been made.

title: Binance Is Shutting Down Its Bitcoin Mining Pool After Six Years
body:
Binance will shut down its mining pool and several related services on Nov. 10, the exchange said in an announcement published Tuesday. The closure covers Binance Pool, Pool Savings, Cloud Mining, and Transaction Accelerator, along with Telegram hashrate alerts, email notifications, and the pool's API.
“As part of our ongoing review of products and services, Binance will discontinue Binance Pool and related services on 2026-11-10,” Binance wrote. “All Binance Pool-related services will be discontinued. Binance Pool will begin disconnecting mining connections, and Binance Mining Pool Stratum URLs and mining endpoints will be disabled. Hashrate submissions and mining shares submitted after this time will no longer be accepted, processed, or credited.”
A mining pool combines the computing power of many miners and splits block rewards among them based on the work each one contributes. Cloud Mining let users buy hashrate, a slice of mining power, without owning any hardware, while Transaction Accelerator helped users push through Bitcoin transactions that were slow to confirm because of low fees or network congestion.
Binance pool launched in April 2020 and ranked ninth among Bitcoin pools at the end of 2025, with about 26 exahashes per second, or 2.3% of the network, according to Hashrate Index . One exahash per second equals a quintillion guesses every second at the puzzle that earns a block.
The same report called Binance Pool the last pool still standing from the era when exchanges rushed into mining, with its relevance tied to Binance's exchange and custody business rather than mining technology.
Seems like Binance, just as Satoshi Nakamoto , wants to move onto other things. The shutdown arrives as Binance expands into traditional finance. On June 1, the exchange opened access to more than 7,000 US stocks and ETFs for customers outside the United States, with zero commission and fractional purchases from $5, according to co-CEO Richard Teng. It also previewed bStocks, a coming feature that lets users mint tokenized versions of the shares they buy on the BNB blockchain.
Quantmap co-founder Ivan Patriki told Decrypt at the time that large exchanges are moving into equities because they no longer want to depend on crypto market cycles. Vytautas Mackonis, COO of RWA protocol ALCUM, told Decrypt the offering is more structurally complex than it appears, with Binance as the interface, Nest Trading as the broker-dealer, and Alpaca Securities as the custodian.
Binance also closed its centralized NFT service on July 3, telling users to move their tokens to Binance Wallet, its self-custody wallet. Then-CEO Changpeng Zhao used the phrase “ smooth sunsetting of old products ” in 2023.
At 07:00 UTC on Nov. 10, Binance Pool will begin disconnecting miners and disable its Stratum URLs, the server addresses miners point their machines at to connect to the pool. Shares, the proofs of work that determine each miner's payout, will stop being credited after that time, while those submitted earlier count toward final rewards. Binance said eligible outstanding rewards, balances and refunds will be processed afterward, subject to its product rules, account status and compliance checks.
Miners must point their hardware to another pool before the cutoff, and Pool Savings users need to unsubscribe or redeem their positions before the service ends. Binance said the pool will keep operating normally until the cutoff. Anyone expecting a final payout has until 23:59 UTC on Nov. 10 to finish any required identity verification. Binance Pool pages will stay viewable until 07:00 UTC on Nov. 24, after which they become permanently inaccessible.

title: BAE Systems unveils new layered air-defense system
body: BAE Systems unveiled new layered air-defense systems designed to counter missiles and drones on Monday at the annual meeting of the Association of the United States Army. The international defense company introduced the Multi-Domain Artillery Cannon System, or MDACS, and the High-Power Microwave, or HPM, as complementary systems for protecting critical installations and field units. Travis Langer, BAE Systems’ communication manager, explained to Military Times that the systems together fill a capability gap created by evolving technological threats and the military’s traditional procurement process. “Both products complement existing air defense systems, but each offer a more cost-effective solution for defense against high-volume, low-cost threats allowing the preservation of high-value missiles for the most critical targets, which extends the life and effectiveness of the entire missile stockpile,” Langer said. The Multi-Domain Artillery Cannon System According to BAE Systems, MDACS forms the kinetic layer of the defensive shield, using precision-guided munitions called Hypervelocity Projectiles, or HVPs, for both offensive and defensive operations. “It fills a gap that traditional artillery cannot, providing a scalable layer of protection that complements existing high-tier systems,” Langer said, adding that it allows the Defense Department “to maintain a sustainable defense without draining the budget on every single engagement.” He explained MDACS combines high-accuracy guidance with the extreme velocity of the HVP. “We reduce the time-to-target and the window the enemy has to maneuver,” he said. “We are collaborating with the Army to integrate the organic sensor network and IBCS to ensure the system remains lethal even when GPS is unavailable.” Compared with traditional missiles, HVPs are smaller and less expensive, allowing troops to carry tens to hundreds of rounds in a magazine. Rather than relying on a rocket motor, the projectiles use what the company describes as a “low drag aerodynamic design” to achieve high velocities, maneuverability and extended range. For offensive operations, MDACS will fire the Scorpio-XR, the latest addition to the HVP family. Designed for artillery units, the projectile is expected to double the range of existing 155mm cannon-launched precision munitions, according to the company. Langer added that MDACs will use HVP rounds to engage air targets, counter-missile and Counter-Unmanned Aircraft System, or C-UAS, while the Scorpio-XR round will be used to defeat fixed and moving ground targets in contested environments. BAE Systems secured an Army agreement to develop a prototype of MDACS in January 2025, according to reports . The Army had planned to spend approximately $646 million on the project through fiscal year 2027. The High-Power Microwave BAE Systems describes its HPM system as a “scalable directed energy weapon” built with an emphasis on affordability. The company said 99% of the system’s components are commercial off-the-shelf parts. Unlike kinetic weapons, the HPM uses “focused electromagnetic energy” to neutralize airborne threats, specifically “high-volume, low-cost” threats, such as drone swarms, that can strain conventional air defenses. A video simulation of the system shows the HPM mounted on a trailer in a field. Its sensors automatically detect an approaching swarm of drones, prompting a large magnet to shift into position before the system unleashes what the company describes as “billions of pulses” at the airborne targets. Although the system remains in the prototype stage, BAE Systems said it has reached Technology Readiness Level 6, or TRL 6. That designation means a technology has been demonstrated in a relevant environment beyond laboratory testing. Layered air-defense Langer explained that the two systems are not specifically designed to be used together, but they could complement each other if the mission set requires it. “MDACS is C-130 transportable, allowing it to deliver rapid, high-rate firepower wherever the fight demands. It is designed to protect critical assets from drone attacks and missile threats, providing a scalable and efficient layer of protection,” he said. Whereas he called the HPM “an effective layer of wide-area protection” that can complement existing kinetic and missile systems. Langer said it creates “a comprehensive shield for armed forces installations and forward-deployed units.” As for when soldiers will begin fielding these new systems, Langer said they’re still prototypes. “Final testing and qualification decisions are made by the government,” he concluded.
