title: Cambridge Heavy Industries has been quietly building a desktop fusion device
body:
Fusion power usually conjures images of massive industrial facilities laced with large lasers or magnets, but a startup in Cambridge, Massachusetts, has been quietly building a device that can fit on a tabletop.
The optics of the device were on display behind Yun Kai, co-founder and CEO of Cambridge Heavy Industries , while he chatted with me on a video call. The company has been operating in stealth out of a small lab near MIT, and Kai gave TechCrunch an exclusive look at the technology it has been developing.
“We purposely built a small modular reactor. It’s tiny, it’s benchtop,” he told me. “Because it’s small, it makes everything easier.”
The small size has allowed Cambridge Heavy to experiment and iterate quickly. “The small module nature can enable 50 to 80 experiments, 50 to 80 shots per day,” he said. Data from those experiments will feed simulations that use AI to optimize the design.
That nimble approach has attracted investor attention. The startup recently raised a $6.2 million seed round led by Azolla Ventures with participation from Overlay, Neta Foundation, P3A, MassCEC, and the Rothrock family.
Cambridge Heavy’s fusion reactor uses lasers to compress a fuel target, similar to the groundbreaking experiment that proved controlled fusion reactions could produce more power than they consume. But unlike other inertial confinement designs, Cambridge Heavy’s minimizes the number of lasers required to spark fusion.
The system uses two main lasers to drive ignition. One laser is split into multiple beam lines that deliver light in concentric rings. Those rings of laser light are timed to hit the flat, round fuel target successively, starting from the outside and working in. The first ring starts a compression wave within the target that starts traveling inward. The subsequent laser rings are timed to boost the wave at just the right moment to further compress the fuel.
As the shock wave reaches the center of the target, a laser fires on the target, generating heat and producing a magnetic field. With the right amount of pressure and heat, fusion occurs.
Cambridge Heavy’s design generates high pressures with relatively low laser power, Kai said. The concept emerged from the lab of Keith Nelson, a chemist at MIT. There, researchers used the laser pulses to study materials under extreme conditions. As they ramped up pressures, they realized they were approaching fusion-ready conditions.
In about a decade, Cambridge Heavy plans to develop a power plant from the concept, though that’ll require scaling up the design. It will be larger than the current benchtop prototype, though not quite as large as other fusion power plants. Kai said it should be about the size of two basketball courts, and it will test whether the approach can generate enough energy to support a power plant.
Before that happens, though, Cambridge Heavy plans to use its smaller-scale devices to make tritium, a rare isotope of hydrogen that will be used by nearly all fusion power plants in the works today. Tritium sells for around $30,000 per gram today.
Each power plant won’t need a lot of tritium — on the order of grams per year — but the substance is so rare that only about 40 kilograms exist today. One recent study predicts that without new sources, the fusion power industry will be short by about 28 kilograms in 2054. At current prices, that’s about $840 million worth of tritium.
Fusion startups are in the process of designing fuel systems that will help the reactors be largely self-sufficient when it comes to tritium supplies, though they may need occasional top-ups. But that process could take up to 10 years, Kai said, giving Cambridge Heavy years of potential revenue as it pursues its power plant.

title: Large-scale Russian missile attack on Kyiv strikes power plants, residential buildings, killing 5, injuring 25
body:
The aftermath of a Russian missile strike on a Kyiv residential building late on Oct. 13, 2026. (Serhii Korovayny/The Kyiv Independent)
Russia launched yet another large-scale ballistic missile attack on Kyiv overnight on Oct. 13-14, wreaking destruction in a residential neighborhood and targeting several energy facilities in Kyiv.
Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi said that all three of the city's combined heat and power stations were attacked, as well as critical infrastructure in the Kyiv Oblast that provide power to Kyiv and central regions.
"The targets of Russian ballistic missiles were power system facilities in Kyiv, Kharkiv, and the region," he said.
"Overnight, the Russians deployed 39 ballistic missiles and more than 120 strike drones and loitering munitions against our energy and critical infrastructure in Kyiv, Kyiv Oblast, and Kharkiv," President Volodymyr Zelensky said in a post on social media , adding 600,000 people were currently without power.
"This was a targeted Russian ballistic strike specifically against the energy sector — an area regarding which the U.S. President had called for a ceasefire. The strike was entirely deliberate and demonstrative in its scale. Russia has never before shown such blatant disrespect toward America," he added.
Explosions were first heard in the capital beginning in the late evening hours of Oct. 13 when a Russian missile , with little warning, struck a nine-story residential building in the city's Desnyanskyi district, igniting a large-scale fire, Kyiv Mayor Vitalii Klitschko reported .
Ukraine received no warning from its partners about the first wave of Russian missile strikes, but did receive warnings during the subsequent three strike waves, Air Force spokesperson Yurii Ihnat said during a national telethon, according to Ukrinform .
At least three women were killed, and another 25 people, including a 7-year-old girl, were injured as a result of the Russian strike on the residential building, Kyiv Police said . Among those injured, 16 people were hospitalized, and four are in serious condition, Klitschko reported.
Over a dozen explosions were again heard in the capital between 4:45 a.m. - 6:45 a.m. local time, according to Kyiv Independent journalists on the ground, amid subsequent waves of missiles attacks. Kyiv Independent journalists reported brief power outages and flickering lights around 5:30 a.m.
Due to the Russian attacks, one of the capital's water pumping stations has been cut off, leading to a reduction in water pressure in the Pechersk district, the Kyiv City State administration (KMDA) said .
In the morning, all three of Kyiv's metro lines temporarily stopped working, according to Kyiv Independent reporters on the ground.
Klitschko reported that another person was killed in the city's Holosiivskyi district following the latest waves of attacks. Kyiv Police later raised the number of people killed in Holosiivskyi district to two.
Ukraine's State Emergency Service reported that an unspecified "non-residential" building, a home, and a vacant building were also damaged across the city.
Ukraine's Air Force said it neutralized four ballistic missiles and 115 Russian drones overnight.
The latest Russian attacks on energy infrastructure come just days after U.S. President Donald Trump declared an energy ceasefire, and demanded that Ukraine stop targeting Russian oil facilities. He claimed that these attacks contributed to heightened oil prices, widely attributed to the US war in Iran.
President Volodymyr Zelensky said he would be willing to agree to an energy ceasefire if Russian forces stop targeting Ukrainian energy infrastructure. Zelensky said earlier in the day that "Ukraine has not carried out strikes on Russian oil refineries or the energy sector in general for the two days since the American president announced an energy ceasefire."
In the aftermath of the attack, presidential adviser Dmytro Lytvyn told reporters that allies had not provided early warning of the launches for the second day in a row. Ukraine's Air Force also said no alerts had been received on either day.
Afterwards, President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed that no early warning was provided to Ukraine, adding that a Kyiv thermal power plant and residential building were targeted.
"Our system detected these missiles almost as they were approaching Kyiv," Zelensky said.
Local resident Maksym told the Kyiv Independent that he and his partner had to evacuate to their building's corridor before heading to a shelter after windows were shattered in a nearby explosion.
"Everything was very fast. We didn't even understand anything," he said.
Russian missile threats also triggered air raid alerts in parts of Lviv, Volyn, and Ivano Frankivsk oblasts in western Ukraine, far from the front lines.
Ukraine did not receive any advance warning of the attack from allies, which is unusual, presidential advisor Lytvyn said when asked by reporters.
Ukraine's Air Force confirmed that Russia had launched ballistic missiles at Kyiv, saying that "no information from partners regarding missile launches from enemy territory has been received," either on Oct. 12 or 13.
In the Russian attack on Oct. 12, at least 12 people were injured, including a 17-year-old, according to the Kyiv City State Administration's Health Department.
Just a day earlier, sources told the Kyiv Independent that the Trump administration threatened senior Ukrainian military and government officials, warning of plans to withdraw support from Ukraine in a push to protect Russian oil refineries.
"They called all the top military officials with threats," one Ukrainian official told the Kyiv Independent. "They're telling everyone that they're going to turn off both the intelligence sharing and PURL."

title: Pope Leo diagnosed with lung cancer after nodule removal, Vatican says
body:
Pope Leo XIV underwent surgery Tuesday that confirmed that he has lung cancer, and doctors removed the lower lobe of his right lung, the Vatican said.
Tests confirmed a diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma, the Vatican said in a medical bulletin after the surgery. It said the diagnosis had been suspected by preoperative tests and was confirmed during surgery.
The statement made no mention of treatment going forward, and the Vatican said doctors were not currently speaking of chemotherapy or other therapies pending the results of other tests. The Vatican press office noted the medical statement spoke of the “radical” removal of the lobe as an indication that doctors removed all suspect tissue in hopes of removing any lingering traces of the cancer.
Leo’s lymph nodes also would have been removed and tested, to determine if the cancer had spread, and there was no word yet on those test results.
“Adenocarcinoma is the most common (type of lung cancer), also with the most favorable prognosis,” said Dr. Stephen Liu, a lung cancer expert at Georgetown’s Lombardi Comprehensive Cancer Center. “While we know the diagnosis we now need to know the stage.”
“We now need to know how big it is, how many spots in the lung are involved. Is it just one nodule, or more than one, and the lymph nodes, are they cancerous?” Liu said.
If the cancer has spread, more tests will be needed to determine what kind of therapy to pursue, he said. Options include chemotherapy, a combination of chemotherapy and immunotherapy or targeted therapy, which involves oral pills for specific cancers.
The 71-year-old was in the operating room for about three hours, the statement said. The surgery itself lasted approximately 90 minutes.
“The surgery was successful, and there were no complications,” the statement said, adding that the pope later returned to his room.
Leo had walked into Rome’s Gemelli hospital through the main entrance earlier in the day and waved to dozens of well-wishers who had gathered to greet him. The Vatican said the surgery would be performed by a team led by Gemelli’s chief thoracic surgeon, Dr. Stefano Margaritora.
The American pontiff has offered a rare level of transparency about the first publicly disclosed major health problem of his 17-month papacy. He revealed the discovery of the localized nodule during his Sunday noon prayer and announced that he would have it removed.
Oncologists said prior to the operation that even if the nodule turned out to be cancerous, Leo’s prognosis would be “excellent” since it would have been removed at an early stage.
The Vatican on Monday canceled all Leo’s audiences through Oct. 20.
While Gemelli has a specific papal apartment that past popes have used, complete with a private chapel on the 10th floor, Leo will actually be staying in a nearby room since the papal apartment is undergoing renovations, according to the Vatican press office.
There was no word on whether Leo would be able to keep his planned trip to South America next month.
Oncologists often advise patients not to fly for three weeks after surgery — which would give the pope just the interval needed to make his planned Nov. 6-17 trip to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, depending on his recovery.
The current itinerary for the trip is ambitious and the longest of his papacy to date, calling for Leo to clock just over 31,000 kilometers (19,000 miles) on a dozen flights and two helicopter rides, and a significant altitude change in Peru.
“He has decided to undergo surgery soon in order to not change his plans for future overseas trips, so there is no need to worry, as it is not an emergency,” said Tokyo Cardinal Kikuchi Tsutomu, who saw Leo on Monday.
A lung nodule is a small abnormal area measuring less than 3 centimeters (1.2 inches) that sometimes appears on a CT scan of the chest or abdomen. Often, the scans are done to investigate trauma or a lung infection, unrelated to a lung cancer screening. A nodule can be benign or malignant, and oftentimes surgical removal is recommended both to establish whether it is cancer and to treat a malignancy while it is still localized.
This is believed to be the second hospitalization for Leo, who is known to be sporty and in good shape, with weekly tennis games and swimming.
As a young missionary priest, he came down with typhoid fever in 1985, soon after arriving in Chulucanas, Peru. The illness and hospitalization were a cathartic moment for him to decide to stay in the poverty and discomfort of Peru after living in relative comfort in Rome — a decision that ultimately paved the way to his papacy, according to an interview Leo gave to Elise Ann Allen in 2025 for “Pope Leo XIV: The Biography.”
According to the book, Leo said he prayed to God to let him die rather than suffer the “horrible” pain of the fever. “I was hooked up to an IV, and I said, ‘If this is your sense of humor, Lord, I think you could do a little better.’
“Obviously, I survived; I recovered, but it turned out to be a very significant moment for me, because it was like, ’Well, you’ve already dealt with the illness; you already see what the needs are here — the order, the Augustinians, the church are telling you, ‘We need you here; go for it.’ I never looked back.”

title: OpenVPX computing evolves with X9-inspired architecture in GMS X10 systems
body:
WASHINGTON, D.C. General Micro Systems (GMS) is bringing design elements from its X9 SPIDER small-form-factor computing family into the OpenVPX ecosystem with its new X10 GENESIS systems, addressing limitations in cooling, connectivity, and processing density as military computing requirements expand, showcasing both products at AUSA.
The X10 reflects a shift in embedded computing toward packing more processing capability and input/output (I/O) connectivity into smaller enclosures while maintaining compatibility with open standards, the company says.
While the X9 SPIDER family focuses on compact computing architectures, X10 applies elements of that design to a three-slot, 3U OpenVPX platform. The approach is intended to overcome constraints associated with traditional OpenVPX systems, particularly heat dissipation and communications between circuit cards, GMS says.
One change involves how data moves between components. X10 uses an interconnect architecture designed to reduce reliance on Ethernet-switched backplanes, while incorporating Thunderbolt 4, Ethernet, and Universal Serial Bus (USB) interfaces to connect external equipment.
Thermal management is another area of focus. As processors generate more heat, conventional cooling approaches can limit the computing power available within a chassis. X10 incorporates heat-pipe cooling and modified wedgelocks to support up to 500 watts of cooling capacity in an enclosure weighing less than 11 pounds, the company says.
The design illustrates how open-architecture military computing is evolving beyond standardized card interfaces toward greater processing density, more flexible connectivity, and improved thermal management -- capabilities relevant to applications including artificial intelligence, electronic warfare, and sensor fusion.
GMS says X10 supports the Modular Open Systems Approach (MOSA) and uses a design aligned with the Sensor Open Systems Architecture, or SOSA, Technical Standard

title: Israel's security tied to diplomatic standing, 'but not at cost of our fighters,' says Ben-Gvir
body: Far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir acknowledged on Monday that Israel's international diplomacy was relevant to the country's national security, but he asserted that it shouldn't take precedence over the nation's soldiers.The minister, whose views are often characterized as extreme and who has been criticized for contributing, through his rhetoric, to the deterioration of Israel's international image, delivered remarks at an English-speaking election campaign event for his Otzma Yehudit party at the Tel Aviv International Salon.He was joined by Yishai Fleisher, the international spokesman for the Jewish community of Hebron. Early last month, Fleisher was tapped for the number 12 spot on the Otzma Yehudit list.“I think there's a great importance to our diplomatic relations and connections,” Ben-Gvir said in response to a question submitted by The Jerusalem Post. “It's important that we look good on the world stage. But not at the expense of our fighters and our soldiers.”Ben-Gvir has been a key partner in Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition. Recent polling has projected Otzma Yehudit to win approximately eight seats in the next Knesset. The minister, however, admitted that he viewed things differently from Netanyahu regarding dealing with Israel's public diplomacy.Ben-Gvir: A soft approach doesn't help Israel's security or international standingHe pointed to the Gaza-bound flotillas that attempted to break Israel's maritime blockade of the Gaza Strip, arguing that taking a softer approach doesn't help Israel's security or move the needle in bolstering Israel's acceptance internationally.“The first time [the flotilla activists] came, Bibi [Netanyahu] said, 'Let's make a good impression on the world. Let's give them big sandwiches,'” Ben-Gvir said.“Female soldiers were brought in. They were told to wear civilian clothes, and they [the activists] were given a Pilates lesson,” he added.“That was because the government wanted to make a good impression and wanted us to look good internationally. Do you think that helped us?” Ben-Gvir asked.He claimed that, on the contrary, the response to the flotilla incident only caused further international condemnation and resulted in additional flotillas attempting to break the blockade.“They came again because they said, 'This is great. The Israelis treat us well; give us sandwiches and exercise classes. Israel is fun,'” Ben-Gvir said.Subsequently, when an additional flotilla arrived in Israel, he had decided to handle the activists in the same manner that terrorist supporters are treated in the United States.Rough approach deterred more activists from joining future flotillas, says Ben-Gvir“They were arrested. They were put in a prison for terrorists,” he said.According to Ben-Gvir, the different approach deterred some activists from returning, with some saying they would only participate in another flotilla once he was no longer in his role as national security minister.“There are people who want to see us weak. Anyone who is a true friend of Israel wants to see us strong,” he said. “I genuinely prefer to see Israel strong, even if some people, particularly in Europe, don't like it very much.”As national security minister, he has also led reforms in Israel's prison service, significantly worsening conditions for Palestinian inmates, arguing that both the death penalty and harsher prison conditions create deterrence.Fleisher, who translated for Ben-Gvir on stage after delivering the opening remarks, also spoke to the Post ahead of the event.Referencing the English-language format of the event, Fleisher confirmed that Otzma Yehudit was looking to reach out to the English-speaking community in Israel ahead of the October 27 election.“Certainly, we're reaching out to anybody who wants a safe and free Israel, and that's English speakers who understand the policies of strength,” Fleisher said. “It's Russian speakers. It's folks around the periphery. The ultra-Orthodox. There's a lot of people that we're reaching out to. We're not embarrassed about that; we are excited about strong policies, and that's what people want right now.”Regarding Israel's public diplomacy, Fleisher told the Post that Israel must “forge new alliances around the world of people who are like-minded.“We have to join a conservative alliance around the world, and we have to keep holding strong, not be afraid,” he added.“We clearly don't want to see Palestine here. Once [the international community sees] that we're sure of ourselves, sure of our Jewish identity, they'll respect us. That's the language of the Middle East,” Fleisher said.

title: Lagos publishes nationwide directory to help GBV survivors access support
body:
The Lagos State government has published a directory of gender-based violence (GBV) coordinators across Nigeria’s 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory to help survivors report abuse and access support services.
The directory, released through the Domestic and Sexual Violence Agency (DSVA), contains office addresses, telephone numbers and email addresses for state-level GBV response contacts.
Onadipe Opebere, head of the agency’s public affairs unit, announced the release in a statement on Monday.
The publication follows a two-day National Convening of GBV State Coordinators hosted by Lagos State to strengthen collaboration among those working on GBV prevention and response.
The initiative received support from the Rule of Law and Anti-Corruption (RoLAC II) Programme, funded by the European Union and implemented by the International Institute for Democracy and Electoral Assistance (International IDEA).
“The directory provides key contact details of GBV State Coordinators, serving as a practical resource to support reporting, referrals, and access to appropriate response services for survivors of Sexual and Gender-Based Violence,” the statement reads.
“It is designed to strengthen coordination and referral pathways among stakeholders working in GBV prevention and response, while making it easier for citizens to identify and connect with the appropriate state-level contacts.”
The agency urged individuals, government institutions, civil society organisations and community groups to use the directory and share it within their networks.
Ms Opebere said the agency remained committed to strengthening partnerships and coordinated responses to GBV, while helping survivors across Nigeria access timely and appropriate support.
The DSVA is a Lagos State government agency responsible for responding to domestic and sexual violence and providing support services to survivors.
Deep-rooted cultural norms, gender inequalities and economic dependence have been identified as factors that contribute to the persistence of GBV in Nigeria.
Societal expectations that men should exercise authority while women remain submissive can reinforce unequal power relations and normalise abusive behaviour.
Economic dependence can also make it difficult for some survivors to leave abusive relationships or seek help, particularly when they lack the financial resources to support themselves and their children.
Although Nigeria has enacted laws to address GBV, including the Violence Against Persons (Prohibition) Act, 2015, enforcement remains uneven across the country. The law criminalises several forms of violence and abuse, but gaps in implementation and access to justice continue to pose challenges to efforts to protect survivors.

title: 'Bennett II': Ben-Gvir refuses to sign vote surplus share agreement with Winter's People of Israel
body: National Security Minister and Otzma Yehudit party leader Itamar Ben-Gvir refused to sign a vote-surplus-sharing agreement with People of Israel party leader Ofer Winter on Tuesday."Winter is [former prime minister and B'Yachad party leader Naftali] Bennett II; therefore, Otzma Yehudit will not sign a surplus agreement with him," Ben-Gvir wrote on X/Twitter.Ben-Gvir was suggesting that a vote for Winter would be like a vote for Bennett.Winter issued a response to Ben-Gvir via People of Israel. "Itamar, grow up. People are tired of the gimmicks, the style, and this way of doing things," he said."Just a moment ago, you said these elections were fateful, and now you are declaring that you will throw votes in the trash," Winter continued."The false campaign you are trying to imitate against a right-wing man who has paid prices that few have paid in Israel is not appreciated, is not catching on, and will not help the right-wing camp," he added."Instead of defeating enemies, you are busy with an unsuccessful attempt to eliminate brothers. No wonder so many right-wing people are repulsed by this approach. Only a strong People of Israel will bring about a broad national government," Winter concluded.People of Israel may not pass electoral threshold, latest Walla Knesset mandate poll findsOtzma Yehudit is forecast to receive eight Knesset mandates while People of Israel falls below the 3.25% electoral threshold, receiving 2.8% of the vote, a Tuesday Walla poll found.Several aligned political parties have signed such vote-surplus-sharing agreements.Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party announced on October 6 that it had signed a surplus-vote sharing agreement with the Religious Zionist Party (RZP), led by Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, ahead of the October 27 elections.The two major haredi (ultra-Orthodox) parties, Shas and United Torah Judaism (UTJ), announced on Sunday that they signed a surplus vote-sharing agreement ahead of the October 27 elections and pledged continued cooperation in the next Knesset.Hadash-Ta'al and Ra'am signed a surplus vote-sharing agreement on September 11, saying the deal is intended to strengthen their position in the allocation of surplus mandates and reduce the risk of losing votes.Meanwhile, the four major parties in the opposition bloc signed surplus vote-sharing agreements on September 10. Two agreements were signed: one between Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar and Yair Golan's The Democrats, and the other between Naftali Bennett's B'Yachad and Avigdor Liberman's Yisrael Beytenu.As part of the agreement, the two parties pool their surplus votes after the initial allocation of Knesset seats following the elections. If the combined surplus is enough to secure an additional seat, one party can receive it, potentially strengthening the bloc to which the parties belong.The deal is only relevant if both parties pass the electoral threshold. All four parties in the opposition bloc have been polling far over the required threshold.Keshet Neev, Yoav Etiel, and Shir Perets contributed to this report.

title: Building agents that transact with Anchor Browser and AgentCore payments
body: AI agents increasingly need to access web resources that are priced per request. For example, premium datasets charge by the query, research APIs meter by the call, and paywalled publishers gate content behind payment. When an AI agent encounters one of these resources, the server returns HTTP 402 Payment Required. The agent has no built-in payment mechanism, no budget attached to the session, and no programmatic way to satisfy the request. The task stalls and requires manual intervention. Anchor Browser with Agentic Payments handles machine-to-machine payment workflows on behalf of the agent. Developed in collaboration with the AWS Generative AI Innovation Center Partner Agent Factory , it’s now available on AWS Marketplace . This post covers how Anchor Browser integrates with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments so that AI agents can pay for x402-protected pages and APIs autonomously. The x402 protocol is an open standard for HTTP-based machine-to-machine payments. A server responds with 402 Payment Required along with the amount, accepted payment methods, and payment address that the agent uses to complete the transaction. Anchor Browser is a cloud-based browser automation solution purpose-built for AI agents. Each agent session runs inside a managed browser environment that maintains authentication state, handles navigation, captures network requests, and provides a live view of page interactions. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore provides capabilities to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments is a fully managed capability within AgentCore that AI agents can use to discover, access, and pay for APIs, Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, and web content autonomously. AgentCore payments manages wallet connectivity, enforces configurable spending limits at the infrastructure layer, and processes payments through the x402 protocol. It also provides observability into payment attempts, approvals, denials, and settlements through Amazon CloudWatch. When an agent running in Anchor Browser encounters a 402 response, AgentCore payments authorizes and completes the transaction within the configured budget. The workflow continues without interruption. Challenges When an autonomous agent encounters an x402-protected resource, the workflow stalls. The agent makes a request, such as fetching a premium research report or calling a paid data enrichment API, and the server responds with HTTP 402 Payment Required. Without a mechanism to pay, the task that was supposed to run autonomously now requires human intervention. Today, developers must build the entire payment stack. This effort spans four categories of complexity: Payment protocol handling Detecting and parsing the 402 challenge from the HTTP response, and distinguishing payment-required responses from other 4xx errors. Constructing the correct payment header with the cryptographic proof in the exact format the merchant expects. Supporting multiple payment schemes (exact, upto, and protocol variants) without hardcoding vendor-specific logic into the agent. Maintaining compatibility across x402 merchant implementations that might vary in challenge format, supported stablecoins, or settlement timing. Security and key management Storing a private key to sign payments, requiring secure key storage within an environment exposed to untrusted inputs. Managing wallet lifecycle operations, including key rotation, credential refresh, and provider failover. Operational resilience Resubmitting the original request with the payment header while preserving session state, cookies, and request context. Providing idempotency, which is essential for wallet operations. Enforcing per-session and per-transaction spend limits with real-time budget tracking across concurrent agent executions. Observability and compliance Capturing every payment attempt, approval, denial, and settlement in audit logs for compliance and reconciliation. Without a managed payment service, the agent must internalize the entire payment stack. On every x402-protected call that returns a 402 response, the agent must orchestrate the full payment flow internally, including: Signing the proof. Attaching the correct header. Retrying the request. Settling the transaction. Logging the result. Each of these steps requires custom code that developers must build, secure, and maintain. Figure 1 illustrates this architecture. The agent contains eight tightly coupled components (Wallet, Private Keys, Budget Controls, Sign Proof, Attach Header, Retry Logic, Settle Payment, and Logging). The agent connects to an x402 API with a 402 challenge flowing back and a retry flowing forward. Figure 1: Agent payment stack The security considerations extend beyond the engineering effort. Uncontrolled spending. Without hard spending limits enforced at the infrastructure level, a bug, retry loop, prompt injection, or inadvertent access can trigger unintended payments. An agent retrying a paid endpoint in a loop continues to authorize payments until manual intervention occurs. Key exposure. When private keys reside inside the agent runtime, they share an execution environment with untrusted web pages, third-party tools, and external dependencies. These vectors might inadvertently disclose the credentials that control real funds. Signing flow exposure. If the signing infrastructure is accessible from the runtime, a threat actor can attempt to access the key or redirect payments to an address under unauthorized control. Effective mitigation requires that the key doesn’t enter the runtime in the first place. Browser-based agents introduce an additional constraint: the payment must occur within the same browser session. Otherwise, session recordings and live view no longer match what actually executed. Solution Anchor Browser and AgentCore payments address this complexity by moving the entire payment stack into managed infrastructure. Unlike a stateless tool call, Anchor Browser provides a real cloud browser with persistent identity, repeatable and deterministic workflows, and the session context needed to log in, navigate, and finish tasks reliably. Authentication, navigation, network requests, recordings, and live view happen inside the same browser session. When a payment is required, the transaction happens within that session. The recording captures the full sequence from request to 402 to payment to content delivery. Anchor agents include a built-in x402 tool that handles paid API calls natively within the browser context. The built-in tool requires no changes to existing Playwright, Puppeteer, or Chrome DevTools Protocol-based workflows. AgentCore payments serves as the payment layer. At the center of the service is the Payment Manager, the top-level resource that coordinates payment operations for the AWS account. Creating a Payment Manager requires specifying an authorizer type and an IAM role. AgentCore then provisions a corresponding workload identity in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity. The remaining components connect the Payment Manager to external wallet infrastructure: A PaymentConnector integrates the Payment Manager with an external wallet provider, either Coinbase Developer Platform (Coinbase CDP) or Stripe Privy. A PaymentCredentialProvider stores wallet provider credentials securely in AgentCore Identity. A PaymentInstrument identifies the specific wallet address from which funds are drawn. Anchor Browser sets up wallets through AgentCore payments using a supported wallet provider, without placing wallet secrets or private keys inside the agent runtime. AgentCore payments handles wallet operations through the configured provider. For endpoint discovery, AgentCore provides a curated Coinbase x402 Bazaar MCP server through Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway , so agents can discover available pay-per-use x402 endpoints programmatically. AgentCore payments restructures the payment architecture. Sensitive operations move out of the agent runtime and into a managed service layer. The Anchor Agent holds only two payment-related components: a budget session and the x402 tool. The infrastructure, including authentication, wallet secrets, payment limits, observability, and payment proof signing, resides in the AgentCore payments layer. Figure 2 shows the Anchor Agent connecting to the AgentCore payments managed layer, which handles wallet provider integration with Coinbase CDP or Stripe Privy. Figure 2: Anchor Browser integrates with AgentCore payments How the payment flow works The following steps describe what happens end to end, from the moment a browser session encounters an x402-protected resource to the moment the agent receives the response and continues the task. Anchor Browser creates a dedicated AgentCore PaymentSession for the browser session. When the session starts with x402 turned on, Anchor Browser provisions a PaymentSession through AgentCore payments, linking the browser session to a configured payment instrument and budget. The browser receives an HTTP 402 Payment Required response. The agent navigates to a URL or makes a fetch or XMLHttpRequest (XHR) request. The merchant responds with a 402 challenge specifying the amount, accepted payment methods, and payment address. The browser selects a compatible payment method. Anchor Browser reads the 402 challenge payload and matches the requested payment method against the instrument linked to the PaymentSession. AgentCore verifies the session budget and generates the cryptographic payment proof. AgentCore payments validates that the payment amount falls within the session spending limit. The service then signs the transaction using the configured wallet provider (Coinbase CDP or Stripe Privy) and returns the cryptographic proof. No key material enters the browser or agent runtime. The browser retries the original request with the payment header. The browser attaches the signed proof as PAYMENT-SIGNATURE for x402 v2 or X-PAYMENT for x402 v1, then retries the original request exactly once. The merchant verifies and settles the payment, then returns the protected resource. The merchant validates the cryptographic proof, settles the transaction on-chain, and serves the content. The agent continues the task. Wallet credentials remain with AgentCore and the configured wallet provider throughout this flow. Prerequisites Before you begin, make sure that you have a valid Anchor Browser API key ( ANCHOR_API_KEY ). To create one, see the Anchor Browser Quick Start guide. Setting up automatic x402 payments Setting up agentic payments for Anchor Browser requires one session property. Set session.x402 to true . The property defaults to false . When enabled, the browser session can automatically access x402-protected websites with payments signed by AgentCore payments and retried inside the same browser session. Enabling session.x402 authorizes the browser to make real payments from the configured payment instrument. The following examples show how to create a payment-enabled session for Anchor Browser using cURL and JavaScript: cURL curl --request POST --url https://api.anchorbrowser.io/v1/sessions --header "anchor-api-key: $ANCHOR_API_KEY" --header "content-type: application/json" --data '{"session":{"x402":true}}' JavaScript const response = await fetch('https://api.anchorbrowser.io/v1/sessions', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'anchor-api-key': process.env.ANCHOR_API_KEY, 'content-type': 'application/json', }, body: JSON.stringify({ session: { x402: true } }), }); const { data: session } = await response.json(); console.log(session.cdp_url); After connected through Chrome DevTools Protocol, the agent navigates normally. You don’t need to include a wallet key or payment header in your automation code. The browser handles 402 challenges, payment signing, and retries transparently for document navigation, fetch, and XHR requests. Payment session limits and behavior Anchor Browser enforces the following guardrails at the session level through AgentCore payments integration. Each payment-ready browser session operates within configured spending and time constraints. For specific limits, refer to the Anchor Browser technical documentation . If the merchant response is malformed, no compatible network is offered, the budget is exhausted, or AgentCore payments rejects the payment, the browser returns the original 402 response to the page unchanged. Your automation code can then handle the 402 as a standard HTTP error. The x402 session property controls payments to third-party resources only. The property doesn’t replace Anchor credits and doesn’t pay for the browser session. Automation code for Anchor Browser Your automation code for Anchor Browser remains unchanged. The following example demonstrates that no payment-specific code is required: const { chromium } = require('playwright'); // Connect to the x402-enabled session via CDP const browser = await chromium.connectOverCDP(session.cdp_url); const page = await browser.newPage(); // Navigate to an x402-protected resource exactly as with a free page await page.goto('https://premium-research.example.com/market-report'); // The page loaded, the payment was handled automatically // Extract content as normal const content = await page.textContent('article'); No wallet logic, no payment header construction, and no retry code. The agent navigates to the URL. If the server returns 402, Anchor Browser coordinates with AgentCore payments to sign the payment proof, retries the request with the appropriate payment header, and delivers the content to the page. Your automation code receives the final rendered page with no indication that a payment occurred. This pattern applies uniformly to paywalled journalism, licensed financial data, gated API documentation, metered research databases, and other resources that gate content behind a 402 challenge. Using the built-in x402 tool for API calls Paid resources aren’t limited to web pages. Many are APIs that expect POST, PUT, or other HTTP methods. Common examples include data enrichment services, premium inference endpoints, and licensed content APIs. For these use cases, Anchor Browser agents include a built-in x402 tool that you call like a standard HTTPS API within the browser context. Your agent makes the API call through fetch or XHR. If the server returns a 402 challenge, the browser coordinates payment signing through AgentCore payments and retries the request with the signed payment header. Your code receives the response as though the endpoint were free. The tool isn’t tied to a specific vendor, model, or framework. Payment operates as a session-level capability beneath your existing tooling, and no changes to agent code are required. // Fetch call to a paid API endpoint within the x402-enabled session const response = await page.evaluate(async () => { const res = await fetch('https://data-enrichment.example.com/api/v1/enrich', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify({ company_domain: 'example.com' }), }); return res.json(); }); // If the API returned 402, AgentCore handled payment automatically // The response contains the enriched data console.log(response); Your automation code doesn’t receive wallet credentials. Automatic payments are available only when session.x402 is set to true and remain subject to the spending and expiration limits described in the previous section. Key benefits This integration moves payment from application code to the infrastructure layer: No payment infrastructure to build. No wallet SDK to integrate, no 402 response parser to write, no retry loop to implement, no header construction logic to maintain, and no custom audit logging to build. AgentCore payments manages the entire payment stack. No changes to existing tooling. Playwright scripts, Puppeteer automations, Chrome DevTools Protocol commands, and agent flows in Anchor Browser continue to function exactly as before. Payment is a session capability attached to the browser, not a modification to agent logic, prompts, or tool definitions. Private keys don’t enter the runtime. Signing and settlement happen inside AgentCore payments. The service communicates with Coinbase CDP or Stripe Privy through secure credential storage in AgentCore Identity. The agent runtime doesn’t have access to key material that can move funds. Budgets are enforced at the infrastructure level. Every session operates within defined spend limits that AgentCore enforces before authorizing a payment. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Observability provides full payment audit trails through Amazon CloudWatch. When a session reaches the spending limit, AgentCore payments denies the payment. Paid tasks complete successfully. Paid GET pages load. Paid API calls return responses. The agent completes the workflow rather than stopping at a 402 response and requiring manual intervention. Billing is consolidated. Anchor Browser settles third-party x402 charges in credits on the same invoice as browser session time. There’s no separate crypto custody to manage, no USDC balance to monitor, and no on-chain settlement for the finance team to reconcile. Conclusion Anchor Browser, integrated with AgentCore payments, equips AI agents to handle x402 payment challenges autonomously for paywalled web pages and paid API endpoints. Wallet credentials stay out of agent code, and no custom payment infrastructure is required. As more of the web moves to per-request pricing, agents that lack a payment mechanism can’t complete tasks involving paid resources. This integration addresses that gap: agents complete paid workflows end to end, operating within defined budgets, with full observability through AgentCore Observability, and without cryptographic key material in the runtime. To get started, explore the following resources: Automatic x402 payments in Anchor Browser AgentCore payments developer guide AgentCore payments with browser integration Anchor Browser on AWS Marketplace About the authors Cher Simon Cher is a Principal Deep Learning Architect at AWS, where she helps customers, startups, and AWS Partners build large-scale, high-performance AI/ML solutions. A published author, she specializes in translating AI research into production-ready solutions. Guy Ben Simhon Guy is a Co-Founder and CPO at Anchor Browser, leading product and strategy. He focuses on building infrastructure that enables AI agents to reliably interact with the web and operate real computer environments at scale. Elay Gelbart Elay is a Founding and Lead Engineer at Anchor Browser, pioneering its browser infrastructure and core engineering. He specializes in large-scale browser infrastructure, distributed systems, and building reliable execution environments for AI agents. Chethan Shriyan Chethan is a Principal Product Manager – Technical at AWS. He has more than 12 years of experience in product and business management. Chethan is passionate about building and delivering technology products that create meaningful impact in customers’ lives. Peter Jiang Peter is a Senior Software Developer at AWS, based in Seattle, WA. He is a core member of the engineering team behind the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments initiative, which enables payment capabilities for AI agents. With over 8 years of experience in the financial and payments industry, Peter has launched multiple greenfield projects spanning banking, crypto, and agentic systems.

title: Atta Akyea denies seeking presidential pardon for Wontumi in galamsey case
body: Private legal practitioner Samuel Atta Akyea has denied formally seeking a presidential pardon for his client, Bernard Antwi Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, in a galamsey-related case. Mr Atta Akyea dismissed suggestions that he had approached President John Dramani Mahama to secure clemency for the former New Patriotic Party (NPP) Ashanti Regional Chairman. “No, please. We didn’t do that,” he said on Accra-based Citi FM on Tuesday, October 13, when asked whether he had sought a presidential pardon for his client. However, Mr Atta Akyea said he had expected President Mahama might consider granting Mr Boasiako a pardon, given the widespread nature of illegal mining in the country. He argued that the President could take into account the scale of galamsey and the involvement of influential individuals in the practice when considering cases related to illegal mining. “Also, when the case was galamsey-related, we thought that the president, in his own mercy, would say that, look, the nation is awash with galamsey,” he said. Mr Atta Akyea added that he had expected the President to be reluctant to impose a lengthy prison sentence in a case linked to illegal mining. “Even we have some evidence that serious people in the party- that is what their daily bread is all about. I will not use a galamsey-tinted criminal matter to detain a man and let him remain there for 20 years. I’ll grant him pardon,” he said, describing what he believed the President might do. His comments follow President Mahama’s decision on October 5 to grant presidential pardons to 863 convicted persons under Article 72(1) of the 1992 Constitution, following consultation with the Council of State. The pardons were announced as part of activities commemorating Ghana’s Independence Anniversary.

title: Quebec flu vaccine appointments open amid warnings of early flu season
body:
Appointments are now open for flu vaccines in Quebec as the province’s health department warns of an early flu season.
The Quebec health and social services department says vulnerable people should get their shots before the holiday season.
People will be able to get vaccinated for the flu, COVID-19 and Respiratory Syncytial Virus in the same appointment.
This year, only some vulnerable Quebecers will be eligible for free shots.
This includes people over 65, people who have chronic illnesses and pregnant women.
Others will need to pay for the shots in Quebec.
Most provinces in Canada will start providing the flu vaccine by the end of the month, and respiratory virus specialists say Canadians should get their flu shot as soon as it becomes available.

title: Rides closed at Canadian theme parks after deadly fall from Six Flags coaster in U.S.
body:
Rides at two Canadian theme parks were closed after a man in the United States fell to this death from a Six Flags roller-coaster in Georgia.
Two rides at Canada’s Wonderland in Toronto and another at La Ronde in Montreal were temporarily shuttered “out of an abundance of caution,” the parks said. Six Flags owns Wonderland and recently sold La Ronde.
A 42-year-old man was killed while riding a roller-coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia on Monday, prompting the theme park operator to close nine similar rides across Canada and the United States. The man was thrown from his seat and struck other patrons before landing below the ride, police said Tuesday.
The Leviathan and Behemoth roller-coasters at Canada’s Wonderland were closed, said a spokesperson for the park. There was no timeline for their reopening.
“The safety of our guests and team members remains on our highest priorities,” the spokesperson said in a written statement.
The Goliath roller-coaster at La Ronde was also closed and the park’s owner said it would carry out a safety review with the ride’s manufacturer.
“We are taking this additional time to carefully review the attraction. It will not reopen until this review is complete and we are fully satisfied that it can be operated safely,” read the statement.
The temporarily shuttered Canadian rides were manufactured by the same company as the coaster involved in the incident in Georgia.
Six Flags Entertainment did not immediately respond Tuesday to emailed questions about why specific rides were shut down and what would be done before they reopen.
This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct 13, 2026.

title: Houthis say Saudi Arabia delivered over 100 strikes against Yemen in past day
body:
DOHA, October 13. /TASS/. The Houthis from the Yemeni rebel movement Ansar Allah say that Saudi Arabia has delivered more than 100 strikes against Yemen during the day.
According to a post on Houthi Spokesman Yahya Saree’s Telegram channel, Saudi warplanes "delivered 104 air and missile strikes" over the past 24 hours, targeting "civilian facilities in the capital city of Sanaa," as well as in the Amran, Dhamar, Lahij, Marib, Saada, Taiz, Hodeidah, and Al Jawf governorates. The overall number of strikes "since the outbreak of the escalation <…> has reached 2,281," he added.
Meanwhile, the Houthi-controlled SABA agency reported, citing the Health Ministry, that two people died and two others were wounded after a Saudi attack on an oil facility near Ras Isa.
The Al Arabiya and Al Jazeera television channels reported earlier that the Saudi-led coalition had hit Houthi logistics depots in Hodeidah. Apart from that, according to the rebels, an oil facility was struck west of Sanaa. Prior to the attack, the coalition urged civilians to leave territories around this facility, while the Houthis warned about retaliation strikes against Riyadh and Saudi Arabia’s facilities.

title: Sasaabi scam centre busted: 19 arrested, 117 trafficking victims identified in global crackdown
body: Nineteen people have been arrested and 117 human trafficking victims identified at Sasaabi, an Accra suburb, as Ghanaian authorities joined an international crackdown on criminal networks operating online scam centres. Authorities also seized 303 electronic devices during the operation, according to the United States Department of Justice. The trafficking victims are awaiting repatriation to Nigeria. Investigators identified an additional 89 victims of the fraud schemes, with losses estimated at $8.3 million, highlighting the financial damage linked to the targeted operations. The Ghana operation formed part of “Joint Disruption Week”, a coordinated international enforcement exercise held during the week beginning October 6. The initiative targeted scam centres in Ghana, Nigeria and other African countries through real-time intelligence sharing between investigators and technology companies. Ghana’s Cyber Security Authority, the Ghana Police Service’s Criminal Investigation Department and the National Security Service led the local operation, supported by the UK’s National Crime Agency, the FBI and Nigeria’s Economic and Financial Crimes Commission. The latest action followed further enforcement in Ghana during the last week of September. Authorities made scores of arrests across six locations, identified 34 trafficking victims and seized 129 electronic devices. The Department of Justice described Joint Disruption Week as the first coordinated international effort focused specifically on West African scam networks. Across the exercise, authorities arrested 28 people — 19 in Ghana and nine in Nigeria. Nigerian authorities also seized 53 electronic devices. The disrupted schemes included criminals impersonating law enforcement officers, so-called digital “arrest” extortion, cryptocurrency investment fraud and other online scams targeting victims in the United States, the UK and elsewhere. The operation also exposed the human exploitation associated with organised scam centres, as well as the financial toll they exact. US Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva praised Ghanaian and Nigerian officers for their role in the crackdown. “I am especially grateful to the courageous law enforcement officers in Ghana and Nigeria who put themselves in harm’s way to seize evidence and arrest the criminals who prey on innocent people,” he said. Beyond the arrests, participating technology companies reported removing more than 3.7 million accounts, Pages and Groups used to target people internationally. They also shared leads on more than 30 suspected scam centres. Private-sector partners identified over $11 million in potentially freezeable funds across the wider initiative. The figure represents funds identified for possible freezing, rather than money confirmed recovered. Hosted by the National Crime Agency in London, the exercise brought together international law enforcement agencies and companies including Meta, Google and Microsoft. Authorities said sustained cooperation would remain critical to dismantling the networks and pursuing those behind them.

title: Drone marketplace expands to allied nations as Army streamlines foreign military sales
body:
WASHINGTON, D.C. The U.S. Army is expanding its marketplace for uncrewed aerial systems (UAS) and counter-UAS technology to additional allied and partner nations, with a new acquisition approach intended to accelerate access to drone defense equipment through streamlined foreign military sales, Army officials said during a signing ceremony at the Association of the United States Army (AUSA) 2026 conference.
Representatives from Albania, Canada, Croatia, Egypt, Japan, Kuwait, Morocco, and Panama participated in the event, which focused on expanding international access to the Army's UAS and counter-UAS marketplace.
Retired Gen. Robert Brown, president and CEO of AUSA, said the initiative was adding 10 signatories, bringing the total to 33. The international effort began with nine European partners signing statements of intent during the Eurosatory defense exhibition in Paris in June.
Brent Ingraham, assistant secretary of the Army for acquisition, logistics, and technology, said the marketplace is intended to address longstanding difficulties in acquiring military equipment through the Foreign Military Sales (FMS) process.
Under the approach, equipment listed on the marketplace is screened by the Army for performance, cybersecurity, and export eligibility before being made available to participating nations, he said.
Pricing is established in advance, while requirements involving technology transfer and foreign disclosure are addressed earlier in the acquisition process. The system also generates purchase agreements automatically, reducing administrative steps associated with government-to-government military sales.
The initiative comes as military forces face growing challenges from inexpensive drones that can be deployed in large numbers, sometimes forcing defenders to use considerably more expensive weapons to defeat them.
Ingraham said countering these threats requires multiple technologies working together, including sensors, command-and-control systems, electronic warfare, interceptors, and directed-energy weapons.
"There's no single answer to that threat. No silver bullet," he said.
The marketplace is intended to provide allied militaries with access to these types of capabilities while supporting interoperability between participating forces.
Army officials said the broader objective is to introduce commercial purchasing practices into the military acquisition process while retaining government oversight of technology transfers and equipment eligibility.

title: West Bank Palestinian family attacked by masked Jewish rioters claiming to be soldiers - report
body: A Palestinian family was injured by masked Jewish attackers posing as IDF soldiers after the settlers attacked them in their home near Kusra in the West Bank in the early morning hours on Tuesday, according to a KAN News report.According to KAN, the family was at home when the attackers knocked on the door around 3 a.m., claiming to be military personnel. The family stated the father opened the door and was grabbed by the extremists, who began beating him with sticks and rocks.The mother and two teenage daughters reportedly tried to help the father and were also beaten. According to KAN, the settlers fled the area after the attack, and the injured family members were taken to a hospital in Nablus for treatment.A relative present at the time told KAN that the family opened the door only because they believed the people knocking were soldiers. The relative added that police were called multiple times about the attack and that there was a military presence in the area.Olive harvest season regarded as sensitive security periodOn Thursday, the IDF's Central Command announced that it had completed preparations ahead of the Palestinian olive harvest in the West Bank as concerns regarding settler extremist violence and terrorism grow.The preparations aim to prevent friction between Palestinian and Israeli populations during the harvest in Areas A and B, as the harvest season is considered a sensitive period from a security standpoint.As violent incidents have continued over the past month, military sources say the situation has deteriorated compared with previous years, including growing disputes over territory and control of land.Amir Bohbot contributed to this report.

title: Netherlands deploys nuclear-capable F-35 fighters for NATO’s Steadfast Noon exercise
body: The F-35 squadron at Volkel Air Base supports the Netherlands’ contribution to NATO’s nuclear mission. Its aircraft are dual-capable, able to employ both conventional and nuclear weapons. The Netherlands’ F-35s have been officially certified to carry nuclear weapons under NATO’s nuclear-sharing arrangements and adapted to employ U.S. B61 tactical nuclear bombs. According to the Ministry of Defence, the Netherlands is the first European country to achieve nuclear certification with the F-35. During Steadfast Noon, allied forces rehearse simulated scenarios to maintain readiness and test defense procedures. The exercise takes place each autumn, with this year’s training comparable in scale to previous editions. The Netherlands was among the first European countries to select the Lockheed Martin F-35A Lightning II to replace its F-16 fleet. Its F-35 fleet reached full operational capability in September 2024 and has since been used extensively in national and allied operations. The aircraft perform a broad range of missions alongside their nuclear role. In September 2025, a Netherlands F-35 shot down a Russian drone that had violated Polish airspace. The ministry said Steadfast Noon is intended to preserve peace, prevent coercion and deter aggression. It described credible deterrence as supporting security and stability across the transatlantic area. The ministry said the exercise is separate from current world events. It is not directed against any country.

title: Ex-gang leader sentenced to minimum 40 years for Tupac murder
body: Duane “Keffe D” Davis, the former Los Angeles gang leader who boasted for years of his involvement in the killing of rapper Tupac Shakur, only to deny it when he came to trial, was sentenced to a minimum 40 years in prison on Tuesday. The sentence, which will likely see him die in custody, comes three decades after the gunning down of one of the most influential hip hop artists of the late 20th century, and after years of criticism over investigations that went nowhere. Davis, 63, formerly ran a branch of the feared Crips, one of a patchwork of rival gangs that controlled parts of Los Angeles in the 1990s. He spent years evading justice and seemingly believed he was beyond the reach of the law when he wrote in his memoir that he had ordered the killing of Shakur. “For three years, I’ve heard you say some variation of the same thing to law enforcement… in your book, and it’s something like, ‘Yeah, I was involved in this, but I’m different. I’ve moved on. I got out of Compton. I’m a grandfather now,'” Judge Carli Kierny told Davis as she handed down the sentence in a Las Vegas courtroom. “I’m here to tell you that’s not how this works.” “You don’t get to take a man from his family. You don’t get to take his very life, his whole future from him, and just walk away from it. Especially when that man is Tupac Shakur,” the judge said. Shakur was a key figure in a hip-hop rivalry pitting the US East Coast against the West Coast. He was just 25 when he was gunned down in Las Vegas. A trial heard how Davis ordered the September 7, 1996 killing of the hip-hop artist after his own nephew had been beaten by members of Shakur’s entourage at a Las Vegas casino. The “California Love” artist was shot about two hours after the casino confrontation by a gunman in a white Cadillac that pulled up at a red light alongside the BMW in which the rapper was riding. Davis handed the gun to someone sitting in the back seat of the Cadillac and ordered that person to shoot Shakur, who died six days later. The name of that person has not been definitively revealed and Davis is the only person who was in the Cadillac that evening who is still alive. The driver of the BMW, Death Row Records co-founder Marion “Suge” Knight, was wounded. – ‘Born an icon’ – The killing of Shakur, also known as 2Pac, was one of America’s most famous cold cases, prompting endless debate among music fans over who did it, and why. Known for hits including “All Eyez on Me,” Shakur — the son of a Black Panther activist — was raised in Harlem and Baltimore, but quickly became the epitome of California hip hop when he signed with Los Angeles-based Death Row Records. His sister Sekyiwa Shakur paid emotional tribute on Tuesday to her brother, a man whom she said “was born an icon.” She said their mother “consciously raised him to be a human rights activist, someone to stand up for those weaker and smaller than he was, and that’s who he was to me and all the family. He was the person that you go to for protection. “He dedicated his career to the advancement of his people. He was gentle and kind to women and children. He fed anyone he knew that didn’t have. He was truly my shining star, my shining prince. He was who God trusted to take care of me.” Davis offered no words of contrition ahead of the sentence being handed down, vowing only to appeal the guilty finding. title: Drones sink ship in Black Sea, unclear who launched strike, Bulgaria says
body:
Drones struck two ships in the Black Sea off Bulgaria on Tuesday, sinking one and prompting emergency rescue operations, Prime Minister Rumen Radev said.
The Guinea-Bissau-flagged cargo ship Dignity sank after it was hit by a military strike. Five sailors were rescued, while a search for the other 11 crew members continued, Varna district Gov. Mario Smrkov said.
Rescuers evacuated all 15 crew members from the Ukrainian-operated coastal freighter Chelsea 3, sailing under the Maltese flag, with five receiving treatment for minor injuries, Radev said in a video posted to social media.
The crew, which included seven Ukrainian citizens and eight Azerbaijani citizens, reported the ship’s deck and hull were hit by three aerial drones.
The strikes on the two ships happened 20 miles and 21 miles (32 and 34 kilometers) from the Bulgarian coast.
During an emergency meeting of Bulgaria’s Security Council on Tuesday, Radev called the attacks “absolutely unacceptable” and said Bulgaria was seeking NATO and European Union assistance.
While authorities do not possess clear evidence on who was responsible for the drone attacks, “it makes no sense for Ukraine to destroy its own ships in the Black Sea, and the results of these strikes favor Russia’s interests,” Radev told the Russian Ambassador in Sofia during a meeting on Tuesday, the government’s press office reported.
The ambassador said she does not have any information from the Russian defense ministry related to the recent attacks on commercial vessels in the Black Sea but added that she did not rule out the possibility that “these attacks represent a provocation by a third party.”
Radev has said that such attacks are unacceptable and that Bulgaria will continue to investigate the attacks together with its EU and NATO allies to establish the truth.
Radev said Bulgaria is suffering significant economic and financial damage and added that his country will initiate talks with neighboring Romania and Turkey on joint proposals to guarantee the safety of shipping in the Black Sea.
Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha in a post on X on Tuesday blamed Russia for the attacks.
“Russia’s latest attack on commercial vessels near Bulgaria’s territorial waters, which injured Ukrainian and Azerbaijani citizens, once again demonstrates Moscow’s deliberate disregard for civilian lives and maritime security in the Black Sea,” Sybiha wrote.
“The Black Sea is a lifeline for global food security. Russia is attacking it to weaponize hunger and hold the world hostage. This must be met with strength,” Sybiha wrote.
“NATO will continue to work closely with our Allies in the Black Sea,” NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte wrote on X. He added that NATO had already strengthened its posture along the eastern flank and will continue to monitor the security environment, adjusting its deterrence and defense posture as needed.
The United Nations condemns attacks on civilian ships, especially the most recent ones off the coast of Bulgaria, U.N. spokesman Stephane Dujarric said Tuesday.
“It’s very worrisome because these attacks on ships carrying grain, food and other products destined for the global market have multiplied and have expanded recently,” Dujarric said. “It has a terrible knock-on effect on the price of commodities worldwide when you’re also seeing the situation around the Strait of Hormuz, in the Red Sea, not to mention the risk — and also the fatal risk faced by seafarers.”
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen “strongly condemned” the drone incidents and said the Black Sea “has become another front of escalation” in Russia’s war in Ukraine.
“This is unacceptable. I strongly condemn the drone attacks on merchant ships near Bulgaria’s coast. Putting the lives of the crew in grave danger and threatening security in the Black Sea,” she said in a post on X.
“We stand with Bulgaria and thank its rescuers for their swift response. Those responsible should be held accountable.”
European Council President Antonio Costa said in a social media post that the EU stood in full solidarity with Bulgaria following the attacks. He said the growing number of Russian hybrid activities would be discussed at the European Council meeting scheduled for Thursday and Friday in Brussels.
The attacks came exactly a week after sea and aerial drones attacked two other commercial vessels in Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone in the Black Sea. A Togo-flagged ship sank, while a Bulgarian ferry evacuated the 18-member crew of a Pulau-flagged vessel.
A day earlier, a Turkish-owned cargo ship carrying corn caught fire following a drone attack and later sank in the Black Sea off the coast of Romania. Two people died and 11 crew members were rescued, Romanian authorities said.

title: What an economics Nobel Prize winner knows about pricing
body:
NPR's Ailsa Chang chats with Michael Woodford of Columbia University, who was one of two Americans awarded the Nobel Prize in Economics.
AILSA CHANG, HOST: All right. Two Americans have just been awarded the Nobel Prize in economics. Robert Hall of Stanford University and Michael Woodford of Columbia University are being honored for their work on how to bring stability to cycles of economic boom and bust. But they base their macroeconomic models off of their microeconomic research into how people actually decide to buy stuff and how businesses actually decide to price that stuff. Economist Michael Woodford is with us now. Welcome, and congratulations on winning the Nobel Prize. I don't get to say that every day on the show (laughter) . MICHAEL WOODFORD: (Laughter) I don't get to hear it every day, either. Thanks a lot. CHANG: So what were your first thoughts when you found out you got the Nobel Prize? WOODFORD: Well, I wasn't terribly awake, I'm afraid (laughter). I was trying to sleep when they called. CHANG: Of course. WOODFORD: Yeah. Because it's six hours later in Stockholm. CHANG: Yeah. From the East Coast. Yeah. WOODFORD: And my wife said I didn't sound very enthusiastic about it... CHANG: (Laughter). WOODFORD: ...But I mean, it was because I was... CHANG: Groggy. WOODFORD: ...At best, half awake. (LAUGHTER) CHANG: Well, I want to better understand your work, and I'm going to try to keep up as best I can, at least on the basic concepts. So part of your research was on how businesses set prices, right? And I want to use a very concrete example. Like, let's say you're a trucking company, and you're thinking about adjusting your rates because the cost of diesel fuel unexpectedly surges. How would your work apply to that example? WOODFORD: Well, a thing that is particularly central to my work is stressing the extent to which decisions that people make often are forward-looking, are not just a response to immediate conditions... CHANG: Yeah. WOODFORD: ...But have to also take into account where you think things are headed. In the case of changes in costs that people have some reason to think is probably very temporary, I think, often, prices don't respond, that something that you think is likely to be lasting is going to be more likely to encourage people, more quickly, to already price it into the prices they're charging. So this issue of the extent to which people are able to make good guesses about where things are headed is something that the work that I've done particularly stresses. CHANG: OK. Let me give you another concrete example. WOODFORD: Sure. CHANG: So, like, yesterday, the president of the Cleveland Federal Reserve Bank said that she heard from a business owner who's planning to raise prices more than his costs have gone up because he just expects those costs to keep climbing. How concerning is that, when businesses start to anticipate higher costs and raise their own prices in response maybe disproportionately? WOODFORD: Well, I think that illustrates that it isn't just the current costs... CHANG: Yeah. WOODFORD: ...That are going to matter for that decision. It matters a lot what people think about where they could be going, you know, their guesses, their fears. And that's one reason why my work has stressed the idea that policymakers should be concerned about trying to give people reassurances about, you know - not false reassurances - but if they themselves intend not to let certain things happen or to make them not very likely to happen, that being able to communicate that to the public so that their expectations about where things can go are, in fact, not significantly out of line with what really happened, that actually is important for the economy. CHANG: If I could just jump in 'cause you're talking... WOODFORD: Yeah. CHANG: ...About something very important. You have stressed in your work that policymakers should make an effort to communicate clearly and accurately and in... WOODFORD: Right. CHANG: ...Proportion so that families and businesses can plan accordingly. How do you think Congress or President Trump or the Federal Reserve are doing on that front, on their communication skills? What do you think? WOODFORD: Well, of course, it's a challenging thing. You know, I don't... CHANG: (Laughter). WOODFORD: ...Want to imply that I could just communicate much better than them. And, you know - but often policymakers don't think as much as they should about how important this is to their role. I think that, often, they take the view that it's enough to react to whatever is happening once it happens. You should think about the fact that your behavior being predictable actually has big benefits for the economy, and that people can see that this fits into a pattern of behavior that they can count on. CHANG: So in this time where people are quite focused on affordability, what advice do you have for people out there feeling just unsettled and unsure about the state of the economy right now? Any words of assurance or warning (laughter)? WOODFORD: Well, I certainly understand why it's an issue. I mean, it's not that economists should tell people to calm down. I think that it's appropriate for the government to indicate that it's keeping its eye on this issue, and to use monetary policy - make it clear that there is a commitment to keeping an eye on prices. I think it is - to some extent, it's a failure of public policy to not have kept a better lid on things. CHANG: Michael Woodford, cowinner of the Nobel Prize in economics. Thank you, and congratulations again, Professor Woodford. WOODFORD: Thanks. Copyright © 2026 NPR. All rights reserved.
