title: ‘To me, it’s Mohammed’: Abdul El-Sayed faces Muslim Brotherhood claims in Michigan Senate race
body: Three times, Abdul El-Sayed answered "no" when asked in an interview whether he or his family had ties to the Muslim Brotherhood. But on Monday, just one day after his appearance on NBC's "Meet the Press," a social media post written by his half-sister 14 years ago began circulating: Their mother, she wrote, had been active in the Islamist movement in Egypt during the 1970s, before immigrating to the United States. For El-Sayed, the Democratic nominee for a U.S. Senate seat in Michigan who hopes to become the first Muslim senator in American history, the revelation is politically explosive just three weeks before the midterm elections. His Republican opponent, Mike Rogers, has already turned the posts into a campaign advertisement in a race that could determine whether Republicans retain control of the Senate or Democrats take it over for the remainder of Donald Trump's presidency.     "I had an amazing conversation with my mom about her activism in the Muslim Brotherhood in the early 1970s, when she was in college," Eman Abdelhadi, now a researcher at the University of Chicago, wrote on Twitter, now X, in 2012, adding the hashtag "#respect." In another post, she wrote: "My family has long been MB," referring to the Muslim Brotherhood, although she added that she believed the movement had handled politics poorly and destructively. In 2013, she wrote that relatives had been imprisoned because of their membership in the Islamist organization and asked followers to pray for family members who supported it in Egypt. Abdelhadi and El-Sayed share the same mother, Fatten Elkomy, but grew up in separate households after their parents divorced. The posts do not establish what exactly their mother did within the movement, whether her son knew about her involvement or whether he himself had any connection to the organization. The posts surfaced after El-Sayed was interviewed on NBC on Sunday and explicitly asked whether he or his family had any ties to the Muslim Brotherhood, the Islamist movement founded in Egypt from which Hamas also emerged. The question came against the backdrop of Republican efforts in recent weeks to portray him as a "radical jihadist" with links to Islamist organizations, allegations he has repeatedly denied. When moderator Kristen Welker asked whether he or his family had ties to the Brotherhood, El-Sayed replied: "No, but let's talk about this." "No, you don't have any ties?" Welker pressed. "No," he answered. "And your family doesn't?" "No," El-Sayed repeated. He argued that Rogers was raising the issue merely to repeatedly emphasize the word "Muslim" and encourage voters to view him with suspicion because of his name and religion.     On Monday, Rogers circulated a new campaign video combining El-Sayed's denials from the interview with his sister's posts, accusing his opponent of lying. El-Sayed's campaign responded that Rogers was using "bad faith attacks on Abdul's faith and family" to divert attention from the cost of living and soaring gasoline and grocery prices. The campaign also maintained that allegations linking El-Sayed to the Muslim Brotherhood had been "debunked as racist and untrue," but did not address the specific post in which his sister described their mother's involvement in the movement. The same half-sister had already caused difficulties for El-Sayed over the summer, after other old social media posts surfaced, including one described as celebrating the October 7 massacre. Support for Mohamed Morsi and indictment of organization where his mother worked El-Sayed, a prominent figure on the Democratic Party's far left and an outspoken critic of Israel, has repeatedly denied ties to extremist organizations. His critics, however, argue that his conduct raises questions about his actual beliefs. Fox News, for example, noted that on the second anniversary of the October 7 attack, El-Sayed sent an email to supporters asking them to donate money to Palestinians. In the message, he compared Hamas to the Israeli government, although he described both as "evil." The network also pointed to his campaign appearances alongside streamer Hasan Piker, who previously declared that the United States "deserved 9/11." El-Sayed described the remark as "stupid" but refused to distance himself from Piker. Although several media outlets, including the conservative Fox News, reported that they had been unable to identify any direct ties between El-Sayed and the Muslim Brotherhood, attention is now focusing on his mother's possible connection to the movement. The Brotherhood is designated a terrorist organization by several countries, including Egypt. The United States has also designated its Egyptian and Jordanian branches as terrorist organizations over their support for Hamas.     The activism attributed to El-Sayed's mother by his sister dates back more than 50 years, before Hamas was founded. However, after moving to the United States, Elkomy worked for an Islamic aid organization that the U.S. government sanctioned in 2004 for supporting al-Qaeda and Hamas. According to American media reports, Elkomy worked for the Islamic American Relief Agency, or IARA. U.S. Treasury Department documents stated that the organization was responsible for transferring funds to Palestinian territories for terrorist activities and, in particular, served as a conduit for money intended for Hamas through a Western European country. In 2007, the organization was indicted. Elkomy was mentioned at least 12 times in the accompanying list of exhibits, although she herself was never charged. The exhibits documented her involvement in financial transfers and recordings of telephone conversations between 1999 and 2002. At the time, Elkomy denied that the organization had any ties to terrorism. In a 2004 interview with the St. Louis Post-Dispatch, she explained that her work involved helping orphans and children who had lost at least one parent, adding that it broke her heart to think they would no longer receive assistance. El-Sayed himself expressed support in 2011 for the revolution then unfolding in Egypt against President Hosni Mubarak. In an opinion article, he called on the United States to support the protesters even if doing so resulted in the Muslim Brotherhood coming to power. He argued that even in that scenario, there were several reasons why the resulting state would look nothing like Iran. In addition, a 2012 document published in an Egyptian newspaper listed a "Dr. Abdel-Rahman El-Sayed" from New York among its signatories. The signatories expressed support for decisions by Egypt's then-president Mohamed Morsi, a Muslim Brotherhood figure, after he expanded his presidential powers. They also called for a "purge" of the media and police. El-Sayed's campaign declined to comment on the letter.     The U.S. midterm elections, scheduled for November 3, will determine control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives, which are currently controlled by Republicans. Midterm elections have historically been viewed as a referendum on the sitting president, and polling has suggested that Democrats have an opportunity to take control of both chambers amid Trump's low popularity and widespread frustration with the cost of living and the sharp rise in prices caused by the war with Iran. In the Senate, where Republicans currently hold a 53-47 majority, a Democratic takeover would depend heavily on the party's ability to retain its Michigan seat, which is being vacated by retiring Democratic Sen. Gary Peters. The contest between El-Sayed and Rogers is therefore considered particularly important. Polls have consistently shown El-Sayed ahead, but only by a narrow margin. El-Sayed, 41, was born to Egyptian immigrant parents. He is a medical doctor and epidemiologist who previously headed the Wayne County Department of Health Services in Michigan. He has never held elected office, although he ran for Michigan governor in 2018 and lost the Democratic primary to Gretchen Whitmer, who went on to become governor. He is considered a member of the Democratic Party's far-left progressive wing. Alongside repeated accusations that Israel committed "genocide" in Gaza, he has called for an end to all U.S. military assistance to Israel, including support for defensive systems. He argues that the money should instead be invested in American communities.     In August, El-Sayed won the Democratic Senate nomination after an especially contentious primary, narrowly defeating Haley Stevens, a moderate, pro-Israel Democrat, by about one percentage point. The contest between El-Sayed and Stevens was widely regarded as a crucial test of the direction of the Democratic Party as a whole. It followed a series of victories this year by progressive candidates challenging the party's established leadership and taking strongly anti-Israel positions in local congressional and mayoral races. Those victories signaled a dramatic increase in the progressive movement's influence. Most of those successes, however, came in liberal strongholds such as New York and California, where Democratic candidates are often effectively assured of victory. Michigan, by contrast, is a swing state that Trump won in 2024 by a narrow 1.4 percentage points. For progressives, the Senate contest offers an opportunity to demonstrate that they can attract broader public support beyond their traditional strongholds. ‘Bin Laden jersey’ and the Israel-Iran comparison: ‘Both are dangerous’ Republicans, meanwhile, see Michigan as one of their best opportunities to capture a Democratic Senate seat and improve their chances of retaining control of the chamber. Against that backdrop, Trump and his allies have intensified their attacks on El-Sayed in recent days, portraying him as a dangerous extremist. Trump has repeatedly referred to the candidate as "Mohammed," even though his name is Abdul, behavior that the president's critics describe as blatant Islamophobia. In one recent social media post, Trump called him "Mohammed El-Sayed," a "RADICAL Extremist" and a "Terrorist Sympathizer." At a rally Saturday, Trump again described El-Sayed as a "radical jihadist" and explained why he had decided to call him Mohammed. "Somebody said, his name isn't Mohammed it's Abdul. I said, to me, it's Mohammed," Trump told the crowd. He added that, as president, he could call the candidate whatever he wanted, and repeated his accusation that El-Sayed was a jihadist. Trump also shared a photograph of himself and first lady Melania Trump alongside a photograph of El-Sayed and his wife, who wears a hijab, with the caption "Two VERY DIFFERENT Americas." Republican Sen. John Kennedy, who is not related to the family of the late President John F. Kennedy, appeared alongside Rogers and said that El-Sayed "sleeps in a Bin Laden jersey." On Monday, Trump shared a video in which singer Kid Rock warned of a "civil war over religious ideology" and described El-Sayed as a "wolf in sheep's clothing." El-Sayed, for his part, argues that Trump is trying to divert attention from the cost of living. "He knows my name is Abdul. He says it every day," El-Sayed responded. "But he's not just attacking me. He's attacking all of us."   He accused Trump of looking down on ordinary Americans and believing that he could use El-Sayed's name and religion to distract voters from the economic hardship caused by his policies. El-Sayed said that hardship was being felt at gas stations, grocery stores and doctors' offices, and that Trump underestimated voters' ability to recognize what was happening. "It's time for change," he concluded. Even without the attacks on his identity, El-Sayed continues to generate controversy over his positions toward Israel. During a debate last week, the moderator asked him which country posed a greater danger to the United States, Israel or Iran. El-Sayed refused to choose. "I think both of them have proven dangerous in their own way," he said. He argued that Iran presented a risk of attacking the United States, while Israel was drawing Washington into wars it had no reason to fight. El-Sayed accused Israel of pushing Washington into the war with Iran. Asked whether he would support supplying defensive weapons to Israel if Iran attacked it, he rejected the idea. "I don't want our tax dollars buying weapons for other countries," he said, reiterating that he wanted public money invested in schools and health care in Michigan. Rogers responded that he would approve such assistance. The March attack on Temple Israel synagogue near Detroit has also continued to trouble El-Sayed's campaign. The attacker, who had lost relatives in an Israeli strike in Lebanon, rammed his vehicle into the synagogue building while children were inside and opened fire at a security guard. Although El-Sayed condemned the attack, he also said that "hurt people hurt people." Members of the Jewish community interpreted the remark as an attempt to justify an antisemitic terrorist attack. In August, El-Sayed apologized to the Michigan Democratic Jewish Caucus, saying that the timing of his remarks had been wrong. His efforts to improve relations with Jewish voters may be having some success. A group called "Jews for Abdul" has been established to help him win the election. This week, the pro-Israel lobbying group AIPAC also returned to the campaign. An organization affiliated with the group sent election materials opposing El-Sayed to approximately 130,000 Jewish voters in Michigan. During the Democratic primary, the lobby spent approximately $30 million supporting his more moderate opponent, Stevens, who ultimately lost. El-Sayed attacked Obama, who is now campaigning for him El-Sayed received support during the Democratic primary from prominent progressive leaders, including Sen. Bernie Sanders and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez. In the final stretch of the campaign, however, he is also working to secure support from the Democratic Party's more moderate establishment, possibly in an effort to attract undecided voters. Former Vice President Kamala Harris recently appeared alongside him at an event in Detroit, and former President Barack Obama is expected to join him at a rally in the city next weekend.   That support comes despite El-Sayed's past criticism of Obama. Fourteen years ago, El-Sayed, whose charismatic style has led some to call him the "Obama of Michigan," accused the then-president of perpetuating wars and undermining civil rights. During Sunday's NBC interview, El-Sayed explained that he had been "young and angry" at the time and had not understood how difficult it was to bring about meaningful change. When interviewer Kristen Welker asked whether America was ready for a Muslim president, he brought the conversation back to Michigan. "I think Michigan is ready for a Muslim senator," he said.

title: Enemies threaten to attack Israel ahead of October 27 Knesset elections — Netanyahu
body:
TEL AVIV, October 13. /TASS/. There are ongoing warnings about the threat of attacks on Israel ahead of the parliamentary elections scheduled for October 27, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said.
"Warnings about threats are coming in. Our enemies are considering testing our resolve in these days before the elections. I warn them: we are ready for any developments," Netanyahu said during a visit to the area of the so·called separation wall in the West Bank, according to his office.
Netanyahu added that the Israel Defense Forces presented him and Defense Minister Israel Katz with a "plan for decisive action." "In such a situation, I would not advise our enemies to test us," he continued, promising those who attack Israel "a confrontation with a force they could not have imagined."

title: US lawmakers urge FAA to pause AI traffic tool at Washington-area airports
body: More than two dozen US lawmakers are urging the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to stop using a new artificial intelligence tool to help manage Washington-area air traffic until it answers questions about safety testing and staff training. The request follows the September 21, 2026, launch of limited operations involving flights at Reagan National (DCA), Washington Dulles (IAD) and Baltimore/Washington International (BWI) airports. Representative April McClain Delaney, a Maryland Democrat, said the congressional letter has been sent to Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford. Lawmakers said they had not seen safety evaluation and testing reports or been made aware of efforts to train aviation safety personnel. “I’m calling on the FAA to pause this rollout, show us the safety testing, and explain who is accountable when something goes wrong,” McClain Delaney said. Called Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories, or SMART, the system draws together about 200 data streams, including weather, flight paths, traffic demand and controller staffing. It uses that information to forecast congestion and suggest scheduling changes before delays begin to cascade. The FAA says SMART technology does not replace air traffic controllers. Agency staff review its recommendations, and local air traffic control leaders can accept or reject them. The lawmakers want details of testing under conditions such as severe weather and equipment outages, along with information on consultation with airport authorities, airlines and aviation safety workers. They also asked how the FAA would assess an initial 90-day evaluation of the technology, what conditions would have to be met before expanding the system nationwide, and who would be accountable if a recommendation contributed to a safety incident. The letter’s co-leaders include Representatives Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Don Beyer, Kweisi Mfume, Suhas Subramanyam and Sarah Elfreth. Air Space Intelligence is developing SMART alongside a replacement for the FAA’s traffic flow management software. The agency says the tools will help airlines and traffic managers adjust routes and departure times earlier, reducing delays and making better use of available airspace. The FAA announced plans for a gradual expansion beyond the Washington area when it launched the system in September. Airline officials also raised concerns before the launch about how SMART would fit into their operations. Those concerns eased after the FAA clarified that the tool would initially have a limited role. By the September 21 rollout start date, executives at United, Delta, American and Southwest had publicly welcomed the initiative. Delta CEO Ed Bastian said the airline supported SMART, while American CEO Robert Isom stressed the need for careful implementation. The post US lawmakers urge FAA to pause AI traffic tool at Washington-area airports appeared first on AeroTime .

title: New Details Emerge About Giorgos Mazonakis’ Sealed Voula Home
body: New details have emerged about the rented Voula residence of Greek singer Giorgos Mazonakis, including the landlord’s position on unpaid rent and the ongoing police seal on the property. The house, which Mazonakis personally helped design in collaboration with the architectural firm of Tasos Zeppos, was not owned by the singer but rented. Known for its striking interiors, artwork and distinctive decoration, the residence was a place Mazonakis particularly loved. He frequently welcomed visitors and showcased the home, which also appeared in interior design magazines, entertainment publications, television series, music videos and social media posts. Recent reports suggested that the singer’s family did not intend to continue maintaining the property. However, journalist Giorgos Liagas addressed the situation on Tuesday, October 13, clarifying the landlord’s position and dismissing reports that the family had been asked to pay outstanding rent. Landlord Seeks Access to Sealed Property Liagas said claims that the landlord had demanded unpaid rent from Mazonakis’ family were incorrect. “It has been reported that the owner of the house has asked the family for the unpaid rent. This is not true,” he said. According to Liagas, the landlord had shown respect following the singer’s death and had not requested any money from the family. Instead, the owner was reportedly seeking police permission to have the property unsealed so it could be cleaned, the family’s belongings could be collected and the residence could eventually be rented again. The house remains sealed as the relevant procedures continue. Light Still On in Mazonakis’ Room Liagas also shared a personal observation about the property, saying he regularly passes the house in Voula and continues to see flowers outside. He said the light in Mazonakis’ upstairs bedroom remains on, despite the house being sealed. “I still go past Mazonakis’ house in Voula, and there are still flowers outside. The light is still on upstairs, in Giorgos Mazonakis’ room. No one has gone to turn it off,” Liagas said. He described the sight as shocking, explaining that he sometimes passes the residence at night and sees the light still burning. The sealed home and the flowers left outside have become poignant reminders of the singer’s absence, as questions remain over when the property will be reopened and what will happen to his belongings. The post New Details Emerge About Giorgos Mazonakis’ Sealed Voula Home appeared first on Greek City Times .

title: Ireland Aims to Open All Remaining EU Accession Clusters for Ukraine by Year-End
body:
Ireland, which holds the rotating presidency of the Council of the EU, aims to open all remaining negotiating clusters in Ukraine’s accession talks before its term ends, Irish Minister of State for European Affairs and Defence Thomas Byrne said on Tuesday, Oct. 13.
Byrne made the remarks speaking during a press conference in Luxembourg after the fourth intergovernmental conference on Ukraine’s EU membership.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“The presidency’s ambitious goal is to open the remaining clusters,” Byrne said according to Interfax-Ukraine . “The Ukrainians have also made enormous efforts to open these clusters, so we will continue to work actively with the member states,” he continued.
The bloc formally opened two additional negotiating clusters on Tuesday, after the move was agreed upon by all 27 member states on Monday, Oct. 12.
The decision came hours after Ukraine adopted a minority education law that Hungary had demanded in exchange for lifting its veto that blocked its accession bid for months.
There are six clusters in total that organize the legal and institutional reforms Ukraine must adopt and implement in order to formally join the EU.
The second accession cluster, internal market, covers the free movement of goods, services, workers and capital, along with EU rules on competition, financial services, company law and consumer protection.
According to the European Council , the competitiveness and inclusive growth cluster covers areas including taxation, economic and monetary policy, industry, digital transformation, employment, education, research and customs.
The current clusters have been opened after months of stagnation. Hungary had blocked Clusters 2 and 3 four times, with its fourth refusal on Sept. 8.
Byrne acknowledged that some EU countries still have reservations about the next steps. “In some cases, member states raise certain issues that need to be resolved,” he said, adding that his team had worked with Ukraine and the European Commission to address each concern.
On June 15, Ukraine and Moldova opened Cluster 1 – Fundamentals , and Cluster 6 – External Relations on July 14.
Accession negotiations cover 33 chapters grouped into six clusters. With Clusters 2 and 3 formally opened on Tuesday, only two clusters remain: Cluster 4 – on the green agenda and sustainable connectivity, and Cluster 5 – on resources, agriculture and cohesion.
Ukraine’s Deputy Prime Minister for European and Euro-Atlantic Integration Vsevolod Chentsov said Kyiv expects the EU to judge its progress on merit and believes both can be opened this year.
“We see no obstacles to this happening by the end of this year, and we look forward to in-depth discussions with the European Commission and member states within the negotiation process to find balanced solutions, even in such specific areas as agriculture,” he said.
The European Commission previously proposed limiting Ukraine’s access to EU farm subsidies and markets for sensitive products even after accession , which Agriculture Minister Taras Vysotskyi rejected on Tuesday, Oct. 5. by saying that Kyiv cannot accept permanent restrictions.
During the same press conference on Tuesday, EU Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos reiterated that Ukraine would join the bloc’s agricultural policy under a special model, with its grain exports continuing to go mainly to its traditional markets in North Africa, Asia and the Middle East rather than to the EU.
The exact terms will be set by member states during talks on Cluster 5.
Europe’s aim remains to protect its farmers “and at the same time help Ukraine sell its products on traditional markets,” according to a separate report from Interfax-Ukraine .
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: UN adopts Durban resolution despite antisemitic legacy of anti-Zionist declaration
body: The UN adopted a resolution calling for the full implementation of the 2001 Durban Declaration, despite arguments that it platforms antisemitism and hatred of Israel.On Monday, the UN General Assembly formally adopted the new political declaration and draft resolution (A/81/L.4) with 95 countries voting in favor, five against, and 37 abstaining. Argentina, Australia, Canada, Micronesia, and Israel voted against. The United Kingdom, Austria, Germany, Italy, New Zealand, Japan, South Korea, and various members of the European Union abstained.The draft calls for the comprehensive implementation of and follow-up to the Durban Declaration and Programme of Action (DDPA). The core focus is on “reparatory justice,” “national anti-racism policies,” and “protections against racial profiling and structural bias embedded within contemporary technologies.”During the debate, Israel's ambassador to the United Nations, Danny Danon, condemned the attempt to grant further legitimacy to the Durban Conference, 25 years after it took place.Danon recalled that images of Hitler were circulated during the conference, Zionism was equated with racism, and Jewish participants were physically assaulted. He also noted that during this year's gathering, Iran's representative described Zionism as a “doctrine of supremacy.”Durban Conference became a platform for antisemitism, hatred of Israel“The Durban Conference was supposed to combat racism, but instead became a platform for antisemitism and hatred of Israel,” said Danon. “25 years later, the United Nations continues to celebrate this disgrace and attempts to rewrite history.”“Israel will not support a resolution that legitimizes antisemitism under the guise of fighting racism. Durban's legacy deserves no further recognition, no further celebration, and no further legitimacy. It is time to remove this stain from the United Nations once and for all.”This follows recent 25th anniversary celebrations of the 2001 Durban Conference at the United Nations.As a result of campaigning by Danon and Israel's Foreign Ministry, a record number of 46 countries boycotted the 25th-anniversary events.According to Mike Waltz, US ambassador to the UN, the US walked out “in protest, as we did at the original conference in 2001.”Original South African conference boycotted by Israel, USThe original World Conference Against Racism in Durban, South Africa, was famously boycotted midway through by both Israel and the United States.During the 2001 events, Jewish attendees faced physical harassment, and thousands of copies of the conspiracy theory antisemitic text The Protocols of the Elders of Zion were distributed. Images of Adolf Hitler were also circulated.The conference has since become synonymous with anti-Zionist discrimination, and is considered by many the birthplace of modern anti-Israel rhetoric.Preceding the conference was the NGO Forum, which had over 7,000 participants gather to create a pre-planned and coordinated anti-Israel strategy. It was here that the intentional use of words such as “genocide,” “war crimes,” and “apartheid” entered the scene.While Israel is not explicitly cited or mentioned by name in the newly updated text of the resolution, it continues to object due to the text's explicit mandate to “reaffirm” the original 2001 Durban Declaration and Programme of Action (DDPA) in its entirety.Israel argues that it is the only country or geopolitical conflict implicitly criticized within the DDPA.

title: Bipartisan group of senators call on Trump to rescind Russian diesel deal
body:
President Trump stops to speak to members of the media as he departs the White House on Oct. 13, 2026. Win McNamee/Getty Images hide caption
A bipartisan group of senators is calling on President Trump to rescind his recent diesel deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin, calling it a "betrayal of the people of Ukraine."
Last week, Trump announced via social media he had struck a deal with Putin, whereby Russia will supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel to the American and global market, followed by an additional 500,000 tons in November and one million tons "immediately thereafter."
"Additionally, based on the condition of their Diesel Refineries, Russia will then deliver, within a short period of time, 3,000,000 Tons of Diesel Fuel," Trump wrote.
His announcement stunned lawmakers, who passed legislation this summer directing the president to impose significant tariffs on the top importers of Russian oil.
Those sanctions are aimed at targeting Russian officials, companies and financial institutions helping fuel Russia's war in Ukraine. The legislation was named in memory of the late GOP Sen. Lindsey Graham , who helped negotiate Trump's support for the package.
"This deal is a gift to our adversary and a betrayal of our allies; it should be rescinded," wrote six Republican and six Democratic senators in a letter Tuesday to the president.
"The deal you struck with President Vladimir Putin on October 9 th will not achieve just ends, nor will it benefit Americans," it read.
Senators said they recognized the need to lower energy costs for Americans — but maintained that allowing Russian diesel into global markets will offer "limited to no relief to Americans."
They added the deal "only provides Putin with more fuel to finance his war machine and enables Russia to continue its brutal attacks on Ukrainian civilians."
When asked about the letter, the White House referred back to comments President Trump made to reporters on Tuesday about concerns that Russia will use proceeds from the diesel agreement to purchase weapons.
"Nobody's telling me anything," Trump said. "That's a diesel deal. Not for us. That's being released into the world. That's not being released to us. That's a diesel deal that's going to be released into the world for the world market, because the world market suffered with high prices."
The letter was signed by Democrats Richard Blumenthal, Chris Coons, Dick Durbin, Jack Reed, Jeanne Shaheen and Sheldon Whitehouse. They were joined by Republicans Alan Armstrong, Susan Collins, John Cornyn, Mitch McConnell, Lisa Murkowski and Thom Tillis.

title: Army re-evaluating munitions procurement goals as Iran war continues
body: The Army’s procurement goals for critical munitions could be shifting, officials said Tuesday in a break from the U.S. government’s typical reticence to talk about the enormous expenditure of weapons during the Trump administration's war on Iran . Increasing annual production of Patriot air defense missiles, particularly the PAC-3 Missile Segment Enhancement , is high on the priority list, Gen. Frank Lozano , the Army’s fires portfolio acquisition executive, said during a panel at the AUSA annual meeting in Washington, D.C. “Our goal has always been to get to 2,000, and we've had a lot of discussions about even more interceptors,” he said, “but when we start talking about overall missile output and we start looking at numbers—is it 4,000, is it 6,000, is it 8,000—we're looking at a diverse set of capabilities. Because we have to address the threat, and we need to address the threat in a complementary way, meaning we need to fight on a cost curve that's affordable for the U.S. Army to maintain and sustain that warfighting capability abroad.” Lozano addressed reports of depleted stockpiles by repeating the government’s insistence that all is well. “We have to win everywhere, and so when you have to win everywhere, you need to really make sure that from a foundational aspect of the joint force, you have enough depth within your magazine, from from a varying perspective of capabilities, that you're able to contribute to that joint fight in a meaningful way,” he said. “I will continue to double down and echo what our department leadership has stated: we have the capabilities we need to have to fight and win, but it's our job to ensure that victory is achievable in the future inside of any dynamic environment, scenario, fight we might find ourselves in.” The Army is also “looking into” buying PAC-2 Guidance Enhanced Missile-Tactical , he said. “Should we buy GEM-Ts? Because they're being produced,” Lozano said. “And so, if it's an effector that's available now, and GEM-Ts are a really good missile in the battle space [in which] they operate…so if we have the opportunity, it's probably something we should take advantage of, and we’re looking into doing that.” The Army’s ability to scale some of these procurement programs will depend on funding from Congress, said Brent Ingraham , the Army’s civilian acquisition chief. “We are looking every day, depending on where the budget lands, what a top line looks like, whether it's a r econciliation or not,” Ingraham said. “We have prioritized the missions that we truly need, we think about today and the near future…and so, depending on where the budget ends up, we will have to do some work to reprioritize our systems to focus on those key initiatives.” ]]>

title: Integrating sensors and weapons a key challenge in counter-drone defense, Honeywell official says
body:
WASHINGTON, D.C. As militaries confront the growing threat of small, inexpensive drones and drone swarms, one of the central challenges for counter-uncrewed aerial system (counter-UAS) technology is connecting sensors, processing data, and coordinating weapons fast enough to respond to incoming threats, a Honeywell executive said in a recent interview.
Tom Konicki, director of business development at Honeywell, said during an interview at the Association of the United States Army (AUSA) 2026 conference said integration is the key challenge in efforts to make counter-drone systems effective against adversaries.
"I don't think that the problem in counter UAS is necessarily the hardware," Konicki said. "I think the problem is tying it all together."
Today's counter-drone defenses can incorporate radar, electro-optical cameras, electronic warfare equipment, acoustic sensors, and kinetic or nonkinetic weapons. But those components often come from different manufacturers and were not designed to communicate with one another, creating challenges for operators attempting to build a coordinated defensive system. Konicki said one approach is to use software to bring those components together, allowing operators to combine data from multiple sensors and direct weapons against identified threats.
Honeywell is pursuing that approach with its Samurai counter-UAS system, which uses software called Unitas to integrate sensors and effectors from different manufacturers rather than requiring customers to purchase a fixed collection of hardware.
The approach also allows military organizations to incorporate equipment they have already purchased, avoiding the need to replace existing sensors or weapons when adding new capabilities.
Another challenge is the speed at which the various components must communicate. Detecting a drone is only part of the problem; a counter-UAS system must identify the threat, determine its location, and direct a weapon toward it before the target moves.
"I can't wait half a second for that thing to fire because in a half second that bad drone has moved over here," Konicki said.
He explained that Honeywell's software can suspend some processing functions to prioritize time-sensitive commands to weapons, reducing delays between detecting a threat and engaging it.
Distinguishing threats from other objects also presents difficulties. Konicki noted that operators may initially be unable to determine whether a radar contact is a drone or a bird, requiring additional sensor information, such as camera imagery, to make a positive identification.
That creates a need for layered detection, in which multiple sensors contribute different types of information as an object approaches a defended location.
The growing number of sensors and engagement options creates another problem: presenting the information in a way that soldiers can understand and act upon. Konicki said Honeywell has focused on combining sensor data and weapon controls into a single operator interface, rather than requiring personnel to monitor multiple independent systems.
For counter-UAS developers, these challenges place increasing emphasis on software integration, sensor fusion, processing latency, and interoperability, he added.

title: David Eby defends his family’s use of $10-a-day daycare program
body:
BC NDP leader David Eby revealed over the weekend that his family has benefited from the province’s $10-a-day childcare program.
Global News asked the question on Monday morning on the campaign trail and Eby said one of his children is part of the program.
The program was started by Eby’s predecessor John Horgan in partnership with the federal government under former prime minister Justin Trudeau and despite growing demand, Eby’s government announced a three-year pause on expanding it this past spring .
That comes as many across B.C. still struggle to find affordable daycare spots.
Advocates say B.C. continues to be the most expensive province for child care, with many parents paying between $40 to $100 a day. Only 10 per cent of B.C. childcare spaces are dedicated as $10 a day.
In response to the criticism, Eby says his child was at the daycare already before it was designated as $10-a-day.
When asked on Tuesday morning, Eby said his family “donated the difference” to the childcare provider so that other families in the area could benefit.
Later, the BC NDP told Global News that Eby’s family has donated $3,200 since mid 2024 for a total of eight months’ enrollment, meaning a monthly donation of $400.
They say the family intends to donate a further $4,800 at the end of this year.
“My focus is to make sure British Columbians benefit from affordable child care,” Eby said.
“That’s why we put it into the agreement with the federal government so more British Columbians could benefit; that’s why we’re expanding before and after school care. And unfortunately, and perhaps because of their total disinterest, frankly, historically, and continuing in young families, the Conservatives are proposing to cut that program.”
In a statement issued on Monday, the BC Conservatives did not state they would cut the program, but did call the admission from Eby “shocking.”
“Nobody begrudges David Eby and his wife for their success,” Margareta Dovgal, Conservative Party of BC candidate for Vancouver-Yaletown, said in the statement.
“The Conservative Party of BC wants more British Columbians to succeed. What families will not accept is a Premier who promised them $10-a-day child care, failed to deliver it, and then took one of the scarce spots for himself while a single mom working two jobs sits on a waitlist.”

title: Show HN: Parsimony – an open-source benchmark for how much code AI models add
body:
Existing benchmarks measure solve rate and cost, but don't punish excess code, which makes a codebase harder to work with in the long term. Parsimony measures how much code AI models add.
It takes the patches that benchmarks already publish and counts syntax units (calls, names, literals and so on) rather than lines: net syntax units = added − removed ( method ).
Chart Scatter: compare two metrics Bars: one metric Show my runs Show other harnesses Show older generations Weights All models Open weights Proprietary
Models are ranked by mean net syntax units added on the tasks they solved, lowest first. "Net syntax units added (mean)" also includes failed attempts. Solved comes from SWE-bench Verified ; tests aren't rerun. Measured is how many solved attempts could be measured.
Each model has its own solved, measured comparison tasks and peer mixture. Missing measurements are not zero; large patches can dominate the ratio. Hover over a ratio for its shared-task count and conditional 95% range, or over Measured for success coverage. These ranges do not cover missingness, peer selection or differing harness/retry policies; configurations are not controlled model-only comparisons. Ranking details and offline diagnostics .
It's an outside score, matched by model and reasoning effort, and doesn't affect the rank.
Faded models were run by me on the first few DeepSWE Python tasks (OpenAI models with pi, and the GPT-6 family with Codex, whose pi runs appear with "Show other harnesses"; Anthropic models with Claude Code) and graded with each task's own tests. They aren't verified or ranked. GPT-5.6 Sol ran both ways: my run added 0.88× the code of its published run.
Swipe the table sideways for more columns.
Missing a model? Request it . A number looks wrong? Report it . Have spare API credits? Run a model on the tasks .
Net syntax units on the intersection of two models' solved, measured tasks, without the three-peer ranking gate. Rank is unchanged. Repeated attempts of one task are averaged first.
Have code-size numbers from another benchmark? Download the example file, fill in your results and open it to get the same chart and table. The file stays in your browser. Format and how to share it .
Code and data: github.com/La5u/Parsimony

title: Ukraine wins seat on UN Human Rights Council, vows to seek accountability for Russian abuses
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Ukraine has been elected to the UN Human Rights Council for the 2027–2029 term, receiving support from 162 UN member states in a vote by the UN General Assembly on 13 October, Ukraine’s Permanent Mission to the UN said. The three-year term gives Ukraine an opportunity to shape international human rights discussions while drawing attention to abuses stemming from Russia’s war. Kyiv says it will work with partners to strengthen accountability mechanisms and protect civilians affected by conflict. Ukraine’s Permanent Mission to the UN called the result a major diplomatic achievement, saying its team had spent more than a year securing support for the candidacy. Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said Kyiv would use its membership to push for accountability for Russian human rights violations, support international investigations, and advocate for prisoners of war and civilians unlawfully detained by Russia. Ukraine will also continue efforts to secure the return of Ukrainian children deported or forcibly transferred by Russia, Sybiha said. Ukraine to focus on accountability for Russian violations Ukraine’s election comes as Russia continues its full-scale war against the country, which has brought grave violations of human rights and international humanitarian law consistently since 2022. As a council member, Ukraine plans to work with international partners to strengthen mechanisms for documenting and investigating abuses, protect human dignity, and reinforce international human rights institutions, Sybiha said. Ukraine has been elected to the UN Human Rights Council for 2027-2029. I thank all UN Member States that supported Ukraine’s candidacy. Ukraine joins the Council while continuing to defend its people and its sovereignty against Russia’s ongoing aggression, which has brought… — Andrii Sybiha (@andrii_sybiha) October 13, 2026 Ukraine is returning to the council after previously serving multiple terms, most recently from 2021 to 2023. It was among the council’s founding members when the body was established in 2006. Russia was suspended from the UN Human Rights Council in April 2022 following reports of gross and systematic human rights violations during its war against Ukraine. Moscow subsequently announced it was withdrawing from the council. 15 countries elected to the council Alongside Ukraine, the General Assembly elected Brazil, Ghana, the Dominican Republic, Zambia, Ireland, Jordan, Kuwait, Moldova, Nepal, Nigeria, Germany, Uruguay, and Japan to the Human Rights Council. The 47-member council is the UN’s principal intergovernmental body responsible for promoting and protecting human rights worldwide. Members serve three-year terms. title: Appeal court panel hands off SERAP’s N101m defamation appeal
body: The Court of Appeal in Abuja on Tuesday returned the case files in two appeals arising from a N101 million defamation judgment in favour of two operatives of the Department of State Services (DSS) to the Presiding Judge for reassignment. The appeals were filed by the Incorporated Trustees of the Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP) and by its Deputy Director, Kolawole Ogundare. The High Court of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) awarded the damages in May. The panel had earlier heard the first appeal and reserved judgment. It later vacated that order, ruling that the two appeals, which emanated from one judgment, should be heard together for a composite judgment. The development was the second setback in the matter. Last week, proceedings in Ogundare’s appeal were halted midway. Before the panel vacated its order, a brief drama played out when SERAP’s lead counsel, Tayo Oyetibo, SAN, told the court that an application was pending for certain persons to be joined as amici curiae (friends of the court). Prof Olarewaju Fagbohun, SAN, a former Vice-Chancellor of the University of Lagos, rose to address the panel. He said he appeared for the Columbia Global Freedom of Expression Initiative of Columbia University and for the United Nations Special Rapporteurs on the rights to freedom of peaceful assembly and of association, and to freedom of opinion and expression. He said the application, filed on October 12 under Order 6 Rule 1 of the Court of Appeal Rules 2021 and Section 6(6)(a) of the 1999 Constitution, sought leave to participate in the appeal. “We’re seeking the leave of this Hon court to participate in this appeal and assist the court with independent submissions,” he said. He added that the proposed brief would offer independent legal analysis and relevant comparative and international jurisprudence. The panel’s lead judge, Justice Danlami Senchi, was unimpressed. “Did the court invite you? Let’s be serious. This is the kind of image we create that is not good for us. We didn’t invite you. On behalf of whom?” he asked. He added: “I said earlier that we are not here to speak long grammar or waste the court’s time. We didn’t seek for any assistance.” Fagbohun replied: “We are not adversarial. We’re actually trying to assist this court.” Justice Senchi said every matter is decided on its merits and that an outsider could be heard only if its interests would be injured. “But you’re not a party in the lower court and in this court,” he said, asking the professor to withdraw the application “so that we can make progress.” Fagbohun withdrew the application and apologised to the court. The judge commended him: “Your juniors here will be happy for that.” Mojirayo Ogunlana, who appeared for the Southern African Litigation Centre, also withdrew her application to be admitted as amicus curiae. The panel then turned to Ogundare’s appeal, the same one that stalled last Friday. Midway into the hearing of an application for enlargement of time by the appellant’s counsel, Oluwatosin Adesoye, the court voiced displeasure with his presentation, saying he “should have sought the counsel of your seniors.” “Look at the way and manner you couched your prayers. We can’t grant this. You have to withdraw and refile it,” Justice Senchi said. “This is a court of record. You’re before the Court of Appeal.” The judge then announced: “We are sending this case file back for reassignment.” In its appeal, SERAP argues that the judgment was legally and procedurally flawed. Its Appellant’s Brief of Argument, filed by Oyetibo, raises 24 grounds challenging the finding of liability, the damages and the consequential orders. The group says the central question is whether the claimants proved by credible evidence that the publications referred to them. “The publications did not name the respondents, and the descriptions relied upon were general physical descriptions which did not, without more, identify the particular individuals who brought the action,” SERAP said. The publications followed SERAP’s call on President Bola Tinubu to investigate alleged corruption at the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) and reverse fuel price increases. SERAP had alleged that DSS officers entered its Abuja office without proper notice, describing two of them as “a tall, large, dark-skinned woman” and “a slim, dark-skinned man.” SERAP argues that neither publication identified the claimants by name, rank, designation, office or photograph. It adds that the claimants called no independent witness to show that an ordinary member of the public read the publications and understood them to refer to the two officers. “No independent witness was called to establish the alleged identification, while the social-media reactions relied upon by the respondents were not tendered in evidence,” the group said. SERAP also accuses the trial court of supplying the missing identification link by relying, among other things, on its own observation of the claimants’ physical appearance during proceedings. “The issue was whether the publications identified the respondents when they were published, not whether the respondents happened to fit the descriptions when they appeared before the Court,” it said. The group further describes the ₦100 million damages as excessive and unsupported by sufficient evidence. It says the trial court relied on claims that the publications affected the officers “mentally and psychologically” and had “gone viral,” without evidence of the extent of publication or of specific professional, financial or reputational injury. The post Appeal court panel hands off SERAP’s N101m defamation appeal appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: CSLS urges National Assembly to give ACJA amendment bill speedy passage
body:
The Centre for Socio-Legal Studies (CSLS) on Tuesday called for a speedy passage of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act Amendment Bill.
The President of CSLS, Yemi Akinseye-George, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), made the call during the closing ceremony of the centre’s summit on improving the nation’s criminal justice administration through the National Minimum Standards (NMS) project.
Mr Akinseye-George said CSLS, which played pivotal roles in the conception and the subsequent enactment of the Act in 2015, worked with the Federal Ministry of Justice and other stakeholders to conclude the final draft of the ACJA Amendment Bill.
“It is now an Executive Bill, sponsored by the President through the Office of the Attorney-General of the Federation,” said Mr Akinseye-George, a professor of law.
Mr Akinseye-George, whose CSLS, has championed an amendment of the Act in recent years to address the gaps discovered in the law after decade of putting the law into use, urged the National Assembly to give the ACJA Amendment Bill “speedy and thorough consideration.”
He also urged “states and institutions to keep applying the National Minimum Standards,” and vowed support for “evidence-based reform in the sector.”
The ACJA 2015 governs criminal proceedings in federal courts and criminal justice administration regarding federal offences. Most states have since domesticated versions of the laws in their domains.
However, Mr Akinseye said the Act needed amendment, which informed part of the NMS project.
The NMS project was implemented under the Rule of Law and Anti-Corruption (RoLAC) Programme, funded by the European Union and supported by International IDEA.
The project aims close the gap between what Nigeria’s criminal justice laws promise and what happens in practice.
It also sees to the efficient implementation of the provisions of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act (ACJA) in federal courts and the Administration of Criminal Justice Laws (ACJLs) of various states of the federation.
According to Mr Akinseye-George, the NMS “gives the ACJA and related laws a clear, measurable yardstick for the police, courts, prosecutors, legal aid providers and correctional services.”
The NMS is a document compiled so that no state would fall below in the implementation of the ACJA, and for the purpose of uniformity across all states.
Some NMS project focus on pre-trial issues, dealing with interlocutory proceedings, use of remands, confessional statements, front loading, case management and plea-bargaining.
The CSLS implemented the project in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) and seven focal states – Lagos, Kano, Edo, Anambra, Abia, Plateau, and Adamawa.
Through the project, the CSLS equipped judges, magistrates, lawyers, police, and civil society.
It also trained over 700 rangers and engaged 1,700 relevant stakeholders. In April, the centre organised a capacity-building training for 100 rangers. The training equipped the rangers to champion the reform of the Nigerian criminal justice system.
Rangers are those who volunteer to support and to speak in favour of the proper implementation of the ACJA.
The centre also paid inspection visits to courts, correctional centres, ministries of justice, police commands, the Legal Aid Council and the Administration of Criminal Justice Monitoring Committees (ACJMCs). Through the visits, gaps were identified which were reflected in the Bill. Also, 1000 copies of the NMS documents were produced.
Mr Akinseye-George applauded the European Union for funding. Similarly, he commended the International IDEA, the Federal Ministry of Justice and other criminal justice institutions and the media for their partnership and support.

title: Most tokenized stock trading on Solana, BNB Chain occurs outside US market hours
body:
Tokenized equities have reached nearly $3.3 billion in value as investors embrace round-the-clock access beyond Wall Street hours.
Most trading in tokenized stocks on major blockchains now takes place outside regular US market hours, offering an early indication that around-the-clock trading could be one of the biggest advantages of putting equities onchain.
According to Blockworks data cited by The Kobeissi Letter, more than 70% of tokenized stock trading volume on BNB Chain occurs outside the traditional 9:30 am to 4 pm Eastern trading session. The figure is 63% on Solana and nearly 60% on Base.
Meanwhile, Jupiter, a major Solana-based trading platform, reported a 50% month-over-month increase in tokenized asset trading volume.
The figures suggest investors use tokenized stocks to trade when traditional US exchanges are closed, rather than simply replicating activity during regular market hours.
The growth comes as tokenized stock values have increased by 15% over the past 30 days to nearly $3.3 billion, according to RWA.xyz data . A significant portion of that value is concentrated among issuers such as Ondo Global Markets, xStocks and bStocks, whose tokens are issued and traded across different blockchains.
Related: Winners and losers of the SEC’s new tokenized stocks rules
The growth in round-the-clock trading comes as US regulators begin opening the door to tokenized equities in traditional markets. Last month, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) introduced an “innovation exemption” allowing qualifying venues to trade tokenized US-listed stocks on public blockchains.
SEC Commissioner Mark Uyeda said participating venues must publish transaction data in US dollars, including trade prices, sizes, timestamps and daily trading volumes. They must also disclose liquidity pool addresses and balances.
Unlike existing tokenized stock products such as xStocks and Ondo Global Markets, which are generally unavailable to US investors, the SEC exemption allows qualifying venues to offer tokenized US equities domestically, provided they preserve shareholder rights and meet trading and disclosure requirements.

title: Court hands Adjetey Sowah, two others lifetime bans after Amputee Football legal dispute
body: A High Court judgment has handed Francis Adjetey Sowah and two others associated with the Ghana Amputee Football Federation (GAFF) lifetime bans following a decade-long legal dispute. The court rejected claims of the Ghana Amputee Football Federation (GAFF) in its dispute with the National Paralympic Committee of Ghana (NPC-Ghana) and handed the culprits a significant legal setback, while also referencing World Amputee Football Federation (WAFF) correspondence documenting lifetime bans involving three individuals associated with the organisation. The judgment, delivered on July 30, 2026, by Justice Jerome Noble-Nkrumah at the Commercial Division of the High Court in Accra, ruled against GAFF’s claims to exclusive responsibility for the administration and oversight of amputee football in Ghana. The court also granted relief to NPC Ghana on its counterclaim, permanently restraining GAFF and those acting through it from presenting the federation as the lawful body responsible for overseeing amputee football in the country. Court Records Lifetime Bans Against Three Individuals One of the most consequential passages in the judgment appears on page 21, where the court examined an email from WAFF dated September 25, 2019. According to the judgment, the correspondence referred to the banning of Francis Adjetey Sowah, Charles Narh and Benjamin Armah from amputee football for life, citing ethical breaches involving the three individuals. The judgment records the contents of the WAFF correspondence. This distinction is important: the lifetime bans are referenced in the evidence considered by the court, while the operative injunction specifically addresses GAFF’s claim to lawful oversight of amputee football in Ghana. Sowah’s Conduct Comes Under Judicial Scrutiny The court’s assessment of Sowah’s conduct was another significant aspect of the ruling. The judgment states that evidence showed Sowah was promoting GAFF’s affairs while serving as an officer of the Ghana Amputee Football Association, describing the activity as having been carried out “surreptitiously” before he was discovered and removed. The judge also examined correspondence bearing Sowah’s signature on the Association’s letterhead, including letters seeking equipment, logistics and sponsorship. The court contrasted those documents with Sowah’s subsequent use of GAFF letterhead in his capacity as the federation’s president, finding that the evidence seriously weakened GAFF’s claim to being the sole recognised authority responsible for the sport. These findings formed part of the court’s assessment of the federation’s claim to exclusive control over amputee football in Ghana. GAFF’s Incorporation History Raises Questions The court also considered evidence concerning GAFF’s stated objectives when it was incorporated in 2009. According to the judgment, a witness for the federation acknowledged that its original objectives did not include the organisation, administration and management of amputee football. Those objectives were added in 2014. The judge considered this admission alongside the evidence concerning Sowah’s roles within the organisations, further undermining GAFF’s argument that it was entitled to exclusive responsibility for the sport. The court ultimately found that GAFF had failed to establish its claims, while NPC Ghana succeeded on its counterclaim. Court Restrains GAFF From Claiming Lawful Oversight The judgment’s immediate institutional consequence is a permanent injunction restraining GAFF, including those acting through its servants, agents, assigns or privies, from holding itself out as the lawful oversight body for amputee football in Ghana. The court’s decision was based in part on the federation’s lack of recognition from the National Sports Authority, NPC Ghana and WAFF, as outlined in the judgment. Although GAFF argued that its history of official engagement supported its recognition and that amputee football should not fall under NPC Ghana, the court was not persuaded by its case. The judge acknowledged that the institutional placement of the sport could merit further consideration in the future. However, that observation did not alter the outcome of the proceedings. Other Names Mentioned, but No Additional Lifetime Bans Established John Kuuku Dsani and Philip Richter have also featured in public reporting surrounding the dispute. However, the judgment’s specific passage recording lifetime bans names only Francis Adjetey Sowah, Charles Narh and Benjamin Armah. It does not establish separate individual lifetime bans against all five men mentioned in the broader reporting. The ruling represents a major development in the dispute over the governance of amputee football in Ghana. By rejecting GAFF’s claims and granting NPC Ghana relief on its counterclaim, the High Court has placed a clear legal restriction on the federation’s ability to present itself as the country’s lawful amputee-football oversight body. The judgment also brings renewed attention to the WAFF correspondence documenting lifetime bans involving three individuals associated with the dispute. For Ghanaian amputee football, the decision marks a significant moment in the continuing debate over recognition, authority and the administration of the sport. The ruling also clears the air surrounding the leadership of the Black Challenge as they continue to prepare for the upcoming WAFF 2026 Amputee World Cup in Mexico in November.

title: NDC appoints Julius Kwame Anthony as a Deputy Communications Director
body: The National Democratic Congress (NDC) has appointed Julius Kwame Anthony as Deputy Communications Director with immediate effect. In a statement issued on Tuesday, October 13, 2026, and signed by the party’s General Secretary, Fifi Fiavi Kwetey, the NDC said its Functional Executive Committee approved the appointment at a meeting held the same day. The party said the appointment forms part of efforts to strengthen its communications operations, improve public engagement and communicate its policies and programmes. “He brings to the position a sound understanding of communication and its strategic application in advancing the Party’s objectives,” the statement said. The NDC expressed confidence that Mr Anthony would work with the Communications Directorate and other party structures to advance its communication objectives. The party also announced that Godwin Ako Gunn, Kakra Essamuah and Julius Kwame Anthony would serve as its designated contacts for media and other matters concerning the NDC. Mr Anthony’s appointment comes as the party continues to communicate the policies and programmes of the NDC-led government under President John Dramani Mahama, including its Reset Agenda.

title: Ogun hospital workers begin 3-day strike after patient’s relative stabs medical scientist
body: Healthcare workers at the Federal Medical Centre (FMC), Abeokuta, Ogun State, have begun a three-day warning strike following the alleged stabbing of a medical laboratory scientist, Lawal Toheeb Olasunkanmi, by a patient’s relative. Olasunkanmi was reportedly attacked on Sunday night while on duty at the hospital. A video shared on X showed the medical laboratory scientist bleeding from his nose as the alleged assailant threatened him. The incident prompted members of the hospital’s Joint Action Committee, comprising nurses, medical laboratory scientists and other non-academic staff, to commence the industrial action on Monday. In a notice issued on Monday, the committee condemned the attack and demanded measures to ensure the safety of healthcare workers within the facility. “On behalf of the leadership and entire members of our union, we write to express our profound displeasure, outrage, and deep concern over the unfortunate and unacceptable incident in which one of our colleagues (mr Lawal Toheeb Olasunkanmi), a Medical Laboratory Scientist, was stabbed by a patient’s relative last night within our Centre,” the notice read. The committee described the incident as an assault on the dignity, safety and welfare of healthcare professionals, insisting that violence against workers providing essential medical services should not be tolerated. It said hospitals should be safe environments for both patients and healthcare workers, adding that disagreements over medical services could not justify physical attacks. “No healthcare worker deserves to be threatened, assaulted, or stabbed in the course of providing care. Disagreement, frustration, or dissatisfaction with any service rendered in the hospital cannot justify violence under any circumstance,” the union said. The committee further described the attack as a collective concern for the hospital’s workforce, warning that workers could not remain silent while their safety was threatened. It called on the hospital management to formally report the incident to the appropriate law enforcement authorities and ensure that the alleged assailant was investigated and prosecuted in accordance with the law. The unions also warned against attempts to conceal or downplay the incident or resolve it in a manner that would undermine accountability. They demanded prompt and comprehensive medical treatment for Olasunkanmi, psychological support where necessary, and institutional assistance throughout his recovery. Meanwhile, the Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare, Iziaq Salako, has called on the Nigeria Police Force to immediately arrest and prosecute the suspect allegedly involved in the attack. In a statement issued on Tuesday by Ado Bako, Assistant Director of Information and Public Relations, Salako described the incident as “barbaric and unacceptable”. “No grief, frustration or dissatisfaction with care can justify violence against a health worker performing his lawful duties,” the minister said. Salako also urged the striking healthcare workers to return to their duties in the interest of patients and the wider public. He called on the hospital management to ensure that the injured worker received appropriate medical attention and support, while strengthening security arrangements in line with Federal Government directives. The minister also extended his condolences to the family of the deceased patient and advised members of the public to channel complaints about hospital services through appropriate formal procedures. title: General Dynamics Land Systems showing CUAS & armored vehicle at AUSA 2026
body:

General Dynamics Land Systems (GDLS) is exhibiting a one-eight scale model of its Wolf XM30, GDLS's candidate to replace the M2 Bradley armored vehicle, plus several counter-uncrewed aerial systems (CUASs) at this week's AUSA annual meeting and trade show.
The company announcement notes that the Wolf is one of two vehicles competing in the Army's XM30 Abrams tank replacement program; GDLS delivered its first Wolf prototype to the Army in August 2026. title: Kano: NDLEA Arrests 1,860 suspects, seizes 5.4 tonnes of drugs
body: From Abbas Tijjani Madabo, Kano The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) arrested 1,860 suspects and seized 5,409.814 kilogrammes of illicit drugs in Kano State between January and September 2026. The agency also secured 89 convictions and filed 126 new cases in court during the nine-month period, while 135 cases remained pending before the Federal High Court. The NDLEA Kano Strategic Command disclosed this in a statement issued on Tuesday by its Media and Advocacy Officer, Sadiq Muhammad Maigatari. It said the suspects included 92 females, while the seized substances comprised cannabis, cocaine, methamphetamine, psychotropic substances and other illicit drugs. 5-goal Super Falcons crush Comoros, reach Olympics qualifier third round Qatar Emir condoles Tinubu over military plane crash The command said it had also carried out about 1,700 counselling, treatment and rehabilitation interventions for people affected by substance abuse, alongside approximately 420 sensitisation programmes in schools and communities. It said Operation Restore Order, launched under the directive of the NDLEA Chairman, Brig. Gen. Mohamed Buba Marwa (retd.), led to the dismantling of about 35 identified drug joints and the arrest of more than 300 suspects. The operation was part of efforts to disrupt drug distribution networks and improve community safety across the state. The command also reported uncovering underground tunnels and caves in the Rimin Kebe area of Kano metropolis under Operation Sharar Mafaka According to the statement, drug dealers used the underground locations to conceal and conduct illicit activities, highlighting the challenges faced by operatives in tackling established drug networks. The State Commander, CN DY Lawal, commended Marwa for his leadership and commitment to the agency’s mandate. Lawal urged residents to provide timely and credible information to the agency, stressing that public participation and collaboration were essential to tackling drug-related offences.

title: ‘Jon and Kate Plus 8’ star Collin Gosselin accuses mom Kate of abuse
body:
Former Jon & Kate Plus 8 star Collin Gosselin is accusing his mother Kate Gosselin of abuse.
During an interview with ABC News’ Juju Chang , Gosselin, 22, shared what he alleged took place behind the scenes of the popular reality TV show that he grew up on.
“Simply put, my whole life that I lived was a lie,” Gosselin said. “All the things you see on TV, lies.”
Gosselin said that he and his seven siblings were being “overworked” and “exploited” while filming the reality series.
The Gosselins famously had eight children (now 22-year-old sextuplets Aaden, Alexis, Collin, Hannah, Leah and Joel, and a set of 26-year-old twins, Mady and Cara), and their TLC reality show, Jon & Kate Plus 8 , premiered in 2007.
Kate and Jon announced their divorce in 2009 and after the divorce, Kate was granted primary custody of the eight children. The series was later renamed Kate Plus 8 in 2010, focusing on Kate as a divorced mother raising all eight children, with Jon mostly absent from the show. Filming was later suspended after Jon’s lawyers delivered letters to TLC, demanding they halt production. The last episode aired in 2011.
Gosselin alleged that the abuse began after his parents’ divorce and said that one of his teachers noticed he had a swollen earlobe.
“My mom had dragged me across the room by my earlobe and my teacher saw and then I talked to my guidance counselor, and I told them about it,” he said. “And my mom was not very happy that I spoke about that.”
Gosselin said that he was pulled out of school by his mom when he was in the fourth grade.
The Special Forces: World’s Toughest Test star said that he tried to run away from home but his mom allegedly zip-tied his hands and feet together before locking him in a room in their basement.
He said his mother removed him from their home just before his 12th birthday and placed him at Fairmont Behavioral Health System, a mental health facility in Pennsylvania.
“I was told, ‘This is for your own good,'” he said. “I threatened my mom’s income, I threatened her image, and people will do anything to protect their reputation, especially my mom.”
During an appearance on the On Purpose with Jay Shetty podcast , Gosselin spoke more in detail about the abuse he alleged he experienced as a child.
“When it was Jon & Kate Plus 8 , even though it looked like America’s happiest, biggest family, behind the scenes it was not like that,” Gosselin said.
“My mom would be physically and verbally abusive to me,” Gosselin alleged.
When asked about some of the earliest memories he had, Gosselin said he began to face his mother’s “wrath” when he was eight-years-old.
“She had a room specifically built in the storage part of our unfinished basement that was cinder block walls and cement floors with a bolt lock on the outside of the door, where she would keep me” the In The Shadow Of Eight author continued. “She’s denied that previously, publicly, saying that she has never done any of that.”
Gosselin claimed that he has documentation where his mother admitted that she “does in fact have a room where she locks me in.”
Kate has previously denied her son’s allegations of abuse.
In a statement shared to Instagram in 2023 , Kate wrote, “My son Collin, whom I love with all my heart, has received multiple psychiatric diagnoses over the years. For the safety of myself, his brothers and sisters and for his own well-being, he was placed in a facility following years of outpatient treatment which proved insufficient for his needs.”
“The decision to admit him was made by emergency room doctors following one of his many attacks/outbursts—this one involving his use of a weapon. Fast forward to the present day, and following Jon’s removal of Collin from treatment, my son’s unpredictable and violent behaviors have sadly continued regularly towards Jon, Hannah, and others around him,” she continued.
“Collin’s distorted perception of reality is one of the many issues that he has always struggled with. As many people who have family members grappling with mental health issues can attest, it is rarely and sadly surprising when complete fabrications occur, and this is just another heartbreaking facet of this fight,” Kate wrote.
“All parent-child relationships are complex, but when mental illness is involved, it is incredibly complicated and painful, and certainly not easy for others on the outside to understand,” the Kate + Date star added. “All measures that were taken in our home were at the explicit recommendation of his pediatric psychiatrist and/or his team of specialists and were put into place to safeguard every member of our family, our friends as well as our family pets.”
“Unfortunately, I believe Collin remains a very troubled young man who continues to need a lot of help. His brothers and sisters and I have not been directly involved in his life due to his history of unpredictable behavior and violent tendencies towards us,” the post concluded.
Gosselin has been estranged from his mother since 2016.
Gosselin’s father Jon was awarded sole legal and physical custody of Collin in December 2018.

title: US envoy says next UN Secretary General should be chosen on merit, not rotation or gender
body: US President Donald Trump ’s special envoy for global partnerships said on Tuesday that the next UN Secretary General should be chosen on merit rather than regional rotation or gender, as these are “political traditions” rather than “legal rules” under the UN Charter. “The world should choose the best person for the job – based on merit, reform and results,” Paolo Zampolli said on social media. “After 18 years at the United Nations , I believe this is a moment to think bigger about the future of the institution.” The Security Council is to select a successor to Secretary General Antonio Guterres, whose term ends on December 31. The Trump administration has so far kept its preferences private, leaving uncertainty over who it might support in a contest that has drawn seven candidates , including Guyana’s Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett and Argentina’s Rafael Grossi. Costa Rica’s Rebeca Grynspan has emerged as the front-runner, but her support has shown signs of weakening. In the fifth round of informal straw voting on October 7 , Ms Grynspan received nine “encourage” votes and six “discourage” votes, with no council members expressing “no opinion”. That was a setback from the previous round, on September 29, when she won 10 votes in favour, three against and two with no opinion. To secure the post, a candidate must win at least nine votes in the Security Council without a veto from any of its five permanent members – the US, Britain, France, Russia and China. The selection process has long been shaped by unwritten diplomatic conventions, including the expectation that the post should rotate among the world’s regions. Since 1946, the position has been held by leaders from Europe, Asia, Africa and Latin America, although no formal rotation system exists. The organisation has also never been led by a woman in its 81-year history, despite repeated calls from member states for more women's representation. The final decision rests largely with the Security Council’s five permanent members, each of which can block a candidate regardless of how much support that person has. “The UN Charter only offers limited guidance about the process for selecting a new UN Secretary General. It requires the Security Council to recommend an individual for the General Assembly to appoint to the role,” said Daniel Forti, head of UN affairs at the International Crisis Group. Much of the process, he said, had evolved through changes to council procedures and agreements with the General Assembly. The expectation of regional representation developed through decades of diplomatic practice and non-binding General Assembly resolutions. A 1997 General Assembly resolution called for regional rotation and gender to be taken into account when selecting a secretary general, while a 2015 resolution encouraged member states to nominate women. Neither resolution is legally binding. Another long-standing convention has excluded citizens of the five permanent Security Council member states from the post, reflecting concerns that a major power could exert undue influence over the institution. “Many other factors, whether the demand for regional rotation, the push for the UN to select its first woman secretary general, or commitments about the SG not being a P5 national, are all informal conventions,” Mr Forti said. "They are not binding on the Security Council even if they weigh heavily in the court of public opinion." The veto is a different matter. “The UN Charter is indirect, but unequivocal, about the permanent members’ veto privileges in the Secretary General selection process,” Mr Forti said. “No one questions that the recommendation of a new UN leader is a substantive decision, so the permanent members’ veto authorities are inconvenient but undisputed.”
