More AI agents will soon be able to browse and purchase from Shopify listings, marking an expansion of the company’s agentic commerce ambitions.
Shopify announced Tuesday it will let shoppers configure their AI agents to purchase products on their behalf, giving more agents access to over a billion listings in Shopify’s catalog. (The catalog consists of both items on and off Shopify storefronts.) In September, Shopify announced it was partnering with Meta to allow its Muse agent to browse and purchase items on a human’s behalf; now, shoppers can use any agent without a partnership integration.
To set up the feature, customers connect an agent with their account on Shop, a Shopify-owned platform that consolidates orders, tracks packages, and recommends products. Like the Muse partnership, customers use the one-click Shop Pay feature to check out within the conversation with the agent. Orders placed through the agent are funneled back to the Shop app. Shopify is marketing the feature as a “personal shopper” that humans can give rules to, like setting budget guardrails or only displaying products with fast shipping. Buyers must approve each purchase.
E-commerce has become one of the battlegrounds in the era of AI — it’s no coincidence that many demos of agentic tools end with a transaction, whether it’s buying clothing, booking a flight, or ordering takeout on a human’s behalf . The tech industry, including big commerce players like Google and Amazon , are investing in AI-driven shopping tools where the end goal is an “agent” purchasing things for a human user. It’s also the basis of an ongoing fight between Amazon and AI companies like Perplexity — and more recently, Meta’s Muse — over whether agents should be able to shop on a customer’s behalf.

title: Dominion Dynamics and TENCORE to Build UGVs in Canada for Ukraine
body: Dominion Dynamics , an Ottawa-based defence technology company, and TENCORE, a Ukrainian leader in defence technologies, signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to manufacture TENCORE’s TerMIT uncrewed ground vehicle (UGV) in Canada and integrate AuraNet, Dominion’s autonomy stack for pan-domain command and control. AuraNet, Dominion’s Arctic-hardened autonomy stack, will serve as the onboard intelligence layer for TENCORE’s TerMIT, with companies targeting 2027 production The partnership will support the deployment and continued development of AuraNet for Ukraine’s front lines. It will also create high-skilled jobs in Canada and strengthen Canada’s sovereign defence technology base. The MoU follows a joint declaration on defence cooperation that Prime Minister Mark Carney and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy signed in September. Both nations committed to manufacturing thousands of battle-tested drones and uncrewed systems in the next two years, with one-third earmarked for Ukraine’s defence. “When Prime Minister Carney and President Zelenskyy committed our countries to build together, they gave industry a mission. Canada has the workforce and the suppliers to build at scale. This agreement is how two companies start turning that commitment into vehicles, and we intend to move fast,” said Eliot Pence, founder and CEO of Dominion Dynamics. The companies signed the agreement at the Canada Pavilion during the AUSA 2026 defence conference in Washington, DC. Nadia Theodore, Canada’s Deputy Ambassador to the United States, attended the signing ceremony. Dominion plans to manufacture TerMIT in Canadian facilities with initial production targeted for 2027. A TENCORE team will lead the initial technology transfer and train technicians in Canada to build its UGV. Since 2024, TENCORE has delivered more than 5,000 UGVs to Ukrainian military units. TENCORE co-founder Roman Tkachenko said the pace of the war has reshaped how his company operates. “The biggest lesson from Ukraine is speed,” said Tkachenko. “Battlefield requirements change in weeks, so production, operational feedback and engineering have to run as a loop: build, deploy, learn, change, scale. Canada gives us the manufacturing base, suppliers and reliable power to run that loop alongside allies who need these vehicles.” Dominion also aims to develop an Arctic-hardened TerMIT for Canadian operations and for export to NATO allies. The companies will continue to work toward definitive agreements. The post Dominion Dynamics and TENCORE to Build UGVs in Canada for Ukraine appeared first on Canadian Defence Review .

title: Ghana repatriates 120 Nigerians rescued from suspected cybercrime centres
body: The Minister of Communications, Samuel Nartey George, has announced that Ghana has returned 120 Nigerian nationals to their home country following an operation that uncovered suspected cybercrime activities and alleged human trafficking. The exercise, known as Operation Cyberhunt, brought together Ghanaian security agencies and international partners to tackle criminal networks operating in the country. Mr George said the individuals had been brought to Ghana and forced to work in cybercrime operations. He expressed gratitude to the Ghana Air Force and the Ministry of Defence for supporting their repatriation. The operation also yielded a substantial cache of electronic equipment, including 136 mobile phones, 130 laptops and internet connectivity devices. Four vehicles were seized, one of which was reportedly stolen from Canada. Investigators also recovered jewellery and 10 Nigerian passports during the operation. The minister disclosed that eight other individuals were being processed for prosecution but did not specify the offences they were expected to face. The Cyber Security Authority led the operation, working with local security and intelligence agencies and counterparts in the United Kingdom, Nigeria and the United States. Mr George said the exercise formed part of the government’s efforts to disrupt cybercrime networks and prevent the country from becoming a base for criminal activity. “Ghana under President John Dramani Mahama will remain an unfavourable destination for cyber criminals,” he said. The operation underscores the intersection of cybercrime and human trafficking, with authorities seeking to dismantle suspected criminal networks while addressing the alleged exploitation of people recruited into their activities. Investigations into the operation and the individuals involved are continuing. The minister has not publicly provided further details about the identities of those repatriated or the specific activities they were allegedly compelled to undertake.

title: UK ambassador summoned to Iran’s foreign ministry
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 13 (MNA) – The British ambassador to Tehran, Hugo Shorter, was summoned to Iran’s Foreign Ministry on Tuesday over baseless allegations by senior British officials linking Tehran to an alleged incident at RAF Fairford military base.
Alireza Yousefi, assistant foreign minister and director general for Western Europe at Iran’s Foreign Ministry, conveyed the Islamic Republic’s strong protest against what he described as Britain’s irresponsible and destructive approach toward Iran.
Yousefi categorically rejected the British government’s allegations against Iran, stressing that British officials could not evade accountability and their international responsibilities by deflecting blame and making unfounded accusations against Tehran.
He said Britain remained responsible for its participation in the US and Israeli military aggression against Iran, as well as for its long-standing hosting of anti-Iranian terrorist groups and elements.
Condemning Britain’s irresponsible actions as part of what he described as an anti-Iran campaign, Yousefi said such conduct was entirely inconsistent with the British government’s international legal obligations.
He stressed that the British government must provide, without delay, documents and evidence supporting its allegations against Iran concerning the alleged incident at RAF Fairford. Otherwise, the Islamic Republic would seriously reconsider bilateral relations, he warned, adding that the British government would bear responsibility for the consequences.
The British ambassador said he would convey Iran’s position to the officials in his country.

title: NBBF Crisis: Presidential candidates petition Tinubu over alleged manipulation
body: Concerned stakeholders and presidential candidates in the forthcoming Nigeria Basketball Federation (NBBF) elections have petitioned President Bola Ahmed Tinubu over alleged grave irregularities and constitutional breaches in the electoral process for the 2026 elections. In a petition dated October 12, 2026, addressed to the President and copied to the President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio, the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Rt. Hon. Abbas Tajudeen, and the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Senator George Akume, they alleged that the process has been compromised. The petition was jointly signed by three presidential aspirants – Mr. Igoche Mark, Presidential Candidate/North Central Rep, Mr. Olumide Oyedeji, Presidential Candidate/NBBF Member/South West Rep, and Mr. Ejike Ugboaja, Presidential Candidate/South East Rep. “We, the undersigned stakeholders and candidates in the forthcoming Nigeria Basketball Federation (NBBF) elections for the 2026–2030 term, most respectfully wish to draw your attention to grave irregularities and constitutional breaches in the ongoing electoral process. We are deeply concerned that the outgoing President of the NBBF, Engr. Ahmadu Musa Kida, who is also the Chairman of NNPC Ltd, has compromised the process to favour his anointed candidate, Dr. Mustapha Abdullahi, Director-General of the Energy Commission of Nigeria,” the petition reads. The stakeholders alleged that barely two weeks to the Extraordinary and Elective Congresses, the leadership of the federation has embarked on arbitrary removal of legitimate state chairmen and delegates. “Barely two weeks to the Extraordinary and Elective Congresses, over fifteen legitimate State Basketball Association Chairmen and representatives have been arbitrarily removed and replaced with unqualified persons to secure votes for his preferred candidate. The affected states include Zamfara, Kaduna, Gombe, Benue, Kwara, Osun, Ondo, Ekiti, Niger, Edo and Taraba. “This action, executed with huge financial inducement and abuse of influence, including the support of some State Governors, is animical to all principles of fairness, equity and the NBBF Constitution. Some candidates have also been left out of positions they have applied for by the Electoral Committee,” they stated. The petitioners further questioned the eligibility of Dr. Mustapha Abdullahi to lead the basketball federation while still serving as a Chief Executive of a Federal Government agency. They argued that, “It is trite that under the Public Service Rules (PSR) on Part-Time Commercial Activity, under the Nigeria Public Service Rules (2026 Edition), a full time public servant, especially the Chief Accounting Officer (CEO) and Accounting Officer of a Government Agency is prohibited from engaging in any business, occupation or private runnings of organizations that will detract from their full time official duties. Therefore, we are concerned that Dr. Mustapha Abdullahi, being a serving public officer heading a critical Federal Government agency, may not have the full commitment which the leadership of the NBBF demands.” The aggrieved stakeholders therefore appealed to President Tinubu to urgently intervene to save the sport.

title: Sig Sauer’s M250 Machine Gun Gets Shorter And Lighter After Army Feedback
body: Feedback from the U.S. Army has led to an improved A1 version of the service’s still very new 6.8x51mm M250 light machine gun . Manufacturer Sig Sauer has shortened and lightened the barrel, reduced the overall weight, changed the buttstock, and made various other improvements to improve reliability and ease of use. The evolution of the M250 mirrors the transformation of Sig’s M7 rifle for the U.S. Army into the M8 carbine , where weight and bulk were major points of criticism of the original design. Jason St. John, senior director of strategic products for the Defense Strategies Group at Sig Sauer, talked about the new M250A1 with our Howard Altman at the Association of the U.S. Army’s (AUSA) main annual convention today. The U.S. Army has already been acquiring and fielding baseline M250s as part of its Next Generation Squad Weapons (NGSW) program. The NGSW family also includes the M7 rifle and now the M8 carbine from Sig, both also chambered to fire the 6.8x51mm round. The Army chose Sig as the winner of the NGSW competition in 2022. The service is still in the early stages of fielding the NGSW family as replacements for a substantial portion of its existing 5.56x45mm M4A1 carbines and M249 Squad Automatic Weapons (SAW). A promotional image of Sig Sauer’s entrants into the NGSW competition at the time of the company’s win in 2022. Sig Sauer “We continuously and constantly evaluate and evolve our designs, and we discover things,” St. John told us. “Parts that might be able to be manufactured a little bit easier with a little bit of a design change. They might be more reliable, more durable than you currently have. You might look at the system and say, hey, we have an ability to make these recommendations because we see this from other customers across the board. We hear it from our inputs of soldiers that are in our ranks, and you know maybe old relationships out in the field.” “The [NGSW] program office represents the entire formation, so they get feedback in the totality of every single unit that has them [M250s and other guns in the NGSW family] in their hands,” he continued. If “a systemic issue or something that needs to be addressed, then they run the soldier touchpoint events, which we’re fortunate enough to be a part of. And then we get unfiltered feedback from soldiers that day in the field while they’re encountering something that they have a concern about.” As noted at the start, the most immediate standout feature on the M250A1 being shown at AUSA this week is the new 13-inch barrel. M250s entering Army service now have roughly 16-inch-long barrels. The Army’s official fact sheet says the machine gun was originally expected to come with a 17.5-inch barrel. “We shortened the barrel to 13 inches, but the Army’s also buying the 16-inch barrel,” St. John explained. “So in some ways, you could consider it mission-configurable, whether they want to utilize a 13-inch barrel or a 16-inch barrel, to what they’re doing.” “You’re going to maintain the same basic ballistics that you had with the M7 [rifle’s] 13-inch barrel, and then you’re going to have more maneuverability because you’re going to have a shorter weapon system,” he added. “You add the 16-inch barrel, and you get that lethality requirement with the length of barrel that they originally required. So you have some flexibility there.” “You shorten the barrel, you’re going to lose velocity,” St. John did acknowledge. “We did not change the ammo. The Army had determined with the barrel change that they were meeting their ballistic and lethality goals with that length of barrel.” With the current 6.8x51mm ammunition, “we’re operating in the mid-70s [sic; 70,000 pounds per square inch] as far as pressure, and the case has 125K psi potential,” he also noted. “If you wanted to shorten the barrel and you did have some lethality concerns or wanted more performance, all you need to simply do is just increase the little bit more pressure in the cartridge case, and you overcome that shortness.” A graphic showing the components of a typical 6.8x51mm round, which has a hybrid case design with a steel base and brass body. Sig Sauer “We didn’t do that. The Army said it wasn’t necessary, but you know, as the battlefield evolves and defensive postures change, if that becomes necessary, one of the great things about the NGSW program is the ability for the weapon systems and the ammunition to grow in their performance capacity,” he continued. In the case of the 13-inch barrel, “we tapered the barrel down a little bit to add a little bit of weight savings,” he noted. TWZ has reached out to Sig about getting more complete specifications for the M250A1, including overall length and total weight with different barrel options. The baseline version weighs some 13 pounds, empty, and without optics and other accessories, according to the Army’s fact sheet. As already mentioned, the M7 rifle also got progressively shorter and lighter before giving way fully to the M8 carbine, in part through reprofiling of the barrel. The empty weight of the M8 with its 10-inch barrel is close to one pound less than that of the 13-inch barreled M7. A US Army Ranger fires an M250 light machine gun. US Army Different barrels can be readily swapped out on the M250A1, as well as the baseline M250. However, the new variant features significant changes to the quick-change barrel arrangement on the gun and associated elements of the design. “It was interchangeable before, but it didn’t have a quick-change barrel handle. It wasn’t meant to be changed, and therefore it didn’t need the insulation of [sic; for] a hot barrel like you get with a barrel with a quick-change barrel handle,” according to St. John. “I think initially with the [M]250 program, it wasn’t necessary, and potentially might not have been desired initially. And why put that weight burden on there if we weren’t going to utilize it, right?” St. John did not elaborate further on why these features were initially deemed unnecessary. “When you look at the top cover of the forearm, that used to be loose, and now it’s captured, meaning that when you change the barrel, it actually came off completely in your hand,” he also noted. “We utilized a similar design to our .338 MMG [Medium Machine Gun], and then we make it captured now, so you’re not going to lose it.” A picture of soldiers receiving instruction on the baseline M250. The top cover on the example seen in front is open, and it notably lacks a handle to help with barrel changes. US Army “We added a funnel to guide your gas piston in, so that when you’re doing barrel change operations, you don’t have to be precisely lined up,” he added. Now, “you have something that’s going to guide it in a stressful environment, to get that into position to do your barrel change.” The M250A1 features a host of other changes that are unrelated to the barrel. Sig also “improved our gas system a little bit, just to make it more reliable and durable,” to include modifications to keep it better “insulated from carbon and things like that.” “We opened up the trigger guard to incorporate the Arctic fight, the Arctic glove, more so than just the operational normal tactical gloves,” according to St. John. “We opened it up a little bit more to accomplish that.” An M250 seen during cold-weather testing. US Army The Arctic is an ever-more strategic region where the U.S. faces growing geopolitical competition, especially from Russia and now China. Army officials also regularly point out that the harsh environment presents challenges when using standard equipment designed around use in more temperate locales. “We improved the buttstock, and we improved the interface … to the receiver,” St. John explained. “We’ve made the interface between that more robust because through IMTing, and over time, and the buttstock getting slammed on the ground, and just normal military training and operations, we noticed that we had a tendency for some of them to loosen up and have some play in them.” “The entire buttstock is a different buttstock than they had,” he added. “They [Army soldiers] preferred that buttstock over the buttstock that we had on it. So we just put soldiers’ preference on there. … It’s just a commercially available [design from] Magpul that they thought was better than the other Magpul that day one we were using.” Changes were made to points where the M250 is designed to be attached to tripods on the ground or pintle mounts on vehicles. “We put cross-bolts through the receiver to provide more durability,” he explained. “Initially, it was like an M-LOK type of lockup, and you can just think of a steel nut on an aluminum receiver being vibrated over a life cycle of the weapon system, it has some unfortunate wear characteristics. So, putting these cross pins redirects that force, and the way we lock it down with a saddle screw prevents that from happening and provides long-term durability to the receiver in the pintle and T&E [traverse and elevation] tripod-mounted configuration.” The continued evolution of the M250 is not new. Sig talked to TWZ at AUSA last year about changes, including to the bipod and top cover, that were already making their way into the design. The Army has yet to formally adopt the M250A1 configuration, and further changes could be made before service moves to officially acquire an improved version of the gun. “This is likely to be the accepted configuration. We anticipate that acceptance,” Sig’s St. John told us. “We just finalized the acceptance on the M8, and they’re moving into the acceptance of the [M]250s. We anticipate right now, with the feedback that we’re getting from the program office, that the majority, if not all, of these changes are likely to be accepted.” It’s important to reiterate that changes to the M7 rifle, and then the Army’s decision to transition fully to the further evolved M8 carbine, followed significant criticism of the core design of those guns and their ammunition, as well as the underlying doctrine. Sig has repeatedly pushed back on those critiques , and the Army continues to push ahead with the entire NGSW program. Despite the steadily shortening barrels on guns in the NGSW family, the Army’s position remains that the weapons chambered for the new 6.8x51mm round offer essential additional accuracy, range, and terminal effectiveness over existing 5.56x45mm types . The genesis of the NGSW program had been heavily informed by the war in Afghanistan, where there were regular reports of U.S. ground units being outranged by their opponents. Adversary body developments were also a factor. It is also important to point out that teething troubles are not at all uncommon in major weapon system programs, including when it comes to small arms. Sig has drawn attention to the less than positive reception that the AR-15/M16 family initially received in the mid-1960s, which led to a host of changes to that design. Rifles and carbines in that pattern are now in widespread service across the U.S. military and with dozens of armed forces and security services globally. Regardless, even with the Army still very early on in the process of fielding the entire NGSW family of guns, the M250 light machine gun’s design is now evolving significantly. Contact the author: joe@twz.com The post Sig Sauer’s M250 Machine Gun Gets Shorter And Lighter After Army Feedback appeared first on TWZ .

title: A judge blocks the government's tree-clearing spree at a municipal D.C. golf course
body:
The Trump administration abruptly cut down more than 400 trees at Washington, D.C.'s historic East Potomac Golf Links last weekend. A federal judge has ordered testimony from two high-level officials with the Interior Department; the judge plans to hold another hearing Oct. 19. Tyrone Turner/WAMU for NPR hide caption
A federal judge has temporarily barred the Trump administration from cutting down additional trees at a D.C. municipal golf course, the latest example of a court intervening in the government's efforts to reshape pieces of the nation's capital.
The long-simmering fight over East Potomac Golf Links — which President Trump wants to redevelop into a championship-level course — erupted over the weekend, after the administration cut down hundreds of trees with little notice.
U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes had ordered the administration in May to get court approval before cutting down more than 10 trees at the golf course. Officials notified the court just before 5 p.m. on Friday of their plan to remove "up to 529 trees" in phases starting on Saturday — and had razed at least 430 by the end of the day, prompting Reyes to call an emergency hearing on Monday.
"What has happened has cost the government all of its credibility with me in this case," Reyes said during the nearly four-hour hearing, held via videoconference.
Reyes ordered a short-term stop to the tree-clearings, which she extended on Tuesday through Oct. 26. She warned Monday that "if that order is violated by two seconds, there are going to be contempt proceedings."
Reyes also ordered top officials from the Department of Interior and the National Park Service to testify at a hearing next Monday, to shed more light on the government's motivations and the future of the historic course.
"The questions go to whether or not I've been lied to," Reyes said. "Whether I've been lied to in declarations about the plans, whether or not I've been lied to about the timing of things, and whether I've been lied to about what kind of notice the court was going to receive."
East Potomac has emerged as another flashpoint in Trump's unilateral quest to remake D.C ., and it's the subject of a lawsuit by critics who fear it could go the way of the now-lost White House East Wing unless a court intervenes. The D.C. Preservation League, along with two concerned residents, sued the government in February over what it calls an unlawful takeover.
"This is a tactic we're seen before from the Trump-Vance administration – act quickly to irrevocably alter a cherished national landmark, just to advance another one of President Trump's pet vanity projects," Skye Perryman, president and CEO of Democracy Forward — one of the firms involved in the lawsuit — said in a statement this weekend.
Perryman told NPR on Tuesday that the golf course is the latest in a pattern of the Trump administration "undermining the entire checks and balances process in this country, which includes undermining court proceedings."
Trump has long floated the idea of redeveloping East Potomac into a championship-caliber course and announced plans to do so earlier this year, though his target Sept. 1 start date has come and gone without a formal proposal.
The prospect — and the lack of clarity since — has raised alarm among locals concerned about losing access to the historically affordable course and to the surrounding recreational area, which is popular with cyclists, runners, fishers and picnickers.
"This is a broader story than just about golf, especially when there's been this little transparency, … to say, 'Here's what the future of this little man-made peninsula is actually going to look like,'" Alex Rosen, a D.C.-based consultant who started the nonprofit Save East Po, told NPR in July.
A National Park Service official said in a Friday court filing that plans for renovations "remain in the conceptual stage." And the Interior Department told NPR in a statement on Tuesday that it is "committed to continuing the relationships we have built with the local golf communities to ensure these courses are safe, beautiful, open, affordable, enjoyable, accessible, and world-class."
But critics are growing increasingly concerned about the process itself. They worry the Trump administration is using so-called routine maintenance as a pretext to begin redevelopment without the proper authorization.
"You can't continuously say, 'There's no plan' … while you're clearly taking steps to effect a plan," Rosen, who is not involved in the lawsuit, told NPR after watching the hearing. "It's just frankly lying."
At Monday's hearing, Reyes expressed regret that she hadn't issued a formal restraining order earlier, which she said was because "I have done everything humanly possible to give the government the benefit of the doubt in this case."
For example, after the administration quietly removed what it has since said were roughly 150 dying and invasive trees in late August, Reyes acknowledged that people were upset but declined to intervene: "I am not the Lorax ," she said at an early September hearing.
By Monday, that benefit of the doubt was gone. When a government lawyer said they had done their best to notify the court, Reyes offered a sharp rebuke.
"You did not do your best," she said, voice raised. "You did your absolute worst."
Perryman, of Democracy Forward, said, "What was really remarkable about the hearing yesterday is that the government did not appear to have a defense for its failure to notify the court."
In Friday's court filing, National Mall and Memorial Parks Superintendent Kevin Griess described the tree-clearing as part of an effort "to address deferred maintenance needs and implement treatment recommendations to restore the cultural landscape."
Griess specifically cited a 2019 National Park Service report about D.C. municipal golf courses, which says several waves of tree planting at East Potomac over the last century have obscured views and changed the feel of the course from its original 1920s "links-style" design.
Griess said in his filing that NPS was able to act on the report because it had received a temporary surge of "approximately 20 to 50 trained personnel capable of performing labor-intensive grounds maintenance activities." Under questioning in court, he confirmed that surge was connected to the administration's 250th anniversary events, including the IndyCar race on the National Mall in August.
But critics are skeptical, given the president's public statements. Alex Dickson, one of the plaintiffs, said in a statement that "the administration is using a preservation report as cover to begin tearing out the course it was written to save."
Griess said he had gotten the green light last week from Frank Lands, the park service's deputy director of operations. At the judge's request, Lands then joined the hearing from his car in a parking lot. He said he had gotten the directive from Greg Wischer, deputy chief of staff to Interior Secretary Doug Burgum.
Wischer was not reachable to join the hearing, despite Reyes' request that he do so. She has ordered Wischer and Jessica Bowron, the acting director of the National Park Service, to testify at another hearing next Monday.
The Interior Department didn't answer NPR's questions about the timeline and resources for the tree-clearing, but said in a statement that "President Donald J. Trump is fulfilling his commitment to make D.C. Safe and Beautiful as shown by the working fountains, clean parks and safe streets across the district for the first time in decades."
In granting the plaintiffs' request for an extended restraining order on Tuesday, Reyes wrote that they had "proven they will likely suffer irreparable harm absent injunctive relief." She also said the government must provide "three business days' written advance notice prior to making any irreparable modification" to the golf course.

title: Bitcoin Whale That Sat Through Every Crash Since 2020 Just Moved $377M
body:
A Bitcoin wallet that has held 4,581.94 BTC since March 2020 sent its entire balance to five new addresses on Oct. 12, moving about $377 million in a single transaction, according to blockchain data . The transfer confirmed in block 971,126 at about 18:37 UTC, with Bitcoin trading around $82,350.
Four of the receiving addresses got exactly 1,000 BTC each, and the fifth received 581.94 BTC. The transaction paid a fee of 732 satoshis, the hundred-millionth-of-a-bitcoin units known as sats, or about 60 cents. As of block 971,279 on Oct. 13, none of the five addresses has spent anything, and it is unclear who controls the wallet or where the coins are going.
The wallet received its coins on March 3, 2020, in a transaction that split a 5,081.95 BTC balance three ways, with 250 BTC going to each of two other addresses. At roughly $8,830 per Bitcoin, the 4,581.95 BTC that landed in the wallet was worth about $40.5 million. The value of the Bitcoin has nearly increased by 10X since then.
The wallet is an example of patience. The coins have sat through several market shocks since they arrived, starting with the COVID-19 crisis , which started shortly after the wallet got funded. During that time the stash went from about $40.5 million to about $17.6 million.
Tesla’s suspension of Bitcoin payments and China’s mining crackdown followed in May 2021, tanking the wallet from about $291 million at its April peak to $131 million by June. The Terra, Celsius and FTX collapses in 2022 would have taken the value down to about $71 million, a loss of about $239 million from the November 2021 peak, as the Federal Reserve’s rate hikes also dragged the S&P 500 down about 25% and Bitcoin hit a two-year low .
Trump’s tariff shock cut also crashed the markets . Bitcoin has since fallen 54% from a record $124,728 to $57,735 before recovering to its current price. The wallet’s value dropped from $571.5 million to about $265 million during that dip, but overall, hodling has resulted in almost 10X of net gains since day 1.
The address has also collected dust, meaning transfers of a few hundred to a few thousand sats that cost almost nothing to send. Blockchain data shows 22 such deposits between August 2020 and May 2026, ranging from 546 to 6,953 sats, or less than $6 each at current prices. Sixteen arrived in batch transactions that paid out to between 87 and 610 addresses at once.
One deposit matches the pattern of address poisoning, in which an attacker generates an address that copies the first and last characters of a real one, hoping someone later copies it from a transaction history by mistake. On Jan. 28, 2025, an address beginning 18VpNbPc and ending pQ9x sent the wallet 600 sats, and it shares the first three and last four characters with the whale’s address.
The look-alike was funded in a Nov. 12, 2024 transaction that paid out to 1,401 outputs at once, and it was emptied after sending that one payment. Every other sender used a bc1 address, which looks nothing like the wallet’s legacy 18 address.
Large holders of Bitcoin, known as whales, move their coins for different reasons, including privacy and safety. Analysts and traders fear that moves like that precede selling as holders feel tempted to realize significant gains.
That said, this is not the first time dormant wallets move their coins. Back in July 2025, an entity moved 80,000 BTC that had sat for 14 years, worth $8.6 billion, the biggest daily movement of coins aged 10 years or more. Ten days later a Satoshi-era wallet sent 40,009 BTC , about $4.7 billion, to Galaxy, which later said it had executed a sale worth roughly $9 billion for a Satoshi-era client.
As of Oct. 13, the original address holds 23,288 sats in leftover dust, about $19, while the five receiving addresses hold the full 4,581.94 BTC.

title: NPP rejects Emelia Agbenyo’s appointment as Deputy EC Chair, demands withdrawal
body: The opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP) has rejected the appointment of Emelia Afi Agbenyo as a Deputy Chairperson of the Electoral Commission (EC), calling on President John Mahama to withdraw the appointment over concerns about her previous political activities. In a statement issued by the National Communications Director, Miracles Aboagye, on Tuesday, October 13, the party questioned Ms Agbenyo’s ability to demonstrate political neutrality, citing her role as a governance sector spokesperson during the National Democratic Congress (NDC)’s preparation of its 2024 manifesto and her alleged participation in the party’s campaign activities. The NPP argued that her appointment to the leadership of the institution responsible for overseeing Ghana’s elections could undermine public confidence in the Electoral Commission, particularly ahead of the 2028 general elections. The party said Ms Agbenyo had appeared at NDC campaign rallies and worn party-branded T-shirts while advocating for the party, arguing that such activities raised concerns about the perception of impartiality expected of an electoral commissioner. The NPP also cited President Mahama’s criticism in March 2023 of appointments he described as involving political activists at the Electoral Commission. According to the party, the President had called for an amendment to Article 43(2) of the 1992 Constitution to require parliamentary approval for such appointments. It accused the President of acting contrary to the position he had previously expressed and said the issue required public scrutiny. “The consequences are serious,” the party said, warning that a loss of public confidence in the EC could lead to suspicion surrounding voter registration, boundary decisions and the declaration of election results. The NPP called on President Mahama to withdraw Ms Agbenyo’s appointment and urged the Council of State to explain the advice it gave on the nomination. It further appealed to the government to use the ongoing constitutional review process to reform the appointment of Electoral Commission members, in line with the proposal the President reportedly made in 2023. The party maintained that it would use lawful means to protect the integrity of Ghana’s electoral system and called on civil society organisations, religious bodies, the media and other citizens to support its demand. Read also: Mahama swears in Emelia Afi Agbenyo, Joseph Kwaku Asamoah as EC Deputy Commissioners Ms Agbenyo was sworn into office on October 12, 2026, alongside Dr Joseph Kwaku Asamoah, to fill vacancies created by the departure of former Deputy Chairpersons Dr Bossman Eric Asare and Samuel Tettey. President Mahama urged the two appointees to discharge their constitutional responsibilities independently and impartially, without favouring any political party or candidate.

title: Duane 'Keffe D' Davis sentenced to 40 years to life for Tupac Shakur's murder
body:
Davis, 63, is the only person ever charged with Shakur's murder.
Duane "Keffe D" Davis -- the only person ever charged with Tupac Shakur 's 1996 murder -- was sentenced to 40 years to life in prison on Tuesday in a Las Vegas court, following his conviction in August.
Members of the Shakur family gave emotional impact statements in court, articulating not only the generational loss the rap icon's death caused but their personal, human grief.
"I do believe that when you take a life like that, you deserve every minute, every minute of the maximum amount of punishment, time to sit down and contemplate what you've done to this world, not just to me," his sister, Sekyiwa Shakur, said.
Judge Carli Kierny, in sentencing Davis, said despite the decades that had elapsed since the killing, Davis would not just "walk away" from taking a man's life. "At this time, you are going to face justice for what you did," she said.
The sentence comes just over 30 years after the rapper's drive-by shooting near the Las Vegas Strip on Sept. 7, 1996. Shakur succumbed to his gunshot wounds six days after being gunned down.
In the ensuing years, Davis went on to tell a remarkably consistent account of what happened that night. In multiple police interviews, on the pages of his own self-published memoir, and in multiple on-camera interviews for the world to see, Davis allegedly confessed to what prosecutors would describe as his "shot caller" role in the infamous killing.
"I beat the streets, I beat the Feds, and I beat cancer," prosecutor Marc DiGiacomo quoted of Davis' own words to the jury in his closing argument. "Now, he's trying to beat 12 of you... Mr. Davis is attempting to escape responsibility for a crime everybody knows he committed, even him... End of the day, hold him accountable for the crime he committed."
Davis, now 63, has said he plans to appeal his conviction.
A onetime Los Angeles gang leader who later retired to the Vegas suburbs, Davis was arrested in September 2023 and charged with murder with the use of a deadly weapon with the intent to promote, further or assist a criminal gang, in connection with Shakur's murder. He has been in custody ever since. Once arrested, Davis pleaded not guilty and insisted on his innocence.
His lawyers argued he lied about his involvement in the murder and that there wasn't enough proof to put him in Vegas that night, much less in the white Cadillac from which the fatal .40 Glock shots were allegedly fired.
"The danger in this case has always been, just because we say something, is it true?" Davis' lawyer Michael Sanft said in his attempt to persuade the jury.
But in the years prior, Davis had plenty to say about his crucial role in the killing. He repeatedly admitted to his alleged role in Shakur's death, which he said was prompted by an escalating tit-for-tat of diss track and gangland retaliation that all came to a deadly head after the Tyson vs. Seldon boxing match the night of the shooting.
In continuing to tell his story and even profit from it, prosecutors said, Davis violated his own previous immunity agreement with a joint LA-task force. In fact, Vegas investigators credit Davis' many public statements for reinvigorating the case -- statements they worked to corroborate.
A jury of 12 Clark County citizens agreed -- that Davis' own words, bolstered by other evidence brought at trial, were to be believed. After less than three hours' deliberation in August, they unanimously found Davis guilty of first-degree murder with the use of a deadly weapon.
Prosecutors said that, though he did not pull the trigger, Davis orchestrated the rap icon's drive-by shooting that night.

title: Forex inflow rises 23% to $35 billion
body: By Elizabeth Adegbesan Nigeria’s net foreign exchange (forex) inflow grew by 23.2 percent year-on-year, YoY to $35.77 billion in the first half of 2026 (H1’26) from $29.77 in the corresponding period of 2025. Vanguard analysis of data from the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, Quarterly Statistical Bulletin and Data for the review period showed that aggregate forex inflow rose by 12.7 per cent to $63.82 billion in H1’26 from $56.62 billion in H1’25. However, forex outflow declined by 25.5 per cent to $19.98 billion from $26.85 billion recorded in H1’25. According to the report, forex inflow through the CBN fell slightly by 0.27 per cent to $18.28 billion from $18.33 billion in H1’25, while inflow through autonomous sources increased by 18.7 per cent to $45.5 billion in H1’26 from $38.3 billion in H1’25. But forex outflow through the bank dropped by 40.4 per cent to $12.2 billion from $20.47 billion in H1’25. However, outflow through autonomous sources increased by 21.8 per cent to $7.8 billion from $6.4 billion in H1’25. Consequently, autonomous sources recorded a net forex inflow of $37.7 billion in H1’26 compared with $31.89 billion in H1’25. The Bank on its part recorded a net forex inflow of $6.12 billion in H1’26, higher than the -$2.13 billion recorded in H1’25. The post Forex inflow rises 23% to $35 billion appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: US to have so many POWs in Iran in case of ground invasion
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 13 (MNA) – Brigadier General Mohammad Reza Naqdi, a senior adviser to the commander-in-chief of IRGC, said the United States would have so many troops captured if it launched a ground invasion of Iran, which would force it to surrender.
In comments published on Tuesday, Naqdi said that Iran’s armed forces have the capabilities needed to respond to threats and that their decisions and calculations should be trusted, as military operations and their timing are determined by strategic considerations and national interests.
Naqdi dismissed the prospect of a US ground invasion, saying that even in highly private American meetings, the subject might not have been discussed at all.
He said the United States talked about a ground invasion in its media messaging but had not even discussed it privately or whispered about it among themselves because, in his view, American officials understood the consequences.
Naqdi questioned why any rational decision-maker would contemplate a ground invasion of Iran after those experiences. “If they spent $3 trillion or $4 trillion there and their wars lasted 20 years, what would happen here, where the war would not even last 20 days?” he said.
He added that US forces would be captured in such large numbers that Washington would be forced to surrender and raise the flag of surrender.
Naqdi reiterated that he did not believe US officials had even held preliminary discussions about a ground invasion, arguing that they knew they could not carry it out.

title: OpenAI and Anthropic Tell British Lawmakers: Regulate Us
body:
The Business, Innovation, Science, and Trade Committee, comprising a cross-party panel of MPs, held an evidence session on Tuesday with appearances from four frontier AI firms, four former staff of the firms turned whistleblowers and senior British civil servants.
“The rules should be binding,” Anthropic’s head of Europe Liam Booth-Smith told the committee, when asked if the company’s view was that AI safety now needs a statutory framework. The company, he said, has “consistently believed that there should be binding rules on companies and that voluntary commitments are not enough.”
OpenAI vice president Tom Duff Gordon was more cautious but still supportive, backing a statutory framework and an international convention. Duff Gordon said “there should be some elements that should be mandatory,” starting with incident reporting. “We don’t think basing everything on voluntary commitments for frontier risk is a good long-term plan,” he said.
However, their rivals would not follow. Asked directly whether he supported a statutory framework, Google DeepMind’s Owen Larter said: “Focus on the standards is what we would be doing.” Meta’s Rob Sherman pointed to Britain’s existing regulators, telling MPs they were “not writing on a blank page.”
The hearing exposed an existing divide on the subject of regulation, putting the conflicting approaches of AI leaders on the British parliamentary record. Exposing this divide in a second jurisdiction was the point, according to select committee chair Liam Byrne. The committee set out “to light up the wide differences in opinions between some of the wealthiest firms on Earth,” he told WIRED after the hearing, and to show “that you couldn’t rely on voluntary self-regulation.”
While the four executives gave evidence to the committee on AI safety, only a few hundred meters away, Britain’s security service director issued a warning about the dangers of AI.
MI5 director Ken McCallum used his annual threat update to warn of bioweapon misuse as a significant threat from AI. “Not yet realized, but the misuse case to which I’d attach greatest weight, is AI’s potential to change the stakes on existing or even new bioweapons,” McCallum said.
Responding to this comment, Byrne told WIRED: “The fact that the head of MI5 is warning about incredibly dangerous capability uplifts for bioterrorists in one part of Whitehall, and then in another part of Whitehall the permanent secretary of the Cabinet Office is basically admitting that our regulatory regime for AI is voluntary, tells you everything you need to know.”
In the final part of the evidence session, civil servants conceded to the committee how little the current system compels. Britain’s AI Security Institute (AISI) tests frontier models before release, but only when companies choose to hand them over.
Henry de Zoete, director of AISI, acknowledged that the institute was entirely reliant on the cooperation of the companies and foreign governments in order to gain access. Cat Little, the top civil servant at the Cabinet Office, which houses AISI, was pressed on whether the whole regime was voluntary. “At the moment, yes, it is,” she said.
When asked what would happen if AISI judged a model to be too dangerous, but it was released by a company anyway, de Zoete acknowledged AISI had no ability to prevent them from doing so.
“What we’re not doing is kite marking,” de Zoete said, using the British term for a safety certification. “We’re not saying yes or no to any sort of model.” He added: “These companies are either American or Chinese who are building at the frontier … There’s only so much we, as the UK, can do in that kind of context.”
The frontier executives also made plain that British access runs through Washington. “We provide our models predeployment to CAISI,” OpenAI’s Duff Gordon said, referring to AISI’s US counterpart. “We will continue to provide our models pre-deployment to AISI in the UK … and as long as we’re able to do that under the US government, we will continue to do it.”
The tension of the existing arrangement was made clear to British officials by Anthropic’s Booth-Smith. “We unfortunately were not able to provide full unrestricted access to [Mythos 5.1] to UK AISI at that time ... That’s a question for the US government,” he said before adding that AISI now had access.
The session also heard from four former lab researchers, among them ex-OpenAI staffer Daniel Kokotajlo. “I don’t think the companies can be trusted to self-regulate,” he told MPs. Steven Adler, who left OpenAI in late 2024, said he was “not confident in the safety culture across the industry.” Geoffrey Irving said the labs believe they are locked in a race that governments will not interrupt and that they cannot leave. “Both of those are false,” he said. “They could just stop.”
Following the hearing Byrne told WIRED that his committee would now dedicate a lot of time examining the UK’s path forward as a middle power on AI. He wants ministers to use Britain’s coming G20 presidency, alongside South Korea, which follows it in the chair, to broker an international convention that does not depend on the current White House. “The G20 presidency will outlive the US presidency of Trump,” he said.
“The risks,” he added, “are multiplying faster than our safety regime can control.”

title: Tinubu asks Judiciary to block loopholes used to escape justice
body: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has asked the judiciary to overhaul the justice system to ensure that no well-connected individual manipulate technicalities to evade the full weight of the law. This is as he also insisted that corruption cannot be uprooted without independent, reform-minded judicial system. President Tinubu gave the charge on Tuesday in Abuja during the annual EFCC/NJI Capacity Building Workshop for Judges and Justices. Represented by Vice President Kashim Shettima, Tinubu urged the judiciary to interrogate existing statutory frameworks against the backdrop of emerging financial crimes. He called for the probe of prosecution strategies, “dismantle outdated precedents, and seal procedural gaps that politically exposed persons and organised crime actors exploit to delay or frustrate trial”. The President warned that while financial and economic crimes pose an existential threat to Nigeria, corruption has no respect for status and spares no arm of government. According to him, framing the anti-corruption campaign as purely an executive agenda is a fundamental error because compromised public services equally affect the executive, legislature, judiciary, and ordinary citizens. Noting that corruption is a battle for the nation’s collective survival, President Tinubu said, “We must no longer permit legal pyrotechnics and procedural pedantry to shelter criminality. The Bench is not merely a mechanical arbiter of rules, but an active guardian of moral order and social equity. “Law is, by design, an instrument of social engineering; it must invariably prioritise the public good over narrow, selfish interests shielded by technical manoeuvres. Our courts must embody the spirit, and not just the arid letter, of the law.” The President maintained that there will be no meaningful progress in uprooting graft “without an independent, progressive, and reform-minded Bench,” even as he commended the EFCC for convening the 8th edition of the Judges and Justices Workshop. He said the workshop with the theme, “Investigation and Prosecution of Economic and Financial Crimes in a Digital Age,” was timely and necessary in “fostering the institutional cohesion required to confront corruption’s ever-changing architecture in Nigeria. Speaking earlier, the Chief Justice of Nigeria, Hon. Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, said the event reflects the commitment of the NJI and EFCC to sustain efforts aimed at addressing challenges confronting stakeholders in Nigeria’s justice system. She said the trend in technology has impacted how digital evidence is obtained and recorded, noting that the effective administration of criminal justice in the digital era require firm and disciplined case management which, according to her, capacity building programmes such as the EFCC and NJI collaboration, aims to strengthen. The CJN noted that sustained judicial education and capacity development in the justice sector was yielding positive results with the improved conduct of judicial officers especially judges in case management and the dispensation of justice in recent years.

title: Show HN: Faster, Cheaper Databricks Spark with Real-Time ML Config Management
body:
Most Spark jobs run on wrong-sized machines with incorrect configs, leading to slow jobs, wasted spend, or both. We've found that we can get better performance at a lower price by continuously monitoring each job's performance and changing each job's instance type and worker count in real time.
Under the hood, this is a search problem: we're trying to find the lowest-cost configuration that meets your SLA. More generally, we map out the Pareto frontier of runtime vs. cost across compute configurations, and then move your job to it - the vast majority of jobs are not on the frontier today.
Testing every config would be slow and expensive; we use ML, alongside a small number of real samples, to understand the shape of your workload and winnow down the options.
We've found three consistent patterns for why job configurations are wrong:
The settings that control this, instance type and worker count, are usually chosen when somebody creates the job. They're rarely updated afterwards unless something OOMs or goes over SLA - and then jobs are usually upsized coarsely.
Our system reads each job’s CPU, memory, and I/O-wait traces from Databricks system tables. We use those usage patterns to estimate cost and runtime for candidate configurations, then choose the one that matches your SLA with built-in headroom. We then monitor jobs on an ongoing basis, handling retries and changing sizes as your jobs grow or shrink.
Users are seeing job costs go down from 35% to 85% . We're optimizing for cost, not runtime, but we've seen runtime drop by up to 60% as a side effect of moving jobs to machines that match their resource constraints.

title: EOCO grants Suame MP John Darko enquiry bail in GH¢27m SIC investigation
body: The Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO) has granted Suame Member of Parliament John Darko enquiry bail after he reported to investigators to assist with an ongoing investigation into an alleged criminal conspiracy involving SIC Savings and Loans Company Limited. In a news release dated October 13, 2026, EOCO said Mr Darko honoured its invitation and reported to the Office at exactly 12 noon to provide information relevant to the investigation. The EOCO statement comes days after John Darko disclosed on Saturday, October 3, 2026, that he had been told he was also involved in the investigation into Manhyia South MP Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah, saying he would cooperate if invited. “I have been told that I’m also involved. I don’t know. And so I will wait until I get an invitation from them. Then I can go and tell whatever I know,” he said. READ ALSO: ‘I’ve been told I’m also involved’ – John Darko says he’ll cooperate with EOCO if invited over Baffour Awuah case Darko, who is also Legal Counsel to the Minority Caucus, had previously condemned EOCO’s attempt to arrest Baffour Awuah at the Accra High Court on September 23, 2026, describing the incident as unacceptable and warning that no state institution should operate above the Constitution. The investigation concerns alleged unauthorised financial transactions at SIC Life Savings and Loans Company Limited. Baffour Awuah, who is the Senior Partner of Sarkodie Baffour Awuah & Partners, was engaged by SIC Life in May 2020 to recover a debt from Equity Savings and Loans Limited. In July 2024, SIC Life, Equity, and Eco Swiss Investment Limited executed Terms of Settlement under which SIC Life agreed to accept GH¢5,000,000.00 in full and final settlement of a revised judgment debt of GH¢14,850,776.14. The State alleges the MP was instrumental in arranging the transaction and later transferred GH¢1,000,000.00 to the then Managing Director of SIC Life. Baffour Awuah has been charged with conspiracy to commit a crime (intentional dissipation of public funds), intentionally causing financial loss to a public body, and money laundering. He is expected to be arraigned before the High Court’s Specialised Jurisdiction Division. The Office described the MP as cooperative throughout the process. “The Honourable Member was respectful, cooperative and fully responsive throughout the investigative process,” EOCO said. It added that the decision to grant him enquiry bail was based on the circumstances of the case, the applicable law and his level of cooperation with investigators. EOCO said the investigation concerns an alleged criminal conspiracy that has resulted in a revised estimated financial loss of approximately GH¢27 million to SIC Savings and Loans Company Limited. The Office did not provide further details about the specific allegations against Mr Darko in the release. EOCO stressed that investigations were ongoing and that no conclusion had been reached regarding the culpability of any person connected to the matter. The grant of enquiry bail does not, in itself, establish wrongdoing by the MP. EOCO also disclosed that the former Managing Director of SIC Life Savings and Loans, Amma Frimpomaa Dwumah, has honoured its invitation and is cooperating with investigators. EOCO said investigations remain active and no conclusion has been reached regarding the culpability of any person connected to the matter. Further updates are expected as the investigation progresses.

title: Pension: Why we ‘re targeting informal sector- Pencom D-G
body: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The National Pension Commission is targeting Nigeria’s informal sector to secure the participation of the nation’s largest group of workers in the Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS). The Director-General of Pencom, Ms. Omolola Oloworaran, who spoke at the 2026 National Pension Commission Media Conference in Abuja, yesterday, said that with the informal sector accounting for about 92 percent of the nation’s workforce, it must be included in the pension reform for it to be considered successful. She spoke on the theme, “From Reform To Reality, Renewed Hope, Pension Security for Nigerians”. The D-G said that her team was giving the Personal Pension Plan for the informal sector a very strong push to enable them benefit from the various programmes targeting pensioners in the country. According to her, PenCom has engaged accredited pension agents targeting workers in the informal sector and that the commission was in the process on accrediting more agents for the same purpose. She said that the agents were taking the Personal Pension Plan to markets, motor parks, farms and workshops to enroll traders, artisans, farmers and transport workers. Tinubu most Pro-Pensioners President Ms. Oloworaran said President Bola Tinubu was laying the foundation for a sustainable social security in the country through enhanced welfare for retirees with increased pensions and the free health to be launched at the end of this month. The Pencom boss described President Tinubu as, “the most pro-retiree president, going by the achievements recorded so far in the pension industry. “From the very beginning of pensions in the country to all the reforms that have happened, he is the most pro-worker, most pro-retiree President we have seen in the history of Nigeria,” she said. Ms. Oloworaran said that the administration had settled N758 billion inherited pension obligations (with nearly one million pensioners benefiting from the payment), introduced new benefits, accelerated payment of retirement benefits and improved pension security for workers and retirees. She said that for the first time in 21 years, pensions of 2,116 retirees of the defunct Nigerian Social Insurance Trust Fund (NSITF) were reviewed, citing an example of a particular pensioner on N18, 000 monthly, now receiving N206,000. “Twenty-one years of waiting was answered in a single decision,” she said. According to her, retirement benefits that previously took up to 21 months to approve are now approved within 48 hours for federal government workers. The D-G said that two additional initiatives would be unveiled during the National Pension Week scheduled for October 26 to October 30. She said that one of them was “PenCare,” a retiree healthcare programme that would provide eligible low-income retirees with essential healthcare at no cost during its pilot phase. The pilot stage would cover 30,000 retirees. The post Pension: Why we ‘re targeting informal sector- Pencom D-G appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Explosions heard near Aramco’s headquarters in Saudi’s Dhahran — agency
body:
DOHA, October 13. /TASS/. The sounds of explosions were heard in the vicinity of Saudi Aramco’s headquarters in the city of Dhahran in the east of the country, Reuters reported, citing sources.
Shortly after that, the Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted an aerial target over the city. "A ballistic missile launched by Houthi terrorist units toward the city of Dhahran has been intercepted and destroyed," the coalition’s spokesman Turki al-Maliki wrote on X.
According to the spokesman, fragments of the missile fell on a residential area.

title: Zelensky on U.S. talks: Ukraine is ready to meet in coming days
body:
A proposal to that effect has already been conveyed to U.S. President Donald Trump’s envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky made this statement in an evening video address , according to Ukrinform.
“Our teams are in communication. Ukraine is ready for meetings; Ukraine has supported the U.S. president on the issue of an energy ceasefire. It is necessary for Russia to be part of this agreement as well. Our team has sent the U.S. side relevant proposals regarding our possible upcoming meetings and discussions. We are ready to meet in the coming days, and I have conveyed this proposal through my team to Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner,” Zelensky emphasized.
The head of state noted that the Ukrainian side always takes a constructive approach and that Ukraine’s positions are always absolutely clear and aimed at defending the independence of the Ukrainian people.
Separately, he reported that Tuesday involved a great deal of work regarding Kyiv—specifically, the situation in the capital concerning preparations for winter and the protection of critical infrastructure.
“Every Kyiv resident can see that the city is truly unprepared. Now, already in October, the situation is, unfortunately, worse than it was during previous winters of this war. When isolated ‘Shahed’ strikes cut off electricity and water,” the President noted.
The Head of the Ukrainian State reported that, unfortunately, there are many other issues as well.
“As for shelters, preparing schools, building protective structures… The operation of public transportation, preparing buildings in Kyiv for winter… Kyiv is lagging behind our other regions in implementing resilience plans. We need solutions; we need to speed things up,” Zelensky said.
He reported that he discussed this on Tuesday with representatives of communities that have done more, and clarified that some of them have achieved significantly more under conditions that are far more challenging.
“I met here with Kharkiv Mayor Ihor Terekhov. And I also spoke with Ivan Fedorov, who has done a great deal for Zaporizhzhia over the years of the war. And today I spoke with Vasyl Malyuk about security challenges. I also spoke with representatives of the business community who are achieving results—with Maksym Yefimov and Kostiantyn Yefimenko,” the President emphasized.
He expressed his gratitude to everyone for their proposals and willingness to cooperate, noting that “there will be more important meetings.”
As reported by Ukrinform, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Ukraine is ready to negotiate but will not agree to talks without equality and fairness.

title: Massive Ancient Monument Discovered Opposite Greek-Style Temple in Pakistan
body: Archaeologists investigating the ancient city of Taxila in Pakistan have begun uncovering a monumental structure measuring nearly 100 metres long and more than 50 metres wide, offering new opportunities to explore the region’s complex cultural history, including its connections with the Greek world. Known as Jandial D, the structure stands outside the fortified ancient city of Sirkap, directly opposite the famous Jandial Temple, which features distinctive Ionic columns associated with ancient Greek architecture. The discovery is particularly significant because Taxila was an important centre of cultural exchange where Greek, Persian, Central Asian and South Asian traditions interacted over centuries. However, archaeologists have not established a direct Greek connection to the newly excavated monument. Although British archaeologist Alexander Cunningham recorded the site in 1864, the structure had never been systematically investigated. Excavations led by the Italian Archaeological Mission of Ca’ Foscari University of Venice began in August 2026. According to the university’s announcement on October 13, researchers have uncovered substantial walls surviving at least one metre above the ground. The monument’s enormous dimensions suggest that it may have served a public or religious function, but its precise purpose, date and cultural associations remain unknown. A Monument Overlooked for More Than 160 Years Jandial D occupies a strategic position outside Sirkap’s defensive walls, along a route that once connected the city’s northern gate with Gandhara. The surrounding region became a meeting point for different peoples, political powers and religious traditions. Its history includes periods of Achaemenid Persian influence, the campaigns of Alexander the Great and the establishment of Indo-Greek kingdoms in parts of the region. These historical connections provide important context for understanding Taxila’s diverse architectural and cultural heritage. They do not, however, establish who built or used Jandial D. Luca Maria Olivieri, professor of Central Asian and Indian archaeology at Ca’ Foscari University and director of the Italian Archaeological Mission, has highlighted the importance of the monument’s scale and location. Further excavations will be needed to establish its chronology, architectural development and relationship with the ancient city and neighbouring structures. The Greek-Style Temple Opposite the Discovery The Jandial Temple is one of Taxila’s most distinctive ancient buildings. Its Ionic columns and architectural layout resemble features of Greek temples, making it an important example of Greek architectural influence in South Asia. The temple’s plan includes an entrance porch, an inner sanctuary and a rear chamber. These architectural features have attracted scholarly attention because of their similarities to traditions associated with the Greek world. Such similarities must be interpreted within Taxila’s broader multicultural history. Greek architectural forms could be adopted, adapted or incorporated into local building traditions without necessarily indicating that a structure was built by Greek settlers or used exclusively for Greek religious practices. The relationship between the temple and the newly excavated Jandial D monument remains unresolved. Their proximity makes the area particularly interesting for archaeological research, but there is currently no confirmed evidence that the two structures were built at the same time or served related purposes. Taxila: A Meeting Point of Ancient Civilisations Taxila developed through successive periods of cultural and political change. Persian, Greek, Central Asian and South Asian influences contributed to its urban development, religious life and architectural traditions. The fortified city of Sirkap, established around the second century BC, is known for its planned streets and buildings reflecting a variety of architectural styles. The wider archaeological landscape also contains Buddhist monasteries and stupas that demonstrate Gandhara’s importance as a centre of Buddhist learning and artistic production. Taxila’s historical significance is therefore not limited to Greek influence. Its importance lies in the interaction of multiple traditions across different periods. UNESCO inscribed Taxila on the World Heritage List in 1980, recognising the site’s exceptional archaeological record and its evidence of successive stages of urban development in the Indian subcontinent. Further Excavations May Answer Key Questions The investigation at Jandial D forms part of Khyber PATH, an archaeological research and heritage conservation initiative covering eight sites between Taxila and the Swat Valley. The project brings together Ca’ Foscari University and archaeological authorities in Pakistan’s Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, with funding from the Italian Agency for Development Cooperation and support from ISCOS. Other sites under investigation include Barikot, the ancient settlement of Bazira in the Swat Valley, and Sirsukh, another fortified city in the Taxila region. Researchers are also examining the remains of Kacha-Kot, an ancient rammed-earth fortification associated with Sirkap. The newly investigated monument highlights how much remains to be understood about the areas beyond Taxila’s best-known ancient structures. For now, the strongest connection to the Greek world is the Greek-style architecture of the nearby Jandial Temple and the wider historical context of cultural exchange in the region. Whether Jandial D shared that architectural tradition, served a related function or belonged to an entirely different phase of the settlement remains a question for future excavation. The post Massive Ancient Monument Discovered Opposite Greek-Style Temple in Pakistan appeared first on Greek City Times .
