title: Dangote Petroleum Refinery logs $4.7 billion profit in nine months on higher refining throughput
body:
Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals reported $4.7 billion in net profit for the first nine months of 2026, in contrast to a net loss of $117.2 million in the same period of last year, according to its latest unaudited results released on Tuesday.
The corporation attributed the earnings turnaround and improved key performance metrics to higher refining throughput, improved operational reliability, and stronger refining margins.
The refinery, which is currently undertaking a $1.6 billion initial public offering (IPO) to help double current capacity from 700,000 barrels per day to 1.4 million by 2030, recorded a 144 per cent leap in revenue to $22.5 billion during the period.
Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) – a performance indicator that measures the core profit of a business – accelerated ninefold to $5.5 billion. At the same time, the company said EBITDA margin climbed to 24.6 per cent from 6.8 per cent.
Dangote Petroleum Refinery spotlighted the three months to September as the standout quarter as it posted $2.9 billion, representing 61.3 per cent of its entire post-tax profit for the review period, in the quarter, which also delivered $8.6 billion in revenue, equivalent to 38.2 per cent of the turnover of the nine months.
“Our third-quarter performance demonstrates the successful transition from commissioning and ramp-up activities to sustainable commercial operations,” said CEO David Bird.
“With our expansion programme already underway, we remain focused on increasing refining capacity and broadening our product portfolio. We will continue to strengthen our distribution network across Africa and support energy security across the continent, while creating long-term value for stakeholders,” he added.
The strong result also helped the company move from a net debt position of $1.7 billion in September 2025 to net cash of $650.8 million, strengthening its balance sheet.
On Monday, the refinery announced it will extend its ongoing operations, originally planned to close on 13 October, by two weeks to 27 October.
The shares are scheduled for listing on the Nigerian Exchange next month.
The company has benefited greatly from the sweeping fuel shortages the US war against Iran has caused worldwide, notably from increased jet fuel supply to Europe.

title: In blow to Netanyahu, Trump again stops short of endorsing candidate in Israeli election
body: US President Donald Trump on Tuesday left open the possibility of endorsing a candidate in Israel's upcoming elections, but stopped short of committing to support anyone, including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.Speaking to reporters on the White House lawn shortly before boarding Marine One for Joint Base Andrews, where he was scheduled to depart for Alaska, Trump was asked whether he intended to endorse a candidate in the Israeli election."We haven't even thought about it," the president initially replied.When a reporter pointed out that he had endorsed political candidates in the past, Trump appeared to leave the door open. "Well, we may be. I may be doing something," he said, before repeating: "I may be. I may be doing something."The exchange came exactly two weeks before Israel's October 27 election, amid Trump's close political and personal relationship with Netanyahu. Trump did not mention Netanyahu by name in his response, nor did he identify any other Israeli political figure he might consider supporting.His remarks nevertheless left open the question of whether he intends to play a role in the final stages of Israel's election campaign, at a time when an endorsement from the American president could carry significant political weight.Trump confirms US continuing to share intelligence with UkraineOn the Russia-Ukraine war, Trump offered an important clarification after newly appointed White House press secretary Katie Zacharia was unable to answer a question earlier Tuesday about whether Washington had stopped sharing intelligence with Kyiv.Asked directly whether the United States had suspended intelligence sharing, Trump responded unequivocally. "No, we haven't. We help them, but we're really helping them get to a final answer. We want the war ended, Peter."He went on to confirm that American assistance, including intelligence cooperation, was continuing as Washington worked with both sides to negotiate an end to the conflict."We want the war to end, so we're working with them and with Russia on getting the war to end," he said.Asked why he believed Russian President Vladimir Putin was interested in ending the war, Trump pointed to his experience in negotiations. "That's what I've done my whole life: is deals," the president said."I think they both want it to end," he continued, referring to Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. "You know, honestly, they both wanted to end, and they don't know how to get to that point."Trump added: "They don't know how to get there. We're going to get them there."The president also faced questions about Russian attacks and alleged violations of a ceasefire.He responded by pointing to Ukrainian strikes on Russian targets, saying, "Ukraine hit many sites the day before."They're hitting each other. But it'll all come to an end," he added.Trump defends controversial Russian diesel dealTrump also defended his administration's controversial decision to facilitate additional Russian diesel supplies to international markets, despite concerns that the resulting revenues could help Moscow finance its war against Ukraine.Asked whether anyone had assured him that Russia would not use proceeds from the arrangement to purchase weapons, Trump replied: "Nobody told me anything."He insisted that the decision was intended to address global energy shortages rather than provide a direct benefit to the United States."That's a diesel deal, not for us. That's being released into the world. That's not being released to us," he said."That's a diesel deal that's going to be released into the world for the world market because the world market suffered with high prices, and when you knock out diesel refineries, that's not a great thing."Later in the exchange, Trump returned to the subject."It's a deal for the world. It's not a deal for us. It's a way of getting a lot of oil out to the world," he argued.He maintained that the arrangement had contributed to lower energy prices, while rejecting suggestions that it was primarily a bilateral commercial agreement benefiting Washington.Trump on Guilfoyle's removal: 'I didn't speak to her, but she will not be there'Trump also commented publicly on his administration's decision to seek the resignation of Kimberly Guilfoyle, the US ambassador to Greece, shortly after Zacharia confirmed the move during her first White House press briefing.Asked about Guilfoyle, who was previously engaged to his eldest son, Donald Trump Jr., the president sought to distance her from his family."No, she wasn't a member of my family. She, I guess, dated my son a long time ago," Trump said.Although he acknowledged that Guilfoyle had performed well in her diplomatic role, he expressed dissatisfaction with recent reports about her conduct."She was doing a good job, but we didn't like what we were reading," Trump said.Asked whether he had personally spoken to Guilfoyle about her departure, he replied: "I didn't speak to her. No, but she will not be there. I didn't like what I read."The comments followed a series of reports alleging misconduct involving Guilfoyle's dealings with donors and business figures.Guilfoyle's attorneys have denied the allegations against her. The outgoing ambassador has also rejected the claims and said she intends to defend her reputation.Earlier Tuesday, Zacharia announced during her debut briefing that the administration had formally requested Guilfoyle's resignation."We have asked Ambassador Guilfoyle to resign," Zacharia said. "She has been a wonderful asset to the team, and we wish her well."Trump also offered a favorable assessment of his new press secretary's first appearance, describing her performance as "very good."Trump heads to Alaska as midterm campaign intensifiesThe remarks came as Trump continued an intensive campaign tour ahead of the November midterm elections, during which Republicans are seeking to retain control of Congress.Asked whether it would be more difficult for his party to hold the House or the Senate, Trump suggested the challenges were comparable."I would say equal," he replied.He argued that the party of a sitting president traditionally faces a significant disadvantage in midterm elections, regardless of the administration's record.Nevertheless, Trump maintained that his campaign appearances were generating increased enthusiasm for Republican candidates."The level of enthusiasm for the Republican Party is way up, not just where I'm doing them," he said.The president said he was traveling to Alaska to campaign for Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan, part of a packed schedule of rallies in several states."I'm right now going to Alaska to try and help Dan Sullivan, that's a long way away, and I would only do it if I thought he was good, and he's very good," Trump told reporters.He added that he was holding, on average, one rally every day. "You think that's easy? It's not," Trump said before departing for his next campaign stop.

title: NCC Unveils *315# Device Checker In Move Against Fake Phones
body: The Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) has introduced a Device Checker service that allows consumers to verify communications devices by dialling *315#, as part of efforts to curb counterfeit and non-compliant phones on Nigerian mobile networks. The Commission said the initiative formed part of an enhanced Type Approval Compliance framework that took effect on October 7, 2026, aimed at protecting consumers, safeguarding telecommunications networks and ensuring that devices sold and used in Nigeria meet the required technical standards. Speaking at a news conference on the Commission’s Technical Standards and Network Integrity initiatives in Abuja on Tuesday, the Director of Technical Standards and Network Integrity, Edoyemi Ogoh, said the framework would strengthen monitoring and enforcement of existing regulatory requirements. “Type Approval is not merely a regulatory requirement. It is a vital mechanism for protecting consumers, safeguarding network performance and preserving confidence in Nigeria’s digital economy,” he said. Ogoh explained that the Commission had consulted original equipment manufacturers, importers, dealers, telecommunications service providers, government agencies and industry associations following the issuance of the Type Approval Business Rules in August 2024. He added that the NCC had worked with the Nigeria Customs Service and other stakeholders to verify devices already in stock and ensure that newly imported equipment underwent the required checks. The Commission said consumers could verify a device by dialling *315# and following the prompts or visiting its official portal at www.ncc.gov.ng/devicechecker. Those checking a device other than the one they are currently using may need its 15-digit International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI) number, which can be obtained by dialling *#06#. The NCC advised Nigerians to verify devices before making payment, particularly when purchasing second-hand phones. However, it clarified that consumers buying devices from Nigerian sellers were not required to obtain Type Approval themselves, as compliance responsibilities rest primarily with manufacturers, importers, suppliers and businesses placing devices on the market. According to the Commission, devices already connected to Nigerian mobile networks before the framework took effect were automatically verified and generally require no action from their users. The framework covers smartphones, feature phones, cellular tablets, eligible Internet of Things devices, SIM-enabled point-of-sale terminals, cellular laptops and other equipment designed to connect to Nigerian mobile networks. The NCC said devices found to be non-compliant with applicable requirements could be denied access to Nigerian mobile networks. It explained that counterfeit phones imitate genuine products without the original manufacturers’ authorisation, while cloned devices use IMEI numbers assigned to other legitimate devices. However, the Commission cautioned that an unsuccessful verification result did not automatically mean a device was counterfeit, advising consumers to seek clarification from sellers and resolve outstanding verification issues before completing purchases. Addressing privacy concerns, Ogoh said the system was designed for device identification and regulatory verification, not surveillance. He explained that although the framework uses device identification information, including IMEI numbers, it does not give the Commission access to users’ calls, messages, photographs, contacts, financial information or other personal files. The NCC also said the Device Checker does not track users’ physical locations or movements. Earlier, the Director of Public Affairs at the Commission, Nneka Okoha, urged media organisations to intensify public awareness of the service and other regulatory initiatives. Okoha said effective communication was essential to ensuring that regulatory policies achieved their intended objectives, particularly among consumers at the grassroots. She urged journalists to provide accurate and balanced information to help Nigerians understand the Device Checker, its benefits and their responsibilities when purchasing communications equipment. The Commission also warned consumers against fraudsters seeking to exploit the verification process, urging them to use only the official *315# channel and NCC website and never disclose one-time verification codes to sellers, callers or other individuals. It clarified that international roaming with foreign SIM cards would not be affected by the framework. Visitors intending to use a Nigerian SIM card in a device that had never previously connected to a Nigerian network may use it for up to 30 cumulative days within a one-year period without verification, according to the NCC’s guidance. The Commission said the framework was backed by the Nigerian Communications Act 2003, particularly Section 132(2), the Nigerian Communications (Type Approval) Regulations 2024 and the Type Approval Business Rules 2024. Ogoh stressed that the NCC was strengthening enforcement of an existing requirement rather than introducing a new regulatory obligation. The Commission urged manufacturers, importers, dealers, service providers, consumer groups and media organisations to support public sensitisation and compliance. It advised consumers experiencing verification difficulties or network restrictions to contact their service providers or seek assistance through its official support channels, including its toll-free number, 315. The NCC reaffirmed its commitment to consumer protection, stronger technical standards and a safer, more reliable telecommunications environment in support of Nigeria’s digital economy. The post NCC Unveils *315# Device Checker In Move Against Fake Phones appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Gov. Buni Approves Purchase of Dangote Refinery Shares for 43,928 Yobe Women
body: Governor Mai Mala Buni of Yobe State has approved ₦230.62 million for procurement of shares for 43,928 vulnerable women across the 17 Local Government Areas of the State. According to Mamman Mohammed, Director-General Press and Media Affairs to the Governor, the development followed high-level engagements initiated by the state government, represented by the Secretary to the State Government, Dr. Mohammed Goje, exploring opportunities for private-sector partnerships to support vulnerable women and conflict-affected households in Yobe State, at the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York, United States of America. Dr. Goje on behalf of the state government, had at the UNGA discussions solicited for partnership with the Aliko Dangote Foundation to provide 43,928 vulnerable women across the 17 Local Government Areas of Yobe State with an opportunity to become shareholders in Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals. The initiative centered on a shift in women’s economic empowerment to move beyond conventional financial assistance to financial inclusion, investment participation and long-term asset ownership. Under the arrangement, Yobe State government would sponsor the subscription of 10 shares for each of the 43,928 eligible women totaling ₦230.62 million, while the Aliko Dangote Foundation would provide an equivalent matching grant to translate in an investment opportunity valued at approximately ₦461.24 million, subject to the applicable IPO conditions and successful allotment. Each of the 43,928 participating women would have 20 shares in her own name, with the shares credited to her individual Central Securities Clearing System account, promoting personal asset ownership and financial independence. The initiative prioritises women from internally displaced households, widows with multiple dependents, women with disabilities, and those living in extreme poverty. The development further highlights the growing importance of strategic international engagement in attracting practical investment opportunities to Yobe State. “What began as a high-level conversation during UNGA 2026 has progressed into a formal partnership proposal with the potential to directly benefit tens of thousands of women across the State. “The initiative is also consistent with Governor Buni’s broader development agenda of promoting inclusive growth, supporting vulnerable households, strengthening economic resilience and creating opportunities for communities recovering from the effects of insurgency. “Beyond its financial value, this initiative reflects a significant policy direction: empowering vulnerable women not merely as recipients of assistance, but as potential owners of productive financial assets,” Goje said.

title: NPP cannot question EC appointment after appointing own people to Commission – Kwakye Ofosu
body: Minister of State in charge of Government Communications, Felix Kwakye Ofosu, has defended the appointment of Emelia Affi Agbenyo to the Electoral Commission (EC), accusing the New Patriotic Party (NPP) of double standards in its criticism of the decision. The NPP has raised concerns about the appointment, arguing that Ms Agbenyo’s previous association with the National Democratic Congress (NDC), including her role as a spokesperson on the party’s manifesto committee, could raise questions about her impartiality as the Deputy Chairperson of the commission. But speaking on Joy FM’s Top Story on Tuesday, October 13, Mr Kwakye Ofosu argued that the NPP was not in a position to question the appointment, given what he described as the party’s own record of appointing people with known political affiliations to the Commission. “At the last count, there were at least four known NPP deputies on the Electoral Commission,” he said. He cited the EC’s chairperson and other officials, including the recently resigned Deputy Chairperson, Dr Bossman Asare, and Dr Appiahene, whom he described as having publicly acknowledged their NPP affiliations. He also mentioned Madam Salima Tijani, whom he identified as another person associated with the NPP who had been appointed to the Commission. “How can a party that made these appointments to the Electoral Commission turn around and purport to be upset or angry over the appointment of an individual?” he asked. Mr Kwakye Ofosu acknowledged that Ms Agbenyo had worked with the NDC in the past but said he believed she had the qualities needed to perform her new role professionally. “It is true that Affi Agbenyo has worked in some capacities for the NDC, but I know her as a person, that she has the right temperament. She has the academic and professional standing. She has the presence of mind to operate professionally in the role that has been assigned to her,” he said. He conceded that some people might have concerns about whether her political association could affect perceptions of fairness and balance at the Commission. However, he maintained that the NPP’s own appointments to the EC weakened its criticism of the government’s decision.

title: Tribal clashes contained after six killed in South Darfur
body: Authorities in Sudan’s South Darfur State said they had contained tribal clashes that killed six people and wounded others following a dispute over a motorcycle between two clans of the Beni Halba tribe. The clashes occurred over the weekend in the Gunu area of Ed al-Fursan Locality. The dispute escalated into an armed confrontation, leaving six people dead and others injured on both sides. Salah al-Moj, head of the civil administration in South Darfur State, told Radio Tamazuj on Tuesday that the state security committee had travelled to Ed al-Fursan to assess the incident and its security implications. “The state security committee visited Ed al-Fursan following the incidents and met with the relevant people and bodies to discuss measures to resolve the issue,” he said. He said the committee also met with the locality’s security committee to establish how the violence unfolded and review measures to address the crisis. Al-Moj said the committee had reviewed security arrangements and efforts to resolve the dispute through customary tribal mechanisms, including the payment of blood compensation to the families of those killed. The committee also directed the rival groups to disperse their armed gatherings and ordered an increased deployment of regular security forces to restore state authority in the locality, he said. South Darfur police director Lieutenant Colonel Khalid Mohamed Nur said the situation had been brought under control. He said police had responded to residents’ demands for additional personnel and equipment, including vehicles, weapons and uniforms. “We send our sincere condolences to the families of those killed in the tribal conflict, and we would like to tell the public that the situation has been contained,” Nur said. He acknowledged that police in the area face challenges and lack some equipment and transport, adding that plans are under way to provide vehicles, weapons, uniforms and other necessities to strengthen their ability to maintain security. “We urge the people of Ed al-Fursan to ensure that such incidents do not occur again, and we thank the community leaders for their wisdom and patience,” he said. South Darfur is among the states controlled by the Sudan Foundation Alliance (Tasis), a parallel administration aligned with the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), which has been fighting Sudan’s army since April 2023. Tasis announced the formation of a parallel administration in areas under its control in July 2025. RSF commander Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, widely known as Hemedti, heads its presidential council, while civilian politician Mohamed Hassan al-Taishi serves as prime minister. title: 2027: Olawepo-Hashim slams opposition figures in APC campaign council as ‘indiscipline, rascality’
body: The presidential candidate of the Accord Party, Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim, has described the inclusion of opposition figures in the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign council as “indiscipline and rascality”. Olawepo-Hashim made the remarks on Tuesday during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today , where he reacted to the inclusion of opposition figures like Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke and Anambra State Governor Charles Soludo in the APC campaign council ahead of the 2027 general elections. Asked whether the move reflected political maturity or political survival, the Accord Party candidate dismissed both interpretations, describing it instead as a lack of discipline. “No, this is simply indiscipline and rascality,” he said. Olawepo-Hashim also argued that Adeleke’s participation in the APC campaign council would not automatically translate into support for President Bola Tinubu among voters in Osun State. He said the governor’s electoral victory did not give him the power to determine how the people of the state would vote in the presidential election. “Governor Adeleke, the fact that he won his election cannot compel the people of Osun State to vote for Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he said. To support his argument, Olawepo-Hashim recalled the 2011 general election, when he said voters in Osun State did not follow the political direction of then Lagos State Governor, Bola Tinubu, after the latter allegedly backed the Peoples Democratic Party’s candidate, Goodluck Jonathan, instead of the Action Congress of Nigeria’s presidential candidate, Nuhu Ribadu. He said Osun voters supported Ribadu despite the reported political arrangement, arguing that the state’s electorate had a history of making independent political choices. “Osun people are incredibly honourable people, what we call Omoluabi in the Yoruba parlance; they are ideological; they have great history, they are not conquered people, they do what they believe,” he said. The Accord Party candidate maintained that Adeleke’s current political alignment would not prevent his party from seeking votes in Osun State during the presidential election. “I still believe that regardless of what Governor Adeleke is doing, Osun people are still going to vote for Accord Party at the presidential election,” he said. title: Cornell University bans frat parties, vows to address 'disturbing' campus culture
body:
Fraternities on Cornell's campus will not be allowed to host parties or events for the rest of the academic year. Jeongyoon Han for NPR hide caption
Cornell University has banned parties and social events at fraternities for the rest of the school year and will bring sexual assault investigators into its police unit, in response to a former student's allegation of gang rape in 2024.
The changes came on Tuesday as the university said it is committed to addressing a "deeply disturbing" culture of drug and alcohol abuse, and a rise in sexual violence on campus following a civil lawsuit filed by a former student, Jane Doe, which set off national outrage and a crisis at Cornell.
"I am deeply sorry for the harm Jane Doe suffered in 2024, and appalled that this act of sexual violence occurred within our Cornell community," Michael I. Kotlikoff, who is Cornell's president, wrote in a letter addressed to the campus on Tuesday. "It is clear that women on our campus continue to question whether they are safe. We must meet this moment by acknowledging where we have fallen short and taking meaningful action."
The lawsuit, which Doe filed nearly one month ago, alleges that Doe was plied with ketamine and was sexually assaulted by members of the Chi Phi fraternity during a party in October of 2024. The details of the allegations, which disclosed how fraternity members used a Snapchat group chat to discuss the woman and events at the party with openly crude language, sparked fury across the nation.
Doe's lawyer, Thomas Giuffra, told news outlets that Doe has been sent death threats and police swarmed her family's home since she filed the lawsuit.
The administration's changes come after student groups organized protests last week on campus.
"The administration is clearly feeling the heat and needed to make a move," says John Hartnett, a sophomore at Cornell who has helped organize protests. He called the changes a "half measure," and said that banning frats was not a long term solution to systematic issues at the university.
The faculty senate is considering a vote of no confidence in the university administration at a meeting scheduled for Wednesday. It's a rare move that demonstrates the deep seated frustration and distrust stemming from the 2024 case.
"Trust is still eroded on campus — that hasn't changed," says Julia Chang, an associate professor of Hispanic studies in the Department of Romance Studies. "The fact that these changes are coming about now — two years later — is a testament to the power of the student movement and the global conversation it has sparked; not the integrity of the administration."
The moratorium on events at fraternities is expected to have a reverberating effect on campus, where about one-third of all students participate in fraternities and sororities. The university's ties to Greek life, Kotlikoff said, has in part created a toxic culture on campus that requires serious course correction.
"While this is not a problem unique to Cornell, we are committed to setting a higher standard for education, oversight, and enforcement of safe social behavior and citizenship," Kotlikoff wrote.
Ray Epstein, who works with a consent education company, and is one of the organizers of a rally planned just steps away from Cornell's campus on Tuesday, said that while the measures from Cornell are "overall a win," they also serve as an "effort to save face."
"What I think they should be doing, is operating first instead of as a business, the way that they are now, as institutions that are meant to educate and keep their students safe," Epstein said.
Kotlikoff said that in addition to enhancing bystander training programming, the university will also improve its services to survivors of sexual assault by increasing staffing in its civil rights office, which would help individuals navigate the reporting process for incidents.
Additionally, the university will work with the New York State Police's criminal investigators on campus sexual assault investigations. The move allows the investigators, who are independent from the university, to take on cases in which survivors pursue criminal charges.
The university plans to bring in faculty who are experts in sexual assault and rape culture to help reform the Presidential Task Force on Sexual Assault through listening events with the Cornell community.
Kotlikoff's letter did not explain why these events are only being issued now — two years after administrators at Cornell learned about the allegations in 2024.
Although the district attorney did not prosecute the case in 2024, Cornell's Title IX office conducted an investigation in 2025. In March 2025, a panel of staff and faculty at Cornell moved to expel or suspend some of the men. The panel required the remaining men to write "essays" in addition to other sanctions.
Cornell also barred the Chi Phi fraternity chapter, which was closed in 2024.

title: Boeing on pace to increase aircraft deliveries in 2026 as 737 handovers rise
body: Boeing delivered 475 commercial aircraft in the first nine months of 2026, up 8% from a year earlier, putting it on pace to exceed last year’s total as deliveries of the 737 family increased. The latest figures, released on October 13, 2026, show Boeing remains behind Airbus , which delivered 547 aircraft through September. Both manufacturers increased deliveries by about 8% compared with the same period in 2025. Boeing delivered 600 commercial aircraft last year. It needs another 126 in the fourth quarter to surpass that total, after handing over 161 in the third quarter. The 737 accounted for most of Boeing’s year-to-date improvement as deliveries rose to 367 from 330 in the first nine months of 2025. Deliveries of the larger 787 were nearly unchanged at 62, compared with 61 a year earlier, while 777 deliveries fell to 20 from 29. Boeing also delivered 26 aircraft from the 767 line, up from 20. Third-quarter deliveries were close to last year’s level: 161 aircraft compared with 160. This year’s quarterly total comprised 124 737s, 22 787s, 10 767s and five 777s. September 2026 brought an increase from the previous month, with Boeing delivering 57 aircraft, up from 51 in August and 55 in September 2025. Boeing had a strong September for new orders, booking 165 aircraft. A Turkish Airlines order for 100 737 MAX jets accounted for most of Boeing’s monthly sales. Other September orders included 20 737 MAX aircraft for Lufthansa , six 737 MAXs and five 787s for Biman Bangladesh Airlines , and eight 777-8 Freighters and two 777 Freighters for Ethiopian Airlines . Airbus nevertheless remained well ahead in orders for the first nine months. It recorded 1,174 gross orders, or 1,105 after cancellations. Boeing booked 618 orders after cancellations over the same period, according to Dow Jones . Boeing’s official backlog stood at 6,371 aircraft at the end of September, up from 6,156 a month earlier, Reuters reported . The delivery figures come as Boeing works to sustain higher production. CEO Kelly Ortberg said in September that getting 737 output consistently to 47 aircraft a month had taken longer than expected. Boeing is scheduled to report its third-quarter financial results on October 27, 2026. The company said the delivery figures remain preliminary until those results are issued. title: Guilfoyle Resigns as WSJ Names Two Greek Businessmen in Luxury Travel Controversy
body: Kimberly Guilfoyle has resigned as US Ambassador to Greece after President Donald Trump asked her to leave the post, as a series of Wall Street Journal investigations intensifies scrutiny of her alleged relationships with wealthy business figures, luxury travel and possible ethics violations.. Serving as the United States Ambassador to Greece has been the honor of a lifetime. I will forever be grateful to President Donald J. Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio for entrusting me with the extraordinary privilege of representing the greatest country in the history of… — Kimberly Guilfoyle (@kimguilfoyle) October 13, 2026 The White House confirms on Tuesday, October 13, that it has asked Guilfoyle to resign. Guilfoyle subsequently announces her departure on social media, denies wrongdoing and vows to defend her reputation. The latest Wall Street Journal investigation identifies two prominent Greek businessmen, Alexandros Exarchou, chief executive of AKTOR Group, and shipping magnate Nikolas Tsakos, in reporting about Guilfoyle’s alleged luxury travel arrangements. According to the newspaper, the report raises questions about private jet journeys, expensive hotel accommodation and the relationships between the ambassador and businessmen with commercial interests connected to Greece. The allegations have prompted Democratic lawmakers to call for investigations into potential breaches of federal bribery laws and government ethics requirements. Guilfoyle denies wrongdoing, while the US Embassy in Athens maintains that she has complied with applicable ethics rules. Private Jets, Luxury Hotels and Davos According to The Wall Street Journal , Guilfoyle discusses her connections with wealthy Greek businessmen during a recorded conversation in January 2026, while attending the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland. The newspaper reports that she travelled to Davos on a private jet with Exarchou, who leads the Greek construction group AKTOR. During the conversation, Guilfoyle allegedly describes Exarchou as “my man” while discussing his business interests and her efforts to promote American energy exports across the region. The report alleges that Guilfoyle encouraged governments from Bulgaria to Albania to conduct business with Exarchou and purchase billions of dollars worth of American natural gas. These revelations raise questions about the intersection of diplomatic responsibilities, private relationships and the commercial interests of businesses connected to people in the ambassador’s social circle. AKTOR, through its lawyers, declines to comment on the latest allegations. The company’s lawyers have previously argued that Guilfoyle did not improperly promote its commercial interests. Shipping Magnate Linked to Paris Trip The investigation also names Nikolas Tsakos, chief executive of Tsakos Energy Navigation, in connection with Guilfoyle’s reported luxury travel. According to the newspaper, Guilfoyle discusses plans to travel to Paris on a private jet with Tsakos later in January to attend his wife’s fashion show. She also reportedly describes spending Christmas and New Year’s with Tsakos and his family at Gstaad, an exclusive Swiss resort. People familiar with the matter tell the newspaper that Tsakos covers Guilfoyle’s accommodation bill at the Four Seasons Hotel George V in Paris. Guilfoyle subsequently plans to publish photographs from the fashion event to her Instagram audience of approximately two million followers, according to the report. Some of the photographs feature Tsakos. The newspaper says the alleged financial support for her travel had not previously been publicly disclosed. Tsakos and his wife do not respond to the newspaper’s requests for comment. The reported arrangements raise questions about whether the travel and accommodation constitute gifts requiring disclosure under applicable US government ethics rules. Davos Dinner Dispute The investigation also details a dispute involving a dinner organised by Greek House Davos in honour of Eric Trump, the US president’s son. According to the newspaper, Guilfoyle is initially excluded from the guest list and expresses anger while attempting to secure an invitation. The report says she discusses her connections with wealthy Greek businessmen while seeking help from an American businessman who is invited to the event. Guilfoyle ultimately secures a place at the dinner. Irene Vantaraki, president of Greek House Davos, says the organisers have to manage a disruption involving several high-profile guests. She describes Guilfoyle as polite and discreet and says the ambassador leaves early. State Department Faces Questions The controversy extends beyond travel arrangements. According to The Wall Street Journal , the State Department’s inspector general is examining whether Guilfoyle received gifts or favours from private businesspeople. The newspaper also reports that text messages show Guilfoyle asking a Trump donor to deposit $100,000 into her American Express account. The donor reportedly offered assistance with reviewing personal tax and legal issues involving the Trump administration. Guilfoyle’s lawyer disputes the authenticity of the messages. Her legal representatives have also argued that the money sought related to unpaid speaking engagements and consulting services predating her ambassadorial appointment. Trump expresses concern about the reports before the White House announces its decision. “I just heard about it. It’s very bad,” he tells reporters, while also describing Guilfoyle as someone who had always been kind to him. Vice President JD Vance says the allegations must be examined and that people should face consequences if wrongdoing is established. Secretary of State Marco Rubio also faces questions about the controversy during his visit to Athens. He declines to discuss the reported messages at an airport press briefing. Guilfoyle Resigns but Denies Wrongdoing Following the White House announcement, Guilfoyle issues a statement on X confirming that her time as ambassador is coming to an end. She maintains that her support for Trump and Rubio remains unchanged and rejects the allegations against her. “These allegations are false, and I intend to vigorously defend my name, my reputation, and my integrity,” she writes. The departure ends her tenure as Washington’s representative in Athens amid mounting scrutiny of her conduct and relationships with private business interests. Democrats Demand Formal Investigation Democratic lawmakers intensify their calls for an investigation into Guilfoyle’s conduct. Representative Gregory Meeks, the leading Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, requests an immediate investigation into whether the ambassador violated federal laws governing bribery and corruption in public office. Meeks also asks the State Department’s inspector general to examine whether Guilfoyle breached federal laws, departmental regulations or government ethics requirements. Representative Robert Garcia, the leading Democrat on the House Oversight Committee, separately raises concerns about potential public corruption and national security implications. Garcia requests financial records and communications between Guilfoyle and specified government officials. The lawmakers’ demands add pressure on the State Department to establish whether the reported arrangements breached any applicable rules or laws. US Embassy Defends Guilfoyle’s Conduct The US Embassy in Athens maintains that Guilfoyle has complied with the relevant ethics requirements. An embassy spokesperson says the ambassador’s career, both in and outside public service, is guided by established values and that she has followed State Department guidelines concerning the declaration of gifts. “Unsubstantiated allegations simply distract from the important work it is doing in Greece and the wider Eastern Mediterranean,” the spokesperson says. The Greek government has not publicly commented on the allegations described in the reports. Guilfoyle’s resignation does not itself establish that a crime has occurred. The reported travel arrangements, financial requests and business relationships remain subject to scrutiny, while Guilfoyle denies wrongdoing. The case leaves questions about transparency, the declaration of gifts and the safeguards governing relationships between US diplomatic representatives and private business interests as Washington and Athens continue their strategic partnership. Source: Reuters: White House asks US ambassador to Greece to resign and The Wall Street Journal, as quoted in the supplied material. title: BoG deepens public trust with regional stakeholder forum in Techiman
body: As part of its strategic commitment to inclusive central banking and nationwide financial literacy, the Bank of Ghana (BoG) has held a high-level Regional Stakeholder Engagement Forum at the Jemima Grace Hotel, Techiman. The meeting took place on Monday, 12 October 2026, on the theme: Strengthening Stakeholder Relations Through Dialogue and Engagement. The forum forms part of the Bank’s 16-regional outreach programme aimed at demystifying the mandate of the central bank, deepening public confidence in the financial system, and creating direct feedback channels between the regulator and the public. The engagement brought together a broad spectrum of stakeholders in the Bono East Region, including traditional leaders, religious leaders, market queens and trader associations, SMEs, representatives of rural and community banks, microfinance institutions, security agencies, and media practitioners. A total of 150 participants attended the programme. The delegation for the forum was led by Bernard Otabil, Director of Communications, together with Victor Akakpo, Head of Regional Branch Coordinating Office, and Abdulai Lawal Abubakar, Regional Director, Sunyani, who has oversight responsibility for the Bono East Region. Technical presentations were delivered by seasoned experts from key departments of the Bank: Banking Supervision Department (BSD), Other Financial Institutions Supervision Department (OFISD), Financial Stability Department (FSD), and Currency Management Department (CMD) “The Cedi Is Trust” – Director of Communications In his opening remarks, Mr Otabil stressed that central banking cannot thrive in isolation, noting that stakeholder trust is the bedrock of monetary policy effectiveness. “The Cedi is not just paper. It is trust. It is a social contract between the Bank of Ghana and every Ghanaian. We can formulate the best monetary policy, but if the trader in the Techiman market, arguably one of the largest open markets in West Africa, does not understand or trust it, we have failed. That is why we are here, not to lecture, but to listen, to dialogue, and to partner for financial stability,” he stated. He added that BoG has deliberately shifted to a people-centred model where public voices shape policy response, especially in fighting unlicensed financial schemes, currency abuse, and misinformation. Participants were taken through five critical thematic areas: 1. The Role and Mandate of the Bank of Ghana: Clarifying BoG’s core functions of price stability, financial stability, and currency management. 2. Microfinance Sector Reforms: Explaining the rationale behind the Microfinance sector reforms and implications for the industry. 3. Responsible Borrowing and Consumer Protection: Educating the public on their rights, loan disclosure requirements, and the need to avoid over-indebtedness. 4. Currency Education – FEEL, LOOK, TILT: A practical demonstration on how to identify genuine Ghana Cedi banknotes, detect counterfeits, and properly handle notes. 5. Dud Cheques – Causes, Implications and Prevention: Highlighting the legal and financial consequences of issuing dud cheques and measures to curb the practice. Stakeholder Feedback In an open forum, participants commended the Bank for bringing the engagement to their doorstep. They raised pertinent concerns including access to affordable credit for SMEs and farmers, the persistence of high lending rates despite falling inflation, the activities of unregulated lenders and “black market” forex operators, and the need for sustained education on the security features of the new Heritage Series Banknotes. Officials of the Bank provided detailed responses and assured participants that their concerns would be escalated to Management for policy consideration. Mr Otabil reiterated the Bank’s commitment to sustaining open dialogue across all 16 regions as a tool for promoting financial inclusion, financial literacy, and resilience of the financial system. He urged the public to be vigilant and report suspected unlicensed financial institutions, counterfeit currency, and financial fraud cases to the Bank or law enforcement agencies. The forum ended with a renewed call for partnership between the Bank of Ghana and regional stakeholders to protect the value of the Cedi and safeguard the stability of Ghana’s financial system.

title: Russian attacks spark fires at industrial facilities in Khmelnytskyi region
body:
Serhii Tyurin, head of the Khmelnytskyi Regional Military Administration, reported this on Facebook , according to Ukrinform.
“The enemy continues to attack the Khmelnytskyi region . Air defense forces are engaged, and some missiles have been shot down. Details to follow,” Tyurin noted.
As a result of the attack, fires broke out on the premises of industrial facilities in the Khmelnytskyi and Shepetivka districts. Rescue workers are on the scene.
No reports of fatalities or injuries have been received.
As reported by Ukrinform, a truck and a company warehouse were damaged in the Khmelnytskyi region as a result of a Russian attack.

title: How autonomous weapons are changing the way brigades fight
body: At Fort Bragg, soldiers recently tested how unmanned systems could help troops breach obstacles while reducing exposure to battlefield hazards. During Project Sandhills 2.0 , soldiers planned flight routes and operated Bumblebee V2 small unmanned aircraft systems at Range 63. The project tested how unmanned systems could support contested obstacle breaching, while soldiers and industry partners collected feedback to inform future Army capabilities. The Army said the effort included autonomous trucks, robotic breaching payloads, drone swarms, mine detection and counter-UAS tools operating on the same problem. A counter-UAS turret used a human-authorized effector, underscoring that autonomy did not mean removing people from critical decisions. Human decision-making remains central to the Army’s approach. The experiment illustrates the larger question raised by retired Army Col. Dave Rowland and retired Command Sgt. Maj. Brian Hester in a Sept. 29 Modern War Institute analysis : Autonomy becomes consequential not when the Army adds an individual robotic system, but when it has enough autonomous systems, performing enough missions, to change how an entire brigade fights. That difference becomes more consequential as autonomous systems are integrated across a battlefield shaped by drones, sensors, electronic warfare and precision fires. Rowland and Hester argue that persistent observation and long-range fires make large formations easier to find and attack, threatening the maneuver that allows combined-arms forces to concentrate combat power. They envision autonomous systems moving ahead of manned formations to identify enemy positions, obstacles and usable routes. Other systems could provide counter-drone, electronic-warfare, sensing or deception capabilities, while autonomous platforms could move supplies through exposed areas. Beyond experimentation The Army is moving beyond experimentation into acquisition and organizational changes, with its fiscal 2026 budget justification including an “Autonomy Formation” effort intended to accelerate robotics for armored and infantry formations. In July, the Army selected four companies for its Engineer Autonomous Breaching Capability program , which calls for prototypes capable of breaching complex obstacles and minefields under direct observation and fire using beyond-line-of-sight autonomous control. An assessment of the unit is planned for early 2027. On Oct. 1, Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle signed a memorandum directing the establishment of the U.S. Army Futures and Autonomous Systems Command , or FASCOM. The Army announced the move Oct. 2, saying the command will integrate autonomous capabilities into aviation, armor, fires, sustainment, engineer and training formations. It will also prioritize autonomous fires, combat vehicles, watercraft resupply, breaching, reconnaissance, surveillance and target acquisition, and crewed-uncrewed teaming for acquisition and fielding by fiscal 2028. But the Army’s own research shows why turning that ambition into battlefield capability won’t be simple. In a Sept. 30 Army Research Laboratory study, 13 soldiers operated a mixed air-ground formation during a two-week simulation. The formation included a manned control vehicle, two robotic combat vehicles, a Future Vertical Lift platform and shared launched effects, operating against a human-controlled opposing force under contested conditions. Researchers found that the formation adapted rapidly, developed effective coordination patterns and maintained stable subjective workload as mission complexity increased. The findings suggest that air-ground teaming was feasible under the conditions tested and that soldiers could integrate autonomous capabilities without an unsustainable cognitive burden. However, the study did not demonstrate autonomous maneuver by an operational brigade. It tested a specific human-machine formation in a simulation under defined conditions. Another Army Research Laboratory study examining autonomous reconnaissance and screening identified soldier-robot trust, communications, shared understanding and cognitive load as areas requiring further research. Those issues become especially important when communications are degraded or denied. That is where Rowland and Hester envision a fundamental change in command. A brigade cannot scale autonomy if every unmanned vehicle requires a soldier continuously controlling it. The retired Army leaders describe a progression from operating individual systems, to supervising multiple systems, to coordinating mixed manned-unmanned teams and eventually commanding autonomous formations through mission command. Ukraine offers evidence of what unmanned systems can already do, but also a warning against overstating the technology. Rowland and Hester point to Ukrainian use of unmanned ground systems for logistics and casualty evacuation while noting that most remain remotely operated or have only limited autonomy. Their use demonstrates the value of shifting dangerous work from people to machines; it does not establish that fully autonomous formations are ready for combat. Acquisition isn’t the only issue The Army faces a problem bigger than acquiring machines alone. It must determine how many systems formations can absorb, how soldiers should supervise them, how networks can support them under attack and what happens when a machine encounters circumstances its programming does not anticipate. Rowland and Hester argue the Army should learn those lessons before the technology is perfected. They call for brigades to train with meaningful quantities of autonomous systems at home stations, identify failures and refine tactics before those systems reach combat training centers. The Army is now aligning its organizations, acquisition efforts and training around that broader push. The unresolved question is whether those efforts can produce something more difficult than a successful demonstration: a repeatable way for a brigade to see, survive, sustain and maneuver when an adversary is actively disrupting its communications and attacking its forces.

In a Sept. 30 Army Research Laboratory study, 13 soldiers operated a mixed air-ground formation during a two-week simulation. The formation included a manned control vehicle, two robotic combat vehicles, a Future Vertical Lift platform and shared launched effects, operating against a human-controlled opposing force under contested conditions. Researchers found that the formation adapted rapidly, developed effective coordination patterns and maintained stable subjective workload as mission complexity increased. The findings suggest that air-ground teaming was feasible under the conditions tested and that soldiers could integrate autonomous capabilities without an unsustainable cognitive burden. However, the study did not demonstrate autonomous maneuver by an operational brigade. It tested a specific human-machine formation in a simulation under defined conditions. Another Army Research Laboratory study examining autonomous reconnaissance and screening identified soldier-robot trust, communications, shared understanding and cognitive load as areas requiring further research. Those issues become especially important when communications are degraded or denied. That is where Rowland and Hester envision a fundamental change in command. A brigade cannot scale autonomy if every unmanned vehicle requires a soldier continuously controlling it. The retired Army leaders describe a progression from operating individual systems, to supervising multiple systems, to coordinating mixed manned-unmanned teams and eventually commanding autonomous formations through mission command. Ukraine offers evidence of what unmanned systems can already do, but also a warning against overstating the technology. Rowland and Hester point to Ukrainian use of unmanned ground systems for logistics and casualty evacuation while noting that most remain remotely operated or have only limited autonomy. Their use demonstrates the value of shifting dangerous work from people to machines; it does not establish that fully autonomous formations are ready for combat. Acquisition isn’t the only issue The Army faces a problem bigger than acquiring machines alone. It must determine how many systems formations can absorb, how soldiers should supervise them, how networks can support them under attack and what happens when a machine encounters circumstances its programming does not anticipate. Rowland and Hester argue the Army should learn those lessons before the technology is perfected. They call for brigades to train with meaningful quantities of autonomous systems at home stations, identify failures and refine tactics before those systems reach combat training centers. The Army is now aligning its organizations, acquisition efforts and training around that broader push. The unresolved question is whether those efforts can produce something more difficult than a successful demonstration: a repeatable way for a brigade to see, survive, sustain and maneuver when an adversary is actively disrupting its communications and attacking its forces.

title: ‘We have turned the tide’ – Ato Forson says Ghana is ready to take off
body: Finance Minister Dr. Cassiel Ato Forson says Ghana has turned the tide from economic crisis and laid the foundation for sustained progress, but has cautioned that further gains will depend on protecting macroeconomic stability. According to him, the country was moving in the right direction, with the foundation now in place to support economic take-off. “Today we have turned the tide. We are moving the right direction. And I can assure you that based on the foundation that we have laid, this country is ready to take off,” Dr. Forson said. The Finance Minister, however, stressed that the turnaround was not a reason to abandon caution. He said the stability underpinning the recovery must remain central to the country’s next steps. “And we will take off cautiously. Bear in mind that all the gains we have made is dependent on us maintaining the macroeconomic stability,” he cautioned. Dr. Forson said building on the progress achieved must go hand in hand with preserving its foundations. “And so, the gains that we will build on, we should not forget the foundation that we have laid,” he added. He also reminded those entrusted with the country’s leadership that their mandate was to respond to a national crisis and work to the satisfaction of Ghanaians. “We were elected to come and save a country in crisis. Don’t forget that. President Mahama and his members of parliament were elected to save this country because Ghana was in a crisis. Let us not forget that,” he said. The Finance Minister emphasised that delivering on that mandate remained a shared responsibility, even as the country’s circumstances improved. “Together, we have a responsibility. A responsibility to work to the satisfaction of the people of Ghana,” he said.

title: Police arrest man captured in viral video assaulting wife in Agona Nkwanta
body: The Ghana Police Service has arrested a 30-year-old farmer captured in a viral video assaulting his wife, Diana Mensah, 25, at Agona Nkwanta in the Western Region. In a statement issued on Tuesday, October 13, the suspect, identified as Emmanuel Kwofie, was arrested on Monday, October 12, 2026, at about 7:00 p.m. in Agona Nkwanta. According to the Western Regional Police Command, preliminary investigations indicate that the suspect and the victim are married and live together at Domeabra in the Agona Nkwanta Municipality. The victim deals in second-hand clothing. Police said the incident occurred on Thursday, October 8, after the suspect allegedly accused his wife of having an extramarital affair and subjected her to severe beating, as captured in the circulating video. The victim was rescued by a Good Samaritan and taken to the Agona Nkwanta Polyclinic, where she received treatment and was discharged. The suspect is currently in police custody and is expected to be put before court, the police said in a press release dated October 13, 2026. title: Show HN: Guitoro, a virtual guitar you strum with your keyboard
body:
The most realistic virtual guitar online
Guitoro is the most realistic and the most complete virtual guitar you can play online, free in your browser. Play it with your computer keyboard, your left hand on the chords and your right hand strumming, or swipe the strings with your finger on a phone or tablet. Choose a steel-string acoustic, a classic guitar, an electric guitar or a four-string bass.
It's also a way to learn chords and songs that a chord chart or a video lesson can't show you. Each song plays its best-known part close to the original recording, stroke for stroke. Slow it down to 20% and watch it being played: each string lights up the moment it's hit, the pick swings down and up with the strum, and the neck shows which finger goes where.
Then it's your turn. No guitar? Play the song on the keys or the screen, and it waits for you at every chord change. Have a guitar? Pick it up and play along at your own speed, with the strings, the strum and the fingering right in front of you.
Every guitar and bass note is a recording of a real instrument. There's nothing to download and no account to create. If you played the Google guitar doodle, Guitoro takes the idea further: six real strings, 15 chords in every key, and 51 songs to play along with.
No guitar needed. Guitoro is built to be played, not just clicked, on whatever you have in front of you.
Your left hand holds a chord on the letter keys and your right hand strums with H and J , the way you'd play a real guitar. 22 chords sit under your fingers, plus keys for arpeggios, single strings, chucks and palm mutes.
On a phone or tablet, tap a chord pad and swipe the strings with your finger. Up to five fingers at once, and you can tap the frets on the neck to play single notes.
Drag across the strings. A fast swipe plays louder, a slow drag rolls the notes one by one, and a click plucks a single string.
On a computer, switch to Solo and every keyboard row becomes a string and every column a fret, with bends and vibrato on the arrow keys.
In a video lesson the hand moves fast and hides the strings, so you can't tell which ones were really hit. Guitar apps teach the basic chords and stop there. Guitoro plays the song's real part on the guitar in front of you, at the speed you choose, and shows exactly what the hands do. Then you play it, on the virtual guitar or on your own.
Each song plays its best-known part close to the original recording, stroke for stroke. Slow it anywhere from 20% to full speed and the chords, the strum and the band slow down together.
Each string lights up the moment it sounds, then vibrates as it rings. You can see whether a stroke hits all six strings, just the bass strings or only the top three.
Over a strummed part, the pick swings down and up like a real strumming hand, once per step of the pattern. Solid swings hit the strings and faint ones miss them, so you see the hand keep moving through the gaps.
While a chord rings, the neck shows it: finger numbers from 1 to 4, barres, muted strings and the capo. Copy the shape onto your own guitar.
Play a song's chords on the keys or the screen and it follows you. The keys show its chords in order, the next one lights green, and the song holds until you play it. No score and no rush.
Watch a part slowly, copy it on your guitar, then play along as you raise the speed. On a computer, choose My guitar: the on-screen keys step aside and the song box shows the strum or picking pattern, a chord strip you can click to jump around, and the speed.
Most online guitars only let you click single strings or frets, or play a synthesized tone when you click a chord. On Guitoro you strum: swipe across the strings or use the keys, and every string sounds as you cross it, from recordings of real instruments.
Every guitar and bass note is a recording of a real instrument: a steel-string acoustic, a classic guitar with nylon strings, a solid-body electric on its bridge pickup, and a four-string bass.
Each string sounds as your finger or mouse crosses it. Swipe down or up, fast or slow, and you hear the difference, down to a slow roll across the strings.
Chords use the shapes guitarists play, with open strings, barres and muted strings, so a G sounds like a G on a guitar, not on a keyboard.
Chucks, palm mutes, hammer-ons, pull-offs, bends and vibrato, while the strings vibrate on screen as they ring.
Strum real chords and play whole songs with your computer keyboard or your fingers, with a backing band behind you. On a train, at the office or on the sofa, a laptop or a phone and headphones are enough.
Songs like Wonderwall, Hallelujah and Let It Be come set up with the right key, capo, tempo and the strum from the record. Lead the chords from the keys, or pick up your own guitar and play along at any speed.
Slow a song's strum down, watch which way the pick moves on every beat, then strum it yourself over a drum beat until it feels steady.
See where each finger goes, hear how the chord should sound, then copy the shape on a real guitar. Every chord also has its own page in the guitar chord chart .
Paste the chords of a song from a chord site and hear how it goes before you sit down to play it.
Type a chord progression under My songs, loop it with the backing band, and record the idea before it's gone.
Show a class a chord shape or a strum on a big screen, slowed down, with every string and every pick stroke visible.
Singers, keyboard players and songwriters can hear how guitar chords are voiced and see how a progression lies on the fretboard, without learning to hold a guitar first.
The most complete virtual guitar online: four instruments, every key, real chord shapes, songs, a backing band and recording, all free in one place.
Steel-string acoustic, classic guitar, electric and four-string bass, each built from recorded samples. Pick a recording for the acoustic (Warm, Bright or Mellow) and the classic (Natural or Concert), and presets for the electric, from Clean to Crunch, Classic Rock, Metal, Lead and Ambient.
Press C for a C chord, G for G, A to G in all. The keys around them hold Am, Em, Dm and the five sharps and flats, the number row Bm, F#m and other minors, Caps Lock makes any chord minor and Tab makes it a seventh. Or pick one of the 24 major and minor keys and the chord keys fill with the 15 chords that fit it. Edit puts any chord you type, like F#m7 or Dsus2, on a key.
While a chord rings, the neck shows finger numbers, barres, muted strings and the capo. Standard is the shape most players learn first, Easy swaps a barre chord for a smaller shape, and Up plays the same chord higher up the neck.
51 songs and classical pieces come set up to play, from Wonderwall and Hotel California to Canon in D. Slow them to 20%, lead their chords from the keys, or play along on your own guitar.
14 everyday strums from Steady downs and the pop staple D DU U DU to shuffle and 6/8, 4 styles (reggae, funk and country), 26 more rhythms drawn from real songs, and 12 picking patterns like Travis and classical p-i-m-a. Choose one and you hear it straight away.
Drums, bass and strings that follow your chords: 15 drum styles, including rock, funk, reggae, bossa nova and cajon, and 25 bass lines. The Band switch next to Play turns them on. Tempo goes from 10 to 220 BPM, with a metronome.
Paste a song from a chord site or as ChordPro text, pick a strum, and Guitoro plays it with the band. Write "x2" to repeat a line or a part. Lyrics are left out, and your songs stay in your browser.
Play single notes and melodies on the neck from the computer keyboard, with hammer-ons, pull-offs, bends and vibrato.
Overdrive, distortion and fuzz on the electric, plus bass, mid and treble, room or hall reverb, and delay on every instrument.
10 tunings, from Standard, Drop D and half step down to DADGAD and Open G, D and E, a capo up to fret 10, and a left-handed guitar.
Record takes of up to 10 minutes with the band, replay them and save them as WAV or a small compressed file. Takes stay in your browser.
A free guitar tuner that listens through your microphone, with pages for drop D, open tunings, the bass and the ukulele .
From silence to a song you lead yourself. The first two steps take a few seconds.
Pick Acoustic, Classic, Electric or Bass at the top of the page. On a phone, tap the guitar picture. You can switch at any time.
Tap a chord pad, or press its letter on the keyboard: C plays C, G plays G, D plays D. Hold Caps Lock for a minor chord. Strum on chord key starts on, so the chord strums itself.
Turn Auto off, then swipe down across the strings for a downstroke and up for an upstroke. On a keyboard, H strums down and J strums up.
Open the Strum menu and pick a strum or picking pattern. You hear it once on your chord. With Auto and Loop on, it keeps playing while you hold a chord key.
Open Songs & recordings and pick a song. Press Play to hear it, or press the chord key that lights green to lead it yourself. The tempo button next to Play slows it down.
Turn on the Band switch next to Play. Its edit button opens Backing band, where you choose the drums, the bass line and the strings.
Open Songs & recordings, choose Recordings, and press Record. Play, then use Stop next to the recording timer. Your takes stay in Recordings.
Your left hand holds the chords and your right hand strums, just like on a guitar. Chord keys play the letter printed on them, QWERTZ and AZERTY included, the other keys keep their place on a US QWERTY keyboard, and every key on screen shows its letter.
Press G, C and D, then Z for Em: together these four chords play hundreds of pop and folk songs. Press each one and watch the neck: the numbers are your fingers, from 1 for the index to 4 for the little finger. An X marks a string you don't play, and a bar across the strings is a barre.
Play C, then Am. The chord name above the guitar tells you which is major and which is minor, and your ear learns the bright and the sad sound. Do the same with the sevenths: hold Tab as you press a chord.
Put your fingers where the dots are, strum, and compare your sound with Guitoro's. A buzzing or dead string usually means a finger is too far from the fret or touching the next string. Many barre chords have an Easy version for while your hand gets stronger.
Open Songs & recordings and pick a song, or paste one under My songs. Press each chord key as it lights green: the song waits for you at every change. Start slow, then raise the speed a little at a time.
Switch the key to hear the same chords higher or lower, or in a minor key. Put a capo on in Settings and the same shapes sound higher, which is how guitarists play in keys like A or B with easy open chords. Drop D and Open G show how a tuning changes the whole sound.
Low E string on the left. Numbers are fingers, O is an open string, X is a string you don't play.
Strum patterns are written with D for a downstroke and U for an upstroke, and x for a muted chuck. The trick is to keep your hand moving down on every number and up on every "and", even when it misses the strings. In Guitoro you can watch the pick do exactly that.
Counted "1, 2 and, and, 4 and": the down on beat 3 is left out, but the hand still moves.
Choose a pattern from the Strum menu and you hear it once on your chord. The menu shows each pattern as a grid of downs and ups.
Open a song with the strum you want and slow it to 50% or less. The pick swings down on the numbers and up on the "and"s: solid when it hits the strings, faint when it misses. The strings light up to show which ones each stroke hits.
Turn Auto off, turn on the Band switch or the metronome, and strum along with H and J or by swiping the strings.
Record a take and listen for uneven strokes. When it sounds steady, speed up.
Steady downs, then Down-up eighths, then the pop staple, then 6/8 ballad and Shuffle. After that, open songs like Wonderwall, Hallelujah and Knockin' on Heaven's Door and strum their own patterns.
Each song page has its chords with diagrams and its strum or picking pattern written out, and sets the guitar up for you: key, capo, tempo and chords. The easy guitar songs page groups them by how many chords they have.
Playing a real guitar along? The free online guitar tuner listens through your microphone, with pages for drop D, half step down and open tunings. There is a free ukulele tuner too.
Every major, minor and seventh chord in all 12 keys, with finger charts and an easier version where there is one: the guitar chord chart . Search any chord there, hear it strummed, and open it on the guitar.
