title: Jewish writer barred from London group over Zionist beliefs, UKLFI warns of Equality Act breach
body: UK Lawyers for Israel (UKLFI) intervened after a Jewish comedian and writer was barred from a North London writers group on October 6 due to his Zionist beliefs.Harry Deansway, whose real name is Joshua Rinkoff, had participated in the Offbeat Writers Group for six months without issues before group organizer Ruby Sullivan messaged him in response to an online comment about antisemitism in late September.Sullivan stated that she was “very strongly pro-Palestine (NOT antisemitic)” and that “if our opinions on this don't align it will affect our working together as it's very important for me that the offbeat space and where I share my work is pro-Palestine.”Deansway responded that he was “Jewish and a Zionist,” that he was “totally up for having a discussion about it,” and that he had “no issue with someone being pro-Palestine.” He further explained his viewpoint, stating, “I can be a Zionist, which at its core is to believe in the right to Jewish self-determination in their ancestral land and still be against the government of the country and anyone's actions that make that a possibility at the expense of the suffering of another people.”Sullivan replied, “I really can't align with your beliefs as they support the massacre of an entire population. You also feigned an interest in women's and gay rights to promote this belief, which I also can't stand behind. [...] I don't think there is a place in the Offbeat Writers' Group for you because of this.”Ideological declaration prepped for prospective membersSullivan added that she was preparing an ideological declaration for prospective members, noting, “I am looking for a London-based anti-apartheid free zone commitment to sign for the group and am creating a document so when people want to enter the group, they understand our ideologies.”UKLFI subsequently sent a formal warning letter to Sullivan on October 6, arguing that the exclusion potentially violated the Equality Act 2010. The organization noted that Deansway received protection under the statute based on his Jewish ethnic background, religious practices, and philosophical beliefs surrounding Jewish self-determination.Furthermore, UKLFI criticized remarks made by Sullivan, specifically her statement that “because of the horrific past the Jewish people have endured, they should not want to inflict the same suffering on others,” pointing out that attributing the conduct of the State of Israel to the Jewish people as a whole constitutes holding Jews collectively responsible for state actions. UKLFI noted that this conduct is identified as an example of antisemitism under the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance (IHRA) working definition.Venue management canceled bookingThe fallout also impacted a scheduled literary showcase that Deansway organized for October 13 at Bar Gemist. Following Sullivan's withdrawal and the exit of other performers, venue management canceled the booking by October 2, noting that the event was originally agreed upon due to its connection with Sullivan and her group.Although UKLFI warned the venue directors that canceling the event could also constitute unlawful discrimination, directors Marion Zoelle and Uros Dezutelj rejected the accusations in a response issued on October 10. They maintained that their choice stemmed from alterations to the event program and communication breakdowns rather than Deansway's identity or political views.While affirming that Deansway remained welcome to visit the establishment, the directors declined to reinstate the showcase and stated they would contest any legal claims.A spokesperson for UKLFI said, “This is McCarthyism dressed up as progressive politics. A Jewish writer has been subjected to an ideological loyalty test and excluded because he believes in Jewish self-determination. People are entitled to oppose Zionism, but they cannot lawfully exclude Jews from cultural activities because they refuse to renounce their beliefs. Jewish artists should not have to pass a political purity test to participate in London's cultural life.”The Offbeat Writers Group did not respond to a request for comment by publication time.

Days after Ukrainian military drones took down several Russian data centers, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy claimed that the campaign had hurt Russia’s disinformation efforts. “It suddenly became a little easier to breathe on many social platforms,” Zelenskyy said Monday. “There was less hate, less division, and fewer provocations.”
Zelenskyy isn’t the first to assert that the drone operation, which targeted data centers belonging to the Russian technology company Yandex, has cut down on spam and disinformation campaigns fomented by Russian bot farms. Social media users have claimed they’ve noticed less traffic on posts by MAGA-affiliated accounts, as well as those associated with the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party. Some have even said they’ve noticed a steep drop in spam calls and messages.
But these people are wrong. The drone strikes appear to have affected Yandex’s web crawlers, not any disinformation or political operations.
In fact, the account antibot4navalny, which tracks state-sponsored troll farms, reports that bot traffic is steady as ever. On Monday, the same day Zelenskyy claimed that disinformation had died down, antibot4navalny reported that several Kremlin-aligned accounts posted videos falsely claiming that experts are demanding the European Union lift the ongoing sanctions on Russia. Danish analyst Valdemar Osted said interactions on MAGA and AfD accounts have actually increased since the strikes. And the charts purportedly showing a decline in bot activity appear to be AI-generated .
Ironically, claims that the drone strikes hindered Russian disinformation campaigns appears to be a form of disinformation itself, no matter what Zelenskyy says.

title: Formula 1 to return to Africa with Rwanda Grand Prix in early 2030s
body: Formula 1 will return to Africa for the first time since 1993 after signing a 10-year agreement with Rwanda to host the Formula 1 African Grand Prix in the early 2030s. The race, presented by Visit Rwanda, will be held at a purpose-built circuit in Bugesera, about 40 kilometres south of the capital, Kigali. The agreement was announced on Tuesday, October 13, with the circuit expected to be completed early in the next decade. The track will be developed to meet FIA Grade 1 standards, the highest required for hosting Formula 1 races, as part of a wider project led by the Rwanda Development Board. Located close to the new Kigali International Airport, the circuit will use the area’s natural landscape and elevation changes to create a challenging racing experience. Beyond Formula 1, the venue is expected to host other motorsport competitions, international events, conferences and entertainment activities. Formula 1 last raced on the African continent at South Africa’s Kyalami circuit in 1993. The return to Rwanda will mark a major step in the sport’s efforts to expand its global presence. Formula 1 says Africa already has more than 100 million fans, with almost 60 per cent of fans in key sub-Saharan African markets under the age of 35. Formula 1 president and chief executive Stefano Domenicali described the agreement as a landmark moment for the sport. “Africa has always been part of Formula 1’s future, and from the beginning we were determined to return in the right way, with the right partner, a long-term commitment and a clear vision for creating meaningful impact,” he said. Domenicali added that the project was intended to deliver benefits beyond the race weekend through tourism, investment, skills development and opportunities for local businesses. Rwanda President Paul Kagame said the agreement would give African fans the opportunity to experience the sport on the continent while creating opportunities for young people. “Rwanda is proud to host the Formula 1 African Grand Prix, and to share this moment with more than 100 million fans across Africa, many of them young people who deserve to see the sport at home and to see themselves in it: as engineers, technicians, entrepreneurs and, one day, drivers,” he said. Kagame added that the 10-year partnership was an investment in Rwanda’s future, with the circuit and airport expected to support jobs, tourism and business development. FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem also welcomed the agreement, describing the return of Formula 1 to Africa as a historic moment. He said the FIA would work with Formula 1 and its partners to ensure the new circuit meets international standards while helping develop motorsport talent across the continent. Further details, including the inaugural race date, construction milestones and race-weekend plans, are expected to be announced later. The Rwanda Grand Prix will make Africa the final inhabited continent to be represented on the Formula 1 calendar once the race begins.

title: Ukraine's Rada backs preliminary bill limiting court access to National Bank banking secrecy
body:
Ukraine's Verkhovna Rada has adopted at first reading bill No. 15555, which would restrict civil and commercial courts' access to information constituting bank secrecy and obtained by the National Bank of Ukraine (NBU) from foreign banking supervisory authorities.
A total of 284 members of parliament voted in favor of the decision on Tuesday, October 13.
The bill provides for amendments to the Civil Procedure Code and the Commercial Procedure Code stipulating that courts will not be able to compel the disclosure of information constituting bank secrecy that the NBU has obtained from banking supervisory authorities in other countries. Courts will be required to reject motions or applications seeking the production or preservation of such evidence.
In addition, the bill proposes supplementing the Law on Banks and Banking with a provision under which the National Bank may disclose information obtained from a foreign banking supervisory authority only with that authority's consent and exclusively for the purposes specified in the relevant agreements.
According to the explanatory note, the bill was developed to fulfill the conditions for closing negotiating Chapter 9, "Financial Services," in Ukraine's EU accession process, implement the provisions of Directive 2013/36/EU, and take into account the Memorandum of Economic and Financial Policies with the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
The proposed amendments are expected to enable the NBU to receive a positive assessment from the European Banking Authority (EBA) regarding the equivalence of its confidentiality regime and remove obstacles to the full exchange of information with central banks and regulators in EU member states.
As reported, bill No. 15555 was registered with the Verkhovna Rada on August 24, 2026, and on September 10, the parliament's Committee on Finance, Taxation and Customs Policy recommended that it be adopted at first reading.

title: Rivian’s startup Mind Robotics hires former Ford EV chief Doug Field
body:
Doug Field has worked on EVs at Ford and Tesla, the not-so-secret car project at Apple, and was employee No. 1 at Segway. Now the executive is turning his attention to Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe’s latest project: Mind Robotics .
Field has been hired as president of Mind Robotics, an industrial AI and robotics venture created last year by Scaringe and backed by Rivian. The news, shared onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 (taking place October 13-15 in San Francisco), is another sign that Mind Robotics is getting ready to scale up its early operations just one year after its founding.
Scaringe will still be involved with Mind Robotics, but the day-to-day aspects of the business, including product, engineering, and operations, will be handled by Field.
Mind Robotics, which has already amassed more than $1 billion in backing from Accel, Andreessen Horowitz, Eclipse, Kleiner Perkins, and the venture arms of Volkswagen and Salesforce, is building a full stack for industrial manufacturing. The purpose-built robots will run on foundation models with a goal of automating industrial and manufacturing tasks at scale. Rivian’s stake in Mind Robotics has been diluted since it took on additional backed; Rivian holds 32.1% ownership in Mind Robotics as of June 2026, per regulatory filings .
Unlike the humanoid robots being developed by Tesla and others, Scaringe says Mind Robotics won’t attempt to mimic all the biomechanics of a human . The startup is also using Rivian as “a live, high-volume manufacturing environment for model training and deployment,” with Rivian being Mind Robotics’ first customer.
Scaringe said on the Disrupt Stage Tuesday that he wanted someone like Field to help run Mind Robotics, and so he called him up to ask for a recommendation.
“Him and I then really began digging into how important it is that we really think deeply and very intentionally about how we develop robotics and deploy robotics into our society, into our economy, and we found such alignment in how we thought about this from the overall mission of the business, but even more important, we found really deep alignment just in how we both work and how we build teams,” he said.
Field left Ford in April after five years shaping the automaker’s electric vehicle and technology strategies. His departure was part of a wider reorganization of the automaker’s leadership. Prior to Ford, Field led Apple’s Project Titan, the electric, autonomous car project that was canceled in 2024 . He also served as senior vice president of engineering at Tesla, where he oversaw development of the Model 3 and got the sedan through “production hell.”
“Integrating AI and robotics is one of the most important — and difficult — engineering challenges of our time,” Field said in a statement. “Mind has assembled an exceptional team and has a unique advantage: the ability to deploy and learn inside a real, high-volume factory from day one. I’m thrilled to join RJ in building a team, culture, and technology that will redefine what we can make in America.”
Mind Robotics is the second company that Scaringe created outside of Rivian, following Also , a micromobility play that’s starting with high-end e-bikes. Like with Field and Mind Robotics, Scaringe is involved as chairman at Also but has tapped someone to run the day-to-day: Chris Yu, the former chief product officer of Specialized.
Mind Robotics and Also operate as standalone companies, but Rivian has minority stakes in both. The company reported owning about a third of each startup as of June 30, 2026 .
This article has been updated to clarify that Rivian backs Mind Robotics, which was originally created by Rivian founder and CEO RJ Scaringe.

title: Flox Intelligence is building AI to keep wildlife away from trains, airports, and roads
body:
When I was eight, I remember our train to Mumbai ground to a halt with a great noise. When we started moving again, a good eight hours later, someone pointed out a mangled tail, of all things, hanging from a branch close to the tracks.
The train, you see, had apparently hit a wild bison at full speed, and the impact damaged the engine so badly that it had to be towed away for repairs. For a long time, I thought such things only happened in places like rural India, but I learned a few years ago that wildlife and infrastructure do not mix anywhere on the planet.
The FAA estimates that wildlife strikes have cost U.S. civil aviation about $272 million a year on average between 1990 and 2025. In France, the rail operator SNCF says wandering animals affect more than 8,000 trains across the country each year and are among its five leading causes of delays. In Brittany, 120 trains hit animals in 2023 alone, disrupting 660 services and causing more than 15,000 minutes of delays.
Reading about all that damage, to both infrastructure and animals, inspired Sara Nozkova (pictured above on the left) to develop a wildlife-deterrent system that works differently from the sirens, lights, fences, falcons, and culling traditionally used to keep animals away from roads, train tracks, airports, and other infrastructure.
“I was convinced the answer was not a louder deterrent,” she told TechCrunch.
After spending 13 years working in transportation and autonomous vehicles, Nozkova had learned how quickly the systems we build to navigate roads and other controlled environments fail once nature enters the equation.
“We have taught machines to be brilliant, but only inside the environments we engineered for them,” she said. “Cities, factory lines, warehouses. Fixed geometry, known objects. Stepping outside into nature, I saw firsthand how the same machines quickly go blind. Because nature is complex and always alive.”
So instead she joined the AI lab at KTH Royal Institute of Technology in Stockholm and started working on a system that could change its deterrent responses based on what an animal nearby is doing, and even what kind of animal it is.
That work turned into Flox Intelligence , which spun out of KTH in 2020 and is one of the finalists at this year’s Startup Battlefield 200 pitch competition at TechCrunch Disrupt , taking place this year at Moscone West in San Francisco October 13-15.
Flox makes edge devices that process data on-site rather than in the cloud. Like autonomous vehicles, they use perception systems to sense their surroundings, but theirs are trained on wildlife behavior. A motion sensor wakes the device when it detects movement, triggering a camera that uses on-device models to identify nearby animals. The device then emits a species-appropriate sound to scare them away.
Nozkova says the system learns from experience, too, and varies its responses so animals don’t get habituated to repeated signals.
The company currently sells battery-operated devices that can be mounted on poles, trees, and other structures. It also offers a software platform that shows clients where the devices are deployed and what’s happening on the ground. The platform can also generate reports for regulatory compliance and for uses like biodiversity monitoring. The longer-term goal is to make the software portable enough to run on machines that work outside, including trains, cars, and drones.
Nozkova says about 150 Flox devices are live in North America, Europe, and Australia at airfields and airport perimeters, road and rail corridors (especially fence ends and crossings along wildlife corridors), national parks, agricultural land, urban areas, mining sites, and critical infrastructure such as electrical substations.
The company sells edge units up front, then charges an annual software and AI subscription after the first year. Flox also has OEM partnerships with companies that pay an annual fee to deploy its software on vehicles, like trains. Train manufacturer Alstom is one such partner.
The company expects to end 2026 with revenue of about $1.5 million, Nozkova said.
As unique as Flox’s product and approach are, the startup is not without competition. Robin Radar’s Scarecrow also uses species-specific distress calls to disperse birds and it records the activity, while iCHASE sells a system that detects birds with computer vision and targets them with a moving laser, adjusting its response as needed.
Nozkova says her moat is the breadth of the system and the data Flox has collected in the field, which she calls “ground truth on what actually makes a moose or a grizzly bear move safely.”
“Physical AI is walking out of the factory and into the messy, alive outdoors,” Nozkova says. “Every machine that operates outside — trains, trucks, drones, tractors, robots — will need to understand nature, and nature intelligence is the next layer of the perception stack. Almost nobody is building it.”
The company has raised about $5 million across pre-seed and seed rounds so far, with the seed round led by Unconventional Ventures and Tilia Impact Ventures. Co-investors across the rounds include GENIUS NY, Norrsken, Satgana, and angel investors, Nozkova said.
The company is now opening a $10 million Series A, which would mostly go toward growing from about 150 devices to several thousand deployed units and extending the underlying system beyond its current wildlife use cases.

title: Evidence of Western components in Russian Shahed drones presented at Warsaw Security Forum
body:
NAKO representative Yulia Behletsova spoke about this in a comment to Ukrinform.
According to her, the main goal of the exhibition is to clearly demonstrate to the international community that, despite the sanctions imposed, critically important Western-made microelectronics continue to find their way into the Russian military-industrial complex.
“We are displaying control units from ‘ Shahed ’ drones. Unfortunately, microelectronics from the U.S., Germany, Japan, and Taiwan—which are dual-use goods—are still ending up in Russian weapons. The flow of these components continues unabated, as Russia constantly finds new intermediaries to circumvent sanctions,” Behletsova noted.
The NAKO representative highlighted the methods the enemy uses to conceal the origin of the parts: on many microchips, the manufacturers’ markings are laser-erased directly at Russian production sites.
NAKO experts also note an alarming trend toward replacing Western components with Chinese equivalents. Although high-tech drone components currently still require high-quality Western electronics, China is gradually increasing its supply volumes by adapting its solutions for Russian weapons.
In addition to its exhibition display, NAKO served as a program partner for a panel discussion at the forum dedicated to strategies for combating sanctions evasion.
“Such forums are extremely effective because they allow us to convey the truth to influential representatives of other countries. When politicians who have already visited frontline cities like Kharkiv or Zaporizhzhia see the actual size of the ‘Shahed’ and the microchips removed from it, advocacy for sanctions becomes much more effective,” Behletsova concluded.
As is known, the work to identify components of Russian weapons is being carried out jointly with relevant Ukrainian institutions that study military trophies. The data collected serves as the basis for expanding sanctions lists and strengthening controls over the export of dual-use goods.
As reported by Ukrinform, Ukrainian military medic Kateryna Polishchuk, with the call sign “Ptashka,” became the first recipient of the Lord Ashcroft Award for Courage. The award ceremony took place in the Polish capital as part of the Warsaw Security Forum.

Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe’s startup Mind Robotics announced the appointment of Doug Field as president in a major coup for the CEO’s secretive robotics project.
Field was a VP of special projects at Apple, where he was the de facto head of the company’s ultimately unsuccessful Project Titan effort to make an autonomous electric car. He had a previous stint at Apple as VP of Mac hardware engineering, but he left the company in 2013 to become Tesla’s chief vehicle engineer, where he helped oversee the Model 3 sedan . He left Tesla in 2018 and rejoined Apple . In 2021, Field was hired by Ford to run the automaker’s electric vehicle and software division, a position he held until earlier this year .
Mind Robotics said Field will oversee its effort to build “universally capable robots” for the purpose of working in Rivian’s factories, as well as other applications. The startup was founded by Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe in 2025, and has since raised over $1 billion in financing . While the company has yet to show off any of its robots in public, the startup says its robots are being designed with “dexterity and physical reasoning” that’s required for industrial work.
“Doug is a remarkable leader with a track record of delivering new technologies in successful products, and I couldn’t be more excited to be building Mind with him,” Scaringe said in a statement. “He has an incredible ability to foster great teams that take on big, complex ideas and deliver products that reset expectations. That’s exactly what Mind needs as we deploy robots into real factories and beyond.”
Field joins Mind Robotics at a major turning point for the field of robotics, with rapid advances in physical AI colliding with major hurdles in hardware and software development. Several companies, like Tesla and Hyundai, are pursuing humanoid robots for factory and warehouse work — even as experts note that making a robot act like a human is easier than scaling the technology for practical work. Mind Robotics hasn’t confirmed whether it’s working on a humanoid design or something else entirely. The company has been on a hiring spree and currently has 32 open positions .
Scaringe, who serves as acting CEO and chair of Mind Robotics, has said he wants to keep the companies separate, rather than try to combine the work like Tesla. That said, the companies are certainly linked in several ways. Mind Robotics is using AI training data from Rivian, and the robots will be initially tested in Rivian’s factories. Rivian also owns equity in Mind Robotics and will be the first customer for its robots.
Field said he is excited for the challenge in running the new startup.
“Integrating AI and robotics is one of the most important—and difficult—engineering challenges of our time,” he said in a statement. “Mind has assembled an exceptional team and has a unique advantage: the ability to deploy and learn inside a real, high-volume factory from day one. I’m thrilled to join RJ in building a team, culture, and technology that will redefine what we can make in America.”
Correction October 13th: Mind Robotics is a partner of Rivian, but not a spinoff. A previous version of this story misstated the relationship between the companies.

title: DSS Rearraigns Samaila Kaigama Over Alleged Terrorism, Ransom Collection
body: The Department of State Services (DSS) has rearraigned Samaila Kaigama before the Federal High Court in Abuja over allegations of aiding Boko Haram and the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP), collecting ransom and providing financial support to terrorists. Following his rearraignment on Tuesday, Justice Salim Ibrahim ordered that Kaigama be remanded at the Kuje Correctional Centre in Abuja. The defendant is facing seven counts bordering on alleged terrorism, failure to disclose information about terrorist activities, receipt of ransom suspected to be intended to finance terrorism, cybercrime, incitement to public disorder and money laundering. According to the charges, Kaigama allegedly established unauthorised communication with members of Boko Haram and ISWAP and negotiated ransom payments in July 2026. The prosecution also accused him of withholding information about the activities of the terrorist groups that could have assisted security agencies in investigating and prosecuting suspects. In another count, the Federal Government alleged that Kaigama received ransom money from the family of a hostage despite having reasonable grounds to believe that the funds would be used to finance terrorism. He was also accused of soliciting and mobilising financial contributions from families of hostages in support of ISWAP members. The prosecution further alleged that Kaigama used WhatsApp, through a group identified as BOSYA, and Facebook to solicit ransom payments from victims’ families for onward transmission to terrorists. According to the charge, the alleged transactions resulted in a loss of ₦1.8 million to the hostage’s family. Kaigama was also accused of mobilising members of affected communities to protest against Senator Ali Ndume and the Borno State Government, an act the prosecution described as incitement to public disorder. The final count alleges that he knowingly retained ₦1.8 million paid into his account by the hostage’s family, in violation of the Money Laundering (Prevention and Prohibition) Act, 2022. The charges were brought under various provisions of the Terrorism (Prevention and Prohibition) Act, 2022, the Cybercrimes Act and the Criminal Code Act. The case was adjourned until November 13, 2026, for further proceedings. The post DSS Rearraigns Samaila Kaigama Over Alleged Terrorism, Ransom Collection appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Tinubu to Judiciary: Seal loopholes criminals exploit to escape justice
body: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA– PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu has asked the Judiciary to dismantle procedural loopholes and flawed prosecution tactics that allow offenders to escape justice, warning that no well-connected individual should be able to manipulate technicalities to evade the law. The President spoke on Tuesday in Abuja at the annual EFCC/NJI Capacity Building Workshop for Judges and Justices. He was represented by Vice President Kashim Shettima. Tinubu urged the judiciary to interrogate existing statutory frameworks in view of emerging financial crimes. “Probe prosecution strategies, dismantle outdated precedents, and seal procedural gaps that politically exposed persons and organised crime actors exploit to delay or frustrate trial,” he stated. He demanded an aggressive overhaul of the justice system to ensure that no well-connected individual can manipulate technicalities to evade the full, crushing weight of the law. The President, who was represented by the Vice President, Senator Kashim Shettima, warned that financial and economic crimes pose an existential threat to Nigeria, adding that corruption has no respect for status and spares no arm of government. He said framing the anti-corruption campaign as purely an executive agenda is a fundamental error because compromised public services equally affect the executive, legislature, judiciary, and ordinary citizens. “Corruption is a battle for the nation’s collective survival. We must no longer permit legal pyrotechnics and procedural pedantry to shelter criminality. The Bench is not merely a mechanical arbiter of rules, but an active guardian of moral order and social equity. “Law is, by design, an instrument of social engineering; it must invariably prioritise the public good over narrow, selfish interests shielded by technical manoeuvres. Our courts must embody the spirit, and not just the arid letter, of the law,” Tinubu said. He maintained that there will be no meaningful progress in uprooting graft “without an independent, progressive, and reform-minded Bench.” Digital-age crimes Tinubu commended the EFCC for convening the 8th edition of the Judges and Justices Workshop, themed “Investigation and Prosecution of Economic and Financial Crimes in a Digital Age.” He described the workshop as timely and necessary in fostering the institutional cohesion required to confront corruption’s changing architecture in Nigeria. “My Lords, we confront a rapidly shifting criminal landscape. Technology has amplified the audacity and reach of illicit actors, ushering in sophisticated crimes driven by destructive ingenuity. The rise of blockchain technology and artificial intelligence has introduced unprecedented layers of complexity to traditional illicit activities. “Because these modern crimes constantly mutate, law enforcement and judicial authorities must continuously build capacity to adapt and respond effectively,” he added. The President urged the judiciary to adapt to shifting dynamics of financial crime, stressing that realigning the nation’s investigative and prosecutorial strategies is critical to preventing institutional obsolescence. Tinubu said the country was already on the right trajectory, citing the EFCC’s recent momentum in tackling cryptocurrency fraud and recovering virtual assets. “The EFCC’s recent momentum in tackling cryptocurrency fraud and its commendable strides in recovering virtual assets are highly reassuring. The agency has recovered billions of naira in cryptocurrency investment-related fraud cases. “In 2025, the agency secured the forfeiture of $22,417.91 (Twenty-Two Thousand, Four Hundred and Seventeen Dollars, Ninety-One Cents) worth of Bitcoin; 1,001,301.87 USDT (One Million, One Thousand, Three Hundred and One USDT and Eighty-Seven Cents) in digital assets; and US$5.6 million linked to the CBEX scheme, while 192 foreigners arrested for cyber-terrorism and cryptocurrency fraud were successfully prosecuted and deported afterwards,” he said. He said the EFCC’s actions show an agency that is proactive, forward-looking and resolved not to be outpaced by technological innovation, while the judiciary must complement law enforcement by rapidly upscaling its capacity. Tinubu acknowledged the Chief Justice of Nigeria’s efforts in reforming the judiciary and pledged the full support of the executive to ensure the judiciary is adequately equipped for justice delivery in the digital age. Earlier, Chief Justice of Nigeria, Hon. Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, said the 8th edition of the event reflects the commitment of the NJI and EFCC to sustain efforts aimed at addressing challenges confronting stakeholders in Nigeria’s justice system. She said the trend in technology has impacted how digital evidence is obtained and recorded, noting that effective administration of criminal justice in the digital era requires firm and disciplined case management, which capacity-building programmes such as the EFCC and NJI collaboration aim to strengthen. The CJN noted that sustained judicial education and capacity development in the justice sector was yielding positive results, with improved conduct of judicial officers, especially judges, in case management and the dispensation of justice in recent years. Senate Committee Chairman on Anti-Corruption and Financial Crimes, Sen. Emmanuel Udende, said the timing of the workshop was apt given the increasing sophistication of financial crimes and corruption, particularly cases involving politically exposed persons, which directly impact timely case management and the dispensation of justice. He assured stakeholders that the National Assembly remained committed to supporting the enhancement of the war against corruption and financial crimes in Nigeria through proactive legislation. Minister of Justice and Attorney General of the Federation, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, represented by the Director of Public Prosecution, Mr Rotimi Oyedepo, urged synergy among stakeholders in addressing emerging challenges in Nigeria’s fight against corruption, stating that one arm of government alone could not effectively address the problem. He urged judicial officers, especially judges and lawyers, to leverage opportunities provided during the workshop to enhance their capacities to make investigation more thorough and prosecution more diligent. In his welcome address, Administrator of the National Judicial Institute, Justice Babatunde Adejumo, said the collaboration between the EFCC and the NJI in enhancing the capacity of judicial officers has become an integral part of government’s efforts to frontally tackle the dynamics and scale of financial crimes in the digital age. He said the presence of the Vice President at the event was a practical demonstration of the commitment of the Tinubu administration to boost Nigeria’s war against corruption. Executive Chairman of the EFCC, Mr Ola Olukoyede, said the event was a national imperative that has become an important component of the annual programme of both the EFCC and the NJI. He said the commission under his leadership was reform-minded and has recorded unprecedented convictions as well as financial recoveries over the past three years, assuring transparent and judicious handling of recovered money and property. Olukoyede also regretted the impact of advanced technology on financial crimes and other forms of corruption, noting that digital innovation was fast outpacing legal instruments and provisions for prosecution. The post Tinubu to Judiciary: Seal loopholes criminals exploit to escape justice appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Mahama says Ghana is safer today as he commissions 85-bed ward at Police Hospital
body: President John Dramani Mahama has said Ghana is safer today than it was in the past, attributing the improvement to the efforts of the Ghana Police Service in maintaining peace and security across the country. The President made the remarks during the commissioning of an 85-bed ward at the Ghana Police Hospital in Accra, named after Mr Christian Tetteh Yohuno, the Inspector-General of Police (IGP). The commissioning of the three-storey facility formed part of activities marking the Golden Jubilee celebration of the Police Hospital. The ward is equipped with modern healthcare facilities. President Mahama commended Mr Yohuno for his leadership and dedication to ensuring peace and security nationwide. “Our country is safer today than it was before,” the President said. The President cited the testimony of a bus driver, who noted that commercial vehicles can now travel at any hour of the night without fear of highway robbery. “He (the driver) says today, any time the bus is full, even at 2:00 am, they take off because the roads are safer.” He said the country had also witnessed a reduction in unresolved murder cases and praised the Criminal Investigations Department (CID) of the Ghana Police Service for its efforts in crime detection and investigations. President Mahama further commended the Police Intelligence Directorate and the Police Cyber Unit for their contributions to national security. “Indeed, this Police Administration is doing a yeoman’s job, and as Commander-in-Chief and President of the Republic, I want to express the gratitude of our nation to all of you, and urge you to keep up the good work,” he said. The President noted that Ghana continued to be recognised as one of the safest countries in West Africa, making it an attractive destination for visitors and investors. “It’s no wonder everybody wants to visit Ghana because they say it’s the safest country in the whole of West Africa, and I can assure you that we’ll continue to provide you with the logistics that you need to continue to do your job.” The Minister for the Interior, Muntaka Mohammed-Mubarak, said President Mahama’s commitment to improving healthcare infrastructure and enhancing the welfare of security personnel continued to leave a lasting impact on the nation. He said the new facility was a testament to the President’s determination to build a stronger and more inclusive Ghana. The Inspector-General of Police expressed gratitude to President Mahama for his continuous support for the Police Service and the welfare of its personnel. He assured the President that the Police Administration would continue to implement initiatives aimed at improving the health, welfare and operational effectiveness of officers.

title: Russian banks fear massive fines after unprecedented surge in court bailiff inquiries
body: Russian banks received millions of requests for information about debtors from the Federal Bailiff Service (FSSP) over three days between September 18 and 21, an unprecedented volume, the National Financial Market Council reported. One regional bank received 12.8 million requests on September 19 alone — as many as it normally receives in a month. The council’s head, Andrey Yemelin, said the volume of FSSP requests over those three days was at least 10 to 12 times the usual level, and up to 30 times at some banks. More than 90% of the requests concerned people who were not customers of the banks that received them, said Yelena Samokhina, director of the banking development department at the Association of Banks of Russia. Experts believe technical errors may account for the volume of requests, which the FSSP generates automatically. “The service has previously acknowledged that it resends requests if a bank hasn’t confirmed receipt. If those confirmations were lost, the automated system could have sent banks the entire backlog, along with duplicate requests,” said Mikhail Bryukhanov, chairman of Pervouralskbank’s board of directors. Banks are legally required to provide the requested information within three days or face fines of 50,000 to 100,000 rubles for each request. Given the volume, Yemelin said “the fines could add up to amounts that pose a real threat to the financial stability of some banks.” The council asked the Central Bank to look into the situation. The Central Bank said it had “received the inquiry and will review it according to established procedures.” From Meduza’s archives A seven-point crackdown To suppress opposition protests, Moscow has unleashed police, repo men, military recruiters, investigators, courts, prosecutors, and university administrators The evictors For the past five years, loan sharks have forced more than 500 Muscovites from their homes. title: TRENDING: Natasha introduces self at Edo Assembly without 2Baba’s surname (VIDEO)
body:
A video of Edo lawmaker Natasha Osawaru introducing herself during legislative proceedings without using her partner 2Baba’s surname has renewed speculation about their relationship.
In the video posted on her Instagram page on Tuesday, the minority leader identified herself as “Honourable Natasha Irobosa Osawaru,” representing Egor Constituency.
The nameplate before her also bore the Osawaru surname without “Idibia”.
Her use of Osawaru does not, by itself, establish any change in the couple’s relationship. However, it attracted attention weeks after she was absent from 2Baba’s 51st birthday celebration and album listening party in Lagos.
During the proceedings, Natasha supported a bill seeking to strengthen the state’s response to emergencies, describing the proposed legislation as timely.
She cited Section 14(2)(b) of the 1999 Nigerian Constitution, which provides that the security and welfare of the people shall be the primary purpose of government.
“Mr Speaker, my name is Honourable Natasha Irobosa Osawaru, member representing the very great people of Egor Constituency and, by God’s grace, the minority leader of this House,” she said.
“Mr Speaker, I rise this morning to support the second reading of this bill because it is timely.
“The majority leader highlighted that Section 14, subsection 2(b), of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, clearly states that the security and welfare of the people shall be the primary purpose of government.”
The lawmaker raised concerns about Edo State’s exposure to flooding, erosion, fire outbreaks, building collapses and communal crises, describing them as growing threats requiring a coordinated response.
“Every rainy season, our people from Auchi, Ekpoma, Benin City and other parts of the state suffer from flooding, erosion, fire outbreaks, building collapse and communal crises,” Natasha said.
“Mr Speaker, as we speak, we have no strong, legally backed state agency that can respond proactively. Hence, this bill is timely.”
The video also attracted comments about Natasha’s appearance. The lawmaker wore a coloured outfit, departing from the black abayas and tunics that have become a recognisable feature of her recent public appearances.
It appeared to be one of the few recent occasions on which she had been seen publicly in a non-black outfit.
A post shared by Honourable Natasha IDIBIA (@honorableosawaru)
Some social-media users also remarked that she appeared fuller in the video.
The change in her usual style, alongside her fuller appearance, added to the reactions generated by the video.
The video and photographs posted by the lawmaker renewed public interest in her relationship with music veteran Innocent “2Baba” Idibia.
PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that the relationship came under intense scrutiny in August after Natasha made an unexpected appearance at an Abuja nightclub where 2Baba was scheduled to perform.
A video circulated online appeared to show the couple during a heated exchange. However, the footage did not capture what happened before the encounter or establish what triggered the disagreement.
An eyewitness claimed that Natasha arrived at the venue with a group of men and attempted to speak with the singer.
According to the witness, she approached 2Baba’s vehicle shortly after he arrived and requested a conversation with him, leading to a commotion outside the nightclub.
Other eyewitnesses claimed that Natasha had been unable to reach the singer before appearing at the venue. Neither Natasha nor 2Baba publicly provided a detailed account of the incident.
Speculation about a possible rift intensified after Natasha was not seen at 2Baba’s 51st birthday party in Victoria Island, Lagos.
The celebration also served as a listening party for the singer’s forthcoming album, Oldest Young Man.
It was attended by 2Baba’s children, his mother, Rose Idibia, and several entertainment personalities, including Kenny Ogungbe, Dayo “D1” Adeneye, Wande Coal, African China, Ayo Makun, Faze and Tony Tetuila.
The mothers of the singer’s children Annie Macaulay, Sunmbo Adeoye and Pero Adeniyi were also not seen at the event.
Natasha’s absence added to questions about the state of her relationship with the singer. However, as of press time, neither she nor 2Baba had publicly confirmed a separation or explained why she missed the celebration.

title: Olympic Qualifiers: Super Falcons thrash Comoros 5-0, set f Morocco showdown
body:
Nigeria’s Super Falcons thrashed Comoros 5-0 in the second leg of their second-round qualifier for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games at the Remo Stars Stadium in Ikenne, Ogun State, on Tuesday.
The result gave Nigeria a 7-0 aggregate lead following their 2-0 victory in Friday’s first leg, putting the 10-time African champions in a commanding position to advance to the next round, where Morocco await.
Toni Payne scored twice, while Uchenna Kanu also found the net twice and Christy Ucheibe converted a penalty as Nigeria turned their first-leg advantage into a comprehensive victory.
Interim head coach Augustine Eguavoen retained the starting XI that began Friday’s encounter, with captain Rasheedat Ajibade, goalkeeper Chiamaka Nnadozie, Payne and Kanu among those named.
Nigeria dominated the opening exchanges but suffered an early setback when Ajibade was forced off following a collision with a Comoros defender in the 23rd minute. Folashade Ijamilusi replaced the captain.
The Super Falcons eventually broke through in the 41st minute when Kanu capitalised on a goalkeeping error before setting up Payne, who finished to give Nigeria a 1-0 lead on the night and extend their aggregate advantage to 3-0.
Nigeria carried that advantage into half-time before increasing the pressure after the restart.
Blessing Okpe replaced Gift Monday at the beginning of the second half, and the substitute quickly made an impact as the Super Falcons added four more goals.
Kanu doubled Nigeria’s lead in the 58th minute, heading home a cross from Ijamilusi. Although the forward thought she had scored again three minutes later, the assistant referee ruled the effort offside.
Toni Payne scored twice [Credit: NG Super Falcons] Payne extended Nigeria’s lead on the night in the 63rd minute after Okpe dribbled past two Comoros defenders before squaring the ball for the midfielder to finish.
Three minutes later, Ijamilusi delivered another cross that Kanu headed into the net to make it 4-0, completing her brace.
Okpe then won a penalty after being fouled inside the box, allowing Ucheibe to convert from the spot in the 71st minute and take Nigeria’s lead to five goals.
Eguavoen made further changes in the closing stages, bringing on Suliat Abideen and Shakirat Moshood for Jennifer Echegini and Kanu in the 81st minute. Folat Fatimah subsequently replaced Payne in the 87th minute.
Having conquered Comoros in the second round, the Super Falcons now have a tougher task in their hands as they will be battling Morocco’s Lionesses in the third round.
The African qualifying series features five rounds, with only two teams earning places in the women’s football tournament at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games.
Nigeria returned to the Olympics at Paris 2024 after a 16-year absence and are seeking consecutive appearances as they continue their qualifying campaign.

title: Chentsov: Second, third negotiation clusters to help create conditions for participation in EU single market
body:
Ukraine's Deputy Prime Minister for European and Euro-Atlantic Integration Vsevolod Chentsov says the second and third negotiation clusters regarding Ukraine's accession to the European Union will serve to create the conditions for participation in the single market.
He made these remarks on Tuesday in Luxembourg ahead of the start of the fourth intergovernmental conference, at which the second and third negotiation clusters on Ukraine's EU membership are expected to be officially opened.
"Today is a very important day. We are opening two clusters – the second and third – which concern the single market, competitiveness, and inclusive growth. This is about creating the conditions for participation in the single market. It is also very important that just a few days ago, the European Commission put forward a significant proposal regarding the gradual integration of candidate countries, including Ukraine, into the single market," Chentsov said.
The Deputy Prime Minister explained that this involves deepening "our economic and trade ties right now, without waiting for EU accession." "It is also important to maintain momentum, as we have been working hard to open all clusters by the end of the year, and we have a good chance of doing so. In this context, we are very grateful to everyone who has supported us along this path… This is important to us because Ukraine is not only defending itself against Russian aggression but is also carrying out complex reforms – and in this sense, we are unique. So we eagerly await these important and decisive steps today and continue on our path," he said.

title: Senate bill to decriminalise attempted suicide passes second reading
body: The Senate on Tuesday passed for second reading a bill seeking to decriminalise attempted suicide and strengthen support for survivors during plenary. The bill, sponsored by Sen. Asuquo Ekpenyong (Cross River South) seeks to establish a legal and institutional framework for suicide prevention, treatment and support for people experiencing psychological distress. Leading the debate for the bill, Ekpenyong said Nigeria’s existing laws presented conflicting approaches to attempted suicide, with mental health legislation recognising it as a psychiatric emergency while criminal laws prescribed punishment. “At the heart of this bill is a simple question: when a Nigerian survives a suicide attempt, should the first response of the state be prosecution or protection?” he asked. According to him, the National Mental Health Act recognises attempted suicide as a psychiatric emergency requiring immediate intervention, while Sections 327 of the Criminal Code and 231 of the Penal Code exposes survivors to criminal punishment. Ekpenyong said the bill would resolve the contradiction by prioritising prevention, treatment and the preservation of life. He argued that criminalisation could discourage people experiencing suicidal thoughts from seeking help and cause families to conceal suicide attempts for fear of stigma or prosecution. According to him, such practices can delay intervention and undermine reliable data collection, weakening national suicide-prevention efforts. The senator said decriminalising attempted suicide would neither legalise nor encourage suicide, adding that the bill focused on protecting survivors and ensuring access to timely medical care. He said the proposed legislation would establish coordinated prevention services, including crisis helplines, referral pathways and follow-up support for people who survived suicide attempts. Ekpenyong added that the bill would strengthen public education and train healthcare workers, law-enforcement personnel, teachers and emergency responders to recognise warning signs and connect at-risk individuals with appropriate services. He said families affected by suicide or attempted suicide would also require access to psychosocial support, while improved data collection and research would help the government develop effective prevention policies. The senator said the bill would provide an institutional and funding framework for implementing suicide-prevention services, stressing that decriminalisation without accessible care would be incomplete. He added that the committee stage would allow lawmakers to harmonise the proposed legislation with the Criminal Code, Penal Code, National Mental Health Act and relevant state laws. Other lawmakers who took turns to support the bill argued that attempted suicide should be treated primarily as a mental health concern requiring professional care rather than criminal punishment. They said that people experiencing severe emotional distress needed medical attention and support, adding that detention or imprisonment would not address the underlying causes of their conditions. They stressed that suicide prevention required coordinated action involving healthcare professionals, educational institutions, families, law enforcement agencies and relevant government institutions. The proposed legislation, according to them, will provide an opportunity for public consultation and professional contributions before the Senate takes further legislative action. Senate President Godswill Akpabio subsequently put the bill to a voice vote, and it was passed for second reading, and thereafter referred the bill to the committee on health and Judiciary, human rights and legal matters The post Senate bill to decriminalise attempted suicide passes second reading appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: DOW Certifies Production Capacity for Second DDG at Maine’s Bath Iron Works
body: Following a comprehensive, multi-phase due diligence review, the Department of War has determined that significant operational and managerial improvements at General Dynamics Bath Iron Works (BIW) have established the capacity and stability necessary to support the potential construction of a second guided-missile destroyer (DDG). The Department’s thorough review evaluated production throughput, schedule adherence, quality assurance benchmarks, supply chain resilience, and workforce optimization at the Bath, Maine shipyard. Based on verifiable performance enhancements and leadership initiatives implemented across the facility, the Department concluded that building an additional Arleigh Burke-class (DDG 51) destroyer at BIW is feasible and strategically advantageous for the Navy’s fleet, should Congress secure the necessary funding. “Our national security requires an industrial base that can respond to demands for increased speed and volume,” said Deputy Secretary of War Steve Feinberg. “After a rigorous review, Bath Iron Works has proven it has the capacity and stability to support construction of a second destroyer. While the operational improvements we have seen at BIW are a significant step in the right direction, the shipyard must continue this momentum to fully resolve legacy production challenges – sustained performance is essential. The Department will continue to partner with contractors who prioritize execution, accountability, and the rapid modernization of our forces.” “Today’s decision by the Department of War validates the capacity of Bath Iron Works (BIW) and the hard work of its highly skilled 6,800 employees who build the best ships in the world. I have advocated for a second destroyer to be included in this year’s budget, and I worked with the Administration during its careful review and repeated visits to BIW to verify the ability of the shipyard to construct another ship while continuing to complete its current workload,” said Senator Susan Collins (R-Maine). “This certification will help keep our Navy strong and support BIW as a steady source of good-paying Maine jobs. I will continue to work to ensure our shipbuilders have the resources to meet the Navy’s needs at a time when China is relentlessly expanding its fleet.” The decision to certify the shipyard’s capacity for a second destroyer aligns with the Administration’s broader, aggressive campaign to revitalize the U.S. Maritime Industrial Base and outmatch global pacing threats. To counter aggressive ship-construction timelines by foreign adversaries, the Department is prioritizing long-term stability and capacity-building across the domestic shipbuilding supply chain. Through targeted modernization investments, workforce development initiatives, and streamlined procurement processes, the Administration is actively expanding America’s sovereign shipbuilding capacity. Ensuring that key shipyards like Bath Iron Works can reliably scale and sustain high-rate production is a cornerstone of the Department’s strategy to maintain global maritime dominance and protect American interests worldwide. From Pentagon News, Oct. 12, 2026 The post DOW Certifies Production Capacity for Second DDG at Maine’s Bath Iron Works appeared first on Seapower Magazine .

title: 2027: Fubara playing active role in Rainbow Coalition – Wike
body: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Mr Nyesom Wike, says Gov. Siminalayi Fubara of Rivers remains an integral and active part of the ruling political team. Wike stated this during a media chat in Abuja on Tuesday, dismissing insinuations that Gov. Siminalayi Fubara of Rivers has been sidelined in the political architecture of the state. According to him, the governor remains an integral and active part of the ruling political team. Addressing questions about Fubara’s current status and quiet disposition, Wike maintained that the governor’s perceived silence does not equate to exclusion or unhappiness. “Fubara has not been pushed aside. If you know him, he’s been a very quiet person. “He is fully a member of the Rainbow Coalition and fully playing his part in efforts to ensure the re-election of President Bola Tinubu in 2027,” he said. The minister revealed that the governor recently hosted a crucial, high-level strategic meeting at his residence attended by key stakeholders, underscoring his active involvement in the state’s political direction. “Do you know what it takes to hold a meeting in his house? For everybody to be there? “What matters most to Gov. Fubara is ensuring that his political family retains its influence and power moving forward,” he said. Speaking as the campaign coordinator for Rivers, Wike said lists of campaign committee members have been duly submitted, with Fubara slated to serve as one of the primary leaders. Reflecting on past political tensions in the state, Wike blamed external actors and ungrateful elements, including certain opposition governors for trying to drive a wedge between him and Fubara for political mileage. He, however, noted that despite external attempts to exploit the situation, mutual forgiveness and reconciliation have prevailed. Wike also touched on speculation regarding Fubara’s future political trajectory after his tenure, including potential federal appointments. While noting that he does not possess the constitutional prerogative to nominate ministers, Wike maintained an optimistic outlook on the governor’s standing. Wike reiterated that speculations regarding friction between him and the governor are unfounded, stressing that both leaders were actively working together to safeguard the state’s political stability. He explained that the Rainbow Coalition in River was engineered to unite different political factions across party lines—including members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and other groups. He added that the goal was to champion a unified agenda under Tinubu and avoid destructive litigations that previously plagued the state. When pressed on how offices and candidacies were being shared among coalition members, Wike defended the strategy as a display of high-level political ingenuity that respects the peculiarities of different areas while maintaining team solidarity. “When you talk about politicians that agree to form an umbrella, the umbrella does not mean that all the candidates will be one party. “We look at the peculiarities of areas, and say, listen, all of us are together and all of us are supporters of Mr President,” he said. title: Russian Drone Strike on Rivne University Injures 30, Forces Students to Remote Learning
body:
A Russian drone struck a building belonging to Rivne State Humanitarian University in central Rivne on Tuesday, Oct. 13, injuring 30 people and destroying the premises of its music faculty, Ukrainian authorities said.
Oleksandr Koval, head of the Rivne Regional Military Administration, first reported the attack on Tuesday morning, saying a drone had hit the city center, causing extensive damage and injuring people. Before the strike, at 9:35 a.m. local time, Ukraine’s Air Force had warned of a jet-powered drone flying over Rivne region toward neighboring Volyn region.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“Russia continues to deliberately attack education institutions. This is deliberate terror against the civilian population and yet another attempt to disrupt the educational process in the country,” Minister of Education and Science Andrii Butenko wrote in a statement on Facebook.
The number of injured rose steadily following the attack.
By 3:24 p.m., the National Police said 25 people had been hurt, with three more undergoing medical checks. Two people in serious condition were in surgery at the time.
According to the latest assessment by Ukraine’s State Emergency Service (SES), the number of injured is now at 30, after rescuers finished clearing rubble and collapsed structures left by the falling debris of the Russian drone.
A total of 64 rescuers and 13 emergency vehicles were deployed to the scene, SES reported. Police and officers of the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) also worked at the site.
According to the university, all students were in shelters during the attacks. Several members of its administrative staff were among the injured, Butenko said.
The strike set the building of Rivne State Humanitarian University ablaze, nearly burning out the premises of its Faculty of Musical Arts, Butenko said, citing the university’s management.
Firefighters successfully put out the blaze.
However, the building can no longer be used for in-person classes and will have to be rebuilt, the minister said. In the neighboring academic buildings, windows were blown out.
Meanwhile, the full extent of the damage is still being assessed.
The university is considering moving all classes online through the end of the week. Further arrangements will depend on which premises remain available and safe.
“Our priority is the safety of people and ensuring conditions for continued learning. Students and university staff must receive the necessary support,” Butenko said.

title: Finland calls for EU tourist visa ban on Russians until Moscow ends war against Ukraine as bloc weighs tougher restrictions
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Finland’s Foreign Minister Elina Valtonen has called on the European Union to stop issuing tourist visas to Russian citizens until Russia ends its war against Ukraine, urging the bloc to adopt a unified policy. Her call comes as the EU discusses broader restrictions on Russian diplomats, tourists, and former combatants. Russia has intensified its hybrid campaign across Europe in recent months, with suspected sabotage, arson attacks, and other covert operations targeting infrastructure and undermining security. European officials have increasingly called for a coordinated response, arguing that tighter controls on Russian diplomats, travel, and former combatants could help reduce security risks and limit opportunities for Russian intelligence operations. In a statement published on 12 October, Finland’s Ministry for Foreign Affairs said Valtonen was calling on the European Commission to introduce stricter guidelines for processing Russian visa applications and propose changes to EU legislation needed to implement a complete ban on tourist visas. “As long as Russia continues its invasion, Russian citizens should not be issued tourist visas,” Valtonen said. “It is not right that Russians can travel to Europe to enjoy the way of life and freedoms here while their country bombs the homes of Ukrainians.” Finland banned visas for non-essential travel by Russian citizens in 2022. Valtonen said the same restriction should now be adopted at the EU level. The Finnish minister has invited other EU member states to join a joint letter to the European Commission. Beyond a complete ban on tourist visas, the letter proposes barring Schengen visas for people in Russian President Vladimir Putin’s inner circle, restricting visas for Russian athletes, and enforcing an EU-agreed visa ban on former Russian combatants. We must stop issuing tourist visas for Russian citizens across the EU. I have invited other EU Member States to join a letter addressed to the European Commission. I am calling for a complete EU ban on Russian tourist visas for as long as Russia continues its war of aggression.… — Elina Valtonen (@elinavaltonen) October 12, 2026 EU considers wider restrictions on Russians The proposal comes as EU foreign ministers discuss additional measures to counter Russian hybrid threats. EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said after a meeting of the bloc’s foreign ministers in Luxembourg on 12 October that the EU was considering reducing the number of tourist visas issued to Russians, restricting Russian diplomats’ movements within the bloc, and accelerating entry bans for former Russian combatants, Radio Svoboda reported . Kallas said the EU needed a comprehensive response to Russian hybrid threats, including new sanctions, stronger enforcement of existing restrictions, action against Russia’s shadow fleet, accountability for hybrid attacks, and improved intelligence sharing. One proposal would require Russian diplomats to obtain advance permission before traveling to other EU member states, rather than simply notifying authorities of their trips. Polish Deputy Foreign Minister Marcin Bosacki said tighter rules were necessary because some acts of sabotage and subversion were coordinated, at least in part, through Russian diplomatic missions. Kallas said the European External Action Service and European Commission would also prepare proposals for further isolating Russia in international sport. She argued that sport and culture should not be used to whitewash Russian aggression. EU divided over tourist visa restrictions Several EU countries have pushed to reduce tourist visas for Russian citizens. In June, a group of member states jointly called for fewer visas, according to DW. The Finnish ministry said Schengen countries issued nearly 500,000 tourist visas to Russian citizens in 2025. Estonia has also proposed measures to bar former Russian military personnel who fought against Ukraine from entering the EU. Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna warned that large numbers of Russian veterans could try to enter Europe after the war, potentially with support from Russian intelligence services. The European Commission has supported including a mechanism targeting former combatants in the EU’s 21st sanctions package , and officials are working on how to implement it. However, EU countries remain divided over the scope of visa restrictions. France and Italy have previously opposed a blanket isolation of Russian tourists. Member states are also debating how to prevent former Russian combatants from entering the bloc without restricting entry for military deserters or opponents of the war. No timeline has been announced for the proposed restrictions on Russian tourists and diplomats. The measures remain under discussion and have not been adopted as a bloc-wide ban. title: SBI on MiG-29 crash: Preliminary findings indicate abnormal activation of guided missile; black box being examined
body:
One of the possible causes of the MiG-29 fighter jet crash in Odesa region in August of this year is the accidental firing of a guided missile: a series of expert examinations has been ordered, including an analysis of the fighter jet's flight data recorder, according to the State Bureau of Investigations (SBI).
"The Ukrainian Air Force Command conducted an internal investigation. One of the possible causes of the aviation incident cited in the investigation is the unintended firing of a guided missile," the SBI said in a Tuesday post on its website.
At the same time, as noted in the statement, this theory requires confirmation through criminal proceedings and verification by relevant expert analyses.
"Currently, the State Bureau of Investigations has ordered a series of relevant expert examinations. In particular, specialists are examining the fighter jet's flight data recorder – the "black box,"" the agency said.
Investigators are awaiting the results of the expert analyses, which should help establish the causes and all the circumstances of the plane crash.
"Final conclusions regarding the causes of the fighter jet's crash will be drawn only after receiving and evaluating the results of all ordered expert examinations as part of the pre-trial investigation," the SBI said.
On August 10, 2026, a MiG-29 fighter jet of the Armed Forces of Ukraine was carrying out a combat mission to destroy enemy drones in Berezivsky district of Odesa region.
During the mission, an emergency situation arose; the aircraft caught fire, and the pilot lost control. The pilot managed to eject. His life is not in danger.
In connection with the plane crash, the SBI has opened a criminal case under Part 2 of Article 416 of the Criminal Code of Ukraine – violation of flight rules or rules for preparing for flights, as well as rules for the operation of aircraft, resulting in a crash.
Odesa Specialized Prosecutor's Office for Defense Affairs of the Southern Region is overseeing the proceedings.

title: The Truck Did Not Come: What Uncollected Garbage Does to Your Health
body: Anyone who lives in Lagos knows the sound of the garbage collection truck. When it fails to come on the expected day, the whole street feels it within a few days. Bins fill, then overflow. Bags pile up beside them. In no time, the heap smells, attracts a swarm of flies and invites a few stray dogs. Nobody planned it; it is simply what happens when waste waits longer than it should. Timing is the part of waste management we rarely discuss, yet it matters most for health. Garbage is not dangerous the moment it is thrown away. It becomes dangerous when it remains there for long. In tropical heat, food waste starts to rot within a day or two. Flies soon lay eggs in it. Rats are not far behind. Collection on schedule breaks that chain. Collection that comes late or does not come at all gives disease a head start. This situation is a global lesson. The United Nations Environment Programme published its Global Waste Management Outlook in 2024. It estimates that the world produced 2.3 billion tonnes of municipal solid waste in 2023. That figure could reach 3.8 billion tonnes by 2050. The same report found that about 2.7 billion people have no waste collection at all. In richer cities, the truck arrives on a fixed day, and people plan their week around it. Good waste management is boring because it is dependable. In poorer places, the gap between one collection and the next is where open dumping and burning begin. People cannot keep garbage in the house forever. Africa feels this pressure severely. Its cities are growing faster than the services meant to keep them clean. The UNEP report places Sub-Saharan Africa among the regions with the lowest collection rates. Where trucks cannot reach narrow lanes or crowded settlements, households find their own answers. They bury, burn or tip refuse into the nearest drain. None of these choices is healthy. Now, Lagos is the clearest example on the continent of Africa. In July 2026, the managing director of the Lagos Waste Management Authority, known as LAWMA, said the state produces between 13,000 and 15,000 tonnes of waste every day. He put the population at about 22 million. Private operators collect from homes and businesses. The waste then goes to disposal sites such as Olusosun in Ojota, which receives about 10,000 tonnes daily. LAWMA says Olusosun and Solous 3 have reached the end of their operational lives. It says Lagos needs about 2,000 compactor trucks to cope. It also says heavy rain has damaged access roads at Olusosun and slowed collection. Residents complain about paying for a service they barely see. The refuse waits, and the street pays. So what does late collection do to health? Bags split open, and food scraps spill across the ground. Flies move between the heap and the open pot of soup at the corner stall. Typhoid and diarrhoeal diseases travel on those wings. Nigeria had a severe cholera outbreak in 2021. The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control recorded more than 111,000 suspected cases and over 3,600 deaths. Cholera has several causes. Contaminated water and poor sanitation are at its core. Uncollected waste adds to both. Next, consider the rain. A delayed collection in the rainy season is not the same as a delayed collection in January. Loose plastic and polythene wash into drains within hours. Blocked drains hold standing water, and standing water breeds mosquitoes. In recent reports, the World Health Organization has put Nigeria at about 26% of the world’s malaria cases and about 31% of its deaths. Bed nets and treatment matter. So do clear drains. Flooding follows blocked channels. Floodwater in a crowded city carries sewage, sharp objects and bacteria into homes and shops. Rats arrive soon after. They love heaps that are not cleared on time. Lassa fever and leptospirosis are both linked to rodents. Then comes fire. When garbage has waited too long and the smell becomes unbearable, many people set it alight. Burning mixed waste, especially plastic, releases fine particles and harmful chemicals into the air. A child with asthma will feel it first. An older neighbour with a weak chest will feel it next. The fire solves the problem of smell for an hour. The lungs handle the rest. Now, it is fair to ask why collection runs late and expect answers. The government must fund the system properly. Contractors must be paid on time. Trucks must be maintained, and access roads must be protected. More transfer stations must be built so that trucks spend less time queuing at the dump. Residents are right to demand reliability from a service they pay for. However, waiting for perfect collection is a poor health strategy. Delay is a reality in our cities for now. What we do during the delay decides whether it becomes a hazard. This is where personal responsibility comes in. A household that stores waste properly can survive a missed collection without harm. A household that does not will create a problem within two days. Start with the bin itself. Use one with a tight lid. Keep it off the ground, if you can, and away from the kitchen door. Tie bags firmly before putting them out. Separate wet waste from dry waste, since food scraps cause most of the smell and attract most of the pests. Set aside bottles, cans and cardboard, which a collector will buy. If collection is late, keep the garbage in a covered container inside your compound. Do not dump it at the roadside, where animals will tear it open and rain will scatter it. Never use the drain as a shortcut. Not at night, and not when the truck is three days late. That bag will return to your street and probably to your house with the next downpour. Do not burn refuse. If you pay a collector, pay promptly and keep records. Then you can complain with proof when service fails. In Lagos, the Lagos Waste Management Authority (LAWMA) says residents should contact the authority directly if their operator fails to collect. The response tends to come faster when a whole street or estate raises an alarm. Agree with your neighbours on a shared system such as a common bin point that is cleaned daily. Wash your hands after handling refuse. Keep children away from heaps. Clear your own gutter on sanitation day. Train the young ones in your house on these habits. Lagos will not fix its waste system overnight, and neither will any other Nigerian city. The trucks may run late again this week. What matters is what happens between one collection and the next one. How we manage that stretch of time is a health decision. Ojenagbon, a health communication expert and certified management trainer, lives in Lagos.

title: STPT: ‘Sudan’s warring parties bypass sanctions through business networks’
body: A new report by the Sudan Transparency and Policy Tracker urges international governments to target the commercial networks and overseas partners sustaining the war. Sudan’s warring parties continue to circumvent international sanctions through overseas business networks, associated companies and alternative arms suppliers, according to a new report by the Sudan Transparency and Policy Tracker (STPT) . The report, Bypassing Sanctions, Sustaining the War Economy , published in October 2026, examines sanctions imposed since the war began in April 2023. It finds that restrictions have disrupted some financial and procurement channels but have failed to dismantle the wider networks financing the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF). The assessment identifies gaps in sanctions targeting SAF-linked companies, including the military-owned Zadna International Company for Investment, which it says has shifted much of its business towards Egypt and Gulf states and positioned itself to benefit from post-war reconstruction. The report also traces how the RSF-linked Al Junaid conglomerate generates revenue through gold trading networks, including routes that move gold from Sudan through South Sudan to the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Meanwhile, the report documents efforts by the SAF to secure alternative weapons suppliers, including Pakistan, and to develop domestic arms production using imported materials that can be harder to track. However, the authors caution that evidence of alternative procurement routes does not, by itself, prove that sanctions caused these shifts. The STPT argues that targeting individual companies is insufficient when their subsidiaries, joint ventures and commercial partners remain outside sanctions regimes. It urges governments to coordinate designations, strengthen enforcement and engage regional partners, particularly Egypt and Gulf states, to disrupt the networks sustaining the war. The report concludes that sanctions alone cannot end the conflict and must form part of a broader political strategy, alongside stronger regional cooperation and measures to limit harm to civilians.
