title: LA 2028: Black Queens face Zambia in final Olympic qualifier
body: Ghana’s Black Queens will face Zambia in the final qualifying round for the 2028 Olympic Games after cruising past Mauritius with a dominant 10-0 aggregate victory. The Black Queens followed up their 3-0 first-leg win with a commanding 7-0 victory over Mauritius in Sekondi to comfortably advance to the final qualifying round. Their reward is a reunion with Zambia, the same side that denied Ghana qualification for the Paris 2024 Olympic Games after the two teams met in the final qualifying round. The Black Queens have since undergone significant improvement and will be hoping to use their progress to overcome the Copper Queens this time around. With a place at the 2028 Olympic Games at stake, Ghana will be aiming to finally break their Olympic qualification barrier and secure a historic first appearance at the Games.

title: IMF lowers forecast for Russia’s economic growth
body: The International Monetary Fund has lowered its forecast for Russia’s economic growth to 0.9% in both 2026 and 2027. The updated forecast, released on October 13, is down from its July projection of 1.1% for each year. The IMF report says high global energy prices are supporting Russia’s economy despite a decline in supplies caused by Ukrainian strikes that damaged oil infrastructure. The report says the overall outlook is weak for energy-intensive economies and those dependent on oil and gas imports. Russia, however, benefits from “favorable factors associated with increased defense spending” that partially offset this weakness. In late September, Russia’s Economic Development Ministry raised its growth forecast for 2026 from 0.4% to 0.6%. The ministry expects growth to accelerate from 1.4% in 2027 to 2.4% in 2029. Russia’s central bank forecasts growth of 0 to 1% in 2026 and 1.5 to 2.5% in 2027. In early October, the World Bank kept its forecast for Russian GDP growth in 2026 at 0.8%. It expects Russia’s economy to grow by 0.7% in both 2027 and 2028. Read more Russia’s economy is growing faster than expected. It probably won’t last. title: RTX’s Raytheon completes three successful tests of new Coyote upgrades
body: TUCSON, Ariz. — Raytheon, an RTX business, successfully completed three tests of its new Coyote Block 2C+RM upgrades, advancing the program from concept to testing in just 15 months. These Raytheon-funded developmental testing events show rapid progress of current Coyote Block 2C+RM interceptor upgrades to support an urgent joint U.S. military mission to counter evolving drone threats. The Coyote Block 2C+RM upgrade builds on the combat–proven performance of current Coyote variants, which have intercepted hundreds of drones. This effort intends to integrate a rocket motor for faster launch and flight, along with a new seeker and warhead designed to defeat all classes of current and emerging drone threats. “With a common backbone, Raytheon can rapidly scale the Coyote family across counter-drone missions — so we’re accelerating the pace of innovation,” said Tom Laliberty, president of Land & Air Defense Systems at Raytheon. “Coyote Block 2C+RM is the latest example of how we’re investing to deliver critical upgrades to combat-proven technology that give service members a decisive advantage on the battlefield.” The initial test series included several first-of-its-kind events, including confirmation of initial integration with the current counter-drone architecture and the first launches of a Coyote effector equipped with a tactical rocket motor to improve threat engagement times and faster successive shots. title: Governors allied with Flávio Bolsonaro set to lead majority of Brazilian Amazon states
body: Seven of Brazil’s nine Amazonian states are set to be governed by politicians aligned with far-right candidate Flávio Bolsonaro, Lucas Berti reported for Mongabay Brasil. On Oct. 25, Brazil will have an electoral face-off between the top two candidates for several races that were not able to secure more than 50% of the vote in the first round of the elections. The second round election includes the decision for president, where incumbent leftist President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is up against Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of far-right former President Jair Bolsonaro who is barred from public office after being convicted of planning a coup d’état in 2022. The second vote will also define many of the state governments in the Brazilian Amazon. In the first round on Oct. 4, five candidates won a clear majority and have already been elected. Mato Grosso, an agricultural state in the southwest of the Brazilian Amazon, elected agribusinessman Otaviano Pivetta, aligned with the right-wing party Republicanos. Pará elected Daniel Santos, known as Dr. Daniel, with the Podemos party. He has promised to designate Vinícius Borba to lead the environment department. title: World Championships cannot be complete without Russian top gymnasts — diplomat
body:
THE HAGUE, October 13. /TASS/. The upcoming World Artistic Gymnastics Championships in Rotterdam can hardly be considered a genuine international tournament without Russian top athletes who were denied entry visas to The Netherlands, Russian Ambassador to that country Vladimir Tarabrin said.
"It is hardly possible to talk about a full-fledged world championship without the participation of the top athletes. Spectators have been deprived of the opportunity to enjoy the performances of recognized masters, and gymnasts from other countries have been denied the chance to compete against the true leaders of world sports," he told TASS.
The Russian diplomat said the Dutch authorities had only discredited themselves and put the competition organizers in a difficult position.
Earlier, the press service of the Russian Gymnastics Federation reported that the Dutch embassy had refused to issue visas to Olympic champions Angelina Melnikova and Victoria Listunova, as well as Anna Kalmykova, citing their being a "threat to international relations" as a reason.
The World Artistic Gymnastics Championships will be held in Rotterdam from October 17 to 25 and will serve as the first stage of team qualification for the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles.

title: Govt approves changes to reservation system
body:
The Cabinet of Ministers adopted a resolution On certain issues concerning the organization of reservations for conscripts during mobilization and wartime, MP Yaroslav Zhelezniak (from the Holos faction) said; a government source also confirmed this information to Interfax-Ukraine.
"The document was adopted after one day of revisions, and regarding the reservation percentage – after five days. However, my sources say that they apparently managed to remove this provision regarding the 50% calculation basis," Zhelezniak said on social media.
According to him, government officials retained the provision that employees with deferrals (students, caregivers, and parents of three children) can be included in the calculation basis for the quota, as is currently the case.
A government source speaking to the agency also said the calculation of the reservation base in the final document will most likely remain unchanged.
He noted that, in accordance with the approved resolution, a Coordination Center for Allocation Issues will be established, but its membership will include not only representatives of the security and law enforcement agencies but also representatives of the humanitarian sector.
Earlier, Zhelezniak had released a draft government resolution that called for reducing reservation limits for the defense industry and the energy sector from 100% to 85%, for utility companies – from 75% to 60% – as well as a change in the basis for calculating the 50% quota and the creation of a Coordination Center under the Cabinet of Ministers. According to him, it was proposed that the Coordination Center consist of 17 members, including representatives of the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU), the Main Intelligence Agency of Ukraine, the Foreign Intelligence Service of Ukraine, and the National Police. Without a positive recommendation from this body, companies will not be able to obtain "critically important" status or a reservation quota exceeding 50%; moreover, the center will also have the authority to recommend revoking such status, while the document lacks clear deadlines, criteria, and appeal mechanisms.
Interfax-Ukraine reached out to the Cabinet of Ministers for comment.
As previously reported, relevant defense associations – including NAUDI, the Technological Forces of Ukraine, and the Council of Arms Manufacturers – have called on the government to maintain a 100% procurement quota for defense industry enterprises, emphasizing the risks to the fulfillment of defense contracts. The Union of Ukrainian Entrepreneurs announced its intention to send an official request to the relevant ministry to clarify the details of the drafting of the document in question.
The European Business Association (EBA) also expressed concern over possible changes to the procedure for reserving employees subject to military service and called on the government to ensure an open dialogue with the business community before making any decisions.
Regarding the creation of the Coordination Center, Yulia Svyrydenko's government had already adopted a similar decision in July, shortly before her resignation, but it never took effect. At that time, it was envisaged that the Coordination Center would function as a temporary consultative and advisory body to the government, and its tasks would include: coordinating government agencies and finding solutions to problematic situations regarding conscription; reviewing proposals from government agencies regarding the designation of enterprises, institutions, and organizations as critical to the economy and the public's livelihood.

title: Nigeria meets OPEC quota for fifth straight month as oil output hits 1.84m barrels
body:
Nigeria’s average daily production of crude oil and condensate rose 2.34 per cent to 1.72 million barrels in September from 1.68 million barrels in the preceding month, the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission ( NUPRC ) said Tuesday
The commission noted in a statement that Africa’s biggest oil producer logged a peak production of 1.84 million barrels during the month as the country met its OPEC quota for the fifth month in a row.
“Nigeria produced a daily average of 1,717,030 barrels of crude oil and condensate in the month of September 2026, representing a 2.34 per cent increase when compared to the previous month,” the statement said.
NUPRC said the lowest daily production recorded during the period under review was 1.68 million barrels.
Nigeria aspires to ramp up output level to 3 million barrels per day (bpd) by 2030, when the upstream regulator anticipates a minimum of 22 offshore projects, capable of unlocking about $50 billion worth of investment, to have kicked off production.
The government has introduced several reforms, including tax incentives, drill-or-drop policy, fiscal modernisation, among others, to attract new capital and revive idle oil fields.
Excluding condensate, Nigeria produced an average of 1.53 million bpd in September, representing 102 per cent of the 1.5 million bpd quota assigned to it by OPEC.
According to the NUPRC, Nigeria produced 1.53 million bpd in May, 1.55 million bpd in June, 1.51 million bpd in July and 1.5 million bpd in August.
The commission attributed the improvement in September to stable operations across most producing assets and an absence of major pipeline outages during the period, helping boost production uptime and the efficiency of crude oil evacuation.
“The sustained growth recorded in September reflects the continued commitment of operators and industry stakeholders towards improving operational efficiency, maintaining asset integrity, and enhancing production reliability across the Nigerian upstream petroleum sector,” the statement said.
Average daily crude oil and condensate production by terminal and stream showed that Forcados Terminal recorded the highest output at 320,320 barrels per day, followed by Bonny Terminal with 303,270 barrels per day, it said.

title: Strive Buys $280 Million in Bitcoin, Its Largest Purchase in Months
body:
Strive is piling into Bitcoin at its fastest clip of the year, scooping up another 3,311 BTC worth roughly $280 million in its biggest single purchase since January.
The Nasdaq-listed asset manager, which trades under the ticker ASST, disclosed in a filing Monday that it bought the Bitcoin between Oct. 5 and Oct. 9 at an average price of about $84,500 per coin, including fees. The buy lifts Strive’s total holdings to 32,773 BTC, worth roughly $2.73 billion at today’s prices, up from 29,462 BTC a week earlier.
The purchase caps a stretch of aggressive accumulation. Strive added $169 million in Bitcoin earlier this month in what was then its largest buy in four months, after pushing its stack past 27,000 BTC with a $94.5 million purchase in late September.
The latest tranche extends that momentum, and the timing is notable: the firm bought as Bitcoin slid through a rough week, picking up coins at an average price well below the token’s recent highs near $87,000.
Strive, led by CEO Matthew Cole, is among a wave of public companies that have adopted Bitcoin treasury strategies, raising capital to stockpile the asset and tie their share price to its performance.
The model, pioneered by Michael Saylor’s Strategy, has drawn a crowded field, and Strive has moved aggressively since going public through its merger with Asset Entities, recently completing a tie-up with Semler Scientific to bulk up its balance sheet. Beyond its Bitcoin, the company also holds about 505,000 shares of Strategy’s STRC preferred stock, valued near $50 million, and roughly $310 million in cash.
The buying spree arrives amid a flurry of treasury activity across the sector. Strategy itself recently added $21.5 million in Bitcoin while buying back preferred stock, Solana treasury firm DeFi Development Corp. kept accumulating SOL , and Bitmine continued stacking Ethereum , though chairman Tom Lee said that company is nearly finished and will halt purchases once it holds 5% of the token’s supply.
The strategy carries the category’s familiar risk: Strive’s fortunes rise and fall with a notoriously volatile asset. Buying into a dip can pay off if Bitcoin rebounds, but the same exposure cuts the other way, and treasury firms have faced scrutiny over how much their stock premiums depend on continued accumulation.

title: Army eyes changes to emergency war gear stocks amid review
body: As the war with Iran provides the military with new insights on how to prepare for contemporary conflict, the Army is nearing decisions on changes to make to its own emergency stockpiles. The service expects to soon make a decision in light of a wide-ranging review of its prepositioned stocks “within the next calendar year,” Maj. Gen. Gavin Lawrence, deputy commanding general of U.S. Army Materiel Command, told Military Times in an interview. The review, called TAP2E, Total Army Power Projection Equipment, aims to assess the laydown of the Army’s forward-deployed and stored gear, including weapons and large vehicles, that can be activated and distributed rapidly if conflict needs arise. The effort continues through 2032, according to a recently published Army strategy, and will cost $702 million in the next year, per Army budget documents. “Strategically placing TAP2E in key theaters, such as the Indo-Pacific and Europe, shortens deployment timelines and demonstrates a credible commitment to allies, underpinning the nation’s integrated deterrence posture,” a budget overview for Fiscal Year 2027 states. The Army has at least seven publicly identified stockpiles , according to a 2024 congressional report. They include two in North America; two in Asia; one afloat; and two in Europe. The Army’s budget proposal calls for an eighth stockpile in the southwest Indo-Pacific and increases to “comprehensive maintenance and care” funding for the existing prepositioned stock focused on Europe. “Together, these TAP2E investments ensure that forward-positioned assets are maintained at the highest state of readiness, providing a tangible deterrent to adversaries and a rapid response capability for the Joint Force,” the proposal states. According to Lawrence, the work continues. “Is it located in the right places? Do we have the right equipment in the right quantities to support preposition of materiel?” Lawrence said. “That’s critically important, right, as you look at our ability to support and prosecute operations in a contested environment, and so we’re in the process of doing that in lockstep with [the Office of the Secretary of Defense] as they make posture decisions. So we are supporting and prioritizing where we’re putting materiel accordingly.” Last year, the then-commander of Army 8th Theater Sustainment Command, Maj. Gen. Gavin Gardner, outlined some changes that had already been identified , such as stashing less equipment on ships through the program called APS afloat and moving one new set of equipment to the Pacific in light of an increased focus on that region. Lawrence added that another change in motion was increased reliance on Joint Theater Distribution Centers, or stockpile sites that hold more expendable gear such as medical supplies. “We’re working hand-in-hand with the combatant commands to identify where those need to be and provide materiel according to those requirements,” he said. He declined to say how many sites had already been set up or what the total number might be. In June, the Air Force’s Air University compiled a number of proposals dating to 2023 about how to improve Army Prepositioned Stocks for future conflict. Among them were moving maintenance and reset facilities for APS afloat stocks from stateside locations to regions in the Pacific — where the vessels are tethered — and moving prepositioned gear from concentrated “iron mountain” storage locations to smaller and more distributed caches that are harder for an enemy to target. Lawrence emphasized that the Army was “in lockstep” with the Pentagon in carrying out changes to prepositioning stocks and “awaiting some additional guidance” from OSW before making concrete changes.

title: No contact with command, a comrade maimed by a mine. A former TV director fought—and halted the Russians
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); A Ukrainian drone sergeant who volunteered for the infantry held a frontline position for six months, ArmyInform reported . He saved three soldiers in that time, and in one fight he stopped a Russian advance after contact with command was lost. The agency did not say where or when. Senior Sergeant Dmytro, call sign Berezen “March”, spent 20 years as a television director before the invasion. In the 152nd Separate Jaeger Brigade, he served as chief sergeant of a drone platoon, worked with three crews, and trained soldiers. When the need arose to reinforce the infantry, he volunteered to switch. ArmyInform did not say what created that need. “I didn’t come here to a sanatorium. I’m in my third year of fighting, I know what this is. It was my choice,” Dmytro said Two wounded, one firefight One comrade was hit by a mine and lost a leg. As Dmytro treated him, Russian troops began moving toward the position. Another wounded soldier was trying to reach them, and contact with command was lost. He killed two Russian soldiers and halted their advance, ArmyInform reported. He said he barely thought about himself, because a breakthrough could have hurt the soldiers holding positions behind him. Not everyone could be saved. One wounded comrade was about 200 meters away. Dmytro heard his voice on the radio but could not leave his position mid-fight. Over the six months, he saved three soldiers. Two left the position with him, and the third was evacuated wounded. No money, he said, is worth blood. title: Taiwan Coast Guard to Acquire MARTAC Devil Ray T24 Unmanned Surface Vessels
body: MELBOURNE, Fla. — Maritime Tactical Systems, Inc. (MARTAC), a leading U.S. provider of fully autonomous unmanned surface vessels (USVs), today announced that the Taiwan Coast Guard Administration (CGA) is acquiring an undisclosed number of Devil Ray T24 autonomous surface vessels. The sale represents one of the most significant international purchases of U.S.-manufactured USVs to date, underscoring the growing global demand for advanced unmanned maritime capabilities. The opportunity was made possible through the tripartite Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) signed by MARTAC, the National Chung-Shan Institute of Science and Technology (NCSIST), and Confucian Co., Ltd. during the 2025 Taipei Aerospace & Defense Technology Exhibition (TADTE). Confucian, MARTAC’s local partner in Taiwan, and NCSIST, Taiwan’s state-owned defense research and development institution, have served as key partners in advancing this initiative from a framework agreement to procurement. The terms of the deal involve a co-production model, with a number of USVs to be manufactured at one of MARTAC’s strategic partner’s facility in Edgewater, Florida, with the remainder built by Confucian in Taiwan. This co-production arrangement reflects the partnership’s commitment to strengthening Taiwan’s domestic industrial base while leveraging MARTAC’s proven design and manufacturing expertise. “This pursuit by the Taiwan Coast Guard represents a landmark moment for MARTAC and for the adoption of unmanned surface vessels in the Indo-Pacific region,” said Seamus Flatley, Chief Growth Officer, MARTAC. “The scale of this multi-vessel acquisition validates the operational capability and reliability of our systems and demonstrates the strategic value of the partnership we established with NCSIST and Confucian.” “In addition to MARTAC’s leading technology, one of the most important reasons the Taiwan government selected MARTAC was the company’s willingness, from the very beginning, to establish co-production in Taiwan,” said Confucian’s Chief Executive Officer James Lee. “This is the Taiwan Coast Guard’s first Unmanned Surface Vessel (USV) program, making it a project of significant national importance that has attracted close attention from senior government leadership.” The Devil Ray T24 is a 27.5 foot (8.4 m) high-performance autonomous surface vessel capable of burst speeds exceeding 50 knots. The T24 is designed to support a wide range of missions for coast guard and military organizations operating in complex maritime environments. The co-production element of the deal is projected to create workforce development opportunities in both the United States and Taiwan, foster supply chain integration and facilitate technology-sharing initiatives consistent with the terms of the original MOU. The sale further solidifies MARTAC’s position as a leading provider of USV solutions to allied nations and reinforces the importance of U.S.-manufactured autonomous maritime platforms in supporting the security and maritime domain awareness needs of partners across the Indo-Pacific. From MARTAC, Oct. 13, 2026 The post Taiwan Coast Guard to Acquire MARTAC Devil Ray T24 Unmanned Surface Vessels appeared first on Seapower Magazine .

title: Mother, teen son plead not guilty in the death of teen's girlfriend
body:
Karoline Heintz was found dead in her car in August.
Royce and Rachel Moser appeared in court on Tuesday for their arraignments in the killing of Karoline Heintz, a college student who was found dead in her car in August.
Royce and Rachel Moser both pleaded not guilty to multiple charges in the death of Heintz, according to WTAE.
Heintz was found stabbed to death in her car in August, according to Pennsylvania State Police.
Royce Moser, 18, is facing charges including murder, while his mother, 56-year-old Rachel Moser, is facing charges including hindering apprehension of a fugitive, according to court records.
They have both been charged with tampering with or fabricating evidence and abuse of a corpse, according to court records.
The district attorney’s office is requesting a jury trial and the two cases are expected to be consolidated for a single trial, according to WTAE.
The court is awaiting the results of Royce Moser’s psychological evaluation, according to WTAE. A mental health evaluation was also requested for Rachel Moser, according to WTAE.
Investigators alleged Heintz met with her boyfriend, Royce Moser, outside his residence to talk when he reportedly got angry and entered the residence. He then retrieved a large kitchen knife and allegedly stabbed Heintz in the chest, according to Pennsylvania State Police.
After she fell from the vehicle, Moser allegedly put her in the rear hatch area of the Jeep and drove to his mother’s residence, according to police.
Rachel Moser then allegedly helped her son by attempting to clean the vehicle and provide him with latex gloves. She then told him to follow her to PennWest-California University, according to police.
The two then allegedly left the vehicle with Heintz in it near the university’s library and drove back to Rachel Moser’s residence, where Royce Moser cleaned his clothes and showered, according to police.
The mother and son are scheduled to appear in court on Nov. 30, according to WTAE.

title: WAFU Zone B: Black Starlets seal semifinal place with 3-1 win over Benin
body: Ghana’s Black Starlets have booked their place in the semifinals of the WAFU Zone B U17 Championship following a convincing 3-1 victory over Benin in their second Group A game. Issah Alidu scored twice, while Nii Tawiah Odoi was also on target as Ghana secured a second successive win in the competition. The result means the Black Starlets have qualified for the semifinals with a game to spare in the group stage, putting them one step closer to their ultimate goal. Ghana will now turn their attention to their final Group A fixture as they continue their quest for success at the WAFU Zone B U17 Championship, which also serves as a qualifying tournament for the 2027 U17 Africa Cup of Nations.

title: Project Realignment: Makinde’s campaign organisation demands audit of ₦15trn Lagos-Calabar highway
body:
The Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation has demanded an independent audit of the ₦15 trillion Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway project, accusing the federal government of failing to ensure transparency in the procurement and execution of the contract.
The organisation also called on the government to publish engineering assessments, alternative-route analyses, cost implications and details of payments made on the project following the announcement of a realignment of part of the highway in Ondo State.
Felix Hyat, director-general of the Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation, made the demands at a press conference on Tuesday.
Mr Makinde, who is the incumbent governor of Oyo State, is running for president on the platform of Allied People’s Movement (APM) in the 16 January election.
Mr Hyat questioned the circumstances surrounding the contract award in 2024 and the reasons for the route adjustment announced by the Minister of Works, David Umahi.
He said the realignment raised questions about the project’s initial planning, engineering assessments and the government’s handling of public funds.
“While we have nothing against the construction of roads in any part of the country, it is important to state that the afterthought realignment of the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway is an admission of technical incompetence, failure of proper planning and gross underestimation of the project’s engineering challenges,” he said.
The campaign organisation also questioned the minister’s explanation that climate change and environmental challenges necessitated the route adjustment.
Mr Hyat alleged that the circumstances surrounding the realignment raised concerns about whether the necessary environmental impact assessment had been conducted before the project commenced.
He further questioned the procurement process, alleging that the contract was awarded without an approved engineering design, an open and competitive bidding process or budgetary provision and statutory appropriation by the National Assembly.
The allegations were made by the campaign organisation and were not independently established in its statement.
The organisation said the government should explain whether the route adjustment would reduce the project’s overall cost and disclose how much had been spent so far.
It also raised concerns about the reported links between the contractor’s corporate group and a firm whose board allegedly includes individuals connected to the Presidency.
Mr Hyat said the circumstances warranted public disclosure of the procurement process, contractor selection, contract cost and safeguards established to protect public funds.
The organisation also alleged that the highway contract had, from inception, been designed as a conduit for financing the All Progressives Congress (APC)’s election expenses. It did not provide evidence to substantiate the allegation in its statement.
“We demand that the President Tinubu-led government should publish the relevant engineering assessment, alternative-route analysis, accompanying cost implications and comprehensive audit of the work and amount so far spent,” Mr Hyat said.
The Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway is a major federal infrastructure project intended to connect Lagos with coastal communities across several southern states towards Calabar, Cross River State. The proposed route adjustment has renewed questions about the project’s planning, environmental considerations and financial implications.
The organisation said the highway contract should be assessed against the condition of existing federal roads, which it described as being in urgent need of rehabilitation.
It also linked the controversy to Nigeria’s broader economic challenges, citing rising food prices, transportation costs and healthcare expenses, as well as increased university tuition fees.
Beyond the highway controversy, the organisation urged Nigerians to reject President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election.
It called on voters to support Seyi Makinde, the presidential candidate of the Allied People’s Movement (APM), describing him as an alternative to the incumbent.
The organisation said Mr Makinde’s proposed RESET Nigeria agenda offered a vision for national renewal and argued that his leadership could attract support across political parties and regions.
Mr Hyat said the future of Nigeria should take precedence over Mr Tinubu’s re-election ambition.
The campaign organisation’s demands include the immediate publication of procurement and payment records, an independent engineering assessment of the Ondo realignment and a comprehensive audit of the project’s expenditure and future execution plans.

title: A plea not to use uv-build
body:
After seeing yet another dozen packages lose keywords on Gentoo because of a single key dependency switching to uv-build , I would like to plea on behalf of Gentoo users: please don’t use uv-build as a build backend. Just to be clear, this is not about uv itself or any other Astral tools; these are good tools with a nice and responsive upstream. The uv-build backend is one thing we have to disagree on. I’m not saying it’s bad; I’m saying that its benefits don’t outweigh the drawbacks.
What are the drawbacks? It’s really big and it’s written in Rust. Rust has many advantages, but none of them really matter for a build backend that is used to build pure Python packages. It’s a huge dependency (as of 0.13.0, its wheels are between 1.2 MiB and 1.5 MiB, depending on the platform) and it has no benefit over using a small pure Python backend (say, flit-core whose wheel is 45 KiB). It means that all Gentoo users need to build it from source, and given that it’s released quite frequently (12 releases in the 30 days prior to writing this post), that’s a lot of building. Like, for every 100 ms spent running uv-build to install one release of your package, Gentoo users will spend many hours building new uv-build versions over and over again.
However, build times aren’t the biggest problem; portability is. You can run Python pretty much anywhere where you can get a working C compiler. Some minor features may not work, but the core is reasonably portable. The list of platforms supported by Rust is growing slowly, and even if you can get a working Rust compiler on a given platform, uv may not work. The problems can range from bugs in the lot of packages that uv depends on (for example, rustix::fs and its dependencies skipping SPARC, for no apparent reason ), to the resulting executable being so big that the toolchain runs out of address space (and unlike system memory, you can’t really add address space to a system; the Gentoo uv ebuild already carries two hacks to make it possible to build uv on 32-bit platforms). And then, if your platform is not supported at all… well, let’s just say that adding and maintaining a new platform is a full-time job that may involve a lot of swearing at the code churn.
What about the advantages? Well, I’m aware of two reasons to use uv-build. One is consistency with using uv for your project, and it doesn’t really matter. It’s a backend and the whole point of PEP 517 is that you can use any backend with any tool. You can use flit-core, you can use hatchling , and either of them will work just fine with uv (or any other frontend). The other reason is performance and that argument makes even less sense. Even if it mattered, we’re realistically talking about a difference in the ballpark of 100 ms, for an action executed rarely; it is equally possible that any gain will be outweighed by the time needed to fetch the 1.5 MiB wheel for uv-build. But it doesn’t matter, because realistically the backend is only used by project developers, contributors, CI/CD workflows, downstream packagers and users of source distributions; all regular users use wheels instead. Of these groups, source distribution user group is the largest and the most impacted, and any performance gain is defeated by the time spent building uv-build.

title: Govt preparing crisis response scenarios for 2026-2027 winter period – Budanov
body:
Ukraine is developing crisis scenarios and coordinating response plans for potential threats during the period from November 2026 to March 2027, Head of the Presidential Office Kyrylo Budanov reported.
"The main task is to develop clear crisis scenarios and synchronize operational response plans for the period from November 2026 to March 2027. The government, through the State Emergency Service, is preparing a baseline scenario of potential threats taking into account their geography and scale, while the Defense Forces and intelligence will provide a corresponding risk assessment," Budanov wrote on his Telegram channel following a meeting of the Humanitarian Response Coordination Platform.
According to him, during the meeting key challenges were discussed alongside Prime Minister Serhiy Koretsky, NSDC Secretary Ihor Klymenko, the Presidential Office team, representatives of state bodies, and foreign diplomats representing donor countries.
"Available resources must be concentrated where conditions will be toughest for people. Authorities at all levels, relevant ministries and services, the military, international partners, and humanitarian organizations must act in a smooth and coordinated manner," the head of the Presidential Office noted.

title: USS Billings Returns to Naval Station Mayport
body: NAVAL STATION MAYPORT, Fla. — The Freedom-class littoral combat ship USS Billings (LCS 15) returned to Naval Station Mayport Oct. 10, 2026, following a 6-month deployment to U.S. Fourth Fleet area of operations in support of U.S. Southern Command’s (USSOUTHCOM) mission. During the deployment, Billings conducted sustained maritime security operations to support regional counter-illicit trafficking efforts. The crew worked alongside an embarked U.S. Coast Guard Law Enforcement Detachment and a Helicopter Maritime Strike Squadron 48 detachment, supporting multiple successful interdictions that resulted in the seizure of more than 2,500 kilograms of illicit narcotics and the apprehension of suspected traffickers. “The crew of USS Billings exemplified operational agility and dedication throughout this deployment,” said Rear Adm. Carlos Sardiello, commander, U.S. Naval Forces Southern Command/U.S. 4th Fleet. “Whether executing high-stakes interdictions, transporting vital drinking water in support of disaster relief efforts, or contributing to coalition efforts, these Sailors helped impose total systemic friction on narco-terrorist networks, directly supporting the defense of the homeland and the security of the Western Hemisphere.” Billings also strengthened maritime interoperability with Caribbean partners, including the Dominican Republic Navy and Jamaica Defence Force, to enhance information sharing and address shared security challenges. Additionally, the ship demonstrated its versatility by supporting humanitarian-assistance efforts following an earthquake in Venezuela in June, transporting more than 77,000 pounds of drinking water. Billings departed Naval Station Mayport on March 27, 2026. USS Billings is the first U.S. Navy ship to bear the name, honoring the city of Billings, Montana, and the enduring service, sacrifice, and patriotism of south-central Montana and the broader Big Sky region. Sailing under the motto “Big Sky Over Troubled Waters,” the ship connects Montana’s proud heritage with the crew’s dedication to defending freedom. Commander, Naval Surface Force Atlantic is responsible for manning, training, and equipping assigned surface forces and shore activities, ensuring a capable and combat-ready force to support U.S. national interests. The SURFLANT force consists of more than 66 warships and 34 shore commands. From U.S. Naval Surface Force Atlantic, Oct. 13, 2026 The post USS Billings Returns to Naval Station Mayport appeared first on Seapower Magazine .

title: Kongsberg to build new plant in Poland for counter-drone systems
body: WARSAW, Poland — Norway’s Kongsberg has decided to build a new production facility for counter-drone systems in northern Poland, with plans to invest more than 200 million zloty ($51 million) in the plant. The investment is connected to the company’s cooperation with Polish state-run defense group PGZ to deliver the San anti-drone system to the Polish military. “We have been present in Poland for many years. We think it’s important that we establish local sites in Poland,” Eirik Lie, the president and CEO of Kongsberg, told Defense News at the Warsaw Security Forum here on Oct. 12. “We are on good track for deliveries on the San program. But also, we expect export contracts, so this enables us to be prepared for these exports from Poland.” Under the San deal, valued at around PLN 15 billion ($3.8 billion), Kongsberg and PGZ are to supply 18 anti-drone batteries, 52 firing platoons, 18 command platoons, and 703 vehicles to the Polish military, according to data from Poland’s Ministry of National Defence. The contract will be largely financed by loans that Poland has secured from the European Union’s Security Action For Europe (SAFE) scheme. Given the region-wide concern over drone incursions, Lie said Kongsberg expects the demand for its solutions to rise significantly in the coming years. In the future, the envisioned Polish factory could also introduce additional defense solutions to its portfolio. “As a company, we are expanding quite a lot. We want to build on this factory for other elements as well,” the CEO said. In a statement, the Norwegian group said it plans to sign a construction contract by the end of 2026 and begin work immediately afterward. Serial production of counter-drone systems could begin in the first half of 2028. The investment is expected to create more than 100 jobs in Poland once the plant reaches full capacity.

title: Trump administration offering migrant children $3,000 to self-deport
body:
The amount is a $500 increase over the incentive offered last year.
A Department of Homeland Security official said Tuesday that unaccompanied migrant children are being offered $3,000 to self-deport .
The official told ABC News that minors who are in government custody, are 14 years or older, and have no gang affiliation are eligible for the stipend.
A spokesperson said DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin is "leading efforts to rescue these children and stop their exploitation."
Last year, the Department of Homeland Security offered minors $2,500 to voluntarily leave the country as part of the Trump administration's immigration crackdown .
One legal service provider told ABC News that DHS began offering the $3,000 incentive earlier this month. Attorneys and advocates say the tactic comes as the Trump administration increasingly targets unaccompanied children for deportation.
The federal government recently assembled a team of government attorneys to represent migrant children in court after the administration cut ties with a number of immigration advocacy groups that had previously provided those services.
Immigration advocacy groups have raised concerns about the initiative, arguing that the same government seeking to deport the minors under the administration's immigration crackdown should not be representing them in court.
A DHS spokesperson told ABC News, "Many of the children who came across the border unaccompanied were allowed to be placed with sponsors who were smugglers and sex traffickers."
"Unlike the previous administration, President Trump and DHS take the responsibility to protect children seriously and will continue to work with federal, state, and local law enforcement to reunite children with their families," the spokesperson said.

title: Ukraine, EU open second, third clusters of membership negotiations
body:
Ukraine and the European Union have opened the second and third negotiation clusters regarding membership.
The announcement was made Tuesday in Luxembourg at the conclusion of an intergovernmental conference by Thomas Byrne, Minister of State for European Affairs and Defense of Ireland, which currently holds the EU presidency.
Byrne said Ukraine's future lay within the European Union family and that, as part of the fourth intergovernmental conference on Ukraine's accession, the Council had opened Cluster 2, covering the internal market, and Cluster 3, covering competitiveness and inclusive growth. He said he was pleased to announce this important milestone in Ukraine's accession process together with Vsevolod Chentsov, Ukraine's Deputy Prime Minister for European and Euro-Atlantic Integration, and European Commissioner for Enlargement Marta Kos.
Byrne said these were the third and fourth clusters opened by the EU in negotiations with Ukraine, following the opening of Cluster 1, Fundamentals, in June and Cluster 6, External Relations, in July. He welcomed the continued momentum towards Ukraine's EU membership and said that, after a long period of stagnation, most clusters had now been opened.
The minister said that, despite Russia's ongoing war against Ukraine, its civilian population and civilian infrastructure, Ukraine continued to implement the reforms needed to bring its national legislation into line with EU standards in key areas.
He also said that Ireland, as the country holding the EU presidency, would do everything possible to support Ukraine on its path towards EU accession. Byrne described the day as positive for Ukraine's accession process and said all EU member states recognised Ukraine's progress in implementing key reforms in two important policy areas.
The minister explained that Cluster 2, the internal market, constituted the economic foundation of the accession process and covered nine technical chapters governing a candidate country's integration into the EU single market.
He said Cluster 3, competitiveness and inclusive growth, concerned the driving forces behind socioeconomic development in the EU accession process and comprised eight chapters aimed at bringing the candidate country's economy into line with EU standards.
Byrne added that the progress achieved sent an important signal to Ukrainians who were fighting for the European values of freedom, democracy and equality.
He said the EU would continue working in the near future to advance Ukraine's candidacy in accordance with the current enlargement methodology by opening the remaining clusters. At the same time, he urged Ukraine to continue implementing the necessary reforms, particularly in the area of fundamental principles.
Byrne said Ukraine was part of the European family by virtue of geography and added that the EU looked forward to the moment when Ukraine and its citizens could be welcomed into the European Union family.

title: Trump denies that Washington has stopped sharing intelligence with Ukraine
body:
WASHINGTON, October 13. /TASS/. The United States has not stopped sharing intelligence data with Ukraine, US President Donald Trump told reporters.
When asked whether the United States has stopped sharing intel with Ukraine, he said, "No, we haven't."
"We help them. We're really helping them get to a final answer. We want the war ended <…>. We are helping them, and we are sharing intel. We want the war to end, so we're working with them and with Russia on getting the war to end," he said.

title: Winnipeg drug initiative leads to 55 arrests, treatment referrals and detox placements
body:
A joint initiative between Winnipeg police and the city’s outreach organizations yielded the arrest of alleged drug traffickers and prompted some people to seek addictions treatment, police said.
Since the initiative was renewed in August , following the success of an earlier iteration in July , 12 community outreach organizers took part in 14 specific joint outreach and enforcement dates with Winnipeg Police Service (WPS) officers from Aug. 7 to Oct. 6.
Teams attempted to engage with people more than 3,700 times, Const. Claude Chancy, a public information officer with WPS, said at a news conference Tuesday. Of those, 10 resulted in people seeking detox programs with the Main Street Project and 48 saw hand-offs to support services.
Additionally, 553 NARCAN kits were distributed by outreach workers, according to Chancy. The kits contain naloxone, an opioid-overdose-reversing drug.
The joint venture also helped WPS with its law enforcement activities, Chancy continued. Fifty-five arrests were made in the 14 engagement days. The vast majority, 43, were in relation to warrants or breaches. Three people were taken into custody for possessing a scheduled substance.
Outside of the specific outreach days, multiple arrests were made as a result of this project, WPS Staff Sgt. Ryan Howanyk said at Tuesday’s news conference.
On July 29, officers searched a building in the 200 block of Young Street after locals complained about suspicious behaviour, he said. Seven people were arrested and are facing gun and drug trafficking-related charges.
That month also saw two people arrested, and the seizure of approximately $1,500 worth of pills, as well as other illicit items, from a trafficking operation near Portage Place.
Howanyk added that a man was arrested twice last week on the suspicion of drug trafficking. His arrests resulted in the seizure of fentanyl, methamphetamine, cash and a sawed-off shotgun.
“This phase of the initiative is set to conclude at the end of October. While we continue to collaborate with community organizations, and connect individuals with supports and services, we will also continue to target the drug traffickers that contribute to addiction, exploitation and harm in our communities,” Howanyk told reporters.
The project combines police enforcement with community care to try to support people who are struggling with drug addiction and using drugs openly in public, he noted. Two people were taken to a protective care centre as a result of that work.
Referrals were also handed out approximately 170 times to groups including the Downtown Community Safety Project and Main Street Project. Sixteen referrals were made to Winnipeg’s supervised consumption site , according to police, noting that four mentions of other support services were made.
Jackie Anderson is the executive director at Ka Ni Kanichihk, one of the outreach groups involved in the WPS initiative. She said it leverages existing relationships that the community groups have with people who are struggling to encourage them to seek help.
“Over the course of our outreach walks, we have witnessed some pretty meaningful moments. We have been able to transport many of our relatives to shelter, ensuring that they have a warm, safe place to rest,” she said.
“We have watched our relatives recognize the outreach teams, greet them with smiles and approach them because they know that they are people they can trust. They even know some of our outreach members by name, and they ask, ‘what day are you back next week?’”
Having access to immediate resources, such as detox beds, has also made a positive difference for outreach organizations, Anderson said, adding that having the resource ready when a person feels prepared to seek help may be the deciding factor in whether treatment is sought.
“We will not have a 100 per cent success rate. We will face challenges, and yes, we will face criticism. But I believe we have a choice – we can continue to focus on everything that is wrong, or we can put our energy into finding those solutions our relatives need,” she said.
It is unclear whether this project will continue after the end of this month, Winnipeg police Chief Gene Bowers said.

title: Facebook is giving users more control over their algorithm
body:
Facebook is the latest social media platform to give users greater control over the algorithm that determines what appears in their feeds.
Meta announced the launch of its new AI-powered feature, “Your Algorithm,” on Tuesday, a feature it first launched on Instagram. The new tool allows Facebook users to influence the content they see in Feed and Reels by describing their preferences in their own words using natural language. Rather than relying entirely on automated recommendations, users can now communicate directly with the platform about the topics and content they want to see more or less frequently.
According to Meta, the feature is designed to make content recommendations more relevant. Users can adjust their preferences and interact with the algorithms responsible for ranking and recommending posts, with changes reflected in their recommendations in real time.
The company has also updated Facebook’s three-dot menu, making it easier for users to manage their content preferences directly from individual posts. By opening the menu, users can access “Your Algorithm” or select the “Interested” and “Not interested” options to indicate whether particular content aligns with their preferences.
Meta says the platform may ask follow-up questions to better understand what users liked or disliked, allowing them to provide more detailed feedback. Users can explain what they want to see more or less of, helping Facebook refine its recommendations based on their responses.
The introduction of “Your Algorithm” reflects Meta’s broader effort to give people more influence over their social media experiences as AI increasingly shapes content discovery. The move signals a shift away from the traditional recommendation systems that have shaped social media experiences for years, bringing the platform closer to streaming services that allow users to personalize recommendations based on their interests and preferences.
The launch also builds on Meta’s existing personalization efforts across its other platforms. Instagram introduced Your Algorithm in June, extending customization options across Feed and Explore after first launching the feature for Reels in December 2025.
Threads also introduced its own related feature, called “Dear Algo,” which allows users to influence the content recommended to them.

title: Bipartisan US senators urge Trump to abandon Russian diesel deal
body:

title: Forget rockets — Longshot wants to fire cargo into space from a gun. See it at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
body:
Rockets are, infamously, a real pain in the butt. Our old friend physics forces rockets to be built with almost no room for error, and even then only a small fraction of their weight makes it to orbit.
There are, at least in theory, other ways to do the job — space elevators, centrifuges, or a big chain hanging from a satellite in space and scooping up cargo from Earth. (Blue Origin spent some time thinking about that one before the idea wound up in a Neal Stephenson novel .)
And then there’s an idea dating all the way back to Jules Verne: Use a big gun to shoot a projectile into space.
Longshot Space Technology , a startup based in Alameda, California, is working on exactly that. The co-founders, CEO Mike Grace and CTO Nato Saichek, see an opportunity to take a technology that has already proven its worth and apply it to the pressing need for space launch. The startup has raised about $20 million from venture investors in service of its mission.
When it comes to frontier technology, Grace says, “you can build something that has a lot of novelty, or you can do something really hard. You don’t get to do both.” He points to SpaceX as an example of a company that has “taken classically de-risked technology and scaled it aggressively.” What SpaceX did with NASA rocket research, he says, Longshot will do with multi-injection guns — designs that give a projectile extra boosts as it moves down the barrel — built for World War II and during 1960s research programs.
The idea is to take all the work done by the first stage of a launch vehicle and collapse that into a reusable accelerator on the ground. Picture a steel pipe mounted horizontally over the ground, with tanks of high-pressure gas attached at ports spread across its length. When a projectile is fired and moves down the barrel, the tanks fire off at precise times to accelerate it — to speeds as high as Mach 4, thus far.
The company is currently firing a 70-foot gun with a six-inch diameter at its test site near Barstow, California, and says it can accelerate projectiles up to near-hypersonic speeds. Soon, it expects to start firing a 140-foot-long gun with a 30-inch diameter at its Alameda test site. After that, the company is preparing to build out a 30-inch diameter gun that is 328-feet long, with plans to extend it to about 3,000 feet — making it the largest gun on the planet. It will be capable of launching 220-pound payloads up to speeds of Mach 8, the team says.
These guns will let Longshot keep proving its technology works while also generating revenue from performing hypersonic testing for the U.S. military, which has awarded the company several contracts. Grace envisions building one of his guns on a U.S. military installation like Fort Bliss, where it could be part of the infrastructure for testing the next generation of U.S. interceptors. (And no, the guns don’t need to point up at an angle. Longshot’s projectile is a lifting body, meaning its shape generates lift, so it will aerodynamically gain altitude once it exits the barrel.)
“If you want to practice shooting down a Chinese or Russian hypersonic missile, wouldn’t it be nice not to pay $30 million for that?” Grace asks. “This is a way for half a million, a quarter of a million bucks, of doing hypersonic clay pigeons, throw them and shoot them down, and do it really fast and really cheap.”
The ultimate goal, however, is putting large payloads into space. The team is confident it can scale up its current design to accelerate payloads to as much as five kilometers per second (more than 11,000 mph). That’s fast enough to get into space if the payload, which effectively serves as the second stage of a rocket, has its own propulsion system. But doing that would require a gun 10 kilometers (about six miles) long and nearly 10 feet in diameter. As you might imagine, one problem the company faces is simply finding suitable worksites.
“The hard part is not building the thing, it’s finding a place where they will let you build the thing,” Saichek jokes.
But if Longshot can realize its vision, the math is very attractive: The system is cheap to construct and to fuel, and is highly reusable. Grace expects that if everything works out, they can send payloads to space for a hard-to-believe $50 per kilogram (about $22 per pound). Considering that the much-hyped orbital data center industry needs prices to fall to around $300 per kilogram to get off the ground, that leaves Longshot plenty of room to offer a competitive price.
It will require some modification to launch spacecraft in this form factor and conditions, but at that price point, satellite operators will be willing to try.
If you want to learn more about Longshot from the company itself — while also checking out dozens of startups, hearing their pitches, and listening to guest speakers on four different stages — join us this week at Disrupt, Tuesday to Thursday, in San Francisco. Learn more here.

title: Raytheon to advance target-detection capabilities for naval radars
body: PORTSMOUTH, R.I. — Raytheon, an RTX business, has been awarded a contract from the Office of Naval Research (ONR) to develop advanced target‑detection capabilities for naval radar systems. Under the contract, Raytheon’s Advanced Technology team will develop and evaluate advanced signal and data-processing algorithms and integrate targeted software upgrades to significantly extend detection range, increase sensitivity and improve radar-system efficiency. These enhancements will undergo rigorous laboratory and field testing to validate performance and operational use, preparing them for transition into Raytheon’s SPY‑6 family of radars and other future naval radars. “Modernizing fielded radar systems with software-first upgrades is one of the fastest and most cost-effective ways to deliver mission-ready capability,” said Colin Whelan, president of Advanced Technology at Raytheon. “These enhancements will enable naval operators to detect smaller objects at greater distances and classify targets more quickly, providing the fleet with faster, more informed decision‑making.” The program continues Raytheon’s extensive work in software-defined apertures and leverages knowledge gained from prior ONR initiatives, including ASPIRE and STORM, which established foundational hardware and software advancements for next-generation radar capability. Work under this contract will be conducted at Raytheon facilities in Portsmouth, R.I., and Andover, Massachusetts, through 2031. From RTX, Oct. 12, 2026 The post Raytheon to advance target-detection capabilities for naval radars appeared first on Seapower Magazine .

title: NAF sets up 12-member board to investigate Ondo aircraft crash
body:
The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) has constituted a 12-member Aircraft Accident Investigation Board to determine the cause and circumstances of the crash involving its ATR 42 aircraft in Igbokoda, Ondo State.
The aircraft, identified as NAF 931, crashed on 5 October, killing all those on board. The investigation is expected to establish what led to the accident and recommend measures to prevent similar occurrences.
According to a statement on Tuesday by its Director of Public Relations and Information, Ehimen Ejodame, the Chief of the Air Staff, Sunday Aneke, directed sustained search and recovery operations alongside a comprehensive investigation into the crash.
It said the investigation board will be headed by F.O. Ankeli, an air vice marshal, will serve as the president of the 12-member Aircraft Accident Investigation Board. It added that E.O.E. Ebiowe, who led the Investigation and Recovery Team, will coordinate the wider response.
The board comprises personnel with expertise in aviation operations, flight safety, piloting, air traffic control, aircraft engineering, maintenance and medical services, among other relevant disciplines. Representatives of the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority and the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau are also included to provide civilian aviation expertise.
“The Board is mandated to examine relevant operational, technical, environmental, human and organisational factors surrounding the accident. Its work will involve the systematic examination, documentation and preservation of relevant evidence to establish the facts and determine the immediate and underlying causes or the occurrence,” the statement read.
It also noted that the board would make evidence-based recommendations to address any deficiencies identified, strengthen aviation safety and reduce the risk of similar accidents.
“Beyond the operational and investigative response, the NAF remains committed to supporting the bereaved families through this difficult period,” it added.
The NAF acknowledged public interest in the investigation and pledged to provide updates as verified information becomes available. However, it cautioned against drawing conclusions about the cause of the crash before the investigation is completed.
“Conclusions regarding the cause of the accident would be premature until the investigation is completed and its findings are duly considered,” the statement said.

title: Russian Communist Party lawmaker says all citizens should bear the burden of the war against Ukraine equally
body: Russians should share equally in the burden of the war against Ukraine, Anatoly Lokot, a lawmaker from the Communist Party of the Russian Federation (KPRF), said in a speech to the State Duma. “We want the burden of this war, of overcoming the obstacles that arise, to be shared equally by everyone, by all citizens of our country. We want the effort to overcome these difficulties, this struggle, to unite us rather than divide us,” he said.
