title: Trump refuses to accuse Russia of breaking energy ceasefire, says Ukraine 'hit sites the day before'
body:
U.S. President Donald Trump on Oct. 13 did not directly accuse the Kremlin of violating his energy ceasefire, saying Ukraine also previously struck Russian energy sites in response to reporters' questions.
Trump unexpectedly announced an energy ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia on Oct. 11, taking Kyiv by surprise , adding that there was a ceasefire in place " because I said they agreed ."
When asked by reporters whether he thinks Russia violated the ceasefire, he briefly answered , "I'll let you know about that later."
"Well, Ukraine hit many sites the day before," Trump responded to another question.
Just hours after Trump's announcement, Russia violated the ceasefire by striking Kharkiv's CHP-5 power plant.
According to President Volodymyr Zelensky, the Kremlin attacked six energy facilities on Oct. 11, injuring 33 people across the country.
Following the attack, Zelensky disclosed that over the past week, Russia has carried out over 200 strikes on Ukraine's electricity and transmission facilities, in addition to 17 strikes on gas and oil facilities.
Nonetheless, Ukraine has refrained from attacking Russia's oil refineries for the past two days.
"We are ready to respect an energy ceasefire if Russia is ready to do the same," Zelensky said on Oct. 12, noting that a ceasefire focused only on oil refineries makes no sense since Ukraine has a single "badly damaged" refinery previously attacked by Russia.
Russia has yet to formally respond to the ceasefire, stating Putin is not interested in a ceasefire.
"We want long-term peace and are prepared to do everything possible to achieve it," said Kremlin's spokesperson Dmitry Peskov on Oct. 12, without providing further details on what "long-term peace" entails.
"We are working with them (Ukraine) and Russia on getting the war to end," said Trump.

title: Boeing delivers 57 aircraft in September as orders surge to 165 jets
body:
Boeing delivered 57 aircraft in September 2026, its highest monthly total of the year, an increase of 11.8% from the 51 jets delivered in August and 3.6% above the 55 recorded in September 2025.
The U.S. aircraft manufacturer also secured 165 gross orders during the month, compared with just 15 in August. The increase was largely driven by Turkish Airlines, which ordered 100 Boeing 737 MAX passenger jets.
According to figures released on October 13, Boeing delivered 43 737 MAX aircraft, eight 787 Dreamliners, two 777 freighters and four 767s during September.
The company has delivered 475 aircraft in the first nine months of 2026, compared with 440 during the same period last year, an increase of 8%. The total includes 363 737 MAX jets, the highest number delivered by the program during the first nine months of any year.
September also brought Boeing's third-quarter deliveries to 161 aircraft, narrowly above the 160 recorded during the corresponding quarter of 2025.
The 737 MAX accounted for approximately 75% of Boeing's September deliveries, with 43 aircraft handed over to airlines and leasing companies.
Southwest Airlines was the largest individual recipient, taking nine jets, followed by United Airlines with five and VietJet Air with four.
Flydubai and Norwegian Air each received three aircraft, while Singapore Airlines and Virgin Australia took one each.
Leasing companies accounted for another significant portion of the deliveries. AerCap received six 737 MAX jets, followed by Aviation Capital Group and Dubai Aerospace Enterprise with three each.
CDB Leasing took two aircraft, while Bank of Communications Leasing, Everbright Financial Leasing and SMBC Aviation Capital received one each.
Boeing also delivered eight 787 Dreamliners, comprising seven 787-9s and one 787-10.
United Airlines received four 787-9s, while SMBC Aviation Capital took two and Qatar Airways received one. Korean Air was the recipient of the month's only 787-10.
Freighter deliveries included two 777Fs, one each for Air China Cargo and FedEx Express, and a 767-300F for UPS.
The remaining three aircraft were 767-2Cs delivered to Boeing's defense business for completion as KC-46A Pegasus aerial refueling tankers.
Boeing recorded 165 gross orders in September, more than ten times the 15 aircraft booked in August and above the 96 gross orders registered in September 2025.
The 737 MAX accounted for 132 orders, led by Turkish Airlines with 100 aircraft. Lufthansa ordered another 20 jets, while Biman Bangladesh Airlines placed an order for six. The remaining six were attributed to unidentified customers.
The 787 Dreamliner generated 23 orders, including five 787-10s for Biman Bangladesh Airlines .
Unidentified customers accounted for another 17 787-10s and one 787-9, meaning Boeing did not disclose the buyers of 18 of the 23 Dreamliners ordered during the month.
Ethiopian Airlines Group placed the remaining ten orders, comprising eight 777-8 freighters and two conventional 777Fs.
Boeing reported no order cancellations in September.
The manufacturer accumulated 618 net orders during the first nine months of 2026, although this figure differs from gross orders because it accounts for cancellations and other adjustments.
Boeing's 475 deliveries through September included 367 aircraft from the 737 family, 62 Dreamliners, 26 767s and 20 aircraft from the 777 family.
The 737 total includes 363 MAX aircraft, with the remaining deliveries attributed to other variants of the family.
The manufacturer is working to increase 737 MAX production toward 47 aircraft per month, although Boeing Chief Executive Kelly Ortberg acknowledged in September that the production increase has taken longer than expected.
Boeing ended September with an official backlog of 6,371 aircraft, compared with 6,156 at the end of August, an increase of 215.
Despite its higher order intake, Boeing remained behind Airbus in deliveries during September. The European manufacturer handed over 72 aircraft, compared with Boeing's 57.
Airbus accumulated 547 deliveries through September, maintaining a lead of 72 aircraft over its American competitor. Boeing, however, recorded substantially more gross orders during the month, with 165 against Airbus' 17. investors.boeing.com

title: Kaizen as a strategic pathway for micro business scale-up in Ghana
body: Introduction Ghana’s economic landscape is overwhelmingly dominated by micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), which constitute over 90 per cent of all registered businesses and provide approximately 80 per cent of total employment. Within this ecosystem, micro-sized businesses alone account for 90.4 per cent of all establishments, representing a significant rise from 16.6 per cent in 2014. These enterprises, often operating within the informal economy and driven predominantly by women and youth, contribute around 70 per cent of Ghana’s Gross Domestic Product. Despite their numerical dominance, micro businesses face persistent challenges in scaling up, including limited access to finance, inefficient production processes, and weak management systems. Kaizen, the Japanese philosophy of continuous improvement, has emerged as a transformative methodology for addressing these challenges. Since 2012, Ghana has actively promoted Kaizen practices to sustainably improve the quality and productivity of businesses. Through collaborative initiatives involving the Ghana Enterprises Agency (GEA), the United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO), and the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), thousands of Ghanaian micro and small enterprises have been trained in Kaizen principles, with measurable improvements in productivity, product quality, and operational efficiency. This article examines what constitutes a micro business in Ghana and outlines seven strategic points through which Kaizen can be leveraged for scale-up. What Makes a Business a Micro Business in Ghana? The classification of micro enterprises in Ghana is governed by the Classification of MSMEs Regulation, which employs a combination of employment size, turnover, and asset value as defining criteria. According to the Ghana Enterprises Agency (GEA), through Legislative Instrument 2470, a micro enterprise is defined as a business with 1 to 5 permanent employees and either a fixed asset value or annual turnover not exceeding GH¢150,000. This definition aligns with the Ghana Statistical Service’s characterisation of micro enterprises as businesses employing between 1 and 5 workers. The regulatory framework further distinguishes micro enterprises from small enterprises, which employ 6 to 30 permanent employees and have either fixed assets or turnover ranging from GH¢150,000 to GH¢6,000,000. This differentiation is significant because it establishes clear thresholds that micro business owners can target as they pursue growth. Beyond the quantitative metrics, micro businesses in Ghana exhibit several distinctive characteristics. The Integrated Business Establishment Survey reveals that 92.3 per cent of businesses in Ghana remain informal, with the vast majority of micro enterprises operating outside formal regulatory frameworks. Many operate from non-traditional locations pavements, roadside stalls, and mobile setups rather than formal offices or shops. The sector is also characterised by significant income inequality, with approximately 31 per cent of operators earning GH¢100 or less per day. Small start-up capital, proximity to customers, and adaptability to market demand are key drivers of this sector. These characteristics collectively define the micro business landscape in Ghana and underscore both the vulnerabilities and the immense potential of this segment. It is within this context that Kaizen offers a structured yet accessible pathway for incremental growth and formalisation. Seven Strategic Points for Using Kaizen to Scale Up Workplace Organisation through 5S Principles The foundation of Kaizen implementation for micro businesses lies in the 5S methodology Sort, Set in Order, Shine, Standardise, and Sustain. This systematic approach to workplace organisation requires minimal financial investment, making it particularly suitable for resource-constrained micro enterprises. Research from JICA’s Kaizen projects in Ghana confirms that 5S is an initiative that “does not require much resource input and can be easily implemented by local industries that are dominated by micro and small companies”. The practical impact of 5S is evident in the experience of some businesses in an Agro-processing, small-scale gari-manufacturing outfit in Mampong, Ashanti Region. Where the owner has described how Kaizen transformed her operations: “In the past, our factory was distorted, and things were not well arranged. Now, we have compartmentalized our space and labelled each section accordingly. Currently, we have clearly demarcated areas such as the washing, peeling, processing and pressing units”. This reorganisation reduced movement time and improved daily output from one and a half bags to three bags. For micro businesses, such improvements in workspace efficiency directly translate to increased production capacity without the need for additional space or equipment. Waste Reduction and Process Optimisation Kaizen provides micro businesses with practical tools to identify and eliminate the seven types of waste: overproduction, waiting, transportation, over-processing, inventory, motion, and defects. This focus on waste reduction is particularly critical in Ghana, where many MSMEs lose significant inputs and raw materials during production due to unrefined processes. The experience of yet another business in the Garments space in Takoradi exemplifies this strategic advantage. After participating in Kaizen training under a UNIDO project in 2024, the owner identified significant inefficiencies in production, including poor tool organisation, unnecessary movement, and an unstructured factory layout. By reorganising workflows, introducing straight-line production, and assigning specialised tasks such as pattern cutting, the company reduced waste, increased output, and improved consistency. The productivity gains enabled reinvestment in new capabilities, including a fabric printing machine that reduced costs and improved quality control. Human Resource Development and Employee Engagement Kaizen’s emphasis on people, respecting employees, encouraging participation, and creating safe workplaces aligns well with the human-centric nature of micro businesses in Ghana. Research on Kaizen implementation in Ghana’s garment industry has identified workers’ training and development as a critical success factor, alongside leadership commitment and the physical work environment. The Garments business I just spoke about is a case that demonstrates how Kaizen can strengthen employee engagement. Visual target boards now track daily performance, while a suggestion box encourages staff to contribute ideas, reinforcing a culture of continuous improvement. As a result of these Kaizen-driven improvements, the workforce grew from 17 employees to 26, the majority of whom are women. For micro businesses operating with small teams, this approach not only enhances productivity but also improves employee retention and job satisfaction, factors that are critical for sustainable growth. Data-Driven Decision Making One of Kaizen’s most powerful contributions to micro business scale-up is the shift towards data-driven decision making. Many micro enterprises in Ghana operate on intuition and habit rather than systematic measurement, which limits their ability to identify improvement opportunities and track progress. The UNIDO Kaizen Expansion Project in Ghana introduced digital tools such as the Smart and Sustainable Agri-Business (SSAB) dashboard and U-SPARK technology, enabling enterprises to visualise and better manage their performance through real-time data collection on key performance indicators. More than 2,800 enterprises strengthened their capabilities in enterprise performance management through this project, with half of them women-led. For micro businesses, the ability to track productivity metrics, resource efficiency, and quality indicators provides a foundation for informed growth strategies. Quality Improvement and Standardisation Kaizen’s focus on quality improvement is directly linked to market access and competitiveness. Micro businesses that can consistently deliver quality products are better positioned to secure contracts with larger organisations, access formal markets, and command premium prices. The National Kaizen Awards in Ghana have recognised numerous micro and small enterprises that achieved remarkable quality improvements through Kaizen adoption. One such enterprise, a micro and small enterprise specialising in body soaps and creams, was named the overall winner of the 2024 National Kaizen Awards after winning the Micro and Small Enterprise category. The company’s CEO attributed the company’s operational improvements and increased productivity to the effective implementation of Kaizen practices. Other award winners have similarly demonstrated how Kaizen-driven quality improvements can catalyse business growth. Leadership Commitment and Strategic Focus For Kaizen to deliver transformative results in micro businesses, leadership commitment is essential. Research from Ghana’s garment production industry has identified leadership commitment as a critical success factor for Kaizen implementation, alongside workers’ training and development. Micro business owners must be willing to lead by example, allocate time for improvement activities, and sustain momentum over time. The Japan International Cooperation Agency’s Kaizen projects in Ghana have emphasised the importance of embedding Kaizen principles at the leadership level. One of my old colleagues at the Business Resource Centre once noted that “the Japanese government is highly committed to the growth and development of SMEs” and that this institutional commitment has been instrumental in creating effective support systems. For micro business owners in Ghana, adopting this mindset means treating Kaizen not as a one-time training event but as an ongoing management philosophy that guides daily operations and strategic decisions. Accessing Institutional Support and Networks Micro businesses in Ghana do not have to implement Kaizen in isolation. A robust ecosystem of support institutions, including the Ghana Enterprises Agency, JICA, UNIDO, and Business Resource Centres across the country provides training, technical assistance, and networking opportunities. The GEA operates more than 209 Business Advisory Centres across Ghana, providing business development support to enterprises outside the main commercial centres. The GEA has mainstreamed Kaizen into its core operations, training over 33,478 micro and small enterprises through initiatives such as the Mastercard Foundation’s Young Africa Works, the Ghana Jobs and Skills Project, on which i personally taught this in one of the modules, where I took over 800 participants in Ada East & Kpone Katamanso as the lead facilitator and the Bizbox Project. The ILO’s experience in Ghana further demonstrates that management training combining the Start and Improve Your Business (SIYB) programme with basic Kaizen elements significantly improves the performance of small firms. Micro business owners should actively seek out these institutional resources, which are often provided at minimal or no cost, as a strategic lever for scale-up. Conclusion: How Kaizen Has Driven Business Success in Ghana The evidence from Ghana’s experience with Kaizen demonstrates a clear pattern of success that positions this Japanese philosophy as a proven pathway for micro business scale-up. Since the launch of the UNIDO Kaizen Expansion Project in 2022, more than 200 enterprises have improved productivity, product quality, operational efficiency, and overall business performance. Over 2,800 enterprises, half of them women-led, strengthened their capabilities in enterprise performance management. A further 142 firms achieved improvements in productivity, energy efficiency, and waste reduction, while firms adopted 40 new technologies. The success of Kaizen in Ghana is rooted in several factors that make it particularly well-suited to the micro business context. First, Kaizen’s incremental, low-cost approach aligns with the resource constraints that characterise micro enterprises. Unlike expensive technology solutions or large-scale restructuring, Kaizen focuses on small, continuous improvements that can be implemented with existing resources. Second, Kaizen’s emphasis on human development and participation resonates with Ghana’s collectivist cultural values and the people-centred nature of micro businesses. Third, the institutional support ecosystem, including GEA, JICA, UNIDO, and the network of Business Resource Centres has made Kaizen accessible to businesses across all regions of Ghana. The transformative experiences of some Ghanaian businesses illustrate the tangible benefits of Kaizen adoption. Some grew their workforce from 17 to 26 employees, invested in new machinery, and improved product quality through Kaizen-driven process improvements. Others doubled their daily output from one and a half bags to three bags of gari through workplace organisation and process optimisation. Another rose from a micro enterprise to a national Kaizen award winner, demonstrating that scale-up is achievable through sustained commitment to continuous improvement. The call by Ghana’s Deputy Minister for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry to make Kaizen a permanent service within the GEA reflects the growing recognition that this approach is not merely a training programme but a strategic national asset. With GEA positioning itself as a regional centre of excellence for Kaizen in West Africa, the potential for micro businesses to leverage this methodology for growth has never been greater. For Ghanaian micro business owners, the message is clear: Kaizen offers a structured, practical, and proven pathway to scale up. By committing to continuous improvement, one small change at a time, micro enterprises can overcome the constraints that have historically limited their growth and position themselves for sustainable success in Ghana’s evolving economy. *** Kweku Hammond, Senior Sales & Marketing / Faculty, Nova Business School Africa

title: Ukraine war latest: Russian missiles slam central Kyiv before air raid alert sounds
body:
Kyiv came under missile attack shortly after 10 p.m. local time on Oct. 12, with powerful explosions reported before an air raid alert was issued in the Ukrainian capital, according to Kyiv Independent journalists on the ground.
Kyiv Independent staff reported powerful blasts in central Kyiv, with air raid sirens and mobile notifications sounding only afterward. At 11:09 p.m., Kyiv Independent journalists reported further explosions in the capital as the attack continued. The cause of the latest blasts was not immediately confirmed.
Ukraine's Air Force later reported that Russian forces had attacked Kyiv with what appeared to be six ballistic missiles at approximately 10:10 p.m. President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Oct. 13 that it was five ballistic missiles that hit civilian infrastructure.
Zelensky called the strike "particularly vile," adding that there was no early warning from Ukraine's partners about missiles coming.
"Intelligence on Russian ballistic missile launches helps save lives, and this is one of the most critical issues. This is precisely what helps prevent people from being killed – when there is an early warning about ballistic missiles," Zelensky said.
The Air Force said radar systems detected the incoming missiles during the attack, but that it had received no information about launches from Russian territory. It added that it was investigating why it had received no information about the launches.
Air Force spokesperson Yurii Ihnat confirmed during the national news telethon that the alarm had been sounded only during the missile attack, but said that this had occurred previously, according to Ukrainska Pravda .
The delayed air raid alert prompted speculation on Ukrainian social media about whether the lack of advance warning was connected to reported U.S. threats to withdraw intelligence-sharing support for Ukraine.
Ukraine receives intelligence from the United States to help detect and track Russian missile launches and other aerial threats.
The Kyiv Independent reported earlier on Oct. 12 , citing two Ukrainian officials, that Washington had threatened to suspend intelligence sharing unless Kyiv stopped striking Russian energy infrastructure.
Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha said that intelligence sharing between the U.S. and Ukraine was ongoing and had not been stopped, during a speech at the Warsaw Security Forum on Oct. 13.
“You probably ask if we receive intelligence from the American side. Yes, we continue this cooperation," he said.
The French Navy intercepted and boarded a tanker suspected of flying under a false flag as part of Russia's shadow fleet on Oct. 12, French President Emmanuel Macron announced.
The tanker, DF Peak, was allegedly transporting sanctioned Russian fuel and was halted by the French Navy 450 nautical miles (833 kilometers) south of the French territory of Reunion in the Indian Ocean.
"France is determined to combat the ghost fleet, wherever it may be in the world," Macron wrote on X . "This action, carried out in accordance with international maritime law, demonstrates our determination to uphold the rule of law and combat all illicit trafficking, wherever it occurs."
The tanker DF Peak, previously named Kaliningrad, has falsely sailed under the flag of Benin, according to the Ukrainian Defense Intelligence's War and Sanctions portal . The crude oil tanker is sanctioned by the U.S, EU, Switzerland, Canada, and Japan.
The vessel is currently under escort by the French Navy, France's Armed Forces Minister Catherine Vautrin said on X .
"International law is not optional," wrote Vautrin. "Our armed forces are fully mobilized to enforce it and combat illicit activities at sea."
Russian state media TASS said the Russian embassy in Paris told them that "France is violating international law by detaining merchant vessels on the high seas and is attempting to cover up piracy by invoking the provisions of the UN Convention."
The DF Peak is just one tanker of Russia's "shadow fleet" — a group of aging, poorly insured tankers used by Moscow to ship out its oil in violation of international sanctions. Western governments have also accused Moscow of using the fleet to support its hybrid war against Europe.
Speaking to reporters on the White House lawn on Oct. 12, U.S. President Donald Trump once again said that Ukraine and Russia agreed to halt strikes on energy infrastructure, despite the confusion around the alleged ceasefire.
"They agreed," said Trump after a reporter pointed out that neither Moscow nor Kyiv confirmed they would refrain from strikes on energy sites. "Do you know why? Because I said they agreed. That's why. They agreed because I said they agreed. And that thing has to get settled."
The U.S. president's comments came after he unilaterally announced an energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine on Oct. 11, causing confusion in Kyiv. According to a senior Ukrainian official, Ukraine had no prior information about an energy ceasefire.
In a short interview after Trump' s announcement, President Volodymyr Zelensky told Axios, "If President Trump negotiated it with (Vladimir) Putin, please tell us when the ceasefire begins. We are ready, and we will accept it."
Russia has nothing to say yet about an energy ceasefire with Ukraine announced by U.S. President Donald Trump, the Kremlin's spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said on Oct. 12.
When asked by a reporter about his response to Russia continuing to attack Ukraine's energy infrastructure after his announcement, Trump said there had been violations by both sides, without pointing to any evidence.
Hours after Trump's announcement on Oct. 11, Russia struck Kharkiv’s CHP-5 power plant . In Overnight attacks on Oct. 11-12, at least 10 people were killed and 69 others injured across Ukraine as Russia continued to target residential buildings and energy infrastructure across the country.
Ukraine will halt its strikes against Russian refineries only if Moscow ceases its attacks against the Ukrainian power grid, President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Oct. 12, signaling that a refinery-only truce makes little sense for a country with a single, badly damaged refinery .
Two cargo ships were struck by drones near Bulgaria's Black Sea coast overnight on Oct. 13, Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev said.
According to Radev , the Maltese-flagged Chelsea 3, registered in Odesa and owned by a Ukrainian company, was hit by three aerial drones about 18 nautical miles east of the coastal town of Byala in Bulgaria .
All 15 crew members, seven Ukrainians and eight Azerbaijani nationals, were evacuated to the port of Varna, and five received medical assistance, Radev said.
He added that another vessel was struck 17 nautical miles east of Krapets, a Bulgarian village, as he was told at an extraordinary meeting of the Security Council under the Council of Ministers.
The vessel sank, and five crew members were rescued, while 11 crew members were still missing at sea, according to Bulgarian officials, reported Reuters . Reuters further said that Bulgarian media had identified the ship as the ⁠cargo ship Azov Concord.
Radev called the attacks " absolutely unacceptable " and said Bulgaria had informed its permanent representatives to NATO and the European Union. Sofia is seeking assistance to strengthen surveillance of the air and maritime domains and improve its response capabilities.
Bulgarian authorities have not established who was responsible for the attacks. Radev said there was no clear and conclusive evidence to attribute responsibility to either the Ukrainian or Russian side, but argued that "the logic suggests that the outcome benefits the Russian Federation." Radev said he would summon Russia's ambassador for a meeting on Oct. 13.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen condemned the attacks, saying the Black Sea had become "another front of escalation of the Russian war in Ukraine."
Russian forces led a group of civilians toward a gas pipeline, using them as human shields, and afterwards opened fire at them near the front-line city of Kupiansk in Ukraine's Kharkiv Oblast on Oct. 13, the Ukrainian military said, providing alleged drone footage of the incident.
The group included two women, a child, and several men who were being led toward the Shebelinka–Ostrogozhsk gas pipeline, according to Ukraine's 13th Khartia Corps. The group came under repeated mortar and artillery fire as it moved.
Drone footage recorded by Ukrainian reconnaissance units showed casualties among the civilians, Khartia said, adding that Ukrainian troops had not opened fire. Based on the impact patterns, the strike originated from the eastern bank of the Oskil River, where Russian forces are positioned, the corps said.
Khartia called the strike a "deliberate provocation" and warned that Russian media could use footage from the incident to falsely accuse Ukraine of attacking civilians. The corps said it would hand over the materials for a war crimes investigation.
"Civilians are used as human shields by the Russians, and then become their target for disinformation campaigns," Khartia wrote.
Ukraine's Joint Forces grouping separately said on Oct. 13 that Russian forces had struck a column of civilians leaving Kupiansk during what it described as a forced evacuation. The military said it was still establishing the number of casualties.
According to the Joint Forces grouping, Russian troops had conducted similar operations in recent weeks, using civilians as human shields to cover the withdrawal of some of their soldiers.
The Kyiv Independent could not independently verify the claim.
A Russian drone struck a university building in the northwestern city of Rivne , injuring 25 people, Rivne's National Police branch said on Oct. 13.
Of the 25 injured, two were in critical condition, while three others are under medical examination, the police said .
Ukraine's Education and Science Minister Andrii Butenko said that a fire broke out in a building of Rivne State Humanitarian University as a result of the Russian drone strike. The Faculty of Music building was almost completely gutted by the fire, while neighboring teaching facilities had windows smashed, he added.
Oleksandr Koval, head of Rivne Oblast Military Administration, said on Oct. 13 that the drone strike damaged the second floor of the building. The fire in the building had been contained, and emergency services were on site.
"All victims are receiving medical assistance. Rescuers, police, the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU), and municipal services are working at the scene," Koval said .
According to the university, all students were in shelters at the moment of the attack. There were casualties amongst the university's administrative staff.
At around 10:35 a.m., Ukraine's air force had reported a jet-powered drone flying over Rivne. The air alert was issued in the city at 10:10 a.m.

title: 'Even isolated Shahed strikes cause power and water outages' — Zelensky criticizes Kyiv's preparedness for Russian attacks
body:
President Volodymyr Zelensky criticized Kyiv's preparedness for Russian attacks on Oct. 13, saying the capital is staying behind other Ukrainian regions in implementing resilience plans aimed at keeping essential services running during the heating season.
"As of mid-October, virtually across the entire country — even in border and frontline regions — the implementation of resilience plans is further advanced than in Kyiv," Zelensky said in a statement following a meeting of the Staff of the Supreme Commander-in-Chief on Oct. 12.
"And Kyiv residents certainly feel it — when even isolated hits by Shaheds cause electricity and water outages across large parts of the capital," he added.
Zelensky said he had begun consultations on urgent security and administrative measures to address the situation and accelerate the implementation of Kyiv's resilience plan.
The proposed measures include strengthening the protection of energy facilities and critical infrastructure, coordinating efforts with the government and military, and introducing changes to Kyiv's governance procedures.
Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko rejected accusations that the city's authorities had failed to prepare for the heating season.
"Unfounded accusations are being made about an alleged failure of the heating season, spread by outlets linked to the central government," Klitschko wrote on Telegram on Oct. 13.
The mayor also accused the central authorities of attempting to undermine local self-government by removing community leaders on what he described as fabricated grounds.
"The people elected me, and I am working, doing everything possible under extremely difficult conditions to justify the trust of Kyiv residents and keep the city functioning amid constant devastating enemy attacks," Klitschko said.
Russian strikes have repeatedly disrupted essential services in the capital in recent days.
On Oct. 8, Russian attacks left much of Kyiv without electricity and water, disrupting metro services. The city faced further power and water outages on Oct. 11 as Russia continued targeting Ukraine's energy infrastructure.
Ukraine introduced nationwide energy resilience plans in March to protect critical infrastructure, repair damaged facilities, and install backup power and heating systems ahead of winter.

title: Shell to sell Nigeria domestic gas business to Vaaris Energy
body: By Faith Odukomaiya Shell Petroleum B.V. has signed an agreement to sell its full interest in Shell Nigeria Gas Group to Vaaris Energy Limited, a Nigerian energy company, as the oil major refocuses its investments on strategic businesses. Shell’s Country Chair in Nigeria, Elohor Aiboni, said the transaction would provide a platform for the domestic gas distribution business to grow under new ownership. “Shell Nigeria Gas has served industrial and commercial customers in Nigeria for more than 25 years, supported by the commitment and expertise of its people,” Aiboni said. “We believe this agreement provides a much stronger platform for the business’ next chapter under new ownership. Shell continues to focus on strategic Deepwater and Integrated Gas positions in Nigeria.” Established in 1998, Shell Nigeria Gas (SNG) supplies natural gas to industrial and commercial customers through about 170 kilometres of pipeline infrastructure across Ogun, Abia and Rivers states. It serves more than 130 connected customers. The transaction includes Shell Nigeria Gas Holding B.V., established in 2019, which holds all but one of the shares in Shell Nigeria Gas Limited. Shell said the sale was consistent with its strategy of simplifying its portfolio and concentrating investment on areas where it has competitive strengths. In Nigeria, the company will continue to focus on Deepwater and Integrated Gas, including its interest in Nigeria LNG. The proposed sale does not include Shell’s upstream gas production, liquefied natural gas (LNG) or international gas trading businesses. Vaaris Energy has interests across the oil and gas value chain and an existing operational presence in Nigeria. The transaction remains subject to regulatory conditions and approvals. Until completion, Shell Nigeria Gas Group will remain part of Shell and continue to serve its customers and operate as usual. The post Shell to sell Nigeria domestic gas business to Vaaris Energy appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Tinubu: Corruption Can’t Be Uprooted in Nigeria Without Independent, Reform Minded Bench
body: .Tasks judiciary to probe prosecution strategies, seal procedural gaps exploited by criminals Deji Elumoye in Abuja President Bola Tinubu has declared that the cankerworm called corruption on Nigeria can’t be uprooted without an independent and reform minded bench. Speaking on Tuesday in Abuja during the annual EFCC/NJI Capacity Building Workshop for Judges and Justices, Tinubu maintained that there will be no meaningful progress in uprooting graft “without an independent, progressive, and reform-minded Bench.” The President, represented at the occasion by Vice President Kashim Shettima, while commending the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) for convening the 8th edition of the Judges and Justices Workshop said the workshop with the theme, “Investigation and Prosecution of Economic and Financial Crimes in a Digital Age,” was timely and necessary in “fostering the institutional cohesion required to confront corruption’s ever-changing architecture in Nigeria. “My Lords, we confront a rapidly shifting criminal landscape. Technology has amplified the audacity and reach of illicit actors, ushering in sophisticated crimes driven by destructive ingenuity. The rise of blockchain technology and artificial intelligence has introduced unprecedented layers of complexity to traditional illicit activities. “Because these modern crimes constantly mutate, law enforcement and judicial authorities must continuously build capacity to adapt and respond effectively,” he stated. Tinubu also tasked the judiciary to dismantle the procedural loopholes and flawed prosecution tactics that allow for criminals to escape justice. He demanded an aggressive overhaul of the justice system to ensure that no well-connected individual can manipulate technicalities to evade the full, crushing weight of the law. The President urged the judiciary to interrogate existing statutory frameworks against the backdrop of emerging financial crimes. “Probe prosecution strategies, dismantle outdated precedents, and seal procedural gaps that politically exposed persons and organised crime actors exploit to delay or frustrate trial,” he stated. Tinubu warned that while financial and economic crimes pose an existential threat to Nigeria, corruption has no respect for status and spares no arm of government. According to him, framing the anti-corruption campaign as purely an executive agenda is a fundamental error because compromised public services equally affect the executive, legislature, judiciary, and ordinary citizens. Noting that corruption is a battle for the nation’s collective survival, the President said, “We must no longer permit legal pyrotechnics and procedural pedantry to shelter criminality. The Bench is not merely a mechanical arbiter of rules, but an active guardian of moral order and social equity. “Law is, by design, an instrument of social engineering; it must invariably prioritise the public good over narrow, selfish interests shielded by technical manoeuvres. Our courts must embody the spirit, and not just the arid letter, of the law.” Tinubu urged the judiciary to adapt to the shifting dynamics of financial crime, stressing that realigning the nation’s investigative and prosecutorial strategies is critical to preventing institutional obsolescence. According to him: “We are already on the right trajectory. The EFCC’s recent momentum in tackling cryptocurrency fraud and its commendable strides in recovering virtual assets are highly reassuring. The agency has recovered billions of naira in cryptocurrency investment-related fraud cases. “In 2025, the agency secured the forfeiture of $22,417.91 (Twenty-Two Thousand, Four Hundred and Seventeen Dollars, Ninety-One Cents) worth of Bitcoin; 1,001,301.87 USDT (One Million, One Thousand, Three Hundred and One USDT and Eighty-Seven Cents) in digital assets; and US$5.6 million linked to the CBEX scheme, while 192 foreigners arrested for cyber-terrorism and cryptocurrency fraud were successfully prosecuted and deported afterwards.” The President observed that while EFCC’s actions shows agency that is proactive, forward-looking and resolved not to be outpaced by technological innovation, the judiciary “must complement law enforcement by rapidly upscaling its capacity.” He acknowledged efforts by the Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN) in reforming the judiciary, even as he pledged the full support of the executive arm of government to ensure that the Nigerian judiciary is adequately equipped to meet the demands of justice delivery in the digital age.” Earlier, Chief Justice of Nigeria, Hon. Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, said the 8th edition of the event reflects the commitment of the NJI and EFCC to sustain efforts aimed at addressing challenges confronting stakeholders in Nigeria’s justice system. She said the trend in technology has impacted how digital evidence is obtained and recorded, noting that the effective administration of criminal justice in the digital era require firm and disciplined case management which, according to her, capacity building programmes such as the EFCC and NJI collaboration, aims to strengthen. The CJN noted that sustained judicial education and capacity development in the justice sector was yielding positive results with the improved conduct of judicial officers especially judges in case management and the dispensation of justice in recent years. Also speaking, Senate Committee Chairman on AntiCorruption and Financial Crimes, Senator Emmanuel Udende, said the timing of the workshop was apt given the increasing sophistication of financial crimes and corruption particularly cases involving politically exposed persons, which directly impact timely case management and the dispensation of justice. He assured the stakeholders that the National Assembly remained committed to supporting the enhancement of the war against corruption and financial crimes in Nigeria through proactive legislation. On his part, the Minister of Justice and Attorney General of the Federation, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, who was represented by the Director of Public Prosecution, Mr Rotimi Oyedepo, urged synergy among stakeholders in addressing emerging challenges in Nigeria’s fight against corruption, stating that one arm of government alone could not effectively address the problem. He urged judicial officers especially judges and lawyers to leverage opportunities provided during the workshop to enhance their capacities to make investigation more thorough and prosecution more diligent. In his welcome address, Administrator of the National Judicial Institute, Justice Babatunde Adejumo, said the collaboration between the EFCC and the NJI in enhancing the capacity of judicial officers has become an integral part of government’s efforts to frontally tackle the dynamics and scale of financial crimes in the digital age. He said the presence of the Vice President at the event was a practical demonstration of the commitment of the Tinubu administration to boost Nigeria’s war against corruption. Also, Executive Chairman of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), Mr. Ola Olukoyede, said the event was a national imperative that has become an important component of the annual programme of both the EFCC and the NJI. He said the commission under his leadership was reform minded and has recorded unprecedented convictions as well as financial recoveries over the past three years, assuring that transparent and judicious handling of recovered money and property. The EFCC chairman also regretted the impact of advanced technology on financial crimes as well as other forms of corruption, noting that digital innovation was fast outpacing legal instruments and provisions for prosecution.

title: Minister orders suspension of Obuasi SHS headmaster over alleged sexual misconduct following JoyNews investigation
body: The Minister of Education has directed the immediate suspension of the Headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School, Zakaria Abdulai, over allegations of sexual misconduct involving a female student. According to a statement issued by the Ministry of Education, the directive follows a yet-to-be-aired investigation by JoyNews and Manasseh Azure Awuni into the allegations against the headmaster. Inside the Dreaded Headmaster’s Bungalow! https://t.co/J0Nj9OGbJ3 — Manasseh Azure Awuni (@Manasseh_Azure) October 13, 2026 The Ministry said the Minister had instructed the Director-General of the Ghana Education Service (GES) to take immediate steps to suspend Mr Abdulai pending a full investigation into the matter. The Minister has also requested the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) Headquarters of the Ghana Police Service to commence investigations. The Ministry of Education and the GES reiterated their position that alleged misconduct of this nature would not be tolerated in educational institutions across the country. The statement, signed by the Ministry’s Press Secretary, Hashmin Mohammed, stressed that parents and guardians entrust their children to teachers, whose responsibility is to protect and safeguard them rather than abuse them. The suspension is intended to allow investigations into the allegations to proceed.

title: Reps Panel Passes Vote of Confidence in Tinubu, NNPCL, PINL Over Pipeline Security Gains
body: Juliet Akoje In Abuja. The House of Representatives Committee on Host Communities has passed a vote of confidence in President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, management of NNPC Limited, Pipeline Infrastructure Nigeria Limited (PINL) and its Managing Director, Dr. Osahon Okunbor, following reported improvements in pipeline security, crude oil recovery and production. The decision followed the adoption of a subcommittee report on a petition against PINL at a special sitting of the committee on Tuesday. The report recommended an extension of the Federal Government’s pipeline surveillance contract with PINL and declared that the allegations levelled against the company and its managing director were not substantiated. The petition, dated September 5, 2026, was submitted by the Niger Delta Oil-Producing Communities Reform Movement (ND-OCRIM). The group alleged irregularities in the implementation of PINL’s contract, mismanagement of contract funds, the need for a forensic audit of the company’s finances, personal expenditure attributed to its managing director and neglect of surveillance personnel. However, the subcommittee reported that the petitioners failed to honour three invitations issued on September 14, September 22 and October 5, 2026. It also noted that they neither sent representatives to appear before the panel nor presented documentary evidence to substantiate their claims. In contrast, PINL appeared before the subcommittee and submitted a written report titled The Impact of PINL Operations on Oil Production and Stability of the Niger Delta, supported by geotagged photographic evidence of its operations. After reviewing the submissions before it, the subcommittee concluded that the allegations against PINL and Dr. Okunbor remained unsubstantiated. It consequently recommended the dismissal of the petition, the discontinuation of further investigations into the allegations and formal recognition of the company’s contributions to pipeline protection. The report also recommended a vote of confidence in President Tinubu, the National Security Adviser, the management of NNPC Limited and the pipeline surveillance contractors identified in the report. Among the key achievements presented to the subcommittee was a significant increase in the volume of crude oil reaching the Bonny Terminal through the Trans Niger Pipeline (TNP). According to PINL’s submission, the proportion of crude reaching the terminal rose from three per cent in May 2022 to 98 per cent in September 2026. The subcommittee further noted that Oil Mining Lease (OML) 11, which had remained shut for 18 months, resumed operations within 90 days of PINL’s engagement. The report also documented the remediation of 2,049 illegal pipeline connections and the destruction of 1,010 illegal refinery clusters. PINL stated that its operations commenced in August 2022 and covered 215 host communities, with a workforce of more than 35,600 surveillance guards. The operations were supported by 28 forward bases, 130 boats, 175 vehicles, 25 drones and 454 personnel from government security agencies. On community development, the report highlighted the company’s provision of more than 5,000 scholarships, vocational and skills training for over 4,000 women and girls, and flood relief assistance to more than 10 communities in Rivers State. The committee also commended the management of NNPC Limited for creating an enabling environment for pipeline security operations. It urged PINL to maintain its engagement with host communities while giving sustained attention to the welfare of surveillance personnel. The lawmakers’ resolution comes as the Federal Government continues efforts to stabilise the oil and gas sector and increase crude oil production, a critical source of government revenue and foreign exchange earnings. Production figures attributed to the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) put Nigeria’s crude oil output at approximately 1.50 million barrels per day in August 2026, while production including condensates stood at about 1.68 million barrels per day. Average output also reportedly increased from approximately 1.388 million barrels per day in the first quarter of 2026 to 1.525 million barrels per day in the second quarter. Despite the reported gains, crude oil production remained below the 2026 budget benchmark of 1.84 million barrels per day. The shortfall highlights the need to sustain measures aimed at protecting oil and gas infrastructure, combating crude oil theft and bringing shut-in production back on stream. To consolidate the reported achievements, the subcommittee recommended that the Federal Government extend PINL’s pipeline surveillance contract. It also urged the company to sustain its operational performance and continue implementing community development initiatives. The report will however be presented to the full House of Representatives for consideration and adoption.

title: PMMC was turned around by end of 2024 before GoldBod’s establishment – Awuah
body: Former Managing Director of the Precious Minerals Marketing Company (PMMC), Nana Akwasi Awuah, has defended his tenure, insisting that the company had been turned around by the end of 2024 before the establishment of its successor, the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod). In a statement issued on Tuesday, October 13, 2026, Mr Awuah said the final financial audit reports covering PMMC’s books from 2020 to 2024 demonstrated that the company had struggled during the period but had made significant progress by the close of 2024. “It is instructive to note that the final audit reports over the years in question demonstrate a struggling PMMC which was eventually turned around by year end of 2024,” he said. His comments follow GoldBod’s engagement with Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee, during which a report indicated that PMMC’s accounts had not been audited for the years 2020 to 2024 until the new management requested an audit in 2025. Mr Awuah disputed the impression that the audits were initiated only after the change in management, stating that he had written to the Auditor-General on September 2, 2024, to request a comprehensive audit of the company’s accounts for the five-year period. He said the process was delayed by bureaucratic challenges associated with appointing a new external auditor, adding that the Auditor-General’s team began work in September 2024 after receiving the request. The final audit reports were subsequently concluded, signed and submitted in April and June 2025, he said. Mr Awuah also pointed to a performance audit conducted by the Auditor-General in 2023, which he described as the first of its kind at PMMC in about two decades. He maintained that the company’s turnaround by the end of 2024 established a firm foundation for GoldBod’s creation, pushing back against any suggestion that the previous management had failed to initiate the audit process.

title: 'Yallah!': Whoop chief celebrates debut of app's Arabic option
body: Whoop 's decision to provide an Arabic option on its platform is part of a broader commitment to the Middle East, its Egyptian-American chief executive Will Ahmed has said. Arabic has joined English, French, German, Latin American Spanish, European Portuguese and Italian as languages available on the wearable fitness tracker company's app. Mr Ahmed said the addition of Arabic was meaningful for him. “My father is Egyptian and immigrated to the United States, and when I was younger I had the fortune of being able to travel with him throughout the Middle East,” he told The National . “I think the first time I visited the UAE was when I was 14 or 15, and I’ve been coming back to the region ever since.” Whoop is now available in Arabic. The GCC has been the fastest-growing region for us globally. And we will continue to invest there. YALLAH!!! pic.twitter.com/6TAVBoxj0v — Will Ahmed (@willahmed) October 13, 2026 He added that the Gulf was “our fastest-growing market globally” and said the company viewed the expansion of wearable use in the region as “a critical footprint for growth”. “Launching the Whoop experience in Arabic is part of our wider commitment to residents of the GCC, giving native speakers access to personal health insights in the language they use every day,” Mr Ahmed said. Though some technology companies have struggled to implement the nuances and diversity of Arabic , Mr Ahmed said that Whoop spent a lot of time working closely with Arabic-speaking members to ensure that the launch would be seamless. “Their feedback helped us identify where we could improve and get the details right,” he said. The Arabic language option will be rolled out gradually and will be available in the most recent version of the company's app. Whoop's co-founder also said he viewed the region as quick to embrace the idea that technology can empower people to take care of their health. His Boston-based company shares that vision, he added. “Our continued commitment to the GCC comes from a deep respect for the leadership in the region and what they’re trying to accomplish,” he said. On Tuesday, the company announced the launch of the Arabic option with a video posted to its social media accounts showing users throughout the Middle East working out while wearing Whoop devices . “Yallah!” posted Mr Ahmed as he shared the video. He launched Whoop in 2012 into a crowded wearable technology market. The company has grown steadily, amassing a loyal following, particularly among professional athletes. خبر حلو لمستخدمين اساور Whoop اخيراً التطبيق صار يدعم اللغه العربيه ، واذا ما وصلت عندك تاكد انك محدث التطبيق وبيوصل بالتدريج للجميع 👌 pic.twitter.com/v9p1Paayze — بدر منصور (@Gamee_tech) October 13, 2026 In a recent interview with The National , Dr Ami Bhatt, who joined Whoop as its first chief medical officer in July, said she was encouraged to see that more women across the Middle East were turning to the company's devices as a way to better understand their health. “Across the GCC , female member growth has increased more than 90 per cent year-over-year, with strong growth across every market we track,” she said. Her comments about the Middle East echoed the sentiments of Mr Ahmed, who in August said the fitness-tracker company would open a second office in the UAE, calling the move “critical for growth”. In March, Whoop announced $575 million in funding from a group of international investors led by Abu Dhabi and Qatari sovereign wealth funds. The Series G round was led by three Gulf investors: Mubadala Investment Company, 2PointZero Group and the Qatar Investment Authority. Whoop partners with fitness initiatives such as the Dubai Fitness Challenge and Doha Marathon. It also “serves as the official health and performance wearable” of UAE Team Emirates-XRG and Al Nassr Football Club. The company was at the centre of controversy during this year's Australian Open when officials made tennis players, including Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner, remove their Whoop devices. “Data is not steroids,” Mr Ahmed posted on his X account in protest. In April, Mr Ahmed hailed announcements that Whoops can be worn in the French Open, Wimbledon and US Open.

title: Nigeria Elected into UN Human Rights Council
body: Michael Olugbode in Abuja Nigeria has been elected into the United Nations Human Rights Council by the United Nations General Assembly. The country scored 172 votes out of 181 to get a place in the Council of 15 members expected to serve from 2027 to 2029. Other countries elected into the Council are Brazil, Burundi, Dominican Republic, Germany, Ghana, Ireland, Japan, Jordan, Kuwait, Nepal, Republic of Moldovan, Ukraine, Uruguay and Zambia. The roles of the United Nations Human Rights Council (UNHRC) include: Protection of human rights around the world: Promote respect for human rights by all countries; Investigate human rights violations and abuses; Recommend solutions to human rights problems; Review countries’ human rights records regularly; Protect vulnerable groups, including women, children and minorities; Promote equality and fight discrimination. Encourage international cooperation on human rights issues; Support human rights education and awareness and; Respond to emergencies involving serious human rights violations. The benefits of being elected into the UN Human Rights Council include international recognition; influence in decision-making; stronger diplomacy; promotion of national interests; improved human rights protection; greater global visibility; sharing experiences and increased responsibility. Meanwhile, Nigeria Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Dr Jimoh Ibrahim, has sent a congratulatory message to President Bola Tinubu on the election of the country into the council.

title: Saudi attack on Yemeni oil company amounts to war crime
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 13 (MNA) – The Yemeni Sanaa government spokesman described the Saudi attack on the headquarters of the Yemeni Oil Company in Sanaa as a "flagrant war crime" and assured the people of the country not to worry about fuel supplies.
According to Lebanese Al-Mayadeen, the Yemeni government spokesman Omar al-Bukhaiti described the Saudi attack on the oil company in the Al-Sabah district of ​​Sanaa as a "blatant war crime."
According to the report, Omar Al-Bukhiti emphasized that the targeted facilities in Sanaa were empty.
This senior Yemeni official noted that the supply of oil products in the country is stable and will cover the needs of citizens for a long time.
Saudi Arabia targeted the headquarters of the Yemeni Oil Company in the Al-Sabah, located in the Bani Matar district, west of Sanaa, with an airstrike on Tuesday evening.
In response to the attack, the Yemeni armed forces have issued an evacuation warning for King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, the Aramco refinery in Riyadh, and the company's oil facilities in Dhahran.

title: Ukraine base load power prices drop 27% in early Sept, continuing slide
body:
The BASE baseload electricity price index on the Day-Ahead Market (DAM) for the first 10 days of October 2026 stood at UAH 4,197.36 per MWh, 27% below the price for the same period in September (UAH 5,748.97 per MWh).
Thus, according to data from JSC Market Operator, the indicator continued its sharp downward trend for the second consecutive month, as the BASE index fell by 22.1% in the first 10 days of September compared with the same period in August.
Meanwhile, the weighted average electricity trading price on the DAM during the first 10 days of October was recorded at UAH 4,502.75 per MWh, down 21.1% from the first 10 days of the previous month (UAH 5,705.94 per MWh).
At the same time, on the Intraday Market (IDM), the weighted average price of electricity accepted for trading during the first 10 days of October was UAH 3,956.13 per MWh, 37% below the weighted average price recorded in the first 10 days of September, at UAH 6,277.75 per MWh.
"Electricity trading volume on the DAM for the first 10 days of October 2026 totaled 560,723.50 MWh, while 84,472.90 MWh was accepted for trading on the IDM," Market Operator reported.
Compared with the first 10 days of September 2026, trading volumes declined in the first 10 days of October by 26.71% on the DAM and by 24.63% on the IDM.
At the same time, according to former Ukrainian Energy Minister Olha Buslavets, electricity prices at Ukraine's western border increased by an average of 28% on weekdays last week compared with the previous week's figures.
The largest increase was recorded in Hungary, where the average price reached EUR 230 per MWh, 42% above the weekly figure. In other countries, weekday baseload prices ranged from EUR 139 per MWh in Poland to EUR 225 per MWh in Romania.
According to ENTSO-E, during the first 10 days of October, as well as in September and August, Ukraine did not rank first in terms of the highest daily average BASE price index on the DAM when compared with 26 European countries.
Moreover, on October 8, Ukraine recorded the lowest DAM price in Europe.
At the same time, Ukraine topped the European BASE index rankings once in July this year, three times in June, four times in May, 11 times in April, 15 times in March, 21 times in February and 14 times in January.
As reported, the BASE index on the DAM for the first 10 days of September 2026 stood at UAH 5,748.97 per MWh, 22.1% below the price for the same period in August (UAH 7,377.22 per MWh).
Based on its 2025 BASE index on the DAM, calculated using a unified Central European Time (CET) basis, Ukraine ranked second among 27 European countries, with an index of UAH 5,292.62 per MWh.

title: Inside the ‘unique’ tail of Iran’s spider-tailed horned viper
body: The Iranian spider-tailed horned viper, a rare snake endemic to western Iran, hunts by holding its body completely still while twitching its tail. Its body camouflages among the rocks of its semi-arid Zagros Mountains habitat, but its bulbous tail with accompanying leg-like scales looks remarkably like a large chunky spider. The snake, Pseudocerastes urarachnoides, uses its spider tail to lure unsuspecting mammals and birds to their last meal. Scans of a specimen collected in 1968 and kept in the Field Museum of Natural History in Illinois, United States, now reveal what the lure is made of. “The tip actually consists of enlarged, elongated and modified scales, which are unique among all living reptiles,” lead author Georgios Georgalis, an associate professor at the Polish Academy of Sciences’ Institute of Systematics and Evolution of Animals in Kraków, Poland, told Mongabay by email. The scanned P. urarachnoides specimen. Image © Georgalis et al. (2026). Vipers have attracted the interest of researchers for centuries, Georgalis said, but knowledge of the group’s morphology is still limited. Scientists described P. urarachnoides for science in 2006, but only this year did they publish a high-resolution 3D scan to see the mechanism inside the snake’s tail as part of a scientific study. The tail filaments, the authors said, loosely resemble those found on some ornithodiran archosaurs and other forms from the Triassic and Jurassic periods. This doesn’t mean that they are related, it’s more likely a case of convergent evolution: similar environmental demands pushing the evolutionary development of similar characteristics.…This article was originally published on Mongabay

title: US places Nigeria among countries allowing recruitment of child soldiers
body:
The United States has placed Nigeria on its 2026 list of countries whose governments are identified as having armed forces, security forces or government-supported militias that recruit or use child soldiers, exposing the country to restrictions on certain US military assistance and equipment sales.
The designation, contained in the US State Department’s 2026 Trafficking in Persons (TIP) Report, means Nigeria could face restrictions on specific security assistance and commercial licences for military equipment from 1 October, unless the restrictions are waived or an applicable exception is granted by US President Donald Trump.
Nigeria is among 14 countries included on the 2026 Child Soldiers Prevention Act (CSPA) list, alongside Afghanistan, Burma, the Central African Republic, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Ethiopia, Iran, Russia, Rwanda, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Venezuela and Yemen.
Under Section 402 of the CSPA, the US government identifies foreign governments whose armed forces, police, other security forces or government-supported armed groups allegedly recruit or use child soldiers. The latest determinations cover 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026.
The law prohibits certain forms of assistance to listed governments, including International Military Education and Training, Foreign Military Financing and Excess Defence Articles. It also restricts the issuance of licences for direct commercial sales of military equipment, subject to applicable exceptions and presidential waivers.
The restrictions could have implications for Nigeria’s military cooperation with Washington, particularly in areas involving training, financing and the acquisition of US military equipment.
The State Department said its determination draws on multiple sources, including observations by US government personnel, United Nations agencies, international organisations, civil society groups and local and international media reports.
Under the CSPA, a child soldier includes anyone under 18 who is compulsorily recruited into government armed forces or security forces, as well as children recruited or used in hostilities by armed forces distinct from a state’s military.
The definition also covers children serving in support roles, including as cooks, porters, messengers, medics, guards or victims of sexual exploitation.
Nigeria’s inclusion on the list comes amid longstanding concerns about the recruitment and exploitation of children in the country’s conflict zones, particularly in the North-east, where Boko Haram and the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) have abducted and recruited children for combat and support roles.
The designation does not, however, establish that the Nigerian military or security services recruit or use child soldiers.
The listing places pressure on the Nigerian government to address concerns over child recruitment and demonstrate compliance with international standards on the protection of children in armed conflict.

title: Wike’s appointment as campaign coordinator is internal party affairs – Rivers APC
body: By Davies Iheamnachor, PORT HARCOURT The All Progressives Congress, APC, in Rivers State has welcomed the appointment of the Minister of Federal Capital Territory, Chief Nyesom Wike, by its national leadership to head the coordination of the Presidential Campaign in the state. title: Zelensky says Western partners didn’t warn Ukraine about Russian ballistic missile launches before latest attack on Kyiv
body: Ukraine received no intelligence from its Western partners about Russia’s October 12 missile strike on Kyiv, President Volodymyr Zelensky said . “Unfortunately, we received no early warning from our partners about this strike. Intelligence on Russian ballistic missile launches helps save lives, and this is one of the most critical issues. This is precisely what helps prevent people from being killed,” he said on social media. Russia attacked Kyiv with five ballistic missiles on the evening of October 12. Ukrainska Pravda reported that radar detected the missiles during the attack, and the city’s air raid alert sounded only after the first explosions. The Ukrainian Air Force said it had received no information about missile launches from Russian territory. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha attributed the delayed alert to “a particular type of weapon used by Russia.” He said Kyiv and Washington continue to share intelligence. Air Force spokesperson Yurii Ihnat said similar situations had occurred before. “Sometimes this information doesn’t get through. This isn’t the first time… If there were some technical issues this time, I think the specialists will figure it out. And they’ll work with our partners to fix this problem,” he said. Serhii Beskrestnov, the president’s adviser on technological innovation in the Ukrainian armed forces, said the incident did not mean the United States had stopped sharing intelligence with Ukraine. Friends, this isn’t the first time our partners’ intelligence services have failed to detect an S-400 launch. There are some details to consider. We shouldn’t jump to conclusions. Beskrestnov said he did not believe Kyiv and Washington would stop sharing intelligence, since civilians’ lives were at stake. title: Specter Jet-Powered Drone Aims At Low Cost, Multi-Mission, Single Use
body: AEVEX Corp. has publicly shown its Specter jet-powered drone for the first time at the Association of the U.S. Army’s (AUSA) annual meeting in Washington, D.C., where TWZ is in attendance . The aircraft is the latest development from a company that has played a significant role in the U.S. military’s one-way attack drone efforts. Most notably, it built the secretive Phoenix Ghost family that was rushed to Ukraine in 2022. AEVEX announced Specter in September, describing it as a high-speed, low-cost, jet-powered autonomous platform designed for high-risk operational environments. The aircraft is being developed around a modular architecture, with ground-launched and air-launched variants planned. Its interchangeable nose section is intended to accommodate different payloads, including kinetic warheads, electronic warfare equipment, intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR) systems, and other future capabilities. The Specter jet-powered drone shown for the first time at the Association of the U.S. Army’s (AUSA) annual meeting in Washington, D.C. Jamie Hunter That flexibility is central to how AEVEX is pitching the aircraft. The company is aiming for an adaptable system that can be configured for different operational needs while remaining affordable enough to be used basically as a cruise missile in combat applications. The aircraft’s external configuration features a prominent V-shaped lower fuselage, high-mounted, unswept trapezoidal wings, a v-tail and rear-mounted conformal engine intakes. Clearly, low observability was one design driver for Specter, with the goal of balancing survivability with low-cost likely factored in heavily. AEVEX has not publicly discussed Specter’s low-observable characteristics. The company has also not disclosed key performance and technical details, including the aircraft’s range, payload capacity, communications architecture, terminal targeting methods or the extent of its autonomous capabilities. A rendering of the Specter in flight. AEVEX Corp. AEVEX Corp. “We’re really excited to kind of really up our stats on range and speed,” Craig Anders, an AEVEX representative, told TWZ at AUSA, describing Specter’s turbine engine. The aircraft is being designed to reach speeds in the sub-Mach range, he said. Anders also elaborated on how Specter is intended to carry more than a conventional warhead. “This thing is going to have the ability to carry cameras and different types of non-kinetic effect payloads,” he said, describing it as a “multi-mission, multi-domain fighter.” Despite that broader mission set, attrition remains a core part of the concept. Anders said the idea was for the aircraft to be attritable, with a relatively low price tag allowing commanders to send it farther into dangerous areas without putting more expensive capabilities at risk. The distinction is important. Specter is not being presented simply as a disposable munition, nor as a high-end unmanned combat aircraft. Instead, AEVEX appears to be pursuing a middle ground: a jet-powered platform that can perform one-way attack missions but also support reconnaissance and provide other effects in high-threat areas, depending on its configuration. It is also meant to be built economically at scale. AEVEX is developing Specter with Divergent, an engineering and manufacturing company known for its digital production processes and metal additive manufacturing. The partnership is intended to help make the aircraft easier to manufacture at scale while supporting changes to its design and configuration. Anders said Divergent works with AEVEX engineers on the aircraft’s digital design and produces its fuselage. AEVEX is responsible for the internal systems, mission integration, flight characteristics and navigation science, he explained. The manufacturing approach is a significant part of the program’s affordability ambitions. AEVEX says Divergent’s Digital Manufacturing and Production System (DAPS) is being used to support scalable production and manufacturability. However, the companies have not disclosed Specter’s projected unit cost or demonstrated that it can yet be produced at the volumes and prices the concept ultimately requires. AEVEX is also drawing on its CompassX autonomy architecture and experience delivering thousands of autonomous systems. The company says Specter’s open interfaces and software-defined capabilities are intended to allow the platform to evolve as operational requirements change, rather than being optimized around one fixed mission. Specter remains in development, with its first flight planned for December 2026. Anders said the initial flight would be a basic test, with early test aircraft fitted with landing gear so they can be recovered and reused for work on flight characteristics and handling. It isn’t clear if a truly reusable gear-equipped operational version is eyed for the future. Regardless, further testing could include tuning the aircraft’s dive profile. The planned initial configuration uses a ground launch assisted by a rocket, or rocket-assisted takeoff (RATO), system. An air-launched version is also on the roadmap, Anders said, with that capability expected to follow in the relatively near term. AEVEX is pursuing several potential military applications. Anders identified the U.S. Army’s Family of Affordable Mass Missiles (FAMM) effort as a primary focus, while noting that the service has its own high-speed requirements. He also said the company is looking at opportunities associated with Rapid Dragon and other programs. In FY 2027, the US Air Force is requesting $55 Million in discretionary and $300 Million in mandatory (reconciliation) funds for the Family of Affordable Mass Missile (FAMM) to procure 1,000 All Up Rounds covering both the Palletized (FAMM-P) and Lugged (FAMM-L) variants. The… pic.twitter.com/EgVaefmJgY — Air-Power | NatSec Ledger (@NatSecLedger) April 22, 2026 Those comments indicate the range of applications AEVEX hopes Specter could address, not that the aircraft has been selected for any of them. Its performance, cost and ability to meet specific requirements will need to be demonstrated as development and testing progress. Specter’s intended combination of jet propulsion, attritability and modular payloads could offer an enticing balance. It is not being presented as a higher-end ‘exquisite’ cruise missile, but neither is it limited to carrying a single payload type. The challenge for AEVEX will be delivering enough speed, range and mission flexibility to make the aircraft useful across multiple roles without pushing its price beyond what operators can justify for procuring it in large numbers. A stealthy weapon that is jet-powered like Specter, one that can be configured for various types of one-way missions, could bridge the gap between far more advanced and costly autonomous aircraft and cruise missiles and lower-end one-way attack drones. There have been other concepts that are similar to Specter, we are living in a low-cost cruise missile explosion of sorts, but the company’s unique pedigree of innovation and fast fielding in the one-way attack munition space could give Specter additional credence.
