title: Katie Zacharia's White House debut: Three reporters, 13 minutes, and a Freudian slip - analysis
body: It took Katie Zacharia approximately 13 minutes to offer a first glimpse of how she intends to handle one of the most visible jobs in Washington.Making her debut as White House press secretary on Tuesday morning, Zacharia praised President Donald Trump, called on just three reporters, delivered a significant announcement about the future of the US ambassador to Greece, and offered a brief, unexpectedly amusing glimpse of her nerves when she accidentally referred to her husband as "my president."The new press secretary, who succeeded Karoline Leavitt, appeared visibly excited as she stepped up to the podium in the James S. Brady Press Briefing Room. Her voice occasionally sounded tense, with audible breaths between sentences, but she maintained a smile and made her central message unmistakable: She had long wanted to work for Donald Trump."I have wanted to work for him for a very long time," Zacharia said, thanking the president for placing his trust in her.Anyone expecting a lengthy introductory exchange between the new spokesperson and the White House press corps, however, was in for a short encounter.Much of the briefing was devoted to prepared remarks highlighting what Zacharia described as the administration's accomplishments, from wages and prescription drug prices to energy production, foreign investment, manufacturing and border security."President Trump is fighting and delivering for American workers every minute of every day," she declared.With just three weeks remaining until the midterm elections, Zacharia also devoted considerable attention to Trump's campaign rallies, describing record attendance and growing enthusiasm among Republican voters.Three reporters, and little room for improvisationWhen Zacharia finally opened the floor to questions, only three reporters were called upon: Nick Gilbertson of the conservative Breitbart News, Fox News correspondent Peter Doocy, and Elina Shirazi of the Daily Mail.The selection was notable not only because of the outlets represented, but also because of the way the briefing unfolded. Zacharia called on the reporters directly, by name, rather than inviting questions from the room more broadly.There was no indication that the exchanges had been arranged in advance, but the carefully managed format left little room for spontaneous participation by the rest of the press corps.The first question came from Gilbertson, occupying the White House's designated new media seat.After praising Leavitt for opening the briefing room to voices beyond traditional news organizations, Gilbertson asked whether Zacharia intended to continue that approach."My predecessor Karoline Leavitt did an incredible job," she replied. "We are absolutely going to keep it, and we're going to expand on it to the extent possible. We love new media, and we want to be able to embrace it."Asked whether Trump's campaign schedule would intensify ahead of the elections, she answered without hesitation."Absolutely, you can expect more of the midterm blitz."She added that Kentucky had been included in the president's upcoming travel schedule, alongside stops in Georgia and Florida.Where does White House messaging end and campaigning begin?The most substantive question about Zacharia's new role came from Doocy, the Fox News correspondent.He pointed out that she was taking office just three weeks before midterm elections that Trump himself had described as challenging for Republicans."Is your job just to speak about White House matters, or is it to make things less tough for Republicans in the midterms?" Doocy asked.Zacharia did not draw a clear distinction between the two responsibilities."Well, but Peter, I get to do what I was doing on the outside already, which was hoping to amplify, multiply, and expand upon President Trump's incredible agenda for the American people," she replied.She said her aim was to communicate the administration's achievements more effectively, working closely with a president who, in her words, "is his own best spokesperson."Her answer suggested that, at least in her understanding of the role, promoting the president's agenda and helping communicate his political successes are closely intertwined.Doocy then switched to a more direct foreign policy question: Had the United States stopped sharing intelligence with Ukraine?"I'll have to get back to you on that," Zacharia replied.A major announcement: Guilfoyle asked to resignThe briefing's most significant news came in response to a question from Shirazi, who asked about Kimberly Guilfoyle, the US ambassador to Greece.Trump had said the previous day that he was considering firing Guilfoyle amid reports raising questions about her conduct.Shirazi asked whether the administration had established a timeline for a potential dismissal and whether possible replacements were already being considered.Zacharia's response was brief but consequential."We have asked Ambassador Guilfoyle to resign," she announced. "She has been a wonderful asset to the team, and we wish her well."The statement marked a significant development in the controversy surrounding Guilfoyle, a former Fox News personality who was previously engaged to Donald Trump Jr.Reports had raised questions about her conduct in the role and her dealings with donors and business figures. Her attorneys have denied the allegations against her.For Zacharia, it was an unusually consequential announcement to deliver during a first appearance that otherwise focused heavily on celebrating the administration's achievements.My president, excuse me, my husbandThen the questions turned personal.Shirazi noted that Zacharia is the mother of four children and that her family had been living in California. She asked how the new press secretary intended to manage the demands of her White House position while raising a young family.She also asked whether Leavitt, who left her role to spend more time with her own family, had offered any advice.Zacharia became noticeably more animated."Well, first of all, I want to give my husband an amazing shout-out," she began.She explained that she has four children, aged 12, 10, 8 and 6, including three boys."I adore my family. I love them. They are my priority," she said, stressing that spending evenings with her children remained extremely important to her.Then came the moment that briefly interrupted the seriousness of the briefing."So my president, excuse me, my husband," Zacharia said, immediately correcting herself."That's a, that's a good one," she added.The slip was a small but revealing moment in an otherwise controlled debut, with the new press secretary apparently having her boss on her mind even while discussing her husband.Regaining her composure, Zacharia explained that her husband had brought all four children to Washington for the week because the family was celebrating two birthdays."We are very, very protective of celebrating birthdays as a family," she said.The family, she added, plans to relocate to Washington.Zacharia also spoke about stepping away from her professional career between 2014 and 2020 while raising her children, and how she later tried to incorporate family life into her work.She recalled bringing her children to the Fox News bureau, where they would sometimes sit beside her as she prepared for television appearances.Regarding her predecessor, Zacharia said Leavitt had been an important source of support and had offered advice on navigating the demands of the position.Still, she acknowledged that the job might not lend itself to a conventional work-life balance."I think this job is not one you necessarily balance," she said.She then found another opportunity to praise the president."President Trump is the most family-friendly president we've ever had," Zacharia declared.She argued that Trump's willingness to appoint her, knowing she had four children and that the role would be demanding, demonstrated his confidence in her ability to meet those responsibilities.Trump is heading to Alaska - and the briefing is overJust as the exchange became more personal, Zacharia brought the proceedings to an abrupt end."In fact, I am going to end it because President Trump is heading out to Marine One for our historic trip to Alaska, and we can ask him all of the questions out there," she said.The president was preparing to depart the White House for Joint Base Andrews, where Air Force One would take him to Alaska for another campaign rally.As Zacharia prepared to leave, reporters could still be heard attempting to ask additional questions, including whether Trump had personally spoken with Guilfoyle about her departure.But the new spokesperson was already wrapping up.And with that, her first White House briefing was over almost as quickly as it had begun.Zacharia, a conservative political commentator who served as a communications adviser to Trump Media & Technology Group before her appointment, enters the role at a particularly sensitive moment for the administration.Her predecessor, Leavitt, became one of the administration's most recognizable public faces before leaving to focus on her family. Zacharia now faces the task of establishing her own relationship with a press corps accustomed to frequent confrontations, rapid political developments and a president who regularly prefers to speak for himself.Whether Tuesday's tightly controlled, approximately 13-minute briefing represents a lasting approach or merely the caution of a first appearance remains to be seen.What was clear from the outset was Zacharia's determination to defend the president enthusiastically, emphasize his achievements, and leave the central stage to him whenever possible.And judging by that first slip of the tongue, Trump was rarely far from her thoughts - even when she was talking about her husband.

title: Kimberly Guilfoyle resigns as ambassador to Greece after allegations of misconduct
body:
Guilfoyle announced that her time in her post is "coming to an end."
U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle resigned from the role on Tuesday after reports of alleged misconduct.
White House press secretary Katie Zacharia said during a press briefing Tuesday morning that the White House had asked Guilfoyle to resign.
"We have asked Ambassador Guilfoyle to resign," Zacharia said during her first briefing as White House press secretary. "She has been a wonderful asset to the team and we wish her well."
In a social media post, Guilfoyle later announced that her time in her post is "coming to an end."
"It has been the honor of my lifetime to serve the United States of America. God bless President Trump, God bless our incredible diplomats and service members, and God bless the United States of America," Guilfoyle wrote.
Later Tuesday, a White House official confirmed it "has received Ms. Guilfoyle's formal resignation."
Guilfoyle, the former wife of California Gov. Gavin Newsom and ex-fiance of Donald Trump Jr., held the ambassador position for nearly a year.
President Donald Trump tried to distance himself from Guilfoyle on Tuesday. Guilfoyle was a prominent surrogate for the Trump campaign and attended both political and family events including Tiffany Trump's wedding.
"She wasn't a member of my family. She dated my son a long time ago," he told ABC News Senior Political Correspondent Rachel Scott, later adding, "we didn't like what we were reading."
After dating for several years, Guilfoyle and Donald Trump Jr. broke off their engagement in late 2024.
Trump said he had not spoken to Guilfoyle personally.
"I didn't speak to her. No, she will not be there. I didn't like what I read," Trump said.
Her resignation comes after a report that Guilfoyle allegedly offered a Trump donor access to top administration officials in exchange for cash.
Eric Deters -- a former lawyer, conservative media personality and Trump donor -- alleged that Guilfoyle asked him to pay her $100,000 credit card bill in July 2025, days before her Senate confirmation hearing. Deters provided messages to ABC News he says he exchanged with Guilfoyle on the subject.
Wall Street Journal first reported on Deters' accusations that Guilfoyle's alleged actions were a quid pro quo.
An attorney for Guilfoyle sent ABC News a statement after her resignation, saying the text messages "have not been authenticated." When ABC News asked if Guilfoyle was disputing the authenticity of the messages, her attorney responded they had "no comment as to authenticity as the texts have not been analyzed in their original form."
In their statement, Guilfoyle’s attorneys argue Deters owned their client "approximately $150,000 for speeches and consulting work she performed for him long before she was nominated to serve as Ambassador."
"That is what Mr. Deters now calls a 'quid pro quo': a delinquent client being asked to pay an overdue bill," they wrote.
Deters denies he owes Guilfoyle any money.
Asked whether he was considering firing Guilfoyle on Monday, Trump said he was.
"We're looking at it. Yeah, we're not happy," Trump said.
A series of controversies have surrounded Guilfoyle's ambassadorship, including a report earlier this week in the Wall Street Journal that she boasted about private jet trips that were bankrolled by Greek businessmen.
Guilfoyle said in a post on X, "These allegations are false, and I intend to vigorously defend my name, my reputation, and my integrity. I have dedicated my professional life to fighting for justice, standing up for what is right, and defending the values that make America exceptional. I will not allow false accusations to define my decades of public service."
A spokesperson for the U.S. Embassy in Athens earlier responded to the reports, saying that Guilfoyle has "faithfully followed State Department ethics and gift reporting guidelines."
Last week, Rep. Gregory Meeks, the top Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, called for Guilfoyle to be removed from her post after reports of her misconduct.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio, visiting Greece last week, was seen with Guilfoyle by his side during official meetings. The secretary refused to comment on the swirling reports, saying he didn't know if they were true or not.
The State Department's Office of Inspector General is investigating alleged misconduct by Guilfoyle, two officials told ABC News.
While the exact next steps for the probe aren't clear, the information gathered by the State OIG could be shared with the Department of Justice. If the DOJ doesn't launch an investigation of its own, the State Department IG could still continue with its own investigation.
U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia Jeanine Pirro said DOJ would wait for the IG's inquiry to play out.
"I think right now that there is an inspector general investigation in the Department of State," Pirro said. "We probably wait to see what, what happens with that."
ABC News' Shannon K. Kingston, Chris Boccia and Jay O'Brien contributed to this report.

title: Civilian data centers face massive pushback. Army says they won’t ‘repeat that mistake’
body: Army leaders said they’ve watched the public outcry around data centers and are planning to get ahead of it as the service signs agreements to host them on bases. In March, the Army announced that it selected two global investment firms to partner with to build and manage commercial data centers on underused land at Fort Bliss, Texas, and Dugway Proving Ground, Utah. Contracting documents also indicate plans for centers at Fort Bragg, North Carolina, and Fort Hood, Texas. Across the U.S., there are more than 1,300 data centers in operation and almost 2,600 other projects planned . Proposed projects in civilian communities have faced major public backlash, protests and in some cases have led to entire data centers being cancelled. According to Data Center Watch , $64 billion-worth of data center projects were blocked or delayed due to local opposition between May 2024 and March 2025. “We have definitely taken note of the struggles that developers have had outside the gate who have not adequately engaged with the communities,” W. Jordan Gillis, assistant secretary of the Army for Installations, Energy and Environment, said Monday at a roundtable with reporters at the Association of the United States Army convention in Washington, D.C. “We intend to not repeat that mistake.” Top Stories This Week News After two F-16 crashes, Air Force revamps how crews inspect a ‘blind spot’ By Matt White News Army Apache helicopter batters Alabama car show with rotor wash By Austin Campbell News Army activates its fourth multi-domain task force By Nicholas Slayton Gillis said any time the service has plans outside of “normal” military construction projects, they aim to engage with the military families on bases. When pressed for specifics on what that engagement would look like, Gillis said “don’t know yet,” but added that “you can imagine lots of community leadership roundtables, lots of community open houses.” Gillis said the Army or the private companies they’re working with have not broken ground on any of the projects and they’re still in the “agreement phase.” He said they don’t have any other projects to announce, but they’ll “continue to look at” other awards. The Army’s project would serve as civilian power generation and other Army needs. Former Secretary of the Army Dan Driscoll said the centers would be a “critical resource to support that strategic imperative.” Data centers supply infrastructure for a host of digital services like artificial intelligence, cloud storage and high-performance computing. But beyond local community pushback, federal lawmakers have also raised concerns about their strain on local energy grids and resources, and the degradation to surrounding environments. “It can do no harm, both to missions, families, to consultants, to installation, to our infrastructure,” Gillis said. “So we’re open to hosting them, and definitely support the national imperative to promulgate them and serve other users and the Army.” The post Civilian data centers face massive pushback. Army says they won’t ‘repeat that mistake’ appeared first on Task & Purpose .

title: Again, SERAP’s Appeal against N100m Judgment Stalls over Procedural Complications
body: *Panel returns file to presiding justice Alex Enumah in Abuja Hearing in the appeal by the Incorporated Trustees of the Socio-economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP), against a N100 million judgment debt, for the second time in less than one week failed to proceed as scheduled. Recall that SERAP and a Deputy Director, kolawole Ogundare, are in two separate appeals challenging the May 5 judgment of a High Court of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), which found them guilty of defamatory publication against the Department of State Service (DSS) and two of its officials. However, hearing in the appeals was bungled owing to some complications surrounding some applications brought by Ogundare’s lawyer. While the appeal filed by the Non-Governmental Organization is marked: CA/ABJ/CV/1114/2026, that of the deputy director is marked: CA/ABJ/CV/1105/2026. Just like last week Friday, the appellate court heard the case of SERAP and reserved judgment but had to abort further proceedings following their inability to comprehend and proceed with the sister case (Ogundare’s appeal). The development on Tuesday forced the three-member special panel led by Justice Justice Danlami Senchi to hands off from the trial and return the file to the Presiding Justice of the Abuja division of the Court of Appeal, for reassignment to another. It would be recalled that the special panel had slated October 9 for expeditious trial in the two appeals, seeking to reverse the guilty verdict and avoid the payment of the sum of N101 million as damages for defamation against agency and its two officials. The matter was stalled at the last hearing owing to late filing of the deputy director’s appeal against the judgment of the trial court. The appellate court subsequently adjourned to October 13, for hearing and possible adjournment for judgment but, this could not be realized as the panel had to return the file to the Presiding Justice, to be heard on a later date. After reserving judgment in the first appeal, the panel proceeded to hear that of the deputy director. His lawyer, Mr Oluwatosin Adesioye, sought the court’s permission to amend the reliefs in a pending application concerning additional records of appeal and an extension of time to appeal against the ruling and judgment of the lower court. Responding, the panel expressed reservations about the application, adding that the court was “finding it difficult to grant the prayers”. Senchi subsequently advised the counsel to refine the application owing to its complicated nature. Taking the hint from the court, Adesioye subsequently withdrew the application and sought for a short date to enable him amend the processes. But, the panel however noted that they don’t have the luxury of time hence, the decision to return the file to the Presiding Justice for reassignment. “All the two files are hereby returned to the Presiding Justice, Abuja Dvision… for decision on a date for hearing of both appeals that is going to be communicated to the parties,” Justice Senchi said. Adding that, “In the same breath, the earlier appeal numbered CA/ABJ/CV/1114/2026 and… the order reserving the appeal for judgment, is hereby vacated.” Earlier, a mild drama ensued when SERAP’s lead counsel, Tayo Oyetibo, SAN, informed the court that an application was before it for certain persons to be joined as amici curiae (friends if the court) in the appeal. When the court obliged the senior lawyer, Professor Olarewaju Fagbohun, SAN, a former Vice Chancellor of the University of Lagos, to address the court, Fagbohun introduced himself as representing the University of Columbus, acting through its Colombian Global Freedom of Expression Initiative United Nations Special Rapporteurs on Rights to freedom of Assembly and of association. He also told the court that he and other lawyers were of the United Nations Special Rapporteurs on the promotion and protection of rights to freedom of opinion and expression. However, the appellate court declined to entertain them on the grounds that the court did not invite them and that they were not parties both at the trial court and the instant court. “Did the court invite you? Let’s be serious. This is the kind of image we create that is not good for us. We didn’t invite you. On behalf of whom? You’re supposed to be a guide to the junior lawyers in court. “I said earlier that we are not here to speak long grammar or waste the court’s time. We didn’t seek for any assistance. We didn’t invite you,” Senchi declared. Taking a hint from the court, Professor Fagbohun promptly withdrew the application and apologized to the court. The withdrawal and apology promoted the judge to commend him, stressing, “your juniors here will be happy for that.” Apparently taking a cue from the professor, Mojirayo Ogunlana, who represented Southern African Litigation Centre, also withdrew her application to be the court’s amicus curiae. Recall that Justice Halilu Yusuf of the High Court of the FCT had on May 5, slammed a whopping N100 million as damages against SERAP and the deputy director for publishing defamatory materials against the DSS and two of its officials. The two officials, Sarah John and Gabriel Ogundele had in the suit marked: CV/4547/2024, accused SERAP and Oluwadare of making false claims in publications on the group’s website and social media platforms that the claimants invaded their Abuja office on September 9, 2024 and subjected them to harassment. Delivering judgment, Justice Yusuf held among others that claimants led sufficient evidence that effectively established all the ingredients of defamation. Justice Yusuf rejected the defence of justification raised by SERAP and Oluwadare on the grounds that they failed to provide evidence that their publications were not based on falsehood. The judge noted that the words like invasion, forceful entry and harassment were used inaccurately, the defendants having admitted at trial that the DSS officials did not forcefully enter into SERAP’s premises and did not brandish any weapon. He held that the publications made by the defendants injured the reputation of the claimants in their professional capacity and standing in the society. Justice Yusuf said: “Having been unable to establish invasion and harassment, the defence of justification fails. There is no doubt that the publication affected the claimants mentally and psychologically.” The judge said, going forward, it was necessary for care and due diligence on the part of SERAP and its officials before releasing information to the public. He added that in the exercise of their right to tweet and send information out, the defendants should be aware of the rights of others, particularly as it relates to government agencies and their officials. The judge dismissed the objection raised by the defendants against the competence of the suit and held that the claimants possessed the requisite locus standi to file the suit over which the court has the jurisdiction to entertain. He held that as against the defendants’ argument, the claimants must not be named in the publication complained about for defamation to be established. Justice Yusuf noted that from when the claimants complained about the inaccuracy of the publications, the defendants failed to take any steps to pull down the injurious publication. He proceeded to adjudge the publications as defamatory and awarded damages of N100 million against the defendants in addition to N1 million as cost of prosecuting the suit. The judge also ordered the defendants to publish a public apology on SERAP’s website, X handle, two national daily newspapers and two television stations. He held that the judgment sum shall attract 10 percent per annum from the date of the judgment until the sum is paid by the defendants.

title: US Army targets 2028 for first high-energy laser counter-drone weapons
body: The first directed energy weapon selected by the U.S. Army for the Enduring-High Energy Laser (E-HEL) program could be out of testing and ready for counter-drone operations by early 2028, Army officials told Military Times at the Association of the U.S. Army’s annual meeting in Washington. “We would love to be able to keep the first unit off the line for our testing and training. However, what we’ve seen is, with the environment as it is, everything that we produce as a capable counter-UAS system tends to get deployed somewhere,” said Kirk Williams, chief engineer at the U.S. Army Directed Energy Project Office. In September, the Army awarded AeroVironment a $464.8 million contract for LOCUST X3, its modular, palletized high-energy laser system. Earlier generations of the LOCUST system are actively fielded in operational environments, including at the U.S. southern border, according to AeroVironment. The first LOCUST X3 is slated for delivery by Q4 of FY 2027 and will be mounted on the Joint Light Tactical Vehicle. The goal is to push it through testing, validation, verification and “give it to soldiers as soon as possible,” said Brig. Gen. Guy Yelverton, capability program executive for Defensive Fires. “My far-down point would be spring [2028], and if I could get in the December-January timeframe, that would be awesome. That would be a great win for the Army.” It is unclear where the first high-energy counter-drone weapons under H-ELS will be deployed. Yelverton suggested the 7th Infantry Division could be a potential partner. Deputy commanding officer of Support for the 7th Infantry Division, Col. Charles Kean, described directed-energy weapons as a component of defense against high-echelon air threats, including individual UAS or formations, but said they were not a “single bullet” solution. “The more capabilities we put in the hands of soldiers, the easier they are to maintain, the more reliable they are, the better,” Kean told an audience at AUSA’s Warriors Corner. The Army successfully demonstrated eight kills using the directed energy platform prototype during the Army Modernization Day in October. The palletized, modular solutions can be integrated onto a number of vehicles, including the JLTV and Infantry Squad Vehicle, or ISV. The modular system will improve reliability and sustainability by making it possible for soldiers to perform field-level maintenance, according to Williams. It will also allow the Army to “continuously improve the system over time” without replacing the full unit. The counter-drone E-HEL contract is for more than 26 laser weapons units total, according to AeroVironment vice president of Directed Energy, John Garrity, who indicated the initial system is on target for 2027 delivery. “We were able to lean forward with a lot of the long-lead procurements early, so we’re ramping up for production,” Garrity told Military Times. “Because drones aren’t getting any slower and our adversaries aren’t getting any lazier with them.” Directed energy weapons are one of the capabilities the Army is pursuing at speed to counter the growing threat of low-cost, unmanned aircraft systems. During an earlier speech at AUSA, Secretary of the Army Adam Telle highlighted the need to field low-cost interceptors to shoot down missiles and drones. Telle hailed the Army’s work to streamline acquisition and get soldiers the gear they need.

Guy Yelverton, capability program executive for Defensive Fires. “My far-down point would be spring [2028], and if I could get in the December-January timeframe, that would be awesome. That would be a great win for the Army.” It is unclear where the first high-energy counter-drone weapons under H-ELS will be deployed. Yelverton suggested the 7th Infantry Division could be a potential partner. Deputy commanding officer of Support for the 7th Infantry Division, Col. Charles Kean, described directed-energy weapons as a component of defense against high-echelon air threats, including individual UAS or formations, but said they were not a “single bullet” solution. “The more capabilities we put in the hands of soldiers, the easier they are to maintain, the more reliable they are, the better,” Kean told an audience at AUSA’s Warriors Corner. The Army successfully demonstrated eight kills using the directed energy platform prototype during the Army Modernization Day in October. The palletized, modular solutions can be integrated onto a number of vehicles, including the JLTV and Infantry Squad Vehicle, or ISV. The modular system will improve reliability and sustainability by making it possible for soldiers to perform field-level maintenance, according to Williams. It will also allow the Army to “continuously improve the system over time” without replacing the full unit. The counter-drone E-HEL contract is for more than 26 laser weapons units total, according to AeroVironment vice president of Directed Energy, John Garrity, who indicated the initial system is on target for 2027 delivery. “We were able to lean forward with a lot of the long-lead procurements early, so we’re ramping up for production,” Garrity told Military Times. “Because drones aren’t getting any slower and our adversaries aren’t getting any lazier with them.” Directed energy weapons are one of the capabilities the Army is pursuing at speed to counter the growing threat of low-cost, unmanned aircraft systems. During an earlier speech at AUSA, Secretary of the Army Adam Telle highlighted the need to field low-cost interceptors to shoot down missiles and drones. Telle hailed the Army’s work to streamline acquisition and get soldiers the gear they need.

title: DELOREAN TAKES TO THE SKY: racing at the pinnacle of flying car motorsport as the DeLorean Airspeeder Team
body:
Iconic American marque enters the world’s first electric flying car racing series as a constructor, with the DeLorean Airspeeder Team racing from November 2026
Announced at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 , the entry puts the DeLorean name on the grid of the Airspeeder International Series and on the United States race aircraft
DeLorean Motor Company today announced at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 that it will enter the Airspeeder International Series, the world’s first racing series for electric flying cars, as constructor of the United States Airspeeder team. The team will compete as the DeLorean Airspeeder Team and will make its race debut when the 2026–27 season opens in November 2026.
The entry brings one of the most recognizable names in automotive history to the grid of a sport built on electric propulsion, advanced flight control and AI-enabled safety systems. It also makes DeLorean the first American constructor in flying car racing, lining up against national teams from around the world in the first international season of the series.
The aircraft design, pilot line-up and sporting program will be revealed ahead of the season opener.
The road was only ever the beginning DeLorean holds a singular place in automotive culture. For more than four decades the name has stood for bold design, independence and a stubborn fascination with what comes next. For most of that time, the world has pictured a DeLorean leaving the road behind.
Airspeeder was founded on an equally direct idea: that electric flying cars should be developed the way the automobile was, through the pressure, scrutiny and spectacle of racing.
“DeLorean has always stood for the courage to imagine transportation differently,” said Cameron Wynne, Chief Brand Officer, DeLorean Motor Company. “People have pictured a DeLorean in the sky for forty years. We decided it was time to stop picturing it.
Matt Pearson, Founder and CEO, Airspeeder, said: “DeLorean is the original flying car brand. Long before anyone had built one, the whole world already knew what a flying DeLorean looked like. Every great racing series is defined by the constructors who choose to compete in it. To have an American icon line up on our grid in our first international season tells you where this sport is going. America has repeatedly changed how the world moves, on the road, in the air and beyond, and the DeLorean Airspeeder Team carries that ambition into a new arena.”
What it means to be a constructor In the Airspeeder International Series, national teams race electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft in three dimensions through electronically defined courses, rather than around a conventional circuit. For its debut season, the team will race the Airspeeder Mk3C, with DeLorean leading its design identity. The constructor role grows from there. The DeLorean Airspeeder for the 2027–28 season will be designed in collaboration with student engineering teams at universities across the United States, including the University of California , collaborators at UC Berkeley and Georgia Tech , bringing American engineering and design talent into the development of a race aircraft.
Why flying cars matter to DeLorean “Motorsport has always been where mobility brands prove themselves. Competition compresses development cycles: systems are tested in public, teams learn quickly and performance is measured under pressure.
Through its partnership with Airspeeder, DeLorean aims to participate at the ground level, advancing not only the technology behind flying vehicles but also the regulatory, safety and compliance frameworks required for their responsible adoption. While widespread use remains over the horizon, the opportunity is significant. By engaging early, DeLorean is positioning to help turn future mobility from a vision into practical, scalable reality,” Wynne said.
For DeLorean, the Airspeeder International Series is a live proving ground at the moment electric flight moves from prototype to product, in front of a global audience that cares about technology, design, gaming and culture as much as it cares about lap times. It gives the marque a place at the front of advanced air mobility, and gives a new generation of fans a reason to care about the name.
The race program is the first chapter. DeLorean and Airspeeder will share more about where the constructor relationship leads, on and off the grid, in the coming months.

title: Two Egyptians killed in Khartoum as Sudan probes deadly strikes on miners by Egyptian forces
body: Two Egyptian truck drivers were shot dead in Khartoum on Monday, days after reported Egyptian airstrikes killed dozens of Sudanese miners near the Egyptian border, as calls grow for investigations into the deaths and protection for civilians caught up in cross border security operations. Egypt’s Foreign Ministry said a third Egyptian national sustained injuries in the shooting at a local market in Khartoum on Monday afternoon. The ministry said Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty had instructed the country’s ambassador to contact Sudanese authorities, establish the circumstances of the incident and arrange the repatriation of the two bodies. Sudanese authorities arrested a 23-year-old suspect carrying a Kalashnikov rifle, according to sources close to the police. The sources said he initially told investigators that he had acted in revenge for his brother, who died alongside Sudanese miners in the bombing near the Egyptian border. The reported motive has not been independently verified. The shooting comes amid heightened tensions following the deaths of Sudanese miners in the border area , where Egyptian authorities have acknowledged a campaign against reported illegal gold mining. ‘El Burhan orders probe as calls for accountability grow’ Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) Commander and Transitional Sovereignty Council President Lt Gen Abdelfattah El Burhan has ordered a fact-finding committee to investigate the deaths of Sudanese miners near the Egyptian border. This follows a similar probe conducted in the wake of a reported attack by Egyptian forces earlier this year on June 17 and 18. The investigation comes amid conflicting reports about the death toll, which Emergency Lawyers puts at least 72, and growing calls for transparency over the circumstances of the strikes. The Egyptian military said it was conducting what it described as the third phase of a campaign against illegal gold extraction in the Eastern Desert, involving armed forces and civilian police after warnings to those it described as criminal elements. The military said the operation aimed to secure Egypt’s borders and protect its national wealth. It also urged the public to rely on official information and rejected what it described as misleading rumours intended to undermine relations between the Egyptian and Sudanese peoples . Vehicles transported surviving miners and injured people towards Port Sudan, where the city’s resistance committees announced a blood donation campaign for the wounded. ‘UN warns of mounting civilian casualties’ The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) has expressed grave concern over continued airstrikes and drone attacks across Sudan, warning that civilians displaced by the war face renewed danger even in places where they sought refuge. OCHA reported that dozens of people were killed in Saturday’s bombing of traditional gold mining sites near the Egyptian border. It also cited reports of at least four civilian deaths, including a woman and three children, in strikes on Kadugli, South Kordofan, on the same day. In West Kordofan, a drone attack reportedly killed at least 12 civilians and injured eight at a building sheltering displaced families in En Nuhoud on Friday. Another attack in Ghubeish locality killed five civilians, including three children, in a residential neighbourhood housing displaced people. The UN also condemned drone attacks reported to have killed more than 30 civilians near a displacement camp in Wad El Mahi, Blue Nile State, on Friday. OCHA called for compliance with international humanitarian law, the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure, and accountability for serious violations. ‘Egyptian initiative demands transparency and civilian protection’ Shaimaa Sami, executive director of the Egyptian Madad Initiative, called on the Egyptian and Sudanese governments to explain the circumstances of the bombing and disclose the number of people killed and injured. Speaking to Radio Dabanga, Sami urged the authorities to grant journalists, human rights groups and humanitarian organisations access to the affected areas. She also called for medical care for the wounded, compensation for victims’ families and safe routes for civilians fleeing the conflict. Sami warned that gold mining, smuggling , human trafficking and networks financing the war economy overlap along the border, making it difficult to distinguish those involved in illicit activities from civilians caught in the area. She stressed that combating illegal mining and securing borders did not remove states’ obligations to protect civilians. Warning leaflets, she added, did not absolve those carrying out military operations of their duty to distinguish civilians from combatants and take all feasible precautions to prevent civilian casualties . Sami also called for stronger humanitarian and international protection near the border, particularly for women and children fleeing Sudan, who face risks from military operations, exploitation and trafficking. She urged closer involvement by the United Nations refugee agency, the International Organization for Migration and the International Committee of the Red Cross. The initiative stressed that civilians fleeing the war must be able to seek asylum safely and that border security operations must not come at the expense of civilian lives. title: Step-by-step guide: How to locate your home, check your name, address on Nigeria’s new postcode system
body: Nigerians can now find their home addresses and digital postcodes in Nigeria through the Federal Government’s National Digital Alphanumeric Postcode System, launched nationwide by the Nigerian Postal Service (NIPOST) on October 1, 2026. The system assigns an 11-character alphanumeric code to each addressable building to make it easier to identify locations for deliveries, logistics and other services. Residents can search for their properties, check available address details and request corrections where information is missing or inaccurate. Here are six steps to find your home’s digital postcode. 1. Open the official postcode website Visit postcode.gov.ng and select the option to find a postcode. You can also access the NIPOST Postcode application through the official website. 2. Search for your address Enter your house number, street name, neighbourhood or another detail that can help identify your building. The platform also supports searches using place names, postcodes and aliases where available. Check the search results and select the entry that matches your home. 3. Confirm the building on the map Examine the map to ensure the selected location corresponds to your property. Compare nearby roads, landmarks and neighbouring buildings before accepting the result. This is important because properties on the same street may have different postcodes. Once you identify the correct building, check its details and retrieve the assigned code. 4. Check whether your name appears Some building records include homeowners’ names because residents use them to identify properties, particularly in areas without clearly defined street addresses. You can search for your name if it is commonly used to identify your property or inspect the building’s description. However, your name may not appear even if your building is listed. The postcode identifies the building, not its owner or occupants. 5. Use your phone’s location or report a missing address If you are near your home, enable your phone’s location service and allow the application to access it. Select “Find My Postcode” and identify your building among the nearby mapped properties. If your building is missing, use the platform’s request process to submit its address and location details. A Google Maps link may help NIPOST identify the property. For incorrect information on an existing listing, use the available correction option. Requests are subject to review before records are updated. 6. Save and share your postcode After confirming the correct building, save the postcode for future use or share it when necessary. The code can be used alongside your regular written address to help others identify your location. According to the official platform, finding, saving and sharing a digital postcode is free. Always confirm that the code belongs to your intended building before using it for deliveries or other services. Vanguard News The post Step-by-step guide: How to locate your home, check your name, address on Nigeria’s new postcode system appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: The Hague unfit to organize tournaments — Russian ambassador
body:
THE HAGUE, October 13. /TASS/. The Dutch authorities’ decision to deny entry visas to Russian gymnasts set to compete in the world championships has shown that The Netherlands cannot be entrusted with organizing international competitions, Russian Ambassador to The Netherlands Vladimir Tarabrin said.
"They wanted to ‘teach Russia a lesson,’ but only showed that The Netherlands cannot be entrusted with organizing international tournaments," he told TASS and held the Dutch authorities responsible for the disrupted sporting event that was supposed to bring people together.
Earlier, the press service of the Russian Gymnastics Federation reported that the Dutch embassy had refused to issue visas to Olympic champions Angelina Melnikova and Victoria Listunova, as well as Anna Kalmykova, citing their being a "threat to international relations" as a reason.
The World Artistic Gymnastics Championships will be held in Rotterdam from October 17 to 25 and will serve as the first stage of team qualification for the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles.

title: Foundation Seeks FG Partnership as Screening Flags High Blood Pressure in Communities Across 20 States
body: Michael Olugbode in Abuja In Our Mind Foundation, a health and community development organisation, has called on federal and state health authorities to establish a formal partnership with its Healthy Nigeria Movement to expand community screening and improve access to medical care across the country. The foundation, while stating that it has conducted community screening outreaches in 20 states, seeks institutional recognition and an agreed role as a community screening and referral partner working alongside established healthcare services. It said preliminary findings from its outreach programme showed that 48.74 per cent of reported blood pressure readings fell within its high blood pressure category, while 5.74 per cent were classified as low blood pressure. The foundation’s presentation also reported high blood glucose readings in 18.33 per cent of the screening results and low readings in 9.12 per cent. However, the figures have yet to be validated against the underlying records and should not be interpreted as representative of the wider Nigerian population. The foundation said the findings highlighted the need to take routine health checks closer to communities and establish dependable referral pathways through which people with concerning results can receive appropriate clinical assessment. The call comes amid global concern over cardiovascular diseases, which the World Health Organisation identifies as the leading cause of death worldwide. An estimated 19.8 million people died from cardiovascular diseases in 2022, accounting for approximately 32 per cent of global deaths, according to the WHO. More than three-quarters of these deaths occurred in low- and middle-income countries. The organisation’s founder, Iruoma Obiesie Onuko, popularly known as Nurse Angel, while addressing a press conference in Abuja said community-based screening could provide an opportunity to identify potential health concerns before they develop into medical emergencies. She said the foundation was taking blood pressure and blood glucose checks to people’s doorsteps, marketplaces, streets, schools, churches and other places where communities gather. According to her, the outreach combines screening with health education and practical support to help participants understand concerning results and seek further assessment. The foundation noted that high blood pressure may occur without obvious symptoms, meaning people who feel well may still have elevated readings requiring medical attention. It said its teams had encountered participants with concerning blood pressure and blood glucose readings, including people whose results required further assessment. The organisation added that it had supported participants with severely elevated blood pressure to access urgent hospital assessment, assisted with medical costs where resources were available and provided follow-up support. It has also engaged older people, visited hospitals and assisted individuals experiencing difficulties accessing care. The foundation said these interventions were intended to bridge the gap between identifying a potential health problem and helping the affected person reach appropriate healthcare services. Under its proposal, In Our Mind Foundation wants a technical partnership meeting involving federal and state health authorities, primary healthcare organisations and relevant clinical institutions. It proposed that any agreement should clearly define community outreach responsibilities, geographic coverage, clinical oversight, screening standards, team training, equipment requirements and quality-control measures. The proposed framework would also establish referral links with designated healthcare facilities, urgent escalation procedures, follow-up arrangements and a system for transparent reporting and joint evaluation. The foundation said it could contribute community mobilisation, local relationships and organised teams, while healthcare institutions would provide clinical oversight, further assessment and continuing care. It argued that a formal arrangement would help ensure that community screening did not end with the recording of a result but led to appropriate action where necessary. The organisation is also proposing a 12-month programme to strengthen existing outreach activities and expand delivery in line with the readiness of local teams and receiving healthcare facilities. Under the proposed arrangement, participating partners would regularly review the number of people reached, valid checks conducted, referrals made, clinical assessments completed and follow-up actions undertaken. The foundation said it would also account for resources used and protect participants’ personal health information. It maintained that measurable outcomes, clearly defined responsibilities and transparent reporting would be essential to building institutional confidence and ensuring that expansion was sustainable. In Our Mind Foundation said its wider network had a presence in every state, while its community screening programme had completed outreach activities in 20 states. Through the In Our Mind Healthy Nigeria Movement, it provides free blood pressure and blood glucose checks, health education, referral assistance and follow-up support through monthly outreach activities. Local teams mobilise participants, provide information, conduct checks and help people understand the next steps when a concerning result is identified. The foundation said its community relationships offered an opportunity to strengthen collaboration with established healthcare services and improve the connection between community-based interventions and formal medical care. Onuko, a UK-based senior mental health nurse, public speaker and coach, said the foundation’s work reflected the relationship between health, opportunity and human development. She explained that the organisation grew from a youth initiative associated with Nigeria’s centenary programme in 2014, which encouraged young people to contribute ideas and solutions. The initiative’s reflections and activities were consolidated into the book In Our Mind, followed by the establishment of the foundation and its talk show. The organisation has since extended its activities to children, adults and older people, with community health education becoming one of the practical expressions of its broader mission. The World Health Organisation (WHO) has emphasised the importance of early detection and management of cardiovascular risk factors, including raised blood pressure and blood glucose. These factors can be assessed in primary healthcare settings and may indicate an increased risk of heart attack, stroke and other complications. However, screening alone does not establish a diagnosis. A concerning result must be interpreted in context and followed by appropriate clinical assessment, with treatment decisions made by qualified healthcare professionals. The foundation acknowledged the importance of clinical oversight and quality assurance, proposing that any government-supported programme should include agreed screening standards, competent personnel, suitable equipment and clear referral arrangements. It also proposed collaboration with universities, professional organisations, international health bodies and diaspora professionals to support training, evaluation, technical expertise and knowledge exchange. The organisation has invited the media to publicise the initiative and encourage wider participation in efforts to make routine health checks more accessible. It said its immediate priority was to establish a formal delivery agreement with relevant government and healthcare partners before expanding the programme further. The foundation said its objective was to build a more dependable pathway between community screening and appropriate care, allowing people to access understandable health information, timely assessment and follow-up support. It urged prospective partners to work with the organisation to strengthen the clinical connections behind its existing community reach, arguing that accessible screening would be more effective when people who need further care could also reach it.

title: Ukraine's Zelensky says Russia already violated Trump-brokered ceasefire proposal
body: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Monday that Russia violated the ceasefire US President Donald Trump proposed on Sunday, CNN reported.According to the report, Zelensky noted that Moscow "launched a targeted strike on a power plant in Kharkiv, causing further damage to our energy system," and further noted additional strikes on Monday involving Russian drones.Trump claimed on Sunday that both Ukraine and Russia had agreed to what he called an "energy ceasefire," saying at the time that it took effect immediately.Zelensky says Ukraine abiding by ceasefire terms despite Russian aggressionDespite the attacks, “Ukraine has not carried out strikes on Russian oil refineries or the energy sector in general for the two days since the American president announced an energy ceasefire," Zelensky wrote in an X/Twitter post on Tuesday.З вечора й по цей час росіяни атакували Україну більш ніж сотнею різних засобів нападу: реактивними дронами, баражуючими боєприпасами та балістичними ракетами. Значну частину із цих атакувальних засобів вдалося збити. Але, на жаль, не всі. У Харкові був зруйнований звичайний житловий будинок, рятувальна операція тривала фактично всю ніч – шукали людей під завалами. Від цього удару по будинку в Харкові загинули чотири людини. Мої співчуття всім рідним та близьким. Поранено загалом за один вечір і тільки в Харкові 41 людину. Був і доволі підлий удар балістикою по Києву – п'ять ракет, які влучили по цивільній інфраструктурі. Щодо цього удару, на жаль, не було попередження від партнерів. Розвідувальні дані про запуск російських балістичних ракет допомагають рятувати життя людей, і це одне з найбільш критичних питань. Саме це допомагає запобігати вбивствам, коли попередження про балістику є. Україна не завдавала ударів по російській нафтопереробці й загалом енергетиці протягом двох діб із моменту оголошення Президентом Америки припинення вогню в енергетиці. Але Росія не послухалась Президента Америки. За цей час росіяни атакували і наші енергетичні об'єкти, і нашу критичну інфраструктуру й дали абсолютно чіткі сигнали, що вони не збираються утримуватися від ударів по Україні. Під ударами саме за ці дві доби були 19 регіонів нашої країни. Наша позиція незмінна: Україна готова до дзеркальних деескалаційних кроків, і потрібен дієвий тиск на Росію, щоб деескалація була. Війни завершуються тоді, коли агресор відчуває, що у нього немає можливості війну затягувати. Тиск світу на Росію сприяє саме цьому – наближенню миру. Але пряма чи опосередкована підтримка Росії, гальмування допомоги Україні та ускладнення захисту життя від балістики – це те, що точно не спрацює на мир. Мир потрібен всім. Сильна Америка, сильна Європа, сильні партнери потрібні. Дякую всім, хто справді допомагає!— Volodymyr Zelenskyy / Володимир Зеленський (@ZelenskyyUa) October 13, 2026"But Russia did not heed the American President,” he emphasized in the post. “During this time, the Russians have attacked both our energy facilities and our critical infrastructure, sending absolutely clear signals that they have no intention of refraining from strikes on Ukraine.""Our position remains unchanged: Ukraine is ready for reciprocal steps toward de-escalation,” he added.The White House has not yet responded to a CNN request for comment on how the agreement was reached and what the next steps may be.In a later X post, Zelensky reiterated Ukraine's support for de-escalation, emphasizing that "it is important that Russia support it as well."I just spoke with @MarkJCarney, @alexstubb, and @SecGenNATO Mark Rutte. We discussed the energy ceasefire announced by President Trump. Ukraine supports the ceasefire, and it is important that Russia support it as well. We are awaiting details from the American side. For our part, Ukraine always FULLY supports steps toward de-escalation, the protection of lives, and the decisions needed to end the war and guarantee lasting peace. Thank you!— Volodymyr Zelenskyy / Володимир Зеленський (@ZelenskyyUa) October 11, 2026"We are awaiting details from the American side," wrote Zelensky. "For our part, Ukraine always FULLY supports steps toward de-escalation, the protection of lives, and the decisions needed to end the war and guarantee lasting peace."Reuters contributed to this report.

title: Adesina: Africa’s Youth Are Assets, Not Liabilities
body: *Urges leaders to invest in skills, jobs *Former AfDB president says poor education, unemployment, lack of access to finance are wasting continent’s demographic advantage Michael Olugbode in Abuja Former President of the African Development Bank (AfDB), Dr. Akinwumi Adesina, has challenged African governments to stop treating their growing youth population as a potential burden and instead invest in education, healthcare, skills, technology and entrepreneurship to drive economic transformation. Adesina warned that Africa’s demographic advantage would remain unrealised unless governments deliberately equipped young people with the capabilities, resources and opportunities to create businesses, develop technologies and generate employment. He made the call while delivering the keynote address, titled “Africa Next: Building the Demographic Asset Class,” at the inaugural Seyi Tinubu Colloquium in Lagos on Monday. The colloquium, which brought together political leaders, business executives, policymakers and youth advocates, provided a platform for discussions on leadership, enterprise, innovation and the role of young people in shaping Nigeria’s future. Adesina argued that population growth alone could not guarantee prosperity, insisting that the real value of a country’s human resources depended on how effectively its people were educated, skilled, kept healthy and connected to economic opportunities. “People are not liabilities. Young people are not liabilities. A young growing population is not a liability,” he said, according to reports of his address. He maintained that Africa’s challenge was not simply the size of its youthful population but the failure of economic and institutional systems to develop its potential. The former AfDB chief said governments must move beyond measuring demographic growth and ask what young people would be able to create, the businesses they could establish and the technologies they could develop to solve the continent’s problems. He identified quality education as a critical foundation for economic development, arguing that investment in human capability was as important as spending on roads, electricity, transport networks and other physical infrastructure. Adesina described education and the development of intellectual capacity as essential to building societies capable of innovating, competing globally and generating sustainable prosperity. He also urged African youths to embrace artificial intelligence and digital technologies, while developing solutions tailored to the continent’s needs rather than remaining consumers of innovations produced elsewhere. He said a skilled young person with access to technology, capital and markets could progress from being a job seeker to a business owner and, ultimately, an employer. Adesina warned that unemployment and limited opportunities should not automatically be interpreted as evidence of a lack of ambition or ability among young people. Instead, he said, the problem often lay in inadequate education, limited access to finance, unreliable infrastructure and institutions that failed to connect talent with productive opportunities. The development economist called for stronger support for entrepreneurship, particularly through financing systems capable of backing promising young business owners who might lack conventional collateral. He argued that financial institutions and governments needed to look beyond the risks associated with young entrepreneurs and recognise their potential to create businesses, jobs and wealth. Without such support, he warned, Africa risked wasting the productive capacity of a generation that could otherwise help accelerate economic growth and improve the continent’s competitiveness. Adesina also emphasised the importance of reliable electricity, effective institutions and an enabling business environment in allowing young people to turn ideas into viable enterprises. His position reflects a broader development challenge facing African economies: translating a rapidly growing working-age population into productive employment requires not only education and skills but also investment, functioning infrastructure and opportunities to use those capabilities. Adesina urged African youths to position themselves at the forefront of emerging technologies, particularly artificial intelligence, digital services and innovation-driven enterprise. He argued that digital technology could allow African entrepreneurs to develop products and services for international markets, opening opportunities beyond their immediate geographical locations. However, he stressed the need for Africa to develop and adapt technologies to address its own economic and social realities, including challenges in agriculture, healthcare and other essential sectors. The former AfDB president said investment in technical education and practical skills should be accompanied by access to capital and markets, enabling young people to build sustainable businesses rather than remain dependent on limited employment opportunities. He also called for deliberate investment in healthcare, noting that a productive population requires the health and wellbeing necessary to participate in economic activity. Adesina highlighted youth-focused initiatives in Nigeria, including the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), the Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund) and the Investment in Digital and Creative Enterprises (i-DICE) programme. The initiatives target different aspects of education, institutional capacity and enterprise development, but Adesina’s broader argument was that sustained investment must connect learning and skills to productive opportunities. He said young Nigerians needed an environment in which they could acquire relevant knowledge, access affordable financing, develop innovative products and build enterprises capable of creating jobs. For Africa’s demographic potential to translate into economic returns, he argued, governments must make human development a central component of their development strategies. “The more important questions are: What will they be able to do? What will they create? What businesses will they build?” he asked. He urged African leaders to make youth empowerment a core economic priority, warning that the continent’s future prosperity would depend less on the number of young people it had than on what they were enabled to accomplish. The message adds to calls at the colloquium for greater youth participation in national development and stronger collaboration between established leaders and younger generations. Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu also called for greater investment in youth leadership, mentorship, education and innovation, urging established leaders to create opportunities for younger people to gain experience and contribute to nation-building. The colloquium’s discussions underscored the importance of giving young Nigerians opportunities to participate in decision-making and develop the skills needed to assume greater responsibilities. For Adesina, however, the central issue remains whether governments and institutions can create the conditions for young people to convert their abilities into economic value. He maintained that Africa’s demographic advantage would only become a source of prosperity when investment in education, health, technology and skills was matched by access to finance, reliable infrastructure and opportunities to establish businesses. The former AfDB president urged African governments to place young people at the centre of economic planning, arguing that developing their capabilities was essential to building competitive economies, generating employment and securing the continent’s long-term future.

title: ‘Our enemies are thinking of testing us’: Netanyahu issues warning two weeks before election
body: Exactly two weeks before Israel's elections, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu visited the security barrier separating Israel from the West Bank on Tuesday and once again warned of a possible scenario in which Palestinian Authority security forces turn their weapons against Israeli targets. Netanyahu said there were security alerts in the area and suggested that Israel's enemies were considering taking action in the run-up to the October 27 election. "Our enemies are thinking of testing us in these days leading up to the elections," Netanyahu said. "I warn them that we are prepared for every scenario, including what is known as 'turning the guns around.'"   The possibility of Palestinian security forces turning their weapons against Israel has featured increasingly prominently in Israeli political and security discussions over the past month and a half. The issue first emerged during a briefing at the IDF's Central Command, when Netanyahu confronted IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir with a question about what would happen if Palestinian security personnel turned their guns on Israel. At the time, Central Command officers were presenting an assessment of the situation in the West Bank, including riots involving extremist settlers, the damage caused by their actions and the resulting need to divert military forces. Netanyahu subsequently raised the issue in an interview, echoing warnings he and members of his government had made previously. The IDF clarified at the time that the scenario was familiar to the military and had already been included in exercises, but that it had no intelligence indicating the existence of an actual Palestinian plan to carry it out. At the same time, senior military officers warned that the situation in the West Bank was "getting out of control," while security officials cautioned political leaders that the territory was "on the verge of exploding" because of the growing number of incidents of nationalist violence committed by extremist settlers. Netanyahu toured the security barrier Tuesday alongside Defense Minister Israel Katz, the head of the National Security Council and the commander of the IDF's Central Command. According to the Prime Minister's Office, commanders from the IDF, Shin Bet and Border Police briefed Netanyahu on efforts to protect Israeli communities along the barrier, as well as extensive operations in nearby Palestinian villages. The Prime Minister's Office said the operations included efforts carried out day and night to arrest terrorists, confiscate weapons and address potential threats originating from those areas. Speaking near Tulkarm, Netanyahu said the military had presented him and Katz with a forceful operational plan. "The IDF has presented me and the defense minister with a powerful, robust plan," Netanyahu said. "In such a scenario, I wouldn't advise our enemies to test us. You will encounter a level of force here that you never imagined." He added: "We will continue to safeguard Israel's security here, along the security barrier and everywhere. We are establishing communities here, more than 104 of them, and many farms. We are safeguarding the security of the State of Israel." The scenario Netanyahu referred to as "turning the guns around" involves members of the Palestinian Authority's security forces using their weapons against Israeli communities or IDF soldiers. The Palestinian security services legally possess thousands of firearms in the West Bank, with Israel's approval. Under the scenario discussed by Netanyahu, those weapons would instead be directed against Israeli targets. However, the IDF is not aware of any intelligence indicating that the Palestinian Authority is on the verge of carrying out such a dramatic shift. Nevertheless, as Zamir explained in response to Netanyahu during the Central Command briefing approximately six weeks ago, the military is unwilling to take chances. Even without intelligence pointing to an imminent move by Palestinian security forces, the IDF is preparing for the most extreme scenario.

title: FG targets $500m climate investment, approves N83.2bn – Keyamo
body: By Dickson Omobola & Adeyefa Boluwatife Federal Government has reiterated its commitment to strengthening the country’s weather forecasting and climate resilience systems, targeting $500 million in climate-related investments and approving N83.2 billion for interventions to mitigate flooding and other climate-related emergencies. Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, said this at the 2026 Annual Meeting of the Alliance for Hydromet Development in Lagos. Keyamo said the initiatives were part of efforts to strengthen the country’s capacity to anticipate weather-related disasters, protect lives and investments, and support sustainable economic development. He said: “Federal government has developed mechanisms for mobilising domestic and international resources for climate-related investments, including the Nigerian Climate Investment Platform, which was established to help unlock substantial financing in this regard, targeting $500 million for climate-related infrastructure, adaptation and other policy areas. “The accreditation of the Nigerian Social Investment Authority as a direct access entity to the Green Climate Fund also represents an important development in strengthening Nigeria’s capacity to access and deploy international climate finance. In addition, the Development Bank of Nigeria is working to strengthen its institutional capacity to assess climate finance opportunities, while federal government continues to explore green bonds, carbon market mechanisms and other innovative financing instruments. “Specifically, government has approved a national carbon market framework and the operationalisation of a climate change fund. Similarly, in June 2026, the National Economic Council approved N83.2 billion for participatory action task force interventions aimed at mitigating the anticipated impact of flooding and other climate-related emergencies across the country. These developments are significant, as climate finance must ultimately translate into projects that address real developmental issues.” He added that government was also exploring green bonds, carbon market mechanisms and other innovative financing instruments to improve access to climate finance. He said: “We must therefore recognise hydrometeorological services as critical national infrastructure. Sustained investment in weather, water and climate services is necessary to protect lives, safeguard investments and support informed decision-making.” Keyamo said NiMet’s Seasonal Climate Prediction had continued to contribute to national preparedness and planning, enabling relevant authorities to take preventive measures before weather hazards developed into disasters. On the role of the private sector, Keyamo said government could not shoulder the entire responsibility for financing and delivering weather, water and climate services. He said: “Federal government cannot, and should not, bear the entire responsibility for financing and delivering every component of the weather, water and climate information ecosystem.” He called for greater private-sector participation in aviation, satellite services, insurance, agriculture, energy, telecommunications, financial services and data analytics, noting that such partnerships could bring additional capital, technology and innovative approaches to service delivery. title: Six Flags temporarily closes 9 other roller coasters after fatal incident in Georgia
body:
The hypercoasters are located in six theme parks in the U.S. and Canada.
Immediately after a person was killed and others were hurt while riding the Goliath roller coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia on Monday, Six Flags announced it temporarily shut down nine similar hypercoasters in six theme parks across North America.
"The safety of our guests and associates remains one of our highest priorities," Six Flags said in a statement Monday.
The coasters closed include Nitro in Great Adventure; Raging Bull in Great America; Behemoth and Leviathan in Canada's Wonderland; Goliath in Magic Mountain; Fury 325 and Thunder Striker in Carowinds; and Orion and Diamondback in Kings Island.
Some of these coasters exceed 90 miles per hour and stand more than 300 feet, according to Six Flags.
All but one of the coasters were manufactured by roller coaster design company Bolliger & Mabillard, which has designed coasters for many Six Flags parks and other amusement parks around the world since 1988.
The Swiss-based company said in a statement to ABC News Tuesday that it was "actively investigating the incident," and declined to comment "further until we have a better understanding of what happened."
"We are deeply saddened by this tragic accident. Our thoughts are with the family and those affected," Bolliger & Mabillard said.
The Goliath coaster at Magic Mountain was manufactured by the now defunct Swiss-based company Giovanola.
A hypercoaster, as defined by Six Flags , "generally refers to steel roller coasters over 200 feet (61 meters) tall that prioritize airtime and speed over inversions. They often feature large camelback hills designed to maximize weightlessness."
Raging Bull is the oldest of the closed coasters, opening at Great America in Illinois in 1999, seven years before Goliath opened, according to the park.
Six Flags touted the ride as the "world's first hyper-twister roller coaster," with a 202-foot drop and speeds of 73 miles per hour.
Orion in the Ohio-based Kings Island is the newest ride, debuting in the summer of 2020, according to Six Flags. The ride is 5,321 feet long with a 300-foot drop and a max speed of 91 miles per hour, the park says.
Fury 325 is the longest, fastest and tallest of the closed rides, according to Six Flags.
The coaster, part of the North Carolina Carowinds park, has a top speed of 95 miles per hour, a length of 6,600 feet and a peak height of 325 feet, Six Flags said.
-ABC News' Jason Volack contributed to this report.
