title: ideaForge Secures Orders from Survey of India for Q6 V2 UAVs to Support Mapping and Geospatial Applications
body:
ideaForge Technology Limited has received an order from the Survey of India (SOI) for its Q6 V2 UAVs, further expanding the use of its indigenous UAV technology across specialised government applications. The UAVs will support SOI’s surveying and mapping requirements, enabling the collection of high-quality aerial and geospatial data across diverse terrains and project environments. The growing use of UAVs is transforming how geospatial data is collected, processed, and used for planning and decision-making. By enabling aerial data collection across large and difficult-to-access areas, UAVs can complement conventional survey methods while improving the speed, coverage, and frequency of data collection and processing. This is particularly relevant for applications where current and accurate geospatial information is critical to planning, infrastructure development, land administration and public programmes.
The Q6 V2 is a survey-grade UAV designed to provide high-area coverage, enabling large-scale mapping projects to be completed faster and more efficiently. A high-endurance, lightweight, and VTOL-capable platform, the Q6 V2 is designed and developed entirely in India. Equipped with advanced Mapping payloads, autonomous navigation, and encrypted communications systems, it has rapid deployment capability in under 10 minutes. The quadcopter designed UAV has an endurance of 60 minutes, having an operational range of 5 km and a maximum takeoff weight of 6kg. The platform supports daylight, thermal, mapping, and multispectral payloads, offering flexibility across various kinds of survey requirements. Q6 V2 is field-proven across varied terrains, from high-altitude zones to flood-affected areas.
Speaking on the development, Mr. Somil Gautam, Associate Director – Enterprise Business, ideaForge Technology Ltd., said, “The adoption of UAVs in geospatial applications is creating a more efficient way to collect the aerial data that informs how we plan, develop, and manage our physical environment. Our engagement with the Survey of India reflects the growing relevance of indigenous UAV technology in specialised applications where reliable and timely data is important. At ideaForge, we are focused on building platforms that can deliver dependable performance across real-world operating environments, and we see significant potential for UAV-enabled mapping and geospatial intelligence across government and enterprise applications.”
The order adds to the use of ideaForge’s UAV technology in mapping and geospatial applications, in a field where aerial data collection is becoming a regular part of how surveys are planned and carried out. The company’s UAVs have already demonstrated their capabilities across a range of government and enterprise survey requirements, including large-scale deployments under the Government of India’s SVAMITVA Yojana and large-scale mapping. ideaForge looks forward to supporting Survey of India as it applies drone technology to its surveying and mapping needs, and to working with its teams as they put the platform to use.

title: Trump: U.S. continues to share intelligence with Ukraine
body:
This was reported by the BBC , according to Ukrinform.
“No, we haven't,” Trump replied when asked by a reporter whether the U.S. had halted the exchange of intelligence with Ukraine.

title: World Bank successfully interacts with BRICS Bank, AIIB — Executive Director
body:
BANGKOK, October 13. /TASS/. The World Bank is expanding cooperation with other multilateral financial institutions and is successfully interacting at the operational level with the BRICS New Development Bank (NDB) and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB), Executive Director of the World Bank Neelkanth Mishra told TASS on the sidelines of the fall session of IMF and World Bank governing bodies.
"We already have very deep engagement with ADB and with the European Investment Bank. But with the others like, say, NDB and AIIB, I think at the operational level, we collaborate well and we engage very well," Mishra said.
"The World Bank's priority is to eradicate poverty on a livable planet. And one of the key changes in the last four, five years has been greater collaboration with other multilateral banks," he noted.
An expert report was prepared during the Indian presidency in the Group of Twenty, where one of key recommendations "was greater collaboration between the multilateral banks," the executive director added.

title: Gbenga Adeyinka’s Laffmattazz Tour to End in Lagos
body: The 2026 edition of Laffmattazz with Gbenga Adeyinka & Friends will conclude in Lagos on Sunday, November 15, with a grand finale at the Balmoral Convention Centre, Federal Palace Hotel, Victoria Island. Organised by Laughter Incorporated Ventures, the event, tagged “Lagos Gets the Last Laugh,” marks the end of a tour that has visited Ibadan, Akure, Calgary, London, Ontario, Toronto and Abeokuta. For Adeyinka, the Lagos finale, sponsored by First Bank, is a homecoming. The city played a significant role in his entertainment career more than 30 years ago, providing the stages and audiences that helped shape his journey. title: 5-goal Super Falcons crush Comoros, reach Olympics qualifier third round
body: Nigeria defeated Comoros 5-0 in the second leg of the 2028 Olympics women football qualifiers second round tie on Tuesday. The victory at the Remo Stars stadium in Ikenne ensured the Super Falcons sealed a 7-0 aggregate win, and advance to the third round of the qualifiers. Toni Payne (brace), Uchenna Kalu (brace) and Christy Ucheibe were all on the scoresheet as Austin Eguavoen’s team stamped their authority in the second half. Despite losing captain Rasheedat Ajibade to injury in the first half, Nigeria capitalized on the Comoros goalkeeper’s hesitation to steal the ball and take the lead through Payne’s composed finish. The lead was extended twice by Kanu with a header on 58 minutes for 2-0, and Payne with another cool finish for 3-0 on 63 minutes. Kanu joined Payne to become the second player with two goals in the match with another composed finish, before a penalty was awarded on 71 minutes for foul on Blessing Okpe. Midfielder Ucheibe slotted home the kick to seal the deserved win as Nigeria breezed into the third round of the series. The Super Falcons will face Morocco in the third round of the Olympics qualifier, where victory in the two-legged tie will bring the dream of a fifth Olympics participation closer for Nigeria’s female national team.

title: As sand becomes more valuable, Sierra Leone’s Mahera Coast grows more vulnerable
body: PORT LOKO, Sierra Leone — When the tide pulls away from the beach in the agricultural regions in Mahera in Lungi, about 27 kilometers (17 miles) across the sea from the country’s capital, Freetown, the digging commences. Young men shovel sand into cement bags and carry them to a flat open area to pile sand into heaps to be sold by local women to truck drivers. These women are dedicated sand sellers. They negotiate prices, buy sand from the shovelers and sell to heavy-duty truck drivers to be transported to Lungi, Port Loko and other areas. The income helps pay for food, school fees and other basic needs of their families. However, their work relies heavily on the seasonal tide: The sellers can buy sand during low tide but are banned from doing so during high tide. In Mahera, the sand trade began as a survival strategy for 14 women who became family breadwinners, mostly due to absent partners. Aminata Kargbo is the chairperson of the sand sellers in the locality in Mahera, and entered the business to support her seven children after her husband’s death. “Most of these women have lost their husbands, and the money we make goes to support our children,” she said. She oversees about 19 sand sellers, the majority of them women. Many of these women have become widows after losing their husbands to Sierra Leone’s civil war (1991-2002) and various illnesses. title: URCS representatives wounded in Russian shelling of Sloviansk
body:
Three representatives of the Ukrainian Red Cross Society (URCS) were injured in Russian shelling of Sloviansk, Donetsk region.

"Today, October 13, as a result of another Russian shelling of Sloviansk, three representatives of the Lyman city organization of the Ukrainian Red Cross, which had been relocated and continued its activities in Sloviansk due to the security situation, were injured," the URCS reported on Facebook on Tuesday.



As a result of the strike, the URCS representatives suffered shrapnel wounds and burns. All three have been hospitalized and are receiving the necessary medical care.

The building housing the team of the Lyman city URCS organization also sustained significant damage. Property belonging to the organization was damaged.

"We categorically condemn attacks on civilian infrastructure and humanitarian workers," the organization stated.

title: 1 dead, others injured on Six Flags roller coaster in Georgia
body:
A 42-year-old man died while riding a roller coaster at Six Flags over Georgia after he was thrown from his seat and struck other patrons before landing below the ride, police said Tuesday.
The man who died has been identified as Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem, the Cobb County Police Department told Global News.
“Preliminary information gathered through witness and employee interview indicates Kariem was ejected from the ride and struck other patrons before falling beneath the attraction. Investigators continue to examine the circumstances surrounding the incident,” police said.
Officers located Kariem beneath the ride at the theme park near Atlanta, where he was “unresponsive and not breathing,” police added.
Officers immediately secured the scene and requested assistance from the Major Crimes Unit.
Officials have not released any other information about those who were struck and injured.
“We were deeply saddened by the guest incident at one of our parks yesterday. Our thoughts and heartfelt condolences are with the guest’s family, friends, and loved ones. We are also providing support to the guests and team members affected.,” a park spokesperson told Global News in a statement.
“The park team and local authorities responded immediately, and we cooperated fully with local authorities. Out of respect for the family’s privacy, we will not be sharing additional details at this time,” the statement added.
Six Flags temporarily closed nine roller coasters across six amusement parks on Monday, following the incident involving the roller coaster at the Georgia location.
Attractions at the parks that are similar to the coaster in Austell, Georgia, were closed “out of an abundance of caution,” according to a Six Flags Entertainment Corporation spokesperson, who said staff members and local authorities responded immediately and the park is cooperating with the investigation.
“We are deeply saddened by the guest incident at our park today,” the spokesperson told The Associated Press, adding that the company is providing support to guests and staff who were impacted.
The affected rides include a second coaster named Goliath at Six Flags Magic Mountain in California, Raging Bull at Six Flags Great America in Illinois, Nitro at Six Flags Great Adventure in New Jersey, the coasters Fury 325 and Thunder Striker at Carowinds in North Carolina and the rides Leviathan and Behemoth at Canada’s Wonderland in Ontario, Canada.
While the amusement park has not named the ride involved in the incident, a witness told NBC News that he was on Goliath with his fiancée when he saw the man come out of his seat.
“The man started levitating in the air sideways,” Logan Conner told the outlet. “We made direct eye contact with him.”
Britny Landry had been on the ride earlier Monday and was waiting in line to go again.
“We just look, and I just see somebody fly out,” she told KTVU-TV . She said she wasn’t sure at first what she saw. “Maybe somebody had a bag or something.”
The death comes less than two weeks after Six Flags Magic Mountain in Southern California announced the retirement of its X2 rollercoaster amid lawsuits alleging serious brain injury caused by the ride.
In a statement , Six Flags Magic Mountain Park President Brian Oerding said, “Since X2 opened in 2008, it has welcomed more than 16 million guests and earned a passionate following among ride enthusiasts. We recognize the special place X2 holds in the coaster community, and we are grateful to our team members who operated and maintained it throughout its run.”
“While X2 consistently passed a multitude of safety tests, we have decided to close the ride because we believe it’s the right thing to do. Ride safety is a cornerstone of our business, and when we see guest confidence affected, we take it seriously,” Oerding explained.
Oerding said that the amusement park’s purpose is to “create fun, thrills and a lifetime of memories by creating unforgettable experiences that are underpinned by comprehensive safety policies.”
The southern California theme park recently settled a wrongful-death lawsuit from the family of a 22-year-old man who died after riding the coaster in 2022, and three more lawsuits alleging traumatic brain injuries were filed in recent weeks.
The ride has been closed since July 12, after two women who rode the roller coaster less than a week apart both needed to be rushed to the hospital after they exited.
One of the riders, 25-year-old Naomi Greer-Wilkinson, collapsed shortly after the ride ended and was found to have massive brain bleeding inside her skull that required emergency brain surgery, according to a lawsuit filed by her family against Six Flags.
Her lawyers said more than 100 people have claimed they got brain injuries from the roller coaster in the past two years and that the closure of X2 would not keep them from continuing to file lawsuits.
According to the Six Flags Magic Mountain website, the X2 roller coaster reaches a top speed of 76 mph (122 km/h) and has a total length of 3,610 feet. The seats rotate 360 degrees “so your body will be flipping around the entire time,” and the ride features two “raven turns”— half loops that turn into sheer drops midway.

title: Over 38,000 commercial, 150,000 residential customers unbilled – Ghana Water MD
body: The Managing Director of Ghana Water Limited (GWL), Adam Mutawakilu, has disclosed that more than 38,000 commercial customers and 150,000 residential customers are currently not being billed by the company. He said bringing these customers into the billing system was central to efforts to improve revenue collection and achieve financial self-sufficiency by June 2027. Appearing before Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee, Mr Mutawakilu said the company is targeting a 120 per cent increase in its current revenue by June next year through improved customer identification, metering and billing. “We have about 73,000 commercial customers we are yet to interrogate. Only 34,000 are billed. 38,800 are unbilled. I believe that if we capture them, as is being done now, so that means more than 50% of our commercial customers are unbilled,” he said. Mr Mutawakilu said capturing the unbilled commercial customers could significantly increase the company’s monthly revenue. He further disclosed that more than 150,000 residential customers were also unbilled, describing their capture as a major opportunity to boost revenue. “Ensuring that everybody is metered and pay the right water bill. That is a huge addition,” he said. Mr Mutawakilu added that the company had so far metered about 521 commercial customers, with the exercise still ongoing. According to him, management is working to ensure that all customers are properly captured and billed for their water consumption as part of broader efforts to strengthen the company’s finances and reduce its dependence on government support

title: Several injured as Sprinter bus collides with ‘trotro’ at Odorkor
body: Several passengers have been injured in a road crash along the Mallam Market stretch on the Odorkor Highway. The accident involved a Sprinter bus with registration number GW-9581-26, and a mini trotro. According to eyewitness accounts, the collision occurred after the mini trotro allegedly stopped at an unauthorised location to pick up a passenger. The sprinter bus, unaware of the abrupt stop, crashed into the rear side of the trotro. The impact left both cars mangled, while some passengers sustained various degrees of injuries. Injured passengers were reportedly rushed to a hospital for medical attention.

title: Trump links Russian shelling of Ukraine after announced ceasefire to Ukrainian strikes day earlier
body:
U.S. President Donald Trump believes that Russia's shelling of Ukrainian energy facilities following the energy ceasefire he announced can be explained by the fact that the Ukrainian side had struck Russian targets the day before.
While speaking with reporters in Alaska on Tuesday, in response to a reporter's remark that Russia had struck six energy infrastructure facilities in Ukraine after he had announced the ceasefire, the U.S. president said that the day before, Ukraine had struck many facilities.
When asked further whether, in his opinion, Russia had thereby violated the ceasefire, Trump replied: "I'll tell you about that later."
When asked by another journalist where he got the confidence that Vladimir Putin wants to end the war more than Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, the U.S. president replied that it was based solely on his experience in striking deals. "Only in dealing. That's what I've done my whole life is deals. I think they both wanted to end. You know, honestly, they both wanted to end, and they don't know how to get to that point. There's a lot of hatred there between the two of them," Trump said.
He later added: "Bottom line it will all work out. You know why? It always does."
As reported, on October 11, Trump announced that an energy ceasefire had been reached between Ukraine and Russia. However, on the evening of October 12 and into the night of October 13, Russian occupation forces launched massive strikes on Kyiv, Kharkiv, and other Ukrainian cities, targeting civilian and transportation infrastructure with ballistic missiles and loitering munitions. President Zelenskyy stated his willingness to refrain from striking Russian energy facilities only on the condition of a genuine mutual cessation of attacks by Moscow.
On October 13, the U.S. president stated that the agreements on an energy ceasefire were being violated by both sides, but expressed confidence that the leaders of Ukraine and Russia were seeking to reach a peace agreement. Responding to questions from reporters before departing for a rally in Ohio, Trump commented on the overnight strikes and the breakdown of the ceasefire he had announced. When reporters noted that Russia had violated the agreement, he said, "There have been violations on both sides."
Commenting on Zelenskyy's statement supporting an energy ceasefire in the absence of a reciprocal commitment from Putin, Trump asserted that both leaders support the initiative: "I think they want to make a deal, but they don't know how. But we're going to get them to make a deal."

title: Ecclesia Hills Church to Host Sixth Word Conference in November
body: Ecclesia Hills Church will host the sixth edition of its annual Ecclesia Word Conference from November 6 to 8, 2026, at The Hall, 16 Musa Yar’adua Street, Victoria Island, Lagos. The conference, themed “Freedom in Christ,” will explore the meaning of freedom in the Christian faith and how believers can experience it in different areas of their lives. According to the church, the gathering follows last year’s theme, “Custodian of Holy Oracles,” and will address what it describes as the bondages that continue to affect believers, including fear, religious practices, habits, financial pressures and generational patterns. Host pastor Moses Ida-Michaels said the conference aims to help believers understand and experience freedom in Christ. “Many people carry the name of Christ yet remain bound by religion, fear, habits, financial pressure and generational patterns. This gathering is about seeing freedom clearly and walking in it. Together, we will hack the principles that bring true liberty to life,” he said. The three-day conference will feature sessions led by several ministers and speakers. El-Shakar will speak on “Free a Generation,” while Jabar McKellar will address “Freedom from Religion.” Pastor Delvan will lead sessions on “Freedom from Mammon,” “Freedom from Sinful Addictions / Fear of Consequence” and “Free to Serve God’s Purpose.” Prophet Julius-Cudjoe will speak on “Freed Bloodlines, Cycles, Enchantments and Liberty Ideology.” Other sessions include “Freedom in Illumination,” to be delivered by Eva Dan Yusuf, and “Freedom in Innovation / Innovative Liberty,” led by Ida-Michaels. Hills Music and Moses Akoh will lead worship during the conference.

title: Alleged N109bn Fraud: Court to rule on admissibility of former accountant general Idris’ statements
body:
The Federal Capital Territory (FCT) High Court in Maitama, Abuja, on Tuesday, reserved ruling to decide on whether or not to accept some extrajudicial statements obtained from former Accountant General of the Federation, Ahmed Idris, during investigations into the N109 billion corruption charges brought against him.
Judge Yusuf Halilu adjourned for ruling after the prosecution and the defence offered their closing arguments in the trial-within-trial which the court ordered nearly four years ago to determine the voluntariness of the statements.
Mr Idris, through his lawyer, Chris Uche, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), urged the trial court in Abuja not to accept the statements tendered by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), alleging that they were obtained through inducement.
Mr Uche urged the trial judge to “reject the documents (statements) as well as video recordings” accompanying them.
But, EFCC’s prosecution lawyer, Rotimi Jacob, also a SAN, maintained that the statements were voluntary and taken in the presence of persons who testified in the trial-within-trial initiated at the instance of Mr Idris’ lawyer.
The prosecutor recalled two of the witnesses testifying during the trial-within-trial that the statements were “taken in my presence,” and asked the judge to admit them in evidence.
A total of 14 statements in question, taken on 13 different dates, have been the subject of the trial-within-trial which has run for close to four years, leading to a pause of the main trial itself.
The judge ordered the trial-within-trial in November 2022, and has since paused the main trial till when a decision is reached on the admissibility of the contested statements.
The substantive trial started in 2022, when the EFCC arraigned Mr Idris alongside Geoffrey Olusegun Akindele, Mohammed Kudu Usman and Gezawa Commodity Market and Exchange Limited on 14 counts of stealing and fraudulent diversion of N109.5 billion in public funds.
Mr Idris served as Nigeria’s accountant general from June 2015 until his removal from office in May 2022 following an EFCC investigation into the alleged diversion of public funds.
He and his co-defendants denied all charges during their arraignment.
On 22 November 2022, the prosecution’s attempt to tender Mr Idris’ extrajudicial statements to support its case was met with stiff opposition from the defence, which objected to their admissibility on the grounds that they were obtained through deception and inducement.
The defence team alleged that the statements were dictated and not voluntary. It also said the EFCC reneged on an assurance not to charge Mr Idris’ in court. EFCC rejected the claims, prompting the judge that day to order a trial-within-trial to determine the voluntariness, and consequentially, the admissibility of the statements.
During the trial-within-trial, both sides called witnesses to prove their stances on the statements.
Presenting his closing argument on Tuesday, after the years-long trial-within-trial, prosecution lawyer Mr Jacobs said the presence of Mr Idris’ particulars, such as “his name and address in the statements, shows that the statements were not dictated.”
Mr Jacobs also said there was nothing in his statement indicating that the EFCC ever promised not to prosecute him.
He argued that Mr Idris’ lawyers took undue advantage of Section 17 of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act and urged the judge to “accept the statements.”
After listening to their arguments, the judge reserved his ruling and promised to communicate the date to deliver it to the parties.
On 10 June 2022, EFCC arrested Mr Idris in Kano, Kano State, where he hails from, and flew him to Abuja for investigations. He was subsequently charged alongside co-defendants with theft.
EFCC later arraigned Mr Idris alongside his co-defendants on 14 charges, including diversion of N109.5 billion. They all pleaded not guilty.
On 22 November 2022, the judge ordered a trial-within-trial after Mr Idris, through his lawyer, challenged the admissibility of the statements he made to EFCC investigators.
During the trial-within-trial, the prosecution called EFCC investigators who denied entering into any non-prosecution agreement with Mr Idri or inducing to make statements.
Specifically, on 26 June 2024, Abdulhamid Isa Muri, an EFCC official from the commission’s Kano office, testified as the prosecution’s third witness regarding the statement Mr Idris gave in June 2022.
The defence later opened its case and called witnesses to support its challenge to the statements, including officials connected to the office of the accountant general of the federation.
In April, a retired Director of Legal Services in the Office of the Accountant General of the Federation, Haruna Alabi, testified as a witness for Mr Idris. He said he signed a statement written on 17 May 2022 by Mr Idris in EFCC custody.
“As our former boss, we wanted to show empathy,” Mr Alabi told the court during cross-examination by EFCC’s lawyer.
The EFCC accused Mr Idris of, among other offences, diverting up to N109 billion in public funds while he served as the nation’s accountant general.
The charges also accused him of accepting N15 billion gratification from Olusegun Akindele as a motive for accelerating the payment of 13 per cent derivation to the nine (9) oil-producing states in the federation, through the Office of the Accountant General of the Federation.
EFCC also alleged that N84.39 million from the federal government’s account was converted by the first and second defendants between February and November 2021.
The defendants pleaded not guilty to the allegations against them.
In December 2022, EFCC obtained a court order for an interim forfeiture of assets, including $899,900, N304,490,160.95, and 15 properties in Kano and Abuja linked to the alleged crimes.
EFCC chairman, Ola Olukoyede, announced at an event in Abuja in December 2022 that the commission had recovered over N30 billion .
It was not clear if the N30 billion the EFCC chair said had been recovered from Mr Idris covered multi-billion naira assets traced to and recovered from him in the wake of his arrest.
PREMIUM TIMES obtained images of some of the multi-billion naira assets in June.
The assets, mostly in Kano, his home state in Nigeria’s northwestern region, are said to be worth billions of naira, significantly more than his monthly salary as a public officer.
Part of the assets is the Gezawa Commodity Market in Kano State.
One of the assets – Ultra-Modern Mall, located in Kano State – is said to be worth more than N700 million.
Pictures obtained showed the mall was sited on a large expanse of land.
However, while the major exterior works have been completed, work is still ongoing inside, with facilities like elevators and escalators being installed.
In 2021, Mr Idris, in his capacity as the accountant general, launched Gezawa Commodity Market and Exchange Limited, which he had openly admitted to be owned by him.

title: Canadians with children more likely to rely on charities, non-profits: survey
body:
Two out of five Canadians said they relied on the service of a charity or a non-profit in the last 12 months, an Ipsos survey conducted for the Royal Bank of Canada found on Tuesday.
However, the proportion of Canadians needing support is much higher among those who have children.
Canadians with children were far more likely (49 per cent) to seek support compared to those without kids (36 per cent), the RBC survey said.
Charities and non-profits working in the healthcare space found their services were most utilized (68 per cent) followed by food charities in second place (26 per cent) and education services (15 per cent) in third place.
Canadians also sought help from charities and non-profits working in sectors such as housing (12 per cent), social programming (12 per cent), employment (nine per cent), professional/skill development (six per cent) and cultural or recreational programming (six per cent).
Among those who used these services in the last 12 months, nearly four in five (79 per cent) said their use is “occasional” while more than one in five (21 per cent) said they “regularly” use help from charities or non-profit organizations.
The kind of service Canadians use depends on their age, with younger Canadians relying more on education and employment services while older Canadians rely mor heavily on healthcare supports.
Gen Z had the highest use of charities among all generations, with nearly half (44 per cent) having used these services in the last 12 months.

title: Beam Global Signs Definitive Agreement to Acquire Drone Technology Company ScoutDI, Creating a Vertically Integrated U.S. Drone Platform for Industrial and Defense Markets
body:
Beam to manufacture ScoutDI’s Drone Systems in the Company’s U.S. and European factories post-acquisition and market drone and AI-enhanced software solutions across its global footprint
Beam Global (Nasdaq: BEEM), a leading provider of innovative and sustainable infrastructure solutions for energy storage and security, electrification of mobility, and smart city infrastructure, announces it has executed a Share Purchase Agreement (SPA) to acquire drone technology company ScoutDI. ScoutDI develops, manufactures, and sells drone systems and a suite of proprietary AI-enhanced software for the inspection of confined spaces and other hard-to-access industrial assets, serving customers in the maritime, oil and gas, energy and other industries. Upon completion of the acquisition, Beam intends to manufacture ScoutDI’s drone systems for the U.S. market in its existing U.S. factories. Beam intends to serve European and Middle Eastern markets from Beam’s European factories, which will be further enhanced by the retention of ScoutDI’s sales, engineering and manufacturing facilities.
ScoutDI has existing customers in 30 nations, including ExxonMobil, Chevron, Oceaneering and Ørsted, as well as the global testing, inspection and certification companies DEKRA, Applus+, Kiwa and Apave. Its technology is also deployed in the field by Shell, Petrobras and Equinor. Beam intends to expand drone sales across its existing customer base, which includes oil and gas majors, industrial conglomerates, mining, agriculture, utilities, law enforcement, border patrol, state, local and federal governments and U.S. and European defense departments.
The purchase price of approximately $24.0 million will be paid in a combination of cash and Beam common stock. Beam has secured commitments, subject to customary transaction requirements, for non-dilutive financing sufficient to fund the cash portion of the acquisition at closing on terms acceptable to the Company. ScoutDI sellers are further eligible for full earn-out payments in 2026 and 2027 in the event that drone and software revenues exceed 150% and 160% of 2025 revenues, respectively. Earn-outs may be paid in a combination of cash and Beam common stock. The transaction is expected to close in November 2026, subject to customary closing conditions.
ScoutDI’s main shareholders, DNV, Equinor Ventures and Klaveness, will hold Beam stock as a result of the acquisition.
“The ScoutDI acquisition will be a highly advantageous evolution of our current business, as ScoutDI already has an established global drone and software business with impressive margins and recurring revenues, serving Fortune Global 500 and other significant companies. Furthermore, the ScoutDI technology lends itself to many other applications and opportunities for both enterprise and government customers, which we intend to vigorously pursue through our global network. I am confident that both the existing and future opportunities will create significant new growth avenues for us,” said Beam Global’s Chairman and CEO, Desmond Wheatley. “ScoutDI’s Conditional Approval from the U.S. Department of Defense enables its approved drone systems to be marketed in the U.S. We believe our U.S. factories and skilled team are well positioned to deliver the domestic manufacturing that the approval requires without material increases in capital or operating expenditure, while our European facilities, combined with ScoutDI’s, will cover Europe and the Middle East.”
“We currently produce batteries for drones, robots, submersibles and other similar devices which we believe creates a significant differentiator and allows Beam to become what may be the only vertically integrated drone manufacturer in the U.S. that also produces its own batteries. Our patented BeamFlight™ technology, which enables remote recharging of drones without construction or grid infrastructure, adds a further layer of differentiation. We have built a technology platform with global manufacturing and engineering capabilities focused on energy, mobility and intelligence, and we believe Beam has the potential to become a leader in the drone industry because of our depth of experience in developing and manufacturing complex, patented technology solutions for mobility, energy and smart city infrastructure and selling them to exactly the sort of customers who we believe will value the new products and technology we are gaining through this acquisition. I am also very happy to welcome ScoutDI’s leading shareholders, who are all highly respected entities, to the Beam Global shareholder family,” concluded Mr. Wheatley.
“Joining Beam is an exciting next step for ScoutDI. Our customers already rely on our products to inspect confined spaces that are dangerous and costly to enter, and Beam brings the U.S. manufacturing, global footprint, and energy expertise to scale that much faster. Manufacturing in the U.S. is the key to the U.S. commercial, government and defense markets, and together we can take our technology to a far larger customer base. We have long believed that there are many other industries and applications to which our technology, and some of the exciting advances we are developing in our technology pipeline, like fully autonomous operations, can bring value, and we plan to take advantage of Beam’s global footprint and relationships to create growth in new markets for our products. We look forward to becoming an integral part of Beam and to demonstrating our combined value to shareholders and customers alike,” added Nicolai Husteli, CEO of ScoutDI.
Nicolai Husteli will continue to lead ScoutDI within Beam. ScoutDI’s Scout Portal software generates recurring subscription revenue.
ScoutDI’s Scout 137 Gen3 was the first European drone system, and among the first four systems overall, to receive Conditional Approval from the U.S. Department of Defense. As a result of the Conditional Approval, the system has been exempted by the FCC from its Covered List and can be sold in the U.S. The Conditional Approval remains effective subject to compliance with ScoutDI’s U.S. onshoring plan and updated government vetting of the product, and Beam intends to manufacture the product in the U.S. following closing, consistent with that onshoring plan. Beam believes that U.S. manufacturing and a documented domestic supply chain will also position the Scout 137 for U.S. government and defense procurement, subject to satisfying applicable requirements such as the American Security Drone Act and the Blue UAS program.
ScoutDI’s technology is inherently dual-use, with significant potential in defense and security applications, and Beam intends to pursue these opportunities through its U.S. manufacturing, its existing defense customer relationships and its federal procurement channels.
The “Unleashing American Drone Dominance” executive order signed on June 6 2025, directs federal agencies to prioritize the integration of U.S.-manufactured unmanned aircraft systems over foreign-manufactured systems and directs the Department of Defense to prioritize procurement of Section 848-compliant drones made by U.S. companies.
The global drone market has an estimated value of USD 96.4 billion in 2026, up nearly 15% from 2025, and is projected to more than double by 2033, according to a Grand View Research report. North America accounts for roughly 40% of the global drone market, and Europe accounts for nearly 27% of the global market. The drone market has experienced significant growth, driven by increases in defense, public safety, industrial inspection, and delivery applications. Beam believes the same capabilities open further markets, including inspection inside tall buildings, elevator shafts, mines, tunnels and sewers, as well as public safety, security and defense applications where a drone can enter structures ahead of personnel.

title: Foundation Supports Indigent Pupils with School Feeding Programme
body: The Oladele Fajemirokun Foundation has introduced an Early Childhood School Feeding Programme in selected public primary schools to ease the burden on low-income families and improve pupils’ school attendance and learning outcomes. The Executive Director of the foundation, Olawumi Fajemirokun, disclosed this in a statement, explaining that the initiative was introduced after the organisation observed how financial hardship prevented some families from providing their children with adequate nutrition, affecting their education. According to her, teachers have frequently raised concerns about pupils’ inability to concentrate in class because of hunger and the lack of essential learning materials. These challenges, she said, contribute to low enrolment, absenteeism and truancy. “History is replete with examples of leaders, intellectual giants and exceptional change-makers who rose from humble beginnings to attain global prominence, with education serving as a powerful catalyst for their transformation and success,” she said. Through the programme, hundreds of pupils in underserved communities receive nutritious, balanced meals to support their growth and overall well-being. Fajemirokun said the intervention was helping to address classroom hunger while improving school attendance, concentration and learning outcomes. “Beyond addressing hunger, the programme is helping children approach learning with renewed energy, improved concentration, and greater enthusiasm for school. Because of this programme, most children now look forward to going to school to learn and to be well fed,” she said. She stressed that no child should be denied the opportunity to reach their full potential because of hunger, noting that proper nutrition was essential for learning and development. According to her, well-nourished children are better able to concentrate, participate in classroom activities and achieve their academic potential. She added that the foundation planned to extend the programme to three additional schools in the new academic session.

If you’re looking for an e-reader that can easily fit in your pocket (or snap onto your magnet-equipped phone), the tiny Xteink X4 Pro might be worth a look. It features a 4.26-inch, 800 x 480 E Ink display, making it significantly smaller and thinner than Amazon’s smallest six-inch Kindle . It’s also quite a bit cheaper. Right now, you can pick it up for $84.15 ($25 off) at Amazon , which is its best price to date.
The X4 Pro brings several welcome upgrades over its predecessors, including a touchscreen that gives readers another way to interact with it. It still has physical page-turning buttons, though. There’s also a new touch-sensitive button below the display for quickly returning to the home screen, along with a built-in light with adjustable brightness and color temperature, so you can read in the dark. It ships with the excellent CrossPoint Reader software , which makes navigating your library and reading books a much better experience than on previous Xteink models we’ve tested, though it’s still not quite as polished as Amazon’s software.
Understandably, not everyone is a fan of Xteink’s decision to swap the X4 Pro’s USB-C port for a proprietary charging connector. If you can look past that, the X4 Pro is a great, little e-reader that features magnets that let you attach it to compatible smartphones, just like previous models. The magnetic connection is stronger this time around, though we still wish it were a little more secure. All the same, my colleague Andrew Liszewski still considers the X4 Pro the best tiny e-reader you can buy , calling it a device he “won’t leave the house without.”

title: Britain’s domestic intelligence agency is devoting more resources to foreign threats than during the Cold War. Its chief calls Russia ‘aggressor number one.’
body: Britain’s domestic intelligence service is now devoting more resources to countering state threats than it did during the Cold War, MI5 chief Ken McCallum said. Russia remains “aggressor number one” and is trying to wage “hybrid warfare” in Europe, he said. McCallum said Russia is trying to destabilize European countries while making “minimal and horrifically costly” progress in its war against Ukraine. Following the expulsion of Russian agents from the U.K., Russian intelligence services are now “scrambling to pay criminals to do their bidding,” McCallum said. “These are not the actions of a great power with the strategic upper hand,” he said. Officials in several European countries, including Germany , France , and Poland , have previously said Russian authorities are trying to carry out acts of sabotage to intimidate Ukraine’s allies. title: Pluto Security raises $42M as AI gives enterprise security teams a new headache
body:
The problem with giving everyone in a company access to AI tools is that people will use them in unexpected ways. And that fact is steadily seeding fears that companies now have new, gaping security holes in their systems or, at least, will soon.
Illustrating the pace of AI tool adoption within enterprises driving such fears, Shahar Bahat, CEO and co-founder of Pluto Security , says a newly announced AI tool can show up inside companies’ environment within a mere two hours of its release. And about 60% of the risks her company detects across its customer base are in tools vibe-coded by non-developers: Finance departments are the biggest source of such risks, she told TechCrunch, followed by marketing and legal teams. Developers rank fourth, she said.
Her startup’s tools apparently found a vibe-coded app made by a finance employee at a Fortune 500 company to manage customer information and churn, but the app was left exposed to the internet.
Pluto, fresh out of stealth with $42 million in funding, is the latest in a new crop of security startups that have quickly sprung up to help companies address those fears gaps, and all of them are raising big money from investors on the back of the conviction that only using existing security software to monitor and control AI tools, connectors, and usage is a square-peg-round-hole approach.
Bahat tells TechCrunch her startup started selling only in April and has already found some takers for its tech, which helps companies gain context, risk analysis, visibility, and control over how their employees use AI tools. She said Pluto began selling in April and has already crossed $2 million in annual recurring revenue, with more than 30 enterprise customers, including Oscar Health, Workato, Sixt, and AlphaSense.
Pluto’s funding spans an $8.5 million seed round led by TLV Partners, with cybersecurity firm Armis’ founders also investing. The company recently raised a Series A of $34 million led by Jump Capital, with Skinos (Check Point co-founder Shlomo Kramer’s venture firm), Ansa Capital, and other angel investors participating.
That’s decent traction for a young startup, though not unique in this AI era. But it may be because the breadth of the risk isn’t isolated to large tech companies that lead the AI adoption charts.
When I asked Bahat where she’s seeing the biggest risks, she said the issues are differentiated by the mindset of the CISO and how willing the organization is to adopt AI, but there were risks to be found anyway.
“In general, I’ll say there was not one POC in which we entered and didn’t find malicious stuff,” she said. “Whether those are extension packages or skills — some of them had active live attacks while we did the POC. Which again, for me, product-wise is amazing. For the companies, it’s not very good.”
Pluto’s entire bet is that securing such environments will require security tools to pay attention to what AI agents are doing in real time, in addition to keeping track of what and how employees are building and deploying.
“We’re moving from user behavior to agent behavior,” Bahat said.
In line with that vision, the startup’s software monitors the AI tools employees use, the skills, extensions, MCP servers, and other components those tools rely on, as well as the apps and agents being created. The company says it can identify risky components, spot potentially dangerous agent activity, and enforce security policies without stopping employees from using or making AI tools.
To do all that, Pluto connects to endpoint security and device management systems and can deploy its own sensors through them or directly onto devices. It gathers information, including prompts, commands, running processes, permissions, and users’ previous activity, and uses its own “lightweight” models on endpoints to help assess what an agent is trying to do.
What stood out is that Pluto’s system can intervene while an agent is working, Bahat said. If an agent tries to gain permissions beyond what a user intended, for example, the system can stop the action or add instructions into the session that prompt the agent to ask for confirmation.
“We can inject context back to the session, and this way I can change how the agent is working,” Bahat explained.
The startup also takes an unusual approach to finding customers. In April, it launched Plutonium , a free platform that lets anyone check risks associated with publicly available AI skills, connectors, and add-ons. There’s also an MCP scanner and a catalog of verified components. Bahat claims thousands of security professionals use Plutonium and that the community around it has become an important source of feedback and prospective customers.
She said 70% of Pluto’s sales pipeline now comes from inbound interest, although she didn’t break down how much of that comes directly through Plutonium.
Pluto said it plans to invest the new capital in developing its product, expanding its security research efforts, and growing its presence in the U.S. It has 40 employees in the U.S. and Israel.

title: Manage private pricing offers for Amazon Bedrock with managed entitlements
body: Managing AI model access across dozens or hundreds of AWS accounts creates operational friction when each workload account must subscribe and accept AWS Marketplace Private Pricing Offers (MPPOs) individually. Amazon Bedrock with managed entitlements simplifies multi-account access to third-party AI models so you can subscribe once from a central account and distribute access across your organization. In this post, we show you two ways to activate AWS Marketplace Private Pricing Offer (MPPO) entitlements in AWS License Manager. Use the lightweight script when you want a one-time, no-infrastructure fix for received licenses you already trust. Use the CDK automation when you want ongoing event-driven processing that verifies sellers, creates and activates distributed grants. Why automate grant activation With AWS Marketplace Private Pricing Offers, you can negotiate custom rates for third-party models on Amazon Bedrock. After an eligible private offer is accepted, AWS Marketplace creates a license in AWS License Manager. In AWS Organizations with all features enabled, organization-level grants are auto-accepted but remain Disabled until you activate them. Teams often manage this by checking the AWS License Manager console and activating grants manually. Manual checks work, but they add effort and are easy to miss. Until someone activates the grant, negotiated pricing does not apply. The same effort appears as teams adopt new models or renew terms. Solution overview The sample repository provides two paths: Path 1 – The lightweight path is a standalone script that lists received licenses and prints a dry-run plan. It only creates and activates organization-wide grants when you re-run it with --apply --confirm-account-id . It has no seller allow-list, so use it only when you trust every received license in the management account. Path 2 – The event-driven path uses AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) to deploy ongoing automation in your AWS management account. Choose one of the following implementation paths. Use Path 1 for one-time activation without CDK. Use Path 2 for ongoing event-driven automation. Path 1: Lightweight script (one-time activation) Use this path when you need one-time activation without deploying CDK. The script lists every received license in the management account, so use the dry run as your review gate before applying changes. Clone the sample repository locally and move into the project directory. git clone https://github.com/aws-samples/sample-bedrock-managed-entitlements.git cd sample-bedrock-managed-entitlements Run the lightweight script in dry-run mode. python3 lightweight/distribute_licenses.py Review every listed license and confirm that the ISV Partner issuer and account scope match the private offer you expect. Apply the reviewed plan from the same AWS Organizations management account. python3 lightweight/distribute_licenses.py --apply --confirm-account-id ACCOUNT_ID After the grant is active, validate the billing path before you rely on the private offer in production. Billing data in AWS Cost Explorer can lag, so use it to compare the effective charge for covered Amazon Bedrock usage after charges appear. For a repeatable check, adapt the sample scripts/bedrock_discount_check.py utility to match your ISV Partner issuer and confirm the expected discount path. Path 2: CDK automation (ongoing activation) Use this path when you want new private pricing agreements handled automatically. The CDK stack listens for eligible AWS Marketplace agreement events, checks your seller allowlist, creates distributed grants, and retries activation when License Manager needs more time. The solution contains three components: Amazon EventBridge rule : The stack listens for AWS Marketplace agreement events on the default event bus in us-east-1 . The rule matches source aws.agreement-marketplace and detail type Purchase Agreement Created - Acceptor , then invokes the AWS Lambda function. AWS Lambda function : The function receives the AWS Marketplace agreement event, verifies the seller allow-list, discovers the license, creates the distributed grant, and requests activation with CreateGrantVersion(Status=ACTIVE) . The function logs the outcome to Amazon CloudWatch Logs for auditability. AWS License Manager entitlements : The grant targets your organization, selected organizational units (OUs), or specific accounts. Negotiated pricing applies only after the grant is activated and reaches ACTIVE or WORKFLOW_COMPLETED . The following diagram shows the event-driven flow. Figure 1: Sequence diagram showing AWS Marketplace sending a Purchase Agreement Created – Acceptor event to Amazon EventBridge, which invokes an AWS Lambda function. The function verifies the seller, discovers the received license, creates a distributed grant, requests activation with CreateGrantVersion(Status=ACTIVE), and writes the outcome to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Key benefits of this approach: Faster time to negotiated pricing. The negotiated rate applies after the distributed grant reaches ACTIVE or WORKFLOW_COMPLETED , without waiting for a manual console check. Consistent handling across accounts. The same AWS Lambda function and Amazon EventBridge rule pattern can be deployed for each organization that receives third-party model grants, so activation logic doesn’t vary by operator. Built-in audit trail. Every activation attempt or skip decision is logged to CloudWatch Logs, giving you a record of when each grant was activated, deferred, or ignored. Prerequisites Before you deploy this path, confirm these prerequisites: Use the AWS Organizations management account in us-east-1 with Python 3.12+, AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI), and AWS CDK v2 configured. Confirm that AWS Organizations uses all features and that the private offer is for a License Manager-backed Bedrock model. Software as a service (SaaS) products are out of scope for this automation. Implementation steps Clone the sample repository locally and move into the project directory. git clone https://github.com/aws-samples/sample-bedrock-managed-entitlements.git cd sample-bedrock-managed-entitlements Verify or enable organization prerequisites. python3 scripts/bootstrap_prereqs.py --check --region us-east-1 Review any APPLY or MANUAL items before making changes. The bootstrap script can enable License Manager organization integration, License Manager trusted access, AWS Marketplace license-management trusted access, and required service-linked roles. python3 scripts/bootstrap_prereqs.py --apply --region us-east-1 --confirm-account-id ACCOUNT_ID Configure deployment inputs. python3 scripts/setup_config.py Review config/sellers.json . Configure your Organization ID, seller allow-list, notifications, and optional grant targets. By default, grants target the full organization. Use grantTargets to scope grants to selected OUs or AWS accounts. Deploy the CDK stack. cd cdk pip install -r requirements.txt cdk bootstrap aws://ACCOUNT_ID/us-east-1 cdk deploy Seed the Amazon DynamoDB seller allow-list from config/sellers.json . cd .. python scripts/seed_sellers.py --config config/sellers.json Treat the seller allow-list as a security boundary. Verify each seller account ID against your accepted AWS Marketplace private offer or received License Manager license before seeding the table. Don’t add broad or unverified seller entries, because matching sellers can trigger grant creation and activation across your configured grant targets. After deployment and seller seeding, the stack is ready to process eligible AWS Marketplace agreement events. Grant creation and activation happen only for verified sellers in the allowlist, and activation may be deferred until License Manager finishes processing the grant workflow. Validate the deployed automation. python scripts/e2e_validate.py --org-id o-xxxxxxxxxx --seller-account SELLER_ACCOUNT_ID --simulate Verify grant activation after an eligible AWS Marketplace agreement event. aws logs tail /aws/lambda/mppo-grants-handler --follow --region us-east-1 python scripts/bedrock_discount_check.py --issuer "ISV Partner" Activation and billing visibility can take hours or days. After the event-driven workflow accepts and activates the grants, confirm the grant state in AWS License Manager, then validate covered Amazon Bedrock usage in AWS Cost Explorer after billing data appears. For a repeatable check, adapt the sample scripts/bedrock_discount_check.py utility to match your ISV Partner issuer and target linked account. Clean up If you deployed this stack for testing, remove it to avoid the small ongoing Lambda and Amazon EventBridge charges: cdk destroy Voice of customer “As an AI Care Partner supporting millions of clinician consults every week, Heidi Health relies on third-party foundation models at real scale. Private pricing on AWS Marketplace gives us a cost-effective and efficient way to manage that growth: we can granularly attribute usage and pricing across AWS accounts and organizational units, and automate grant management as we adopt new models. That lets our platform team scale cost governance without scaling manual work.” — Marcus Lau , Head of Platform Engineering, Heidi Health Conclusion This post showed two ways to activate managed entitlements for Amazon Bedrock private pricing offers. Use the lightweight script for one-time activation of trusted received licenses, or deploy the CDK automation when you need ongoing event-driven processing for new AWS Marketplace agreements. Both approaches reduce manual effort and help negotiated pricing apply after distributed grants are activated. To get started, try the code sample in your AWS management account to automate model subscriptions. Resources Sample code: Amazon Bedrock with managed entitlements (GitHub) AWS License Manager User Guide AWS License Manager API Reference: CreateGrantVersion Amazon EventBridge User Guide AWS CDK Developer Guide About the authors Daniel Wirjo Daniel is a Solutions Architect at AWS, focused on AI and SaaS startups. As a former startup CTO, he enjoys collaborating with founders and engineering leaders to drive growth and innovation on AWS. Outside of work, Daniel enjoys taking walks with a coffee in hand, appreciating nature, and learning new ideas. Daniel Quang Daniel is a Solutions Architect on the Frontier AI Startups team at AWS, where he helps the world’s largest and most strategic GenAI startups scale their infrastructure on the cloud. He holds a PhD in Computer Science from the University of California, Irvine, with a research focus on machine learning and bioinformatics. Bryn Price Bryn is a technologist, paragliding pilot, and Principal Solutions Architect at AWS. With more than 20 years of experience across telecommunications, banking, and software, he’s spent recent years deep in Applied AI, designing and building multi-agent AI products in production, and helping customers move from experimenting with generative AI to shipping it at scale. He loves defying gravity and talking through anything from agent architectures to how AI is reshaping software engineering itself. title: New Zealand builds an arsenal of tools to battle a ‘wily’ invasive seaweed
body: BAY OF ISLANDS, Aotearoa New Zealand — Since an invasive seaweed called caulerpa was discovered in Aotearoa New Zealand in 2021, forming meadows that blanketed parts of the seabed, it’s taken on an almost mythical status among people who spend time in coastal waters. “It’s so wily and so resilient,” Michele Rogalin-Henderson, a doctoral candidate at the University of Auckland’s Institute of Marine Science, told Mongabay. “Yes, I did say wily,” she added. “I anthropomorphize it. I spend a lot of time in the lab and in the field with this beast.” Stephen Te Tai, a commercial diver who removes the caulerpa, mainly in the Bay of Islands area in New Zealand’s tropical far north, also spoke about the invasive seaweed in such terms. “I know it’s airy fairy but sometimes I feel its energy,” Te Tai told Mongabay. In winter, he said, “it’s real low, it’s almost cowering, but in the summertime, it feels like its chest is puffed out, and it’s real vibrant and strong.” Te Tai is Ngāti Hine, a Māori tribal grouping, and his surname means “coast” or “tide” in Māori. He spoke to Mongabay on the shoreline after he’d worked in the waters off Urupukapuka Island one day in July. “The moana [ocean] is vital to our people,” he later added in a text message. “It is not just something that nourishes us, it is a part of us, it was a part of our ancestors and it will be part of our mokopuna [descendants].…This article was originally published on Mongabay

title: ABS Helps Industry Put Augmented Reality to the Test
body:
Essential news coupled with the finest maritime content sourced from across the globe.
Augmented reality (AR) can help industrial crews perform tasks more efficiently and consistently, but widespread deployment will depend on demonstrating that productivity gains can be achieved without compromising safety.
That’s the core message from ABS in its latest publication, which supports marine and offshore operators as they evaluate whether AR applications are right for their crews. The ABS Advisory on Assessing Augmented Reality for Industrial Operations provides insight into how to evaluate AR’s effects on safety and performance for tasks such as inspection, maintenance, navigation, training and remote assistance, and how those effects compare with current work practices.
“Augmented reality could change how industrial work is performed, bringing expert guidance, operational data and digital workflows directly into the user’s field of view. To unlock that potential responsibly, industry needs a clear understanding of the safety and performance implications. This advisory provides the tools to evaluate the implications rigorously and consistently,” said Patrick Ryan, ABS Senior Vice President and Chief Technology Officer.
AR’s key advantage is its ability to place relevant information directly in the user’s line of sight. The technology can display step-by-step procedures in front of a technician, mark inspection points and tolerances on equipment, and flag hazard zones and exclusion areas as crews move through a space. Real-world benefits, however, depend on the task, the user and the operating environment.
Developed with support from the ABS Laboratory for Ocean Innovation at Texas A&M University, the advisory outlines a structured methodology for comparing AR-enabled tasks with baseline practices across safety and performance dimensions. It highlights how different types of tasks, such as those relying on navigation, hand-eye coordination, memory or information processing, place different demands on users, making it important to evaluate AR for the specific task it would support. The advisory also reviews the trade-offs AR applications can introduce, including distraction, visual occlusion and overreliance on system outputs.
As AR moves from pilot projects to daily use, ABS will continue working with the industry to support the safe adoption of new technology. Download a copy of the advisory here .

title: British Special Forces Probed on Severe War Crimes Against Afghan Civilians
body: British Special Air Service (SAS) personnel are refusing to answer questions from a public inquiry into alleged unlawful killings during British military operations in Afghanistan, raising further questions over the conduct of elite units and the adequacy of previous investigations. Lord Justice Charles Haddon-Cave, who chairs the Independent Inquiry relating to Afghanistan, said on October 12 that a high proportion of personnel approached by investigators had invoked their privilege against self-incrimination. The inquiry is examining allegations of extrajudicial killings during operations between 2010 and 2013, alongside claims that evidence of unlawful activity was concealed and that subsequent investigations by the Royal Military Police (RMP) were inadequate. The discovery severe war crimes by NATO personnel in Afghanistan is far from unprecedented. Australian special forces were in 2020 revealed by the recent Brereton Afghanistan Inquiry Report, to have intentionally widely targeted civilians including children, in one case killing 39 Afghans, including two 14 year old boys, slitting their throats, bagging their bodies and dumping them in a river. The inquiry found that this was not an uncommon practice, with Australian personnel often required by superior officers to murder prisoners to get their first kills - a practice known as "blooding." "Typically, the patrol commander would take a person under control and the junior member, who would then be directed to kill the person under control," the report stated, indicating that the reported incident represented part of a much larger phenomenon relating to general Australian conduct. The Australian investigation further found that Australian forces would carry arms for the purpose of planting them on Afghan civilians they had killed in order to avoid blame for such massacres. The Brereton Afghanistan Inquiry Report highlighted a ‘cover up culture,' under which allegations of atrocities were routinely ignored by senior officers. Australian personnel were notably found a few weeks prior to have shot an Afghan prisoner because they had no room in their transport. The latest proceedings in the United Kingdom have uncovered substantial quantities of material that were apparently not examined during earlier investigations. Haddon-Cave disclosed that the inquiry had obtained approximately 10,000 high-resolution photographs taken during the deliberate detention operations that did not appear to have formed part of previous RMP inquiries, and which could provide additional evidence about the circumstances of individual incidents. The latest British inquiry was established following allegations that members of an SAS unit killed 54 Afghans in suspicious circumstances during a six-month deployment to Helmand province between November 2010 and May 2011. A broader investigation is examining alleged unlawful killings during deliberate detention operations conducted by British special forces between mid-2010 and mid-2013. The inquiry is also considering whether senior personnel were aware of concerns about the operations, whether possible criminal conduct was covered up and whether military police investigations were sufficiently rigorous to establish what happened. These remain allegations under investigation rather than findings of criminal guilt against individual personnel.

title: Anduril reveals family of surface-to-air interceptor missiles
body: Anduril released a new family of surface-to-air interceptor missiles in an effort to create a more diverse range of defensive measures while building at scale. Steelfin, a family of highly configurable, mass-producible, surface-to-air interceptor missiles, has been developed to deliver cost, volume and capability across a variety of threats, according to a release . Steefin uses a two-stage architecture compatible with different fielded designs, allowing the defense company to configure interceptor performance while reusing the same parts, production processes, and design across its family of interceptors. The missile has a two-stage design with a booster and terminal interceptor, the release states. The first-stage booster can accommodate various solid rocket motor boosters to meet a set range, performance, booster types, launch configurations or packing density requirements. The second stage terminal interceptor shares the same baseline airframe, avionics, software, flight control system and interfaces across all Steelfin variants. “Steelfin delivers a diversity of effects to meet a diversity of threats,” the release says. “Unlike legacy missiles that carry fixed, inflexible designs that are resistant to change, Steelfin offers a common interceptor architecture that produces a family of interceptor missiles, each of which can be configured for a specific mission.” The interceptor family was built to address threats across the air-and-missile defense spectrum, such as point defense, integrated air and missile defense and ballistic missile defense, while aiming to come at a fraction of the cost of other interceptors in mission classes. To address issues with manufacturing volume and high demand, Anduril expects to “surge” production for any Steelfin variant by moving the interceptor through the same production line, with the same tooling, techniques and facilities, since they share a common architecture and components. Anduril anticipates producing several thousand Steelfin variants per year in the short term, the announcement says. The variants are compatible with established land- and sea-based launch infrastructure, including the M903A2, Mk 41 Vertical Launch System and Typho systems. Steelfin is meant to be able to integrate with any fielded fire control software systems, like AEGIS and IBCS, to ensure it fits into established battle management processes and procedures. “By making Steelfin compatible with fielded air defense hardware and software infrastructure, Anduril has streamlined the path to fielding, accelerated deployment, and ensured that Steelfin will multiply the combat power of the joint force on an operationally-relevant timeline,” the release reads. Anduril has completed ballistic testing with representative air vehicles, and flight testing for Steelfin variants is slated to begin next year. The company’s current plan is an ambitious effort to expand air defense stockpiles after the Iran war dwindled America’s munitions supply, with analysis detailing that it would take at least three years to replenish to pre-war levels . The news comes as the U.S. Army recently awarded Anduril a contract to increase delivery of a “common data layer,” meaning software foundation, baseline for Next Generation Command and Control, or NGC2, beginning with 1 Corps, which commands service members across the Indo-Pacific. The contract’s base period is valued at $162.8 million, but it includes options that could bring the total value up to $1.8 billion over five years.

title: Kanu, Toni Payne Bag Brace As Nigeria’s Super Falcons Rout Comoros In Olympic Qualifiers
body: A brace each from Uchenna Kanu and Toni Payne and another strike from Christy Ucheibe handed Nigeria’s Super Falcons a 5–0 victory over Comoros in the second leg of the 2028 Olympic qualifiers. The victory means the Super Falcons have reached the third round of the African qualifiers for the women’s football event of the Olympic Games with a 7-0 aggregate victory over the Southern Africans. The Super Falcons dominated the game and took the lead in the 41st minute of the clash at the Remo Stars home ground in Ikenne, Ogun State, on Tuesday. Kanu capitalised on a defensive mistake and squared the ball to Payne, who fired into the net. While the first half ended 1-0 in Nigeria’s favour, Kanu doubled the score for Nigeria with 58 minutes on the clock after heading home from a Folashade Ijamilusi delivery. In Control https://t.co/2dMmaqyjrF — NGSuper_Falcons (@NGSuper_Falcons) October 13, 2026 The Cruz Azul Femenil star thought she had gotten her second of the night three minutes later. However, her effort, again from an Ijamilusi cross, was ruled off for offside. But in the 63rd minute, Payne scored her second for the night after forward Blessing Okpe dribbled past two Comoros defenders before finding the Inter Milan Femeni star, who finished with aplomb. Kanu got her brace three minutes later after Ijamilusi delivered another inviting cross to the 29-year-old. FC Dnepr Mogilev of Belarus’s Okpe, who had been a handful since her in troduction in the second half, then won a penalty for Nigeria after being fouled in the box. We are through to the next round of the LA 2028 Olympics! #SoarSuperFalcons https://t.co/jwDND2RMCX — NGSuper_Falcons (@NGSuper_Falcons) October 13, 2026 Christy Ucheibe coolly converted from the spot in the 71st minute to make it 5-0. Nigeria finished both legs with seven goals. They will meet Morocco in the next round of qualifiers to be played early next year. title: Indonesia returns 20 green sea turtles to the ocean after Bali smuggling raid
body: SERANGAN ISLAND, Indonesia (AP) — Indonesian authorities on the tourist island of Bali released 20 protected green sea turtles back into the ocean Tuesday after they were found and seized on an empty boat seemingly abandoned by wildlife smugglers fleeing a police raid. Officers conducted final checks on the turtles at a conservation center on Serangan Island, also known as Turtle Island, in southern Bali. They then carefully lifted the turtles using blue cloths and transported them by small truck to the shoreline. Marine police officers in Bali on Saturday foiled an attempt to smuggle 22 green sea turtles, known by the scientific name Chelonia mydas, in the waters off Serangan Island after receiving a report from residents who suspected sea turtle smuggling activity in the area. Two of the 22 turtles are still sick and need to be treated before they can also be released, Gusti Agung Purnama Wirahadi from the Bali Water and Air Police said Tuesday. All of the turtles, which are protected species in Indonesia, were found alive on the boat, but the suspected smugglers had already fled the scene by the time officers arrived. “We hope that no one will dare to capture, keep, or trade these protected species anymore,” Wirahadi said. Turtle species in Indonesia have been legally protected under conservation and fisheries laws since 1990. A 2018 Environment Ministry regulation further clarified protections for the six species of sea turtles found in the country’s waters. Additional government regulations also prohibit their trade.
