title: PVC collection in Kano impressive, says INEC
body: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Kano State has recorded an impressive turnout of voters collecting their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) across the 44 local government areas of the state. The commission said both newly issued PVCs and previously uncollected cards were being collected by eligible voters. The Public Relations Officer of INEC in Kano, Nahila Bello Dandago, who disclosed this to Daily Trust said the commission deployed 171,000 PVCs in the first batch for distribution. “People are turning up to collect their PVCs, and even those with old cards that they have not collected are coming to collect theirs.” Lassa fever spreads across 119 LGAs as death toll hit 268 FG pays N1.23trn power debt, targets full settlement next year “We have them across all the local government offices, and so far, the turnout for the collection is impressive,” she said. Dandago said the cards had been distributed to INEC offices across the state’s 44 local government areas to make collection accessible to eligible voters. She urged voters who had yet to collect their cards to visit the designated INEC offices to do so. The collection exercise is part of the commission’s efforts to ensure that eligible voters obtain their PVCs ahead of forthcoming elections.

title: Machine learning pioneer Michael I. Jordan dismantles AI doom rhetoric as "grand moralizing performance"
body:
Michael I. Jordan, described by Science in 2016 as "the most influential computer scientist," calls warnings about existential AI threats pure science fiction. In a wide-ranging interview, he takes aim at doomers, company founders, and naive junior researchers.
Jordan, professor emeritus at UC Berkeley, pushed back hard against AI doom rhetoric in an interview with Libération . The 70-year-old machine learning pioneer now works full-time at Inria, the French National Institute for Research in Digital Science and Technology in Paris, where he heads the new "markets and learning" chair. When asked about the summer's AI discourse, he called it "totally frustrating."
Jordan warned about the reckless overuse of the term AI back in 2019 . "I wasn't the only one saying it. It was obvious that it would create the hysteria we're seeing now," he says. "You've seen what happened: AI wasn't enough, so they started talking about AGI, and now it's 'superintelligence'..." Ad
Jordan dismisses AI companies' demands for regulation as "theater," a way of saying "Look, we're the good guys" while they "would like to have total control over how they are regulated." Ad
The resignation of young Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon , which sparked a wave of collective hysteria over an "AIpocalypse" scenario in early September, is a textbook example in Jordan's view. Many young employees at these companies "aren't really engineers," he says. "They come from the humanities, philosophy, or other disciplines. They're 25 years old, they're naive, they don't do engineering work, they've never worked at large companies where real products are developed for real people, with discipline."
They "get together, a bit like in Parisian cafés in the 1920s, to talk about these grand science-fiction ideas." When they resign, they know they're going to attract attention. "It allows them to feel virtuous and to be seen as very important figures. They claim to be giving up money, but in reality, they already have their stock options." Jordan sees the whole thing as "a grand moralizing performance that doesn't serve the real objective it claims to pursue. There's a great deal of naiveté here, which goes hand in hand with a certain cynicism..." Ad
"Superintelligence" is "a science-fiction term," Jordan says, "and a large part of the debates I've witnessed belong to the realm of science fiction." Occasionally discussing far-fetched scenarios is fine. "Talking about it behind the scenes, as a science-fiction topic, is fine. But when it becomes the dominant discourse, it's very, very harmful. For technological development, for young people, and for the mindset of countries alike." The term is currently being pushed on the US tech elite by President Trump, who are happy to play along .
Jordan is especially harsh on Nobel laureate Geoffrey Hinton, who has a track record of making bold claims that don't always hold up . "Geoffrey Hinton has never created a company that offers real services for real people," he says. "Hinton believes that we have figured out how the brain works and that we can reproduce it in silicon; we would therefore be able to copy it as many times as we wanted and, by combining what all these copies learn, we would obtain a kind of exponential growth and, there you have it: superintelligence. None of the steps in this argument is credible. Here, we're in the land of science fiction." Ad
He's slightly more generous toward Yoshua Bengio . "Yoshua is a little different; he takes action and does things that directly focus on safety." Bengio's warnings tend to target shortcomings in current AI technology, such as agent swarms spiraling out of control . Ad
Jordan frames the hack of Hugging Face by OpenAI agents as bad engineering. "In chemical engineering, we would never have had a situation where explosions were allowed to happen just to see how badly things could go wrong." OpenAI was "conducting rather stupid experiments, letting the agents do whatever they wanted and encouraging this behavior." The doomers then loved turning it into something scary. "My God, these agents are self-aware and are trying to find a way to destroy humans." That, too, is science fiction, according to Jordan.
Jordan considers the massive data center investments "just an enormous bet, but we have absolutely no idea whether it will pay off." LLMs are already capable enough for natural language tasks, and trillions spent on data centers won't necessarily deliver much more . "Instead, we often will want to add a bit of specialized knowledge in a particular field based on local knowledge. But you don't need a gigantic data center to do that. Particularly if you use open-weight models that you integrate into your company."

title: Hezbollah explosive smuggling, illegal finance network leads to calls for probe by Lebanese PMs
body: Hezbollah has remained largely silent amid growing public anger and evidence of an explosives-smuggling plot believed to have been intended to facilitate political assassinations in Beirut, making an announcement on Tuesday that only addressed the issue of compensation funds for displaced individuals.Lebanese forces seized 500 kilograms of explosives from a vehicle at a checkpoint in Dahr al-Baidar in the Bekaa Valley late last week, arresting two individuals connected to Hezbollah during what some reports are claiming was an accidental discovery. Embedded within the explosives were metal balls and nails, which are used to maximize damage.Though credit was given to the Lebanese Military for locating the explosives, in addition to another nearly 200 kg. along the Lebanese-Syrian border earlier this week, some Lebanese officials and media have reported that the explosives were uncovered when the vehicle transporting them was involved in an accident.The Alma Education and Research Center noted that the Dahr al-Baidar checkpoint, where the explosives passed through, is a permanent and well-known Internal Security Forces checkpoint, and they questioned why Hezbollah would feel bold enough to risk such a hefty shipment if it had reason to believe the vehicle would undergo inspection.منذ اكثر من ٦ اشهر لفتنا الى ظاهرة تحطيم كاميرات المراقبة في شتورا والمريجات، ولم يتحرك احد. ها ان الغرض من ذلك يتضح اليوم: هناك من كان يحضّر لتمرير متفجرات دون رقيب. هل من يسمع او يتحرّك ؟— George Okais (@OkaisGeorge) October 11, 2026Based on this observation, the center concluded that Hezbollah was certain that there would be no significant inspection, which raises the possibility that similar shipments had previously passed through.Security cameras smashed, possibly linked to explosive smugglingFormer judge and Lebanese Parliament member representing the Zahle district, George Okais, also confirmed that he had complained back in March that security cameras in the Chtoura Municipality and in the town of Jalala had been repeatedly smashed, in what he now believes to be a series of incidents connected to the smuggling of explosives.Alternatively, the center suggested, Hezbollah might have always intended for the shipment to be discovered with the aim of sending a threatening psychological message to the political and security figures working to disarm the organization. Hezbollah's leadership, set against both disarming and Beirut's negotiated ceasefire with Jerusalem, has frequently threatened civil war over the past few months.إنّ إعلان حزب الله عن تخصيص مبالغ مالية كبيرة لإيواء العائلات المتضرّرة يطرح أسئلة خطيرة حول مصادر هذه الأموال، وكيفية إدخالها إلى لبنان ونقلها وتوزيعها خارج الأطر المالية الرسمية. وتزداد خطورة هذه المسألة في ضوء العقوبات التي فرضتها وزارة الخزانة الأميركية على أفراد وشبكات متّهمة بتمويل حزب الله ونقل الأموال عبر قنوات غير شرعية. إنّ مساعدة أهلنا المتضرّرين واجب وطني، لكن معاناتهم لا يمكن أن تشكّل غطاءً لمنظومات مالية موازية أو ذريعة لتجاوز القوانين اللبنانية. لذلك، نطالب الحكومة ومصرف لبنان وهيئة التحقيق الخاصة والسلطات القضائية والأمنية المختصة بالتحرّك الفوري للتحقّق من مصادر هذه الأموال ومساراتها، وكشف أيّ ارتباط محتمل بشبكات خاضعة للعقوبات، ومحاسبة كلّ من يثبت تورّطه في مخالفات مالية. فلا سيادة لدولة لا تحتكر السلاح ولا تفرض سلطتها على حركة الأموال. ولا يمكن القبول بدولة داخل الدولة، لا عسكرياً ولا مالياً. لبنان يحتاج إلى دولة واحدة، وسلاح شرعي واحد، وقانون يُطبَّق على الجميع دون استثناء.— Fouad Makhzoumi (@fmakhzoumi) October 13, 2026MP Najat Saliba claimed to Al Jadeed News that the same type of explosives located in the van had been used to assassinate former Lebanese Prime Minister Rafic Hariri, killed by Hezbollah on February 14, 2005, in Beirut, after a massive truck bomb targeted his motorcade. The attack killed 22 people and wounded over 200.A Lebanese political source told Kan News that the Iran-backed terror group had been mounting pressure on the Lebanese government to bury the incident. However, both Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salman and Lebanese Justice Minister Adel Nassar have committed to full investigations going ahead without delay.Nassar told MTV Lebanon that “there are serious questions about whether these explosives are for internal use or to create new pretexts to plunge Lebanon into new wars.”He added that the explosives were “capable of blowing up an entire neighborhood, and merely storing them in a populated area is considered a crime and warrants prosecution.”Since news of the incident broke, there has been anger and criticism not only in the opposition camp but also among those aligned with Hezbollah on the issue of Israel.Lebanese MP Wadhah al-Sadiq, a hardcore critic of Israel, published that even if the explosives had been intended to target the Jewish state, “Whoever wants to confront Israel does not smuggle explosives into Lebanese territory, nor turn Beirut into a destination for shipments of death…”He added, “We will not accept that the security of the Lebanese remains hostage to Hezbollah's weapons, nor that Beirut once again becomes an arena for assassinations, bombings, and settling scores under any pretext.”من يريد مواجهة إسرائيل لا ينقل المتفجرات إلى الداخل اللبناني، ولا يجعل من بيروت وجهةً لشحنات الموت. 500 كيلوغرام من المتفجرات ضُبطت في ضهر البيدر، وقبل أيام نحو 250 كيلوغراماً أخرى. والسؤال الأخطر: كم شحنة متفجرات مرت من دون أن تُضبط؟ المطلوب من القضاء كشف من أصدر الأوامر، ومن نقل المتفجرات وسهل مرورها، ومن كان سيتسلمها، والأهم من كان سيُستهدف بها. لن نقبل أن يبقى أمن اللبنانيين رهينة سلاح حزب الله، ولا أن تتحول بيروت مجدداً إلى ساحة للاغتيالات والتفجيرات وتصفية الحسابات تحت أي ذريعة.— Waddah Sadek - وضاح صادق (@WaddahSadek) October 11, 2026Hezbollah's Tuesday announcement of $14,000 compensation for displaced individuals has been overshadowed by the incident, with officials paying closer attention to where the funds are coming from.Questions about sources of funds, Iranian linksLebanese MP Fouad Makhzoumi said that there were “serious questions about the sources of these funds, how they were brought into Lebanon, and how they were transported and distributed outside official financial frameworks.”“Assisting our affected people is a national duty, but their suffering cannot serve as a cover for parallel financial systems or a pretext for circumventing Lebanese laws…,” he said.“There can be no sovereignty for a state that does not monopolize arms nor assert its authority over the movement of money. Nor can we accept a state within a state, neither militarily nor financially. Lebanon needs one state, one legitimate weapon, and a law applied to all without exception.”Despite Hezbollah issuing no official response to the allegations, a few figures within or aligned with the group have spoken in its defense.Hezbollah MP Ibrahim Mousawi insisted that the group had “nothing to be ashamed or embarrassed about,” adding that making allegations against it were unacceptable and denying that Hezbollah had ever used its military capabilities internally.Likewise, sanctioned Hezbollah financier Madi Aqil insisted that it was necessary for Hezbollah to transport the explosives into Lebanon for the next war with Israel and admitted that the group had been responsible for the explosives imported through Syria.“If Hezbollah claims responsibility for this matter, it would be making clear to the Lebanese state that it does not accept the state's decision,” he told Al-Jadeed, arguing the Lebanese Republic did not have the right to decide on negotiations or arms.

title: Hezbollah to distribute up to $14,000 per family following war with Israel, official says
body: Lebanon's Hezbollah will provide up to $14,000 in financial assistance to families whose primary homes have been destroyed or rendered uninhabitable during this year's war with Israel, the chairman of the group's Executive Council said on Tuesday.Reuters reported last week that Hezbollah had received $200 million from Iran to help displaced Lebanese families, citing two people with direct knowledge of the transfer, though the US disputed Tehran's ability to provide such financial assistance.Under the plan presented by Hezbollah Executive Council chairman Ali Damoush, eligible families in Beirut and its southern suburbs will reportedly receive $14,000, including $8,000 for furniture and $6,000 for rent. Families elsewhere in Lebanon will reportedly receive $12,000, comprising $8,000 for furniture and $4,000 for rent, maintaining the same rates as in 2024.Damoush claimed the assistance would cover families whose homes were destroyed, deemed uninhabitable following technical assessments, or severely damaged, as well as those displaced from Israeli-occupied areas or nearby locations.The aid will be restricted to families who used the affected properties as their primary residences and do not own a second home, excluding summer homes and abandoned properties, according to the terror group.Payments will be made in four installments over one year, starting with $3,500 for families in Beirut and its southern suburbs and $3,000 elsewhere.Damoush said that eligibility and the type of assistance would be determined based on a set of criteria assessing the extent of damage to each property.US economic pressure on Iran is boosting difficulty in transferring funds to terror proxy HezbollahHezbollah received the cash last month despite tightening US economic pressure on Iran and increasing difficulties in getting funds to Tehran's Lebanese ally, according to the two people who spoke to Reuters.At the time, a Hezbollah official ​said an amount had been secured and that a plan for distributing it would be announced in the coming days, without elaborating on the source of the funds.The United States disputed the Reuters report, saying the money was "not there." Iran has not commented.Damoush on Tuesday declined to comment on either the Reuters report or the US reaction, and declined to provide a figure for the total amount Hezbollah would dedicate to shelter support.

title: On This Day: Final living hostages return from Gaza, as Trump addresses Knesset following ceasefire
body: One year ago, on October 13, 2025, the final 20 living hostages returned from their captivity in the Gaza Strip after over two years of being held in terror captivity.The 20 hostages were: Elkana Bohbot, Matan Angrest, Avinatan Or, Yosef-Haim Ohana, Alon Ohel, Evyatar David, Guy Gilboa-Dalal, Rom Braslavski, Gali Berman, Ziv Berman, Eitan Mor, Segev Kalfon, Nimrod Cohen, Maxim Herkin, Eitan Horn, Matan Zangauker, Bar Kupershtein, David Cunio, Ariel Cunio, and Omri Miran.The Israeli government's official social media pages commemorated the anniversary by posting pictures of some of the 20 hostages reuniting with their respective families.Some embraces say everything words cannot. On October 13, 2025, the final 20 living hostages returned from Gaza following two years in Palestinian Hamas' captivity. Their families could finally hold them again after 738 days, and an entire nation shared their relief, even as we hold deep grief for those who did not return home alive. One year later, we hold the survivors and their families close as they continue to heal and carry the memory of those we lost with us always.  #unforgo7ten— Israel ישראל (@Israel) October 13, 2026Several of the released hostages were suffering from serious medical conditions.Elkana Bohbot, Yosef-Chaim Ohana, Bar Kuperstein, twin brothers Ziv and Gali Berman, David and Ariel Cunio, Rom Braslavski, and Maxim Harkin were taken to Sheba Medical Center in Tel Hashomer for treatment, The Jerusalem Post reported at the time.Several hostages hospitalized for medical treatment following injuries, wounds suffered during captivityEstimates from health care professionals expected the released hostages to be suffering from severe malnutrition and extreme salt and vitamin deficiencies. Additionally, because of the conditions they were kept in, they were at risk of developing refeeding syndrome.The hostages suffered from the long-term consequences of two years of captivity, as extreme starvation leads to loss of muscle and fat, depletion of essential lipids, and the use of whatever muscle remains as a source of energy.More specifically, Alon Ohel suffered a shrapnel injury to his eye, Elkana Bohbot suffered from stomach pain due to overfeeding prior to his release, as well as pain in his legs and lower back, Matan Angrest was reportedly treated for injuries to his hands and fingers without anesthetic, which caused further complications during his time in captivity, and Evyatar David was suffering from nutrient and mineral deficiencies.Alon Ohel was chained in the same tunnel for almost the entire two years he was in captivity, and moved only once to a new tunnel 40 days before being released, Channel 12 reported at the time.Alon was moved unexpectedly to the new tunnel located in the center of the Gaza Strip after hours of journeying. The IDF reported that the move was to use him as a human shield to prevent the military from taking over the area.One year ago today, after two years in Hamas captivity, Israeli hostages were finally reunited with their families. ️ The first hugs. The tears. The overwhelming relief after 738 days of unimaginable suffering at the hands of the Hamas terrorist organization. For two years, an entire nation held its breath, waiting for these moments. And finally, we could breathe again. ❤️ #unforgo7ten #israel #hostages #familyreunion #october7— Israel ישראל (@Israel) October 13, 2026Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his wife, Sara, wrote a handwritten letter to each of the hostages. "On behalf of the entire Jewish people, welcome back! We have been waiting for you; we embrace you. Sara and Benjamin Netanyahu," the notes read.Trump addresses Knesset amid hostage releaseOn the same day, US President Donald Trump flew to Jerusalem and addressed the Knesset plenum following the October 9 announcement of the Gaza ceasefire and his 20-point peace plan, becoming only the fourth sitting US president to address the Israeli legislature.“The hostages are back! It feels so good to say it,” Trump told the attendees. “Like the US right now, it will be the golden age for Israel.” He added that “a lot of people said we were wasting our time” regarding a ceasefire agreement, but thanks to several “great American patriots, we achieved this.”The State Department released a statement on Tuesday commemorating the one-year since the Sharm el-Sheikh Peace Summit."One year ago today, leaders from across the world joined President Trump in Sharm el-Sheikh, Egypt, for the Gaza Peace Summit to affirm their commitment to President Trump's Comprehensive Plan to End the Gaza Conflict. President Trump's leadership ended a war that had no end in sight. Since that historic breakthrough, a series of remarkable achievements have built the foundations for a new Gaza: an enduring ceasefire, the return of every hostage both living and deceased, the establishment of the Board of Peace and a Palestinian technocratic administration to run Gaza, and a fully costed recovery plan.  Humanitarian assistance has also increased so that food support is reaching more Palestinians, while Hamas theft of aid has dwindled.  These achievements, while remarkable, represent only the beginning," the State Department said."Rebuilding Gaza will be an arduous, multi-year process, and implementation will be difficult.  But we are making real progress toward a demilitarized Gaza, where Palestinians can live without Hamas rule, and Israel can have genuine and lasting security," the statement added.Hamas downplayed release of hostages as Israeli 'failure, surrender'Additionally, Hamas's military wing, the Izzadin al-Qassam Brigades, claimed that Israel "failed to recover" the hostages through military pressure, and has now "surrendered.""We declare our commitment to the agreement and its associated timetables, as long as the occupation [Israel] adheres to them," the terror group also claimed.Meanwhile, 1,716 Palestinians from Gaza detained by Israel are expected to be released at Gaza's Nasser Hospital, an official involved in the operation told Reuters at the time.Additionally, 250 Palestinians who had been serving life sentences in Israeli prisons are expected to be released to the West Bank, Jerusalem, and abroad.Remains of four murdered hostages returned later that dayAdditionally, the remains of four murdered hostages, Yossi Sharabi, Guy Illouz, Bipin Joshi, and Captain Daniel Peretz, were returned to Israel that evening for burial.In response to the Hamas announcement that the terror organization would only return four of the deceased hostages on Monday evening, the Hostage Families Forum called for an immediate suspension of Israel's agreement with Hamas until every deceased hostage was returned."Hamas's violation of the agreement must be met with a very serious response from the government and the mediators," a statement from the forum read. "An agreement must be honored by both sides. If Hamas does not fulfill their part, Israel should not fulfill its part either."After the return of the remains of the four murdered hostages, there were still 18 Israelis whose remains were held captive in the Gaza Strip. The final hostage, St.-Sgt.-Maj. Ran Gvili's remains were returned on January 26.Amichai Stein, Jerusalem Post Staff, and Reuters contributed to this report.

title: Who is Yuki Imai, the Japanese journalist Russia has arrested on espionage charges?
body: A Japanese journalist has been detained on suspicion of espionage on Sakhalin , Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB) said. The agency identified him as a Japanese national and a correspondent for the newspaper Hokkaido Shimbun but did not release his name. He was detained in Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk shortly before he planned to leave Russia and taken to Moscow. The FSB released footage of the operation with the detainee’s face blurred. Officers appear to have seized him at a hotel. The footage shows officers forcing him to unlock his devices, and he appears surprised when they accuse him of espionage. The FSB said the journalist was gathering information about Russian military personnel on instructions from Japanese intelligence. According to the agency, he was collecting data on the number of Kuril Islands residents mobilized for the war in Ukraine and on residents who volunteered to fight. The detainee is 34-year-old Yuki Imai , according to the case record from Moscow’s Lefortovsky District Court. On October 13, the court ordered him held in custody in an espionage case under Article 276 of Russia’s Criminal Code. He faces up to 20 years in prison. Imai had been visiting Russia since 2014. His most recent visit began in the summer of 2026 , according to the news outlet Ostorozhno, Novosti ( 1, 2) . He studied at St. Petersburg State University and posted photographs from his trips around Moscow and St. Petersburg. He said he had “a bit of an interest in Soviet military equipment,” as well as Russian culture — classical music, ballet, and Soviet cinema. The footage of his detention showed a book by Ivan Bunin in his suitcase. According to Ostorozhno, Novosti, Imai had recently published articles about the State Duma elections and the unveiling of a monument in Khabarovsk commemorating the Soviet Union’s victory over Japan . He also wrote about Russia’s strengthening ties with North Korea. During his most recent trip, Imai visited Primorsky Krai, with stops in Vladivostok and Nakhodka and a visit to a children’s arts center there. He interviewed Russian-speaking residents of Japan and took an interest in life in the Russian Far East, the Soviet-Japanese War, and friendship between Russia and Japan. Imai’s most recent article, published on October 5, is a report from Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk about the presence of North Korean nationals in the region. News of Imai’s detention came amid reports that Tokyo had extradited a member of the Russian group Qilin to Germany , according to the news outlet Agentstvo. Japanese authorities detained the 28-year-old Russian national in May on suspicion of involvement in a September 2024 cyberattack on a logistics company in Germany. Qilin is ransomware used by hackers, including those linked to North Korea. Related reading ‘He’s an idiot.’ Evan Gershkovich says Putin spent more than an hour trying to convince a world leader that the WSJ reporter really was a spy. The last time a Japanese journalist was detained in Russia on espionage allegations was in 2019 . He was accused of trying to obtain classified materials about Russia’s military capabilities in the Far East and was expelled from the country. Russian authorities use detained foreigners in exchanges for Russians facing prosecution abroad . For example, in 2023, Russia charged Wall Street Journal correspondent Evan Gershkovich with espionage. A court sentenced him to 16 years in a penal colony. Gershkovich was freed in a prisoner exchange with Western countries in 2024. Relations between Russia and Japan deteriorated after Putin made his first trip to the Kuril Islands in August , visiting Iturup. In response, Japan summoned the Russian ambassador and lodged a “strong protest.” Further reading For decades, Putin has offered Japan a compromise on the Kuril Islands. So why, on his first visit to the islands this week, did he talk about Russians’ ‘genetic code of winners’ instead? The story you’re reading was written by one of our living, breathing journalists and translated from Russian using an AI model configured to follow our strict editorial standards. This translation process is the result of extensive testing and refinements to ensure our English-language coverage is timely and accurate. A Meduza editor reviews every draft before publication. If you find any errors in this translation, please contact us at reports@meduza.io . To read Meduza’s exclusive content in English, please subscribe to our newsletter .

title: PAU Alumni Conference to Bring 400+ Leaders Together to Connect Ideas, Opportunities
body: The Pan-Atlantic University Alumni Association (PAUAA) has announced its 2026 International Alumni Conference, scheduled for Thursday, October 22, at the Ecobank Pan African Centre (EPAC), Victoria Island, Lagos, bringing together more than 400 business leaders, entrepreneurs, academics and alumni to explore how professional networks can become engines of enterprise, innovation and economic growth. Themed ‘The Advantage: Connecting People, Ideas and Opportunities,’ the conference is anchored on the conviction that an alumni community should be more than a network for reunions; it should be a productive force that builds businesses, scales enterprises and creates lasting economic value. The conference will feature distinguished guests, including Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer of Coleman Cables, George Olutope Onafowokan; Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer of West African Exploration and Production Company (WEPC), part of the Dangote Group, and President of the Nigerian Association of Petroleum Explorationists (NAPE), Mrs Olajumoke Cecilia Ajaye; and Vice-Chancellor of Pan-Atlantic University, Professor Enase Okonedo. Speaking ahead of the conference, President of the Pan-Atlantic University Alumni Association, Dr Onyebuchi Odianjo, said the event would harness the collective strength of the university’s alumni community to create meaningful opportunities for individuals, businesses and the wider economy. “The true advantage of an alumni community lies in its ability to connect people, ideas and opportunities that create lasting value. Through this conference, we aim to move beyond networking to meaningful engagement, partnerships and practical collaboration that support individual success and contribute to the growth of Nigerian businesses and the wider economy,” she said. The full-day conference will feature two plenary panel discussions designed to explore both the practical realities of building successful enterprises and the diverse paths through which alumni achieve professional and personal fulfilment. The first session, ‘Built to Scale,’ will examine the strategies, challenges and decisions involved in transforming business ideas and entrepreneurial ventures into sustainable, scalable enterprises. Discussions will focus on business growth, innovation, leadership and the capacity to build organisations that endure. The second session, ‘Beyond the Classroom: Alumni Who Redefined Success,’ will explore how alumni have challenged conventional definitions of achievement, navigated career transitions and pursued alternative paths to professional fulfilment and impact. The first panel will feature Deputy Vice-Chancellor, Pan-Atlantic University, Dr Peter Bamkole; Co-Founder and Chief Technology Officer, Seamless Technologies, Mr Deji Lana; broadcaster and media and communications professional, Mrs Titilayo Oyinsan; Mrs Temi Salami, popularly known as Global Temi; and Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer, Midwestern Oil and Gas, Mrs. Elozino Olaniyan. The session will be moderated by Mr Eyo O. Eyo. The second panel will feature Director, Commercial and Communications, News Central TV, Mrs Rosemary Egabor-Afolahan; Public Relations Manager, MTN Nigeria, Dr Goodluck Lakinbofa; content creator, digital educator and Co-Founder of Crea8torium, Mr Salem King; and award-winning event host, television presenter, actress, model and strategic communications consultant, Mojibade Show. The session will be moderated by Mrs Onyinyechi Aderibigbe. Ms Jemimah Ugiagbe will serve as the compere and master of ceremonies, guiding proceedings throughout the conference. Beyond the panel sessions, the programme will include a keynote address, interactive question-and-answer sessions, an alumni recognition segment and networking opportunities. The event will provide a platform for alumni, industry leaders and other stakeholders to exchange ideas, strengthen professional relationships and explore collaborations that can translate shared knowledge and connections into tangible business opportunities. The conference will commence at 8:00 a.m. and conclude with a networking cocktail. The Pan-Atlantic University Alumni Association is the official alumni body of Pan-Atlantic University, committed to fostering lifelong engagement among graduates and creating opportunities for leadership, innovation and enterprise.

title: US continues sharing intelligence with Ukraine, Trump says amid Russia deal backlash. Questions remain over missed warning for latest attack
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); US President Donald Trump said on 13 October that the US continues to share intelligence with Ukraine, following reports that Washington had threatened to suspend intelligence assistance unless Kyiv stopped striking Russian oil refineries, POLITICO reported. The comments came after Ukraine received no advance warning from its partners ahead of Russia's latest ballistic missile strike, raising fresh questions about intelligence sharing between Kyiv and Washington. “We are helping them, and we are sharing intel. We want the war to end,” Trump told reporters at the White House, according to POLITICO, reaffirming US support after his recent efforts to reach an agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin drew criticism over his approach to the war. Trump reaffirms support after backlash over Russia deal Last week, the US threatened to cut intelligence sharing if Ukraine did not stop attacking Russian oil refineries. Zelenskyy did not publicly confirm the reported threat. The reports came amid criticism of Trump’s announcement of a deal to buy Russian oil and his pressure on Kyiv to make concessions, even as Russia continued attacking Ukraine. Zelenskyy said Ukraine had refrained from striking Russian oil refineries and the energy sector for two days after Trump announced an energy ceasefire. Russia, however, continued attacking Ukrainian energy facilities and critical infrastructure, he said, with 19 Ukrainian regions coming under attack during those two days. Trump said Monday that both Russia and Ukraine had violated the energy ceasefire, arguing that each side was responsible. He also said Putin wanted a deal and that Washington needed to persuade Zelenskyy to agree. Trump's latest comments publicly reaffirm that intelligence sharing is continuing. However, the circumstances surrounding the latest Russian strike have raised questions about whether Ukraine is receiving the early warnings it needs to protect civilians. Ukraine received no warning before latest Russian strike Early warnings of incoming Russian ballistic missiles give Ukrainians a brief window to reach shelter before impact. US intelligence helps make those warnings possible, giving civilians crucial time to protect themselves. Zelenskyy said Russia's latest attack involved five ballistic missiles and more than 100 drones, and that Ukraine received no warning from its partners before the strike. “Intelligence on Russian ballistic missile launches helps save lives,” Zelenskyy said Tuesday. “This is precisely what helps prevent people from being killed — when there is an early warning about ballistic missiles.” He added that Ukraine had received no warning ahead of the attack. Explore further Russian ballistic missiles hit Kyiv before sirens, gap that lands hard amid fears that Washington could cut data that warns of launches Ukraine normally receives alerts about impending Russian missile launches through the Battlespace Command and Control Center, a system operated by the US military and NATO members, among others, POLITICO reported. Citing an unnamed official familiar with the matter, POLITICO reported that US officials attributed the missing warning to bad weather. The explanation reportedly raised doubts among Ukrainian officials. Ukrainian Air Force spokesperson Yurii Ihnat said the warning system had failed to transmit information on previous occasions. He said specialists would work with international partners to resolve any technical problems. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said Tuesday that intelligence sharing through the platform was continuing, according to POLITICO. title: Four-year courses must end in four years, Alausa tells varsities as FG unveils new agreement
body: expands monitoring committee to cover academic, non-teaching unions By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The federal government has pledged to honour its agreements with tertiary institution workers, declaring that Nigerian students must no longer lose precious academic years to strikes triggered by unfulfilled government commitments. Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, gave the assurance on Tuesday in Abuja while unveiling the 2026 agreements between the Federal Government and staff unions in universities, polytechnics and colleges of education. Alausa, who described the agreements as a major step towards restoring confidence in government-union relations, said the administration of President Bola Tinubu was determined to end the cycle of broken promises, industrial disputes and disruptions to academic calendars that had plagued the country’s tertiary education system for decades. He declared that a four-year degree programme must be completed in four years, insisting that the Federal Government would fulfil its obligations under the newly unveiled agreements. “During his campaign, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu promised that a four-year course would be completed in four years. Today, through his leadership, these agreements give practical expression to that pledge: A promise made, a promise kept, and trust restored,” the minister said. The agreements cover the Consolidated Academic Tools Allowance, CATA, for the Academic Staff Union of Polytechnics, ASUP, and the Colleges of Education Academic Staff Union, COEASU, as well as the Consolidated Non-Teaching Tools Allowance, CONTTA, for non-teaching staff unions across universities,polytechnics and colleges of education. The allowances are to take effect from January 1, 2026, in line with the agreements and applicable implementation guidelines. Alausa, however, acknowledged that the unveiling of the agreements was only the beginning, stressing that their credibility would ultimately depend on the government’s ability to implement the provisions faithfully. “Let me state clearly, on behalf of the Federal Government: We will fulfil our own part of these historic agreements. We recognise that public confidence will depend on the obligations we honour after this ceremony,” he said. In a move aimed at preventing future disputes over the implementation of agreements, the minister announced the expansion of the existing Implementation and Monitoring Committee, IMC, established for the agreement with the Academic Staff Union of Universities, ASUU. Under the new arrangement, the committee will become a single monitoring platform for agreements with academic and non-academic staff unions across tertiary institutions. Its membership will be broadened to accommodate the relevant unions and stakeholders, with responsibility for tracking agreed milestones, assessing progress, resolving implementation challenges and ensuring accountability through periodic reports. According to Alausa, the committee will monitor both achievements and outstanding obligations to ensure that commitments are implemented within agreed timelines. He said the government intended to identify implementation difficulties early and resolve them before they degenerated into disputes capable of disrupting academic activities. The minister urged government agencies to discharge their responsibilities diligently, while governing councils and institutional managements were directed to maintain accurate records, comply with implementation guidelines and cooperate fully with the committee. He also urged union leaders to keep their members informed and channel emerging concerns through established mechanisms. Alausa recalled that agreements between successive governments and staff unions had, for decades, been undermined by delayed, incomplete or unfulfilled commitments, leading to recurring industrial disputes. The consequences, he said, extended beyond the negotiating parties, with students losing valuable learning time, families bearing additional financial burdens and teaching and research suffering repeated setbacks. He noted that prolonged strikes had created uncertainty around academic calendars, making it difficult for students to complete their programmes within the prescribed periods. The minister said the Tinubu administration was determined to reverse the trend by building a system in which agreements were respected and academic activities proceeded without unnecessary interruptions. He maintained that industrial harmony was indispensable to educational excellence, adding that stable academic calendars would enable institutions to plan effectively, sustain research and allow students to concentrate on their studies. “We must strengthen early consultation and resolve differences through constructive dialogue, mutual respect and good-faith engagement. Our students and their families must remain at the centre of these efforts,” he said. Explaining the significance of the agreements, Alausa said CATA and CONTTA were designed to support the professional and operational needs of eligible academic and non-academic personnel. He said the allowances reflected the government’s recognition that the quality of tertiary education was inseparable from the welfare, motivation and professional wellbeing of the workforce. According to him, improved staff welfare must go beyond financial allowances to include fair treatment, transparent promotion processes, occupational safety and opportunities for career advancement. He pledged that the Federal Ministry of Education would continue to work with relevant agencies, governing councils, institutional managements and unions to create an environment in which personnel could perform their duties effectively. The minister also commended the leadership of ASUP, COEASU and the non-teaching staff unions for their participation in the negotiations, while acknowledging the contributions of relevant ministries, departments, agencies and technical teams. Alausa reserved special commendation for the Federal Government Tertiary Institutions Expanded Negotiation Committee, chaired by Malam Yayale Ahmed, whose work he said had brought the negotiations to a successful conclusion. He praised Ahmed and members of the committee for their patience, experience and dedication in resolving the issues involved in the negotiations. The minister also credited President Tinubu’s support and guidance for making the agreements possible, describing them as evidence of the administration’s commitment to the welfare of education workers and the future of Nigerian students. Signed agreements were presented to representatives of academic and non-academic staff unions, including ASUP, COEASU, the Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities, SSANU, the Non-Academic Staff Union of Educational and Associated Institutions, NASU, the National Association of Academic Technologists, NAAT, and other unions representing staff in polytechnics and colleges of education. The ultimate test of the agreements, however, will be whether the allowances are implemented as stipulated and the monitoring mechanism can prevent outstanding obligations from triggering another round of industrial disputes. To prevent future disputes from escalating into industrial action, the Minister announced plans to expand the existing implementation and monitoring committee established for ASUU into a single body responsible for monitoring all agreements with academic and non-academic staff unions in tertiary institutions. He said the committee’s membership had been broadened to accommodate the unions and other relevant stakeholders, adding that the government would also work towards making it a permanent structure. According to him, the decision followed the success of having a single committee negotiate with the various unions, which helped accelerate the renegotiation process. He said the expanded panel would provide a platform for identifying implementation challenges early and resolving grievances before they disrupt academic activities. He urged union leaders to channel complaints through the committee rather than resorting to public confrontations or threats of strikes. Alausa added that the agreements contained a provision for review every three years, allowing the government and unions to reopen discussions on emerging concerns and mutually agreed adjustments. In his remarks, Ahmed who served as Permanent Secretary in the Federal Ministry of Education between 1997 and 2000, said the success of the negotiations depended on a spirit of give-and-take between the government and labour unions. According to him, union leaders demonstrated responsibility by defending their members’ interests while also appreciating the financial and administrative constraints facing the government. The elder statesman, however, stressed that unveiling the agreement was only the beginning, insisting that its successful implementation would be the real test of the negotiations. “To me, this is the beginning of our job. The most important thing is for us to have a seamless agreement collectively, which the government is not only willing but comfortable to implement to the letter,” he said. He expressed confidence in the commitment of Dr Alausa and the Minister of State for Education, Prof. Suwaiba Ahmad, to ensure that the pact was implemented, while commending President Tinubu for what he described as the political will to address longstanding challenges in the education sector. The negotiation chairman also disclosed that discrepancies had been identified in parts of the agreement, assuring the unions that the issues would be addressed in collaboration with the Ministry of Education and the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission. Earlier in their separate remarks, the National President, Academic Staff Union of Polytechnics ,ASUP, Comrade Shammah Kpanja; his counterpart at the Colleges of Education Academic Staff Union,COEASU, Dr. Lawal Bazza; and the President of the Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities,SSANU, Comrade Ibrahim Mohammed, commended the Federal Government for the speedy renegotiation of the agreement and the progress made in its implementation. Kpanja described the process as the fastest in the history of the union’s negotiations, noting that talks began in December 2025 and culminated in the signing of the agreement in April 2026. He disclosed that implementation had commenced, with members receiving outstanding arrears between July and September, but urged the government to ensure that all other provisions of the agreement were fully implemented. He also welcomed the planned inauguration of a joint implementation committee, expressing hope that it would accelerate implementation before the end of the year. Similarly, Bazza said the Colleges of Education subsector had already achieved more than 70 per cent implementation of the agreement, expressing confidence that the committee would help address the outstanding provisions. The post Four-year courses must end in four years, Alausa tells varsities as FG unveils new agreement appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Ghana records progress on reparatory justice agenda – Ablakwa
body: Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa says Ghana has made significant progress in its campaign for reparatory justice following the adoption of a Ghana-led United Nations resolution declaring the transatlantic slave trade the greatest crime against humanity. He said the resolution, which received the support of 123 UN member states, had helped build international momentum for restitution, apologies and other measures to address the historical injustices associated with slavery. Speaking in an interview on TV3 on Saturday, October 10, 2026, Mr Ablakwa said several countries and international institutions had begun taking steps towards addressing the legacy of the transatlantic slave trade. He attributed the progress to the leadership of President John Dramani Mahama, who serves as the African Union Champion for Reparatory Justice, and Ghana’s diplomatic engagements at the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in New York. According to the minister, Ghana’s participation in the global meeting was strategic, with engagements spanning railway development, artificial intelligence governance, agriculture, agribusiness and trade expansion, alongside efforts to advance the reparatory justice agenda. He said a side event organised by Ghana on reparatory justice had attracted significant international support, including participation from several European countries that had previously abstained from the resolution. Mr Ablakwa said some of the countries had expressed their willingness to work with Ghana on restitution and had presented catalogues of cultural artefacts they were prepared to return. He also described the participation of the United States in the side event as a significant development, saying it suggested a shift towards engagement, although the country did not make a statement at the event. The minister said the passage of the resolution itself was a major achievement, but added that Ghana was already witnessing concrete developments arising from its advocacy. He cited an apology by French President Emmanuel Macron, the repeal of France’s Code Noir, and plans to establish a scientific commission with Ghana in Accra to conduct further research on the history and legacy of slavery. Mr Ablakwa also said Denmark had apologised and pledged resources to support the preservation of Ghana’s forts and castles, which he described as important sites for historical education and truth-telling. He noted that some of the historical structures had deteriorated, citing sites in Keta, Shama and the Awutu Senya area, and said the renewed international interest presented an opportunity to preserve them. The minister further welcomed apologies from Pope Leo XIV and the Archbishop of Canterbury over the historical role of religious institutions in justifying slavery. He said the Church of England had pledged a £100 million fund to support young African entrepreneurs and scholars, adding that the government was working with the church to agree on the modalities for implementing the initiative. Mr Ablakwa also disclosed that the Netherlands and Germany had presented Ghana with catalogues of more than 2,000 artefacts they were prepared to return. He said the Netherlands had already returned the head of King Badu II, a traditional leader who resisted enslavers. According to him, the return of the historical artefact was significant because it demonstrated the resistance mounted by African traditional leaders against slave raiders and offered an important symbol of African courage and capability for future generations. Mr Ablakwa said Ghana had also established three global panels to advance the reparatory justice agenda. The panels include one on reparatory justice, chaired by President Mahama; a restitution panel chaired by Professor Gavua; and a panel of international legal experts examining possible legal grounds for compelling those responsible for slavery to make amends and provide compensation. He said preliminary reports from the legal experts showed progress in exploring the legal dimensions of the campaign. The minister also commended Jamaica for presenting a petition to the United Kingdom’s Privy Council, saying Ghana was closely monitoring the response as preparations continued for the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua and Barbuda. Mr Ablakwa maintained that the developments recorded since the adoption of the UN resolution demonstrated that Ghana’s campaign was producing tangible results and strengthening international cooperation on reparatory justice.

title: New Brunswick gets $219 million loan from Ottawa for hydroelectric dam repair work
body:
The federal government is investing nearly $270 million in loans and grants to help New Brunswick modernize energy facilities that officials say are key to Ottawa’s plan to double the capacity of Canada’s electrical grid by 2050.
The bulk of the money is a $219-million loan from the Canada Infrastructure Bank to extend the life of the province’s largest hydroelectric dam, located west of Fredericton on the Saint John River.
The province will also receive a $50-million grant to upgrade its Salisbury Terminal near Moncton, which officials say is key to managing the flow of electricity across the provincial grid.
Federal Energy Minister Tim Hodgson made the announcements Tuesday during a news conference in front of the massive Mactaquac Dam.
“New Brunswick is critical to this plan and so are today’s investments,” he said. “Together, these two projects will strengthen New Brunswick’s electricity system while creating jobs, attracting investment, supporting affordability, and lowering emissions.”
New Brunswick’s Crown-owned electric utility is preparing the 672-megawatt Mactaquac Generation Station for a multibillion-dollar overhaul aimed at extending its operational life to 2068.
The new funding will pay for technical studies, regulatory reviews, First Nations engagement and planning for the Mactaquac Life Achievement Project, according to Natural Resources Canada.
In 2016, NB Power agreed to a plan in 2016 to spend up to $3.6 billion to prolong the life of the dam, which would have otherwise been decommissioned by 2030 due to concrete swelling.
The federal government is investing $269 million in loans and grants to help New Brunswick modernize a pair of energy facilities that officials say are key to the country’s electricity goals. (Oct. 13, 2026)
The new funding will support technical studies, regulatory reviews, First Nations engagement and planning for the Mactaquac Life Achievement Project, according to Natural Resources Canada.
On Tuesday, NB Power CEO Lori Clark said the total cost for the project is now expected to be close to $9 billion.
Hodgson would not commit the federal Liberal government to spending more on the dam, noting that electricity generation is within provincial jurisdiction.
However, he said the federal government will need to help provinces and territories keep costs low as they work to meet federal clean energy regulations that call for a net-zero electricity grid by 2050.
“In the budget coming up, you will see a number of initiatives we are working on to work … with provinces and territories to help them realize the growth that they need in an affordable way,” the minister told reporters.
“This is clearly an indication that we understand how important it is for our prosperity to grow our electricity generating capabilities and we understand that the federal government needs to do its part in helping to make that affordable.”
New Brunswick Premier Susan Holt said the Mactaquac Generating Station is important to the entire Maritime region.
In the event of a system-wide blackout, the dam can start generating electricity without relying on an external power supply, making the largest so-called “black-start” facility in the region.
“We often call it the battery of the Maritimes,” said Holt. “Having this kind of renewable energy that we can turn on and off is critical, not only to our province, but to our neighbours in Prince Edward Island and in Nova Scotia and beyond.” The dam supplies 30 per cent of the province’s renewable energy requirements and 20 per cent of its overall electricity demand, officials said.
The investments come as NB Power is looking for ways to fix ageing infrastructure without imposing massive rate hikes on its customers.
Since the 1980s, concrete portions of the the dam have been affected by a chemical process called alkali-aggregate reaction. The reaction causes concrete to swell and crack, requiring substantial repairs and maintenance.
Just last week, NB Power applied to the provincial regulator to raise rates by 17.4 per cent over the next three years as it plans to spend $4 billion on maintaining the provincial grid.
Some of that money will be used to transition the province’s only remaining coal-fired generating plant to a facility that burns wood pellets to generate electricity.

title: Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid announces Dh2.1 trillion of projects under way in Dubai
body: Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid, Vice President and Ruler of Dubai, has announced a Dh2.1 trillion portfolio of active projects in the emirate that cover housing, transport, aviation and infrastructure. Speaking at the Mohammed bin Rashid Leadership Forum at Dubai World Trade Centre, Sheikh Mohammed said the emirate was “building a city within a city” with further projects set to be announced. The annual forum brought together 1,000 government and private sector leaders, alongside experts, decision-makers and academics. “Our momentum is continuous and our achievements are ongoing. This is a remarkable period for growth and development; the ideal time to invest in Dubai and its infrastructure,” Sheikh Mohammed said. He said the emirate was investing heavily in housing, transport and infrastructure to prepare for a new phase of economic growth. “Cities that aspire for progress act before others,” he said, calling for leaders capable of translating ideas into tangible outcomes. The projects include Dh1.1 trillion allocated for real estate development to 2030, with about 350,000 residential units planned. Aviation investment also features prominently, with Dh128 billion for Al Maktoum International Airport – designed to handle up to 260 million passengers annually, alongside Dh328 billion to expand the Emirates and flydubai fleets and Dh18.7 billion for a new Emirates engineering and maintenance complex. Infrastructure spending includes Dh100 billion for road upgrades and the Dubai Metro Blue and Gold lines, Dh151 billion for new power and water grid infrastructure and Dh80 billion for the Dubai Strategic Sewerage Tunnels system. A further Dh100 billion has been set aside to develop Phase 2 of the Dubai International Financial Centre.

title: The Amount of Bitcoin on Exchanges Is Shrinking. Is a Rally Imminent?
body: Bitcoin Magazine The Amount of Bitcoin on Exchanges Is Shrinking. Is a Rally Imminent? Bitcoin’s price could be due a move upwards as the supply of the leading cryptocurrency on exchanges shrinks. That’s according to a researcher at data firm CryptoQuant, who wrote in a Monday report that bitcoin on exchanges has dropped to 2.67 million from 2.8 million since February. The price of bitcoin was recently $83,485, unmoved over a 24-hour period but up 8% over the past 30 days after having its best quarter in years. Its surge in August and September has led a number of analysts to declare the bear market is over. “If buying demand continues to improve while exchange supply remains low, BTC could benefit from a supply-demand imbalance, creating favorable conditions for a longer-term upward trend,” the report by on-chain researcher Rei Researcher read. It added: “More importantly, in recent weeks, bitcoin has recovered from its lows while exchange reserves have continued to decline. This is a notable development, suggesting that the supply readily available for trading is decreasing even as the market recovers.” The report further noted that it was possible investors were taking bitcoin off exchanges to put in cold storage solutions. Bitcoin’s price was mostly trading under $65,000 for the first half of 2026. The coin spent most of this year in a bear market following the all-time high of $126,080 it hit in October 2025. But that all changed in August. News that the U.S. Treasury would double the size of its liquidity-support buyback operations, weakening the dollar but strengthening bitcoin and other non-yield bearing assets. Now, the so-called debasement trade — where investors throw money at an asset to hedge against a currency losing its value — is hot again. Bitcoin is benefiting from the trade, analysts say, as it did in 2024 and 2025. Bitcoin’s price is still more than 30% below its record. This post The Amount of Bitcoin on Exchanges Is Shrinking. Is a Rally Imminent? first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Mathew Di Salvo .

title: OpenAI's AI agent platform is used by twice as many companies as Anthropic's, new VentureBeat survey finds
body:
Twice as many companies use OpenAI's agent orchestration platform as Anthropic's, VentureBeat Intelligence found in its September survey on agent orchestration . OpenAI holds that lead even though Anthropic may lead OpenAI on other important indicators. For example, Ramp, the corporate card and spending company, reports that more businesses now pay for Anthropic than for OpenAI.
An agent orchestration platform is the software that hands tasks to AI agents , calls tools, and keeps agents within their permissions. Among companies using one, 43% said they use OpenAI's, 22% said they use Anthropic's, and 21% said they use Google's. The survey named the products: OpenAI’s Agents SDK and Responses API, Anthropic’s Claude Agent SDK and Managed Agents, and Google’s Enterprise Agent Platform.
Of 107 companies using an agent orchestration platform, 43% use OpenAI's, 22% Anthropic's and 21% Google's. Source: VB Pulse survey, September 2026.
We also asked companies to name their primary agent orchestration platform. Of the companies using one, 25% named OpenAI's, 18% named Google's, and 16% named Anthropic's. The rest named platforms such as Salesforce’s Agentforce, Microsoft’s Copilot Studio, Amazon Bedrock, and open-source frameworks such as LangChain.
A second September survey, on AI infrastructure and compute , asked which cloud and model providers companies use to run AI in production. For cloud, 51% of respondents said they use Google Cloud, 36% Microsoft Azure, and 23% Amazon Web Services. For models, 41% said they use OpenAI’s, 39% Google’s Gemini, and 15% Anthropic’s.
When asked which provider is their main used in production, 32% named Google Cloud or Gemini, and 22% named OpenAI. Just 6% named Anthropic. It's important to note that, some companies that run OpenAI's models through Microsoft Azure, or Anthropic's Claude models through Amazon's or Google's clouds, may have named those clouds instead.
To give customers choice, Google sells both a major cloud and its own leading models. Counting either offering, 68% of respondents use Google Cloud or Gemini, against 62% that use Microsoft Azure or OpenAI.
Home Depot is a good example of how a company can run mostly on Google and still use other providers' models. "We're a pretty hefty Google shop, so we've got a lot of Google ADK running around there," Angie Brown, Home Depot's EVP and CIO, said in an interview for VentureBeat's Beyond the Pilot podcast, which will air later this month. ADK is Google's Agent Development Kit software for building AI agents. Brown said the vast majority of Home Depot's data sits in Google's BigQuery data warehouse. Home Depot also uses OpenAI's models through Microsoft Azure to judge the results it gets from Google's models, and it uses Anthropic's Claude to write code and OpenAI's models to review that code, Brown said. "So it's not that we are a Google-only shop," Brown said.
Anthropic, which said in June that it had confidentially filed for an initial public offering, plans to host selected institutional investors at a pre-IPO investor day at its San Francisco headquarters on Wednesday, Bloomberg reports . Ramp, which tracks what U.S. businesses on its platform pay for, reported on September 9 that 43.8% paid Anthropic for subscriptions or tokens, against 39.8% for OpenAI.
However, it’s important to note that Ramp’s data is biased toward the customers it tracks, which tend to be more tech-forward companies than average . Ramp’s figures cover only businesses that use Ramp’s cards and software, and Ramp counts each business once, so a 50-person company counts the same as a 50,000-person one. Because small companies far outnumber large ones, they weigh heavily in Ramp’s figures.
Ramp and VentureBeat measure different things in different groups of companies. Ramp counts how many businesses on its platform pay each company. VentureBeat asked people at organizations with 100 or more employees, and consultants serving them, which agent orchestration platforms they use, and which providers they use to run AI in production. A business can pay for Anthropic’s Claude subscriptions, and for Claude’s API to run coding tools, while running its agents on OpenAI’s platform.
Revenue comparisons between OpenAI and Anthropic also depend on what exactly is counted. OpenAI's annualized revenue is about $50 billion, roughly $20 billion below the $70 billion figure widely reported in September, according to Axios . The $70 billion figure counted OpenAI's sales through cloud partners, the way Anthropic counts its own. Tech stocks dropped on October 8 after the lower figure was reported, according to CNN . Our surveys did not ask about either company's revenue or Anthropic's planned IPO.
We asked companies planning to adopt a new, additional, or replacement agent orchestration platform within 12 months which platforms they are considering, and told them they could name several. Of the 61 companies that named at least one, 33% named Anthropic's, 30% named OpenAI's and 25% named Google's.
So, Anthropic's platform shows up on about as many shopping lists as OpenAI's.
Of the companies considering Anthropic's agent orchestration platform, 60% do not currently use it.
Businesses on Ramp's platform are switching AI model providers more often than at any time in Ramp's data. Ramp reported on October 6 that 8% of businesses switched providers in an average month over the three months through September. Our agent orchestration survey also asked about a related step: Whether companies had replaced the AI model inside a production app in the past year while keeping the app around it. A replacement can mean moving to another provider's model, or to a newer model from the same provider. Of the companies surveyed, 62% had replaced a model inside a production app. Among those companies, 59% saw performance drop and had to rework the app, or went back to the original model.
Only 19% of the companies that swapped a model said the swap took almost no engineering work. For 75% of the companies that swapped, the switch took a few days of engineering work or more, or they stopped before finishing.
Brown described why switching models is costly at Home Depot: "One of the things is the context training that has to be done anytime there's a switch, so there's a stickiness level there that comes in."
Consultants reported swaps at a higher rate than in-house respondents, meaning people who work on AI for their own employer. Of consultants, 81% said their main client had swapped a model in the past year, against 51% of in-house respondents at their own companies. So, consultants pushed the overall 62% above what in-house respondents reported.
In a third September survey on agentic context layers , 58% of companies running retrieval in production said they use OpenAI’s retrieval and 50% use Google’s Vertex AI Search. The most-used standalone tools, Pinecone and Elasticsearch, are each used by 12% to 14%, and 40% use at least one standalone tool.
Well over half (59%) of companies that swapped a model in a live app reworked the app or went back to the original model. This data suggests that technical leaders planning to swap an AI model inside a live app should budget for rework. This means retesting the prompts, tools, and evaluations built around the old model.
VentureBeat Intelligence will ask the same questions in its October VB Pulse survey, so readers will see whether OpenAI's lead in agent orchestration platform use shows up again in a new group of respondents.
The full research reports can be found here.
About the data: VentureBeat Intelligence fielded five VB Pulse surveys in September 2026. Three are cited in this article: the Agentic Orchestration survey, with 109 qualified respondents; the AI Infrastructure and Compute survey, with 102; and the Agentic Context Layers survey, with 113. Respondents qualified if they work at an organization with 100 or more employees, or consult for one as their main client.
Each monthly survey is a snapshot of a different group of respondents who opt into the surveys. They come from VentureBeat’s readers and a research panel. Because September’s screening questions differed from August’s, the Google comparison counts only because it passed the statistical test on all September respondents and again on in-house respondents alone.
The results describe these specific respondents and may not hold for all companies. OpenAI's lead in agent orchestration platform use passed a statistical test at 95% confidence, including among in-house respondents alone. The group of companies considering Anthropic's platform is small, at 20 companies.

title: Providing free health insurance in Eti-Osa, By Gbolahan Olusegun Yishawu
body:
The Eti-Osa I want to help build is a community where residents have greater opportunities to live well. I want children to learn and thrive. I want young people to acquire useful skills and pursue meaningful livelihoods. I want traders, artisans and working families to have a stronger foundation for the future they are trying to build. Health belongs at the centre of that vision.
Health is one of the clearest tests of whether public service has meaning in the everyday life of the citizen. He may not immediately understand a motion on the floor of the House. He may not follow every debate on policy, budgetary allocation or public finance, but understands the difference between being able to take a sick child to hospital and having to postpone treatment. He understands the fear that comes with an unexpected diagnosis and the quiet pain of watching a manageable medical condition worsen because timely medical attention is beyond reach.
I believe access to healthcare should be available to everyone at an affordable cost, irrespective of class. I understand the anxiety of having to choose between a visit to the hospital and other pressing needs for the vulnerable, which is why I have, over the years, championed different programmes and initiatives to improve health conditions and outcomes for everyone, especially the vulnerable members of our society.
For our people in Eti-Osa Constituency 02, those programmes include free annual medical check-ups, breast and cervical cancer screening with vaccinations, dental care and surgery, as well as eye examinations with cataract surgery and eyeglasses provided where needed. These programmes have run consistently every year over the past decade.
On the floor of the Lagos State House of Assembly, I have proposed different initiatives to widen access to healthcare for Lagosians. I campaigned for a health insurance scheme and vigorously supported it upon adoption by the Lagos State Ministry of Health. I also moved a motion for free rotavirus vaccines for young children to protect them against diarrhoea. I am glad that, following that motion and the House of Assembly’s resolution, the initiative was adopted as Lagos State Government policy, and thousands of young children have since benefited from it. The Lagos Patient Bill of Rights, which I proposed, is currently under consideration by the House.
I believe that representation must be felt in the everyday lives of the people. While our debates, motions, and decisions in the House matter because that is how we get to address the fundamental issues, I believe that ultimately, these must connect with the needs of the people we represent. The question has always been: what solutions can I proffer that can directly improve people’s lives and make their burden lighter? That inspired the two-year free health-insurance programme for the residents of Eti-Osa Constituency 02. For me, reaching the programme’s initial target of 5,000 residents is not simply hitting an enrolment figure; it represents people whose health and peace of mind deserve our attention. We are grateful for the privilege and opportunity we have to provide that support.
This initiative grows out of our long-term commitment to accessible healthcare for the people. Our desire is to create a more dependable pathway through which people can seek care when they need it. This programme offers a practical starting point by removing the cost of enrolment for beneficiaries, while also helping them to become familiar with a system that many have not used or do not fully understand, simultaneously addressing the twin issues of affordability and awareness.
For those who have enrolled in the scheme, the two-year coverage commenced on 10 th October. Beneficiaries can now access a defined range of services, including general and specialist consultations, medical tests, dental and eye care, minor surgeries and other covered treatments. Maternity benefits include antenatal care, drugs, scans and delivery services, alongside 28 days of care for newborns, subject to the package’s terms and limits.
We hope that with enrolment in the scheme, families will have greater confidence to seek care. A mother with a sick child needs more than reassuring words. A pregnant woman worried about the cost of delivery needs more than promises. An elderly resident who cannot afford treatment needs a practical route to care. I want parents to focus on getting their children treated rather than thinking about other things. I want that pregnant woman to approach childbirth with less anxiety. I want that elderly resident in our constituency to seek medical attention without feeling that every request for help places an unbearable burden on the family. If our work helps a mother obtain care, an elderly resident receive treatment with dignity, or a family face a difficult moment with greater reassurance, then we have succeeded in giving representation its proper meaning.
The Eti-Osa I want to help build is a community where residents have greater opportunities to live well. I want children to learn and thrive. I want young people to acquire useful skills and pursue meaningful livelihoods. I want traders, artisans and working families to have a stronger foundation for the future they are trying to build. Health belongs at the centre of that vision.
Our healthcare interventions sit alongside education support, skills acquisition and ICT initiatives as part of a broader commitment to residents’ wellbeing and opportunities. I want our residents to feel supported, not forgotten. I want families to have more room to hope and less reason to fear. Ultimately, the future I seek for Eti-Osa is one not only measured by projects completed or programmes announced, but by the difference those efforts make in people’s lives directly.
My appeal to residents is simple: if you have enrolled, make use of your health-insurance cover when it takes effect. Familiarise yourself with the services available, know your designated healthcare provider, and seek care promptly when you need it. If you need information about enrolment or how to use the scheme, please contact our constituency office. Let us work together to make good health a shared priority in every household in Eti-Osa. I remain committed to making wellbeing a central part of our shared future. Ilera l’oro – health is wealth.
Gbolahan Olusegun Yishawu , an engineer, is a member of the Lagos State House of Assembly, representing Eti-Osa Constituency 02.

title: INEC Introduces QR Codes To Help Lagos Voters Locate PVC Collection Centres
body: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Lagos State has introduced QR codes to help eligible voters locate designated Permanent Voter Card (PVC) collection centres ahead of the 2027 general elections. The Commission said the codes could be scanned through its official social media platforms and website, giving voters another way to identify where to collect their cards. Speaking at a press conference at INEC’s Lagos headquarters, the Resident Electoral Commissioner, Professor Ayobami Salami, urged eligible voters to collect their PVCs, verify their registration details and rely on official sources for election-related information. He stressed the importance of voter participation as the Commission intensifies preparations for the 2027 general elections. INEC said preparations were also ongoing in other operational areas, including the procurement and testing of voter accreditation devices, improvements to election-result transmission systems, logistics planning, and the recruitment and training of election personnel. The Commission added that it was working to strengthen its operational readiness to ensure a smooth electoral process. The introduction of the QR codes is part of INEC Lagos’s efforts to improve access to voter information and encourage eligible voters to confirm their details and collect their PVCs ahead of election day.
