title: Lockheed eyes fresh PAC-3 interceptor production options for Ukraine, Europe
body: Lockheed Martin is weighing new industry partnerships to produce urgently needed PAC-3 Patriot interceptors in Europe, an avenue that could also help fill Ukraine’s shortfalls, a company executive said. Discussions about producing more Patriot interceptors outside the United States have picked up steam since Ukrainian leaders said over the summer they were promised by the Trump administration a license to make them in Ukraine to defend against Russian missile and drone barrages. U.S. government officials are still expected to make a decision, which could entail the production of PAC-2 interceptors, made by Raytheon, or Lockheed’s PAC-3. “From a PAC-3 perspective, we’re absolutely willing to talk to Ukraine,” Jason Reynolds, vice president and general manager of the company’s integrated air and missile defense division, told Defense News in an interview at the Association of the United States Army annual convention in Washington, DC. Patriot interceptor deliveries to Poland will be delayed, top general says “It’s really a matter of what’s their industrial capability, what’s the parts availability, those types of things,” he continued. “It might be something like an ACE, as opposed to an MSE, that we would start with for Ukraine.” Lockheed announced development of an ACE variant during the summer, billing it as a cheaper option against relatively simple threats — at half the cost of an MSE missile designed to go against sophisticated missiles. The new interceptor will make do with a single-pulse motor, compared with a dual-pulse of the MSE interceptor, and utilize a blast fragmentation warhead, versus the direct hit-to-kill mechanics of the MSE missile. Reynolds cautioned that setting up interceptor missile production of whatever variant in Ukraine comes with the risk of Russian attacks on the plant. “The first question is, ‘Can we build a factory that’s survivable in a war zone?’” he said. That’s why the company is considering options to make them in nearby safe countries instead, and quickly ferrying them into Ukraine as they are needed. “There is a whole number of countries that are interested in potentially producing ACE,” Reynolds said. “If we can get that started, get the supply chain started and then migrate to Ukraine as an option, that would make a lot of sense to me.” Germany is among the countries where leaders have offered to host PAC-3 production . Raytheon, in partnership with MBDA, already makes the PAC-2 product line in the country. For an eventual PAC-3 production, Lockheed is considering partnering with Diehl Defence, with which there is a cooperation agreement on interceptor parts in place dating from October 2025, Reynolds said. “If we were to go forward with exploring any kind of production in Germany, we would likely do that with a company like Diehl,” he told Defense News. A Diehl spokesperson confirmed consultations ongoing with Lockheed Martin, pointing to the October 2025 agreement. The German company has been ramping up its production capabilities at all its sites, the spokesperson added. A new facility is in the works in Lübben, Brandenburg, which comes with requisite licensing for explosives handling because it was used by the German Democratic Republic for military equipment manufacturing. The U.S. government has the final say about where sensitive defense products can be produced outside the United States, including Patriot air-defense equipment. “We at Lockheed don’t have the authority to just build factories wherever we want,” Reynolds noted.

Facebook’s new “Your Algorithm” feature will let you directly add and manage topics you want to see in your feed and Facebook Reels. Meta says your recommendations “respond right away” after you make updates using the new feature by hitting “interested” or “not interested” for different topics. Your Algorithm previously launched on Instagram earlier this year, and Meta also launched a similar “Dear Algo” feature on Threads.
Facebook users will be able to access Your Algorithm or select “interested” or “not interested” from the three dots menu on individual posts. The “interested” and “not interested” buttons may also appear under posts, and Meta says it “may ask follow up questions for more detail on what you liked or disliked. You can easily tell us, in your own words, what you want to see more or less of, and your recommendations will update in real time.”
The new feature is part of a set of “AI-powered” tools Meta says it’s using to customize what users see on Facebook. It also says it’s using LLMs more in its ranking systems: “LLMs can incorporate the interests, context, and intent behind natural language, unlocking an algorithm you can actually talk to. Tell it what you want more or less of, and your recommendations respond in real time, adapting within the same session to reflect what matters to you right now.”

title: Nigeria’s Capital Market Master Plan: Building the Market a Nation Deserves
body: With the economy’s foundations reset and a new law in force, the Nigeria Capital Market Master Plan 2026-2036 sets out how the savings of Nigerians can become the engine of the nation’s growth, writes Emomotimi Agama A Rare Alignment Every great economy has, at its heart, a capital market that turns the savings of ordinary people into the factories, roads, homes and businesses that create jobs. Nigeria has the people, the enterprise and the ambition. What we are now building is a market to match them. That work could not begin at a better time. Nigeria’s capital market stands at its most favourable policy juncture in recent history. The unification of foreign exchange windows, the removal of distortionary subsidies and the restoration of macroeconomic discipline have reset the foundations of the economy. Difficult as those reforms have been, they have cleared the ground on which a deep and trusted market can stand. The law has moved, too. The Investments and Securities Act 2025 has given the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) its most expansive mandate to date. Systemic risk oversight, the regulation of digital and tokenised assets, and stronger enforcement powers now sit firmly within the capital market perimeter. The question is no longer whether we have the tools. It is what we will build with them. A Ten-year Blueprint With a Clear Destination The Nigeria Capital Market Master Plan 2.0, (NCMMP 2.0) is how we intend to seize this moment. It is a 10-year strategic blueprint for the development of our capital market, aligned with Nigeria Agenda 2050 and the Renewed Hope Development Plan (2026–2030). Its vision is simple to state and demanding to deliver: a diverse, efficient, transparent and innovative capital market that positions Nigeria as a regional financial hub. That market must also carry its share of the national drive towards a US$1 trillion economy by 2030. Over the life of the plan, we aim to grow the market from a baseline of N250 trillion to N750 trillion. “The question is no longer whether we have the tools.It is what we will build with them.” These are not abstractions. For the pensioner, a deeper market means retirement savings that are safer and better rewarded. For the small business owner, it means long-term finance beyond the bank overdraft. For the young graduate with a smartphone, it means an investment account opened in minutes. For a state government, it means funding for roads and hospitals its citizens can see and use. That is what a capital market is for. Five Pillars, One Purpose The vision rests on five interrelated pillars. Each reinforces the others; none succeeds alone. 1. Regulatory clarity, coordination and enforcement Investors commit capital where the rules are clear and fairly applied. We will harmonise regulation through unified rules and closer collaboration between agencies, so that issuers and investors face one coherent framework rather than many. Supervision will become more risk-based and market monitoring sharper. Above all, investor protection will be strengthened through proactive enforcement and stronger safeguards. The goal is a regulatory environment that is transparent, efficient and, most importantly, trusted. 2. Modernising market infrastructure A modern economy needs modern market plumbing. We will improve connectivity and interoperability across market infrastructure, and expand Nigeria’s commodity, derivatives and repo markets. Digital onboarding will make it easier to participate, while greater transparency will make it easier to trust what one sees. And as more of the market moves online, cybersecurity and operational resilience will be treated as non-negotiable. 3. Product and issuance diversification A market is only as useful as the choices it offers. We will deepen the markets for federal and sub-national government debt, and widen the routes through which private companies, including small and medium-sized enterprises, can raise funds. The range of investment products will grow to include more non-interest, commodity-linked and securitised instruments. Together, these measures will boost liquidity and attract the patient, long-term capital that nation-building requires. 4. Deepening the investor base A resilient market is one owned by many. We will mobilise institutional, retail, Diaspora and foreign investors alike. Digital channels and inclusion initiatives will bring investment within reach of Nigerians who have never owned a share or a bond. For foreign investors, we will simplify onboarding and the repatriation of funds. Our sons and daughters in the Diaspora, in particular, should find it as easy to invest at home as they do abroad. 5. Institutional capacity and professional development None of this endures without capable institutions and skilled people. We will strengthen the commission’s own regulatory and supervisory capabilities, and improve the resilience and governance of market intermediaries. Through education, certification and training, we will develop the next generation of capital market talent. This is how growth becomes sustainable rather than a passing cycle. From Blueprint to Delivery The Master Plan will be formally launched at the National Capital Market Conference in Abuja on October 19, 2026, alongside the National Savings Scheme. The pairing is deliberate. Savings are the raw material of investment, and a nation that saves through its own capital market builds with its own resources. But a plan is only as good as the will to carry it out, and this one belongs to all of us. To issuers: the market is ready to fund your growth. To investors at home and abroad: the rules are clearer, the protections stronger and the opportunities wider than ever. To state governments: there is a better way to finance development. To market operators and professionals: your skills and integrity are the foundation on which everything else rests. Nigeria has spent the past few years doing the hard work of reform. The next 10 years are about harvesting it. With NCMMP 2.0, we intend to build a capital market worthy of a great nation, one that works for every Nigerian who dares to save, invest and believe in our shared future. * Dr. Agama is the Director-General and Chief Executive Officer of the Securities and Exchange Commission, Nigeria. He is Vice-Chair of the IOSCO Africa/Middle East Regional Committee and Chairman of the West Africa Securities Regulators Association

title: Coris (YC S22) Is Hiring Back End Engineer
body:
AI risk and ops platform for Payment Processors, Banks, SaaS…
Coris is the AI platform for risk and financial operations. Platforms, marketplaces, payment providers, and banks - GoFundMe, Clio, Cherry, and a growing list - use Coris to onboard merchants faster, monitor them continuously, and act on fraud without adding headcount. One customer described us as "Cursor + Lovable for risk teams."
We're backed by Y Combinator, Lux Capital, and Pathlight, founded by payments-domain experts, and growing quickly on customer pull. We're a small team; this hire owns a large share of the backend.
Coris was started by Vinodh (CEO) and Shyam (CTO). We've each spent 20+ years in fraud and risk management, running risk engineering, operations and product teams at Google, eBay, PayPal and WePay. You'll work directly with both of us in Palo Alto.
Every Coris decision runs on data we pull from payment processors and platforms: Stripe, Adyen, Fiserv, TSYS, Repay, and more, over APIs, webhooks, and SFTP file feeds - hundreds of millions of events a month, billions of rows in Postgres. On top of that sits a signals and rules engine, an account graph, and the partner-facing API our customers build on.
Here's the honest version of the work. Files arrive out of order over SFTP. One processor sends dates in UTC, another in the merchant's local time, and neither says which. A processor's decline code lives in a different column than the spec says. A webhook ships malformed JSON at 2am. A backfill worker runs out of memory on a 40B-row table. A customer's risk lead says "our numbers look off" and needs an answer today.
We're hiring the engineer who will own all of that end-to-end, and who thinks it's the interesting part - because every integration we make reliably is one a competitor hasn't, and that's the moat. Getting the boring work right every time is how enduring companies are built!
Nobody matches every line below. If most of it sounds like you and the work above is the kind you want to do, we'd like to hear from you.
Coris is building the AI layer for payments risk and operations. We work with the most ambitious platforms, marketplaces, and payment providers around the globe such as GoFundMe, Kajabi, Clio and Cherry to automate and accelerate merchant onboarding, monitoring, and decision-making. What risk teams only imagined two years ago, Coris is delivering today with our risk platform and AI agents.
We’re backed by Y Combinator, Lux Capital, Pathlight Ventures, and other world-class investors.

title: Google Play now lets anyone build private, vibe-coded apps that run on Android
body:
Your vibe-coded applications can now be easily run on Android smartphones without having to first go public on the Google Play Store, the tech giant announced on Tuesday. A new feature will allow users to launch their own personal apps on their device via Google Play using their standard Google account, but they will remain completely private.
These personal apps won’t show up in Google Play’s search or listing pages, and won’t be shared with anyone except for the app’s creator.
The idea comes as more people are experimenting with building their own applications via AI for specific, personal needs. However, being able to use that app on their own Android device has meant publishing to Google Play, making it accessible to the Play Store’s some 3 billion users. That led many to limit their vibe-coding efforts to web apps that could run on any device instead of something built natively for Android.
Now, Google says Android device owners can vibe-code an app using Google AI Studio, then launch it for their own use.
These apps are still required to comply with Google Play’s existing policies but allow users to experiment more directly with building apps for Android.
Initially, the feature will be available to users in the U.S., age 18 and up.
“That’s why the future of apps on Google Play is personal, secure, and built by everyone — and it’s why Play is leading the charge and moving from ‘there’s an app for that’ to ‘there’s an app for me,’” said Sam Bright, Google’s VP and GM for the Google Play and Developer Ecosystem, in a press briefing ahead of Tuesday’s launch. “We started Google Play with a simple goal: to connect you with the apps you love. But after today, we hope it’s clear: Play has evolved to become so much more than that.”
In the months ahead, the company said that users will be able to share their vibe-coded creations with a network of trusted friends. That means the apps you built for family or friends, or maybe your child’s T-ball league, could be used with a small group of people, without having to go public on the Play Store.
And if the app ever really becomes popular, there will be a way to shift the personal app to one that’s published on the Google Play Store for everyone to try, after completing the trust and safety reviews.
Related to AI’s impact on app development, Google said it’s also building better ways to curate the Google Play experience — for instance, by leveraging Google’s AI to create a personalized game recommendation engine, called Game Finder. The feature, first available in the U.S. in English, will be based on what the user likes to play combined with Google’s knowledge derived from its game community’s 1.2 billion players.
Google will also allow users to curate their own lists of games, post questions about games to a new Community Posts section, and join new 48-hour gaming challenges called Sprints, among other gaming-related feature updates.
Plus, the Play Store’s built-in AI assistant, Ask Play, is being updated to offer comparisons, allowing users to see the key differences between similar applications. Google Play apps and games will also be more deeply integrated into Gemini’s conversations.
The changes are rolling out alongside Google Play’s new support for an age-range feature that allows parents to share their child’s age range, but not their exact birthdate, with developers to get an age-appropriate experience.

title: MIT startup says it can turn diesel trucks into cheaper hydrogen haulers — see it at Disrupt
body:
Diesel fuel powers everything from shipping to agriculture, and with prices hitting record highs in recent weeks, governments around the world are scrambling to contain the fallout.
For now, that’s meant releasing fuel from stockpiles, but in the coming years, the answer might be a new technology from an MIT startup called LNK Energies .
LNK has created a way to convert existing heavy-duty trucks from diesel to hydrogen, slashing pollution and costs while shielding operators from the price spikes that result from geopolitical instability like the war in Iran. “If you look at total cost of ownership of a Class 8 truck, it’s 13% cheaper than diesel,” Alexis Huynh, chief technology officer at LNK Energies, told TechCrunch. (Class 8 is the heaviest category of trucks, including big rigs.)
Automotive companies have been exploring the use of hydrogen in long-haul trucking in part because refilling a hydrogen tank is faster than recharging the massive batteries those trucks require. But hydrogen is challenging to move to refilling stations, and the pressure tanks required to store it on the truck are large and costly.
LNK’s approach is to carry hydrogen chemically attached to another compound. Liquid organic hydrogen carriers, or LOHCs, are liquids that can absorb and later release hydrogen, and they have been widely studied, but mostly for moving large quantities of hydrogen from refineries to fueling stations. The equipment needed to separate hydrogen from the LOHC, known as a reactor, has been too big to fit onto a truck.
“A lot of the reactors that LOHC companies have today are really large. They’re about the size of a shipping container,” Huynh said. “We have shrunk that basically to the size of a mini fridge.”
Moving the reactor onto the truck saves a surprising amount of energy. When hydrogen is stored on a truck, it must be pressurized to more than 11,000 psi (800 bar), roughly 800 times normal air pressure, and squeezing it that hard takes a lot of power. Because LNK’s fuel carries the hydrogen in liquid form and releases it on board as needed, that step goes away. “We’re eliminating the expensive compression step,” Sayandeep Biswas, co-founder and CEO of LNK Energies, told TechCrunch.
In LNK’s system, once the hydrogen is released on the truck, it can be burned in a conventional internal combustion engine, the kind in today’s diesel trucks, with just a few modifications. The company uses waste heat from the engine to help power the on-board reactor. Or, if the trucking company wants to fully eliminate combustion emissions, it can use fuel cells instead, which convert hydrogen into electricity to power electric motors.
The LOHC can be stored in a traditional fuel tank and dispensed using pumps, just like diesel. “The entire hydrogen infrastructure doesn’t need to exist,” Biswas said. “It’s just a standard diesel station.”
Biswas and Huynh have a demonstration reactor working in the lab that can power an engine from a lawnmower. In 18 months, they plan to install a larger version in a commercial truck.
The trucks will cost more up front, but promise to be cheaper to operate. The duo are confident that they can undercut diesel at a price of $6.50 per gallon after they’ve made just 50 to 100 trucks. None of their projections include government subsidies. “The idea isn’t to have a technology that is cheaper at scale, but one that is cheaper even during that adoption period,” Biswas said.
LNK will present live onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt , taking place October 13-15 in San Francisco, as part of our Startup Battlefield pitch competition. Come join us in San Francisco and take part in the action.

title: China’s $3 Billion Qatar LNG Deal Raises an Awkward Question
body: Qatar's highly sensitive geographical positioning -- between a western land border with Saudi Arabia and a northeastern maritime border with Iran -- has necessitated it treading a delicate diplomatic path between regional superpowers and their global superpower backers since it gained independence from being a British protectorate in 1971. For much of the period from the 1945 landmark relationship foundation deal between Riyadh and Washington was signed, as fully analysed in my latest book on thenew global oil market order, Sunni Muslim powerhouse Saudi Arabia was geopolitically aligned with Washington and its allies. On the other hand, since the Islamic Revolution of 1979, Shia Muslim powerhouse Iran has been geopolitically aligned with Beijing and Moscow. Qatar also shares the world's largest gas reservoir with Iran -- the South Pars/North Dome field containing 51 trillion cubic metres of gas. Depending on whether one was sitting in Washington or Beijing in recent years, where Qatar fitted into the global geopolitical matrix was open to debate, while the emirate itself would simply have pointed to it taking a pragmatic approach.  In the run-up to Russia's invasion of Ukraine on 24 February 2022, this approach saw it act as a vast LNG supply depot for China, which over the 12 months before the invasion had suddenly been seized by an overriding desire to stock up on what would become the world's emergency energy source. There followed a burst of long-dated LNG supply agreements made between Chinese buyers and Qatar, with the first landing in March 2021, when Sinopec and Qatar Petroleum agreed a decade-long deal for 2 million metric tons per year mtpy of LNG. Another followed that December, this time between QatarEnergy and Guangdong Energy Group Natural Gas Co., covering 1 million mtpy from 2024 through 2034, with scope for extension. Several similarly weighty contracts were signed in quick succession. After the Ukraine invasion, though, Qatari LNG supplies to Europe played a critical role in ensuring that the 28 European Union EU member countries took a decisive stand in punishing Russia for its action. In U.S., UK, and French circles, the EU's previous reluctance -- led by Germany -- to meaningfully cut its dependence on cheap Russian hydrocarbons after the 2014 annexation of Crimea had long been viewed as a key factor in Putin's calculation that a full-scale assault on Ukraine in 2022 would again carry limited consequences. Instead, by late March 2022, a series of high-level meetings between Qatari and senior Western officials had secured pledges for emergency LNG volumes from Qatar to the European countries that most needed them. After one such meeting -- involving Qatar's Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, German economy minister Robert Habeck, and U.S. representation -- thenPresident Joe Biden publicly designated Qatar a 'Major Non-NATO Ally'. Two months later, Qatar and Germany signed a declaration of intent on energy cooperation, laying the groundwork for Doha to become a core LNG supplier to Berlin. The momentum continued into December 2022, when QatarEnergy and ConocoPhillips finalised two long-term sales and purchase agreements to deliver LNG to Germany for at least 15 years starting in 2026.  Related Japanese Refiners Buy Middle East Crude Through Ship-to-Ship Transfers  Whether Iran, and its key superpower backer China, took this designation or the presence of the largest American military installation in the Middle East Al Udeid Air Base seriously is a matter of speculation. However, what is known is that Qatar was not excluded from Tehran's wave of attacks on regional countries this year, which effectively meant that Beijing was fine with that happening too. Under the full terms of the all-encompassing 'Iran-China 25-Year Comprehensive Cooperation Agreement', first revealed anywhere in the world in my 3 September 2019 article and analysed in full in my latest book on the new global oil market order, China exercises huge control over all major elements of Iran's foreign policy. This has been further enhanced by the fact that China remains the key financier of Iran through the enormous volumes of oil it continues to buy from the country. These volumes are always officially underestimated because, as also analysed in the book, any oil that does not officially go through China's General Administration of Customs GAC is not entered into the country's customs data and thus does not show up. In reality, many millions of barrels of Iranian oil have continued to be moved to the refineries where they are required or stored on land or at sea effectively as part of China's Strategic Petroleum Reserve, with no official record of them. In short, if it suited Beijing, Iran would not have launched any of the attacks on its regional neighbours that it did, nor have allowed the Strait of Hormuz or the Bab al-Mandab Strait to close, nor have allowed the Iran-backed Houthi terrorist group to take up where Hamas and Hezbollah left off. The most serious of the attacks launched by Iran on Qatar this year in terms of its key energy infrastructure occurred in March, with long-term damage inflicted on its primary LNG facilities at Ras Laffan Industrial City. This knocked offline 17% of the emirate's entire LNG export capacity. The strikes on the 18th and 19th of March damaged two major LNG processing 'trains' production facilities and struck Shell's wholly owned Pearl GTL gas-to-liquids facility, which is fed directly by Qatar's North Field. QatarEnergy's CEO, Saad Sherida Al-Kaabi, confirmed that losing this 12.8 mtpy of capacity equates to roughly US$20 billion in lost annual revenue.  At that point, Qatar said that the extensive technical damage to the LNG trains meant that full repairs were projected to take three to five years. Having said that, and only six months or so after the strikes, Qatar has made notable progress. Shell announced recently that it has successfully partially restarted the Pearl GTL plant, although for the moment it is focused on building limited inventory, while repairs on the damaged half of the plant will not be fully complete until Q1 2027. Nonetheless, to counter these massive infrastructure losses, QatarEnergy has aggressively accelerated its North Field East NFE expansion project. Overall, the NFE expansion programme will see six major new developments in the NFE and North Field South NFS by 2029. Four new trains -- each with 8 million mtpy  will be built on the NFE site, and two with the same production capacity on the NFS site, totalling 48 million mtpy of new LNG production. At the end of last February, QatarEnergy announced another set of projects -- focused on its North Field West NFW -- that would increase its LNG output from the then-current 77 million mtpy to 142 million mtpy before the end of this decade. This compares to the 404 million mtpy of LNG traded globally in 2023, and to industry estimates that this figure will reach around 625-685 million mtpy in 2040.  Extraordinarily in this context, several reports emerged last week indicating that the first LNG train under the NFE expansion programme will be ready to start operation as early as next month. The process will begin with the introduction of feed gas, followed by a gradual progression over several weeks toward the first LNG production. This signals a significantly earlier start than the H1 2027 timeline mentioned by QatarEnergy's al-Kaabi last month. The news followed reports of a US$3 billion loan secured by QatarEnergy from four Chinese banks last week -- a development verified exclusively to OilPrice.com by a senior source close to the EU's energy security complex. This is the largest exclusively Chinese-underwritten corporate loan secured by a Qatari state entity to date. According to a detailed analysis by Bloomberg, the five-year syndicated debt facility is financed entirely by Bank of China, Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, Agricultural Bank of China, and China Construction Bank Asia at an exceptionally competitive 50 basis points over the US Secured Overnight Financing Rate SOFR. Quite aside from the financial metrics, the deal appears to demonstrate China's supreme confidence that Qatar's facilities will not be targeted by Iran in the future. For those of a certain generation, it carries the distinct ring of an old-style protection racket "Nice factory you've got there, shame if anything happened to it." This would mark an interesting twist on Beijing's standard Belt and Road Initiative BRI playbook. To wit rather than extending loans for infrastructure improvements and then seizing geo-strategically vital waterways upon default, China may be using the threat and reality of Iran's official and unofficial military forces to push loans for critical repairs to infrastructure damaged by Tehran to gain further influence in the victims of these attacks across the Middle East. It is a strategy clearly backed by huge capital commitment, as Bloomberg figures show Chinese bank lending to Gulf borrowers excluding bilateral loans surged more than fivefold last year to a record US$11.5 billion.  By Simon Watkins for Oilprice.com

The Google Play Store is getting a big update for cars with Google built-in. On Tuesday, the company announced that the Play Store’s layout will now automatically adapt to the size and layout of your car’s screen while making it easier to find and download new apps.
The update, which is rolling out in the coming weeks, will put featured apps on the Play Store’s homepage and allow you to download them with a single tap. It also comes with what Google says is a “streamlined navigation” menu that puts “Apps,” “Games,” “Search,” and “More” options on the left side of your screen (or on the top if your car’s screen has a vertical orientation).
Cars with Google built-in differ from the company’s infotainment operating system, Android Automotive, in that it allows vehicle manufacturers to integrate Google’s services and support for native Android apps directly into their vehicles. The company brought an early version of its software integration to the Polestar 2, before rolling it out to the Honda Accord Touring in 2023 .
Along with an overhauled Play Store, Google is also adding new apps, like Starz, Firefox, Ludo King, and JioHotstar, that you can use while parked. Google will also allow you to watch YouTube videos on your dashboard when parked and continue listening to audio while driving, though this feature is only available to YouTube Premium subscribers.
Google has been gradually adding more apps and features to cars with Google built-in and recently replaced Google Assistant with Gemini AI across a range of supported vehicles from Ford, GM, Honda, Nissan, Volvo, and others.

The next time you vibe-code a custom app with Google’s AI Studio, you won’t have to connect your phone to a computer to install it. On Tuesday, Google announced a new feature in the US that will allow you to launch personal apps directly through the Play Store.
Google first launched the ability to vibe-code personal Android apps in May. Even though you can now launch your custom apps in Google Play, the company notes it will continue to keep them “secure, private, and separate from the public store catalog.” You can also launch them using a standard Google account, and the company will soon add the ability to share your app with a select group of people, too.
Though this might make it easier to play around with experimental apps, Google is positioning it as an on-ramp of sorts for fledgling developers. “If you want to share your app with the world, Google Play helps you graduate to a professional developer account with the same Trust & Safety reviews and high-quality standards as professional developers,” Sam Bright, Google’s vice president and general manager of Google Play, writes in the announcement.

title: Russian forces strike water collection point in Kramatorsk three times in one day, causing casualties
body:
According to Ukrinform, the Kramatorsk City Council reported this on Telegram .
“Today, Russian troops struck a water distribution point in Kramatorsk —which was set up by charitable organizations—three times,” the statement reads.
According to the city council, three people are currently known to have been injured: two women and one man. Both women are in serious condition and are receiving the necessary medical care.
Information regarding the consequences of the attack is being clarified.
“The Russians are deliberately targeting places where people are trying to obtain the bare necessities for life. Even the ability to collect water in one’s own city has become a danger to health and life,” the Kramatorsk City Council noted.
They also emphasized that this is yet another manifestation of Russian terror against the civilian population: “Attacks on civilian infrastructure and people who have come to get water are unacceptable and must be subject to appropriate legal scrutiny.”
As reported by Ukrinform, the Donetsk region has expanded the zone of mandatory evacuation for children from certain areas of Kramatorsk.

title: Zelenskyy: Ukraine submits proposals to US for upcoming meetings, ready in coming days
body:
Ukraine has submitted proposals to the United States regarding upcoming meetings and is ready for them in the coming days, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy reported.

"Ukraine is ready for meetings; Ukraine supported the President of America on the issue of an energy ceasefire. Russia must also be part of this agreement. Our team has sent the American side relevant proposals regarding our possible next meetings, our next talks. In the coming days we are ready to meet, and I conveyed this proposal through my team to Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner," Zelenskyy said in an evening address on Tuesday.

The president noted that "we are in constant communication with the American side. Our teams are speaking. And we need to work toward peace; we need to seek options for correct actions."

According to him, "there is always constructivism from the Ukrainian side, and our positions are always absolutely clear and aimed at protecting the independence of the Ukrainian people."

title: Nana Akwasi Awuah says Auditor-General began PMMC audits in September 2024
body: Former Precious Minerals Marketing Company (PMMC) Managing Director, Nana Akwasi Awuah, says the Auditor-General began work on the company’s outstanding financial audits in September 2024, following a request he submitted earlier that month. His comments come after a report from GoldBod’s appearance before Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee on Tuesday, October 13, 2026, suggested that PMMC’s books and accounts for 2020 to 2024 had remained unaudited until new management requested an audit in 2025. In a statement responding to the report, Mr Awuah said he formally wrote to the Auditor-General on September 2, 2024, requesting a multi-year audit covering the period. He added that Parliament’s Select Committee on State Enterprises subsequently wrote to the Auditor-General in support of his request. “The Auditor General accordingly put together a team that immediately commenced work in the same month of September 2024,” he said. Mr Awuah explained that the delay in completing the audits stemmed from bureaucratic challenges surrounding the appointment of a new external auditor by the Ghana Audit Service. He insisted that the delay was not caused by management and said the final reports were completed, signed and submitted in April and June 2025. He further cited a performance audit conducted by the Auditor-General in 2023, describing it as the first of its kind at PMMC in about two decades. According to him, the audits provided a record of the company’s financial position and demonstrated the improvements made before the end of 2024. Mr Awuah said PMMC had been turned around by the end of that year, creating a firm foundation for the establishment of GoldBod as its successor.

title: English football regulator chief threatens to resign over Man City interference
body: By Adegboyega Adeleye The chairman of English football’s Independent Football Regulator (IFR), David Kogan, has vowed to resign if he faces political interference over the future of Manchester City amid the club’s appeal against findings that it breached Premier League financial rules. According to the BBC, Kogan said no politician had attempted to influence the regulator’s work and insisted that its decisions would be guided by the law and established procedures. Asked what he would do if he came under political pressure over the case, Kogan said: “I would resign.” “The Prime Minister is entirely entitled to make his own observations on anything,” he said, referring to Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s earlier comments about Manchester City’s ownership. “We are independent. That is in the name. I am the chairman of the Independent Football Regulator and independence absolutely runs through everything we’re doing. “And no politician has tried to influence and would try to influence anything we do on that.” Burnham had previously said he would be “really concerned” if Manchester City’s Abu Dhabi owners decided to sell the club, prompting criticism from opposition politicians and concerns among some Premier League clubs about possible political interference in the case. The prime minister later denied that his remarks had downplayed the seriousness of the findings against City. Details of his meetings with senior club figures were released by the government on Monday following calls for greater transparency. Kogan, however, insisted that the regulator would follow its statutory responsibilities regardless of comments from politicians or other individuals. “As far as we, as the regulator, are concerned, we have a very, very clear course of action that is governed by statute and we are going to follow that course of action and no comment by any politician or indeed any individual is going to affect what we do,” he said. “Process is going to drive what we do. Process will lead us to a conclusion. “We cannot reach any conclusion at this stage because we don’t know the outcome of any appeal and once we do then we will act accordingly.” What happens next in Man City case? An independent commission found Manchester City had breached financial rules over a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018. The commission’s findings included allegations that the club used commercial agreements to channel more than £830m into its football operations. The commission also concluded that some club witnesses had given false or dishonest evidence in key respects. City have denied wrongdoing and appealed the verdict. A separate independent panel is expected to hold a sanctions hearing to determine the punishment, although the process could take months. City can also appeal any sanction imposed. Possible punishments reported include a substantial fine, a points deduction, expulsion from the Premier League or the removal of titles won during the period under investigation. Kogan said the case raised serious issues if the findings were upheld following the appeal and confirmed that the regulator would consider whether to exercise its own powers. “We are waiting like everybody else to see what the independent panel will do… and then we will bring in a view in terms of our own investigation and statutory powers if we need to do so,” he said. “Our powers relate to individual owners, directors and senior executives. They refer to whether people are in a position to run a club in a way that is safe, coherent and done with probity, and we will be examining those things.” The regulator’s role includes assessing whether club owners and senior officials are suitable to run their teams. If the findings against City are upheld, the watchdog could consider whether action involving the club’s ownership or executives is necessary. The post English football regulator chief threatens to resign over Man City interference appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Key figure in Pearson airport gold heist testifying at trial of another accused man
body:
A man who admitted his role in the massive gold heist at Toronto’s Pearson airport says he took 30 per cent of the gold and started melting and selling it before travelling to Pakistan, where he claims he was kidnapped and abused to give it up.
Arsalan Chaudhary is testifying in the trial of Parmpal Sidhu, who has pleaded not guilty to charges of theft over $5,000 and conspiracy to commit an indictable offence in the 2023 heist.
Chaudhary told a Brampton, Ont., court today he planned the heist with Simran Preet Panesar, who is wanted by authorities, and they divided boxes full of one-ounce gold bars, adding that he took 30 per cent and Panesar took 70 per cent of the boxes.
He says he took the gold to a condo in the Greater Toronto Area and started melting it for sale, acquiring $200,000 to $300,000 in cash, and he travelled to Mexico and Portugal before he ended up in Pakistan.
Chaudhary testified that a group of people in police uniforms abducted him in Pakistan and abused him, so he was forced to let people they worked with take the remaining gold from his condo unit in Canada and take his cash from his cousin’s house in Pakistan.
He says the kidnappers let him go and he went to Dubai, where he stayed until he came back to Canada on Jan. 12.
Chaudhary was sentenced this spring to four years in prison after pleading guilty to theft over $5,000, and he was given 40 years to pay back $22 million in restitution.
Prosecutors allege that Sidhu, an Air Canada employee at the time, provided a doctored waybill that allowed another man to pick up more than $22 million in gold and currency from a Pearson airport cargo bay in what investigators have called one of the largest gold heists in Canadian history.
Peel regional police have said 6,600 gold bars weighing more than 400 kilograms were stolen from the airport on April 17, 2023.

title: I tried out Apple’s HomeView smart display
body:
Apple has just announced the HomeView, its first smart home display — and I just got hands-on with the device, which features a gorgeous 7-inch square touchscreen and built-in Siri AI. It’s designed as a smart home controller, personal assistant, and home hub for your household, so there was a lot to check out.
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/LR6B6049.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/LR6B6046.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/LR6B6036.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/IMG_0250-1.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all]
The first thing that struck me about the HomeView was its size. It’s much smaller than I expected, and the screen almost entirely hides the small aluminum base that acts as a speaker. The Liquid Retina display is bright and responsive to touch, and it displays photos and the HomeView “faces” brilliantly.
You can swipe to change faces easily and choose from dozens of options, most of which resemble Apple Watch faces. The display feels like a giant Apple Watch paired with the functionality of an iPhone and the room to breathe of an iPad.
[Media: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/y-MODo3Hye4]
Apple offers both a wall-mounted and tabletop version of the HomeView, and the wall-mounted model looks like it will make a great smart home controller.
A dedicated Home Widget face pulls devices from the Apple Home app; I could walk up and tap to control a thermostat and door lock and activate a scene, or I could swipe right to get a live view of HomeKit Secure Video cameras and tap into one to access nearby accessories, such as opening the garage door. When I tried to unlock a door, it stopped me, asking me to authenticate with my face or iPhone.
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/LR6B6079.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/IMG_0256_633c28.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
The Home Widget is a skin of the Home app, so it offers all the controls you have with that app on your iPhone, just on a bigger screen designed for walk-up-and-tap interaction.
There’s a lot of swiping on the HomeView. Swipe left to get to new home faces, tap widgets to access deeper controls in apps, then swipe right for more features. You swipe up to return to the main screen, then up again to access the onboard apps, which automatically populate from your phone. Swiping down from the top of the screen brings up a control center, just like on an iPhone. You can even enable the 12MP camera from here, giving you a de facto mirror.
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/IMG_0308.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/IMG_0309.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/IMG_0313.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/IMG_0276.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/IMG_0249.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/IMG_0252.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/IMG_0267.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/IMG_0246.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/IMG_0253.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
The HomeView is built around Siri AI, and it can pull personal context such as text messages and calendar appointments based on voice requests. I didn’t get to try this myself, but saw a demo where it was asked what time Andrew would arrive from the airport, pulling context together to take actions:
“Hey, Siri, what time did Andrew say he’s getting in from JFK?”
Siri: Andrew Dean sent a message saying his flight lands at JFK Airport at 6:30AM on October 16th.
“How long will it take him to get to my place if he takes the train from JFK? Okay, I know he didn’t pack any bags.”
Siri: It will take about 1 hour and eight minutes to get from JFK to your place by transit.
“Okay, let’s turn on the coffee maker 15 minutes before he’ll arrive.”
Siri: Sets a routine to turn on the coffee maker at the correct time.
This integration of your personal context with the smart home, all orchestrated by the HomeView, is a big jump up in capability for Apple Home, and I’m looking forward to testing it myself.
[Image: The iPhone handing off a recipe to the HomeView. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/IMG_0292.jpeg?quality=90&strip=all]
One of my favorite features, being a big home chef, is the guided cooking experience on the HomeView. You can bring your iPhone, with a recipe pulled up in Siri, to the screen, and it will use Handoff to transfer the data, then reformat the recipe into an easy-to-follow onscreen experience, complete with in-line timers for each step. Apple says most recipes that use Google formatting will work this way. I’m wondering how it will handle TikTok recipes.
Another Siri AI demo had the user asking Siri to play that song her friend texted, and it started playing Bad Bunny. It took about eight seconds to pull up the song, but considering what it was doing, that felt fairly fast. I also saw a FaceTime demo where we were centered on the screen thanks to Center Stage, and I see this as a great countertop calling device.
I only got to try a few HomeView features today, but I’m looking forward to testing more soon. It costs $299 and is available for preorder today. It starts shipping on November 13th.
Photography by Jennifer Pattison Tuohy / The Verge

title: U.S. Army orders nine Hanwha wheeled howitzer prototypes, unveils XM1776 designation
body: The confirmed order has increased from six prototypes announced in August, while the remaining options have decreased from 12 to nine. The potential total remains 18 systems. XM1776 is the American version of Hanwha’s K9 Mobile Howitzer, acquired for operational trials. The August agreement, which called for accelerated prototype delivery, marked Hanwha Defense USA’s first major Army contract. “The XM-1776 Mobile Tactical Cannon represents the launch of the U.S. Army’s new long-range precision fires modernization effort and its powerful partnership with HDUSA to produce this system at speed and scale,” said Mike Smith, Hanwha Defense USA’s chief operating officer and president of Land Systems. “As we celebrate America’s 250th anniversary, Hanwha is committed to delivering industrial strength, mature capability and proven technologies that accelerate U.S. production and expand America’s artillery industrial base.” The K9 Mobile Howitzer places a fully automated turret at the rear of a truck chassis. The turret draws on the tracked K9A2’s design and carries a 155 mm, 52-caliber gun. The system holds 40 ammunition sets and has a reported maximum firing rate of approximately eight to nine rounds per minute. Its firing range depends on the ammunition used. The K9MH has been presented on a Tatra 815-7 8×8 chassis, although other suitable carriers are possible. The available information does not confirm the final chassis configuration for the Army’s XM1776 prototypes. Reported K9MH performance figures include deployment in less than 30 seconds and a maximum road speed of 100 kilometers per hour. Road range is stated at up to 700 kilometers, and the turret can work with the tracked K10 ammunition resupply vehicle. Hanwha is establishing a Phase I facility in Opelika, Alabama, to integrate and test XM1776 and other K9 Mobile Howitzers. The company disclosed a three-year lease for the site in August. Its leadership plans to meet more than 70 existing and potential U.S. suppliers to develop an Artillery Industrial Base Coalition. Hanwha is also evaluating further sites and production phases as it expands its American artillery operations. “We’re focused on creating a U.S.-anchored K9 Mobile Howitzer manufacturing network—with Opelika, Alabama, as the current phase I launch point—that can deliver advanced Mobile Tactical Cannons at the speed and scale the U.S. Army needs,” said Jason Pak, Hanwha Defense USA’s head of Land Systems – Artillery, in August. The company’s localization strategy includes domestic production, support and workforce development. Hanwha said more than 2,500 K9 howitzers are already fielded worldwide. It said the K9MH is compatible with the Army’s full suite of munitions and draws on an industrial network shared by nearly a dozen allies. “Hanwha’s global supply chain and local production experience in Australia, Egypt, Poland and Romania demonstrate a proven commitment to local execution we’re excited to bring to the U.S.,” said Michael Coulter, Hanwha Defense USA’s chief executive, in the August announcement. “Localization is central to Hanwha’s global business model, leveraging our global leading industrial technology and process in Korea to create sovereign industrial strength in the U.S., whether it be in shipbuilding, munitions or combat vehicles.” “This award reflects Hanwha’s enduring commitment to the United States and to strengthening the U.S. defense industrial base,” said Alex Wong, Hanwha Group’s chief strategy officer, in August. “We are not simply delivering a system—we are building an American manufacturing enterprise, transferring technology and creating a lasting foundation for broad industrial collaboration.” The naming ceremony took place at Hanwha’s booth during the October 12–14 AUSA exhibition at the Walter E. Washington Convention Center. The company did not disclose the orders’ value or delivery schedule in the announcements.

title: Mahama commissions Christian Tetteh Yohuno Ward Complex at Police Hospital
body: President John Dramani Mahama has commissioned an 85-bed ward complex at the Police Hospital in Accra, named after the Inspector General of Police (IGP), Christian Tetteh Yohuno. The facility, commissioned on Tuesday, October 13, under the theme: “ Christian Tetteh Yohuno Ward Complex ”, was constructed to commemorate the Golden Jubilee celebration of the Police Hospital and is fully equipped with ultramodern healthcare facilities. President Mahama described the new facility as an important investment in the health and welfare of personnel of the Ghana Police Service and a significant enhancement to the hospital’s capacity to serve the wider Ghanaian public. He recalled that nearly a year ago, he joined the IGP and the Police Management Board at the Police Training School in Tesano for the Police Remembrance Day observance, during which officers who died in the line of duty were honoured and solidarity was shown to their families. The President said that on that solemn occasion he discussed with the IGP the need to pay greater attention to the welfare of serving police officers. “And today, we see a tangible outcome of that discussion. I commend the Inspector General of Police and the Police Management Board for their leadership in delivering this new hospital block, which is equipped with the most modern facilities,” he stated. President Mahama also expressed appreciation to the health professionals and all those whose efforts contributed to the successful completion of the project. He noted that men and women of the Ghana Police Service undertake difficult and often dangerous assignments, including responding to emergencies, confronting violent crime and maintaining peace and security in communities. According to him, the demands of policing affect both the physical and mental well-being of officers, making it imperative for them to have access to timely and high-quality healthcare whenever they are injured or fall ill. The President said the responsibility of the State also extended to supporting the families of officers, whose sacrifices often enable them to perform their duties effectively. “An officer’s ability to protect the public is closely linked to the support the police service provides. Access to appropriate healthcare is therefore essential for operational readiness,” the President said. President Mahama disclosed that even before the formal commissioning of the facility, seven police officers who sustained injuries in the line of duty in Bunkpurugu and Porto had been admitted to the new ward complex. He said the officers had been transported to Accra and were receiving treatment at the facility. He said they would get the best care at the new facility. The President stated that the new block would strengthen the hospital’s capacity to provide quality healthcare services, particularly for officers injured in the line of duty and patients requiring urgent medical attention. He also underscored the importance of addressing the psychological impact of policing, noting that repeated exposure to violence, tragedy and distress could have lasting effects on officers. He said mental health support, counselling and appropriate treatment should be readily accessible without fear of stigma. “When officers know that their health and welfare is being taken seriously, they can serve with greater confidence and focus. Investing in their care strengthens our collective national security.” President Mahama noted that the Police Hospital’s role extended beyond serving police personnel, as it formed part of Ghana’s national healthcare system and provided emergency medical services to the public. He said the expanded facility would help strengthen healthcare delivery, particularly during emergencies, road accidents and public health crises. The President emphasised that every patient who visited the hospital deserved to be treated with dignity and compassion. He stated that the true value of the facility would be measured by the quality of healthcare provided and how well it was maintained over time. President Mahama therefore urged the hospital’s management to uphold the highest standards of hygiene, patient safety and clinical practice. He stressed the need for regular maintenance of medical equipment, uninterrupted availability of essential medicines and supplies, and continuous capacity-building for healthcare personnel. The President also commended the doctors, nurses, pharmacists, laboratory technicians and support staff who would serve in the new block. “And behind every patient record is a person who may be frightened, in pain, or uncertain about their future,” he said. “And so, when you are confronted with such patients, listen to them carefully, explain to them clearly, and treat every patient with the respect you would wish for your own family.” President Mahama reiterated the Government’s commitment to improving the safety, welfare and operational effectiveness of personnel of the Ghana Police Service. The Minister for the Interior, Muntaka Mohammed-Mubarak, said President Mahama’s commitment to improving healthcare infrastructure and enhancing the welfare of security personnel continued to leave a lasting impact on the nation. He said the facility stood as a visible symbol of the President’s dedication to building a stronger and more inclusive Ghana. The IGP, on his part, expressed gratitude to President Mahama for his continuous support for the Police Service and his concern for the welfare of officers. He assured that the Police Administration would continue to pursue initiatives aimed at improving the health, welfare and operational effectiveness of personnel of the Service.

title: Vice President calls for wider access to Ghana’s political party histories
body: Vice President Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang has called for wider access to publications documenting Ghana’s political party histories, stressing the importance of historical knowledge in deepening public understanding of the country’s governance institutions and constitutional arrangements. She said making such records accessible to the public would enable citizens to better understand the political experiences that have shaped the Republic and equip them to participate more meaningfully in the country’s political life. Speaking at the launch of six historiographies of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) on Tuesday, October 13, the Vice President emphasised that knowledge of political history should not be confined to people who experienced the events first-hand. According to her, documenting the country’s political journey and making the resulting publications widely available would help preserve important historical records for present and future generations. “Familiarity with our governance institutions, with our constitutional arrangements, and the political experiences that have shaped our Republic” is important for meaningful civic participation, she said. Professor Opoku-Agyemang explained that citizens who have access to such knowledge are better positioned to understand the institutions and processes that govern the country, as well as the historical developments that have influenced Ghana’s political system. She noted that historical understanding should extend beyond those who lived through particular political periods, arguing that younger generations and other members of the public should also have opportunities to learn from the country’s political experiences. “When that knowledge is accessible, citizens are better placed to participate meaningfully in political life. The knowledge of history is also not restricted to those who have lived through it,” she added. The Vice President expressed the hope that the newly launched publications would be distributed to a broad range of institutions and individuals to ensure that the historical accounts reach a wider audience. “It is my hope that these publications will reach libraries, research institutions, private spaces, and public officials too,” she said. She also encouraged regional and constituency executives of the NDC to keep copies of the publications in their offices, alongside other important historical documents. According to her, making the books available at the party’s various organisational levels would provide members and visitors with opportunities to engage with the party’s history and learn more about the developments that have shaped its evolution. The launch of the six historiographies provides an opportunity to preserve accounts of the NDC’s political journey and make them available for research, institutional reference and public education. The publications, she indicated, should therefore be treated as important reference materials that can contribute to a deeper understanding of Ghana’s governance structures, constitutional development and political experiences.

title: How the SEC’s lack of leadership could facilitate crypto rulemaking
body:
A recent change in the SEC’s rules on quorum could make it easier for the agency to amend its approach to crypto regulation in the absence of a market structure bill.
After US lawmakers failed to pass a comprehensive digital asset market structure bill, financial regulators stepped up efforts to change rules around the oversight and enforcement of crypto companies and offerings.
However, the two primary regulators, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), are understaffed at the leadership level, leaving the decisions for regulating aspects of the $3 trillion crypto market largely in the hands of just three individuals, two of whom were nominated by US President Donald Trump.
At the SEC, two commissioners — Chair Paul Atkins and former Acting Chair Mark Uyeda — remain following the departure of Commissioner Hester Peirce earlier this month. The dearth of leadership at the CFTC is even more stark, with Michael Selig serving as the only Senate-confirmed chair and commissioner since December 2025. The agencies are intended to each have five commissioners.
Both agencies have proposed rules that appear to be attempting to take the place of legislation from Congress in regulating cryptocurrencies.
The SEC proposed rules to provide companies with a safe harbor from tokens being treated as “investment contracts” in August, and the CFTC followed suit in October, with Selig saying the agency would use its “existing statutory authorities“ to address crypto regulation through proposed rules on exchanges. Atkins added on Oct. 2 that “more regulatory proposals [were] on the horizon” for crypto.
On Sept. 30, the SEC made these regulatory avenues even easier with a lack of commissioners. The agency released a final rule which went into effect on Oct. 2 that it said amended quorum requirements for what it called “promot[ing] flexibility and finality of agency rulemaking.” The rule reduces the number of commissioners required for a quorum to just one person if only two are present in many cases.
“[...] with now just two commissioners around and it being entirely possible that one of them might have to recuse themselves from an issue (or be otherwise MIA), just one is now enough to pass a formal rule that applies to America’s vast multitrillion-dollar securities markets,” wrote Robin Wigglesworth in an Oct. 5 op-ed for the Financial Times.
Related: Crypto regulation at SEC, CFTC to come down to 3 commissioners following key resignation
Uyeda responded in his own Financial Times op-ed on Sunday, claiming that the SEC’s “commitment to its mission remains unchanged” despite having only two commissioners and no announcement from Trump about additional nominations to fill the empty seats. The policymaker said that the rule change “clarifies that the Commission can establish a quorum if all but one commissioner is disqualified from a matter.”
“Suggesting that the SEC is ‘hastily revamp[ing]’ its quorum rule so that the remaining commissioners can ‘have their way’ makes for a colourful comparison to fictional dystopian regimes but misleads readers about why the Commission revised its quorum rule and why it’s for the better,” said Uyeda.
As of Tuesday, the White House had not announced any nominations for the SEC and CFTC, potentially leaving the rulemaking process in the hands of just one person at each agency for months, if not longer. Congress still has time to vote on the market structure bill at the center of the controversy, the Digital Asset Market Clarity (CLARITY) Act, but some experts don’t see lawmakers advancing the legislation in a lame duck session between the 2026 midterm elections and when the next session is sworn into office in January.

title: Adebayo Calls For Release of Five ‘Tinubu Must Go’ Protesters in Borno
body: Kasim Sumaina in Abuja Prince Adewale Adebayo, the Social Democratic Party (SDP) presidential candidate, has called for the immediate release of five detained protesters in Borno State, describing their continued detention as an infringement on democratic freedoms. The protesters, identified as Ba’ana Grema, Mustapha Abba, Abacha Mohammed Ali, Adam Umar Gubio and Abdulhamid Mohammed, are reportedly being held in a correctional facility in the state over their participation in a protest against President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s administration. Adebayo, in a statement issued on Tuesday by the Movement Adebayo for President (MAP), condemned what it described as an attempt to criminalise dissent and suppress opposition voices. He maintained that citizens had the constitutional right to express their political opinions and peacefully demonstrate against government policies and performance. According to him, wearing T-shirts bearing the inscription ‘Tinubu Must Go’ does not constitute an offence where those involved conduct themselves peacefully. The SDP presidential candidate challenged the Borno State Government, led by Governor Babagana Zulum, the police and the Federal Government to respect the fundamental rights of citizens. He said there was no evidence, in the account presented by his movement, suggesting that the five protesters engaged in violent conduct. Adebayo warned that any attempt to suppress peaceful opposition would be resisted through lawful means, adding that democratic freedoms must be protected irrespective of political affiliations. He also urged the Nigeria Police Force to remain neutral as political activities intensify ahead of the 2026/2027 campaign season. “The police must protect and defend the rights of citizens to peacefully sell their candidates, and they must refuse to be used against opposition parties and candidates,” he said. Adebayo further warned against the use of law enforcement agencies to intimidate opposition figures and citizens who hold views contrary to those of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC). He stressed that democracy could not thrive where citizens were denied the right to express dissenting opinions or pursue their political beliefs peacefully. The SDP candidate called on Nigerians, statesmen and other stakeholders to support efforts to secure the release of the five detainees. He reaffirmed his commitment to building a Nigeria free from oppression, poverty and insecurity, declaring that no citizen should be punished for holding a contrary political opinion. The statement was signed by the Movement Adebayo for President, under the slogan, ‘MAP… The RoadMAP To A New Nigeria.’

title: Ukraine's Asset Recovery Agency prepares Rybas Karpaty hotel complex for launch
body:
Ukraine's Asset Recovery and Management Agency (ARMA) is preparing the Ribas Karpaty hotel complex in the village of Polyanytsia, Ivano-Frankivsk region, for management, according to a statement on ARMA's website.
The asset was transferred to ARMA's management pursuant to a ruling by the High Anti-Corruption Court dated July 6, 2026, in case No. 991/8670/26, criminal proceedings No. 52020000000000309. As reported, in May the High Anti-Corruption Court ordered the detention of Serhiy Tupalsky, a former deputy head of Kyiv Customs, who is suspected of legalizing more than $2 million in illegally obtained funds during the construction of the hotel complex in Bukovel.
The transferred asset includes a building with an area of 2,767 square meters, featuring 47 rooms in various categories, a restaurant, a spa complex, an indoor swimming pool, a Finnish sauna, a Roman-style steam room, massage rooms, a children's room, a coworking area, a room for storing ski equipment and a parking lot, together with land plots bearing cadastral numbers 2611092001:22:002:2558 and 2611092001:27:002:0206.
Ribas Hotels Group told Interfax-Ukraine that, as of now, the management status of Ribas Karpaty remains unchanged and that the hotel has not been transferred to another company for management.
Ribas Hotels Group added that, as a management company, it does not comment on processes concerning ownership rights to properties. "If there are any changes to the terms of hotel management, including the signing of a new agreement or a decision to terminate management, we will certainly issue an announcement," the company added.

title: Tinubu writes Senate, forwards 5 bills on drug enforcement, transport, others
body: By Henry Umoru President Bola Tinubu has written the Senate, transmitting a series of bills for consideration and the bills include proposed legislation to amend the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau Act, establish a National School of Government and reform the legal framework governing the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency, NDLEA, among others. The bills, in accordance with the provisions of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, were conveyed by the President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio. The Executive communications were read on Tuesday by Akpabio. One of the proposals, the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau Amendment Bill 2026, seeks to amend the existing 2022 Act to reposition the bureau as an independent authority and expand its mandate. The proposed amendment also seeks to transfer supervisory oversight of the bureau to the Presidency, alongside changes to its administrative structure. According to the letter, “The Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau Amendment Bill seeks to reposition the Bureau as an independent multimodal safety investigation authority, expanding its mandate beyond aviation to maritime and other transport occurrences. “It also proposes transferring the Bureau’s oversight to the Presidency and strengthening its institutional, operational, administrative and constitutional framework. Another proposal, the NDLEA Bill 2026, seeks to establish a consolidated legal framework for the operations of the NDLEA. The bill is expected to strengthen the agency’s powers, including its capacity to investigate individuals suspected of involvement in illicit drug-related activities. According to the letter, “The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency Bill seeks to repeal the existing NDLEA Act and the Indian Hemp Act, both contained in the Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004. “The proposed legislation is intended to establish a consolidated legal framework for combating the cultivation, processing, trafficking and use of illicit drugs. “It also seeks to empower the agency to investigate persons suspected of involvement in drug-related activities.” President Tinubu also transmitted the National School of Government Bill (ASCON) 2026, which seeks to repeal the Administrative staff college of Nigeria act and establish a National School of Government. The proposed institution is intended to serve as a national centre for governance training, public sector capacity development and institutional strengthening. The National School of Government Bill seeks to repeal the Administrative Staff College of Nigeria Act and establish a new institution to serve as a national centre for leadership development, policy delivery and executive capacity-building. The President equally transmitted a bill seeking to domesticate the four Geneva Conventions of 1949 and their two Additional Protocols of 1977, which provide for the protection of victims of armed conflict, as well as the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court, providing for the enforcement of punishment on genocide, war crimes, crimes against humanity and aggression. The letter reads further, “The Geneva Conventions and Additional Protocols Bill seeks to repeal the existing Geneva Conventions Act and give effect in Nigeria to the 1949 Geneva Conventions and the two Additional Protocols adopted in 1977. “The Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court (Enforcement) Bill seeks to domesticate the Rome Statute and establish a framework for the enforcement and punishment of genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes and related offences. “It also provides for Nigeria’s cooperation with the International Criminal Court in the performance of its functions”. Akpabio thereafter referred the bills to the Committee on Rules and Business for further legislative action. Meanwhile, the Senate received notification of President Tinubu’s assent to two amendment bills providing for the inclusion of federal universities in Yaba, Lagos, and Kaduna in the relevant laws governing federal universities of technology. Akpabio said the Federal University of Technology Amendment No. 2 Bill, 2026, provides for the inclusion of the Federal University of Technology and Vocational Studies in Yaba in the relevant Act. “The Federal University of Technology Amendment Bill, 2026, seeks to amend the Federal Universities of Technology Act to include the Federal University of Technology and Vocational Studies in Kaduna”. He thereafter referred the documents to the Clerk to the National Assembly for further action. Akpabio commended Tinubu for assenting to the two bills, describing the development as an important step towards promoting education in Nigeria.
