title: Sybiha after meeting with Grossi: IAEA to send missions to 19 electrical substations
body:
The IAEA will send missions to 19 electrical substations in Ukraine, Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha has said.
"In Warsaw, I continued our dialogue with IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi. We discussed the situation at and around the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant, the security threats posed by the ongoing Russian militarization, and the need to ensure nuclear safety and security," the ministry's press service said citing Sybiha on its Telegram channel on Tuesday.
According to the press service, Sybiha expressed his gratitude to the IAEA Director General for his decision to send IAEA missions to 19 electrical substations that are critical to the safe operation of Ukrainian nuclear power plants.
"This will be the IAEA's largest deployment of its kind to date, and a timely step to protect nuclear safety and security amid ongoing Russian attacks on Ukraine's energy system," Sybiha said.
"I also expressed my sincere appreciation for this summer's recovery programme for the children of Ukrainian nuclear workers, organised in cooperation with the Director General and the governments of Austria and Poland. We agreed to continue such valuable humanitarian initiatives," the Ukrainian minister added.
"Thank you, Rafael, for your personal engagement and for the IAEA's continued work in Ukraine," he added.

title: Indian police detain Cockroach Janta Party leaders demanding election chief stand down
body: India's "cockroach" youth movement leaders were detained on Tuesday after they jumped barricades to enter a historic Delhi site popular for protests, demanding that the chief election commissioner resign over a revision of voter lists.Supporters of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and opposition groups have held almost daily protests this month to demand commissioner Gyanesh Kumar stand down over the revisions critics say favor Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) by removing the names of millions of voters.The Election Commission has denied favoring any party and said voters whose names were wrongly deleted can re-enroll, while the BJP has accused rivals of trying to undermine democracy by questioning legitimate electoral processes.Thousands joined a protest march by opposition groups on Monday, after a clampdown foiled CJP plans for a weekend demonstration, with police detaining thousands of protesters, including CJP leaders.Delhi Police announced on Monday that the Jantar Mantar open-air observatory, in the national capital's central business district, was no longer designated as an official protest site, and said three new venues had been identified.The CJP said its leaders, Ashutosh Ranka, Saurav Das, and Ajinkya Shinde, were among about 20 people who "sneaked" into the observatory to "reclaim" it and were detained.Greatest political challenge for Indian prime ministerA CJP livestream showed about a dozen people jumping a gate and barricades to reach the site, where they waved the Indian flag and chanted slogans before police detained them.Delhi Police did not respond to a request for comment.The youth movement, which has mobilized protests in recent months against issues ranging from government school infrastructure to jobs, is among the biggest political challenges to Modi and his BJP in his 12 years in power.A weeks-long sit-in by its supporters at Jantar Mantar earlier this year forced the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over exam paper leaks.Sporadic demonstrations broke out elsewhere on Tuesday, including in Delhi's business hub Connaught Place, where television footage showed dozens of members of the student unit of the main opposition Congress party being hauled into buses by police as they attempted to stage a sit-in protest.A small group of protesters, including from left-wing student groups, tried to breach police barricades during a march in the eastern city of Patna.Nearly 150 journalists gathered at the Press Club of India in New Delhi to march in protest against the detention of reporters covering events over the weekend.Concerns raised over voter list revisions, registration procedures, digital systemsThe demonstrations erupted after the Indian Express newspaper reported last month that Kumar's two deputies raised several concerns internally about voter list revisions, registration procedures and digital systems.The change, which started last year, removed over 130 million names - more than the population of Japan - from voter lists, including 28 million who died, 63 million who relocated, and 30 million who could not be traced.Opposition parties allege the deletions disproportionately affect Muslim voters and other minorities, who are unlikely to support the Hindu nationalist ruling party - allegations the poll panel and BJP reject.

title: NNPC’s 2026 revenue hits N28.5trn, jumps 21% in August
body: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja The Nigerian National Petroleum Company, NNPC, Limited recorded cumulative revenue of N28.54 trillion in the first eight months of 2026, with revenue rising by 21.1 per cent month-on-month to N3.74 trillion in August. Read Also: NAF Plane Crash: Igbokoda residents lament stench, fear disease outbreak, as body parts float The company’s August 2026 Monthly Report Summary showed that revenue increased from N3.087 trillion in July to N3.737 trillion in August, while profit after tax rose by 54.5 per cent to N431 billion from N279 billion in the preceding month. An analysis of the company’s reports in 2026 indicated that NNPC generated N2.571 trillion in January, N2.680 trillion in February and N2.774 trillion in March before revenue surged to N4.971 trillion in April. Revenue subsequently stood at N4.335 trillion in May and N4.389 trillion in June before declining to N3.087 trillion in July and recovering in August. The monthly figures showed that profit after tax stood at N385 billion in January, N236 billion in February, N276 billion in March, N481 billion in April, N462 billion in May and N535 billion in June before falling to N279 billion in July and rebounding to N431 billion in August. Cumulatively, the company’s profit after tax amounted to N2.985 trillion in the first eight months of the year. NNPC’s statutory payments to the government in August was N1.574 trillion bringing total payment to N9.487 trillion in 2026. On production, the report put average crude oil and condensate output at 1.69 million barrels per day in August, slightly higher than the 1.68 million barrels per day recorded in July. Natural gas production stood at 7,680 million standard cubic feet per day in August, up from 7,489 million standard cubic feet per day in July. However, the August figure was below the 7,841 million standard cubic feet per day recorded in June, the highest level shown in the 12-month production chart. Gas sales increased to 4,737 million standard cubic feet per day in August from 4,581 million standard cubic feet per day in July. Similarly, crude oil and condensate sales rose to 24.56 million barrels in August from 22.53 million barrels in July. NNPC reported 100 per cent availability of upstream pipelines, adding that Obiafu-Obrikom-Oben (OB3) gas pipeline project had reached 100 per cent completion, while the Ajaokuta-Kaduna-Kano (AKK) gas pipeline was 95 per cent complete. On the AKK project, NNPC said construction and installation activities were continuing, with the objective of delivering gas to Abuja in 2026. For the OB3 pipeline, the company reported a major milestone with the successful commissioning and full operationalisation of the pipeline, which is intended to link the eastern and western gas network systems. title: Bitcoin Shakes Off Spooky Season Jitters: Can Bulls Keep It Going?
body:
Bitcoin is bouncing today following a week that had traders swapping "Uptober" memes for "spooky szn" ones after BTC cut its September gains in half .
The price of Bitcoin today slid to $80,953.41 early Tuesday, extending a Monday sell-off, then reversed to $83,591.79, up 2.24% on the day.
The Crypto Fear and Greed Index , a 0-to-100 sentiment gauge built from momentum, volatility, options positioning and social data, fell to 53 from an "extreme greed" reading of 82 on Aug. 26. It reads 56 today , a neutral score. What it boils down to is this: The August euphoria is gone, but traders aren’t panicking either.
Bitcoin ETFs are down a net $386.3 million in October, and outflows force funds to sell actual Bitcoin. Wednesday's Consumer Price Index report, expected to show annual inflation rising to 3.6% from 3.4%, is the next test: a hotter print would boost rate-hike bets and likely pressure Bitcoin. The Federal Reserve meets Oct. 27-28.
Traders on Myriad , a prediction market developed by Decrypt 's parent company Dastan, give 54% odds that Bitcoin falls to $80,000 this month, down from 56% on Monday. The BTC highs in October market holds at 45% for $87,500. So, overall, sentiment has improved today, even if slightly.
Today's low stopped about $588 above $80,365.12, the swing low where the bounce began. That higher low is what traders want in an uptrend. Bitcoin also reclaimed the Fibonacci "golden zone" between $81,847.57 and $82,305.50, an area where pullbacks within uptrends often draw buyers.
The Average Directional Index, or ADX, measures trend strength, and readings above 25 confirm a trend. It reads 29.9 with buyers in control, but it was 42.8 on Oct. 7, so the uptrend is coasting rather than accelerating. The 50-day exponential moving average stayed above the 200-day, a golden cross traders read as an intact long-term uptrend.
The Relative Strength Index, a 0-to-100 momentum gauge, sits at 53.4, just above the 50 line that separates bullish from bearish momentum. The Squeeze Momentum Indicator has been on for seven sessions, meaning volatility is compressed like a coiled spring, and its -0.52 reading leans slightly bearish.
A daily close above $84,245.88 would open $86,644.19, then the $87,422.70 high, about $77 shy of Myriad's $87,500 line. Losing $81,603.02 would bring the daily trend band's upper edge into play just above $80,000. A close below it would expose $77,500.
Until Wednesday's CPI print, the active squeeze points to a market that is winding up rather than picking a direction. Oil and Iran headlines, Treasury yields, and daily ETF flows remain the short-term catalysts to track.

title: Belgian ambassador in Moscow called in to Russian Foreign Ministry
body:
MOSCOW, October 13. /TASS/. Belgian ambassador to Moscow Michel Gerebtzoff was summoned to the Russian Foreign Ministry on Tuesday over the country’s authorities’ anti-Russian statements, the Foreign Ministry said.
"The Belgian diplomat was informed that the Russian side firmly rejects the unsubstantiated and increasingly frequent claims by the kingdom’s military and political leadership about mounting hybrid, sabotage, and direct military threats against Belgium and Europe allegedly originating from Russia," the ministry said.
Gerebtzoff was informed that "the overtly aggressive statements by certain representatives of the Belgian authorities, who deliberately cast Russia as an enemy, are contributing to further escalation and the risk of the confrontation they are fomenting spiraling out of control."
"The Belgian side is urged to consider the consequences of such statements and to ease the intensity of anti-Russian rhetoric, which is fueling rising tensions on the European continent.".

title: Infantino received undisclosed $1.72m World Cup payment — Reports
body: By Adegboyega Adeleye Embattled FIFA president Gianni Infantino received a previously undisclosed $1.72 million payment from the organisation responsible for managing the 2026 World Cup, according to FIFA and US Internal Revenue Service (IRS) documents obtained by ESPN. According to the report published on Tuesday, the lack of transparency surrounding the compensation raises questions over compliance with FIFA statutes, which require the individual compensation of the organisation’s president to be made public. The payment was made in 2024 by FWC2026, the US-based entity established by FIFA to manage and operate the 2026 World Cup, according to IRS records. The $1.72 million compensation was in addition to Infantino’s regular salary and benefits from FIFA, which amounted to 4.274 million Swiss francs, or approximately $4.86 million, in 2024, according to the organisation’s financial report. The additional payment was not disclosed in FIFA’s 2024 annual report, the latest year for which FWC2026’s IRS Form 990 is publicly available, ESPN reported. Article 43, paragraph 13 of FIFA’s statutes states that the organisation’s Compensation Sub-Committee determines the compensation of the FIFA president, council members and secretary general, adding that their individual compensation “shall be made public”. However, FIFA has denied violating its disclosure obligations, insisting that its financial reporting complies with applicable requirements. A FIFA spokesperson told ESPN that the organisation “fully complies with all reporting requirements and strongly rejects any suggestion there has been a violation of FIFA’s Statutes”. In a separate statement, the spokesperson said FIFA did not pay Infantino a second salary and that his annual compensation and other contractual benefits were determined by the independent Compensation Sub-Committee. “FIFA strongly rejects any claims that it has failed to disclose any financial information and has violated FIFA’s Statutes,” the spokesperson said, adding that FIFA’s accounts were independently audited and its declarations complied with tax regulations in Switzerland, the United States and elsewhere. The Times first reported Infantino’s additional compensation from FWC2026 and the questions surrounding its disclosure. Miguel Maduro, former chairman of FIFA’s governance committee, told the newspaper that failing to make additional payments from FIFA-related entities public would contravene the organisation’s transparency rules. Maduro argued that FIFA’s statutes imposed an obligation of full transparency, adding that the compensation committee should not authorise alternative forms of remuneration that were not publicly disclosed. The latest revelation adds to the scrutiny surrounding Infantino, who has faced criticism over his leadership and a proposal earlier this year to sell a 20 per cent stake in the World Cup to private investors. The proposed investment plan, which Infantino reportedly called FIFA Forward Enterprise, drew opposition from football officials concerned about transparency and the management of the sport’s commercial interests. Infantino has also faced pressure following his close relationship with US President Donald Trump ahead of the 2026 World Cup, which was hosted by the United States, Canada and Mexico. The FIFA president is expected to meet members of the FIFA Council in Zurich on Thursday, amid continuing discussions about the organisation’s governance and financial arrangements. Infantino has confirmed plans to seek re-election in March 2027, despite criticism from some football officials over his leadership. title: General Dynamics showcases Wolf XM30, new counter-drone systems at AUSA
body: The Army is developing a replacement for the M2 Bradley while testing new ways to put loitering munitions under armor. General Dynamics Land Systems is showcasing a 1/8 model of the Wolf XM30, the company’s candidate to replace the M2 Bradley, along with PERCH 2.0, M-SHORAD Increment 4 and the F600 Leonidas at the Association of the United States Army’s annual meeting this week. The Wolf is one of two vehicles competing in the Army’s XM30 program , with American Rheinmetall delivering its first Lynx XM30 prototype to the Army in September. Retired Army officer Scott Taylor, General Dynamics Land Systems’ director of U.S. growth, told Military Times that the Bradley has reached the limits of its ability to accommodate additional capabilities and weight. The Wolf is designed with greater capacity in mind, while improving fightability, lethality and survivability, Taylor said. General Dynamics Land Systems delivered its first Wolf prototype to the Army in August. PERCH 2.0 allows M1A2 Abrams main battle tanks and Stryker vehicles to launch Switchblade 300 loitering munitions while keeping operators under armor. One PERCH 2.0 prototype has been provided to the Army for experimentation, with three more on the way. Soldiers with 2nd Battalion, 12th Cavalry Regiment, 1st Brigade Combat Team, known as “Thunder Horse,” are currently testing the prototype at Fort Hood, Texas, Taylor noted. The system grew out of General Dynamics Land Systems’ development of PERCH 1.0, which the company developed in less than four months after senior Army leaders discussed observations from the war in Ukraine during a 2025 event, Taylor said. Soldiers with the 1st Cavalry Division then tested the system at Fort Hood and provided feedback that led to changes in loading procedures, use of space and integration with the tank’s loader display. The Army initially experimented with Switchblade 600 before asking the company to focus on the smaller Switchblade 300, according to Taylor. General Dynamics Land Systems continued developing PERCH 2.0 with its own independent research and development funding before the Army contracted for three additional prototypes under the Abrams program office. The Army will evaluate the design after the experimentation and could compete the capability or purchase it, depending on the results, Taylor explained. “In many ways, it’s become attrition-based warfare over there, and that’s not the way the U.S. Army or the U.S. Marine Corps or many of our allies fight,” Taylor said. Also on the AUSA floor is the M-SHORAD Increment 4 , a platform-agnostic air-defense system built around a Self-Loading Equipment Dock, or SLED, that can be mounted on different vehicles. Charles Woody, the company’s program manager for M-SHORAD Increment 4, told Military Times that the system is designed in part to reduce the cognitive burden on soldiers conducting air-defense and counter-UAS missions. The configuration includes a 7.62mm machine gun, an intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance drone, a loitering munition and a counter-drone system. The F600 Leonidas combines Epirus’ high-powered microwave technology for defeating drones with a commercially based Ford F-600 chassis modified for military use. The Army is expected to use a prototype to determine where the capability fits in its future air-defense plans.

title: General Dynamics showcases Wolf XM30, new counter-drone systems at AUSA
body: The Army is developing a replacement for the M2 Bradley while testing new ways to put loitering munitions under armor. General Dynamics Land Systems is showcasing a 1/8 model of the Wolf XM30, the company’s candidate to replace the M2 Bradley, along with PERCH 2.0, M-SHORAD Increment 4 and the F600 Leonidas at the Association of the United States Army’s annual meeting this week. The Wolf is one of two vehicles competing in the Army’s XM30 program , with American Rheinmetall delivering its first Lynx XM30 prototype to the Army in September. Retired Army officer Scott Taylor, General Dynamics Land Systems’ director of U.S. growth, told Military Times that the Bradley has reached the limits of its ability to accommodate additional capabilities and weight. The Wolf is designed with greater capacity in mind, while improving fightability, lethality and survivability, Taylor said. General Dynamics Land Systems delivered its first Wolf prototype to the Army in August. PERCH 2.0 allows M1A2 Abrams main battle tanks and Stryker vehicles to launch Switchblade 300 loitering munitions while keeping operators under armor. One PERCH 2.0 prototype has been provided to the Army for experimentation, with three more on the way. Soldiers with 2nd Battalion, 12th Cavalry Regiment, 1st Brigade Combat Team, known as “Thunder Horse,” are currently testing the prototype at Fort Hood, Texas, Taylor noted. The system grew out of General Dynamics Land Systems’ development of PERCH 1.0, which the company developed in less than four months after senior Army leaders discussed observations from the war in Ukraine during a 2025 event, Taylor said. Soldiers with the 1st Cavalry Division then tested the system at Fort Hood and provided feedback that led to changes in loading procedures, use of space and integration with the tank’s loader display. The Army initially experimented with Switchblade 600 before asking the company to focus on the smaller Switchblade 300, according to Taylor. General Dynamics Land Systems continued developing PERCH 2.0 with its own independent research and development funding before the Army contracted for three additional prototypes under the Abrams program office. The Army will evaluate the design after the experimentation and could compete the capability or purchase it, depending on the results, Taylor explained. “In many ways, it’s become attrition-based warfare over there, and that’s not the way the U.S. Army or the U.S. Marine Corps or many of our allies fight,” Taylor said. Also on the AUSA floor is the M-SHORAD Increment 4 , a platform-agnostic air-defense system built around a Self-Loading Equipment Dock, or SLED, that can be mounted on different vehicles. Charles Woody, the company’s program manager for M-SHORAD Increment 4, told Military Times that the system is designed in part to reduce the cognitive burden on soldiers conducting air-defense and counter-UAS missions. The configuration includes a 7.62mm machine gun, an intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance drone, a loitering munition and a counter-drone system. The F600 Leonidas combines Epirus’ high-powered microwave technology for defeating drones with a commercially based Ford F-600 chassis modified for military use. The Army is expected to use a prototype to determine where the capability fits in its future air-defense plans.

title: VIDEO: NAFDAC Clamps Down On Fake Drinks Manufacturers In Lagos, Arrests Suspects
body: The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) has uncovered and sealed shops at the Trade Fair Complex in Lagos where a syndicate allegedly manufactured and distributed fake and adulterated alcoholic drinks and wines. NAFDAC disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday, saying the operation followed credible intelligence. The agency said its operatives discovered unhygienic production rooms where suspects allegedly purchased empty bottles of expensive wines, replaced their labels with fake ones and refilled them with adulterated alcoholic drinks. Pictures and videos from the operation showed empty containers, counterfeit labels and concoctions being prepared under insanitary conditions, posing serious health risks to consumers. Several suspects were arrested during the raid. ﻿ NAFDAC urged Nigerians to remain vigilant, assuring the public of its commitment to safeguarding public health. The agency said it conducts daily enforcement operations to rid the market of fake and unwholesome regulated products. It added that its Director-General, Professor Mojisola Christianah Adeyeye, remained committed to ensuring that Nigerians had access to wholesome food and safe, effective medicines. NAFDAC warned those involved in the production and distribution of counterfeit and adulterated products to desist or face the full weight of the law. The agency said it would continue to pursue and prosecute offenders as part of efforts to protect public health. title: 4-year courses must end in 4 years, Alausa tells varsities
body: By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The federal government has pledged to honour its agreements with tertiary institution workers, declaring that Nigerian students must no longer lose precious academic years to strikes triggered by unfulfilled government commitments. Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, gave the assurance on Tuesday in Abuja while unveiling the 2026 agreements between the Federal Government and staff unions in universities, polytechnics and colleges of education. Alausa, who described the agreements as a major step towards restoring confidence in government-union relations, said the administration of President Bola Tinubu was determined to end the cycle of broken promises, industrial disputes and disruptions to academic calendars that had plagued the country’s tertiary education system for decades. He declared that a four-year degree programme must be completed in four years, insisting that the Federal Government would fulfil its obligations under the newly unveiled agreements. “During his campaign, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu promised that a four-year course would be completed in four years. Today, through his leadership, these agreements give practical expression to that pledge: A promise made, a promise kept, and trust restored,” the minister said. The agreements cover the Consolidated Academic Tools Allowance, CATA, for the Academic Staff Union of Polytechnics, ASUP, and the Colleges of Education Academic Staff Union, COEASU, as well as the Consolidated Non-Teaching Tools Allowance, CONTTA, for non-teaching staff unions across universities, polytechnics and colleges of education. The allowances are to take effect from January 1, 2026, in line with the agreements and applicable implementation guidelines. Alausa, however, acknowledged that the unveiling of the agreements was only the beginning, stressing that their credibility would ultimately depend on the government’s ability to implement the provisions faithfully. “Let me state clearly, on behalf of the Federal Government: We will fulfil our own part of these historic agreements. We recognise that public confidence will depend on the obligations we honour after this ceremony,” he said. In a move aimed at preventing future disputes over the implementation of agreements, the minister announced the expansion of the existing Implementation and Monitoring Committee, IMC, established for the agreement with the Academic Staff Union of Universities, ASUU. Under the new arrangement, the committee will become a single monitoring platform for agreements with academic and non-academic staff unions across tertiary institutions. Its membership will be broadened to accommodate the relevant unions and stakeholders, with responsibility for tracking agreed milestones, assessing progress, resolving implementation challenges and ensuring accountability through periodic reports. According to Alausa, the committee will monitor both achievements and outstanding obligations to ensure that commitments are implemented within agreed timelines. He said the government intended to identify implementation difficulties early and resolve them before they degenerated into disputes capable of disrupting academic activities. The minister urged government agencies to discharge their responsibilities diligently, while governing councils and institutional managements were directed to maintain accurate records, comply with implementation guidelines and cooperate fully with the committee. He also urged union leaders to keep their members informed and channel emerging concerns through established mechanisms. Alausa recalled that agreements between successive governments and staff unions had, for decades, been undermined by delayed, incomplete or unfulfilled commitments, leading to recurring industrial disputes. The consequences, he said, extended beyond the negotiating parties, with students losing valuable learning time, families bearing additional financial burdens and teaching and research suffering repeated setbacks. He noted that prolonged strikes had created uncertainty around academic calendars, making it difficult for students to complete their programmes within the prescribed periods. The minister said the Tinubu administration was determined to reverse the trend by building a system in which agreements were respected and academic activities proceeded without unnecessary interruptions. He maintained that industrial harmony was indispensable to educational excellence, adding that stable academic calendars would enable institutions to plan effectively, sustain research and allow students to concentrate on their studies. “We must strengthen early consultation and resolve differences through constructive dialogue, mutual respect and good-faith engagement. Our students and their families must remain at the centre of these efforts,” he said. Explaining the significance of the agreements, Alausa said CATA and CONTTA were designed to support the professional and operational needs of eligible academic and non-academic personnel. He said the allowances reflected the government’s recognition that the quality of tertiary education was inseparable from the welfare, motivation and professional wellbeing of the workforce. According to him, improved staff welfare must go beyond financial allowances to include fair treatment, transparent promotion processes, occupational safety and opportunities for career advancement. He pledged that the Federal Ministry of Education would continue to work with relevant agencies, governing councils, institutional managements and unions to create an environment in which personnel could perform their duties effectively. The minister also commended the leadership of ASUP, COEASU and the non-teaching staff unions for their participation in the negotiations, while acknowledging the contributions of relevant ministries, departments, agencies and technical teams. Alausa reserved special commendation for the Federal Government Tertiary Institutions Expanded Negotiation Committee, chaired by Malam Yayale Ahmed, whose work he said had brought the negotiations to a successful conclusion. He praised Ahmed and members of the committee for their patience, experience and dedication in resolving the issues involved in the negotiations. The minister also credited President Tinubu’s support and guidance for making the agreements possible, describing them as evidence of the administration’s commitment to the welfare of education workers and the future of Nigerian students. Signed agreements were presented to representatives of academic and non-academic staff unions, including ASUP, COEASU, the Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities, SSANU, the Non-Academic Staff Union of Educational and Associated Institutions, NASU, the National Association of Academic Technologists, NAAT, and other unions representing staff in polytechnics and colleges of education. The ultimate test of the agreements, however, will be whether the allowances are implemented as stipulated and the monitoring mechanism can prevent outstanding obligations from triggering another round of industrial disputes. To prevent future disputes from escalating into industrial action, the Minister announced plans to expand the existing implementation and monitoring committee established for ASUU into a single body responsible for monitoring all agreements with academic and non-academic staff unions in tertiary institutions. He said the committee’s membership had been broadened to accommodate the unions and other relevant stakeholders, adding that the government would also work towards making it a permanent structure. According to him, the decision followed the success of having a single committee negotiate with the various unions, which helped accelerate the renegotiation process. He said the expanded panel would provide a platform for identifying implementation challenges early and resolving grievances before they disrupt academic activities. He urged union leaders to channel complaints through the committee rather than resorting to public confrontations or threats of strikes. Alausa added that the agreements contained a provision for review every three years, allowing the government and unions to reopen discussions on emerging concerns and mutually agreed adjustments. In his remarks, Ahmed who served as Permanent Secretary in the Federal Ministry of Education between 1997 and 2000, said the success of the negotiations depended on a spirit of give-and-take between the government and labour unions. According to him, union leaders demonstrated responsibility by defending their members’ interests while also appreciating the financial and administrative constraints facing the government. The elder statesman, however, stressed that unveiling the agreement was only the beginning, insisting that its successful implementation would be the real test of the negotiations. “To me, this is the beginning of our job. The most important thing is for us to have a seamless agreement collectively, which the government is not only willing but comfortable to implement to the letter,” he said. He expressed confidence in the commitment of Dr Alausa and the Minister of State for Education, Prof. Suwaiba Ahmad, to ensure that the pact was implemented, while commending President Tinubu for what he described as the political will to address longstanding challenges in the education sector. The negotiation chairman also disclosed that discrepancies had been identified in parts of the agreement, assuring the unions that the issues would be addressed in collaboration with the Ministry of Education and the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission. Earlier in their separate remarks, the National President, Academic Staff Union of Polytechnics, ASUP, Comrade Shammah Kpanja; his counterpart at the Colleges of Education Academic Staff Union, COEASU, Dr. Lawal Bazza; and the President of the Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities, SSANU, Comrade Ibrahim Mohammed, commended the Federal Government for the speedy renegotiation of the agreement and the progress made in its implementation. Kpanja described the process as the fastest in the history of the union’s negotiations, noting that talks began in December 2025 and culminated in the signing of the agreement in April 2026. He disclosed that implementation had commenced, with members receiving outstanding arrears between July and September, but urged the government to ensure that all other provisions of the agreement were fully implemented. He also welcomed the planned inauguration of a joint implementation committee, expressing hope that it would accelerate implementation before the end of the year. Similarly, Bazza said the Colleges of Education subsector had already achieved more than 70 per cent implementation of the agreement, expressing confidence that the committee would help address the outstanding provisions. title: Zelenskyy announces 'good decisions' in support of Ukraine this week
body:
President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy has announced "good decisions" in support of Ukraine this week, in particular following negotiations with the European Union, Denmark, Lithuania, and the United Kingdom.
"There will be good decisions in support of Ukraine this week – we are preparing them now. I continue to be in contact with all our partners who can help us and who are always effective. And I will speak with Denmark today, I will speak with Lithuania – with the prime ministers. Tomorrow – important negotiations in Britain," he said in an evening address on Tuesday published on his Telegram channel.
According to the president, negotiations with the European Union are also scheduled for this week. "There will be support packages for Ukraine, and we are also moving forward in negotiations on accession to the European Union," Zelenskyy said.
"This week marks the opening of two clusters. Two were already opened in the summer, and by the end of the year we must open all six negotiation clusters. This is our plan. And this is a priority. This is political and moral support for our people, this is proof of the irreversibility of Ukraine's course – to be a normal, strong, European country. We are also working to ensure full financial support for Ukraine and Ukrainians, and to fulfill our agreements with Europe," Zelenskyy said.
Zelenskyy also expressed gratitude to Ukrainian parliamentarians and government officials: "This week there are necessary decisions – necessary laws, necessary government decisions."

title: Oman Air launches winter schedule with new codeshare destinations
body:
Oman Air’s Winter 2026/27 schedule begins this month with the introduction of additional frequencies and increased capacity across its global network. Commencing October 25, 2026, the winter programme includes significant expansion across the GCC, Europe, Russia and Far-East, as well as an expanding portfolio of codeshare partnerships. Europe features prominently in Oman Air's winter schedule. Capacity to Zurich will triple compared to the summer season, supported by the deployment of widebody aircraft on up to five weekly services. Frequencies to Paris, Frankfurt, Munich, Milan and Istanbul will also increase to as many as five flights per week, while Moscow will grow from four weekly services during summer to up to eight flights per week throughout the winter schedule. Combined with Oman Air's 11-city European network, the expanded schedule offers guests greater flexibility and connectivity to some of the continent's most sought-after winter destinations, while creating more opportunities to attract visitors to Oman. The season also marks the first full winter programme for several destinations introduced earlier this year as part of the airline's network expansion strategy. Services to Singapore will operate four times weekly, while Tashkent will continue with twice-weekly flights and Sochi with a weekly service, providing guests with an even broader range of travel options across Asia and beyond. To meet strong demand on high-performing routes, Oman Air will also introduce select widebody services on flights to Mumbai and Dhaka once per week, increasing capacity and offering guests the enhanced comfort of the airline's B787 fleet. Continuing to prioritise domestic connectivity, the airline will increase its services between Muscat and Khasab to up to four weekly flights, while flights between Muscat and Salalah will operate up to five times daily throughout the winter season. Oman Air’s winter schedule is further complemented by a growing codeshare network. Through expanded agreements with Lufthansa and SWISS, guests can connect via Frankfurt to Edinburgh, Wrocław, Poznań, Gdańsk, Bergen, Billund; via Munich to Edinburgh and Wrocław; and Zurich to Gothenburg and Oslo. A milestone expansion of the airline's existing codeshare partnership with Malaysia Airlines has also opened up new travel opportunities across Greater China with the addition of Shanghai, Beijing Daxing and Guangzhou. Members of both airlines' loyalty programmes will also benefit from seamless oneworld recognition, enjoying tier privileges and service benefits throughout their journey.

title: It’s ‘incomprehensible’ that Instagram allowed an AI image of Mia Goth to spread, say her reps

A viral photo purporting to show Mia Goth in a T-shirt seemingly referencing her divorce spread from Instagram across the web. It was AI.﻿

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.
Earlier this month, news broke that actress Mia Goth had filed for divorce from actor and filmmaker Shia LaBeouf. An Instagram post from the account miagoth_ — marked with a blue verified checkmark — quickly spread.
The post shows Goth in a T-shirt that reads “MY EX IS MY BIGGEST FAN” in bold black letters. The Beyoncé song “Single Ladies (Put a Ring on It)” had been added to the Instagram post. Hundreds of thousands of people — including some in the entertainment industry — liked the image, and entertainment outlets like OK! and even People wrote about it as if it were authentic. Soon, screenshots of the post were shared widely on other social media platforms .
But the image, Goth’s representatives say, was AI-generated, posted by an account they had asked Instagram to remove.
“Mia Goth does not have ownership of, nor does she engage in social media on any platform. We have filed multiple complaints with Instagram to remove the verified fan account which continues to post counterfeit, AI images of Mia Goth,” Christine Tripicchio, a representative for Goth, told The Verge in an email. “The fact that this fan account meets Instagram’s criteria to qualify for a ‘blue check’ is disconcerting on a fundamental level. Beyond that, it is incomprehensible that Instagram evidently prioritizes the dissemination of forged and manipulated images over the protection and integrity of a public figure’s likeness.”
The miagoth_ account was labeled as fan-run, but the blue checkmark — which for years signaled an official, authentic entity — likely caused confusion for many in and out of the industry (the page had over a million followers). Meta began selling blue checkmarks several years ago as part of a new program, allowing accounts like the fan page to secure “verified” badges even if they weren’t run by the person being depicted in content.
Meta spokesperson Alex Dziedzan told The Verge the miagoth_ account was removed for impersonating a public figure.
Rather than ban AI-generated content of real people, Meta has taken the approach of labeling some content created with generative AI. Photorealistic AI videos of people, for example, may require an AI label — but Meta’s own rules include a carve-out that the label is not required for still images. AI-generated content featuring real people, including public figures, regularly racks up millions of views on Instagram, and Meta executives have signaled that AI-generated content will be a key part of how users engage on the company’s platforms going forward.
Entertainers including musicians and actors have for years raised concerns about their likenesses being used to generate AI content. In 2024, Scarlett Johansson said that OpenAI had used a soundalike for the voice of ChatGPT even after she declined to work with the company on the project. That same year, Taylor Swift endorsed Kamala Harris for president, saying AI-generated images of her posted by Donald Trump made her realize she needed to “combat misinformation” around who she would be voting for.
Update, October 13th: Added response from Meta.
Correction, October 13th: Clarified in headline that the statement came from Goth’s representatives.

title: Republic Bank JoyNews Habitat Fair to connect prospective homeowners with exhibitors in Ho from October 16 to 18
body: Financial constraints and difficulties saving enough money remain major obstacles for some prospective homeowners, as the Republic Bank JoyNews Habitat Fair prepares to open in Ho from October 16 to 18, 2026. The three-day event, scheduled for the Ho Sports Stadium, will connect prospective homeowners with exhibitors and give participants the opportunity to explore options related to construction, interior decoration, furniture, home security, and other aspects of home improvement. For Cecilia Asare, who currently lives with her parents, the cost of living independently remains a major concern. She said moving out without sufficient financial resources could leave her struggling to meet her basic needs. “Hmm, first, money. Second, if I leave my parents’ house, I’ll go hungry,” she said. Despite the financial challenges, Cecilia hopes to gain ideas from the fair on how to create a comfortable home that reflects her needs and personality. She said she would prefer interior designs and furniture that express who she is. “When it comes to the design, I’ll go for something that really talks about my personality. The moment it comes to my home, it should show you that this is who I am without talking so much,” she said. Another prospective homeowner, Michael Akomeah, identified saving towards a home as a challenge because of his existing investment commitments. “I’m doing some investment. That’s why,” he said, explaining why he had found it difficult to save towards homeownership. He welcomed the opportunity to participate in the fair, which is intended to help prospective homeowners explore products and services that could support their plans. The Republic Bank JoyNews Habitat Fair aims to bring prospective homeowners closer to their homeownership goals by connecting them with businesses and service providers across the housing industry. The event will run from October 16 to 18, 2026, at the Ho Sports Stadium, with activities scheduled from 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. daily. Participants will have the opportunity to explore options in construction, interior decoration, furniture, home security and other home-related services. The fair is expected to provide a platform for prospective homeowners to discover available products and services as they work towards turning their homeownership aspirations into reality.

title: Ukraine advances EU membership bid with 4 of 6 integration to-do lists unlocked
body:
Editor's note: this article was updated with comments made at a press conference following the opening of the two enlargement clusters.
LUXEMBOURG — Ukraine celebrated the opening of two more EU enlargement clusters at a ceremony in Luxembourg on Oct. 13, a key milestone in the process to eventually become a member state.
Ukraine and Moldova have been advancing their EU membership bids in tandem and are currently trying to open all six of the bloc's enlargement clusters — to-do lists of reforms that must be completed to join the bloc.
"We welcome the continued momentum on Ukraine's candidacy, now the majority of clusters are open, following a prolonged period without movement," said Thomas Byrne, Ireland's Europe Minister, who is chairing enlargement discussions until the end of 2026
On Oct. 13, Ukraine and Moldova unlocked clusters 2 and 3, titled "internal market" and "competitiveness" respectively. They are the two largest clusters by number of policy files.
"Behind these technical names will be real benefits for Ukrainians," said the EU's Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos .
Among the benefits Kos mentioned: more support for businesses, better working conditions, better consumer protection, and more investments and jobs.
"Ukraine is fully committed to the reforms required for membership and intends to move through this work as quickly as possible," said Deputy Prime Minister for European Integration Vsevolod Chentsov.
The move was made possible the day after the Verkhovna Rada, Ukraine's parliament, passed a law bolstering the rights of the country's Hungarian-speaking minority — a demand that Hungary had said must be fulfilled before it would allow further progress.
In June, Kyiv and Chisinau opened the first cluster , on the rule of law, followed by another on external relations in July.
That leaves only two clusters remaining to be opened, which the European Commission and the Irish Council Presidency of the EU hope to be done with by the end of 2026.
The two remaining clusters risk being harder to get through, as they encompass sectors of the economy such as agriculture and transport, where Ukraine has a competitive edge, and some EU countries fear losing out.
However, two potential opponents, France and Poland, reiterated their support on Oct. 13 for opening all six clusters.
On Oct. 6, the European Commission issued a set of proposals on the future of EU enlargement , which also suggested that Ukraine's agricultural sector would require special treatment, to be handled during the enlargement process rather than used as a block on progress.
Kos told the Kyiv Independent ahead of the opening of the clusters that "once Ukraine will be so far that we will think of what will go in the accession treaty, we will put down the solutions for both sides."
Kos was clear that the process needs to both protect European farmers and help Ukraine export to feed the world, all while Kyiv adopts EU standards.
But Kos' mention of the accession treaty, which is only being drafted near the very end of the EU enlargement process, indicates that she does not expect the strength of Ukraine's agricultural sector to be used as a reason to block progress at this stage.

title: Akpabio insists on jail term for suicide attempt; bill scales second reading
body: By Henry Umoru Moves by the Senate to establish a framework for suicide prevention, decriminalise attempted suicide and provide for the establishment of persons who attempt suicide got a boost as the bill to this effect scaled second reading in the Senate. The bill scaled second despite the position of the President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio, who insisted that the act should remain punishable by imprisonment. Akpabio argued that removing the penalties could encourage the act, arguing thus, “If you attempt suicide, make sure you die. Anyone who attempts and fails will go to jail.” Akpabio added that the issue involves both the Criminal Code and the Penal Code, requiring input from State Houses of Assembly during a public hearing to avoid legal conflicts. The proposed bill seeks to remove the conflict between existing criminal laws that punish attempted suicide and the National Mental Health Act, which recognises the need for medical intervention in mental health emergencies, just as it seeks to address what he described as a contradiction in Nigeria’s laws. It is titled A Bill to establish framework for Suicide Prevention, decriminalise attempted suicide and provide for the establishment of persons who attempt suicide, and for related Matters 2006(SB.730) it was sponsored by Senator Ekpenyong Asuquo, APC, Cross River South. The bill was on Tuesday referred to the Senate Committee on Health ( Secondary and Tertiary) and Committee on Judiciary, Human Rights and Legal Matters for further legislative action. In his lead debate on the general principles of the bill, Senator Asuquo explained that the proposed amendment would establish a legal framework for suicide prevention, treatment and support for people who survive suicide attempts, and that the central question before the Senate was whether the state should punish or protect a person who survives an attempt to take their own life. Ekpenyong argued that while the National Mental Health Act recognises attempted suicide as a psychiatric emergency requiring treatment, Section 327 of the Criminal Code and Section 231 of the Penal Code still criminalise the act. He said the proposed legislation would replace punitive responses with appropriate medical assessment, treatment and continuing support for survivors. “The police station or correctional facility should not be the default destination for a person who requires urgent clinical care,” Ekpenyong said. “At the heart of this bill is a simple question. When a Nigerian survives a suicide attempt, should the first response of the state be persecution or protection?” he asked. Ekpenyong, who noted that while the National Mental Health Act recognised attempted suicide as a psychiatric emergency requiring immediate intervention, Section 327 of the Criminal Code and Section 231 of the Penal Code continued to expose survivors to criminal punishment, said, “Our law presently speaks with two voices,” arguing that the contradiction needed to be resolved to ensure that people experiencing mental health crises received appropriate care. He however warned that criminalising attempted suicide could discourage people from seeking help, encourage families to conceal incidents and prevent health workers from reporting cases promptly, adding that treating suicide attempts as criminal offences could also deepen the stigma surrounding mental health conditions and undermine efforts to gather reliable data for national suicide prevention programmes. Ekpenyong, who further explained that the bill would provide for coordinated suicide prevention services, crisis response mechanisms, referral pathways and support for people who survive suicide attempts, said it would also promote public education and training for health workers, teachers, law enforcement personnel and emergency responders to enable them to recognise warning signs and connect people at risk with appropriate services. According to him, decriminalisation alone would not be sufficient without accessible medical and psychological care, calling for institutional arrangements and funding to support the implementation of suicide prevention policies, just as he urged his colleagues to support the bill, saying Nigeria needed a system that recognised distress and responded before a crisis became irreversible. Supporting the proposal, lawmakers argued that survivors of suicide attempts should receive medical and psychological care rather than face criminal prosecution. In his contribution, Senator Dayo Faduyile, APC, Ondo South, who cited his experience practising medicine, said attempted suicide should be approached as a medical emergency rather than a criminal offence, and argued that depression and other mental health conditions could impair a person’s judgement, making it necessary to prioritise treatment and recovery. The senator, who noted that some people who survived suicide attempts had subsequently taken their lives while in detention, warned that imprisonment or police custody could not adequately address the underlying medical condition, adding, “The best way to treat anybody who did not succumb to a suicide attempt is actually not to criminalise it. They need help.” According to him, placing people experiencing such crises in police stations or correctional facilities would not resolve their problems, insisting that they required proper medical attention. Also in his contribution, Senator Abdul Ningi, Bauchi Central, who hailed Ekpenyong for bringing the issue before the Senate, describing it as an important legal and public health debate that had not received sufficient attention, said the second reading would allow the proposal to proceed for further scrutiny, public consultation and contributions from professionals and other stakeholders. According to him, the circumstances surrounding suicide attempts required a broader understanding of mental health and the social pressures confronting individuals, adding that the proposed legislation would provide an opportunity for psychologists, medical practitioners and other experts to contribute to the development of a more effective national response. Ningi said people responded differently to life’s difficulties and that those who could not cope with particular circumstances should not automatically be treated as criminals. In his contribution, the Senate Leader, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele, APC, Ekiti Central, however, cautioned that some provisions of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act were not automatically applicable across all states, depending on the legal framework adopted by their respective Houses of Assembly. According to him, the Senate needed to establish the extent to which the proposed amendment would apply nationally before proceeding with the legislation. The post Akpabio insists on jail term for suicide attempt; bill scales second reading appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Anthropic’s red team ran AI on 15 cheap TV boxes. Then the math got unsettling.
body: For roughly $825, Anthropic’s Frontier Red Team built a cluster of 15 off-brand Android TV boxes that runs an AI model at 0.39 tokens per second, painfully slow for a chatbot but fine for software with nowhere to be and nobody waiting on it. That experiment anchors new research from Anthropic researchers William Zhou and Daniel Freeman , published Monday, suggesting small open-weight models may be only months away from copying themselves across cheap, internet-connected hardware without relying on a datacenter. The researchers haven’t built an AI worm that can spread across the public internet on its own, and their experiments took place inside controlled environments with shortcuts that made replication easier. But the results suggest several of the remaining technical barriers may be temporary. The researchers haven’t built an AI worm that can spread across the public internet on its own, and their experiments took place inside controlled environments with shortcuts that made replication easier. Inference is the real hurdle Zhou and Freeman identify four steps an AI needs to take to replicate itself, which are finding a target, gaining access, getting inference running, and moving on to the next machine. Previous benchmarks such as CyberGym and ExploitBench suggest smaller models can already handle some of the exploitation work, and frontier agents escaped their test sandboxes using basic exploits earlier this year. The bigger challenge may be getting a model running on unfamiliar hardware, where it has to sort out whatever operating system, dependencies, and installation problems it runs into. In Anthropic’s tests, Qwen3.5-9B deployed a working Llama3.1-8B inference server on eight of nine hardware types, including Jetson Nanos, Macs, and RTX 4090 machines, while the larger GLM-5.2 handled the same work more reliably and with higher throughput. The team then built a firewalled Google Cloud environment with eight nodes running Android emulators, and starting from a single worm instance, the system had to reach the other nodes and establish a working inference server on each one. A fresh copy of the worm was spawned whenever a node’s server passed correctness and anti-cheating checks, and GLM-5.2 reached all eight nodes in four of five trials and seven nodes in the fifth. GLM-5.2 ran on a separate inference server because the target machines couldn’t hold it, so the worm installed a smaller 8B model in its place, and the researchers made exploitation easy by leaving an unauthenticated Android Debug Bridge port open. A fresh copy of the worm was spawned whenever a node’s server passed correctness and anti-cheating checks, and GLM-5.2 reached all eight nodes in four of five trials and seven nodes in the fifth. Worms that take notes The agents got better at setting up inference on unfamiliar hardware when they could read notes left by earlier attempts. The researchers ran Qwen3.5-9B through 20 separate lineages, each lasting six generations, and success climbed from 45% in the first generation to between 61% and 84% in later ones. The researchers call this Lamarckian inheritance, where one agent passes what it learned to the next without any retraining of the model. It’s a mechanism familiar to developers using persistent agent runtimes such as OpenClaw and Hermes Agent , but here that memory helps successive copies work through installation failures on hardware they’ve never seen. The researchers call this Lamarckian inheritance, where one agent passes what it learned to the next without any retraining of the model The team also tried giving Qwen3.5-9B access to the much more capable Opus 4.8 model for advice, and it produced no statistically significant improvement because the small model tended not to know the right questions to ask. The end-of-2026 trend line The paper identifies two constraints that have kept this scenario theoretical. A model needs to be capable enough to replicate reliably and small enough to run on compromised hardware, and right now those requirements don’t overlap. GLM-5.2 showed the necessary competence in the simplified test but is too large for the cheap devices the researchers have in mind, while smaller models can fit on those devices, particularly when inference is distributed across several machines, but can’t yet complete the entire process consistently. Using the Epoch Capabilities Index , the researchers tracked open-weight models with 30 billion parameters or fewer and found that, by the end of 2026, the trend line puts the strongest of them at GLM-5.2’s general capability level. It’s a rough estimate, since general capability scores don’t necessarily predict replication performance, and the team’s end-to-end experiment used favorable conditions. By the researchers’ calculations, typical 4GB TV boxes running 4-bit weights can host a 9B model across four or more devices, and a 26B model across ten or more, which is how their own 15-box cluster runs Gemma4-26B-A4B. A single inference setup on this class of hardware could take roughly 28 to 150 hours depending on the model, and the researchers argue that lightweight agents may be far more willing than human attackers to grind through that kind of effort across huge numbers of devices. They compare the possibility to a digital slime mold, spreading slowly through whatever resources it can reach. Cheap boxes, borrowed compute The Kimwolf botnet infected more than two million devices, most of them cheap Android TV boxes, and the researchers used that figure to calculate what an AI replicator could do with a network of equivalent size. Dividing those devices into clusters of 15 running Gemma4-26B-A4B would yield roughly 133,000 copies of the model generating a combined 80,000 tokens per second. That’s equivalent to no more than about 40 Nvidia H100 GPUs, which is modest by datacenter standards, but the hardware and operating costs would belong to someone else. The researchers also examined edge accelerators such as Nvidia Jetsons, which are used in everything from security cameras and conference room equipment to robots and drones. Those devices are generally harder to reach because they communicate through outbound cloud-management connections. Stopping software that copies itself The researchers aren’t suggesting there’s no way to stop a self-replicating AI worm, and some of its traits could make it easier to detect. Moving multi-gigabyte models between devices creates network traffic that ISPs can monitor, and a worm that spreads aggressively won’t go unnoticed. During the Mirai botnet cleanup, one ISP’s quarantine of infected subscribers cleared 92% of infections within 14 days , and the researchers expect a similar approach to work as a first line of defense. Eliminating a replicator completely, however, would mean coordinating every ISP with infected customers. The post Anthropic’s red team ran AI on 15 cheap TV boxes. Then the math got unsettling. appeared first on The New Stack .

title: The Ore Wars: an interactive history 2002–2026
body: In 2002 iron ore sold for about $13 a tonne under a contract hammered out once a year behind closed doors between Brazilian and Australian miners and Japanese steelmakers. Today it is the second most traded commodity after crude oil, priced daily on futures exchanges in Singapore and Dalian, and the commodity behind some of the fattest profits mining has ever seen. The Ore Wars , MINING.COM’s new interactive timeline, tells that story in 49 moments across seven acts, each pinned to a running price line that starts at $13, crashes to $37 in December 2015, hits a record $237.57 in May 2021 and closes this month near $91. Seven acts The Benchmark Years (2002–2008): secret annual talks, a 71.5% price shock and BHP’s abandoned $140 billion bid for Rio Tinto. Prompt Delivery (2009–2011): the benchmark dies, Stern Hu is arrested and iron ore mints the fattest margins mining has ever seen. Iron ageing (2012–2014): the majors flood the market and the $120 floor gives way. The Long Winter (2015–2016): the Samarco disaster, $4,000-a-day capesizes and $37 a tonne. Taking Inventory (2016–2018): a futures feeding frenzy, a scrap over scrap and record portside piles. Disaster & Disruption (2019–2021): Brumadinho, Juukan Gorge, a pandemic and the highest price ever paid. The Sequel (2022–2026): China’s single buyer, a yuan-priced crack in the dollar system and Simandou at long last. Explore The Ore Wars interactive timeline →

title: Parking prices are set to rise 400% to 500% at Penticton airport
body:
Parking at Penticton Regional Airport is about to get significantly more expensive, with rates set to increase between 400 and 500 per cent starting November 1.
The changes are substantial across the board, with every parking category seeing a steep increase, as the comparison below shows.
“Everyone wants to get on the bandwagon to get more money,” says Donna, a Penticton resident frustrated by the rising costs.
Transport Canada, which owns and operates the airport, says the increases are necessary because existing fees no longer reflect market rates.
In a federal regulatory notice published in the Canada Gazette, the department says the rules governing parking fees were last updated in 2012. It says operating costs at its five federally owned airports are growing and the airports are running at a deficit.
Penticton is one of five airports affected by the federal initiative. The others are Port Hardy and Sandspit in B.C., Sept-Îles in Quebec, and Wabush in Labrador. While Penticton’s new rates have been announced, it is not yet clear how much parking fees will change at the other four airports.
Some travellers acknowledge that Penticton’s parking rates may have been low, particularly compared with larger airports. One traveller says some locals have even used the airport lot for long-term parking without flying, taking advantage of rates that were cheaper than some paid parking lots around town.
But while there may be room for an increase, an employee who works at the airport says the size of the jump goes too far.
“I think they have made a big mistake,” the airport employee says. “I don’t mind them putting it up a little because it was pretty cheap, but they put it up to its equal to Kelowna.”
Most of the parking at the Penticton airport is unpaved and does not have the same infrastructure, such as lighting, that larger airports have.
For many Penticton residents, the parking increases come as everyday expenses continue to climb, from filling up at the gas pump to putting groceries on the table.
Donna says her household has already had to make changes to keep up with the rising cost of living, cutting back on things they used to enjoy.
“We don’t go out for meals as much as we used to,” she says.
And with airport parking rates set to jump by hundreds of per cent, residents like Donna say it’s another expense they’ll have to think twice about, especially when travelling is already costing more.
Travellers will have to decide whether leaving their cars at the airport is still worth the cost.

title: First Lady Melania Trump Launches 2027 Presidential SI Challenge and Establishes First Lady Seal of SI Readiness
body: Office of the First Lady Briefings & Statements Search Select Category All News Briefings & Statements All Presidential Actions Executive Orders Nominations & Appointments Presidential Memoranda Proclamations Fact Sheets Releases Remarks Research All Briefings & Statements Presidential Actions All Executive Orders Nominations & Appointments Presidential Memoranda Proclamations Fact Sheets Releases Remarks Research First Lady Melania Trump launched her 2027 Presidential Super Intelligence (SI) Challenge and established a new First Lady Seal of AI Readiness—inviting K-12 students, educators, and schools across America to participate in the nationwide initiative. “America’s next groundbreaking idea is already sitting in a classroom,” said Mrs. Trump. “We must give our children the knowledge, tools, and opportunities to bring those ideas to life.” Following the success of the inaugural Challenge earlier this year, which engaged more than 20,000 students from all 50 states and U.S. schools around the world, the 2027 Presidential SI Challenge will continue to give students the opportunity to use SI to dream, build, and develop solutions to real-world challenges. “America’s future security, prosperity, and global leadership depend on our next generation. Building on last year’s success, the 2027 Presidential Super Intelligence Challenge will empower our children to lead the world,” said First Lady Melania Trump. New this year, all participating schools will have the opportunity to earn the First Lady Seal of SI Readiness by completing and submitting evidence of a rigorous set of milestones focused on SI readiness. The Seal recognizes schools that are taking meaningful steps to prepare students and educators to understand, use, and responsibly engage with super intelligence. The Presidential SI Challenge will continue its project-based competition, encouraging students to explore super intelligence through creative and innovative projects that address challenges in their schools, communities, and beyond. To watch First Lady Melania Trump’s launch video, to learn more, and to sign up for the Challenge, please visit SI.Gov . title: Fire Forces Crew to Abandon Research Vessel Off Louisiana
body:
Essential news coupled with the finest maritime content sourced from across the globe.
A U.S. Coast Guard Air Station New Orleans helicopter aircrew lowers a rescue swimmer to assist mariners aboard a life raft 100 miles south of Grand Isle, Louisiana, Oct. 12, 2026. U.S. Coast Guard image
A fire aboard a seismic research vessel in the Gulf of Mexico forced dozens of crew members to abandon ship Monday, with nearby offshore supply vessels helping bring the evacuees safely ashore.
The Cyprus-flagged Rem Andes was operating approximately 100 nautical miles south of Grand Isle, Louisiana, when the fire broke out on October 12, according to the U.S. Coast Guard.
A Coast Guard C-27 Spartan aircraft from Air Station Clearwater intercepted the vessel’s mayday call and diverted to assist. Crew members who had evacuated into life rafts were picked up by responding offshore supply vessels and transported to Port Fourchon, Louisiana.
Local reports indicated that 46 people were aboard the vessel, including 38 who evacuated into life rafts and eight who remained aboard to fight the fire and assess the damage. The Coast Guard had initially reported 42 people aboard. No injuries were reported.
The fire was subsequently extinguished, and the vessel was coordinating commercial salvage operations, the Coast Guard said.
The rescue response also involved an HC-144 Ocean Sentry aircraft from Coast Guard Aviation Training Center Mobile and an MH-60 Jayhawk helicopter from Air Station New Orleans.
The 88-meter Rem Andes, built in 2012, is operated by Norway-based Rem Offshore and is equipped for offshore seismic surveys and geophysical data collection in support of energy exploration activities.
The cause of the fire and the extent of the vessel’s damage have not been disclosed.
