title: Leonardo DRS launches cxMHR radar for air and missile defense, begins production
body: The C-Band Extended Multi-Mission Hemispheric Radar is a fully digital, software-defined system that uses active electronically scanned array technology. Four radar panels provide continuous 360-degree hemispheric coverage. The system is designed to detect, track and identify multiple aerial threats simultaneously. These include tactical ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, rockets and uncrewed aircraft. Leonardo DRS reports detection ranges exceeding 90 kilometers against drones and loitering munitions. Its stated detection range against transport aircraft exceeds 330 kilometers. The radar panels, Identification Friend or Foe equipment, command-and-control functions and supporting equipment are integrated into one ISO-containerized system. The package can be transported by air, land or sea and deployed on a single vehicle. Leonardo DRS lists expeditionary and fixed-site air defense among its applications. Other roles include force protection, tactical surveillance and engagement support. “The cxMHR gives our customers a deployable, single-vehicle capability that delivers persistent 360-degree surveillance, long-range detection, and fire-control-quality tracking against today’s most challenging air threats,” said Max Cohen, senior vice president and general manager of Leonardo DRS RADA Technologies. “We are ready to deliver this advanced IAMD capability at the speed and scale required by our customers.” The cxMHR uses AI-enabled tracking and classification to provide fire-control-quality tracks and rapid target updates. Its software-defined architecture is built to Modular Open Systems Approach standards for integration into broader air and missile defense networks. Supported interfaces include FAAD, Medusa, Sapient, Lattice, Asterix, MICAD and RAFT. The announcement did not identify initial customers or disclose production quantities and delivery schedules.

title: GoldBod boosts local jobs as 90% of gold undergoes refining in Ghana – Sammy Gyamfi
body: The Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) is strengthening local value addition in the gold sector, with between 80 and 90 per cent of the gold it purchases and exports now refined in Ghana, its Chief Executive Officer, Sammy Gyamfi, has disclosed. He said the development was helping to create employment opportunities, retain revenue within the domestic economy and support the growth of local industries. Speaking before Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee on Tuesday, October 13, Mr Gyamfi said the shift towards local refining represented a significant departure from previous practices, under which much of the country’s gold was exported without being refined locally. He explained that the increased use of domestic refineries was helping Ghana capture more economic benefits from its mineral resources instead of allowing such opportunities to be realised in foreign destinations. “I’m happy to report to this honourable committee that, as we speak, about 80 to 90 per cent of the gold we purchase and export is refined here locally,” he said. According to him, the refineries operate around the clock and employ Ghanaians, particularly young people, while ensuring that refining fees that would otherwise be paid abroad remain in the country. Mr Gyamfi added that the benefits extended beyond gold refining, as silver recovered during the process was also being retained locally to generate foreign exchange and provide raw materials for Ghana’s fabrication industry. He said the approach was helping to strengthen domestic industrial activity, create jobs and increase the economic returns from the country’s gold resources, while advancing GoldBod’s broader mandate of supporting foreign exchange generation and the regulation of Ghana’s gold trading sector.

title: Lost evidence in 1988 cold case leads to murder charge being withdrawn
body:
All charges in a decades-old murder cold case that were laid two years ago after genetic genealogy testing have been withdrawn in Prince Edward Island, after police said they had lost the majority of the physical evidence.
The P.E.I. Crown Attorney’s Office said Charlottetown Police lost “extensive crucial evidence” from the investigation into Byron Carr’s 1988 death, meaning there is no longer a reasonable likelihood of conviction.
Todd Joseph Gallant, 59, who was also known as Todd Joseph Irving, was charged with first-degree murder and interfering with human remains in 2024.
Gallant had pleaded not guilty to the charges and a jury trial was scheduled for next month.
The Crown Attorney’s Office said in a statement it was informed in August that a “substantial portion of the physical evidence” could not be located.
A review by police confirmed the “overwhelming majority” of the evidence collected as part of the investigation has been lost, the Crown added.
“This is a deeply disappointing outcome for our office and for the Crown Attorneys who have worked diligently over the past several years to bring this matter to trial,” the office said about the charges being withdrawn.
“Most importantly, the Crown Attorneys’ Office recognizes the impact this outcome will have on the family of Byron Carr, who after nearly four decades will be denied the opportunity for closure that a trial may have provided. We extend our sincerest condolences to them.”
In a statement, interim police Chief Darren MacDougall said the force recognizes the seriousness of the concerns identified in the review, and thanked the Crown for its work on the file.
MacDougall said personnel and operational policies have “significantly changed” since 1988.
“And although investigative practices, technology and evidence management procedures have evolved considerably, this does not diminish the seriousness of the identified issues,” he said.
“Our thoughts are with the victim’s family and loved ones, who have waited decades for this matter to be resolved. We recognize how difficult and disappointing this outcome is for them and for our entire community.”
Carr, a former teacher, was 36 years old when he was found strangled and stabbed to death in his bedroom on Nov. 11, 1988.
One of the most chilling details at the crime scene was a note written on a wall in the killer’s apparent handwriting: “I WILL KILL AGAIN.”
The cold case was reopened in 2007, and while there were no new leads at the time, investigators did have DNA evidence. Specifically, underwear that was believed to belong to the killer was found at the scene.
During a news conference in January 2024, then-police Chief Brad MacConnell said the “bigger development” in the case began in 2022 when police started using genetic genealogy.
He went on to say that crime scene exhibits were used to create a DNA profile that was uploaded to family genealogy sites to find common relatives.
“Genetic genealogy is a game-changer for police in how we investigate major crimes,” MacConnell said.
MacConnell said Gallant, who would have been 21 at the time of the murder, had been identified as a suspect much earlier in the investigation.
There were also questions whether the murder was hate-motivated. Investigators have said it was believed Carr was killed after a sexual encounter with another man.
MacConnell said in 2024 that Carr’s death “occurred during a dark and unfortunate time in our province’s history when members of the LGBTQIA2S+ community did not feel welcomed or accepted forcing many, like Byron, to socialize in the shadows and take unnecessary risks.”

title: GTA 6 could come to PC as early as Q1 2027, leak claims
body: Grand Theft Auto VI, or as its friends call it, GTA 6, will be a console-only game when it goes on sale on November 19. But while Rockstar Games has yet to confirm when PC gamers will be able to get in on the action, a new GamesBeat report claims that it will be within the first three months of 2027. With GTA 6 launching on Xbox Series X|S and PS5 in around a month, PC gamers have been left wondering if they should consider picking up the console version — and even buying a whole new console to play it. But GamesBeat reports that might not be necessary, with a Q1 2027 release potentially sooner than a lot of gamers had worried may be the case. Those gamers had plenty of reasons to be worried that a longer wait could be in the cards, too. GTA V was released on consoles around a year and a half before the PC version. Console gamers were able to put the game through its paces in September 2013, with PC owners waiting until April of 2015. While far from official, the news comes from industry sources "familiar with the studio's plans," although they were given anonymity for obvious reasons. It's perhaps no surprise that Rockstar Games is keen to open GTA 6 up to as many potential buyers as possible. It's thought to have cost upwards of $2 billion to create, and making that money back is a lot easier when you add PC gamers to your list of customers. Rockstar Games will also likely want to get its money-making online version of GTA 6 into the hands of players as soon as possible, too. It won't be ready at launch, but is expected to debut in 2027. While GTA games have historically been popular among console gamers, there are reasons to choose the PC version if it's available to you. The console version of GTA 6 is expected to run at just 30 FPS at launch , for example. GTA 6's development hasn't been an easy one. The game itself is thought to be in the hands of "Cyberleek," someone who has already shared clips of the game and has threatened to leak the entire game if their demands are not met. Those demands include their memecoin reaching a $30 million valuation, perhaps hinting at their true motivation.

title: The search for the politically unblemished: Are we asking the impossible of public appointees?
body: The controversy surrounding President John Dramani Mahama’s appointment of Emelia Afi Agbenyo as a Deputy Chairperson of Ghana’s Electoral Commission (EC) raises a question that deserves serious national reflection. How do we determine whether a person appointed to a sensitive public office can be trusted to discharge the responsibilities of that office fairly, independently and without political interference? The question is important because the credibility of our elections depends, in part, on public confidence in those entrusted with managing them. On 12 October 2026, President Mahama swore in Emelia Afi Agbenyo and Dr Joseph Kwaku Asamoah as Deputy Chairpersons of the Electoral Commission, urging them to perform their duties without favour towards any political party, candidate or government. The appointments have prompted renewed political debate about impartiality and the selection of persons for positions of national importance. Source: Ghana News Agency, 12 October 2026. Mindset Transformation Initiative (MTI) believes this debate presents an opportunity to look beyond the immediate political contest and examine a more fundamental issue: Are we placing so much emphasis on finding individuals without perceived political associations that we risk neglecting the stronger safeguards needed to protect our public institutions? The Difficult Search for a Politically Unblemished Person In a politically divided society, the demand for neutral and impartial public officers is understandable. Citizens want judges who dispense justice without political considerations, electoral commissioners who administer elections without favour, and public officials who serve the Republic rather than the interests of the government that appointed them. These are reasonable expectations. However, we must also confront a practical difficulty. In a society where political parties influence public discourse, professional networks, civic participation and national debate, how easy is it to identify a competent individual who has never held a political opinion, associated with a politically active person, supported a public policy or been perceived as sympathetic to one political tradition? The expression politically unblemished can become an elusive standard if it means that an appointee must have no past association, opinion, or circumstance that a political opponent might question. A person may have a political history and still possess the integrity to serve impartially. Another may have no known political affiliation yet lack the courage to resist pressure, the discipline to follow the law or the moral strength to act against the interests of those who appointed them. Political neutrality cannot therefore be established solely by examining a person’s background. It must also be demonstrated through conduct, decisions and a willingness to uphold the law, even when doing so displeases powerful interests. This does not mean that a candidate’s political history should be ignored. Relevant associations, conflicts of interest and evidence of partisan conduct deserve careful scrutiny. It means that such scrutiny should be based on credible evidence and fair standards rather than political suspicion alone. Consistency Matters, but So Does Institutional Integrity MTI recognises the concerns being raised by political parties about consistency in public appointments. Where one party demands strict standards of neutrality while in opposition but applies a different standard when in government, public confidence suffers. Political parties must be prepared to defend the same principles regardless of which party holds power. If a party believes that an electoral commissioner should not have a close and demonstrable relationship with a political organisation, that principle should apply whether the appointment is made by an NDC or NPP administration. If a party argues that appointments to the judiciary must be protected from political influence, it should support the same protections when its political interests are not directly affected. The test of a principle is whether its supporters are prepared to uphold it when doing so is inconvenient. Nevertheless, political consistency alone will not guarantee institutional independence. Even where an appointment process is transparent, and the appointee has an impressive professional record, the institution must still have systems that prevent improper interference and make misconduct difficult to conceal. The central question must therefore extend beyond who has been appointed to include the conditions under which that person will exercise authority. Institutions Must Be Stronger Than the Individuals Who Lead Them Ghana’s Electoral Commission is a constitutional institution with a responsibility that extends beyond the interests of any government or political party. Article 46 of the 1992 Constitution provides that, in performing its functions, the Commission shall not be subject to the control or direction of any person or authority, except as provided by the Constitution or other applicable law. This principle is fundamental. The Commission must serve the Republic and its citizens. Yet constitutional independence must be supported by practical arrangements that protect the electoral process from manipulation, undue pressure, administrative abuse and individual misconduct. No democratic country should have to depend entirely on the personal virtue of the people appointed to administer its elections. Good people can make mistakes. People can face pressure. People can change their positions. Institutions must be designed to withstand these human realities. The same principle applies to the judiciary. We need judges of integrity, but we also need transparent judicial processes, clear rules of professional conduct, independent disciplinary procedures and decisions that can be examined against the law and the evidence. The objective should be to create institutions in which the rules are stronger than personal loyalties, and accountability is more powerful than political influence. What Would Stronger Electoral Safeguards Look Like? MTI proposes that Ghana’s national conversation should give greater attention to the practical safeguards that protect the integrity of elections, irrespective of who occupies the leadership of the Electoral Commission. First, strengthen the transparency of electoral procedures The processes for voter registration, collation, transmission, verification and declaration of results must be governed by clear, publicly available rules. Any changes to those procedures should be properly explained, legally authorised and communicated in good time Second, establish effective independent verification Election results should be supported by verifiable records at each stage of the process. Party agents, accredited observers and other legally authorised stakeholders should have meaningful opportunities to observe procedures, obtain the records they are entitled to receive and raise objections through established channels. Where electronic systems are used, they should be supported by appropriate security controls, independent technical audits and reliable contingency arrangements. Third, strengthen accountability for electoral misconduct There should be clear procedures for investigating credible allegations of interference, falsification, deliberate obstruction or abuse of electoral authority. Investigations must be impartial, timely and subject to the law. Proven misconduct should attract appropriate sanctions, regardless of the rank or political connections of the person involved. Fourth, protect the independence of election officials at every level Electoral integrity cannot rest on the character of the Chairperson and Deputy Chairpersons alone. Regional and district officials, returning officers, collation teams and other personnel must work under professional standards that protect them from improper political pressure. Their duties, reporting lines and disciplinary arrangements should be clearly defined. Fifth, make electoral processes more open to public scrutiny Public confidence grows when citizens can understand how results are produced and how disputes are resolved. Clear documentation, timely publication of legally releasable results, transparent reconciliation procedures and accessible complaint mechanisms can help reduce suspicion and strengthen trust. Sixth, improve the appointment process itself The selection of persons for sensitive constitutional offices should be transparent, merit-based and supported by credible scrutiny of professional competence, integrity, independence and potential conflicts of interest. The public should be able to understand the criteria applied and the reasons candidates are considered suitable. The Constitution Review Committee’s December 2025 recommendations on Electoral Commission appointments provide a useful starting point for examining reforms, including open competitive recruitment, a more structured selection process and parliamentary approval of nominees. These recommendations should be considered on their merits as part of the wider national reform debate. The purpose of these safeguards is straightforward: to make electoral manipulation difficult, detectable and punishable, whoever might attempt it Should We Abandon the Search for Neutrality? MTI does not suggest that impartiality is unimportant or that political history should be irrelevant to public appointments. Nor should we lower the standards expected of people entrusted with sensitive constitutional responsibilities. Rather, we must distinguish between demanding impartial conduct and expecting to find a person whom nobody can accuse of political sympathy. The first is a necessary democratic standard. The second may become an endless political exercise, particularly when rival parties judge the same individual according to their competing interests. Perhaps, therefore, Ghana should reconsider the weight it places on searching for a supposedly politically spotless candidate. We should retain rigorous scrutiny of an appointee’s record, but direct more of our national energy towards building systems that ensure that no appointee can easily compromise the institution they serve. This is particularly important because public appointments are made within a constitutional and political framework. The fact that an officeholder was appointed by a President does not, by itself, establish that the individual will act in the President’s interest. Equally, the absence of a known party affiliation does not automatically establish impartiality. The fair approach is to examine the appointment process, the candidate’s qualifications and record, any credible evidence of conflicts or partisan conduct, and the safeguards that will govern the exercise of the office. In the case of the Electoral Commission, the ultimate test should be whether the electoral system can produce credible, verifiable and legally defensible results, irrespective of the political identity of the people managing it. A Call for a Change in National Mindset As a civic organisation committed to responsibility, integrity, discipline and national development, Mindset Transformation Initiative believes that Ghana’s democratic maturity requires a shift in how we approach these matters. We must move from a political culture that concentrates almost exclusively on the perceived loyalties of individuals to one that demands competence, accountability and institutional resilience. Political parties have a legitimate responsibility to scrutinise appointments. Civil society has a duty to ask difficult questions. The media must investigate and report responsibly. Citizens must insist on transparency. Appointees must understand that public office is a trust held on behalf of the Republic. All these responsibilities are complementary. We must also resist the temptation to pronounce individuals guilty of political bias without credible evidence. Public confidence is not strengthened when allegations are treated as established facts simply because they suit a political argument. Equally, allegations should not be dismissed merely because they concern an appointee of the governing party. The same standards must apply to everyone. A mature democracy should be able to scrutinise an appointment firmly while respecting the appointee’s right to be assessed fairly. It should also be able to demand stronger institutional safeguards without making assumptions about the intentions of any particular officeholder. Conclusion: Let Us Protect the Sanctity of the Vote Mindset Transformation Initiative appreciates the concerns being expressed by political parties about consistency, impartiality and public confidence in appointments to the Electoral Commission. These concerns deserve a fair hearing, and the appointment process must always be open to legitimate scrutiny. However, we believe Ghana must look beyond the search for a person who is perceived to have no political blemish. That search can become subjective, politically selective and difficult to conclude. Perhaps it is time to place less emphasis on the impossible expectation of finding a politically unblemished individual and greater emphasis on creating an electoral system that no individual can easily manipulate. We should insist on qualified, ethical and impartial public officers. At the same time, we must establish safeguards that make interference difficult, ensure that irregularities can be detected, provide effective remedies for disputes and hold offenders accountable under the law. The sanctity of the vote must never depend solely on the goodwill of the person occupying an office. It must be protected by sound laws, transparent procedures, independent verification, professional electoral administration and effective accountability. Whether the Electoral Commission is led by persons appointed under an NDC, NPP or any future administration, the same safeguards must apply. No political party should have to trust the personal goodwill of its opponent to believe that an election has been conducted fairly. Our national objective should be to build an electoral system in which the results reflect the will of the Ghanaian people, where that will can be independently verified, and where no amount of attempted manipulation can overturn the lawful outcome without detection and appropriate remedy. The ultimate safeguard for Ghana’s democracy is not merely the hope that we appoint the right people. It is the determination to build institutions that compel every person, regardless of political affiliation or personal interest, to do what is right under the law. That is the mindset Ghana must cultivate. ******* By Sidney Justin Tehoda

title: Frozen assets, embargoes, entry bans: Ukraine names the pressure it wants the EU to put on Moscow
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Ukraine wants the EU to force Moscow into a ceasefire with frozen Russian assets, trade and transit embargoes, maritime bans, and entry bans, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha wrote on X after the EU Foreign Affairs Council in Luxembourg on 12 October 2026. He also welcomed new EU sanctions listings adopted that day and progress in Ukraine’s EU accession talks. Kyiv has spent this month laying out truce formats it would accept while awaiting Russia’s position on talks, and the levers it is pressing the EU to use include frozen Russian assets that EU leaders failed to agree on tapping last December. The pressure Kyiv wants from the EU Sybiha called it “devastating pressure.” He also wants Russian combatants and their families barred from the EU, maximum visa restrictions, and Russia’s isolation in culture and sports. I was pleased to attend the EU Foreign Affairs Council today. It is time for Europe to define its strong role. Our future and our security are in our hands. Now is the time for real European pressure on Moscow. Not half-measures, but devastating pressure: frozen assets, trade… pic.twitter.com/AnI8h6HXbs — Andrii Sybiha (@andrii_sybiha) October 12, 2026 His post named three types of ceasefire—energy, food security, and a full ceasefire—without saying whether Kyiv would accept them separately. Earlier this month, he told journalists Ukraine was ready for an energy and Black Sea ceasefire “but only in such a combination.” New sanctions listings and two more accession clusters The minister welcomed the EU’s 12 October adoption of new sanctions listings against Russia—the largest single expansion of the bloc’s blacklist. EU ambassadors agreed on the 1,646 names on 7 October. They include 1,569 tied to Russia’s military industry and 77 to its so-called State Duma elections. The listings are separate from the EU’s 22nd sanctions package, which the EU has yet to adopt. He also welcomed the EU’s “green light” for opening two more clusters in Ukraine’s EU accession talks: Internal Market, and Competitiveness and Inclusive Growth. The formal opening was scheduled for an intergovernmental conference on 13 October. Front-line briefing and aid requests Sybiha said he briefed European colleagues on the front-line situation, Russia’s plans, and ways to deprive it of its advantages, and that he passed partners specific requests for aid. He reaffirmed Ukraine’s commitment to reforms. title: Why Home Advantage Matters in Football, Tennis and Basketball
body: Home advantage is one of the most widely accepted beliefs in modern athletics. It is the idea that teams often perform better in front of their fans. However, this does not mean that the home team will always win in reality. Anything can happen in football, tennis, and basketball, and the win can go either way irrespective of how hostile the condition is. Although the general home-field advantage is worth considering, it’s just that it works quite differently for each sport. In team sports like football and basketball, the collective roar of thousands of fans can instantly shift momentum or even influence the referee’s decisions. So, don’t be surprised when the odds change drastically in the blink of an eye when betting on live matches at 1xBet Ghana , to reflect the match’s current momentum. Bettors should pay close attention to the smallest details that can contribute to the match’s outcome. How Home Advantage Works in Sports Home advantage is the belief that athletes and sports teams win more often and perform better at home than when they travel to face an opponent. In team sports, this usually means playing in front of the club’s own supporters. In tennis, it can mean playing in a player’s home country or at a tournament where they are comfortable with the conditions. Below are some factors that contribute to home advantage in sport: Support from home crowds: A roaring stadium has a massive psychological impact on the players. The noise triggers an adrenaline rush, which helps home players fight through exhaustion during the dying minutes. A loud crowd can also make communication harder for the visiting team and add pressure during important moments. Reduced travel demands: Traveling is stressful and can affect sleeping patterns, diets, and overall concentration. Home teams don’t experience these disruptions, giving them an edge. Familiar playing surfaces and conditions: Home teams already understand their own training grounds and stadium layout. This makes it easier for them to easily execute tactics and play to instruction. The demand to impress the fans: The natural instinct to give the fans bragging rights can bring a major mental boost during the game. Players naturally play with more aggression and confidence when playing in front of their fans. Note that home advantage is not all it takes to win a match. A team with poor form can still lose at home. A strong away team can also perform well in hostile conditions. Football vs Tennis vs Basketball: Which Has the Strongest Home Advantage? Home advantage doesn’t work the same way across these three sports. For instance, Chelsea were unbeaten at home for 86 consecutive Premier League games from 2004 to 2008. During that time, they won multiple League titles, domestic cups, and played in several Champions League knockout matches. Moreover, a tennis player may perform better at a certain tennis surface or tournament than another. For example, Rafael Nadal has a 90.5% career win percentage on clay, losing just 51 times and winning 484 games on the surface. Another notable home record win in the NBA is held by San Antonio Spurs in the 2015/16 season. The Spurs did 40-1 at home, and the single loss didn’t happen until game 39 of the home schedule. So, it is difficult to conclude that a particular sport has the strongest home advantage over the other. Fans should instead focus on the entertainment that each sport has to offer. Why Home Advantage Changes from Match to Match Home advantage is only one of the things that can play a part in the outcome of a match. There are other contributing factors to consider. For instance, the quality of the competing teams can play a crucial role in how the game outcome will be. A bottom-tier football or basketball team will rarely beat a championship team simply because they are playing at home. In the same way, a major football match in a famous stadium can create a different environment from a low-profile league game. Therefore, the importance of the game, the health of the roster, and the distance the visitors had to travel can also influence the match. In tournament formats, a massive cross-country road trip can drastically affect a team’s physical freshness compared to short, regular travel. How Home Advantage Can Influence Football, Tennis and Basketball Betting Home advantage is one metric gamblers should consider when forecasting sports betting selections. It is advisable to use home advantage as part of a wider analysis of sports bet , but it should not be treated as a guaranteed way to predict results. In football, the most familiar market is the home win, draw or away win. A team’s home record can make it easier to forecast the possibility of getting any of these three outcomes. For example, a team that performs well at home may have an advantage over an opponent that struggles on the road. However, recent form, injuries, squad quality and the strength of the opposition still need to be considered. A strong home record alone does not mean a home win is the best choice. In basketball, home advantage can be considered in both the moneyline and point spread markets. The moneyline focuses on which team wins the game, while the point spread gives the stronger team a points handicap. A home team may be more likely to win, but the spread can still make the matchup less straightforward if the visiting team is expected to keep the game close. Tennis has its own set of betting options. The match-winner market is the most direct option, while set markets focus on how the match may develop. A player’s home advantage may come from crowd support, knowledge of the court and local playing conditions. But surface form can be more important than simply playing in front of a home crowd. Other Factors to Consider Beyond Home Advantage Home advantage should also be used carefully when analyzing the outcome of a match. A team’s old home record may include different players, coaches and opponents. A tennis player’s results from several years ago may say little about current form. The same applies to basketball teams after major roster changes. The best approach is to treat home advantage as one piece of information, since it doesn’t reveal the full picture. The table below reveals the different factors that can affect football, tennis and basketball performances and results. Factor Football Tennis Basketball Crowd influence High Moderate High Travel demands High Moderate to High High Familiar playing conditions Moderate High High Team communication High Not really High Pressure from home fans High High High Venue familiarity Moderate High High Home Advantage in the Modern Professional Sport Era In modern professional sports, there is growing evidence that the traditional weight of home advantage is gradually shrinking. Professional athletes have better travel arrangements, training facilities and recovery methods than in the past. Teams also use data to prepare for different opponents and playing environments. Players are now more accustomed to international travel. Many compete in different countries throughout the year, so unfamiliar surroundings may not be as difficult as they once were. While the physical gap between hosting and traveling is narrower today than it has ever been in sports history, Supporters still create noise. As such, the emotional spark of a passionate home crowd and the baseline comfort of local conditions will always matter. When Home Advantage Matters Less in Sports Home advantage doesn’t sometimes count in some matches. However, that doesn’t take away the game’s intensity and competitiveness. It’s just that playing at home doesn’t matter as much. Below are some conditions where the home advantage matters less: Neutral venues: When neither side plays in its usual stadium, both teams have to adapt to an unfamiliar environment. The crowd may also be split between the two sides. Low attendance: If there are few supporters, the home team may receive less of the energy normally associated with playing at home. Players’ experience: Elite teams and athletes travel regularly and have professional support staff who help them manage their wellbeing. This can reduce some of the problems associated with playing away from home. Opponent’s strength: A very strong team may be able to control a match despite playing away. In the same way, a weak home side does not automatically become a strong team because it is playing in familiar surroundings. Conclusion The venue in which a match will be played can dictate the atmosphere of the game. As such, home advantage can bring confidence, concentration, energy, and preparation to players. Football teams can benefit from their stadium, supporters and familiarity with the pitch. Basketball teams can use crowd energy and court familiarity to their advantage. Tennis players can gain from local support, familiar surfaces and reduced travel. However, none of these factors guarantees success. The better football team can still win away from home and the better tennis player can also win even when the surface conditions are not favorable. In the end, an outstanding performance will overcome any disadvantage caused by not playing at home. title: Airport: Tinubu writes Senate, seeks approval to reimburse N100bn to Yobe govt
body:
President Bola Tinubu has asked the Senate to approve the reimbursement of N100.5 billion to Yobe State Government for the construction of the Muhammadu Buhari International Cargo Airport in Damaturu, the state capital.
Mr Tinubu’s request was contained in a letter read by Senate President Godswill Akpabio during plenary on Tuesday.
In the letter, the president said the federal government had taken over the ownership and control of the airport, necessitating the reimbursement to the state government through a promissory note.
He said the Federal Executive Council (FEC) had approved the takeover, following which the Bureau of Public Procurement (BPP) reviewed the project and recommended N100,509,017,234.55 as the amount to be reimbursed to the state government.
After reading the letter, Mr Akpabio referred the request to the Senate Committee on Local and Foreign Debts for further scrutiny.
The proposed reimbursement comes against the backdrop of the constitutional provisions governing aviation in Nigeria.
Item 3 of Part I of the Second Schedule to the 1999 Constitution, as amended, places aviation, including airports, aircraft safety and the carriage of passengers and goods by air, on the Exclusive Legislative List. This means the National Assembly has exclusive authority to make laws on these matters, to the exclusion of state Houses of Assembly, subject to the provisions of the Constitution.
Section 4(2) and (3) of the Constitution empower the National Assembly to legislate on matters on the Exclusive Legislative List. The constitutional arrangement provides the basis for federal regulation of aviation and the administration of airports under relevant federal laws.
The Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) Act also empowers the authority to maintain and manage airports transferred to it under the law, as well as other airports provided for under the relevant legislation.
However, the placement of aviation on the Exclusive Legislative List does not, by itself, establish that every airport must be owned by the federal government or automatically entitle a state that constructs an airport to reimbursement.

title: Israeli Missile Protection System Certified for Global 7500
body:
Israeli company BIRD Aerosystems has completed the installation and European Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) certification of its Airborne Missile Protection System (AMPS) with Directional Infrared Countermeasures (DIRCM) on a Bombardier Global 7500 business jet. The certification enables the aircraft to operate with the integrated missile protection system as part of its approved configuration, addressing growing concerns over the proliferation of man-portable air defence systems (MANPADS) and the vulnerability of high-value civilian aircraft. The installation marks another step in the expansion of BIRD Aerosystems’ missile protection technology into the business aviation and VVIP transport markets. While airborne missile protection systems have traditionally been associated primarily with military aircraft and government transports, operators of civilian business jets are increasingly considering such capabilities when flying into regions where shoulder-launched missiles may pose a threat. According to the Israeli manufacturer, the successful certification confirms that the integration of AMPS on the Global 7500 meets applicable European airworthiness requirements. This is particularly significant for business aircraft, where modifications to avionics, electrical systems and the aircraft structure must satisfy stringent certification standards. Detecting and Defeating Infrared-Guided Missiles BIRD Aerosystems’ AMPS is designed to protect aircraft against MANPADS and other infrared-guided missile threats. The system combines missile warning sensors, threat detection and confirmation, tracking and directional infrared countermeasures. When an incoming missile is detected and identified as a threat, the DIRCM subsystem directs infrared countermeasure energy towards the missile’s seeker in order to disrupt its guidance. Unlike conventional expendable countermeasures such as flares, DIRCM systems are intended to interfere directly with the missile’s infrared seeker without relying on the release of pyrotechnic decoys. According to BIRD Aerosystems , the integrated architecture is designed to provide rapid and accurate responses while reducing false alarms to virtually zero. The manufacturer has not disclosed the specific sensor configuration or performance parameters of the installation on the Global 7500. The system is also designed to be adaptable to different aircraft types and operational requirements. BIRD Aerosystems provides services covering the entire programme lifecycle, including system design, integration, certification, installation and operational support. EASA Certification for the Global 7500 The Bombardier Global 7500 is a long-range business aircraft used for executive and VIP transport. Its combination of range, cabin capacity and operating flexibility makes it suitable for missions requiring long-distance travel without intermediate stops. The integration of an airborne missile protection system on such an aircraft involves more than mounting sensors and countermeasure equipment. The installation must also be compatible with the aircraft’s existing systems and comply with applicable airworthiness and safety requirements. The EASA certification therefore represents an important element of the programme, allowing the protection equipment to form part of the aircraft’s certified configuration. BIRD Aerosystems did not identify the aircraft operator or disclose the number of Global 7500 aircraft expected to receive the system. “The Global 7500 is another aircraft now protected by BIRD Aerosystems, joining a growing number of high-value platforms equipped with our airborne missile protection suite,” said Ronen Factor, Co-CEO and Founder of BIRD Aerosystems. He added that the programme reflected the company’s expanding presence in the market and increasing demand for protection against MANPADS and other missile threats. Growing Demand from Business Jet Operators According to Israeli industry sources, interest in airborne missile protection systems has increased in recent months, particularly among operators of business jets flying to destinations where MANPADS are believed to be accessible to terrorist organisations or other non-state armed groups. Israeli manufacturers of aircraft protection systems have reportedly received enquiries from operators concerned about the vulnerability of their aircraft during take-off and landing, when aircraft are generally operating at lower altitudes and may be exposed to shoulder-launched missile threats. Israeli sources told ESD that part of the growing demand may be connected to humanitarian flights associated with the war in Ukraine. Some of these missions reportedly involve business jets operating in or near regions where the security situation presents additional risks. However, the sources did not provide figures establishing how much of the recent demand is directly attributable to humanitarian operations. MANPADS Proliferation Remains a Security Concern The interest in aircraft protection systems comes against the background of the continued proliferation of portable surface-to-air missiles. Although MANPADS are primarily held in government arsenals, some have reached terrorist organisations, insurgent groups and other non-state actors through illicit transfers, theft or diversion from military stockpiles. Research by the Small Arms Survey, cited by the Arms Control Association, has identified reports of illicit MANPADS possession or transfers in more than 32 countries and territories since 2011. The reported cases include advanced systems obtained by non-state armed groups, including Russian-backed forces operating in Ukraine before the full-scale Russian invasion in 2022 and ethnic armed organisations in Myanmar. These findings illustrate the difficulties of controlling the circulation of portable air defence weapons, even where international efforts seek to prevent their illicit transfer. For civilian aircraft, the potential threat is particularly relevant during operations at airports in unstable regions. MANPADS are designed to engage aircraft at relatively low altitudes, making the departure and approach phases of flight a particular concern. Missile Protection Beyond Military Aviation The Global 7500 installation highlights a broader development in the airborne protection market. Technologies originally developed primarily for military and government aircraft are increasingly being considered for civilian platforms operating in elevated-threat environments. For business jet operators, however, the adoption of such systems depends not only on the availability of suitable technology but also on aircraft compatibility, certification requirements, installation complexity and long-term support. By completing the EASA certification of its AMPS installation on the Global 7500, BIRD Aerosystems has demonstrated an additional integration option for operators seeking protection against infrared-guided missiles. Whether the growing interest reported by Israeli sources will translate into larger-scale installations across the business aviation sector remains to be seen. BIRD Aerosystems’ AMPS is designed to protect aircraft against MANPADS and other infrared-guided missile threats. The system combines missile warning sensors, threat detection and confirmation, tracking and directional infrared countermeasures. When an incoming missile is detected and identified as a threat, the DIRCM subsystem directs infrared countermeasure energy towards the missile’s seeker in order to disrupt its guidance. Unlike conventional expendable countermeasures such as flares, DIRCM systems are intended to interfere directly with the missile’s infrared seeker without relying on the release of pyrotechnic decoys. According to BIRD Aerosystems , the integrated architecture is designed to provide rapid and accurate responses while reducing false alarms to virtually zero. The manufacturer has not disclosed the specific sensor configuration or performance parameters of the installation on the Global 7500. The system is also designed to be adaptable to different aircraft types and operational requirements. BIRD Aerosystems provides services covering the entire programme lifecycle, including system design, integration, certification, installation and operational support. MANPADS are designed to engage aircraft at relatively low altitudes, making the departure and approach phases of flight a particular concern. Missile Protection Beyond Military Aviation The Global 7500 installation highlights a broader development in the airborne protection market. Technologies originally developed primarily for military and government aircraft are increasingly being considered for civilian platforms operating in elevated-threat environments. For business jet operators, however, the adoption of such systems depends not only on the availability of suitable technology but also on aircraft compatibility, certification requirements, installation complexity and long-term support. By completing the EASA certification of its AMPS installation on the Global 7500, BIRD Aerosystems has demonstrated an additional integration option for operators seeking protection against infrared-guided missiles. Whether the growing interest reported by Israeli sources will translate into larger-scale installations across the business aviation sector remains to be seen. title: Trump’s Diesel Deal Irks Allies and Is Unlikely to Reduce Prices
body:
Essential news coupled with the finest maritime content sourced from across the globe.
FILE PHOTO: U.S. President Donald Trump attends an event to sign executive orders in the Oval Office at the White House in Washington, D.C., U.S., August 6, 2026. REUTERS/Evelyn Hockstein/File Photo
By Nick Wadhams (Bloomberg) — President Donald Trump’s deal for Russian diesel exposed the US to legal questions, opened a rift with his Republican allies and European leaders and heightened tensions with Ukraine — all in exchange for an outcome that experts suggest is unlikely to succeed.
Under the agreement — announced late last week — Russian President Vladimir Putin would begin releasing diesel supplies into global markets as part of a US effort to bring down prices from their record highs before the Nov. 3 midterm elections. Trump has also intensified demands on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to stop attacking Russian refineries and announced an energy ceasefire between the two sides.
The decisions and the ceasefire are all a bet that lowering fuel prices will be the best way to win more votes next month despite the risk of a backlash from political friends and foes alike. On Sunday, a bipartisan group of senators argued that Trump should “reverse course” on his plan to cut a diesel deal with Russia.
“The United States should not provide Putin with a financial lifeline while Russia continues to kill Ukrainian civilians,” the senators said in a statement.
The accord also provoked fresh tension with Europe, where officials warned that it would bolster Moscow’s war effort in Ukraine. They said the US should impose more sanctions instead.
“We would call on the US to put the sanctions in place so that actually we could finish this war, so that all the effects of these attacks on refineries would not be there,” top European Union diplomat Kaja Kallas told reporters in Luxembourg on Monday before meeting with the bloc’s foreign ministers.
There’s also the legal challenge. A 2022 law prohibits the US from buying most Russian energy products. It’s still not clear how Trump plans to get around that, and some lawmakers, including Senator Roger Wicker, a Mississippi Republican, have already said they don’t expect the deal to go through.Play Video
Trump acknowledged on Monday that neither side had actually committed to stop attacking each other’s energy infrastructure.
“They agreed. You know why? Because I said you agree,” Trump told reporters. “That’s why they agreed — because I said they agreed.”
“I think actually Putin wants to make a deal more than Zelenskyy,” Trump said.
Keith Kellogg, the president’s former envoy to Kyiv, dismissed Trump’s latest disagreement with Zelenskyy as “noise.” He said he didn’t expect it to escalate to anything similar to their infamous face-to-face argument in the Oval Office in February 2025.
“The rhetoric will kind of take care of itself,” Kellogg said. “Look at what’s happening on the ground.”
That’s all in exchange for an effort to bring down global diesel prices that have remained stubbornly high, mostly because of the Iran war, which has throttled traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. Russia’s conflict with Ukraine also played a role, after Russia extended a ban on diesel exports through September following a wave of Ukrainian drone strikes on the country’s refineries.
Unfortunately for Trump, even if Russian diesel reaches the global market in the coming weeks, it probably won’t offer much relief for American farmers and truckers before the midterms.
The first release of 2.25 million barrels in October is 1.4 million barrels less than American consumers used in a single day as of early in the month. Shipments from Russia to the East Coast typically take more than two weeks, and record-high shipping costs would also likely push prices higher.
If Russian refineries are able to resume some exports, it would provide marginal relief to a global oil market that’s sorely missed the supply, analysts say. Yet whether those shipments restart in earnest depends on the durability of an energy ceasefire that Trump announced over the weekend. Neither Russia nor Ukraine said they had agreed to such a deal.
Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said monthly diesel exports of 3 million tons — near levels seen before Ukraine’s drone campaign — will only be possible after December.
“There is no indication that any diesel is making its way to the US just yet,” Bloomberg geoeconomics analyst Alex Kokcharov wrote in a note. “Given questions around the legality of easing sanctions and Russia’s own export capacity, it’s not clear this will result in any net increase to global diesel supplies.”

title: Appeal Court Quashes Kwara govt’s Case Against Saraki
body: The Court of Appeal has dismissed the criminal defamation and cyberbullying case filed by the Kwara State Government against former Senate President, Dr. Abubakar Bukola Saraki, as the court declared that the charge and the evidence produced, disclosed no offence committed by the appellant. In a judgement read by Hon.Justice Ridwan Maiwada Abdullahi on behalf of his two brother judges, Hon. Justice Gabriel Omoniyi Kolawole and Hon. Justice Abdu Dogo, the appellate court held that there was nothing in the statement by Dr. Saraki being complained of by Mr. Abdulrahman Abdulrazaq, Governor of Kwara State, was capable of inciting violence in any part of Kwara State or moving anybody to resort to the breakdown of law and order The judge noted that all the evidence and witnesses’ statements supplied in support of the charge did not disclose that Saraki’s statement led to any breach of the peace in the state; rather, they merely showed that those who testified felt dissatisfied with the statement. He added that the Administration of Criminal Justice Act, the Penal Code Law of Kwara State, and the Cybercrime and Cyberbullying law were not enacted for the purpose of protecting individuals against statements that they were uncomfortable with. He added that while the Attorney General of a state and that of the federation have wide powers to institute criminal cases, such powers cannot be exercised in a manner that is prejudicial and oppressive of any individual or to violate the fundamental human rights of citizens. The judge therefore ordered that the case instituted at the Kwara State High Court against Dr. Saraki over his statement in which he alleged that Mr. Abdulrahman Abdulrazaq did not complete secondary education and that his level of education is affecting his judgement can not be sustained, having not disclosed any offence or included any statutory ingredient of the offence he was being charged for. In his reaction to the judgement, Dr. Saraki noted that he has once again been vindicated in his unflinching belief that nobody, no matter how powerful, can successfully muffle the voice of dissent particularly when those in government fail in their responsibility to the people. He also expressed his gratitude to the judiciary for once again standing for the truth and defending the cause of justice. Saraki noted that if the need arises, he will not hesitate to reiterate his position on the level of education of Governor Abdulrazaq and that he will not keep quiet when there are issues of public interest that deserve his comment.

title: Russia used civilians as human shields, then shelled them near Kupiansk, Ukraine’s Khartiia says

The group included two women, a child, and several men, according to the Ukrainian military unit. Khartiia warned that Russian media could use footage of the incident to accuse Ukrainian forces of attacking civilians. The corps said the shelling came from Russian-held territory and described the incident as a deliberate provocation. title: US Army to stand up command for unmanned and autonomous warfare
body: The U.S. Army has ordered the creation of its own command for autonomous systems, a day after Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced a new four-star military command for unmanned and autonomous warfare. An Oct. 1 memo signed by Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle directs the Army vice chief of staff to establish the U.S. Army Futures and Autonomous Systems Command, or FASCOM. It also tells the assistant secretary of the Army for acquisition, logistics and technology, who oversees how the Army buys weapons, to put one office in charge of purchasing its priority autonomous systems. Telle wrote that he issued the memo under guidance from Hegseth’s Sept. 30 State of the Force address . The memo does not say who will lead FASCOM, where it will be based or when it will be established. “Specifics on structure, command, mission, etc. will be announced at a future date,” Col. Marty Meiners, an Army spokesperson, told Defense News. The new acquisition office, a Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Autonomy, would have single authority over buying the Army’s priority autonomous systems. The Army reorganized its weapons buying last year under six portfolio acquisition executives, each overseeing a group of related programs. This would add another for autonomy. The memo also directs the assistant secretary to prioritize buying and fielding several types of autonomous systems no later than fiscal 2028. The list includes fires, the Army’s term for artillery, rockets and missiles; combat vehicles; watercraft resupply; breaching systems that clear obstacles such as minefields; reconnaissance, surveillance and target acquisition systems; and drones and robots working alongside crewed vehicles and aircraft. The Army said in its release that the memo’s initiatives build on work already underway, including an office set up earlier this year to work autonomous technology into weapons programs across the Army. Neither the memo nor the release says whether that office, the Capability Program Executive Office for Mission Autonomy, will move under the new acquisition office. The memo tasks the Army staff’s force management office, which shapes how units are organized and equipped, with quickly working out how to fit autonomous systems into at least six existing types of units: aviation, armor, fires, sustainment, engineer and training. It also tells the assistant secretary of the Army who oversees manpower and personnel policy to add drone and robotics specialist positions to all applicable Army units. Both specialties already exist: the 15X tactical unmanned aircraft systems specialist for enlisted soldiers, and the 390A robotics technician for warrant officers. “The Army is rapidly advancing to maintain our lethal edge,” Telle said in a statement released by the Army . “We are forging the U.S. Army Futures and Autonomous Systems Command to get cutting-edge technology into the hands of soldiers, while prioritizing autonomy in our formations, our acquisitions, and our training to dominate the future of warfare.” Hegseth announced the Autonomous Warfare Command, or AutoWarCom, during his Sept. 30 State of the Force address at Marine Corps Base Quantico, Virginia, Military Times reported . He said the command would have service-like authorities to scale autonomous and robotic capabilities across the military. Hegseth’s own memo, “ Project Agincourt: Pathway to the Autonomous Warfare Command ,” signed the same day as his address, puts the Pentagon’s unmanned systems office in charge of Project Agincourt, an effort to lay the groundwork for AutoWarCom. Hegseth said in his address that the project is named for the 1415 battle in which an outnumbered English army used the longbow to defeat a larger, heavily armored French force. The memo argues that cheap, precise weapons built at massive scale now threaten the expensive aircraft, ships and vehicles the military has long relied on. The Agincourt memo describes AutoWarCom as a four-star functional combatant command, a headquarters organized around a mission rather than a region, like U.S. Cyber Command. It says the command would have dedicated manpower, budget and authority to buy equipment. Powers like those require an act of Congress, which gave U.S. Special Operations Command a similar setup when it was created in 1987. The memo directs the unmanned systems office to work with Congress on the needed legislation, with a goal of establishing AutoWarCom by Oct. 1, 2027. The Agincourt memo says AutoWarCom will “define joint needs and integrate Service-provided forces in support of geographic combatant commanders,” the four-star officers who lead U.S. forces in regions such as the Middle East and the Pacific. A plan due by Oct. 30 is to lay out command relationships and what forces each service will contribute. Telle’s memo does not say how FASCOM will fit into that structure. The new command’s name revives “Futures” a year after the Army inactivated Army Futures Command. In October 2025, the service merged Futures Command with Training and Doctrine Command to form the Army Transformation and Training Command, or T2COM, headquartered in Austin, Texas . The memo does not address how FASCOM will relate to T2COM. A T2COM spokesperson referred questions about the new command to Army headquarters. Asked how FASCOM will relate to T2COM and AutoWarCom and how the changes will be paid for, Meiners said the Army had no information to provide beyond its release.

title: Trezor Cuts Its Resellers After Ledger Finds Spy Implant in Crypto Wallets
body:
Trezor is cutting its network of authorized resellers, telling partners their authorization ends on January 1, 2027, days after rival hardware wallet manufacturer Ledger started an investigation that eventually confirmed a hidden spy implant in crypto wallets sold through a third-party store.
The company announced the move on X on Tuesday, saying “there is not a single piece of evidence” that Trezor devices have been compromised. It described the cut as a preventive step taken out of caution.
“Following recent supply-chain incidents, we decided to reduce the number of resellers so we can more effectively check those we work with,” Trezor wrote.
A hardware wallet is a small device that keeps the secret keys to your crypto offline, away from hackers. Setting one up produces a 24-word recovery phrase that works as a master password: whoever has those words can empty the wallet from anywhere in the world.
Ledger's Donjon security team says wallets sold by CryptoBilis, a reseller in Southeast Asia, contained an unauthorized component that reads the screen and decodes the recovery phrase when it appears. The spy implant then sends the words out over LTE, the same mobile data network your phone uses, through an eSIM, a SIM card built into the hardware. Ledger says the implant does not alter the chip that stores the keys or the device's operating system, so a tampered wallet looks and works normally.
Trezor CCO Danny Sanders shared the letter that the company sent to those providers that Trezor is ditching. “If you are receiving this letter, your authorization ends on 1 January 2027. On that date we will remove you from our list of authorized Trezor resellers,” the letter reads. “I am sorry. This decision says nothing about your effort or the way you represented us.”
This is a precautionary measure to protect our supply chain and our customers,” he wrote. “If things change in the future we will review it.”
Affected resellers will get no new stock, but they can keep selling what they have through Black Friday and the holiday season. Sanders said the decision just reflects how many partners Trezor can vet closely itself.
Neither the post nor the letter says how many resellers are affected. Trezor says it reviewed each country on its own, weighing revenue and distribution against its own presence there, and that resellers who stay will face an updated legal framework and tighter rules on how devices are sourced, stored, and handled.
Trezor said on X earlier this week that CryptoBilis was already off its seller list and that it had received no reports of tampered Trezors from the retailer.
Hi, don’t open it. Forcing the casing open can damage the device, and if it’s a Safe 7, the built-in battery makes that genuinely risky. If something about your device worries you, reach out via https://t.co/wzwW038oLv , and we’ll take a look.
In May 2022, Trezor warned that counterfeit Model T wallets were being sold on a Russian marketplace by a seller that was not an authorized reseller. The devices had been opened, resealed, and fitted with replaced internal components, and Trezor said the recovery phrases they generated were predictable or predefined, meaning someone else could already know the words.
Trezor's advice then was to buy only from its official shop or an authorized reseller. The second option is the network it is now shrinking.
In August, shipping partner ShipMonk exposed Trezor customer data after unauthorized access, and Trezor's September update put the total at 80,689 customers . Trezor says its systems, devices, private keys, and wallet backups were not affected.
Ledger told anyone who bought from CryptoBilis in the past 90 days not to set up their device, and told those who already did to move their funds to a new seed phrase on a device bought from Ledger. Ledger and Trezor have each warned buyers against unauthorized sellers.
