title: Housekeeper cleared of stealing Jordanian princess’s jewels
body: A long-serving housekeeper has been found not guilty of stealing expensive jewellery from her employer, a Jordanian princess. A jury in London took less than two hours to clear Maria Virgelina Taborda Henao, 71, of theft. She had been accused of stealing several items from the home in Belgravia when Princess Firyal, 81, flew to Jordan at the outbreak of Covid in 2020. Princess Firyal was married to Prince Muhammad bin Talal, the younger brother of King Hussein of Jordan, from 1964 to 1978. She had told Southwark Crown Court that she had been alerted that items from her jewellery collection were missing when a jeweller friend called to tell her they had appeared for auction in Canterbury. The items included a custom-made sapphire and diamond ring. The court heard police found Princess Firyal’s wedding ring, a pair of earrings and a necklace during a search of Ms Taborda Henao’s home in Fulham. The princess thought the wedding ring had been lost years earlier. Ms Taborda Henao, who is from Colombia and had worked for Princess Firyal for 11 years, told the court, through a Spanish interpreter, that the princess had called her a thief and made similar accusations against other people. Ms Taborda Henao’s nephew, Julian Ramirez, was said to have acted as a conduit for the sale of the items. He was also arrested but fled to Colombia in October 2023 while on police bail.

title: Russian gymnasts denied Dutch visas over threat to international ties
body:
MOSCOW, October 13. /TASS/. The official reason cited by The Netherlands for refusing entry visas to Russian athletes seeking to participate in the World Artistic Gymnastics Championships was a threat to international relations, Russia’s Gymnastics Federation said.
Earlier, the Dutch embassy refused to issue visas to Olympic champions Angelina Melnikova and Victoria Listunova, as well as Anna Kalmykova. The World Artistic Gymnastics Championships will be held in Rotterdam from October 17 to 25.
"The official notifications about visa denials for Angelina Melnikova, Viktoria Listunova, and Anna Kalmykova cite the following reason: ‘one or more member states of the Schengen Area consider the athletes a threat to their international relations.’ This was precisely the reason given for denying visas to the three leading Russian gymnasts four days before the start of the World Championships in Rotterdam," it said.
TASS reported earlier that gymnasts Daniel Marinov, Arseny Dukhno, Sergey Naidin, and Alena Glotova, who were granted Schengen visas, have arrived in The Netherlands. Five more Russian athletes who are to take part in the tournament - Lyudmila Roshchina, Milana Kayumova, Ilya Zaika, Savely Syedin, and Mukhammadzhon Yakubov - are awaiting their entry visas.
The tournament in Rotterdam will be the first stage of team qualification for the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles. Following the competition, the top three men’s and women’s teams will receive Olympic licenses.

title: IRGC kills terrorists, rescues kidnapped engineer in SE
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 13 (MNA) – The IRGC Ground Force servicemen dismantled a kidnapping team affiliated with the terrorist group Jaish al-Adl in southeastern Iran, killing five of its members and rescuing a kidnapped engineer.
The Quds Base of the Islamic Revolution Guards Corps Ground Force (IRGC) announced in a statement that the operation took place in the Kourin area of Zahedan, Sistan and Balouchestan Province.
The statement said the kidnapping team had abducted a construction project engineer in western Zahedan on Monday and intended to transfer him to a neighboring country.
Following the kidnapping, IRGC Ground Force personnel from the Quds Base used their intelligence capabilities to locate the team’s hideout in Kourin and launched a surprise operation against its members, the statement added.
Five members of the kidnapping team were killed during the operation, and the abducted engineer was freed.
One IRGC serviceman was martyred in the clashes, the statement said.
It added that clashes with the remaining members of the terrorist team were still underway.
It was later repored another member of the terrorist team was killed, bringing the total number of the terrorists to six in the Korin's operation.

title: ‎Ghana seeks climate finance access for debt-restructuring countries
body: Minister of State in Charge of Climate Change and Sustainability,‎ Issifu Seidu, has called for climate-vulnerable countries undergoing debt restructuring to retain access to climate finance, insisting that exclusion could undermine development gains and efforts to achieve debt sustainability. ‎The country said timely financing was essential to help vulnerable economies respond to climate shocks without diverting scarce domestic resources from development priorities or resorting to emergency borrowing. ‎He made the call in an interview with Ghanaian journalists after a ministerial dialogue on the margins of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank Group (WBG) annual meetings in Bangkok. ‎The dialogue formally initiated the process to establish a US$500 million Lifeline Fund by the V20 group of climate-vulnerable economies. ‎The proposed facility is intended to provide rapid financial support to countries facing climate shocks. ‎Mr Seidu credited Barbados with leading advocacy for reforms to the international climate finance architecture to better address the needs of climate-vulnerable countries. ‎He said climate shocks repeatedly reversed development progress, compelling governments to redirect limited domestic resources towards emergency response and recovery. ‎“We realise that anytime these countries go through debt restructuring, they are excluded from the financing arrangement. So, if they are taking difficult decisions, these difficult decisions should not exclude them from these opportunities of climate fund,” he said. ‎Mr Seidu said the exclusion created competing fiscal demands for governments, which had to meet debt-servicing obligations, finance development programmes and respond to floods, droughts and other climate-related disasters. ‎He said the proposed Lifeline Fund would help address the financing gap by providing quicker access to resources for climate interventions, avoiding the lengthy bureaucratic processes associated with traditional climate funds. ‎The Minister said the exclusion of countries undergoing debt restructuring was counterproductive, particularly when they had taken difficult but necessary measures to restore debt sustainability in line with international expectations. ‎“If they are taking difficult decisions, those decisions should not exclude them from opportunities for climate finance,” he said. ‎Mr Seidu reaffirmed Ghana’s commitment to sustained advocacy to address structural inequalities at the intersection of climate justice and debt sustainability. ‎He said responding promptly to climate shocks could also support debt sustainability by preventing costly reversals in development and reducing the need for emergency borrowing after disasters. ‎The Minister called on strategic partners to complement government efforts to support vulnerable countries and communities. ‎He also urged investors to collaborate in developing sustainable solutions and share resilience-building successes across the Global South.

title: France accuses Elon Musk of ‘online harassment’ of Europe leaders
body: France’s foreign minister on Tuesday accused the billionaire tycoon and owner of the X social media platform Elon Musk of “online harassment” of European leaders, as he sounded the alarm over the risks of interference in the French 2027 presidential election. Jean-Noel Barrot warned that ahead of the April-May election — in which far-right candidate Marine Le Pen has her best ever chance of winning the Elysee — “the enemies of democracy will do everything to destabilise us”. “They exploit our divisions and exploit issues such as immigration, secularism, and the Israeli-Palestinian conflict to stoke hatred and tension,” he said at a conference organised by the Paris-based Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD). He singled out an Israeli company — which he did not identify — that he said had created fake French accounts to post over the Israel-Palestinian conflict. But Barrot also took aim at the “massive online harassment campaigns by Elon Musk against European leaders, aimed at influencing national debates by exploiting the viral nature of his social network.” With France rocked by several weeks of protests by high school students over their conditions, Barrot complained that some coverage of the demonstrations online had been marked by “hostile narratives originating from Russia and China, as well as Iran and the MAGA community” in reference to the supporters of US President Donald Trump. Trump had last week written on his Truth Social network that “what’s happening in France is nothing less than out of control mass migration.” Musk had then commented to his 241.5 million followers on X: “It’s an invasion in slow motion, but an invasion nonetheless. And those who support the invasion are traitors who deserve the fate of all traitors.” Barrot vowed that France would hit back. “We do not tolerate any foreign interference, from wherever it may come. It is a matter of sovereignty,” he said. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Monday it was “clear” Russia had interfered in the UK’s bitter 2016 Brexit referendum that resulted in its exit from the European Union. AFP The post France accuses Elon Musk of ‘online harassment’ of Europe leaders appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Afenyo-Markin urges stronger media scrutiny of public institutions
body: The Minority Leader in Parliament, Alexander Kwamena Afenyo-Markin, has called on journalists to intensify their investigative work and hold public institutions accountable, following recent major narcotics-related incidents. Speaking at the launch of the 30th Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) Media Awards and the inauguration of the Awards Committee last week, Mr Afenyo-Markin said the media had a constitutional responsibility to pursue matters of national concern, particularly where parliamentary attempts to investigate them had encountered procedural obstacles. The Minority Leader’s comment followed the Speaker of Parliament’s decision not to admit a Minority-sponsored motion seeking a parliamentary inquiry. He maintained that the freedom and independence of the press, as guaranteed under Chapter 12 of the 1992 Constitution, remained essential to democratic accountability and the protection of national interest. Referring to Article 162(5) of the Constitution, the Minority Leader reminded journalists of the media’s responsibility to uphold the accountability of government to Ghanaians. Concern over narcotics trafficking Mr Afenyo-Markin expressed concern about reports of increasing narcotics-related incidents involving the country and the potential consequences for the country’s international reputation, border security and legitimate export trade. Citing research published by JoyNews, he stated that 28 drug busts involving Ghana had been recorded since March 2025, including 11 major cocaine cases, with the estimated street value of the cocaine seizures ranging between US$1.3 billion and US$1.7 billion. He also referred to information attributed to Belgian Customs concerning Ghana’s ranking among countries of origin for cocaine entering Belgium. The Minority Leader argued that the developments required a thorough investigation into the effectiveness of Ghana’s port surveillance, border security and narcotics enforcement systems. He further expressed concern that the heightened international scrutiny associated with narcotics trafficking could adversely affect legitimate Ghanaian exporters through additional cargo inspections and related costs. Parliamentary oversight On the Minority Caucus’ recent attempt to secure a parliamentary investigation into major narcotics incidents, the leader said the caucus had initiated a recall of Parliament and presented a motion seeking a bipartisan inquiry into the country’s narcotics enforcement and border security systems. He said the Speaker’s decision not to admit the motion had prevented the house from considering the proposed investigation. He maintained that the development made independent media scrutiny even more important, particularly where questions of public accountability remained unresolved. The Minority Leader also criticised the actions of state security institutions in connection with the arrest of Salomey Awiti Bafoh and the reported attempted arrest of the Member of Parliament for Manhyia South, Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah, on the premises of the High Court. He described these developments as part of what he considered a diversion from the larger questions surrounding narcotics trafficking and national security. Charge to journalists On the significance of the GJA Media Awards, Mr Afenyo-Markin commended the association for sustaining three decades of recognition for excellence in journalism. He said the awards provided an important opportunity to recognise journalists who demonstrated independence, professional integrity and a commitment to exposing wrongdoing in the public interest. He encouraged the newly inaugurated Awards Committee to attach particular importance to courage, independence and measurable public impact when evaluating entries for the 30th edition. Mr Afenyo-Markin reaffirmed the Minority Caucus’ commitment to defending press freedom and protecting journalists against state overreach. He congratulated the GJA leadership and members of the Awards Committee, expressing the hope that the anniversary edition would further strengthen journalism and its contribution to democratic accountability.

title: Russian Drone Attack Kills 1, Injures 2 in Pavlohrad
body:
A Russian drone attack on the city of Pavlohrad in the Dnipropetrovsk region killed one person and injured two others on the evening of Tuesday, Oct. 13, according to regional officials.
Oleksandr Hanzha, head of the Dnipropetrovsk Regional Military Administration, reported the casualties around 6:51 p.m. local time, adding that the strike set off a fire in the city center.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
It was not immediately clear who the victims were or what had been struck at the time of the report.
In the afternoon, Hanzha said Russian forces had attacked four districts of the region almost 40 times with drones and artillery, injuring two people.
The Nikopol area, which sits across the Dnipro River from Russian-occupied territory, bore the brunt of the strikes.
Nikopol and the Marhanets and Pokrovske communities were primarily targeted, damaging apartment blocks, private homes and vehicles. A 31-year-old man and a 73-year-old woman were injured and received outpatient treatment.
In the regional capital, Dnipro, the attacks caused fires, while a private house was damaged in the nearby Solone community of Dnipro district.
Infrastructure was damaged in the Malomykhailivka community of Synelnykove district, and a private home was hit in the Zelenodolsk community in the Kryvyi Rih area, Hanzha said.
In total, Russian attacks on the Dnipropetrovsk region killed one person and injured five on Tuesday.
Earlier on Tuesday, Russian forces attacked Dnipro with guided aerial bombs (KABs), damaging apartment buildings, vehicles, and transport infrastructure and injuring a 64-year-old man.
On Monday, Oct. 12, Russian forces also attacked the city of Dnipro and the surrounding Dniprovskyi district, killing one person and sparking a fire in the shopping center in the region’s suburbs.
An 11-year-old boy was killed and two other children were injured on Saturday, Oct. 10, when Russian forces dropped an explosive munition from an unmanned aerial vehicle in the Nikopol district.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

body:
We just got a closer look at Apple’s new video doorbell, security cameras, door lock, and thermostats, following the company’s “Welcome home” event on Tuesday. The six new devices are part of a new Apple Home Collection, which the company codeveloped with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric.

title: GoldBod recovers GH¢38.7m in legacy PMMC debts, targets remaining arrears
body: The Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) has recovered GH¢38.71 million out of GH¢55.88 million owed to its predecessor, the Precious Minerals Marketing Company (PMMC), by third parties, representing approximately 69.2 per cent of the outstanding debt. Chief Executive Officer of GoldBod, Sammy Gyamfi, disclosed the recovery when he appeared before Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee (PAC) on Tuesday, October 13, 2026, adding that management was pursuing the remaining debts through legal and other civil recovery measures. Mr Gyamfi said the debts were uncovered during an audit of PMMC’s financial statements covering 2020 to 2024, after the company’s accounts had gone unaudited for five consecutive years. “When we assumed office in January 2025, we found out that the financials of the PMMC, the antecedent of the Gold Board, had not been audited for five consecutive years, which is from the year 2020 to 2024,” he told the committee. The audit identified GH¢55.88 million owed by third parties as of December 31, 2023. According to the GoldBod CEO, management issued demand notices to the debtors and had recovered GH¢38.71 million as of September 30, 2026. He said approximately GH¢17.1 million remained outstanding, with GH¢7.5 million tied up in court proceedings and GH¢9.6 million being pursued through demand notices, negotiations and other civil recovery options. “Of the remaining amount of GH¢17.1 million, approximately GH¢7.5 million is involved in matters before courts of competent jurisdiction, and an amount of approximately GH¢9.6 million relates to debts that we are currently pursuing through various civil options like demand notices and negotiations with the parties concerned,” he said. Mr Gyamfi expressed optimism that the Board would recover a larger portion of the outstanding amount before the end of 2026. “We hope that by the end of this year we will have even increased what we have recovered so far,” he said.

title: Google makes Gemini 4 Argon broadly available with limited-time low API pricing of $2/$10 per 1M token
body:
Credit: VentureBeat made with OpenAI ChatGPT-Images-2.5
Google is making its new, flagship Gemini 4 Argon multimodal language AI model broadly available today, October 13.
The model was previously available only to a limited group of early testers. Now developers and enterprises are getting a powerful new option for software engineering, financial analysis, legal work, cybersecurity and scientific research — at limited-time discounted API prices substantially below some leading competitors.
The rollout comes just 13 days after Google first unveiled Argon on September 30 , initially restricting access to approved cybersecurity defenders through its Fairwind Program while conducting additional safety testing and participating in a voluntary U.S. government pre-release model access process.
At the time, Google promised broader availability as soon as possible, but did not commit to a specific date. Now the company is offering Argon through the paid Gemini API, Google AI Studio, its Antigravity agentic development environment and eligible Gemini Enterprise subscriptions. Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers can also access the model in the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search, although Antigravity access for individual subscribers requires the more expensive Ultra tier.
The launch gives enterprise customers their first widespread opportunity to test Google's most capable publicly offered model against rival systems from OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta, while providing fresh evidence of how Google itself is deploying Argon across complex engineering and business operations.
According to the company's new announcement, more than 100,000 Google employees use Argon through an internal version of Antigravity each month. Over a four-week period, Google says its engineering teams increased agentic code submissions by 35% while reducing post-submission code rollbacks by 30%.
But while Google's benchmarks show substantial improvements in professional and technical work, independent testing paints a more complicated picture of the model's competitive standing.
Sam Witteveen, CEO and co-founder of enterprise AI consulting and education company Red Dragon AI, and a VentureBeat host and partner, has been testing Argon ahead of its broader release.
"This is a really, really, really good model. But is it the best model out there? I actually don't think it is," Witteveen says in a video review shared with VentureBeat ahead of publication .
His assessment suggests Google's biggest achievement may be more strategic than technical: building a sufficiently capable general-purpose foundation for increasingly sophisticated products and enterprise workflows.
Google is backing its release with detailed examples of Argon performing tasks that would ordinarily require specialized engineering teams and substantial development time.
Perhaps the most striking example involves Chrome. Google says Argon helped reorganize a legacy folder containing approximately 6 million lines of browser feature code within Chromium's roughly 40-million-line codebase.
The model assisted in separating the browser's core webpage-handling capabilities from feature-specific code, enabling an architectural overhaul spanning hundreds of files.
Google says the work, previously expected to take months, was completed in weeks. The changes are intended to eventually allow webpages to move between tabs, side panels and floating windows without reloading, while eliminating certain crashes.
Elsewhere, Google's Agent Development Kit team tasked Argon with finding opportunities to improve the performance of its open-source Python framework for building AI agents.
After receiving a short objective and the team's existing instructions, Argon worked overnight and identified optimizations that Google says reduced in-memory session preparation time by 40% for long-running sessions and accelerated cold imports by 21%. The improvements have been incorporated into the public ADK Python codebase.
Google also reports that Argon helped optimize inference for its smaller Gemma 4 E2B model, increasing throughput from approximately 37,900 to more than 108,000 tokens per second on an Nvidia A100 GPU while preserving identical output.
These examples illustrate one of Google's central arguments: the model's value comes not merely from writing code, but from investigating large systems, proposing modifications, testing outcomes and iterating toward measurable improvements.
In another internal example, Argon examined 134 aging software bugs and identified 97 as stale or duplicated in under three hours, using commit histories and production telemetry to document its findings.
Google's examples offer unusually concrete descriptions of AI-assisted work, although they remain company-reported results rather than independently replicated enterprise evaluations.
Two major independent testing organizations offer contrasting perspectives on Argon's capabilities.
Vals AI , which evaluates models on professional tasks across finance, legal services, coding and tax work, ranks Argon first on its GDP-weighted Vals Index.
As of October 12, Argon scores 68.90%, ahead of Claude Sonnet 5.5 at 67.04% and Claude Opus 5.5 at 66.97%.
Vals also reports that Argon achieves a 65.40% score on its Finance Agent v2 benchmark, placing first among the models tested.
These results support Google's argument that Argon is particularly competitive on professional workflows requiring domain knowledge and sustained reasoning.
They also reinforce several advantages Google highlighted when it originally announced the model on September 30.
In the company's earlier benchmark comparisons, Argon scored 19.6% on Harvey's Legal Agent Benchmark, compared with 5.4% for OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra and 3.8% for Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5. On Zapier's AutomationBench, which measures AI systems' ability to carry out multi-step business processes, Argon achieved 51.3%, ahead of Opus 5.5 at 42.5% and Astra at 41.4%.
The model also performed well on DeepSWE v1.1, a benchmark of extended software engineering tasks, scoring 77.9% against 74.2% for Opus and 74.1% for Astra.
However, Google's own comparisons showed areas where competitors maintained advantages. On Terminal-Bench 4.0, an evaluation of coding tasks performed through command-line tools, Opus 5.5 scored 66.4% versus Argon's 57.4%.
These are Google's previously disclosed benchmark comparisons, not a new set of independently replicated launch-day tests. They nevertheless help illustrate why different kinds of enterprise tasks can produce different winners.
More broadly, Artificial Analysis , which measures capabilities across reasoning, knowledge, mathematics, coding and agentic tasks, assigns Argon a score of 53 on its Intelligence Index.
That ties the model with OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra and Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.1, but places it below Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Meta's Muse Wonder Full, released yesterday.
Sources: Artificial Analysis model evaluations, as available October 13, 2026. Higher scores indicate better performance. Results reflect the evaluated reasoning configurations, and not all models have the same public API availability.
That distinction matters for enterprise buyers. An aggregate benchmark can reveal broad technical performance, but it cannot establish which model will work best within an organization's particular software, data and operational environment.
Witteveen argues that Argon's strengths are especially apparent on tasks combining visual understanding, software generation and creative media production.
In one demonstration, he asked Argon to create a browser-based music production application modeled on Propellerheads' ReBirth software, complete with synthesized sounds, drum machines, filters and a step sequencer inspired by classic Roland equipment.
Using a relatively short prompt in the Gemini app, Argon produced an interactive interface along with functioning audio-generation code.
Witteveen also highlights Google's demonstrations involving Blender animations, 3D environments and interactive visualizations. These tasks require AI systems to generate code, render results, inspect their output and revise their work.
"This model seems to be very good at generalization," he says.
Nevertheless, he remains skeptical that Google's existing coding environment can displace established alternatives for developers focused primarily on autonomous software engineering.
"I still don't think, for example, Antigravity is anywhere near as good as Claude Code or Codex," Witteveen says.
His criticism distinguishes the underlying model's capabilities from the quality of the surrounding development tools — a consideration enterprises should weigh when evaluating complete AI coding systems rather than standalone API performance.
Google is also highlighting Argon's potential in cybersecurity, scientific computing and physical robotics.
The company says Wiz has used Argon through its Scan for Good initiative to identify and remediate a serious vulnerability in healthcare software. According to Google, the vulnerability exposed a master key that could allow administrator-level access and potentially compromise large quantities of sensitive patient information.
Google is expanding access through its Fairwind Program to hundreds of additional approved cybersecurity partners, including access to versions of the model without certain cybersecurity restrictions for authorized defensive work.
The company reports a 0.7% attack success rate on the Gray Swan Indirect Prompt Injection benchmark across 15 adaptive attempts. It also says Argon was trained to respect system boundaries and pause before irreversible actions, with unauthorized shortcut attempts dropping to 2% on its coding evaluations.
These figures are encouraging but do not eliminate the need for enterprise testing, access controls and human approval of consequential actions.
On the scientific side, Google's researchers report using Argon to accelerate quantum-computing calculations, optimize molecular modeling software and help design five new enzymes whose catalytic activity was subsequently confirmed through laboratory experiments.
Robotics presents another potential area of differentiation.
Google reports that Argon achieved an 87% score on the Embodied Reasoning Question Answering benchmark, which tests spatial and physical reasoning, exceeding Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra in the comparison supplied with its release.
In one demonstration, Argon studied video of a person playing cornhole, constructed simulation code and generated a motion sequence subsequently transferred to Apptronik's Apollo humanoid robot. Google says the robot successfully landed seven consecutive throws.
Another demonstration shows Argon generating a simulated robotic task environment from a hand-drawn sketch.
The broader implication is that Google's frontier model is being developed not just to interpret language or generate software, but to help create, evaluate and control simulated physical environments that can inform real-world robotics.
Google is offering Argon at introductory rates of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, with a 95% discount on cached input.
Unlike the September 30 announcement, which did not specify when the introductory period would end, Google now confirms that the reduced pricing expires November 30, 2026.
Beginning December 1, the standard public API price doubles to $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens.
That gives enterprise buyers a defined, relatively short window to evaluate Argon at lower prices before calculating the economics of longer-term production deployments.
Standard API list prices per million tokens. Prices exclude additional costs associated with tools, infrastructure and other services. Gemini 4 Argon's introductory cached-input rate is $0.10 per million tokens.
At its introductory price, Argon costs half as much per input and output token as Claude Opus 5.5 and one-fifth as much as GPT-6 Astra.
From December, its base price moves into the same category as Claude Opus 5.5 and Meta Muse Wonder.
Of course, raw token pricing tells only part of the story. Different models consume different amounts of reasoning tokens, require different numbers of attempts and vary in how effectively they complete a task.
Argon also offers an unusually large reasoning budget through the API. Google describes a unified limit of up to 1 million input and output tokens, using a continuation protocol intended for exceptionally demanding tasks.
That description introduces an important qualification to Google's original September 30 announcement, which described a new ceiling of 1 million output tokens, up from 64,000.
The new announcement instead emphasizes a combined input/output limit supported through a specialized API protocol. Google has not clarified in the supplied materials precisely how that limit relates to the maximum number of tokens developers can receive in one uninterrupted response.
Witteveen similarly cautions that developers should not mistake this specialized capability for the model's normal operating behavior in the Gemini app or other consumer products.
The extended capability requires API configuration, and he believes its strongest potential applications involve scientific or highly specialized workflows requiring hundreds of thousands of reasoning tokens.
For most enterprises, he recommends evaluating established workflows before redesigning systems to exploit the expanded limit.
Argon's launch arrives as Google, OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta compete increasingly on the usefulness of their complete AI platforms, not simply model intelligence.
The broader release also represents an important moment for Google's AI organization, which has faced scrutiny over its pace of frontier-model development and a series of changes to its research leadership.
As VentureBeat reported when Argon was first announced , Google's previous flagship Gemini 3 family arrived in November 2025, while OpenAI and Anthropic subsequently introduced newer models that overtook it in important evaluations.
In July, Reuters reported investor concerns over delays to Gemini 3.5 Pro, substantial infrastructure spending and departures from Google's AI teams.
An August leadership reorganization reported by Axios saw longtime Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis move into a chairman and chief scientist role at Alphabet, while Kavukcuoglu assumed leadership of DeepMind.
Against that backdrop, Google's ability to build, deploy and now commercialize Argon provides an answer to questions about whether the company can keep pace with the leading frontier-model developers — even if it does not decisively surpass them across every evaluation.
Google's advantage is the breadth of infrastructure and products through which it can distribute Argon.
The model is available in the Gemini API and Google's enterprise offerings, while Antigravity integrates it into coding workflows. Android developers can use it through Android Studio and Firebase AI Logic.
Meanwhile, the Gemini app gains more agentic functionality, including persistent tasks that can continue while users are away from their computers and connections to more than 40 external applications.
Witteveen sees this product ecosystem as central to Google's strategy.
He argues that Google does not necessarily need to win every independent evaluation to succeed with Argon. Instead, it needs a sufficiently advanced frontier model that existing Google customers can incorporate into increasingly capable software and business processes.
That could be particularly important for enterprises already invested in Google Cloud, Gemini and Workspace, which may prefer extending their current deployments rather than adopting another vendor's AI stack for every specialized task.
Witteveen also expects Google to continue improving the Gemini 4 family, although the company has not announced a public release date for a successor to Argon.
Indeed, Business Insider reported on October 10 that Google employees were already testing updated internal versions of Gemini 4 under the codenames Barium and Carbon, with some testers reporting substantially improved coding capabilities. Google declined to comment on the internal testing or its future release plans.
That possibility underscores how quickly the competitive landscape may change, even before Argon's introductory pricing expires.
For enterprise technology leaders, the immediate question is therefore less whether Argon can claim the highest score on every AI leaderboard, and more whether its combination of reasoning, visual intelligence, automation, development-tool integration and pricing can deliver reliable results on their own workloads.
The answer will depend on production testing. But with Argon now broadly available to paying customers, Google has substantially strengthened its position in the competition for enterprise AI deployments.

title: 62 out of every 100 commercial meters inspected missing from Ghana Water database – MD
body: The Managing Director of Ghana Water Limited (GWL), Adam Mutawakilu, has disclosed that 62 out of every 100 commercial meters inspected by the company are not captured in its database. He described the finding as worrying, saying it highlights gaps in the company’s records that could be affecting revenue mobilisation. According to Mr Mutawakilu, Ghana Water is replacing meters as part of efforts to strengthen revenue collection and reduce its dependence on government funding. “We are doing replacement of meters as we speak, and it is good to know that so far, what we are covering is quite worrying, because for every hundred commercial meters that we are on estimates, we discover 62 that are not in our database,” he said when he appeared before Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee on Tuesday, October 13. He said improving revenue collection was a key priority, noting that the company was currently raising less than half of the revenue it should be generating. “The first one is revenue. I believe that what we are raising now is less than 50% of what we should have raised, and we are working round the clock to improve our revenue to be able to financially sustain us,” he said. Mr Mutawakilu expressed optimism that the ongoing measures would help Ghana Water become financially self-sustaining by 2027, with sufficient revenue to finance its projects without depending on government support. He, however, said the company would also need government assistance to address legacy loans and improve its balance sheet. According to him, converting legacy loans that have largely been repaid into equity would strengthen the company’s financial position and help it manage foreign exchange losses associated with loan repayments. He said the company’s weak equity position was limiting its ability to attract significant investment, making government intervention necessary alongside efforts to improve revenue collection.

title: PHOTOS: Five Injured As Truck Rams Into Buses At Berger Bus Stop In Lagos
body: Five people have been seriously injured after a 40-foot HOWO truck rammed into two commercial buses at Berger Bus Stop, inward Kara Bridge, in Lagos State. The accident occurred shortly after 1 p.m. when the truck, reportedly travelling from Lagos towards Kara Bridge, crashed into the buses parked by the roadside. ﻿ An official of the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) at the scene said the truck suffered brake failure before hitting the two buses. Photo showing people gathered at an accident scene after a 40-foot HOWO truck rammed into two commercial buses at Berger Bus Stop, inward Kara Bridge, in Lagos State. (Photo by: Emmanuel Monye / Channels Television) “He was coming from Lagos, here, and he had a brake failure there. So, he now hit these two cars. I think there’s no casualty anyway, but they were wounded, so they’ve taken them to emergency,” the official said. However, the Lagos State Traffic Management Authority (LASTMA) later confirmed that five passengers, comprising three women and two men, including the driver, sustained serious injuries in the crash. Photo showing people gathered at an accident scene after a 40-foot HOWO truck rammed into two commercial buses at Berger Bus Stop, inward Kara Bridge, in Lagos State. (Photo by: Emmanuel Monye / Channels Television) In a statement on Tuesday, LASTMA said its operatives rescued the injured passengers and facilitated their evacuation to the Lagos State Emergency and Trauma Centre at Toll Gate for medical attention. Personnel from Isheri Police Station also provided security support at the scene. The agency said the crash caused significant traffic congestion, with queues stretching back to Otedola Bridge. LASTMA operatives subsequently removed the vehicles, including the truck, from the carriageway to prevent secondary accidents and restore traffic flow. Photo showing people gathered at an accident scene after a 40-foot HOWO truck rammed into two commercial buses at Berger Bus Stop, inward Kara Bridge, in Lagos State. (Photo by: Emmanuel Monye / Channels Television) The vehicles were later handed over to the police for investigation into the circumstances of the crash. The agency’s General Manager, Olalekan Bakare-Oki, expressed sympathy with the injured passengers and wished them a speedy recovery. Photo showing a 40-foot HOWO truck that rammed into two commercial buses at Berger Bus Stop, inward Kara Bridge, in Lagos State. (Photo by: Emmanuel Monye / Channels Television) He urged motorists, particularly operators of heavy-duty vehicles, to ensure their vehicles are roadworthy, maintain them regularly and comply with road safety regulations. LASTMA reiterated its commitment to protecting lives and ensuring smooth traffic movement across Lagos State. Photo showing a 40-foot HOWO truck that rammed into two commercial buses at Berger Bus Stop, inward Kara Bridge, in Lagos State. (Photo by: Emmanuel Monye / Channels Television) The post PHOTOS: Five Injured As Truck Rams Into Buses At Berger Bus Stop In Lagos appeared first on Channels Television .

title: 11 Missing as Drone Attacks Strike Two Ships Near NATO Waters
body:
Essential news coupled with the finest maritime content sourced from across the globe.
General cargo vessel ALFA WATAN, one of the two vessels attacked in drone strikes in the Black Sea off NATO member Bulgaria, according to a October 6, 2026 statement by Bulgarian PM Radev, sails in Istanbul, Turkey October 5, 2026 in this screengrab obtained from a handout video. YORUK ISIK/Handout via REUTERS THIS IMAGE HAS BEEN SUPPLIED BY A THIRD PARTY. REFILE - ADDING INFORMATION.?
SOFIA, Oct 13 (Reuters) – Eleven sailors were missing at sea on Tuesday from a ship sunk by a drone attack off the coast of Bulgaria, possibly the second deadly sinking of a cargo vessel in the area in a week, prompting Bulgaria to summon Russia’s ambassador.
Two cargo ships were hit by drones overnight and one was sunk, Bulgarian officials said. Bulgaria stopped short of explicitly accusing Russia of carrying out the attacks but Prime Minister Rumen Radev said their outcome “benefits the Russian Federation.”
There was no immediate comment from Moscow on the incidents.
“This is absolutely unacceptable — another attack in the immediate vicinity of Bulgarian territorial waters,” Radev said in a televised address.
The attacks were also condemned by Ukraine and the EU.
“The Black Sea has become another front of escalation of the Russian war in Ukraine,” European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said on X. “Those responsible should be held accountable.”
Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said on X on Tuesday that the strike “once again demonstrates Moscow’s deliberate disregard for civilian lives.”
“The Black Sea is a lifeline for global food security. Russia is attacking it to weaponise hunger and hold the world hostage,” he said.
Speaking with von der Leyen and NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte by telephone on Tuesday, Radev urged their support to bolster his country’s maritime and airspace surveillance, the Bulgarian government said in a statement.
NATO would continue to adjust its military presence on its eastern flank “as needed,” Rutte said.
Defense Minister Dimitar Stoyanov spoke on the phone with his counterparts from Romania and Turkey and discussed security in the Black Sea region.
Bulgarian officials said five crew members had been rescued but 11 were still listed as missing from the ship which sank off the coast of the village of Krapets, near the Romanian border. President Iliana Iotova identified the vessel as the Guinea-Bissau-flagged cargo ship HS Dignity and said a search and rescue operation was ongoing.
Another ship, the Chelsea-3 sailing under a Maltese flag, was also hit by three drones overnight, Bulgarian officials said. All crew from that ship — seven Ukrainians and eight Azerbaijanis — were rescued and none seriously injured.
The Chelsea-3 called at the Romanian port of Tulcea on October 3 before sailing towards the Bulgarian coast, according to ship tracking data on LSEG and MarineTraffic. The vessel was showing it was at 72% of its full load, indicating it had cargo onboard.
The sunken HS Dignity , which was also part-loaded, was sailing to the Romanian port of Braila and had previously called at the Algerian port of Mostaganem, ship tracking data showed.
A week ago nine Syrian sailors and one Egyptian were lost at sea from a ship that sank when hit by drones in Bulgaria’s Black Sea exclusive economic zone. Another ship was also hit that night but the crew was rescued.
After meeting Radev in Sofia, Russian Ambassador Eleonora Mitrofanova said she had no information from the Russian Defence Ministry about attacks on commercial vessels in the Black Sea but did not rule out they could be a provocation by a third party, the Bulgarian government said.
More than four and a half years into the war that Moscow launched with its full-scale invasion in 2022, Black Sea shipping has increasingly been drawn into a prolonged battle of economic endurance.
Ukraine and Russia are both among the world’s largest exporters of grain.
Russia has been bombing Ukraine’s Black Sea ports, forcing Ukraine to rely increasingly on river ports on the Danube and shipping routes close to the coasts of NATO members Bulgaria and Romania.
Ukraine, for its part, has increasingly targeted Russian grain-exporting ships in other parts of the Black Sea and the Azov Sea at the mouth of the Don River.
(Reporting by Alex Lefkowitz and Ivana Sekularac; Additional reporting Jonathan Saul in London; Editing by Edward McAllister, Peter Graff and Alex Richardson)

title: Selma Blair charged with assault after allegedly attacking flight attendants
body:
Actor Selma Blair was arrested after she was accused of injuring two flight attendants during a trip from Los Angeles to New York on a Delta Air Lines flight.
Blair is also accused of kicking a police officer taking her to the hospital and kicking a nurse once she got there.
The 54-year-old actor pleaded not guilty on Monday to two counts of assault for state charges involving the officer and the nurse, The Associated Press reports.
Blair also faces separate federal charges based on what happened on the flight, which her representatives said was brought on by a severe medical emergency.
On the plane, Blair allegedly punched one flight attendant and bit another. She also reportedly attempted to open the plane door while in the air, according to court documents, viewed by Variety .
Global News has not independently viewed the court documents.
A spokesperson for Delta Air Lines told Global News that there was no operational impact to the flight that landed ahead of schedule at John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK) and law enforcement responded upon the flight’s arrival.
“Delta has zero tolerance for unruly or unlawful behavior, as the safety of our customers and crew always comes first,” the Delta spokesperson added.
The Cruel Intentions actor was detained by police around 11 p.m. local time on Sunday after the Delta Air Lines jet parked at the gate at JFK, the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey said in a statement to The Associated Press.
The Port Authority said that Blair and one of the flight attendants were taken to a hospital for evaluation.
A police officer taking Blair to Jamaica Hospital Medical Center said in charging documents, viewed by Global News, that while she was securing Blair to a stretcher, Blair pulled a leg from the straps and kicked her repeatedly around the face, neck and chest, causing serious pain and substantial swelling.
Later, a nurse moving Blair claimed that the actor kicked her in the chest, causing substantial pain, according to the charging documents.
Following the incident, a representative for Blair told Variety: “Selma experienced a medical emergency that led to the alleged conduct. Upon landing, she received immediate medical attention and is currently in stable condition.”
When entering her not guilty plea on Monday, the Legally Blonde actor’s lawyer Shawn Barnes reportedly told a judge that Blair’s action were not intentional.
He said the actor, who has multiple sclerosis (MS), missed several doses of “a powerful medication that controls severe neurological symptoms.”
Barnes said she had gotten on the flight in Los Angeles after a heavy workload and hit her head during the flight. He said these factors along with the altitude led to “a state of severe confusion and disorientation.”
The judge set Blair’s bail at US$20,000 cash or $60,000 bond and she left court with her lawyers. Her next hearing is set for Jan. 19.
The matter has been taken over by the FBI, according to The Hollywood Reporter .
Global News has reached out to the New York Port Authority Police Department and the FBI for further comment, but has not received a response.
This is not the first time Blair has been involved in an incident aboard a plane.
In 2016, Blair apologized for an outburst on a plane, during which she was removed from a flight on a stretcher.
In a statement to Variety , Blair admitted to having mixed alcohol and medication.
“I take this very seriously, and I apologize to all of the passengers and crew that I disturbed and am thankful to all of the people who helped me in the aftermath,” Blair said at the time. “I am a flawed human being who makes mistakes and am filled with shame over this incident.”
Blair revealed that she was diagnosed with MS in 2018 in an Instagram post, writing, “I am disabled. I fall sometimes. I drop things. My memory is foggy. And my left side is asking for directions from a broken GPS.”
She added, however, that thanks to the support of the cast and crew of a Netflix show she was filming, as well as her friends and family, “We are doing it. And I laugh and I don’t know exactly what I will do precisely but I will do my best.”
Blair thanked her doctor, saying that she had been trying to get a diagnosis for a long time.
“I am in the thick of it but I hope to give some hope to others,” Blair wrote.
“I am a forthcoming person and I want my life to be full somehow. I want to play with my son again. I want to walk down the street and ride my horse. I have MS and I am OK.”
Statistics Canada reports that it’s estimated that over 93,500 Canadians of all ages currently live with MS — an inflammatory neurological disease of the central nervous system that impacts one’s brain, spinal cord and optic nerves — and the Public Health Agency of Canada anticipates that number to rise to 133,635 by 2031.

title: Bike lane advocates to challenge Ford government’s removal plans at Supreme Court
body:
Cycling advocates are looking to escalate the legal battle over bike lanes on three major Toronto streets, asking the Supreme Court of Canada to take on the Ford government’s years-long effort to tear them out.
In a mid-August ruling, the Ontario Court of Appeal overturned a lower court’s decision that removing bike lanes violated the Canadian Charter, allowing the government to proceed with its plan.
The decision reactivated a policy that the Ford government first put in place at the end of 2024 to restore space for vehicles — and remove bike lanes — from portions of Bloor Street West, Yonge Street and University Avenue.
On Tuesday, the government said it would begin that work by reverting a 600-metre section of Bloor to vehicle-only lanes.
Ahead of the removal, CycleTO and EcoJustice, two groups that launched the charter challenge, revealed they are appealing the case to Canada’s highest court asking it to strike down the policy as unconstitutional and weigh in on the government’s ability to implement potentially life-threatening legislation.
“The consequences of this case reach far beyond bike lanes and beyond Ontario,” said Bronwyn Roe with Ecojustice.
“We are asking the Supreme Court to hear this case in order to provide clarity about the scope of the rights to life and security of the person protected by Section 7 of the Charter.”
In response to the groups appealing to the Supreme Court, Transportation Minister Prabmeet Sarkaria’s office told Global News that the August ruling in their favour was “clear” and as a result the government is removing the bike lanes on Bloor Street West beginning Tuesday.
In the August ruling that paved the way for the lanes’ removal, Justice Grant Huscroft took issue with the lower court allegedly meddling in the business of the legislature.
Huscroft wrote “it is illegitimate for courts to involve themselves in matters of legislative policy.”
While Minister Sarkaria said the ruling underscored the government’s “clear and direct mandate” to fight gridlock, advocates argue their substantive arguments still apply.
“The Ontario Court of Appeal found that, as a matter of law, removing protected bike lanes could not infringe the Charter if there was no positive right to the bike lanes in the first place. The court did not consider, let alone overturn, the superior court’s factual findings,” Roe said.
Michael Longfield, the executive director of Cycle Toronto said their principal arguments will be reintroduced in front of the supreme court, if the case is heard.
“Bike lanes do not cause traffic congestion, ripping them out will put people’s lives at risk, there’s no network of side streets that can replace the bike lanes that are here,” Longfield said.
The Supreme Court of Canada will only hear an appeal if the case “raises a question of public importance,” the court states on its website.
According to the Court, a case that meets that bar for appeal could include one that involves the interpretation of constitutional rights, or if it raises a new issue of law or if it requires the Court to resolve conflicting decisions from courts of appeal.
Ontario NDP Leader Marit Stiles told reporters Tuesday that CycleTO should “do what they need to do” and lambasted Ford for “wasting money” by ripping up Toronto’s bike lanes. She accused the premier of having an “obsession” with the city’s cyclists instead of focusing on the province’s fledgling healthcare system.
“We should have never gotten to this place,” said Stiles. “It’s absolutely absurd. It’s also government overreach,” she said.

title: GoldBod gets BoG authorisation to sell forex, Sammy Gyamfi tells PAC
body: The Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod), Sammy Gyamfi, has disclosed that the institution has received authorisation and guidance from the Bank of Ghana (BoG) to sell foreign exchange generated through its statutory operations. Appearing before Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee (PAC) on Tuesday, October 13, Mr Gyamfi stressed that GoldBod does not trade in currencies but sells foreign exchange earned from its gold-related activities to the central bank. “We are a major foreign exchange earner for the country. We only sell foreign exchange that we generate from our statutory functions to the Bank of Ghana,” he said. His clarification comes amid scrutiny of the Board’s operations and its role in generating foreign exchange to support Ghana’s economy and strengthen the country’s external reserves. Mr Gyamfi also told the committee that GoldBod was on course to meet or exceed its 2025 gold purchase and export performance while substantially increasing its foreign exchange earnings. He said the institution remained committed to its statutory mandate of generating foreign exchange, supporting national reserve accumulation and regulating the country’s gold trading sector. “This year we are on track to at least meet and possibly exceed our 2025 gold purchase and export targets, as well as substantially exceeding our foreign exchange generation targets for the year 2025, which was 10.8 billion United States dollars,” he said. The GoldBod CEO further disclosed that between 80 and 90 per cent of the gold purchased and exported by the Board was now being refined locally before export, creating jobs and retaining refining fees within the domestic economy. “That means jobs for the unemployed youth because these refineries are operating 24/7, employing Ghanaians, and the refining fees which would have ended up in export destinations are being retained in our economy,” he said. He added that silver recovered as a by-product of gold refining was also being retained in Ghana, generating foreign exchange and supplying raw materials to the local fabrication industry.

title: ‘We've been given the chance to live again’: Alon Ohel and Eli Sharabi talk about life after Hamas captivity
body: A year after Alon Ohel was released from Hamas captivity, he and fellow former hostage Eli Sharabi reunited Tuesday for a joint interview at ynet's "People of the Nation" conference, reflecting on the friendship they formed during a year and two months together in Gaza tunnels, their lives since returning home and the everyday freedoms they no longer take for granted. Sharabi, a resident of Kibbutz Be'eri, was released in February 2025 after 491 days in captivity. Ohel, a pianist abducted at age 22 from the Nova music festival, was freed in October 2025 alongside the last living hostages, after 738 days.   ‘All of Israel was part of it’ Neither man imagined what life would look like after his release from captivity. "We never imagined we'd become such well-known figures," Sharabi said. Following his release after 491 days, he became one of the most prominent voices advocating for the hostages who remained in Gaza. "We couldn't believe that all of Israel was so involved in this," he said. Sharabi had imagined his wife and daughters running toward him at the border upon his return. Only after his release did he learn that his wife, Lianne, and their daughters, Noiya and Yahel, had been murdered in Be'eri. His brother Yossi had also been abducted and killed in captivity. "Everything that came afterward was completely unexpected," Sharabi continued. "But ultimately, there are certain realities you wake up to in the morning, and you have to figure out what to do with them. And that's it. The rest is history." Ohel said he had expected to have to take care of everything himself after returning home. "When I got out, I realized my parents had taken care of me," he said. "Today, I'm mainly focused on my rehabilitation and my music."   Asked whether people they encounter on the street tend to cry or hug them, Ohel answered: "Both together." "Sometimes you practically have to pick people up off the floor, really. They're so incredibly emotional, and I give all that love back," Sharabi added. "I'm the most approachable person in the world." He acknowledged that his approach to public attention had changed. "I used to be a private person, but after everything the people of Israel did for us, it's the least I can do." ‘I'm incredibly proud of it’ The friendship the two men developed in captivity has continued since their release. "We talk, we meet. We're both very busy people, and we try to do it as much as possible," Sharabi said. Asked about the private jokes they share, he explained: "There are things that stayed with us from there. Of course, we laugh about them, remember them and get emotional together."   "We're also very different people," Sharabi said. "There are a lot of similarities, too," Ohel added. Sharabi pointed to a few unexpected connections between them. "He was born on February 10, and I was born on February 13. I worked 200 meters from his father and simply didn't know it." More important than those coincidences, Sharabi said, was the fact that they shared similar values. "That was the foundation on which we were able to build this incredibly close and caring friendship, and I'm prouder of it than anything in the world." The little things that are no longer taken for granted Asked what ordinary activity they appreciate most after being deprived of it in captivity, Ohel had a simple answer: "Opening the refrigerator." For Sharabi, it was taking a hot shower. "You don't take it for granted after showering with half a bucket of cold water once every six weeks, sometimes once every two months," he said. "Begging for showers, begging to shave, begging for everything." Even the frustration of sitting in traffic has returned, although Sharabi said it rarely lasts. "Very quickly, you tell yourself, 'I have all the time in the world.'" Asked when they had last felt happy, Ohel replied: "All the time, all the time." Sharabi added: "Every day I have my family beside me, my friends and the things I do."  "We're alive," Ohel said. "We've been given the chance to live again." ‘I'm in an amazing relationship’ Ohel is in a relationship with Goni, a childhood friend who campaigned for his release. Asked whether he had brought her to Sharabi for his approval, Sharabi replied: "Far from it." Ohel explained what he valued about being in a relationship with someone who knew him before captivity. "She really knows you, not just what people said or told her about you," he said. "I think it's much more open and free, without defenses." Sharabi revealed that he, too, has been in a relationship for about six months. "I'm in an amazing relationship. I'm happy, and everything is good." When asked to share more about his partner, however, he drew a firm boundary. "That's my private life. Absolutely not." ‘There isn't a day I don't cry’ The two men offered different perspectives on how their time in captivity had changed them. "I haven't changed at all," Sharabi insisted. "The situation changed, but Eli is still Eli." Ohel saw things differently. "I was kidnapped at 22. Today I'm 25. Without a doubt, what I went through shaped me." Sharabi said his sense of humor had always been an essential part of his personality. "I'm a joker. I don't know how to get through a day or even an hour without joking around. It's always been part of me." He said he also finds himself crying frequently. "I think I'm making up for all the days in captivity when I didn't cry. There isn't a day I don't cry," he said. "Most of the time, I cry because I'm moved. But of course, I also cry because of an enormous sense of longing. It exists alongside life. It doesn't stop me from living." Ohel said he also sees crying as an important emotional release. "I think it's a way of letting things out, and it's important. I don't try to hide it, either." From diving in Thailand to a stroller and a baby Asked what moment from before October 7 he would most like to share with Ohel, Sharabi recalled his travels in Thailand. "I would have liked him to go diving with me," he said. "I had incredible days of diving in Thailand, and we talked about it throughout our entire captivity." When asked where he hoped to see Ohel in three years, Sharabi offered a particularly personal wish. "I'd love to see him with a stroller, with a baby. He'll be an amazing father," he said. "And in those moments when he says, 'Enough, I've had it,' I'll take the baby and look after him. I'll be there for him." "That will definitely happen," Ohel replied. Asked what he wished for Sharabi, Ohel said: "That you live your life and travel nonstop, just like we always talked about. Just enjoy yourself." ‘We must stay united, not only when things are hard’ At the end of the interview, three years after October 7, the two men were asked to share a message with the Israeli public. "Every day that passes never comes back. Enjoy yourselves," Sharabi said. "Don't take your family for granted. Hug them every day. Appreciate the basic things in life, the things that really matter, not material possessions." Ohel concluded with a call for unity. "We need so much to remain united and together. Not to be united only when things are hard, but also when things are good, and to keep it that way."

title: Police indict Israeli citizen for plotting terror attack in Jerusalem, pledging allegiance to ISIS
body: An 18-year-old resident of Umm el-Fahm was indicted on Tuesday for planning a terrorist attack against IDF soldiers in the Old City of Jerusalem and pledging allegiance to the Islamic State (ISIS) terrorist organization.The indictment came after a month-long investigation by Israel Police and the Shin Bet (Israel Security Agency) into suspicions that the man was involved in serious offenses against national security, maintained membership in a terrorist organization, and was preparing to commit a terrorist act.The suspect was arrested as part of the investigation, and police searched his home, seizing digital materials and evidence that substantiated suspicions that the 18-year-old was involved in terrorist activity and planning an attack.Multiple ISIS-related indictments filed in past monthsThe indictment was the most recent in a series of arrests and indictments of individuals suspected to be involved with ISIS. In late August and early September, authorities arrested four individuals, including one minor, on suspicion of similar offenses. Most recently, a 19-year-old resident of the northern Israeli village of Shibli was indicted for membership in a terrorist organization on September 7.Investigators alleged that the 19-year-old had expressed support for ISIS, watched material about the terrorist organization, and pledged allegiance to it.Sarah Ben-Nun contributed to this report.
